1.4.s:
..sūta uvāca..
tato dvijauḥ parivṛtaṃ nāradaṃ devapūjitam..
abhigamyopajagrāha sarvānatha sa pāṇḍavaḥ.. 2.1 ..
1.4.d:
..सूत उवाच..
ततो द्विजौः परिवृतं नारदं देवपूजितम्..
अभिगम्योपजग्राह सर्वानथ स पाण्डवः.. 2.1 ..
1.4.m: Sūta said: / Then that son of Pāṇḍu, having approached Nārada who was surrounded by brahmins and worshipped by the gods, paid homage to them all.

1.4.s:
tatastaṃ nāradaḥ prāha jayārātidhanaṃjaya..
dharme bhavati te buddhirdeveṣu brāhmaṇeṣu ca.. 2.2 ..
1.4.d:
ततस्तं नारदः प्राह जयारातिधनंजय..
धर्मे भवति ते बुद्धिर्देवेषु ब्राह्मणेषु च.. 2.2 ..
1.4.m: Then Nārada said to him: “O Dhanañjaya, conqueror of enemies, / your mind is devoted to righteousness, to the gods, and to the brahmins.

1.4.s:
kaccidetāṃ mahāyātrāṃ vīra dvādaśavāraṣikīm..
ācarankhidyase naivamatha vā kupyase na ca.. 2.3 ..
1.4.d:
कच्चिदेतां महायात्रां वीर द्वादशवारषिकीम्..
आचरन्खिद्यसे नैवमथ वा कुप्यसे न च.. 2.3 ..
1.4.m: I hope that while performing this great pilgrimage of twelve years, O hero, / you do not feel distress or anger in this way.

1.4.s:
munīnāmapi cetāṃsi tīrthayātrāsu pāṃḍava..
khidyaṃti parikṛpyaṃti śreyasāṃ vighnamūlataḥ.. 2.4 ..
1.4.d:
मुनीनामपि चेतांसि तीर्थयात्रासु पांडव..
खिद्यंति परिकृप्यंति श्रेयसां विघ्नमूलतः.. 2.4 ..
1.4.m: Even the minds of sages, O son of Pāṇḍu, on pilgrimages to sacred fords, / are distressed and agitated due to obstacles to spiritual welfare.

1.4.s:
kaccinnaitena doṣeṇa samāśliṣṭo'si pāṃḍava..
atra cāṃgirasā gītāṃ gāthāmetāṃ hi śuśruma.. 2.5 ..
1.4.d:
कच्चिन्नैतेन दोषेण समाश्लिष्टोऽसि पांडव..
अत्र चांगिरसा गीतां गाथामेतां हि शुश्रुम.. 2.5 ..
1.4.m: I hope you are not touched by this fault, O son of Pāṇḍu. / In this regard, we have indeed heard this verse sung by Aṅgiras:

1.4.s:
yasya hastau ca pādau ca manaścaiva susaṃyatam..
nirvikārāḥ kriyāḥ sarvāḥ sa tīrthaphalamaśnute.. 2.6 ..
1.4.d:
यस्य हस्तौ च पादौ च मनश्चैव सुसंयतम्..
निर्विकाराः क्रियाः सर्वाः स तीर्थफलमश्नुते.. 2.6 ..
1.4.m: ‘He whose hands, feet, and mind are well restrained, / and all of whose actions are free from agitation, obtains the fruit of a sacred ford.’

1.4.s:
tadidaṃ hṛdi dhāryaṃ te kiṃ vā tvaṃ tāta manyase..
bhrātā yudhiṣṭhiro yasya sakhā yasya sa keśavaḥ.. 2.7 ..
1.4.d:
तदिदं हृदि धार्यं ते किं वा त्वं तात मन्यसे..
भ्राता युधिष्ठिरो यस्य सखा यस्य स केशवः.. 2.7 ..
1.4.m: Therefore, this is to be held in your heart; or what do you think, dear friend? / You whose brother is Yudhiṣṭhira, and whose companion is Keśava!

1.4.s:
punaretatsamucitaṃ yadvipraiḥ śikṣaṇaṃ nṛṇām..
vayaṃ hi dharmaguravaḥ sthāpitāstena viṣṇunā.. 2.8 ..
1.4.d:
पुनरेतत्समुचितं यद्विप्रैः शिक्षणं नृणाम्..
वयं हि धर्मगुरवः स्थापितास्तेन विष्णुना.. 2.8 ..
1.4.m: Moreover, it is appropriate that brahmins instruct men; / for we have been established as the teachers of righteousness by that Viṣṇu.

1.4.s: viṣṇunā cātra śrṛṇumo gītāṃ gāthāṃ dvijānprati.. 2.9 ..
1.4.d: विष्णुना चात्र श्रृणुमो गीतां गाथां द्विजान्प्रति.. 2.9 ..
1.4.m: And here we have heard a verse sung by Viṣṇu concerning brahmins:

1.4.s:
yasyāmalāmṛtayaśaḥśravaṇāvagāhaḥ sadyaḥ punāti jagadā śvapacādvikuṃṭhaḥ..
sohaṃ bhavadbhirupalabdha sutīrthakīrtiśchadyāṃ svabāhumapi yaḥ pratikūlavartī.. 2.10 ..
1.4.d:
यस्यामलामृतयशःश्रवणावगाहः सद्यः पुनाति जगदा श्वपचाद्विकुंठः..
सोहं भवद्भिरुपलब्ध सुतीर्थकीर्तिश्छद्यां स्वबाहुमपि यः प्रतिकूलवर्ती.. 2.10 ..
1.4.m: ‘Plunging into hearing the spotless, nectar-like fame of him who is Vaikuṇṭha instantly purifies the world down to an outcaste. / Such am I, whose fame concerning excellent sacred fords has been attained through you; I would cut off even my own arm if it acts contrary to them.’

1.4.s:
priyaṃ ca pārtha te brūmo yeṣāṃ kuśalakāmukaḥ..
sarve kuśalinaste ca yādavāḥ pāṃḍavāstathā.. 2.11 ..
1.4.d:
प्रियं च पार्थ ते ब्रूमो येषां कुशलकामुकः..
सर्वे कुशलिनस्ते च यादवाः पांडवास्तथा.. 2.11 ..
1.4.m: And we tell you pleasing news, O son of Pṛthā, concerning those whose welfare you desire: / they are all well—both the Yādavas and the Pāṇḍavas.

1.4.s:
adhunā bhīmasenena kurūṇāmupatāpakaḥ..
śāsanāddhṛtarāṣṭrasya vīravarmā nṛpo hataḥ.. 2.12 ..
1.4.d:
अधुना भीमसेनेन कुरूणामुपतापकः..
शासनाद्धृतराष्ट्रस्य वीरवर्मा नृपो हतः.. 2.12 ..
1.4.m: Just now King Vīravarmā, the tormentor of the Kurus, / has been slain by Bhīmasena by order of Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

1.4.s:
sa hi rājñāmajeyo'bhūdyathāpūrvaṃ balirbalī..
kaṃṭakaṃ kaṃṭakeneva dhṛtarāṣṭro jigāya tam.. 2.13 ..
1.4.d:
स हि राज्ञामजेयोऽभूद्यथापूर्वं बलिर्बली..
कंटकं कंटकेनेव धृतराष्ट्रो जिगाय तम्.. 2.13 ..
1.4.m: For he was invincible to kings, just as the mighty Bali was in former times; / Dhṛtarāṣṭra conquered him, removing a thorn with a thorn.

1.4.s:
ityādināradaproktāṃ vācamākarṇya phālgunaḥ..
atīva muditaḥ prāha teṣāmakuśalaṃ kutaḥ.. 2.14 ..
1.4.d:
इत्यादिनारदप्रोक्तां वाचमाकर्ण्य फाल्गुनः..
अतीव मुदितः प्राह तेषामकुशलं कुतः.. 2.14 ..
1.4.m: Having heard these and other words spoken by Nārada, Phālguna, / exceedingly delighted, said: “Whence could ill fortune come to them,

1.4.s:
ye brāhmaṇamate nityaṃ ye ca brāhmaṇapūjakāḥ..
ahaṃ ca śaktyā niyatastīrthāni vicarannanu.. 2.15 ..
1.4.d:
ये ब्राह्मणमते नित्यं ये च ब्राह्मणपूजकाः..
अहं च शक्त्या नियतस्तीर्थानि विचरन्ननु.. 2.15 ..
1.4.m: who always follow the counsel of brahmins and who worship brahmins? / And I, properly self-restrained, wandering among sacred fords according to my ability,

1.4.s:
āgatastīrthametaddhi pramodo'tīva me hṛdi..
tīrthānāṃ darśanaṃ dhanyamavagāhastato'dhikaḥ.. 2.16 ..
1.4.d:
आगतस्तीर्थमेतद्धि प्रमोदोऽतीव मे हृदि..
तीर्थानां दर्शनं धन्यमवगाहस्ततोऽधिकः.. 2.16 ..
1.4.m: have come to this sacred ford, and there is great joy in my heart. / Seeing sacred fords is auspicious, but bathing in them is still greater;

1.4.s:
māhātmyaśravaṇaṃ tasmādaurvopi munirabravīt..
tadahaṃ śrotumicchāmi tīrthasyāsya guṇānmune.. 2.17 ..
1.4.d:
माहात्म्यश्रवणं तस्मादौर्वोपि मुनिरब्रवीत्..
तदहं श्रोतुमिच्छामि तीर्थस्यास्य गुणान्मुने.. 2.17 ..
1.4.m: and hearing the māhātmya is even greater than that—so the sage Aurva said. / Therefore, O sage, I wish to hear the merits of this sacred ford.

1.4.s:
etenaiva śrāvyametadyattvayāṃgīkṛtaṃ mune..
tvaṃ hi trilokīṃ vicaranvetsi sarvāṃ hi sāratām.. 2.18 ..
1.4.d:
एतेनैव श्राव्यमेतद्यत्त्वयांगीकृतं मुने..
त्वं हि त्रिलोकीं विचरन्वेत्सि सर्वां हि सारताम्.. 2.18 ..
1.4.m: This is especially worthy of being heard since it has been accepted by you, O sage. / For wandering through the three worlds, you know all the essential truth.

1.4.s: tadetatsarvatīrthebhyo'dhikaṃ manye tvadā hṛtam.. 2.19 ..
1.4.d: तदेतत्सर्वतीर्थेभ्योऽधिकं मन्ये त्वदा हृतम्.. 2.19 ..
1.4.m: Therefore, I consider this, which has been embraced by you, superior to all sacred fords.”

1.4.s:
..nārada uvāca..
ucitaṃ tava pārthaitadyatpṛcchasi guṇinguṇān..
guṇināmeva yujyante śrotuṃ dharmodbhavā guṇāḥ..
sādhūnāṃ dharmaśravaṇaiḥ kīrtanairyāti cānvaham.. 2.20 ..
1.4.d:
..नारद उवाच..
उचितं तव पार्थैतद्यत्पृच्छसि गुणिन्गुणान्..
गुणिनामेव युज्यन्ते श्रोतुं धर्मोद्भवा गुणाः..
साधूनां धर्मश्रवणैः कीर्तनैर्याति चान्वहम्.. 2.20 ..
1.4.m: Nārada said: / “It is proper for you, O son of Pṛthā, that as a virtuous man you ask about virtues; / virtues born of righteousness are suitable to be heard only by the virtuous. / The life of the good passes day by day in hearing and proclaiming righteousness,

1.4.s:
pāpānāmasadālāpairāyuryāti yathānvaham..
tadahaṃ kīrtayiṣyāmi tīrthasyāsya guṇānbahūn.. 2.21 ..
1.4.d:
पापानामसदालापैरायुर्याति यथान्वहम्..
तदहं कीर्तयिष्यामि तीर्थस्यास्य गुणान्बहून्.. 2.21 ..
1.4.m: just as the life of sinners passes day by day in idle and wicked chatter. / Therefore I shall proclaim the many virtues of this sacred ford,

1.4.s:
yathā śrutvā vijānāsi yuktamaṃgīkṛtaṃ mayā..
purāhaṃ vicaranpārtha trilokīṃ kapilānugaḥ.. 2.22 ..
1.4.d:
यथा श्रुत्वा विजानासि युक्तमंगीकृतं मया..
पुराहं विचरन्पार्थ त्रिलोकीं कपिलानुगः.. 2.22 ..
1.4.m: so that, having heard, you may know it was rightly accepted by me. / Formerly, wandering through the three worlds following Kapila, O son of Pṛthā,

1.4.s:
gatavānbrahmaṇo lokaṃ tatrāpaśyaṃ pitāmaham..
sa hi rājarṣidevar‌ṣimūrtāmūrtaiḥ susaṃvṛtaḥ.. 2.23 ..
1.4.d:
गतवान्ब्रह्मणो लोकं तत्रापश्यं पितामहम्..
स हि राजर्षिदेवर्‌षिमूर्तामूर्तैः सुसंवृतः.. 2.23 ..
1.4.m: I went to the world of Brahmā, and there I saw the Grandfather. / He was surrounded by royal seers and divine seers, both embodied and formless.

1.4.s:
vibhāti vimalo brahmā nakṣatrairuḍurāḍiva..
tamahaṃ praṇipatyātha cakṣuṣā kṛtasvāgataḥ.. 2.24 ..
1.4.d:
विभाति विमलो ब्रह्मा नक्षत्रैरुडुराडिव..
तमहं प्रणिपत्याथ चक्षुषा कृतस्वागतः.. 2.24 ..
1.4.m: Spotless Brahmā shone like the moon, the king of stars, amid the constellations. / Having bowed to him, after being welcomed by him with his glance,

1.4.s:
uviṣṭaḥ pramuditaḥ kapilena sahaiva ca..
etasminnaṃtare tatra vārtikāḥ samupāgatāḥ.. 2.25 ..
1.4.d:
उविष्टः प्रमुदितः कपिलेन सहैव च..
एतस्मिन्नंतरे तत्र वार्तिकाः समुपागताः.. 2.25 ..
1.4.m: I sat down delighted, together with Kapila. / In the meantime, messengers arrived there.

1.4.s:
prahīyaṃte hi te nityaṃ jagaddraṣṭuṃ hi brahmaṇā..
kṛtapraṇāmānatha tānsamāsīnānpitāmahaḥ.. 2.26 ..
1.4.d:
प्रहीयंते हि ते नित्यं जगद्द्रष्टुं हि ब्रह्मणा..
कृतप्रणामानथ तान्समासीनान्पितामहः.. 2.26 ..
1.4.m: For they are constantly sent forth by Brahmā to observe the world. / Then to those who had bowed and were seated, the Grandfather,

1.4.s:
cakṣuṣāmṛtakalpena plāvayanniva cābravīt..
kutra kutra vicīrṇaṃ vo dṛṣṭaṃ śrutamathāpi vā.. 2.27 ..
1.4.d:
चक्षुषामृतकल्पेन प्लावयन्निव चाब्रवीत्..
कुत्र कुत्र विचीर्णं वो दृष्टं श्रुतमथापि वा.. 2.27 ..
1.4.m: as though showering them with his nectar-like gaze, said: / ‘Where and where have you wandered? What has been seen or heard?

1.4.s:
kiṃcidevādbhutaṃ brūta śravaṇādyena puṇyatā..
evamukte bhagavatā teṣāṃ yaḥ pravaro mataḥ.. 2.28 ..
1.4.d:
किंचिदेवाद्भुतं ब्रूत श्रवणाद्येन पुण्यता..
एवमुक्ते भगवता तेषां यः प्रवरो मतः.. 2.28 ..
1.4.m: Tell of something wondrous, by hearing which purity is attained.’ / When spoken to in this way by the Lord, the one who was considered the foremost among them,

1.4.s:
suśravānāma brahmāṇaṃ praṇipatyedamūcivān..
prabhoragre ca vijñaptiryathā dīpo ravestathā.. 2.29 ..
1.4.d:
सुश्रवानाम ब्रह्माणं प्रणिपत्येदमूचिवान्..
प्रभोरग्रे च विज्ञप्तिर्यथा दीपो रवेस्तथा.. 2.29 ..
1.4.m: named Suśravas, bowed to Brahmā and said this: / ‘An address before the Lord is like a lamp before the sun;

1.4.s:
tathāpi khalu vācyaṃ me parārthaṃ preritena te..
muniḥ kātyāyanonāma śrutvā dharmānpunarbahūn.. 2.30 ..
1.4.d:
तथापि खलु वाच्यं मे परार्थं प्रेरितेन ते..
मुनिः कात्यायनोनाम श्रुत्वा धर्मान्पुनर्बहून्.. 2.30 ..
1.4.m: nevertheless, it must be spoken by me, impelled by you for the sake of others. / A sage named Kātyāyana, having repeatedly heard of many duties,

1.4.s:
sārajijñāsayā tasthāvekāṃguṣṭhaḥ śataṃ samāḥ..
tataḥ provāca taṃ divyā vāṇī kātyāyana śrṛṇu.. 2.31 ..
1.4.d:
सारजिज्ञासया तस्थावेकांगुष्ठः शतं समाः..
ततः प्रोवाच तं दिव्या वाणी कात्यायन श्रृणु.. 2.31 ..
1.4.m: stood on a single big toe for a hundred years out of a desire to know the essence. / Then a divine voice spoke to him: “Listen, Kātyāyana!

1.4.s:
puṇye sarasvatītīre pṛccha sārasvataṃ munim..
sa te sāraṃ dharmasādhyaṃ dharmajño'bhivadiṣyati.. 2.32 ..
1.4.d:
पुण्ये सरस्वतीतीरे पृच्छ सारस्वतं मुनिम्..
स ते सारं धर्मसाध्यं धर्मज्ञोऽभिवदिष्यति.. 2.32 ..
1.4.m: On the holy bank of the Sarasvatī, ask the sage Sārasvata. / He, knower of righteousness, will declare to you the essence to be attained through righteousness.”

1.4.s:
iti śrutvā munivaro muniśreṣṭhamupetya tam..
praṇamya śirasā bhūmau papracchedaṃ hṛdi sthitam.. 2.33 ..
1.4.d:
इति श्रुत्वा मुनिवरो मुनिश्रेष्ठमुपेत्य तम्..
प्रणम्य शिरसा भूमौ पप्रच्छेदं हृदि स्थितम्.. 2.33 ..
1.4.m: Having heard this, the best of sages approached that foremost among sages; / bowing with his head to the earth, he asked this which was in his heart:

1.4.s:
satyaṃ kecitpraśaṃsaṃtitapaḥ śaucaṃ tathā pare..
sāṃkhyaṃ kecitpraśaṃsaṃti yogamanye pracakṣate.. 2.34 ..
1.4.d:
सत्यं केचित्प्रशंसंतितपः शौचं तथा परे..
सांख्यं केचित्प्रशंसंति योगमन्ये प्रचक्षते.. 2.34 ..
1.4.m: “Some praise truth; others praise austerity and purity; / some praise Sāṃkhya; others declare Yoga [to be the best].

1.4.s:
kṣamāṃ kecitpraśaṃsaṃti tathaiva bhṛśamārjjavam..
kecinmaunaṃ praśaṃsaṃti kecidāhuḥ paraṃ śrutam.. 2.35 ..
1.4.d:
क्षमां केचित्प्रशंसंति तथैव भृशमार्ज्जवम्..
केचिन्मौनं प्रशंसंति केचिदाहुः परं श्रुतम्.. 2.35 ..
1.4.m: Some praise forgiveness, and likewise utmost uprightness; / some praise silence, while others say sacred learning is supreme.

1.4.s:
samyagjñānaṃ praśaṃsaṃti kecidvairāgyamuttamam..
agniṣṭomādikarmāṇi tathā kecitparaṃ viduḥ.. 2.36 ..
1.4.d:
सम्यग्ज्ञानं प्रशंसंति केचिद्वैराग्यमुत्तमम्..
अग्निष्टोमादिकर्माणि तथा केचित्परं विदुः.. 2.36 ..
1.4.m: Some praise correct knowledge, others supreme dispassion; / and likewise some consider rituals such as the Agniṣṭoma supreme.

1.4.s:
ātmajñānaṃ paraṃ kecitsamaloṣṭāśmakāṃcanam..
itthaṃ vyavasthite loke kṛtyākṛtyavidhau janāḥ.. 2.37 ..
1.4.d:
आत्मज्ञानं परं केचित्समलोष्टाश्मकांचनम्..
इत्थं व्यवस्थिते लोके कृत्याकृत्यविधौ जनाः.. 2.37 ..
1.4.m: Some consider self-knowledge supreme, regarding a clod of earth, a stone, and gold as equal. / In this way, when the world is divided concerning what ought and ought not to be done, people

1.4.s:
vyāmohameva gacchaṃti kiṃ śreya iti vādinaḥ..
yadeteṣu paraṃ kṛtyam nuṣṭheyaṃ mahātmabhiḥ.. 2.38 ..
1.4.d:
व्यामोहमेव गच्छंति किं श्रेय इति वादिनः..
यदेतेषु परं कृत्यम् नुष्ठेयं महात्मभिः.. 2.38 ..
1.4.m: fall into delusion, arguing about what is the highest good. / What, among these, is the supreme duty to be performed by great souls?

1.4.s: vaktumarhasi dharmajña mama sarvārthasādhakam.. 2.39 ..
1.4.d: वक्तुमर्हसि धर्मज्ञ मम सर्वार्थसाधकम्.. 2.39 ..
1.4.m: You ought to tell me, O knower of righteousness, that which accomplishes all aims.”

1.4.s:
..sārasvata uvāca..
yanmāṃ sarasvatī prāha sāraṃ vakṣyāmi tacchṛṇu..
chāyākāraṃ jagatsarvamutpattikṣayadharmi ca..
vārāṃganānetrabhaṃgasvadvadbhaṃgurameva tat.. 2.40 ..
1.4.d:
..सारस्वत उवाच..
यन्मां सरस्वती प्राह सारं वक्ष्यामि तच्छृणु..
छायाकारं जगत्सर्वमुत्पत्तिक्षयधर्मि च..
वारांगनानेत्रभंगस्वद्वद्भंगुरमेव तत्.. 2.40 ..
1.4.m: Sārasvata said: / “Listen to that essence which the Sarasvatī told me, and which I shall tell you: / The entire world is like a shadow, subject to origination and destruction;

1.4.s:
dhanāyuryauvanaṃ bhogāñjalacaṃdravadasthirān..
buddhyā samyakparāmṛśya sthāṇudānaṃ samāśrayet.. 2.41 ..
1.4.d:
धनायुर्यौवनं भोगाञ्जलचंद्रवदस्थिरान्..
बुद्ध्या सम्यक्परामृश्य स्थाणुदानं समाश्रयेत्.. 2.41 ..
1.4.m: it is as transient as the sweet flickering glance of a courtesan. / Reflecting properly with the intellect on wealth, life, youth, and pleasures as unsteady as the moon reflected in water, / one should resort to devotion to Sthāṇu and to giving.

1.4.s:
dānavānpuruṣaḥ pāpaṃ nālaṃ kartumiti śrutiḥ..
sthāṇubhakto janmamṛtyū nāpnotīti śruti stathā.. 2.42 ..
1.4.d:
दानवान्पुरुषः पापं नालं कर्तुमिति श्रुतिः..
स्थाणुभक्तो जन्ममृत्यू नाप्नोतीति श्रुति स्तथा.. 2.42 ..
1.4.m: ‘A man who gives is incapable of committing sin’—so says scripture. / ‘One devoted to Sthāṇu does not incur birth and death’—so likewise says scripture.

1.4.s:
sāvarṇinā ca gāthe dve kīrtite śrṛṇu ye purā..
vṛṣo hi bhagavāndharmo vṛṣabho yasya vāhanam.. 2.43 ..
1.4.d:
सावर्णिना च गाथे द्वे कीर्तिते श्रृणु ये पुरा..
वृषो हि भगवान्धर्मो वृषभो यस्य वाहनम्.. 2.43 ..
1.4.m: And listen to the two verses that were sung in former times by Sāvarṇi: / ‘Lord Dharma is indeed the Bull, and the bull is his mount.

1.4.s:
pūjyate sa mahādevaḥ sa dharmaḥ para ucyate..
duḥkhāvarte tamoghore dharmādharmajale tathā.. 2.44 ..
1.4.d:
पूज्यते स महादेवः स धर्मः पर उच्यते..
दुःखावर्ते तमोघोरे धर्माधर्मजले तथा.. 2.44 ..
1.4.m: That Mahādeva is worshipped; that is called the highest dharma. / In the whirlpool of suffering, terrible with darkness, and in the waters of dharma and adharma,

1.4.s:
krodhapaṃke madagrāhe lobhabudbadasaṃkaṭe..
mānagaṃbhīrapātāle sattvayānavibhūṣite.. 2.45 ..
1.4.d:
क्रोधपंके मदग्राहे लोभबुद्बदसंकटे..
मानगंभीरपाताले सत्त्वयानविभूषिते.. 2.45 ..
1.4.m: In the mire of anger, the crocodile of arrogance, crowded with the bubbles of greed, / In the deep underworld of conceit, adorned with creatures for vehicles,

1.4.s:
majjaṃtaṃ tārayatyeko haraḥ saṃsārasāgarāt..
dānaṃ vṛttaṃ vrataṃ vācaḥ kīrtidharmau tathāyuṣaḥ.. 2.46 ..
1.4.d:
मज्जंतं तारयत्येको हरः संसारसागरात्..
दानं वृत्तं व्रतं वाचः कीर्तिधर्मौ तथायुषः.. 2.46 ..
1.4.m: Hara alone rescues the drowning [man] from the ocean of worldly existence. / Generosity, good conduct, observance, speech, fame, dharma, and likewise lifespan—

1.4.s:
paropakaraṇaṃ kāyādasārātsāramuddharet..
dharme rāgaḥ śrutau ciṃtā dāne vyasanamuttamam.. 2.47 ..
1.4.d:
परोपकरणं कायादसारात्सारमुद्धरेत्..
धर्मे रागः श्रुतौ चिंता दाने व्यसनमुत्तमम्.. 2.47 ..
1.4.m: One should extract the essence, helping others, from the essenceless body. / Attachment to dharma, contemplation on sacred tradition, supreme addiction to giving,

1.4.s:
iṃdriyārtheṣu vairāgyaṃ saṃprāptaṃ janmanaḥ phalam..
deśe'sminbhārate janma prāpya mānuṣyamadhruvam.. 2.48 ..
1.4.d:
इंद्रियार्थेषु वैराग्यं संप्राप्तं जन्मनः फलम्..
देशेऽस्मिन्भारते जन्म प्राप्य मानुष्यमध्रुवम्.. 2.48 ..
1.4.m: Dispassion regarding sensory objects—[thus] the fruit of birth is attained. / Having obtained unsteady human birth in this land of Bhārata,

1.4.s:
na kuryādātmanaḥ śreyastenātmā vaṃcataściram..
devāsurāṇāṃ sarveṣāṃ mānuṣyamatidurlabham.. 2.49 ..
1.4.d:
न कुर्यादात्मनः श्रेयस्तेनात्मा वंचतश्चिरम्..
देवासुराणां सर्वेषां मानुष्यमतिदुर्लभम्.. 2.49 ..
1.4.m: If one does not work for the welfare of oneself, by that one deceives oneself for a long time. / Human birth is extremely difficult to attain for all gods and demons.

1.4.s:
tatsaṃprāpya tathā kuryānna gacchennarakaṃ yathā..
sarvasya mūlaṃ mānuṣyaṃ tathā sarvārthasādhakam.. 2.50 ..
1.4.d:
तत्संप्राप्य तथा कुर्यान्न गच्छेन्नरकं यथा..
सर्वस्य मूलं मानुष्यं तथा सर्वार्थसाधकम्.. 2.50 ..
1.4.m: Having obtained it, one should act in such a way that one does not go to hell. / Human birth is the root of everything, and the accomplisher of all aims.

1.4.s:
yadi lābhe na yatnaste mūlaṃ rakṣa prayatnataḥ..
mahatā puṇyamūlyena krīyate kāyanaustvayā.. 2.51 ..
1.4.d:
यदि लाभे न यत्नस्ते मूलं रक्ष प्रयत्नतः..
महता पुण्यमूल्येन क्रीयते कायनौस्त्वया.. 2.51 ..
1.4.m: If you have no effort toward gain, protect the root with diligence. / With the great price of merit, you have bought the boat of the body,

1.4.s:
gaṃtuṃ duḥkhodadheḥ pāraṃ tara yāvanna bhidyate..
avikāriśarīratvaṃ duṣprāpyaṃ vai tataḥ.. 2.52 ..
1.4.d:
गंतुं दुःखोदधेः पारं तर यावन्न भिद्यते..
अविकारिशरीरत्वं दुष्प्राप्यं वै ततः.. 2.52 ..
1.4.m: To go to the other shore of the ocean of sorrow; cross over while it does not break! / A state of the body free from illness is indeed hard to obtain; then,

1.4.s:
nāpakrāmati saṃsārādātmahā sa narādhamaḥ..
tapastapyanti yatayo juhvate cātra yajvinaḥ..
dānāni cātra dīyaṃte paralokārthamādarāt.. 2.53 ..
1.4.d:
नापक्रामति संसारादात्महा स नराधमः..
तपस्तप्यन्ति यतयो जुह्वते चात्र यज्विनः..
दानानि चात्र दीयंते परलोकार्थमादरात्.. 2.53 ..
1.4.m: He who does not depart from worldly existence is a destroyer of himself, the lowest of men. / Here ascetics perform austerity, and here sacrificers offer oblations; / And here gifts are given with respect for the sake of the next world.

1.4.s:
..kātyāyana uvāca..
dānasya tapaso vāpi bhagavankiṃ ca duṣkaram..
kiṃ vā mahatphalaṃ pretya sārasvata bravīhi tat.. 2.54 ..
1.4.d:
..कात्यायन उवाच..
दानस्य तपसो वापि भगवन्किं च दुष्करम्..
किं वा महत्फलं प्रेत्य सारस्वत ब्रवीहि तत्.. 2.54 ..
1.4.m: Kātyāyana said: / O Lord, what is harder to perform—giving or austerity? / Or what yields great fruit after death? O Sārasvata, tell me that!

1.4.s:
..sārasvata uvāca..
na dānādduṣkarataraṃ pṛthivyāmasti kiṃcana..
mune pratyakṣamevaitaddṛśyate lokasākṣikam.. 2.55 ..
1.4.d:
..सारस्वत उवाच..
न दानाद्दुष्करतरं पृथिव्यामस्ति किंचन..
मुने प्रत्यक्षमेवैतद्दृश्यते लोकसाक्षिकम्.. 2.55 ..
1.4.m: Sārasvata said: / There is nothing on earth more difficult to perform than giving. / O sage, this is witnessed before one's eyes with the world as a witness.

1.4.s:
parityajya priyānprāṇāndhanārthe hi mahābhayam..
praviśaṃti mahālobhātsamudramaṭavīṃ girim.. 2.56 ..
1.4.d:
परित्यज्य प्रियान्प्राणान्धनार्थे हि महाभयम्..
प्रविशंति महालोभात्समुद्रमटवीं गिरिम्.. 2.56 ..
1.4.m: Having abandoned their dear lives for the sake of wealth, into great danger / They enter the ocean, the forest, and the mountain out of extreme greed.

1.4.s:
sevāmanye prapadyaṃte śvavṛttiriti yā smṛtā..
hiṃsāprāyāṃ bahukleśāṃ kṛṣiṃ caiva tathā pare.. 2.57 ..
1.4.d:
सेवामन्ये प्रपद्यंते श्ववृत्तिरिति या स्मृता..
हिंसाप्रायां बहुक्लेशां कृषिं चैव तथा परे.. 2.57 ..
1.4.m: Others take up service, which is remembered as 'a dog's livelihood'; / And others still [take up] agriculture, full of violence and involving much misery.

1.4.s:
tasya duḥkhārjitasyeha prāṇebhyopi garīyasaḥ..
āyāsaśatalabdhasya parityāgaḥ suduṣkaraḥ.. 2.58 ..
1.4.d:
तस्य दुःखार्जितस्येह प्राणेभ्योपि गरीयसः..
आयासशतलब्धस्य परित्यागः सुदुष्करः.. 2.58 ..
1.4.m: Of that [wealth] acquired with difficulty in this world, dearer even than life, / Obtained through hundreds of labors, renunciation is exceedingly difficult.

1.4.s:
yaddadāti yadaśnāti tadeva dhanino dhanam..
anye mṛtasya krīḍaṃti dārairapi dhanairapi.. 2.59 ..
1.4.d:
यद्ददाति यदश्नाति तदेव धनिनो धनम्..
अन्ये मृतस्य क्रीडंति दारैरपि धनैरपि.. 2.59 ..
1.4.m: What he gives away and what he eats, that alone is the wealth of the wealthy man; / When he is dead, others play with both his wives and his wealth.

1.4.s:
ahanyahani yācaṃtamahaṃ manye guruṃ yathā..
mārjanaṃ darpaṇasyeva yaḥ karoti dinedine.. 2.60 ..
1.4.d:
अहन्यहनि याचंतमहं मन्ये गुरुं यथा..
मार्जनं दर्पणस्येव यः करोति दिनेदिने.. 2.60 ..
1.4.m: Day after day I consider the beggar like a spiritual master, / Who day by day polishes [the mind] like a mirror.

1.4.s:
dīyamānaṃ hi nāpaiti bhūya evābhivardhate..
kūpa utsicyamāno hi bhavecchuddho bahūdakaḥ.. 2.61 ..
1.4.d:
दीयमानं हि नापैति भूय एवाभिवर्धते..
कूप उत्सिच्यमानो हि भवेच्छुद्धो बहूदकः.. 2.61 ..
1.4.m: For what is being given away does not diminish; indeed, it increases all the more. / A well being drawn from becomes pure and full of water.

1.4.s:
ekajanmasukhasyārthe sahasrāṇi vilāpayet..
prājño janmasahasreṣu saṃcinotyekajanmani.. 2.62 ..
1.4.d:
एकजन्मसुखस्यार्थे सहस्राणि विलापयेत्..
प्राज्ञो जन्मसहस्रेषु संचिनोत्येकजन्मनि.. 2.62 ..
1.4.m: For the sake of happiness in a single birth, [a fool] would waste thousands [of lives]; / The wise man amasses in a single birth [merit] for thousands of births.

1.4.s:
mūrkho hi na dadātyarthāniha dāridryaśaṃkayā..
prājñastu visṛjatyarthānamutra tasya śaṃkayā.. 2.63 ..
1.4.d:
मूर्खो हि न ददात्यर्थानिह दारिद्र्यशंकया..
प्राज्ञस्तु विसृजत्यर्थानमुत्र तस्य शंकया.. 2.63 ..
1.4.m: The fool indeed does not give away wealth out of fear of poverty in this world; / But the wise man distributes wealth out of fear of it in the other world.

1.4.s:
kiṃ dhanena kariṣyaṃti dehino bhaṃgurāśrayāḥ..
yadarthaṃ dhanamicchaṃti taccharīramaśāśvatam.. 2.64 ..
1.4.d:
किं धनेन करिष्यंति देहिनो भंगुराश्रयाः..
यदर्थं धनमिच्छंति तच्छरीरमशाश्वतम्.. 2.64 ..
1.4.m: What will embodied beings, who have a perishable refuge, do with wealth? / That body for the sake of which they desire wealth is impermanent.

1.4.s:
akṣaradvayamabhyastaṃ nāstināstīti yatpurā..
tadidaṃ dehidehiti viparītamupasthitam.. 2.65 ..
1.4.d:
अक्षरद्वयमभ्यस्तं नास्तिनास्तीति यत्पुरा..
तदिदं देहिदेहिति विपरीतमुपस्थितम्.. 2.65 ..
1.4.m: The two syllables, 'There is not, there is not,' which were repeated formerly— / That very thing has presented itself in reverse: 'Give, give!'

1.4.s:
bodhayaṃti ca yāvaṃto dehīti kṛpaṇaṃ janāḥ..
avastheyamadānasya mā bhūdevaṃ bhavānapi.. 2.66 ..
1.4.d:
बोधयंति च यावंतो देहीति कृपणं जनाः..
अवस्थेयमदानस्य मा भूदेवं भवानपि.. 2.66 ..
1.4.m: And all those people who wake one up [saying] miserably: 'Give!' [are saying]: / 'This is the state of nongiving; may you not also become like this!'

1.4.s:
dāturevopakārāya vadatyarthīti dehi me..
yasmāddātā prayātyūrdhvamadhastiṣṭhetpratigrahī.. 2.67 ..
1.4.d:
दातुरेवोपकाराय वदत्यर्थीति देहि मे..
यस्माद्दाता प्रयात्यूर्ध्वमधस्तिष्ठेत्प्रतिग्रही.. 2.67 ..
1.4.m: The requester says 'Give to me' solely for the benefit of the giver, / Because the giver ascends above, while the recipient stays below.

1.4.s:
daridrā vyādhitā mūrkhāḥ parapreṣyakarāḥ sadā..
adattadānājjāyaṃte duḥkhasyaiva hi bhājanāḥ.. 2.68 ..
1.4.d:
दरिद्रा व्याधिता मूर्खाः परप्रेष्यकराः सदा..
अदत्तदानाज्जायंते दुःखस्यैव हि भाजनाः.. 2.68 ..
1.4.m: The poor, the diseased, the foolish, and those who are always servants of others, / Are born from not having given gifts, receptacles of sorrow alone.

1.4.s:
dhanavaṃtamadātāraṃ daridraṃ vā'tapasvinam..
ubhāvaṃbhasi moktavyau kaṃṭhe baddhā mahāśilām.. 2.69 ..
1.4.d:
धनवंतमदातारं दरिद्रं वाऽतपस्विनम्..
उभावंभसि मोक्तव्यौ कंठे बद्धा महाशिलाम्.. 2.69 ..
1.4.m: A rich man who is not a giver, or a poor man who does not practice austerity— / Both should be cast into the water having bound a great stone around the neck.

1.4.s:
śateṣu jāyate śūraḥ sahasreṣu ca paṃḍitaḥ..
vaktā śatasahasreṣu dātā jāyeta vā na vā.. 2.70 ..
1.4.d:
शतेषु जायते शूरः सहस्रेषु च पंडितः..
वक्ता शतसहस्रेषु दाता जायेत वा न वा.. 2.70 ..
1.4.m: A hero is born among hundreds, and a scholar among thousands; / An orator among hundreds of thousands; a giver may or may not be born.

1.4.s:
gobhirvipraiśca vedaiśca satībhiḥ satyavādibhiḥ..
alubdhairdānaśīlaiśca saptabhirdhāryate mahī.. 2.71 ..
1.4.d:
गोभिर्विप्रैश्च वेदैश्च सतीभिः सत्यवादिभिः..
अलुब्धैर्दानशीलैश्च सप्तभिर्धार्यते मही.. 2.71 ..
1.4.m: By cows, brahmins, the Vedas, virtuous women, truthful people, / Those free from greed, and generous people—by these seven the earth is upheld.

1.4.s:
śibirauśīnaroṅgāni sutaṃ ca priyamaurasam..
brāhmaṇārthamupākṛtya nākapṛṣṭhamito gataḥ.. 2.72 ..
1.4.d:
शिबिरौशीनरोङ्गानि सुतं च प्रियमौरसम्..
ब्राह्मणार्थमुपाकृत्य नाकपृष्ठमितो गतः.. 2.72 ..
1.4.m: Śibi, king of Uśīnara, having offered his limbs and his dear legitimate son / For the sake of a brahmin, went from here to the surface of heaven.

1.4.s:
pratarddanaḥ kāśipati pradāya nayane svake..
brāhmaṇāyātulāṃ kīrtimiha cāmutra cāśnute.. 2.73 ..
1.4.d:
प्रतर्द्दनः काशिपति प्रदाय नयने स्वके..
ब्राह्मणायातुलां कीर्तिमिह चामुत्र चाश्नुते.. 2.73 ..
1.4.m: Pratardana, the king of Kāśi, having given his own two eyes / To a brahmin, enjoys matchless fame both in this world and in the next.

1.4.s:
nimī rāṣṭraṃ ca vaideho jāmadagnyo vasuṃdharām..
brāhmaṇebhyo dadau cāpi gayaścorvīṃ sapattanām.. 2.74 ..
1.4.d:
निमी राष्ट्रं च वैदेहो जामदग्न्यो वसुंधराम्..
ब्राह्मणेभ्यो ददौ चापि गयश्चोर्वीं सपत्तनाम्.. 2.74 ..
1.4.m: Nimi the king of Videha gave his kingdom, and the son of Jamadagni the earth / To brahmins; and Gaya gave the earth together with its cities.

1.4.s:
avarṣati ca parjanye sarvabhūtanivāsakṛt..
vasiṣṭho jīvayāmāsa prajāpatiriva prajāḥ.. 2.75 ..
1.4.d:
अवर्षति च पर्जन्ये सर्वभूतनिवासकृत्..
वसिष्ठो जीवयामास प्रजापतिरिव प्रजाः.. 2.75 ..
1.4.m: When the rain-cloud did not shower, Vasiṣṭha, who gives refuge to all beings, / Sustained the subjects like Prajāpati [sustains] his creatures.

1.4.s:
brahmadattaśca pāṃcālyo rājā buddhimatāṃ varaḥ..
nidhiṃ śaṃkhaṃ dvijāgryebhyo dattvā svargamavāptavān.. 2.76 ..
1.4.d:
ब्रह्मदत्तश्च पांचाल्यो राजा बुद्धिमतां वरः..
निधिं शंखं द्विजाग्र्येभ्यो दत्त्वा स्वर्गमवाप्तवान्.. 2.76 ..
1.4.m: And Brahmadatta, the king of the Pāñcālas, best among the wise, / Having given the Śaṅkha treasure to eminent brahmins, attained heaven.

1.4.s:
sahasrajicca rājarṣiḥ prāṇāniṣṭānmahāyaśāḥ..
brāhmaṇārthe parityajya gato lokānanuttamān.. 2.77 ..
1.4.d:
सहस्रजिच्च राजर्षिः प्राणानिष्टान्महायशाः..
ब्राह्मणार्थे परित्यज्य गतो लोकाननुत्तमान्.. 2.77 ..
1.4.m: And the royal seer Sahasrajit of great renown, having surrendered / His dear life for the sake of a brahmin, went to the highest worlds.

1.4.s:
ete cānye ca bahavaḥ sthāṇordānena bhaktitaḥ..
rudralokaṃ gatā nityaṃ śāntātmāno jitendriyāḥ.. 2.78 ..
1.4.d:
एते चान्ये च बहवः स्थाणोर्दानेन भक्तितः..
रुद्रलोकं गता नित्यं शान्तात्मानो जितेन्द्रियाः.. 2.78 ..
1.4.m: These and many others, through giving to Sthāṇu with devotion, / Have gone permanently to the world of Rudra, calmed in soul, with senses conquered.

1.4.s:
eṣāṃ pratiṣṭhitā kīrtiryāvatsthāsyati medinī..
iti saṃciṃtya sārārthī sthāṇudānaparo bhava.. 2.79 ..
1.4.d:
एषां प्रतिष्ठिता कीर्तिर्यावत्स्थास्यति मेदिनी..
इति संचिंत्य सारार्थी स्थाणुदानपरो भव.. 2.79 ..
1.4.m: Their fame is established as long as the earth shall endure; / Reflecting thus, desirous of the essence, be devoted to giving to Sthāṇu!

1.4.s: so'pi moha parityajya tathā kātyāyano'bhavat.. 2.80 ..
1.4.d: सोऽपि मोह परित्यज्य तथा कात्यायनोऽभवत्.. 2.80 ..
1.4.m: He too, abandoning delusion, became likewise, [namely] Kātyāyana.

1.4.s:
..nārada uvāca..
evaṃ suśravasā proktāṃ kathāmākarṇya padmabhūḥ..
harṣāśrusaṃyuto'tīva praśaśaṃsa muhurmuhuḥ.. 2.81 ..
1.4.d:
..नारद उवाच..
एवं सुश्रवसा प्रोक्तां कथामाकर्ण्य पद्मभूः..
हर्षाश्रुसंयुतोऽतीव प्रशशंस मुहुर्मुहुः.. 2.81 ..
1.4.m: Nārada said: / Having heard the story narrated thus by Suśravas, the Lotus-born [Brahmā], / Filled with tears of joy, praised [him] again and again exceedingly:

1.4.s:
sādhu te vyāhṛtaṃ vatsa evametanna cānyathā..
satyaṃ sārasvataḥ prāha satyā caivaṃ tathā śrutiḥ.. 2.82 ..
1.4.d:
साधु ते व्याहृतं वत्स एवमेतन्न चान्यथा..
सत्यं सारस्वतः प्राह सत्या चैवं तथा श्रुतिः.. 2.82 ..
1.4.m: Well spoken by you, dear child! It is thus and not otherwise. / Sārasvata spoke the truth, and the sacred tradition is also true in this way:

1.4.s: dānaṃ yajñānāṃ varūthaṃ dakṣiṇā loke dātāram̐sarvabhūtānyupajīvaṃti dānenārātīram̐pānudaṃta dānena dviṣaṃto mitrā bhavaṃti dāne sarvaṃ pratiṣṭhitaṃ tasmāddānaṃ paramaṃ vadaṃtīti.. 2.83 ..
1.4.d: दानं यज्ञानां वरूथं दक्षिणा लोके दातारम्̐सर्वभूतान्युपजीवंति दानेनारातीरम्̐पानुदंत दानेन द्विषंतो मित्रा भवंति दाने सर्वं प्रतिष्ठितं तस्माद्दानं परमं वदंतीति.. 2.83 ..
1.4.m: 'Giving is the armor of sacrifices; in the world all creatures live off the giver of the sacrificial fee; by giving they drive away enemies; through giving, foes become friends; in giving everything is established; therefore they say giving is supreme.'

1.4.s:
saṃsārasāgare ghore dharmādharmormisaṃkule..
dānaṃ tatra niṣeveta tacca nauriva nirmitam.. 2.84 ..
1.4.d:
संसारसागरे घोरे धर्माधर्मोर्मिसंकुले..
दानं तत्र निषेवेत तच्च नौरिव निर्मितम्.. 2.84 ..
1.4.m: In the terrible ocean of worldly existence, turbulent with the waves of dharma and adharma, / One should resort there to giving, and that is fashioned like a boat.

1.4.s:
iti saṃciṃtya ca mayā puṣkare sthāpitā dvijāḥ..
gaṅgāyamunayormadhye madhyadeśe dvijāḥ sṛte.. 2.85 ..
1.4.d:
इति संचिंत्य च मया पुष्करे स्थापिता द्विजाः..
गङ्गायमुनयोर्मध्ये मध्यदेशे द्विजाः सृते.. 2.85 ..
1.4.m: Thinking thus, brahmins were settled at Puṣkara by me; / Brahmins were created in the middle country, between the Gaṅgā and the Yamunā.

1.4.s:
sthāpitāḥ śrīharibhyāṃ tu śrīgauryā vedavittamāḥ..
rudreṇa nāgarāścaiva pārvatyā śaktipūrbhavāḥ.. 2.86 ..
1.4.d:
स्थापिताः श्रीहरिभ्यां तु श्रीगौर्या वेदवित्तमाः..
रुद्रेण नागराश्चैव पार्वत्या शक्तिपूर्भवाः.. 2.86 ..
1.4.m: The best knowers of the Veda were settled by Śrī and Hari, and by holy Gaurī; / The Nāgaras were settled by Rudra, and those born in Śaktipura by Pārvatī.

1.4.s:
śrīmāle ca tathā lakṣmyā hyevamādisurottamaiḥ..
nānāgrahārāḥ saṃdattā lokoddharaṇakāṃkṣayā.. 2.87 ..
1.4.d:
श्रीमाले च तथा लक्ष्म्या ह्येवमादिसुरोत्तमैः..
नानाग्रहाराः संदत्ता लोकोद्धरणकांक्षया.. 2.87 ..
1.4.m: And likewise in Śrīmāla by Lakṣmī, and thus by the foremost gods, / various land-grants were bestowed with the desire to deliver the world. // 2.87

1.4.s:
na hi dānaphale kāṃkṣā kācinna'sti surottamāḥ..
sādhusaṃrakṣaṇārthaṃ hi dānaṃ naḥ parikīrtitam.. 2.88 ..
1.4.d:
न हि दानफले कांक्षा काचिन्नऽस्ति सुरोत्तमाः..
साधुसंरक्षणार्थं हि दानं नः परिकीर्तितम्.. 2.88 ..
1.4.m: Indeed, O foremost among gods, there is no desire whatsoever for the fruit of gift-giving; / for giving gifts is proclaimed by us for the protection of the virtuous. // 2.88

1.4.s:
brāhmaṇāśca kṛtasthānā nānādharmopadeśanaiḥ..
samuddharaṃti varṇāṃstrīṃstataḥ pūjyatamā dvijāḥ.. 2.89 ..
1.4.d:
ब्राह्मणाश्च कृतस्थाना नानाधर्मोपदेशनैः..
समुद्धरंति वर्णांस्त्रींस्ततः पूज्यतमा द्विजाः.. 2.89 ..
1.4.m: And the brahmins, once established in their settlements, by teachings of diverse duties, / deliver the three castes; therefore the twice-born are most worthy of worship. // 2.89

1.4.s:
dānaṃ caturvidhaṃ dānamutsargaḥ kalpitaṃ tathā..
saṃśrutaṃ ceti vividhaṃ tatkramātparikīrtitam.. 2.90 ..
1.4.d:
दानं चतुर्विधं दानमुत्सर्गः कल्पितं तथा..
संश्रुतं चेति विविधं तत्क्रमात्परिकीर्तितम्.. 2.90 ..
1.4.m: Giving is fourfold: a simple gift, formal dedication, an intentional vow, / and a promised gift—thus diverse, it is proclaimed in order. // 2.90

1.4.s:
vāpīkūpataḍāgānāṃ vṛkṣavidyāsuraukasām..
maṭhaprapāgṛhakṣetradānamutsarga ityasau.. 2.91 ..
1.4.d:
वापीकूपतडागानां वृक्षविद्यासुरौकसाम्..
मठप्रपागृहक्षेत्रदानमुत्सर्ग इत्यसौ.. 2.91 ..
1.4.m: The donation of stepwells, wells, ponds, groves, learning, temples of the gods, / monasteries, water-booths, houses, and fields is called formal dedication. // 2.91

1.4.s:
upajīvannimānyaśca puṇyaṃ ko'pi carennaraḥ..
ṣaṣṭhamaṃśaṃ sa labhate yāvadyo visṛjeddvijaḥ.. 2.92 ..
1.4.d:
उपजीवन्निमान्यश्च पुण्यं कोऽपि चरेन्नरः..
षष्ठमंशं स लभते यावद्यो विसृजेद्द्विजः.. 2.92 ..
1.4.m: And whichever man, living off these, should practice merit, / the twice-born who dedicated them obtains a sixth share as long as it lasts. // 2.92

1.4.s:
tadeṣāmeva sarveṣāṃ viprasaṃsthāpanaṃ param..
devasaṃsthāpanaṃ caiva dharmastanmūla eva yat.. 2.93 ..
1.4.d:
तदेषामेव सर्वेषां विप्रसंस्थापनं परम्..
देवसंस्थापनं चैव धर्मस्तन्मूल एव यत्.. 2.93 ..
1.4.m: Therefore, above all these, establishing brahmins is supreme, / as is establishing deities, since dharma is rooted in that alone. // 2.93

1.4.s:
devatāyatanaṃ yāvadyāvacca brāhmaṇagṛham..
tāvaddātuḥ pūrvajānāṃ puṇyāṃśaścopatiṣṭhati.. 2.94 ..
1.4.d:
देवतायतनं यावद्यावच्च ब्राह्मणगृहम्..
तावद्दातुः पूर्वजानां पुण्यांशश्चोपतिष्ठति.. 2.94 ..
1.4.m: As long as a temple of a deity lasts, and as long as a brahmin's house lasts, / for that long a share of merit attends upon the donor's ancestors. // 2.94

1.4.s:
etatsvalpaṃ hi vāṇijyaṃ punarbahuphalapradam..
jīrṇoddhāre ca dviguṇametadeva prakīrtitam.. 2.95 ..
1.4.d:
एतत्स्वल्पं हि वाणिज्यं पुनर्बहुफलप्रदम्..
जीर्णोद्धारे च द्विगुणमेतदेव प्रकीर्तितम्.. 2.95 ..
1.4.m: This is indeed a small trade, yet yielding great fruit; / and in restoring what is dilapidated, this very [merit] is proclaimed to be doubled. // 2.95

1.4.s:
tasmādidaṃ tvahamapibravīmi surasattamāḥ..
nāsti dānasamaṃ kiṃcitsatyaṃ sārasvato jagau.. 2.96 ..
1.4.d:
तस्मादिदं त्वहमपिब्रवीमि सुरसत्तमाः..
नास्ति दानसमं किंचित्सत्यं सारस्वतो जगौ.. 2.96 ..
1.4.m: Therefore I too say this, O best of the gods: / there is nothing equal to a gift; truly has the sage belonging to Sarasvatī sung." // 2.96

1.4.s:
..nārada uvāca..
iti sārasvataproktāṃ tathā padmabhuveritām..
sādhusādhvityamodaṃta surāścāhaṃ suvismitāḥ.. 2.97 ..
1.4.d:
..नारद उवाच..
इति सारस्वतप्रोक्तां तथा पद्मभुवेरिताम्..
साधुसाध्वित्यमोदंत सुराश्चाहं सुविस्मिताः.. 2.97 ..
1.4.m: Nārada said: / Hearing what was spoken by the sage belonging to Sarasvatī and thus uttered by the lotus-born [Brahmā], / the gods and I rejoiced, exceedingly astonished, saying, "Well done! Well done!" // 2.97

1.4.s:
tataḥ sabhāvisargāṃte suramye merumūrdhani..
upaviśya śilāpṛṣṭhe ahametadaciṃtayam.. 2.98 ..
1.4.d:
ततः सभाविसर्गांते सुरम्ये मेरुमूर्धनि..
उपविश्य शिलापृष्ठे अहमेतदचिंतयम्.. 2.98 ..
1.4.m: Then, at the end of the assembly's dispersal, on the delightful summit of Meru, / sitting down upon a rock surface, I reflected on this: // 2.98

1.4.s:
satyamāha viraṃcistu sa kimarthaṃ tu jīvati..
yenaikamapi taddhṛttaṃ naiva yena kṛtārthatā.. 2.99 ..
1.4.d:
सत्यमाह विरंचिस्तु स किमर्थं तु जीवति..
येनैकमपि तद्धृत्तं नैव येन कृतार्थता.. 2.99 ..
1.4.m: "Brahmā spoke the truth; but for what purpose does he live / who has not fulfilled even one such deed, by which fulfillment is attained? // 2.99

1.4.s:
tadahaṃ dānapuṇyaṃ hi kariṣyāmi kathaṃ sphuṭam..
kaupīnadaṇḍātmadhano dhanaṃ svalpaṃ hi nāsti me.. 2.100 ..
1.4.d:
तदहं दानपुण्यं हि करिष्यामि कथं स्फुटम्..
कौपीनदण्डात्मधनो धनं स्वल्पं हि नास्ति मे.. 2.100 ..
1.4.m: How, clearly, shall I then perform the merit of giving? / Having only a loincloth and a staff as my wealth, I do not possess even a little wealth. // 2.100

1.4.s:
anarhate yaddadāti na dadāti tathārhate..
arhānarhaparijñānāddānadharmo hi duṣkaraḥ.. 2.101 ..
1.4.d:
अनर्हते यद्ददाति न ददाति तथार्हते..
अर्हानर्हपरिज्ञानाद्दानधर्मो हि दुष्करः.. 2.101 ..
1.4.m: What one gives to the unworthy, and does not give likewise to the worthy— / because of discerning the worthy and unworthy, the duty of giving is indeed difficult. // 2.101

1.4.s:
deśekāle ca pātre ca śuddhena manasā tathā..
nyāyārjitaṃ ca yo dadyādyauvane sa tadaśnute.. 2.102 ..
1.4.d:
देशेकाले च पात्रे च शुद्धेन मनसा तथा..
न्यायार्जितं च यो दद्याद्यौवने स तदश्नुते.. 2.102 ..
1.4.m: In the right place, time, and to a worthy recipient, with a pure mind, / whoever gives what is earned righteously, he enjoys that in his youth. // 2.102

1.4.s:
tamovṛtastu yo dadyātkrodhāttathaiva ca..
bhuṃkte dāna phalaṃ taddhi garbhastho nātra saṃśayaḥ.. 2.103 ..
1.4.d:
तमोवृतस्तु यो दद्यात्क्रोधात्तथैव च..
भुंक्ते दान फलं तद्धि गर्भस्थो नात्र संशयः.. 2.103 ..
1.4.m: Enveloped in darkness, however, whoever gives out of anger, / he enjoys the fruit of that gift while in the womb; there is no doubt about this. // 2.103

1.4.s:
bālatve'pi ca so'śrāti yaddattaṃ dambhakāraṇāt..
dattamanyāyato vittaṃ vai cārthakāraṇam.. 2.104 ..
1.4.d:
बालत्वेऽपि च सोऽश्राति यद्दत्तं दम्भकारणात्..
दत्तमन्यायतो वित्तं वै चार्थकारणम्.. 2.104 ..
1.4.m: In childhood too he enjoys what was given out of ostentation, / or wealth that was given unlawfully for the sake of material gain. // 2.104

1.4.s:
vṛddhatve hi samaśrāti naro vai nātra bhaviṣyati..
tasmāddeśe ca kāle ca supātre vidhinā naraḥ..
śubhārjitaṃ prayuñjīta śraddhayā śāṭhyavarjitaḥ.. 2.105 ..
1.4.d:
वृद्धत्वे हि समश्राति नरो वै नात्र भविष्यति..
तस्माद्देशे च काले च सुपात्रे विधिना नरः..
शुभार्जितं प्रयुञ्जीत श्रद्धया शाठ्यवर्जितः.. 2.105 ..
1.4.m: In old age indeed a man enjoys [it], or he will not do so [at all]; / therefore, in the right place, at the right time, and to an excellent recipient according to the rule, / a man should bestow what is acquired auspiciously, with faith and free from deceit. // 2.105

1.4.s:
tadetannirdhanatvācca kathaṃ nāma bhaviṣyati..
satyamāhuḥ purā vākyaṃ purāṇamunayo'malāḥ.. 2.106 ..
1.4.d:
तदेतन्निर्धनत्वाच्च कथं नाम भविष्यति..
सत्यमाहुः पुरा वाक्यं पुराणमुनयोऽमलाः.. 2.106 ..
1.4.m: Then, because of being destitute, how indeed will this come to be? / Truly did the pure ancient sages speak the saying: // 2.106

1.4.s:
nādhanasyāstyayaṃ loko na paraśca kathaṃcana..
abhiśastaṃ prapaśyaṃti daridraṃ pārśvataḥ sthitam.. 2.107 ..
1.4.d:
नाधनस्यास्त्ययं लोको न परश्च कथंचन..
अभिशस्तं प्रपश्यंति दरिद्रं पार्श्वतः स्थितम्.. 2.107 ..
1.4.m: 'For the penniless, neither this world exists nor the next in any way; / people look upon a poor man standing nearby as one accursed.' // 2.107

1.4.s:
dāridryaṃ pātakaṃ loke kastacchaṃsitumarhati..
patitaḥ śocyate sarvairnirdhanaścāpi śocyate.. 2.108 ..
1.4.d:
दारिद्र्यं पातकं लोके कस्तच्छंसितुमर्हति..
पतितः शोच्यते सर्वैर्निर्धनश्चापि शोच्यते.. 2.108 ..
1.4.m: Poverty is a sin in this world; who is capable of praising it? / A fallen man is lamented by all, and a destitute man is also lamented. // 2.108

1.4.s:
yaḥ kṛśāśvaḥ kṛśadhanaḥ kṛśabhṛtyaḥ kṛśātithiḥ..
sa vai proktaḥ kṛśonāma na śarīrakṛśaḥ kṛśaṛ.. 2.109 ..
1.4.d:
यः कृशाश्वः कृशधनः कृशभृत्यः कृशातिथिः..
स वै प्रोक्तः कृशोनाम न शरीरकृशः कृशऋ.. 2.109 ..
1.4.m: He whose horses are lean, whose wealth is lean, whose servants are lean, and whose guests are lean— / he is indeed called 'lean'; one lean in body is not lean. // 2.109

1.4.s:
arthavānduṣkulīno'pi loke pūjyatamo naraḥ..
śaśinastulyavaṃśo'pi nirdhanaḥ paribhūyate.. 2.110 ..
1.4.d:
अर्थवान्दुष्कुलीनोऽपि लोके पूज्यतमो नरः..
शशिनस्तुल्यवंशोऽपि निर्धनः परिभूयते.. 2.110 ..
1.4.m: A man possessed of wealth, even if of low birth, is most honored in the world; / even one born in a lineage equal to the moon, if devoid of wealth, is despised. // 2.110

1.4.s:
jñānavṛddhāstapovṛddhā ye ca vṛddhā bahuśrutāḥ..
te sarve dhanavṛddhasya dvāri tiṣṭhanti kiṃkarāḥ.. 2.111 ..
1.4.d:
ज्ञानवृद्धास्तपोवृद्धा ये च वृद्धा बहुश्रुताः..
ते सर्वे धनवृद्धस्य द्वारि तिष्ठन्ति किंकराः.. 2.111 ..
1.4.m: Those advanced in knowledge, those advanced in austerity, and those advanced in learning who are widely heard— / they all stand at the door of the one rich in wealth like servants. // 2.111

1.4.s:
yadyapyayaṃ tribhuvane artho'smākaṃ parāgnahi..
tathāpyanyaprārthito hi tasyaiva phalado bhavet.. 2.112 ..
1.4.d:
यद्यप्ययं त्रिभुवने अर्थोऽस्माकं पराग्नहि..
तथाप्यन्यप्रार्थितो हि तस्यैव फलदो भवेत्.. 2.112 ..
1.4.m: Even if this wealth is beyond us in the three worlds, / nevertheless, what is begged from another would bear fruit for that [giver] alone. // 2.112

1.4.s:
athavaitatpurā sarvaṃ ciṃtayiṣyāmi susphuṭam..
vilokayāmi pūrvaṃ tu kiṃcidyogyaṃ hi sthānakam.. 2.113 ..
1.4.d:
अथवैतत्पुरा सर्वं चिंतयिष्यामि सुस्फुटम्..
विलोकयामि पूर्वं तु किंचिद्योग्यं हि स्थानकम्.. 2.113 ..
1.4.m: Or rather, I shall think all this over very clearly first; / but first I shall look around for some suitable place." // 2.113

1.4.s:
sa ciṃtayitveti bahuprakāraṃ deśāṃśca grāmānnagarāṇi cāśramān..
bahūnahaṃ paryaṭannāptavānhi sthānaṃ hitaṃ sthāpaye yatra viprān.. 2.114 ..
iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ prathame māheśvarakhaṇḍe kaumārikākhaṇḍe nāradārjunasaṃvāde dānapraśaṃsāvarṇanaṃnāma dvitīya'dhyāyaḥ.. 2 .. cha ..
1.4.d:
स चिंतयित्वेति बहुप्रकारं देशांश्च ग्रामान्नगराणि चाश्रमान्..
बहूनहं पर्यटन्नाप्तवान्हि स्थानं हितं स्थापये यत्र विप्रान्.. 2.114 ..
इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां प्रथमे माहेश्वरखण्डे कौमारिकाखण्डे नारदार्जुनसंवादे दानप्रशंसावर्णनंनाम द्वितीयऽध्यायः.. 2 .. छ ..
1.4.m:
Having thought thus in many ways, wandering about through many / regions, villages, towns, and hermitages, I did not find a beneficial place where I might settle the brahmins. // 2.114
Thus ends the second chapter, entitled "Description of the Praise of Giving", in the dialogue between Nārada and Arjuna, in the Kaumārikākhaṇḍa of the first [section], the Māheśvarakhaṇḍa, in the Mahāpurāṇa of Skanda consisting of eighty-one thousand verses. // 2

1.4.s:
.. nārada uvāca..
tatastvahaṃ ciṃtayāmi kathaṃ sthānamidaṃ bhavet..
mamāyattaṃ yato rājñāṃ bhūmireṣā sadā vaśe.. 4.1 ..
1.4.d:
.. नारद उवाच..
ततस्त्वहं चिंतयामि कथं स्थानमिदं भवेत्..
ममायत्तं यतो राज्ञां भूमिरेषा सदा वशे.. 4.1 ..
1.4.m: Nārada said: / "Then I reflected: 'How can this place / become subject to my control, since this earth is always under the dominion of kings? // 4.1

1.4.s:
yattvahaṃ dharmavarṇāṇaṃ gatvā yāce ha medinīm..
arpayatyeva sa ca me yācito na punaḥ paraḥ.. 4.2 ..
1.4.d:
यत्त्वहं धर्मवर्णाणं गत्वा याचे ह मेदिनीम्..
अर्पयत्येव स च मे याचितो न पुनः परः.. 4.2 ..
1.4.m: If I, going to a righteous king, beg for the earth, / when solicited, he would surely bestow it upon me, but no other. // 4.2

1.4.s:
tathā hi munibhiḥ proktaṃ dravyaṃ trividhamuttamam..
śuklaṃ madhyaṃ ca śabalamadhamaṃ gṛṣṇamucyate.. 4.3 ..
1.4.d:
तथा हि मुनिभिः प्रोक्तं द्रव्यं त्रिविधमुत्तमम्..
शुक्लं मध्यं च शबलमधमं गृष्णमुच्यते.. 4.3 ..
1.4.m: For thus have the sages spoken of wealth as threefold: the best, / white; intermediate, speckled; and the lowest is called black. // 4.3

1.4.s:
śruteḥ saṃpādanācchiṣyātprāptaṃ śuklaṃ ca knyayayā..
tathā kusīdavāṇijyakṛṣiyācitameva ca.. 4.4 ..
1.4.d:
श्रुतेः संपादनाच्छिष्यात्प्राप्तं शुक्लं च क्न्ययया..
तथा कुसीदवाणिज्यकृषियाचितमेव च.. 4.4 ..
1.4.m: Acquired through the Veda, from a pupil, and through a daughter—this is white; / likewise, that obtained by usury, trade, agriculture, and begging. // 4.4

1.4.s:
śabalaṃ procyate sadbhirdyūtacauryeṇa sāhasaiḥ..
vyājenopārjitaṃ yacca tatkṛṣṇaṃ samudāhṛtam.. 4.5 ..
1.4.d:
शबलं प्रोच्यते सद्भिर्द्यूतचौर्येण साहसैः..
व्याजेनोपार्जितं यच्च तत्कृष्णं समुदाहृतम्.. 4.5 ..
1.4.m: is called speckled by the virtuous; and what is acquired through gambling, theft, violence, / or deceit is proclaimed as black. // 4.5

1.4.s:
śuklavittena yo dharmaṃ prakuryācchraddhayānvitaḥ..
tīrthaṃ pātraṃ samāsādya devatve tatsamaśnute.. 4.6 ..
1.4.d:
शुक्लवित्तेन यो धर्मं प्रकुर्याच्छ्रद्धयान्वितः..
तीर्थं पात्रं समासाद्य देवत्वे तत्समश्नुते.. 4.6 ..
1.4.m: Whoever performs dharma with white wealth, endowed with faith, / having found a sacred ford and a worthy recipient, enjoys it in godhood. // 4.6

1.4.s:
rājasena ca bhāvena vittena śabalena ca..
pradadyāddānamarthibhyo mānuṣyatve tadaśnute.. 4.7 ..
1.4.d:
राजसेन च भावेन वित्तेन शबलेन च..
प्रदद्याद्दानमर्थिभ्यो मानुष्यत्वे तदश्नुते.. 4.7 ..
1.4.m: And if with a passionate disposition and speckled wealth / one should bestow a gift upon petitioners, one enjoys it in human state. // 4.7

1.4.s:
tamovṛtastu yo dadyātkṛṣṇavittena mānavaḥ..
tiryaktve tatphalaṃ pretya samaśrāti narādhamaḥ.. 4.8 ..
1.4.d:
तमोवृतस्तु यो दद्यात्कृष्णवित्तेन मानवः..
तिर्यक्त्वे तत्फलं प्रेत्य समश्राति नराधमः.. 4.8 ..
1.4.m: Enveloped in darkness, however, whatever man gives with black wealth, / having died, that lowest of men enjoys that fruit in an animal state. // 4.8

1.4.s:
tattu yācitadravyaṃ me rājasaṃ hi sphuṭaṃ bhavet..
atha brāhmaṇabhāvena nṛpaṃ yāce pratigraham.. 4.9 ..
1.4.d:
तत्तु याचितद्रव्यं मे राजसं हि स्फुटं भवेत्..
अथ ब्राह्मणभावेन नृपं याचे प्रतिग्रहम्.. 4.9 ..
1.4.m: Then wealth obtained by begging would clearly be passionate for me. / Or, in the character of a brahmin, I might ask a king for an acceptance of a gift. // 4.9

1.4.s:
tadapyaho cātikaṣṭa hetunā tena me matam..
ayaṃ pratigraho ghoro madhvāsvādo viṣopamaḥ.. 4.10 ..
1.4.d:
तदप्यहो चातिकष्ट हेतुना तेन मे मतम्..
अयं प्रतिग्रहो घोरो मध्वास्वादो विषोपमः.. 4.10 ..
1.4.m: Yet even that, alas, is considered by me as exceedingly difficult for that reason; / this accepting of gifts is dreadful, having the taste of honey, yet like poison. // 4.10

1.4.s:
pratīgraheṇa saṃyuktaṃ hyamīvamāviśoddvijam..
tasmādahaṃ nivṛttaśca pāpādasmātpratigrahāt.. 4.11 ..
1.4.d:
प्रतीग्रहेण संयुक्तं ह्यमीवमाविशोद्द्विजम्..
तस्मादहं निवृत्तश्च पापादस्मात्प्रतिग्रहात्.. 4.11 ..
1.4.m: For affliction enters the twice-born who is joined with acceptance of gifts; / therefore, I have turned away from this sin of acceptance of gifts. // 4.11

1.4.s:
tataḥ kenāpyupāyena dvayoranyatareṇa tu..
svāyattaṃ sthānaka kurma etatsañciṃtaye muhuḥ.. 4.12 ..
1.4.d:
ततः केनाप्युपायेन द्वयोरन्यतरेण तु..
स्वायत्तं स्थानक कुर्म एतत्सञ्चिंतये मुहुः.. 4.12 ..
1.4.m: Then, by some means or other, by one of the two, / let us make a place subject to our own control'—this I contemplated again and again. // 4.12

1.4.s:
yathā kubhāryaḥ puruṣaścintāṃtaṃ na prapadyate..
tathaiva vimṛśaṃścāhaṃ ciṃtāṃtaṃ na labhāmyaṇu.. 4.13 ..
1.4.d:
यथा कुभार्यः पुरुषश्चिन्तांतं न प्रपद्यते..
तथैव विमृशंश्चाहं चिंतांतं न लभाम्यणु.. 4.13 ..
1.4.m: Just as a man with a bad wife finds no end to his anxiety, / exactly so, reflecting upon it, I did not find the slightest end to my anxiety." // 4.13

1.4.s:
etasminnantare pārtha snātuṃ tatra samāgatāḥ..
bahavo munayaḥ puṇye mahīsāgarasaṃgame.. 4.14 ..
1.4.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे पार्थ स्नातुं तत्र समागताः..
बहवो मुनयः पुण्ये महीसागरसंगमे.. 4.14 ..
1.4.m:
In the meantime, O Pārtha, many sages arrived there
to bathe at the holy confluence of the Mahī and the ocean.

1.4.s:
ahaṃ tānabravaṃ sarvānkuto yūyaṃ samāgatāḥ..
te māmūcuḥ praṇamyātha saurāṣṭraviṣaye mune.. 4.15 ..
1.4.d:
अहं तानब्रवं सर्वान्कुतो यूयं समागताः..
ते मामूचुः प्रणम्याथ सौराष्ट्रविषये मुने.. 4.15 ..
1.4.m:
I asked them all: "From where have you come?"
Having bowed down, they then said to me: "O sage, in the region of Saurāṣṭra,

1.4.s:
dharmavarmeti nṛpatiryo'sya deśasya bhūpatiḥ..
sa tu dānasya tattvārthī tepe varṣagaṇānbahūn.. 4.16 ..
1.4.d:
धर्मवर्मेति नृपतिर्योऽस्य देशस्य भूपतिः..
स तु दानस्य तत्त्वार्थी तेपे वर्षगणान्बहून्.. 4.16 ..
1.4.m:
there is a ruler named Dharmavarmā, the king of this country.
Seeking to understand the true nature of giving, he practiced austerity for many years.

1.4.s:
tatastaṃ prāha khe vāṇī ślokamekaṃ nṛpa śrṛṇu..
dvihetu ṣaḍadhiṣṭhānaṃ ṣaḍaṃgaṃ ca dvipākayuk.. 4.17 ..
1.4.d:
ततस्तं प्राह खे वाणी श्लोकमेकं नृप श्रृणु..
द्विहेतु षडधिष्ठानं षडंगं च द्विपाकयुक्.. 4.17 ..
1.4.m:
Then an incorporeal voice in the sky said to him: 'Hear one verse, O king:
"With two motives, six foundations, six limbs, and two fruits;

1.4.s:
catuḥprakāraṃ trividhaṃ trināśaṃ dānamucyate..
ityekaṃ ślokamābhāṣya khe vāṇī virarāma ha.. 4.18 ..
1.4.d:
चतुःप्रकारं त्रिविधं त्रिनाशं दानमुच्यते..
इत्येकं श्लोकमाभाष्य खे वाणी विरराम ह.. 4.18 ..
1.4.m:
having four forms, of three kinds, with three ruins is giving said to be."'
Having spoken this single verse, the voice in the sky fell silent.

1.4.s:
ślokasyārthaṃ nāvabhāṣe pṛcchamānāpi nārada..
tato rājā dharmavarmā paṭahenānvaghoṣayat.. 4.19 ..
1.4.d:
श्लोकस्यार्थं नावभाषे पृच्छमानापि नारद..
ततो राजा धर्मवर्मा पटहेनान्वघोषयत्.. 4.19 ..
1.4.m:
It did not reveal the meaning of the verse, though being questioned, O Nārada.
Thereupon King Dharmavarmā made a proclamation by beat of drum:

1.4.s:
yastu ślokasya caivāsya labdhasya tapasā mayā..
karoti samyagavyākhyānaṃ tasya caitaddadāmyaham.. 4.20 ..
1.4.d:
यस्तु श्लोकस्य चैवास्य लब्धस्य तपसा मया..
करोति सम्यगव्याख्यानं तस्य चैतद्ददाम्यहम्.. 4.20 ..
1.4.m:
'Whoever provides a complete and correct explanation of this verse
obtained by me through austerity, to him I will give this:

1.4.s:
gavāṃ ca sapta niyutaṃ suvarṇaṃ tāvadeva tu..
saptagrāmānprayacchāmi ślokavyākhyāṃ karoti yaḥ.. 4.21 ..
1.4.d:
गवां च सप्त नियुतं सुवर्णं तावदेव तु..
सप्तग्रामान्प्रयच्छामि श्लोकव्याख्यां करोति यः.. 4.21 ..
1.4.m:
seven hundred thousand cows, and just as much gold;
I shall grant seven villages to whoever explains the verse.'

1.4.s:
paṭaheneti nṛpateḥ śrutvā rājño vaco mahat..
ājagmurbahudeśīyā brāhmaṇāḥ koṭiśo mune.. 4.22 ..
1.4.d:
पटहेनेति नृपतेः श्रुत्वा राज्ञो वचो महत्..
आजग्मुर्बहुदेशीया ब्राह्मणाः कोटिशो मुने.. 4.22 ..
1.4.m:
Having heard this great proclamation of the king announced by drum,
millions of brahmins from many lands arrived, O sage.

1.4.s:
punardurbodhavinyāsaḥ ślokastairviprapuṃgavaiḥ..
ākhyātuṃ śakyate naiva guḍo mūkairyathā mune.. 4.23 ..
1.4.d:
पुनर्दुर्बोधविन्यासः श्लोकस्तैर्विप्रपुंगवैः..
आख्यातुं शक्यते नैव गुडो मूकैर्यथा मुने.. 4.23 ..
1.4.m:
Yet, because of its difficult construction, that verse could not be explained
by those foremost brahmins at all, just as molasses [cannot be described] by mutes, O sage.

1.4.s:
vayaṃ ca tatra yātāḥ smo dhanalobhena nārada..
durbodhatvānnamaskṛtya ślokaṃ cātra samāgatāḥ.. 4.24 ..
1.4.d:
वयं च तत्र याताः स्मो धनलोभेन नारद..
दुर्बोधत्वान्नमस्कृत्य श्लोकं चात्र समागताः.. 4.24 ..
1.4.m:
We too went there out of desire for wealth, O Nārada;
but bowing before the verse due to its incomprehensibility, we have come here.

1.4.s:
durvyākhyeyastvayaṃ śloko dhanaṃ labhyaṃ na caiva naḥ..
tīrthayātrāṃ kathaṃ yāmītyevāciṃtyātra cāgatāḥ.. 4.25 ..
1.4.d:
दुर्व्याख्येयस्त्वयं श्लोको धनं लभ्यं न चैव नः..
तीर्थयात्रां कथं यामीत्येवाचिंत्यात्र चागताः.. 4.25 ..
1.4.m:
'This verse is impossible to explain, and wealth is not to be obtained by us;
how shall I go on a pilgrimage?' Thinking thus, we have arrived here."

1.4.s:
evaṃ phālguna teṣāṃ tu vacaḥ śrutvā mahātmanām..
atīva saṃprahṛṣṭo'haṃ tānvisṛjyetyaciṃtayam.. 4.26 ..
1.4.d:
एवं फाल्गुन तेषां तु वचः श्रुत्वा महात्मनाम्..
अतीव संप्रहृष्टोऽहं तान्विसृज्येत्यचिंतयम्.. 4.26 ..
1.4.m:
Having heard those words of those great-souled men, O Phālguna,
I was exceedingly overjoyed, and sending them off, I reflected:

1.4.s:
aho prāpta upāyo me sthānaprāptau na saṃśayaḥ..
ślokaṃ vyākhyāya nṛpaterlapsye sthānaṃ dhanaṃ tathā.. 4.27 ..
1.4.d:
अहो प्राप्त उपायो मे स्थानप्राप्तौ न संशयः..
श्लोकं व्याख्याय नृपतेर्लप्स्ये स्थानं धनं तथा.. 4.27 ..
1.4.m:
"Ah, a means has been found for me to obtain a dwelling place, without doubt!
By explaining the verse to the king, I shall obtain a place and wealth as well.

1.4.s:
vidyāmūlyena naivaṃ ca yācitaḥ syātpratigrahaḥ..
satyamāha purāṇārṣirvāsudevo jagadguruḥ.. 4.28 ..
1.4.d:
विद्यामूल्येन नैवं च याचितः स्यात्प्रतिग्रहः..
सत्यमाह पुराणार्षिर्वासुदेवो जगद्गुरुः.. 4.28 ..
1.4.m:
And thus, being the price of learning, it would not be a begged gift.
Truly did the ancient seer Vāsudeva, the teacher of the world, speak:

1.4.s:
dharmasya yasya śraddhā syānna ca sā naiva pūryate..
pāpasya yasya śraddhāsyānna ca sāpi na pūryate.. 4.29 ..
1.4.d:
धर्मस्य यस्य श्रद्धा स्यान्न च सा नैव पूर्यते..
पापस्य यस्य श्रद्धास्यान्न च सापि न पूर्यते.. 4.29 ..
1.4.m:
'Whoever has faith in righteousness, that [desire] is never unfulfilled;
whoever has faith in sin, even that is not left unfulfilled.'

1.4.s:
evaṃ viciṃtya vidvāṃsaḥ prakurvaṃti yathāruci..
satyametadvibhorvākyaṃ durlabho'pi yathā hi me.. 4.30 ..
1.4.d:
एवं विचिंत्य विद्वांसः प्रकुर्वंति यथारुचि..
सत्यमेतद्विभोर्वाक्यं दुर्लभोऽपि यथा हि मे.. 4.30 ..
1.4.m:
Reflecting thus, the wise act according to their inclination.
This word of the Lord is true, seeing that for me, though difficult to obtain,

1.4.s:
manoratho'yaṃ saphalaḥ saṃbhūtoṃkuritaḥ sphuṭam..
enaṃ ca durvidaṃ ślokamahaṃ jānāmi susphuṭam.. 4.31 ..
1.4.d:
मनोरथोऽयं सफलः संभूतोंकुरितः स्फुटम्..
एनं च दुर्विदं श्लोकमहं जानामि सुस्फुटम्.. 4.31 ..
1.4.m:
this desire of mine has clearly sprouted and borne fruit.
And I understand this hard-to-comprehend verse very clearly;

1.4.s:
amūrtaiḥ pitṛbhiḥ pūrvameva khyāto hi me purā..
evaṃ harṣānvitaḥ pārtha saṃciṃtyā'haṃ tato muhuḥ.. 4.32 ..
1.4.d:
अमूर्तैः पितृभिः पूर्वमेव ख्यातो हि मे पुरा..
एवं हर्षान्वितः पार्थ संचिंत्याऽहं ततो मुहुः.. 4.32 ..
1.4.m:
for it was indeed declared to me long ago by the formless ancestors."
Filled with joy, O Pārtha, pondering this again and again,

1.4.s:
praṇamya tīrthaṃ calito mahīsāgarasaṃgamam..
vṛddhabrāhmaṇarūpeṇa tatohaṃ yātavānnṛpam.. 4.33 ..
1.4.d:
प्रणम्य तीर्थं चलितो महीसागरसंगमम्..
वृद्धब्राह्मणरूपेण ततोहं यातवान्नृपम्.. 4.33 ..
1.4.m:
I bowed to the sacred ford of the confluence of the Mahī and the ocean and set forth.
Then, in the form of an old brahmin, I went to the king.

1.4.s:
idaṃ bhaṇitavānasmi ślokavyākhyāṃ nṛpa śrṛṇu..
yatte paṭahavikhyātaṃ dānaṃ ca praguṇīkuru.. 4.34 ..
1.4.d:
इदं भणितवानस्मि श्लोकव्याख्यां नृप श्रृणु..
यत्ते पटहविख्यातं दानं च प्रगुणीकुरु.. 4.34 ..
1.4.m:
I said this: "Hear the explanation of the verse, O king!
And prepare the gift that was proclaimed by you with drums."

1.4.s:
evamukte nṛpaḥ prāha procurevaṃ hi koṭiśaḥ..
dvijottamāḥ punarnasyaṃ proktumartho hi śakyate.. 4.35 ..
1.4.d:
एवमुक्ते नृपः प्राह प्रोचुरेवं हि कोटिशः..
द्विजोत्तमाः पुनर्नस्यं प्रोक्तुमर्थो हि शक्यते.. 4.35 ..
1.4.m:
When this was said, the king replied: "Indeed, millions spoke thus,
foremost brahmins, but could not state its meaning.

1.4.s:
ke dvihetū ṣaḍākhyātānyadhiṣṭhānāni kāni ca..
kāni caiva ṣaḍaṃgāni kau dvau pākau tathā smṛtau.. 4.36 ..
1.4.d:
के द्विहेतू षडाख्यातान्यधिष्ठानानि कानि च..
कानि चैव षडंगानि कौ द्वौ पाकौ तथा स्मृतौ.. 4.36 ..
1.4.m:
What are the two motives, what are the six foundations declared to be,
what are the six limbs, and what are remembered as the two fruits?

1.4.s:
ke ca prakārāścatvāraḥ kiṃsvittattrividhaṃ dvija..
payo nāśāśca ke proktā dānasyaitatsphuṭaṃ vada.. 4.37 ..
1.4.d:
के च प्रकाराश्चत्वारः किंस्वित्तत्त्रिविधं द्विज..
पयो नाशाश्च के प्रोक्ता दानस्यैतत्स्फुटं वद.. 4.37 ..
1.4.m:
What are the four forms, what is that threefold nature, O twice-born one,
and what are declared to be the three ruins of giving? Tell this clearly.

1.4.s:
sphuṭānpraśnānimānsapta yadi vakṣyasi brāhmaṇa..
tato gavāṃ saptaniyutaṃ suvarṇaṃ tāvadeva tu.. 4.38 ..
1.4.d:
स्फुटान्प्रश्नानिमान्सप्त यदि वक्ष्यसि ब्राह्मण..
ततो गवां सप्तनियुतं सुवर्णं तावदेव तु.. 4.38 ..
1.4.m:
If you answer these seven clear questions, O brahmin,
then seven hundred thousand cows, and just as much gold,

1.4.s:
sapta grāmāṃśca dāsyāmi no cedyāsyasi svaṃ gṛham..
ityuktvā vacanaṃ pārtha saurāṣṭrasvāminaṃ nṛpam.. 4.39 ..
1.4.d:
सप्त ग्रामांश्च दास्यामि नो चेद्यास्यसि स्वं गृहम्..
इत्युक्त्वा वचनं पार्थ सौराष्ट्रस्वामिनं नृपम्.. 4.39 ..
1.4.m:
and seven villages I will give; if not, you shall return to your own home."
Having listened to this speech, O Pārtha, [spoken] to the king, the lord of Saurāṣṭra,

1.4.s:
dharmavarmāṇamastvevaṃ prāvocamavadhāraya..
ślokavyākhyāṃ sphuṭāṃ vakṣye dānahetū ca tau śrṛṇu.. 4.40 ..
1.4.d:
धर्मवर्माणमस्त्वेवं प्रावोचमवधारय..
श्लोकव्याख्यां स्फुटां वक्ष्ये दानहेतू च तौ श्रृणु.. 4.40 ..
1.4.m:
to Dharmavarmā, I replied: "So be it! Listen with attention!
I shall declare the clear explanation of the verse; hear first the two motives of giving.

1.4.s:
alpatvaṃ vā bahutvaṃ vā dānasyābhyudayāvaham..
śraddhā śaktiśca dānānāṃ vṛddhyakṣayakarehi te.. 4.41 ..
1.4.d:
अल्पत्वं वा बहुत्वं वा दानस्याभ्युदयावहम्..
श्रद्धा शक्तिश्च दानानां वृद्ध्यक्षयकरेहि ते.. 4.41 ..
1.4.m:
Whether small or great, giving brings about prosperity;
faith and capacity indeed cause gifts to increase and become imperishable.

1.4.s:
tatra śraddhāviṣaye ślokā bhavanti..
kāyakleśaiśca bahubhirna caivārathasya rāśibhiḥ.. 4.42 ..
1.4.d:
तत्र श्रद्धाविषये श्लोका भवन्ति..
कायक्लेशैश्च बहुभिर्न चैवारथस्य राशिभिः.. 4.42 ..
1.4.m:
On the subject of faith, there are these verses:
Not through many bodily mortifications, nor through heaps of wealth,

1.4.s:
dharmaḥ saṃprāpyate sūkṣmaḥ śraddhā dharmo'dbhutaṃ tapaḥ..
śraddhā svargaśca mokṣaśca śraddhā sarvamidaṃ jagat.. 4.43 ..
1.4.d:
धर्मः संप्राप्यते सूक्ष्मः श्रद्धा धर्मोऽद्भुतं तपः..
श्रद्धा स्वर्गश्च मोक्षश्च श्रद्धा सर्वमिदं जगत्.. 4.43 ..
1.4.m:
is subtle righteousness attained; faith is righteousness, [faith is] wonderful austerity;
faith is heaven, and [faith is] liberation; faith is this entire world.

1.4.s:
sarvasvaṃ jīvitaṃ cāpi dadyādaśraddhayā yadi..
nāpnuyātsa phalaṃ kiṃcicchraddadhānastato bhavet.. 4.44 ..
1.4.d:
सर्वस्वं जीवितं चापि दद्यादश्रद्धया यदि..
नाप्नुयात्स फलं किंचिच्छ्रद्दधानस्ततो भवेत्.. 4.44 ..
1.4.m:
Even if one were to give all one's possessions and one's life without faith,
one would not obtain any fruit; therefore, one should be full of faith.

1.4.s:
śraddhayā sādhyate dharmo mahadbhirnārtharāśibhiḥ..
akiṃcanā hi munayaḥ śraddhāvaṃto divaṃ gatāḥ.. 4.45 ..
1.4.d:
श्रद्धया साध्यते धर्मो महद्भिर्नार्थराशिभिः..
अकिंचना हि मुनयः श्रद्धावंतो दिवं गताः.. 4.45 ..
1.4.m:
Righteousness is accomplished through faith, not through great heaps of wealth;
for sages possessing nothing, endowed with faith, have gone to heaven.

1.4.s:
trividhā bhavati śraddhā dehināṃ sā svabhāvajā..
sāttvikī rājasī caiva tāmasī ceti tāṃ śrṛṇu.. 4.46 ..
1.4.d:
त्रिविधा भवति श्रद्धा देहिनां सा स्वभावजा..
सात्त्विकी राजसी चैव तामसी चेति तां श्रृणु.. 4.46 ..
1.4.m:
The faith of embodied beings is threefold, born of their inherent nature:
sāttvika, rājasa, and tāmasa; hear of it.

1.4.s:
yajaṃte sāttvikā devānyakṣarakṣāṃsi rājasāḥ..
pretānbhūtapiśācāṃśca yajaṃte tāmasā janāḥ.. 4.47 ..
1.4.d:
यजंते सात्त्विका देवान्यक्षरक्षांसि राजसाः..
प्रेतान्भूतपिशाचांश्च यजंते तामसा जनाः.. 4.47 ..
1.4.m:
Sāttvika people worship the gods; rājasa people, the yakṣas and rākṣasas;
and tāmasa people worship spirits, bhūtas, and piśācas.

1.4.s:
tasmācchraddhāvatā pātre dattaṃ nyāyārjitaṃ hi yat..
tenaiva bhagavānrudraḥ svalpakenāpi tuṣyati.. 4.48 ..
1.4.d:
तस्माच्छ्रद्धावता पात्रे दत्तं न्यायार्जितं हि यत्..
तेनैव भगवान्रुद्रः स्वल्पकेनापि तुष्यति.. 4.48 ..
1.4.m:
Therefore, whatever is given to a worthy recipient by a faithful person, earned by just means—
with that, even if very small, Lord Rudra is pleased.

1.4.s:
śaktiviṣaye ca ślokā bhavaṃti..
kuṭuṃbabhuktavasanāddeyaṃ yadatiricyate..
madhvāsvādo viṣaṃ paścāddāturdharmo'nyathā bhavet.. 4.49 ..
1.4.d:
शक्तिविषये च श्लोका भवंति..
कुटुंबभुक्तवसनाद्देयं यदतिरिच्यते..
मध्वास्वादो विषं पश्चाद्दातुर्धर्मोऽन्यथा भवेत्.. 4.49 ..

1.4.s:
śakte parajane dātā svajane duḥkhajīvini..
madhvāpānaviṣādaḥ sa dharmāṇāṃ pratirūpakaḥ.. 4.50 ..
1.4.d:
शक्ते परजने दाता स्वजने दुःखजीविनि..
मध्वापानविषादः स धर्माणां प्रतिरूपकः.. 4.50 ..
1.4.m:
He who gives to outsiders while capable, while his own kin live in misery,
is like one who drinks poison disguised as honey—a mere semblance of righteousness.

1.4.s:
bhṛtyānāmuparodhena yatkarotyaurdhvadaihikam..
tadbhavatyasukhodakaṃ jīvato'sya mṛtasya ca.. 4.51 ..
1.4.d:
भृत्यानामुपरोधेन यत्करोत्यौर्ध्वदैहिकम्..
तद्भवत्यसुखोदकं जीवतोऽस्य मृतस्य च.. 4.51 ..
1.4.m:
Whatever rite for the hereafter one performs by distressing one's dependents,
that results in unhappiness both while he is alive and when he is dead.

1.4.s:
sāmānyaṃ yācitaṃ nyāsamādhirdārāśca darśanam..
anvāhitaṃ ca nikṣepaḥ sarvasvaṃ cānvaye sati.. 4.52 ..
1.4.d:
सामान्यं याचितं न्यासमाधिर्दाराश्च दर्शनम्..
अन्वाहितं च निक्षेपः सर्वस्वं चान्वये सति.. 4.52 ..
1.4.m:
Common property, what is borrowed, a bailment, a pledge, a wife, a surety,
a secondary deposit, a deposit, and one's entire property when there is lineage—

1.4.s:
āpatsvapi na deyāni navavastūni paṃḍitaiḥ..
yo dadāti sa mūḍhātmā prāyāścittīyate naraḥ.. 4.53 ..
1.4.d:
आपत्स्वपि न देयानि नववस्तूनि पंडितैः..
यो ददाति स मूढात्मा प्रायाश्चित्तीयते नरः.. 4.53 ..
1.4.m:
these nine things are not to be given by the wise even in times of distress;
the man of foolish mind who gives [them] must perform expiation.

1.4.s:
iti te gaditau rājandvau hetū śrūyatāmataḥ..
adhiṣṭhānāni vakṣyāmi ṣaḍeva śrṛṇu tānyapi.. 4.54 ..
1.4.d:
इति ते गदितौ राजन्द्वौ हेतू श्रूयतामतः..
अधिष्ठानानि वक्ष्यामि षडेव श्रृणु तान्यपि.. 4.54 ..
1.4.m:
Thus the two motives have been declared to you, O king; hear now further:
I shall explain the six foundations; listen to them also.

1.4.s:
dharmamarthaṃ ca kāmaṃ ca vrīḍāharṣabhayāni ca..
adhiṣṭhānāni dānānāṃ ṣaḍetāni pracakṣate.. 4.55 ..
1.4.d:
धर्ममर्थं च कामं च व्रीडाहर्षभयानि च..
अधिष्ठानानि दानानां षडेतानि प्रचक्षते.. 4.55 ..
1.4.m:
Righteousness, wealth, desire, shame, joy, and fear:
these are declared to be the six foundations of giving.

1.4.s:
pātrebhyo dīyate nityamanapekṣya prayojanam..
kevalaṃ dharmabuddhyā yaddharmadānaṃ taducyate.. 4.56 ..
1.4.d:
पात्रेभ्यो दीयते नित्यमनपेक्ष्य प्रयोजनम्..
केवलं धर्मबुद्ध्या यद्धर्मदानं तदुच्यते.. 4.56 ..
1.4.m:
That which is given constantly to worthy recipients without expecting any purpose,
solely with the thought of righteousness, is called the gift of righteousness.

1.4.s:
dhaninaṃ dhanalobhena lobhayitvārthamāharet..
tadarthadānamityāhuḥ kāmadānamataḥ śrṛṇu.. 4.57 ..
1.4.d:
धनिनं धनलोभेन लोभयित्वार्थमाहरेत्..
तदर्थदानमित्याहुः कामदानमतः श्रृणु.. 4.57 ..
1.4.m: If one allures a wealthy man through greed for wealth and takes his wealth, / they call that gift based on profit (arthadāna). Hear now of the gift based on desire (kāmadāna):

1.4.s:
prayojanamapekṣyaiva prasaṃgādyatpradīyate..
anarheṣu sarāgeṇa kāmadānaṃ taducyate.. 4.58 ..
1.4.d:
प्रयोजनमपेक्ष्यैव प्रसंगाद्यत्प्रदीयते..
अनर्हेषु सरागेण कामदानं तदुच्यते.. 4.58 ..
1.4.m: That which is given out of self-interest, through association, / to the unworthy, with passion—that is called a gift based on desire.

1.4.s:
saṃsadi vrīḍayā''śrutya ārthibhyaḥ pradadāti ca..
pratidīyate ca yaddānaṃ vrīḍādānamiti śrutam.. 4.59 ..
1.4.d:
संसदि व्रीडया'ऽश्रुत्य आर्थिभ्यः प्रददाति च..
प्रतिदीयते च यद्दानं व्रीडादानमिति श्रुतम्.. 4.59 ..
1.4.m: When one gives to petitioners having promised in an assembly out of shame, / and a gift is thus rendered, it is known as a gift based on shame (vrīḍādāna).

1.4.s:
dṛṣṭvā priyāṇi śrutvā vā harṣavadyatpradīyate..
harṣadānamiti proktaṃ dānaṃ taddharmaciṃtakaiḥ.. 4.60 ..
1.4.d:
दृष्ट्वा प्रियाणि श्रुत्वा वा हर्षवद्यत्प्रदीयते..
हर्षदानमिति प्रोक्तं दानं तद्धर्मचिंतकैः.. 4.60 ..
1.4.m: That which is given joyfully, having seen or heard pleasing things, / has been declared by thinkers on dharma to be a gift based on joy (harṣadāna).

1.4.s:
ākrośānarthahiṃsānāṃ pratīkārāya yadbhavet..
dīyate'nupakartṛbhyo bhayadānaṃ taducyate.. 4.61 ..
1.4.d:
आक्रोशानर्थहिंसानां प्रतीकाराय यद्भवेत्..
दीयतेऽनुपकर्तृभ्यो भयदानं तदुच्यते.. 4.61 ..
1.4.m: That which is given to non-benefactors to counter / abuse, injury, or violence—that is called a gift based on fear (bhayadāna).

1.4.s:
proktāni ṣaḍadhiṣṭhānānyaṃgānyapi ca ṣaṭcchruṇu..
dātā pratigrahītā ca śuddhirdeyaṃ ca dharmayuk.. 4.62 ..
1.4.d:
प्रोक्तानि षडधिष्ठानान्यंगान्यपि च षट्च्छ्रुणु..
दाता प्रतिग्रहीता च शुद्धिर्देयं च धर्मयुक्.. 4.62 ..
1.4.m: The six grounds have been spoken; now hear also of the six limbs: / the donor, the recipient, purity, the gift itself endowed with righteousness,

1.4.s:
deśakālau ca dānānāmaṃgānyetāni ṣaḍviduḥ..
aparogī ca dharmātmā ditsuravyasanaḥ śuciḥ.. 4.63 ..
1.4.d:
देशकालौ च दानानामंगान्येतानि षड्विदुः..
अपरोगी च धर्मात्मा दित्सुरव्यसनः शुचिः.. 4.63 ..
1.4.m: and the place and time—these they know as the six limbs of gifts. / A donor is praised on account of six qualities: being free from disease, righteous, willing to give, free from vices, pure,

1.4.s:
aniṃdyājīvakarmā ca ṣaḍbhirdātā praśasyate..
anṛjuścāśraddadhāno'śāṃtātmā dhṛṣṭabhīrukaḥ.. 4.64 ..
1.4.d:
अनिंद्याजीवकर्मा च षड्भिर्दाता प्रशस्यते..
अनृजुश्चाश्रद्दधानोऽशांतात्मा धृष्टभीरुकः.. 4.64 ..
1.4.m: and having an unblameworthy livelihood. / One who is crooked, without faith, uncontrolled in mind, insolent, timid,

1.4.s:
asatyasaṃdho nidrālurdātāyaṃ tāmaso'dhamaḥ..
triśuklaḥ kṛśavṛttiśca ghṛṇāluḥ sakaleṃdriyaḥ.. 4.65 ..
1.4.d:
असत्यसंधो निद्रालुर्दातायं तामसोऽधमः..
त्रिशुक्लः कृशवृत्तिश्च घृणालुः सकलेंद्रियः.. 4.65 ..
1.4.m: untrue to his word, and indolent—such a donor is base, characterized by darkness (tamas). / Pure in three ways (descent, learning, conduct), of modest livelihood, compassionate, with all senses intact,

1.4.s:
vimukto yonidoṣebhyo brāhmaḥ pātramucyate..
saumukhyādabhisaṃprītirarthināṃ darśane sadā..
satkṛtiścānasūyā ca tadā śuddhiriti smṛtā.. 4.66 ..
1.4.d:
विमुक्तो योनिदोषेभ्यो ब्राह्मः पात्रमुच्यते..
सौमुख्यादभिसंप्रीतिरर्थिनां दर्शने सदा..
सत्कृतिश्चानसूया च तदा शुद्धिरिति स्मृता.. 4.66 ..
1.4.m: freed from defects of birth—such a brahmin is called a worthy recipient (pātra). / Delight through pleasantness of countenance always upon seeing petitioners, / hospitality, and freedom from envy—that is remembered as purity.

1.4.s:
aparābādhamakleśaṃ svayatnenārjitaṃ dhanam..
svalpaṃ vā vipulaṃ vāpi deyamityabhidhīyate.. 4.67 ..
1.4.d:
अपराबाधमक्लेशं स्वयत्नेनार्जितं धनम्..
स्वल्पं वा विपुलं वापि देयमित्यभिधीयते.. 4.67 ..
1.4.m: Wealth acquired by one's own effort, causing no harm to others and without distress, / whether small or abundant, is designated as the worthy gift.

1.4.s:
tenāpi kila dharmeṇa uddiśya kila kiṃcana..
deyaṃ taddharmayugiti śūnye śūnyaṃ phalaṃ matam.. 4.68 ..
1.4.d:
तेनापि किल धर्मेण उद्दिश्य किल किंचन..
देयं तद्धर्मयुगिति शून्ये शून्यं फलं मतम्.. 4.68 ..
1.4.m: That gift which is given aiming at someone according to dharma / is considered 'endowed with righteousness'; where there is a void, the fruit is considered void.

1.4.s:
nyāyena durlabhaṃ dravyaṃ deśe kālepi vā punaḥ..
dānārhau deśakālau tau syātāṃ śreṣṭhau na cānyathā.. 4.69 ..
1.4.d:
न्यायेन दुर्लभं द्रव्यं देशे कालेपि वा पुनः..
दानार्हौ देशकालौ तौ स्यातां श्रेष्ठौ न चान्यथा.. 4.69 ..
1.4.m: Moreover, when an article is difficult to obtain lawfully in a [particular] place or time, / that place and time become worthy of giving and are the best, not otherwise.

1.4.s:
ṣaṃḍagānīti coktāni dvau ca pākāvataḥ śrṛṇu..
dvau pākau dānajau prāhuḥ paratrātha tvihocyate.. 4.70 ..
1.4.d:
षंडगानीति चोक्तानि द्वौ च पाकावतः श्रृणु..
द्वौ पाकौ दानजौ प्राहुः परत्राथ त्विहोच्यते.. 4.70 ..
1.4.m: Thus the six limbs have been spoken. Hear next of the two fruitions: / They speak of two fruitions born of gifts: in the next world and in this one.

1.4.s:
sadbhyo yaddīyate kiṃcittatparatropatiṣṭhati..
asatsu dīyate kiṃcittaddānamiha bhujyate.. 4.71 ..
1.4.d:
सद्भ्यो यद्दीयते किंचित्तत्परत्रोपतिष्ठति..
असत्सु दीयते किंचित्तद्दानमिह भुज्यते.. 4.71 ..
1.4.m: Whatever is given to the virtuous waits for one in the next world; / whatever is given to the unvirtuous, that gift is enjoyed here [in this world].

1.4.s:
dvau pākāviti nirdiṣṭau prakārāṃścaturaḥ śrṛṇu..
dhruvamāhustrikaṃ kāmyaṃ naimittikamiti kramāt.. 4.72 ..
1.4.d:
द्वौ पाकाविति निर्दिष्टौ प्रकारांश्चतुरः श्रृणु..
ध्रुवमाहुस्त्रिकं काम्यं नैमित्तिकमिति क्रमात्.. 4.72 ..
1.4.m: Two fruitions have thus been indicated. Hear of the four types: / in order, they speak of the constant (dhruva), the trika, the desired (kāmya), and the occasional (naimittika).

1.4.s:
vaidiko dānamārgo'yaṃ caturdhā varṇyate dvijaiḥ..
prapārāmataḍāgādisarvakāmaphalaṃ dhruvam.. 4.73 ..
1.4.d:
वैदिको दानमार्गोऽयं चतुर्धा वर्ण्यते द्विजैः..
प्रपारामतडागादिसर्वकामफलं ध्रुवम्.. 4.73 ..
1.4.m: This Vedic path of gifts is described in four ways by the twice-born. / The constant (dhruva) brings the fruit of all desires, such as water-sheds, gardens, and ponds.

1.4.s:
tadāhustrikāmityāhurdīyate yaddinedine..
apatyavijayaiśvaryastrībālārthaṃ pradīyate.. 4.74 ..
1.4.d:
तदाहुस्त्रिकामित्याहुर्दीयते यद्दिनेदिने..
अपत्यविजयैश्वर्यस्त्रीबालार्थं प्रदीयते.. 4.74 ..
1.4.m: They speak of that which is given day after day as the trika. / That which is given for the sake of offspring, victory, sovereignty, women, and children,

1.4.s:
icchāsaṃsthaṃ ca yaddānaṃ kāmyamityabhidhīyate..
kālāpekṣaṃ kriyāpekṣaṃ guṇāpekṣamiti smṛtau.. 4.75 ..
1.4.d:
इच्छासंस्थं च यद्दानं काम्यमित्यभिधीयते..
कालापेक्षं क्रियापेक्षं गुणापेक्षमिति स्मृतौ.. 4.75 ..
1.4.m: and the gift which rests upon a specific wish, is designated as the desired (kāmya). / Dependent on time, dependent on a rite, and dependent on virtues—in the legal tradition,

1.4.s:
tridhā naumittikaṃ proktaṃ sadā homavivarjitam..
iti proktāḥ prakārāste traividhyamabhidhīyate.. 4.76 ..
1.4.d:
त्रिधा नौमित्तिकं प्रोक्तं सदा होमविवर्जितम्..
इति प्रोक्ताः प्रकारास्ते त्रैविध्यमभिधीयते.. 4.76 ..
1.4.m: the occasional (naimittika) is declared to be threefold, always free from oblations (homa). / Thus the types have been spoken to you. The threefold classification is now stated:

1.4.s:
aṣṭottamāni catvāri madhyamāni vidhānataḥ..
kānīyasāni śeṣāṇi trividhatvamidaṃ viduḥ.. 4.77 ..
1.4.d:
अष्टोत्तमानि चत्वारि मध्यमानि विधानतः..
कानीयसानि शेषाणि त्रिविधत्वमिदं विदुः.. 4.77 ..
1.4.m: Eight are superior, four are intermediate by rule, / and the rest are inferior: thus they know this threefold classification.

1.4.s:
gṛhaprāsādavidyābhūgokūpaprāṇahāṭakam..
etānyuttamadānāni uttamadravyadānataḥ.. 4.78 ..
1.4.d:
गृहप्रासादविद्याभूगोकूपप्राणहाटकम्..
एतान्युत्तमदानानि उत्तमद्रव्यदानतः.. 4.78 ..
1.4.m: A house, a temple, knowledge, land, a cow, a well, life-saving protection, and gold: / these are superior gifts, owing to the donation of superior articles.

1.4.s:
annārāmaṃ ca vāsāṃsi hayaprabhṛtivāhanam..
dānāni madhyamānīti madhyamadravyadānataḥ.. 4.79 ..
1.4.d:
अन्नारामं च वासांसि हयप्रभृतिवाहनम्..
दानानि मध्यमानीति मध्यमद्रव्यदानतः.. 4.79 ..
1.4.m: Food, a grove, garments, and a conveyance such as a horse: / these are intermediate gifts, owing to the donation of intermediate articles.

1.4.s: upānacchatrapātrādidadhimadhvāsanāni ca.. 4.80 ..
1.4.d: उपानच्छत्रपात्रादिदधिमध्वासनानि च.. 4.80 ..
1.4.m: Shoes, an umbrella, utensils, curds, honey, and seats,

1.4.s:
dīpakāṣṭhopalādīni caramaṃ bahuvārṣikam..
iti kānīyasānyāhurdānanāśatrayaṃ śrṛṇu.. 4.81 ..
1.4.d:
दीपकाष्ठोपलादीनि चरमं बहुवार्षिकम्..
इति कानीयसान्याहुर्दाननाशत्रयं श्रृणु.. 4.81 ..
1.4.m: lamps, firewood, stones, and the like, and finally things lasting for many years: / thus they speak of the inferior gifts. Hear of the three destroyers of gifts:

1.4.s:
yaddattvā tapyate paścādāsuraṃ taddhṛthā matam..
aśraddhayā yaddadāti rākṣasaṃ syādvṛthaiva tat.. 4.82 ..
1.4.d:
यद्दत्त्वा तप्यते पश्चादासुरं तद्धृथा मतम्..
अश्रद्धया यद्ददाति राक्षसं स्याद्वृथैव तत्.. 4.82 ..
1.4.m: That which, after giving, one regrets, is considered demonic (āsura) and useless. / That which one gives without faith is monstrous (rākṣasa) and entirely in vain.

1.4.s:
yaccākruśya dadātyaṃga dattvā vākrośati dvijam..
paiśācaṃ tadvṛthā dānaṃdānanāśāstrayastvamī.. 4.83 ..
1.4.d:
यच्चाक्रुश्य ददात्यंग दत्त्वा वाक्रोशति द्विजम्..
पैशाचं तद्वृथा दानंदाननाशास्त्रयस्त्वमी.. 4.83 ..
1.4.m: And that which one gives after reviling, O dear one, or having given, one reviles the twice-born— / that is ghostly (paiśāca), a futile gift. These are the three destroyers of gifts.

1.4.s:
iti saptapadairbaddhaṃ dānamāhātmya muttamam..
śaktyā te kīrtitaṃ rājansādhu vā'sādhu vā vada.. 4.84 ..
1.4.d:
इति सप्तपदैर्बद्धं दानमाहात्म्य मुत्तमम्..
शक्त्या ते कीर्तितं राजन्साधु वाऽसाधु वा वद.. 4.84 ..
1.4.m: Thus the excellent greatness of gifts, composed of seven elements, / has been recited to you according to my ability, O King; tell me whether it is good or not good.

1.4.s:
..dharmavarmovāca..
adya me saphalaṃ janma adya me saphalaṃ tapaḥ..
adya te kṛtakṛtyo'smi kṛtaḥ kṛtimatāṃ vara.. 4.85 ..
1.4.d:
..धर्मवर्मोवाच..
अद्य मे सफलं जन्म अद्य मे सफलं तपः..
अद्य ते कृतकृत्योऽस्मि कृतः कृतिमतां वर.. 4.85 ..
1.4.m: Dharmavarmā said: / Today my birth is fruitful; today my austerity is fruitful; / today, O best among the accomplished, I have been made successful by you.

1.4.s:
paṭhitvā sakalaṃ janma brahmacāri yathā vṛthā..
bahukleśātprāptabhāryaḥ sāvṛthā'priyavādinī.. 4.86 ..
1.4.d:
पठित्वा सकलं जन्म ब्रह्मचारि यथा वृथा..
बहुक्लेशात्प्राप्तभार्यः सावृथाऽप्रियवादिनी.. 4.86 ..
1.4.m: Just as a student of the Veda, having studied his whole life, is in vain; / just as a wife obtained through great trouble, if she speaks unpleasant words, is in vain;

1.4.s:
kleśena kṛtvā kūpaṃ vā sa ca kṣārodako vṛthā..
bahukleśairjanma nītaṃ vinā dharmaṃ tathā vṛthā.. 4.87 ..
1.4.d:
क्लेशेन कृत्वा कूपं वा स च क्षारोदको वृथा..
बहुक्लेशैर्जन्म नीतं विना धर्मं तथा वृथा.. 4.87 ..
1.4.m: or just as a well made with great trouble, if its water is saline, is in vain; / so is a life spent through many troubles in vain without dharma.

1.4.s:
evaṃ me yadvṛthā nāma jātaṃ tatsaphalaṃ tvayā..
kṛtaṃ tasmānnamastubhyaṃ dvijebhyaśca namonamaḥ.. 4.88 ..
1.4.d:
एवं मे यद्वृथा नाम जातं तत्सफलं त्वया..
कृतं तस्मान्नमस्तुभ्यं द्विजेभ्यश्च नमोनमः.. 4.88 ..
1.4.m: Thus, that which was called my futile existence has been made fruitful by you; / therefore, obeisance to you, and repeated obeisance to the twice-born!

1.4.s: satyamāha purā viṣṇuḥ kumārānviṣṇusadbhani.. 4.89 ..
1.4.d: सत्यमाह पुरा विष्णुः कुमारान्विष्णुसद्भनि.. 4.89 ..
1.4.m: Truly did Viṣṇu say of old to the Kumāras in Viṣṇu's abode:

1.4.s:
nāhaṃ tathādbhi yajamānahavirvitānaścayotad‌ghṛtaplutamadanhutabhuṅmukhena..
yadbrāhmaṇasya mukhataścaratonughāsaṃ tuṣṭasya mayyavahitairnijakarmapākaiḥ.. 4.90 ..
1.4.d:
नाहं तथाद्भि यजमानहविर्वितानश्चयोतद्‌घृतप्लुतमदन्हुतभुङ्मुखेन..
यद्ब्राह्मणस्य मुखतश्चरतोनुघासं तुष्टस्य मय्यवहितैर्निजकर्मपाकैः.. 4.90 ..
1.4.m: 'I do not eat through the mouth of the fire-god consuming offerings flooded with dripping clarified butter from the expanse of the sacrificer's oblations, / as I eat through the mouth of a brahmin partaking of morsels, one who is satisfied and intent upon me through the fruition of his own duties.'

1.4.s:
tanmayā'śarmaṇā vāpi yadvipreṣvapriyaṃ kṛtam..
sarvasya prabhavo viprāstatkṣamatāṃ prasādaye.. 4.91 ..
1.4.d:
तन्मयाऽशर्मणा वापि यद्विप्रेष्वप्रियं कृतम्..
सर्वस्य प्रभवो विप्रास्तत्क्षमतां प्रसादये.. 4.91 ..
1.4.m: Therefore, whatever unpleasant thing was done by miserable me towards the brahmins— / for brahmins are the masters of everything—may they forgive that; I seek their favor.

1.4.s:
tvaṃ ca kosi na sāmānyaḥ praṇamyāhaṃ prasādaye..
ātmānaṃ khyāpaya mune proktaścetyabravaṃ tadā.. 4.92 ..
1.4.d:
त्वं च कोसि न सामान्यः प्रणम्याहं प्रसादये..
आत्मानं ख्यापय मुने प्रोक्तश्चेत्यब्रवं तदा.. 4.92 ..
1.4.m: And who are you? You are no ordinary person. Bowing down, I propitiate you. / Make yourself known, O sage!" Having been thus addressed, I then spoke:

1.4.s:
..nārada uvāca..
nārado'smi nṛpaśreṣṭha sthānakārthī samāgataḥ..
proktaṃ ca dehi me dravyaṃ bhūmiṃ ca sthānahetave.. 4.93 ..
1.4.d:
..नारद उवाच..
नारदोऽस्मि नृपश्रेष्ठ स्थानकार्थी समागतः..
प्रोक्तं च देहि मे द्रव्यं भूमिं च स्थानहेतवे.. 4.93 ..
1.4.m: Nārada said: / "I am Nārada, O best of kings, arrived here seeking a site. / And I say: grant me wealth and land for the sake of a site.

1.4.s:
yadyapīyaṃ devatānāṃ bhūmirdravyaṃ ca pārthiva..
tathāpi yasminyaḥ kāle rājā prārthyaḥ sa niścitam.. 4.94 ..
1.4.d:
यद्यपीयं देवतानां भूमिर्द्रव्यं च पार्थिव..
तथापि यस्मिन्यः काले राजा प्रार्थ्यः स निश्चितम्.. 4.94 ..
1.4.m: Although this land and wealth belong to the gods, O king, / nevertheless, whoever is king at a given time is indeed the one to be petitioned.

1.4.s:
sahīśvarasyāvatāro bharttā dātā'bhayasya saḥ..
tathaiva tvāmahaṃ yāce dravyaśuddhipsayā..
pūrva mamālayaṃ dehi deyārthe prārthanāparaḥ.. 4.95 ..
1.4.d:
सहीश्वरस्यावतारो भर्त्ता दाताऽभयस्य सः..
तथैव त्वामहं याचे द्रव्यशुद्धिप्सया..
पूर्व ममालयं देहि देयार्थे प्रार्थनापरः.. 4.95 ..
1.4.m: For he is an incarnation of the Lord (Īśvara), the protector, and the granter of fearlessness. / Just so do I ask you, desiring purity of the wealth. / First give me an abode, being intent upon requesting what is to be given."

1.4.s:
..rājovāca..
yadi tvaṃ nārado vipra rājyamastvakhilaṃ tava..
ahaṃ hi brāhmaṇānāṃ te dāsyaṃ kartā na saṃśayaḥ.. 4.96 ..
1.4.d:
..राजोवाच..
यदि त्वं नारदो विप्र राज्यमस्त्वखिलं तव..
अहं हि ब्राह्मणानां ते दास्यं कर्ता न संशयः.. 4.96 ..
1.4.m: The king said: / "If you are Nārada, O brahmin, let the entire kingdom be yours! / For I shall indeed render service to you brahmins, without doubt."

1.4.s:
..nārada uvāca..
yadyasmākaṃ bhavānbhaktastatte kāryaṃ ca no vacaḥ.. 4.97 ..
1.4.d:
..नारद उवाच..
यद्यस्माकं भवान्भक्तस्तत्ते कार्यं च नो वचः.. 4.97 ..
1.4.m: Nārada said: / "If you are devoted to us, then our word must be carried out by you:

1.4.s:
sarvaṃ yattaddehi me dravyamuktaṃ bhuvaṃ ca me saptagavyūtimātrām..
bhūyāttvattopyasya rakṣeti so'pi mene tvahaṃ ciṃtaye cārthaśeṣam.. 4.98 ..
iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ prathame māheśvarakhaṇḍe kaumāri kākhaṇḍe nāradārjunasaṃvāde dānabhedapraśaṃsāvarṇanaṃnāma caturtho'dhyāyaḥ.. 4 .. cha ..
'
1.4.d:
सर्वं यत्तद्देहि मे द्रव्यमुक्तं भुवं च मे सप्तगव्यूतिमात्राम्..
भूयात्त्वत्तोप्यस्य रक्षेति सोऽपि मेने त्वहं चिंतये चार्थशेषम्.. 4.98 ..
इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां प्रथमे माहेश्वरखण्डे कौमारि काखण्डे नारदार्जुनसंवादे दानभेदप्रशंसावर्णनंनाम चतुर्थोऽध्यायः.. 4 .. छ ..
'
1.4.m:
Grant me all that wealth which was mentioned, and land measuring seven gavyūtis. / May protection also come from you for this." He assented, while I thought about the remaining matter.
Thus ends the fourth chapter, titled “Description of the Praise of the Varieties of Gifts,” in the dialogue between Nārada and Arjuna, in the Kaumārikākhaṇḍa of the first section, the Māheśvarakhaṇḍa, in the Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.
'

1.4.s:
.. nārada uvāca..
tato'haṃ dharmavarmāṇaṃ procya tiṣṭheddhanaṃ tvayi..
kṛtyakāle grahīṣyāmītyāgamaṃ raivataṃ girim.. 5.1 ..
1.4.d:
.. नारद उवाच..
ततोऽहं धर्मवर्माणं प्रोच्य तिष्ठेद्धनं त्वयि..
कृत्यकाले ग्रहीष्यामीत्यागमं रैवतं गिरिम्.. 5.1 ..

1.4.s:
āsaṃ pramuditaścāhaṃ paśyaṃstaṃ girisattamam..
āhvayānaṃ narānsādhūnbhūmerbhujamivocchritam.. 5.2 ..
1.4.d:
आसं प्रमुदितश्चाहं पश्यंस्तं गिरिसत्तमम्..
