आह्वयानं नरान्साधून्भूमेर्भुजमिवोच्छ्रितम्.. 5.2 ..
1.4.m:
And I was overjoyed seeing that best of mountains,
which seemed to beckon virtuous men, like an upraised arm of the earth,

1.4.s:
yasminnānāvidhā vṛkṣāḥ prakāśaṃte samaṃtataḥ..
sādhuṃ gṛhapatiṃ prāpya putrabhāryādayo yathā.. 5.3 ..
1.4.d:
यस्मिन्नानाविधा वृक्षाः प्रकाशंते समंततः..
साधुं गृहपतिं प्राप्य पुत्रभार्यादयो यथा.. 5.3 ..
1.4.m:
on which trees of various kinds shine on all sides,
just as sons, wives, and others do upon gaining a virtuous householder;

1.4.s:
muditā yatra saṃtṛptā vāśaṃte kokilādayaḥ..
sadgurorjñānasaṃpannā yathā śiṣyagaṇā bhuvi.. 5.4 ..
1.4.d:
मुदिता यत्र संतृप्ता वाशंते कोकिलादयः..
सद्गुरोर्ज्ञानसंपन्ना यथा शिष्यगणा भुवि.. 5.4 ..
1.4.m:
where cuckoos and other birds sing joyfully and contentedly,
just as groups of disciples on earth do, endowed with knowledge from a good teacher;

1.4.s:
yatra taptvā tapo martyā yathepsitamavāpnuyuḥ..
śrīmahādevamāsādya bhakto yadvanmanoratham.. 5.5 ..
1.4.d:
यत्र तप्त्वा तपो मर्त्या यथेप्सितमवाप्नुयुः..
श्रीमहादेवमासाद्य भक्तो यद्वन्मनोरथम्.. 5.5 ..
1.4.m:
where mortals, having performed austerity, obtain their desire,
just as a devotee obtains his heart's wish upon approaching the venerable Mahādeva.

1.4.s:
tasyāhaṃ ca gireḥ pārtha samāsādya mahāśilām..
śītasaurabhyamaṃdena prīṇīto'ciṃtayaṃ hṛdi.. 5.6 ..
1.4.d:
तस्याहं च गिरेः पार्थ समासाद्य महाशिलाम्..
शीतसौरभ्यमंदेन प्रीणीतोऽचिंतयं हृदि.. 5.6 ..
1.4.m:
Having approached a great rock on that mountain, O son of Pṛthā,
refreshed by a cool, fragrant, gentle breeze, I reflected in my heart:

1.4.s:
tāvanmayā sthānamāptaṃ yadatīva sudurlabham..
idānīṃ brāhmaṇārthe'haṃ kurve tāvadupakramam.. 5.7 ..
1.4.d:
तावन्मया स्थानमाप्तं यदतीव सुदुर्लभम्..
इदानीं ब्राह्मणार्थेऽहं कुर्वे तावदुपक्रमम्.. 5.7 ..
1.4.m:
“I have attained a place that is exceedingly difficult to find;
now I shall begin my undertaking for the sake of the brahmins.

1.4.s:
brāhmaṇāśca vilokya me ye hi pātratamā matāḥ..
tathā hi cātra śrūyaṃte vacāṃsi śrutivādinām.. 5.8 ..
1.4.d:
ब्राह्मणाश्च विलोक्य मे ये हि पात्रतमा मताः..
तथा हि चात्र श्रूयंते वचांसि श्रुतिवादिनाम्.. 5.8 ..
1.4.m:
And I must seek out brahmins who are considered most worthy recipients;
for indeed, the words of the teachers of the Vedas are heard in this regard:

1.4.s:
na jalottaraṇe śaktā yadvannauḥ karṇavarjitā..
tadvacchreṣṭho'pyanācāro vipro noddharaṇakṣamaḥ.. 5.9 ..
1.4.d:
न जलोत्तरणे शक्ता यद्वन्नौः कर्णवर्जिता..
तद्वच्छ्रेष्ठोऽप्यनाचारो विप्रो नोद्धरणक्षमः.. 5.9 ..
1.4.m:
‘Just as a boat lacking a rudder is not capable of crossing the water,
so even an eminent twice-born who lacks proper conduct cannot rescue [others].

1.4.s:
brāhmaṇo hyanadhīyānastṛṇāgniriva śāmyati..
tasmai havyaṃ na dātavyaṃ na hi bhasmani hūyate.. 5.10 ..
1.4.d:
ब्राह्मणो ह्यनधीयानस्तृणाग्निरिव शाम्यति..
तस्मै हव्यं न दातव्यं न हि भस्मनि हूयते.. 5.10 ..
1.4.m:
For a brahmin who does not study goes out like a fire of grass;
sacrificial offering should not be given to him, for an offering is not poured into ashes.

1.4.s:
dānapātramatikramya yadapātre pradīyate..
taddattaṃ gāmatikramya gardabhasya gavāhnikam.. 5.11 ..
1.4.d:
दानपात्रमतिक्रम्य यदपात्रे प्रदीयते..
तद्दत्तं गामतिक्रम्य गर्दभस्य गवाह्निकम्.. 5.11 ..
1.4.m:
When, bypassing a worthy recipient, a gift is given to an unworthy recipient,
that gift is like bypassing a cow and feeding the cow's daily portion to a donkey.’

1.4.s:
ūṣare vāpitaṃ bījaṃ bhinnabhāṃḍe ca goduham..
bhasmanīva hutaṃ havyaṃ mūrkhe dānamaśāśvatam.. 5.12 ..
1.4.d:
ऊषरे वापितं बीजं भिन्नभांडे च गोदुहम्..
भस्मनीव हुतं हव्यं मूर्खे दानमशाश्वतम्.. 5.12 ..
1.4.m: Seed sown in barren soil, cow's milk placed in a broken pot, / an oblation offered into ashes, and a gift given to a fool are not lasting.

1.4.s:
vidhihīne tathā'pātre yo dadāti pratigraham..
na kevalaṃ hi tadyāti śeṣaṃ puṇyaṃ praṇaśyati.. 5.13 ..
1.4.d:
विधिहीने तथाऽपात्रे यो ददाति प्रतिग्रहम्..
न केवलं हि तद्याति शेषं पुण्यं प्रणश्यति.. 5.13 ..
1.4.m: Whoever gives a gift contrary to sacred injunction and to an unworthy recipient, / not only does that [gift] go in vain, but the rest of his merit also perishes.

1.4.s:
bhūrāptā gaustathā bhogāḥ suvarṇaṃ dehameva ca..
aśvaścakṣustathā vāso ghṛtaṃ tejastilāḥ prajāḥ.. 5.14 ..
1.4.d:
भूराप्ता गौस्तथा भोगाः सुवर्णं देहमेव च..
अश्वश्चक्षुस्तथा वासो घृतं तेजस्तिलाः प्रजाः.. 5.14 ..
1.4.m: The earth, if received, [destroys] his body; a cow, his pleasures; gold, his bodily form; / a horse, his sight; a garment, his splendor; ghee, his vigor; and sesame seeds, his offspring.

1.4.s:
ghnaṃti tasmādavidvāṃstu bibhiyācca pratigrahāt..
svalpaka kenāpyavidvāṃstu paṃke gauriva sīdati.. 5.15 ..
1.4.d:
घ्नंति तस्मादविद्वांस्तु बिभियाच्च प्रतिग्रहात्..
स्वल्पक केनाप्यविद्वांस्तु पंके गौरिव सीदति.. 5.15 ..
1.4.m: They destroy [him]; therefore, an unlearned person should fear accepting gifts. / Even by a little [acceptance], an unlearned man sinks like a cow in mud.

1.4.s:
tasmādye gūḍhatapaso gūḍhasvādhyāyasādhakāḥ..
svadāraniratāḥ śāṃtāsteṣu dattaṃ sadā'kṣayam.. 5.16 ..
1.4.d:
तस्माद्ये गूढतपसो गूढस्वाध्यायसाधकाः..
स्वदारनिरताः शांतास्तेषु दत्तं सदाऽक्षयम्.. 5.16 ..
1.4.m: Therefore, what is given to those of secret austerity, practitioners of secret Vedic study, / devoted to their own wives, and peaceful, is forever imperishable.

1.4.s:
deśe kāla upāyena dravyaṃ śraddhāsamanvitam..
pātre pradīyate yattatsakalaṃ dharmalakṣaṇam.. 5.17 ..
1.4.d:
देशे काल उपायेन द्रव्यं श्रद्धासमन्वितम्..
पात्रे प्रदीयते यत्तत्सकलं धर्मलक्षणम्.. 5.17 ..
1.4.m: That which is given in proper place and time, by proper means, / with wealth accompanied by faith to a worthy recipient—all that is the mark of righteousness.

1.4.s:
na vidyayā kevalayā tapasā vāpi pātratā..
yatra vṛttimime cobhe tadvi pātraṃ pracakṣate.. 5.18 ..
1.4.d:
न विद्यया केवलया तपसा वापि पात्रता..
यत्र वृत्तिमिमे चोभे तद्वि पात्रं प्रचक्षते.. 5.18 ..
1.4.m: Worthiness does not come by mere learning, nor even by austerity; / where conduct and both of these exist, that alone they declare to be a worthy recipient.

1.4.s:
teṣāṃ trayāṇāṃ madhye ca vidyā mukhyo mahāguṇaḥ..
vidyāṃ vināṃdhavadviprāścakṣuṣmaṃto hi te matāḥ.. 5.19 ..
1.4.d:
तेषां त्रयाणां मध्ये च विद्या मुख्यो महागुणः..
विद्यां विनांधवद्विप्राश्चक्षुष्मंतो हि ते मताः.. 5.19 ..
1.4.m: And among these three, learning is the foremost, great quality; / brahmins without learning are like the blind, while those [with it] are considered to have eyes.

1.4.s:
tasmāccakṣuṣmato vidvāndeśe deśe parīkṣayet..
praśrānye mama vakṣyaṃti tebhyo dāsyāmyahaṃ tataḥ.. 5.20 ..
1.4.d:
तस्माच्चक्षुष्मतो विद्वान्देशे देशे परीक्षयेत्..
प्रश्रान्ये मम वक्ष्यंति तेभ्यो दास्याम्यहं ततः.. 5.20 ..
1.4.m: Therefore, the wise man should test in every region those who have eyes: / 'To those who will answer my questions, I shall then give.'

1.4.s:
iti saṃciṃtya manasā tasmāddeśātsamutthitaḥ..
āśrameṣu maharṣīṇāṃ vicarāmyasmi phālguna.. 5.21 ..
1.4.d:
इति संचिंत्य मनसा तस्माद्देशात्समुत्थितः..
आश्रमेषु महर्षीणां विचराम्यस्मि फाल्गुन.. 5.21 ..
1.4.m: Having reflected thus in my mind, having arisen from that place, / I wander through the hermitages of the great seers, O Phālguna,

1.4.s:
imāñchlokāngāyamānaḥ praśrarūpāñchṛṇuṣva tān..
mātṛkāṃ ko vijānāti katidhā kīdṛśākṣarām.. 5.22 ..
1.4.d:
इमाञ्छ्लोकान्गायमानः प्रश्ररूपाञ्छृणुष्व तान्..
मातृकां को विजानाति कतिधा कीदृशाक्षराम्.. 5.22 ..
1.4.m: singing these verses that take the form of questions; hear them: / 'Who knows the alphabet (mātṛkā)—of how many kinds and of what letters?

1.4.s:
paṃcapaṃcādbhutaṃ gehaṃ ko vijānāti vā dvijaḥ..
bahurūpāṃ striyaṃ kartumekarūpāṃ ca vetti kaḥ.. 5.23 ..
1.4.d:
पंचपंचाद्भुतं गेहं को विजानाति वा द्विजः..
बहुरूपां स्त्रियं कर्तुमेकरूपां च वेत्ति कः.. 5.23 ..
1.4.m: Or which twice-born knows the marvelous house of five times five? / And who knows how to make a woman of many forms, and one of a single form?

1.4.s:
ko vā citrakathābaṃdhaṃ vetti saṃsāragocaraḥ..
ko vārṇavamahāgrāhaṃ vetti vidyāparāyaṇaḥ.. 5.24 ..
1.4.d:
को वा चित्रकथाबंधं वेत्ति संसारगोचरः..
को वार्णवमहाग्राहं वेत्ति विद्यापरायणः.. 5.24 ..
1.4.m: Or who, moving in the world of rebirth, knows the composition of wondrous tales? / Or who, devoted to learning, knows the great crocodile of the ocean?

1.4.s:
ko vāṣṭavidhaṃ brāhmaṇyaṃ vetti brāhmaṇasattamaḥ..
yugānāṃ ca caturṇāṃ vā ko mūladivasānvadet.. 5.25 ..
1.4.d:
को वाष्टविधं ब्राह्मण्यं वेत्ति ब्राह्मणसत्तमः..
युगानां च चतुर्णां वा को मूलदिवसान्वदेत्.. 5.25 ..
1.4.m: Or what best of brahmins knows the eightfold state of a brahmin? / Or who can tell the initial days of the four yugas?

1.4.s:
caturdaśamanūnāṃ vā mūlavāsaraṃ vetti kaḥ..
kasmiṃścaiva dine prāpa pūrvaṃ vā bhāskaro ratham.. 5.26 ..
1.4.d:
चतुर्दशमनूनां वा मूलवासरं वेत्ति कः..
कस्मिंश्चैव दिने प्राप पूर्वं वा भास्करो रथम्.. 5.26 ..
1.4.m: Or who knows the initial days of the fourteen Manus? / And on which day did the sun formerly obtain his chariot?

1.4.s:
udvejayati bhūtāni kṛṣṇāhiriva vetti kaḥ..
ko vāsminghorasaṃsāre dakṣadakṣatamo bhavet.. 5.27 ..
1.4.d:
उद्वेजयति भूतानि कृष्णाहिरिव वेत्ति कः..
को वास्मिन्घोरसंसारे दक्षदक्षतमो भवेत्.. 5.27 ..
1.4.m: Who knows what agitates creatures like a black serpent? / Or who in this dreadful worldly existence is the most skillful of the skillful?

1.4.s:
paṃthānāvapi dvau kaścidvetti vakti ca brāhmaṇaḥ..
iti me dvādaśa praśrānye vidurbrāhmaṇottamāḥ.. 5.28 ..
1.4.d:
पंथानावपि द्वौ कश्चिद्वेत्ति वक्ति च ब्राह्मणः..
इति मे द्वादश प्रश्रान्ये विदुर्ब्राह्मणोत्तमाः.. 5.28 ..
1.4.m: Does any brahmin also know and declare the two paths?' / If any excellent brahmins know these twelve questions of mine,

1.4.s:
te me pūjyatamāsteṣāmahāmārādhakaściram..
ityahaṃ gāyamāno vai bhramitaḥ sakalāṃ mahīm.. 5.29 ..
1.4.d:
ते मे पूज्यतमास्तेषामहामाराधकश्चिरम्..
इत्यहं गायमानो वै भ्रमितः सकलां महीम्.. 5.29 ..
1.4.m: they are most worthy of my worship, and I shall be their worshiper for a long time. / Singing thus, indeed, I wandered over the entire earth.

1.4.s:
te cāhurduḥkhadāḥ khyātāḥ praśrāste kurmahe namaḥ..
ityahaṃ sakalāṃ pṛthvīṃ viciṃtyālabdhabrāhmaṇaḥ.. 5.30 ..
1.4.d:
ते चाहुर्दुःखदाः ख्याताः प्रश्रास्ते कुर्महे नमः..
इत्यहं सकलां पृथ्वीं विचिंत्यालब्धब्राह्मणः.. 5.30 ..
1.4.m: And they said: 'Your well-known questions cause distress; we bow to you!' / Thus, having searched the entire earth without finding [such] a brahmin,

1.4.s:
himādriśikharāsīno bhūyaściṃtāmavāptavān..
sarve vilokitā viprāḥ kimataḥ kartumutsahe.. 5.31 ..
1.4.d:
हिमाद्रिशिखरासीनो भूयश्चिंतामवाप्तवान्..
सर्वे विलोकिता विप्राः किमतः कर्तुमुत्सहे.. 5.31 ..
1.4.m: seated on the peak of the Himalaya mountain, I again fell into anxiety: / 'All the brahmins have been seen; what can I venture to do henceforth?'

1.4.s:
tato me ciṃtayānasya punarjātā matistviyam..
adyāpi na gataścāhaṃ kalāpagrāmamuttamam.. 5.32 ..
1.4.d:
ततो मे चिंतयानस्य पुनर्जाता मतिस्त्वियम्..
अद्यापि न गतश्चाहं कलापग्राममुत्तमम्.. 5.32 ..
1.4.m: Then, as I was pondering, this thought occurred to me again: / 'Even until today, I have not gone to the supreme Kalāpagrāma,

1.4.s:
yasminviprāḥ saṃvasaṃti mūrtānīva tapāṃsi ca..
caturāśītisāhasrāḥ śrutādhyayanaśālinaḥ.. 5.33 ..
1.4.d:
यस्मिन्विप्राः संवसंति मूर्तानीव तपांसि च..
चतुराशीतिसाहस्राः श्रुताध्ययनशालिनः.. 5.33 ..
1.4.m: in which dwell brahmins who are austerities embodied, as it were, / eighty-four thousand in number, endowed with Vedic study and recitation.

1.4.s:
sthāne tasmingamiṣyāmītyuktvāhaṃ calitastadā..
khecaro himamākramya paraṃ pāraṃ gatastataḥ.. 5.34 ..
1.4.d:
स्थाने तस्मिन्गमिष्यामीत्युक्त्वाहं चलितस्तदा..
खेचरो हिममाक्रम्य परं पारं गतस्ततः.. 5.34 ..
1.4.m: I will go to that place'—having said this, I then set out; / moving through the sky, crossing over the snow, I then went to the farther shore.

1.4.s:
adrākṣaṃ puṇyabhūmisthaṃ grāmaratnamahaṃ mahat..
śatayojanavistīrṇaṃ nānāvṛkṣasamākulam.. 5.35 ..
1.4.d:
अद्राक्षं पुण्यभूमिस्थं ग्रामरत्नमहं महत्..
शतयोजनविस्तीर्णं नानावृक्षसमाकुलम्.. 5.35 ..
1.4.m: Situated on sacred ground, I beheld that great gem of a village, / a hundred yojanas wide, crowded with various trees,

1.4.s:
yatra puṇyavatāṃ saṃti śataśaḥ pravarāśramāḥ..
sarveṣāmapi jīvānāṃ yatrānyonyaṃ na duṣṭatā.. 5.36 ..
1.4.d:
यत्र पुण्यवतां संति शतशः प्रवराश्रमाः..
सर्वेषामपि जीवानां यत्रान्योन्यं न दुष्टता.. 5.36 ..
1.4.m: where there are hundreds of eminent hermitages of the meritorious, / and where among all living beings there is no mutual malice;

1.4.s:
yajñabhājāṃ munīnāṃ yadupakārakaraṃ sadā..
satāṃ dharmavatāṃ yadvadupakāro na śāmyati.. 5.37 ..
1.4.d:
यज्ञभाजां मुनीनां यदुपकारकरं सदा..
सतां धर्मवतां यद्वदुपकारो न शाम्यति.. 5.37 ..
1.4.m: which always confers benefit upon the sages who participate in sacrifices, / just as the benefaction of the good and righteous never ceases;

1.4.s:
munīnāṃ yatra paramaṃ sthānaṃ cāpyavināśakṛt..
svāhāsvadhāvaṣaṭkāra hantakāro na naśyati.. 5.38 ..
1.4.d:
मुनीनां यत्र परमं स्थानं चाप्यविनाशकृत्..
स्वाहास्वधावषट्कार हन्तकारो न नश्यति.. 5.38 ..
1.4.m: where there is the supreme and imperishable abode of the sages, / and the utterances svāhā, svadhā, vaṣaṭ, and hanta never perish;

1.4.s:
yatra kṛtayugastārthaṃ bījaṃ pārthāvaśiṣyate..
sūryasya somavaṃśasya brāhmaṇānāṃ tathaiva ca.. 5.39 ..
1.4.d:
यत्र कृतयुगस्तार्थं बीजं पार्थावशिष्यते..
सूर्यस्य सोमवंशस्य ब्राह्मणानां तथैव च.. 5.39 ..
1.4.m: where the seed remains for the sake of the Kṛta age, O son of Pṛthā, / of the solar dynasty, of the lunar dynasty, and likewise of the brahmins.

1.4.s:
sthānakaṃ tatsamāsādya praviṣṭo'haṃ dvijāśramān..
tatra te vividhānvādānvivadaṃte dvijottamāḥ.. 5.40 ..
1.4.d:
स्थानकं तत्समासाद्य प्रविष्टोऽहं द्विजाश्रमान्..
तत्र ते विविधान्वादान्विवदंते द्विजोत्तमाः.. 5.40 ..
1.4.m: Having reached that place, I entered the hermitages of the twice-born. / There, those excellent twice-born were disputing in various debates,

1.4.s:
parasparaṃ ciṃtayānā vedā mūrtidharā yathā..
tatra medhāvinaḥ kecidarthamanyaiḥ prapūritam.. 5.41 ..
1.4.d:
परस्परं चिंतयाना वेदा मूर्तिधरा यथा..
तत्र मेधाविनः केचिदर्थमन्यैः प्रपूरितम्.. 5.41 ..
1.4.m: debating with one another like the Vedas embodied. / There, some intelligent, great-souled men tore apart the meaning

1.4.s:
vicikṣipurmahātmāno nabhogatamivāmiṣam..
tatrā'haṃ karamudyamya prāvocaṃ pūryatāṃ dvijāḥ.. 5.42 ..
1.4.d:
विचिक्षिपुर्महात्मानो नभोगतमिवामिषम्..
तत्राऽहं करमुद्यम्य प्रावोचं पूर्यतां द्विजाः.. 5.42 ..
1.4.m: completed by others, like meat falling through the sky. / There, raising my hand, I said: 'Cease, O twice-born!

1.4.s:
kākārāvaiḥ kimatairvo yadyasti jñānaśālitā..
vyākurudhvaṃ tataḥ praśrānmama durviṣahānbahūn.. 5.43 ..
1.4.d:
काकारावैः किमतैर्वो यद्यस्ति ज्ञानशालिता..
व्याकुरुध्वं ततः प्रश्रान्मम दुर्विषहान्बहून्.. 5.43 ..
1.4.m: What is the use of these crow-like cawings of yours? If you possess knowledge, / then expound my many unbearable questions!'

1.4.s:
..brāhmaṇā ūcuḥ..
vada brāhmaṇa praśrānsvāñchrutvā''dhāsyāmahe vayam..
paramo hyeṣa no lābhaḥ praśnānpṛcchati yadbhavān.. 5.44 ..
1.4.d:
..ब्राह्मणा ऊचुः..
वद ब्राह्मण प्रश्रान्स्वाञ्छ्रुत्वा'ऽधास्यामहे वयम्..
परमो ह्येष नो लाभः प्रश्नान्पृच्छति यद्भवान्.. 5.44 ..
1.4.m: The brahmins said: / 'State your questions, O brahmin; having heard them, we shall resolve them. / For this is our supreme gain, that you ask questions.'

1.4.s:
ahaṃ pūrvikayā te vai nyaṣedhaṃta parasparam..
ahaṃ pūrvamahaṃ pūrvamiti vīrā yathā raṇe.. 5.45 ..
1.4.d:
अहं पूर्विकया ते वै न्यषेधंत परस्परम्..
अहं पूर्वमहं पूर्वमिति वीरा यथा रणे.. 5.45 ..
1.4.m: Each striving to be first, they restrained one another, / like heroes in battle shouting, 'I first! I first!'

1.4.s:
tatastānabravaṃ praśrānahaṃ dvādaśa pūrvakān..
śrutvā te māmavocaṃta līlāyaṃto munīśvarāḥ.. 5.46 ..
1.4.d:
ततस्तानब्रवं प्रश्रानहं द्वादश पूर्वकान्..
श्रुत्वा ते मामवोचंत लीलायंतो मुनीश्वराः.. 5.46 ..
1.4.m: Then I spoke to them those twelve previous questions. / Having heard them, those lords of sages said to me playfully:

1.4.s:
kiṃ te dvija bālapraśnairamībhiḥ svalpakairapi..
asmākaṃ yannihīnaṃ tvaṃ manyase sa bravītvamūn.. 5.47 ..
1.4.d:
किं ते द्विज बालप्रश्नैरमीभिः स्वल्पकैरपि..
अस्माकं यन्निहीनं त्वं मन्यसे स ब्रवीत्वमून्.. 5.47 ..
1.4.m: 'O twice-born, what is the use of these childish, insignificant questions to you? / Let the one among us whom you consider the lowest speak them.'

1.4.s:
tatotivismitaścāhaṃ manyamānaḥ kṛtārthatām..
teṣāṃ nihīnaṃ saṃciṃtya prāvocaṃ prabravītvayam.. 5.48 ..
1.4.d:
ततोतिविस्मितश्चाहं मन्यमानः कृतार्थताम्..
तेषां निहीनं संचिंत्य प्रावोचं प्रब्रवीत्वयम्.. 5.48 ..
1.4.m: Then, greatly astonished and considering myself fulfilled, / having thought of the lowest among them, I said: 'Let this one speak.'

1.4.s:
tataḥ sutanunāmā sa bālo'bālo'bhyuvāca mām..
mama maṃdāyate vāṇī praśnaiḥ svalpaistava dvija..
tathāpi vacmi māṃ yasmānnihīnaṃ manyate bhavān.. 5.49 ..
1.4.d:
ततः सुतनुनामा स बालोऽबालोऽभ्युवाच माम्..
मम मंदायते वाणी प्रश्नैः स्वल्पैस्तव द्विज..
तथापि वच्मि मां यस्मान्निहीनं मन्यते भवान्.. 5.49 ..
1.4.m: Then that young boy named Sutanu, though no child [in wisdom], said to me: / 'My speech is dulled by your trivial questions, O twice-born; / nevertheless, I shall speak, since you consider me the lowest.'

1.4.s:
..sutanuruvāca..
akṣarāstu dvipaṃcāśanmātṛkāyāḥ prakīrtitāḥ.. 5.50 ..
1.4.d:
..सुतनुरुवाच..
अक्षरास्तु द्विपंचाशन्मातृकायाः प्रकीर्तिताः.. 5.50 ..
1.4.m: Sutanu said: / 'Fifty-two letters of the alphabet are proclaimed.

1.4.s:
oṃkāraḥ prathamastatra caturdaśa svarāstathā..
sparśāścaiva trayastriṃśadanusvārastathaiva ca.. 5.51 ..
1.4.d:
ओंकारः प्रथमस्तत्र चतुर्दश स्वरास्तथा..
स्पर्शाश्चैव त्रयस्त्रिंशदनुस्वारस्तथैव च.. 5.51 ..
1.4.m: The syllable Oṃ is the first among them, and likewise fourteen vowels, / and thirty-three consonants (sparśa), and likewise the anusvāra,

1.4.s:
visarjjanīyaśca paro jihvāmūlīya eva ca..
upadhmānīya evāpi dvipaṃcāśadamī smṛtāḥ.. 5.52 ..
1.4.d:
विसर्ज्जनीयश्च परो जिह्वामूलीय एव च..
उपध्मानीय एवापि द्विपंचाशदमी स्मृताः.. 5.52 ..
1.4.m: and next the visarjanīya, and also the jihvāmūlīya, / and also the upadhmānīya—these are remembered as fifty-two.

1.4.s:
iti te kathitā saṃkhyā arthaṃ caiṣāṃ śrṛṇu dvija..
asminnarthe cetihāsaṃ tava vakṣyāmi yaḥ purā.. 5.53 ..
1.4.d:
इति ते कथिता संख्या अर्थं चैषां श्रृणु द्विज..
अस्मिन्नर्थे चेतिहासं तव वक्ष्यामि यः पुरा.. 5.53 ..
1.4.m: Thus the number has been told to you; now hear their meaning, O twice-born. / Regarding this meaning, I will tell you a traditional story that formerly

1.4.s:
mithilāyāṃ pravṛtto'bhūdbrāhmaṇasya niveśane..
mithilāyāṃ purā puryāṃ brāhmaṇaḥ kauthumābhidhaḥ.. 5.54 ..
1.4.d:
मिथिलायां प्रवृत्तोऽभूद्ब्राह्मणस्य निवेशने..
मिथिलायां पुरा पुर्यां ब्राह्मणः कौथुमाभिधः.. 5.54 ..
1.4.m: occurred in Mithilā, in the dwelling of a brahmin. / In ancient times, in the city of Mithilā, there was a brahmin named Kauthuma,

1.4.s:
yena vidyāḥ prapaṭhitā vartaṃte bhuvi yā dvija..
ekatriṃśatsahasrāṇi varṣāṇāṃ sa kṛtādaraḥ.. 5.55 ..
1.4.d:
येन विद्याः प्रपठिता वर्तंते भुवि या द्विज..
एकत्रिंशत्सहस्राणि वर्षाणां स कृतादरः.. 5.55 ..
1.4.m: by whom were thoroughly studied whatever branches of learning exist on earth, O twice-born. / For thirty-one thousand years he, full of devotion,

1.4.s:
kṣaṇamapyanavacchinnaṃ paṭhitvā gehavānabhūt..
tataḥ kenāpi kālena kauthumasyābhavatsutaḥ.. 5.56 ..
1.4.d:
क्षणमप्यनवच्छिन्नं पठित्वा गेहवानभूत्..
ततः केनापि कालेन कौथुमस्याभवत्सुतः.. 5.56 ..
1.4.m: Having studied without interruption for even a moment, he became a householder. / Then, after some time, a son was born to Kauthuma.

1.4.s:
jaḍavadvarttamānaḥ sa mātṛkāṃ pratyapadyata..
paṭhitvā mātṛkāmanyannādhyeti sa kathaṃcana.. 5.57 ..
1.4.d:
जडवद्वर्त्तमानः स मातृकां प्रत्यपद्यत..
पठित्वा मातृकामन्यन्नाध्येति स कथंचन.. 5.57 ..
1.4.m: Living like an idiot, he undertook the alphabet. / Having recited the alphabet, he would not study anything else whatsoever.

1.4.s:
tataḥ pitā khinnarūpī jaḍaṃ taṃ samabhāṣata..
adhīṣva putrakādhīṣva tava dāsyāmi modakān.. 5.58 ..
1.4.d:
ततः पिता खिन्नरूपी जडं तं समभाषत..
अधीष्व पुत्रकाधीष्व तव दास्यामि मोदकान्.. 5.58 ..
1.4.m: Then his distressed father spoke to that idiot: / “Study, my boy, study! I will give you sweetmeats.

1.4.s: athānyasmai pradāsyāmi karṇāvutpāṭayāmi te.. 5.59 ..
1.4.d: अथान्यस्मै प्रदास्यामि कर्णावुत्पाटयामि ते.. 5.59 ..
1.4.m: Otherwise, I will give [them] to another, [and] I will tear off your ears!”

1.4.s:
..putra uvāca..
tāta kiṃ modakārthāya paṭhyate lobhahetave..
paṭhanaṃnāma yatpuṃsāṃ parāmārthaṃ hi tatsmṛtam.. 5.60 ..
1.4.d:
..पुत्र उवाच..
तात किं मोदकार्थाय पठ्यते लोभहेतवे..
पठनंनाम यत्पुंसां परामार्थं हि तत्स्मृतम्.. 5.60 ..
1.4.m: The son said: / “Father, is studying recited for the sake of sweetmeats, for the purpose of greed? / That which is study for men is remembered as aimed at the supreme goal.

1.4.s:
..kauthuma uvāca..
evaṃ te vadamānasya āyurbhavatu brahmaṇaḥ..
sādhvī buddhiriyaṃ te'stu kuto nādhyeṣyataḥ param.. 5.61 ..
1.4.d:
..कौथुम उवाच..
एवं ते वदमानस्य आयुर्भवतु ब्रह्मणः..
साध्वी बुद्धिरियं तेऽस्तु कुतो नाध्येष्यतः परम्.. 5.61 ..
1.4.m: Kauthuma said: / “May you, speaking thus, have the lifespan of Brahmā! / May this intellect of yours remain noble; why will you not study further?”

1.4.s:
..putra uvāca..
tāta sarvaṃ parijñeyaṃ jñānamatraiva vai yataḥ..
tataḥ paraṃ kaṃṭhaśoṣaḥ kimarthaṃ kriyate vada.. 5.62 ..
1.4.d:
..पुत्र उवाच..
तात सर्वं परिज्ञेयं ज्ञानमत्रैव वै यतः..
ततः परं कंठशोषः किमर्थं क्रियते वद.. 5.62 ..
1.4.m: The son said: / “Father, because all knowledge that is to be known is right here, / tell me, why is dryness of the throat produced beyond that?”

1.4.s:
..pitovāca..
vicitraṃ bhāṣase bāla jñāto'trārthaśca kastvayā..
brūhi brūhi punarvatsa śrotumicchāmi te giram.. 5.63 ..
1.4.d:
..पितोवाच..
विचित्रं भाषसे बाल ज्ञातोऽत्रार्थश्च कस्त्वया..
ब्रूहि ब्रूहि पुनर्वत्स श्रोतुमिच्छामि ते गिरम्.. 5.63 ..
1.4.m: The father said: / “You speak strange things, child! What meaning has been understood by you here? / Speak, speak again, my child! I wish to hear your words.”

1.4.s:
..putra uvāca..
ekatriṃśatsahasrāṇi paṭhitvāpi tvayā pitaḥ..
nānātarkānbhrāṃtireva saṃdhitā manasi svake.. 5.64 ..
1.4.d:
..पुत्र उवाच..
एकत्रिंशत्सहस्राणि पठित्वापि त्वया पितः..
नानातर्कान्भ्रांतिरेव संधिता मनसि स्वके.. 5.64 ..
1.4.m: The son said: / “Even though you have studied for thirty-one thousand [years], father, / only confusion about various arguments has been established in your mind.

1.4.s:
ayamayaṃ cāyamiti dharmo yo darśanoditaḥ..
teṣu vātāyate cetastava tannāśayāmi te.. 5.65 ..
1.4.d:
अयमयं चायमिति धर्मो यो दर्शनोदितः..
तेषु वातायते चेतस्तव तन्नाशयामि ते.. 5.65 ..
1.4.m: ‘This is duty, and this, and this,’ as declared by philosophical systems— / your mind acts like the wind in them; I shall destroy that [confusion] of yours.

1.4.s:
upadeśaṃ paṭhasyeva naivārthajño'si tattvataḥ..
pāṭhamātrā hi ye viprā dvipadāḥ paśavo hi te.. 5.66 ..
1.4.d:
उपदेशं पठस्येव नैवार्थज्ञोऽसि तत्त्वतः..
पाठमात्रा हि ये विप्रा द्विपदाः पशवो हि ते.. 5.66 ..
1.4.m: You merely recite instruction; you do not know the real meaning in truth. / For brahmins who are mere reciters are indeed two-legged animals.

1.4.s: tatte bravīmi tadvākyaṃ mohamārtaṃḍamadbhutam.. 5.67 ..
1.4.d: तत्ते ब्रवीमि तद्वाक्यं मोहमार्तंडमद्भुतम्.. 5.67 ..
1.4.m: Therefore I shall speak to you that wonderful discourse, a sun to the darkness of delusion.

1.4.s:
akāraḥ kathito brahmā ukāro viṣṇurucyate..
makāraśca smṛto rudrastrayaścaite guṇāḥ smṛtāḥ.. 5.68 ..
1.4.d:
अकारः कथितो ब्रह्मा उकारो विष्णुरुच्यते..
मकारश्च स्मृतो रुद्रस्त्रयश्चैते गुणाः स्मृताः.. 5.68 ..
1.4.m: The syllable ‘a’ is declared to be Brahmā; the syllable ‘u’ is called Viṣṇu; / and the syllable ‘ma’ is remembered as Rudra. These three are also remembered as the guṇas.

1.4.s:
ardhamātrā ca yā mūrdhni paramaḥ sa sadāśivaḥ..
evamoṃkāramāhātmyaṃ śrutireṣā sanātanī.. 5.69 ..
1.4.d:
अर्धमात्रा च या मूर्ध्नि परमः स सदाशिवः..
एवमोंकारमाहात्म्यं श्रुतिरेषा सनातनी.. 5.69 ..
1.4.m: And the half-measure on the crown is the supreme Sadāśiva. / Such is the greatness of the Omkāra; this is the eternal Vedic revelation.

1.4.s:
oṃkārasya ca māhātmyaṃ yāthātmyena na śakyate..
varṣāṇāmayutenāpi graṃthakoṭibhireva vā.. 5.70 ..
1.4.d:
ओंकारस्य च माहात्म्यं याथात्म्येन न शक्यते..
वर्षाणामयुतेनापि ग्रंथकोटिभिरेव वा.. 5.70 ..
1.4.m: And the greatness of the Omkāra cannot be [exhausted] properly / even in ten thousand years, or even by crores of books.

1.4.s:
punaryatsārasarvasvaṃ proktaṃ tacchrūyatāṃ param..
aḥkārāṃtā akārādyā manavaste caturdaśa.. 5.71 ..
1.4.d:
पुनर्यत्सारसर्वस्वं प्रोक्तं तच्छ्रूयतां परम्..
अःकारांता अकाराद्या मनवस्ते चतुर्दश.. 5.71 ..
1.4.m: Listen further to that which is proclaimed as the ultimate essence of all: / Beginning with ‘a’ and ending with ‘aḥ’, those are the fourteen Manus:

1.4.s:
svāyaṃbhuvaśca svārocirauttamo raivatastathā..
tāmasaścākṣuṣaḥ ṣaṣṭhastathā vaivasvato'dhunā.. 5.72 ..
1.4.d:
स्वायंभुवश्च स्वारोचिरौत्तमो रैवतस्तथा..
तामसश्चाक्षुषः षष्ठस्तथा वैवस्वतोऽधुना.. 5.72 ..
1.4.m: Svāyambhuva, Svārociṣa, Auttama, and Raivata; / Tāmasa, Cākṣuṣa the sixth, and now Vaivasvata;

1.4.s:
sāvarṇirbrahmasāvarṇī rudrasāvarṇireva ca..
dakṣasāvarṇirevāpi dharmasāvarṇireva ca.. 5.73 ..
1.4.d:
सावर्णिर्ब्रह्मसावर्णी रुद्रसावर्णिरेव च..
दक्षसावर्णिरेवापि धर्मसावर्णिरेव च.. 5.73 ..
1.4.m: Sāvarṇi, Brahma-sāvarṇi, and Rudra-sāvarṇi; / Dakṣa-sāvarṇi, and Dharma-sāvarṇi;

1.4.s:
raucyo bhautyastathā cāpi manavo'mī caturdaśa..
śvetaḥ pāṃḍustathā raktastāmraḥ pītaśca kāpilaḥ.. 5.74 ..
1.4.d:
रौच्यो भौत्यस्तथा चापि मनवोऽमी चतुर्दश..
श्वेतः पांडुस्तथा रक्तस्ताम्रः पीतश्च कापिलः.. 5.74 ..
1.4.m: Raucya, and also Bhautya—these are the fourteen Manus. / White, pale, red, copper-colored, yellow, tawny,

1.4.s:
kṛṣṇaḥ śyāmastathā dhūmraḥ supiśaṃgaḥ piśaṃgakaḥ..
trivarṇaḥ śabalo varṇaiḥ karkaṃdhura iti kramāt.. 5.75 ..
1.4.d:
कृष्णः श्यामस्तथा धूम्रः सुपिशंगः पिशंगकः..
त्रिवर्णः शबलो वर्णैः कर्कंधुर इति क्रमात्.. 5.75 ..
1.4.m: black, dark, smoky, very reddish-brown, reddish-brown, / three-colored, mottled with colors, and jujube-colored, in succession.

1.4.s:
vaivasvataḥ kṣakāraśca tāta kṛṣṇaḥ pradṛśyate..
kakārādya hakārāṃtāstrayastriṃśacca devatāḥ.. 5.76 ..
1.4.d:
वैवस्वतः क्षकारश्च तात कृष्णः प्रदृश्यते..
ककाराद्य हकारांतास्त्रयस्त्रिंशच्च देवताः.. 5.76 ..
1.4.m: Vaivasvata and the syllable ‘kṣa’, father, appear black. / Beginning with ‘ka’ and ending with ‘ha’ are the thirty-three deities.

1.4.s:
kakārādyāṣṭhakārāṃtā ādityā dvādaśa smṛtāḥ..
dhātā mitro'ryamā śakro varuṇāścāṃśureva ca.. 5.77 ..
1.4.d:
ककाराद्याष्ठकारांता आदित्या द्वादश स्मृताः..
धाता मित्रोऽर्यमा शक्रो वरुणाश्चांशुरेव च.. 5.77 ..
1.4.m: Beginning with ‘ka’ and ending with ‘ṭha’ are remembered as the twelve Ādityas: / Dhātṛ, Mitra, Aryaman, Śakra, Varuṇa, and Aṃśu,

1.4.s:
bhago vivasvānpūṣā ca savitā daśamastathā..
ekādaśastathā tvaṣṭā viṣṇurdvādaśa ucyate.. 5.78 ..
1.4.d:
भगो विवस्वान्पूषा च सविता दशमस्तथा..
एकादशस्तथा त्वष्टा विष्णुर्द्वादश उच्यते.. 5.78 ..
1.4.m: Bhaga, Vivasvat, Pūṣan, and Savitṛ as the tenth, / Tvaṣṭṛ as the eleventh, and Viṣṇu is declared the twelfth.

1.4.s:
jaghanyajaḥ sa sarveṣāmādityānāṃ guṇādhikaḥ..
ḍakārādyā bakārāṃtā rudrāścaikādaśaiva tu.. 5.79 ..
1.4.d:
जघन्यजः स सर्वेषामादित्यानां गुणाधिकः..
डकाराद्या बकारांता रुद्राश्चैकादशैव तु.. 5.79 ..
1.4.m: He, the youngest of all the Ādityas, is superior in virtue. / Beginning with ‘ḍa’ and ending with ‘ba’ are the eleven Rudras:

1.4.s:
kapālī piṃgalo bhīmo virupākṣo vilohitaḥ..
ajakaḥ śāsanaḥ śāstā śaṃbhuścaṇḍo bhavastathā.. 5.80 ..
1.4.d:
कपाली पिंगलो भीमो विरुपाक्षो विलोहितः..
अजकः शासनः शास्ता शंभुश्चण्डो भवस्तथा.. 5.80 ..
1.4.m: Kapālin, Piṅgala, Bhīma, Virūpākṣa, Vilohita, / Ajaka, Śāsana, Śāstṛ, Śambhu, Caṇḍa, and Bhava.

1.4.s:
bhakārādyāḥ ṣakārāṃtā aṣṭau hi vasavo matāḥ..
dhruvo ghoraśca somaśca āpaścaiva nalo'nilaḥ.. 5.81 ..
1.4.d:
भकाराद्याः षकारांता अष्टौ हि वसवो मताः..
ध्रुवो घोरश्च सोमश्च आपश्चैव नलोऽनिलः.. 5.81 ..
1.4.m: Beginning with ‘bha’ and ending with ‘ṣa’ are considered the eight Vasus: / Dhruva, Ghora, Soma, Āpas, Nala, Anila,

1.4.s:
pratyūṣaśca prabhāsaśca aṣṭau te vasavaḥ smṛtāḥ..
sau haścetyaśvinau khyātau trayastriṃśadime smṛtāḥ.. 5.82 ..
1.4.d:
प्रत्यूषश्च प्रभासश्च अष्टौ ते वसवः स्मृताः..
सौ हश्चेत्यश्विनौ ख्यातौ त्रयस्त्रिंशदिमे स्मृताः.. 5.82 ..
1.4.m: Pratyūṣa, and Prabhāsa—these are remembered as the eight Vasus. / ‘Sa’ and ‘ha’ are renowned as the two Aśvins; these are remembered as the thirty-three [gods].

1.4.s:
anusvāro visargaśca jihvāmūlīya eva ca..
upadhmānīya ityete jarāyujāstathāṃḍajāḥ.. 5.83 ..
1.4.d:
अनुस्वारो विसर्गश्च जिह्वामूलीय एव च..
उपध्मानीय इत्येते जरायुजास्तथांडजाः.. 5.83 ..
1.4.m: The anusvāra, the visarga, the jihvāmūlīya, / and the upadhmānīya: these are the womb-born, the egg-born,

1.4.s:
svedajāścodbhijāśceti tata jīvāḥ prakīrtitāḥ..
bhāvārthaḥ kathitaścāyaṃ tattvārthaṃ śrṛṇu sāṃpratam.. 5.84 ..
1.4.d:
स्वेदजाश्चोद्भिजाश्चेति तत जीवाः प्रकीर्तिताः..
भावार्थः कथितश्चायं तत्त्वार्थं श्रृणु सांप्रतम्.. 5.84 ..
1.4.m: the sweat-born, and the sprout-born living beings proclaimed, father. / This implied meaning has been told; now listen to the true meaning.

1.4.s:
ye pumāṃsastvamūndevānsamāśritya kriyāparāḥ..
ardhamātrātmake nitye pade līnāsta eva hi.. 5.85 ..
1.4.d:
ये पुमांसस्त्वमून्देवान्समाश्रित्य क्रियापराः..
अर्धमात्रात्मके नित्ये पदे लीनास्त एव हि.. 5.85 ..
1.4.m: Those men who, having taken refuge in these gods, are dedicated to ritual actions, / they alone merge into the eternal state consisting of the half-measure.

1.4.s:
caturṇāṃ jīvayonīnāṃ tadaiva parimucyate..
yadābhūnmanasā vācā karmaṇā ca yajetsurān.. 5.86 ..
1.4.d:
चतुर्णां जीवयोनीनां तदैव परिमुच्यते..
यदाभून्मनसा वाचा कर्मणा च यजेत्सुरान्.. 5.86 ..
1.4.m: One is completely released from the four wombs of living beings only when / he worships the gods with mind, speech, and action.

1.4.s:
yasmiñchāstre tvamī devā mānitā naiva pāpibhiḥ..
tacchāstraṃ hi na maṃtavyaṃ yadi brahmā svayaṃ vadet.. 5.87 ..
1.4.d:
यस्मिञ्छास्त्रे त्वमी देवा मानिता नैव पापिभिः..
तच्छास्त्रं हि न मंतव्यं यदि ब्रह्मा स्वयं वदेत्.. 5.87 ..
1.4.m: That scripture in which these gods are not honored by sinners / must not be respected, even if Brahmā himself should speak it.

1.4.s:
amī ca devāḥ sarvatra śraute mārge pratiṣṭhitāḥ..
pāṣaṇḍaśāstre sarvatra niṣiddhāḥ pāpakarmabhiḥ.. 5.88 ..
1.4.d:
अमी च देवाः सर्वत्र श्रौते मार्गे प्रतिष्ठिताः..
पाषण्डशास्त्रे सर्वत्र निषिद्धाः पापकर्मभिः.. 5.88 ..
1.4.m: And these gods are established everywhere in the Vedic path; / in heretical scriptures they are everywhere forbidden by sinful doers.

1.4.s:
tadamūnye vyatikramya tapo dānamatho japam..
prakurvaṃti durātmāno vepate marutaḥ pathi.. 5.89 ..
1.4.d:
तदमून्ये व्यतिक्रम्य तपो दानमथो जपम्..
प्रकुर्वंति दुरात्मानो वेपते मरुतः पथि.. 5.89 ..
1.4.m: Therefore, when wicked souls perform austerity, charity, or recitation bypassing these [gods], / their wind trembles on the path.

1.4.s:
aho mohasya māhātmyaṃ paśyatāvijitātmanām..
paṭhaṃti mātṛkāṃ pāpā manyaṃte na surāniha.. 5.90 ..
1.4.d:
अहो मोहस्य माहात्म्यं पश्यताविजितात्मनाम्..
पठंति मातृकां पापा मन्यंते न सुरानिह.. 5.90 ..
1.4.m: Ah, look at the power of delusion among those of uncontrolled minds! / Sinners recite the alphabet, but do not acknowledge the gods here.”

1.4.s:
..sutanuruvāca..
iti tasya vacaḥ śrutvā pitābhūdativismitaḥ..
papraccha ca bahūnpraśrānsopyavādīttathātathā.. 5.91 ..
1.4.d:
..सुतनुरुवाच..
इति तस्य वचः श्रुत्वा पिताभूदतिविस्मितः..
पप्रच्छ च बहून्प्रश्रान्सोप्यवादीत्तथातथा.. 5.91 ..
1.4.m: Sutanu said: / Having heard his words, the father became exceedingly amazed, / and he asked many questions; he also answered them accordingly.

1.4.s:
mayāpi tava prokto'yaṃ mātṛkāpraśra uttamaḥ..
dvitīyaṃ śrṛṇu taṃ praśnaṃ paṃcapaṃcādbhutaṃ gṛham.. 5.92 ..
1.4.d:
मयापि तव प्रोक्तोऽयं मातृकाप्रश्र उत्तमः..
द्वितीयं श्रृणु तं प्रश्नं पंचपंचाद्भुतं गृहम्.. 5.92 ..
1.4.m: [The son said:] / “This excellent question regarding the alphabet has been explained by me to you. / Hear that second question: the wonderful house of twenty-five [principles].

1.4.s:
paṃcabhūtāni pañcaiva karmajñāneṃdriyāṇi ca..
paṃca paṃcāpi viṣayā manobuddhyahameva ca.. 5.93 ..
1.4.d:
पंचभूतानि पञ्चैव कर्मज्ञानेंद्रियाणि च..
पंच पंचापि विषया मनोबुद्ध्यहमेव च.. 5.93 ..
1.4.m: The five gross elements, and the five organs of action and perception, / and the five sense objects, along with mind, intellect, and ego,

1.4.s:
prakṛtiḥ puruṣaścaiva pañcaviṃśaḥ sadāśivaḥ..
pañcapañcabhiretataistu niṣpannaṃ gṛhamucyate.. 5.94 ..
1.4.d:
प्रकृतिः पुरुषश्चैव पञ्चविंशः सदाशिवः..
पञ्चपञ्चभिरेततैस्तु निष्पन्नं गृहमुच्यते.. 5.94 ..
1.4.m: prakṛti, puruṣa, and Sadāśiva as the twenty-fifth— / the house is said to be accomplished by these twenty-five.

1.4.s:
dehametadidaṃ veda tattvato yātyasau śivam..
bahurūpāṃ striyaṃ prāhurbuddhiṃ vedāṃtavādinaḥ.. 5.95 ..
1.4.d:
देहमेतदिदं वेद तत्त्वतो यात्यसौ शिवम्..
बहुरूपां स्त्रियं प्राहुर्बुद्धिं वेदांतवादिनः.. 5.95 ..
1.4.m: He who knows this body in truth attains Śiva. / The teachers of Vedānta speak of the intellect as a multiform woman.

1.4.s:
sā hi nānārthabhajanānnānārūpaṃ prapadyate..
dharmasyaikasya saṃyogādbahudhāpyekikaiva sā.. 5.96 ..
1.4.d:
सा हि नानार्थभजनान्नानारूपं प्रपद्यते..
धर्मस्यैकस्य संयोगाद्बहुधाप्येकिकैव सा.. 5.96 ..
1.4.m: For she assumes many forms through enjoyment of manifold objects; / though manifold through connection with a single quality, she remains solitary.

1.4.s:
iti yo vede tattvārthaṃ nāsau narakamāpnuyāt..
munibhiryaśca na proktaṃ yanna manyeta daivatān.. 5.97 ..
1.4.d:
इति यो वेदे तत्त्वार्थं नासौ नरकमाप्नुयात्..
मुनिभिर्यश्च न प्रोक्तं यन्न मन्येत दैवतान्.. 5.97 ..
1.4.m: He who knows the real meaning thus would not go to hell. / And what is not spoken by the sages, what does not acknowledge the gods,

1.4.s:
vacanaṃ tadbudhāḥ prahurbaṃdhaṃ citrakathaṃ tviti..
yacca kāmānvitaṃ vākyaṃ paṃcamaṃ vāpyataḥ śruṇu.. 5.98 ..
1.4.d:
वचनं तद्बुधाः प्रहुर्बंधं चित्रकथं त्विति..
यच्च कामान्वितं वाक्यं पंचमं वाप्यतः श्रुणु.. 5.98 ..
1.4.m: the wise call such speech a bondage, a mere entertaining story. / Now hear about speech accompanied by desire, or the fifth [topic]:

1.4.s:
eko lobho mahāngrāho lobhātpāpaṃ pravartate..
lobhātkrodhaḥ prabhavati lobhātkāmaḥ pravartate.. 5.99 ..
1.4.d:
एको लोभो महान्ग्राहो लोभात्पापं प्रवर्तते..
लोभात्क्रोधः प्रभवति लोभात्कामः प्रवर्तते.. 5.99 ..
1.4.m: Greed alone is a great crocodile; from greed sin proceeds. / From greed anger arises; from greed desire proceeds.

1.4.s:
lobhānmohaśca māyā ca mānaḥ stambhaḥ pareṣsutā..
avidyā'prajñatā caiva sarvaṃ lobhātpravartate.. 5.100 ..
1.4.d:
लोभान्मोहश्च माया च मानः स्तम्भः परेष्सुता..
अविद्याऽप्रज्ञता चैव सर्वं लोभात्प्रवर्तते.. 5.100 ..
1.4.m: From greed arise delusion and deceit, pride, obstinacy, and desire for what belongs to others; / nescience and lack of wisdom—all these proceed from greed.

1.4.s:
haraṇaṃ paravittānāṃ paradārābhimarśanam..
sāhasānāṃ ca sarveṣāmakāryāṇaāṃ kriyāstathā.. 5.101 ..
1.4.d:
हरणं परवित्तानां परदाराभिमर्शनम्..
साहसानां च सर्वेषामकार्याणआं क्रियास्तथा.. 5.101 ..
1.4.m: The seizing of others' wealth, the touching of another's wife, / and all manner of reckless deeds and improper actions [arise likewise].

1.4.s:
sa lobhaḥ saha mohena vijetavyo jitātmanā..
dambho drohaśca niṃdā ca paiśunyaṃ matsarastathā.. 5.102 ..
1.4.d:
स लोभः सह मोहेन विजेतव्यो जितात्मना..
दम्भो द्रोहश्च निंदा च पैशुन्यं मत्सरस्तथा.. 5.102 ..
1.4.m: That greed, together with delusion, must be conquered by one who has conquered himself. / Hypocrisy, malice, slander, backbiting, and envy—

1.4.s:
bhavantyetāni sarvāṇi lubdhānāmakṛtātmanām..
sumahāṃ tyapi sāstrāṇi dhārayaṃti bahuśrutāḥ.. 5.103 ..
1.4.d:
भवन्त्येतानि सर्वाणि लुब्धानामकृतात्मनाम्..
सुमहां त्यपि सास्त्राणि धारयंति बहुश्रुताः.. 5.103 ..
1.4.m: all these belong to greedy persons of undisciplined mind. / Even those who retain very great scriptures and are widely learned,

1.4.s:
chettāraḥ saṃśayānāṃ ca lobhagrastā vrajaṃtyadhaḥ..
lobhakrodhaprasaktāśca śiṣṭācārabahiṣkṛtāḥ.. 5.104 ..
1.4.d:
छेत्तारः संशयानां च लोभग्रस्ता व्रजंत्यधः..
लोभक्रोधप्रसक्ताश्च शिष्टाचारबहिष्कृताः.. 5.104 ..
1.4.m: and are dispellers of doubts, fall down when seized by greed. / Addicted to greed and anger, excluded from the conduct of the virtuous,

1.4.s:
antaḥkṣurā vāṅmadhurāḥ kūpāśdhannāstṛṇauriva..
kurvate ye bahūnmārgāṃstāṃstānhetubalanvitāḥ.. 5.105 ..
1.4.d:
अन्तःक्षुरा वाङ्मधुराः कूपाश्धन्नास्तृणौरिव..
कुर्वते ये बहून्मार्गांस्तांस्तान्हेतुबलन्विताः.. 5.105 ..
1.4.m: having a razor within while speaking sweetly, like wells concealed with grass, / they who devise various ways, relying upon reasoning,

1.4.s:
sarvamārgaṃ viluṃmapaṃti lobhājjātiṣu niṣṭhurāḥ..
dharmāvataṃsakāḥ kṣudrā muṣṇaṃti dhvajino jagat.. 5.106 ..
1.4.d:
सर्वमार्गं विलुंमपंति लोभाज्जातिषु निष्ठुराः..
धर्मावतंसकाः क्षुद्रा मुष्णंति ध्वजिनो जगत्.. 5.106 ..
1.4.m: plunder every path, being cruel towards men out of greed; / wearing dharma as a mere ornament, vile and hypocritical, they rob the world.

1.4.s:
ete'tipāpino jñeyā nityaṃ lobhasamanvitāḥ..
janako yuvanāśvaśca vṛṣādarbhiḥ prasenajit.. 5.107 ..
1.4.d:
एतेऽतिपापिनो ज्ञेया नित्यं लोभसमन्विताः..
जनको युवनाश्वश्च वृषादर्भिः प्रसेनजित्.. 5.107 ..
1.4.m: These should be known as extreme sinners, ever accompanied by greed. / Janaka, Yuvanāśva, Vṛṣādarbhi, and Prasenajit,

1.4.s:
lobhakṣayāddivaṃ prāptāstathaivānye janādhipāḥ..
tasmāttyajaṃti ye lobhaṃ te'tikrāmaṃti sāgaram.. 5.108 ..
1.4.d:
लोभक्षयाद्दिवं प्राप्तास्तथैवान्ये जनाधिपाः..
तस्मात्त्यजंति ये लोभं तेऽतिक्रामंति सागरम्.. 5.108 ..
1.4.m: as well as other rulers of men, attained heaven through the destruction of greed. / Therefore, those who abandon greed cross over the ocean

1.4.s:
saṃsārākhyamato'naye ye grāhagrastā na saṃśayaḥ..
atha brāhmaṇabhedāṃstvamaṣṭo viprāvadhāraya.. 5.109 ..
1.4.d:
संसाराख्यमतोऽनये ये ग्राहग्रस्ता न संशयः..
अथ ब्राह्मणभेदांस्त्वमष्टो विप्रावधारय.. 5.109 ..
1.4.m: called mundane existence; others, seized by the crocodile [of greed], do not, without doubt. / Now listen, O brahmin, to the eight distinctions of brahmins.

1.4.s:
mātraśca brāhmaṇaścaiva śrotriyaśca tataḥ param..
anūcānastathā bhrūṇa ṛṣikalpa ṛṣirmuniḥ.. 5.110 ..
1.4.d:
मात्रश्च ब्राह्मणश्चैव श्रोत्रियश्च ततः परम्..
अनूचानस्तथा भ्रूण ऋषिकल्प ऋषिर्मुनिः.. 5.110 ..
1.4.m: The Mātra, the Brāhmaṇa, and then after that the Śrotriya; / the Anūcāna, then the Bhrūṇa, the Ṛṣikalpa, the Ṛṣi, and the Muni.

1.4.s:
ete hyaṣṭau samuddiṣṭā brāhmaṇāḥ prathamaṃ śrutau..
teṣāṃ paraḥ paraḥ śreṣṭho vidyāvṛttaviśeṣataḥ.. 5.111 ..
1.4.d:
एते ह्यष्टौ समुद्दिष्टा ब्राह्मणाः प्रथमं श्रुतौ..
तेषां परः परः श्रेष्ठो विद्यावृत्तविशेषतः.. 5.111 ..
1.4.m: These eight brahmins are indeed set forth originally in the Veda. / Among them, each succeeding one is superior by virtue of learning and conduct.

1.4.s:
brāhmaṇānāṃ kule jāto jātimātro yadā bhavet..
anupetaḥ kriyāhīno mātra ityabhidhīyate.. 5.112 ..
1.4.d:
ब्राह्मणानां कुले जातो जातिमात्रो यदा भवेत्..
अनुपेतः क्रियाहीनो मात्र इत्यभिधीयते.. 5.112 ..
1.4.m: When one is born in a family of brahmins merely by caste, / uninitiated and devoid of rites, he is designated a Mātra.

1.4.s:
ekoddeśyamatikramya vedasyācāravānṛjuḥ..
sa brāhmaṇa iti prokto nibhṛtaḥ satyavāgghṛṇī.. 5.113 ..
1.4.d:
एकोद्देश्यमतिक्रम्य वेदस्याचारवानृजुः..
स ब्राह्मण इति प्रोक्तो निभृतः सत्यवाग्घृणी.. 5.113 ..
1.4.m: One who, going beyond a single objective, possesses Vedic conduct, is upright, / modest, truthful in speech, and compassionate, is called a Brāhmaṇa.

1.4.s:
ekāṃ śākhāṃ sakalpāṃ ca ṣaḍbhiraṃgairadhītya ca..
ṣaṭkarmanirato vipraḥ śrotriyonāma dharmavit.. 5.114 ..
1.4.d:
एकां शाखां सकल्पां च षड्भिरंगैरधीत्य च..
षट्कर्मनिरतो विप्रः श्रोत्रियोनाम धर्मवित्.. 5.114 ..
1.4.m: Having studied one Vedic recension along with the Kalpa and the six limbs, / devoted to the six duties, knowing dharma, that brahmin is named a Śrotriya.

1.4.s:
vedavedāṃgatattvajñaḥ śuddhātmā pāpavarjitaḥ..
śreṣṭhaḥ śrotriyavānprājñaḥ so'nūcāna iti smṛtaḥ.. 5.115 ..
1.4.d:
वेदवेदांगतत्त्वज्ञः शुद्धात्मा पापवर्जितः..
श्रेष्ठः श्रोत्रियवान्प्राज्ञः सोऽनूचान इति स्मृतः.. 5.115 ..
1.4.m: Knowing the reality of the Vedas and Vedāṅgas, pure-souled, free from sin, / eminent, possessing the qualities of a Śrotriya, and wise, he is remembered as an Anūcāna.

1.4.s:
anūcānaguṇopeto yajñasvādhyāyayaṃtritaḥ..
bhrūṇa ityucyate śiṣṭaiḥ śeṣabhojī jiteṃdriyaḥ.. 5.116 ..
1.4.d:
अनूचानगुणोपेतो यज्ञस्वाध्याययंत्रितः..
भ्रूण इत्युच्यते शिष्टैः शेषभोजी जितेंद्रियः.. 5.116 ..
1.4.m: Endowed with the virtues of an Anūcāna, restrained by sacrifice and Vedic recitation, / eating what remains [of offerings], self-controlled—he is called a Bhrūṇa by the virtuous.

1.4.s:
vaidikaṃ laukikaṃ caiva sarvajñānamavāpya yaḥ..
āśramastho vaśī nityamṛṣikalpa iti smṛtaḥ.. 5.117 ..
1.4.d:
वैदिकं लौकिकं चैव सर्वज्ञानमवाप्य यः..
आश्रमस्थो वशी नित्यमृषिकल्प इति स्मृतः.. 5.117 ..
1.4.m: He who, having attained all knowledge, both Vedic and secular, / remains in his hermitage, ever master of himself, is remembered as an Ṛṣikalpa.

1.4.s:
ūrdhvaretā bhavatyagryo niyatāśī nasaṃśa yī..
śāpānugrahayoḥ śaktaḥ satyasaṃdho bhavedṛṣiḥ.. 5.118 ..
1.4.d:
ऊर्ध्वरेता भवत्यग्र्यो नियताशी नसंश यी..
शापानुग्रहयोः शक्तः सत्यसंधो भवेदृषिः.. 5.118 ..
1.4.m: Foremost, with semen drawn upward, eating moderately, free from doubt, / capable of both curse and boon, true to his word—he is an Ṛṣi.

1.4.s:
nivṛttaḥ sarvatattvajñaḥ kāmakrodhavivarjitaḥ..
dhyānasthāniṣkriyo dāṃtastulyamṛtkāṃcano muniḥ.. 5.119 ..
1.4.d:
निवृत्तः सर्वतत्त्वज्ञः कामक्रोधविवर्जितः..
ध्यानस्थानिष्क्रियो दांतस्तुल्यमृत्कांचनो मुनिः.. 5.119 ..
1.4.m: Renounced, knowing all realities, free from desire and anger, / absorbed in meditation, inactive, restrained, regarding a clod of earth and gold as equal—he is a Muni.

1.4.s:
evamanvayavidyābhyāṃ vṛttena ca samucchritāḥ..
triśuklānāma vipreṃdrāḥ pūjyante savanādiṣu.. 5.120 ..
1.4.d:
एवमन्वयविद्याभ्यां वृत्तेन च समुच्छ्रिताः..
त्रिशुक्लानाम विप्रेंद्राः पूज्यन्ते सवनादिषु.. 5.120 ..
1.4.m: Thus elevated by lineage, learning, and righteous conduct, / these foremost brahmins, thrice-pure, are honoured at sacrificial sessions and other rites.

1.4.s:
ityevaṃvidhavipratvamuktaṃ śrṛṇu yugādayaḥ..
navamī kārtike śuklā kṛtādiḥ parikīrtitā.. 5.121 ..
1.4.d:
इत्येवंविधविप्रत्वमुक्तं श्रृणु युगादयः..
नवमी कार्तिके शुक्ला कृतादिः परिकीर्तिता.. 5.121 ..
1.4.m: Such has brahminhood been spoken of; now listen to the beginnings of the yugas: / The bright ninth day of Kārtika is proclaimed as the beginning of the Kṛta yuga.

1.4.s:
vaiśākhasya tṛtīyā yā śuklā tretādirucyate..
māghe pañcadaśīnāma dvāparādiḥ smṛtā budhaiḥ.. 5.122 ..
1.4.d:
वैशाखस्य तृतीया या शुक्ला त्रेतादिरुच्यते..
माघे पञ्चदशीनाम द्वापरादिः स्मृता बुधैः.. 5.122 ..
1.4.m: The bright third day of Vaiśākha is called the beginning of the Tretā yuga; / the fifteenth day in Māgha is remembered by the wise as the beginning of the Dvāpara yuga.

1.4.s:
trayodaśī nabhasye ca kṛṣṇā sā hi kaleḥ smṛtā..
yugādayaḥ smṛtā hyetā dattasyākṣayakārakāḥ.. 5.123 ..
1.4.d:
त्रयोदशी नभस्ये च कृष्णा सा हि कलेः स्मृता..
युगादयः स्मृता ह्येता दत्तस्याक्षयकारकाः.. 5.123 ..
1.4.m: The dark thirteenth day in Nabhasya (Bhādrapada) is remembered as the beginning of the Kali yuga. / These are remembered as the beginnings of the yugas, making gifts imperishable.

1.4.s:
etāścatasrastithayo yugādyā dattaṃ hutaṃ cākṣayamāśu vidyāt..
yugeyuge varṣaśatena dānaṃ yugādikāle divasena tatphalam.. 5.124 ..
1.4.d:
एताश्चतस्रस्तिथयो युगाद्या दत्तं हुतं चाक्षयमाशु विद्यात्..
युगेयुगे वर्षशतेन दानं युगादिकाले दिवसेन तत्फलम्.. 5.124 ..
1.4.m: One should know that what is given and offered on these four lunar days, the beginnings of the yugas, becomes imperishable at once: / the gift given during a hundred years in each yuga yields that same fruit in a single day at the time of a yuga's beginning.

1.4.s:
yugādyāḥ kathitā hyetā manvādyāḥ śrṛṇu sāṃpratam..
aśvayukchuklanavamī dvādaśī kārtike tathā.. 5.125 ..
1.4.d:
युगाद्याः कथिता ह्येता मन्वाद्याः श्रृणु सांप्रतम्..
अश्वयुक्छुक्लनवमी द्वादशी कार्तिके तथा.. 5.125 ..
1.4.m: These beginnings of the yugas have been declared; now listen to the beginnings of the manvantaras: / The bright ninth of Aśvina, and likewise the twelfth of Kārtika;

1.4.s:
tṛtīyā caitramāsasya tathā bhādrapadasya ca..
phālgunasya tvamāvāsyā pauṣasyaikādaśī tathā.. 5.126 ..
1.4.d:
तृतीया चैत्रमासस्य तथा भाद्रपदस्य च..
फाल्गुनस्य त्वमावास्या पौषस्यैकादशी तथा.. 5.126 ..
1.4.m: the third of the month of Caitra, and likewise of Bhādrapada; / the new-moon day of Phālguna, and the eleventh of Pauṣa;

1.4.s:
āṣāḍhasyāpi daśamī māghamāsasya saptamī..
śrāvaṇasyāṣṭamī kṛṣṇā tathāṣāḍhī ca pūrṇimā.. 5.127 ..
1.4.d:
आषाढस्यापि दशमी माघमासस्य सप्तमी..
श्रावणस्याष्टमी कृष्णा तथाषाढी च पूर्णिमा.. 5.127 ..
1.4.m: the tenth of Āṣāḍha, the seventh of the month of Māgha, / the dark eighth of Śrāvaṇa, and the full-moon day of Āṣāḍha;

1.4.s:
kārtikī phālgunī caitrī jyeṣṭhe pañcadaśī sitā..
manvaṃtarādayaścaitā dattasyākṣayakārakāḥ.. 5.128 ..
1.4.d:
कार्तिकी फाल्गुनी चैत्री ज्येष्ठे पञ्चदशी सिता..
मन्वंतरादयश्चैता दत्तस्याक्षयकारकाः.. 5.128 ..
1.4.m: the full moons of Kārtika, Phālguna, and Caitra, and the bright fifteenth of Jyeṣṭha— / these are the beginnings of the manvantaras, rendering gifts imperishable.

1.4.s:
yasyāṃ tithau rathaṃ pūrvaṃ prāpa devo divākaraḥ..
sā tithiḥ kathitā viprairmāghe yā rathasaptamī.. 5.129 ..
1.4.d:
यस्यां तिथौ रथं पूर्वं प्राप देवो दिवाकरः..
सा तिथिः कथिता विप्रैर्माघे या रथसप्तमी.. 5.129 ..
1.4.m: The lunar day on which the divine Sun obtained his chariot in the beginning / is spoken of by brahmins as the Rathasaptamī in Māgha.

1.4.s:
tasyāṃ dattaṃ hutaṃ ceṣṭaṃ sarvamevākṣayaṃ matam..
sarvadāridryaśamanaṃ bhāskaraprītaye matam.. 5.130 ..
1.4.d:
तस्यां दत्तं हुतं चेष्टं सर्वमेवाक्षयं मतम्..
सर्वदारिद्र्यशमनं भास्करप्रीतये मतम्.. 5.130 ..
1.4.m: Whatever is given, offered in fire, or sacrificed on that day is regarded as entirely imperishable, / allaying all poverty, pleasing to the Sun.

1.4.s:
nityodvejakamāhuryaṃ budhāstaṃ śrṛṇu tattvataḥ..
yaśca yācaniko nityaṃ na sa svargasya bhājanam.. 5.131 ..
1.4.d:
नित्योद्वेजकमाहुर्यं बुधास्तं श्रृणु तत्त्वतः..
यश्च याचनिको नित्यं न स स्वर्गस्य भाजनम्.. 5.131 ..
1.4.m: Listen in truth to him whom the wise call a perpetual agitator: / he who is perpetually begging is not fit for heaven.

1.4.s:
udvejayati bhūtāni yathā caurāstathaiva saḥ..
narakaṃ yāti pāpātmā nityodvegakarastvasau.. 5.132 ..
1.4.d:
उद्वेजयति भूतानि यथा चौरास्तथैव सः..
नरकं याति पापात्मा नित्योद्वेगकरस्त्वसौ.. 5.132 ..
1.4.m: Just as thieves agitate living beings, so does he; / that sinful soul, causing perpetual anxiety, goes to hell.

1.4.s:
ihopapattirmama kena karmaṇā kva ca prayātavyamito mayeti..
vicārya caivaṃ pratikārakārī budhaiḥ sa cokto dvija dakṣadakṣaḥ.. 5.133 ..
1.4.d:
इहोपपत्तिर्मम केन कर्मणा क्व च प्रयातव्यमितो मयेति..
विचार्य चैवं प्रतिकारकारी बुधैः स चोक्तो द्विज दक्षदक्षः.. 5.133 ..
1.4.m: 'By what action was my birth here caused, and where must I go from here?'— / having thus reflected, he who applies the remedy is called exceptionally clever by the wise, O twice-born.

1.4.s:
māsairaṣṭabhirahnā ca pūrveṇa vayasāyuṣā..
tatkarma puruṣaḥ kuryādyenāṃte sukhamedhate.. 5.134 ..
1.4.d:
मासैरष्टभिरह्ना च पूर्वेण वयसायुषा..
तत्कर्म पुरुषः कुर्याद्येनांते सुखमेधते.. 5.134 ..
1.4.m: Through eight months, through the day, through the earlier stage of life, and through life itself, / a person should perform that deed by which happiness flourishes in the end.

1.4.s:
arcirdhūmaśca mārgau dvāvāhurvedāṃtavādinaḥ..
arciṣā yāti mokṣaṃ ca dhūmenāvartate punaḥ.. 5.135 ..
1.4.d:
अर्चिर्धूमश्च मार्गौ द्वावाहुर्वेदांतवादिनः..
अर्चिषा याति मोक्षं च धूमेनावर्तते पुनः.. 5.135 ..
1.4.m: The knowers of the Vedānta speak of two paths: the flame and the smoke. / By the flame one attains liberation, and by the smoke one returns again.

1.4.s:
yajñairāsādyate dhūmo naiṣkarmyeṇārcirāpyate..
etayoraparo mārgaḥ pākhaṃḍa iti kīrtyate.. 5.136 ..
1.4.d:
यज्ञैरासाद्यते धूमो नैष्कर्म्येणार्चिराप्यते..
एतयोरपरो मार्गः पाखंड इति कीर्त्यते.. 5.136 ..
1.4.m: Smoke is reached through sacrifices; flame is attained through actionlessness. / A path other than these two is proclaimed as heresy.

1.4.s:
yo devānmanyate naiva dharmāṃśca manusūcitān..
naitau sa yāti paṃthānau tattvārtho'yaṃ nirūpitaḥ.. 5.137 ..
1.4.d:
यो देवान्मन्यते नैव धर्मांश्च मनुसूचितान्..
नैतौ स याति पंथानौ तत्त्वार्थोऽयं निरूपितः.. 5.137 ..
1.4.m: He who does not believe in the gods nor in the duties taught by Manu / does not go by these two paths; this is the true conclusion determined.

1.4.s:
ite te kīrtitāḥ praśrāḥ śaktyā brāhmaṇasattama..
sādhu vā'sādhu vā brūhī khyāpayātmānameva ca.. 5.138 ..
iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ prathame māheśvarakhaṇḍe kalāpagrāmavāsisutanubrāhmaṇena nāradapraśnottarakathanaṃnāma paṃcamo'dhyāyaḥ.. 5 .. cha ..
upadhmānīya ityete...svedajāścodbhijāśceti --
upūpadhmānīyā oṣṭhyāḥ . ^pa ^pha iti paphābhyāṃ prāk
ardhavisargasadṛśaḥ upadhmānīyaḥ . ^ka ^kha iti kakhābhyāṃ
prāk ardhavisargasadṛśo jihvamūlīyaḥ - nāṭyaśāstram 14.11
1.4.d:
इते ते कीर्तिताः प्रश्राः शक्त्या ब्राह्मणसत्तम..
साधु वाऽसाधु वा ब्रूही ख्यापयात्मानमेव च.. 5.138 ..
इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां प्रथमे माहेश्वरखण्डे कलापग्रामवासिसुतनुब्राह्मणेन नारदप्रश्नोत्तरकथनंनाम पंचमोऽध्यायः.. 5 .. छ ..
उपध्मानीय इत्येते...स्वेदजाश्चोद्भिजाश्चेति --
उपूपध्मानीया ओष्ठ्याः . ^प ^फ इति पफाभ्यां प्राक्
अर्धविसर्गसदृशः उपध्मानीयः . ^क ^ख इति कखाभ्यां
प्राक् अर्धविसर्गसदृशो जिह्वमूलीयः - नाट्यशास्त्रम् 14.11
1.4.m:
Thus your questions have been spoken according to ability, O best of brahmins; / whether good or bad, speak, and make yourself known.
Thus ends the fifth chapter, entitled 'The Recital of the Answers to Nārada's Questions by the Brahmin Sutanu, Resident of Kalāpagrāma', in the first [part], the Māheśvarakhaṇḍa, of the Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.
[Citation:] Upadhmānīya and so forth... sweat-born and sprout-born —
[Citation:] 'U, p, and the upadhmānīya are labial. Before the sounds pa and pha, the semi-visarga-like sound is the upadhmānīya. Before the sounds ka and kha, the semi-visarga-like sound is the jihvāmūlīya.' — Nāṭyaśāstra 14.11

1.4.s:
..śrīnārada uvāca..
iti śrutvā phālgunāhaṃ romāṃcapulakīkṛtaḥ..
svarūpaṃ prakaṭīkṛtya brāhmaṇānidamabravam.. 6.1 ..
1.4.d:
..श्रीनारद उवाच..
इति श्रुत्वा फाल्गुनाहं रोमांचपुलकीकृतः..
स्वरूपं प्रकटीकृत्य ब्राह्मणानिदमब्रवम्.. 6.1 ..
1.4.m: Śrī Nārada said: / Hearing this, O Phālguna, with my body thrilling and hairs standing on end, / having revealed my true form, I said this to the brahmins:

1.4.s:
aho dhanyaḥ pitāsmākaṃ yasya sṛṣṭasya pālakāḥ..
yuṣmadvidhā brāhmaṇeṃdrāḥ satyamāha purā hariḥ.. 6.2 ..
1.4.d:
अहो धन्यः पितास्माकं यस्य सृष्टस्य पालकाः..
युष्मद्विधा ब्राह्मणेंद्राः सत्यमाह पुरा हरिः.. 6.2 ..
1.4.m: 'Ah, fortunate is our father, whose creation has guardians / such as you, eminent brahmins! Truly spoke Hari in former times:

1.4.s:
matto'pyanaṃtātparataḥ parasmātsamastabhūtādhipaterna kiṃcit..
teṣāṃ kimusyāditareṇa yeṣāṃ dvijeśvarāṇāṃ mama mārgavādinām.. 6.3 ..
1.4.d:
मत्तोऽप्यनंतात्परतः परस्मात्समस्तभूताधिपतेर्न किंचित्..
तेषां किमुस्यादितरेण येषां द्विजेश्वराणां मम मार्गवादिनाम्.. 6.3 ..
1.4.m: "Nothing is higher even than me, the infinite, the highest, the lord of all beings; / what could there be [higher] to others than those lords among the twice-born who proclaim my path?"

1.4.s:
tatsarvathādyā dhanyo'smi saṃprāptaṃ janmanaḥ phalam..
yadbhavanto mayā dṛṣṭāḥ pāpopadravavarjitāḥ.. 6.4 ..
1.4.d:
तत्सर्वथाद्या धन्योऽस्मि संप्राप्तं जन्मनः फलम्..
यद्भवन्तो मया दृष्टाः पापोपद्रववर्जिताः.. 6.4 ..
1.4.m: Therefore, I am completely blessed today; the fruit of my birth has been attained, / since you, free from sin and afflictions, have been seen by me.'

1.4.s:
tataste sahasotthāya śātātapapurogamāḥ..
arghyapādyādisatkāraiḥ pūjayāmāsurmāṃ dvijāḥ.. 6.5 ..
1.4.d:
ततस्ते सहसोत्थाय शातातपपुरोगमाः..
अर्घ्यपाद्यादिसत्कारैः पूजयामासुर्मां द्विजाः.. 6.5 ..
1.4.m: Then, rising up suddenly with Śātātapa at their head, / those twice-born honored me with marks of respect, such as the guest-offering and foot-water.

1.4.s:
proktavantaśca māṃ pārtha vacaḥ sādhujano citam..
dhanyā vayaṃ hi devarṣe tvamasmānyadihāgataḥ.. 6.6 ..
1.4.d:
प्रोक्तवन्तश्च मां पार्थ वचः साधुजनो चितम्..
धन्या वयं हि देवर्षे त्वमस्मान्यदिहागतः.. 6.6 ..
1.4.m: And they addressed to me, O Pārtha, words worthy of virtuous people: / 'Blessed indeed are we, O divine seer, since you have come here to us.

1.4.s:
kuto vā''gamanaṃ tubhyaṃ gantavyaṃ vā kva sāṃpratam..
atrāpyāgamane kāryamucyatāṃ munisattama.. 6.7 ..
1.4.d:
कुतो वा'ऽगमनं तुभ्यं गन्तव्यं वा क्व सांप्रतम्..
अत्राप्यागमने कार्यमुच्यतां मुनिसत्तम.. 6.7 ..
1.4.m: From where did you come, or where must you go now? / Let the purpose of your arrival here also be stated, O best of sages.'

1.4.s:
śrutvā prītikaraṃ vākyaṃ dvijānāmiti pāṃḍava..
pratyavocaṃ munīndrāṃstāñchrūyatāṃ dvijasattamāḥ.. 6.8 ..
1.4.d:
श्रुत्वा प्रीतिकरं वाक्यं द्विजानामिति पांडव..
प्रत्यवोचं मुनीन्द्रांस्ताञ्छ्रूयतां द्विजसत्तमाः.. 6.8 ..
1.4.m: Having heard those delightful words of the twice-born, O Pāṇḍava, / I replied to those foremost sages: 'Listen, O best of the twice-born!

1.4.s:
ahaṃ hi brahmaṇo vākyādviprāṇāṃ sthānakaṃ śubham..
dātukāmo mahātīrthe mahīsāgarasaṃgame.. 6.9 ..
1.4.d:
अहं हि ब्रह्मणो वाक्याद्विप्राणां स्थानकं शुभम्..
दातुकामो महातीर्थे महीसागरसंगमे.. 6.9 ..
1.4.m: At the command of Brahmā, wishing to grant an auspicious place to brahmins / at the great tīrtha, the confluence of the Mahī and the ocean,

1.4.s:
parīkṣanbrāhmaṇānatra prāpto yūyaṃ parīkṣitāḥ..
ahaṃ vaḥ sthāyiṣyāmi cānujānīta taddvijāḥ.. 6.10 ..
1.4.d:
परीक्षन्ब्राह्मणानत्र प्राप्तो यूयं परीक्षिताः..
अहं वः स्थायिष्यामि चानुजानीत तद्द्विजाः.. 6.10 ..
1.4.m: I came here testing brahmins, and you have been tested. / I shall settle you there; give your assent to that, O twice-born.'

1.4.s:
evamukto vilokyaiva dvijāñchātātapo'bravīt..
devānāmapi duṣprāpyaṃ satyaṃ nārada bhāratam.. 6.11 ..
1.4.d:
एवमुक्तो विलोक्यैव द्विजाञ्छातातपोऽब्रवीत्..
देवानामपि दुष्प्राप्यं सत्यं नारद भारतम्.. 6.11 ..
1.4.m: Having been addressed thus, looking at the twice-born, Śātātapa said: / 'Even for the gods, Bhārata is difficult to attain, O Nārada, it is true.

1.4.s:
kiṃ punaścāpi tatraiva mahī sāgarasaṃgamaḥ..
yatra snāto mahātīrthaphalaṃ sarvamupāśnute.. 6.12 ..
1.4.d:
किं पुनश्चापि तत्रैव मही सागरसंगमः..
यत्र स्नातो महातीर्थफलं सर्वमुपाश्नुते.. 6.12 ..
1.4.m: What more [to say of] the confluence of the Mahī and the ocean right there, / where one who bathes attains all the fruits of a great tīrtha?

1.4.s:
punareko mahāndoṣo bibhīmo nitarāṃ yataḥ..
tatra caurāḥ subahavo nirghṛṇāḥ priyasāhasāḥ.. 6.13 ..
1.4.d:
पुनरेको महान्दोषो बिभीमो नितरां यतः..
तत्र चौराः सुबहवो निर्घृणाः प्रियसाहसाः.. 6.13 ..
1.4.m: Yet there is one great fault, of which we are exceedingly afraid: / there are very many thieves there, merciless and fond of violence.

1.4.s:
sparśeṣu ṣoḍaśaṃ caikaviṃśaṃ gṛhṇaṃti no dhanam..
dhanena tena hīnānāṃ kīdṛśaṃ janma no bhavet.. 6.14 ..
1.4.d:
स्पर्शेषु षोडशं चैकविंशं गृह्णंति नो धनम्..
धनेन तेन हीनानां कीदृशं जन्म नो भवेत्.. 6.14 ..
1.4.m: At eclipses, they take the sixteenth or twenty-first portion of our wealth; / deprived of that wealth, what kind of life would ours be?

1.4.s:
varaṃ bubhukṣayā vāso mā caurakaragā vayam..
..arjuna uvāca..
adbhutaṃ varṇyate vipra ke hi caurāḥ prakīrtitāḥ.. 6.15 ..
1.4.d:
वरं बुभुक्षया वासो मा चौरकरगा वयम्..
..अर्जुन उवाच..
अद्भुतं वर्ण्यते विप्र के हि चौराः प्रकीर्तिताः.. 6.15 ..
1.4.m: Better is living in hunger, lest we fall into the hands of thieves.' / Arjuna said: / 'A wondrous thing is described, O brahmin: who indeed are these renowned thieves?

1.4.s:
kiṃ dhanaṃ ca haraṃtyete yebhyo bibhyati brāhmaṇāḥ..
..nārada uvāca..
kāmakrodhādayaścaurāstapa eva dhanaṃ tathā.. 6.16 ..
1.4.d:
किं धनं च हरंत्येते येभ्यो बिभ्यति ब्राह्मणाः..
..नारद उवाच..
कामक्रोधादयश्चौरास्तप एव धनं तथा.. 6.16 ..
1.4.m: And what wealth do they steal, of which the brahmins are afraid?' / Nārada said: / 'Thieves are desire, anger, and the like, and wealth is austerity.

1.4.s:
tasyāpahārabhītāste māmūcuriti brāhmaṇāḥ..
tānahaṃ prābravaṃ paścādvi jānīta dvijottamāḥ.. 6.17 ..
1.4.d:
तस्यापहारभीतास्ते मामूचुरिति ब्राह्मणाः..
तानहं प्राब्रवं पश्चाद्वि जानीत द्विजोत्तमाः.. 6.17 ..
1.4.m: Afraid of its robbery, those brahmins spoke thus to me. / Afterward, I said to them: 'Understand, O best of the twice-born!

1.4.s:
jāgratāṃ tu manuṣyāṇāṃ caurāḥ kurvaṃti kiṃ khalāḥ..
bhayabhītaścālasaśca tathā cāśucireva yaḥ.. 6.18 ..
1.4.d:
जाग्रतां तु मनुष्याणां चौराः कुर्वंति किं खलाः..
भयभीतश्चालसश्च तथा चाशुचिरेव यः.. 6.18 ..
1.4.m: What can wicked thieves do to men who are vigilant? / But he who is terrified, lazy, and likewise impure—

1.4.s: tena kiṃ nāma saṃsādhyaṃ bhūmistaṃ grasate naram.. 6.19 ..
1.4.d: तेन किं नाम संसाध्यं भूमिस्तं ग्रसते नरम्.. 6.19 ..
1.4.m: what can indeed be accomplished by him? The earth swallows up that man.'

1.4.s:
..śātātapa uvāca..
vayaṃ caurabhayādbhītāste haraṃti dhanaṃ mahat..
kartuṃ tadā kathaṃ śakyamaṃga jāgaraṇaṃ tathā.. 6.20 ..
1.4.d:
..शातातप उवाच..
वयं चौरभयाद्भीतास्ते हरंति धनं महत्..
कर्तुं तदा कथं शक्यमंग जागरणं तथा.. 6.20 ..
1.4.m: Śātātapa said: / 'We are frightened by fear of thieves; they steal great wealth. / How, then, is it possible to maintain vigilance in that manner, dear sir?

1.4.s:
khalāścaurā gatāḥ kvāpi tato natvā''gatā vayam..
tasmāsarvaṃ saṃtyajāmo bhayabhītā vayaṃ mune.. 6.21 ..
1.4.d:
खलाश्चौरा गताः क्वापि ततो नत्वा'ऽगता वयम्..
तस्मासर्वं संत्यजामो भयभीता वयं मुने.. 6.21 ..
1.4.m: The wicked thieves have gone somewhere; having bowed, we came from there. / Therefore, terrified, we abandon everything, O sage.

1.4.s:
pratigrahaśca vai ghoraḥ ṣaṣṭhāṃ'śaphaladastathā..
evaṃ bruvati tasmiṃśca hārītonāma cābravīt.. 6.22 ..
1.4.d:
प्रतिग्रहश्च वै घोरः षष्ठांऽशफलदस्तथा..
एवं ब्रुवति तस्मिंश्च हारीतोनाम चाब्रवीत्.. 6.22 ..
1.4.m: And acceptance of gifts is terrible, yielding a sixth share [of others' sins].' / While he was speaking thus, one named Hārīta said:

1.4.s:
mūḍhabuddhyā hi ko nāma mahīsāgarasaṃgamam..
tyajecca yatra mokṣaśca svargaśca karago'tha vā.. 6.23 ..
1.4.d:
मूढबुद्ध्या हि को नाम महीसागरसंगमम्..
त्यजेच्च यत्र मोक्षश्च स्वर्गश्च करगोऽथ वा.. 6.23 ..
1.4.m: 'Who indeed, out of foolish intellect, would abandon the confluence of the Mahī and the ocean, / where liberation or heaven is within one's grasp?

1.4.s:
kalāpādiṣu grāmeṣu ko vaseta vicakṣaṇaḥ..
yadi vāsaḥ stambhatīrthe kṣaṇārdhamapi labhyate.. 6.24 ..
1.4.d:
कलापादिषु ग्रामेषु को वसेत विचक्षणः..
यदि वासः स्तम्भतीर्थे क्षणार्धमपि लभ्यते.. 6.24 ..
1.4.m: What discerning person would reside in villages such as Kalāpa, / if dwelling at Stambhatīrtha can be obtained even for half a moment?

1.4.s:
bhayaṃ ca caurajaṃ sarvaṃ kiṃ kariṣyati tatra na..
kumāranāthaṃ manasi pālakaṃ kurvatāṃ dṛḍham.. 6.25 ..
1.4.d:
भयं च चौरजं सर्वं किं करिष्यति तत्र न..
कुमारनाथं मनसि पालकं कुर्वतां दृढम्.. 6.25 ..
1.4.m: And what will all that fear born of thieves do to us there, / as we firmly keep Kumāranātha in our hearts as our protector?

1.4.s:
sāhasaṃ ca vinā bhūtirna kathaṃcana prāpyate..
tasmānnārada tatrāhamāyāsye tava vākyataḥ.. 6.26 ..
1.4.d:
साहसं च विना भूतिर्न कथंचन प्राप्यते..
तस्मान्नारद तत्राहमायास्ये तव वाक्यतः.. 6.26 ..
1.4.m: Without daring, prosperity is never attained in any way. / Therefore, O Nārada, I shall come there at your word.

1.4.s:
ṣaḍviṃśatisahasrāṇi brāhmaṇā me parigrahe..
ṣaṭkarmaniratāḥ śuddhā lobhadambhavivarjitāḥ.. 6.27 ..
1.4.d:
षड्विंशतिसहस्राणि ब्राह्मणा मे परिग्रहे..
षट्कर्मनिरताः शुद्धा लोभदम्भविवर्जिताः.. 6.27 ..
1.4.m: There are twenty-six thousand brahmins in my retinue, / devoted to the six duties, pure, and free from greed and deceit.

1.4.s:
taiḥ sārdhamāgamiṣyāmi mamedaṃ matamuttamam..
ityukte vacane tāṃśca kṛtvāhaṃ daṃḍamūrdhani.. 6.28 ..
1.4.d:
तैः सार्धमागमिष्यामि ममेदं मतमुत्तमम्..
इत्युक्ते वचने तांश्च कृत्वाहं दंडमूर्धनि.. 6.28 ..
1.4.m: Together with them I shall come; this is my firm opinion.' / When this statement was made, placing them on the top of my staff,

1.4.s:
nivṛttaḥ sahasā pārtha khecaro'timudānvitaḥ..
śatayojanamātraṃ tu himamārgamatītya ca.. 6.29 ..
1.4.d:
निवृत्तः सहसा पार्थ खेचरोऽतिमुदान्वितः..
शतयोजनमात्रं तु हिममार्गमतीत्य च.. 6.29 ..
1.4.m: I quickly returned moving through the sky, filled with great joy, O Pārtha. / Having crossed the snowy path of just a hundred yojanas,

1.4.s:
kedāraṃ samupāyāto yuktastairdvijasattamaiḥ..
ākāśena suśakyaśca bilenātha sa deśakaḥ.. 6.30 ..
1.4.d:
केदारं समुपायातो युक्तस्तैर्द्विजसत्तमैः..
आकाशेन सुशक्यश्च बिलेनाथ स देशकः.. 6.30 ..
1.4.m: I arrived at Kedāra together with those best among the twice-born. / That region can easily be traversed through the sky or through a subterranean passage,

1.4.s: atikrāṃtuṃ nānyathā ca tathā skaṃdaprasādataḥ.. 6.31 ..
1.4.d: अतिक्रांतुं नान्यथा च तथा स्कंदप्रसादतः.. 6.31 ..
1.4.m: and not otherwise, as well as by the grace of Skanda.

1.4.s:
..arjuna uvāca..
kva kalāpaṃ ca tadgrāmaṃ kathaṃ śakyaṃ bilena ca..
kathaṃ skaṃdaprasādaḥ syādetanme brūhi nārada.. 6.32 ..
1.4.d:
..अर्जुन उवाच..
क्व कलापं च तद्ग्रामं कथं शक्यं बिलेन च..
कथं स्कंदप्रसादः स्यादेतन्मे ब्रूहि नारद.. 6.32 ..
1.4.m: Arjuna said: / Where is that village of Kalāpa, and how is it accessible through a subterranean passage? / How may the favor of Skanda be attained? Tell me this, O Nārada.

1.4.s:
..nārada uvāca..
kedārāddhimasaṃyuktaṃ yojanānāṃ śataṃ smṛtam..
tadaṃte yojanaśataṃ vistṛtaṃ tatkalāpakam.. 6.33 ..
1.4.d:
..नारद उवाच..
केदाराद्धिमसंयुक्तं योजनानां शतं स्मृतम्..
तदंते योजनशतं विस्तृतं तत्कलापकम्.. 6.33 ..
1.4.m: Nārada said: / Beyond Kedāra, covered with snow, is traditionally known [a tract of] one hundred yojanas. / At its end lies that Kalāpa, extending for one hundred yojanas.

1.4.s:
tadaṃte yojanaśataṃ vāsukārṇava mucyate..
śatayojanamātraḥ sa bhūmisvargastataḥ smṛtaḥ.. 6.34 ..
1.4.d:
तदंते योजनशतं वासुकार्णव मुच्यते..
शतयोजनमात्रः स भूमिस्वर्गस्ततः स्मृतः.. 6.34 ..
1.4.m: At its end is said to be the ocean of Vāsuki for one hundred yojanas. / It is thus traditionally known as heaven on earth, measuring just a hundred yojanas.

1.4.s:
bilena ca yathā śakyaṃ gaṃtuṃ tatra śrṛṇuṣva tat..
nirannaṃ vai nirudakaṃ devamārādhayedguham.. 6.35 ..
1.4.d:
बिलेन च यथा शक्यं गंतुं तत्र श्रृणुष्व तत्..
निरन्नं वै निरुदकं देवमाराधयेद्गुहम्.. 6.35 ..
1.4.m: Now hear how it is possible to go there by a subterranean passage: / without food and without water, one should worship the god Guha.

1.4.s:
dakṣiṇāyāṃ diśi tato niṣpāpaṃ manyate yadā..
tadā guho'sya svapne gaccheti bhārata.. 6.36 ..
1.4.d:
दक्षिणायां दिशि ततो निष्पापं मन्यते यदा..
तदा गुहोऽस्य स्वप्ने गच्छेति भारत.. 6.36 ..
1.4.m: Then, in the southern direction, when he considers [the devotee] free from sin, / then, O Bhārata, Guha [says] to him in a dream: "Go!"

1.4.s:
tato guhātpaścimato bilamasti bṛhattaram..
tatra praviśya gaṃtavyaṃ kramāṇāṃ śatasaptakam.. 6.37 ..
1.4.d:
ततो गुहात्पश्चिमतो बिलमस्ति बृहत्तरम्..
तत्र प्रविश्य गंतव्यं क्रमाणां शतसप्तकम्.. 6.37 ..
1.4.m: Then, to the west of Guha, there is a very large cavern. / Entering there, one must advance seven hundred steps.

1.4.s:
tatra mārakataṃ liṃgamasti sūryasamaprabham..
tadagre mṛttikā cāsti svarṇavarṇā sunirmalā.. 6.38 ..
1.4.d:
तत्र मारकतं लिंगमस्ति सूर्यसमप्रभम्..
तदग्रे मृत्तिका चास्ति स्वर्णवर्णा सुनिर्मला.. 6.38 ..
1.4.m: There is an emerald liṅga, radiant like the sun; / and before it lies clay, gold-colored and utterly pure.

1.4.s:
namaskṛtya ca talliṃgaṃ gṛhītvā mṛttikāṃ ca tām..
āgaṃtavyaṃ staṃbhatīrthe samārādhya kumārakam.. 6.39 ..
1.4.d:
नमस्कृत्य च तल्लिंगं गृहीत्वा मृत्तिकां च ताम्..
आगंतव्यं स्तंभतीर्थे समाराध्य कुमारकम्.. 6.39 ..
1.4.m: Having bowed to that liṅga and taken that clay, / one should come to Stambhatīrtha, having worshiped Kumāra.

1.4.s:
kolaṃ vā kūpato grāhyaṃ bhūtāyāṃ niśi tajjalam..
tenodakena mṛttikayā kṛtvā netradvayāñjanam.. 6.40 ..
1.4.d:
कोलं वा कूपतो ग्राह्यं भूतायां निशि तज्जलम्..
तेनोदकेन मृत्तिकया कृत्वा नेत्रद्वयाञ्जनम्.. 6.40 ..
1.4.m: Water from a kolawell is to be taken on the night of the fourteenth. / Having made an eye-salve with that water and the clay for both eyes,

1.4.s:
udvartanaṃ ca dehasya kadācitṣaṣṭime pade..
netrāṃjanaprabhāvācca bilaṃ paśyati śobhanam.. 6.41 ..
1.4.d:
उद्वर्तनं च देहस्य कदाचित्षष्टिमे पदे..
नेत्रांजनप्रभावाच्च बिलं पश्यति शोभनम्.. 6.41 ..
1.4.m: and an anointing of the body, perchance at the sixtieth step, / by the power of the eye-salve he sees the beautiful passage.

1.4.s:
tanmadhyena tato yāti gātrodvarttaprabhāvataḥ..
kārīṣairnāma cātyugrairbhakṣyate naiva kīṭakaiḥ.. 6.42 ..
1.4.d:
तन्मध्येन ततो याति गात्रोद्वर्त्तप्रभावतः..
कारीषैर्नाम चात्युग्रैर्भक्ष्यते नैव कीटकैः.. 6.42 ..
1.4.m: He then proceeds through the middle of it; and by the power of anointing his limbs, / he is not at all devoured by the fierce insects called kārīṣa.

1.4.s:
bilamadhye ca saṃpaśyansiddhānbhāskarasannibhān..
yātyevaṃ yātyasau pārtha kalāpaṃ grāmamuttamam.. 6.43 ..
1.4.d:
बिलमध्ये च संपश्यन्सिद्धान्भास्करसन्निभान्..
यात्येवं यात्यसौ पार्थ कलापं ग्राममुत्तमम्.. 6.43 ..
1.4.m: Beholding inside the cave the perfected beings radiant like the sun, / thus he goes, O Pārtha, he goes to the excellent village of Kalāpa.

1.4.s:
tatra varṣasahasrāṇi catvāryāyuḥprakīrtitam..
phalānāṃ bhojanaṃ ca syātpunaḥ puṇyaṃ ca nārjjayet.. 6.44 ..
1.4.d:
तत्र वर्षसहस्राणि चत्वार्यायुःप्रकीर्तितम्..
फलानां भोजनं च स्यात्पुनः पुण्यं च नार्ज्जयेत्.. 6.44 ..
1.4.m: The lifespan there is declared to be four thousand years; / his sustenance would be fruits, and he would not accrue further merit.

1.4.s:
ityetatkathitaṃ tubhyamataścābhūcchṛṇuṣva tat..
tapaḥ sāmarthyataḥ sūkṣmāndaṇḍasyāgre nidhāya tān.. 6.45 ..
1.4.d:
इत्येतत्कथितं तुभ्यमतश्चाभूच्छृणुष्व तत्..
तपः सामर्थ्यतः सूक्ष्मान्दण्डस्याग्रे निधाय तान्.. 6.45 ..
1.4.m: Thus this has been told to you. Now hear what happened next: / by the power of austerity, having placed those subtle [forms of the brahmins] on the tip of my staff,

1.4.s: dvijānahaṃ samāyāto mahīsāgarasaṃgamam.. 6.46 ..
1.4.d: द्विजानहं समायातो महीसागरसंगमम्.. 6.46 ..
1.4.m: I, along with those brahmins, arrived at the confluence of the Mahī and the ocean.

1.4.s:
tadottārya mayā muktāstīre puṇyajalāśaye..
tato mayā kṛtaṃ snānaṃ saha tairdvijasattamaiḥ.. 6.47 ..
1.4.d:
तदोत्तार्य मया मुक्तास्तीरे पुण्यजलाशये..
ततो मया कृतं स्नानं सह तैर्द्विजसत्तमैः.. 6.47 ..
1.4.m: Then, having brought them down, they were set down by me on the bank at the sacred reservoir. / Then a ritual ablution was performed by me together with those best of brahmins

1.4.s:
niḥśeṣadoṣadāvāgnau mahīsāgarasaṃgame..
pitṝṇāṃ devatānāṃ ca kṛtvā tarpaṇasatkriyāḥ.. 6.48 ..
1.4.d:
निःशेषदोषदावाग्नौ महीसागरसंगमे..
पितॄणां देवतानां च कृत्वा तर्पणसत्क्रियाः.. 6.48 ..
1.4.m: at the confluence of the Mahī and the ocean, a forest fire consuming all faults without remainder. / Having performed the rites of libation to the ancestors and the deities,

1.4.s:
japamānāḥ paraṃ japyaṃ niviṣṭāḥ saṃgame vayam..
bhāskaraṃ samavekṣaṃtaściṃtayaṃto hariṃ hṛdi.. 6.49 ..
1.4.d:
जपमानाः परं जप्यं निविष्टाः संगमे वयम्..
भास्करं समवेक्षंतश्चिंतयंतो हरिं हृदि.. 6.49 ..
1.4.m: muttering the supreme prayer, we sat at the confluence, / gazing at the sun, meditating on Hari in our hearts.

1.4.s:
tasmiṃścaivāṃtare pārtha devāḥ śakrapurogamāḥ..
ādityādyā grahāḥ sarve lokapālāśca saṃgatāḥ.. 6.50 ..
1.4.d:
तस्मिंश्चैवांतरे पार्थ देवाः शक्रपुरोगमाः..
आदित्याद्या ग्रहाः सर्वे लोकपालाश्च संगताः.. 6.50 ..
1.4.m: And in that interval, O Pārtha, the gods led by Śakra, / all the planets headed by the Sun, and the world-guardians gathered.

1.4.s:
devānāṃ yonayo hyaṣṭau gaṃdharvāpsarasāṃ gaṇāḥ..
mahotsave tatastasmingītavāditra uttame.. 6.51 ..
1.4.d:
देवानां योनयो ह्यष्टौ गंधर्वाप्सरसां गणाः..
महोत्सवे ततस्तस्मिन्गीतवादित्र उत्तमे.. 6.51 ..
1.4.m: The eight classes of divine beings, the hosts of gandharvas and apsarases [came]. / Then, during that great festival filled with excellent songs and instrumental music,

1.4.s:
pādaprakṣālanaṃ kartuṃ viprāṇāmudyatastvaham..
tasminkāle cāśrṛṇavamahamātithyavākyatām.. 6.52 ..
1.4.d:
पादप्रक्षालनं कर्तुं विप्राणामुद्यतस्त्वहम्..
तस्मिन्काले चाश्रृणवमहमातिथ्यवाक्यताम्.. 6.52 ..
1.4.m: I was about to wash the feet of the brahmins; / and at that moment I heard the utterance of words requesting hospitality,

1.4.s:
sāmadhvanisamāyuktāṃ tṛtīyasvaranāditām..
atīva manaso ramyāṃ śiva bhaktimivottamām.. 6.53 ..
1.4.d:
सामध्वनिसमायुक्तां तृतीयस्वरनादिताम्..
अतीव मनसो रम्यां शिव भक्तिमिवोत्तमाम्.. 6.53 ..
1.4.m: endowed with the sound of Sāmaveda chanting, resonating in the third tone, / exceedingly charming to the mind, like supreme devotion to Śiva.

1.4.s:
viprairutthāya saṃpṛṣṭaḥ kastvaṃ vipra kva cāgataḥ..
kiṃ vā prārthayase brūhi yatte manasi rocate.. 6.54 ..
1.4.d:
विप्रैरुत्थाय संपृष्टः कस्त्वं विप्र क्व चागतः..
किं वा प्रार्थयसे ब्रूहि यत्ते मनसि रोचते.. 6.54 ..
1.4.m: Rising, the brahmins asked: "Who are you, O brahmin, and from where have you come? / Or what do you request? Tell us what pleases your heart."

1.4.s:
..vipra uvāca..
muniḥ kapilanāmāhaṃ nāradāya nivedyatām..
āgataḥ prārthanāyaiva tacchrutvāhamathābravam.. 6.55 ..
1.4.d:
..विप्र उवाच..
मुनिः कपिलनामाहं नारदाय निवेद्यताम्..
आगतः प्रार्थनायैव तच्छ्रुत्वाहमथाब्रवम्.. 6.55 ..
1.4.m: The brahmin said: / "I am the sage named Kapila; let this be announced to Nārada: / I have come solely with a request." Hearing that, I then said:

1.4.s:
dhanyohaṃ yadihāyātaḥ kapila tvaṃ mahāmune..
nāstyadeyaṃ tavāsmābhiḥ pātraṃ nāsti tavādhikam.. 6.56 ..
1.4.d:
धन्योहं यदिहायातः कपिल त्वं महामुने..
नास्त्यदेयं तवास्माभिः पात्रं नास्ति तवाधिकम्.. 6.56 ..
1.4.m: "I am blessed that you have come here, O great sage Kapila! / There is nothing that cannot be given to you by us; there is no recipient superior to you."

1.4.s:
..kapila uvāca..
brahmaputra tvayā deyaṃ yadi me tvaṃ śrṛṇuṣva tat..
aṣṭau viprasahasrāṇi mama dehīti nārada.. 6.57 ..
1.4.d:
..कपिल उवाच..
ब्रह्मपुत्र त्वया देयं यदि मे त्वं श्रृणुष्व तत्..
अष्टौ विप्रसहस्राणि मम देहीति नारद.. 6.57 ..
1.4.m: Kapila said: / "O son of Brahmā, if something is to be given to me by you, hear this: / give me eight thousand brahmins, O Nārada!

1.4.s:
bhūmidānaṃ kariṣyāmi kalāpagrāmavāsinām..
brāhmaṇānāmahaṃ caiṣāṃ tadidaṃ kriyatāṃ vibho.. 6.58 ..
1.4.d:
भूमिदानं करिष्यामि कलापग्रामवासिनाम्..
ब्राह्मणानामहं चैषां तदिदं क्रियतां विभो.. 6.58 ..
1.4.m: I shall make a gift of land to these brāhmaṇas who dwell in the village of Kalāpa. / Therefore let this be done, O lord!"

1.4.s:
tato mayā pratijñātamevamastu mahāmune..
tvayāpi kriyatāṃ sthānaṃ kāpilaṃ kapilottamam.. 6.59 ..
1.4.d:
ततो मया प्रतिज्ञातमेवमस्तु महामुने..
त्वयापि क्रियतां स्थानं कापिलं कपिलोत्तमम्.. 6.59 ..
1.4.m: Then it was promised by me: "So be it, O great sage! / May you also establish a site sacred to Kapila, the best of Kapilas.

1.4.s:
śrāddhe vā prāptakāle vā hyatithirvimukhībhavet..
yasyāśramamupāyātasyasya sarvaṃ hi niṣphalam.. 6.60 ..
1.4.d:
श्राद्धे वा प्राप्तकाले वा ह्यतिथिर्विमुखीभवेत्..
यस्याश्रममुपायातस्यस्य सर्वं हि निष्फलम्.. 6.60 ..
1.4.m: If a guest turns away in disappointment during a śrāddha or at an opportune time, / having arrived at anyone's hermitage, all of that [host's merit] becomes fruitless.

1.4.s:
sa gacchedrauravām̐llokānyo'tithiṃ nābhipūjayet..
atithiḥ pūjito yena sa devairapi pūjyate.. 6.61 ..
1.4.d:
स गच्छेद्रौरवाम्̐ल्लोकान्योऽतिथिं नाभिपूजयेत्..
अतिथिः पूजितो येन स देवैरपि पूज्यते.. 6.61 ..
1.4.m: He who does not honor a guest would go to the Raurava hells; / but he by whom a guest is honored is honored even by the gods."

1.4.s:
dānairyajñaista tastasminbhojitaḥ kapilo muniḥ..
tato mahāmuniḥ śrīmānhārīto hvayitastadā.. 6.62 ..
1.4.d:
दानैर्यज्ञैस्त तस्तस्मिन्भोजितः कपिलो मुनिः..
ततो महामुनिः श्रीमान्हारीतो ह्वयितस्तदा.. 6.62 ..
1.4.m: The sage Kapila was then fed there with gifts and sacrifices. / Then the glorious great sage Hārīta was summoned at that time

1.4.s:
pādaprakṣālanārthāya siddhadevasamāgame..
hārītaśca puraskṛtya vāmapādaṃ tadā sthitaḥ.. 6.63 ..
1.4.d:
पादप्रक्षालनार्थाय सिद्धदेवसमागमे..
हारीतश्च पुरस्कृत्य वामपादं तदा स्थितः.. 6.63 ..
1.4.m: for the purpose of having his feet washed in that assembly of perfected beings and gods. / And putting forward his left foot, Hārīta then stood [before me].

1.4.s:
tato hāso mahāñjajñe siddhāpsaraḥ suparvaṇām..
viciṃtya bahudhā pṛthvīṃ sādhu sādhukṛtā dvijāḥ.. 6.64 ..
1.4.d:
ततो हासो महाञ्जज्ञे सिद्धाप्सरः सुपर्वणाम्..
विचिंत्य बहुधा पृथ्वीं साधु साधुकृता द्विजाः.. 6.64 ..
1.4.m: Then a great laughter arose among the perfected beings, apsarases, and gods. / Having pondered the earth in many ways, [they thought], "Well done, well done, O brahmins!"

1.4.s:
tato mamāpi manasi śokavego mahānabhūt..
satyāṃ caiva tathā mene gāthāṃ pūrvabudheritām.. 6.65 ..
1.4.d:
ततो ममापि मनसि शोकवेगो महानभूत्..
सत्यां चैव तथा मेने गाथां पूर्वबुधेरिताम्.. 6.65 ..
1.4.m: Then in my mind too a great rush of grief arose, / and I regarded as true the ancient saying uttered by the wise:

1.4.s:
sarveṣvapi ca kāryeṣu hetiśabdo vigarhitaḥ..
kurvatāmatikāryāṇi śilāpāto dhruvaṃ bhavet.. 6.66 ..
1.4.d:
सर्वेष्वपि च कार्येषु हेतिशब्दो विगर्हितः..
कुर्वतामतिकार्याणि शिलापातो ध्रुवं भवेत्.. 6.66 ..
1.4.m: "In all undertakings, the sound of mockery is condemned. / For those who perform excessive actions, a fall of stones is certain to occur."

1.4.s:
tatohamabraṃvaṃ viprānyūyaṃ mūrkhā bhaviṣyatha..
dhanadhānyālpasaṃyuktā dāridryakalilāvṛtāḥ.. 6.67 ..
1.4.d:
ततोहमब्रंवं विप्रान्यूयं मूर्खा भविष्यथ..
धनधान्याल्पसंयुक्ता दारिद्र्यकलिलावृताः.. 6.67 ..
1.4.m: Then I said to the brahmins: "You will become fools, / possessing little wealth and grain, enveloped in the filth of poverty!"

1.4.s:
evamukte prahasyaiva hārītaḥ prābravīdidam..
tavaiveyaṃ mune hāniryadasmāñchapate bhavān.. 6.68 ..
1.4.d:
एवमुक्ते प्रहस्यैव हारीतः प्राब्रवीदिदम्..
तवैवेयं मुने हानिर्यदस्माञ्छपते भवान्.. 6.68 ..
1.4.m: When this was said, laughing indeed, Hārīta replied: / "This loss is only yours, O sage, since you curse us!

1.4.s:
kaḥ śāpo dīyate tubhyaṃ śāpoyamayameva te..
tato vimṛśya bhūyo'habravaṃ kimahaṃdvija.. 6.69 ..
1.4.d:
कः शापो दीयते तुभ्यं शापोयमयमेव ते..
ततो विमृश्य भूयोऽहब्रवं किमहंद्विज.. 6.69 ..
1.4.m: What curse could be given to you? This very curse is your own." / Then, reflecting again, I said: "Why, O brahmin,

1.4.s: tathāvidhasya bhavato vāmapādapradānataḥ.. 6.70 ..
1.4.d: तथाविधस्य भवतो वामपादप्रदानतः.. 6.70 ..
1.4.m: since you, being of such a kind, offered your left foot?"

1.4.s:
..hārīta uvāca..
śrṛṇu tatkāraṇaṃ dhīmañchūnyatā me yato bhavet.. 6.71 ..
1.4.d:
..हारीत उवाच..
श्रृणु तत्कारणं धीमञ्छून्यता मे यतो भवेत्.. 6.71 ..
1.4.m: Hārīta said: / "Hear the reason for that, O wise one, whence my absentmindedness arose.

1.4.s:
iti ciṃtayataścitte hā duḥkho'yaṃ pratigrahaḥ..
pratigraheṇa viprāṇāṃ brāhmyaṃ tejo hi śāmyati.. 6.72 ..
1.4.d:
इति चिंतयतश्चित्ते हा दुःखोऽयं प्रतिग्रहः..
प्रतिग्रहेण विप्राणां ब्राह्म्यं तेजो हि शाम्यति.. 6.72 ..
1.4.m: As I reflected thus in my mind: 'Alas, this acceptance of a gift is full of sorrow! / For by the acceptance of gifts, the brahminical splendor of brahmins is extinguished.

1.4.s:
mahādānaṃ hi gṛhṇāno brāhmaṇaḥ svaṃ śubhaṃ hi yat..
dadāti dāturdātā ca aśubhaṃ yacchati svakam.. 6.73 ..
1.4.d:
महादानं हि गृह्णानो ब्राह्मणः स्वं शुभं हि यत्..
ददाति दातुर्दाता च अशुभं यच्छति स्वकम्.. 6.73 ..
1.4.m: A brāhmaṇa who accepts a great gift gives whatever auspicious merit is his own / to the giver, and the giver imparts his own inauspicious [evil] to him.

1.4.s:
dātā pratigrahītā ca vacanaṃ hi parasparam..
manyate'dhaḥkaro yasya so'lpabuddhiḥ prahīyate.. 6.74 ..
1.4.d:
दाता प्रतिग्रहीता च वचनं हि परस्परम्..
मन्यतेऽधःकरो यस्य सोऽल्पबुद्धिः प्रहीयते.. 6.74 ..
1.4.m: For such is the agreement between giver and receiver; / he whose hand is below is considered to decline in poor intellect.'

1.4.s:
iti ciṃtayato mahyaṃ śūnyatābhūddhi nārada..
nidrārtaśca bhayārtaśca kāmārtaḥ śokapīḍitaḥ.. 6.75 ..
1.4.d:
इति चिंतयतो मह्यं शून्यताभूद्धि नारद..
निद्रार्तश्च भयार्तश्च कामार्तः शोकपीडितः.. 6.75 ..
1.4.m: As I was pondering this, an absentmindedness came upon me, O Nārada. / One afflicted by sleep, one afflicted by fear, one afflicted by lust, one tormented by grief,

1.4.s:
hṛtasvaścānyacittaśca śūnyāhyete bhavaṃti ca..
tadeṣu matimānkopaṃ na kurvīta yadi tvayā.. 6.76 ..
1.4.d:
हृतस्वश्चान्यचित्तश्च शून्याह्येते भवंति च..
तदेषु मतिमान्कोपं न कुर्वीत यदि त्वया.. 6.76 ..
1.4.m: one robbed of his property, and one whose mind is elsewhere—these are indeed absentminded. / Therefore, a wise man should not show anger toward them, if by you..."

1.4.s:
kṛtaḥ kopastatastubhyamevaṃ hāniriyaṃ mune..
tatastāpānvitaścāhaṃ tānvi prānabravaṃ punaḥ.. 6.77 ..
1.4.d:
कृतः कोपस्ततस्तुभ्यमेवं हानिरियं मुने..
ततस्तापान्वितश्चाहं तान्वि प्रानब्रवं पुनः.. 6.77 ..
1.4.m: If anger was displayed, then such a loss has come to you, O sage. / Then, filled with remorse, I addressed those brahmins again:

1.4.s:
dhiṅmāmastu ca durbuddhimavimṛśyārthakāriṇam..
kurvatāmavimṛśyaiva tatkimasti na yadbhavet.. 6.78 ..
1.4.d:
धिङ्मामस्तु च दुर्बुद्धिमविमृश्यार्थकारिणम्..
कुर्वतामविमृश्यैव तत्किमस्ति न यद्भवेत्.. 6.78 ..
1.4.m: "Fie on me, wicked-minded, who act without deliberating on consequences! / What [bad outcome] is there that may not happen to those who act without reflection?

1.4.s:
sahasā na kriyāṃ kuryātpadametanmahāpadām..
vimṛśyakāriṇaṃ dhīraṃ vṛṇate sarvasaṃpadaḥ.. 6.79 ..
1.4.d:
सहसा न क्रियां कुर्यात्पदमेतन्महापदाम्..
विमृश्यकारिणं धीरं वृणते सर्वसंपदः.. 6.79 ..
1.4.m: One should not act in haste; this is the seat of great misfortunes. / All fortunes choose the steadfast man who acts after reflection.

1.4.s:
satyamāha mahābuddhiścirakārī purā hi saḥ..
purā hi brāhmaṇaḥ kaścitprakhyātoṃ girasāṃ kule.. 6.80 ..
1.4.d:
सत्यमाह महाबुद्धिश्चिरकारी पुरा हि सः..
पुरा हि ब्राह्मणः कश्चित्प्रख्यातों गिरसां कुले.. 6.80 ..
1.4.m: Truly spoke that Cirakārī of great intellect long ago. / Long ago, indeed, there was a certain brahmin renowned in the lineage of the Aṅgirases.

1.4.s:
cirakāri mahāprājño gautamasyābhavatsutaḥ..
cireṇa sarvakāryāṇi yo vimṛśya prapadyate.. 6.81 ..
1.4.d:
चिरकारि महाप्राज्ञो गौतमस्याभवत्सुतः..
चिरेण सर्वकार्याणि यो विमृश्य प्रपद्यते.. 6.81 ..
1.4.m: Cirakārī was the wise son of Gautama. / Because he undertook all actions slowly, after reflecting,

1.4.s:
cirakāryābhisaṃpateścirakārī tathocyate..
alasagrahaṇaṃ prāpto durmedhāvī tathocyate.. 6.82 ..
1.4.d:
चिरकार्याभिसंपतेश्चिरकारी तथोच्यते..
अलसग्रहणं प्राप्तो दुर्मेधावी तथोच्यते.. 6.82 ..
1.4.m: and accomplished tasks by lingering, he was called Cirakārī. / Regarded as sluggish, he was called foolishly slow

1.4.s:
buddhilāghavayuktena janenādīrghadarśinā..
vyabhicāreṇa kasminsa vyatikramyā parānsutān.. 6.83 ..
1.4.d:
बुद्धिलाघवयुक्तेन जनेनादीर्घदर्शिना..
व्यभिचारेण कस्मिन्स व्यतिक्रम्या परान्सुतान्.. 6.83 ..
1.4.m: by people of shallow intellect, devoid of foresight. / On account of a transgression, having bypassed his other sons,

1.4.s:
pitroktaḥ kupitenātha jahīmāṃ jananīmiti..
sa tatheti cireṇoktaḥ svabhāvāccirakārakaḥ.. 6.84 ..
1.4.d:
पित्रोक्तः कुपितेनाथ जहीमां जननीमिति..
स तथेति चिरेणोक्तः स्वभावाच्चिरकारकः.. 6.84 ..
1.4.m: he was ordered by his father, who was enraged: 'Kill this mother!' / Saying 'So be it' after a long time, he who was by nature slow to act,

1.4.s:
vimṛśya cirakāritvācciṃ tayāmāsa vai ciram..
piturājñāṃ kathaṃ kuryāṃ na hanyāṃ mātaraṃ katham.. 6.85 ..
1.4.d:
विमृश्य चिरकारित्वाच्चिं तयामास वै चिरम्..
पितुराज्ञां कथं कुर्यां न हन्यां मातरं कथम्.. 6.85 ..
1.4.m: reflecting because of his habit of lingering, pondered for a long time: / 'How may I fulfill my father's command? How may I not kill my mother?

1.4.s:
