kathaṃ dharmacchalenāsminnimajjeyamasādhuvat..
piturājñā paro dharmo hyadharmo mātṛrakṣaṇam.. 6.86 ..
1.4.d:
कथं धर्मच्छलेनास्मिन्निमज्जेयमसाधुवत्..
पितुराज्ञा परो धर्मो ह्यधर्मो मातृरक्षणम्.. 6.86 ..
1.4.m: How might I not plunge like a wicked person into this under the pretext of righteousness? / The father's command is supreme righteousness, but protecting one's mother is also [righteous].

1.4.s:
asvataṃtraṃ ca putratvaṃ kiṃ tu māṃ nātra pīḍayet..
striyaṃ hatvā mātaraṃ ca ko hi jātu sukhī bhavet.. 6.87 ..
1.4.d:
अस्वतंत्रं च पुत्रत्वं किं तु मां नात्र पीडयेत्..
स्त्रियं हत्वा मातरं च को हि जातु सुखी भवेत्.. 6.87 ..
1.4.m: A son's state is one of dependence, yet what may not torment me here? / Having killed a woman, and a mother, who indeed could ever be happy?

1.4.s:
pitaraṃ cāpyavajñāya kaḥ pratiṣṭhāmavāpnuyāt..
anavajñā pituryuktā yuktaṃ mātuśca rakṣaṇam.. 6.88 ..
1.4.d:
पितरं चाप्यवज्ञाय कः प्रतिष्ठामवाप्नुयात्..
अनवज्ञा पितुर्युक्ता युक्तं मातुश्च रक्षणम्.. 6.88 ..
1.4.m: And having dishonored his father, who could attain standing? / Non-disrespect toward a father is proper, and protecting a mother is proper.

1.4.s:
kṣamāyogyāvubhāvetau nātivarteta vai katham..
pitā hyātmānamādhatte jāyāyāṃ jajñivāniti.. 6.89 ..
1.4.d:
क्षमायोग्यावुभावेतौ नातिवर्तेत वै कथम्..
पिता ह्यात्मानमाधत्ते जायायां जज्ञिवानिति.. 6.89 ..
1.4.m: Both of these deserve forbearance; how indeed could one not overstep? / For a father places himself in his wife, having been born [as a son]

1.4.s:
śīlacāritragotrasya dhāraṇārthaṃ kulasya ca..
so'hamātmā svayaṃ pitrā putratve parikalpitaḥ.. 6.90 ..
1.4.d:
शीलचारित्रगोत्रस्य धारणार्थं कुलस्य च..
सोऽहमात्मा स्वयं पित्रा पुत्रत्वे परिकल्पितः.. 6.90 ..
1.4.m: for the preservation of good conduct, moral lineage, and family. / Thus I myself have been fashioned by my father as his own self in the state of sonship.

1.4.s:
jātakarmaṇi yatprāha pitā yaccopakarmaṇi..
paryāptaḥ sa dṛḍhīkāraḥ piturgauravalipsayā.. 6.91 ..
1.4.d:
जातकर्मणि यत्प्राह पिता यच्चोपकर्मणि..
पर्याप्तः स दृढीकारः पितुर्गौरवलिप्सया.. 6.91 ..
1.4.m: What the father pronounced at the birth-rite and at the sacred thread investiture, / that was a sufficient confirmation, desiring honor toward the father.

1.4.s:
śarīrādīni deyāni pitā tvekaḥ prayaccati..
tasmātpiturvacaḥ kāryaṃ na vicāryaṃ kathaṃcana.. 6.92 ..
1.4.d:
शरीरादीनि देयानि पिता त्वेकः प्रयच्चति..
तस्मात्पितुर्वचः कार्यं न विचार्यं कथंचन.. 6.92 ..
1.4.m: It is the father alone who bestows the body and other [gifts] to be given; / therefore the father's word must be obeyed, and never questioned in any way.

1.4.s:
pātakānyapi cūryaṃte piturvacanakāriṇaḥ..
pitā svargaḥ pitā dharmaḥ pitā paramakaṃ tapaḥ.. 6.93 ..
1.4.d:
पातकान्यपि चूर्यंते पितुर्वचनकारिणः..
पिता स्वर्गः पिता धर्मः पिता परमकं तपः.. 6.93 ..
1.4.m: Even major sins are destroyed for one who obeys his father's command. / The father is heaven, the father is righteousness, the father is supreme austerity.

1.4.s:
pitari prītimāpanne sarvāḥ prīṇaṃti devatāḥ..
āśiṣastā bhajaṃtyenaṃ puruṣaṃ prāha yāḥ pitā.. 6.94 ..
1.4.d:
पितरि प्रीतिमापन्ने सर्वाः प्रीणंति देवताः..
आशिषस्ता भजंत्येनं पुरुषं प्राह याः पिता.. 6.94 ..
1.4.m: When the father is pleased, all the gods rejoice. / Those blessings that a father speaks attend upon that man.

1.4.s:
niṣkṛtiḥ sarvapāpānāṃ pitā yadabhinaṃdati..
mucyate baṃdhanātpuṣpaṃ phalaṃ vṛṃtātpramucyate.. 6.95 ..
1.4.d:
निष्कृतिः सर्वपापानां पिता यदभिनंदति..
मुच्यते बंधनात्पुष्पं फलं वृंतात्प्रमुच्यते.. 6.95 ..
1.4.m: That a father rejoices is the expiation of all sins. / A flower is released from its bond; a fruit is released from its stem.

1.4.s:
kliśyannapi sutaḥ snehaṃ pitā snehaṃ na muṃcati..
etadviciṃtyataṃ tāvatputrasya pitṛgauravam.. 6.96 ..
1.4.d:
क्लिश्यन्नपि सुतः स्नेहं पिता स्नेहं न मुंचति..
एतद्विचिंत्यतं तावत्पुत्रस्य पितृगौरवम्.. 6.96 ..
1.4.m: Though suffering, a son does not abandon love, nor does a father abandon love. / So far, this greatness of a father has been considered by the son;

1.4.s:
pitā nālpataraṃ sthānaṃ ciṃtayiṣyāmi mātaram..
yo hyayaṃ mayi saṃghāto martyatve pāṃcabhautikaḥ.. 6.97 ..
1.4.d:
पिता नाल्पतरं स्थानं चिंतयिष्यामि मातरम्..
यो ह्ययं मयि संघातो मर्त्यत्वे पांचभौतिकः.. 6.97 ..
1.4.m: a father is not an inferior station; [now] I shall consider the mother. / For this aggregate consisting of the five elements in my mortal state,

1.4.s:
asya me jananī hetuḥ pāvakasya yathāraṇiḥ..
mātā dehāraṇiḥ puṃsaḥ sarvasyārthasya nirvṛtiḥ.. 6.98 ..
1.4.d:
अस्य मे जननी हेतुः पावकस्य यथारणिः..
माता देहारणिः पुंसः सर्वस्यार्थस्य निर्वृतिः.. 6.98 ..
1.4.m: my mother is the cause of it, just as the fire-drill is of fire. / The mother is the body's fire-drill for a man, the fulfillment of every purpose.

1.4.s:
mātṛlābhe sanāthatvamanāthatvaṃ viparyaye..
na sa śocati nāpyenaṃ sthāvaryamapi karṣati.. 6.99 ..
1.4.d:
मातृलाभे सनाथत्वमनाथत्वं विपर्यये..
न स शोचति नाप्येनं स्थावर्यमपि कर्षति.. 6.99 ..
1.4.m: Possessing a mother means having a protector; the reverse means being helpless. / He does not grieve, nor does decrepitude emaciate him,

1.4.s:
śriyā hīno'pi yo gehe aṃbeti pratipadyate..
putrapautrasamāpanno jananīṃ yaḥ samāśritaḥ.. 6.100 ..
1.4.d:
श्रिया हीनोऽपि यो गेहे अंबेति प्रतिपद्यते..
पुत्रपौत्रसमापन्नो जननीं यः समाश्रितः.. 6.100 ..
1.4.m: who, even though bereft of wealth, addresses [her] at home: 'O mother!' / Endowed with sons and grandsons, he who has resorted to his mother,

1.4.s:
api varṣaśatasyāṃte sa dvihāyanavaccaret..
samarthaṃ vā'samarthaṃ vā kṛśaṃ vāpyakṛśaṃ tathā.. 6.101 ..
1.4.d:
अपि वर्षशतस्यांते स द्विहायनवच्चरेत्..
समर्थं वाऽसमर्थं वा कृशं वाप्यकृशं तथा.. 6.101 ..
1.4.m: even at the end of a hundred years, walks like a two-year-old child. / Whether capable or incapable, thin or stout,

1.4.s:
rakṣayecca sutaṃ mātā nānyaḥ poṣyavidhānataḥ..
tadā sa vṛddho bhavati tadā bhavati duḥkhitaḥ.. 6.102 ..
1.4.d:
रक्षयेच्च सुतं माता नान्यः पोष्यविधानतः..
तदा स वृद्धो भवति तदा भवति दुःखितः.. 6.102 ..
1.4.m: the mother protects her son; no other does so by way of nourishment. / Then he becomes old, then he becomes sorrowful,

1.4.s:
tadā śunyaṃ jagattasya yadā mātrā viyujyate..
nāsti mātṛsamā cchāyā nāsti mātṛsamā gatiḥ.. 6.103 ..
1.4.d:
तदा शुन्यं जगत्तस्य यदा मात्रा वियुज्यते..
नास्ति मातृसमा च्छाया नास्ति मातृसमा गतिः.. 6.103 ..
1.4.m: then the world is empty for him, when he is separated from his mother. / There is no shade like a mother, there is no refuge like a mother,

1.4.s:
nāsti mātṛsamaṃ trāṇaṃ nāsti mātṛsamā prapā..
kukṣisaṃdhāraṇāddhātrī jananājjananī tathā.. 6.104 ..
1.4.d:
नास्ति मातृसमं त्राणं नास्ति मातृसमा प्रपा..
कुक्षिसंधारणाद्धात्री जननाज्जननी तथा.. 6.104 ..
1.4.m: there is no protection like a mother, there is no water station like a mother. / Because of carrying him in her belly, she is the sustainer; because of giving birth, she is the mother;

1.4.s:
aṃgānāṃ vardhanādaṃbā vīrasūtve ca vīrasūḥ..
śiśoḥ śuśrūṣaṇācchvaśrūrmātā syānmānanāttathā.. 6.105 ..
1.4.d:
अंगानां वर्धनादंबा वीरसूत्वे च वीरसूः..
शिशोः शुश्रूषणाच्छ्वश्रूर्माता स्यान्माननात्तथा.. 6.105 ..
1.4.m: because of growing his limbs, she is the mother; and when bearing a hero, she is the mother of heroes; / because of tending to the infant, she is the protector; and because of commanding respect, she is the mother.

1.4.s:
devatānāṃ samāvāpamekatvaṃ pitaraṃ viduḥ
martyānāṃ devatānāṃ ca pūgo nātyeti mātaram.. 6.106 ..
1.4.d:
देवतानां समावापमेकत्वं पितरं विदुः
मर्त्यानां देवतानां च पूगो नात्येति मातरम्.. 6.106 ..
1.4.m: They know the father as a collection of deities unified into one; / but the host of mortals and deities does not surpass a mother.

1.4.s:
patitā guravastyājyā mātā ca na kathaṃcana..
garbhadhāraṇapoṣābhyāṃ tena mātā garīyasī.. 6.107 ..
1.4.d:
पतिता गुरवस्त्याज्या माता च न कथंचन..
गर्भधारणपोषाभ्यां तेन माता गरीयसी.. 6.107 ..
1.4.m: Fallen teachers are to be abandoned, but a mother never. / By bearing in the womb and nourishing, the mother is weightier.'

1.4.s:
evaṃ sa kauśikītīre baliṃ rājānamīkṣatīm..
strīvṛttiṃ cirakālatvāddhantuṃ diṣṭaḥ svamātaram.. 6.108 ..
1.4.d:
एवं स कौशिकीतीरे बलिं राजानमीक्षतीम्..
स्त्रीवृत्तिं चिरकालत्वाद्धन्तुं दिष्टः स्वमातरम्.. 6.108 ..
1.4.m: Thus, commanded to slay his own mother, who on the bank of the Kauśikī / had looked upon King Bali as is the nature of women, on account of his tardiness,

1.4.s:
vimṛśya cirakālaṃ hi ciṃtāṃtaṃ nābhyapadyata..
etasminnaṃtare śakro rūpamāsthitaḥ.. 6.109 ..
1.4.d:
विमृश्य चिरकालं हि चिंतांतं नाभ्यपद्यत..
एतस्मिन्नंतरे शक्रो रूपमास्थितः.. 6.109 ..
1.4.m: reflecting for a long time, he did not reach an end to his thought. / In the meantime, Śakra, having assumed a [disguised] form,

1.4.s:
gāyangākhāmupāyātaḥ pitustasyāśramāṃtike..
anṛnā hi striyaḥ sarvāḥ sūtrakāro yadabravīt.. 6.110 ..
1.4.d:
गायन्गाखामुपायातः पितुस्तस्याश्रमांतिके..
अनृना हि स्त्रियः सर्वाः सूत्रकारो यदब्रवीत्.. 6.110 ..
1.4.m: approached singing a verse near the hermitage of his father: / 'All women are indeed blameless, as the author of the aphorisms has said;

1.4.s:
atastābhyaḥ phalaṃ grāhyaṃ na syāddoṣekṣaṇaḥ sudhīḥ..
iti śrutvā tamānarca medhātithirudāradhīḥ.. 6.111 ..
1.4.d:
अतस्ताभ्यः फलं ग्राह्यं न स्याद्दोषेक्षणः सुधीः..
इति श्रुत्वा तमानर्च मेधातिथिरुदारधीः.. 6.111 ..
1.4.m: therefore fruit should be taken from them; a wise man should not look for fault.' / Having heard this, Medhātithi of noble mind paid respect to him.

1.4.s:
duḥkhitaściṃtayanprāpto bhṛśamaśrūṇi vartayan..
aho'hamīrṣyayākṣipto magno'haṃ duḥkhasāgare.. 6.112 ..
1.4.d:
दुःखितश्चिंतयन्प्राप्तो भृशमश्रूणि वर्तयन्..
अहोऽहमीर्ष्ययाक्षिप्तो मग्नोऽहं दुःखसागरे.. 6.112 ..
1.4.m: Grieved and reflecting, he arrived, shedding tears profusely: / 'Alas, driven by jealousy, I am sunk in an ocean of sorrow!

1.4.s:
hatvā nārīṃ ca sādhvīṃ ca ko nu māṃ tārayiṣyati..
satvareṇa mayājñaptaścirakārī hyudāradhīḥ.. 6.113 ..
1.4.d:
हत्वा नारीं च साध्वीं च को नु मां तारयिष्यति..
सत्वरेण मयाज्ञप्तश्चिरकारी ह्युदारधीः.. 6.113 ..
1.4.m: Having killed a woman and a virtuous wife, who indeed will deliver me? / In haste I commanded Cirakārī of noble mind.

1.4.s:
yadyayaṃ cirakārī syātsa māṃ trāyeta pātakāt..
cirakārika bhadraṃ te bhadraṃ te cirakārika.. 6.114 ..
1.4.d:
यद्ययं चिरकारी स्यात्स मां त्रायेत पातकात्..
चिरकारिक भद्रं ते भद्रं ते चिरकारिक.. 6.114 ..
1.4.m: If he acted slowly, he might protect me from sin. / O Cirakārika, hail to you! Hail to you, O Cirakārika!

1.4.s:
yadadya cirakārī tvaṃ tato'si cirakārikaḥ..
trāhi māṃ mātaraṃ caiva tapo yaccārjitaṃ mayā.. 6.115 ..
1.4.d:
यदद्य चिरकारी त्वं ततोऽसि चिरकारिकः..
त्राहि मां मातरं चैव तपो यच्चार्जितं मया.. 6.115 ..
1.4.m: Since you act slowly today, for that reason you are Cirakārika. / Protect me, and my mother as well, and whatever austerity has been accumulated by me,

1.4.s:
ātmānaṃ pātake viṣṭaṃ śubhāhva cirakārika..
evaṃ sa duḥkhitaḥ prāpto gautamo'ciṃtayattadā.. 6.116 ..
1.4.d:
आत्मानं पातके विष्टं शुभाह्व चिरकारिक..
एवं स दुःखितः प्राप्तो गौतमोऽचिंतयत्तदा.. 6.116 ..
1.4.m: and yourself entered into sin, O auspiciously named Cirakārika!' / Thus arriving sorrowful, Gautama reflected at that time.

1.4.s:
cirakārikaṃ dadarśātha putraṃ māturupāṃtike..
cirakārī tu pitaraṃ dṛṣṭvā paramaduḥkhitaḥ.. 6.117 ..
1.4.d:
चिरकारिकं ददर्शाथ पुत्रं मातुरुपांतिके..
चिरकारी तु पितरं दृष्ट्वा परमदुःखितः.. 6.117 ..
1.4.m: Then he saw his son Cirakārika in the presence of his mother. / Seeing his father, Cirakārī, deeply distressed,

1.4.s:
śastraṃ tyaktvā sthito mūrdhnā prasādāyopacakrame..
medhātithiḥ sutaṃ dṛṣṭvā śirasā patitaṃ bhuvi.. 6.118 ..
1.4.d:
शस्त्रं त्यक्त्वा स्थितो मूर्ध्ना प्रसादायोपचक्रमे..
मेधातिथिः सुतं दृष्ट्वा शिरसा पतितं भुवि.. 6.118 ..
1.4.m: dropped the weapon and bowed with his head, proceeding to propitiate him. / Medhātithi, seeing his son fallen with his head on the ground,

1.4.s:
patnīṃ caiva tu jīvaṃtīṃ parāmabhyagamanmudam..
hanyāditi na sā veda śastrapāṇau sthite sute.. 6.119 ..
1.4.d:
पत्नीं चैव तु जीवंतीं परामभ्यगमन्मुदम्..
हन्यादिति न सा वेद शस्त्रपाणौ स्थिते सुते.. 6.119 ..
1.4.m: and his wife still living, experienced supreme joy. / While her son stood with weapon in hand, she did not know that he might kill [her];

1.4.s:
buddhirāsītsutaṃ dṛṣṭvā pituścaraṇayornatam..
śastragrahaṇacāpalyaṃ saṃvṛṇoti bhayāditi.. 6.120 ..
1.4.d:
बुद्धिरासीत्सुतं दृष्ट्वा पितुश्चरणयोर्नतम्..
शस्त्रग्रहणचापल्यं संवृणोति भयादिति.. 6.120 ..
1.4.m: seeing her son bowed at his father's feet, her thought was: / 'Out of fear, he is concealing his rashness in taking up a weapon.'

1.4.s:
tataḥ pitrā ciraṃ smṛtvā ciraṃ cāghrāya mūrdhani..
ciraṃ dorbhyāṃ pariṣvajya ciraṃjīvetyu dāhṛtaḥ.. 6.121 ..
1.4.d:
ततः पित्रा चिरं स्मृत्वा चिरं चाघ्राय मूर्धनि..
चिरं दोर्भ्यां परिष्वज्य चिरंजीवेत्यु दाहृतः.. 6.121 ..
1.4.m: Then, having pondered for a long time, having smelled [his] head for a long time, / having embraced [him] with both arms for a long time, [his] father addressed him: 'Live long!'

1.4.s:
ciraṃ mudānvitaḥ putraṃ medhātithirathābravīt..
cirakārika bhadraṃ te cirakārī bhavecciram.. 6.122 ..
1.4.d:
चिरं मुदान्वितः पुत्रं मेधातिथिरथाब्रवीत्..
चिरकारिक भद्रं ते चिरकारी भवेच्चिरम्.. 6.122 ..
1.4.m: Filled with great joy for a long time, Medhātithi then said to his son: / 'O Cirakārika, may good betide you; may you ever be one who acts slowly.

1.4.s:
cirāya yatkṛtaṃ saumya ciramasmin duḥkhitaḥ..
gāthāścāpyabravīdvidvāngautamo munisattamaḥ.. 6.123 ..
1.4.d:
चिराय यत्कृतं सौम्य चिरमस्मिन् दुःखितः..
गाथाश्चाप्यब्रवीद्विद्वान्गौतमो मुनिसत्तमः.. 6.123 ..
1.4.m: Because you delayed, gentle one, I [only] grieved for a long time.' / And the wise Gautama, the best among sages, spoke these verses:

1.4.s:
cireṇa maṃtraṃ saṃdhīyāccirema ca kṛtaṃ tyajet..
cireṇa vihataṃ mitraṃ ciraṃ dhāraṇamarhati.. 6.124 ..
1.4.d:
चिरेण मंत्रं संधीयाच्चिरेम च कृतं त्यजेत्..
चिरेण विहतं मित्रं चिरं धारणमर्हति.. 6.124 ..
1.4.m: 'One should deliberate upon counsel slowly; what is done slowly one should abandon [slowly]. / A friend injured slowly deserves to be maintained for a long time.

1.4.s:
roge darpe ca māne ca drohe pāpe ca karmaṇi..
apriye caiva kartavye cirakārī praśasyate.. 6.125 ..
1.4.d:
रोगे दर्पे च माने च द्रोहे पापे च कर्मणि..
अप्रिये चैव कर्तव्ये चिरकारी प्रशस्यते.. 6.125 ..
1.4.m: In disease, in arrogance, in pride, in treachery, and in sinful deeds, / and when an unpleasant duty must be done, one who acts slowly is praised.

1.4.s:
baṃdhūnāṃ suhṛdāṃ caiva bhṛtyānāṃ strījanasya ca..
avyakteṣvaparādheṣu cirakārī praśasyate.. 6.126 ..
1.4.d:
बंधूनां सुहृदां चैव भृत्यानां स्त्रीजनस्य च..
अव्यक्तेष्वपराधेषु चिरकारी प्रशस्यते.. 6.126 ..
1.4.m: Towards relatives, friends, servants, and womenfolk, / when offenses are unmanifest, one who acts slowly is praised.

1.4.s:
ciraṃ dharmānniṣeveta kuryāccānveṣaṇaṃ ciram..
ciramanvāsya viduṣaściramiṣṭānupāsya ca.. 6.127 ..
1.4.d:
चिरं धर्मान्निषेवेत कुर्याच्चान्वेषणं चिरम्..
चिरमन्वास्य विदुषश्चिरमिष्टानुपास्य च.. 6.127 ..
1.4.m: One should practice virtues for a long time; one should investigate for a long time; / having attended upon the learned for a long time, and having waited upon cherished ones for a long time,

1.4.s:
ciraṃ vinīya cātmānaṃ ciraṃ yātyanavajñatām..
bruvataśca parasyāpi vākyaṃ dharmopasaṃhitam.. 6.128 ..
1.4.d:
चिरं विनीय चात्मानं चिरं यात्यनवज्ञताम्..
ब्रुवतश्च परस्यापि वाक्यं धर्मोपसंहितम्.. 6.128 ..
1.4.m: and having disciplined oneself for a long time, one long escapes disregard. / And when another speaks words joined with righteousness,

1.4.s:
ciraṃ pṛcchecca śrṛṇuyācciraṃ na paribhūyate..
dharme śatrau śastrahaste pātre ca nikaṭasthite.. 6.129 ..
1.4.d:
चिरं पृच्छेच्च श्रृणुयाच्चिरं न परिभूयते..
धर्मे शत्रौ शस्त्रहस्ते पात्रे च निकटस्थिते.. 6.129 ..
1.4.m: one should inquire for a long time and listen for a long time; one is not long humiliated. / But in righteousness, against an enemy, when a weapon is in hand, and when a worthy recipient is at hand,

1.4.s:
bhaye ca sādhupūjāyāṃ cirakārī na śasyate..
evamuktvā putrabhāryāsahitaḥ prāpya cāśramam.. 6.130 ..
1.4.d:
भये च साधुपूजायां चिरकारी न शस्यते..
एवमुक्त्वा पुत्रभार्यासहितः प्राप्य चाश्रमम्.. 6.130 ..
1.4.m: in danger, and in the worship of the virtuous, one who acts slowly is not praised.' / Having spoken thus, accompanied by his son and wife, he reached the hermitage.

1.4.s:
tataściramupāsyātha divaṃ yātiściraṃ muniḥ..
vayaṃ tvevaṃ bruvanto'pi mohenaivaṃ pratāritāḥ.. 6.131 ..
1.4.d:
ततश्चिरमुपास्याथ दिवं यातिश्चिरं मुनिः..
वयं त्वेवं ब्रुवन्तोऽपि मोहेनैवं प्रतारिताः.. 6.131 ..
1.4.m: Then, having worshipped for a long time, the sage went to heaven forever. / Yet we, though speaking thus, were deceived by delusion.

1.4.s:
kalau ca bhavatāṃ viprā macchāpo nipatiṣyati..
kecitsadā bhaviṣyaṃti viprāḥ sarvaguṇairyutāḥ.. 6.132 ..
1.4.d:
कलौ च भवतां विप्रा मच्छापो निपतिष्यति..
केचित्सदा भविष्यंति विप्राः सर्वगुणैर्युताः.. 6.132 ..
1.4.m: And in the Kali age, O brahmins, my curse will fall upon you; / [only] some brahmins will always remain endowed with all virtues.

1.4.s:
pādaprakṣālanaṃ kṛtvā tato'haṃ dharmavarmaṇaḥ..
samīpe sākṣiṇo devānkṛtvā saṃkalpamācaram.. 6.133 ..
1.4.d:
पादप्रक्षालनं कृत्वा ततोऽहं धर्मवर्मणः..
समीपे साक्षिणो देवान्कृत्वा संकल्पमाचरम्.. 6.133 ..
1.4.m: Then, having washed the feet of Dharmavarman, / and making the gods witnesses in his presence, I made the solemn resolve.

1.4.s:
kāṃcanairarnopradānaiśca gṛhadānairdhanādibhiḥ..
bhāryābhūṣaṇavastraiśca kṛtārthā brāhmaṇāḥ kṛtāḥ.. 6.134 ..
1.4.d:
कांचनैरर्नोप्रदानैश्च गृहदानैर्धनादिभिः..
भार्याभूषणवस्त्रैश्च कृतार्था ब्राह्मणाः कृताः.. 6.134 ..
1.4.m: By gifts of gold and food, by gifts of houses, wealth, and the like, / and with ornaments and garments for wives, the brahmins were made content.

1.4.s:
tataḥ karaṃ samudyamya prāhendro devasaṃgame..
harāṃgaruddhavāmārddha yāvaddevī gireḥ sutā.. 6.135 ..
1.4.d:
ततः करं समुद्यम्य प्राहेन्द्रो देवसंगमे..
हरांगरुद्धवामार्द्ध यावद्देवी गिरेः सुता.. 6.135 ..
1.4.m: Then Indra raised his hand and spoke in the assembly of the gods: / 'As long as the goddess, daughter of the mountain, occupies the left half of Hara's body,

1.4.s:
gaṇādhīśo vayaṃ yāvadyāvattribhuvanaṃ tvidam..
tāvannandyādide sthānaṃ nāradasthāpitaṃ surāḥ.. 6.136 ..
1.4.d:
गणाधीशो वयं यावद्यावत्त्रिभुवनं त्विदम्..
तावन्नन्द्यादिदे स्थानं नारदस्थापितं सुराः.. 6.136 ..
1.4.m: as long as the lord of the gaṇas and we remain, as long as these three worlds endure, / so long, O gods, this place established by Nārada [shall remain], beginning with Nandyā.

1.4.s:
brahmaśāpo rudraśāpo viṣṇuśāpastathaiva ca..
dvijaśāpastathā bhūyādidaṃ sthānaṃ viluṃpataḥ.. 6.137 ..
1.4.d:
ब्रह्मशापो रुद्रशापो विष्णुशापस्तथैव च..
द्विजशापस्तथा भूयादिदं स्थानं विलुंपतः.. 6.137 ..
1.4.m: May the curse of Brahmā, the curse of Rudra, and likewise the curse of Viṣṇu, / as well as the curse of brahmins fall upon whoever plunders this sacred place!'

1.4.s:
tatastatheti taiḥ sarvairhṛṣṭaistatra tathoditam..
evaṃ mayā sthāpite sthānake'sminsaṃsthāpayāmāsa ca kāpilaṃ muniḥ..
sthāne ubhe devakṛte prasannāstato yayurdevatā devasadma.. 6.138 ..
iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ prathame māheśvarakhaṇḍe kaumārikākhaṃḍe nārīyasthānapratiṣṭhāvarṇanaṃnāma ṣaṣṭho'dhyāyaḥ 6 .. cha ..
1.4.d:
ततस्तथेति तैः सर्वैर्हृष्टैस्तत्र तथोदितम्..
एवं मया स्थापिते स्थानकेऽस्मिन्संस्थापयामास च कापिलं मुनिः..
स्थाने उभे देवकृते प्रसन्नास्ततो ययुर्देवता देवसद्म.. 6.138 ..
इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां प्रथमे माहेश्वरखण्डे कौमारिकाखंडे नारीयस्थानप्रतिष्ठावर्णनंनाम षष्ठोऽध्यायः 6 .. छ ..
1.4.m:
Then, 'So be it!' was uttered by all of them delighted there. / In this sacred place thus established by me, the sage also established Kāpila; / both places having been created by the gods, the deities, well-pleased, then departed to the abode of the gods.
Thus ends the sixth chapter, named 'Description of the Consecration of the Sacred Place of the Women', in the Kaumārikākhaṇḍa of the first [section], the Māheśvarakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa of eighty-one thousand verses.

1.4.s:
.. arjuna uvāca..
mahīsāgaramāhātmyamadbhutaṃ kīrtitaṃ tvayā..
vismayaḥ paramo mahyaṃ praharṣaścopajāyate.. 7.1 ..
1.4.d:
.. अर्जुन उवाच..
महीसागरमाहात्म्यमद्भुतं कीर्तितं त्वया..
विस्मयः परमो मह्यं प्रहर्षश्चोपजायते.. 7.1 ..
1.4.m: Arjuna said: / The wonderful māhātmya of Mahīsāgara has been proclaimed by you; / the greatest wonder and delight have arisen in me.

1.4.s:
tadahaṃ vistarācchrotumidamicchāmi nārada..
kasya yajñe mahī glānā vahnitāpābhitāpitā.. 7.2 ..
1.4.d:
तदहं विस्तराच्छ्रोतुमिदमिच्छामि नारद..
कस्य यज्ञे मही ग्लाना वह्नितापाभितापिता.. 7.2 ..
1.4.m: Therefore I wish to hear this in detail, O Nārada: / at whose sacrificial session was the earth exhausted, scorched by the heat of the fire?

1.4.s:
..nārada uvāca..
mahādākhyānamākhyāsye yathā jātā mahīnadī..
śrṛṇvannetāṃ kathāṃ puṇyāṃ puṇyamāpsyasi pāṃḍava.. 7.3 ..
1.4.d:
..नारद उवाच..
महादाख्यानमाख्यास्ये यथा जाता महीनदी..
श्रृण्वन्नेतां कथां पुण्यां पुण्यमाप्स्यसि पांडव.. 7.3 ..
1.4.m: Nārada said: / I shall narrate the great account of how the river Mahī was born; / hearing this sacred tale, O descendant of Pāṇḍu, you will attain merit.

1.4.s:
purābhūdbhūpatirbhūmāvindradyumna iti śrutaḥ..
vadānyaḥ sarvadharmajño mānyo mānayitā prabhuḥ.. 7.4 ..
1.4.d:
पुराभूद्भूपतिर्भूमाविन्द्रद्युम्न इति श्रुतः..
वदान्यः सर्वधर्मज्ञो मान्यो मानयिता प्रभुः.. 7.4 ..
1.4.m: Formerly on earth there was a king known as Indradyumna, / generous, knowing all righteousness, venerable, one who honors others, a mighty lord,

1.4.s:
ucitajño vivekasya nivāso guṇasāgaraḥ..
na tadasti dharāpṛṣṭhe nagaraṃ grāmapattanam.. 7.5 ..
1.4.d:
उचितज्ञो विवेकस्य निवासो गुणसागरः..
न तदस्ति धरापृष्ठे नगरं ग्रामपत्तनम्.. 7.5 ..
1.4.m: knowing what is fitting, an abode of discernment, an ocean of virtues. / There was no town, village, or city on the face of the earth

1.4.s:
tadīyapūrtadharmasya cihnena na yadaṃkitam..
kanyādānāni bahudhā brāhmeṇa vidhinā vyadhāt.. 7.6 ..
1.4.d:
तदीयपूर्तधर्मस्य चिह्नेन न यदंकितम्..
कन्यादानानि बहुधा ब्राह्मेण विधिना व्यधात्.. 7.6 ..
1.4.m: that was not marked by the emblem of his pious works of public welfare. / He performed gifts of maidens in marriage in many ways according to the rite of Brahmā.

1.4.s:
bhūpālo'sau dadau dānamāsahasrāddhanārthinām..
daśamīdivase rātrau gajapṛṣṭhena dundubhiḥ.. 7.7 ..
1.4.d:
भूपालोऽसौ ददौ दानमासहस्राद्धनार्थिनाम्..
दशमीदिवसे रात्रौ गजपृष्ठेन दुन्दुभिः.. 7.7 ..
1.4.m: That king gave gifts up to thousands to those seeking wealth. / On the night of the tenth day, upon an elephant's back, a drum

1.4.s:
tāḍyate tatpure prātaḥ kāryamekādaśīvratam..
yajvanā tena bhūpena vicchinnaṃ somapāyinām.. 7.8 ..
1.4.d:
ताड्यते तत्पुरे प्रातः कार्यमेकादशीव्रतम्..
यज्वना तेन भूपेन विच्छिन्नं सोमपायिनाम्.. 7.8 ..
1.4.m: was beaten in his city: 'The observance of Ekādaśī is to be performed at dawn!' / By that king, a performer of sacrifices, [the offering] of soma-drinkers was never interrupted.

1.4.s:
svaraṇairāstṛtā darbhairdvyaṃgulotsedhitā mahī..
gaṃgāyāṃ sikatā dhārā varṣato divi tārakāḥ.. 7.9 ..
1.4.d:
स्वरणैरास्तृता दर्भैर्द्व्यंगुलोत्सेधिता मही..
गंगायां सिकता धारा वर्षतो दिवि तारकाः.. 7.9 ..
1.4.m: The earth was strewn with sacrificial darbha-grass raised two finger-breadths high. / The sands in the Gaṅgā, the raindrops falling from a shower, and the stars in the sky

1.4.s:
śakyā gaṇayituṃ prājñaistadīyaṃ sukṛtaṃ na tu..
īdṛśaiḥ sukṛtaireṣa tenaiva vapuṣā nṛpaḥ.. 7.10 ..
1.4.d:
शक्या गणयितुं प्राज्ञैस्तदीयं सुकृतं न तु..
ईदृशैः सुकृतैरेष तेनैव वपुषा नृपः.. 7.10 ..
1.4.m: might be counted by the wise, but his good deeds could not be. / By such good deeds, in that very physical body, that king

1.4.s:
dhāma prajāpateḥ prāpto vimānena kurūdvaha..
bubhuje sa tadā bhogāndurlabhānamarairapi.. 7.11 ..
1.4.d:
धाम प्रजापतेः प्राप्तो विमानेन कुरूद्वह..
बुभुजे स तदा भोगान्दुर्लभानमरैरपि.. 7.11 ..
1.4.m: reached the realm of Prajāpati in an aerial chariot, O best of the Kurus. / He then enjoyed pleasures hard to attain even for the immortals.

1.4.s:
atha kalpaśatasyāṃte vyatīte taṃ mahīpatim..
prāha prajāpatiḥ sevāvasarāyātamātmanaḥ.. 7.12 ..
1.4.d:
अथ कल्पशतस्यांते व्यतीते तं महीपतिम्..
प्राह प्रजापतिः सेवावसरायातमात्मनः.. 7.12 ..
1.4.m: Then, at the end of a hundred kalpas, when they had passed, Prajāpati said / to that king who had come for the occasion of attending upon him:

1.4.s:
..brahmovāca..
iṃdradyumna drutaṃ gaccha dharāpṛṣṭhaṃ nṛpottama..
na stātavyaṃ madīyedya loke kṣaṇamapi tvayā.. 7.13 ..
1.4.d:
..ब्रह्मोवाच..
इंद्रद्युम्न द्रुतं गच्छ धरापृष्ठं नृपोत्तम..
न स्तातव्यं मदीयेद्य लोके क्षणमपि त्वया.. 7.13 ..
1.4.m: Brahmā said: / 'O Indradyumna, best of kings, go quickly to the surface of the earth! / Today you must not remain even for a moment in my world.'

1.4.s:
..iṃdradyumna uvāca..
kasmādbrahmannito bhūmau māṃ preṣayasi samprati..
sati puṇye madīye tu bahule vada kāraṇam.. 7.14 ..
1.4.d:
..इंद्रद्युम्न उवाच..
कस्माद्ब्रह्मन्नितो भूमौ मां प्रेषयसि सम्प्रति..
सति पुण्ये मदीये तु बहुले वद कारणम्.. 7.14 ..
1.4.m: Indradyumna said: / 'Why, O Brahmā, do you send me now from here to earth, / when my merit is abundant? Tell me the reason!'

1.4.s:
..brahmovāca..
na puṇyaṃ kevalaṃ rājanguptaṃ svargasya sādhakam..
vinā niṣkalmaṣāṃ kīrti trilokītalavistṛtām.. 7.15 ..
1.4.d:
..ब्रह्मोवाच..
न पुण्यं केवलं राजन्गुप्तं स्वर्गस्य साधकम्..
विना निष्कल्मषां कीर्ति त्रिलोकीतलविस्तृताम्.. 7.15 ..
1.4.m: Brahmā said: / 'Merit alone, kept hidden, does not accomplish heaven, O king, / without spotless fame spread over the surface of the three worlds.

1.4.s:
tava kīrtisamucchedaḥ sāṃprataṃ vasudhātale..
saṃjātaścirakālena gatvā tāṃ kuru nūtanām.. 7.16 ..
1.4.d:
तव कीर्तिसमुच्छेदः सांप्रतं वसुधातले..
संजातश्चिरकालेन गत्वा तां कुरु नूतनाम्.. 7.16 ..
1.4.m: The extinction of your fame on the surface of the earth / has now occurred due to the long lapse of time; go and make it fresh,

1.4.s: yadi vāṃchā mahīpāla mama dhāmani saṃsthitau.. 7.17 ..
1.4.d: यदि वांछा महीपाल मम धामनि संस्थितौ.. 7.17 ..
1.4.m: if you desire, O king, to remain in my abode.'

1.4.s:
..indradyumna uvāca..
madīyaṃ sukṛtaṃ brahmankathaṃ bhūmau bhavediti..
kiṃ kartavyaṃ mayā naitanmama cetasi tiṣṭhati.. 7.18 ..
1.4.d:
..इन्द्रद्युम्न उवाच..
मदीयं सुकृतं ब्रह्मन्कथं भूमौ भवेदिति..
किं कर्तव्यं मया नैतन्मम चेतसि तिष्ठति.. 7.18 ..
1.4.m: Indradyumna said: / 'How, O Brahmā, can my good deeds still exist on earth? / What must I do? This does not occur to my mind.'

1.4.s:
..brahmovāca..
balavāneṣa bhūpāla kālaḥ kalayati svayam.. 7.19 ..
1.4.d:
..ब्रह्मोवाच..
बलवानेष भूपाल कालः कलयति स्वयम्.. 7.19 ..
1.4.m: Brahmā said: / 'Powerful is this Time, O king, which impels [all things] itself.

1.4.s:
brahmāṃḍānyapi māṃ caiva gaṇanā kā bhavādṛśām..
tadetadeva manye'haṃ tava bhūpāla sāṃpratam.. 7.20 ..
1.4.d:
ब्रह्मांडान्यपि मां चैव गणना का भवादृशाम्..
तदेतदेव मन्येऽहं तव भूपाल सांप्रतम्.. 7.20 ..
1.4.m: It [destroys] even the cosmic eggs and me; what reckoning is there of those like you? / Therefore, O king, I consider this alone [best] for you now:

1.4.s:
yatkīrtimātmano vyaktiṃ nītvābhyehi punardivam..
śuśruvāniti vācaṃ sa brahmaṇaḥ pṛthivīpatiḥ.. 7.21 ..
1.4.d:
यत्कीर्तिमात्मनो व्यक्तिं नीत्वाभ्येहि पुनर्दिवम्..
शुश्रुवानिति वाचं स ब्रह्मणः पृथिवीपतिः.. 7.21 ..
1.4.m: bring your own fame to manifestation, and then return to heaven.' / Having heard these words of Brahmā, that lord of the earth

1.4.s:
paśyatisma tathātmānaṃ mahītalamupāgatam..
kāṃpilyanagare bhūyaḥ papracchātmānamātmanā.. 7.22 ..
1.4.d:
पश्यतिस्म तथात्मानं महीतलमुपागतम्..
कांपिल्यनगरे भूयः पप्रच्छात्मानमात्मना.. 7.22 ..
1.4.m: saw himself thus arrived at the surface of the earth. / In the city of Kāmpilya, he again questioned himself within himself.

1.4.s:
nagaraṃ sa tadā deśamaprākṣīditi vismitaḥ..
..janā ūcuḥ..
na jānīmo vayaṃ bhūpamiṃdradyumnaṃ na tatpuram.. 7.23 ..
1.4.d:
नगरं स तदा देशमप्राक्षीदिति विस्मितः..
..जना ऊचुः..
न जानीमो वयं भूपमिंद्रद्युम्नं न तत्पुरम्.. 7.23 ..
1.4.m: Then, astonished, he questioned [the people about] the city and the land. / The people said: / 'We do not know King Indradyumna, nor his city.'

1.4.s:
yattvaṃ pṛcchasi bho bhadra kañcitpṛccha cirāyuṣam..
..indradyumna uvāca..
kaḥ saṃprati dharāpṛṣṭhe cirāyuḥ prathito janāḥ.. 7.24 ..
1.4.d:
यत्त्वं पृच्छसि भो भद्र कञ्चित्पृच्छ चिरायुषम्..
..इन्द्रद्युम्न उवाच..
कः संप्रति धरापृष्ठे चिरायुः प्रथितो जनाः.. 7.24 ..
1.4.m: "Regarding what you ask, good sir, ask someone who is long-lived." / Indradyumna said: / "Who, O people, is known to be long-lived on the surface of the earth right now, 7.24

1.4.s:
pṛthivījayarājyesminyatra prabūta mā ciram..
..janā ūcuḥ..
śrūyate naimiṣāraṇye saptakalpasmaro muniḥ.. 7.25 ..
1.4.d:
पृथिवीजयराज्येस्मिन्यत्र प्रबूत मा चिरम्..
..जना ऊचुः..
श्रूयते नैमिषारण्ये सप्तकल्पस्मरो मुनिः.. 7.25 ..
1.4.m: in this kingdom victorious over the earth, where he may have lived? Speak without delay!" / The people said: / "It is heard that in the Naimiṣāraṇya there is a sage who remembers seven cosmic ages, 7.25

1.4.s:
mārkaṃḍeya iti khyātastaṃ gatvā pṛccha saṃśayam..
tathopadiṣṭastairgatvā tatra taṃ munipuṃgavam.. 7.26 ..
1.4.d:
मार्कंडेय इति ख्यातस्तं गत्वा पृच्छ संशयम्..
तथोपदिष्टस्तैर्गत्वा तत्र तं मुनिपुंगवम्.. 7.26 ..
1.4.m: known as Mārkaṇḍeya. Go and ask him your doubt." / Having been thus advised by them, he went there to that bull among sages. 7.26

1.4.s:
niśamya praṇipatyāha nṛpaḥ svahṛdayasthitam..
..iṃdradyumna uvāca..
cirāyurbhagavānbhūmau viśrutaḥ sāṃprataṃ tataḥ.. 7.27 ..
1.4.d:
निशम्य प्रणिपत्याह नृपः स्वहृदयस्थितम्..
..इंद्रद्युम्न उवाच..
चिरायुर्भगवान्भूमौ विश्रुतः सांप्रतं ततः.. 7.27 ..
1.4.m: Having listened and bowed down, the king stated what was in his heart: / Indradyumna said: / "The venerable one is celebrated on earth as long-lived; therefore now 7.27

1.4.s: pṛcchāmyahaṃ bhavānvetti iṃdradyumnaṃ nṛpaṃ na vā.. 7.28 ..
1.4.d: पृच्छाम्यहं भवान्वेत्ति इंद्रद्युम्नं नृपं न वा.. 7.28 ..
1.4.m: I ask: Do you know King Indradyumna or not?" 7.28

1.4.s:
..śrīmārkaṃḍeya uvāca..
saptakalpāntare nābhūtkopīṃdradyumnasaṃjñitaḥ..
bhūpāla kimahaṃ vacmi tavānyatpṛccha saṃśayam.. 7.29 ..
1.4.d:
..श्रीमार्कंडेय उवाच..
सप्तकल्पान्तरे नाभूत्कोपींद्रद्युम्नसंज्ञितः..
भूपाल किमहं वच्मि तवान्यत्पृच्छ संशयम्.. 7.29 ..
1.4.m: The venerable Mārkaṇḍeya said: / "In the interval of seven cosmic ages there has been no one named Indradyumna. / What can I say, O king? Ask me another doubt of yours." 7.29

1.4.s:
sa nirāśastadākarṇya vaco bhūpognisādhane..
samudyogaṃ tadā cakre taṃ dṛṣṭvāha tadā muniḥ.. 7.30 ..
1.4.d:
स निराशस्तदाकर्ण्य वचो भूपोग्निसाधने..
समुद्योगं तदा चक्रे तं दृष्ट्वाह तदा मुनिः.. 7.30 ..
1.4.m: Hearing his words, the king, then despairing, / made preparation to commit [himself to] fire. Seeing him, the sage then said: 7.30

1.4.s:
..mārkaṃḍeya uvāca..
mā sāhasamidaṃ kārṣīrbhadra vācaṃ śrṛṇuṣva me..
eti jīvaṃtamānaṃdo naraṃ varṣaśatādapi.. 7.31 ..
1.4.d:
..मार्कंडेय उवाच..
मा साहसमिदं कार्षीर्भद्र वाचं श्रृणुष्व मे..
एति जीवंतमानंदो नरं वर्षशतादपि.. 7.31 ..
1.4.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / "Do not commit this rash act, good sir! Listen to my words: / 'Joy comes to a living person even after a hundred years.' 7.31

1.4.s:
tatkaromi pratīkāraṃ tava duḥkhopaśāṃtaye..
śrṛṇu bhadra mamāstīha bako mitraṃ ciraṃtanaḥ.. 7.32 ..
1.4.d:
तत्करोमि प्रतीकारं तव दुःखोपशांतये..
श्रृणु भद्र ममास्तीह बको मित्रं चिरंतनः.. 7.32 ..
1.4.m: Therefore I will provide a remedy to appease your grief. / Listen, good sir: I have here an ancient friend, a crane, 7.32

1.4.s:
nāḍījaṃgha iti khyātaḥ sa tvā jñāsyatyasaṃśayam..
tasmādehi drutaṃ yāvadāvāṃ tatra vrajāvahe.. 7.33 ..
1.4.d:
नाडीजंघ इति ख्यातः स त्वा ज्ञास्यत्यसंशयम्..
तस्मादेहि द्रुतं यावदावां तत्र व्रजावहे.. 7.33 ..
1.4.m: known as Nāḍījaṅgha; he will undoubtedly know you. / Therefore come quickly, so that the two of us may go there. 7.33

1.4.s:
paropakāraikaphalaṃ jīvitaṃ hi mahātmanām..
yadi jñāsyatyasaṃdigdhamiṃdradyumnaṃ sa vakṣyati.. 7.34 ..
1.4.d:
परोपकारैकफलं जीवितं हि महात्मनाम्..
यदि ज्ञास्यत्यसंदिग्धमिंद्रद्युम्नं स वक्ष्यति.. 7.34 ..
1.4.m: For the life of great-souled men has doing good to others as its sole fruit. / If he knows, he will surely speak of Indradyumna." 7.34

1.4.s:
tau prasthitāviti tadā vipreṃdranṛpapuṃgavau..
himācalaṃ prati prītau nāḍījaṃghālayaṃ prati.. 7.35 ..
1.4.d:
तौ प्रस्थिताविति तदा विप्रेंद्रनृपपुंगवौ..
हिमाचलं प्रति प्रीतौ नाडीजंघालयं प्रति.. 7.35 ..
1.4.m: Thus both of them set out, that eminent brahmin and the best of kings, / delighted, toward the Himālayas, toward Nāḍījaṅgha's dwelling. 7.35

1.4.s:
bako'tha mitraṃ svaṃ vīkṣya cirakālādupāgatam..
mārkaṃḍeyaṃ yayau prītyutkaṃṭhitaḥ sammukhaṃ dvijaiḥ.. 7.36 ..
1.4.d:
बकोऽथ मित्रं स्वं वीक्ष्य चिरकालादुपागतम्..
मार्कंडेयं ययौ प्रीत्युत्कंठितः सम्मुखं द्विजैः.. 7.36 ..
1.4.m: Then the crane, seeing his friend Mārkaṇḍeya arrived after a long time, / approached him eagerly and affectionately, along with the brahmins. 7.36

1.4.s:
kṛtasaṃvidabhūtpūrvaṃ kuśalasvāgatādinā..
papracchānaṃtaraṃ kāryaṃ vadāgamanakāraṇam.. 7.37 ..
1.4.d:
कृतसंविदभूत्पूर्वं कुशलस्वागतादिना..
पप्रच्छानंतरं कार्यं वदागमनकारणम्.. 7.37 ..
1.4.m: Mutual greetings took place first, with enquiries of welfare, welcome, and the like. / Thereupon he asked the business: "State the cause of your arrival!" 7.37

1.4.s:
mārkaṃḍeyotha taṃ prāha bakaṃ prastutamīpsitam..
iṃdradyumnaṃ bhavānvetti bhūpālaṃ pṛthivītale.. 7.38 ..
1.4.d:
मार्कंडेयोथ तं प्राह बकं प्रस्तुतमीप्सितम्..
इंद्रद्युम्नं भवान्वेत्ति भूपालं पृथिवीतले.. 7.38 ..
1.4.m: Then Mārkaṇḍeya spoke to that crane the desired subject at hand: / "Do you know King Indradyumna on the surface of the earth? 7.38

1.4.s:
etasya mama mitrasya tena jñātena kāraṇam..
no vāyaṃ tyajati prāṇānpurā vahnipraveśanāt.. 7.39 ..
1.4.d:
एतस्य मम मित्रस्य तेन ज्ञातेन कारणम्..
नो वायं त्यजति प्राणान्पुरा वह्निप्रवेशनात्.. 7.39 ..
1.4.m: By knowing this, this friend of mine has his purpose [fulfilled]; / otherwise, he will abandon his life-breaths before entering the fire. 7.39

1.4.s: etasya prāṇarakṣārthaṃ brūhi jānāsi cennṛpam.. 7.40 ..
1.4.d: एतस्य प्राणरक्षार्थं ब्रूहि जानासि चेन्नृपम्.. 7.40 ..
1.4.m: For the sake of saving his life, speak if you know the king!" 7.40

1.4.s:
..naḍījaṃgha uvāca..
caturdaśa smarāmyasmi kalpānvipreṃdra sāṃpratam..
āstāṃ taddarśanaṃ vārtāmapi vā na smarāmyaham.. 7.41 ..
1.4.d:
..नडीजंघ उवाच..
चतुर्दश स्मराम्यस्मि कल्पान्विप्रेंद्र सांप्रतम्..
आस्तां तद्दर्शनं वार्तामपि वा न स्मराम्यहम्.. 7.41 ..
1.4.m: Nāḍījaṅgha said: / "I now remember fourteen cosmic ages, O eminent brahmin; / let alone seeing him, I do not even remember hearing report of him! 7.41

1.4.s:
iṃdradyumno mahīpālaḥ ko'pi nāsīnmahītale..
etāvanmātramevāhaṃ jānāmi dvijapuṃgava.. 7.42 ..
1.4.d:
इंद्रद्युम्नो महीपालः कोऽपि नासीन्महीतले..
एतावन्मात्रमेवाहं जानामि द्विजपुंगव.. 7.42 ..
1.4.m: There was no king whatsoever named Indradyumna on the face of the earth. / This much alone do I know, O bull among brahmins." 7.42

1.4.s:
..nārada uvāca..
tataḥ sa vismayāviṣṭastasyāyuriti śuśruvān..
papraccha rājā ko heturdānasya tapaso'tha vā..
yadāyurīdṛśaṃ dīrghaṃ saṃjātamiti vismitaḥ.. 7.43 ..
1.4.d:
..नारद उवाच..
ततः स विस्मयाविष्टस्तस्यायुरिति शुश्रुवान्..
पप्रच्छ राजा को हेतुर्दानस्य तपसोऽथ वा..
यदायुरीदृशं दीर्घं संजातमिति विस्मितः.. 7.43 ..
1.4.m: Nārada said: / Then, filled with astonishment upon hearing of his lifespan, / the king, bewildered, asked: "What was the cause, whether gift or austerity, / by which such a long lifespan came about?" 7.43

1.4.s:
..nāḍījaṃgha uvāca..
ghṛtakaṃbalamāhātmyānmama devasya śūlinaḥ..
dīrghamāyuridaṃ vipra śāpādbakavapuḥ śrṛṇu.. 7.44 ..
1.4.d:
..नाडीजंघ उवाच..
घृतकंबलमाहात्म्यान्मम देवस्य शूलिनः..
दीर्घमायुरिदं विप्र शापाद्बकवपुः श्रृणु.. 7.44 ..
1.4.m: Nāḍījaṅgha said: / "O brahmin, by the power of the ghee-blanket for my Lord who holds the trident / is this long life; hear how by a curse I gained the body of a crane: 7.44

1.4.s:
purā janmanyahaṃ bālo brāhmaṇasyābhavaṃ bhuvi..
pārāśaryasagotrasya viśvarūpasya sanmuneḥ.. 7.45 ..
1.4.d:
पुरा जन्मन्यहं बालो ब्राह्मणस्याभवं भुवि..
पाराशर्यसगोत्रस्य विश्वरूपस्य सन्मुनेः.. 7.45 ..
1.4.m: In a previous life I was a boy on earth, [the son] of a brahmin, / the virtuous sage Viśvarūpa, belonging to the lineage of Parāśara. 7.45

1.4.s:
bālako baka ityevaṃ pratīto'tipriyaḥ pituḥ..
capalo'tīva bālatve nisargādeva bhadraka.. 7.46 ..
1.4.d:
बालको बक इत्येवं प्रतीतोऽतिप्रियः पितुः..
चपलोऽतीव बालत्वे निसर्गादेव भद्रक.. 7.46 ..
1.4.m: As a boy, known indeed as Baka, I was very dear to my father, / but exceedingly fickle in childhood, by my very nature, good sir. 7.46

1.4.s:
atha mārakataṃ liṃgaṃ devatāvasarātpituḥ..
cāpalyādvālabhāvāccāpahṛtya nihitaṃ mayā.. 7.47 ..
1.4.d:
अथ मारकतं लिंगं देवतावसरात्पितुः..
चापल्याद्वालभावाच्चापहृत्य निहितं मया.. 7.47 ..
1.4.m: Then, during my father's worship of the deity, out of childishness and fickleness, / taking away the emerald liṅga, I placed it 7.47

1.4.s:
ghṛtasya kuṃbhe saṃkrāṃtau makarasyottarāyaṇe..
atha prātarvyatītāyāṃ niśi yāvatpitā mama.. 7.48 ..
1.4.d:
घृतस्य कुंभे संक्रांतौ मकरस्योत्तरायणे..
अथ प्रातर्व्यतीतायां निशि यावत्पिता मम.. 7.48 ..
1.4.m: into a pot of ghee on the Makarasaṃkrānti, during the northern course of the sun. / Then, when the morning arrived after the night had passed, as my father 7.48

1.4.s:
nirmālyāpanayaṃ cakre tāvacchūnyaṃ śivālayam..
niśamya kāṃdiśīko māṃ papraccha madhurasvaram.. 7.49 ..
1.4.d:
निर्माल्यापनयं चक्रे तावच्छून्यं शिवालयम्..
निशम्य कांदिशीको मां पप्रच्छ मधुरस्वरम्.. 7.49 ..
1.4.m: removed the previous day's floral offerings, the abode of Śiva was empty. / Perplexed, upon seeing [this], he asked me in a gentle voice: 7.49

1.4.s:
vatsa kva nu tvayā liṃgaṃ nūnaṃ vinihitaṃ vada..
dāsyāmi vāṃchitaṃ yatte bhakṣyamanyattavepsitam.. 7.50 ..
1.4.d:
वत्स क्व नु त्वया लिंगं नूनं विनिहितं वद..
दास्यामि वांछितं यत्ते भक्ष्यमन्यत्तवेप्सितम्.. 7.50 ..
1.4.m: "My child, where indeed have you placed the liṅga? Speak! / I will give you whatever you desire—food or whatever else you wish." 7.50

1.4.s:
tato mayā bālabhāvādbhakṣyalubdhena tatpituḥ..
ghṛtakuṃbhāṃtarākṛṣya bhadraliṃgaṃ samarpitam.. 7.51 ..
1.4.d:
ततो मया बालभावाद्भक्ष्यलुब्धेन तत्पितुः..
घृतकुंभांतराकृष्य भद्रलिंगं समर्पितम्.. 7.51 ..
1.4.m: Then, out of childishness, greedy for the food, / I pulled out the auspicious liṅga from within the pot of ghee and gave it to my father. 7.51

1.4.s:
atha kāle tu saṃprāpte pramīto'haṃ nṛpālaye..
jāto jātismārastāvadānartādhipateḥ sutaḥ.. 7.52 ..
1.4.d:
अथ काले तु संप्राप्ते प्रमीतोऽहं नृपालये..
जातो जातिस्मारस्तावदानर्ताधिपतेः सुतः.. 7.52 ..
1.4.m: Then, when the time came, I died and was born in a king's palace, / remembering my previous births, as the son of the ruler of Ānarta. 7.52

1.4.s:
ghṛtakaṃbalamāhātmyānmakarasthe divākare..
api bālyādavajñānātsaṃyogād‌ghṛtaliṃgayoḥ.. 7.53 ..
1.4.d:
घृतकंबलमाहात्म्यान्मकरस्थे दिवाकरे..
अपि बाल्यादवज्ञानात्संयोगाद्‌घृतलिंगयोः.. 7.53 ..
1.4.m: By the power of the ghee-blanket when the sun was in Capricorn, / even though done in childhood, through disregard, by the contact of the ghee and the liṅga, 7.53

1.4.s:
tataḥ saṃsthāpitaṃ liṃgaṃ prāgjanma smaratā mayā..
tataḥ prabhṛti liṃgāni ghṛtenācchādayāmyaham.. 7.54 ..
1.4.d:
ततः संस्थापितं लिंगं प्राग्जन्म स्मरता मया..
ततः प्रभृति लिंगानि घृतेनाच्छादयाम्यहम्.. 7.54 ..
1.4.m: I, remembering my previous birth, then installed a liṅga; / from that time on, I covered liṅgas with ghee. 7.54

1.4.s:
pitṛpaitāmahaṃ prāpya rājyaṃ śaktyanurūpataḥ..
tataḥ prasanno bhagavānpārvatīpatirāha mām.. 7.55 ..
1.4.d:
पितृपैतामहं प्राप्य राज्यं शक्त्यनुरूपतः..
ततः प्रसन्नो भगवान्पार्वतीपतिराह माम्.. 7.55 ..
1.4.m: Having obtained the ancestral kingdom, according to my ability, / the Lord, the husband of Pārvatī, being pleased, said to me: 7.55

1.4.s:
pūrvajanmani tuṣṭo'haṃ ghṛtakaṃbalapūjayā..
prayacchāmyasmi ta rājyamadhunābhimataṃ vṛṇu.. 7.56 ..
1.4.d:
पूर्वजन्मनि तुष्टोऽहं घृतकंबलपूजया..
प्रयच्छाम्यस्मि त राज्यमधुनाभिमतं वृणु.. 7.56 ..
1.4.m: "I was pleased with your worship of the ghee-blanket in your previous birth. / I grant you your kingdom; now choose a boon of your liking." 7.56

1.4.s:
tato mayā vṛtaḥ prādādgāṇapatyaṃ madīpsitam..
kailāse māṃ śivo nityaṃ saṃtuṣṭaḥ prāha ceti ca.. 7.57 ..
1.4.d:
ततो मया वृतः प्रादाद्गाणपत्यं मदीप्सितम्..
कैलासे मां शिवो नित्यं संतुष्टः प्राह चेति च.. 7.57 ..
1.4.m: Then, chosen by me, he granted the rank of gaṇa-leader that I desired; / and on Kailāsa, Śiva, ever delighted, said to me: 7.57

1.4.s:
tenaiva hi śarireṇa praṇataṃ purataḥ sthitam..
adyaprabhṛti saṃkrāṃtau makarasyāparopi yaḥ.. 7.58 ..
1.4.d:
तेनैव हि शरिरेण प्रणतं पुरतः स्थितम्..
अद्यप्रभृति संक्रांतौ मकरस्यापरोपि यः.. 7.58 ..
1.4.m: as I stood bowed before him in that very body: / "From this day forth, whenever any other person also, at the transit into Capricorn, 7.58

1.4.s:
ghṛtena pūjāṃ kartāsau bhāvī mama gaṇaḥ sphuṭam..
ityuktvā māṃ śivo bhadra gaṇakoṭīśvaraṃ vyadhāt.. 7.59 ..
1.4.d:
घृतेन पूजां कर्तासौ भावी मम गणः स्फुटम्..
इत्युक्त्वा मां शिवो भद्र गणकोटीश्वरं व्यधात्.. 7.59 ..
1.4.m: shall perform worship with ghee, he will clearly become my gaṇa." / Having spoken thus to me, good sir, Śiva made me lord of ten million gaṇas, 7.59

1.4.s:
pratīpapālakaṃnāma saṃsthitaṃ śivaśāsanam..
tataḥ kāmādibhiḥ ṣaḍbhiḥ padaiścaṃkramaṇātmikām.. 7.60 ..
1.4.d:
प्रतीपपालकंनाम संस्थितं शिवशासनम्..
ततः कामादिभिः षड्भिः पदैश्चंक्रमणात्मिकाम्.. 7.60 ..
1.4.m: established by the command of Śiva under the name Pratīpapālaka. / Then, having obtained that fortune which wanders by the six steps of passion and the rest, 7.60

1.4.s:
nisargacapalāṃ prāpya bhramarīmiva tāṃ śriyam..
naivālamabhavaṃ tasyā dhāraṇe daivayogataḥ.. 7.61 ..
1.4.d:
निसर्गचपलां प्राप्य भ्रमरीमिव तां श्रियम्..
नैवालमभवं तस्या धारणे दैवयोगतः.. 7.61 ..
1.4.m: naturally fickle like a female bee, / I was by no means able to sustain it, due to the turn of fate. 7.61

1.4.s:
vicacāra tadā mattaḥ kilāhaṃ vāraṇo yathā..
kṛtyākṛtyavicāreṇa vimukto'tīva garvitaḥ.. 7.62 ..
1.4.d:
विचचार तदा मत्तः किलाहं वारणो यथा..
कृत्याकृत्यविचारेण विमुक्तोऽतीव गर्वितः.. 7.62 ..
1.4.m: I roamed about intoxicated, like a rutting elephant, / free from deliberation over what should and should not be done, exceedingly arrogant. 7.62

1.4.s:
vidyāmabhijanaṃ lakṣmīṃ prāpya nīcanaro yathā..
āpadāṃ pātratāmeti siṃdhūnāmiva sāgaraḥ.. 7.63 ..
1.4.d:
विद्यामभिजनं लक्ष्मीं प्राप्य नीचनरो यथा..
आपदां पात्रतामेति सिंधूनामिव सागरः.. 7.63 ..
1.4.m: Just as a base man, on obtaining learning, noble birth, or wealth, / becomes a receptacle of misfortunes, as the ocean is of rivers, 7.63

1.4.s:
atha kāle vyatikrāṃte kiyanmātre yadṛcchayā..
vicarannagamaṃ śailaṃ himānīruddhakaṃdaram.. 7.64 ..
1.4.d:
अथ काले व्यतिक्रांते कियन्मात्रे यदृच्छया..
विचरन्नगमं शैलं हिमानीरुद्धकंदरम्.. 7.64 ..
1.4.m: so, when a certain amount of time had passed, while wandering at will, / I went to a mountain whose caves were blocked with snow. 7.64

1.4.s:
tapasyati munistatra gālavo bhāryayā saha..
sadaiva tīvratapasā kṛśo dhamanisaṃtataḥ.. 7.65 ..
1.4.d:
तपस्यति मुनिस्तत्र गालवो भार्यया सह..
सदैव तीव्रतपसा कृशो धमनिसंततः.. 7.65 ..
1.4.m: There the sage Gālava was performing austerity along with his wife, / emaciated, his veins standing out all over, from his constantly intense austerity. 7.65

1.4.s:
brāhmaṇasya hi dehoyaṃ naivaihikaphalapriyaḥ..
kṛcchrāya tapase ceha pretyānaṃtasukhāya ca.. 7.66 ..
1.4.d:
ब्राह्मणस्य हि देहोयं नैवैहिकफलप्रियः..
कृच्छ्राय तपसे चेह प्रेत्यानंतसुखाय च.. 7.66 ..
1.4.m: For this body of a brahmin is not fond of worldly reward; / here it is for difficult austerity, and after death for endless happiness. 7.66

1.4.s:
tasya bhāryā'tirūpeṇa vijigye viśvavarṇinī..
tanvī śyāmā mṛgākṣī sā pīnonnatapayodharā.. 7.67 ..
1.4.d:
तस्य भार्याऽतिरूपेण विजिग्ये विश्ववर्णिनी..
तन्वी श्यामा मृगाक्षी सा पीनोन्नतपयोधरा.. 7.67 ..
1.4.m: His wife surpassed all women in her excessive beauty; / slender, youthful, deer-eyed, with full and high breasts,

1.4.s:
haṃsagadgadasaṃbhāṣā mattamātaṃgagāminī..
vistīrṇajaghanā madhye kṣāmā dīrghaśiroruhā.. 7.68 ..
1.4.d:
हंसगद्गदसंभाषा मत्तमातंगगामिनी..
विस्तीर्णजघना मध्ये क्षामा दीर्घशिरोरुहा.. 7.68 ..
1.4.m: her voice soft and sweet like a swan's, walking like an elephant in rut, / broad-hipped, slender of waist, and with long hair.

1.4.s:
nimnanābhirvidhātraiṣā nirmitā saṃdidṛkṣuṇā..
vikīrṇamiva sauṃdaryamekapātramiva sthitam.. 7.69 ..
1.4.d:
निम्ननाभिर्विधात्रैषा निर्मिता संदिदृक्षुणा..
विकीर्णमिव सौंदर्यमेकपात्रमिव स्थितम्.. 7.69 ..
1.4.m: With a deep navel, she was created by the Creator wishing to see, / as it were, scattered beauty assembled together in a single vessel.

1.4.s:
tato'vinītastāṃ vīkṣya bhadra gālavavallabhām..
ahamāsaṃ śaravrātaistāḍitaḥ puṣpadhanvinā..
vivekino'pi munayastāvadeva vivekinaḥ.. 7.70 ..
1.4.d:
ततोऽविनीतस्तां वीक्ष्य भद्र गालववल्लभाम्..
अहमासं शरव्रातैस्ताडितः पुष्पधन्विना..
विवेकिनोऽपि मुनयस्तावदेव विवेकिनः.. 7.70 ..
1.4.m: Then, having seen that beloved [wife] of Gālava, O good sir, undisciplined / I was struck by a shower of arrows from the Flower-Bowed One. / Even discriminating sages possess discrimination only so long,

1.4.s:
yāvanna hariṇākṣīṇāmapāṃgavivarekṣitāḥ..
mayā vyavasitaṃ citte tadānīṃ tāṃ jihīrṣuṇā.. 7.71 ..
1.4.d:
यावन्न हरिणाक्षीणामपांगविवरेक्षिताः..
मया व्यवसितं चित्ते तदानीं तां जिहीर्षुणा.. 7.71 ..
1.4.m: as they are not glanced at through the corners of the eyes of deer-eyed women. / Then I resolved in my mind, wishing to carry her off:

1.4.s:
iti ceti hariṣyāmi tapasā rakṣitāṃ muneḥ..
asyāḥ kṛte yadi śapenmunistatra parābhavaḥ.. 7.72 ..
1.4.d:
इति चेति हरिष्यामि तपसा रक्षितां मुनेः..
अस्याः कृते यदि शपेन्मुनिस्तत्र पराभवः.. 7.72 ..
1.4.m: “How and in what way shall I carry off [her who is] protected by the sage’s austerity? / If on her account the sage should curse [me], there will be my ruin;

1.4.s:
mama bhāvī bhavedeṣā bhāryā mṛtyurutāpi me..
tasmācchiṣyo bhavāmyasya śuśrūṣānirato muneḥ.. 7.73 ..
1.4.d:
मम भावी भवेदेषा भार्या मृत्युरुतापि मे..
तस्माच्छिष्यो भवाम्यस्य शुश्रूषानिरतो मुनेः.. 7.73 ..
1.4.m: she might become my wife, or indeed [she might become] my death. / Therefore, I shall become this sage’s pupil, devoted to his service.

1.4.s:
prāpyāṃtaraṃ hariṣyāmi nāsya yogyeyamaṃganā..
iti vyavasya vidyārthimūrtimāsthāya gālavam.. 7.74 ..
1.4.d:
प्राप्यांतरं हरिष्यामि नास्य योग्येयमंगना..
इति व्यवस्य विद्यार्थिमूर्तिमास्थाय गालवम्.. 7.74 ..
1.4.m: Finding an opportunity, I shall carry [her] off; this woman is not suitable for him.” / Having thus resolved and assumed the guise of a student seeking knowledge, [I approached] Gālava,

1.4.s:
namaskṛtya vaco'vocamiti bhāvyarthanoditaḥ..
tathā matistathā mitraṃ vyavasāyastathā nṛṇām.. 7.75 ..
1.4.d:
नमस्कृत्य वचोऽवोचमिति भाव्यर्थनोदितः..
तथा मतिस्तथा मित्रं व्यवसायस्तथा नृणाम्.. 7.75 ..
1.4.m: bowed down, and spoke these words, impelled by what was destined to happen. / As the intellect, as a friend, and as men's endeavor,

1.4.s:
bhavedavaśyaṃ tadbhāvi yathā puṃbhiḥ purā kṛtam..
vivekavairāgyayuto bhagavaṃstvāsamupasthitaḥ.. 7.76 ..
1.4.d:
भवेदवश्यं तद्भावि यथा पुंभिः पुरा कृतम्..
विवेकवैराग्ययुतो भगवंस्त्वासमुपस्थितः.. 7.76 ..
1.4.m: so inevitably comes to pass what is destined, according to deeds previously done by men. / “Endowed with discrimination and detachment, O venerable one, I have approached you.

1.4.s:
śiṣyo'haṃ bhavatā pāṭhyaṃ karṇadhāraṃ mahāmunim..
apārapāradaṃ viṣṇuṃ vipramūrtimupāśritam.. 7.77 ..
1.4.d:
शिष्योऽहं भवता पाठ्यं कर्णधारं महामुनिम्..
अपारपारदं विष्णुं विप्रमूर्तिमुपाश्रितम्.. 7.77 ..
1.4.m: I am a pupil to be instructed by you, the great sage who is the helmsman, / the guide across the boundless [ocean of worldly existence], Viṣṇu taking refuge in the form of a brahmin.

1.4.s:
namasye cetanaṃ brahmā pratyakṣaṃ gālavākhyayā..
avidyākṛṣṇasarpeṇa daṣṭaṃ tadviṣapīḍitam.. 7.78 ..
1.4.d:
नमस्ये चेतनं ब्रह्मा प्रत्यक्षं गालवाख्यया..
अविद्याकृष्णसर्पेण दष्टं तद्विषपीडितम्.. 7.78 ..
1.4.m: I bow to you, the living Brahmā directly visible under the name of Gālava. / Bitten by the black serpent of ignorance and afflicted by its poison,

1.4.s:
upadeśamahāmaṃtrairmāṃ jāṃgulika jīvaya..
mahāmohamahā vṛkṣo hṛdyāvāpasamutthitaḥ.. 7.79 ..
1.4.d:
उपदेशमहामंत्रैर्मां जांगुलिक जीवय..
महामोहमहा वृक्षो हृद्यावापसमुत्थितः.. 7.79 ..
1.4.m: revive me, O snake-doctor, with the great mantras of your teaching! / The great tree of immense delusion, sprouted in the nursery of my heart,

1.4.s:
tvadvākyatīkṣṇadhāreṇa kuṭhāreṇa kṣayaṃ vrajet..
apavargapathavyāpī mūḍhasaṃsargasecanaḥ.. 7.80 ..
1.4.d:
त्वद्वाक्यतीक्ष्णधारेण कुठारेण क्षयं व्रजेत्..
अपवर्गपथव्यापी मूढसंसर्गसेचनः.. 7.80 ..
1.4.m: shall go to destruction by the sharp-edged axe of your word. / Obstructing the path to liberation, watered by association with fools,

1.4.s:
chidyatāṃ sūtradhāreṇa vidyāparaśunādhunā..
bhajāmi tava śiṣyo'haṃ varivasyāparaściram.. 7.81 ..
1.4.d:
छिद्यतां सूत्रधारेण विद्यापरशुनाधुना..
भजामि तव शिष्योऽहं वरिवस्यापरश्चिरम्.. 7.81 ..
1.4.m: let it now be felled by you, the master builder, with the axe of knowledge! / I, your pupil, resort to you, devoted to your service for a long time.

1.4.s:
samiddarbhānmūlaphalaṃ dārūṇi jalameva ca..
āhariṣye'nugṛhṇīṣva vinītaṃ māmupasthitam.. 7.82 ..
1.4.d:
समिद्दर्भान्मूलफलं दारूणि जलमेव च..
आहरिष्येऽनुगृह्णीष्व विनीतं मामुपस्थितम्.. 7.82 ..
1.4.m: I will bring sacrificial wood, kuśa grass, roots, fruits, logs, and water; / take favor upon me who have approached in humility.”

1.4.s:
itthaṃ purā bakābhikhyaṃ bakavṛttimupāśritam..
tadā''rjave kṛtamatiranujagrāha māṃ muniḥ.. 7.83 ..
1.4.d:
इत्थं पुरा बकाभिख्यं बकवृत्तिमुपाश्रितम्..
तदा'ऽर्जवे कृतमतिरनुजग्राह मां मुनिः.. 7.83 ..
1.4.m: Then the sage, his mind inclined toward honesty, favored me / who had formerly borne the name of Baka and had now adopted the behavior of a heron.

1.4.s:
tato'tīva vinīto'haṃ bhūtvā taṃ brāhmaṇīyutam..
viśvāsanāya sudṛḍhaṃ toṣayāmi dinedine.. 7.84 ..
1.4.d:
ततोऽतीव विनीतोऽहं भूत्वा तं ब्राह्मणीयुतम्..
विश्वासनाय सुदृढं तोषयामि दिनेदिने.. 7.84 ..
1.4.m: Then, having become extremely humble, in order to firmly win trust, / I pleased him together with his brahmin wife day after day.

1.4.s:
sa ca jānanmuniḥ patnīṃ pātrabhūtāmaviśvasan..
strīcaritravidaṃke tāṃ vidhāya svapiti dvijaḥ.. 7.85 ..
1.4.d:
स च जानन्मुनिः पत्नीं पात्रभूतामविश्वसन्..
स्त्रीचरित्रविदंके तां विधाय स्वपिति द्विजः.. 7.85 ..
1.4.m: And that sage, knowing his wife to be a proper recipient [of temptation] and mistrusting, / having placed her on his lap, knowing women's nature, the twice-born slept.

1.4.s:
athānyasmindine sābhūdbrāhmaṇyatha rajasvalā..
taddūraśāyinī rātrau viśvāsānme tapasvinī.. 7.86 ..
1.4.d:
अथान्यस्मिन्दिने साभूद्ब्राह्मण्यथ रजस्वला..
तद्दूरशायिनी रात्रौ विश्वासान्मे तपस्विनी.. 7.86 ..
1.4.m: Then, on another day, that brahmin woman was in her courses; / therefore, out of trust in me, the ascetic woman slept at a distance that night.

1.4.s:
idamantaramityaṃtarviciṃtyāhaṃ praharṣitaḥ..
malimlucākṛtirbhūtvā niśīthe tāmathāharam.. 7.87 ..
1.4.d:
इदमन्तरमित्यंतर्विचिंत्याहं प्रहर्षितः..
मलिम्लुचाकृतिर्भूत्वा निशीथे तामथाहरम्.. 7.87 ..
1.4.m: Thinking within, “This is the opportunity,” I was overjoyed; / having assumed the form of a thief, at midnight I then carried her off.

1.4.s:
vilalāpa tadā bālā hriyamāṇā mayoccakaiḥ..
maivaṃ maivamiti jñātvā māṃ svareṇābravīnmunim.. 7.88 ..
1.4.d:
विललाप तदा बाला ह्रियमाणा मयोच्चकैः..
मैवं मैवमिति ज्ञात्वा मां स्वरेणाब्रवीन्मुनिम्.. 7.88 ..
1.4.m: Then the young woman wailed loudly as she was being borne away by me. / Recognizing me, she cried, “Not so! Not so!” and said to the sage with her voice:

1.4.s:
bakavṛttirayaṃ duṣṭo dharmakaṃcukamāśritaḥ..
harate māṃ durācārastasmāttvaṃ trāhi gālava.. 7.89 ..
1.4.d:
बकवृत्तिरयं दुष्टो धर्मकंचुकमाश्रितः..
हरते मां दुराचारस्तस्मात्त्वं त्राहि गालव.. 7.89 ..
1.4.m: “This wicked one, of heron-like deceit, having donned the garment of righteousness, / this villain is carrying me off; therefore, rescue me, O Gālava!

1.4.s:
tava śiṣyaḥ purā bhūtvā kopveṣodya malimlucaḥ..
māṃ jihīrṣati tadrakṣa śaraṇya śaraṇaṃ bhava.. 7.90 ..
1.4.d:
तव शिष्यः पुरा भूत्वा कोप्वेषोद्य मलिम्लुचः..
मां जिहीर्षति तद्रक्ष शरण्य शरणं भव.. 7.90 ..
1.4.m: Having formerly become your pupil, who is this thief in disguise today! / He desires to carry me off; therefore protect [me], O protector, be my refuge!”

1.4.s:
tadvākyasamakālaṃ sa prabuddho gālavo muniḥ..
tiṣṭhatiṣṭheti māmuktvā gatistambhaṃ vyadhānmama.. 7.91 ..
1.4.d:
तद्वाक्यसमकालं स प्रबुद्धो गालवो मुनिः..
तिष्ठतिष्ठेति मामुक्त्वा गतिस्तम्भं व्यधान्मम.. 7.91 ..
1.4.m: At the very moment of her words, the sage Gālava awoke, / said to me, “Halt! Halt!” and arrested my movement.

1.4.s:
tataścitrākṛtirahaṃ stambhito muninā'bhavam..
vrīḍitaṃ praviśāmīva svāṃgāni kila lajjayā.. 7.92 ..
1.4.d:
ततश्चित्राकृतिरहं स्तम्भितो मुनिनाऽभवम्..
व्रीडितं प्रविशामीव स्वांगानि किल लज्जया.. 7.92 ..
1.4.m: Then, immobilized by the sage, I stood as though painted in a picture; / ashamed, I seemed to withdraw into my own limbs through sheer modesty.

1.4.s:
tataḥ prakupitaḥ prāha māmabhyetyātha gālavaḥ..
tadvajraduḥsahaṃ vākyaṃ yenāhamabhavaṃ bakaḥ.. 7.93 ..
1.4.d:
ततः प्रकुपितः प्राह मामभ्येत्याथ गालवः..
तद्वज्रदुःसहं वाक्यं येनाहमभवं बकः.. 7.93 ..
1.4.m: Then Gālava, having approached me in great fury, spoke / that word intolerable as a thunderbolt, by which I became a heron.

1.4.s:
..gālava uvāca..
bakavṛttimupāśritya vaṃcito'haṃ yatastvayā..
tasmādbakastvaṃ bhavitā cirakālaṃ narādhama.. 7.94 ..
1.4.d:
..गालव उवाच..
बकवृत्तिमुपाश्रित्य वंचितोऽहं यतस्त्वया..
तस्माद्बकस्त्वं भविता चिरकालं नराधम.. 7.94 ..
1.4.m: Gālava said: / “Since by adopting the conduct of a heron I was deceived by you, / therefore you shall become a heron for a long time, O lowest of men!”

1.4.s:
iti śapto'hamabhavaṃ muninā'dharmamāśritaḥ..
paradāropasevārthamanarthamimamāgataḥ.. 7.95 ..
1.4.d:
इति शप्तोऽहमभवं मुनिनाऽधर्ममाश्रितः..
परदारोपसेवार्थमनर्थमिममागतः.. 7.95 ..
1.4.m: Thus cursed by the sage, having resorted to unrighteousness, / desiring to pursue another man’s wife, I met with this disaster.

1.4.s:
na hīdṛśamanāyuṣyaṃ loke kiṃcana vidyate..
yādṛśaṃ puruṣasyeha paradāropasevanam.. 7.96 ..
1.4.d:
न हीदृशमनायुष्यं लोके किंचन विद्यते..
यादृशं पुरुषस्येह परदारोपसेवनम्.. 7.96 ..
1.4.m: For in the world there is nothing that shortens life / as much as a man’s pursuit of another's wife does here.

1.4.s:
tataḥ satī sā matsparśadūṣitāṃgī tapasvinī..
mayā vimuktā snātvā māṃ tathaivānuśaśāpa ha.. 7.97 ..
1.4.d:
ततः सती सा मत्स्पर्शदूषितांगी तपस्विनी..
मया विमुक्ता स्नात्वा मां तथैवानुशशाप ह.. 7.97 ..
1.4.m: Then that virtuous, ascetic woman, her body defiled by my touch, / having been released by me and having bathed, also cursed me in the very same way.

1.4.s:
evaṃ tābhyāmahaṃ śapto hyaśvatthaparṇavadbhayāt..
kaṃpamānaḥ praṇamyobhāvavocaṃ tatra dampatī.. 7.98 ..
1.4.d:
एवं ताभ्यामहं शप्तो ह्यश्वत्थपर्णवद्भयात्..
कंपमानः प्रणम्योभाववोचं तत्र दम्पती.. 7.98 ..
1.4.m: Thus cursed by the two of them, trembling out of fear like a leaf of the holy fig tree, / having bowed down to both husband and wife, I said to them:

1.4.s:
gaṇo'hamīśvarasyaiva durvinītataro yuvām..
nirodhamevaṃ kurutaṃ bhagavaṃtāvanugraham.. 7.99 ..
1.4.d:
गणोऽहमीश्वरस्यैव दुर्विनीततरो युवाम्..
निरोधमेवं कुरुतं भगवंतावनुग्रहम्.. 7.99 ..
1.4.m: “I am an attendant of Īśvara, highly undisciplined; / as you two impose restraint, so also, O venerable ones, grant your favor.

1.4.s:
vāci kṣuro nāvanītaṃ hṛdayaṃ hi dvijanmanām..
prakupyaṃti prasīdaṃti kṣaṇenāpi prasāditāḥ.. 7.100 ..
1.4.d:
वाचि क्षुरो नावनीतं हृदयं हि द्विजन्मनाम्..
प्रकुप्यंति प्रसीदंति क्षणेनापि प्रसादिताः.. 7.100 ..
1.4.m: A razor is in the speech, but fresh butter is in the heart of the twice-born; / though angered, they are pleased in a single moment when propitiated.

1.4.s:
tvayi vipratipannasya tvameva śaraṇaṃ mama..
bhūmau skhalitapādānāṃ bhūmirevāvalaṃbanam.. 7.101 ..
1.4.d:
त्वयि विप्रतिपन्नस्य त्वमेव शरणं मम..
भूमौ स्खलितपादानां भूमिरेवावलंबनम्.. 7.101 ..
1.4.m: For me who have offended against you, you alone are my refuge; / for those whose feet have slipped upon the ground, the ground itself is the only support.

1.4.s:
gaṇādhipatyamapi me jātaṃ paribhavāspadam..
viṣadaṃtā hi jāyante durvinītasya sampadaḥ.. 7.102 ..
1.4.d:
गणाधिपत्यमपि मे जातं परिभवास्पदम्..
विषदंता हि जायन्ते दुर्विनीतस्य सम्पदः.. 7.102 ..
1.4.m: Even my leadership over the gaṇas has become the seat of humiliation; / indeed, the prosperities of an undisciplined person become poisonous fangs.

1.4.s:
vidureṣyaddhiyā'pāyaṃ parato'nye vivekinaḥ..
naivobhayaṃ vidurnīcā vinā'nubhavamātmanaḥ.. 7.103 ..
1.4.d:
विदुरेष्यद्धियाऽपायं परतोऽन्ये विवेकिनः..
नैवोभयं विदुर्नीचा विनाऽनुभवमात्मनः.. 7.103 ..
1.4.m: Through foresight, others who have discrimination perceive danger in advance; / the base perceive neither [danger nor consequence] without their own direct experience.

1.4.s:
durvīnītaḥ śriyaṃ prāpya vidyāmaiśvaryameva vā..
na tiṣṭhati ciraṃ sthāne yathāhaṃ madagarvitaḥ.. 7.104 ..
1.4.d:
दुर्वीनीतः श्रियं प्राप्य विद्यामैश्वर्यमेव वा..
न तिष्ठति चिरं स्थाने यथाहं मदगर्वितः.. 7.104 ..
1.4.m: An undisciplined person, having gained fortune, learning, or sovereignty, / does not remain long in his position, just as I, blinded by arrogance [did not].

1.4.s:
vidyāmado dhanamadastṛtīyo'bhijano madaḥ..
ete madā madāṃdhānāmeta eva satāṃ damāḥ.. 7.105 ..
1.4.d:
विद्यामदो धनमदस्तृतीयोऽभिजनो मदः..
एते मदा मदांधानामेत एव सतां दमाः.. 7.105 ..
1.4.m: Pride of learning, pride of wealth, and third, pride of noble birth— / these are intoxicants for those blinded by pride; these very things are self-restraints for the virtuous.

1.4.s:
nodarkaśālinī buddhiryeṣāmavijitātmanām..
taiḥ śriyaścapalā vācyaṃ nīyaṃte mādṛśairjanaiḥ.. 7.106 ..
1.4.d:
नोदर्कशालिनी बुद्धिर्येषामविजितात्मनाम्..
तैः श्रियश्चपला वाच्यं नीयंते मादृशैर्जनैः.. 7.106 ..
1.4.m: Those whose minds lack foresight and whose selves are unconquered, / by such persons like me, fleeting fortunes are led to reproach.

1.4.s:
tatprasīda muniśreṣṭha śāpāṃtaṃ me'dhunā kuru..
durvinīteṣvapi sadā kṣamācārā hi sādhavaḥ.. 7.107 ..
1.4.d:
तत्प्रसीद मुनिश्रेष्ठ शापांतं मेऽधुना कुरु..
दुर्विनीतेष्वपि सदा क्षमाचारा हि साधवः.. 7.107 ..
1.4.m: Therefore be gracious, O best of sages, and grant me an end to the curse now; / for the virtuous always practice forbearance even toward the undisciplined.”

1.4.s:
itthaṃ vacasi vijñapte vinītenāpi vai mayā..
prasādapravaṇo bhūtvā śāpāṃtaṃ me tadā vyadhāt.. 7.108 ..
1.4.d:
इत्थं वचसि विज्ञप्ते विनीतेनापि वै मया..
प्रसादप्रवणो भूत्वा शापांतं मे तदा व्यधात्.. 7.108 ..
1.4.m: When these words were thus spoken by me in humility, / becoming inclined toward grace, he then granted me an end to the curse.

1.4.s:
..gālava uvāca..
channakīrtisamuddhārasahāyastvaṃ bhaviṣyasi..
yadendradyumnabhūpasya tadā mokṣamavāpsyasi.. 7.109 ..
1.4.d:
..गालव उवाच..
छन्नकीर्तिसमुद्धारसहायस्त्वं भविष्यसि..
यदेन्द्रद्युम्नभूपस्य तदा मोक्षमवाप्स्यसि.. 7.109 ..
1.4.m: Gālava said: / “When you become an assistant in recovering the lost renown / of King Indradyumna, then you will attain liberation.”

1.4.s:
ityahaṃ muniśāpena tadāprabhṛti parvate..
himācale bako bhūtvā kāśyapeyo vasāmi ca.. 7.110 ..
1.4.d:
इत्यहं मुनिशापेन तदाप्रभृति पर्वते..
हिमाचले बको भूत्वा काश्यपेयो वसामि च.. 7.110 ..
1.4.m: Thus, by the sage's curse, from that time onward, / having become a heron, I, the son of Kaśyapa, dwell upon the Himācala mountain.

1.4.s:
rājyaṃ cirāyuriti me ghṛtakambalasya jātismaratvamadhunāpi tathānu bhāvān..
śāpādbakatvamabhavanmunigālavasya tadbhadra sarvamuditaṃ bhavatādya pṛṣṭam.. 7.111 ..
iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ prathame māheśvarakhaṇḍe kaumārikākhaṃḍe mahīprādurbhāve saptamo'dhyāyaḥ.. 7 .. cha ..
1.4.d:
राज्यं चिरायुरिति मे घृतकम्बलस्य जातिस्मरत्वमधुनापि तथानु भावान्..
शापाद्बकत्वमभवन्मुनिगालवस्य तद्भद्र सर्वमुदितं भवताद्य पृष्टम्.. 7.111 ..
इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां प्रथमे माहेश्वरखण्डे कौमारिकाखंडे महीप्रादुर्भावे सप्तमोऽध्यायः.. 7 .. छ ..
1.4.m:
My kingdom and long life were due to the Ghṛtakambala ceremony, and through its power I retain memory of my past lives even now. / The state of being a heron came about from the curse of the sage Gālava. Thus, good sir, everything you asked has been told today.
Thus ends the seventh chapter, entitled 'The Manifestation of Mahī,' in the Kaumārikākhaṇḍa of the first [part], the Māheśvarakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.

1.4.s:
..nārada uvāca..
nāḍījaṃghabakenoktāṃ vācamākarṇyabhūpatiḥ..
mārkaṃḍeyena saṃyukto babhūvātīva duḥkhitaḥ.. 8.1 ..
1.4.d:
..नारद उवाच..
नाडीजंघबकेनोक्तां वाचमाकर्ण्यभूपतिः..
मार्कंडेयेन संयुक्तो बभूवातीव दुःखितः.. 8.1 ..
1.4.m: Nārada said: / Hearing the words spoken by the heron Nāḍījaṅgha, the king, together with Mārkaṇḍeya, became exceedingly sorrowful.

1.4.s:
taṃ niśamya munirbhūpaṃ duḥkhitaṃ sāśrulocanam..
samānavyasanaḥ prāha tadarthaṃ sa punarbakam.. 8.2 ..
1.4.d:
तं निशम्य मुनिर्भूपं दुःखितं साश्रुलोचनम्..
समानव्यसनः प्राह तदर्थं स पुनर्बकम्.. 8.2 ..
1.4.m: Seeing that king distressed with tears in his eyes, the sage, sharing his grief, spoke again to the heron on his behalf:

1.4.s:
vidhāyāśāṃ mahābhāga tvadaṃtikamupāgatau..
āvāṃ cirāyurjñātāṃśāvindradyumnamiti dvija.. 8.3 ..
1.4.d:
विधायाशां महाभाग त्वदंतिकमुपागतौ..
आवां चिरायुर्ज्ञातांशाविन्द्रद्युम्नमिति द्विज.. 8.3 ..
1.4.m: "O fortunate one, having formed hope, we two came into your presence, [knowing you] as long-lived, to learn of Indradyumna, O twice-born one.

1.4.s:
niṣpannaṃ nāsya tatkāryaṃ prāṇāneṣa mumukṣati..
vahnipraveśena paraṃ vairāgyaṃ samupāgataḥ.. 8.4 ..
1.4.d:
निष्पन्नं नास्य तत्कार्यं प्राणानेष मुमुक्षति..
वह्निप्रवेशेन परं वैराग्यं समुपागतः.. 8.4 ..
1.4.m: His business has not been accomplished, and he wishes to abandon his life-breaths. Having attained supreme dispassion, [he intends to die] by entering fire.

1.4.s:
tanmāmupāgato'haṃ ca tvāṃ siddhaṃ nāsya vāṃchitam..
tadenamanuyāsyāmi maraṇena tvayā śape.. 8.5 ..
1.4.d:
तन्मामुपागतोऽहं च त्वां सिद्धं नास्य वांछितम्..
तदेनमनुयास्यामि मरणेन त्वया शपे.. 8.5 ..
1.4.m: He came to me, and I came to you, yet his desired purpose has not been accomplished. Therefore I swear by you that I will follow him in death.

1.4.s:
āśāṃ kṛtvābhyupāyātaṃ nirāśaṃ nekṣituṃ kṣamāḥ..
bhavaṃti sādhavastasmājjīvitānmaraṇaṃ varam.. 8.6 ..
1.4.d:
आशां कृत्वाभ्युपायातं निराशं नेक्षितुं क्षमाः..
भवंति साधवस्तस्माज्जीवितान्मरणं वरम्.. 8.6 ..
1.4.m: Good people cannot bear to look upon one who has approached with hope leaving despondent. Therefore, death is better than life.

1.4.s:
prārthitaṃ cāmunā hṛtsthaṃ mayā cāsmai pratiśrutam..
tvāṃ mitraṃ tatparijñāne dhṛtvā hṛdi cirāyuṣam.. 8.7 ..
1.4.d:
प्रार्थितं चामुना हृत्स्थं मया चास्मै प्रतिश्रुतम्..
त्वां मित्रं तत्परिज्ञाने धृत्वा हृदि चिरायुषम्.. 8.7 ..
1.4.m: What was in his heart was requested by him, and promised to him by me, holding you in my heart as a long-lived friend to gain that knowledge.

1.4.s:
asaṃpādayato nārthaṃ pratijñātaṃ mamāyuṣā..
kaluṣeṇārthinā māśāpūrakeṇa sakhedhunā.. 8.8 ..
1.4.d:
असंपादयतो नार्थं प्रतिज्ञातं ममायुषा..
कलुषेणार्थिना माशापूरकेण सखेधुना.. 8.8 ..
1.4.m: If I do not accomplish the purpose promised by my life, what use to me now, O friend, is this tainted life that does not fulfill the hope of a supplicant?

1.4.s:
pratiśrutaṃ kṛtaṃ ślāghyā dāsatāṃtyajapakvaṇe..
hariścaṃdrasyeva nṛṇāṃ na ślāghyā satyasaṃdhatā.. 8.9 ..
1.4.d:
प्रतिश्रुतं कृतं श्लाघ्या दासतांत्यजपक्वणे..
हरिश्चंद्रस्येव नृणां न श्लाघ्या सत्यसंधता.. 8.9 ..
1.4.m: To fulfill what has been promised—even slavery in an outcaste settlement, like Hariścandra's—is praised; infidelity to truth is not praised for men.

1.4.s:
mitrasnehasya paryāyastacca sāptapadaṃ smṛtam..
snehaḥ sa kīdṛśo mitre duḥkhito yo na dṛśyate.. 8.10 ..
1.4.d:
मित्रस्नेहस्य पर्यायस्तच्च साप्तपदं स्मृतम्..
स्नेहः स कीदृशो मित्रे दुःखितो यो न दृश्यते.. 8.10 ..
1.4.m: Friendship is traditionally remembered as being formed within seven steps. What kind of affection for a friend is that which is not seen when he is in sorrow?

1.4.s:
tadavaśyamahaṃ sākamadhunā vahnisādhanam..
kariṣye kīrtivapuṣaḥ kṛte satyamidaṃ sakhe.. 8.11 ..
1.4.d:
तदवश्यमहं साकमधुना वह्निसाधनम्..
करिष्ये कीर्तिवपुषः कृते सत्यमिदं सखे.. 8.11 ..
1.4.m: Therefore, for the sake of the body of fame, I will surely now resort to fire together with him; this is the truth, O friend.

1.4.s:
anujānīhi māmetaddarśanaṃ tava paścimam..
tvayā saha mahābhāga nāḍījaṃgha dvijottama.. 8.12 ..
1.4.d:
अनुजानीहि मामेतद्दर्शनं तव पश्चिमम्..
त्वया सह महाभाग नाडीजंघ द्विजोत्तम.. 8.12 ..
1.4.m: Permit me, O fortunate one, best of the twice-born, Nāḍījaṅgha; this is my last meeting with you."

1.4.s:
..nārada uvāca..
vajravadduḥsahāṃ vācaṃ mārkaṃḍeyasamīritām..
śuśruvānsa kṣaṇaṃ dhyātvā pratītaḥ prāha tāvubhau.. 8.13 ..
1.4.d:
..नारद उवाच..
वज्रवद्दुःसहां वाचं मार्कंडेयसमीरिताम्..
शुश्रुवान्स क्षणं ध्यात्वा प्रतीतः प्राह तावुभौ.. 8.13 ..
1.4.m: Nārada said: / Having heard the words uttered by Mārkaṇḍeya, unendurable like a thunderbolt, he meditated for a moment, and, convinced, spoke to them both:

1.4.s:
..nāḍījaṃgha uvāca..
yadyevaṃ tadidaṃ mitraṃ viśaṃtaṃ jvalane'dhunā..
nivāraya muniśreṣṭha matto'sti cirajīvitaḥ.. 8.14 ..
1.4.d:
..नाडीजंघ उवाच..
यद्येवं तदिदं मित्रं विशंतं ज्वलनेऽधुना..
निवारय मुनिश्रेष्ठ मत्तोऽस्ति चिरजीवितः.. 8.14 ..
1.4.m: Nāḍījaṅgha said: / "If this is so, then, O best of sages, restrain this friend now from entering the fire; there is someone who has lived longer than I.

1.4.s:
prākārakarṇanāmāsāvulūkaḥ śivaparvate..
sa jñāsyati mahīpālamiṃdradyumnaṃ na saṃśayaḥ.. 8.15 ..
1.4.d:
प्राकारकर्णनामासावुलूकः शिवपर्वते..
स ज्ञास्यति महीपालमिंद्रद्युम्नं न संशयः.. 8.15 ..
1.4.m: There is an owl named Prākārakarṇa on Śiva's mountain. He will know the ruler of the earth, Indradyumna, without doubt.

1.4.s:
tasmādahaṃ tvayā sārdhamamunā ca śivālayam..
vrajāmi taṃ śikhariṇaṃ mitrakāryaprasiddhaye.. 8.16 ..
1.4.d:
तस्मादहं त्वया सार्धममुना च शिवालयम्..
व्रजामि तं शिखरिणं मित्रकार्यप्रसिद्धये.. 8.16 ..
1.4.m: Therefore, I will go to that mountain, Śiva's abode, together with you and him, for the fulfillment of our friend's purpose."

1.4.s:
ityeva muktvā te jagmustrayo'pi dvijapuṃgavāḥ..
kailāsaṃ dadṛśustatra tamulūkaṃ svanīḍagam.. 8.17 ..
1.4.d:
इत्येव मुक्त्वा ते जग्मुस्त्रयोऽपि द्विजपुंगवाः..
कैलासं ददृशुस्तत्र तमुलूकं स्वनीडगम्.. 8.17 ..
1.4.m: Having spoken thus, all three eminent twice-born ones went to Kailāsa, and there they saw that owl residing in his nest.

1.4.s:
kṛtasaṃvidasau tena bakaḥ svāgatapūjayā..
pṛṣṭaśca tāvubhau prāha tatsarvamabhivāṃchitam.. 8.18 ..
1.4.d:
कृतसंविदसौ तेन बकः स्वागतपूजया..
पृष्टश्च तावुभौ प्राह तत्सर्वमभिवांछितम्.. 8.18 ..
1.4.m: Having exchanged greetings with him through the honor of a welcome, the heron, being questioned, told him all that was desired by those two:

1.4.s:
cirāyurasi jānīṣe yadīndradyumnabhūpatim..
tadbrūhi tena jñānena kāryaṃ jīvāmahe vayam.. 8.19 ..
1.4.d:
चिरायुरसि जानीषे यदीन्द्रद्युम्नभूपतिम्..
तद्ब्रूहि तेन ज्ञानेन कार्यं जीवामहे वयम्.. 8.19 ..
1.4.m: "You are long-lived; if you know King Indradyumna, then tell us; through that knowledge our purpose will be served, and we shall live."

1.4.s:
iti pṛṣṭaḥ sa vimanā mitrakāryaprasādhanāt..
kauśikaḥ prāha jānāmi nendradyumnamahaṃ nṛpam.. 8.20 ..
1.4.d:
इति पृष्टः स विमना मित्रकार्यप्रसाधनात्..
कौशिकः प्राह जानामि नेन्द्रद्युम्नमहं नृपम्.. 8.20 ..
1.4.m: Thus questioned, that owl, dejected because he could not accomplish his friend's purpose, said: "I do not know King Indradyumna.

1.4.s:
aṣṭāviṃśatpramāṇā me kalpā jātasya bhūtale..
na dṛṣṭo na śruto vāsāviṃdradyumno nṛpaḥ kṣitau.. 8.21 ..
1.4.d:
अष्टाविंशत्प्रमाणा मे कल्पा जातस्य भूतले..
न दृष्टो न श्रुतो वासाविंद्रद्युम्नो नृपः क्षितौ.. 8.21 ..
1.4.m: Twenty-eight kalpas have passed since I was born on the earth. King Indradyumna has neither been seen nor heard of by me on the earth."

1.4.s:
tacchrutvā vismito bhūpastasyāyuratimātrataḥ..
duḥkhito'pi tadā hetuṃ papracchāsau tadāyuṣaḥ.. 8.22 ..
1.4.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा विस्मितो भूपस्तस्यायुरतिमात्रतः..
दुःखितोऽपि तदा हेतुं पप्रच्छासौ तदायुषः.. 8.22 ..
1.4.m: Hearing that, the king was astonished at his extraordinary lifespan; and, though sorrowful, he then asked the cause of that lifespan:

1.4.s:
evamāyuryadi tava kathaṃ prāptaṃ bravīhi tat..
ulūkatvaṃ kathamidaṃ jugupsitamatīva ca.. 8.23 ..
1.4.d:
एवमायुर्यदि तव कथं प्राप्तं ब्रवीहि तत्..
उलूकत्वं कथमिदं जुगुप्सितमतीव च.. 8.23 ..
1.4.m: "If your life is such, tell me how it was attained. And how did this exceedingly despicable state of an owl come about?"

1.4.s:
..prākārakarṇa uvāca..
śrṛṇu bhadra yathā dīrghamāyurmeśivapūjanāt..
jugupsitamulūkatvaṃ śāpena ca mahāmuneḥ.. 8.24 ..
1.4.d:
..प्राकारकर्ण उवाच..
श्रृणु भद्र यथा दीर्घमायुर्मेशिवपूजनात्..
जुगुप्सितमुलूकत्वं शापेन च महामुनेः.. 8.24 ..
1.4.m: Prākārakarṇa said: / "Hear, good sir, how my long life arose from the worship of Śiva, and the despicable state of an owl from the curse of a great sage.

1.4.s:
vasiṣṭhakulasaṃbhūtaḥ purāhamabhavaṃ dvijaḥ..
ghaṃṭa ityabhivikhyāto vārāṇasyāṃ śiverataḥ.. 8.25 ..
1.4.d:
वसिष्ठकुलसंभूतः पुराहमभवं द्विजः..
घंट इत्यभिविख्यातो वाराणस्यां शिवेरतः.. 8.25 ..
1.4.m: Long ago, I was a brahmin born in the lineage of Vasiṣṭha, renowned as Ghaṇṭa, devoted to Śiva in Vārāṇasī.

1.4.s:
dharmaśravaṇaniṣṭhasya sādhūnāṃ saṃsadi svayam..
śrutvāsmi pūjayāmīśaṃ bilvapatrairakhaṃḍitaiḥ.. 8.26 ..
1.4.d:
धर्मश्रवणनिष्ठस्य साधूनां संसदि स्वयम्..
श्रुत्वास्मि पूजयामीशं बिल्वपत्रैरखंडितैः.. 8.26 ..
1.4.m: Devoted to hearing dharma, having myself heard it in the assembly of the virtuous, I worship the Lord with unbroken bilva leaves.

1.4.s:
na mālatī na maṃdāraḥ śatapatraṃ na mallikā..
tathā priyāṇi śrīvṛkṣo yathā madanavidviṣaḥ.. 8.27 ..
1.4.d:
न मालती न मंदारः शतपत्रं न मल्लिका..
तथा प्रियाणि श्रीवृक्षो यथा मदनविद्विषः.. 8.27 ..
1.4.m: Neither the mālatī, nor the mandāra, nor the hundred-petaled lotus, nor the mallikā is so dear to the enemy of Madana as the bilva tree.

1.4.s:
akhaṃḍabilvapatreṇa ekena śivamūrdhani..
nihitena naraiḥ puṇyaṃ prāpyate lakṣapuṣpajam.. 8.28 ..
1.4.d:
अखंडबिल्वपत्रेण एकेन शिवमूर्धनि..
निहितेन नरैः पुण्यं प्राप्यते लक्षपुष्पजम्.. 8.28 ..
1.4.m: By a single unbroken bilva leaf placed on Śiva's head, men obtain the religious merit born of a hundred thousand flowers.

1.4.s:
akhaṃḍitairbilvapatraiḥ śraddhayā svayamāhṛtaiḥ..
liṃgaprapūjanaṃ kṛtvā varṣalakṣaṃ vaseddivi.. 8.29 ..
1.4.d:
अखंडितैर्बिल्वपत्रैः श्रद्धया स्वयमाहृतैः..
लिंगप्रपूजनं कृत्वा वर्षलक्षं वसेद्दिवि.. 8.29 ..
1.4.m: Having worshipped the liṅga with unbroken bilva leaves gathered by oneself with faith, one shall dwell in heaven for a hundred thousand years.

1.4.s:
sacchāstrebhya iti śrutvā pūjayāmyahamīśvaram..
trikālaṃ śraddhayā patraiḥ śrīvṛkṣasya tribhistribhiḥ.. 8.30 ..
1.4.d:
सच्छास्त्रेभ्य इति श्रुत्वा पूजयाम्यहमीश्वरम्..
त्रिकालं श्रद्धया पत्रैः श्रीवृक्षस्य त्रिभिस्त्रिभिः.. 8.30 ..
1.4.m: Hearing this from the genuine scriptures, I worship the Lord thrice daily with faith, using three leaves of the bilva tree each time.

1.4.s:
tato varṣaśatasyāṃte tutoṣa śaśiśekharaḥ..
pratyakṣībhūya māmāha meghagaṃbhīrayā girā.. 8.31 ..
1.4.d:
ततो वर्षशतस्यांते तुतोष शशिशेखरः..
प्रत्यक्षीभूय मामाह मेघगंभीरया गिरा.. 8.31 ..
1.4.m: Then, at the end of a hundred years, the moon-crested Lord was pleased; appearing visibly before me, he spoke to me in a voice deep as a thundercloud:

1.4.s:
..īśvara uvāca..
tuṣṭosmi tava vipreṃdrākhaṃḍabilvadalārcanāt..
vṛṇīṣvābhimataṃ yatte dāsyamyapi ca durlabham.. 8.32 ..
1.4.d:
..ईश्वर उवाच..
तुष्टोस्मि तव विप्रेंद्राखंडबिल्वदलार्चनात्..
वृणीष्वाभिमतं यत्ते दास्यम्यपि च दुर्लभम्.. 8.32 ..
1.4.m: Īśvara said: / 'I am pleased with you, O best of brahmins, because of your worship with unbroken bilva leaves. Choose what is desired by you, and I will grant it, even if hard to attain.

1.4.s:
akhaṃḍabilvapatreṇa mahātuṣṭiḥ prajāyate..
ekanāpi yathānyeṣāṃ tathā na mama koṭibhiḥ.. 8.33 ..
1.4.d:
अखंडबिल्वपत्रेण महातुष्टिः प्रजायते..
एकनापि यथान्येषां तथा न मम कोटिभिः.. 8.33 ..
1.4.m: Great satisfaction arises for me from even a single unbroken bilva leaf, such as does not come from tens of millions of other [flowers].'

1.4.s:
ityukto'haṃ bhagavatā śaṃbhunā svamanaḥ sthitam..
vṛṇomi sma varaṃ deva kuru māmajarāmaram.. 8.34 ..
1.4.d:
इत्युक्तोऽहं भगवता शंभुना स्वमनः स्थितम्..
वृणोमि स्म वरं देव कुरु मामजरामरम्.. 8.34 ..
1.4.m: Thus addressed by the blessed Śambhu, I chose the boon that was in my mind: 'O God, make me ageless and immortal.'

1.4.s:
atha līlāvilāso māṃ tathetyuktvā'vicāritam..
yayāvadarśanaṃ prītimahaṃ ca mahatīṃ gataḥ.. 8.35 ..
1.4.d:
अथ लीलाविलासो मां तथेत्युक्त्वाऽविचारितम्..
ययावदर्शनं प्रीतिमहं च महतीं गतः.. 8.35 ..
1.4.m: Then the playful Lord, having said 'So be it' to me without hesitation, vanished from sight, and I experienced great joy.

1.4.s:
kṛtakṛtyaṃ tadātmānamajñāsipamahaṃ kṣitau..
etasminneva kāle tu bhṛguvaṃśyo'bhavaddvijaḥ.. 8.36 ..
1.4.d:
कृतकृत्यं तदात्मानमज्ञासिपमहं क्षितौ..
एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु भृगुवंश्योऽभवद्द्विजः.. 8.36 ..
1.4.m: I then considered myself to have accomplished my purpose on earth. At that very time, however, there was a brahmin of Bhṛgu's lineage,

1.4.s:
avadātatrijanmāsavakṣaviccākṣarārthavit..
sudarśaneti prathitā priyā tasyābhavatsatī.. 8.37 ..
1.4.d:
अवदातत्रिजन्मासवक्षविच्चाक्षरार्थवित्..
सुदर्शनेति प्रथिता प्रिया तस्याभवत्सती.. 8.37 ..
1.4.m: Pure across three generations, skilled in dice and knowledgeable in the meaning of the sacred syllables. His beloved, devoted wife was renowned as Sudarśanā.

1.4.s:
atīva muditā patyurmukhaṃ prekṣyāsya darśanāt..
tanayā devalasyaipā rūpeṇāpratimā bhuvi.. 8.38 ..
1.4.d:
अतीव मुदिता पत्युर्मुखं प्रेक्ष्यास्य दर्शनात्..
तनया देवलस्यैपा रूपेणाप्रतिमा भुवि.. 8.38 ..
1.4.m: She was exceedingly delighted from beholding the face of her husband; this daughter of Devala was peerless in beauty on earth.

1.4.s:
tasyāṃ tasmādabhūtkanyā nirviśeṣā nijāraṇeḥ..
nivṛttabālabhāvābhūtkumārī yauvanonmukhī.. 8.39 ..
1.4.d:
तस्यां तस्मादभूत्कन्या निर्विशेषा निजारणेः..
निवृत्तबालभावाभूत्कुमारी यौवनोन्मुखी.. 8.39 ..
1.4.m: To him, through her, a daughter was born, no different from fire emerging from its kindling stick; when her childhood had ended, she became a young maiden on the verge of youth.

1.4.s:
nālaṃ babhūva tāṃ dātuṃ tanayāṃ guṇaśālinīm..
kasyāpi janakaḥ sā ca vayaḥsaṃdhau mayekṣitā.. 8.40 ..
1.4.d:
नालं बभूव तां दातुं तनयां गुणशालिनीम्..
कस्यापि जनकः सा च वयःसंधौ मयेक्षिता.. 8.40 ..
1.4.m: Her father was not able to give away that virtuous daughter to anyone, and she was seen by me at the juncture of ages [between girlhood and youth],

1.4.s:
praviśdyauvanābhogabhāvairatimanoharā..
nirvāsyamānairaparaistilataṃdulitākṛtiḥ.. 8.41 ..
1.4.d:
प्रविश्द्यौवनाभोगभावैरतिमनोहरा..
निर्वास्यमानैरपरैस्तिलतंदुलिताकृतिः.. 8.41 ..
1.4.m: Exceedingly charming with the fullness and sentiment of entering youth, while other childhood traits were being cast off, her form [a blend of girlhood and youth] like mixed sesamum and rice.

1.4.s:
krīḍamānā vayasyābhirlāvaṇyapratimeva sā..
vyaciṃtayamahaṃ vipra tāṃ nirīkṣya sumadhyamām.. 8.42 ..
1.4.d:
क्रीडमाना वयस्याभिर्लावण्यप्रतिमेव सा..
व्यचिंतयमहं विप्र तां निरीक्ष्य सुमध्यमाम्.. 8.42 ..
1.4.m: Playing with her friends, she seemed the very image of beauty. / Looking at her slender waist, O brahmin, I thought:

1.4.s:
ananyākṛtimanyo'sau vidhiryeneti nirmitā..
tataḥ sāttvikabhāvānāṃ tatkṣaṇādasmi gocaram.. 8.43 ..
1.4.d:
अनन्याकृतिमन्योऽसौ विधिर्येनेति निर्मिता..
ततः सात्त्विकभावानां तत्क्षणादस्मि गोचरम्.. 8.43 ..
1.4.m: “This must be another Creator of peerless skill who fashioned her!” / Instantly, I became the vessel of involuntary emotional states,

1.4.s:
prāpito līlayāhatya bāṇaiḥ kusumadhanvinā..
tato mayā skhaladvālaṃ pṛṣṭā kasyeti tatsakhī.. 8.44 ..
1.4.d:
प्रापितो लीलयाहत्य बाणैः कुसुमधन्विना..
ततो मया स्खलद्वालं पृष्टा कस्येति तत्सखी.. 8.44 ..
1.4.m: Struck sportively with arrows by the God of the Flower-Bow. / Then, with stumbling words, I asked her friend whose [daughter] she was.

1.4.s:
prāheti bhṛguvaṃśyasya kanyeyaṃ dvijajanmanaḥ..
anūḍhādyāpi kenāpi samāyātātra khelitum.. 8.45 ..
1.4.d:
प्राहेति भृगुवंश्यस्य कन्येयं द्विजजन्मनः..
अनूढाद्यापि केनापि समायातात्र खेलितुम्.. 8.45 ..
1.4.m: She said: “This is the daughter of a twice-born of the Bhṛgu lineage. / Unmarried to anyone as yet, she has come here to play.”

1.4.s:
tataḥ kusumabāṇena śaravrātairbhṛśaṃ hataḥ..
pitaraṃ praṇato gatvā yayāce tāṃ bhṛgūdvaham.. 8.46 ..
1.4.d:
ततः कुसुमबाणेन शरव्रातैर्भृशं हतः..
पितरं प्रणतो गत्वा ययाचे तां भृगूद्वहम्.. 8.46 ..
1.4.m: Then, severely wounded by the flower-arrowed [god] with volleys of shafts, / I went, bowed to her father, that eminent Bhṛgu, and begged for her.

1.4.s:
sa ca māṃ sadṛśaṃ jñātvā śīlena ca kulena ca..
atīva cārthinaṃ mahyaṃ dadau vācā puraḥ kramāt.. 8.47 ..
1.4.d:
स च मां सदृशं ज्ञात्वा शीलेन च कुलेन च..
अतीव चार्थिनं मह्यं ददौ वाचा पुरः क्रमात्.. 8.47 ..
1.4.m: Knowing me to be well-matched in character and family, / and seeing me intensely eager, he pledged her to me beforehand by word of mouth according to custom.

1.4.s:
tataḥ sā tanayā tasya bhārgavasyā śrṛṇoditi..
dattāsmi tasmai viprāya virūpāyeti jalpatām.. 8.48 ..
1.4.d:
ततः सा तनया तस्य भार्गवस्या श्रृणोदिति..
दत्तास्मि तस्मै विप्राय विरूपायेति जल्पताम्.. 8.48 ..
1.4.m: Then that daughter of the Bhārgava heard people talking, / saying: “I have been promised to that misshapen brahmin!”

1.4.s:
rorūyamāṇā jananīmāha paśya yathā kṛtam..
atīvānucitaṃ dattvā janakena tathā vare.. 8.49 ..
1.4.d:
रोरूयमाणा जननीमाह पश्य यथा कृतम्..
अतीवानुचितं दत्त्वा जनकेन तथा वरे.. 8.49 ..
1.4.m: Weeping loudly, she said to her mother: “See what has been done! / My father has committed a grave impropriety by giving [me] to such a bridegroom!

1.4.s:
viṣamāloḍya pāsyāmi pravekṣyāmi hutāśanam..
varaṃ na tu virūpasyodvoḍhurbhāryā kathaṃcana.. 8.50 ..
1.4.d:
विषमालोड्य पास्यामि प्रवेक्ष्यामि हुताशनम्..
वरं न तु विरूपस्योद्वोढुर्भार्या कथंचन.. 8.50 ..
1.4.m: I will stir up poison and drink it, or enter the fire; / it is better, but by no means will I become the wife of a misshapen husband!”

1.4.s:
tataḥ saṃbodhya jananī tāṃ sutāmāha bhārgavam..
na deyāsmai tvayā kanyā virūpāyeti cāgrahāt.. 8.51 ..
1.4.d:
ततः संबोध्य जननी तां सुतामाह भार्गवम्..
न देयास्मै त्वया कन्या विरूपायेति चाग्रहात्.. 8.51 ..
1.4.m: Then the mother, having consoled her daughter, said to the Bhārgava: / “You must not give your daughter to this misshapen man,” persistently pleading.

1.4.s:
sa vallabhāvacaḥ śrutvā dharmaśāstrāṇyavekṣya ca..
dattāmapi haretpūrvāṃ śreyāṃścedvara āvrajet.. 8.52 ..
1.4.d:
स वल्लभावचः श्रुत्वा धर्मशास्त्राण्यवेक्ष्य च..
दत्तामपि हरेत्पूर्वां श्रेयांश्चेद्वर आव्रजेत्.. 8.52 ..
1.4.m: He, hearing his beloved wife's words and examining the treatises on dharma, [recalled]: / “Even if pledged before, one may take her back if a better bridegroom should arrive;

1.4.s:
arvākchilākramaṇato niṣṭhā syātsaptame pade..
iti vyavasya pradadāvanyasmai tāṃ dvijaḥ sutām.. 8.53 ..
1.4.d:
अर्वाक्छिलाक्रमणतो निष्ठा स्यात्सप्तमे पदे..
इति व्यवस्य प्रददावन्यस्मै तां द्विजः सुताम्.. 8.53 ..
1.4.m: before the treading on the millstone, the definitive rite is concluded at the seventh step.” / Having thus resolved, the twice-born gave his daughter to another.

1.4.s:
śvobhāvini vivāhe tu tacca sarvaṃ mayā śrutam..
tatotīva vilakṣyohaṃ vayasyānāṃ purastadā.. 8.54 ..
1.4.d:
श्वोभाविनि विवाहे तु तच्च सर्वं मया श्रुतम्..
ततोतीव विलक्ष्योहं वयस्यानां पुरस्तदा.. 8.54 ..
1.4.m: When the wedding was to take place on the morrow, I heard all that. / Then, feeling utterly humiliated before my companions,

1.4.s:
nāśakaṃ vadanaṃ bhadra tathā darśayituṃ nijam..
kāmārtotīva tāṃ suptāmarvāgniśi tadāharam.. 8.55 ..
1.4.d:
नाशकं वदनं भद्र तथा दर्शयितुं निजम्..
कामार्तोतीव तां सुप्तामर्वाग्निशि तदाहरम्.. 8.55 ..
