1.4.m: This hundred of liṅgas, and likewise the hundred worshipers, / and the hundred names, are remembered as the destroyer of all faults.

1.4.s:
viśeṣādeṣu liṃgeṣu yaḥ paṭhiṣyati paṃcasu..
paṃcabhirviṣayodbhūtaiḥ sa doṣaiḥ parimucyate.. 13.204 ..
1.4.d:
विशेषादेषु लिंगेषु यः पठिष्यति पंचसु..
पंचभिर्विषयोद्भूतैः स दोषैः परिमुच्यते.. 13.204 ..
1.4.m: Especially he who recites [this] among these five liṅgas, / is completely freed from the faults arising from the five sense-objects.

1.4.s:
..nārada uvāca..
niśamyaivaṃ prārthyate'pi guptakṣetre mudānvitāḥ..
paṃcaliṃgānayarcayaṃtaḥ śivadhyānaparābhavan.. 13.205 ..
1.4.d:
..नारद उवाच..
निशम्यैवं प्रार्थ्यतेऽपि गुप्तक्षेत्रे मुदान्विताः..
पंचलिंगानयर्चयंतः शिवध्यानपराभवन्.. 13.205 ..
1.4.m: Nārada said: / Hearing this, even while making supplication in the Guptakṣetra, filled with joy, / worshiping these five liṅgas, they became absorbed in meditation on Śiva.

1.4.s:
tato bahutithe kāle pratyakṣībhūya śaṃkaraḥ..
prāhatānmudito devasteṣāṃ bhaktiviśeṣataḥ.. 13.206 ..
1.4.d:
ततो बहुतिथे काले प्रत्यक्षीभूय शंकरः..
प्राहतान्मुदितो देवस्तेषां भक्तिविशेषतः.. 13.206 ..
1.4.m: Then after a long time, Śaṃkara, having become visible, / the delighted god spoke to them on account of their extraordinary devotion.

1.4.s:
..śiva uvāca..
bakolūkagṛdhrakūrmā indradyumna ca pārthiva..
sārūpyāṃ muktimāpannā malloke nivasiṣyatha.. 13.207 ..
1.4.d:
..शिव उवाच..
बकोलूकगृध्रकूर्मा इन्द्रद्युम्न च पार्थिव..
सारूप्यां मुक्तिमापन्ना मल्लोके निवसिष्यथ.. 13.207 ..
1.4.m: Śiva said: / Crane, owl, vulture, and tortoise, and King Indradyumna! / Having attained liberation consisting of having my form, you will dwell in my realm.

1.4.s:
lomaśaścāpi mārkaṃḍo jīvanmuktau bhaviṣyataḥ..
ityukte devadevena liṃgaṃ sthāpitavānnṛpaḥ.. 13.208 ..
1.4.d:
लोमशश्चापि मार्कंडो जीवन्मुक्तौ भविष्यतः..
इत्युक्ते देवदेवेन लिंगं स्थापितवान्नृपः.. 13.208 ..
1.4.m: Lomaśa and Mārkaṇḍa will also become liberated while living. / When this was spoken by the god of gods, the king installed a liṅga,

1.4.s:
indradyumneśvaraṃ nāma mahākālākhyamityuta..
jñātvā tīrthaguṇānrājā kīrtimicchaṃściraṃtanīm.. 13.209 ..
1.4.d:
इन्द्रद्युम्नेश्वरं नाम महाकालाख्यमित्युत..
ज्ञात्वा तीर्थगुणान्राजा कीर्तिमिच्छंश्चिरंतनीम्.. 13.209 ..
1.4.m: named Indradyumneśvara, also called Mahākāla. / Knowing the virtues of the tīrtha and desiring everlasting renown,

1.4.s:
triramyamatulaṃ liṃgaṃ saṃsthāpyedamuvāca ha..
yāvaccaṃdraśca sūryaśca yāvattiṣṭhati medinī.. 13.210 ..
1.4.d:
त्रिरम्यमतुलं लिंगं संस्थाप्येदमुवाच ह..
यावच्चंद्रश्च सूर्यश्च यावत्तिष्ठति मेदिनी.. 13.210 ..
1.4.m: having installed this peerless liṅga, thrice delightful, he said: / 'As long as the moon and the sun, as long as the earth endures,

1.4.s:
indradyumneśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ naṃdatācchāśvatīḥ samāḥ..
tatastatheti bhagavācchivaḥ procyābravītpunaḥ.. 13.211 ..
1.4.d:
इन्द्रद्युम्नेश्वरं लिंगं नंदताच्छाश्वतीः समाः..
ततस्तथेति भगवाच्छिवः प्रोच्याब्रवीत्पुनः.. 13.211 ..
1.4.m: may the Indradyumneśvara liṅga flourish for eternal years!' / Then Lord Śiva, having said 'So be it,' spoke again:

1.4.s:
atra yo niyataṃ liṃgamaiṃdradyumnaṃ prapūjayet..
sa gaṇo jāyate nūnaṃ mama loke nivatsyati.. 13.212 ..
1.4.d:
अत्र यो नियतं लिंगमैंद्रद्युम्नं प्रपूजयेत्..
स गणो जायते नूनं मम लोके निवत्स्यति.. 13.212 ..
1.4.m: 'Whoever regularly worships this Indradyumneśvara liṅga here, / he surely becomes an attendant and will dwell in my realm.'

1.4.s:
ityuktvā saha taiścaiva paṃcabhiḥ śaśiśekharaḥ..
rudralokama gāddevaste'pi jātā gaṇāḥ punaḥ.. 13.213 ..
1.4.d:
इत्युक्त्वा सह तैश्चैव पंचभिः शशिशेखरः..
रुद्रलोकम गाद्देवस्तेऽपि जाता गणाः पुनः.. 13.213 ..
1.4.m: Having said this, the moon-crested god went to the realm of Rudra together with those five; / and they too became attendants.

1.4.s:
evaṃ prabhāvo rājābhūdiṃdradyumno mahīpatiḥ..
yajatā yena vīreṇa nirmiteyaṃ mahīnadī.. 13.214 ..
1.4.d:
एवं प्रभावो राजाभूदिंद्रद्युम्नो महीपतिः..
यजता येन वीरेण निर्मितेयं महीनदी.. 13.214 ..
1.4.m: Of such power was King Indradyumna, ruler of the earth, / through performing a sacrifice by which hero this river Mahī was created.

1.4.s:
evaṃvidhaḥsa puṇyo'yaṃ mahīsāgarasaṃgamaḥ..
abhūttato'pi saṃkṣepāttava pārtha prakīrtitaḥ.. 13.215 ..
1.4.d:
एवंविधःस पुण्योऽयं महीसागरसंगमः..
अभूत्ततोऽपि संक्षेपात्तव पार्थ प्रकीर्तितः.. 13.215 ..
1.4.m: Such is this holy confluence of the Mahī and the ocean / that came to be; it has thus been described in brief to you, son of Pṛthā.

1.4.s:
snātvātra saṃgame yaśca indradyumneśvaraṃ naraḥ..
pūjayettasya vāsaḥ syādyatreśaḥ pārvatīpatiḥ.. 13.216 ..
1.4.d:
स्नात्वात्र संगमे यश्च इन्द्रद्युम्नेश्वरं नरः..
पूजयेत्तस्य वासः स्याद्यत्रेशः पार्वतीपतिः.. 13.216 ..
1.4.m: And whatever man, having bathed here at the confluence, / worships Indradyumneśvara, his abode shall be where the Lord, the husband of Pārvatī, resides.

1.4.s:
sarvabandhaharaṃ liṃgaṃ gāṇapatyapradaṃ tvidam..
yato bandhānvihāyaiva sthāpitaṃ tena phālalguna.. 13.217 ..
1.4.d:
सर्वबन्धहरं लिंगं गाणपत्यप्रदं त्विदम्..
यतो बन्धान्विहायैव स्थापितं तेन फालल्गुन.. 13.217 ..
1.4.m: This liṅga destroys all bondage and bestows the status of an attendant, / because it was installed by him, O Phālguna, after abandoning his bonds.

1.4.s:
itīdamuktaṃ tava puṇyakāri māhātmyamasyottamasaṃgamasya..
māhātmyamatyadbutapuṇyamindradyumneśvarasyāpi ca puṇyakāri.. 13.218 ..
iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ prathame māheśvarakhaṇḍe kaumārikākhaṇḍe mahīsāgarasaṃgamamāhātmyaśatarudriyaliṃgamāhātmyendradyumneśvaraliṃgamāhātmya varṇanaṃnāma trayodaśo'dhyāyaḥ.. 13 .. cha ..
1.4.d:
इतीदमुक्तं तव पुण्यकारि माहात्म्यमस्योत्तमसंगमस्य..
माहात्म्यमत्यद्बुतपुण्यमिन्द्रद्युम्नेश्वरस्यापि च पुण्यकारि.. 13.218 ..
इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां प्रथमे माहेश्वरखण्डे कौमारिकाखण्डे महीसागरसंगममाहात्म्यशतरुद्रियलिंगमाहात्म्येन्द्रद्युम्नेश्वरलिंगमाहात्म्य वर्णनंनाम त्रयोदशोऽध्यायः.. 13 .. छ ..
1.4.m:
Thus has been spoken to you this merit-making māhātmya of this highest confluence; / the merit-making māhātmya of Indradyumneśvara is also exceedingly wonderful and meritorious.
Thus ends the thirteenth chapter, titled 'The Description of the Māhātmya of the Confluence of the Mahī and the Ocean, the Māhātmya of the Śatarudrīya Liṅgas, and the Māhātmya of the Indradyumneśvara Liṅga,' in the Kaumārikākhaṇḍa of the first section, the Māheśvarakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.

1.4.s:
..arjuna uvāca..
kumāranāthamāhātmyaṃ yattvayoktaṃ kathāṃtare..
tadahaṃ śrotumicchāmi vistareṇa mahāmune.. 14.1 ..
1.4.d:
..अर्जुन उवाच..
कुमारनाथमाहात्म्यं यत्त्वयोक्तं कथांतरे..
तदहं श्रोतुमिच्छामि विस्तरेण महामुने.. 14.1 ..
1.4.m: Arjuna said: / The māhātmya of Kumāranātha which you mentioned in another narration, / that I desire to hear in detail, O great sage.

1.4.s:
..nārada uvāca..
tārakaṃ vinihatyaiva vajrāṃgatanayaṃ prabhuḥ..
guhaḥ saṃsthāpayāmāsa liṃgametacca phālguna.. 14.2 ..
1.4.d:
..नारद उवाच..
तारकं विनिहत्यैव वज्रांगतनयं प्रभुः..
गुहः संस्थापयामास लिंगमेतच्च फाल्गुन.. 14.2 ..
1.4.m:
Nārada said:
Having slain Tāraka, the son of Vajrāṅga, the lord
Guha established this liṅga, O Phālguna.

1.4.s:
darśanācchravaṇāddhyānātpūjayā śrutivaṃdanaiḥ..
sarvapāpāpahaḥ pārtha kumāreśo na saṃśayaḥ.. 14.3 ..
1.4.d:
दर्शनाच्छ्रवणाद्ध्यानात्पूजया श्रुतिवंदनैः..
सर्वपापापहः पार्थ कुमारेशो न संशयः.. 14.3 ..
1.4.m:
By seeing, hearing, meditating upon, worshipping, and singing praises from the scriptures,
Kumāreśa removes all sins, O Pārtha; there is no doubt.

1.4.s:
..arjuna uvāca..
atyāścaryamayī ramyā katheyaṃ pāpanāśinī..
vistareṇa ca me brūhi yāthātathyena nārada.. 14.4 ..
1.4.d:
..अर्जुन उवाच..
अत्याश्चर्यमयी रम्या कथेयं पापनाशिनी..
विस्तरेण च मे ब्रूहि याथातथ्येन नारद.. 14.4 ..
1.4.m:
Arjuna said:
This charming story, which destroys sin, is full of great wonder.
Tell it to me in detail and as it truly happened, O Nārada.

1.4.s:
vajrāṃgaḥ kopyasau daityaḥ kiṃprabhāvaśca tārakaḥ..
kathaṃ sa nihataścaiva jātaścaiva kathaṃ guhaḥ.. 14.5 ..
1.4.d:
वज्रांगः कोप्यसौ दैत्यः किंप्रभावश्च तारकः..
कथं स निहतश्चैव जातश्चैव कथं गुहः.. 14.5 ..
1.4.m:
Who was this Daitya Vajrāṅga, and what was the power of Tāraka?
How was he slain, and how was Guha born?

1.4.s:
kathaṃ saṃsthāpitaṃ liṃgaṃ kumāreśvarasaṃjñitam..
kiṃ phalaṃ cāsya liṃgasya brūhi tadvistarānmama.. 14.6 ..
1.4.d:
कथं संस्थापितं लिंगं कुमारेश्वरसंज्ञितम्..
किं फलं चास्य लिंगस्य ब्रूहि तद्विस्तरान्मम.. 14.6 ..
1.4.m:
How was the liṅga named Kumāreśvara established,
and what is the fruit of this liṅga? Tell me that at length.

1.4.s:
..nārada uvāca..
praṇipatya kumārāya senānye ceśvarāya ca..
śrṛṇu caikamanāḥ pārtha kumāracaritaṃ mahat.. 14.7 ..
1.4.d:
..नारद उवाच..
प्रणिपत्य कुमाराय सेनान्ये चेश्वराय च..
श्रृणु चैकमनाः पार्थ कुमारचरितं महत्.. 14.7 ..
1.4.m:
Nārada said:
Bowing down to Kumāra, the commander of the army and the Lord,
listen with a single mind, O Pārtha, to the great deed of Kumāra.

1.4.s:
mānaso brahmaṇaḥ putro dakṣo nāma prajāpatiḥ..
ṣaṣṭiṃ so'janayatkanyā vīriṇyāṃ nāma phālguna.. 14.8 ..
1.4.d:
मानसो ब्रह्मणः पुत्रो दक्षो नाम प्रजापतिः..
षष्टिं सोऽजनयत्कन्या वीरिण्यां नाम फाल्गुन.. 14.8 ..
1.4.m:
The mind-born son of Brahmā was the Prajāpati named Dakṣa.
He begot sixty daughters upon Vīriṇī, O Phālguna.

1.4.s:
dado sa daśa dharmāya kaśyapāya trayodaśa..
saptaviṃśatiṃ somāya catasroriṣṭanemine.. 14.9 ..
1.4.d:
ददो स दश धर्माय कश्यपाय त्रयोदश..
सप्तविंशतिं सोमाय चतस्रोरिष्टनेमिने.. 14.9 ..
1.4.m:
He gave ten to Dharma, thirteen to Kaśyapa,
twenty-seven to Soma, and four to Ariṣṭanemi.

1.4.s:
bhūtāṃgiraḥ kṛśāśvebhyo dvedve caiva dadau prabhuḥ..
nāmadheyānyamūṣāṃ ca sapatnīnāṃ ca me śrṛṇu.. 14.10 ..
1.4.d:
भूतांगिरः कृशाश्वेभ्यो द्वेद्वे चैव ददौ प्रभुः..
नामधेयान्यमूषां च सपत्नीनां च मे श्रृणु.. 14.10 ..
1.4.m:
The lord gave two each to Bhūta, Aṅgiras, and Kṛśāśva.
Hear from me their names and those of their co-wives,

1.4.s:
yāsāṃ prasūtiprabhavā lokā āpūritāstrayaḥ..
bhānurlambā kakudbhūmirviśvā sādhyā marutvatī.. 14.11 ..
1.4.d:
यासां प्रसूतिप्रभवा लोका आपूरितास्त्रयः..
भानुर्लम्बा ककुद्भूमिर्विश्वा साध्या मरुत्वती.. 14.11 ..
1.4.m:
by whose offspring the three worlds were filled:
Bhānu, Lambā, Kakud, Bhūmi, Viśvā, Sādhyā, Marutvatī,

1.4.s:
vasursuhūrtā saṃkalpā dharmapatnyaḥ sutāñchṛṇu..
bhānostu devaṛṣabha suto'bhavat.. 14.12 ..
1.4.d:
वसुर्सुहूर्ता संकल्पा धर्मपत्न्यः सुताञ्छृणु..
भानोस्तु देवऋषभ सुतोऽभवत्.. 14.12 ..
1.4.m:
Vasu, Muhūrtā, and Saṃkalpā were the wives of Dharma; hear their sons:
To Bhānu was born the son Devarṣabha.

1.4.s:
vidyota āsīllaṃbāyāṃ tataśca stanayitnavaḥ..
kakudaḥ śakaṭaḥ putraḥ kīkaṭastanayo yataḥ.. 14.13 ..
1.4.d:
विद्योत आसील्लंबायां ततश्च स्तनयित्नवः..
ककुदः शकटः पुत्रः कीकटस्तनयो यतः.. 14.13 ..
1.4.m:
In Lambā was Vidyota, and from him the thunderclouds.
The son of Kakud was Śakaṭa, from whom was born the son Kīkaṭa.

1.4.s:
bhuvo durgastathā svargo naṃdaścaiva tato'bhavat..
viśvedevāśca viśvāyā aprajāṃstānpracakṣate.. 14.14 ..
1.4.d:
भुवो दुर्गस्तथा स्वर्गो नंदश्चैव ततोऽभवत्..
विश्वेदेवाश्च विश्वाया अप्रजांस्तान्प्रचक्षते.. 14.14 ..
1.4.m:
From Bhūmi arose Durga, Svarga, and Nanda.
From Viśvā were the Viśvedevas; they are declared to be childless.

1.4.s:
sādhyā dvādaśa sādhyāyā arthasiddhistu tatsutaḥ..
marutvānsujayaṃtaśca marutvatyā babhūvatuḥ.. 14.15 ..
1.4.d:
साध्या द्वादश साध्याया अर्थसिद्धिस्तु तत्सुतः..
मरुत्वान्सुजयंतश्च मरुत्वत्या बभूवतुः.. 14.15 ..
1.4.m:
The twelve Sādhyas were born of Sādhyā, and Arthasiddhi was her son.
Marutvān and Sujayanta were born of Marutvatī.

1.4.s:
naranārāyaṇau prāhuryau tau jñānavido janāḥ..
vasośca vasavaścāṣṭau muhūrtāyāṃ muhūrtakāḥ.. 14.16 ..
1.4.d:
नरनारायणौ प्राहुर्यौ तौ ज्ञानविदो जनाः..
वसोश्च वसवश्चाष्टौ मुहूर्तायां मुहूर्तकाः.. 14.16 ..
1.4.m:
Those who know wisdom speak of those two as Nara and Nārāyaṇa.
From Vasu came the eight Vasus, and in Muhūrtā the Muhūrtakas,

1.4.s:
ye vai phalaṃ prayacchaṃti bhūtānāṃ svaṃ svakālajam..
saṃkalpāyāśca saṃkalpaḥ kāmaḥ saṃkalpajaḥ sutaḥ.. 14.17 ..
1.4.d:
ये वै फलं प्रयच्छंति भूतानां स्वं स्वकालजम्..
संकल्पायाश्च संकल्पः कामः संकल्पजः सुतः.. 14.17 ..
1.4.m:
who indeed grant to living beings the fruit born of their respective times.
Of Saṃkalpā was Saṃkalpa; Kāma was the son born of Saṃkalpa.

1.4.s:
surūpāsūta tanayānrudrānekādaśaiva tu..
kapālī piṃgalo bhīmo virupākṣo vilohitaḥ.. 14.18 ..
1.4.d:
सुरूपासूत तनयान्रुद्रानेकादशैव तु..
कपाली पिंगलो भीमो विरुपाक्षो विलोहितः.. 14.18 ..
1.4.m:
Surūpā gave birth to eleven sons, the Rudras:
Kapālin, Piṅgala, Bhīma, Virūpākṣa, Vilohita,

1.4.s:
ajakaḥ śāsanaḥ śāstā śaṃbhuścāṃtyo bhavastathā..
rudrasya pārṣadāścānye virūpāyāḥ sutāḥ smṛtāḥ.. 14.19 ..
1.4.d:
अजकः शासनः शास्ता शंभुश्चांत्यो भवस्तथा..
रुद्रस्य पार्षदाश्चान्ये विरूपायाः सुताः स्मृताः.. 14.19 ..
1.4.m:
Ajaka, Śāsana, Śāstṛ, Śambhu, and the last was Bhava.
Other attendants of Rudra are remembered as the sons of Virūpā.

1.4.s:
prajāpateraṃgirasaḥ svadhā patnī pitṝnatha..
jajñe sanī(cī?)tathā putramatharvāgirasaṃ prabhum.. 14.20 ..
1.4.d:
प्रजापतेरंगिरसः स्वधा पत्नी पितॄनथ..
जज्ञे सनी(ची?)तथा पुत्रमथर्वागिरसं प्रभुम्.. 14.20 ..
1.4.m:
Svadhā, the wife of the Prajāpati Aṅgiras, bore the ancestors,
as well as a daughter [Sanīcī] and the powerful son Atharvāṅgiras.

1.4.s:
kṛśāśvasya ca dve bhārye arciśca diṣaṇā tathā..
astragāmo yayoḥ putraḥ sasaṃhāraḥ prakīrtitaḥ.. 14.21 ..
1.4.d:
कृशाश्वस्य च द्वे भार्ये अर्चिश्च दिषणा तथा..
अस्त्रगामो ययोः पुत्रः ससंहारः प्रकीर्तितः.. 14.21 ..
1.4.m:
Kṛśāśva had two wives, Arcis and Dhiṣaṇā,
whose sons are proclaimed to be the weapons along with their withdrawal.

1.4.s:
pataṃgī yāminī tāmrā timiścāriṣṭaneminaḥ..
pataṃgyasūta patagānyāminī śalabhānatha.. 14.22 ..
1.4.d:
पतंगी यामिनी ताम्रा तिमिश्चारिष्टनेमिनः..
पतंग्यसूत पतगान्यामिनी शलभानथ.. 14.22 ..
1.4.m:
Pataṅgī, Yāminī, Tāmrā, and Timi were [the wives] of Ariṣṭanemi.
Pataṅgī gave birth to birds, and Yāminī to locusts.

1.4.s:
tāmrāyāḥ śyenagṛdhrādyāstimeryādogaṇāstathā..
atha kaśyapapatnīnāṃ yatprasūdamidaṃ jagat.. 14.23 ..
1.4.d:
ताम्रायाः श्येनगृध्राद्यास्तिमेर्यादोगणास्तथा..
अथ कश्यपपत्नीनां यत्प्रसूदमिदं जगत्.. 14.23 ..
1.4.m:
From Tāmrā came hawks, vultures, and the like, and from Timi aquatic creatures.
Now, concerning the wives of Kaśyapa, from whose offspring this world arose:

1.4.s:
śrṛṇu nāmāni lokānāṃ mātṝṇāṃ śaṃkarāṇi ca..
aditirditirdanuḥ siṃhī danāyuḥ surabhistathā.. 14.24 ..
1.4.d:
श्रृणु नामानि लोकानां मातॄणां शंकराणि च..
अदितिर्दितिर्दनुः सिंही दनायुः सुरभिस्तथा.. 14.24 ..
1.4.m:
Hear the auspicious names of the mothers of the worlds:
Aditi, Diti, Danu, Siṃhī, Danāyu, and Surabhi;

1.4.s:
ariṣṭā vinatā grāvā dayā krodhavaśā irā..
kadrurmuniśca te cobhe mātarastāḥ prakīrtitāḥ.. 14.25 ..
1.4.d:
अरिष्टा विनता ग्रावा दया क्रोधवशा इरा..
कद्रुर्मुनिश्च ते चोभे मातरस्ताः प्रकीर्तिताः.. 14.25 ..
1.4.m:
Ariṣṭā, Vinatā, Grāvā, Dayā, Krodhavaśā, Irā,
Kadrū, and Muni—these are proclaimed as the mothers.

1.4.s:
ādityāścāditeḥ putrā diterdaityāḥ prakīrtitāḥ..
danośca dānavāḥ proktā rāhuḥ siṃhīsuto grahaḥ.. 14.26 ..
1.4.d:
आदित्याश्चादितेः पुत्रा दितेर्दैत्याः प्रकीर्तिताः..
दनोश्च दानवाः प्रोक्ता राहुः सिंहीसुतो ग्रहः.. 14.26 ..
1.4.m:
The Ādityas are proclaimed the sons of Aditi, the Daityas of Diti,
the Dānavas of Danu, and Rāhu the planet is the son of Siṃhī.

1.4.s:
danāyuṣastathā jāto danāyuśca gaṇo balī..
gāvaśca surabherjātāriṣṭāputrā yugaṃdharāḥ.. 14.27 ..
1.4.d:
दनायुषस्तथा जातो दनायुश्च गणो बली..
गावश्च सुरभेर्जातारिष्टापुत्रा युगंधराः.. 14.27 ..
1.4.m:
From Danāyu was born the powerful troop of Danāyus.
Cattle were born of Surabhi, and the sons of Ariṣṭā were the Yugandharas.

1.4.s:
vinatāsūta aruṇaṃ garuḍaṃ ca mahābalam..
grāvāyāḥ śvāpadāḥ putrā gaṇaḥ krodhavaśastathā.. 14.28 ..
1.4.d:
विनतासूत अरुणं गरुडं च महाबलम्..
ग्रावायाः श्वापदाः पुत्रा गणः क्रोधवशस्तथा.. 14.28 ..
1.4.m:
Vinatā gave birth to Aruṇa and Garuda of great strength.
The sons of Grāvā were beasts of prey, and likewise the troop of Krodhavaśas

1.4.s:
jātaḥ krodhavaśāyāśca irāyā bhūruhāḥ smṛtāḥ..
kadrūsutāḥ smṛtā nāgā munerapsarasāṃ gaṇāḥ.. 14.29 ..
1.4.d:
जातः क्रोधवशायाश्च इराया भूरुहाः स्मृताः..
कद्रूसुताः स्मृता नागा मुनेरप्सरसां गणाः.. 14.29 ..
1.4.m:
was born of Krodhavaśā; plants are remembered as [born] of Irā.
The serpent Nāgas are remembered as Kadrū’s sons, and the hosts of apsarases from Muni.

1.4.s:
tatra dvau tanayau yau ca ditestau viṣṇunā hatau..
hiraṇyakaśipurvīro hiraṇyākṣastathā'paraḥ.. 14.30 ..
1.4.d:
तत्र द्वौ तनयौ यौ च दितेस्तौ विष्णुना हतौ..
हिरण्यकशिपुर्वीरो हिरण्याक्षस्तथाऽपरः.. 14.30 ..
1.4.m:
Among them, the two sons of Diti were slain by Viṣṇu:
the heroic Hiraṇyakaśipu, and the other, Hiraṇyākṣa.

1.4.s:
tato nihataputrā sā ditirārādhya kaśyapam..
ayācata varaṃ devī putramanyaṃ mahābalam.. 14.31 ..
1.4.d:
ततो निहतपुत्रा सा दितिराराध्य कश्यपम्..
अयाचत वरं देवी पुत्रमन्यं महाबलम्.. 14.31 ..
1.4.m:
Then Diti, whose sons had been slain, worshipped Kaśyapa,
and the goddess asked for a boon: another son of great strength

1.4.s:
samare śakrahaṃtāraṃ sa tasyā adadātprabhuḥ..
niyame cāpi vartasva varṣāṇāṃ ca sahasrakam.. 14.32 ..
1.4.d:
समरे शक्रहंतारं स तस्या अददात्प्रभुः..
नियमे चापि वर्तस्व वर्षाणां च सहस्रकम्.. 14.32 ..
1.4.m:
who would slay Śakra in battle. The lord gave it to her, [saying]:
“Remain in religious observance for a thousand years.”

1.4.s:
ityuktā sā tathā cakre puṣkarasthā samāhitā..
vartaṃtyā niyame tasyāḥ sahasrākṣaḥ samāhitaḥ.. 14.33 ..
1.4.d:
इत्युक्ता सा तथा चक्रे पुष्करस्था समाहिता..
वर्तंत्या नियमे तस्याः सहस्राक्षः समाहितः.. 14.33 ..
1.4.m:
Thus addressed, she, concentrated in mind, did so while staying at Puṣkara.
While she was observing the vow, the thousand-eyed [Indra], with concentrated mind,

1.4.s:
upāsāmācaradbhaktyā sā cainamanvamanyata..
daśavatsaraśeṣasya sahasrasya tadā ditiḥ.. 14.34 ..
1.4.d:
उपासामाचरद्भक्त्या सा चैनमन्वमन्यत..
दशवत्सरशेषस्य सहस्रस्य तदा दितिः.. 14.34 ..
1.4.m:
attended upon her with devotion, and she favored him.
Then, when ten years remained of the thousand, Diti

1.4.s:
uvāca śakraṃ suprītā bhaktyā śakrasya toṣitā..
..ditiruvāca..
atrottīrṇavrataprāyāṃ viddhi devasattama.. 14.35 ..
1.4.d:
उवाच शक्रं सुप्रीता भक्त्या शक्रस्य तोषिता..
..दितिरुवाच..
अत्रोत्तीर्णव्रतप्रायां विद्धि देवसत्तम.. 14.35 ..
1.4.m:
spoke to Śakra, highly pleased and gratified by Śakra’s devotion:
Diti said:
“Know that my vow is almost completed here, O best of the gods!

1.4.s:
bhaviṣyati tava bhrātā tena sārdhamimāṃ śriyam..
bhokṣyase tvaṃ yathānayāyaṃ trailokyaṃ hatakaṃṭakam.. 14.36 ..
1.4.d:
भविष्यति तव भ्राता तेन सार्धमिमां श्रियम्..
भोक्ष्यसे त्वं यथानयायं त्रैलोक्यं हतकंटकम्.. 14.36 ..
1.4.m:
You will have a brother; along with him, you will enjoy
this royal fortune and the three worlds cleared of thorns, in accordance with justice.”

1.4.s:
ityuktvā nidrayāviṣṭā caraṇākrāṃtamūrdhajā..
divā suptā ditirdevī bhāvyarthabalanoditā.. 14.37 ..
1.4.d:
इत्युक्त्वा निद्रयाविष्टा चरणाक्रांतमूर्धजा..
दिवा सुप्ता दितिर्देवी भाव्यर्थबलनोदिता.. 14.37 ..
1.4.m:
Having spoken thus, overcome by sleep, with her hair touching her feet,
the goddess Diti slept during the day, impelled by the force of what was destined to happen.

1.4.s:
tattu raṃdhramavekṣyaiva yogamūrtistadāviśat..
jaṭharasthaṃ ditergarbhaṃ cakre vajreṇa saptadhā.. 14.38 ..
1.4.d:
तत्तु रंध्रमवेक्ष्यैव योगमूर्तिस्तदाविशत्..
जठरस्थं दितेर्गर्भं चक्रे वज्रेण सप्तधा.. 14.38 ..
1.4.m:
Perceiving that breach, he entered then in yogic form;
he cut the embryo resting in Diti’s belly into seven parts with his thunderbolt.

1.4.s:
ekaikaṃ ca punaḥ khaṇḍaṃ cakāra maghavā tataḥ..
saptadhā saptadhā kopādudbudhya ca tato ditiḥ.. 14.39 ..
1.4.d:
एकैकं च पुनः खण्डं चकार मघवा ततः..
सप्तधा सप्तधा कोपादुद्बुध्य च ततो दितिः.. 14.39 ..
1.4.m:
Then Maghavan divided each single piece again,
into seven and seven parts out of anger; and then Diti woke up.

1.4.s:
na haṃtavyo na haṃtavya iti sā śakramabravīt..
vajreṇa kṛttyamānānāṃ buddhā sā rodanena ca.. 14.40 ..
1.4.d:
न हंतव्यो न हंतव्य इति सा शक्रमब्रवीत्..
वज्रेण कृत्त्यमानानां बुद्धा सा रोदनेन च.. 14.40 ..
1.4.m:
“Do not kill him! Do not kill him!” she said to Śakra,
having awakened to the crying of those being cut with the thunderbolt.

1.4.s:
tataḥ śakraśca mā rodīriti tāṃstānyathā'vadat..
nirgatya jaṭharāttasmāttataḥ prāṃjaliragrataḥ.. 14.41 ..
1.4.d:
ततः शक्रश्च मा रोदीरिति तांस्तान्यथाऽवदत्..
निर्गत्य जठरात्तस्मात्ततः प्रांजलिरग्रतः.. 14.41 ..
1.4.m:
Then Śakra said to each of them: “Do not weep!”
Coming out of that belly, then, with folded hands before her,

1.4.s:
uvāca vākyaṃ cātrasto mātaraṃ riṣapūritām..
divāsvāpaṃ kṛthā mātaḥ pādākrāṃtaśiroruhā.. 14.42 ..
1.4.d:
उवाच वाक्यं चात्रस्तो मातरं रिषपूरिताम्..
दिवास्वापं कृथा मातः पादाक्रांतशिरोरुहा.. 14.42 ..
1.4.m:
unafraid, he spoke these words to his mother, who was filled with rage:
“O mother, you slept by day, your hair touching your feet;

1.4.s:
suptātha suciraṃ vāte dhinno garbho mayā tava..
kṛtā ekonapaṃcāśadbhāgā vajreṇa te sutāḥ.. 14.43 ..
1.4.d:
सुप्ताथ सुचिरं वाते धिन्नो गर्भो मया तव..
कृता एकोनपंचाशद्भागा वज्रेण ते सुताः.. 14.43 ..
1.4.m:
when you had thus slept for a long time, the embryo in your womb was divided by me;
your sons were made into forty-nine parts with the thunderbolt.

1.4.s:
satyaṃ bhavatu te vākyaṃ sārdhaṃ bhokṣyāmi taiḥ śriyam..
dāsyāmi teṣāṃ sthānāni divi yāvadahaṃ dite.. 14.44 ..
1.4.d:
सत्यं भवतु ते वाक्यं सार्धं भोक्ष्यामि तैः श्रियम्..
दास्यामि तेषां स्थानानि दिवि यावदहं दिते.. 14.44 ..
1.4.m:
May your word come true: I will enjoy the royal fortune together with them.
I shall grant them places in heaven as long as I [am there], O Diti.

1.4.s:
mā rodīriti me proktāḥ khyātāśca marutastviti..
ityuktā sā ca savrīḍā ditirjātā niruttarā.. 14.45 ..
1.4.d:
मा रोदीरिति मे प्रोक्ताः ख्याताश्च मरुतस्त्विति..
इत्युक्ता सा च सव्रीडा दितिर्जाता निरुत्तरा.. 14.45 ..
1.4.m:
Because I told them, ‘Do not weep’ (mā rudīḥ), they shall be renowned as the Maruts.”
Thus addressed, Diti became ashamed and had no answer.

1.4.s:
sārdhaṃ tairgatavāniṃdro digaṃte vāyavaḥ smṛtāḥ..
tataḥ punaśca bhartāraṃ ditiḥ provāca duḥkhitā.. 14.46 ..
1.4.d:
सार्धं तैर्गतवानिंद्रो दिगंते वायवः स्मृताः..
ततः पुनश्च भर्तारं दितिः प्रोवाच दुःखिता.. 14.46 ..
1.4.m: Indra departed together with them; they are known as the winds at the ends of the directions. / Then the grieving Diti spoke once more to her husband:

1.4.s:
putraṃ me bhagavandehi śakrahaṃtāramūrjitam..
yo nāstraśastrairvadhyatvaṃ gacchettridivavāsinām.. 14.47 ..
1.4.d:
पुत्रं मे भगवन्देहि शक्रहंतारमूर्जितम्..
यो नास्त्रशस्त्रैर्वध्यत्वं गच्छेत्त्रिदिववासिनाम्.. 14.47 ..
1.4.m: "Lord, give me a powerful son who will slay Śakra, / one who cannot be killed by any missile or weapon of the dwellers of heaven.

1.4.s:
na dadāsyuttaraṃ viddhi mṛtāmeva prajāpate..
ityuktaḥ sa tadovāca tāṃ patnīmatiduḥkhitām.. 14.48 ..
1.4.d:
न ददास्युत्तरं विद्धि मृतामेव प्रजापते..
इत्युक्तः स तदोवाच तां पत्नीमतिदुःखिताम्.. 14.48 ..
1.4.m: If you do not grant me an answer, know me to be as good as dead, O Prajāpati!" / Thus addressed, he then said to that deeply sorrowful wife:

1.4.s:
daśavarṣasahasrāṇi taponiṣṭhā tu tapsyase..
vajrasāramayairaṃgairacchedyairāyasairdṛḍhaiḥ.. 14.49 ..
1.4.d:
दशवर्षसहस्राणि तपोनिष्ठा तु तप्स्यसे..
वज्रसारमयैरंगैरच्छेद्यैरायसैर्दृढैः.. 14.49 ..
1.4.m: "You shall perform austerity, steadfast in tapas, for ten thousand years. / [A son] with limbs of the essence of a vajra, unbreakable, iron-firm and strong,

1.4.s:
vajrāṃgonāma putraste bhavitā dharmavatsalaḥ..
sā tu labdhavarā devī jagāma tapase vanam.. 14.50 ..
1.4.d:
वज्रांगोनाम पुत्रस्ते भविता धर्मवत्सलः..
सा तु लब्धवरा देवी जगाम तपसे वनम्.. 14.50 ..
1.4.m: named Vajrāṅga, devoted to dharma, will be your son." / Having obtained her boon, the goddess went to the forest for austerity.

1.4.s:
daśavarṣasahasrāṇi tapo ghoraṃ samācarat..
tapasoṃ'te bhagavatī janayāmāsa durjayam.. 14.51 ..
1.4.d:
दशवर्षसहस्राणि तपो घोरं समाचरत्..
तपसोंऽते भगवती जनयामास दुर्जयम्.. 14.51 ..
1.4.m: She performed severe austerity for ten thousand years. / At the end of her austerity, the blessed woman gave birth to an invincible [son],

1.4.s:
putramapratikarmāṇamajeyaṃ vajraduśchidam..
sa jātāmātra evābhūtsarvaśā strārthapāragaḥ.. 14.52 ..
1.4.d:
पुत्रमप्रतिकर्माणमजेयं वज्रदुश्छिदम्..
स जातामात्र एवाभूत्सर्वशा स्त्रार्थपारगः.. 14.52 ..
1.4.m: a son of peerless deeds, unconquerable, difficult even for the vajra to cut. / As soon as he was born, he was a master of the meaning of all śāstras.

1.4.s:
uvāca mātaraṃ bhaktyā mātaḥ kiṃ karavāṇyaham..
tamuvāca tato hṛṣṭā ditirdaityādhipaṃ sutam.. 14.53 ..
1.4.d:
उवाच मातरं भक्त्या मातः किं करवाण्यहम्..
तमुवाच ततो हृष्टा दितिर्दैत्याधिपं सुतम्.. 14.53 ..
1.4.m: He spoke to his mother with devotion: "Mother, what shall I do?" / Then Diti, delighted, said to her son, the lord of the Daityas:

1.4.s:
bahavo me hatāḥ putrāḥ sahasrākṣeṇa putraka..
teṣaāmapacitiṃ kartumicche śakravadhādaham.. 14.54 ..
1.4.d:
बहवो मे हताः पुत्राः सहस्राक्षेण पुत्रक..
तेषआमपचितिं कर्तुमिच्छे शक्रवधादहम्.. 14.54 ..
1.4.m: "Many of my sons were killed by the thousand-eyed [Indra], dear son. / I wish to take vengeance on them by the slaying of Śakra."

1.4.s:
bāḍhamityeva saṃ procya jagāma tridivaṃ balī..
sasainyaṃ samare śakraṃ sa ca bāhvāyudho'jayat.. 14.55 ..
1.4.d:
बाढमित्येव सं प्रोच्य जगाम त्रिदिवं बली..
ससैन्यं समरे शक्रं स च बाह्वायुधोऽजयत्.. 14.55 ..
1.4.m: Saying, "So be it!", the mighty one went to the third heaven. / Having his arms as weapons, he conquered Śakra along with his army in battle.

1.4.s:
pādenākṛṣya deveṃdraṃ siṃhaḥ kṣudramṛgaṃ yathā..
māturaṃtikamāgacchadyācamānaṃ bhayāturam.. 14.56 ..
1.4.d:
पादेनाकृष्य देवेंद्रं सिंहः क्षुद्रमृगं यथा..
मातुरंतिकमागच्छद्याचमानं भयातुरम्.. 14.56 ..
1.4.m: Dragging the lord of gods by the foot like a lion drags a small deer, / he approached his mother while [Indra] was begging [for mercy], stricken with fear.

1.4.s:
etasminnaṃtare brahmā kaśyapaśca mahātapāḥ..
āgatā tatra saṃtrastāvatho brahmā jagāda tam.. 14.57 ..
1.4.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे ब्रह्मा कश्यपश्च महातपाः..
आगता तत्र संत्रस्तावथो ब्रह्मा जगाद तम्.. 14.57 ..
1.4.m: In the meantime, Brahmā and Kaśyapa of great austerity / arrived there in alarm; then Brahmā spoke to him:

1.4.s:
muṃcāmuṃ putra yācaṃtaṃ kimanena prayojanam..
avamāno vadhaḥ prokto vīrasaṃbhāvitasya ca.. 14.58 ..
1.4.d:
मुंचामुं पुत्र याचंतं किमनेन प्रयोजनम्..
अवमानो वधः प्रोक्तो वीरसंभावितस्य च.. 14.58 ..
1.4.m: "Release this one, son, who is begging; what is to be gained by this? / Humiliation is said to be death for one considered a hero.

1.4.s:
asmadvākyena yo mukto jīvannapi mṛto hi saḥ..
śatruṃ ye ghnaṃti samare na te vīrāḥ prakīrtitāḥ.. 14.59 ..
1.4.d:
अस्मद्वाक्येन यो मुक्तो जीवन्नपि मृतो हि सः..
शत्रुं ये घ्नंति समरे न ते वीराः प्रकीर्तिताः.. 14.59 ..
1.4.m: He who is released on our word is indeed dead even while living. / Those who kill an enemy in battle are not proclaimed heroes;

1.4.s:
kṛtvā mānapariglaniṃ ye muṃcaṃti varā hi te..
yatāmānyatamaṃ matvā tvayā māturvacaḥ kṛtam.. 14.60 ..
1.4.d:
कृत्वा मानपरिग्लनिं ये मुंचंति वरा हि ते..
यतामान्यतमं मत्वा त्वया मातुर्वचः कृतम्.. 14.60 ..
1.4.m: those who release [an enemy] after crushing his pride are the truly noble ones. / Considering it the foremost duty, you carried out the word of your mother;

1.4.s:
tathā piturvacaḥ kāryaṃ muṃcāmuṃ putra vāsavam..
etacchrutvā tu vajrāṃgaḥ praṇato vākyamabravīt.. 14.61 ..
1.4.d:
तथा पितुर्वचः कार्यं मुंचामुं पुत्र वासवम्..
एतच्छ्रुत्वा तु वज्रांगः प्रणतो वाक्यमब्रवीत्.. 14.61 ..
1.4.m: so also must the word of your father be carried out: release this Vāsava, son!" / Hearing this, Vajrāṅga bowed and spoke these words:

1.4.s:
na me kṛtyamanenāsti māturājñā kṛtā mayā..
tvaṃ surāsuranātho vai mama ca prapitāmahaḥ.. 14.62 ..
1.4.d:
न मे कृत्यमनेनास्ति मातुराज्ञा कृता मया..
त्वं सुरासुरनाथो वै मम च प्रपितामहः.. 14.62 ..
1.4.m: "I have no business with him; my mother's command was fulfilled by me. / You are indeed the lord of gods and asuras, and my great-grandfather.

1.4.s:
kariṣye tvadvaco deva eṣa muktaḥ śatakratuḥ..
na ca kāṃkṣe śakrabhuktāmimāṃ trailokyarājatām.. 14.63 ..
1.4.d:
करिष्ये त्वद्वचो देव एष मुक्तः शतक्रतुः..
न च कांक्षे शक्रभुक्तामिमां त्रैलोक्यराजताम्.. 14.63 ..
1.4.m: I will do your bidding, Lord; this Śatakratu is released. / Nor do I desire this sovereignty over the three worlds, enjoyed by Śakra,

1.4.s:
parabhuktā yathā nārī parabhuktāmivasrajam..
yacca tribhuvaneṣvasti sāraṃ tanmama kathyatām.. 14.64 ..
1.4.d:
परभुक्ता यथा नारी परभुक्तामिवस्रजम्..
यच्च त्रिभुवनेष्वस्ति सारं तन्मम कथ्यताम्.. 14.64 ..
1.4.m: just like a woman enjoyed by another, or like a garland worn by another. / Tell me that which is the essence in the three worlds."

1.4.s:
..brahmovāca..
tapaso na paraṃ kiṃcittapo hi mahatāṃ dhanam..
tapasā prāpyate sarvaṃ tapoyogyo'si putraka.. 14.65 ..
1.4.d:
..ब्रह्मोवाच..
तपसो न परं किंचित्तपो हि महतां धनम्..
तपसा प्राप्यते सर्वं तपोयोग्योऽसि पुत्रक.. 14.65 ..
1.4.m: Brahmā said: / "There is nothing higher than tapas; tapas indeed is the wealth of the great. / Everything is attained through tapas; you are worthy of tapas, dear son."

1.4.s:
..vajrāṃga uvāca..
tapase me ratirdeva na vighnaṃ tatra me bhavet..
tvatprasādena bhagavannityuktvā virarāma saḥ.. 14.66 ..
1.4.d:
..वज्रांग उवाच..
तपसे मे रतिर्देव न विघ्नं तत्र मे भवेत्..
त्वत्प्रसादेन भगवन्नित्युक्त्वा विरराम सः.. 14.66 ..
1.4.m: Vajrāṅga said: / "My delight is in tapas, Lord; let there be no obstacle to me there / by your grace, O Blessed One." Having spoken thus, he fell silent.

1.4.s:
..brahmovāca..
krūrabhāvaṃ parityajya yadīcchasi tapaḥ suta..
anayā cittabuddhyā tattvayāptaṃ janmanaḥ phalam.. 14.67 ..
1.4.d:
..ब्रह्मोवाच..
क्रूरभावं परित्यज्य यदीच्छसि तपः सुत..
अनया चित्तबुद्ध्या तत्त्वयाप्तं जन्मनः फलम्.. 14.67 ..
1.4.m: Brahmā said: / "Abandoning cruelty of disposition, if you desire tapas, son, / by this intention of mind, you have obtained the fruit of your birth."

1.4.s:
ityuktvā padmajaḥ kanyāṃ sasarjjayatalocanām..
tāmasmai pradadau devaḥ patnyarthaṃ padmasaṃbhavaḥ.. 14.68 ..
1.4.d:
इत्युक्त्वा पद्मजः कन्यां ससर्ज्जयतलोचनाम्..
तामस्मै प्रददौ देवः पत्न्यर्थं पद्मसंभवः.. 14.68 ..
1.4.m: Having spoken thus, the lotus-born Lord, born of the lotus, / created a long-eyed maiden and gave her to him for a wife.

1.4.s:
varāṃgīti ca nāmāsyāḥ kṛtavāṃśca pitāmahaḥ..
jagāma ca tato brahmā kaśyapena samaṃ divam.. 14.69 ..
1.4.d:
वरांगीति च नामास्याः कृतवांश्च पितामहः..
जगाम च ततो ब्रह्मा कश्यपेन समं दिवम्.. 14.69 ..
1.4.m: The grandfather gave her the name Varāṅgī. / And then Brahmā went to heaven together with Kaśyapa.

1.4.s:
vajrāṃgo'pi tayā sārdhaṃ jagāma tapase vanam..
ūrddhūbāhuḥ sa daityeṃdro'tiṣṭhadabdasahasrakam.. 14.70 ..
1.4.d:
वज्रांगोऽपि तया सार्धं जगाम तपसे वनम्..
ऊर्द्धूबाहुः स दैत्येंद्रोऽतिष्ठदब्दसहस्रकम्.. 14.70 ..
1.4.m: Vajrāṅga too, along with her, went to the forest for austerity. / That lord of Daityas stood with raised arms for a thousand years;

1.4.s:
kālaṃ kamalapatrākṣaḥ śuddhabuddhirmahātapāḥ..
tāvānadhomukhaḥ kālaṃ tāvatpaṃcāgnisādhakaḥ.. 14.71 ..
1.4.d:
कालं कमलपत्राक्षः शुद्धबुद्धिर्महातपाः..
तावानधोमुखः कालं तावत्पंचाग्निसाधकः.. 14.71 ..
1.4.m: the lotus-petal-eyed one of pure intellect and great tapas [stood thus] for that long; / for the same period head downwards, and for the same period practicing the five fires.

1.4.s:
nirāhāro ghoratapāstaporāśirajāyata..
tataḥ soṃ'tarjale cakre kālaṃ varṣasahasrakam.. 14.72 ..
1.4.d:
निराहारो घोरतपास्तपोराशिरजायत..
ततः सोंऽतर्जले चक्रे कालं वर्षसहस्रकम्.. 14.72 ..
1.4.m: Without food, performing fierce austerity, he became an embodiment of tapas. / Then he spent a thousand years under water.

1.4.s:
jalāṃtarapraviṣṭasya tasya patnī mahāvratā..
tasyaiva tīre sarasastatparā maunamāśritā.. 14.73 ..
1.4.d:
जलांतरप्रविष्टस्य तस्य पत्नी महाव्रता..
तस्यैव तीरे सरसस्तत्परा मौनमाश्रिता.. 14.73 ..
1.4.m: While he was submerged in the water, his wife of great vows, / devoted to him, maintained silence on the bank of that very lake.

1.4.s:
nirāhāraṃ patiṃ matvā tapastepe pativratā..
tasyāstapasi vartaṃtyā iṃdraścakre vibhīṣikām.. 14.74 ..
1.4.d:
निराहारं पतिं मत्वा तपस्तेपे पतिव्रता..
तस्यास्तपसि वर्तंत्या इंद्रश्चक्रे विभीषिकाम्.. 14.74 ..
1.4.m: Knowing her husband to be without food, the devoted wife performed austerity. / As she was engaged in tapas, Indra created terrifying apparitions.

1.4.s:
bhūtvā tu markaṭākārastasyāabhyāśamāgataḥ..
apavidhya dṛśaṃ tasyā mūtraviṣṭhe cakāra saḥ.. 14.75 ..
1.4.d:
भूत्वा तु मर्कटाकारस्तस्याअभ्याशमागतः..
अपविध्य दृशं तस्या मूत्रविष्ठे चकार सः.. 14.75 ..
1.4.m: Assuming the form of a monkey, he came near her; / casting his gaze away from her, he passed urine and feces.

1.4.s:
tathā vilolavasanāṃ vilolavadanāṃ tathā..
vilolakeśāṃ tāṃ cakre vidhitsustapasaḥ kṣatim.. 14.76 ..
1.4.d:
तथा विलोलवसनां विलोलवदनां तथा..
विलोलकेशां तां चक्रे विधित्सुस्तपसः क्षतिम्.. 14.76 ..
1.4.m: He made her garments disheveled, her face agitated, / and her hair disheveled, wishing to destroy her austerity.

1.4.s:
tataśca meṣarūpeṇa kleśaṃ tasyāścakāra saḥ..
tato bhujaṃgarūpeṇa baddhā caraṇayordvayoḥ.. 14.77 ..
1.4.d:
ततश्च मेषरूपेण क्लेशं तस्याश्चकार सः..
ततो भुजंगरूपेण बद्धा चरणयोर्द्वयोः.. 14.77 ..
1.4.m: Then, in the form of a ram, he inflicted torment on her. / Then, in the form of a serpent, having bound both her feet,

1.4.s:
apākarṣata dūraṃ sa tasmāddevabhṛtastathā..
tapobālācca sā tasya na vadhyatvaṃ jagāma ha.. 14.78 ..
1.4.d:
अपाकर्षत दूरं स तस्माद्देवभृतस्तथा..
तपोबालाच्च सा तस्य न वध्यत्वं जगाम ह.. 14.78 ..
1.4.m: he dragged her far away from that place where the god resided. / Yet by the power of his austerity, she did not meet with death.

1.4.s:
kṣamayā ca mahābhāgā krodhamaṇvapi nākarot..
tato gomāyurūpeṇa tamadūṣayadāśramam.. 14.79 ..
1.4.d:
क्षमया च महाभागा क्रोधमण्वपि नाकरोत्..
ततो गोमायुरूपेण तमदूषयदाश्रमम्.. 14.79 ..
1.4.m: And through forbearance, the noble woman did not display even the slightest anger. / Then, in the form of a jackal, he defiled that hermitage.

1.4.s:
agnirūpeṇa tasyāśca sa dadāha mahāśramam..
cakarṣa vāyurūpeṇa mahogreṇa ca tāṃ śubhām..
evaṃ sihavṛkādyābhirbhīṣikābhiḥ punaḥpunaḥ.. 14.80 ..
1.4.d:
अग्निरूपेण तस्याश्च स ददाह महाश्रमम्..
चकर्ष वायुरूपेण महोग्रेण च तां शुभाम्..
एवं सिहवृकाद्याभिर्भीषिकाभिः पुनःपुनः.. 14.80 ..
1.4.m: In the form of fire, he burned her great hermitage; / and in the form of a terribly fierce wind, he dragged that auspicious woman. / Thus, repeatedly with terrors such as lions and wolves,

1.4.s:
virarāma yadā naiva vajrāṃgamahiṣī tadā..
śailasya duṣṭatāṃ matvā śāpaṃ dātuṃ vyavasyata.. 14.81 ..
1.4.d:
विरराम यदा नैव वज्रांगमहिषी तदा..
शैलस्य दुष्टतां मत्वा शापं दातुं व्यवस्यत.. 14.81 ..
1.4.m: when the queen of Vajrāṅga did not desist at all, / then, thinking the mountain to be wicked, she prepared to utter a curse.

1.4.s:
tāṃ śāpābhimukhīṃ dṛṣṭvā śailaḥ puruṣāvigrahaḥ..
uvāca tāṃ varārohāṃ tvarayātha sulocanām.. 14.82 ..
1.4.d:
तां शापाभिमुखीं दृष्ट्वा शैलः पुरुषाविग्रहः..
उवाच तां वरारोहां त्वरयाथ सुलोचनाम्.. 14.82 ..
1.4.m: Seeing her about to curse, the mountain, assuming a human form, / quickly said to that fair-hipped, beautiful-eyed woman:

1.4.s:
..śaila uvāca..
nāhaṃ mahāvrate duṣṭaḥ sevyo'haṃ sarvadehinām..
atikhedaṃ karotyeṣa tataḥ kruddhastu vṛtrahā.. 14.83 ..
1.4.d:
..शैल उवाच..
नाहं महाव्रते दुष्टः सेव्योऽहं सर्वदेहिनाम्..
अतिखेदं करोत्येष ततः क्रुद्धस्तु वृत्रहा.. 14.83 ..
1.4.m: The mountain said: / "O woman of great vows, I am not wicked; I am to be sought for refuge by all embodied beings. / The slayer of Vṛtra [Indra], enraged, is the one causing excessive distress."

1.4.s:
etasminnaṃtare jātaḥ kālo varṣasahasrikaḥ..
tasminyāte sa bhagavānkāle kamalasaṃbhavaḥ.. 14.84 ..
1.4.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे जातः कालो वर्षसहस्रिकः..
तस्मिन्याते स भगवान्काले कमलसंभवः.. 14.84 ..
1.4.m: In the meantime, a period of a thousand years had passed. / When that time had passed, the blessed one born of the lotus,

1.4.s: tuṣṭaḥ provāca vajrāṃgaṃ tamāgamya jalāśaye.. 14.85 ..
1.4.d: तुष्टः प्रोवाच वज्रांगं तमागम्य जलाशये.. 14.85 ..
1.4.m: pleased, came to Vajrāṅga at the lake and said:

1.4.s:
..brahmovāca..
dadāmi sarvakāmāṃste uttiṣṭha ditinandana..
evamuktastadotthāya daityeṃdrastapaso nidhiḥ..
uvāca prāṃjalirvākyaṃ sarvalokapitāmaham.. 14.86 ..
1.4.d:
..ब्रह्मोवाच..
ददामि सर्वकामांस्ते उत्तिष्ठ दितिनन्दन..
एवमुक्तस्तदोत्थाय दैत्येंद्रस्तपसो निधिः..
उवाच प्रांजलिर्वाक्यं सर्वलोकपितामहम्.. 14.86 ..
1.4.m: Brahmā said: / "I grant you all your desires; arise, O son of Diti!" / Thus addressed, the lord of Daityas, a treasury of tapas, then arose / and, with folded hands, spoke words to the grandfather of all worlds:

1.4.s:
..vajrāṃga uvāca..
āsuro me'stu mā bhāvaḥ śakrarājye ca mā ratiḥ..
tapodharmaratiścāstu vṛṇomyetatpitāmaha.. 14.87 ..
1.4.d:
..वज्रांग उवाच..
आसुरो मेऽस्तु मा भावः शक्रराज्ये च मा रतिः..
तपोधर्मरतिश्चास्तु वृणोम्येतत्पितामह.. 14.87 ..
1.4.m: Vajrāṅga said: / "May I not have a demonic disposition, nor any delight in the kingdom of Śakra; / rather, let my delight be in austerity and dharma; this I choose, O Grandfather."

1.4.s:
evamastviti taṃ brahmā prāha vismitamānasaḥ..
upekṣate ca śakraṃ sa bhāvyarthaṃ ko'tivartate.. 14.88 ..
1.4.d:
एवमस्त्विति तं ब्रह्मा प्राह विस्मितमानसः..
उपेक्षते च शक्रं स भाव्यर्थं कोऽतिवर्तते.. 14.88 ..
1.4.m: Brahmā, his mind astonished, said to him: "So be it!" / And he disregarded Śakra: who can transcend that which is destined?

1.4.s:
ṛṣayo manujā devāḥ śivabrahmamukhā api..
bhāvyarthaṃ nāti vartaṃte velāmiva mahodadhiḥ.. 14.89 ..
1.4.d:
ऋषयो मनुजा देवाः शिवब्रह्ममुखा अपि..
भाव्यर्थं नाति वर्तंते वेलामिव महोदधिः.. 14.89 ..
1.4.m:
Seers, men, and gods, even Śiva, Brahmā, and the rest,
do not overstep what is destined to be, just as the great ocean [does not cross] the shore.

1.4.s:
iti ciṃtya viriṃco'pi tatraivāṃtaradhīyata..
vajrāṃgo'pi samāpte tu tapasi sthirasaṃyamaḥ.. 14.90 ..
1.4.d:
इति चिंत्य विरिंचोऽपि तत्रैवांतरधीयत..
वज्रांगोऽपि समाप्ते तु तपसि स्थिरसंयमः.. 14.90 ..
1.4.m:
Reflecting thus, Viriñca vanished right there.
Vajrāṅga too, when his austerity was completed, steady in self-restraint,

1.4.s:
āhāramicchansvāṃ bhāryāṃ na dadarśāśrame svake..
bhāryāhīno'phalaśceti sa saṃciṃtya itastataḥ.. 14.91 ..
1.4.d:
आहारमिच्छन्स्वां भार्यां न ददर्शाश्रमे स्वके..
भार्याहीनोऽफलश्चेति स संचिंत्य इतस्ततः.. 14.91 ..
1.4.m:
desiring food, did not see his wife in his hermitage.
Thinking, "Without a wife one is fruitless," he looked here and there

1.4.s:
vilokayansvakāṃ bhāryāṃ vidhitsuḥ karma naityakam..
vilokayandadarśātha ihāmutra sahayinīm.. 14.92 ..
1.4.d:
विलोकयन्स्वकां भार्यां विधित्सुः कर्म नैत्यकम्..
विलोकयन्ददर्शाथ इहामुत्र सहयिनीम्.. 14.92 ..
1.4.m:
seeking his wife, wishing to perform his daily rite.
As he looked, he then saw his companion for this world and the next,

1.4.s:
rudantīṃ svāṃ priyāṃ dīnāṃ tarupracchāditānanām..
tāṃ vilokya tato daityaḥ provāca parisāṃtvayan.. 14.93 ..
1.4.d:
रुदन्तीं स्वां प्रियां दीनां तरुप्रच्छादिताननाम्..
तां विलोक्य ततो दैत्यः प्रोवाच परिसांत्वयन्.. 14.93 ..
1.4.m:
his dear wife weeping, miserable, her face covered by trees.
Seeing her then, the daitya spoke, consoling her:

1.4.s:
..vajrāṃga uvāca..
kena te'pakṛtaṃ bhīru vartaṃtyāstapasi svake..
kathaṃ rodiṣi vā bāle mayi jīvati bhartari..
kaṃ vā kāmaṃ prayacchāmi śīghraṃ prabrūhi bhāmini.. 14.94 ..
1.4.d:
..वज्रांग उवाच..
केन तेऽपकृतं भीरु वर्तंत्यास्तपसि स्वके..
कथं रोदिषि वा बाले मयि जीवति भर्तरि..
कं वा कामं प्रयच्छामि शीघ्रं प्रब्रूहि भामिनि.. 14.94 ..
1.4.m:
Vajrāṅga said:
By whom have you been wronged, timid one, while remaining in your own austerity?
Or why do you weep, young woman, while I, your husband, am alive?
Or what desire shall I fulfill for you? Speak quickly, radiant lady.

1.4.s:
gṛheśvarīṃ sadguṇabhūṣitāṃ śubhāṃ paṃgvaṃdhayogena patiṃ sametām..
na lālayetpūrayennaiva kāmaṃ sa kiṃ pumānna pumānme matosti.. 14.95 ..
iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ prathame māheśvarakhaṇḍe kaumārikākhaṇḍe kumāreśvaramāhātmye vajrāṃgetihāsavarṇanaṃ nāma caturdaśo'dhyāyaḥ.. 14 .. cha ..
1.4.d:
गृहेश्वरीं सद्गुणभूषितां शुभां पंग्वंधयोगेन पतिं समेताम्..
न लालयेत्पूरयेन्नैव कामं स किं पुमान्न पुमान्मे मतोस्ति.. 14.95 ..
इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां प्रथमे माहेश्वरखण्डे कौमारिकाखण्डे कुमारेश्वरमाहात्म्ये वज्रांगेतिहासवर्णनं नाम चतुर्दशोऽध्यायः.. 14 .. छ ..
1.4.m:
He who would not cherish the mistress of his house, adorned with good virtues, auspicious,
who has joined her husband like the union of the lame and the blind, nor fulfill her desire—
is he a man? In my opinion, he is no man.
Thus ends the fourteenth chapter, named "Description of the Account of Vajrāṅga," in the Kumāreśvaramāhātmya of the Kaumārikākhaṇḍa, in the first [book], the Māheśvarakhaṇḍa, of the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.

1.4.s:
..varāṃgyuvāca..
nāśitāsmyapaviddhāsmi trāsitā pīḍitāsmi ca..
raudroṇa devanāthena naṣṭanāthena bhūriśaḥ.. 15.1 ..
1.4.d:
..वरांग्युवाच..
नाशितास्म्यपविद्धास्मि त्रासिता पीडितास्मि च..
रौद्रोण देवनाथेन नष्टनाथेन भूरिशः.. 15.1 ..
1.4.m:
Varāṅgī said:
I have been ruined, cast away, terrified, and tormented
repeatedly by the terrible lord of the gods, who acted like one having no master.

1.4.s:
duḥkhapāramapaśyaṃtī prāṇāṃstyaktuṃ vyavasthitā..
putraṃ me ghoraduḥkhasya tārakaṃ dehi cetkṛpā.. 15.2 ..
1.4.d:
दुःखपारमपश्यंती प्राणांस्त्यक्तुं व्यवस्थिता..
पुत्रं मे घोरदुःखस्य तारकं देहि चेत्कृपा.. 15.2 ..
1.4.m:
Seeing no end to my sorrow, I have resolved to give up my life.
Grant me a son who will be a deliverer from this dreadful sorrow, if you have compassion.

1.4.s:
evamuktastu daityeṃdro duḥkhito'ciṃtayaddhṛdi..
āsureṣvapi bhāveṣu spṛhā yadyapi nāsti me.. 15.3 ..
1.4.d:
एवमुक्तस्तु दैत्येंद्रो दुःखितोऽचिंतयद्धृदि..
आसुरेष्वपि भावेषु स्पृहा यद्यपि नास्ति मे.. 15.3 ..
1.4.m:
Addressed thus, the lord of the daityas, distressed, thought in his heart:
"Even though I have no desire for demonic states of mind,

1.4.s:
tathāpi manye śāstraibhyastvanukaṃpyā priyeti yat..
sarvāśramānupādāya svāśrameṇa kalatravān.. 15.4 ..
1.4.d:
तथापि मन्ये शास्त्रैभ्यस्त्वनुकंप्या प्रियेति यत्..
सर्वाश्रमानुपादाय स्वाश्रमेण कलत्रवान्.. 15.4 ..
1.4.m:
nevertheless, from the scriptures I consider that a beloved wife is to be pitied,
because a man with a wife, having taken up all life-stages into his own life-stage,

1.4.s:
vyasanārṇavamatyeti jalayānairivārṇavam..
yāmāśrityeṃdriyārātīndurjayānitarāśrayaiḥ.. 15.5 ..
1.4.d:
व्यसनार्णवमत्येति जलयानैरिवार्णवम्..
यामाश्रित्येंद्रियारातीन्दुर्जयानितराश्रयैः.. 15.5 ..
1.4.m:
crosses over the ocean of misfortune as if [crossing] an ocean with water-vessels.
Relying upon whom, householders easily conquered the enemies [that are] the senses,

1.4.s:
gehino helayā jigyurdasyūndūrga patiryathā..
na ke'pi prabhavastāṃ cāpyanukartuṃ gṛheśvarīm.. 15.6 ..
1.4.d:
गेहिनो हेलया जिग्युर्दस्यून्दूर्ग पतिर्यथा..
न केऽपि प्रभवस्तां चाप्यनुकर्तुं गृहेश्वरीम्.. 15.6 ..
1.4.m:
which are hard to conquer by other stages of life, just as a fortress commander [vanquishes] bandits;
and no one is able to emulate the mistress of the house.

1.4.s:
athāyuṣā vā kārtsnyena dharme ditsuryathaiva ca..
yasyāṃ bhavati cātmaiva tato jāyā nigadyate.. 15.7 ..
1.4.d:
अथायुषा वा कार्त्स्न्येन धर्मे दित्सुर्यथैव च..
यस्यां भवति चात्मैव ततो जाया निगद्यते.. 15.7 ..
1.4.m:
Moreover, as one wishes to apply oneself to duty throughout life or in its entirety;
because one's self comes to be in her, she is therefore called jāyā.

1.4.s:
bhartavyā eva yasmācca tasmādbhāryeti sā smṛtā..
sā eva gṛhamuktaṃ ca gṛhīṇī sā tataḥ smṛtā.. 15.8 ..
1.4.d:
भर्तव्या एव यस्माच्च तस्माद्भार्येति सा स्मृता..
सा एव गृहमुक्तं च गृहीणी सा ततः स्मृता.. 15.8 ..
1.4.m:
And since she must be maintained, she is therefore remembered as bhāryā.
She alone is called the house, and therefore she is remembered as the housewife (gṛhiṇī).

1.4.s:
saṃsārakalmaṣāttrātrī kalatramiti sā tataḥ..
evaṃvidhāṃ priyāṃ ko vai nānukaṃpitumarhati.. 15.9 ..
1.4.d:
संसारकल्मषात्त्रात्री कलत्रमिति सा ततः..
एवंविधां प्रियां को वै नानुकंपितुमर्हति.. 15.9 ..
1.4.m:
She protects from the taint of worldly existence, hence she is [called] a wife (kalatra).
Who indeed ought not to have compassion for such a beloved?

1.4.s:
trīṇi jyotīṃṣi puruṣa iti vai devalo'bravīt..
bhāryā karma ca vidyā ca saṃsādhyaṃ yatnatastrayam.. 15.10 ..
1.4.d:
त्रीणि ज्योतींषि पुरुष इति वै देवलोऽब्रवीत्..
भार्या कर्म च विद्या च संसाध्यं यत्नतस्त्रयम्.. 15.10 ..
1.4.m:
Devala indeed said that a man has three lights:
wife, ritual action, and sacred knowledge; these three must be secured with effort.

1.4.s:
tadenāṃ pīḍitāṃ cedyaḥ patirbhūtvā na pālaye..
tato yāsye śāstravādānnarakāṃtaṃ na saṃśayaḥ.. 15.11 ..
1.4.d:
तदेनां पीडितां चेद्यः पतिर्भूत्वा न पालये..
ततो यास्ये शास्त्रवादान्नरकांतं न संशयः.. 15.11 ..
1.4.m:
Therefore, if I, being her husband, do not protect her when she is tormented,
then according to the declarations of the scriptures I shall go to the depth of hell, without a doubt.

1.4.s:
aha mapyenamiṃdraṃ vai śakto jetuṃ yathā'nṛṇām..
punaḥ kāmaṃ kariṣye'syā dāsye putraūṃ mahābalam.. 15.12 ..
1.4.d:
अह मप्येनमिंद्रं वै शक्तो जेतुं यथाऽनृणाम्..
पुनः कामं करिष्येऽस्या दास्ये पुत्रऊं महाबलम्.. 15.12 ..
1.4.m:
I too am capable of conquering this Indra so as to be free from debt.
I shall fulfill her desire again; I will give her a son of great strength."

1.4.s:
iti saṃciṃtya vajrāṃgaḥ kopavyākulalocanaḥ..
pratikartuṃ maheṃdrāya tapo bhūyo vyavasyata.. 15.13 ..
1.4.d:
इति संचिंत्य वज्रांगः कोपव्याकुललोचनः..
प्रतिकर्तुं महेंद्राय तपो भूयो व्यवस्यत.. 15.13 ..
1.4.m:
Reflecting thus, Vajrāṅga, his eyes agitated with anger,
resolved upon austerity once more in order to retaliate against the great Indra.

1.4.s:
jñātvā tu tasya saṃkalpaṃ brahmā krūrataraṃ punaḥ..
ājagāma tvarāyukto yatrā'sau ditinaṃdanaḥ.. 15.14 ..
1.4.d:
ज्ञात्वा तु तस्य संकल्पं ब्रह्मा क्रूरतरं पुनः..
आजगाम त्वरायुक्तो यत्राऽसौ दितिनंदनः.. 15.14 ..
1.4.m:
Knowing his intention, which was even fiercer,
Brahmā came with haste to where that son of Diti was.

1.4.s: uvācainaṃ sa bhagavānprabhurmadhurayā girā.. 15.15 ..
1.4.d: उवाचैनं स भगवान्प्रभुर्मधुरया गिरा.. 15.15 ..
1.4.m: The Lord, the master, spoke to him with sweet words.

1.4.s:
..brahmovāca..
kimarthaṃ bhūya eva tvaṃ niyamaṃ krūramicchasi..
āhārābhimukho daitya tanme brūhi mahāvrataḥ.. 15.16 ..
1.4.d:
..ब्रह्मोवाच..
किमर्थं भूय एव त्वं नियमं क्रूरमिच्छसि..
आहाराभिमुखो दैत्य तन्मे ब्रूहि महाव्रतः.. 15.16 ..
1.4.m:
Brahmā said:
For what purpose do you wish for a harsh observance yet again?
Having turned toward food, O daitya of great vows, tell that to me.

1.4.s:
yāvadabdasahasreṇa nirāhāreṇa vai phalam..
tyajatā prāptamāhāraṃ labdhaṃ te kṣaṇamātrataḥ.. 15.17 ..
1.4.d:
यावदब्दसहस्रेण निराहारेण वै फलम्..
त्यजता प्राप्तमाहारं लब्धं ते क्षणमात्रतः.. 15.17 ..
1.4.m:
The fruit that is obtained by fasting for a thousand years,
was obtained by you in merely an instant when you gave up food that was received.

1.4.s:
tyāgo hyaprāptakāmānāṃ na tathā ca guruḥ smṛtaḥ..
yathā prāptaṃ parityajya kāmaṃ kamalalocana..
śrutvaitadbrahmaṇo vākyaṃ daityaḥ prāṃjalirabravīt.. 15.18 ..
1.4.d:
त्यागो ह्यप्राप्तकामानां न तथा च गुरुः स्मृतः..
यथा प्राप्तं परित्यज्य कामं कमललोचन..
श्रुत्वैतद्ब्रह्मणो वाक्यं दैत्यः प्रांजलिरब्रवीत्.. 15.18 ..
1.4.m:
For the abandonment [of pleasures] by those who have not obtained their desires is not considered as great
as when one renounces a desire that has been obtained, O lotus-eyed one.
Having heard these words of Brahmā, the daitya, with folded hands, said:

1.4.s:
..daitya uvāca..
patnyarthe'haṃ kariṣyāmi tapo ghoraṃ pitāmaha..
putrārthamudyataścāhaṃ yaḥ syādgīrvāṇadarpahā.. 15.19 ..
1.4.d:
..दैत्य उवाच..
पत्न्यर्थेऽहं करिष्यामि तपो घोरं पितामह..
पुत्रार्थमुद्यतश्चाहं यः स्याद्गीर्वाणदर्पहा.. 15.19 ..

1.4.s:
etacchrutvā vaco devaḥ padmagarbhodbhavastadā..
uvāca daityarājānaṃ prasannaścaturānanaḥ.. 15.20 ..
1.4.d:
एतच्छ्रुत्वा वचो देवः पद्मगर्भोद्भवस्तदा..
उवाच दैत्यराजानं प्रसन्नश्चतुराननः.. 15.20 ..
1.4.m:
Hearing this speech, the god born from the lotus womb,
the four-faced one, then, pleased, spoke to the king of the daityas:

1.4.s:
..brahmovāca..
alaṃ te tapasā vatsa mā kleśe vistare viśa..
putraste tārakonāma bhaviṣyati mahābalaḥ.. 15.21 ..
1.4.d:
..ब्रह्मोवाच..
अलं ते तपसा वत्स मा क्लेशे विस्तरे विश..
पुत्रस्ते तारकोनाम भविष्यति महाबलः.. 15.21 ..
1.4.m:
Brahmā said:
Enough of your austerity, my child; do not enter into the extent of distress.
You shall have a son of great strength named Tāraka,

1.4.s:
devasīmaṃtinīkāmyadhammillakavimokṣaṇaḥ..
ityukto daityarājastu praṇamya prapitāmaham.. 15.22 ..
1.4.d:
देवसीमंतिनीकाम्यधम्मिल्लकविमोक्षणः..
इत्युक्तो दैत्यराजस्तु प्रणम्य प्रपितामहम्.. 15.22 ..
1.4.m:
who will loosen the braids of hair desired by the women of the gods.
Spoken to thus, the king of the daityas, bowing to the Great-grandfather,

1.4.s:
visṛjya gatvā mahiṣīṃ naṃdayā māsa tāṃ mudā..
tau daṃpatī kṛtārthau ca jagmatuścāśramaṃ tadā.. 15.23 ..
1.4.d:
विसृज्य गत्वा महिषीं नंदया मास तां मुदा..
तौ दंपती कृतार्थौ च जग्मतुश्चाश्रमं तदा.. 15.23 ..
1.4.m:
having taken leave and gone to his queen, delighted her with joy.
And the couple, having achieved their purpose, then went to their hermitage.

1.4.s:
āhitaṃ ca tato garbhaṃ varāṃgī varavarṇinī..
pūrṇaṃ varṣasahasraṃ tu dadhārodara eva hi.. 15.24 ..
1.4.d:
आहितं च ततो गर्भं वरांगी वरवर्णिनी..
पूर्णं वर्षसहस्रं तु दधारोदर एव हि.. 15.24 ..
1.4.m:
And then the fair-complexioned Varāṅgī, having conceived an embryo,
bore it in her womb indeed for a full thousand years.

1.4.s:
tato varṣasahasrāṃte varāṃgī samasūyata..
jāyamāne tu daityeṃdre tasmim̐llokabhayaṃkare.. 15.25 ..
1.4.d:
ततो वर्षसहस्रांते वरांगी समसूयत..
जायमाने तु दैत्येंद्रे तस्मिम्̐ल्लोकभयंकरे.. 15.25 ..
1.4.m:
Then, at the end of the thousand years, Varāṅgī gave birth.
While that lord of the daityas, terrifying to the worlds, was being born,

1.4.s:
cacāla sakalā pṛthvī proddhūtāśca mahārṇavā..
celurdharādharāścāpi vavurvātā vibhīṣaṇāḥ.. 15.26 ..
1.4.d:
चचाल सकला पृथ्वी प्रोद्धूताश्च महार्णवा..
चेलुर्धराधराश्चापि ववुर्वाता विभीषणाः.. 15.26 ..
1.4.m:
the entire earth trembled, and the great oceans were agitated;
the mountains also shook, and terrifying winds blew.

1.4.s:
jepurjapyaṃ munivarā vyādhaviddhā mṛgā iva..
jahuḥ kāṃtiṃ ca sūryādyā nīhārāśchāṃdayandiśaḥ.. 15.27 ..
1.4.d:
जेपुर्जप्यं मुनिवरा व्याधविद्धा मृगा इव..
जहुः कांतिं च सूर्याद्या नीहाराश्छांदयन्दिशः.. 15.27 ..
1.4.m:
The best of seers muttered prayers like deer pierced by a hunter;
the sun and the others lost their luster, and mists covered the directions.

1.4.s:
jāte mahāsure tasminsarva eva mahāsurāḥ..
ājagmurharṣitāstatra tathā cāsurayoṣitaḥ.. 15.28 ..
1.4.d:
जाते महासुरे तस्मिन्सर्व एव महासुराः..
आजग्मुर्हर्षितास्तत्र तथा चासुरयोषितः.. 15.28 ..
1.4.m:
When that great asura was born, all the great asuras
arrived there, delighted, and likewise the asura women.

1.4.s:
jagurharṣasamāviṣṭā nanṛtuścāsurāṃganāḥ..
tato mahotsave jāte dānavānāṃ pṛthāsuta.. 15.29 ..
1.4.d:
जगुर्हर्षसमाविष्टा ननृतुश्चासुरांगनाः..
ततो महोत्सवे जाते दानवानां पृथासुत.. 15.29 ..
1.4.m:
Filled with joy, the asura women sang and danced.
Then, when the great festival of the dānavas took place, O son of Pṛthā,

1.4.s:
viṣaṇṇamanaso devāḥ samaheṃdrāstadābhavan..
jātāmātrastu daityeṃdrastārakaścaṃḍavikramaḥ.. 15.30 ..
1.4.d:
विषण्णमनसो देवाः समहेंद्रास्तदाभवन्..
जातामात्रस्तु दैत्येंद्रस्तारकश्चंडविक्रमः.. 15.30 ..
1.4.m:
the gods, along with the great Indra, became despondent in mind.
As soon as he was born, Tāraka, the lord of the daityas of fierce valor,

1.4.s:
abhiṣikto'suro daityaiḥ kuraṃgamahiṣādibhiḥ..
sarvāsuramahārājye yutaḥ sarvairmahāsuraiḥ.. 15.31 ..
1.4.d:
अभिषिक्तोऽसुरो दैत्यैः कुरंगमहिषादिभिः..
सर्वासुरमहाराज्ये युतः सर्वैर्महासुरैः.. 15.31 ..
1.4.m:
was consecrated by the daityas Kuraṅga, Mahiṣa, and others,
joined by all the great asuras, into the great sovereignty of all asuras.

1.4.s:
sa tu prāptamahārājyastārakaḥ pāṃḍusattama..
uvāca dānavaśreṣṭhānyuktiyuktamidaṃ vacaḥ.. 15.32 ..
1.4.d:
स तु प्राप्तमहाराज्यस्तारकः पांडुसत्तम..
उवाच दानवश्रेष्ठान्युक्तियुक्तमिदं वचः.. 15.32 ..
1.4.m:
Having attained the great sovereignty, Tāraka, O best of Pāṇḍus,
spoke these words endowed with reason to the foremost dānavas:

1.4.s:
śrṛṇudhvamasurāḥ sarve vākyaṃ mama mahābalāḥ..
śrutvā vaḥ stheyasī buddhiḥ kriyatāṃ vacane mama.. 15.33 ..
1.4.d:
श्रृणुध्वमसुराः सर्वे वाक्यं मम महाबलाः..
श्रुत्वा वः स्थेयसी बुद्धिः क्रियतां वचने मम.. 15.33 ..
1.4.m:
"Listen, all you asuras of great strength, to my words.
Having heard, let your intellect remain firm upon my instruction.

1.4.s:
asmākaṃ jātidharmeṇa virūḍhaṃ vairamakṣayam..
kariṣyāmyahaṃ tadvairaṃ teṣāṃ ca vijayāya ca.. 15.34 ..
1.4.d:
अस्माकं जातिधर्मेण विरूढं वैरमक्षयम्..
करिष्याम्यहं तद्वैरं तेषां च विजयाय च.. 15.34 ..
1.4.m:
By the nature of our kind, an imperishable enmity has grown;
I shall wage that enmity both [for our duty] and for victory over them."

1.4.s:
kiṃ tu tattapasā sādhyaṃ manyehaṃ surasaṃgamam..
tasmādādau kariṣyāmi tapo ghoraṃ danoḥ sutāḥ.. 15.35 ..
1.4.d:
किं तु तत्तपसा साध्यं मन्येहं सुरसंगमम्..
तस्मादादौ करिष्यामि तपो घोरं दनोः सुताः.. 15.35 ..
1.4.m: "However, I consider that confronting the gods must be accomplished through austerity. / Therefore, O sons of Danu, I shall first perform severe austerity.

1.4.s:
tataḥ surānvijeṣyāmo bhokṣyāmo'tha jagattrayam..
yuktopāyo'hi puruṣaḥ sthiraśrīreva jāyate.. 15.36 ..
1.4.d:
ततः सुरान्विजेष्यामो भोक्ष्यामोऽथ जगत्त्रयम्..
युक्तोपायोऽहि पुरुषः स्थिरश्रीरेव जायते.. 15.36 ..
1.4.m: Then we will conquer the gods and enjoy the three worlds. / For a man who employs the proper means is indeed one whose fortune becomes stable.

1.4.s:
ayuktaścapalaḥ prāptāmapi rakṣitumakṣamaḥ..
tacchrutvā dānavāḥ sarve vākyaṃ tasyāsurasya tu.. 15.37 ..
1.4.d:
अयुक्तश्चपलः प्राप्तामपि रक्षितुमक्षमः..
तच्छ्रुत्वा दानवाः सर्वे वाक्यं तस्यासुरस्य तु.. 15.37 ..
1.4.m: One who is improper and unsteady is unable to preserve even what has been obtained." / Having heard that speech of that asura, all the dānavas,

1.4.s:
sādhusādhvityathocuste vacanaṃ tasya vismitāḥ..
so'gacchatpāriyātrasya gireḥ kaṃdaramuttamam.. 15.38 ..
1.4.d:
साधुसाध्वित्यथोचुस्ते वचनं तस्य विस्मिताः..
सोऽगच्छत्पारियात्रस्य गिरेः कंदरमुत्तमम्.. 15.38 ..
1.4.m: amazed, said to him: "Excellent! Excellent!" / He then went to an excellent cave of the Pāriyātra mountain,

1.4.s:
sarvartukusumākīrṇanānauṣadhividipitam..
nānādhāturasasrāvicitranānāgṛhāśrayam.. 15.39 ..
1.4.d:
सर्वर्तुकुसुमाकीर्णनानौषधिविदिपितम्..
नानाधातुरसस्राविचित्रनानागृहाश्रयम्.. 15.39 ..
1.4.m: strewn with flowers of all seasons, illuminated by various herbs, / affording shelter in diverse caverns that were wondrous with the flow of essences of various minerals,

1.4.s:
anekākārabahulaṃ pṛthakpakṣikulākulam..
nānāprasravaṇopetaṃ nānāvidhajalāśayam.. 15.40 ..
1.4.d:
अनेकाकारबहुलं पृथक्पक्षिकुलाकुलम्..
नानाप्रस्रवणोपेतं नानाविधजलाशयम्.. 15.40 ..
1.4.m: filled with manifold forms, teeming with various flocks of birds, / endowed with diverse cascades, and possessing various bodies of water.

1.4.s:
prāpya tatkaṃdaraṃ daityaścakāra vipulaṃ tapaḥ..
vahanpāśupatīṃ dīkṣāṃ paṃca maṃtrāñjajāpa saḥ.. 15.41 ..
1.4.d:
प्राप्य तत्कंदरं दैत्यश्चकार विपुलं तपः..
वहन्पाशुपतीं दीक्षां पंच मंत्राञ्जजाप सः.. 15.41 ..
1.4.m: Having reached that cave, the daitya performed immense austerity. / Holding the Pāśupata initiation, he chanted the five mantras.

1.4.s:
nirāhāraḥ paṃcatapā varṣāyutamabhūtkila..
tataḥ svadehādutkṛttya karṣaṃkarṣaṃ dinedine.. 15.42 ..
1.4.d:
निराहारः पंचतपा वर्षायुतमभूत्किल..
ततः स्वदेहादुत्कृत्त्य कर्षंकर्षं दिनेदिने.. 15.42 ..
1.4.m: Without food, performing the five fires austerity, he spent ten thousand years indeed. / Then, cutting a karṣa [of flesh] from his own body day after day,

1.4.s:
māṃsasyāgnau juhāvaiva tato nirmāṃsatāṃ gataḥ..
tato nirmāṃsadehaḥ sa taporāśirajāyata.. 15.43 ..
1.4.d:
मांसस्याग्नौ जुहावैव ततो निर्मांसतां गतः..
ततो निर्मांसदेहः स तपोराशिरजायत.. 15.43 ..
1.4.m: he offered flesh into the fire; thereby he became fleshless. / Then, his body stripped of flesh, he became a mass of austerity.

1.4.s:
jajvaluḥ sarvabhūtāni tejasā tasya sarvataḥ..
udvignāśca surāḥ sarve tapasā tasya bhīṣitāḥ.. 15.44 ..
1.4.d:
जज्वलुः सर्वभूतानि तेजसा तस्य सर्वतः..
उद्विग्नाश्च सुराः सर्वे तपसा तस्य भीषिताः.. 15.44 ..
1.4.m: All living beings blazed up on all sides from his brilliance, / and all the gods became agitated, terrified by his austerity.

1.4.s:
etasminnaṃtare brahmā paramaṃ toṣamāgataḥ..
tārakasya varaṃ dātuṃ jagāma śikharaṃ gireḥ.. 15.45 ..
1.4.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे ब्रह्मा परमं तोषमागतः..
तारकस्य वरं दातुं जगाम शिखरं गिरेः.. 15.45 ..
1.4.m: At that juncture, Brahmā attained the highest satisfaction. / To grant a boon to Tāraka, he went to the peak of the mountain.

1.4.s:
prāpya taṃ śailarājānaṃ haṃsasyaṃdanamāsthitaḥ..
uvāca tārakaṃ devo girā madhurayā tadā.. 15.46 ..
1.4.d:
प्राप्य तं शैलराजानं हंसस्यंदनमास्थितः..
उवाच तारकं देवो गिरा मधुरया तदा.. 15.46 ..
1.4.m: Having reached that king of mountains, seated upon his swan-vehicle, / the god then addressed Tāraka in a sweet voice:

1.4.s:
..brahmovāca..
uttiṣṭha putra tapaso nāstyasādhyaṃ tavādhunā..
varaṃ vṛṇīṣvābhimataṃ yatte manasi vartate.. 15.47 ..
1.4.d:
..ब्रह्मोवाच..
उत्तिष्ठ पुत्र तपसो नास्त्यसाध्यं तवाधुना..
वरं वृणीष्वाभिमतं यत्ते मनसि वर्तते.. 15.47 ..
1.4.m: Brahmā said: / "Arise, son, from your austerity! Nothing is impossible for you now. / Choose the desired boon that dwells in your mind."

1.4.s: ityuktastārako daityaḥ prāṃjaliḥ prāha taṃ vibhum.. 15.48 ..
1.4.d: इत्युक्तस्तारको दैत्यः प्रांजलिः प्राह तं विभुम्.. 15.48 ..
1.4.m: Being thus addressed, the daitya Tāraka, with folded palms, spoke to the lord:

1.4.s:
..tāraka uvāca..
vayaṃ prabho jātidharmāḥ kṛtavairāḥ sahamaraiḥ..
taiśca niḥśeṣitā daityāḥ kṛtāḥ krūrainṛśaṃ savat.. 15.49 ..
1.4.d:
..तारक उवाच..
वयं प्रभो जातिधर्माः कृतवैराः सहमरैः..
तैश्च निःशेषिता दैत्याः कृताः क्रूरैनृशं सवत्.. 15.49 ..
1.4.m: Tāraka said: / "O Lord, by our inherent nature we have incurred enmity with the immortals, / and by them the daityas were wiped out, being treated cruelly and mercilessly.

1.4.s:
teṣāmahaṃ samuddhartā bhaveyamiti me matiḥ..
avadhyaḥ sarvabhūtānāmastrāṇāṃ ca mahaujasām.. 15.50 ..
1.4.d:
तेषामहं समुद्धर्ता भवेयमिति मे मतिः..
अवध्यः सर्वभूतानामस्त्राणां च महौजसाम्.. 15.50 ..
1.4.m: My thought is: 'May I be their rescuer! / May I be invulnerable to all living beings, and to weapons of great power,

1.4.s:
syāmahaṃ cāmaraiścaiṣa varo mama hṛdisthitaḥ..
etanme dehi deveśa nānyaṃ vai rocaye varam.. 15.51 ..
1.4.d:
स्यामहं चामरैश्चैष वरो मम हृदिस्थितः..
एतन्मे देहि देवेश नान्यं वै रोचये वरम्.. 15.51 ..
1.4.m: and also to the immortals!' This is the boon that lies in my heart. / Grant this to me, O Lord of the gods; I do not desire any other boon."

1.4.s:
tamuvāca tato daityaṃ viraṃco'maranāyakaḥ..
na yujyate vinā mṛtyuṃ dehino dehadhāraṇam..
jātasya hi dhruvo mṛtyuḥ satyametacchrutīritam.. 15.52 ..
1.4.d:
तमुवाच ततो दैत्यं विरंचोऽमरनायकः..
न युज्यते विना मृत्युं देहिनो देहधारणम्..
जातस्य हि ध्रुवो मृत्युः सत्यमेतच्छ्रुतीरितम्.. 15.52 ..
1.4.m: Then Virañci, the leader of the immortals, said to that daitya: / "For an embodied being, holding a body without death is not proper; / for death is certain for one who is born—this is the truth stated by the sacred tradition.

1.4.s:
iti saṃciṃtya varaya varaṃ yasmānna śaṃkase..
tataḥ saṃciṃtya daityeṃdraḥ śiśutaḥ saptavāsarāt.. 15.53 ..
1.4.d:
इति संचिंत्य वरय वरं यस्मान्न शंकसे..
ततः संचिंत्य दैत्येंद्रः शिशुतः सप्तवासरात्.. 15.53 ..
1.4.m: Reflecting on this, choose a boon from which you have no fear." / Then the lord of the daityas, having reflected, [chose death only] from an infant of seven days.

1.4.s:
..tāraka uvāca..
vāsarāṇāṃ ca saptānāṃ varjayitvā tu bālakam..
devānāmapyavadhyo'haṃ bhūyāsaṃ tena yācitaḥ.. 15.54 ..
1.4.d:
..तारक उवाच..
वासराणां च सप्तानां वर्जयित्वा तु बालकम्..
देवानामप्यवध्योऽहं भूयासं तेन याचितः.. 15.54 ..
1.4.m: Tāraka said: / "Except for an infant of seven days, / may I be invulnerable even to the gods—this is requested by me!"

1.4.s:
vavre mahāsuro mṛtyuṃ brahmāṇaṃ mānamohitaḥ..
brahmā proce tatastaṃ ca tatheti haravākyataḥ.. 15.55 ..
1.4.d:
वव्रे महासुरो मृत्युं ब्रह्माणं मानमोहितः..
ब्रह्मा प्रोचे ततस्तं च तथेति हरवाक्यतः.. 15.55 ..
1.4.m: Deluded by pride, the great asura chose [his] death from Brahmā. / Brahmā then said to him, "So be it," according to the word of Hara.

1.4.s:
jagāma tridivaṃ devo daityo'pi svakamālayam..
uttīrṇaṃ tapasastaṃ ca daityaṃ daityeśvarāstadā.. 15.56 ..
1.4.d:
जगाम त्रिदिवं देवो दैत्योऽपि स्वकमालयम्..
उत्तीर्णं तपसस्तं च दैत्यं दैत्येश्वरास्तदा.. 15.56 ..
1.4.m: The god went to heaven, and the daitya also went to his own abode. / When that daitya emerged from his austerity, the lords of the daityas then

1.4.s:
parivavruḥ phalākīrṇaṃ vṛkṣaṃ śakunayo yathā..
tasminmahati rājyasthe tārake ditinaṃdane.. 15.57 ..
1.4.d:
परिवव्रुः फलाकीर्णं वृक्षं शकुनयो यथा..
तस्मिन्महति राज्यस्थे तारके दितिनंदने.. 15.57 ..
1.4.m: surrounded him, just as birds surround a tree laden with fruit. / When that Tāraka, the son of Diti, was established in his great kingdom,

1.4.s:
brahmaṇābhihi tasthāne mahārṇavataṭottare..
taravo jajñire pārtha tatra sarvartavaḥ śubhāḥ.. 15.58 ..
1.4.d:
ब्रह्मणाभिहि तस्थाने महार्णवतटोत्तरे..
तरवो जज्ञिरे पार्थ तत्र सर्वर्तवः शुभाः.. 15.58 ..
1.4.m: in the place designated by Brahmā on the northern shore of the great ocean, / O son of Pṛthā, auspicious trees of all seasons sprang up there.

1.4.s:
kāṃtirdyutirdhṛtirmedhā śrīrakhaṃḍā ca dānavam..
parivavrurguṇā kīrṇaṃ niśchidrāḥ sarva eva hi.. 15.59 ..
1.4.d:
कांतिर्द्युतिर्धृतिर्मेधा श्रीरखंडा च दानवम्..
परिवव्रुर्गुणा कीर्णं निश्छिद्राः सर्व एव हि.. 15.59 ..
1.4.m: Radiance, splendour, resolve, intelligence, and unbroken sovereignty / surrounded that dānava, all of them without defect, filled with virtues.

1.4.s:
kālāgaruviliptāṃgaṃ mahāmukuṭamaṃḍitam..
rucirāṃgadasannaddhaṃ mahāsiṃhāsane sthitam.. 15.60 ..
1.4.d:
कालागरुविलिप्तांगं महामुकुटमंडितम्..
रुचिरांगदसन्नद्धं महासिंहासने स्थितम्.. 15.60 ..
1.4.m: His limbs anointed with black aloe, adorned with a great crown, / equipped with beautiful armlets, seated upon a great lion-throne,

1.4.s:
nṛtyaṃtyapsarasaḥ śreṣṭhā gandharvā gāyayaṃti ca..
candrārkau dīpamārgeṣu vyajaneṣu ca mārutaḥ..
grahā agresarāstasya jīvādeśaprabhāṣiṇaḥ.. 15.61 ..
1.4.d:
नृत्यंत्यप्सरसः श्रेष्ठा गन्धर्वा गाययंति च..
चन्द्रार्कौ दीपमार्गेषु व्यजनेषु च मारुतः..
ग्रहा अग्रेसरास्तस्य जीवादेशप्रभाषिणः.. 15.61 ..
1.4.m: the foremost apsarases danced, and the gandharvas sang; / the moon and the sun served as lights, and the wind functioned as fans; / the planets were his heralds, declaring the decree of his life.

1.4.s:
evaṃ svakādbāhubalātsa daityaḥ saṃprāpya rājyaṃ parimodamānaḥ..
kadācidābhāṣya jagāda maṃtriṇaḥ proddhṛttasarvāṃgabalena darpitaḥ.. 15.62 ..
iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ prathame māheśvarakhaṇḍe kaumārikakhaṇḍe kumāreśamāhātmaye tārakāsurotpattivarṇanaṃnāma paṃcadaśo'dhyāyaḥ.. 15 .. cha ..
1.4.d:
एवं स्वकाद्बाहुबलात्स दैत्यः संप्राप्य राज्यं परिमोदमानः..
कदाचिदाभाष्य जगाद मंत्रिणः प्रोद्धृत्तसर्वांगबलेन दर्पितः.. 15.62 ..
इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां प्रथमे माहेश्वरखण्डे कौमारिकखण्डे कुमारेशमाहात्मये तारकासुरोत्पत्तिवर्णनंनाम पंचदशोऽध्यायः.. 15 .. छ ..
1.4.m:
Thus, having attained the kingdom through his own arm-strength, rejoicing exceedingly, / that daitya, proud of the strength of all his fully raised limbs, once summoned and spoke to his ministers.
Thus ends the fifteenth chapter, named "Description of the Rise of Tārakāsura," in the Māhātmya of Kumāreśa, in the Kaumārikākhaṇḍa of the first section, the Māheśvarakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skandapurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses.

1.4.s:
.. tāraka uvāca..
rājyena bud‌budābhena strībhirakṣaiśca pānakaiḥ..
mohito janma labdhvātra tyajate pauruṣaṃ naraḥ.. 16.1 ..
1.4.d:
.. तारक उवाच..
राज्येन बुद्‌बुदाभेन स्त्रीभिरक्षैश्च पानकैः..
मोहितो जन्म लब्ध्वात्र त्यजते पौरुषं नरः.. 16.1 ..
1.4.m: Tāraka said: / "A man who, having gained a birth here, is infatuated with royalty that resembles a bubble, / with women, dice, and intoxicating drinks, abandons manly valour.

1.4.s: janma tasya vṛthā sarvamākalpāṃtaṃ na saṃśayaḥ.. 16.2 ..
1.4.d: जन्म तस्य वृथा सर्वमाकल्पांतं न संशयः.. 16.2 ..
1.4.m: His birth is entirely in vain until the end of an aeon, there is no doubt.

1.4.s:
mātāpitṛbhyāṃ na karoti kāmānbandhūnaśokānna karoti yo vā..
kīrtiṃ hi vā nārjayate na mānaṃ naraḥ sa jāto'pi mṛto'tra loke.. 16.3 ..
1.4.d:
मातापितृभ्यां न करोति कामान्बन्धूनशोकान्न करोति यो वा..
कीर्तिं हि वा नार्जयते न मानं नरः स जातोऽपि मृतोऽत्र लोके.. 16.3 ..
1.4.m: The man who does not fulfill the desires of his parents, or who does not make his kinsmen sorrow-free, / or who acquires neither fame nor honour, though born, is dead in this world.

1.4.s:
tasmājjayāyāmarapuṃgavānāṃ trailokyalakṣmīharaṇāya śīghram..
saṃyojyatāṃ me rathamaṣṭacakraṃ balaṃ ca me durjayadaityacakram.. 16.4 ..
1.4.d:
तस्माज्जयायामरपुंगवानां त्रैलोक्यलक्ष्मीहरणाय शीघ्रम्..
संयोज्यतां मे रथमष्टचक्रं बलं च मे दुर्जयदैत्यचक्रम्.. 16.4 ..
1.4.m: Therefore, for the defeat of the foremost immortals and for the swift seizure of the fortune of the three worlds, / let my eight-wheeled chariot be harnessed, along with my army, an invincible host of daityas!

1.4.s:
dhvajaṃ ca me kāṃcanapaṭṭabandhaṃ chatraṃ ca me mauktikajālabaddham..
adyāhamāsāṃ surakāminīnāṃ dhammīllakāṃścāgrathitānkariṣye.. 16.5 ..
1.4.d:
ध्वजं च मे कांचनपट्टबन्धं छत्रं च मे मौक्तिकजालबद्धम्..
अद्याहमासां सुरकामिनीनां धम्मील्लकांश्चाग्रथितान्करिष्ये.. 16.5 ..
1.4.m: And [bring] my banner bound with gold ribbons, and my parasol hung with nets of pearls! / Today I shall untie the braided chignons of these lovely celestial women!

1.4.s: yathā purā markaṭako jananyāstasyāśca satyena tu tārakaḥ syām.. 16.6 ..
1.4.d: यथा पुरा मर्कटको जनन्यास्तस्याश्च सत्येन तु तारकः स्याम्.. 16.6 ..
1.4.m: Just as the monkey was formerly [rescued] by his mother, so by her truth may I be Tāraka [the rescuer]!"

1.4.s:
..nārada uvāca..
tārakasya vacaḥ śrutvā grasanonāma dānavaḥ..
senānīrdaityarājasya tathā cakre'vilaṃbitam.. 16.7 ..
1.4.d:
..नारद उवाच..
तारकस्य वचः श्रुत्वा ग्रसनोनाम दानवः..
सेनानीर्दैत्यराजस्य तथा चक्रेऽविलंबितम्.. 16.7 ..
1.4.m: Nārada said: / Having heard the words of Tāraka, the dānava named Grasana, / the commander-in-chief of the king of the daityas, immediately did so.

1.4.s:
āhatya bherīṃ gambhīrāṃ daityānāhūya satvaraḥ..
sajjaṃ cakre rathaṃ daityo daityarājasya dhīmataḥ.. 16.8 ..
1.4.d:
आहत्य भेरीं गम्भीरां दैत्यानाहूय सत्वरः..
सज्जं चक्रे रथं दैत्यो दैत्यराजस्य धीमतः.. 16.8 ..
1.4.m: Striking the deep-sounding kettledrum and swiftly summoning the daityas, / the daitya prepared the chariot of the wise king of the daityas,

1.4.s:
garuḍānāṃ sahasreṇa garuḍopamitatviṣā..
te hi putrāḥ suparṇasya saṃsthitā merukandare.. 16.9 ..
1.4.d:
गरुडानां सहस्रेण गरुडोपमितत्विषा..
ते हि पुत्राः सुपर्णस्य संस्थिता मेरुकन्दरे.. 16.9 ..
1.4.m: drawn by a thousand garuḍas whose lustre equalled that of Garuḍa. / For they, the sons of Suparṇa, who resided in the caves of Mount Meru,

1.4.s:
vijitya daityarājena vāhanatve prakalpitāḥ..
aṣṭāṣṭacakraḥ sarathaścaturyojanavistṛtaḥ.. 16.10 ..
1.4.d:
विजित्य दैत्यराजेन वाहनत्वे प्रकल्पिताः..
अष्टाष्टचक्रः सरथश्चतुर्योजनविस्तृतः.. 16.10 ..
1.4.m: had been conquered by the king of the daityas and assigned to serve as mounts. / The chariot had eight-times-eight wheels and was four yojanas wide;

1.4.s:
nānākrīḍāgṛhayuto gītavādyamanoharaḥ..
gaṃdharvanagarākāraḥ saṃyuktaḥ pratyadṛsyata.. 16.11 ..
1.4.d:
नानाक्रीडागृहयुतो गीतवाद्यमनोहरः..
गंधर्वनगराकारः संयुक्तः प्रत्यदृस्यत.. 16.11 ..
1.4.m: furnished with various pleasure chambers, charming with singing and musical instruments, / it appeared like a city of the gandharvas.

1.4.s:
ājagmustatra daityāśca daśā caṃḍaparākramāḥ..
koṭikoṭiparivārā anye ca bahavo raṇe.. 16.12 ..
1.4.d:
आजग्मुस्तत्र दैत्याश्च दशा चंडपराक्रमाः..
कोटिकोटिपरिवारा अन्ये च बहवो रणे.. 16.12 ..
1.4.m: And there arrived ten daityas of fierce valour, / with retinues of millions upon millions, and many others in battle.

1.4.s:
teṣāmagresaro jambhaḥ kujambhonaṃtarastathā..
mahiṣaḥ kuñjaro meṣaḥ kālanemirnimistathā.. 16.13 ..
1.4.d:
तेषामग्रेसरो जम्भः कुजम्भोनंतरस्तथा..
महिषः कुञ्जरो मेषः कालनेमिर्निमिस्तथा.. 16.13 ..
1.4.m: Their leader was Jambha, and next was Kujambha, / Mahiṣa, Kuñjara, Meṣa, Kālanemi, and Nimi.

1.4.s:
mathano jaṃbhakaḥ śumbho daityeṃdrā daśa nāyakāḥ..
daityeṃdrā girivarṣmāṇaḥ saṃti caṃḍaparākramāḥ.. 16.14 ..
1.4.d:
मथनो जंभकः शुम्भो दैत्येंद्रा दश नायकाः..
दैत्येंद्रा गिरिवर्ष्माणः संति चंडपराक्रमाः.. 16.14 ..
1.4.m: Mathana, Jambhaka, and Śumbha: these were the ten commanders, lords of Daityas. / The lords of Daityas had bodies like mountains, endowed with fierce prowess.

1.4.s:
nānāvidhapraharaṇā nānāśastrāstrapāragāḥ..
tārakasyābhavatketurbahūrūpo mahābhayaḥ.. 16.15 ..
1.4.d:
नानाविधप्रहरणा नानाशस्त्रास्त्रपारगाः..
तारकस्याभवत्केतुर्बहूरूपो महाभयः.. 16.15 ..
1.4.m: Equipped with various weapons and masters of all kinds of arms and missiles, / Tāraka had a banner of manifold shapes, terrifying to behold.

1.4.s:
kvacicca rākṣaso ghoraḥ piśācadhvāṃkṣagṛdhrakaḥ..
evaṃ bahuvidhākāraḥ sa ketuḥ pratyadṛśyata.. 16.16 ..
1.4.d:
क्वचिच्च राक्षसो घोरः पिशाचध्वांक्षगृध्रकः..
एवं बहुविधाकारः स केतुः प्रत्यदृश्यत.. 16.16 ..
1.4.m: At times a dreadful Rākṣasa, a Piśāca, a crow, or a vulture: / thus the banner was seen to take on manifold forms.

1.4.s:
ketunā makareṇāpi senānīrgrasano babhau..
paiśācaṃ yatra vadanaṃ jaṃbhasyāsīdayasmayam.. 16.17 ..
1.4.d:
केतुना मकरेणापि सेनानीर्ग्रसनो बभौ..
पैशाचं यत्र वदनं जंभस्यासीदयस्मयम्.. 16.17 ..
1.4.m: The general Grasana shone with an alligator on his standard, / whereas on Jambha’s banner was a demonic face made of iron.

1.4.s:
kharo vidhutalāṃgūlaḥ kujambhasyābhavaddhvaje..
mahiṣasya ca gomāyuḥ kāṃto haimastathāṃ babhau.. 16.18 ..
1.4.d:
खरो विधुतलांगूलः कुजम्भस्याभवद्ध्वजे..
महिषस्य च गोमायुः कांतो हैमस्तथां बभौ.. 16.18 ..
1.4.m: A donkey with a wagging tail was on Kujambha’s banner, / and for Mahiṣa a jackal, charming and made of gold, shone upon his.

1.4.s:
gṛdhro vai kuṃjarasyāsīnmeṣasyābhūcca rākṣasaḥ..
kālanemermahākālo nimerāsīnmahātimiḥ.. 16.19 ..
1.4.d:
गृध्रो वै कुंजरस्यासीन्मेषस्याभूच्च राक्षसः..
कालनेमेर्महाकालो निमेरासीन्महातिमिः.. 16.19 ..
1.4.m: A vulture was upon Kuñjara's [flag], and a Rākṣasa upon Meṣa's; / Kālanemi had Mahākāla, and Nimi had a great whale.

1.4.s:
rākṣasī mathanasyāpi dhvāṃkṣo'bhūjjaṃbhakasya ca..
mahāvṛkaśca śumbhasya dhvajā evaṃvidhā babhuḥ.. 16.20 ..
1.4.d:
राक्षसी मथनस्यापि ध्वांक्षोऽभूज्जंभकस्य च..
महावृकश्च शुम्भस्य ध्वजा एवंविधा बभुः.. 16.20 ..
1.4.m: A Rākṣasī was for Mathana, and a crow for Jambhaka; / a great wolf was on Śumbha’s: such were their splendid standards.

1.4.s:
anekākāravinyāsādanyeṣāṃ ca dhvajā bhavan..
śatena śīghravegānāṃ vyāghrāṇāṃ hemamālinām.. 16.21 ..
1.4.d:
अनेकाकारविन्यासादन्येषां च ध्वजा भवन्..
शतेन शीघ्रवेगानां व्याघ्राणां हेममालिनाम्.. 16.21 ..
1.4.m: Other banners too were formed in diverse shapes. / Yoked with a hundred swift-paced tigers adorned with golden garlands,

1.4.s:
grasanasya ratho yukto mahāmegharavo babhau..
śatena cāpi siṃhānāṃ ratho jaṃbhasya yojitaḥ.. 16.22 ..
1.4.d:
ग्रसनस्य रथो युक्तो महामेघरवो बभौ..
शतेन चापि सिंहानां रथो जंभस्य योजितः.. 16.22 ..
1.4.m: Grasana’s chariot shone, roaring like a great cloud. / And Jambha’s chariot was yoked with a hundred lions.

1.4.s:
kujaṃbhasya ratho yuktaḥ piśācavadanaiḥ kharaiḥ..
tāvadbhirmahiṣasyoṣṭairgajasya ca hayairyutaḥ.. 16.23 ..
1.4.d:
कुजंभस्य रथो युक्तः पिशाचवदनैः खरैः..
तावद्भिर्महिषस्योष्टैर्गजस्य च हयैर्युतः.. 16.23 ..
1.4.m: Kujambha’s chariot was yoked with Piśāca-faced donkeys; / Mahiṣa’s was yoked with as many camels, and Kuñjara’s with horses.

1.4.s:
meṣasya dvīpibhirbhīmaiḥ kuñjaraiḥ kālaneminaḥ..
parvataṃ vai samārūḍho niścitya vidhṛtaṃ gajaiḥ.. 16.24 ..
1.4.d:
मेषस्य द्वीपिभिर्भीमैः कुञ्जरैः कालनेमिनः..
पर्वतं वै समारूढो निश्चित्य विधृतं गजैः.. 16.24 ..
1.4.m: Meṣa’s was yoked with fierce leopards, and Kālanemi’s with elephants. / [Nimi] indeed mounted a mountain held firmly by elephants—

1.4.s:
caturdaṃṣṭrairgaṃdhavadbhiścarbhirmeghasannibhaiḥ..
śatahastāyate kṛṣṇe turaṃge hemabhūṣaṇe.. 16.25 ..
1.4.d:
चतुर्दंष्ट्रैर्गंधवद्भिश्चर्भिर्मेघसन्निभैः..
शतहस्तायते कृष्णे तुरंगे हेमभूषणे.. 16.25 ..
1.4.m: by four four-tusked, fragrant [elephants] resembling clouds. / Mounted on a black horse one hundred cubits long, adorned with golden ornaments,

1.4.s:
sitacāmarajālena śobhite puṣpadāmani..
mathanonāma daityendraḥ pāśahasto vyarājata.. 16.26 ..
1.4.d:
सितचामरजालेन शोभिते पुष्पदामनि..
मथनोनाम दैत्येन्द्रः पाशहस्तो व्यराजत.. 16.26 ..
1.4.m: embellished with white chowries and garlands of flowers, / the lord of Daityas named Mathana shone with a noose in his hand.

1.4.s:
kiṃkiṇīmālinaṃ coṣṭramārūḍho'bhūcca jaṃbhakaḥ..
kālamuṃcaṃ mahāmeghamārūḍhaḥ śumbhadānavaḥ.. 16.27 ..
1.4.d:
किंकिणीमालिनं चोष्ट्रमारूढोऽभूच्च जंभकः..
कालमुंचं महामेघमारूढः शुम्भदानवः.. 16.27 ..
1.4.m: Jambhaka was mounted on a camel adorned with a garland of small bells, / and the Dānava Śumbha was mounted on a great cloud that rained death.

1.4.s:
anye ca dānavā vīrā nānāvāhanahetayaḥ..
pracaṇḍacitravarmāṇaḥ kuṇḍaloṣṇīṣabhūṣitāḥ.. 16.28 ..
1.4.d:
अन्ये च दानवा वीरा नानावाहनहेतयः..
प्रचण्डचित्रवर्माणः कुण्डलोष्णीषभूषिताः.. 16.28 ..
1.4.m: And other heroic Dānavas with various mounts and weapons, / wearing fierce, colourful armour, adorned with earrings and turbans,

1.4.s:
nānāvidhottarāsaṃgā nānāmālyavibhūṣaṇāḥ..
nānāsugaṃdhagaṃdhāḍhyā nānābaṃdhiśatastutāḥ.. 16.29 ..
1.4.d:
नानाविधोत्तरासंगा नानामाल्यविभूषणाः..
नानासुगंधगंधाढ्या नानाबंधिशतस्तुताः.. 16.29 ..
1.4.m: with diverse upper garments, adorned with diverse garlands, / rich in diverse sweet fragrances, praised by hundreds of varied bards,

1.4.s:
nānāvādyaparisyaṃdasāgresaramahārathāḥ..
nānāśauryakathāsaktāstasminsainye mahārathāḥ.. 16.30 ..
1.4.d:
नानावाद्यपरिस्यंदसाग्रेसरमहारथाः..
नानाशौर्यकथासक्तास्तस्मिन्सैन्ये महारथाः.. 16.30 ..
1.4.m: with great chariots leading the flow of diverse musical instruments, / great chariot-warriors in that army engaged in tales of varied heroism.

1.4.s:
tadbalaṃ daityasiṃhasya bhīmarūpaṃ vyadṛśyata..
bhūmireṇusamāliṃgatturaṃgarathapattikam.. 16.31 ..
1.4.d:
तद्बलं दैत्यसिंहस्य भीमरूपं व्यदृश्यत..
भूमिरेणुसमालिंगत्तुरंगरथपत्तिकम्.. 16.31 ..
1.4.m: That army of the lion among Daityas appeared dreadful, / its horses, chariots, and foot-soldiers embracing the dust of the earth.

1.4.s:
sa ca daityeśvaraḥ kruddhaḥ samārūḍho mahāratham..
daśabhiḥ śuśube daityairdaśabāhuriveśvaraḥ..
jagaddhaṃtuṃ pravṛtto vā pratasthe'sau surānprati.. 16.32 ..
1.4.d:
स च दैत्येश्वरः क्रुद्धः समारूढो महारथम्..
दशभिः शुशुबे दैत्यैर्दशबाहुरिवेश्वरः..
जगद्धंतुं प्रवृत्तो वा प्रतस्थेऽसौ सुरान्प्रति.. 16.32 ..
1.4.m: Enraged, that lord of Daityas mounted his great chariot. / He shone with the ten Daityas, like ten-armed Īśvara; / or as if setting out to destroy the world, he marched against the gods.

1.4.s:
etasminnaṃtare vāyurdevadūtaḥ surālayam..
dṛṣṭvā taddānava balaṃ jagāmeṃdrasya śaṃsitum.. 16.33 ..
1.4.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे वायुर्देवदूतः सुरालयम्..
दृष्ट्वा तद्दानव बलं जगामेंद्रस्य शंसितुम्.. 16.33 ..
1.4.m: In the meantime Vāyu, the messenger of the gods, / having seen that army of Dānavas, went to the abode of the gods to report to Indra.

1.4.s:
sa gatvā tu sabhāṃ divyāṃ maheṃdrasya mahātmanaḥ..
śaśaṃsa madhye devānāmidaṃ kāryamupasthitam.. 16.34 ..
1.4.d:
स गत्वा तु सभां दिव्यां महेंद्रस्य महात्मनः..
शशंस मध्ये देवानामिदं कार्यमुपस्थितम्.. 16.34 ..
1.4.m: Having gone to the divine assembly of high-souled Mahendra, / he reported in the midst of the gods this crisis that had arisen.

1.4.s:
tacchrutvā devarājaḥ sa nimīlitavilocanaḥ..
bṛhaspatimuvācedaṃ vākyaṃ kāle mahāmatiḥ.. 16.35 ..
1.4.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा देवराजः स निमीलितविलोचनः..
बृहस्पतिमुवाचेदं वाक्यं काले महामतिः.. 16.35 ..
1.4.m: Hearing that, the king of the gods closed his eyes; / then, in due time, the highly intelligent one addressed these words to Bṛhaspati:

1.4.s:
..indra uvāca..
saṃprāpto'tivimardo'yaṃ devānāṃ dānavaiḥ saha..
kāryaṃ kimatra tadbruhi nītyupāyopabṛṃhitam.. 16.36 ..
1.4.d:
..इन्द्र उवाच..
संप्राप्तोऽतिविमर्दोऽयं देवानां दानवैः सह..
कार्यं किमत्र तद्ब्रुहि नीत्युपायोपबृंहितम्.. 16.36 ..
1.4.m: Indra said: / “This fierce clash of the gods with the Dānavas has arrived. / Tell me what should be done here, bolstered by political expedients.”

1.4.s:
etacchrutvā ca vacanaṃ maheṃdrasya girāṃpatiḥ..
pratyuvāca mahābhāgo baॉhaspati rudāradhīḥ.. 16.37 ..
1.4.d:
एतच्छ्रुत्वा च वचनं महेंद्रस्य गिरांपतिः..
प्रत्युवाच महाभागो बॉहस्पति रुदारधीः.. 16.37 ..
1.4.m: Having heard these words of Mahendra, the lord of speech, / the illustrious Bṛhaspati of noble intellect replied:

1.4.s:
..bṛhaspatiruvāca..
sāmapūrvaṃ smṛtā nītiścaturaṃgāmanīkinīm..
jigīṣatāṃ suraśreṣṭha sthitireṣā sanātanī.. 16.38 ..
1.4.d:
..बृहस्पतिरुवाच..
सामपूर्वं स्मृता नीतिश्चतुरंगामनीकिनीम्..
जिगीषतां सुरश्रेष्ठ स्थितिरेषा सनातनी.. 16.38 ..
1.4.m: Bṛhaspati said: / “Policy preceded by conciliation is remembered for those who wish to conquer / a fourfold army, O best of the gods; this is the eternal rule.

1.4.s:
sāma dānaṃ ca bhedaśca caturtho daṃḍa eva ca..
nītau kramātprayojyāśca deśakālaviśeṣataḥ.. 16.39 ..
1.4.d:
साम दानं च भेदश्च चतुर्थो दंड एव च..
नीतौ क्रमात्प्रयोज्याश्च देशकालविशेषतः.. 16.39 ..
1.4.m: Conciliation, gift, sowing discord, and fourthly punishment: / these are to be applied in order in political counsel according to distinctions of time and place.

1.4.s:
tatra sāma prayoktavyamāryeṣu guṇavatsu ca..
dānaṃ lubdheṣu bhedaśca śaṃkitoṣvito niścayaḥ.. 16.40 ..
1.4.d:
तत्र साम प्रयोक्तव्यमार्येषु गुणवत्सु च..
दानं लुब्धेषु भेदश्च शंकितोष्वितो निश्चयः.. 16.40 ..
1.4.m: Among them, conciliation should be applied towards noble and virtuous people, / gift to the greedy, and discord among the suspicious: this is certain.

1.4.s:
daṇḍaścāpi prayoktavyo nityakālaṃ durātmasu..
sāma daityeṣu naivāsti nirguṇatvāddurātmasu.. 16.41 ..
1.4.d:
दण्डश्चापि प्रयोक्तव्यो नित्यकालं दुरात्मसु..
साम दैत्येषु नैवास्ति निर्गुणत्वाद्दुरात्मसु.. 16.41 ..
1.4.m: And punishment should always be applied against the evil-minded. / Conciliation cannot apply to the Daityas, since they are evil-minded and devoid of virtue.

1.4.s:
śriyā teṣāṃ ca kiṃ kāryaṃ samṛddhānāṃ tathāpi yat..
jātidharmeṇa cābhedyā vidhāturapi te matāḥ.. 16.42 ..
1.4.d:
श्रिया तेषां च किं कार्यं समृद्धानां तथापि यत्..
जातिधर्मेण चाभेद्या विधातुरपि ते मताः.. 16.42 ..
1.4.m: And what need do they have of wealth, prosperous as they are? / Moreover, by the nature of their race they cannot be divided, even in the judgment of the Creator.

1.4.s:
eko hyupāyo daṃḍo'tra bhavatāṃ yadi rocate..
durjanaḥ sujanatvāya kalpate na kadācana.. 16.43 ..
1.4.d:
एको ह्युपायो दंडोऽत्र भवतां यदि रोचते..
दुर्जनः सुजनत्वाय कल्पते न कदाचन.. 16.43 ..
1.4.m: Therefore punishment is the single expedient here, if it pleases you. / A wicked person is never capable of becoming a good person.

1.4.s:
lālitaḥ pālito vāpi svasvabhāvaṃ na muṃcati..
evaṃ me manyate buddhirbhavaṃto yadvyavasyatām.. 16.44 ..
1.4.d:
लालितः पालितो वापि स्वस्वभावं न मुंचति..
एवं मे मन्यते बुद्धिर्भवंतो यद्व्यवस्यताम्.. 16.44 ..
1.4.m: Even if pampered or cared for, he does not abandon his innate nature. / This is what my intellect thinks; let you all decide.”

1.4.s:
evamuktaḥ sahasrākṣa evamevetyuvāca ha..
kartavyatāṃ ca saṃciṃtya provācāmarasaṃsadi.. 16.45 ..
1.4.d:
एवमुक्तः सहस्राक्ष एवमेवेत्युवाच ह..
कर्तव्यतां च संचिंत्य प्रोवाचामरसंसदि.. 16.45 ..
1.4.m: Thus addressed, the Thousand-Eyed [Indra] said, “So be it indeed!” / And having considered what ought to be done, he spoke in the assembly of the immortals:

1.4.s: bahumānena me vācaṃ śrṛṇudhvaṃ nākavāsinaḥ.. 16.46 ..
