अथोग्रैक प्रहारेण रथमश्वं गजं सुरम्.. 21.84 ..
1.4.m: By them, all the Gandharva cities were shattered, / and with a single fierce strike, chariot, horse, elephant, and god

1.4.s:
cūrṇayāmāsa tatkṣipraṃ śataśo'tha sahasraśaḥ..
tataḥ surādhipaḥ sakrastvāṣṭramastramudairayat.. 21.85 ..
1.4.d:
चूर्णयामास तत्क्षिप्रं शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः..
ततः सुराधिपः सक्रस्त्वाष्ट्रमस्त्रमुदैरयत्.. 21.85 ..
1.4.m: were crushed swiftly by the hundreds and the thousands. / Then Śakra, lord of the gods, discharged the Tvāṣṭra missile.

1.4.s:
saṃdhyamāne tataścāstre niśceruḥ pāvakārciṣaḥ..
tato yaṃtramayā vidyāḥ prādurāsansahasraśaḥ.. 21.86 ..
1.4.d:
संध्यमाने ततश्चास्त्रे निश्चेरुः पावकार्चिषः..
ततो यंत्रमया विद्याः प्रादुरासन्सहस्रशः.. 21.86 ..
1.4.m: As the missile was being aimed, flames of fire burst forth; / then magical devices made of mechanical contraptions appeared by the thousands.

1.4.s:
tairyaṃtrairabhavadyuddhamaṃtarikṣaṃ vitārakam..
tairyaṃtrairmauśalaṃ bhagnaṃ hanyaṃte cāsurāstadā.. 21.87 ..
1.4.d:
तैर्यंत्रैरभवद्युद्धमंतरिक्षं वितारकम्..
तैर्यंत्रैर्मौशलं भग्नं हन्यंते चासुरास्तदा.. 21.87 ..
1.4.m: With those devices a battle took place in the intermediate space that eclipsed the stars; / by those devices the Mauśala [missile] was shattered, and the Asuras were struck down.

1.4.s:
śailāstraṃ mumuce jaṃbho yaṃtrasaṃghātacūrṇanam..
vyāmapramāṇairupalaistato varṣaḥ pravartata.. 21.88 ..
1.4.d:
शैलास्त्रं मुमुचे जंभो यंत्रसंघातचूर्णनम्..
व्यामप्रमाणैरुपलैस्ततो वर्षः प्रवर्तत.. 21.88 ..
1.4.m: Jambha discharged the mountain-missile that crushes hosts of mechanical devices. / Then a rain of boulders measuring a fathom began to fall.

1.4.s:
tvāṣṭroṇa nirmitānyāśu yāni yaṃtrāṇi bhārata..
tenopala nipātena gatāni tilaśastataḥ.. 21.89 ..
1.4.d:
त्वाष्ट्रोण निर्मितान्याशु यानि यंत्राणि भारत..
तेनोपल निपातेन गतानि तिलशस्ततः.. 21.89 ..
1.4.m: Those machines that had been fashioned by the Tvāṣṭra [missile], O Bhārata, / were ground into sesame seeds by that shower of falling stones.

1.4.s:
tataḥ śirassu devānāṃ śilāḥ peturmahājavāḥ..
dārayaṃtyaśca vasudhāṃ caturaṃgabalaṃ ca tat.. 21.90 ..
1.4.d:
ततः शिरस्सु देवानां शिलाः पेतुर्महाजवाः..
दारयंत्यश्च वसुधां चतुरंगबलं च तत्.. 21.90 ..
1.4.m: Then boulders fell with tremendous speed upon the heads of the gods, / splitting the earth and that fourfold army.

1.4.s:
tato vajrāstramakarotsasrākṣaḥ puraṃdaraḥ..
śilāmahārṣaṃvyaśīryata samaṃtataḥ.. 21.91 ..
1.4.d:
ततो वज्रास्त्रमकरोत्सस्राक्षः पुरंदरः..
शिलामहार्षंव्यशीर्यत समंततः.. 21.91 ..
1.4.m: Then Purandara, the thousand-eyed, employed the Vajra missile; / [by it] the great rain of stones was shattered on every side.

1.4.s:
tataḥ praśāṃtaiḥ śailāstrairjaṃbho bhūdharasannibhaḥ..
aiṣīkamastramakaroccūrṇitānyaparākramaḥ.. 21.92 ..
1.4.d:
ततः प्रशांतैः शैलास्त्रैर्जंभो भूधरसन्निभः..
ऐषीकमस्त्रमकरोच्चूर्णितान्यपराक्रमः.. 21.92 ..
1.4.m: When the mountain-missiles were pacified, Jambha, resembling a mountain, / whose prowess was crushing to others, discharged the Aiṣīka missile.

1.4.s:
aiṣīkeṇāgamannāśaṃ vajrāstraṃ giridāraṇam..
vijṛṃbhatyatha caiṣīke paramāstre'tidāruṇe.. 21.93 ..
1.4.d:
ऐषीकेणागमन्नाशं वज्रास्त्रं गिरिदारणम्..
विजृंभत्यथ चैषीके परमास्त्रेऽतिदारुणे.. 21.93 ..
1.4.m: By the Aiṣīka missile, the Vajra missile that splits mountains was destroyed; / and as that supreme and most terrible Aiṣīka missile expanded,

1.4.s:
jajvalurdevasainyāni sasyaṃdanagajāni ca..
dahyamāneṣva nīkeṣu tejasāstrasya sarvataḥ.. 21.94 ..
1.4.d:
जज्वलुर्देवसैन्यानि सस्यंदनगजानि च..
दह्यमानेष्व नीकेषु तेजसास्त्रस्य सर्वतः.. 21.94 ..
1.4.m: the armies of the gods, along with their chariots and elephants, burst into flames. / As the battalions were burning all around with the brilliance of the missile,

1.4.s:
āgneyamastramakarodbalahā pākaśāsanaḥ..
tenāstreṇa ca tannāśamaiṣīkamagamattadā.. 21.95 ..
1.4.d:
आग्नेयमस्त्रमकरोद्बलहा पाकशासनः..
तेनास्त्रेण च तन्नाशमैषीकमगमत्तदा.. 21.95 ..
1.4.m: the slayer of Bala, the chastiser of Pāka, employed the Āgneya missile; / and by that missile, the Aiṣīka missile met its destruction.

1.4.s:
tasminpratihate cāstre pāvakāstraṃ vyajṛṃbhata..
jajvāla senā jaṃbhasya rathaḥ sārathireva ca.. 21.96 ..
1.4.d:
तस्मिन्प्रतिहते चास्त्रे पावकास्त्रं व्यजृंभत..
जज्वाल सेना जंभस्य रथः सारथिरेव च.. 21.96 ..
1.4.m: When that missile was countered, the fire-missile flared up; / the army of Jambha, along with his chariot and charioteer, burst into flame.

1.4.s:
taḥ pratihatāstro'sau daityeṃdraḥ pratibhānavān..
vāruṇāstraṃ mumocāthaśamanaṃ pāvakārciṣām.. 21.97 ..
1.4.d:
तः प्रतिहतास्त्रोऽसौ दैत्येंद्रः प्रतिभानवान्..
वारुणास्त्रं मुमोचाथशमनं पावकार्चिषाम्.. 21.97 ..
1.4.m: His missile thwarted, that resourceful lord of the Daityas / then released the Vāruṇa missile, which extinguishes flames of fire.

1.4.s:
tato jaladharairvyoma sphuradvidyullatākulaiḥ..
gaṃbhīrākṣasamādhāraiścābhyapūryata modinī.. 21.98 ..
1.4.d:
ततो जलधरैर्व्योम स्फुरद्विद्युल्लताकुलैः..
गंभीराक्षसमाधारैश्चाभ्यपूर्यत मोदिनी.. 21.98 ..
1.4.m: Then the sky was filled with clouds thick with flashing streaks of lightning, / and the earth was flooded with deep downpours.

1.4.s:
karīṃdrakaratulyābhirdhārābhiḥ pūritaṃ jagat..
śāṃtamāgneyamastraṃ ca vilokyeṃdraścakāra ha.. 21.99 ..
1.4.d:
करींद्रकरतुल्याभिर्धाराभिः पूरितं जगत्..
शांतमाग्नेयमस्त्रं च विलोक्येंद्रश्चकार ह.. 21.99 ..
1.4.m: The world was inundated with torrents like the trunks of lordly elephants. / Seeing the fire-missile extinguished, Indra unleashed

1.4.s:
vāyavyamastramatulaṃ tena meghā yayuḥ kṣayam..
vāyavyāstrabalenātha nirdhūte meghamaṃḍale.. 21.100 ..
1.4.d:
वायव्यमस्त्रमतुलं तेन मेघा ययुः क्षयम्..
वायव्यास्त्रबलेनाथ निर्धूते मेघमंडले.. 21.100 ..
1.4.m: the matchless Vāyavya missile, by which the clouds were destroyed. / When the circle of clouds was dispersed by the power of the Vāyavya missile,

1.4.s:
babhūvānāvilaṃ vyoma nīlotpaladalaprabham..
vāyunā cātirūpeṇa kaṃpitāścaiva dānavāḥ.. 21.101 ..
1.4.d:
बभूवानाविलं व्योम नीलोत्पलदलप्रभम्..
वायुना चातिरूपेण कंपिताश्चैव दानवाः.. 21.101 ..
1.4.m: the sky became clear, shining with the luster of a blue lotus petal. / Trembling on account of the violent wind, the Dānavas

1.4.s:
na śekustatra te sthātuṃ raṇe'pi balino'pi ye..
jabhastato'bhavacchaulo daśayojanavistṛtaḥ.. 21.102 ..
1.4.d:
न शेकुस्तत्र ते स्थातुं रणेऽपि बलिनोऽपि ये..
जभस्ततोऽभवच्छौलो दशयोजनविस्तृतः.. 21.102 ..
1.4.m: could not stand their ground there, even those who were mighty in battle. / Then Jambha became a mountain ten yojanas wide,

1.4.s:
mārutapratighātārthaṃ dānavānāṃ balādhipaḥ..
nānāścaryasamāyukto nānādrumalatāvṛtaḥ.. 21.103 ..
1.4.d:
मारुतप्रतिघातार्थं दानवानां बलाधिपः..
नानाश्चर्यसमायुक्तो नानाद्रुमलतावृतः.. 21.103 ..
1.4.m: in order to resist the wind, as the commander of the Dānavas' forces, / filled with diverse wonders and covered with diverse trees and creepers.

1.4.s:
tataḥ praśamite vāyau daityeṃdra parvatākṛtau..
mahāśaniṃ vajramayīṃ mumocāśu śatakratuḥ.. 21.104 ..
1.4.d:
ततः प्रशमिते वायौ दैत्येंद्र पर्वताकृतौ..
महाशनिं वज्रमयीं मुमोचाशु शतक्रतुः.. 21.104 ..
1.4.m: When the wind was pacified by the lord of the Daityas in the form of a mountain, / Śatakratu swiftly hurled a great thunderbolt made of adamantine vajra.

1.4.s:
tayāśanyā patitayā daityasyāca larūpiṇaḥ..
kaṃdarāṇi vyaśīryaṃtaṃ samaṃtānnirjharāṇi ca.. 21.105 ..
1.4.d:
तयाशन्या पतितया दैत्यस्याच लरूपिणः..
कंदराणि व्यशीर्यंतं समंतान्निर्झराणि च.. 21.105 ..
1.4.m: As that thunderbolt fell upon the Daitya in the form of a mountain, / its caves and mountain torrents were shattered on every side.

1.4.s:
tataḥ sā dānaveṃdrasya śailamāyā nyavartata..
nivṛttaśailamāyo'tha dānaveṃdro madotkaṭaḥ.. 21.106 ..
1.4.d:
ततः सा दानवेंद्रस्य शैलमाया न्यवर्तत..
निवृत्तशैलमायोऽथ दानवेंद्रो मदोत्कटः.. 21.106 ..
1.4.m: Then that mountain-illusion of the lord of the Dānavas ceased. / His mountain-illusion vanished, the lord of the Dānavas, furious with intoxication,

1.4.s:
babhūva kuṃjaro bhīmo mahāśailamayākṛtiḥ..
mamarda ca surānīkaṃ daṃtaiścābhyahanatsurān.. 21.107 ..
1.4.d:
बभूव कुंजरो भीमो महाशैलमयाकृतिः..
ममर्द च सुरानीकं दंतैश्चाभ्यहनत्सुरान्.. 21.107 ..
1.4.m: became a terrifying elephant with the form of a great mountain. / He trampled the ranks of the gods and struck the gods with his tusks.

1.4.s:
babhaṃja pṛṣṭhataḥ kāṃścitkareṇākṛṣya dānavaḥ..
tataḥ kṣapayatastasya surasainyāni vṛtrahā.. 21.108 ..
1.4.d:
बभंज पृष्ठतः कांश्चित्करेणाकृष्य दानवः..
ततः क्षपयतस्तस्य सुरसैन्यानि वृत्रहा.. 21.108 ..
1.4.m: Dragging some by his trunk, the Dānava broke their backs. / Then, as he was destroying the divine armies, the slayer of Vṛtra

1.4.s:
astraṃ trailokyadurdharṣaṃ nārasiṃhaṃ mumoca ha..
tataḥ siṃhasasrāṇi niścerurmaṃtratejasā.. 21.109 ..
1.4.d:
अस्त्रं त्रैलोक्यदुर्धर्षं नारसिंहं मुमोच ह..
ततः सिंहसस्राणि निश्चेरुर्मंत्रतेजसा.. 21.109 ..
1.4.m: released the Nārasiṃha missile, invincible in the three worlds. / Then thousands of lions sprang forth by the power of the mantra,

1.4.s:
hṛṣṭadaṃṣṭrāṭṭahāsāni krakacābhanakhāni ca..
tairvipāṭitagātro'sau gajamāyāṃ vyapohayat.. 21.110 ..
1.4.d:
हृष्टदंष्ट्राट्टहासानि क्रकचाभनखानि च..
तैर्विपाटितगात्रोऽसौ गजमायां व्यपोहयत्.. 21.110 ..
1.4.m: with bared fangs, booming roars, and claws like saws. / His body torn open by them, he abandoned the elephant-illusion.

1.4.s:
tataścāśīviṣo ghoro'bhavatphaṇasamākulaḥ..
viṣaniḥśvāsanirdagdhasurasainyamahārathaḥ.. 21.111 ..
1.4.d:
ततश्चाशीविषो घोरोऽभवत्फणसमाकुलः..
विषनिःश्वासनिर्दग्धसुरसैन्यमहारथः.. 21.111 ..
1.4.m: Then he became a terrible venomous serpent, covered with hoods, / burning the great charioteers of the divine army with the venom of his breath.

1.4.s:
tato'straṃ gāruḍaṃ cakre śakraḥ saṃpraharanraॅṇe..
tatastasmādgarutmaṃtaḥ sahasrāṇi viniryayuḥ.. 21.112 ..
1.4.d:
ततोऽस्त्रं गारुडं चक्रे शक्रः संप्रहरन्रॅणे..
ततस्तस्माद्गरुत्मंतः सहस्राणि विनिर्ययुः.. 21.112 ..
1.4.m: Then Śakra, striking in battle, employed the Gāruḍa weapon; / thereupon thousands of eagles came forth from it.

1.4.s:
tairgarutmadbhirāsādya jaṃbhaṃ bhujagarūpiṇam..
kṛtastu saṃḍhaśo daityaḥ sāsya māyā vyanaśyata.. 21.113 ..
1.4.d:
तैर्गरुत्मद्भिरासाद्य जंभं भुजगरूपिणम्..
कृतस्तु संढशो दैत्यः सास्य माया व्यनश्यत.. 21.113 ..
1.4.m: Approaching Jambha who had assumed the form of a serpent, those eagles / tore that Daitya to pieces; that illusion of his vanished.

1.4.s:
māyāyāma ca pranaṣṭāyāṃ tato jaṃbho mahāsuraḥ..
cakāra rūpamatulaṃ caṃdrādityapadānugam.. 21.114 ..
1.4.d:
मायायाम च प्रनष्टायां ततो जंभो महासुरः..
चकार रूपमतुलं चंद्रादित्यपदानुगम्.. 21.114 ..
1.4.m: And when his illusion was destroyed, then the great Asura Jambha / assumed an incomparable form that reached the sphere of the moon and the sun.

1.4.s:
vivṛttanayano grastumiyeṣa surapuṃgavān..
tato'sya praviśadvaktra samahārathakuṃjarā.. 21.115 ..
1.4.d:
विवृत्तनयनो ग्रस्तुमियेष सुरपुंगवान्..
ततोऽस्य प्रविशद्वक्त्र समहारथकुंजरा.. 21.115 ..
1.4.m: With rolling eyes he sought to swallow the foremost gods; / then the divine army, with its great chariots and elephants,

1.4.s:
surasenā'bhavadbhīmaṃ pātālottālatālukam..
sainyeṣu grasyamāneṣu dānavena balīyasā.. 21.116 ..
1.4.d:
सुरसेनाऽभवद्भीमं पातालोत्तालतालुकम्..
सैन्येषु ग्रस्यमानेषु दानवेन बलीयसा.. 21.116 ..
1.4.m: entered his dreadful mouth, whose palate was as vast as Pātāla. / As the armies were being swallowed by the mighty Dānava,

1.4.s:
śakro dīnatvamāpannaḥ śrāṃtavāhanavāhanaḥ..
kartavyatāṃ nādhyagacchatprovācedaṃ janārdanam.. 21.117 ..
1.4.d:
शक्रो दीनत्वमापन्नः श्रांतवाहनवाहनः..
कर्तव्यतां नाध्यगच्छत्प्रोवाचेदं जनार्दनम्.. 21.117 ..
1.4.m: Śakra fell into dejection, his vehicles and mounts exhausted; / not knowing what should be done, he spoke these words to Janārdana:

1.4.s:
kimanaṃtaramevāsti kartavyaṃ no viśeṣataḥ..
tadādiśa ghaṭāmo'sya dānavasya yuyutsataḥ.. 21.118 ..
1.4.d:
किमनंतरमेवास्ति कर्तव्यं नो विशेषतः..
तदादिश घटामोऽस्य दानवस्य युयुत्सतः.. 21.118 ..
1.4.m: “What in particular is to be done next by us? / Direct us in that; let us join battle against this Dānava who is eager to fight.”

1.4.s:
tato hariruvācedaṃ vajrāyudhamudāradhīḥ..
na sāṃprataṃ raṇaṃ tyājyaṃ śatrukātarabhairavam.. 21.119 ..
1.4.d:
ततो हरिरुवाचेदं वज्रायुधमुदारधीः..
न सांप्रतं रणं त्याज्यं शत्रुकातरभैरवम्.. 21.119 ..
1.4.m: Then Hari of noble intellect said this to the wielder of the thunderbolt weapon: / “It is not fitting now to abandon the battle, terrifying [even] to cowardly foes.

1.4.s:
mā gaccha mohaṃ mā gaccha kṣipramastraṃ smara prabho..
nārāyaṇāstraṃ prayataḥ śrutveti mumuce sa ca.. 21.120 ..
1.4.d:
मा गच्छ मोहं मा गच्छ क्षिप्रमस्त्रं स्मर प्रभो..
नारायणास्त्रं प्रयतः श्रुत्वेति मुमुचे स च.. 21.120 ..
1.4.m: Do not succumb to delusion, do not succumb! Quickly recall a weapon, O lord!” / Hearing this, he restrained himself and released the Nārāyaṇa weapon.

1.4.s:
etasminnaṃtare daityo vivṛtāsyo'grasatkṣaṇāt..
trīṇitrīṇi ca lakṣāṇi kiṃnaroragarakṣasām.. 21.121 ..
1.4.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे दैत्यो विवृतास्योऽग्रसत्क्षणात्..
त्रीणित्रीणि च लक्षाणि किंनरोरगरक्षसाम्.. 21.121 ..
1.4.m: In the meantime, the Daitya opened his mouth wide and in an instant swallowed / three times a hundred thousand Kinnaras, Uragas, and Rākṣasas.

1.4.s:
tato nārāyaṇāstraṃ ca nipapātāsya vakṣasi..
mahāstrabhinnahṛdayaḥ susrāva rudhiraṃ ca saḥ.. 21.122 ..
1.4.d:
ततो नारायणास्त्रं च निपपातास्य वक्षसि..
महास्त्रभिन्नहृदयः सुस्राव रुधिरं च सः.. 21.122 ..
1.4.m: Then the Nārāyaṇa weapon fell upon his chest; / with his heart split open by that great weapon, he poured forth blood.

1.4.s:
tataḥ svatejasā rūpaṃ tasya daityasya nāśitaṃm..
tataścāṃ tardadhe daityaḥ kṛtvā hāsaṃ mahotkaṭam.. 21.123 ..
1.4.d:
ततः स्वतेजसा रूपं तस्य दैत्यस्य नाशितंम्..
ततश्चां तर्दधे दैत्यः कृत्वा हासं महोत्कटम्.. 21.123 ..
1.4.m: Then, by its own brilliance, that form of the Daitya was destroyed; / and then the Daitya vanished, uttering a loud, fierce laugh.

1.4.s:
gaganasthaḥ sa daityendraḥ śastrāśanimatīṃdriyaḥ..
mumoca surasainyānāṃ sahārakaraṇīṃ parām.. 21.124 ..
1.4.d:
गगनस्थः स दैत्येन्द्रः शस्त्राशनिमतींद्रियः..
मुमोच सुरसैन्यानां सहारकरणीं पराम्.. 21.124 ..
1.4.m: Standing in the sky, that king of Daityas, imperceptible to the senses, / loosed a lightning-bolt of weapons that wrought the supreme destruction of the divine armies.

1.4.s:
tathā paraśvadhāṃścakravajrabāṇānsamudgarān..
kuṃtānkhaḍgānbhiṃḍipālānayomukhaguḍāṃstathā.. 21.125 ..
1.4.d:
तथा परश्वधांश्चक्रवज्रबाणान्समुद्गरान्..
कुंतान्खड्गान्भिंडिपालानयोमुखगुडांस्तथा.. 21.125 ..
1.4.m: Axes, discuses, thunderbolts, arrows, clubs, / spears, swords, throwing rods, and iron-headed balls—

1.4.s:
vavarṣa dānavo roṣādavadhyānakṣayānapi..
tairastrairdānavonmuktairdevānīkeṣu bhīṣaṇaiḥ.. 21.126 ..
1.4.d:
ववर्ष दानवो रोषादवध्यानक्षयानपि..
तैरस्त्रैर्दानवोन्मुक्तैर्देवानीकेषु भीषणैः.. 21.126 ..
1.4.m: these the Dānava wrathfully rained down, deadly and inexhaustible. / By those dreadful weapons loosed by the Dānava against the divine forces,

1.4.s:
bāhubhirdharaṇī pūrṇā śirobhiśca sakuṃḍalaiḥ..
ūrubhirgajahastābhaiḥ karīṃdraiścācalopamaiḥ.. 21.127 ..
1.4.d:
बाहुभिर्धरणी पूर्णा शिरोभिश्च सकुंडलैः..
ऊरुभिर्गजहस्ताभैः करींद्रैश्चाचलोपमैः.. 21.127 ..
1.4.m: the earth became filled with arms and heads adorned with earrings, / with thighs resembling elephants' trunks, and with lordly elephants like mountains.

1.4.s:
bhagneṣā daṃḍacakrākṣai rathaibhiḥ saha..
duḥsaṃcārābhavatpṛthvī māṃsaśoṇitakardamā.. 21.128 ..
1.4.d:
भग्नेषा दंडचक्राक्षै रथैभिः सह..
दुःसंचाराभवत्पृथ्वी मांसशोणितकर्दमा.. 21.128 ..
1.4.m: Together with chariots whose shafts, yokes, wheels, and axles were broken, / the earth, a mire of flesh and blood, became impassable.

1.4.s:
rudhiraughahradāvartā gajadehaśiloccayā..
kabaṃdhanṛtyabahulā mahā surapravāhinī.. 21.129 ..
1.4.d:
रुधिरौघह्रदावर्ता गजदेहशिलोच्चया..
कबंधनृत्यबहुला महा सुरप्रवाहिनी.. 21.129 ..
1.4.m: With swirling eddies of flood-like pools of blood, with piles of rocks that were the bodies of elephants, / crowded with the dancing of headless trunks, a great river [flowed through] the gods' [army],

1.4.s:
śrṛgālagṛdhradhvāṃkṣāṇāṃ paramānaṃdakāriṇī..
piśācajātibhiḥ kīrṇaṃ pītvā''miṣaṃ saśoṇitam.. 21.130 ..
1.4.d:
श्रृगालगृध्रध्वांक्षाणां परमानंदकारिणी..
पिशाचजातिभिः कीर्णं पीत्वा'ऽमिषं सशोणितम्.. 21.130 ..
1.4.m: causing supreme delight to jackals, vultures, and crows, / teeming with varieties of Piśācas who had drunk meat and blood,

1.4.s:
asaṃbhramābhirbhāryābhiḥ saha nṛtyadbhiruddhatā..
kācitpatnī prakupitā gajakuṃbhāṃtamauktikaiḥ.. 21.131 ..
1.4.d:
असंभ्रमाभिर्भार्याभिः सह नृत्यद्भिरुद्धता..
काचित्पत्नी प्रकुपिता गजकुंभांतमौक्तिकैः.. 21.131 ..
1.4.m: boisterous and dancing together with their untroubled wives. / A certain wife, infuriated with pearls from the temples of elephants,

1.4.s:
piśāco yatra cāśvānāṃ khurānekatra cākarot..
karṇapūreṣu modaṃte paśyaṃtyanyāḥ saroṣataḥ.. 21.132 ..
1.4.d:
पिशाचो यत्र चाश्वानां खुरानेकत्र चाकरोत्..
कर्णपूरेषु मोदंते पश्यंत्यन्याः सरोषतः.. 21.132 ..
1.4.m: where a Piśāca had gathered horses' hooves in one place, / delighted in ear-ornaments, while other [females] looked on with anger.

1.4.s:
prasādayaṃti bahudhā mahākarṇārthakovidāḥ..
kecidvadanti bho devā bho daityāḥ prārthayāmahe.. 21.133 ..
1.4.d:
प्रसादयंति बहुधा महाकर्णार्थकोविदाः..
केचिद्वदन्ति भो देवा भो दैत्याः प्रार्थयामहे.. 21.133 ..
1.4.m: Skilled in the aims of large ear-ornaments, they pacified them in many ways. / Some said: “O gods! O Daityas! We pray:

1.4.s:
ākalpamevaṃ yoddhavyamasmākaṃ tṛptihetave..
kecidūcurayaṃ daityo devoyamatimāṃsalaḥ.. 21.134 ..
1.4.d:
आकल्पमेवं योद्धव्यमस्माकं तृप्तिहेतवे..
केचिदूचुरयं दैत्यो देवोयमतिमांसलः.. 21.134 ..
1.4.m: Thus should you fight until the end of the kalpa for the sake of our satisfaction!” / Some said: “This Daitya, this god is very fleshy;

1.4.s:
mriyate yadi saṃgrāme dhāturdadbho'payācitam..
kecidyudhyatsu vīreṣu sṛkkiṇī saṃlihaṃti ca.. 21.135 ..
1.4.d:
म्रियते यदि संग्रामे धातुर्दद्भोऽपयाचितम्..
केचिद्युध्यत्सु वीरेषु सृक्किणी संलिहंति च.. 21.135 ..
1.4.m: if he dies in battle, the reward promised to the Creator will be paid.” / As the heroes fought, some licked the corners of their mouths,

1.4.s:
etena payasā vidmo durjanaḥ sujano yathā..
kecidraktanadīnāṃ ca tīreṣvāstikyabuddhayaḥ.. 21.136 ..
1.4.d:
एतेन पयसा विद्मो दुर्जनः सुजनो यथा..
केचिद्रक्तनदीनां च तीरेष्वास्तिक्यबुद्धयः.. 21.136 ..
1.4.m: saying: “By this water we know [them], just as a bad man [knows] a good man.” / On the banks of the rivers of blood, some with pious faith

1.4.s:
pitṝndevāṃstarpayaṃti śoṇitaiścāmiṣaiḥ śubhaiḥ..
kecidāmiṣarāśisthā dṛṣṭvānyasya karāmiṣam.. 21.137 ..
1.4.d:
पितॄन्देवांस्तर्पयंति शोणितैश्चामिषैः शुभैः..
केचिदामिषराशिस्था दृष्ट्वान्यस्य करामिषम्.. 21.137 ..
1.4.m: gratified the ancestors and the gods with blood and auspicious flesh. / Standing on a heap of flesh, some, seeing the flesh in another’s hand,

1.4.s:
dehidehīti vāśāṃto dhaninaḥ kṛpaṇā yathā..
kecitsvayaṃ pratṛptāśca dṛṣṭvā vai khādataḥ parān.. 21.138 ..
1.4.d:
देहिदेहीति वाशांतो धनिनः कृपणा यथा..
केचित्स्वयं प्रतृप्ताश्च दृष्ट्वा वै खादतः परान्.. 21.138 ..
1.4.m: cried out, “Give! Give!” like miserable paupers before a rich man. / Others, having sated themselves, on seeing others eating,

1.4.s:
saroṣamoṣṭhau nirbhujya paśyaṃtyevātyasūyayā..
kecitsvamudaraṃ kruddhā niṃdaṃti tāḍayaṃti ca.. 21.139 ..
1.4.d:
सरोषमोष्ठौ निर्भुज्य पश्यंत्येवात्यसूयया..
केचित्स्वमुदरं क्रुद्धा निंदंति ताडयंति च.. 21.139 ..
1.4.m: twisted their lips angrily and glared with extreme jealousy. / Others, enraged, rebuked their own bellies and struck them,

1.4.s:
sarvabhakṣamabhīpsaṃtastṛptāḥ paradhanaṃ yathā..
kecidāhuradya eva ślāghyā sṛṣṭistu vedhasaḥ.. 21.140 ..
1.4.d:
सर्वभक्षमभीप्संतस्तृप्ताः परधनं यथा..
केचिदाहुरद्य एव श्लाघ्या सृष्टिस्तु वेधसः.. 21.140 ..
1.4.m: wishing to consume everything, like sated men [coveting] another’s wealth. / Others said: “Only today is the creation of the Ordainer praiseworthy;

1.4.s:
suprabhātaṃ sunakṣatraṃ pūrvamāsīddhṛthaiva tat..
evaṃ bahuvidhālāpe palādānāṃ tatastataḥ.. 21.141 ..
1.4.d:
सुप्रभातं सुनक्षत्रं पूर्वमासीद्धृथैव तत्..
एवं बहुविधालापे पलादानां ततस्ततः.. 21.141 ..
1.4.m: auspicious was the dawn, auspicious the lunar mansion—all that came before was in vain!” / While the flesh-eaters were engaged in such diverse talk on every side,

1.4.s:
adṛśyaḥ samare jaṃbho devāñṭhastrairacūrṇayat..
tataḥ śakrodhaneśaśca varuṇaḥ pavano'nalaḥ.. 21.142 ..
1.4.d:
अदृश्यः समरे जंभो देवाञ्ठस्त्रैरचूर्णयत्..
ततः शक्रोधनेशश्च वरुणः पवनोऽनलः.. 21.142 ..
1.4.m: Jambha, invisible in battle, pulverized the gods with his weapons. / Then Śakra, the Lord of Wealth, Varuṇa, Pavana, Anala,

1.4.s:
yamo'tha nirṛtiścāpi divyāstrāṇi mahābalāḥ..
ākāśe mumucuḥ sarve dānavāyābhisaṃdhya tu.. 21.143 ..
1.4.d:
यमोऽथ निरृतिश्चापि दिव्यास्त्राणि महाबलाः..
आकाशे मुमुचुः सर्वे दानवायाभिसंध्य तु.. 21.143 ..
1.4.m: Yama, and also Nirṛti—mighty beings, all aiming at the Dānava— / released divine weapons into the sky.

1.4.s:
vyarthatāṃ jagmurastrāṇi devānāṃ dānavaṃ prati..
yathātikrūracittānāmārye kṛtyaśatānyapi.. 21.144 ..
1.4.d:
व्यर्थतां जग्मुरस्त्राणि देवानां दानवं प्रति..
यथातिक्रूरचित्तानामार्ये कृत्यशतान्यपि.. 21.144 ..
1.4.m: The weapons of the gods became futile against the Dānava, / just as even hundreds of services by those of extremely cruel heart [are futile] toward a noble person.

1.4.s:
gatiṃ na vividuścāpi śrāṃtā daityāśca devatāḥ..
daityāstrabhinnasarvāṃgā gāvaḥ śītārditā iva.. 21.145 ..
1.4.d:
गतिं न विविदुश्चापि श्रांता दैत्याश्च देवताः..
दैत्यास्त्रभिन्नसर्वांगा गावः शीतार्दिता इव.. 21.145 ..
1.4.m: Exhausted, the gods and [even] the Daityas could find no refuge; / their whole bodies pierced by the Daitya’s weapons, like cows afflicted by cold,

1.4.s:
parasparaṃ vyalīyaṃta hāhākiṃbhāvivādinaḥ..
tāmavasthāṃ harirdṛṣṭvā devāñchakramuvāca ha.. 21.146 ..
1.4.d:
परस्परं व्यलीयंत हाहाकिंभाविवादिनः..
तामवस्थां हरिर्दृष्ट्वा देवाञ्छक्रमुवाच ह.. 21.146 ..
1.4.m: they clung to one another, lamenting, “Alas, alas, what will happen?” / Seeing that plight of the gods, Hari said to Śakra:

1.4.s:
aghoramaṃtraṃ smara devarāja astraṃ hi yatpāśupataprabhāvam..
rudreṇa tuṣṭena tava pradattamavyāhataṃ vīravarābhighāti.. 21.147 ..
1.4.d:
अघोरमंत्रं स्मर देवराज अस्त्रं हि यत्पाशुपतप्रभावम्..
रुद्रेण तुष्टेन तव प्रदत्तमव्याहतं वीरवराभिघाति.. 21.147 ..
1.4.m: “Remember the Aghora mantra, O King of Gods, for it is the weapon having the power of the Pāśupata, / bestowed upon you by Rudra when he was pleased—irresistible, slayer of foremost heroes.”

1.4.s:
evaṃ sa śakro haribodhitastadā praṇamya devaṃ vṛṣaketumīśvaram..
samādade bāṇamamitraghātanaṃ saṃpūjitaṃ daivaraṇe'rddhacaṃdram.. 21.148 ..
1.4.d:
एवं स शक्रो हरिबोधितस्तदा प्रणम्य देवं वृषकेतुमीश्वरम्..
समाददे बाणममित्रघातनं संपूजितं दैवरणेऽर्द्धचंद्रम्.. 21.148 ..
1.4.m: Thus awakened by Hari, Śakra bowed to the lord god whose banner bears a bull; / he took up the crescent-shaped arrow that destroys enemies, revered in divine warfare.

1.4.s: dhanuṣyajayye viniyojya buddhimānnyayojayattatra aghoramaṃtram.. 21.149 ..
1.4.d: धनुष्यजय्ये विनियोज्य बुद्धिमान्न्ययोजयत्तत्र अघोरमंत्रम्.. 21.149 ..
1.4.m: Fitting it to his invincible bow, the wise one charged it with the Aghora mantra.

1.4.s:
tato vadhāyāśu mumoca tasya vā ākṛṣya karṇāṃtamakuṃṭhadīdhitim..
athāsuraḥ prekṣya mahāstramāpatadvisṛjya māyāṃ sahasā vyavasthitaḥ.. 21.150 ..
1.4.d:
ततो वधायाशु मुमोच तस्य वा आकृष्य कर्णांतमकुंठदीधितिम्..
अथासुरः प्रेक्ष्य महास्त्रमापतद्विसृज्य मायां सहसा व्यवस्थितः.. 21.150 ..
1.4.m: Then, drawing it to the edge of his ear, he loosed that arrow of unblunted radiance for his swift destruction. / Thereupon the Asura, seeing the great weapon falling upon him, instantly abandoned his illusion and stood firm.

1.4.s:
pravepamānena mukhena yujyatācalena gātreṇa ca saṃbhramākulaḥ..
tatastu tasyāstravarābhimaṃtritaḥ śarordhacaṃdraḥ prasabhaṃ mahāraṇe.. 21.151 ..
1.4.d:
प्रवेपमानेन मुखेन युज्यताचलेन गात्रेण च संभ्रमाकुलः..
ततस्तु तस्यास्त्रवराभिमंत्रितः शरोर्धचंद्रः प्रसभं महारणे.. 21.151 ..
1.4.m: With trembling mouth and steady body, confused with perturbation, / then, energized by that supreme weapon, the crescent arrow in that great battle,

1.4.s: puraṃdarasyeṣvasanapramukto madhyārkaviṃvaṃ vapuṣā viḍaṃbayan.. 21.152 ..
1.4.d: पुरंदरस्येष्वसनप्रमुक्तो मध्यार्कविंवं वपुषा विडंबयन्.. 21.152 ..
1.4.m: shot from the bow of Puraṃdara, imitating with its form the orb of the midday sun,

1.4.s:
kirīṭakūṭasphurakāṃtisaṃkulaṃ sugaṃdhinānākusumādhivāsitam..
prakīrṇadhūmajvalanābhamūrdhajaṃ nyapātayajjaṃbhiśiraḥ sakuṃḍalam.. 21.153 ..
1.4.d:
किरीटकूटस्फुरकांतिसंकुलं सुगंधिनानाकुसुमाधिवासितम्..
प्रकीर्णधूमज्वलनाभमूर्धजं न्यपातयज्जंभिशिरः सकुंडलम्.. 21.153 ..
1.4.m: struck down Jambha’s head adorned with earrings—thick with the flashing brilliance of a crest of diadems, perfumed with various fragrant flowers, / with hair resembling scattered smoke and fire.

1.4.s:
tasminniṃdrahate jaṃbhe praśaśaṃsuḥ surā bahu..
vāsudevo'pi bhagavānsādhu sādhviti cābravīt.. 21.154 ..
1.4.d:
तस्मिन्निंद्रहते जंभे प्रशशंसुः सुरा बहु..
वासुदेवोऽपि भगवान्साधु साध्विति चाब्रवीत्.. 21.154 ..
1.4.m: When Jambha was slain by Indra, the gods praised him greatly; / and the blessed Vāsudeva also said, “Well done! Well done!”

1.4.s:
tato jaṃbhaṃ hataṃ dṛṣṭvā dānavendrāḥ parāṅ‌mukhāḥ..
sarve te bhagnasaṃkalpā dudruvustārakaṃ prati.. 21.155 ..
1.4.d:
ततो जंभं हतं दृष्ट्वा दानवेन्द्राः पराङ्‌मुखाः..
सर्वे ते भग्नसंकल्पा दुद्रुवुस्तारकं प्रति.. 21.155 ..
1.4.m: Then, seeing Jambha slain, the chiefs of the Dānavas turned their backs; / with their resolves shattered, they all fled toward Tāraka.

1.4.s:
tāṃśca trastānsamālokya śrutvā sa caturo hatān..
sārathiṃ prerayāmāsa yāhīṃdraṃ laghu saṃgare.. 21.156 ..
1.4.d:
तांश्च त्रस्तान्समालोक्य श्रुत्वा स चतुरो हतान्..
सारथिं प्रेरयामास याहींद्रं लघु संगरे.. 21.156 ..
1.4.m: Seeing them terrified and hearing that the four had been killed, / he urged his charioteer: 'Drive quickly toward Indra in battle!'

1.4.s:
tathetyuktvā sa ca prāyāttārake rathamāsthite..
sāvalepaṃ ca sakrodhaṃ sagarvaṃ saparākramam.. 21.157 ..
1.4.d:
तथेत्युक्त्वा स च प्रायात्तारके रथमास्थिते..
सावलेपं च सक्रोधं सगर्वं सपराक्रमम्.. 21.157 ..
1.4.m: Saying 'So be it,' he drove forth as Tāraka mounted his chariot— / full of haughtiness, wrath, pride, and prowess,

1.4.s:
sāviṣkāraṃ sadhikkāraṃ prayāto dānaveśvaraḥ..
sa yuktaṃ rathamāsthāya sahasreṇa garutmatām.. 21.158 ..
1.4.d:
साविष्कारं सधिक्कारं प्रयातो दानवेश्वरः..
स युक्तं रथमास्थाय सहस्रेण गरुत्मताम्.. 21.158 ..
1.4.m: manifesting [his power] and shouting defiance, the lord of the Dānavas advanced. / He mounted a chariot yoked with a thousand eagles,

1.4.s:
sarvāyudhapariṣkāraṃ sarvāstraparirakṣitam..
trailokyaṛddhisaṃpannaṃ kalpāṃtāṃtakanāditam.. 21.159 ..
1.4.d:
सर्वायुधपरिष्कारं सर्वास्त्रपरिरक्षितम्..
त्रैलोक्यऋद्धिसंपन्नं कल्पांतांतकनादितम्.. 21.159 ..
1.4.m: equipped with every weapon, protected by every missile, / filled with the prosperity of the three worlds, resounding like the Destroyer at the end of an eon.

1.4.s:
sainyena mahatā yukto nādayanvidiśo diśaḥ..
sahasrākṣaśca taṃ dṛṣṭvā tyaktvā vāhanadaṃtinam.. 21.160 ..
1.4.d:
सैन्येन महता युक्तो नादयन्विदिशो दिशः..
सहस्राक्षश्च तं दृष्ट्वा त्यक्त्वा वाहनदंतिनम्.. 21.160 ..
1.4.m: Accompanied by a great army, making the cardinal and intermediate directions resound, / the thousand-eyed [Indra], seeing him, abandoned his elephant mount,

1.4.s:
rathaṃ mātalinā yuktaṃ taptahemapariṣkṛtam..
caturyojanavistīrṇaṃ siddhasaṃghapariṣkṛtam.. 21.161 ..
1.4.d:
रथं मातलिना युक्तं तप्तहेमपरिष्कृतम्..
चतुर्योजनविस्तीर्णं सिद्धसंघपरिष्कृतम्.. 21.161 ..
1.4.m: and [boarded] the chariot driven by Mātali, adorned with refined gold, / four yojanas in breadth, surrounded by hosts of Siddhas,

1.4.s: gaṃdharvakiṃnarodgītamapsaronṛtyasaṃkulam.. 21.162 ..
1.4.d: गंधर्वकिंनरोद्गीतमप्सरोनृत्यसंकुलम्.. 21.162 ..
1.4.m: celebrated in song by Gandharvas and Kinnaras, crowded with the dancing of apsarases,

1.4.s:
sarvāyudhamahābādhaṃ mahāratnasamācitam..
adhyatiṣṭhattaṃ rathaṃ ca parivārya samaṃtataḥ.. 21.163 ..
1.4.d:
सर्वायुधमहाबाधं महारत्नसमाचितम्..
अध्यतिष्ठत्तं रथं च परिवार्य समंततः.. 21.163 ..
1.4.m: greatly formidable with all kinds of weapons, and encrusted with magnificent jewels. / Having surrounded that chariot on all sides, they stood,

1.4.s:
dāṃśitā lokapālāśca tasathuḥ sagaruḍadhvajāḥ..
tataścacāla vasudhā vavau rūkṣo marudgaṇaiḥ.. 21.164 ..
1.4.d:
दांशिता लोकपालाश्च तसथुः सगरुडध्वजाः..
ततश्चचाल वसुधा ववौ रूक्षो मरुद्गणैः.. 21.164 ..
1.4.m: the guardians of the quarters, clad in mail, standing with the eagle-bannered [Viṣṇu]. / Then the earth trembled, and a harsh wind blew through the troops of Maruts;

1.4.s:
celuśca sāgarāḥ sapta tathā'naśyadraveḥ prabhā..
tato jajvalurastrāṇi tato'kaṃpaṃta vāhanāḥ.. 21.165 ..
1.4.d:
चेलुश्च सागराः सप्त तथाऽनश्यद्रवेः प्रभा..
ततो जज्वलुरस्त्राणि ततोऽकंपंत वाहनाः.. 21.165 ..
1.4.m: the seven oceans stirred, and the radiance of the sun perished; / then the missiles blazed, and then the mounts trembled.

1.4.s:
tataḥ samastamudvṛttaṃ tatodṛsyata tārakaḥ..
ekatastārako daityaḥ surasaṃghāstathaikataḥ.. 21.166 ..
1.4.d:
ततः समस्तमुद्वृत्तं ततोदृस्यत तारकः..
एकतस्तारको दैत्यः सुरसंघास्तथैकतः.. 21.166 ..
1.4.m: Then everything was agitated, and then Tāraka was seen: / on one side stood the Daitya Tāraka, and on the other, the hosts of gods;

1.4.s:
lokāvasāda mekatra lokoddharaṇamekataḥ..
carācarāṇi bhūtāni bhayavismayavaṃti ca.. 21.167 ..
1.4.d:
लोकावसाद मेकत्र लोकोद्धरणमेकतः..
चराचराणि भूतानि भयविस्मयवंति च.. 21.167 ..
1.4.m: on one side was the ruin of the world, on the other the world's deliverance; / and all moving and unmoving creatures were filled with fear and wonder.

1.4.s: praśaśaṃsuḥ surāḥ pārtha tadā tasminsamāgame.. 21.168 ..
1.4.d: प्रशशंसुः सुराः पार्थ तदा तस्मिन्समागमे.. 21.168 ..
1.4.m: O Pārtha, the gods shouted praise in that encounter:

1.4.s:
astrāṇi tejāṃsi dhanāni yodhā yaśo balaṃ vīraparākramāśca..
sattvaujasānyaṃga babhūvureṣāṃ devāsurāṇāṃ tapasaḥ paraṃ tu naḥ.. 21.169 ..
1.4.d:
अस्त्राणि तेजांसि धनानि योधा यशो बलं वीरपराक्रमाश्च..
सत्त्वौजसान्यंग बभूवुरेषां देवासुराणां तपसः परं तु नः.. 21.169 ..
1.4.m: 'Missiles, splendors, riches, warriors, renown, strength, and heroic valor, / were the courage and vigor of these gods and Asuras; but our [strength] comes entirely from austerity!'

1.4.s:
athābhimukhamāyāṃtaṃ devā vinatarpavabhiḥ..
bāṇairanalakalpāgrārvivyadhustārakaṃ prati.. 21.170 ..
1.4.d:
अथाभिमुखमायांतं देवा विनतर्पवभिः..
बाणैरनलकल्पाग्रार्विव्यधुस्तारकं प्रति.. 21.170 ..
1.4.m: Then, as he approached, the gods with straight-flying shafts / tipped with fire-like points shot against Tāraka.

1.4.s:
sa tānaciṃtya daityeṃdro devabāṇakṣatānhṛdi..
bāṇairvyoma diśaḥ pṛthvīṃ pūrayāmāsa dānavaḥ.. 21.171 ..
1.4.d:
स तानचिंत्य दैत्येंद्रो देवबाणक्षतान्हृदि..
बाणैर्व्योम दिशः पृथ्वीं पूरयामास दानवः.. 21.171 ..
1.4.m: Taking no heed of those gods' arrows striking his chest, that lord of Daityas, / the Dānava filled the sky, the quarters, and the earth with his arrows.

1.4.s:
nārāyaṇaṃ ca saptatyā navatyā ca hutāśanam..
daśabhirmārutaṃ mūrdhni yamaṃ daśabhireva ca.. 21.172 ..
1.4.d:
नारायणं च सप्तत्या नवत्या च हुताशनम्..
दशभिर्मारुतं मूर्ध्नि यमं दशभिरेव च.. 21.172 ..
1.4.m: He pierced Nārāyaṇa with seventy, the Fire-god with ninety, / the Wind on the head with ten, and Yama with ten as well;

1.4.s:
dhanadaṃ caiva saptyā varuṇaṃ ca tathāṣṭabhiḥ..
viṃśatyā nirṛtiṃ daityaḥ punaścāṣṭabhireva ca.. 21.173 ..
1.4.d:
धनदं चैव सप्त्या वरुणं च तथाष्टभिः..
विंशत्या निरृतिं दैत्यः पुनश्चाष्टभिरेव च.. 21.173 ..
1.4.m: and the Giver of Wealth with seventy, and likewise Varuṇa with eight, / the Daitya struck Nirṛti with twenty, and again with eight;

1.4.s:
vivyādha punarekaikaṃ daśabhirmarmabhedibhiḥ..
tathā ca mātaliṃ daityo vivyādha tribhirāśugaiḥ.. 21.174 ..
1.4.d:
विव्याध पुनरेकैकं दशभिर्मर्मभेदिभिः..
तथा च मातलिं दैत्यो विव्याध त्रिभिराशुगैः.. 21.174 ..
1.4.m: again he pierced each one with ten arrows that penetrate vital spots; / and likewise the Daitya pierced Mātali with three swift shafts,

1.4.s:
garuḍaṃ daśabhiścaiva mahiṣaṃ navabhistathā..
punardairtyo'tha devānāṃ tilaśo nataparvabhiḥ.. 21.175 ..
1.4.d:
गरुडं दशभिश्चैव महिषं नवभिस्तथा..
पुनर्दैर्त्योऽथ देवानां तिलशो नतपर्वभिः.. 21.175 ..
1.4.m: and Garuḍa with ten, and the buffalo [of Yama] with nine. / Then the Daitya, with straight-jointed arrows, reduced to sesame-sized pieces

1.4.s:
cakāra varmajālāni ciccheda ca dhanūṃṣi ca..
tato vikavacā devā vidhanuṣkāḥ prapīḍitāḥ.. 21.176 ..
1.4.d:
चकार वर्मजालानि चिच्छेद च धनूंषि च..
ततो विकवचा देवा विधनुष्काः प्रपीडिताः.. 21.176 ..
1.4.m: the gods' coats of mail and severed their bows. / Then the gods, deprived of armor and bows, severely afflicted,

1.4.s:
cāpānyanyāni saṃgṛhya yāvanmuṃcaṃti sāyakān..
tāvadbāṇaṃ samādhāya kālānalasamaprabham.. 21.177 ..
1.4.d:
चापान्यन्यानि संगृह्य यावन्मुंचंति सायकान्..
तावद्बाणं समाधाय कालानलसमप्रभम्.. 21.177 ..
1.4.m: seized other bows, but as they were releasing their arrows, / he aimed an arrow blazing like the fire of cosmic dissolution,

1.4.s:
tāḍayāmāsa śakraṃ sa hṛdi sopi mumocaha..
tatoṃ'tarikṣamālokya dṛṣṭvā sūryaśatākṛtī.. 21.178 ..
1.4.d:
ताडयामास शक्रं स हृदि सोपि मुमोचह..
ततोंऽतरिक्षमालोक्य दृष्ट्वा सूर्यशताकृती.. 21.178 ..
1.4.m: and struck Śakra in the chest; he too fainted. / Then, looking up into the sky and seeing those two who resembled a hundred suns,

1.4.s:
tārkṣyaviṣṇū samājaghne śarābhyāṃ tāvamuhyatām..
pretanāthasya vahneśca varuṇasya śitaiḥ śaraiḥ.. 21.179 ..
1.4.d:
तार्क्ष्यविष्णू समाजघ्ने शराभ्यां तावमुह्यताम्..
प्रेतनाथस्य वह्नेश्च वरुणस्य शितैः शरैः.. 21.179 ..
1.4.m: he struck Tārkṣya and Viṣṇu with two arrows so that both swooned. / With sharp arrows, he confounded the lord of spirits, Agni, and Varuṇa,

1.4.s:
nirṛteścākarotkāryaṃ bhītabītaṃ vimohayan..
nirucchvāsaṃ samāhṛtya cakre bāṇaiḥ samīraṇam.. 21.180 ..
1.4.d:
निरृतेश्चाकरोत्कार्यं भीतबीतं विमोहयन्..
निरुच्छ्वासं समाहृत्य चक्रे बाणैः समीरणम्.. 21.180 ..
1.4.m: and rendered Nirṛti utterly helpless, making them tremble in terror; / trapping the Wind with his arrows, he left him breathless.

1.4.s:
tataḥ prāpya hariḥ saṃjñāṃ protsāhya ca diśāṃ patīn..
bāṇena sāratheḥ kāyācchiro'hārṣītsakuṇḍalam.. 21.181 ..
1.4.d:
ततः प्राप्य हरिः संज्ञां प्रोत्साह्य च दिशां पतीन्..
बाणेन सारथेः कायाच्छिरोऽहार्षीत्सकुण्डलम्.. 21.181 ..
1.4.m: Then Hari, regaining consciousness and rallying the lords of the quarters, / severed with an arrow the head of [Tāraka's] charioteer, earring and all, from his body.

1.4.s:
dhūmaketorjvalātkruddhastasya cchittvā nyapātayat..
daityarājakirīṭayaṃ ca ciccheda vāsavastataḥ.. 21.182 ..
1.4.d:
धूमकेतोर्ज्वलात्क्रुद्धस्तस्य च्छित्त्वा न्यपातयत्..
दैत्यराजकिरीटयं च चिच्छेद वासवस्ततः.. 21.182 ..
1.4.m: Enraged, he cut down the flaming comet-banner [of the chariot]; / then Vāsava sheared off the crown of the Daitya king;

1.4.s:
dhaneśaśca dhanuḥ kruddho bibhedabahudhā śaraiḥ..
vāyuścakre ca tilaśo rathaṃ vā kṣoṇikūbaram.. 21.183 ..
1.4.d:
धनेशश्च धनुः क्रुद्धो बिभेदबहुधा शरैः..
वायुश्चक्रे च तिलशो रथं वा क्षोणिकूबरम्.. 21.183 ..
1.4.m: and the lord of wealth, angered, shattered his bow in many pieces with arrows; / Vāyu reduced the chariot and its axle to sesame-sized fragments;

1.4.s:
nirṛtistilaśo varṇa cakre bāṇaistato raṇe..
kṛtvaitadatulaṃ karmatiṣṭhatiṣṭheti cābruvan.. 21.184 ..
1.4.d:
निरृतिस्तिलशो वर्ण चक्रे बाणैस्ततो रणे..
कृत्वैतदतुलं कर्मतिष्ठतिष्ठेति चाब्रुवन्.. 21.184 ..
1.4.m: then in the battle, Nirṛti sliced his armor into sesame-sized pieces with arrows. / Having performed this peerless deed, they cried, 'Halt! Halt!'

1.4.s:
lihaṃtaḥ sṛkkiṇīṃ devā vāsudevādayastadā..
dṛṣṭvā tatkarma devānāṃ tārako'tulavikramaḥ.. 21.185 ..
1.4.d:
लिहंतः सृक्किणीं देवा वासुदेवादयस्तदा..
दृष्ट्वा तत्कर्म देवानां तारकोऽतुलविक्रमः.. 21.185 ..
1.4.m: Licking the corners of their mouths, the gods headed by Vāsudeva stood firm. / Seeing that deed of the gods, Tāraka of matchless prowess

1.4.s:
mumoca mudgaraṃ bhīmaṃ sahasrākṣāya saṃgare..
dṛṣṭvā mudgaramāyāṃtamanivāryaṃ raṇājire.. 21.186 ..
1.4.d:
मुमोच मुद्गरं भीमं सहस्राक्षाय संगरे..
दृष्ट्वा मुद्गरमायांतमनिवार्यं रणाजिरे.. 21.186 ..
1.4.m: hurled a dread club at the thousand-eyed [Indra] in the battle. / Seeing the irresistible club coming across the battlefield,

1.4.s:
rathādāplutya dharaṇīmagamatpākaśāsanaḥ..
mudgaro'pi rathopasthe papāta paruṣasvanaḥ.. 21.187 ..
1.4.d:
रथादाप्लुत्य धरणीमगमत्पाकशासनः..
मुद्गरोऽपि रथोपस्थे पपात परुषस्वनः.. 21.187 ..
1.4.m: the subduer of Pāka leaped from the chariot and went to the ground; / the club fell upon the chariot-seat with a harsh roar.

1.4.s:
sa rathaṃ cūrṇayāmāsa na mamāra ca mātaliḥ..
gṛhītvā paṭṭiśaṃ daityo jadhānorasi keśavam.. 21.188 ..
1.4.d:
स रथं चूर्णयामास न ममार च मातलिः..
गृहीत्वा पट्टिशं दैत्यो जधानोरसि केशवम्.. 21.188 ..
1.4.m: It pulverized the chariot, but Mātali did not die. / Grasping a spear, the Daitya struck Keśava on the chest;

1.4.s:
skandhe garutmataḥ so'pi niṣasāda vicetanaḥ..
khaḍgena rākṣasendraṃ ca bhittvā bhūmāvapātayat.. 21.189 ..
1.4.d:
स्कन्धे गरुत्मतः सोऽपि निषसाद विचेतनः..
खड्गेन राक्षसेन्द्रं च भित्त्वा भूमावपातयत्.. 21.189 ..
1.4.m: he sank down unconscious on the shoulder of Garutmat. / Piercing the king of the Rākṣasas with a sword, he felled him to the earth,

1.4.s:
yamaṃ ca pātayāmāsa bhūmau daityo mukhe hatam..
vahniṃ ca bhiṃḍipālena cakre hatvā vicetanam.. 21.190 ..
1.4.d:
यमं च पातयामास भूमौ दैत्यो मुखे हतम्..
वह्निं च भिंडिपालेन चक्रे हत्वा विचेतनम्.. 21.190 ..
1.4.m: and the Daitya felled Yama to the earth, having struck him in the face; / and striking Agni with a sling-missile, he rendered him senseless.

1.4.s:
vāyuṃ padā tadākṣipya pātayāmāsa bhūtale..
dhaneśaṃ taddhanuṣkoṭyā kuṭṭayāmāsa kopanaḥ.. 21.191 ..
1.4.d:
वायुं पदा तदाक्षिप्य पातयामास भूतले..
धनेशं तद्धनुष्कोट्या कुट्टयामास कोपनः.. 21.191 ..
1.4.m: Then, kicking Vāyu with his foot, he threw him down to the ground; / enraged, he beat the lord of wealth with the tip of his bow.

1.4.s:
tato devanikāyānāmekaikaṃ kṣaṇamātrataḥ..
teṣāmeva jaghānāsau śastrairbālānyathā guruḥ.. 21.192 ..
1.4.d:
ततो देवनिकायानामेकैकं क्षणमात्रतः..
तेषामेव जघानासौ शस्त्रैर्बालान्यथा गुरुः.. 21.192 ..
1.4.m: Then, in merely a moment, he struck down each of the hosts of gods / with their very own weapons, like a teacher striking boys.

1.4.s:
labdhasaṃjñastato viṣṇuścakraṃ jagrāha durdharam..
rānaveṃdravasāmedorudhireṇābhiraṃjitam.. 21.193 ..
1.4.d:
लब्धसंज्ञस्ततो विष्णुश्चक्रं जग्राह दुर्धरम्..
रानवेंद्रवसामेदोरुधिरेणाभिरंजितम्.. 21.193 ..
1.4.m: Then Viṣṇu, having regained his senses, seized his irresistible discus / stained with the fat, marrow, and blood of lordly Dānavas.

1.4.s:
mumoca dānaveṃdrasya dṛḍhaṃ vakṣasi keśavaḥ..
papāta cakraṃ daityasya patitaṃ bhāskaradyuti.. 21.194 ..
1.4.d:
मुमोच दानवेंद्रस्य दृढं वक्षसि केशवः..
पपात चक्रं दैत्यस्य पतितं भास्करद्युति.. 21.194 ..
1.4.m: Keśava hurled it hard against the chest of the lord of Dānavas; / the discus, radiant as the sun, struck the Daitya,

1.4.s:
vyaśīryatātha kāye'sya nīlotpalamivāśmani..
tato vajraṃ mahendro'pi pramumocārcitaṃ ciram.. 21.195 ..
1.4.d:
व्यशीर्यताथ कायेऽस्य नीलोत्पलमिवाश्मनि..
ततो वज्रं महेन्द्रोऽपि प्रमुमोचार्चितं चिरम्.. 21.195 ..
1.4.m: and shattered against his body like a blue lotus against a stone. / Then Mahendra too hurled his thunderbolt, long worshiped,

1.4.s:
tasmiñjayāśā śakrasya dānavendrāya saṃyuge..
tārakasya ca saṃprāpya śarīraṃ śauryaśālinaḥ.. 21.196 ..
1.4.d:
तस्मिञ्जयाशा शक्रस्य दानवेन्द्राय संयुगे..
तारकस्य च संप्राप्य शरीरं शौर्यशालिनः.. 21.196 ..
1.4.m: in which rested Śakra's hope of victory against the Dānava king in battle; / but striking the body of the valiant Tāraka,

1.4.s:
viśīryata vikīrṇārciḥ śatadhā khaṇḍaśo gatam..
tato vāyuradīnātmā vegena mahatā nadan.. 21.197 ..
1.4.d:
विशीर्यत विकीर्णार्चिः शतधा खण्डशो गतम्..
ततो वायुरदीनात्मा वेगेन महता नदन्.. 21.197 ..
1.4.m: it shattered, its flames scattered, broken into a hundred pieces. / Then the dauntless Vāyu, roaring with great speed,

1.4.s:
jvalitajvalanābhāsamaṃkuśaṃ pramumoca ha..
viśīrṇaṃ tasya taccāṃge dṛṣṭvā vāyurmahāruṣā.. 21.198 ..
1.4.d:
ज्वलितज्वलनाभासमंकुशं प्रमुमोच ह..
विशीर्णं तस्य तच्चांगे दृष्ट्वा वायुर्महारुषा.. 21.198 ..
1.4.m: hurled an elephant-goad resembling blazing fire; / seeing that it too was shattered on his body, Vāyu, in great wrath,

1.4.s:
tataḥ śailendramutpāṭya puṣpitadrumakaṃdaram..
cikṣepa dānavendrāya daśayojanavistṛtam.. 21.199 ..
1.4.d:
ततः शैलेन्द्रमुत्पाट्य पुष्पितद्रुमकंदरम्..
चिक्षेप दानवेन्द्राय दशयोजनविस्तृतम्.. 21.199 ..
1.4.m: then uprooted a lordly mountain, rich in blossoming trees and caves, / ten yojanas wide, and hurled it at the Dānava king.

1.4.s:
mahīdharaṃ tamāyāṃtaṃ sasmitaṃ daityapuṃgavaḥ..
jagrāha vāmahastena bālaḥ kandukalīlayā.. 21.200 ..
1.4.d:
महीधरं तमायांतं सस्मितं दैत्यपुंगवः..
जग्राह वामहस्तेन बालः कन्दुकलीलया.. 21.200 ..
1.4.m:
As that mountain was hurtling toward him, the best of Daityas, smiling,
caught it with his left hand, like a boy playfully catching a ball.

1.4.s:
tatastenaiva cāhatya pātayāmāsa cāṃtakam..
daṇḍaṃ tataḥ samudyamya kṛtāṃtaḥ krodhamūrchitaḥ.. 21.201 ..
1.4.d:
ततस्तेनैव चाहत्य पातयामास चांतकम्..
दण्डं ततः समुद्यम्य कृतांतः क्रोधमूर्छितः.. 21.201 ..
1.4.m:
Then, striking with that very mountain, he felled Antaka.
Thereupon Kṛtānta, having raised his staff, stupefied with rage,

1.4.s:
daityendramūrdhni cikṣepa bhrāmya vegena durjayam..
so'surasyāpatanmūrdhni daityastaṃ jagṛhe smayan.. 21.202 ..
1.4.d:
दैत्येन्द्रमूर्ध्नि चिक्षेप भ्राम्य वेगेन दुर्जयम्..
सोऽसुरस्यापतन्मूर्ध्नि दैत्यस्तं जगृहे स्मयन्.. 21.202 ..
1.4.m:
whirled it with speed and hurled the unconquerable weapon at the Daitya lord's head.
It fell upon the Asura's head; the Daitya, smiling, seized it.

1.4.s:
kalpāṃtalokadahano jvalano roṣasaṃjvalan..
śaktiṃ cikṣepadurdharṣāṃ dānavendrāya saṃyuge.. 21.203 ..
1.4.d:
कल्पांतलोकदहनो ज्वलनो रोषसंज्वलन्..
शक्तिं चिक्षेपदुर्धर्षां दानवेन्द्राय संयुगे.. 21.203 ..
1.4.m:
Jvalana, who burns the worlds at the end of an aeon, flaring up with anger,
hurled an unassailable lance at the lord of Dānavas in the battle.

1.4.s:
tataḥ śirīṣamāleva sāsya vakṣasyarājata..
tataḥ khaḍgaṃ samākṛṣya kośādākāśanirmalam.. 21.204 ..
1.4.d:
ततः शिरीषमालेव सास्य वक्षस्यराजत..
ततः खड्गं समाकृष्य कोशादाकाशनिर्मलम्.. 21.204 ..
1.4.m:
Then it shone upon his chest like a garland of śirīṣa flowers.
Then Nirṛti, a guardian of the world, drawing from its sheath a sword clear as the sky,

1.4.s:
dyuti bhāsitatrailokyaṃ lokapālo'pi nirṛtiḥ..
cikṣepa dānavendrāya tasya mūrdhni papāta ha.. 21.205 ..
1.4.d:
द्युति भासितत्रैलोक्यं लोकपालोऽपि निरृतिः..
चिक्षेप दानवेन्द्राय तस्य मूर्ध्नि पपात ह.. 21.205 ..
1.4.m:
which illuminated the three worlds with its splendour,
hurled it at the lord of Dānavas; it fell upon his head.

1.4.s:
patitaścāgamatkhaḍgaḥ sa śīghraṃ śatakhaṇḍatām..
jaleśaśca tataḥ kruddho mahābhairavarūpiṇam.. 21.206 ..
1.4.d:
पतितश्चागमत्खड्गः स शीघ्रं शतखण्डताम्..
जलेशश्च ततः क्रुद्धो महाभैरवरूपिणम्.. 21.206 ..
1.4.m:
And no sooner had the sword fallen than it quickly shattered into a hundred pieces.
Then the lord of waters, enraged, desiring to bind the Daitya lord's arms,

1.4.s:
mumoca pāśaṃ daityendrabhujabandhābilāṣukaḥ..
sa daityabhujamāsādya pāśaḥ sadyo vyapadyata.. 21.207 ..
1.4.d:
मुमोच पाशं दैत्येन्द्रभुजबन्धाबिलाषुकः..
स दैत्यभुजमासाद्य पाशः सद्यो व्यपद्यत.. 21.207 ..
1.4.m:
released his noose, which had assumed a terrifying form.
Reaching the Daitya's arm, that noose instantly perished;

1.4.s:
sphuṭitaḥ krakacakrūradaśanālirahīśvaraḥ..
tato'śvinau sacaṃdrārkau sādhyāśca vasavaśca ye.. 21.208 ..
1.4.d:
स्फुटितः क्रकचक्रूरदशनालिरहीश्वरः..
ततोऽश्विनौ सचंद्रार्कौ साध्याश्च वसवश्च ये.. 21.208 ..
1.4.m:
the lord of serpents burst apart, its rows of teeth as cruel as a saw.
Then the two Aśvins, along with the moon and sun, the Sādhyas, the Vasus,

1.4.s:
yakṣarākṣasaganadharvāḥ sarpāścāstraiḥ pṛthagvidhaiḥ..
jaghnurdaityeśvaraṃ sarve bhūyaśaste mahābalāḥ.. 21.209 ..
1.4.d:
यक्षराक्षसगनधर्वाः सर्पाश्चास्त्रैः पृथग्विधैः..
जघ्नुर्दैत्येश्वरं सर्वे भूयशस्ते महाबलाः.. 21.209 ..
1.4.m:
Yakṣas, Rākṣasas, Gandharvas, and serpents, all mighty warriors,
struck the lord of Daityas repeatedly with various kinds of missiles.

1.4.s:
na cāstrāṇyasyāsajjanta gātre vajrācalopame..
tato devanavaplutya tārako dānavādipaḥ.. 21.210 ..
1.4.d:
न चास्त्राण्यस्यासज्जन्त गात्रे वज्राचलोपमे..
ततो देवनवप्लुत्य तारको दानवादिपः.. 21.210 ..
1.4.m:
Yet the missiles did not even adhere to his body, which was like an adamantine mountain.
Then Tāraka, the ruler of Dānavas, leaping upon the gods,

1.4.s:
jaghāna koṭiśaḥ kruddho muṣṭipārṣṇibhireva ca..
tathāvidhaṃ tasya vīryamālokya bhagavānhariḥ.. 21.211 ..
1.4.d:
जघान कोटिशः क्रुद्धो मुष्टिपार्ष्णिभिरेव च..
तथाविधं तस्य वीर्यमालोक्य भगवान्हरिः.. 21.211 ..
1.4.m:
enraged, struck down millions of them with fists and heels.
Beholding such prowess belonging to him, the blessed Hari,

1.4.s:
palāyadhvamaho devā vadannantarhito'bhavat..
śakrādayastato devāḥ palāyanakṛtādarāḥ.. 21.212 ..
1.4.d:
पलायध्वमहो देवा वदन्नन्तर्हितोऽभवत्..
शक्रादयस्ततो देवाः पलायनकृतादराः.. 21.212 ..
1.4.m:
saying, “Flee, O gods!”, vanished.
Then Śakra and the other gods, eager to flee,

1.4.s:
kālanemimukhairdaityeruparuddhā madotkaṭaiḥ..
muṣṭibhiḥ pādaghātaiśca keśaṣvākṛṣya tairmudā.. 21.213 ..
1.4.d:
कालनेमिमुखैर्दैत्येरुपरुद्धा मदोत्कटैः..
मुष्टिभिः पादघातैश्च केशष्वाकृष्य तैर्मुदा.. 21.213 ..
1.4.m:
were blocked by Daityas headed by Kālanemi, who were fierce with arrogance.
With fists and kicks, dragging them gleefully by the hair,

1.4.s:
tāritāḥ śuṣkasaritaṃ devamārgāśca daṃśitāḥ..
bahudhā cāpyakṛṣyaṃta lokapālā mahāsuraiḥ.. 21.214 ..
1.4.d:
तारिताः शुष्कसरितं देवमार्गाश्च दंशिताः..
बहुधा चाप्यकृष्यंत लोकपाला महासुरैः.. 21.214 ..
1.4.m:
they were made to cross dry riverbeds and their paths were obstructed;
the guardians of the world were dragged about in many ways by the great Asuras.

1.4.s:
tato ninādaḥ saṃjajñe daityānāṃ balaśālinām..
kampayanpṛthivīṃ dyāṃ ca pātālāni ca bhārata.. 21.215 ..
1.4.d:
ततो निनादः संजज्ञे दैत्यानां बलशालिनाम्..
कम्पयन्पृथिवीं द्यां च पातालानि च भारत.. 21.215 ..
1.4.m:
Then an uproar arose from the mighty Daityas,
shaking the earth, the sky, and the subterranean realms, O Bhārata.

1.4.s:
jayeti muditā daityāstuṣṭuvustārakaṃ tadā..
śaṃkhāṃśca pūrayāmāsuḥ kundendusadṛśaprabhān.. 21.216 ..
1.4.d:
जयेति मुदिता दैत्यास्तुष्टुवुस्तारकं तदा..
शंखांश्च पूरयामासुः कुन्देन्दुसदृशप्रभान्.. 21.216 ..
1.4.m:
The joyous Daityas then praised Tāraka, crying, “Victory!”,
and blew conches possessing a radiance like the kunda flower and the moon.

1.4.s:
dhanurbāṇaravāṃścogrānkarāghātāṃśca cakrire..
bhṛśaṃ harṣānvitā daityā neduśca nanṛturmuhuḥ.. 21.217 ..
1.4.d:
धनुर्बाणरवांश्चोग्रान्कराघातांश्च चक्रिरे..
भृशं हर्षान्विता दैत्या नेदुश्च ननृतुर्मुहुः.. 21.217 ..
1.4.m:
They made fierce twangs of bows and arrows and clapped their hands.
Exceedingly filled with joy, the Daityas roared and danced again and again.

1.4.s:
tato devānpuraskṛtya paśupālaḥ paśūniva..
daityendro rathamāsthāya jagāma sahito'suraiḥ.. 21.218 ..
1.4.d:
ततो देवान्पुरस्कृत्य पशुपालः पशूनिव..
दैत्येन्द्रो रथमास्थाय जगाम सहितोऽसुरैः.. 21.218 ..
1.4.m:
Then, driving the gods before him like a cowherd driving cattle,
the lord of Daityas mounted his chariot and set out accompanied by the Asuras

1.4.s:
mahīsāgarakūlasthaṃ tārakaḥ sa puraṃ balī..
yojanadvādaśāyāmaṃ tāmraprākāraśobhitam.. 21.219 ..
1.4.d:
महीसागरकूलस्थं तारकः स पुरं बली..
योजनद्वादशायामं ताम्रप्राकारशोभितम्.. 21.219 ..
1.4.m:
to his city situated on the shore of the ocean at Mahī—the mighty Tāraka—
twelve yojanas in length, adorned with ramparts of copper,

1.4.s:
prāsādarbahubhiḥ kīrṇaṃ divyāścaryopaśobhitam..
yatra śabdāstrayo naiva jīryaṃte cāniśaṃpure.. 21.220 ..
1.4.d:
प्रासादर्बहुभिः कीर्णं दिव्याश्चर्योपशोभितम्..
यत्र शब्दास्त्रयो नैव जीर्यंते चानिशंपुरे.. 21.220 ..
1.4.m:
thronged with many palaces and embellished with divine marvels,
where three sounds never cease day and night in the city:

1.4.s:
gītaghoṣaśca vyāghoṣo bhujyaṃtāṃ viṣayāstviti..
tatpraviśya puraṃ rājā jagāma svakamālayam.. 21.221 ..
1.4.d:
गीतघोषश्च व्याघोषो भुज्यंतां विषयास्त्विति..
तत्प्रविश्य पुरं राजा जगाम स्वकमालयम्.. 21.221 ..
1.4.m:
the sound of singing, shouting, and [the call]: “Let sensory pleasures be enjoyed!”
Entering that city, the king went to his own abode

1.4.s:
mahotsavena mahatā putrastrīpratinaṃditaḥ..
tatra divyāṃ sabhāṃ rājā prāpya siṃhāsanasthitaḥ.. 21.222 ..
1.4.d:
महोत्सवेन महता पुत्रस्त्रीप्रतिनंदितः..
तत्र दिव्यां सभां राजा प्राप्य सिंहासनस्थितः.. 21.222 ..
1.4.m:
amid a great celebration, welcomed joyfully by sons and women.
There the king, having reached the divine assembly hall, sat upon the lion-throne,

1.4.s:
stūyamāno ditisutairapsarobhirvinoditaḥ..
divyāsanasthairdaityeṃdrairvṛtaḥ siṃhairiva prabhuḥ.. 21.223 ..
1.4.d:
स्तूयमानो दितिसुतैरप्सरोभिर्विनोदितः..
दिव्यासनस्थैर्दैत्येंद्रैर्वृतः सिंहैरिव प्रभुः.. 21.223 ..
1.4.m:
praised by the sons of Diti and entertained by apsarases,
the sovereign surrounded by Daitya lords seated on divine thrones, like [a king of beasts surrounded] by lions.

1.4.s:
etasminnaṃtare kāci ddivyastrī tatpure'bhavat..
vismitastairvṛto daityaiḥ provācedaṃ smayanniva.. 21.224 ..
1.4.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे काचि द्दिव्यस्त्री तत्पुरेऽभवत्..
विस्मितस्तैर्वृतो दैत्यैः प्रोवाचेदं स्मयन्निव.. 21.224 ..
1.4.m:
In the meantime, a certain divine woman appeared in that city.
Surrounded by those Daityas, he said this, astonished and smiling as it were:

1.4.s:
rūpeṇānupamā pārtha nānābharaṇabhūṣitā..
tāṃ dṛṣṭavā tārako rājā bhṛśaṃ vai vismito'bhavat.. 21.225 ..
1.4.d:
रूपेणानुपमा पार्थ नानाभरणभूषिता..
तां दृष्टवा तारको राजा भृशं वै विस्मितोऽभवत्.. 21.225 ..
1.4.m:
“Incomparable in beauty, O Pārtha, adorned with various ornaments!”
Seeing her, King Tāraka was greatly astonished:

1.4.s:
kāsi devī mama brūhi kiṃ mayā rūpasuṃdari..
tvatsamāṃ yoṣitaṃ naiva dṛṣṭavaṃtaḥ purā vayam.. 21.226 ..
1.4.d:
कासि देवी मम ब्रूहि किं मया रूपसुंदरि..
त्वत्समां योषितं नैव दृष्टवंतः पुरा वयम्.. 21.226 ..
1.4.m:
“Who are you, O goddess? Tell me, beautiful one, what can I do for you?
Never before have we seen a woman equal to you.”

1.4.s:
..stryuvāca..
ahaṃ trailokyalakṣmīti viddhi māṃ daityasattama..
arjitā tapasā cāsmi tvayā vīryeṇa vā vibho.. 21.227 ..
1.4.d:
..स्त्र्युवाच..
अहं त्रैलोक्यलक्ष्मीति विद्धि मां दैत्यसत्तम..
अर्जिता तपसा चास्मि त्वया वीर्येण वा विभो.. 21.227 ..

1.4.s:
vīryavaṃtaṃ tvanalasaṃ tapasvinamakātaram..
dātāraṃ cāpi bhoktāraṃ yuktyā sevāmi taṃ naram.. 21.228 ..
1.4.d:
वीर्यवंतं त्वनलसं तपस्विनमकातरम्..
दातारं चापि भोक्तारं युक्त्या सेवामि तं नरम्.. 21.228 ..
1.4.m:
I serve with devotion that man who is heroic, diligent, ascetic, undaunted,
a giver and also an enjoyer.

1.4.s:
bhīruṃ nirviṇṇmatyarthaṃ sādhvīpīḍākaraṃ naram..
sarvātiśaṃkinaṃ sadyastyajāmi ditinaṃdana.. 21.229 ..
1.4.d:
भीरुं निर्विण्ण्मत्यर्थं साध्वीपीडाकरं नरम्..
सर्वातिशंकिनं सद्यस्त्यजामि दितिनंदन.. 21.229 ..
1.4.m:
A man who is timid, excessively despondent, an afflicter of virtuous women,
and suspicious of everything, I abandon at once, O son of Diti.

1.4.s:
maheṃdraṇa ca mātā te yadā sā vyapamānitā..
tadaiva tyaktaprāyo'sāvidānīṃ tava saṃvaśe.. 21.230 ..
1.4.d:
महेंद्रण च माता ते यदा सा व्यपमानिता..
तदैव त्यक्तप्रायोऽसाविदानीं तव संवशे.. 21.230 ..
1.4.m:
And when that mother of yours was insulted by Mahendra,
at that very time he was virtually abandoned [by me]; now he is under your control.”

1.4.s:
tārakaśca tataḥ prāha paramaṃ ceti tāṃ tadā..
sā cāviveśa taṃ devī trijagatpūjitā ramā.. 21.231 ..
1.4.d:
तारकश्च ततः प्राह परमं चेति तां तदा..
सा चाविवेश तं देवी त्रिजगत्पूजिता रमा.. 21.231 ..
1.4.m:
And Tāraka then said to her, “Splendid!”
And that goddess, Ramā, worshipped by the three worlds, entered him.

1.4.s:
tato daityādhipaṃ nāryo dānavānāṃ vibhūṣitāḥ..
vīrakāṃsyamupādāya vardhayāṃcakrire mudā.. 21.232 ..
1.4.d:
ततो दैत्याधिपं नार्यो दानवानां विभूषिताः..
वीरकांस्यमुपादाय वर्धयांचक्रिरे मुदा.. 21.232 ..
1.4.m:
Then the adorned women of the Dānavas, taking up the hero's bronze dish,
joyously performed rites of congratulation for the lord of Daityas.

1.4.s:
devāśca dvāri tiṣṭhaṃti baddhā daityairbhṛśāturāḥ..
upahasyamānā nārībhirdaityairanyaiśca nāgaraiḥ.. 21.233 ..
1.4.d:
देवाश्च द्वारि तिष्ठंति बद्धा दैत्यैर्भृशातुराः..
उपहस्यमाना नारीभिर्दैत्यैरन्यैश्च नागरैः.. 21.233 ..
1.4.m:
Meanwhile, the gods stood at the gate, bound by the Daityas, deeply distressed,
mocked by the women, the Daityas, and other citizens.

1.4.s:
etasminnaṃtare viṣṇurdaityarūpaṃ samāsthitaḥ..
upahāsakamadhyastho gāthe dve prāha buddhimān.. 21.234 ..
1.4.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे विष्णुर्दैत्यरूपं समास्थितः..
उपहासकमध्यस्थो गाथे द्वे प्राह बुद्धिमान्.. 21.234 ..
1.4.m:
At that moment, the wise Viṣṇu, having assumed the form of a Daitya,
stood in the midst of the scoffers and spoke two verses:

1.4.s:
idamalpataraṃnāma yadamīṣāṃ ca dṛśyate..
mātṛkrodhaṃ smaranrājā kiṃkiṃ yanna kariṣyati.. 21.235 ..
1.4.d:
इदमल्पतरंनाम यदमीषां च दृश्यते..
मातृक्रोधं स्मरन्राजा किंकिं यन्न करिष्यति.. 21.235 ..
1.4.m:
“This that is seen happening to these [gods] is indeed very trifling;
remembering his mother's anger, what will the king not do?

1.4.s:
balīyāṃsaṃ samāsādya na namedyo na cāsti saḥ..
markavacchvetabākīyairupāyaiḥ sthīyatāṃ surāḥ.. 21.236 ..
1.4.d:
बलीयांसं समासाद्य न नमेद्यो न चास्ति सः..
मर्कवच्छ्वेतबाकीयैरुपायैः स्थीयतां सुराः.. 21.236 ..
1.4.m:
Having encountered someone stronger, who is there that would not bow?
O gods, remain [safe] like monkeys through the tricks of the white crane.”

1.4.s:
upahāsamukhenāmī upadeśaṃ harermukhāt..
samākarṇya tato devā markkarūpeṇa saṃsthitāḥ.. 21.237 ..
1.4.d:
उपहासमुखेनामी उपदेशं हरेर्मुखात्..
समाकर्ण्य ततो देवा मर्क्करूपेण संस्थिताः.. 21.237 ..
1.4.m:
Hearing this counsel from Hari's mouth under the guise of mockery,
the gods then assumed the form of monkeys.

1.4.s:
nṛtyaṃtaste ca bahudhā daityāścāsurayoṣitaḥ..
bhṛśaṃ ca nodayāmāsurmudā bhojyāni te daduḥ.. 21.238 ..
1.4.d:
नृत्यंतस्ते च बहुधा दैत्याश्चासुरयोषितः..
भृशं च नोदयामासुर्मुदा भोज्यानि ते ददुः.. 21.238 ..
1.4.m:
Dancing in many ways, the Daityas and Asura women
urged them on intensely and joyfully gave them foodstuffs.

1.4.s:
viṣṇurdaityapratīhāraṃ tataḥ provāca buddhimān..
vinodāya mahārājño markānetānprakīrtaya.. 21.239 ..
1.4.d:
विष्णुर्दैत्यप्रतीहारं ततः प्रोवाच बुद्धिमान्..
विनोदाय महाराज्ञो मर्कानेतान्प्रकीर्तय.. 21.239 ..
1.4.m:
Then the wise Viṣṇu spoke to the Daitya doorkeeper:
“Proclaim these monkeys for the entertainment of the great king.”

1.4.s:
pratīhārastato hṛṣṭaḥ sabhāmadhye viveśa saḥ..
jānubhyāṃ dharaṇīṃ gatvā baddhā ca karasaṃpuṭam.. 21.240 ..
1.4.d:
प्रतीहारस्ततो हृष्टः सभामध्ये विवेश सः..
जानुभ्यां धरणीं गत्वा बद्धा च करसंपुटम्.. 21.240 ..
1.4.m:
The doorkeeper then, delighted, entered the assembly hall;
falling to his knees upon the earth and joining his palms,

1.4.s:
uvācānāvilaṃ vākyamalpākṣaraparisphuṭam..
daityeṃdra markavṛṃdāni dvāri tiṣṭhaṃti te prabho.. 21.241 ..
1.4.d:
उवाचानाविलं वाक्यमल्पाक्षरपरिस्फुटम्..
दैत्येंद्र मर्कवृंदानि द्वारि तिष्ठंति ते प्रभो.. 21.241 ..
1.4.m:
he spoke clear words, concise and distinct:
“O lord of Daityas, troops of monkeys stand at your gate, O master,

1.4.s:
bhṛśaṃ vinodakāriṇi spṛhā ceddraṣṭumarhasi..
tanniśamyābravīdrājā kiṃ ciraṃ kriyate tvayā.. 21.242 ..
1.4.d:
भृशं विनोदकारिणि स्पृहा चेद्द्रष्टुमर्हसि..
तन्निशम्याब्रवीद्राजा किं चिरं क्रियते त्वया.. 21.242 ..
1.4.m:
providing great amusement; if you desire, you should see them.”
Hearing that, the king said: “Why are you delaying?”

1.4.s:
kṣattā ceti vacaḥ śrutvā kālanemiṃ tadābravīt..
markānetānmahārājo draṣṭumicchati śīghrataḥ.. 21.243 ..
1.4.d:
क्षत्ता चेति वचः श्रुत्वा कालनेमिं तदाब्रवीत्..
मर्कानेतान्महाराजो द्रष्टुमिच्छति शीघ्रतः.. 21.243 ..
1.4.m:
And hearing that word, the doorkeeper then said to Kālanemi:
“The great king wishes to see these monkeys at once.”

1.4.s:
rakṣapāla sahaibhistvaṃ rājānamanukūlaya..
kālanemirupādāya markānyāto nṛpaṃ tataḥ.. 21.244 ..
1.4.d:
रक्षपाल सहैभिस्त्वं राजानमनुकूलय..
कालनेमिरुपादाय मर्कान्यातो नृपं ततः.. 21.244 ..
1.4.m:
"O guard, gratify the king along with these!"
Then Kālanemi took the monkeys and went to the king.

1.4.s:
markamadhye viṣṇumarko yātastyaktvā ca daityatām..
tatastārakadaityasya purato nanṛturbhṛśam.. 21.245 ..
1.4.d:
मर्कमध्ये विष्णुमर्को यातस्त्यक्त्वा च दैत्यताम्..
ततस्तारकदैत्यस्य पुरतो ननृतुर्भृशम्.. 21.245 ..
1.4.m:
Among the monkeys, the monkey Viṣṇu went, having cast off his Daitya disguise.
Then they danced profusely before the Daitya Tāraka.

1.4.s:
markā daityakarottālairharṣanādavinoditaiḥ..
tato'timudito rājā teṣāṃ nṛtyena so'bravīt.. 21.246 ..
1.4.d:
मर्का दैत्यकरोत्तालैर्हर्षनादविनोदितैः..
ततोऽतिमुदितो राजा तेषां नृत्येन सोऽब्रवीत्.. 21.246 ..
1.4.m:
The monkeys [danced] to the clappings of the Daityas' hands, delighted by their joyous shouts.
Then the king, exceedingly pleased by their dance, said:

1.4.s:
abhayaṃ vo markadevāstuṣṭo yacchāmyahaṃ tvidam..
madgṛhe sthīyatāmeva na ca kāryaṃ bhayaṃ hṛdi.. 21.247 ..
1.4.d:
अभयं वो मर्कदेवास्तुष्टो यच्छाम्यहं त्विदम्..
मद्गृहे स्थीयतामेव न च कार्यं भयं हृदि.. 21.247 ..
1.4.m:
"O monkey-gods, I, being pleased, grant you freedom from fear:
Stay right here in my house, and let no fear be harboured in your heart!"

1.4.s:
iti śrutvā viṣṇumarkaḥ pranṛtyanni damabravīt..
rājanvijñātumicchāmastava gehāvadhiṃ vayam.. 21.248 ..
1.4.d:
इति श्रुत्वा विष्णुमर्कः प्रनृत्यन्नि दमब्रवीत्..
राजन्विज्ञातुमिच्छामस्तव गेहावधिं वयम्.. 21.248 ..
1.4.m:
Hearing this, the monkey Viṣṇu, dancing about, said this:
"O King, we wish to know the boundary of your house."

1.4.s:
evamukte prahasyāha tārako daityasattamaḥ..
tribhūmikaṃ hi me gehamidaṃ yadbhuvanatrayam.. 21.249 ..
1.4.d:
एवमुक्ते प्रहस्याह तारको दैत्यसत्तमः..
त्रिभूमिकं हि मे गेहमिदं यद्भुवनत्रयम्.. 21.249 ..
1.4.m:
When this was said, Tāraka, the best of Daityas, laughed and said:
"My house has three levels, for it is this triad of worlds."

1.4.s:
harimarkastataḥ prāha yadyevaṃ svaṃ vacaḥ smara..
trailokye vicaraṃtvete markā rājansunirbhayāḥ.. 21.250 ..
1.4.d:
हरिमर्कस्ततः प्राह यद्येवं स्वं वचः स्मर..
त्रैलोक्ये विचरंत्वेते मर्का राजन्सुनिर्भयाः.. 21.250 ..
1.4.m:
Then the monkey Hari said: "If that is so, remember your word!
Let these monkeys wander throughout the three worlds, O King, completely free from fear.

1.4.s:
aśvamedhaśatasyāpi satyaṃ rājanviśiṣyate..
dharmamenaṃ smaransatyaṃ vacanaṃ kuru daityapa.. 21.251 ..
1.4.d:
अश्वमेधशतस्यापि सत्यं राजन्विशिष्यते..
धर्ममेनं स्मरन्सत्यं वचनं कुरु दैत्यप.. 21.251 ..
1.4.m:
Truth surpasses even a hundred horse-sacrifices, O King.
Remembering this dharma, O ruler of Daityas, keep your word!"

1.4.s:
tataḥ suvismito daityaḥ prāhedaṃ vacanaṃ tadā..
markaṭāho prabuddho'si satyaṃ brūhi ca ko bhavān.. 21.252 ..
1.4.d:
ततः सुविस्मितो दैत्यः प्राहेदं वचनं तदा..
मर्कटाहो प्रबुद्धोऽसि सत्यं ब्रूहि च को भवान्.. 21.252 ..
1.4.m:
Then the Daitya, greatly astonished, said these words:
"Ah, monkey, you are enlightened! Tell the truth: who are you?"

1.4.s:
..śrībhagavānuvāca..
ahaṃ nārāyaṇonāma yadi śrotramupāgataḥ..
devānāṃ rakṣaṇārthāya markarūpamupāśritaḥ.. 21.253 ..
1.4.d:
..श्रीभगवानुवाच..
अहं नारायणोनाम यदि श्रोत्रमुपागतः..
देवानां रक्षणार्थाय मर्करूपमुपाश्रितः.. 21.253 ..
1.4.m:
The Blessed Lord said:
"I am known as Nārāyaṇa, if [the name] has come to your ear.
For the protection of the gods I have assumed the form of a monkey.

1.4.s:
taccenmānyatamo dharmastava tadvacanaṃ svakam..
paripālaya te gehaṃ vicaraṃtu surāstvamī.. 21.254 ..
1.4.d:
तच्चेन्मान्यतमो धर्मस्तव तद्वचनं स्वकम्..
परिपालय ते गेहं विचरंतु सुरास्त्वमी.. 21.254 ..
1.4.m:
If that dharma is most respected by you, then keep your word.
Let these gods wander through your house.

1.4.s:
avalopaśca rājeṃdra na kartavyastvayā hṛdī..
vīro'hamiti saṃcintya paśyatā kālajaṃ balam.. 21.255 ..
1.4.d:
अवलोपश्च राजेंद्र न कर्तव्यस्त्वया हृदी..
वीरोऽहमिति संचिन्त्य पश्यता कालजं बलम्.. 21.255 ..
1.4.m:
And, O lord of kings, you must not harbour defiance in your heart,
thinking 'I am a hero', seeing the power born of time.

1.4.s:
paryāyairhanyamānānāmabhihaṃtā na vidyate..
mauḍhyametattu yaddveṣṭā kartāhamiti manyate.. 21.256 ..
1.4.d:
पर्यायैर्हन्यमानानामभिहंता न विद्यते..
मौढ्यमेतत्तु यद्द्वेष्टा कर्ताहमिति मन्यते.. 21.256 ..
1.4.m:
Of those struck down in turn, there is no [individual] slayer;
it is mere delusion that an enemy thinks: 'I am the doer.'

1.4.s:
ṛṣīṃśca devāṃśca mahāsurāṃśca traividyavṛddhāṃśca vane munīṃśca..
kaṃ vāpado nopanamaṃti kāle kālasya vīryaṃ na tu karturetat.. 21.257 ..
1.4.d:
ऋषींश्च देवांश्च महासुरांश्च त्रैविद्यवृद्धांश्च वने मुनींश्च..
कं वापदो नोपनमंति काले कालस्य वीर्यं न तु कर्तुरेतत्.. 21.257 ..
1.4.m:
Seers, gods, great Asuras, elders learned in the three Vedas, and sages in the forest—
to whom do misfortunes not arrive in time? This is the power of time, not of the agent.

1.4.s:
na maṃtrabalavīryeṇa prajñayā pauruṣeṇa vā..
alabhyaṃ labhyate kāle kāle suptopi viṃdati.. 21.258 ..
1.4.d:
न मंत्रबलवीर्येण प्रज्ञया पौरुषेण वा..
अलभ्यं लभ्यते काले काले सुप्तोपि विंदति.. 21.258 ..
1.4.m:
Neither by the power and valour of mantras, nor by intellect or human effort,
is the unattainable obtained: in time, even one who is asleep obtains it.

1.4.s:
na mātṛpitṛśuśrūṣā na ca daivatapūjanam..
nānyo guṇasamācāraḥ puraṣasya sukhāvahaḥ.. 21.259 ..
1.4.d:
न मातृपितृशुश्रूषा न च दैवतपूजनम्..
नान्यो गुणसमाचारः पुरषस्य सुखावहः.. 21.259 ..
1.4.m:
Neither attendance upon mother and father, nor worship of a deity,
nor any other virtuous conduct brings happiness to a man [independently of time].

1.4.s:
na vidyā na tapo dānaṃ na mitrāṇi na vāṃdhavāḥ..
śaknuvaṃti paritrātuṃ naraṃ kālena pīḍitam.. 21.260 ..
1.4.d:
न विद्या न तपो दानं न मित्राणि न वांधवाः..
शक्नुवंति परित्रातुं नरं कालेन पीडितम्.. 21.260 ..
1.4.m:
Neither learning, nor austerity, nor gifts, nor friends, nor relatives
are able to protect a man afflicted by time.

1.4.s:
nāgāmigamanārthaṃ hi pratighātaśatairapi..
śaknuvaṃti prativyoḍhumṛte kālabalaṃ narāḥ.. 21.261 ..
1.4.d:
नागामिगमनार्थं हि प्रतिघातशतैरपि..
शक्नुवंति प्रतिव्योढुमृते कालबलं नराः.. 21.261 ..
1.4.m:
Indeed, without the power of time, men are unable with even a hundred obstacles
to ward off the course of what is to come.

1.4.s:
dehavatpuṇyakarmāṇi jīvavatkāla ucyate..
dvayoḥ samāgame daitya kāryāṇāṃ siddhiriṣyate.. 21.262 ..
1.4.d:
देहवत्पुण्यकर्माणि जीववत्काल उच्यते..
द्वयोः समागमे दैत्य कार्याणां सिद्धिरिष्यते.. 21.262 ..
1.4.m:
Meritorious deeds are like the body; time is said to be like the soul.
When the two unite, O Daitya, the success of actions is recognized.

1.4.s:
aho daitya tvadviśiṣṭā daityānāṃ koṭayaḥ purā..
śālmalestūlavatkṣiptāḥ kālavātena durdaśāḥ.. 21.263 ..
1.4.d:
अहो दैत्य त्वद्विशिष्टा दैत्यानां कोटयः पुरा..
शाल्मलेस्तूलवत्क्षिप्ताः कालवातेन दुर्दशाः.. 21.263 ..
1.4.m:
Ah, O Daitya! Formerly, crores of Daityas superior to you
were tossed like cotton from a silk-cotton tree by the wind of time into misery.

1.4.s:
idaṃ tu labdhvā tvaṃ sthānamātmānaṃ bahu manyase..
sarvabhūtabhavaṃ devaṃ brahmāṇamiva śāśvatam.. 21.264 ..
1.4.d:
इदं तु लब्ध्वा त्वं स्थानमात्मानं बहु मन्यसे..
सर्वभूतभवं देवं ब्रह्माणमिव शाश्वतम्.. 21.264 ..
1.4.m:
Having obtained this position, you think highly of yourself,
as if you were eternal, like the god Brahmā who is the origin of all beings.

1.4.s:
na cedamacalaṃ sthānamanaṃtaṃ cāpi kasyacit..
tvaṃ tu bāliśayā buddhyā mamedamiti manyase.. 21.265 ..
1.4.d:
न चेदमचलं स्थानमनंतं चापि कस्यचित्..
त्वं तु बालिशया बुद्ध्या ममेदमिति मन्यसे.. 21.265 ..
1.4.m:
This position is not unshakeable, nor is it endless for anyone;
and yet you, with childish intellect, think: 'This is mine!'

1.4.s:
aviśvāsye viśvasiṣi manyase cā'dhruvaṃ dhruvam..
mamedamiti mohāttvaṃ trilokīśriyamīpsasi.. 21.266 ..
1.4.d:
अविश्वास्ये विश्वसिषि मन्यसे चाऽध्रुवं ध्रुवम्..
ममेदमिति मोहात्त्वं त्रिलोकीश्रियमीप्ससि.. 21.266 ..
1.4.m:
You place trust in the untrustworthy, and you think the non-eternal is eternal.
Out of delusion you desire the sovereignty of the three worlds, thinking: 'This is mine!'

1.4.s:
neyaṃ tava na cāsmākaṃ na cānyeṣāṃ sthirā matā..
atikramya bahūnyāṃstvayi tāvadiyaṃ sthitā.. 21.267 ..
1.4.d:
नेयं तव न चास्माकं न चान्येषां स्थिरा मता..
अतिक्रम्य बहून्यांस्त्वयि तावदियं स्थिता.. 21.267 ..
1.4.m:
This [sovereignty] is considered permanent neither for you, nor for us, nor for others.
Passing by many, it has remained with you for a while.

1.4.s:
kaṃcitkālamiyaṃ sthitvā tvayi tāraka caṃcalā..
puṃścalīvāticapalā punaranyaṃ gamiṣyati.. 21.268 ..
1.4.d:
कंचित्कालमियं स्थित्वा त्वयि तारक चंचला..
पुंश्चलीवातिचपला पुनरन्यं गमिष्यति.. 21.268 ..
1.4.m:
Having remained with you for some time, O Tāraka, this fickle [fortune],
like an exceedingly wanton woman, will go to another again.

1.4.s:
saratnauṣadisaṃpannaṃ sasaritparvatākaram..
tānidānīṃ na paśyāmi yairbhuktaṃ bhuvanatrayam.. 21.269 ..
1.4.d:
सरत्नौषदिसंपन्नं ससरित्पर्वताकरम्..
तानिदानीं न पश्यामि यैर्भुक्तं भुवनत्रयम्.. 21.269 ..
1.4.m:
Filled with jewels and herbs, with rivers, mountains, and mines—
I do not see those now who enjoyed this triad of worlds:

1.4.s:
hiraṇyakaśipurvīro hiraṇyākṣaśca durjayaḥ..
prahrādo namucirvīro vipracittirvirocanaḥ.. 21.270 ..
1.4.d:
हिरण्यकशिपुर्वीरो हिरण्याक्षश्च दुर्जयः..
प्रह्रादो नमुचिर्वीरो विप्रचित्तिर्विरोचनः.. 21.270 ..
1.4.m:
the hero Hiraṇyakaśipu, the invincible Hiraṇyākṣa,
Prahrāda, the hero Namuci, Vipracitti, Virocana,

1.4.s:
kīrtiḥ śūraśca vīraśca vātāpirilvalastathā..
aśvagrīvaḥ śaṃbaraśca pulomā madhukaiṭabhau.. 21.271 ..
1.4.d:
कीर्तिः शूरश्च वीरश्च वातापिरिल्वलस्तथा..
अश्वग्रीवः शंबरश्च पुलोमा मधुकैटभौ.. 21.271 ..
1.4.m:
Kīrti, Śūra, Vīra, as well as Vātāpi and Ilvala,
Aśvagrīva, Śambara, Puloman, Madhu, and Kaiṭabha,

1.4.s:
viśvajitpramukhāścānye dānaveṃdrā mahābalāḥ..
kālena nihatāḥ sarve kālo hi balavattaraḥ.. 21.272 ..
1.4.d:
विश्वजित्प्रमुखाश्चान्ये दानवेंद्रा महाबलाः..
कालेन निहताः सर्वे कालो हि बलवत्तरः.. 21.272 ..
1.4.m:
and other mighty chiefs of the Dānavas headed by Viśvajit—
all have been struck down by time, for time is mightier indeed.

1.4.s:
sarvairvarṣāyutaṃ taptaṃ na tvameko mahātapāḥ..
sarve satyavrataparāḥ sarve cāsanbahuśrutāḥ.. 21.273 ..
1.4.d:
सर्वैर्वर्षायुतं तप्तं न त्वमेको महातपाः..
सर्वे सत्यव्रतपराः सर्वे चासन्बहुश्रुताः.. 21.273 ..
1.4.m:
Austerity was performed by all for ten thousand years; you alone are not the one of great austerity.
All were dedicated to vows of truth, and all were well-versed in sacred lore.

1.4.s:
sarve yathārhadātāraḥ sarve dākṣāyaṇīsutāḥ..
jvalaṃtaḥ prajayaṃtaśca kālena pratisaṃhatāḥ.. 21.274 ..
1.4.d:
सर्वे यथार्हदातारः सर्वे दाक्षायणीसुताः..
ज्वलंतः प्रजयंतश्च कालेन प्रतिसंहताः.. 21.274 ..
1.4.m:
All gave gifts according to desert, all were sons of Dakṣa's daughter [Diti];
radiant and victorious, they were destroyed by time.

1.4.s:
muṃcecchāṃ kāmabhogeṣu muṃcemaṃ śrībhavaṃ madam..
etadaiśvaryanāśe tvāṃ śokaḥ saṃpīḍayiṣyati.. 21.275 ..
1.4.d:
मुंचेच्छां कामभोगेषु मुंचेमं श्रीभवं मदम्..
एतदैश्वर्यनाशे त्वां शोकः संपीडयिष्यति.. 21.275 ..
1.4.m:
Abandon desire for sensual pleasures; abandon this pride born of fortune!
When this sovereignty is lost, sorrow will torment you.

1.4.s:
śokakāle śuco mātvaṃ harṣakāle ca mā hṛṣaḥ..
atītānāgate hi tvā pratyutpannena vartaya.. 21.276 ..
1.4.d:
शोककाले शुचो मात्वं हर्षकाले च मा हृषः..
अतीतानागते हि त्वा प्रत्युत्पन्नेन वर्तय.. 21.276 ..
1.4.m:
In time of sorrow, do not grieve; and in time of joy, do not rejoice!
Setting aside the past and the future, conduct yourself in the present.

1.4.s:
iṃdraṃ cedāgataḥ kālaḥ sadā yukta mataṃdritam..
kṣamasva na cirāddaitya tvāmapyupagamiṣyati.. 21.277 ..
1.4.d:
इंद्रं चेदागतः कालः सदा युक्त मतंद्रितम्..
क्षमस्व न चिराद्दैत्य त्वामप्युपगमिष्यति.. 21.277 ..
1.4.m:
If time has overtaken Indra, who is ever vigilant and unwearied,
bear it, O Daitya: before long, it will come to you as well.

1.4.s:
ko hi sthātumalaṃ loke mama kruddhasya saṃyuge..
kālastu balavānprāptastena tiṣṭhāmi tāraka.. 21.278 ..
1.4.d:
को हि स्थातुमलं लोके मम क्रुद्धस्य संयुगे..
कालस्तु बलवान्प्राप्तस्तेन तिष्ठामि तारक.. 21.278 ..
1.4.m:
For who in the world is able to stand before me when I am angered in battle?
Yet powerful time has arrived, therefore I wait, O Tāraka.

1.4.s:
tvameva vetsi māṃ daitya yohaṃ yādṛkparākramaḥ..
kalpekalpe mahādaityāḥ koṭiśo'rbudaśohatāḥ.. 21.279 ..
1.4.d:
त्वमेव वेत्सि मां दैत्य योहं यादृक्पराक्रमः..
कल्पेकल्पे महादैत्याः कोटिशोऽर्बुदशोहताः.. 21.279 ..
1.4.m:
You yourself know me, O Daitya—who I am and what my valour is.
In aeon after aeon, great Daityas have been slain in crores and hundreds of millions,

1.4.s:
yeṣāṃ tvaṃ koṭibhāge'pi paripūrṇo na tāraka..
kalpekalpe sṛjāmīdaṃ brahmādi sakalaṃ jagat.. 21.280 ..
1.4.d:
येषां त्वं कोटिभागेऽपि परिपूर्णो न तारक..
कल्पेकल्पे सृजामीदं ब्रह्मादि सकलं जगत्.. 21.280 ..
1.4.m:
compared to whom you do not make up even a croreth part, O Tāraka!
In aeon after aeon I create this entire universe, beginning with Brahmā.

1.4.s:
icchansaṃjīvayāmyetadanicchannāśaye kṣaṇāt..
na hi tvāṃ notsahe haṃtuṃ sarvadaityasamāyutam.. 21.281 ..
1.4.d:
इच्छन्संजीवयाम्येतदनिच्छन्नाशये क्षणात्..
न हि त्वां नोत्सहे हंतुं सर्वदैत्यसमायुतम्.. 21.281 ..
1.4.m:
Willing it, I make it live; not willing it, I destroy it in an instant.
Indeed, it is not that I lack the power to slay you along with all the Daityas

1.4.s:
aṃgulyagreṇa daityeṃdra punardharmaṃ nalopaye..
yadyahaṃ pravaro bhūtvā dharmaṃ brahmavarātmakam.. 21.282 ..
1.4.d:
अंगुल्यग्रेण दैत्येंद्र पुनर्धर्मं नलोपये..
यद्यहं प्रवरो भूत्वा धर्मं ब्रह्मवरात्मकम्.. 21.282 ..
1.4.m:
with the tip of my finger, O lord of Daityas; yet I would not transgress dharma.
If I, being supreme, should violate dharma

1.4.s:
lopayāmi tataḥ kaṃ ca dharmo'yaṃ śaraṇaṃ vrajet..
ahaṃ karteti mā maṃsthāḥ kartāyastu sadā prabhuḥ.. 21.283 ..
1.4.d:
लोपयामि ततः कं च धर्मोऽयं शरणं व्रजेत्..
अहं कर्तेति मा मंस्थाः कर्तायस्तु सदा प्रभुः.. 21.283 ..
1.4.m:
which consists of the boon granted by Brahmā, to whom then could this dharma go for refuge?
Do not think: 'I am the doer!' He who is the agent is ever the Lord.

1.4.s:
so'yaṃ kālaḥ pacedviśvaṃ vṛkṣe phalamivāgatam..
yaireva karmabhiḥ saukhyaṃ duḥkhaṃ tairevakarmabhiḥ.. 21.284 ..
1.4.d:
सोऽयं कालः पचेद्विश्वं वृक्षे फलमिवागतम्..
यैरेव कर्मभिः सौख्यं दुःखं तैरेवकर्मभिः.. 21.284 ..
1.4.m:
It is this time that ripens the universe, like a fruit that has arrived on a tree.
Through the very same actions happiness comes, and through the very same actions sorrow

1.4.s:
prāpnoti puruṣo daitya paśya kālasya citratām..
sarvaṃ kālavaśādeva bodvavyaṃ dhīryuternaraiḥ.. 21.285 ..
1.4.d:
प्राप्नोति पुरुषो दैत्य पश्य कालस्य चित्रताम्..
सर्वं कालवशादेव बोद्वव्यं धीर्युतेर्नरैः.. 21.285 ..
1.4.m:
is obtained by a man, O Daitya: behold the marvelous nature of time!
All is subject to the power of time alone—this should be understood by wise men.

1.4.s:
svakarmaparipākasya phaladaṃ vai vidurbudhāḥ..
tasmātkarma śubhaṃ kāryaṃ puṇyātpuṇyātmakaṃ ca yat.. 21.286 ..
1.4.d:
स्वकर्मपरिपाकस्य फलदं वै विदुर्बुधाः..
तस्मात्कर्म शुभं कार्यं पुण्यात्पुण्यात्मकं च यत्.. 21.286 ..
1.4.m:
The wise know that time grants the fruit of the ripening of one's own actions.
Therefore, one should perform auspicious action, which is of the nature of merit resulting from merit.

1.4.s:
puṇyena tatra sokhyaṃ syāddṛḥkhaṃ pāpena niścitam..
iti saṃciṃtya daityeṃdra svaṃ vacaḥ paripālaya..
maduktaṃ vacanaṃ sarvaṃ yadi maṃtumihārhasi.. 21.287 ..
1.4.d:
पुण्येन तत्र सोख्यं स्याद्दृःखं पापेन निश्चितम्..
इति संचिंत्य दैत्येंद्र स्वं वचः परिपालय..
मदुक्तं वचनं सर्वं यदि मंतुमिहार्हसि.. 21.287 ..
1.4.m:
"From merit there is happiness, and misery certainly from sin.
Reflecting thus, O lord of Daityas, keep your word,
if you can accept all the words spoken by me."

1.4.s:
..tāraka uvāca..
māmatra saṃsthitaṃ dṛṣṭvā kālanemimukhairyutam.. 21.288 ..
1.4.d:
..तारक उवाच..
मामत्र संस्थितं दृष्ट्वा कालनेमिमुखैर्युतम्.. 21.288 ..
1.4.m:
Tāraka said:
"Seeing me standing here, accompanied by leaders such as Kālanemi,

1.4.s:
kasyeha na vyathedburmṛtyorapi jivāṃsataḥ..
sā te na vyathate buddhiracalā tattvadarśinī.. 21.289 ..
1.4.d:
कस्येह न व्यथेद्बुर्मृत्योरपि जिवांसतः..
सा ते न व्यथते बुद्धिरचला तत्त्वदर्शिनी.. 21.289 ..
1.4.m:
whose mind in this world would not tremble, when even Death seeks to live?
Yet your mind does not tremble, firm and seeing the truth.

1.4.s:
bravīṣi yadyattvaṃ vākyaṃ tatathaiva na saṃśayaḥ..
ko hi viśvāsamartheṣu śarīre vā śarīrabhṛt.. 21.290 ..
1.4.d:
ब्रवीषि यद्यत्त्वं वाक्यं ततथैव न संशयः..
को हि विश्वासमर्थेषु शरीरे वा शरीरभृत्.. 21.290 ..
1.4.m:
Whatever word you speak is indeed so, without doubt.
For what embodied being can bring himself to place trust

1.4.s:
kartumutsahate loke dṛṣṭvā saṃprasthitaṃ jagat..
ahamapyevamevainaṃ lokaṃ jānāmyaśāśvatam.. 21.291 ..
1.4.d:
कर्तुमुत्सहते लोके दृष्ट्वा संप्रस्थितं जगत्..
अहमप्येवमेवैनं लोकं जानाम्यशाश्वतम्.. 21.291 ..
1.4.m:
in worldly possessions or in the body, seeing the world departing?
I too know this world to be truly impermanent in this very way,

1.4.s:
kālāgnāvāhitaṃ ghore guhye satatagatvare..
idamadya kariṣyāmi śvaḥkartāsmītivādinaḥ.. 21.292 ..
1.4.d:
कालाग्नावाहितं घोरे गुह्ये सततगत्वरे..
इदमद्य करिष्यामि श्वःकर्तास्मीतिवादिनः.. 21.292 ..
1.4.m:
placed within the terrible, secret, ever-passing fire of Time.
While men say, 'I shall do this today, and I will do that tomorrow,'

1.4.s:
kālo harati saṃprāpte nadīvega ivonmukhān..
idānīṃ tāvadevāsau mayā dṛṣṭo na vismṛtaḥ.. 21.293 ..
1.4.d:
कालो हरति संप्राप्ते नदीवेग इवोन्मुखान्..
इदानीं तावदेवासौ मया दृष्टो न विस्मृतः.. 21.293 ..
1.4.m:
Time, when it arrives, sweeps them away, as the rush of a river sweeps those looking up.
Just now, indeed, it was seen by me and is not forgotten.

1.4.s:
kālena hriyamāṇānāṃ pralāpaḥ śrūyate nṛṇām..
īrṣyābhimānalobheṣu kāmakro dhabhayeṣu ca.. 21.294 ..
1.4.d:
कालेन ह्रियमाणानां प्रलापः श्रूयते नृणाम्..
ईर्ष्याभिमानलोभेषु कामक्रो धभयेषु च.. 21.294 ..
1.4.m:
The lamentation of men being swept away by Time is heard.
Attached to envy, arrogance, greed, lust, anger, and fear,

1.4.s:
spṛhāmohātivādeṣu lokaḥ sakto na budhyate..
guruṃ vāpyaguruṃ vāpi kṛtyākṛtyaṃ ca keśava.. 21.295 ..
1.4.d:
स्पृहामोहातिवादेषु लोकः सक्तो न बुध्यते..
गुरुं वाप्यगुरुं वापि कृत्याकृत्यं च केशव.. 21.295 ..
1.4.m:
as well as to desire, delusion, and boasting, the world does not understand
what is weighty or trivial, or what ought or ought not to be done, O Keśava.

1.4.s:
jānāmi tvāmahaṃ viṣṇo sarvabhūtavaraṃ prabhum..
kiṃ kurmaḥ svasvabhāvena balinā tvāṃ na manmahe.. 21.296 ..
1.4.d:
जानामि त्वामहं विष्णो सर्वभूतवरं प्रभुम्..
किं कुर्मः स्वस्वभावेन बलिना त्वां न मन्महे.. 21.296 ..
1.4.m:
I know you, O Viṣṇu, to be the supreme Lord of all beings.
What can we do? By our own overpowering nature, we do not heed you.

1.4.s:
kecidbhajaṃti tvāṃ bhaktyā vaireṇa helayā pare..
sarvenukaṃpyāste tubhyamatarātmāsi dehinām.. 21.297 ..
1.4.d:
केचिद्भजंति त्वां भक्त्या वैरेण हेलया परे..
सर्वेनुकंप्यास्ते तुभ्यमतरात्मासि देहिनाम्.. 21.297 ..
1.4.m:
Some worship you with devotion, others with enmity or in sport;
all of them are to be pitied by you, for you are the inner Self of embodied beings.

1.4.s:
purāṇaḥ śāśvato dharmaḥ sarvaprāṇabhṛtāṃ samaḥ..
māmālaṃbya mayā muktā yāṃtu sarve divaukasaḥ.. 21.298 ..
1.4.d:
पुराणः शाश्वतो धर्मः सर्वप्राणभृतां समः..
मामालंब्य मया मुक्ता यांतु सर्वे दिवौकसः.. 21.298 ..
1.4.m:
Ancient and eternal is the dharma, equal toward all living beings.
Relying on me and released by me, let all the gods go.

1.4.s:
punarmarkasvarūpeṇa bhrāṃtavyaṃ bhuvanatrayam..
spṛhāpi yajñabhāgānāṃ na kāryā samayastvayam.. 21.299 ..
1.4.d:
पुनर्मर्कस्वरूपेण भ्रांतव्यं भुवनत्रयम्..
स्पृहापि यज्ञभागानां न कार्या समयस्त्वयम्.. 21.299 ..
1.4.m:
Yet in the form of monkeys they must wander the three worlds,
and no longing for sacrificial shares must be held—this is the agreement."

1.4.s:
evamukte tārakeṇa devā harṣaṃ prapedire..
mucyate hṛtalomāpi meṣo lābho hi saunikāt.. 21.300 ..
1.4.d:
एवमुक्ते तारकेण देवा हर्षं प्रपेदिरे..
मुच्यते हृतलोमापि मेषो लाभो हि सौनिकात्.. 21.300 ..
1.4.m:
When this was said by Tāraka, the gods attained joy;
for even a ram shorn of its wool is a gain when released by a butcher.

1.4.s:
..śrībhagavānuvāca..
daityeṃdra bhava tattvajño vidyājñānataponvitaḥ..
kālaṃ paśyasi suvyaktaṃ pāṇāvāmalakaṃ yathā.. 21.301 ..
1.4.d:
..श्रीभगवानुवाच..
दैत्येंद्र भव तत्त्वज्ञो विद्याज्ञानतपोन्वितः..
कालं पश्यसि सुव्यक्तं पाणावामलकं यथा.. 21.301 ..
1.4.m:
The Blessed Lord said:
"O lord of Daityas, you are a knower of truth, endowed with learning, knowledge, and austerity.
You see Time clearly, like a myrobalan fruit in the hand.

1.4.s:
kālacāritratattvajña śivabhakta mahāmate..
vajrāṃgasuta dhanyo'si spṛhaṇīyo'si dhīmatām.. 21.302 ..
1.4.d:
कालचारित्रतत्त्वज्ञ शिवभक्त महामते..
वज्रांगसुत धन्योऽसि स्पृहणीयोऽसि धीमताम्.. 21.302 ..
1.4.m:
O knower of the truth of Time's course, devotee of Śiva, of great intellect,
O son of Vajrāṅga, you are blessed and worthy of the wise men's praise.

1.4.s:
yāvatte tapaso vīryaṃ tāvadbhuṃkṣvajagattrayam..
etena samayenaite cariṣyaṃti surā jagat.. 21.303 ..
1.4.d:
यावत्ते तपसो वीर्यं तावद्भुंक्ष्वजगत्त्रयम्..
एतेन समयेनैते चरिष्यंति सुरा जगत्.. 21.303 ..
1.4.m:
As long as the strength of your austerity lasts, so long enjoy the three worlds.
Under this agreement, these gods will wander the world."

1.4.s:
ityuktvā markayūthena vṛto nārāyaṇaḥ prabhuḥ..
sthānādasmādapākramya meruṃ prati yayau tadā.. 21.304 ..
1.4.d:
इत्युक्त्वा मर्कयूथेन वृतो नारायणः प्रभुः..
स्थानादस्मादपाक्रम्य मेरुं प्रति ययौ तदा.. 21.304 ..
1.4.m:
Having spoken thus, the lord Nārāyaṇa, surrounded by the troop of monkeys,
departed from that place and went toward Meru at that time.

1.4.s:
tato meruṃ samāgamya provāca vacanaṃ hariḥ..
bhavaṃto yāṃtu brahmaṇaṃ sa dhāsyati ca vo hitam.. 21.305 ..
1.4.d:
ततो मेरुं समागम्य प्रोवाच वचनं हरिः..
भवंतो यांतु ब्रह्मणं स धास्यति च वो हितम्.. 21.305 ..
1.4.m:
Then, arriving at Meru, Hari spoke these words:
"Go to Brahmā; he will arrange what is good for you.

1.4.s:
apramattaiḥ sadā bhāvyaṃ pālyaśca samayastathā..
ityuktvā bhagavānviṣṇustatraivāṃtaradhīyata.. 21.306 ..
1.4.d:
अप्रमत्तैः सदा भाव्यं पाल्यश्च समयस्तथा..
इत्युक्त्वा भगवान्विष्णुस्तत्रैवांतरधीयत.. 21.306 ..
1.4.m:
You must always remain vigilant, and the agreement must be kept."
Having spoken thus, the Lord Viṣṇu vanished right there.

1.4.s: praṇataḥ saṃstuto devairbrahmāṇaṃ ca surā yayuḥ.. 21.307 ..
1.4.d: प्रणतः संस्तुतो देवैर्ब्रह्माणं च सुरा ययुः.. 21.307 ..
1.4.m: Having bowed and praised him, the gods went to Brahmā.

1.4.s:
divyottamaistatra gatairabhiṣṭuto vidīptatejā bhuvanatraye'pi..
vajrāṃgaputro'pi mumoda vīraḥ śivaprasādena maharddhimāpya.. 21.308 ..
1.4.d:
दिव्योत्तमैस्तत्र गतैरभिष्टुतो विदीप्ततेजा भुवनत्रयेऽपि..
वज्रांगपुत्रोऽपि मुमोद वीरः शिवप्रसादेन महर्द्धिमाप्य.. 21.308 ..
1.4.m:
Praised by the foremost celestial beings who had gone there, his splendor blazing across the three worlds,
the heroic son of Vajrāṅga also rejoiced, having obtained great prosperity through the grace of Śiva.

1.4.s:
svayamindro nimirvahniḥ kālanemiryamo'pi ca..
stambhaśca nirṛtisthāne mahiṣo varuṇāstathā.. 21.309 ..
1.4.d:
स्वयमिन्द्रो निमिर्वह्निः कालनेमिर्यमोऽपि च..
स्तम्भश्च निरृतिस्थाने महिषो वरुणास्तथा.. 21.309 ..
1.4.m:
He himself became Indra, Nimi became the fire-god, and Kālanemi became Yama;
Stambha was in Nirṛti's station, and Mahiṣa became Varuṇa.

1.4.s:
meṣo vātādhikāri ca kujaṃbho dhanado'bhavat..
anyeṣāṃ cādhikārāṃśca daityānāṃ tārako dadau.. 21.310 ..
iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ prathame māheśvarakhaṇḍe kaumārikākhaṇḍe devāsurasaṃgrāme tārakavijayavarṇananāmaikaviṃśatitamo'dhyāyaḥ.. 21 .. cha ..
1.4.d:
मेषो वाताधिकारि च कुजंभो धनदोऽभवत्..
अन्येषां चाधिकारांश्च दैत्यानां तारको ददौ.. 21.310 ..
