इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां प्रथमे माहेश्वरखण्डे कौमारिकाखण्डे देवासुरसंग्रामे तारकविजयवर्णननामैकविंशतितमोऽध्यायः.. 21 .. छ ..

1.4.s:
..nārada uvāca..
evaṃ viprakṛtā devā maheṃdrasahitāstadā..
yayuḥ svāyaṃbhuvaṃ dāma markarūpamupāśritāḥ.. 22.1 ..
1.4.d:
..नारद उवाच..
एवं विप्रकृता देवा महेंद्रसहितास्तदा..
ययुः स्वायंभुवं दाम मर्करूपमुपाश्रिताः.. 22.1 ..
1.4.m:
Nārada said:
Thus humiliated, the gods, along with great Indra at that time,
resorting to the form of monkeys, went to the abode of the Self-born One.

1.4.s:
tataśca vismito brahmā prāha tānsurapuṃgavān..
svarūpeṇeha tiṣṭhadhvaṃ nātra vastārakādbhayam.. 22.2 ..
1.4.d:
ततश्च विस्मितो ब्रह्मा प्राह तान्सुरपुंगवान्..
स्वरूपेणेह तिष्ठध्वं नात्र वस्तारकाद्भयम्.. 22.2 ..
1.4.m:
Then Brahmā, astonished, said to those foremost of gods:
"Stand here in your own forms; there is no fear for you from Tāraka here."

1.4.s:
tato devāḥ svarūpasthāḥ pramlānavadanāṃbujāḥ..
tuṣṭuvuḥ praṇatāḥ sarve pitaraṃ putrakā yathā.. 22.3 ..
1.4.d:
ततो देवाः स्वरूपस्थाः प्रम्लानवदनांबुजाः..
तुष्टुवुः प्रणताः सर्वे पितरं पुत्रका यथा.. 22.3 ..
1.4.m:
Then the gods, assuming their own forms with lotus faces withered,
bowed down and all praised him, like sons praising their father:

1.4.s:
namo jagatprasūtyai te hetave pālakāya ca..
saṃhartre ca namastubhyaṃ tisro'vasthāstava prabho.. 22.4 ..
1.4.d:
नमो जगत्प्रसूत्यै ते हेतवे पालकाय च..
संहर्त्रे च नमस्तुभ्यं तिस्रोऽवस्थास्तव प्रभो.. 22.4 ..
1.4.m:
"Salutations to you, the source of the universe, the cause, the protector,
and the destroyer—salutations to you; three are your states, O Lord!

1.4.s:
tvamapaḥ prathamaṃ sṛṣṭvā tāsu vīryamavāsṛjaḥ..
tadaṇḍamabhavaddhaimaṃ yasmillokāścarācarāḥ.. 22.5 ..
1.4.d:
त्वमपः प्रथमं सृष्ट्वा तासु वीर्यमवासृजः..
तदण्डमभवद्धैमं यस्मिल्लोकाश्चराचराः.. 22.5 ..
1.4.m:
Having first created the waters, you cast your seed into them;
that became a golden egg, in which are all moving and unmoving worlds.

1.4.s:
vedeṣvāhurvirāḍ‌rūpaṃ tvāmekarūpamīdṛśam..
pātālaṃ pādamūlaṃ ca pārṣṇipāde rasātalam.. 22.6 ..
1.4.d:
वेदेष्वाहुर्विराड्‌रूपं त्वामेकरूपमीदृशम्..
पातालं पादमूलं च पार्ष्णिपादे रसातलम्.. 22.6 ..
1.4.m:
In the Vedas they speak of you as the cosmic form, endowed with a single form like this:
Pātāla is the soles of the feet, and Rasātala the heels and feet.

1.4.s:
mahātalaṃ cāsya gulphau jaṃghe cāpi talātalam..
sutalaṃ jānunī cāsya ūrū ca vitalātale.. 22.7 ..
1.4.d:
महातलं चास्य गुल्फौ जंघे चापि तलातलम्..
सुतलं जानुनी चास्य ऊरू च वितलातले.. 22.7 ..
1.4.m:
Mahātala is his ankles, and Talātala his shanks;
Sutala is his knees, and the two thighs are in Vitala.

1.4.s:
mahītalaṃ ca jaghanaṃ nābhiścāsya nabhastalam..
jyotiḥ padamuraḥ sthānaṃ svarloko bāhurucyate.. 22.8 ..
1.4.d:
महीतलं च जघनं नाभिश्चास्य नभस्तलम्..
ज्योतिः पदमुरः स्थानं स्वर्लोको बाहुरुच्यते.. 22.8 ..
1.4.m:
The earth is the hips, and the region of the sky is his navel;
the realm of the luminaries is the chest, and the celestial world is called his arms.

1.4.s:
grīvā mahaścavadanaṃ janalokaḥ prakīrtyate..
lalāṭaṃ ca tapolokaḥ śīrṣa satyamudāhṛtam.. 22.9 ..
1.4.d:
ग्रीवा महश्चवदनं जनलोकः प्रकीर्त्यते..
ललाटं च तपोलोकः शीर्ष सत्यमुदाहृतम्.. 22.9 ..
1.4.m:
The neck is Maharloka, and Janaloka is proclaimed as the face;
Tapoloka is the forehead, and Satyaloka is declared to be the head.

1.4.s:
candrasūryau ca nayane diśaḥ śrotre nāsikāśvinau..
ātmānaṃ brahmaraṃdhrasthamāhustvāṃ vedavādinaḥ.. 22.10 ..
1.4.d:
चन्द्रसूर्यौ च नयने दिशः श्रोत्रे नासिकाश्विनौ..
आत्मानं ब्रह्मरंध्रस्थमाहुस्त्वां वेदवादिनः.. 22.10 ..
1.4.m:
The moon and the sun are the two eyes, the directions the ears, and the Aśvins the nose;
those who know the Vedas speak of you as the Self residing in the aperture of the crown.

1.4.s:
evaṃ ye te virāḍ‌rūpaṃ saṃsmaraṃta upāsate..
janmabandhavinirmuktā yāṃti tvāṃ paramaṃ padam.. 22.11 ..
1.4.d:
एवं ये ते विराड्‌रूपं संस्मरंत उपासते..
जन्मबन्धविनिर्मुक्ता यांति त्वां परमं पदम्.. 22.11 ..
1.4.m:
Those who thus worship your cosmic form, remembering it,
freed from the bondage of birth, attain you, the supreme state.

1.4.s:
evaṃ sthūlaṃ prāṇimadhyaṃ ca śūkṣmaṃ bhāvebhāve bhāvitaṃ tvāṃ gṛṇaṃti..
sarvatrasthaṃ tvāmataḥ prāhurvedāstasmai tubhyaṃ padamja idvidhema.. 22.12 ..
1.4.d:
एवं स्थूलं प्राणिमध्यं च शूक्ष्मं भावेभावे भावितं त्वां गृणंति..
सर्वत्रस्थं त्वामतः प्राहुर्वेदास्तस्मै तुभ्यं पदम्ज इद्विधेम.. 22.12 ..
1.4.m:
Thus they praise you, gross and subtle within living beings, conceived in every state of being;
therefore the Vedas speak of you as dwelling everywhere. To you, O lotus-born one, we offer worship.

1.4.s:
evaṃ stuto viraṃcistu kṛpayābhipariplutaḥ..
jānannapi tadā prāha teṣāmāśvāsahetave.. 22.13 ..
1.4.d:
एवं स्तुतो विरंचिस्तु कृपयाभिपरिप्लुतः..
जानन्नपि तदा प्राह तेषामाश्वासहेतवे.. 22.13 ..
1.4.m:
Thus praised, the Creator, flooded with compassion,
though knowing [the reason], spoke to them to bring them comfort:

1.4.s:
sarve bhavanto duḥkhārtāḥ parimlānamukhāṃbujāḥ..
bhraṣṭāyudāstathā'kasmādbhraṣṭā bharaṇavāsasaḥ.. 22.14 ..
1.4.d:
सर्वे भवन्तो दुःखार्ताः परिम्लानमुखांबुजाः..
भ्रष्टायुदास्तथाऽकस्माद्भ्रष्टा भरणवाससः.. 22.14 ..
1.4.m:
"All of you are afflicted with grief, your lotus faces utterly withered,
your weapons cast aside, and suddenly bereft of ornaments and garments.

1.4.s:
mamaivayaṃ kṛtirdevā bhavatāṃ yadvaḍambanā..
yadvairājaśarīre me bhavanto bāhusaṃjñakāḥ.. 22.15 ..
1.4.d:
ममैवयं कृतिर्देवा भवतां यद्वडम्बना..
यद्वैराजशरीरे मे भवन्तो बाहुसंज्ञकाः.. 22.15 ..
1.4.m:
This humiliation of yours, O gods, is indeed my own affliction;
since in my cosmic body you are designated as the arms.

1.4.s:
yadyadvibhūtimatsattvaṃ dhārmikaṃ corjitaṃ mahat..
tatrāsīdbāhunāśo me bāhusthāne ca te mama.. 22.16 ..
1.4.d:
यद्यद्विभूतिमत्सत्त्वं धार्मिकं चोर्जितं महत्..
तत्रासीद्बाहुनाशो मे बाहुस्थाने च ते मम.. 22.16 ..
1.4.m:
Whatever being is endowed with power, righteous, mighty, and great,
there was the loss of my arm, for you are in the place of my arms.

1.4.s:
tannūnaṃ mama bhagnau ca bāhū tena durātmanā..
yena copahṛtaṃ devāstanmamākhyātu marhatha.. 22.17 ..
1.4.d:
तन्नूनं मम भग्नौ च बाहू तेन दुरात्मना..
येन चोपहृतं देवास्तन्ममाख्यातु मर्हथ.. 22.17 ..
1.4.m:
Surely, then, my two arms were broken by that evil-minded one.
By whom was this brought about, O gods? You should tell me that."

1.4.s:
..devā ūcuḥ..
yo'sau vajrāṃgatanayastvayā dattavaraḥ prabho..
bhṛśaṃ viprakṛtāstena tattvaṃ jānāsi tattvataḥ.. 22.18 ..
1.4.d:
..देवा ऊचुः..
योऽसौ वज्रांगतनयस्त्वया दत्तवरः प्रभो..
भृशं विप्रकृतास्तेन तत्त्वं जानासि तत्त्वतः.. 22.18 ..
1.4.m:
The gods said:
That son of Vajrāṅga, unto whom a boon was granted by you, O Lord—
by him we have been greatly tormented; in truth, you know this in reality.

1.4.s:
yattanmahīsamudrasya taṭaṃ śārvikatīrthakam..
tadākramya kṛtaṃ tena marubhūmisamaṃ prabhoḥ.. 22.19 ..
1.4.d:
यत्तन्महीसमुद्रस्य तटं शार्विकतीर्थकम्..
तदाक्रम्य कृतं तेन मरुभूमिसमं प्रभोः.. 22.19 ..
1.4.m:
That which was the shore of the earth’s ocean, a sacred ford dedicated to Śarva—
having invaded that, he has turned the place of the Lord into something like a desert.

1.4.s:
ṛddhayaḥ sarvadevānāṃ gṛhītāstena sarvataḥ..
mahābhūtasvarūpeṇa sa eva ca jagatpatiḥ.. 22.20 ..
1.4.d:
ऋद्धयः सर्वदेवानां गृहीतास्तेन सर्वतः..
महाभूतस्वरूपेण स एव च जगत्पतिः.. 22.20 ..
1.4.m:
The prosperities of all the gods have been seized by him from all sides;
in the form of the great elements, he alone is the lord of the world.

1.4.s:
caṃdrasūryau grahāstārā yaccānyaddevapakṣataḥ..
tacca sarvaṃ nirākṛtya sthāpito daityapakṣakaḥ.. 22.21 ..
1.4.d:
चंद्रसूर्यौ ग्रहास्तारा यच्चान्यद्देवपक्षतः..
तच्च सर्वं निराकृत्य स्थापितो दैत्यपक्षकः.. 22.21 ..
1.4.m:
The moon, the sun, the planets, the stars, and whatever else belonged to the faction of the gods—
having cast all that aside, the faction of the Daityas has been established [in their places].

1.4.s:
vayaṃ ca vidhṛtā stena bahūpahasitāstathā..
prasādānmuktāśca kathaṃcidiva kaṣṭataḥ.. 22.22 ..
1.4.d:
वयं च विधृता स्तेन बहूपहसितास्तथा..
प्रसादान्मुक्ताश्च कथंचिदिव कष्टतः.. 22.22 ..
1.4.m:
And we have been restrained by him, and greatly mocked as well;
somehow, with great distress, we were released by his favor.

1.4.s:
tadvayaṃ śaraṇaṃ prāptāḥ pīḍitāḥ kṣuttṛṣārditāḥ..
dharmarakṣā karāśceti saṃciṃtya trātumarhasi.. 22.23 ..
1.4.d:
तद्वयं शरणं प्राप्ताः पीडिताः क्षुत्तृषार्दिताः..
धर्मरक्षा कराश्चेति संचिंत्य त्रातुमर्हसि.. 22.23 ..
1.4.m:
Therefore, afflicted and tormented by hunger and thirst, we have sought refuge;
considering that we are the protectors of dharma, you ought to deliver us.

1.4.s:
ityuktaḥ svātmabhūrdevaḥ surairdaityaviceṣṭitam..
surānuvāca bhagavānataḥ saṃciṃtya tattvataḥ.. 22.24 ..
1.4.d:
इत्युक्तः स्वात्मभूर्देवः सुरैर्दैत्यविचेष्टितम्..
सुरानुवाच भगवानतः संचिंत्य तत्त्वतः.. 22.24 ..
1.4.m:
Thus addressed by the gods concerning the actions of the Daitya,
the self-born lord, the Blessed One, having considered [it] truly from that [perspective], spoke to the gods:

1.4.s:
avadhyastārako daityaḥ sarvairapi surāsuraiḥ..
yasya vadhyaśca nādyāpi sa jāto bhagavānpunaḥ.. 22.25 ..
1.4.d:
अवध्यस्तारको दैत्यः सर्वैरपि सुरासुरैः..
यस्य वध्यश्च नाद्यापि स जातो भगवान्पुनः.. 22.25 ..
1.4.m:
The Daitya Tāraka cannot be slain even by all the gods and Asuras together;
and the Blessed One by whom he is to be slain has not even yet been born.

1.4.s: mayā ca varadānena cchandayitvā nivāritaḥ.. 22.26 ..
1.4.d: मया च वरदानेन च्छन्दयित्वा निवारितः.. 22.26 ..
1.4.m: And he was restrained by me, having been gratified with the granting of a boon.

1.4.s:
tapasā sa hidīpto'bhūttrailokyadahanātmakaḥ..
sa ca vavre vadhaṃ daityaḥ śiśataḥ saptavāsarāt.. 22.27 ..
1.4.d:
तपसा स हिदीप्तोऽभूत्त्रैलोक्यदहनात्मकः..
स च वव्रे वधं दैत्यः शिशतः सप्तवासरात्.. 22.27 ..
1.4.m:
For through his austerity he had become ablaze, capable of burning up the three worlds;
and that Daitya chose his slaying by a child seven days old.

1.4.s:
sa ca saptadino bālaḥ śaṃkarādyo bhaviṣyati..
tārakasya ca vīrasya vadhakartā bhaviṣyati.. 22.28 ..
1.4.d:
स च सप्तदिनो बालः शंकराद्यो भविष्यति..
तारकस्य च वीरस्य वधकर्ता भविष्यति.. 22.28 ..
1.4.m:
And that seven-day-old child who will be born from Śaṃkara
shall become the slayer of the heroic Tāraka.

1.4.s:
satīnāmā tu yā devī vinaṣṭā dakṣahelayā..
sā bhaviṣyati kalyāṇī himācalaśarīrajā.. 22.29 ..
1.4.d:
सतीनामा तु या देवी विनष्टा दक्षहेलया..
सा भविष्यति कल्याणी हिमाचलशरीरजा.. 22.29 ..
1.4.m:
Now, that goddess named Satī who perished through Dakṣa’s disrespect,
that auspicious one will be born from the body of Himācala.

1.4.s:
śaṃkarasya ca tasyāśca yatnaḥ kāryaḥ samāgame..
ahamapyasya kāryasya śeṣaṃ kartā na saṃśayaḥ.. 22.30 ..
1.4.d:
शंकरस्य च तस्याश्च यत्नः कार्यः समागमे..
अहमप्यस्य कार्यस्य शेषं कर्ता न संशयः.. 22.30 ..
1.4.m:
And an effort must be made to bring about the union of Śaṃkara and her;
I too shall accomplish the rest of this task, without a doubt.

1.4.s:
ityuktāstridaśāstena sākṣātkalayoninā..
jagmurmeruṃ praṇamyeśaṃ markarūpeṇa saṃvṛtāḥ.. 22.31 ..
1.4.d:
इत्युक्तास्त्रिदशास्तेन साक्षात्कलयोनिना..
जग्मुर्मेरुं प्रणम्येशं मर्करूपेण संवृताः.. 22.31 ..
1.4.m:
Having been thus addressed by him, the creator born from the lotus,
the thirty [gods], having bowed to the Lord, went to Meru, disguised in the form of monkeys.

1.4.s:
tato gateṣu deveṣu brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ..
niśāṃ sasmāra bhagavānsvāṃ tanuṃ pūrvasaṃbhavām.. 22.32 ..
1.4.d:
ततो गतेषु देवेषु ब्रह्मा लोकपितामहः..
निशां सस्मार भगवान्स्वां तनुं पूर्वसंभवाम्.. 22.32 ..
1.4.m:
Then, when the gods had departed, Brahmā, the grandfather of the worlds,
the Blessed One, called to mind Night, his own body that had originated previously.

1.4.s:
tato bhagavatī rātrirupatasthe pitāmaham..
tāṃ vivikte samālokya tathovāca vibhāvarīm.. 22.33 ..
1.4.d:
ततो भगवती रात्रिरुपतस्थे पितामहम्..
तां विविक्ते समालोक्य तथोवाच विभावरीम्.. 22.33 ..
1.4.m:
Then the blessed Night approached the Grandfather;
beholding that Night in a secluded spot, he spoke to her thus:

1.4.s:
vibhāvari mahākāryaṃ vibudhānāmupasthitam..
tatkartavyaṃ tvayā devi śrṛṇu kāryasya niścayam.. 22.34 ..
1.4.d:
विभावरि महाकार्यं विबुधानामुपस्थितम्..
तत्कर्तव्यं त्वया देवि श्रृणु कार्यस्य निश्चयम्.. 22.34 ..
1.4.m:
O Night, a great task for the gods has presented itself;
that must be accomplished by you, O goddess; hear the determination of the task.

1.4.s:
tārakonāma daityeṃdraḥ suraketuranirjjitaḥ..
tasyābhāvāya bhagavāñjanayiṣyati yaṃ śivaḥ.. 22.35 ..
1.4.d:
तारकोनाम दैत्येंद्रः सुरकेतुरनिर्ज्जितः..
तस्याभावाय भगवाञ्जनयिष्यति यं शिवः.. 22.35 ..
1.4.m:
There is a lord of Daityas named Tāraka, the banner of the gods’ defeat, invincible;
for his destruction, the son whom the blessed Śiva will engender—

1.4.s:
sutaḥ sa bhavitā tasya tārakasyāṃtakārakaḥ..
ahaṃ tvādau yadā jātastadāpaśyaṃ puraḥsthitam.. 22.36 ..
1.4.d:
सुतः स भविता तस्य तारकस्यांतकारकः..
अहं त्वादौ यदा जातस्तदापश्यं पुरःस्थितम्.. 22.36 ..
1.4.m:
that son of his shall be the cause of Tāraka’s end.
When I was born in the beginning, I saw standing before me

1.4.s:
ardhanārīśvaraṃ devaṃ vyāpya viśvamavasthitam..
dṛṣṭvā tamabruvaṃ devaṃ bhajasveti ca bhaktitaḥ.. 22.37 ..
1.4.d:
अर्धनारीश्वरं देवं व्याप्य विश्वमवस्थितम्..
दृष्ट्वा तमब्रुवं देवं भजस्वेति च भक्तितः.. 22.37 ..
1.4.m:
the god Ardhanārīśvara, who abides pervading the universe;
seeing him, I said to that god with devotion: ‘Share [yourself].’

1.4.s:
tato nārī pṛthagjātā puruṣaśca tathā pṛthak..
tasyāścaivāṃśajāḥ sarvāḥ striyastribhuvane smṛtāḥ.. 22.38 ..
1.4.d:
ततो नारी पृथग्जाता पुरुषश्च तथा पृथक्..
तस्याश्चैवांशजाः सर्वाः स्त्रियस्त्रिभुवने स्मृताः.. 22.38 ..
1.4.m:
Thereupon the woman became separate, and the man likewise separate;
and all women in the three worlds are remembered as born from her portion.

1.4.s:
ekādaśa ca rudrāśca puruṣāstasya cāṃśajāḥ..
tāṃ nārīmahāmālokya putraṃ dakṣamathā bravam.. 22.39 ..
1.4.d:
एकादश च रुद्राश्च पुरुषास्तस्य चांशजाः..
तां नारीमहामालोक्य पुत्रं दक्षमथा ब्रवम्.. 22.39 ..
1.4.m:
And the eleven Rudras and men were born from his portion;
beholding that woman, I then spoke to my son Dakṣa:

1.4.s:
bhajasva putrīṃ jagatī mamāpi ca tavāpi ca..
puṃduḥkhanakāttrātrī putrī te bhāvinī tviyam.. 22.40 ..
1.4.d:
भजस्व पुत्रीं जगती ममापि च तवापि च..
पुंदुःखनकात्त्रात्री पुत्री ते भाविनी त्वियम्.. 22.40 ..
1.4.m:
‘Accept this daughter of the universe, who belongs to me and also to you;
for she is to become your daughter, the protectress from the distress of men.’

1.4.s:
evamukto mayā dakṣaḥ putrītve pari kalpitām..
rudrāya dattavānbhaktyā nāma dattvā satīti yat.. 22.41 ..
1.4.d:
एवमुक्तो मया दक्षः पुत्रीत्वे परि कल्पिताम्..
रुद्राय दत्तवान्भक्त्या नाम दत्त्वा सतीति यत्.. 22.41 ..
1.4.m:
Being thus addressed by me, Dakṣa gave her, who was assigned daughterhood,
to Rudra with devotion, having bestowed the name Satī [upon her].

1.4.s:
tataḥ kāle cam̐ kasmiṃścidavamene ca tāṃ pitā..
mumūrṣuḥ pāpasaṃkalpo durātmā kulakajjalaḥ.. 22.42 ..
1.4.d:
ततः काले चम्̐ कस्मिंश्चिदवमेने च तां पिता..
मुमूर्षुः पापसंकल्पो दुरात्मा कुलकज्जलः.. 22.42 ..
1.4.m:
Then, in the course of time, her father slighted her—
about to die, evil in intent, wicked, a stain upon his lineage.

1.4.s:
ye rudraṃ naiva manyaṃte te sphuṭaṃ kulakajjalāḥ..
piśācāste durātmāno bhavaṃti brahmarākṣasāḥ.. 22.43 ..
1.4.d:
ये रुद्रं नैव मन्यंते ते स्फुटं कुलकज्जलाः..
पिशाचास्ते दुरात्मानो भवंति ब्रह्मराक्षसाः.. 22.43 ..
1.4.m:
Those who do not honor Rudra are clearly a stain upon their lineage;
those wicked ones become piśācas and brahmarākṣasas.

1.4.s:
avamānena tasyāpi yathā devī jahau tanum..
yathā yajñaḥ sa ca dhvasto bhavena viditaṃ hi te'.. 22.44 ..
1.4.d:
अवमानेन तस्यापि यथा देवी जहौ तनुम्..
यथा यज्ञः स च ध्वस्तो भवेन विदितं हि ते'.. 22.44 ..
1.4.m:
How, through his insult, the goddess abandoned her body,
and how that sacrifice was destroyed by Bhava, is indeed known to you.

1.4.s:
adhunā himaśailasya bhavitrī duhitā ca sā..
maheśvaraṃ patiṃ sā ca punaḥ prāpsyati niścitam.. 22.45 ..
1.4.d:
अधुना हिमशैलस्य भवित्री दुहिता च सा..
महेश्वरं पतिं सा च पुनः प्राप्स्यति निश्चितम्.. 22.45 ..
1.4.m:
Now she is to become the daughter of the snowy mountain,
and she will surely obtain Maheśvara again as her husband.

1.4.s:
tadidaṃ ca tvayā kāryaṃ menāgarbhe praviśya ca..
tasyāśchaviṃ kuru kṛṣṇāṃ yathā kālī bhavettu sā.. 22.46 ..
1.4.d:
तदिदं च त्वया कार्यं मेनागर्भे प्रविश्य च..
तस्याश्छविं कुरु कृष्णां यथा काली भवेत्तु सा.. 22.46 ..
1.4.m:
Therefore, this must be done by you: having entered the womb of Menā,
make her complexion dark, so that she will be Kālī.

1.4.s:
yadā rudropahasitā tapastapsyati sā mahat..
samāptaniyamā devī yadā cogrā bhaviṣyati.. 22.47 ..
1.4.d:
यदा रुद्रोपहसिता तपस्तप्स्यति सा महत्..
समाप्तनियमा देवी यदा चोग्रा भविष्यति.. 22.47 ..
1.4.m:
When, mocked by Rudra, she performs great austerity—
when, having completed her vow, the goddess becomes fierce—

1.4.s:
svayameva yadā rūpaṃ sugauraṃ pratipatsyate..
viraheṇa haraścāsyā matvā śūnyaṃ jagattrayam.. 22.48 ..
1.4.d:
स्वयमेव यदा रूपं सुगौरं प्रतिपत्स्यते..
विरहेण हरश्चास्या मत्वा शून्यं जगत्त्रयम्.. 22.48 ..
1.4.m:
when of her own accord she assumes a very fair form—
and Hara, considering the three worlds empty due to separation from her,

1.4.s:
tasyaiva himaśailasya kaṃdare siddhasevite..
pratīkṣamāṇastāṃ devīmugraṃ saṃtapsyate tapaḥ.. 22.49 ..
1.4.d:
तस्यैव हिमशैलस्य कंदरे सिद्धसेविते..
प्रतीक्षमाणस्तां देवीमुग्रं संतप्स्यते तपः.. 22.49 ..
1.4.m:
in a cave of that very snowy mountain frequented by Siddhas,
awaiting that goddess, will perform fierce austerity.

1.4.s:
tayoḥ sutaptatapasorbhavitā yo mahānsutaḥ..
bhaviṣyati sa daityasya tārakasya nivārakaḥ.. 22.50 ..
1.4.d:
तयोः सुतप्ततपसोर्भविता यो महान्सुतः..
भविष्यति स दैत्यस्य तारकस्य निवारकः.. 22.50 ..
1.4.m:
The great son who will be born to the two of them, who have performed severe austerity,
shall be the slayer of the Daitya Tāraka.

1.4.s:
tapaso hi vinā nāsti siddhiḥ kutrāpi śobhane..
sarvāsāṃ karmasiddhīnāṃ mūlaṃ hi tapa ucyate.. 22.51 ..
1.4.d:
तपसो हि विना नास्ति सिद्धिः कुत्रापि शोभने..
सर्वासां कर्मसिद्धीनां मूलं हि तप उच्यते.. 22.51 ..
1.4.m:
For without austerity there is no success anywhere, O fair one;
indeed, austerity is said to be the root of all achievements of actions.

1.4.s:
tvayāpi dānavo devi dehanirgatayā tadā..
caṃḍamuṃḍapurogāśca haṃtavyā lokadurjayāḥ.. 22.52 ..
1.4.d:
त्वयापि दानवो देवि देहनिर्गतया तदा..
चंडमुंडपुरोगाश्च हंतव्या लोकदुर्जयाः.. 22.52 ..
1.4.m:
By you as well, O goddess, having departed from her body at that time,
the Danavas led by Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa, who are invincible to the worlds, must be slain.

1.4.s:
yasmāccaṃḍaṃ ca muṃḍaṃ ca tvaṃ devi nihaniṣyasi..
cāmuṃḍeti tato loke khyātā devi bhaviṣyasi.. 22.53 ..
1.4.d:
यस्माच्चंडं च मुंडं च त्वं देवि निहनिष्यसि..
चामुंडेति ततो लोके ख्याता देवि भविष्यसि.. 22.53 ..
1.4.m:
Because you will slay Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa, O goddess,
therefore you will become renowned in the world as Cāmuṇḍā, O goddess.

1.4.s:
tatastvāṃ varade devī lokaḥ saṃpūjayiṣyati..
bhederbahuvidhākāraiḥ sarvagāṃ kāmasādhanīm.. 22.54 ..
1.4.d:
ततस्त्वां वरदे देवी लोकः संपूजयिष्यति..
भेदेर्बहुविधाकारैः सर्वगां कामसाधनीम्.. 22.54 ..
1.4.m:
Then, O boon-giver, the world will worship you, the goddess,
through distinctions of many kinds of forms, as all-pervading and fulfilling desires.

1.4.s:
oṃkāravaktrāṃ gāyatrīṃ tvāmarcaṃti dvijottamāḥ..
ūrjitāṃ baladāṃ pāpi rājānaḥ sumahābalāḥ.. 22.55 ..
1.4.d:
ओंकारवक्त्रां गायत्रीं त्वामर्चंति द्विजोत्तमाः..
ऊर्जितां बलदां पापि राजानः सुमहाबलाः.. 22.55 ..
1.4.m:
Best of brahmins worship you as Gāyatrī whose face is the syllable Oṃ;
exceedingly powerful kings [worship you] as powerful, granting strength, and protecting.

1.4.s:
vaiśyāśca bhūtimityeva śivāṃ śūdrāstathā śubhe..
kṣāṃtirmunīnāmakṣobhyā dayā niyamināmapi.. 22.56 ..
1.4.d:
वैश्याश्च भूतिमित्येव शिवां शूद्रास्तथा शुभे..
क्षांतिर्मुनीनामक्षोभ्या दया नियमिनामपि.. 22.56 ..
1.4.m:
Vaiśyas [worship you] as prosperity, and Śūdras as auspicious, O fair one;
[you are] the unshakable forbearance of sages and the compassion of the self-restrained.

1.4.s:
tvaṃ mahopāya sandohā nītirnayavisarpiṇām..
paristhitistvamarthānāṃ tvamaho prāṇikā matā.. 22.57 ..
1.4.d:
त्वं महोपाय सन्दोहा नीतिर्नयविसर्पिणाम्..
परिस्थितिस्त्वमर्थानां त्वमहो प्राणिका मता.. 22.57 ..
1.4.m:
You are the assemblage of great means, the policy of those who practice statesmanship;
you are the abiding state of wealth, and oh, you are regarded as the life-force of living beings.

1.4.s:
tvaṃ yuktiḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ tvaṃ gatiḥ sarvadehinām..
ratistvaṃ raticittānāṃ prītistvaṃ hṛdyadarśinām.. 22.58 ..
1.4.d:
त्वं युक्तिः सर्वभूतानां त्वं गतिः सर्वदेहिनाम्..
रतिस्त्वं रतिचित्तानां प्रीतिस्त्वं हृद्यदर्शिनाम्.. 22.58 ..
1.4.m:
You are the expedient of all beings, you are the goal of all embodied beings;
you are pleasure for minds inclined to pleasure, you are love for those who behold what is dear.

1.4.s:
tvaṃ kāṃtiḥ śubharūpāṇāṃ tvaṃ śāṃti śubhakarmiṇām..
tvaṃ bhrāṃtirmūḍhacittānāṃ tvaṃ phalaṃ kratuyājinām.. 22.59 ..
1.4.d:
त्वं कांतिः शुभरूपाणां त्वं शांति शुभकर्मिणाम्..
त्वं भ्रांतिर्मूढचित्तानां त्वं फलं क्रतुयाजिनाम्.. 22.59 ..
1.4.m:
You are the luster of auspicious forms, you are the peace of those of auspicious deeds;
you are the delusion of confused minds, you are the fruit of those who perform sacrifices.

1.4.s:
jaladhīnāṃ mahāvelā tvaṃ ca līlā vilāsinām..
saṃbhūtistvaṃ padārthānāṃ sthitistvaṃ lokapālinī.. 22.60 ..
1.4.d:
जलधीनां महावेला त्वं च लीला विलासिनाम्..
संभूतिस्त्वं पदार्थानां स्थितिस्त्वं लोकपालिनी.. 22.60 ..
1.4.m:
You are the great tide of the oceans, and you are the play of the playful;
you are the origin of existing things, you are the maintenance that protects the world.

1.4.s:
tvaṃ kālarātrirniḥśeṣa bhuvanāvalināśinī..
priyakaṃṭhagrahānandadāyinī tvaṃ vibhāvarī.. 22.61 ..
1.4.d:
त्वं कालरात्रिर्निःशेष भुवनावलिनाशिनी..
प्रियकंठग्रहानन्ददायिनी त्वं विभावरी.. 22.61 ..
1.4.m:
You are Kālarātri, the destroyer of the entire series of worlds;
you are the night, granting the bliss of an embrace around a beloved's neck.

1.4.s: prasīda praṇatānasmānsaumyadṛṣṭyā vilokaya.. 22.62 ..
1.4.d: प्रसीद प्रणतानस्मान्सौम्यदृष्ट्या विलोकय.. 22.62 ..
1.4.m: Be pleased; look upon us who are bowed down with a gentle gaze.

1.4.s:
iti stuvaṃto ye devi pūjayiṣyaṃti tvāṃ śubhe..
te sarvakāmānāpsyaṃti niyatā nātra saṃśayaḥ.. 22.63 ..
1.4.d:
इति स्तुवंतो ये देवि पूजयिष्यंति त्वां शुभे..
ते सर्वकामानाप्स्यंति नियता नात्र संशयः.. 22.63 ..
1.4.m: "Those who praise and worship you thus, O auspicious goddess, / will surely attain all their desires; of this there is no doubt."

1.4.s:
ityuktā tu niśādevī tathetyuktvā kṛtāñjaliḥ..
jagāma tvaritā pūrvaṃ gṛhaṃ himagirermahat.. 22.64 ..
1.4.d:
इत्युक्ता तु निशादेवी तथेत्युक्त्वा कृताञ्जलिः..
जगाम त्वरिता पूर्वं गृहं हिमगिरेर्महत्.. 22.64 ..
1.4.m: Thus addressed, the goddess Night said, "So be it," and with folded hands, / swiftly went first to the great mansion of the Himalaya.

1.4.s:
tatrā''sīnāṃ mahāharmye ratnabhittisamāśraye..
dadarśa menāmāpāṃḍucchavivaktrasaroruhām.. 22.65 ..
1.4.d:
तत्रा'ऽसीनां महाहर्म्ये रत्नभित्तिसमाश्रये..
ददर्श मेनामापांडुच्छविवक्त्रसरोरुहाम्.. 22.65 ..
1.4.m: There, seated in the great palace supported by jeweled walls, / she saw Menā, whose lotus-like face had a pale complexion,

1.4.s:
kiṃcicchayāmamukhodagrastanabhāgāvanāmitām..
mahauṣadhigaṇabaddhamaṃtrarājaniṣevitām.. 22.66 ..
1.4.d:
किंचिच्छयाममुखोदग्रस्तनभागावनामिताम्..
महौषधिगणबद्धमंत्रराजनिषेविताम्.. 22.66 ..
1.4.m: bent down by the weight of breasts whose nipples were slightly dark, / and attended by sovereign mantras bound with hosts of great medicinal herbs.

1.4.s:
tataḥ kiṃcitpramilite menānetrāṃbujadvaye..
āviveśamukhaṃ rātrirbrahmaṇo vacanāttadā.. 22.67 ..
1.4.d:
ततः किंचित्प्रमिलिते मेनानेत्रांबुजद्वये..
आविवेशमुखं रात्रिर्ब्रह्मणो वचनात्तदा.. 22.67 ..
1.4.m: Then, as Menā's pair of lotus eyes gently closed, / Night entered her mouth at that moment by the command of Brahmā.

1.4.s:
janmadāyā jaganmātuḥ krameṇa jaṭharāṃtaram..
araṃjayacchaviṃ devyā guhamāturvibhāvarī.. 22.68 ..
1.4.d:
जन्मदाया जगन्मातुः क्रमेण जठरांतरम्..
अरंजयच्छविं देव्या गुहमातुर्विभावरी.. 22.68 ..
1.4.m: [Entering] by degrees into the belly of the mother of the universe who was to give birth, / the Night gave color to the complexion of the goddess, the mother of Guha.

1.4.s:
tato jaganmaṃ galadā menā himagireḥ priyā..
brāhme muhūrte subhage prāsūyata śubhānanām.. 22.69 ..
1.4.d:
ततो जगन्मं गलदा मेना हिमगिरेः प्रिया..
ब्राह्मे मुहूर्ते सुभगे प्रासूयत शुभाननाम्.. 22.69 ..
1.4.m: Then Menā, the beloved of the Himalaya, bestowing auspiciousness on the universe, / gave birth to the auspicious-faced one during the lovely muhūrta sacred to Brahmā.

1.4.s:
tasyāṃ tu jāyamānāyāṃ jaṃtavaḥ sthāṇujaṃgamāḥ..
abhavansukhinaḥ sarve sarvalokanivāsinaḥ.. 22.70 ..
1.4.d:
तस्यां तु जायमानायां जंतवः स्थाणुजंगमाः..
अभवन्सुखिनः सर्वे सर्वलोकनिवासिनः.. 22.70 ..
1.4.m: While she was being born, the creatures, both immobile and mobile, / all dwelling throughout all the worlds, became happy.

1.4.s:
abhavatkrūrasattvānāṃ cetaḥ śāṃtaṃ ca dehinām..
jyotiṣāmapi tejastvamabhavatsutarāṃ tadā.. 22.71 ..
1.4.d:
अभवत्क्रूरसत्त्वानां चेतः शांतं च देहिनाम्..
ज्योतिषामपि तेजस्त्वमभवत्सुतरां तदा.. 22.71 ..
1.4.m: The minds of cruel beings and embodied souls became tranquil, / and the brilliance of the heavenly luminaries then increased exceedingly.

1.4.s:
vanāśritāścauṣadhayaḥ svādavaṃti phalāni ca..
gaṃdhavaṃti ca mālyāni vimalaṃ ca nabho'bhavat.. 22.72 ..
1.4.d:
वनाश्रिताश्चौषधयः स्वादवंति फलानि च..
गंधवंति च माल्यानि विमलं च नभोऽभवत्.. 22.72 ..
1.4.m: The medicinal herbs dwelling in the forests [bore] sweet fruits, / garlands were fragrant, and the sky became spotless.

1.4.s:
mārutaśca sukhasparśo diśaśca sumanoharāḥ..
vismṛtā ni ca śāstrāṇi prādurbhāvaṃ prapedire.. 22.73 ..
1.4.d:
मारुतश्च सुखस्पर्शो दिशश्च सुमनोहराः..
विस्मृता नि च शास्त्राणि प्रादुर्भावं प्रपेदिरे.. 22.73 ..
1.4.m: The wind was pleasant to the touch, and the quarters of the sky were utterly delightful; / and forgotten scriptures manifested anew.

1.4.s:
prabhāvastīrthamukhyānāṃ tadā puṇyatamo'bhavat..
satye dharme cādhyayane yajñe dāne tapasyapi.. 22.74 ..
1.4.d:
प्रभावस्तीर्थमुख्यानां तदा पुण्यतमोऽभवत्..
सत्ये धर्मे चाध्ययने यज्ञे दाने तपस्यपि.. 22.74 ..
1.4.m: The power of the principal sacred fords then became most sacred; / in truth, in righteousness, in Vedic study, in sacrifice, in donation, and in austerity,

1.4.s:
sarveṣāmabhavacchraddhā janmakāle guhāraṇeḥ..
aṃtarikṣemarāścāpi praharṣotphullalocanāḥ.. 22.75 ..
1.4.d:
सर्वेषामभवच्छ्रद्धा जन्मकाले गुहारणेः..
अंतरिक्षेमराश्चापि प्रहर्षोत्फुल्ललोचनाः.. 22.75 ..
1.4.m: faith arose in everyone at the time of the birth of the kindling-stick of Guha; / and the gods in the sky, their eyes wide with joy,

1.4.s:
haribrahmamaheṃdrārkavāyuvahnipurogamāḥ..
puṣpavṛṣṭiṃ pramumucustasminmenāgṛhe śubhe.. 22.76 ..
1.4.d:
हरिब्रह्ममहेंद्रार्कवायुवह्निपुरोगमाः..
पुष्पवृष्टिं प्रमुमुचुस्तस्मिन्मेनागृहे शुभे.. 22.76 ..
1.4.m: led by Hari, Brahmā, Mahendra, the Sun, Vāyu, and Agni, / showered down a rain of flowers upon that auspicious dwelling of Menā.

1.4.s:
meruprabhṛtayaścāpi mūrtimaṃto mahānagāḥ..
tasminmahotsave prāptā vīrakāṃsyopaśobhitāḥ.. 22.77 ..
1.4.d:
मेरुप्रभृतयश्चापि मूर्तिमंतो महानगाः..
तस्मिन्महोत्सवे प्राप्ता वीरकांस्योपशोभिताः.. 22.77 ..
1.4.m: The great mountains also, beginning with Meru, embodied in form, / arrived at that great festival, adorned with brave bronze vessels.

1.4.s: sāgarāḥ saritaścaiva samājagmuśca sarvaśaḥ.. 22.78 ..
1.4.d: सागराः सरितश्चैव समाजग्मुश्च सर्वशः.. 22.78 ..
1.4.m: And the oceans and rivers also arrived from every side.

1.4.s:
himaśailo'bhavalloke tadā sarvaiścarācaraiḥ..
sevyaścāpyabhigamyaśca pūjanīyaśca bhārata.. 22.79 ..
1.4.d:
हिमशैलोऽभवल्लोके तदा सर्वैश्चराचरैः..
सेव्यश्चाप्यभिगम्यश्च पूजनीयश्च भारत.. 22.79 ..
1.4.m: The snowy mountain then became in the world, to all mobile and immobile beings, / worthy of service, to be approached, and to be worshipped, O Bhārata.

1.4.s:
anubhūyotsavaṃ te ca jagmuḥ svānālayāṃstadā.. 22.80 ..
iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ prathame māheśvarakhaṇḍe kaumārikākhaṃḍe kumāreśa māhātmye pārvatījanmavarṇanaṃnāma dvāviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ.. 22 .. cha ..
1.4.d:
अनुभूयोत्सवं ते च जग्मुः स्वानालयांस्तदा.. 22.80 ..
इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां प्रथमे माहेश्वरखण्डे कौमारिकाखंडे कुमारेश माहात्म्ये पार्वतीजन्मवर्णनंनाम द्वाविंशोऽध्यायः.. 22 .. छ ..
1.4.m:
Having experienced the festival, they then departed to their own abodes.
Thus ends the twenty-second chapter, titled "Description of the Birth of Pārvatī," in the Kumāreśamāhātmya of the Kaumārikākhaṇḍa, in the first Māheśvarakhaṇḍa of the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand [verses].

1.4.s:
..nārada uvāca..
tataśca śailajā devī cikrīḍa subhagā tadā..
devagaṃdharvakanyābhirnagakiṃnarasaṃbhavāḥ..
munīnāṃ cāpi yāḥ kanyāstābhiḥ sārdhaṃ ca śobhanā.. 23.1 ..
1.4.d:
..नारद उवाच..
ततश्च शैलजा देवी चिक्रीड सुभगा तदा..
देवगंधर्वकन्याभिर्नगकिंनरसंभवाः..
मुनीनां चापि याः कन्यास्ताभिः सार्धं च शोभना.. 23.1 ..
1.4.m: Nārada said: / Then the fair goddess born of the mountain played / with daughters of gods and gandharvas, those born of mountains and kinnaras, / and the daughters of the sages, the radiant one together with them.

1.4.s:
kadācidatha merustho vāsavaḥ pāṃḍunaṃdana..
sasmārā māṃ yayau cāhaṃ saṃsmṛto vāsavaṃ tadā.. 23.2 ..
1.4.d:
कदाचिदथ मेरुस्थो वासवः पांडुनंदन..
सस्मारा मां ययौ चाहं संस्मृतो वासवं तदा.. 23.2 ..
1.4.m: Once, O son of Pāṇḍu, Vāsava, staying on Meru, / remembered me, and being remembered, I then went to Vāsava.

1.4.s:
māṃ dṛṣṭvā ca sahasrākṣaḥ samutthāyātiharṣitaḥ..
pūjayāmāsa tāṃ pūjāṃ pratigṛhyāhamabruvam.. 23.3 ..
1.4.d:
मां दृष्ट्वा च सहस्राक्षः समुत्थायातिहर्षितः..
पूजयामास तां पूजां प्रतिगृह्याहमब्रुवम्.. 23.3 ..
1.4.m: Seeing me, the thousand-eyed Indra arose, exceedingly delighted, / and worshipped [me]. Accepting that worship, I spoke:

1.4.s:
mahāsura mahonmādakālānala divaspate..
kuśalaṃ vidyate kaccicca naṃdasi.. 23.4 ..
1.4.d:
महासुर महोन्मादकालानल दिवस्पते..
कुशलं विद्यते कच्चिच्च नंदसि.. 23.4 ..
1.4.m: "O Lord of Heaven, [destroying like] the fire of time the great pride of the great asuras! / Is all well with you, and do you rejoice?"

1.4.s:
pṛṣṭastvevaṃ mayā śakraḥ provāca vacanaṃ smayan..
kuśalasyāṃkurastāvatsaṃbhūto bhuvanatraye.. 23.5 ..
1.4.d:
पृष्टस्त्वेवं मया शक्रः प्रोवाच वचनं स्मयन्..
कुशलस्यांकुरस्तावत्संभूतो भुवनत्रये.. 23.5 ..
1.4.m: Thus questioned by me, Śakra smilingly uttered these words: / "The sprout of well-being has indeed arisen in the three worlds.

1.4.s:
tatphalodayasaṃpattau tadbhavānsaṃsmṛto mune..
vetsi sarvamataṃ tvaṃ vai tathāpi parinodakaḥ.. 23.6 ..
1.4.d:
तत्फलोदयसंपत्तौ तद्भवान्संस्मृतो मुने..
वेत्सि सर्वमतं त्वं वै तथापि परिनोदकः.. 23.6 ..
1.4.m: For the attainment of its fruit, you have been remembered, O sage. / You indeed know the views of all; nevertheless, an instigator

1.4.s: nirvṛtiṃ paramāṃ yāti nivedyārthaṃ suhṛjjane.. 23.7 ..
1.4.d: निर्वृतिं परमां याति निवेद्यार्थं सुहृज्जने.. 23.7 ..
1.4.m: attains the highest relief by confiding the matter to a friend.

1.4.s:
tadbhavāñchailajāṃ devīṃ śailaṃdraṃ śailavallabhām..
haraṃ saṃbhāvaya varaṃ yannānyaṃ rocayaṃti te.. 23.8 ..
1.4.d:
तद्भवाञ्छैलजां देवीं शैलंद्रं शैलवल्लभाम्..
हरं संभावय वरं यन्नान्यं रोचयंति ते.. 23.8 ..
1.4.m: Therefore, do you honor Hara as the groom to the goddess born of the mountain, the mountain king, and the mountain's beloved wife, / so that they fancy no other."

1.4.s:
tatastadvākyamākarṇya gato'haṃ śailasattamam..
oṣadhiprasthanilayaṃ sākṣādiva divaspatim.. 23.9 ..
1.4.d:
ततस्तद्वाक्यमाकर्ण्य गतोऽहं शैलसत्तमम्..
ओषधिप्रस्थनिलयं साक्षादिव दिवस्पतिम्.. 23.9 ..
1.4.m: Then, having heard his words, I went to that best of mountains, / whose abode is Oṣadhiprastha, as if to the Lord of Heaven in visible form.

1.4.s:
tatra haime svayaṃ tena mahābhaktyā nivedite..
mahāsane pūjitohamupaviṣṭo mahāsukham.. 23.10 ..
1.4.d:
तत्र हैमे स्वयं तेन महाभक्त्या निवेदिते..
महासने पूजितोहमुपविष्टो महासुखम्.. 23.10 ..
1.4.m: There, having been worshipped, I sat in great comfort upon a great golden throne / offered personally by him with great devotion.

1.4.s:
gṛhītārghyaṃ tato māṃ ca papraccha ślakṣṇayā girā..
kuśalaṃ tapasaḥ śailaḥ śanaiḥ phullānanāṃbujaḥ.. 23.11 ..
1.4.d:
गृहीतार्घ्यं ततो मां च पप्रच्छ श्लक्ष्णया गिरा..
कुशलं तपसः शैलः शनैः फुल्लाननांबुजः.. 23.11 ..
1.4.m: Then, when the arghya offering had been received by me, the mountain, with his lotus-face gently blossoming, / asked in a pleasant voice about the welfare of my austerity.

1.4.s:
ahamapyasya tatprocya pratyavocaṃ girīśvaram..
tvayā śaileṃdra pūrvāṃ vāpyaparāṃ ca diśaṃ tathā.. 23.12 ..
1.4.d:
अहमप्यस्य तत्प्रोच्य प्रत्यवोचं गिरीश्वरम्..
त्वया शैलेंद्र पूर्वां वाप्यपरां च दिशं तथा.. 23.12 ..
1.4.m: I too, having told him that, replied to the lord of the mountains: / "By you, O king of mountains, who stand plunging into both the eastern

1.4.s:
avagāhya sthitavatā kriyate prāṇipālanā..
aho dhanyosi vipreṃdrāḥ sāhāyyena tavācala.. 23.13 ..
1.4.d:
अवगाह्य स्थितवता क्रियते प्राणिपालना..
अहो धन्योसि विप्रेंद्राः साहाय्येन तवाचल.. 23.13 ..
1.4.m: and the western quarters, the protection of living beings is performed. / Ah, you are blessed, O mountain! With your assistance, best of brahmins

1.4.s:
tapojapavratasnānauḥ sādhyaṃtyātmanaḥ param..
yajñāṃgasādhanaiḥ kāṃścitkaṃdādiphaladānataḥ.. 23.14 ..
1.4.d:
तपोजपव्रतस्नानौः साध्यंत्यात्मनः परम्..
यज्ञांगसाधनैः कांश्चित्कंदादिफलदानतः.. 23.14 ..
1.4.m: accomplish their highest end through austerities, recitations, vows, and ritual ablutions. / Some with the implements for sacrifice, and some by providing roots and fruits,

1.4.s:
tvaṃ samuddharasi viprānkimataḥ procyate tava..
anye'pi jīva bahudhātvāmupāśritya bhūdhara.. 23.15 ..
1.4.d:
त्वं समुद्धरसि विप्रान्किमतः प्रोच्यते तव..
अन्येऽपि जीव बहुधात्वामुपाश्रित्य भूधर.. 23.15 ..
1.4.m: you deliver the brahmins; what more can be said of you? / Other living creatures too, taking refuge in you in many ways, O mountain,

1.4.s:
muditāḥ prativartaṃte gṛhasthamiva prāṇinaḥ..
śītamātapavarṣāṃśca kleśānnānāvidhānsahan.. 23.16 ..
1.4.d:
मुदिताः प्रतिवर्तंते गृहस्थमिव प्राणिनः..
शीतमातपवर्षांश्च क्लेशान्नानाविधान्सहन्.. 23.16 ..
1.4.m: dwell joyfully, as living beings [live depending on] a householder. / Enduring cold, heat, rain, and various hardships,

1.4.s:
upākaroṣi jaṃtūnāmevaṃrūpā hi sādhavaḥ..
kimataḥ procyate tubhyaṃ dhanyastvaṃ pṛthivīdhara.. 23.17 ..
1.4.d:
उपाकरोषि जंतूनामेवंरूपा हि साधवः..
किमतः प्रोच्यते तुभ्यं धन्यस्त्वं पृथिवीधर.. 23.17 ..
1.4.m: you render service to creatures; for such indeed is the nature of the virtuous. / What more can be said to you? Blessed are you, O supporter of the earth,

1.4.s:
kaṃdaraṃ yasya cādhyāste svayaṃ tava maheśvaraḥ..
ityuktavati vākyaṃ ca yathārthaṃ mayiphālguna.. 23.18 ..
1.4.d:
कंदरं यस्य चाध्यास्ते स्वयं तव महेश्वरः..
इत्युक्तवति वाक्यं च यथार्थं मयिफाल्गुन.. 23.18 ..
1.4.m: in whose cave Maheśvara himself resides!" / When I had spoken these truthful words, O Phālguna,

1.4.s:
himaśailasya mahiṣī menā āgāddidṛkṣayā..
anuyātā duhitrā ca svalpāśca paricārikāḥ.. 23.19 ..
1.4.d:
हिमशैलस्य महिषी मेना आगाद्दिदृक्षया..
अनुयाता दुहित्रा च स्वल्पाश्च परिचारिकाः.. 23.19 ..
1.4.m: Menā, the queen of the snowy mountain, arrived wishing to see [me], / accompanied by her daughter and a few female attendants.

1.4.s:
lajjayānatasarvāṃgī praviveśa sado mahat..
tato māṃ śailamahiṣī vavaṃde praṇipatya sā.. 23.20 ..
1.4.d:
लज्जयानतसर्वांगी प्रविवेश सदो महत्..
ततो मां शैलमहिषी ववंदे प्रणिपत्य सा.. 23.20 ..
1.4.m: With all her limbs bent low in modesty, she entered the great assembly hall. / Then the mountain queen prostrated and bowed down to me,

1.4.s:
vastranirgūḍhavadanā pāṇipadmakṛtāṃjaliḥ..
tāmahaṃ satyarūpābhirāśīrbhiḥ samavardhayam.. 23.21 ..
1.4.d:
वस्त्रनिर्गूढवदना पाणिपद्मकृतांजलिः..
तामहं सत्यरूपाभिराशीर्भिः समवर्धयम्.. 23.21 ..
1.4.m: her face concealed by her garment, making an añjali with her lotus hands. / I congratulated her with blessings of truthful power:

1.4.s:
pativratā śubhācārā subagā vīrasūḥ śubhe..
sadā vīravatī cāpi bhava vaṃśonnatiprada.. 23.22 ..
1.4.d:
पतिव्रता शुभाचारा सुबगा वीरसूः शुभे..
सदा वीरवती चापि भव वंशोन्नतिप्रद.. 23.22 ..
1.4.m: "Be devoted to your husband, well-behaved, fortunate, mother of a hero, O auspicious one, / ever blessed with heroic sons, and one who elevates the family!"

1.4.s:
tato'haṃ vismitākṣīṃ ca himavadgiriputrikām..
mṛduvāṇyā pratyavocamehi bāle mamāṃtikam.. 23.23 ..
1.4.d:
ततोऽहं विस्मिताक्षीं च हिमवद्गिरिपुत्रिकाम्..
मृदुवाण्या प्रत्यवोचमेहि बाले ममांतिकम्.. 23.23 ..
1.4.m: Then I spoke in gentle speech to the daughter of the Himalaya, whose eyes were wide with wonder: / "Come, little girl, near me."

1.4.s:
tato devī jaganmātā bālabāvaṃ svakaṃ mayi..
darśayaṃtī svapitaraṃ kaṃṭhe gṛhyāṃkamāvi śat.. 23.24 ..
1.4.d:
ततो देवी जगन्माता बालबावं स्वकं मयि..
दर्शयंती स्वपितरं कंठे गृह्यांकमावि शत्.. 23.24 ..
1.4.m: Then the goddess, the mother of the universe, displaying her childlike nature / before me, embraced her father around the neck and sat upon his lap.

1.4.s:
uvāca vācaṃ tāṃ maṃdaṃ muniṃ vaṃdaya putrike..
muneḥ prasādato'vaśyaṃ patimāpsyasi saṃmatam.. 23.25 ..
1.4.d:
उवाच वाचं तां मंदं मुनिं वंदय पुत्रिके..
मुनेः प्रसादतोऽवश्यं पतिमाप्स्यसि संमतम्.. 23.25 ..
1.4.m: He spoke softly to her: "Bow to the sage, O daughter; / through the grace of the sage, you will certainly obtain an approved husband."

1.4.s:
ityuktā sā tato bālā vastrāṃtapi hitānanā..
kiṃcitsahuṃkṛtotkaṃpaṃ procya novāca kiṃcana.. 23.26 ..
1.4.d:
इत्युक्ता सा ततो बाला वस्त्रांतपि हितानना..
किंचित्सहुंकृतोत्कंपं प्रोच्य नोवाच किंचन.. 23.26 ..
1.4.m: Thus addressed, the young girl then covered her face with the hem of her garment, / and trembling slightly with a gentle sound of protest, said nothing at all.

1.4.s:
tato vismitacittohamupacāravidāṃvaraḥ..
pratyavocaṃ punardevīmehi dāsyāmi te śubhe.. 23.27 ..
1.4.d:
ततो विस्मितचित्तोहमुपचारविदांवरः..
प्रत्यवोचं पुनर्देवीमेहि दास्यामि ते शुभे.. 23.27 ..
1.4.m: Then, with my mind astonished, I, the foremost of those who know etiquette, / spoke again to the goddess: 'Come, auspicious girl, I will give [something] to you.

1.4.s:
ratnakrīḍanakaṃ ramyaṃ stāpitaṃ suciraṃ mayā..
ityuktā sā tadotthāya pituraṃkātsavegataḥ.. 23.28 ..
1.4.d:
रत्नक्रीडनकं रम्यं स्तापितं सुचिरं मया..
इत्युक्ता सा तदोत्थाय पितुरंकात्सवेगतः.. 23.28 ..
1.4.m: A charming jewel-toy that I have kept for a very long time.' / Addressed thus, she then quickly rose from her father's lap,

1.4.s:
vaṃdamānā ca me pādau mayā nītāṃka mātmanaḥ..
manyatā tāṃ jagatpūjyāmuktaṃ bāle tavocitam.. 23.29 ..
1.4.d:
वंदमाना च मे पादौ मया नीतांक मात्मनः..
मन्यता तां जगत्पूज्यामुक्तं बाले तवोचितम्.. 23.29 ..
1.4.m: and bowing at my feet, she was placed by me upon my own lap. / Considering her, the one adored by the universe, I said: 'O child, what is fitting for you?

1.4.s:
na tatpaśyāmi yattubhyaṃ dadmyāśīḥ kā tavocitā..
ityukte mātṛvātsalyācchailendra mahiṣī tadā.. 23.30 ..
1.4.d:
न तत्पश्यामि यत्तुभ्यं दद्म्याशीः का तवोचिता..
इत्युक्ते मातृवात्सल्याच्छैलेन्द्र महिषी तदा.. 23.30 ..
1.4.m: I see nothing that I might give you. What blessing is appropriate for you?' / When this was said, the queen of the lord of mountains then, out of maternal love,

1.4.s:
nodayāmāsa māṃ maṃdamānaśīḥśaṃkitā tadā..
bhagavanvetsi sarvaṃ tvamatītānāgataṃ prabho.. 23.31 ..
1.4.d:
नोदयामास मां मंदमानशीःशंकिता तदा..
भगवन्वेत्सि सर्वं त्वमतीतानागतं प्रभो.. 23.31 ..
1.4.m: gently prompted me, anxious because no blessing [had been given]: / 'O lord, you know everything, past and future, O master.

1.4.s:
tadahaṃ jñātumicchāmi kīdṛśo'syāḥ patirbhavet..
śrutveti sasmitamukhaḥ prāvocaṃ narmavallabhaḥ.. 23.32 ..
1.4.d:
तदहं ज्ञातुमिच्छामि कीदृशोऽस्याः पतिर्भवेत्..
श्रुत्वेति सस्मितमुखः प्रावोचं नर्मवल्लभः.. 23.32 ..
1.4.m: Therefore, I wish to know: what kind of husband will she have?' / Hearing this, with a smiling face, fond of jest, I said:

1.4.s:
na jāto'syāḥ patirbhadre vartate ca kulakṣaṇaḥ..
nagno'tinirdhanaḥ krodhīvṛtaḥ krūraiśca sarvadā.. 23.33 ..
1.4.d:
न जातोऽस्याः पतिर्भद्रे वर्तते च कुलक्षणः..
नग्नोऽतिनिर्धनः क्रोधीवृतः क्रूरैश्च सर्वदा.. 23.33 ..
1.4.m: 'Her husband is unborn, O auspicious lady, and he exists destroying family lines; / naked, utterly destitute, wrathful, and always surrounded by cruel beings.'

1.4.s:
śrutveti saṃbhramāviṣṭo dhvastavīryo himācalaḥ..
māṃ tadā pratyuvācedaṃ sāśrukaṇṭho mahāgiriḥ.. 23.34 ..
1.4.d:
श्रुत्वेति संभ्रमाविष्टो ध्वस्तवीर्यो हिमाचलः..
मां तदा प्रत्युवाचेदं साश्रुकण्ठो महागिरिः.. 23.34 ..
1.4.m: Hearing this, seized with confusion, his vigor shattered, / the great mountain Himācala then replied to me with tears in his throat:

1.4.s:
aho vicitraḥ saṃ sāro durvedyo mahatāmapi..
pravarastvapi śaktyā yo nareṣu na kṛpāyate.. 23.35 ..
1.4.d:
अहो विचित्रः सं सारो दुर्वेद्यो महतामपि..
प्रवरस्त्वपि शक्त्या यो नरेषु न कृपायते.. 23.35 ..
1.4.m: 'Ah, transmigratory existence is strange, difficult to comprehend even for the great! / He who is superior in power shows no pity towards men.

1.4.s:
yatnena mahatā tāvatpuṇyairbahuvidhairapi..
sādhayatyātmano loko mānuṣya matidurlabham.. 23.36 ..
1.4.d:
यत्नेन महता तावत्पुण्यैर्बहुविधैरपि..
साधयत्यात्मनो लोको मानुष्य मतिदुर्लभम्.. 23.36 ..
1.4.m: With great exertion indeed, and through manifold merits, / a person attains the extremely rare human state for himself.

1.4.s:
adhruvaṃ taddhravatve ca kathaṃcitparikalpyate..
tatrāpi durlabhānāma samānavratacāriṇī.. 23.37 ..
1.4.d:
अध्रुवं तद्ध्रवत्वे च कथंचित्परिकल्प्यते..
तत्रापि दुर्लभानाम समानव्रतचारिणी.. 23.37 ..
1.4.m: That is impermanent, and permanence in it is somehow imagined; / even there, hard to obtain is she who observes the same vows,

1.4.s:
sādhvī mahākulotpannā bhāryāyā syātpativratā..
tatrāpi durlabhaṃ yacca tayā dharmaniṣevaṇam.. 23.38 ..
1.4.d:
साध्वी महाकुलोत्पन्ना भार्याया स्यात्पतिव्रता..
तत्रापि दुर्लभं यच्च तया धर्मनिषेवणम्.. 23.38 ..
1.4.m: a virtuous wife born of a noble family, devoted to her husband. / Even there, what is hard to obtain is the performance of dharma with her,

1.4.s:
saha vedapurāṇoktaṃ jagattrayahitāvaham..
etatsudurlabhaṃ yacca tasyāṃ caiva prajāyate.. 23.39 ..
1.4.d:
सह वेदपुराणोक्तं जगत्त्रयहितावहम्..
एतत्सुदुर्लभं यच्च तस्यां चैव प्रजायते.. 23.39 ..
1.4.m: together, as stated in the Vedas and Purāṇas, bringing welfare to the three worlds. / And extremely hard to obtain is this: that on her is born

1.4.s:
tadapatyamapatyārthaṃ saṃsāre kila nārada..
eteṣāṃ durlabhānāṃ hi kiṃcitprāpnoti puṇyavān.. 23.40 ..
1.4.d:
तदपत्यमपत्यार्थं संसारे किल नारद..
एतेषां दुर्लभानां हि किंचित्प्राप्नोति पुण्यवान्.. 23.40 ..
1.4.m: that offspring, for the sake of lineage in this worldly cycle, O Nārada! / Indeed, out of these rare things, a virtuous person obtains only some.

1.4.s:
sarvametadavāpnoti sa kopi yadivā na vā..
kiṃcitkenāpi hi nyūnaṃ saṃsāraḥ kurute naram.. 23.41 ..
1.4.d:
सर्वमेतदवाप्नोति स कोपि यदिवा न वा..
किंचित्केनापि हि न्यूनं संसारः कुरुते नरम्.. 23.41 ..
1.4.m: Does anyone at all obtain all this, or perhaps not? / Worldly existence always makes a person deficient in some respect.

1.4.s:
atha saṃsāriko doṣaḥ svakṛtaṃ yatra bhujyate..
gārhasthyaṃ ca praśaṃsaṃti vedāḥ sarve'pi nārada.. 23.42 ..
1.4.d:
अथ संसारिको दोषः स्वकृतं यत्र भुज्यते..
गार्हस्थ्यं च प्रशंसंति वेदाः सर्वेऽपि नारद.. 23.42 ..
1.4.m: Now this worldly defect arises where the fruits of one's own deeds are experienced. / Yet all the Vedas praise the householder stage, O Nārada.

1.4.s:
neti kecittatra punaḥ kathaṃ te yadi no gṛhī..
ato dhātrā ca śāstreṣu sutalābhaḥ praśaṃsitaḥ.. 23.43 ..
1.4.d:
नेति केचित्तत्र पुनः कथं ते यदि नो गृही..
अतो धात्रा च शास्त्रेषु सुतलाभः प्रशंसितः.. 23.43 ..
1.4.m: Some say, "Not so"; but how could they exist if there were no householder? / Therefore, the Creator in the scriptures has praised the attainment of a son

1.4.s:
punaścasṛṣṭivṛddhyarthaṃ narakatrāṇanāya ca..
tatra strīṇāṃ samutpattiṃ vinā sṛṣṭirna jāyate.. 23.44 ..
1.4.d:
पुनश्चसृष्टिवृद्ध्यर्थं नरकत्राणनाय च..
तत्र स्त्रीणां समुत्पत्तिं विना सृष्टिर्न जायते.. 23.44 ..
1.4.m: for the increase of creation and for deliverance from hell. / In that respect, without the birth of women, creation cannot take place.

1.4.s:
sā ca jātiprakṛtyaiva kṛpaṇā dainyabhāginī..
tāsāmupari māvajñā bhavediti ca vedhasā..
śāstreṣūktamasaṃdigdhaṃ vākyametanmahātphalam.. 23.45 ..
1.4.d:
सा च जातिप्रकृत्यैव कृपणा दैन्यभागिनी..
तासामुपरि मावज्ञा भवेदिति च वेधसा..
शास्त्रेषूक्तमसंदिग्धं वाक्यमेतन्महात्फलम्.. 23.45 ..
1.4.m: And by her very nature, that class is wretched, bearing helplessness. / "Let there be no contempt toward them"—thus by the Creator / this unequivocal statement of great fruit has been uttered in the scriptures:

1.4.s:
daśaputrasamā kanyā daśaputrānpravarddhayan..
yatphalaṃ labhate martyastallabhyaṃ kanyayaikayā.. 23.46 ..
1.4.d:
दशपुत्रसमा कन्या दशपुत्रान्प्रवर्द्धयन्..
यत्फलं लभते मर्त्यस्तल्लभ्यं कन्ययैकया.. 23.46 ..
1.4.m: "A daughter is equal to ten sons. Bringing up ten sons, / whatever fruit a mortal obtains, that may be obtained through a single daughter."

1.4.s: tasmātkanyā pituḥ śocyā sadā duḥkhavivardhinī.. 23.47 ..
1.4.d: तस्मात्कन्या पितुः शोच्या सदा दुःखविवर्धिनी.. 23.47 ..
1.4.m: Therefore, a daughter is an object of grief for a father, always increasing distress.

1.4.s:
yāpi syātpūrṇasarvārthā patiputradhanānvitā..
tvayoktaṃ ca kṛte hyasyāstadvākyaṃ mama śokadam.. 23.48 ..
1.4.d:
यापि स्यात्पूर्णसर्वार्था पतिपुत्रधनान्विता..
त्वयोक्तं च कृते ह्यस्यास्तद्वाक्यं मम शोकदम्.. 23.48 ..
1.4.m: Even she who possesses all goals fulfilled, endowed with husband, son, and wealth— / yet the word spoken by you regarding her brings sorrow to me.

1.4.s:
kena doṣeṇa me putrī na yogyā āśiṣāmatā..
na jāto'syāḥ patiḥ kasmādvartate vā kulakṣaṇaḥ.. 23.49 ..
1.4.d:
केन दोषेण मे पुत्री न योग्या आशिषामता..
न जातोऽस्याः पतिः कस्माद्वर्तते वा कुलक्षणः.. 23.49 ..
1.4.m: By what fault is my daughter considered unfit for blessings? / Why is her husband unborn, or why is he a destroyer of families?

1.4.s:
nirdhanaśca mune kasmātsarveṣāṃ sarvadaḥ kutaḥ..
iti durghaṭavākyaṃ te mano mohayatīva me.. 23.50 ..
1.4.d:
निर्धनश्च मुने कस्मात्सर्वेषां सर्वदः कुतः..
इति दुर्घटवाक्यं ते मनो मोहयतीव मे.. 23.50 ..
1.4.m: And why is he destitute, O sage, and whence is he the giver of everything to all? / This contradictory statement of yours seems to bewilder my mind.'

1.4.s:
iti taṃ putravātsalyātsabhāryaṃ śokasaṃplutam..
ahamāśvāsayaṃ vāgbhiḥ satyābhiḥ pāṃḍunaṃdana.. 23.51 ..
1.4.d:
इति तं पुत्रवात्सल्यात्सभार्यं शोकसंप्लुतम्..
अहमाश्वासयं वाग्भिः सत्याभिः पांडुनंदन.. 23.51 ..
1.4.m: To him, overwhelmed with sorrow along with his wife out of love for their child, / I offered comfort with true words, O son of Pāṇḍu:

1.4.s:
mā śucaḥ śailarāja tvaṃ harṣasthāne'tipuṇyabhāk..
śrṛṇu tadvacanaṃ mahyaṃ yanmayoktaṃ ca hyarthavat.. 23.52 ..
1.4.d:
मा शुचः शैलराज त्वं हर्षस्थानेऽतिपुण्यभाक्..
श्रृणु तद्वचनं मह्यं यन्मयोक्तं च ह्यर्थवत्.. 23.52 ..
1.4.m: 'Do not grieve, O king of mountains! In this occasion of joy, you are exceedingly fortunate. / Listen to that word of mine, for what I said was meaningful.

1.4.s:
jaganmātā tviyaṃ bālā putrī te sarvasiddhidā..
purā bhave'bhavadbhāryā satīnāmnā bhavasya yā.. 23.53 ..
1.4.d:
जगन्माता त्वियं बाला पुत्री ते सर्वसिद्धिदा..
पुरा भवेऽभवद्भार्या सतीनाम्ना भवस्य या.. 23.53 ..
1.4.m: This girl, your daughter, is the mother of the universe, granting all perfections. / Formerly, she was the wife of Bhava in a previous life, named Satī.

1.4.s:
tadasyāḥ kimahaṃ dadmi raverdīpamivālpakaḥ..
saṃciṃtyeti mahādevyā nāśiṣaṃ dattavānaham.. 23.54 ..
1.4.d:
तदस्याः किमहं दद्मि रवेर्दीपमिवाल्पकः..
संचिंत्येति महादेव्या नाशिषं दत्तवानहम्.. 23.54 ..
1.4.m: So what could I, like a tiny lamp before the sun, give to her? / Reflecting thus, I did not bestow a blessing upon the great goddess.

1.4.s:
na jāto'bhavadbhāryā patiśceti vartate ca bhavo hi saḥ..
na sa jāto mahādevo bhūtabhavyabhavodbhavaḥ.. 23.55 ..
1.4.d:
न जातोऽभवद्भार्या पतिश्चेति वर्तते च भवो हि सः..
न स जातो महादेवो भूतभव्यभवोद्भवः.. 23.55 ..
1.4.m: The husband of the unborn wife exists indeed, and he is Bhava himself. / He is unborn, the Great God, the source of past, present, and future,

1.4.s: śaraṇyaḥ śāśvataḥ śāstā śaṃkaraḥ parameśvaraḥ.. 23.56 ..
1.4.d: शरण्यः शाश्वतः शास्ता शंकरः परमेश्वरः.. 23.56 ..
1.4.m: the refuge, eternal, the ruler, Śaṃkara, the supreme lord.

1.4.s:
sarve devā yatpadamāmanaṃti vedaiśca sarvairapi yo na labhyaḥ..
brahmādiviśvaṃ nanu yasya śaila bālasya vā krīḍanakaṃ vadaṃti.. 23.57 ..
1.4.d:
सर्वे देवा यत्पदमामनंति वेदैश्च सर्वैरपि यो न लभ्यः..
ब्रह्मादिविश्वं ननु यस्य शैल बालस्य वा क्रीडनकं वदंति.. 23.57 ..
1.4.m: All the gods recite whose state, who cannot be attained even by all the Vedas, / whose plaything they declare the universe beginning with Brahmā to be, like a child's toy, O mountain!

1.4.s:
sa cāmaṃgalyaśīlo'pi maṃgalāṃ yatano haraḥ..
nirdhanaḥ sarvadaścāsau veda svaṃ svayameva saḥ.. 23.58 ..
1.4.d:
स चामंगल्यशीलोऽपि मंगलां यतनो हरः..
निर्धनः सर्वदश्चासौ वेद स्वं स्वयमेव सः.. 23.58 ..
1.4.m: And though having inauspicious conduct, Hara is the abode of auspiciousness. / Destitute and the giver of all, he alone knows his own [wealth].

1.4.s:
sa ca devo'calaḥ sthāṇurmahādevo'jaro haraḥ..
bhaviṣyati patiḥ so'syāstatkimarthaṃ tu śocasi.. 23.59 ..
iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ prathame māheśvarakhaṇḍe kaumārikākhaṇḍe kumāreśamāhātmye himavadāśvāsanaṃnāma trayoviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ.. 23 .. cha ..
1.4.d:
स च देवोऽचलः स्थाणुर्महादेवोऽजरो हरः..
भविष्यति पतिः सोऽस्यास्तत्किमर्थं तु शोचसि.. 23.59 ..
इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां प्रथमे माहेश्वरखण्डे कौमारिकाखण्डे कुमारेशमाहात्म्ये हिमवदाश्वासनंनाम त्रयोविंशोऽध्यायः.. 23 .. छ ..
1.4.m:
He, the immovable god, Sthāṇu, the Great God, ageless Hara, / shall be her husband; therefore, why do you grieve?'
Thus ends the twenty-third chapter, named "Consolation of Himavat," in the Kumāreśamāhātmya of the Kaumārikākhaṇḍa, in the first [section], the Māheśvarakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa of eighty-one thousand verses.

1.4.s:
..nārada uvāca..
evaṃ śrutvā sabhāryaḥ sa pramodaplutamānasaḥ..
praṇamya māmiti prāha yadyevaṃ puṇyavānaham.. 24.1 ..
1.4.d:
..नारद उवाच..
एवं श्रुत्वा सभार्यः स प्रमोदप्लुतमानसः..
प्रणम्य मामिति प्राह यद्येवं पुण्यवानहम्.. 24.1 ..
1.4.m: Nārada said: / Having heard this along with his wife, his mind flooded with joy, / he bowed to me and said: 'If this is so, I am fortunate.

1.4.s:
punaḥ kiṃcitpravakṣyāmi putryā me dakṣiṇaḥ karaḥ..
uttānaḥ kāraṇaṃ kiṃ tacchrotumicchāmi nārada.. 24.2 ..
1.4.d:
पुनः किंचित्प्रवक्ष्यामि पुत्र्या मे दक्षिणः करः..
उत्तानः कारणं किं तच्छ्रोतुमिच्छामि नारद.. 24.2 ..
1.4.m: I will ask something further: my daughter's right hand / is upturned. What is the cause of that? I wish to hear it, O Nārada.'

1.4.s:
iti pṛṣṭo'smi śailena prāvocaṃ kāraṇaṃ tadā..
sarvadaiva karo hyasyāḥ sarveṣāṃ prāṇināṃ prati.. 24.3 ..
1.4.d:
इति पृष्टोऽस्मि शैलेन प्रावोचं कारणं तदा..
सर्वदैव करो ह्यस्याः सर्वेषां प्राणिनां प्रति.. 24.3 ..
1.4.m: Thus questioned by the mountain, I then stated the reason: / 'Her hand is always extended towards all living beings.

1.4.s:
abhayasya pradātā'sāvuttānastu karastataḥ..
eṣā bhāryā jagadbharturvṛṣāṃkasya mahīdhara.. 24.4 ..
1.4.d:
अभयस्य प्रदाताऽसावुत्तानस्तु करस्ततः..
एषा भार्या जगद्भर्तुर्वृषांकस्य महीधर.. 24.4 ..
1.4.m: It is the bestower of fearlessness; therefore her hand is upturned. / She is the wife of the lord of the universe, whose banner bears a bull, O mountain-bearer,

1.4.s:
jananī sarvalokasya bhāvinī bhūtabhāvinī..
tadyathā śīghramevaiṣā yogaṃ yātu pinākinā.. 24.5 ..
1.4.d:
जननी सर्वलोकस्य भाविनी भूतभाविनी..
तद्यथा शीघ्रमेवैषा योगं यातु पिनाकिना.. 24.5 ..
1.4.m: the mother of all worlds, the future goddess, the creator of beings. / Therefore, in such a way that she may soon achieve union with Pinākin,

1.4.s:
tvayā vidheyaṃ vidhivattathā śailendrasattama..
astyatra sumahatakāryaṃ devānāṃ himabhūdhara.. 24.6 ..
1.4.d:
त्वया विधेयं विधिवत्तथा शैलेन्द्रसत्तम..
अस्त्यत्र सुमहतकार्यं देवानां हिमभूधर.. 24.6 ..
1.4.m: it must be properly arranged by you, O best of the mountain lords! / In this matter there is a very great task for the gods, O snow-mountain.'

1.4.s:
iti procya tamāpṛcchya prāvocaṃ vāsavāya tat..
mama bhūyastu kartavyaṃ tanmayā kṛtameva hi.. 24.7 ..
1.4.d:
इति प्रोच्य तमापृच्छ्य प्रावोचं वासवाय तत्..
मम भूयस्तु कर्तव्यं तन्मया कृतमेव हि.. 24.7 ..
1.4.m: Having said this and taken leave of him, I reported that to Vāsava: / 'What remained as my duty, that has indeed been accomplished by me.

1.4.s:
kiṃ tu paṃcaśaraḥ preryaḥ kāryaśeṣe'tra vāsava..
ityādiśya gataścāhaṃ tārakaṃ prati phālguna.. 24.8 ..
1.4.d:
किं तु पंचशरः प्रेर्यः कार्यशेषेऽत्र वासव..
इत्यादिश्य गतश्चाहं तारकं प्रति फाल्गुन.. 24.8 ..
1.4.m: However, the five-arrowed [Kāma] must be dispatched for the remainder of the work here, O Vāsava.' / Having instructed thus, I went towards Tāraka, O Phālguna,

1.4.s:
kalipriyatvāttasyainamarthaṃ kathayituṃ sphuṭam..
himādrirapi me vākyapreritaḥ pārvatīṃ prati.. 24.9 ..
1.4.d:
कलिप्रियत्वात्तस्यैनमर्थं कथयितुं स्फुटम्..
हिमाद्रिरपि मे वाक्यप्रेरितः पार्वतीं प्रति.. 24.9 ..
1.4.m: due to my love of strife, in order to disclose this matter clearly to him. / And the snow-mountain, prompted by my words regarding Pārvatī,

1.4.s:
bhavasyārādhanāṃ kartuṃ sasakhīmādiśattadā..
sā taṃ paricacāreśaṃ tasyā dṛṣṭvā suśīlatām.. 24.10 ..
1.4.d:
भवस्याराधनां कर्तुं ससखीमादिशत्तदा..
सा तं परिचचारेशं तस्या दृष्ट्वा सुशीलताम्.. 24.10 ..
1.4.m: Then [Himavat] instructed [Pārvatī] along with her female companions to worship Bhava. / Seeing her good conduct, she attended upon the Lord.

1.4.s:
puṣpatoyaphalādyāni niyuktā pārvatī vyadhāt..
mahendropi ca madvākyātsmaraṃ sasmāra bhārata.. 24.11 ..
1.4.d:
पुष्पतोयफलाद्यानि नियुक्ता पार्वती व्यधात्..
महेन्द्रोपि च मद्वाक्यात्स्मरं सस्मार भारत.. 24.11 ..
1.4.m: Appointed thus, Pārvatī offered flowers, water, fruits, and other gifts. / And Mahendra also, at my word, remembered Smara, O Bhārata.

1.4.s:
sa ca tatsmaraṇaṃ jñātvā vasaṃtaratisaṃyutaḥ..
cūtāṃkurāstraḥṛ sahasā prādurāsīnmanobhavaḥ.. 24.12 ..
1.4.d:
स च तत्स्मरणं ज्ञात्वा वसंतरतिसंयुतः..
चूतांकुरास्त्रःऋ सहसा प्रादुरासीन्मनोभवः.. 24.12 ..
1.4.m: Knowing that recollection of him, Manobhava, accompanied by Spring and Rati, / armed with a mango-sprout arrow, suddenly appeared.

1.4.s:
tamāha ca vaco dhīmānsmaranniva ca taṃ spṛśan..
upadeśena bahunā kiṃ tvāṃ prati ratipriya.. 24.13 ..
1.4.d:
तमाह च वचो धीमान्स्मरन्निव च तं स्पृशन्..
उपदेशेन बहुना किं त्वां प्रति रतिप्रिय.. 24.13 ..
1.4.m: The wise [Indra], as if recalling [his purpose] and touching him, spoke these words to him: / "What need is there of much instruction to you, O lover of Rati?

1.4.s:
citte vasasi tena tvaṃ vetsi bhūtamanogatam..
tathāpi tvāṃ vadiṣyāmi svakāryaparatāṃ smaran.. 24.14 ..
1.4.d:
चित्ते वससि तेन त्वं वेत्सि भूतमनोगतम्..
तथापि त्वां वदिष्यामि स्वकार्यपरतां स्मरन्.. 24.14 ..
1.4.m: You dwell in the heart; therefore you know what is in the minds of living beings. / Nevertheless, mindful of devotion to my own duty, I shall speak to you.

1.4.s:
mamaikaṃ sumahatkāryaṃ kartumarhasi manmatha..
maheśvaraṃ kṛpānāthaṃ satībhāryāviyojitam.. 24.15 ..
1.4.d:
ममैकं सुमहत्कार्यं कर्तुमर्हसि मन्मथ..
महेश्वरं कृपानाथं सतीभार्यावियोजितम्.. 24.15 ..
1.4.m: You ought to perform one very great task for me, O Manmatha: / Maheśvara, the lord of compassion, has been separated from his wife Satī;

1.4.s:
saṃyojaya punardevyā himādrigṛhajātayā..
devī devaśca tuṣṭau te kariṣyata ihepsitam.. 24.16 ..
1.4.d:
संयोजय पुनर्देव्या हिमाद्रिगृहजातया..
देवी देवश्च तुष्टौ ते करिष्यत इहेप्सितम्.. 24.16 ..
1.4.m: unite him again with the Goddess born in the house of the Snowy Mountain. / The Goddess and the God, being pleased, will fulfill your desire here."

1.4.s:
..madana uvāca..
alīkametaddevendra sa hi devasya poratiḥ..
nānyāsādayitavyāni tejāṃsi munarabravīt.. 24.17 ..
1.4.d:
..मदन उवाच..
अलीकमेतद्देवेन्द्र स हि देवस्य पोरतिः..
नान्यासादयितव्यानि तेजांसि मुनरब्रवीत्.. 24.17 ..
1.4.m: Madana said: / "This is false, O king of the gods, for he is the chief of the gods. / The sage declared: 'Other radiances are not to be approached.'

1.4.s:
vedānteṣu ca māṃ viprā garhasaṃyati punaḥpunaḥ..
mahāśano mahāpāpmā kāmo'yama nalo gahān.. 24.18 ..
1.4.d:
वेदान्तेषु च मां विप्रा गर्हसंयति पुनःपुनः..
महाशनो महापाप्मा कामोऽयम नलो गहान्.. 24.18 ..
1.4.m: And in the Vedāntas, the brahmins rebuke me again and again: / 'This desire is a great devourer, a great evil, an insatiable fire.'

1.4.s:
āvṛtaṃ jñānametena jñānināṃ nityavairiṇā..
tasmādayaṃ sadā tyājyaḥ kāma'hiriva sattamaiḥ.. 24.19 ..
1.4.d:
आवृतं ज्ञानमेतेन ज्ञानिनां नित्यवैरिणा..
तस्मादयं सदा त्याज्यः कामऽहिरिव सत्तमैः.. 24.19 ..
1.4.m: 'Knowledge is veiled by this eternal enemy of the wise.' / Therefore, this desire is always to be abandoned by the best of beings, like a serpent.

1.4.s:
evaṃ śīlasya me kasmātpratuṣyati maheśvaraḥ..
madyapasyeva pāpasya vāsudevo jagadguraḥ.. 24.20 ..
1.4.d:
एवं शीलस्य मे कस्मात्प्रतुष्यति महेश्वरः..
मद्यपस्येव पापस्य वासुदेवो जगद्गुरः.. 24.20 ..
1.4.m: Why should Maheśvara be pleased with one of such nature as mine, / as Vāsudeva, the guru of the world, [is displeased] with a sinful drunkard?"

1.4.s:
..iṃdra uvāca..
maivaṃ brūhi mahābhāga tvāṃ vinākaḥ pumānbhuvi..
dharmamarthaṃ tathā kāmaṃ mokṣaṃ vā prāptumīśvaraḥ.. 24.21 ..
1.4.d:
..इंद्र उवाच..
मैवं ब्रूहि महाभाग त्वां विनाकः पुमान्भुवि..
धर्ममर्थं तथा कामं मोक्षं वा प्राप्तुमीश्वरः.. 24.21 ..
1.4.m: Indra said: / "Do not speak thus, O highly fortunate one! Without you, what man on earth / is capable of attaining virtue, wealth, desire, or liberation?

1.4.s:
yatkiṃcitsādhyate loke mūlaṃ tasya ca kāmanā..
kathaṃ kāmaṃ viniṃdati tasmātte mokṣasādhakāḥ.. 24.22 ..
1.4.d:
यत्किंचित्साध्यते लोके मूलं तस्य च कामना..
कथं कामं विनिंदति तस्मात्ते मोक्षसाधकाः.. 24.22 ..
1.4.m: Whatever is accomplished in the world, the root of it is desire. / Why, then, do those seekers of liberation condemn desire?

1.4.s:
satyaṃ cāpi śrutervākyaṃ tava rūpaṃ tridhāgatam..
tāmasaṃ rājasaṃ caiva sāttvikaṃ cāpi manmatha.. 24.23 ..
1.4.d:
सत्यं चापि श्रुतेर्वाक्यं तव रूपं त्रिधागतम्..
तामसं राजसं चैव सात्त्विकं चापि मन्मथ.. 24.23 ..
1.4.m: And true is the word of the Veda: your form has become threefold, / tāmasic, rājasic, and also sāttvic, O Manmatha.

1.4.s:
amuktitaḥ kāmanayā rūpaṃ tattāmasaṃ tava..
sukhabuddhyā spṛhā yā ca rūpaṃ tadrājasaṃ tava.. 24.24 ..
1.4.d:
अमुक्तितः कामनया रूपं तत्तामसं तव..
सुखबुद्ध्या स्पृहा या च रूपं तद्राजसं तव.. 24.24 ..
1.4.m: Desire apart from liberation is that tāmasic form of yours; / longing with the thought of pleasure is that rājasic form of yours;

1.4.s:
kevalaṃ yāvadarthārthaṃ tadrūpaṃ sāttvikaṃ tava..
tatte rūpatrayamidaṃ brūhi nopāsate hi ke.. 24.25 ..
1.4.d:
केवलं यावदर्थार्थं तद्रूपं सात्त्विकं तव..
तत्ते रूपत्रयमिदं ब्रूहि नोपासते हि के.. 24.25 ..
1.4.m: that which is merely for the sake of what is necessary is that sāttvic form of yours. / Tell me, who indeed does not worship this threefold form of yours?

1.4.s:
tvaṃ sākṣātparamaḥ pūjyaḥ kuru kāryamidaṃ hi naḥ..
atha vā pīḍitāndṛṣṭvā sāmānyānapi paṃḍitāḥ..
svaprāṇairapi trāyāṃti parametanmahāphalam.. 24.26 ..
1.4.d:
त्वं साक्षात्परमः पूज्यः कुरु कार्यमिदं हि नः..
अथ वा पीडितान्दृष्ट्वा सामान्यानपि पंडिताः..
स्वप्राणैरपि त्रायांति परमेतन्महाफलम्.. 24.26 ..
1.4.m: You are directly supreme and venerable; perform this task of ours. / Moreover, seeing even ordinary beings afflicted, the wise / protect them even with their own lives; this is the highest, great fruit.

1.4.s: iti saṃciṃtya kāryaṃ tvaṃ sarvathā kuru tatsphuṭam.. 24.27 ..
1.4.d: इति संचिंत्य कार्यं त्वं सर्वथा कुरु तत्स्फुटम्.. 24.27 ..
1.4.m: Considering this, perform the task in every way, clearly."

1.4.s:
ityā karṇya tathetyuktvā vasaṃtaratisaṃyutaḥ..
pikādisainyasaṃpanno himādriṃ prayayau smaraḥ.. 24.28 ..
1.4.d:
इत्या कर्ण्य तथेत्युक्त्वा वसंतरतिसंयुतः..
पिकादिसैन्यसंपन्नो हिमाद्रिं प्रययौ स्मरः.. 24.28 ..
1.4.m: Hearing this and saying 'So be it,' Smara, accompanied by Spring and Rati, / equipped with an army of cuckoos and other creatures, set out for the Snowy Mountain.

1.4.s:
tatrāpaśyata śaṃbhoḥ sa puṇyamāśramamaṃḍalam..
nānāvṛkṣasamākīrṇaṃ śāṃtasattvasamākulam.. 24.29 ..
1.4.d:
तत्रापश्यत शंभोः स पुण्यमाश्रममंडलम्..
नानावृक्षसमाकीर्णं शांतसत्त्वसमाकुलम्.. 24.29 ..
1.4.m: There he saw Śambhu's holy hermitage grounds, / filled with various trees and crowded with peaceful animals.

1.4.s:
tatrāpaśyattrinetrasya vīrakaṃnāma dvārapam..
yathā sākṣānmaheśānaṃ gaṇaāṃścāyutaśo'sya ca.. 24.30 ..
1.4.d:
तत्रापश्यत्त्रिनेत्रस्य वीरकंनाम द्वारपम्..
यथा साक्षान्महेशानं गणआंश्चायुतशोऽस्य च.. 24.30 ..
1.4.m: There he saw the Three-eyed God's doorkeeper named Vīraka, / who looked just like Maheśāna in person, and tens of thousands of his gaṇas.

1.4.s:
dadarśa ca maheśānaṃ nāsāgrakṛtalocanam..
devadārudrumacchāyāvedikā madhyamāśritam..
samākāyaṃ sukhāsīnaṃ samādhisthaṃ maheśvaram.. 24.31 ..
1.4.d:
ददर्श च महेशानं नासाग्रकृतलोचनम्..
देवदारुद्रुमच्छायावेदिका मध्यमाश्रितम्..
समाकायं सुखासीनं समाधिस्थं महेश्वरम्.. 24.31 ..
1.4.m: And he saw Maheśāna, whose eyes were fixed on the tip of his nose, / seated in the center of an altar beneath the shade of a deodar tree, / his body straight, seated at ease, established in meditation, the great lord,

1.4.s:
nistaraṃgaṃ vinirgṛhya sthitamiṃdriyagocarān..
ātmānamātmanā devaṃ praviṣṭaṃ tapaso nidhim.. 24.32 ..
1.4.d:
निस्तरंगं विनिर्गृह्य स्थितमिंद्रियगोचरान्..
आत्मानमात्मना देवं प्रविष्टं तपसो निधिम्.. 24.32 ..
1.4.m: motionless, restraining the range of his senses, / the God, a treasure of austerity, absorbed in the Self by the Self.

1.4.s:
taṃ tathāvidhamālokya soṃtarbhedāya yatnavān..
bhramaradhvanivyājena viveśa madano manaḥ.. 24.33 ..
1.4.d:
तं तथाविधमालोक्य सोंतर्भेदाय यत्नवान्..
भ्रमरध्वनिव्याजेन विवेश मदनो मनः.. 24.33 ..
1.4.m: Beholding him thus, Madana made an effort to penetrate inside, / and entered his mind under the guise of the humming of bees.

1.4.s:
etasminnaṃtare devo vikāsitavilocanaḥ..
sasmāra nagarājasya tanayāṃ raktamānasaḥ.. 24.34 ..
1.4.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे देवो विकासितविलोचनः..
सस्मार नगराजस्य तनयां रक्तमानसः.. 24.34 ..
1.4.m: In the meantime, the God opened his eyes, / and, his heart filled with passion, remembered the daughter of the king of mountains.

1.4.s:
niveditā vīrakeṇa viveśa ca gireḥ sutā..
tasminkāle mahābhāgā sadā yadvadupaiti sā.. 24.35 ..
1.4.d:
निवेदिता वीरकेण विवेश च गिरेः सुता..
तस्मिन्काले महाभागा सदा यद्वदुपैति सा.. 24.35 ..
1.4.m: Announced by Vīraka, the mountain's daughter entered, / the highly fortunate one, at that time, just as she always approached.

1.4.s:
tatastasyāṃ manaḥ svīyamanuraktamavekṣya ca..
nigṛhya līlayā devaḥ svakaṃ pṛṣṭhamavaikṣata..
tāvadāpūrṇadhanuṣamapaśyata ratipriyam.. 24.36 ..
1.4.d:
ततस्तस्यां मनः स्वीयमनुरक्तमवेक्ष्य च..
निगृह्य लीलया देवः स्वकं पृष्ठमवैक्षत..
तावदापूर्णधनुषमपश्यत रतिप्रियम्.. 24.36 ..
1.4.m: Then, observing that his own mind had become enamored of her, / the God playfully restrained it and looked behind him; / just then he saw the lover of Rati, his bow fully drawn.

1.4.s:
tannāśakṛpayā devo nānāsthāneṣu so'gamat..
tāvatpasyati pṛṣṭhastamākṛṣya dhanuṣaḥ śaram.. 24.37 ..
1.4.d:
तन्नाशकृपया देवो नानास्थानेषु सोऽगमत्..
तावत्पस्यति पृष्ठस्तमाकृष्य धनुषः शरम्.. 24.37 ..
1.4.m: Out of compassion to avert his destruction, the God moved to various places; / yet he saw him standing behind him, having drawn the arrow to his bow.

1.4.s:
sa nadīḥ parvatāścaiva āśramānsarasīstathā..
paribhramanmahādevaḥ pṛṣṭhasthaṃ tamavaikṣata.. 24.38 ..
1.4.d:
स नदीः पर्वताश्चैव आश्रमान्सरसीस्तथा..
परिभ्रमन्महादेवः पृष्ठस्थं तमवैक्षत.. 24.38 ..
1.4.m: Wandering across rivers, mountains, hermitages, and lakes, / Mahādeva still saw him standing behind him.

1.4.s:
jagattrayaṃ paribhramya punarāgātsvamāśramam..
pṛṣṭhasthameva taṃ vīkṣya niḥśvāsaṃ mumuce haraḥ.. 24.39 ..
1.4.d:
जगत्त्रयं परिभ्रम्य पुनरागात्स्वमाश्रमम्..
पृष्ठस्थमेव तं वीक्ष्य निःश्वासं मुमुचे हरः.. 24.39 ..
1.4.m: Having wandered through the three worlds, he returned again to his own hermitage; / seeing him still standing behind him, Hara breathed a sigh.

1.4.s:
tatastṛtīyanetrotthavahninā nākavāsinām..
krośatāṃ gamitaḥ kāmo bhasmatvaṃ pāṃḍunaṃdana.. 24.40 ..
1.4.d:
ततस्तृतीयनेत्रोत्थवह्निना नाकवासिनाम्..
क्रोशतां गमितः कामो भस्मत्वं पांडुनंदन.. 24.40 ..
1.4.m: Then, by the fire sprung from his third eye, while the dwellers of heaven / cried out, Kāma was reduced to ashes, O son of Pāṇḍu.

1.4.s:
sasa tu taṃ bhasmasātkṛtvā haranetrodbhavo'nalaḥ..
vyajṛṃbhata jagaddagdhuṃ jvālāpūritadiṅ‌mukhaḥ.. 24.41 ..
1.4.d:
सस तु तं भस्मसात्कृत्वा हरनेत्रोद्भवोऽनलः..
व्यजृंभत जगद्दग्धुं ज्वालापूरितदिङ्‌मुखः.. 24.41 ..
1.4.m: Having reduced him to ashes, the fire born from Hara's eye / flared up to burn the world, the quarters of space filled with its flames.

1.4.s:
tato bhavo jagaddhetorvyabhajajjātavedasam..
sāhaṃkāre jane caṃdre sumanassu ca gītake.. 24.42 ..
1.4.d:
ततो भवो जगद्धेतोर्व्यभजज्जातवेदसम्..
साहंकारे जने चंद्रे सुमनस्सु च गीतके.. 24.42 ..
1.4.m: Then, for the sake of the world, Bhava distributed the fire / among arrogant people, in the moon, in flowers, and in songs,

1.4.s:
bhṛṃgeṣu kokilāsyeṣu vihāreṣu smarānalam..
tatprāptau snehasaṃyuktaṃ kāmināṃ hṛdayaṃ kila.. 24.43 ..
1.4.d:
भृंगेषु कोकिलास्येषु विहारेषु स्मरानलम्..
तत्प्राप्तौ स्नेहसंयुक्तं कामिनां हृदयं किल.. 24.43 ..
1.4.m: in bees, in the mouths of cuckoos, and in amorous sports—the fire of Smara. / When it is attained, that fire, difficult to cure and bringing distress,

1.4.s:
jvālayatyaniśaṃ so'gnirduścikitsyo'sukhāvahaḥ..
vilokya haraniḥśvāsajvālābhasmīkṛtaṃ smaram.. 24.44 ..
1.4.d:
ज्वालयत्यनिशं सोऽग्निर्दुश्चिकित्स्योऽसुखावहः..
विलोक्य हरनिःश्वासज्वालाभस्मीकृतं स्मरम्.. 24.44 ..
1.4.m: constantly inflames the hearts of impassioned lovers with affection. / Beholding Smara reduced to ashes by the flame of Hara's breath,

1.4.s:
vilalāpa ratirddīnā madhunā baṃdhunā saha..
vilapaṃtī subahuśo madhunā parisāṃtvitā.. 24.45 ..
1.4.d:
विललाप रतिर्द्दीना मधुना बंधुना सह..
विलपंती सुबहुशो मधुना परिसांत्विता.. 24.45 ..
1.4.m: the miserable Rati lamented alongside her kinsman Madhu. / As she lamented again and again, she was consoled by Madhu.

1.4.s:
ratyāḥ pralāpamākarṇya devadevo vṛṣadhvajaḥ..
kṛpayā parayā prāha kāmapatnīṃ nirīkṣya ca.. 24.46 ..
1.4.d:
रत्याः प्रलापमाकर्ण्य देवदेवो वृषध्वजः..
कृपया परया प्राह कामपत्नीं निरीक्ष्य च.. 24.46 ..
1.4.m: Hearing Rati's lament, the God of gods whose banner bears the bull, / with supreme compassion looked at Kāma's wife and said:

1.4.s:
amūrto'pi hyayaṃ bhadre kāryaṃ sarvaṃ patistava..
ratikāle dhruvaṃ bāle kariṣyati na saṃśayaḥ.. 24.47 ..
1.4.d:
अमूर्तोऽपि ह्ययं भद्रे कार्यं सर्वं पतिस्तव..
रतिकाले ध्रुवं बाले करिष्यति न संशयः.. 24.47 ..
1.4.m: "Even though bodiless, O auspicious one, this husband of yours / will certainly accomplish all your tasks at the time of lovemaking, O young girl; there is no doubt.

1.4.s:
yadā viṣṇuśca bhavitā vasudevātmajo vibhuḥ..
tadai tasya suto yaḥ syātsapatiste bhaviṣyati.. 24.48 ..
1.4.d:
यदा विष्णुश्च भविता वसुदेवात्मजो विभुः..
तदै तस्य सुतो यः स्यात्सपतिस्ते भविष्यति.. 24.48 ..
1.4.m: When the all-pervading Viṣṇu becomes the son of Vasudeva, / then he who will be his son shall become your husband."

1.4.s:
sā praṇamya tato rudramiti proktā ratistataḥ..
jagāma svecchayā gatyā vasaṃtādibhiranvitā.. 24.49 ..
iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ prathame māheśvarakhaṇḍe kaumārikākhaṇḍe kumāreśvaramāhātmye kāmadahanonāma caturviśo'dhyāyaḥ.. 24 .. cha ..
1.4.d:
सा प्रणम्य ततो रुद्रमिति प्रोक्ता रतिस्ततः..
जगाम स्वेच्छया गत्या वसंतादिभिरन्विता.. 24.49 ..
इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां प्रथमे माहेश्वरखण्डे कौमारिकाखण्डे कुमारेश्वरमाहात्म्ये कामदहनोनाम चतुर्विशोऽध्यायः.. 24 .. छ ..
1.4.m:
Having bowed to Rudra after being spoken to thus, Rati / went at her own pleasure, accompanied by Spring and the others.
Thus ends the twenty-fourth chapter, named 'The Burning of Kāma,' in the Kumāreśvaramāhātmya of the Kaumārikākhaṇḍa of the first section, the Māheśvarakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skandapurāṇa, a collection of eighty-one thousand verses.

1.4.s:
..arjuna uvāca..
devarṣe varṇyate ceyaṃ kathā pīyūṣasodarā..
punaretanmune brūhi yadā vetti maheśvaraḥ.. 25.1 ..
1.4.d:
..अर्जुन उवाच..
देवर्षे वर्ण्यते चेयं कथा पीयूषसोदरा..
पुनरेतन्मुने ब्रूहि यदा वेत्ति महेश्वरः.. 25.1 ..
1.4.m: Arjuna said: / "O divine seer, this story being narrated is equal to nectar! / Tell this again, O sage, when Maheśvara becomes aware [of it]."

1.4.s:
bhagavānsvāṃ satīṃ bhāryāṃ vadhārthaṃ cāpi tārakam..
satyāśca virahāttapyandadāha kimasau smaram.. 25.2 ..
1.4.d:
भगवान्स्वां सतीं भार्यां वधार्थं चापि तारकम्..
सत्याश्च विरहात्तप्यन्ददाह किमसौ स्मरम्.. 25.2 ..
1.4.m: [The Blessed One was intent on] his wife Satī and on the slaying of Tāraka. / Burning with the separation from Satī, why did he burn Smara?

1.4.s:
tvayaivoktaṃ sa virahātsatyāstapyati vai tapaḥ..
himādrimāsthito devastasyāḥ saṃgamavāṃchayā.. 25.3 ..
1.4.d:
त्वयैवोक्तं स विरहात्सत्यास्तप्यति वै तपः..
हिमाद्रिमास्थितो देवस्तस्याः संगमवांछया.. 25.3 ..
1.4.m: You yourself said that, out of separation from Satī, he was performing austerity, / the god remaining on the Snow-Mountain desiring union with her.

1.4.s:
..nārada uvāca..
satyametatpurā pārtha bhavasyedaṃ manīṣitam..
ataptatapasā yogo na kartavyo mayā'nayā.. 25.4 ..
1.4.d:
..नारद उवाच..
सत्यमेतत्पुरा पार्थ भवस्येदं मनीषितम्..
अतप्ततपसा योगो न कर्तव्यो मयाऽनया.. 25.4 ..
1.4.m: Nārada said: / That is true, O Pārtha; formerly, Bhava's intention was this: / 'I should not enter into union with this [maiden] whose austerity has not been performed.'

1.4.s:
tapo vinā śuddhadeho na kathaṃcana jāyate..
asuddhadehena samaṃ saṃyogo naiva daihikaḥ.. 25.5 ..
1.4.d:
तपो विना शुद्धदेहो न कथंचन जायते..
असुद्धदेहेन समं संयोगो नैव दैहिकः.. 25.5 ..
1.4.m: Without austerity, a body is never made pure. / There can be no bodily union with an impure body.

1.4.s:
mahatkarmāṇi yānīha teṣāṃ mūlaṃ sadā tapaḥ..
nātaptatapasāṃ siddhirmahatkarmāṇi yāṃti vai.. 25.6 ..
1.4.d:
महत्कर्माणि यानीह तेषां मूलं सदा तपः..
नातप्ततपसां सिद्धिर्महत्कर्माणि यांति वै.. 25.6 ..
1.4.m: Whatever great undertakings exist here, their root is always austerity. / Success never comes to great undertakings for those whose austerity is not performed.

1.4.s:
etasmātkāraṇāddevo darpitaṃ taṃ dadāha tu..
tato dagdhe smare cāpi pārvatīmapi vrītitām.. 25.7 ..
1.4.d:
एतस्मात्कारणाद्देवो दर्पितं तं ददाह तु..
ततो दग्धे स्मरे चापि पार्वतीमपि व्रीतिताम्.. 25.7 ..
1.4.m: For this reason, the god burned that arrogant one. / Then, when Smara was burned and Pārvatī was ashamed,

1.4.s:
vihāya sagaṇo devaḥ kailāsaṃ samapadyata..
devī ca paramodvignā praskhalaṃtī padepade.. 25.8 ..
1.4.d:
विहाय सगणो देवः कैलासं समपद्यत..
देवी च परमोद्विग्ना प्रस्खलंती पदेपदे.. 25.8 ..
1.4.m: leaving [her] behind, the god went with his attendants to Kailāsa. / And the goddess, extremely distressed, stumbling at every step,

1.4.s:
jīvitaṃ svaṃ viniṃdaṃtī babhrāmetastataścasā..
himādrirapi sve śrṛṃge rudatīṃ pṛṣṭavānratim.. 25.9 ..
1.4.d:
जीवितं स्वं विनिंदंती बभ्रामेतस्ततश्चसा..
हिमाद्रिरपि स्वे श्रृंगे रुदतीं पृष्टवान्रतिम्.. 25.9 ..
1.4.m: censuring her own life, wandered here and there. / The Snow-Mountain too questioned Rati, who was weeping on his peak:

1.4.s:
kāsi kasyāsi kalyāṇi kimarthaṃ cāpi rodiṣi..
pṛṣṭā sā ca ratiḥ sarvaṃ yathāvṛttaṃ nyavedayat.. 25.10 ..
1.4.d:
कासि कस्यासि कल्याणि किमर्थं चापि रोदिषि..
पृष्टा सा च रतिः सर्वं यथावृत्तं न्यवेदयत्.. 25.10 ..
1.4.m: 'Who are you? Whose are you, auspicious one? And for what reason do you weep?' / Thus questioned, Rati related everything as it had happened.

1.4.s:
nivedite tathā ratyā śailaḥ saṃbhrāṃtamānasaḥ..
prāpya svāṃ tanayāṃ pāṇāvādāyāgātsvakaṃ puram.. 25.11 ..
1.4.d:
निवेदिते तथा रत्या शैलः संभ्रांतमानसः..
प्राप्य स्वां तनयां पाणावादायागात्स्वकं पुरम्.. 25.11 ..
1.4.m: When it was thus related by Rati, the Mountain, his mind agitated, / reached his daughter, took her by the hand, and went to his own city.

1.4.s:
sā tatra pitarau prāha sakhīnāṃ vadanena ca..
durbhagena śarīreṇa kimanena hi kāraṇam.. 25.12 ..
1.4.d:
सा तत्र पितरौ प्राह सखीनां वदनेन च..
दुर्भगेन शरीरेण किमनेन हि कारणम्.. 25.12 ..
1.4.m: There she spoke to her parents through the mouth of her female companions: / 'Indeed, what purpose is there with this unfortunate body?

1.4.s:
dehavāsaṃ parityakṣye prāpsye vābhimataṃ patim..
asādhyaṃ cāpyabhīṣṭaṃ ca kathaṃ prāpyaṃ tapo vinā.. 25.13 ..
1.4.d:
देहवासं परित्यक्ष्ये प्राप्स्ये वाभिमतं पतिम्..
असाध्यं चाप्यभीष्टं च कथं प्राप्यं तपो विना.. 25.13 ..
1.4.m: I will cast off my bodily abode, or I will attain the husband I desire. / And how can what is difficult to attain and desired be gained without austerity?

1.4.s:
niyamairvividhaistasmācchoṣayiṣye kalevaram..
anujānīta māṃ tatra yadi vaḥ karuṇā mayi.. 25.14 ..
1.4.d:
नियमैर्विविधैस्तस्माच्छोषयिष्ये कलेवरम्..
अनुजानीत मां तत्र यदि वः करुणा मयि.. 25.14 ..
1.4.m: Therefore, I shall wither my body with various observances. / Permit me in that, if you have compassion for me.'

1.4.s:
śrutveti vacanaṃ mātā pitā ca prāha tāṃ śubhām..
u meti capale putri na kṣamaṃ tāvakaṃ vapuḥ.. 25.15 ..
1.4.d:
श्रुत्वेति वचनं माता पिता च प्राह तां शुभाम्..
उ मेति चपले पुत्रि न क्षमं तावकं वपुः.. 25.15 ..
1.4.m: Hearing these words, the mother and father spoke to the auspicious one: / 'U mā (Oh, do not), fickle daughter! Your body is not fit

1.4.s:
soḍhuṃ kleśātmarūpasya tapasaḥ saumyadarśane..
bhāvīnyapyani vāryāṇi vastūni ca sadaiva tu.. 25.16 ..
1.4.d:
सोढुं क्लेशात्मरूपस्य तपसः सौम्यदर्शने..
भावीन्यप्यनि वार्याणि वस्तूनि च सदैव तु.. 25.16 ..
1.4.m: to endure austerity whose nature is affliction, O gentle-faced one. / And things destined to happen are always unavoidable.

1.4.s:
bhāvinorthā bhavaṃtyeva narasyānicchatopi hi..
tasmānna tapasā te'sti bāle kiṃcitprayojanam.. 25.17 ..
1.4.d:
भाविनोर्था भवंत्येव नरस्यानिच्छतोपि हि..
तस्मान्न तपसा तेऽस्ति बाले किंचित्प्रयोजनम्.. 25.17 ..
1.4.m: Predestined events certainly happen to a man, even against his will. / Therefore, child, you have no need for austerity.'

1.4.s:
..śrīdevyuvāca..
yadidaṃ bhavato vākyaṃ na samyagiti me matiḥ..
kevalaṃ na hi daivena prāptumartho hi śakyate.. 25.18 ..
1.4.d:
..श्रीदेव्युवाच..
यदिदं भवतो वाक्यं न सम्यगिति मे मतिः..
केवलं न हि दैवेन प्राप्तुमर्थो हि शक्यते.. 25.18 ..
1.4.m: The Goddess said: / 'These words of yours are not correct, in my opinion. / An aim cannot be achieved by fate alone.

1.4.s:
tkiṃciddaivāddhaṭhātkiṃcitkiṃcideva svabhāvataḥ..
puruṣaḥ phalamāpnoti caturthaṃ nātra kāraṇam.. 25.19 ..
1.4.d:
त्किंचिद्दैवाद्धठात्किंचित्किंचिदेव स्वभावतः..
पुरुषः फलमाप्नोति चतुर्थं नात्र कारणम्.. 25.19 ..
1.4.m: A person obtains a result partly through fate, partly through effort, / and partly indeed by nature; there is no fourth cause in this.

1.4.s:
brahmaṇā cāpi brahmatvaṃ prāptaṃ kilatapobalāt..
anyairapi ca yallabdhaṃ tannasaṃkhyātumutsahe.. 25.20 ..
1.4.d:
ब्रह्मणा चापि ब्रह्मत्वं प्राप्तं किलतपोबलात्..
अन्यैरपि च यल्लब्धं तन्नसंख्यातुमुत्सहे.. 25.20 ..
1.4.m: Brahmā attained his state as Brahmā surely through the power of austerity. / And as for what was gained by others, I am unable even to count it.

1.4.s:
adhruveṇa śarīreṇa yadyabhīṣṭaṃ na sādhyate..
paścātsa śocyate maṃdaḥ patite'smiñcharīrake.. 25.21 ..
1.4.d:
अध्रुवेण शरीरेण यद्यभीष्टं न साध्यते..
पश्चात्स शोच्यते मंदः पतितेऽस्मिञ्छरीरके.. 25.21 ..
1.4.m: If one's desired aim is not accomplished with this impermanent body, / afterwards, that foolish one grieves when this body has fallen.

1.4.s:
yasya dehasya dharmo'yaṃ kvacijjāyetkvacinmriyet..
kvacidgarbhagataṃ naśyejjātamātraṃ kvacittathā.. 25.22 ..
1.4.d:
यस्य देहस्य धर्मोऽयं क्वचिज्जायेत्क्वचिन्म्रियेत्..
क्वचिद्गर्भगतं नश्येज्जातमात्रं क्वचित्तथा.. 25.22 ..
1.4.m: Such is the nature of this body: somewhere it is born, somewhere it dies; / somewhere it perishes while in the womb, and somewhere as soon as it is born.

1.4.s:
bālye ca yauvane cāpi vārdhakyepi vinaśyati..
tena caṃcaladehena ko'rthaḥ svārtho na cedbhavet.. 25.23 ..
1.4.d:
बाल्ये च यौवने चापि वार्धक्येपि विनश्यति..
तेन चंचलदेहेन कोऽर्थः स्वार्थो न चेद्भवेत्.. 25.23 ..
1.4.m: It is destroyed in childhood, in youth, and even in old age. / What purpose is there with this unstable body if one's own purpose is not fulfilled?'

1.4.s:
ityuktvā svasakhīyuktā pitṛbhyāṃ sāśru vīkṣitā..
śrṛṃgaṃ himavataḥ puṇyaṃ nānāścaryaṃ jagāma sā.. 25.24 ..
1.4.d:
इत्युक्त्वा स्वसखीयुक्ता पितृभ्यां साश्रु वीक्षिता..
श्रृंगं हिमवतः पुण्यं नानाश्चर्यं जगाम सा.. 25.24 ..
1.4.m: Having said this, accompanied by her female companions and watched with tears by her parents, / she went to the holy peak of the Himālaya, full of various wonders.

1.4.s:
tatrāṃ barāṇi saṃtyajya bhūṣaṇāni ca śailajā..
saṃvītā valkalairdivyaistapo'tapyata saṃyatā.. 25.25 ..
1.4.d:
तत्रां बराणि संत्यज्य भूषणानि च शैलजा..
संवीता वल्कलैर्दिव्यैस्तपोऽतप्यत संयता.. 25.25 ..
1.4.m: There, casting off her garments and ornaments, the Mountain-born one, / clothed in divine bark-garments, self-restrained, performed austerity.

1.4.s:
īśvaraṃ hṛdi saṃsthāpya praṇavābhyasanādṛtā..
munīnāmapya bhūnmānyā tadānīṃ pārtha pārvatī.. 25.26 ..
1.4.d:
ईश्वरं हृदि संस्थाप्य प्रणवाभ्यसनादृता..
मुनीनामप्य भून्मान्या तदानीं पार्थ पार्वती.. 25.26 ..
1.4.m: Fixing Īśvara in her heart, devoted to the practice of the Praṇava, / Pārvatī was then venerable even to the sages, O Pārtha.

1.4.s:
trisnātā pāṭalāpatrabhakṣakābhūcchataṃ samāḥ..
śaṃta ca bilvapatreṇa śīrṇona kṛtabhojanā.. 25.27 ..
1.4.d:
त्रिस्नाता पाटलापत्रभक्षकाभूच्छतं समाः..
शंत च बिल्वपत्रेण शीर्णोन कृतभोजना.. 25.27 ..
1.4.m: Bathing thrice a day, she ate only trumpet-flower leaves for a hundred years; / and she took her food for a hundred [years] on dry bilva leaves.

1.4.s:
jalabhakṣā śataṃ cābhūcchataṃ vai vāyubhojanā..
tato niyamamādāya pādāṃguṣṭhasthitābhavat.. 25.28 ..
1.4.d:
जलभक्षा शतं चाभूच्छतं वै वायुभोजना..
ततो नियममादाय पादांगुष्ठस्थिताभवत्.. 25.28 ..
1.4.m: For a hundred years she consumed only water, and for a hundred she lived on air alone. / Then, taking up an observance, she stood on the tip of her big toe.

1.4.s:
nirāhārā tatastāpaṃ prāpustattapaso janāḥ..
tato jagatsamālokya tadīyatapasorjitam.. 25.29 ..
1.4.d:
निराहारा ततस्तापं प्रापुस्तत्तपसो जनाः..
ततो जगत्समालोक्य तदीयतपसोर्जितम्.. 25.29 ..
1.4.m: Foodless, people then felt torment from her austerity. / Then, observing the world overwhelmed by her austerity,

1.4.s:
harastatrāyayau sākṣādbrahmacārivapurddharaḥ..
vasāno valkalaṃ divyaṃ rauravājinasaṃvṛtaḥ.. 25.30 ..
1.4.d:
हरस्तत्राययौ साक्षाद्ब्रह्मचारिवपुर्द्धरः..
वसानो वल्कलं दिव्यं रौरवाजिनसंवृतः.. 25.30 ..
1.4.m: Hara came there in person, bearing the form of a celibate student, / wearing divine bark and covered with the skin of a spotted antelope,

1.4.s:
sulakṣaṇāṣāḍhadharaḥ sadvṛttaḥ prati bhānavān..
tatastaṃ pūjayāmāsustatsakhyo bahumānataḥ.. 25.31 ..
1.4.d:
सुलक्षणाषाढधरः सद्वृत्तः प्रति भानवान्..
ततस्तं पूजयामासुस्तत्सख्यो बहुमानतः.. 25.31 ..
1.4.m: carrying an auspicious staff of āṣāḍha wood, well-behaved, radiant. / Then her female companions honoured him with great respect.

1.4.s:
vaktumicchuḥ śailaputrīṃ sakhībhiriti coditaḥ..
brahmanniyaṃ mahābhāgā gṛhītaniyamā śubhā.. 25.32 ..
1.4.d:
वक्तुमिच्छुः शैलपुत्रीं सखीभिरिति चोदितः..
ब्रह्मन्नियं महाभागा गृहीतनियमा शुभा.. 25.32 ..
1.4.m: Desiring to speak to the daughter of the Mountain, he was addressed by the companions thus: / 'O brahmin, this highly fortunate, auspicious maiden has undertaken an observance.

1.4.s:
muhūrtapaṃcamātreṇa niyamo'syāḥ samāpyate..
tatpratīkṣasva taṃ kālaṃ paścādasmatsakhīsamam.. 25.33 ..
1.4.d:
मुहूर्तपंचमात्रेण नियमोऽस्याः समाप्यते..
