मंदिरे हर्षजनने कलधौतमये शुभे.. 27.24 ..
1.4.m:
Thus the origin of Gaṇeśa.
Then, on one occasion, the Lord with Umā on Mandara,
in a delightful and auspicious mansion made of gold,

1.4.s:
prakīrṇakusumāmodamahālikulakūjite..
kiṃnarodgītasaṃgīta pratiśabditamadhyake.. 27.25 ..
1.4.d:
प्रकीर्णकुसुमामोदमहालिकुलकूजिते..
किंनरोद्गीतसंगीत प्रतिशब्दितमध्यके.. 27.25 ..
1.4.m:
resounding with the humming of swarms of large bees drawn by the fragrance of scattered flowers,
its interior echoing with the music sung by Kinnaras,

1.4.s:
krīḍāmayūrairhasaiśca śrutaiścaivābhinādite..
mauktikairvividha ratnairvinirmitagavākṣake.. 27.26 ..
1.4.d:
क्रीडामयूरैर्हसैश्च श्रुतैश्चैवाभिनादिते..
मौक्तिकैर्विविध रत्नैर्विनिर्मितगवाक्षके.. 27.26 ..
1.4.m:
echoing with pet peacocks, swans, and parrots,
with windows fashioned from pearls and various jewels—

1.4.s:
tatra puṇyakathābhiśca krīḍato rubhayostayoḥ..
prādurabhūnmahāñchabdaḥ pūritāṃbaragocaraḥ.. 27.27 ..
1.4.d:
तत्र पुण्यकथाभिश्च क्रीडतो रुभयोस्तयोः..
प्रादुरभून्महाञ्छब्दः पूरितांबरगोचरः.. 27.27 ..
1.4.m:
while the two were amusing themselves there with sacred tales,
a great sound arose that filled the realm of the sky.

1.4.s:
taṃ śrutvā kautukāddevī kimetaditi śaṃkaram..
paryapṛcchacchubhatanūrharaṃ vismayapūrvakam.. 27.28 ..
1.4.d:
तं श्रुत्वा कौतुकाद्देवी किमेतदिति शंकरम्..
पर्यपृच्छच्छुभतनूर्हरं विस्मयपूर्वकम्.. 27.28 ..
1.4.m:
Hearing it, the goddess of lovely form out of curiosity and with wonder
asked Śaṃkara, Hara: "What is this?"

1.4.s:
tāmāha devīṃ giriśo dṛṣṭapūrvāstu te tvayā..
ete gaṇā me krīḍaṃti śaile'smiṃstvatpriyāḥ śubhe.. 27.29 ..
1.4.d:
तामाह देवीं गिरिशो दृष्टपूर्वास्तु ते त्वया..
एते गणा मे क्रीडंति शैलेऽस्मिंस्त्वत्प्रियाः शुभे.. 27.29 ..
1.4.m:
The mountain-dweller said to the goddess: "They have been seen by you before;
these are my gaṇas, dear to you, sporting on this mountain, O auspicious lady.

1.4.s:
tapasā brahmacaryeṇa kleśena kṣetrasādhanaiḥ..
yairahaṃ toṣitaḥ pṛthvyāṃ ta ete manujottamāḥ.. 27.30 ..
1.4.d:
तपसा ब्रह्मचर्येण क्लेशेन क्षेत्रसाधनैः..
यैरहं तोषितः पृथ्व्यां त एते मनुजोत्तमाः.. 27.30 ..
1.4.m:
Through austerity, celibacy, mortification, and practices at sacred fields,
they satisfied me on earth; these are the best of men.

1.4.s:
matsamīpamanuprāptā mama lokaṃ varānane..
carācarasya jagataḥ sṛṣṭisaṃhāraṇakṣamāḥ.. 27.31 ..
1.4.d:
मत्समीपमनुप्राप्ता मम लोकं वरानने..
चराचरस्य जगतः सृष्टिसंहारणक्षमाः.. 27.31 ..
1.4.m: They have attained my presence and my world, O fair-faced one; / they are capable of creating and destroying the universe of moving and unmoving beings.

1.4.s:
vinaitānnaiva me prītirnaibhirvirahito rame..
ete ahamahaṃ caite tānetānpasya pārvati.. 27.32 ..
1.4.d:
विनैतान्नैव मे प्रीतिर्नैभिर्विरहितो रमे..
एते अहमहं चैते तानेतान्पस्य पार्वति.. 27.32 ..
1.4.m: Without them I have no pleasure at all, nor do I rejoice bereft of them. / These are I, and I am these; behold each of them, O Pārvatī.

1.4.s:
ityuktā vismitā devī dadṛśe tāngavākṣake..
sthitā padmapalāśākṣī mahādevena bhāṣitā.. 27.33 ..
1.4.d:
इत्युक्ता विस्मिता देवी ददृशे तान्गवाक्षके..
स्थिता पद्मपलाशाक्षी महादेवेन भाषिता.. 27.33 ..
1.4.m: Thus addressed, the astonished goddess looked at them from the window; / standing there, the lotus-petal-eyed lady was spoken to by Mahādeva.

1.4.s:
kecitkṛśā hrasvadīrghāḥ kecitsthūlamahodarāḥ..
vyāghrebhameṣājamukhā nānāprāṇimahāmukhāḥ.. 27.34 ..
1.4.d:
केचित्कृशा ह्रस्वदीर्घाः केचित्स्थूलमहोदराः..
व्याघ्रेभमेषाजमुखा नानाप्राणिमहामुखाः.. 27.34 ..
1.4.m: Some were lean, short, or tall; some were fat and big-bellied; / with faces of tigers, elephants, rams, and goats, having the huge faces of various creatures.

1.4.s:
vyāghracarmaparīdhānā nagnā jvālāmukhāḥ pare..
gokarṇā gajakarṇāśca bahupādamukhekṣaṇāḥ.. 27.35 ..
1.4.d:
व्याघ्रचर्मपरीधाना नग्ना ज्वालामुखाः परे..
गोकर्णा गजकर्णाश्च बहुपादमुखेक्षणाः.. 27.35 ..
1.4.m: Dressed in tiger skins, others were naked, with flaming faces; / cow-eared and elephant-eared, with many feet, faces, and eyes.

1.4.s:
vicitravāhanāścaiva nānāyudhadharāstathā..
gītavāditratattvajñāḥ sattvagītarasapriyāḥ.. 27.36 ..
1.4.d:
विचित्रवाहनाश्चैव नानायुधधरास्तथा..
गीतवादित्रतत्त्वज्ञाः सत्त्वगीतरसप्रियाः.. 27.36 ..
1.4.m: Having diverse mounts, and bearing various weapons, / knowing the true nature of singing and musical instruments, delighting in the essence of noble songs.

1.4.s: tāndṛṣṭvā pārvatī prāha katisaṃkhyābhidhāstvamī.. 27.37 ..
1.4.d: तान्दृष्ट्वा पार्वती प्राह कतिसंख्याभिधास्त्वमी.. 27.37 ..
1.4.m: Seeing them, Pārvatī said: “How many are they in number and name?”

1.4.s:
..śrīśaṃkara uvāca..
asaṃkhye yāstvamī devī asaṃkhyeyābhidhāstathā..
jagadāpūritaṃ sarvametairbhīmairmahābalaiḥ.. 27.38 ..
1.4.d:
..श्रीशंकर उवाच..
असंख्ये यास्त्वमी देवी असंख्येयाभिधास्तथा..
जगदापूरितं सर्वमेतैर्भीमैर्महाबलैः.. 27.38 ..
1.4.m: Śrī Śaṃkara said: / “Countless are they, O goddess, and countless are their names; / the entire universe is filled by these terrible ones of great strength.

1.4.s:
siddhakṣetreṣu rathyāsu jīrṇodyāneṣu veśmasu..
dānavānāṃ śarīreṣu bāleṣūnmattakeṣu ca.. 27.39 ..
1.4.d:
सिद्धक्षेत्रेषु रथ्यासु जीर्णोद्यानेषु वेश्मसु..
दानवानां शरीरेषु बालेषून्मत्तकेषु च.. 27.39 ..
1.4.m: In sacred fields of perfection, in roads, in ruined gardens, and in houses, / in the bodies of Dānavas, in children, and in madmen,

1.4.s:
ete viśati muditā nānāhāravihāriṇaḥ..
ūṣmapāḥ phenapāścaiva dhūmrapā madhupāyinaḥ..
madāhārāḥ sarvabhakṣyāstathānye cāpyabhojanāḥ.. 27.40 ..
1.4.d:
एते विशति मुदिता नानाहारविहारिणः..
ऊष्मपाः फेनपाश्चैव धूम्रपा मधुपायिनः..
मदाहाराः सर्वभक्ष्यास्तथान्ये चाप्यभोजनाः.. 27.40 ..
1.4.m: these enter, joyous, sporting with various foods: / some drinking steam, some drinking foam, some drinking smoke, some drinking wine, / feeding on intoxicants, eaters of everything, and others without food.

1.4.s:
gītanṛtyopahārāśca nānāvādyaravapriyāḥ..
anaṃtatvādamīṣāṃ ca vaktuṃ śakyā na vai guṇāḥ.. 27.41 ..
1.4.d:
गीतनृत्योपहाराश्च नानावाद्यरवप्रियाः..
अनंतत्वादमीषां च वक्तुं शक्या न वै गुणाः.. 27.41 ..
1.4.m: Bearing offerings of song and dance, loving the sounds of various instruments; / and because of their endlessness, their qualities cannot indeed be told.”

1.4.s:
..śrīdevyuvāca..
manaḥśilena kalkena ya eṣa cchuritānanaḥ..
tejasā bhāskarākāro rūpeṇa sadṛśastava.. 27.42 ..
1.4.d:
..श्रीदेव्युवाच..
मनःशिलेन कल्केन य एष च्छुरिताननः..
तेजसा भास्कराकारो रूपेण सदृशस्तव.. 27.42 ..
1.4.m: The goddess said: / “He whose face is smeared with the paste of realgar, / having the form of the sun in radiance, resembling your appearance,

1.4.s:
ākarṇyākarṇya te deva gaṇairgītānmahāguṇān..
muhurnṛtyati hāsyaṃ ca vidadhāti muhurmuhuḥ.. 27.43 ..
1.4.d:
आकर्ण्याकर्ण्य ते देव गणैर्गीतान्महागुणान्..
मुहुर्नृत्यति हास्यं च विदधाति मुहुर्मुहुः.. 27.43 ..
1.4.m: hearing repeatedly your great qualities sung by the attendants, O Lord, / dances again and again, and bursts into laughter repeatedly;

1.4.s:
sadāśivaśivetyevaṃ vihvalo vakti yo muhuḥ..
dhanyo'mīdṛśī yasya bhaktistvayi maheśvare.. 27.44 ..
1.4.d:
सदाशिवशिवेत्येवं विह्वलो वक्ति यो मुहुः..
धन्योऽमीदृशी यस्य भक्तिस्त्वयि महेश्वरे.. 27.44 ..
1.4.m: who, overcome, says over and over, ‘Sadāśiva! Śiva!’ / Fortunate is he whose devotion toward you, Maheśvara, is like this!

1.4.s:
enaṃ vijñātumicchāmi kiṃnāmāsau gaṇastava..
..śrīśaṃkara uvāca..
sa eṣa vīraka devī sadā medrisute priyaḥ.. 27.45 ..
1.4.d:
एनं विज्ञातुमिच्छामि किंनामासौ गणस्तव..
..श्रीशंकर उवाच..
स एष वीरक देवी सदा मेद्रिसुते प्रियः.. 27.45 ..
1.4.m: I wish to know him. What is the name of this attendant of yours?” / Śrī Śaṃkara said: / “He is Vīraka, O goddess, ever dear to me, O daughter of the mountain.

1.4.s:
nānāścaryaguṇādhāraḥ pratīhāro matoṃ'bike..
..devyuvāca..
īdṛśasya sutasyāpi mamo'kaṃṭhā purāṃtaka.. 27.46 ..
1.4.d:
नानाश्चर्यगुणाधारः प्रतीहारो मतोंऽबिके..
..देव्युवाच..
ईदृशस्य सुतस्यापि ममोऽकंठा पुरांतक.. 27.46 ..
1.4.m: The receptacle of various wondrous qualities, he is considered my doorkeeper, O Ambikā.” / The goddess said: / “I have a longing for such a son too, O Destroyer of the Cities.

1.4.s:
kadāhamīdṛśaṃ putraṃ lapsyāmyānaṃdadāyakam..
..śarva uvāca..
eṣa eva sutastestu yāvadīdṛkparo bhavet.. 27.47 ..
1.4.d:
कदाहमीदृशं पुत्रं लप्स्याम्यानंददायकम्..
..शर्व उवाच..
एष एव सुतस्तेस्तु यावदीदृक्परो भवेत्.. 27.47 ..
1.4.m: When shall I obtain such a son who gives joy?” / Śarva said: / “Let him indeed be your son, until another such one is born.”

1.4.s:
ityuktā vijayāṃ prāha śīghramānaya vīrakam..
vijayā ca tato gatvā vīrakaṃ vākyamabravīt.. 27.48 ..
1.4.d:
इत्युक्ता विजयां प्राह शीघ्रमानय वीरकम्..
विजया च ततो गत्वा वीरकं वाक्यमब्रवीत्.. 27.48 ..
1.4.m: Thus addressed, she said to Vijayā: “Bring Vīraka quickly.” / And Vijayā, going then, spoke these words to Vīraka:

1.4.s:
ehi vīraka te devī girijā toṣitā śubhā..
tvamamāhvayati sā devī bhavasyānumate svayam.. 27.49 ..
1.4.d:
एहि वीरक ते देवी गिरिजा तोषिता शुभा..
त्वममाह्वयति सा देवी भवस्यानुमते स्वयम्.. 27.49 ..
1.4.m: “Come, Vīraka; the auspicious goddess Girijā is pleased with you. / With the consent of Bhava, that goddess is calling you herself.”

1.4.s:
ityuktaḥ saṃbhramayuto mukhaṃ saṃmārjya pāṇinā..
devyāḥ samīpamāgacchajjayayā'nugataḥ śanaiḥ.. 27.50 ..
1.4.d:
इत्युक्तः संभ्रमयुतो मुखं संमार्ज्य पाणिना..
देव्याः समीपमागच्छज्जययाऽनुगतः शनैः.. 27.50 ..
1.4.m: Thus spoken to, filled with agitation, wiping his face with his hand, / he approached the goddess, followed slowly by Jayā.

1.4.s:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā girijā prāha girāmadhuravarṇayā..
ehyehi putra dattastvaṃ bhavena mama putrakaḥ.. 27.51 ..
1.4.d:
तं दृष्ट्वा गिरिजा प्राह गिरामधुरवर्णया..
एह्येहि पुत्र दत्तस्त्वं भवेन मम पुत्रकः.. 27.51 ..
1.4.m: Seeing him, Girijā said with words of sweet syllables: / “Come, come, my son; you have been given to me as a son by Bhava.

1.4.s:
ityukto daṃḍavaddevīṃ praṇamyāvasthitaḥ puraḥ..
mātā tatastamāliṃgya kṛtvotsaṃge ca vīrakam.. 27.52 ..
1.4.d:
इत्युक्तो दंडवद्देवीं प्रणम्यावस्थितः पुरः..
माता ततस्तमालिंग्य कृत्वोत्संगे च वीरकम्.. 27.52 ..
1.4.m: Thus addressed, he bowed down like a staff before the goddess and stood before her. / Then his mother embraced him, placed Vīraka on her lap,

1.4.s:
cucuṃba ca kapole taṃ gātrāṇi ca pramārjayat..
bhūṣayāmāsa divyaistaṃ svayaṃ nānāvibhūṣaṇaiḥ.. 27.53 ..
1.4.d:
चुचुंब च कपोले तं गात्राणि च प्रमार्जयत्..
भूषयामास दिव्यैस्तं स्वयं नानाविभूषणैः.. 27.53 ..
1.4.m: and kissed him on the cheek, and wiped his limbs; / she adorned him herself with various divine ornaments.

1.4.s:
evaṃ saṃkalpya taṃ putraṃ lālayitvā umāciram..
uvāca putra krīḍeti gaccha sārdhaṃ gaṇairiti.. 27.54 ..
1.4.d:
एवं संकल्प्य तं पुत्रं लालयित्वा उमाचिरम्..
उवाच पुत्र क्रीडेति गच्छ सार्धं गणैरिति.. 27.54 ..
1.4.m: Having thus accepted him as her son, Umā fondled him for a long time, / and said: “Go and play, my son, along with the attendants.”

1.4.s:
tataścikrīḍa madhye sa gaṇānāṃ pārvatīsutaḥ..
muhurmuhuḥ svamanasi stuvanbhaktiṃ sa śāṃkarīm.. 27.55 ..
1.4.d:
ततश्चिक्रीड मध्ये स गणानां पार्वतीसुतः..
मुहुर्मुहुः स्वमनसि स्तुवन्भक्तिं स शांकरीम्.. 27.55 ..
1.4.m: Then that son of Pārvatī played in the midst of the attendants, / praising repeatedly in his mind devotion to Śaṃkara:

1.4.s:
praṇamya sarvabhūtāni prārthayāmyasmi duṣkaram..
bhaktyā bhajadhvamīśānaṃ yasyā bhakteridaṃ phalam.. 27.56 ..
1.4.d:
प्रणम्य सर्वभूतानि प्रार्थयाम्यस्मि दुष्करम्..
भक्त्या भजध्वमीशानं यस्या भक्तेरिदं फलम्.. 27.56 ..
1.4.m: “Bowing down to all beings, I make this difficult prayer: / worship Īśāna with devotion, for of that devotion this is the fruit!”

1.4.s:
krīḍituṃ vīrake yāte tato devī ca pārvatī..
nānākathābhiscikrīḍa punareva jaṭābhṛtā.. 27.57 ..
1.4.d:
क्रीडितुं वीरके याते ततो देवी च पार्वती..
नानाकथाभिस्चिक्रीड पुनरेव जटाभृता.. 27.57 ..
1.4.m: When Vīraka had gone to play, then the goddess Pārvatī / played again with the matted-haired Lord with various conversations.

1.4.s:
tato girisutākaṇṭhe kṣiptabāhurmaheśvaraḥ..
tapasastu viśeṣārthaṃ narma devīṃ kilābravīt.. 27.58 ..
1.4.d:
ततो गिरिसुताकण्ठे क्षिप्तबाहुर्महेश्वरः..
तपसस्तु विशेषार्थं नर्म देवीं किलाब्रवीत्.. 27.58 ..
1.4.m: Then Maheśvara, having thrown his arm around the neck of the mountain's daughter, / spoke jesting words to the goddess, indeed for the special purpose of her austerity:

1.4.s:
sa hi gauratanuḥ śarvo viśeṣācchaśiśobhitaḥ..
raṃjitā ca vibhāvaryā devī nīlotpalacchaviḥ.. 27.59 ..
1.4.d:
स हि गौरतनुः शर्वो विशेषाच्छशिशोभितः..
रंजिता च विभावर्या देवी नीलोत्पलच्छविः.. 27.59 ..
1.4.m: For Śarva was fair of body, especially adorned with the moon; / and the goddess, tinted like the night, had the luster of a blue lotus.

1.4.s:
..śarva uvāca..
śarīre mama tanvaṃgī site bhāsyasitadyutiḥ..
bhujaṃgīvāsitā śubhre saṃśliṣṭā candane tarau.. 27.60 ..
1.4.d:
..शर्व उवाच..
शरीरे मम तन्वंगी सिते भास्यसितद्युतिः..
भुजंगीवासिता शुभ्रे संश्लिष्टा चन्दने तरौ.. 27.60 ..
1.4.m: Śarva said: / “O slender-limbed lady, you of dark radiance shine upon my white body / like a dark female snake clinging to a white sandalwood tree,

1.4.s:
caṃdrajyotsnābhisaṃpṛktā tāmasī rajanī yathā..
rajanī vā site pakṣe dṛṣṭidoṣaṃ dadāsi me.. 27.61 ..
1.4.d:
चंद्रज्योत्स्नाभिसंपृक्ता तामसी रजनी यथा..
रजनी वा सिते पक्षे दृष्टिदोषं ददासि मे.. 27.61 ..
1.4.m: or like a dark night mixed with moonlight; / like a night during the bright fortnight, you offend my sight!”

1.4.s:
ityuktā girijā tena kaṇṭhaṃ śarvādvimucya sā..
uvāca koparaktākṣī bhṛkuṭīvikṛtānanā.. 27.62 ..
1.4.d:
इत्युक्ता गिरिजा तेन कण्ठं शर्वाद्विमुच्य सा..
उवाच कोपरक्ताक्षी भृकुटीविकृतानना.. 27.62 ..
1.4.m: Thus addressed by him, Girijā, releasing her neck from Śarva, / with eyes red with anger and face distorted with a frown, said:

1.4.s:
svakṛtena janaḥ sarvo janena paribhūyate..
avaśyamarthī prāpnoti khaṇḍanāṃ śaśikhaṃḍabhṛt.. 27.63 ..
1.4.d:
स्वकृतेन जनः सर्वो जनेन परिभूयते..
अवश्यमर्थी प्राप्नोति खण्डनां शशिखंडभृत्.. 27.63 ..
1.4.m: “Every person is humiliated by a person according to their own doing; / an applicant inevitably receives rejection, O Bearer of the Crescent Moon!

1.4.s:
tapobhirdīptacaritairyattvāṃ prārthitavatyaham..
tasya me niyamasyaivamavamānaḥ padepade.. 27.64 ..
1.4.d:
तपोभिर्दीप्तचरितैर्यत्त्वां प्रार्थितवत्यहम्..
तस्य मे नियमस्यैवमवमानः पदेपदे.. 27.64 ..
1.4.m: In that I prayed for you through austerities of blazing deeds, / to that vow of mine, there is this insult at every step!

1.4.s:
naivāhaṃ kuṭilā śarva viṣamā na ca dhūrjaṭe..
svadoṣaistvaṃ gataḥ kṣāṃtiṃ tathā doṣākaraśriyaḥ.. 27.65 ..
1.4.d:
नैवाहं कुटिला शर्व विषमा न च धूर्जटे..
स्वदोषैस्त्वं गतः क्षांतिं तथा दोषाकरश्रियः.. 27.65 ..
1.4.m: I am not crooked, O Śarva, nor am I harsh, O Dhūrjaṭi; / by your own faults have you reached patience, and thus the splendors of the moon.

1.4.s:
nāhaṃ muṣṇāmi nayane netrahaṃtā bhavānbhava..
bhagastatte vijānāti tathaivedaṃ jagattrayamā.. 27.66 ..
1.4.d:
नाहं मुष्णामि नयने नेत्रहंता भवान्भव..
भगस्तत्ते विजानाति तथैवेदं जगत्त्रयमा.. 27.66 ..
1.4.m: I do not steal eyes; you, Bhava, are the destroyer of eyes; / Bhaga knows that of yours, and so do these three worlds!

1.4.s:
mūrdhni śūlaṃ janayase svairdoṣairmāmadikṣipan..
yattvaṃ māmāha kṛṣṇeti mahākālo'si viśrutaḥ.. 27.67 ..
1.4.d:
मूर्ध्नि शूलं जनयसे स्वैर्दोषैर्मामदिक्षिपन्..
यत्त्वं मामाह कृष्णेति महाकालोऽसि विश्रुतः.. 27.67 ..
1.4.m: You produce a pain in my head, reviling me with your own faults; / as for your calling me ‘black,’ you are renowned as Mahākāla!

1.4.s:
yāsyāmyahaṃ parityaktumātmānaṃ tapasā girim..
jīvaṃtyā nāsti me kṛtyaṃ dhūrtena paribhūtayā.. 27.68 ..
1.4.d:
यास्याम्यहं परित्यक्तुमात्मानं तपसा गिरिम्..
जीवंत्या नास्ति मे कृत्यं धूर्तेन परिभूतया.. 27.68 ..
1.4.m: I shall go to the mountain to abandon myself through austerity; / by living on, humiliated by a rogue, I have no purpose!”

1.4.s:
niśamya tasyā vacanaṃ kopatīkṣṇākṣaraṃ bhavaḥ..
uvācātha ca saṃbhrāṃto durjñeyacarito haraḥ.. 27.69 ..
1.4.d:
निशम्य तस्या वचनं कोपतीक्ष्णाक्षरं भवः..
उवाचाथ च संभ्रांतो दुर्ज्ञेयचरितो हरः.. 27.69 ..
1.4.m: Hearing her words of anger and sharp syllables, Bhava, / Hara of inscrutable conduct, was bewildered and said:

1.4.s:
na tattvajñāsi girije nāhaṃ niṃdāparastava..
cāṭūktibuddhyā kṛtavāṃsta vāhaṃ narmakīrtanam.. 27.70 ..
1.4.d:
न तत्त्वज्ञासि गिरिजे नाहं निंदापरस्तव..
चाटूक्तिबुद्ध्या कृतवांस्त वाहं नर्मकीर्तनम्.. 27.70 ..
1.4.m: “You do not know the truth, O Girijā; I was not intent on censuring you. / With a thought toward playful flattery, I spoke in jest.

1.4.s:
vikalpaḥ svacchacitteti girijaiṣā mama priyā..
prāyeṇa bhūtiliptānāmanyathā ciṃtitā hṛdi.. 27.71 ..
1.4.d:
विकल्पः स्वच्छचित्तेति गिरिजैषा मम प्रिया..
प्रायेण भूतिलिप्तानामन्यथा चिंतिता हृदि.. 27.71 ..
1.4.m: It was a doubt of pure mind, [thinking] ‘This Girijā is my beloved’; / usually, in the hearts of those smeared with ashes, thoughts are conceived differently.

1.4.s:
asmādṛśānāṃ kṛṣṇāṃgi pravartaṃte'nyathā giraḥ..
yadyevaṃ kupitā bhīru na te vakṣyāmyahaṃ punaḥ.. 27.72 ..
1.4.d:
अस्मादृशानां कृष्णांगि प्रवर्तंतेऽन्यथा गिरः..
यद्येवं कुपिता भीरु न ते वक्ष्याम्यहं पुनः.. 27.72 ..
1.4.m: From people like us, O dark-limbed one, words proceed otherwise. / If you are angry in this way, O timid one, I shall not speak to you again.

1.4.s:
narmavādī bhaviṣyāmi jahi kopaṃ sucismite..
śirasā praṇataste'haṃ racitaste mayāñjaliḥ.. 27.73 ..
1.4.d:
नर्मवादी भविष्यामि जहि कोपं सुचिस्मिते..
शिरसा प्रणतस्तेऽहं रचितस्ते मयाञ्जलिः.. 27.73 ..
1.4.m: I shall speak only in jest; give up your anger, O lady of sweet smiles! / With bowed head I bow to you; I have made a folded-hands gesture to you.

1.4.s:
dīnenāpyapamānena niṃditā nami vikriyām..
varamasmi vinamro'pi na tvaṃ devi guṇānvitā.. 27.74 ..
1.4.d:
दीनेनाप्यपमानेन निंदिता नमि विक्रियाम्..
वरमस्मि विनम्रोऽपि न त्वं देवि गुणान्विता.. 27.74 ..
1.4.m: Even with poor humiliation, censured, do not fall into distress; / it is better that I am humble; are you not endowed with virtues, O goddess?”

1.4.s:
ityanekaiścāṭuvākyaiḥ sūktairdevena bodhitā..
kopaṃ tīvraṃ na tatyāja satī marmaṇi ghaṭṭitā.. 27.75 ..
1.4.d:
इत्यनेकैश्चाटुवाक्यैः सूक्तैर्देवेन बोधिता..
कोपं तीव्रं न तत्याज सती मर्मणि घट्टिता.. 27.75 ..
1.4.m:
Addressed thus with many flattering words and sweet speeches by the god,
Satī, wounded to the quick, did not abandon her fierce anger.

1.4.s:
avaṣṭabdhāvatha kṣiptvā pādau śaṃkarapāṇinā..
viparyastālakā vegādgantumaicchata śailajā.. 27.76 ..
1.4.d:
अवष्टब्धावथ क्षिप्त्वा पादौ शंकरपाणिना..
विपर्यस्तालका वेगाद्गन्तुमैच्छत शैलजा.. 27.76 ..
1.4.m:
Then, tossing away her feet that had been seized by Śaṃkara's hand,
with disheveled curls, the Mountain's daughter swiftly sought to depart.

1.4.s:
tasyāṃ vrajantyāṃ kopena punarāha purāṃtakaḥ..
satyaṃ sarvairavayavaiḥ suteti sadṛśī pituḥ.. 27.77 ..
1.4.d:
तस्यां व्रजन्त्यां कोपेन पुनराह पुरांतकः..
सत्यं सर्वैरवयवैः सुतेति सदृशी पितुः.. 27.77 ..
1.4.m:
As she was departing in anger, the Destroyer of the [Three] Cities spoke again:
"It is true: in every limb, a daughter resembles her father.

1.4.s:
himācalasya śrṛṃgaistairmeghamālākulairmanaḥ..
tathā duravāgāhyo'sau hṛdayebhyastavāśayaḥ.. 27.78 ..
1.4.d:
हिमाचलस्य श्रृंगैस्तैर्मेघमालाकुलैर्मनः..
तथा दुरवागाह्योऽसौ हृदयेभ्यस्तवाशयः.. 27.78 ..
1.4.m:
Just like the peaks of the snowy mountain that are enveloped by rows of clouds,
so too is your mind: the intention of your heart is impassable.

1.4.s:
kāṭhinyaṃ kaṣṭamasmiṃste vanebhyo bahudhā gatam..
kuṭilatvaṃ nadībhyaste duḥsevyatvaṃ himādapi.. 27.79 ..
1.4.d:
काठिन्यं कष्टमस्मिंस्ते वनेभ्यो बहुधा गतम्..
कुटिलत्वं नदीभ्यस्ते दुःसेव्यत्वं हिमादपि.. 27.79 ..
1.4.m:
Painful hardness has passed into you in many ways from the forests;
crookedness from the rivers, and difficult accessibility even from the frost.

1.4.s:
saṃkrāṃtaṃ sarvamevaitattava devī himācalāt..
ityuktā sā punaḥ prāha giriśaṃ sailajā tadā.. 27.80 ..
1.4.d:
संक्रांतं सर्वमेवैतत्तव देवी हिमाचलात्..
इत्युक्ता सा पुनः प्राह गिरिशं सैलजा तदा.. 27.80 ..
1.4.m:
All this has passed onto you, O goddess, from the snowy mountain."
Spoken to thus, the Mountain's daughter then replied to Giriśa:

1.4.s:
kopakaṃpitadhūmrāsyā prasphuraddaśanacchadā..
mā śarvātmopamānena niṃda tvaṃ guṇino janān.. 27.81 ..
1.4.d:
कोपकंपितधूम्रास्या प्रस्फुरद्दशनच्छदा..
मा शर्वात्मोपमानेन निंद त्वं गुणिनो जनान्.. 27.81 ..
1.4.m:
Her face trembling and darkened with anger, her lips quivering:
"O Śarva, do not reproach virtuous people by your own standard!

1.4.s:
tavāpi duṣṭasaṃparkātsaṃkrāṃtaṃ sarvamevahi..
vyālebhyo'nekajihvatvaṃ bhasmanaḥ snehavandhyatā.. 27.82 ..
1.4.d:
तवापि दुष्टसंपर्कात्संक्रांतं सर्वमेवहि..
व्यालेभ्योऽनेकजिह्वत्वं भस्मनः स्नेहवन्ध्यता.. 27.82 ..
1.4.m:
Indeed, all [evil] has passed onto you as well from evil contact:
multiple tongues from serpents, and absence of affection from ashes;

1.4.s:
hṛtkāluṣyaṃ śaśāṃkātte durbodhatvaṃ vṛṣādapi..
athavā bahunoktena alaṃ vācā śrameṇa me.. 27.83 ..
1.4.d:
हृत्कालुष्यं शशांकात्ते दुर्बोधत्वं वृषादपि..
अथवा बहुनोक्तेन अलं वाचा श्रमेण मे.. 27.83 ..
1.4.m:
turbidity of heart from the moon, and dullness of wit even from the bull.
Or rather, what is the use of saying much? Enough with the labor of my words!

1.4.s:
śmaśānavāsa āsīstvaṃ nagnatvānna tava trapā..
nirghṛṇatvaṃ kapālitvādevaṃ kaḥ śaknuyāttavaṃ.. 27.84 ..
iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśī tisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ prathame māheśvarakhaṇḍe kaumārikākhaṇḍe kumāreśvaramāhātmye pārvatīprakopavarṇanaṃnāma saptaviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ.. 27 .. cha ..
1.4.d:
श्मशानवास आसीस्त्वं नग्नत्वान्न तव त्रपा..
निर्घृणत्वं कपालित्वादेवं कः शक्नुयात्तवं.. 27.84 ..
इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशी तिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां प्रथमे माहेश्वरखण्डे कौमारिकाखण्डे कुमारेश्वरमाहात्म्ये पार्वतीप्रकोपवर्णनंनाम सप्तविंशोऽध्यायः.. 27 .. छ ..

1.4.s:
..nārada uvāca..
vrajaṃtī girijā'paśyatsakhīṃ māturmahāprabhām..
kusumāmodinīṃnāma tasya śailasya devatām.. 28.1 ..
1.4.d:
..नारद उवाच..
व्रजंती गिरिजाऽपश्यत्सखीं मातुर्महाप्रभाम्..
कुसुमामोदिनींनाम तस्य शैलस्य देवताम्.. 28.1 ..
1.4.m:
Nārada said:
As she was going, Girijā saw a radiant companion of her mother,
named Kusumāmodinī, the deity of that mountain.

1.4.s:
sāpi dṛṣṭvā girisutāṃ snehaviklavamānasā..
kvapunargacchasītyuccairāliṃgyovāca devatā.. 28.2 ..
1.4.d:
सापि दृष्ट्वा गिरिसुतां स्नेहविक्लवमानसा..
क्वपुनर्गच्छसीत्युच्चैरालिंग्योवाच देवता.. 28.2 ..
1.4.m:
She too, seeing the mountain's daughter, her mind agitated by affection,
embraced her and said aloud, "Where are you going again?"

1.4.s:
sā cāsyai sarvamācakhyau śaṃkarātkopakāraṇam..
punaścovāca girijā devatāṃ mātṛsaṃmatām.. 28.3 ..
1.4.d:
सा चास्यै सर्वमाचख्यौ शंकरात्कोपकारणम्..
पुनश्चोवाच गिरिजा देवतां मातृसंमताम्.. 28.3 ..
1.4.m:
And she related to her everything, the reason for her anger at Śaṃkara;
and Girijā spoke again to the deity honored by her mother:

1.4.s:
nityaṃ śailādhirājasya devatā tvamaniṃdite..
sarvaṃ ca sannidhānaṃ ca mayi cātīva vatsalā.. 28.4 ..
1.4.d:
नित्यं शैलाधिराजस्य देवता त्वमनिंदिते..
सर्वं च सन्निधानं च मयि चातीव वत्सला.. 28.4 ..
1.4.m:
"You are constantly the deity of the king of mountains, O blameless one;
you are everywhere present, and exceedingly affectionate toward me.

1.4.s:
tadahaṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi yadvidheyaṃ tavādhunā..
athānya strīpraveśe tu samīpe tu pinākinaḥ.. 28.5 ..
1.4.d:
तदहं संप्रवक्ष्यामि यद्विधेयं तवाधुना..
अथान्य स्त्रीप्रवेशे तु समीपे तु पिनाकिनः.. 28.5 ..
1.4.m:
Therefore, I shall tell you what you must do now:
if another woman should enter into the presence of Pinākin,

1.4.s:
tvayākhyeyaṃ mama śube yuktaṃ paścātkaromyaham..
tathetyukte tayā devyā yayau devī giriṃ prati.. 28.6 ..
1.4.d:
त्वयाख्येयं मम शुबे युक्तं पश्चात्करोम्यहम्..
तथेत्युक्ते तया देव्या ययौ देवी गिरिं प्रति.. 28.6 ..
1.4.m:
you must inform me, O auspicious one; I shall do what is fitting afterwards."
When she said, "So be it," the goddess departed toward the mountain.

1.4.s:
ramye tatra mahāśṛṃge nānāścaryopaśobhite..
vibhūṣaṇādi sanyasya vṛkṣavalkaladhāriṇī.. 28.7 ..
1.4.d:
रम्ये तत्र महाशृंगे नानाश्चर्योपशोभिते..
विभूषणादि सन्यस्य वृक्षवल्कलधारिणी.. 28.7 ..
1.4.m:
There on that delightful great peak adorned with various wonders,
setting aside ornaments and the like, wearing the bark of trees,

1.4.s:
tapastepe girisutā putreṇa paripālitā..
grīṣme paṃcāgnisaṃtaptā varṣāsu ca jaloṣitā.. 28.8 ..
1.4.d:
तपस्तेपे गिरिसुता पुत्रेण परिपालिता..
ग्रीष्मे पंचाग्निसंतप्ता वर्षासु च जलोषिता.. 28.8 ..
1.4.m:
the mountain's daughter performed tapas, protected by her son,
tormented by five fires in summer, and staying in water during the rains.

1.4.s:
yathā na kācitpraviśedyoṣidatra harāṃtike..
dṛṣṭvā parāṃ striyaṃ cātra vadethā mama putraka.. 28.9 ..
1.4.d:
यथा न काचित्प्रविशेद्योषिदत्र हरांतिके..
दृष्ट्वा परां स्त्रियं चात्र वदेथा मम पुत्रक.. 28.9 ..
1.4.m:
"Take care that no woman enters here near Hara;
and having seen another woman here, tell me, my son.

1.4.s:
śīghrameva kariṣyāmi tato yuktamanaṃtaram..
evamastviti tāṃ devīṃ vīrakaḥ prāha sāṃpratam.. 28.10 ..
1.4.d:
शीघ्रमेव करिष्यामि ततो युक्तमनंतरम्..
एवमस्त्विति तां देवीं वीरकः प्राह सांप्रतम्.. 28.10 ..
1.4.m:
I shall immediately thereafter do what is fitting."
Vīraka then said to the goddess, "So be it."

1.4.s:
māturājñā suto hlāda plāvitāṃgo gatajvaraḥ..
jagāma tryakṣaṃ saṃdraṣṭuṃ praṇipatya ca mātaram.. 28.11 ..
1.4.d:
मातुराज्ञा सुतो ह्लाद प्लावितांगो गतज्वरः..
जगाम त्र्यक्षं संद्रष्टुं प्रणिपत्य च मातरम्.. 28.11 ..
1.4.m:
Having received his mother's command, his limbs flooded with joy, his anxiety gone,
the son bowed down to his mother and went to see the Three-eyed One.

1.4.s:
gajavaktraṃ tataḥ prāha praṇamya samavasthitam..
sāśrukaṃṭhaṃ prayācaṃtaṃ naya māmapi pārvati.. 28.12 ..
1.4.d:
गजवक्त्रं ततः प्राह प्रणम्य समवस्थितम्..
साश्रुकंठं प्रयाचंतं नय मामपि पार्वति.. 28.12 ..
1.4.m:
Then she spoke to the Elephant-faced One, who bowed and stood before her,
begging with a tearful throat, "Take me also, O Pārvatī!"

1.4.s:
gajavaktraṃ hi tvāṃ bāla māmivopahasiṣyati..
tadāgaccha mayā sārdhaṃ yā gatirme tavāpi sā.. 28.13 ..
1.4.d:
गजवक्त्रं हि त्वां बाल मामिवोपहसिष्यति..
तदागच्छ मया सार्धं या गतिर्मे तवापि सा.. 28.13 ..
1.4.m:
"Because of your elephant face, O child, he will surely mock you just as [he mocked] me.
Therefore, come with me; whatever my fate is, yours will be too.

1.4.s:
parābhavāddhi dhūrtānāṃ maraṇaṃ sādhu putraka..
evamuktvā samādāya himādriṃ prati sā yayau.. 28.14 ..
1.4.d:
पराभवाद्धि धूर्तानां मरणं साधु पुत्रक..
एवमुक्त्वा समादाय हिमाद्रिं प्रति सा ययौ.. 28.14 ..
1.4.m:
For death is better, my son, than humiliation by wicked ones."
Having spoken thus and taken him along, she departed toward the snowy mountain.

1.4.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ prathame māheśvarakhaṇḍe kaumārikākhaṇḍe kumāreśvaramāhātmye pārvatyastaporthaṃ gamanavarṇanaṃnāmāṣṭāviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ.. 28 .. cha ..
1.4.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां प्रथमे माहेश्वरखण्डे कौमारिकाखण्डे कुमारेश्वरमाहात्म्ये पार्वत्यस्तपोर्थं गमनवर्णनंनामाष्टाविंशोऽध्यायः.. 28 .. छ ..
1.4.m: Thus ends the twenty-eighth chapter, entitled "The Description of Pārvatī's Departure for Tapas", in the Kumāreśvaramāhātmya of the Kaumārikākhaṇḍa, in the first Māheśvarakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.

vrajaṃtī girijā'paśyatsakhīṃ māturmahāprabhām..
kusumāmodinīṃnāma tasya śailasya devatām.. 29.1 ..

..नारद उवाच..

क्वपुनर्गच्छसीत्युच्चैरालिंग्योवाच देवता.. 29.2 ..

1.4.s:

पुनश्चोवाच गिरिजा देवतां मातृसंमताम्.. 29.3 ..
1.4.m:
And she related to her everything, the reason for her anger at Śaṃkara;
and Girijā spoke again to the deity honored by her mother:

1.4.s:
nityaṃ śailādhirājasya devatā tvamaniṃdite..
sarvaṃ ca sannidhānaṃ ca mayi cātīva vatsalā.. 29.4 ..
1.4.d:
नित्यं शैलाधिराजस्य देवता त्वमनिंदिते..
सर्वं च सन्निधानं च मयि चातीव वत्सला.. 29.4 ..
1.4.m:
"You are constantly the deity of the king of mountains, O blameless one;
you are everywhere present, and exceedingly affectionate toward me.

1.4.s:
tadahaṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi yadvidheyaṃ tavādhunā..
athānya strīpraveśe tu samīpe tu pinākinaḥ.. 29.5 ..
1.4.d:
तदहं संप्रवक्ष्यामि यद्विधेयं तवाधुना..
अथान्य स्त्रीप्रवेशे तु समीपे तु पिनाकिनः.. 29.5 ..
1.4.m:
Therefore, I shall tell you what you must do now:
if another woman should enter into the presence of Pinākin,

1.4.s:
tvayākhyeyaṃ mama śubhe yuktaṃ paścātkaromyaham..
tathetyukte tayā devyā yayau devī giriṃ prati.. 29.6 ..
1.4.d:
त्वयाख्येयं मम शुभे युक्तं पश्चात्करोम्यहम्..
तथेत्युक्ते तया देव्या ययौ देवी गिरिं प्रति.. 29.6 ..
1.4.m:
you must inform me, O auspicious one; I shall do what is fitting afterwards."
When she said, "So be it," the goddess departed toward the mountain.

1.4.s:
ramye tatra mahāśṛṃge nānāścaryopaśobhite..
vibhūṣaṇādi saṃnyasya vṛkṣavalkaladhāriṇī.. 29.7 ..
1.4.d:
रम्ये तत्र महाशृंगे नानाश्चर्योपशोभिते..
विभूषणादि संन्यस्य वृक्षवल्कलधारिणी.. 29.7 ..
1.4.m:
There on that delightful great peak adorned with various wonders,
setting aside ornaments and the like, wearing the bark of trees,

1.4.s:
tapastepe girisutā putreṇa paripālitā..
grīṣme paṃcāgnisaṃtaptā varṣāsu ca jaloṣitā.. 29.8 ..
1.4.d:
तपस्तेपे गिरिसुता पुत्रेण परिपालिता..
ग्रीष्मे पंचाग्निसंतप्ता वर्षासु च जलोषिता.. 29.8 ..
1.4.m:
the mountain's daughter performed tapas, protected by her son,
tormented by five fires in summer, and staying in water during the rains.

1.4.s:
sthaṃḍilasthā ca hemaṃte nirāhārā tatāpa sā..
etasminnaṃtare daityo hyaṃdhakasya suto balī.. 29.9 ..
1.4.d:
स्थंडिलस्था च हेमंते निराहारा तताप सा..
एतस्मिन्नंतरे दैत्यो ह्यंधकस्य सुतो बली.. 29.9 ..
1.4.m:
And in winter she dwelt on bare ground, fasting and performing austerities.
In the meantime, the mighty Daitya, son of Andhaka,

1.4.s:
jñātvā gatāṃ girisutāṃ piturvairamanusmaran..
āḍirnāma bakabhrātā rahasyāṃtaraprekṣakaḥ.. 29.10 ..
1.4.d:
ज्ञात्वा गतां गिरिसुतां पितुर्वैरमनुस्मरन्..
आडिर्नाम बकभ्राता रहस्यांतरप्रेक्षकः.. 29.10 ..
1.4.m:
knowing that the mountain's daughter had left and remembering his father's enmity,
named Āḍi, brother of Baka, watching for a secret opportunity—

1.4.s:
jite kilāṃdhake daitye giriśenāmaradviṣi..
āḍiścakāra vipulaṃ tapo harajigīṣayā.. 29.11 ..
1.4.d:
जिते किलांधके दैत्ये गिरिशेनामरद्विषि..
आडिश्चकार विपुलं तपो हरजिगीषया.. 29.11 ..
1.4.m:
when indeed the Daitya Andhaka, enemy of the gods, had been defeated by Giriśa,
Āḍi performed vast tapas, desiring to conquer Hara.

1.4.s:
tamāgatyābravīdbrahmā tapasā paritoṣitaḥ..
brūhi kiṃ vāsuraśreṣṭha tapasā prāptumicchasi.. 29.12 ..
1.4.d:
तमागत्याब्रवीद्ब्रह्मा तपसा परितोषितः..
ब्रूहि किं वासुरश्रेष्ठ तपसा प्राप्तुमिच्छसि.. 29.12 ..
1.4.m:
Brahmā, delighted by his tapas, approached him and said:
"Speak, O best of asuras, what do you wish to obtain through tapas?"

1.4.s:
brahmāṇamāha daityastu nirmṛtyutvamahaṃ vṛṇe..
..brahmovāca..
na kaścicca vinā mṛtyuṃ jaṃturāsura vidyate.. 29.13 ..
1.4.d:
ब्रह्माणमाह दैत्यस्तु निर्मृत्युत्वमहं वृणे..
..ब्रह्मोवाच..
न कश्चिच्च विना मृत्युं जंतुरासुर विद्यते.. 29.13 ..
1.4.m:
The Daitya said to Brahmā, "I choose freedom from death."
Brahmā said:
"There is no creature, O asura, that is without death.

1.4.s:
yatastato'pi daityeṃdra mṛtyuḥ prāpyaḥ śarīriṇā..
ityuktastaṃ tathetyāha tuṣṭaḥ kamalasaṃbhavam.. 29.14 ..
1.4.d:
यतस्ततोऽपि दैत्येंद्र मृत्युः प्राप्यः शरीरिणा..
इत्युक्तस्तं तथेत्याह तुष्टः कमलसंभवम्.. 29.14 ..
1.4.m:
From one source or another, O lord of Daityas, death must be reached by an embodied being."
Addressed thus, he, being pleased, said to the Lotus-born One, "So be it:

1.4.s:
rūpasya parivarto me yadā syātpadmasaṃbhava..
tadā mṛtyurmama bhavedanyathā tvamaro hyaham.. 29.15 ..
1.4.d:
रूपस्य परिवर्तो मे यदा स्यात्पद्मसंभव..
तदा मृत्युर्मम भवेदन्यथा त्वमरो ह्यहम्.. 29.15 ..
1.4.m:
When there is a change in my form, O Lotus-born One,
then let my death occur; otherwise, may I be immortal."

1.4.s:
ityuktastaṃ tathetyāha tuṣṭaḥ kamalasaṃbhavaḥ..
ityukto'maratāṃ mene daityarājyasthito'suraḥ.. 29.16 ..
1.4.d:
इत्युक्तस्तं तथेत्याह तुष्टः कमलसंभवः..
इत्युक्तोऽमरतां मेने दैत्यराज्यस्थितोऽसुरः.. 29.16 ..
1.4.m:
Addressed thus, the Lotus-born One, pleased, said to him, "So be it."
Told this, the asura, established in the sovereignty of the Daityas, considered himself immortal.

1.4.s:
ājagāma sa ca sthānaṃ tadā tripuraghātinaḥ..
āgato dadṛśe taṃ ca vīrakaṃ dvāryavasthitam.. 29.17 ..
1.4.d:
आजगाम स च स्थानं तदा त्रिपुरघातिनः..
आगतो ददृशे तं च वीरकं द्वार्यवस्थितम्.. 29.17 ..
1.4.m:
He then went to the abode of the Slayer of Tripura,
and having arrived, he saw Vīraka standing at the doorway.

1.4.s:
taṃ cāsau vaṃcayitvā ca āḍiḥ sarpaśarīrabhṛt..
avārito vīrakeṇa praviveśa harāṃtikam.. 29.18 ..
1.4.d:
तं चासौ वंचयित्वा च आडिः सर्पशरीरभृत्..
अवारितो वीरकेण प्रविवेश हरांतिकम्.. 29.18 ..
1.4.m: Deceiving him, Āḍi assumed the body of a serpent / and, unobstructed by Vīraka, entered the presence of Hara.

1.4.s:
bhujaṃgarūpaṃ saṃtyajya babhūvātha mahāsuraḥ..
umārūpī chalayituṃ giriśaṃ mūḍhacetanaḥ.. 29.19 ..
1.4.d:
भुजंगरूपं संत्यज्य बभूवाथ महासुरः..
उमारूपी छलयितुं गिरिशं मूढचेतनः.. 29.19 ..
1.4.m: Then, casting off his serpent form, that great Asura, / his mind deluded, took the form of Umā to deceive Giriśa.

1.4.s:
kṛtvomāyāstato rūpamapratarkyamanoharam..
sarvāvayavasaṃpūrṇaṃ sarvābhijñānasaṃvṛtam.. 29.20 ..
1.4.d:
कृत्वोमायास्ततो रूपमप्रतर्क्यमनोहरम्..
सर्वावयवसंपूर्णं सर्वाभिज्ञानसंवृतम्.. 29.20 ..
1.4.m: Having assumed Umā's form, unimaginably beautiful, / complete in all limbs and endowed with all her characteristic marks,

1.4.s:
cakre bhagāṃtare daityo daṃtānvajropamāndṛḍhān..
tīkṣṇāgrānbuddhimohena giriśaṃ haṃtumudyataḥ.. 29.21 ..
1.4.d:
चक्रे भगांतरे दैत्यो दंतान्वज्रोपमान्दृढान्..
तीक्ष्णाग्रान्बुद्धिमोहेन गिरिशं हंतुमुद्यतः.. 29.21 ..
1.4.m: the Daitya placed within the vulva teeth firm as vajra / with sharp points, eager to kill Giriśa out of foolish delusion.

1.4.s:
kṛtvomārūpamevaṃ sa sthito daityo harāṃtike..
tāṃ dṛṣṭvā giriśastuṣuṭaḥ samāliṃgya mahāsuram.. 29.22 ..
1.4.d:
कृत्वोमारूपमेवं स स्थितो दैत्यो हरांतिके..
तां दृष्ट्वा गिरिशस्तुषुटः समालिंग्य महासुरम्.. 29.22 ..
1.4.m: Having thus assumed the form of Umā, the Daitya stood near Hara. / Seeing her, Giriśa was pleased, and embracing the great Asura,

1.4.s:
manyamāno girisutāṃ sarvai ravayavāṃtaraiḥ..
apṛcchatsādhu te bhāvo giriputrī hyakṛtrimā.. 29.23 ..
1.4.d:
मन्यमानो गिरिसुतां सर्वै रवयवांतरैः..
अपृच्छत्साधु ते भावो गिरिपुत्री ह्यकृत्रिमा.. 29.23 ..
1.4.m: believing him to be the daughter of the mountain in every limb, / he asked: “Noble is your feeling, for you are indeed the genuine daughter of the mountain,

1.4.s:
yā tvaṃ madaśayaṃ jñātvā prāpteha varavarṇini..
tvayā virahitaḥ śūnyaṃ manyosminbhuvanatraye.. 29.24 ..
1.4.d:
या त्वं मदशयं ज्ञात्वा प्राप्तेह वरवर्णिनि..
त्वया विरहितः शून्यं मन्योस्मिन्भुवनत्रये.. 29.24 ..
1.4.m: who, knowing my disposition, have come here, O fair-complexioned lady! / Deprived of you, I consider this threefold world empty.

1.4.s:
prāptā prasannā yā tvaṃ māṃ yuktamevaṃvidhaṃ tvayi..
ityukte gūhayaṃśceṣṭāmumārūpyasuro'bravīt.. 29.25 ..
1.4.d:
प्राप्ता प्रसन्ना या त्वं मां युक्तमेवंविधं त्वयि..
इत्युक्ते गूहयंश्चेष्टामुमारूप्यसुरोऽब्रवीत्.. 29.25 ..
1.4.m: That you have arrived well-pleased with me is truly worthy of you.” / When this was said, the Asura in the form of Umā, concealing his design, said:

1.4.s:
yātāsmi tapasaścartuṃ kālīvākyāttavātulam..
ratiśca tatra me nābhūttataḥ prāptā tavāṃtikam.. 29.26 ..
1.4.d:
यातास्मि तपसश्चर्तुं कालीवाक्यात्तवातुलम्..
रतिश्च तत्र मे नाभूत्ततः प्राप्ता तवांतिकम्.. 29.26 ..
1.4.m: “I went to perform matchless austerity at your words, ‘O Kālī!’ / But I found no pleasure there, and therefore I have returned to your side.”

1.4.s:
ityuktaḥ śaṃkaraḥ śaṃkāṃ kiṃcitprāpyavadhārayat..
kupitā mayi tanvaṃgī pratyakṣā ca dṛḍhavratā.. 29.27 ..
1.4.d:
इत्युक्तः शंकरः शंकां किंचित्प्राप्यवधारयत्..
कुपिता मयि तन्वंगी प्रत्यक्षा च दृढव्रता.. 29.27 ..
1.4.m: Addressed thus, Śaṃkara felt a slight doubt and reflected: / “The slender-limbed lady was angry with me, and she is openly firm in her vows.

1.4.s:
aprāptakāmā saṃprāptā kimetatsaṃśayo mama..
rahasīti viciṃtyātha abhijñānādvicārayan.. 29.28 ..
1.4.d:
अप्राप्तकामा संप्राप्ता किमेतत्संशयो मम..
रहसीति विचिंत्याथ अभिज्ञानाद्विचारयन्.. 29.28 ..
1.4.m: How has she arrived without having attained her desire? This is my doubt.” / Thus pondering in secret, he then examined her signs.

1.4.s:
nāpaśyadvāmapārśve tu tasyāṃkaṃ padmalakṣaṇam..
lomnāmāvartacaritaṃ tato devaḥ pinākadhṛk.. 29.29 ..
1.4.d:
नापश्यद्वामपार्श्वे तु तस्यांकं पद्मलक्षणम्..
लोम्नामावर्तचरितं ततो देवः पिनाकधृक्.. 29.29 ..
1.4.m: On her left side he did not see the mark of the lotus / or the whorl of hair; thereupon the god who bears the Pināka,

1.4.s:
buddhā tāṃ dānavīṃ māyāṃ kiṃcitprahasitānanaḥ..
meḍhre raudrāstramādhāya cakre daityamanoratham.. 29.30 ..
1.4.d:
बुद्धा तां दानवीं मायां किंचित्प्रहसिताननः..
मेढ्रे रौद्रास्त्रमाधाय चक्रे दैत्यमनोरथम्.. 29.30 ..
1.4.m: perceiving that demonic illusion, his face smiling slightly, / placed the Raudra weapon upon his member and fulfilled the Daitya's desire.

1.4.s:
sa rudanbhairavānrāvānavasādaṃ gato'suraḥ..
abudhyadvīrako naitadasureṃdraniṣūdanam.. 29.31 ..
1.4.d:
स रुदन्भैरवान्रावानवसादं गतोऽसुरः..
अबुध्यद्वीरको नैतदसुरेंद्रनिषूदनम्.. 29.31 ..
1.4.m: The Asura, uttering terrifying shrieks, met his destruction. / Vīraka did not realize this slaying of the lord of the Asuras.

1.4.s:
hate ca mārutenāśugāminā nagadevatā..
aparicchinnatattvārthā śailaputryāṃ nyavedayat.. 29.32 ..
1.4.d:
हते च मारुतेनाशुगामिना नगदेवता..
अपरिच्छिन्नतत्त्वार्था शैलपुत्र्यां न्यवेदयत्.. 29.32 ..
1.4.m: When he was slain, the swift-moving wind reported it to the mountain deity, / who, not understanding the true nature of the fact, reported it to the daughter of the mountain.

1.4.s:
śrutvā vāyumukhāddevī krodharaktātilocanā..
apasyadvīrakaṃ putraṃ hṛdayena vidūyatā.. 29.33 ..
1.4.d:
श्रुत्वा वायुमुखाद्देवी क्रोधरक्तातिलोचना..
अपस्यद्वीरकं पुत्रं हृदयेन विदूयता.. 29.33 ..
1.4.m: Hearing this from the mouth of the wind, the goddess, her eyes exceedingly red with rage, / looked upon her son Vīraka, her heart grieving:

1.4.s:
mātaraṃ māṃ parityajya yasmāttvaṃ snehavihvalām..
vihitāvasaraḥ strīṇāṃ śaṃkarasya rahovidhau.. 29.34 ..
1.4.d:
मातरं मां परित्यज्य यस्मात्त्वं स्नेहविह्वलाम्..
विहितावसरः स्त्रीणां शंकरस्य रहोविधौ.. 29.34 ..
1.4.m: “Because you, abandoning me, your mother, distracted with love, / gave admittance to [other] women into Śaṃkara's private quarters,

1.4.s:
tasmātte paruṣā rūkṣā jaḍā hṛdaya varjitā..
gaṇeśākṣarasadṛśā śilā mātā bhaviṣyati.. 29.35 ..
1.4.d:
तस्मात्ते परुषा रूक्षा जडा हृदय वर्जिता..
गणेशाक्षरसदृशा शिला माता भविष्यति.. 29.35 ..
1.4.m: therefore a harsh, rough, inert stone, devoid of heart, / like the letters of a gaṇeśa, shall become your mother!”

1.4.s:
evamutsṛṣṭaśāpāyā giriputryāstvanaṃtaram..
nirjagāma mukhātkrodhaḥ siṃharūpī mahābalaḥ.. 29.36 ..
1.4.d:
एवमुत्सृष्टशापाया गिरिपुत्र्यास्त्वनंतरम्..
निर्जगाम मुखात्क्रोधः सिंहरूपी महाबलः.. 29.36 ..
1.4.m: Immediately after the daughter of the mountain had uttered this curse, / from her mouth emerged wrath in the form of a lion of great strength.

1.4.s:
paścāttāpaṃ samaśritya tayā devyā visarjitaḥ..
sa tu siṃhaḥ karālāsyo mahākesarakaṃdharaḥ.. 29.37 ..
1.4.d:
पश्चात्तापं समश्रित्य तया देव्या विसर्जितः..
स तु सिंहः करालास्यो महाकेसरकंधरः.. 29.37 ..
1.4.m: Stricken with remorse, the goddess sent him away. / But that lion had a terrifying mouth and a neck with a great mane;

1.4.s:
proddhūtabalalāṃgūladaṃṣṭrotkaṭa guhāmukhaḥ..
vyāvṛtāsyo lalajjihvaḥ kṣāmakukṣiścikhādiṣuḥ.. 29.38 ..
1.4.d:
प्रोद्धूतबललांगूलदंष्ट्रोत्कट गुहामुखः..
व्यावृतास्यो ललज्जिह्वः क्षामकुक्षिश्चिखादिषुः.. 29.38 ..
1.4.m: his strong tail lashed about, his cavernous mouth was frightful with fangs; / his jaws agape, his tongue licking, his belly emaciated, he was eager to devour.

1.4.s:
tasyāsye vartituṃ devī vyavasyata satī tadā..
jñātvā manogataṃ tasyā bhagavāṃścaturānanaḥ.. 29.39 ..
1.4.d:
तस्यास्ये वर्तितुं देवी व्यवस्यत सती तदा..
ज्ञात्वा मनोगतं तस्या भगवांश्चतुराननः.. 29.39 ..
1.4.m: The faithful goddess Satī then resolved to enter his mouth. / Knowing what was in her heart, the four-faced Blessed Lord [Brahmā]

1.4.s:
ājagāmāśramapaṃda saṃpadāmāśrayaṃ tataḥ..
āgamyovāca tāṃ brahmā girijāṃ mṛṣṭayā girā.. 29.40 ..
1.4.d:
आजगामाश्रमपंद संपदामाश्रयं ततः..
आगम्योवाच तां ब्रह्मा गिरिजां मृष्टया गिरा.. 29.40 ..
1.4.m: came to the precinct of the hermitage, the resort of prosperities. / Arriving there, Brahmā spoke to Girijā with gentle words:

1.4.s:
kiṃ devī prāptukāmāsi kimalabhyaṃ dadāmi te..
tacchrutvovāca girijā gurugauravagarbhitam.. 29.41 ..
1.4.d:
किं देवी प्राप्तुकामासि किमलभ्यं ददामि ते..
तच्छ्रुत्वोवाच गिरिजा गुरुगौरवगर्भितम्.. 29.41 ..
1.4.m: “What do you wish to obtain, O goddess? What unachievable thing may I grant you?” / Hearing that, Girijā said, full of deep respect:

1.4.s:
tapasā duṣkareṇāptaḥ patitve śaṃkaro mayā..
sa māṃ śyāmalavarṇeti bahuśaḥ proktavānbhavaḥ.. 29.42 ..
1.4.d:
तपसा दुष्करेणाप्तः पतित्वे शंकरो मया..
स मां श्यामलवर्णेति बहुशः प्रोक्तवान्भवः.. 29.42 ..
1.4.m: “By arduous austerity Śaṃkara was obtained by me as a husband. / Yet Bhava has repeatedly spoken to me, calling me dark-complexioned.

1.4.s:
syāmahaṃ kāṃcanākārā vāllabhyena ca saṃyutā..
bharturbhūtapateraṃge hyekato nirviśaṃkitā.. 29.43 ..
1.4.d:
स्यामहं कांचनाकारा वाल्लभ्येन च संयुता..
भर्तुर्भूतपतेरंगे ह्येकतो निर्विशंकिता.. 29.43 ..
1.4.m: May I become golden-hued and endowed with beloved status, / without any misgiving on one side of the body of my husband, the lord of beings!”

1.4.s:
tasyāstadbhāṣitaṃ śrutvā provāca jalajāsanaḥ..
evaṃ bhavatu bhūyastvaṃ bharturdehārdhadhāriṇī.. 29.44 ..
1.4.d:
तस्यास्तद्भाषितं श्रुत्वा प्रोवाच जलजासनः..
एवं भवतु भूयस्त्वं भर्तुर्देहार्धधारिणी.. 29.44 ..
1.4.m: Hearing these words of hers, the lotus-seated [Brahmā] said: / “So be it! You shall further bear half of your husband's body.”

1.4.s:
tatastasyāḥ śarīrāttu strī sunīlāṃbujatviṣā..
nirgatā sābhavadbhīmā ghaṃṭāhastā trilocanā.. 29.45 ..
1.4.d:
ततस्तस्याः शरीरात्तु स्त्री सुनीलांबुजत्विषा..
निर्गता साभवद्भीमा घंटाहस्ता त्रिलोचना.. 29.45 ..
1.4.m: Then from her body came forth a woman with the lustre of a dark-blue lotus; / she was fierce, held a bell in her hand, and had three eyes.

1.4.s:
nānābharaṇapūrṇāṃgī pītakauśeyavāsinī..
tāmabravīttato brahmā devīṃ nīlāṃbujatviṣam.. 29.46 ..
1.4.d:
नानाभरणपूर्णांगी पीतकौशेयवासिनी..
तामब्रवीत्ततो ब्रह्मा देवीं नीलांबुजत्विषम्.. 29.46 ..
1.4.m: Her limbs were adorned with various ornaments, and she was clad in yellow silk. / Then Brahmā spoke to that goddess who had the lustre of a dark-blue lotus:

1.4.s:
asmādbhūdharajā dehasaṃparkāttvaṃ mamājñayā..
saṃprāptā kṛtakṛtyatvamekānaṃśā purākṛtiḥ.. 29.47 ..
1.4.d:
अस्माद्भूधरजा देहसंपर्कात्त्वं ममाज्ञया..
संप्राप्ता कृतकृत्यत्वमेकानंशा पुराकृतिः.. 29.47 ..
1.4.m: “From this contact with the body of the mountain-born [goddess], by my command / you have attained the fulfillment of your purpose, having your ancient form as Ekānaṃśā.

1.4.s:
ya eṣa siṃhaḥ prodbhūto devyāḥ krodhādvarānane..
sa testu vāhano devī ketau cāstu mahābalaḥ.. 29.48 ..
1.4.d:
य एष सिंहः प्रोद्भूतो देव्याः क्रोधाद्वरानने..
स तेस्तु वाहनो देवी केतौ चास्तु महाबलः.. 29.48 ..
1.4.m: This lion that has arisen from the goddess's wrath, O fair-faced one, / let him be your mount, O goddess, and let the mighty one be on your banner.

1.4.s:
gaccha viṃdhyācale tatra surakāryaṃ kariṣyati..
atra śuṃbhaniśuṃbhau ca hatvā tārakasainyapau.. 29.49 ..
1.4.d:
गच्छ विंध्याचले तत्र सुरकार्यं करिष्यति..
अत्र शुंभनिशुंभौ च हत्वा तारकसैन्यपौ.. 29.49 ..
1.4.m: Go to the Vindhya mountain; there you will accomplish the purpose of the gods, / having slain Śumbha and Niśumbha, the two generals of Tāraka's army.

1.4.s:
pāṃcālonāma yakṣo'yaṃ yakṣalakṣapadānugaḥ..
dattaste kiṃkaro devī mahāmāyāśatairyutaḥ.. 29.50 ..
1.4.d:
पांचालोनाम यक्षोऽयं यक्षलक्षपदानुगः..
दत्तस्ते किंकरो देवी महामायाशतैर्युतः.. 29.50 ..
1.4.m: This Yakṣa named Pāñcāla, who is followed by a hundred thousand Yakṣas / and possesses hundreds of great illusions, is given to you as a servant, O goddess.”

1.4.s:
ityuktā kauśikī devī tathetyāha pitāmaham..
nirgatāyāṃ ca kauśikyāṃ jātā svairāśritā guṇaiḥ.. 29.51 ..
1.4.d:
इत्युक्ता कौशिकी देवी तथेत्याह पितामहम्..
निर्गतायां च कौशिक्यां जाता स्वैराश्रिता गुणैः.. 29.51 ..
1.4.m: Thus addressed, the goddess Kauśikī said “So be it” to the Grandsire. / When Kauśikī had departed, [Umā] became endowed with her natural virtues,

1.4.s:
sarvaiḥ pūrvabhavopāttaistadā svayamupastitaiḥ..
umāpi prāptasaṃkalpā paścāttāpaparāyaṇā.. 29.52 ..
1.4.d:
सर्वैः पूर्वभवोपात्तैस्तदा स्वयमुपस्तितैः..
उमापि प्राप्तसंकल्पा पश्चात्तापपरायणा.. 29.52 ..
1.4.m: all of which had been acquired in previous births and now returned of their own accord. / Umā too, having accomplished her desire, devoted herself to remorse.

1.4.s:
muhuḥ svaṃ pariniṃdaṃtī jagāma giriśāṃtikam..
saṃprayāṃtīṃ ca tāṃ dvārī apavārya samāhitaḥ.. 29.53 ..
1.4.d:
मुहुः स्वं परिनिंदंती जगाम गिरिशांतिकम्..
संप्रयांतीं च तां द्वारी अपवार्य समाहितः.. 29.53 ..
1.4.m: Reproaching herself repeatedly, she went into the presence of Giriśa. / As she approached, Vīraka, vigilant at the doorway,

1.4.s:
rurodha vīrako devīṃ hemavetralatādharaḥ..
tāmuvāca ca kopena tiṣṭha tiṣṭha kva yāsi ca.. 29.54 ..
1.4.d:
रुरोध वीरको देवीं हेमवेत्रलताधरः..
तामुवाच च कोपेन तिष्ठ तिष्ठ क्व यासि च.. 29.54 ..
1.4.m: holding a cane of gold, stopped the goddess, / and said to her in anger: “Halt, halt! Where are you going?

1.4.s:
prayojanaṃ na te'stīha gaccha yāvanna bhartsyase..
devyā rūpadharo daityo devaṃ vaṃcayituṃ tviha.. 29.55 ..
1.4.d:
प्रयोजनं न तेऽस्तीह गच्छ यावन्न भर्त्स्यसे..
देव्या रूपधरो दैत्यो देवं वंचयितुं त्विह.. 29.55 ..
1.4.m: You have no business here. Depart before you are reproached! / A Daitya bearing the form of the goddess entered here

1.4.s:
praviṣṭo na ca dṛṣṭo'sau sa ca devena ghātitaḥ..
ghātite cāhamākṣipto nīlakaṇṭhena dhīmatā.. 29.56 ..
1.4.d:
प्रविष्टो न च दृष्टोऽसौ स च देवेन घातितः..
घातिते चाहमाक्षिप्तो नीलकण्ठेन धीमता.. 29.56 ..
1.4.m: to deceive the god, and he was not seen; but he was slain by the god. / And when he was slain, I was rebuked by the wise blue-throated god [Śiva]:

1.4.s:
kāpi strī nāpi moktavyā tvayā putreti sādaram..
tasmāttvamatra dvāristhā varṣapūgānyanekaśaḥ.. 29.57 ..
1.4.d:
कापि स्त्री नापि मोक्तव्या त्वया पुत्रेति सादरम्..
तस्मात्त्वमत्र द्वारिस्था वर्षपूगान्यनेकशः.. 29.57 ..
1.4.m: ‘No woman whatsoever is to be permitted [entrance] by you, O son!’ / Therefore, even though you stand here at the door for many multitudes of years,

1.4.s:
bhaviṣyasi na cāpyatra praveśaṃ lapsyase vraja..
ekā me praviśedatra mātā yā snehavatsalā.. 29.58 ..
1.4.d:
भविष्यसि न चाप्यत्र प्रवेशं लप्स्यसे व्रज..
एका मे प्रविशेदत्र माता या स्नेहवत्सला.. 29.58 ..
1.4.m: you shall not obtain entrance here. Go away! / Only my mother, who is tender with affection,

1.4.s:
nagādhirājatanayā pārvatī rudravallabhā..
ityuktā tu tato devī ciṃtayāmāsa cetasā.. 29.59 ..
1.4.d:
नगाधिराजतनया पार्वती रुद्रवल्लभा..
इत्युक्ता तु ततो देवी चिंतयामास चेतसा.. 29.59 ..
1.4.m: the daughter of the king of mountains, Pārvatī, beloved of Rudra, may enter here.” / Being thus addressed, the goddess then reflected in her heart:

1.4.s:
na sā nārī tu daityo'sau vāyornaivāvabāsata..
vṛthaiva vīrakaḥ śapto mayā krodhaparītayā.. 29.60 ..
1.4.d:
न सा नारी तु दैत्योऽसौ वायोर्नैवावबासत..
वृथैव वीरकः शप्तो मया क्रोधपरीतया.. 29.60 ..
1.4.m: “That was not a woman; it was that Daitya; it did not shine clear to the wind! / In vain indeed was Vīraka cursed by me overcome with anger.

1.4.s:
akāryaṃ kriyate mūḍhaiḥ prāyaḥ krodhasamanvitaiḥ..
krodhena naśyate kīrtiḥ krodho haṃti sthirāṃ śriyam.. 29.61 ..
1.4.d:
अकार्यं क्रियते मूढैः प्रायः क्रोधसमन्वितैः..
क्रोधेन नश्यते कीर्तिः क्रोधो हंति स्थिरां श्रियम्.. 29.61 ..
1.4.m: Improper deeds are often done by fools possessed of anger; / through anger fame is destroyed, anger slays enduring prosperity.

1.4.s:
aparicchinnasarvārthā putraṃ śāpitavatyaham..
viparītārthaboddhṝṇāṃ sulabhā vipado yataḥ.. 29.62 ..
1.4.d:
अपरिच्छिन्नसर्वार्था पुत्रं शापितवत्यहम्..
विपरीतार्थबोद्धॄणां सुलभा विपदो यतः.. 29.62 ..
1.4.m: Without discerning the whole truth, I have cursed my son; / for misfortunes easily befall those who misunderstand the truth.”

1.4.s:
saṃciṃtyaivamuvācedaṃ vīrakaṃ prati śailajā..
adho lajjāvikāreṇa vadanenāṃbujatviṣā.. 29.63 ..
1.4.d:
संचिंत्यैवमुवाचेदं वीरकं प्रति शैलजा..
अधो लज्जाविकारेण वदनेनांबुजत्विषा.. 29.63 ..
1.4.m: Having reflected thus, the daughter of the mountain spoke this to Vīraka, / with her lotus-bright face lowered in embarrassed alteration: 29.63

1.4.s:
ahaṃ vīraka te mātā mā te'stu manaso bhramaḥ..
śaṃkarasyāsmi dayitā sutā tu himabhūbhṛtaḥ.. 29.64 ..
1.4.d:
अहं वीरक ते माता मा तेऽस्तु मनसो भ्रमः..
शंकरस्यास्मि दयिता सुता तु हिमभूभृतः.. 29.64 ..
1.4.m: “Vīraka, I am your mother; let there be no confusion in your mind. / I am the beloved wife of Śaṃkara and the daughter of the snow-mountain. 29.64

1.4.s:
mama gātrasthitibhrāṃtyā mā śaṃkāṃ putra bhāvaya..
tuṣṭena gauratā dattā mameyaṃ padmayoninā.. 29.65 ..
1.4.d:
मम गात्रस्थितिभ्रांत्या मा शंकां पुत्र भावय..
तुष्टेन गौरता दत्ता ममेयं पद्मयोनिना.. 29.65 ..
1.4.m: Do not foster doubt, my son, deceived by the state of my body; / this fair complexion was granted to me by the lotus-born [Brahmā] when he was pleased. 29.65

1.4.s:
mayā śapto'syavidite vṛttāṃte daityanirmite..
jñātvā nārīpraveśaṃ tu śaṃkare rahasi stite.. 29.66 ..
1.4.d:
मया शप्तोऽस्यविदिते वृत्तांते दैत्यनिर्मिते..
ज्ञात्वा नारीप्रवेशं तु शंकरे रहसि स्तिते.. 29.66 ..
1.4.m: You were cursed by me when this event arranged by the Daitya was unknown [to me], / thinking that a woman had entered while Śaṃkara was in private. 29.66

1.4.s:
na nivartayituṃ śakyaḥ śāpaḥ kiṃ tu bravīmi te..
mānuṣyāṃ tu śilāyāṃ tvaṃ śilādātsaṃbhaviṣyasi.. 29.67 ..
1.4.d:
न निवर्तयितुं शक्यः शापः किं तु ब्रवीमि ते..
मानुष्यां तु शिलायां त्वं शिलादात्संभविष्यसि.. 29.67 ..
1.4.m: The curse cannot be revoked, yet I say this to you: / you will be born as a mortal upon a rock from Śilāda, 29.67

1.4.s:
puṇye cāpyarbudāraṇye svargamokṣaprade nṛṇām..
acaleśvaraliṃgaṃ tu vartate yatra vīraka.. 29.68 ..
1.4.d:
पुण्ये चाप्यर्बुदारण्ये स्वर्गमोक्षप्रदे नृणाम्..
अचलेश्वरलिंगं तु वर्तते यत्र वीरक.. 29.68 ..
1.4.m: and in the sacred forest of Arbuda, which grants heaven and liberation to men, / where, O Vīraka, the Acaleśvara liṅga stands. 29.68

1.4.s:
vārāṇasyāṃ viśvanāthasamaṃ tatphaladaṃ nṛṇām..
prabhāsasya ca yātrābhirdaśabhiryatphalaṃ nṛṇām.. 29.69 ..
1.4.d:
वाराणस्यां विश्वनाथसमं तत्फलदं नृणाम्..
प्रभासस्य च यात्राभिर्दशभिर्यत्फलं नृणाम्.. 29.69 ..
1.4.m: It yields the same fruit to men as Viśvanātha in Vārāṇasī. / Whatever fruit men obtain from ten pilgrimages to Prabhāsa, 29.69

1.4.s:
tadekayātrayā proktamarbudasya mahāgireḥ..
yatra taptvā tapo martyā dehadhātūnvihāya ca.. 29.70 ..
1.4.d:
तदेकयात्रया प्रोक्तमर्बुदस्य महागिरेः..
यत्र तप्त्वा तपो मर्त्या देहधातून्विहाय च.. 29.70 ..
1.4.m: that is said [to be gained] by a single pilgrimage to the great mountain of Arbuda, / where, after practicing austerity and casting off the bodily elements, mortals 29.70

1.4.s:
saṃsārī na punarbhūyānmaheśvaravaco yathā..
arbudo yadi labhyeta sevituṃ janmaduḥkhitaiḥ.. 29.71 ..
1.4.d:
संसारी न पुनर्भूयान्महेश्वरवचो यथा..
अर्बुदो यदि लभ्येत सेवितुं जन्मदुःखितैः.. 29.71 ..
1.4.m: will never again become transmigrating beings, according to the word of Maheśvara. / If Arbuda can be reached and worshipped by those tormented by rebirth, 29.71

1.4.s:
vārāṇasīṃ ca kedāraṃ kiṃ smaraṃti vṛthaiva te..
tatrārādhya bhavaṃ devaṃ bhavānnandīti nāmabhṛt.. 29.72 ..
1.4.d:
वाराणसीं च केदारं किं स्मरंति वृथैव ते..
तत्राराध्य भवं देवं भवान्नन्दीति नामभृत्.. 29.72 ..
1.4.m: why would they vainly remember Vārāṇasī and Kedāra? / There, having worshipped Lord Bhava, bearing the name Nandī, 29.72

1.4.s:
śīghrameṣyasi cātraiva pratīhāratvamāpsyasi..
evamukte hṛṣṭaromā vīrakaḥ praṇipatya tām.. 29.73 ..
1.4.d:
शीघ्रमेष्यसि चात्रैव प्रतीहारत्वमाप्स्यसि..
एवमुक्ते हृष्टरोमा वीरकः प्रणिपत्य ताम्.. 29.73 ..
1.4.m: you will swiftly come right here and attain the office of door-keeper.” / When she had spoken thus, his hair standing on end, Vīraka bowed down to her 29.73

1.4.s:
saṃstūya vividhairvākyairmātaraṃ samabhāṣata..
dhanyo'haṃ devi yo lapsye mānuṣyamatidurlabham.. 29.74 ..
1.4.d:
संस्तूय विविधैर्वाक्यैर्मातरं समभाषत..
धन्योऽहं देवि यो लप्स्ये मानुष्यमतिदुर्लभम्.. 29.74 ..
1.4.m: and, praising her with diverse words, spoke to his mother: / “Blessed am I, O goddess, who shall obtain the most difficult mortal birth! 29.74

1.4.s:
śāpo'nugraharūpo'yaṃ viśeṣādarbudācale..
samīpe yasya puṇyo'sti mahīsāgarasaṃgamaḥ.. 29.75 ..
1.4.d:
शापोऽनुग्रहरूपोऽयं विशेषादर्बुदाचले..
समीपे यस्य पुण्योऽस्ति महीसागरसंगमः.. 29.75 ..
1.4.m: This curse has the nature of a blessing, especially upon Mount Arbuda, / near which lies the sacred confluence of the Mahī and the ocean. 29.75

1.4.s:
ūdhaḥ pṛthivyā deśo'yaṃ yo gireścārṇavāṃtare..
tatra gatvā mahatpuṇyamavāpya bhavabhaktitaḥ.. 29.76 ..
1.4.d:
ऊधः पृथिव्या देशोऽयं यो गिरेश्चार्णवांतरे..
तत्र गत्वा महत्पुण्यमवाप्य भवभक्तितः.. 29.76 ..
1.4.m: This region between the mountain and the ocean is the very udder of the earth. / Having gone there, obtaining great merit through devotion to Bhava, 29.76

1.4.s:
punareṣyāmi bho mātarityuktvābhūcchilāsutaḥ..
devī ca praviveśātha bhavanaṃ śaśimaulinaḥ.. 29.77 ..
1.4.d:
पुनरेष्यामि भो मातरित्युक्त्वाभूच्छिलासुतः..
देवी च प्रविवेशाथ भवनं शशिमौलिनः.. 29.77 ..
1.4.m: I shall return again, O mother!” Having said this, he became the son of Śilā. / Then the goddess entered the palace of the moon-crested [Śiva]. 29.77

1.4.s:
..ityārbudākhyānam..
tato dṛṣṭvā ca tāṃ prāha dhignārya iti tryaṃbakaḥ.. 29.78 ..
1.4.d:
..इत्यार्बुदाख्यानम्..
ततो दृष्ट्वा च तां प्राह धिग्नार्य इति त्र्यंबकः.. 29.78 ..
1.4.m: — Thus ends the Arbuda-narrative. — / Then, seeing her, the three-eyed Lord said, “Woe to women!” 29.78

1.4.s:
sā ca praṇmya taṃ prāha satyametanna mithyayā..
jaḍaḥ prakṛtibhāgoyaṃ nāryaścārhaṃti nindanām.. 29.79 ..
1.4.d:
सा च प्रण्म्य तं प्राह सत्यमेतन्न मिथ्यया..
जडः प्रकृतिभागोयं नार्यश्चार्हंति निन्दनाम्.. 29.79 ..
1.4.m: And bowing to him, she said: “This is true, not false; / this portion of nature is inert, and women deserve reproach. 29.79

1.4.s:
puruṣāṇāṃ prasādena mucyaṃte bhavasāgarāt..
tataḥ prahṛṣṭastāmāha haro yogyā'dhunā śubhe.. 29.80 ..
1.4.d:
पुरुषाणां प्रसादेन मुच्यंते भवसागरात्..
ततः प्रहृष्टस्तामाह हरो योग्याऽधुना शुभे.. 29.80 ..
1.4.m: By the grace of the Puruṣa, they are freed from the ocean of worldly existence.” / Thereupon Hara, delighted, said to her: “You are fit now, auspicious one! 29.80

1.4.s:
putraṃ dāsyāmi yena tvaṃ khyātimāpsyasi śobhane..
tato rema hi devyā sa nānāścaryālayo haraḥ.. 29.81 ..
1.4.d:
पुत्रं दास्यामि येन त्वं ख्यातिमाप्स्यसि शोभने..
ततो रेम हि देव्या स नानाश्चर्यालयो हरः.. 29.81 ..
1.4.m: I will give you a son through whom you will attain fame, beautiful one.” / Then Hara, the abode of diverse wonders, sported with the goddess. 29.81

1.4.s:
tato varṣasahasreṣu devāstvaritamānasāḥ..
jvalanaṃ nodayāmāsurjñātuṃ śaṃkaraceṣṭitam.. 29.82 ..
1.4.d:
ततो वर्षसहस्रेषु देवास्त्वरितमानसाः..
ज्वलनं नोदयामासुर्ज्ञातुं शंकरचेष्टितम्.. 29.82 ..
1.4.m: Then, after a thousand years, the gods, eager in their minds, / urged Agni forward to find out Śaṃkara’s doings. 29.82

1.4.s:
dvāri sthitaṃ pratihāraṃ vaṃcayitvā ca pāvakaḥ..
pārāvatasya rūpeṇa praviveśa harāṃtikam.. 29.83 ..
1.4.d:
द्वारि स्थितं प्रतिहारं वंचयित्वा च पावकः..
पारावतस्य रूपेण प्रविवेश हरांतिकम्.. 29.83 ..
1.4.m: Having deceived the door-keeper standing at the gate, Agni / entered the presence of Hara in the form of a pigeon. 29.83

1.4.s:
dadṛśe taṃ ca deveśo vinatāṃ prekṣya pārvatīm..
tatastāṃ jvalanaṃ prāha naitadyogyaṃ tvayā kṛtam.. 29.84 ..
1.4.d:
ददृशे तं च देवेशो विनतां प्रेक्ष्य पार्वतीम्..
ततस्तां ज्वलनं प्राह नैतद्योग्यं त्वया कृतम्.. 29.84 ..
1.4.m: The lord of gods saw him, seeing Pārvatī bow [in shame]. / Then he said to Agni: “This was not right for you to do. 29.84

1.4.s:
yadidaṃ bhukṣutaṃ sthānānmama tejo hyanuttamam..
gṛhāṇa tvaṃ sudurbuddhe no vā dhakṣyāmi tvāṃ ruṣā.. 29.85 ..
1.4.d:
यदिदं भुक्षुतं स्थानान्मम तेजो ह्यनुत्तमम्..
गृहाण त्वं सुदुर्बुद्धे नो वा धक्ष्यामि त्वां रुषा.. 29.85 ..
1.4.m: Since this peerless fiery energy of mine has been shaken from its place, / take it yourself, foolish one, or else I shall burn you in wrath!” 29.85

1.4.s:
bhītastato'sau jagrāha sarvadevamukhaṃ ca saḥ..
tena te vahnisahitā vihvalāśca surāḥ kṛtāḥ.. 29.86 ..
1.4.d:
भीतस्ततोऽसौ जग्राह सर्वदेवमुखं च सः..
तेन ते वह्निसहिता विह्वलाश्च सुराः कृताः.. 29.86 ..
1.4.m: Terrified, he received it, and he is the mouth of all gods; / thereby the gods, together with Agni, were thrown into distress. 29.86

1.4.s:
vipāṭya jaṭharāṇyeṣāṃ vīryaṃ māheśvaraṃ tataḥ..
niṣkrāṃtaṃ tatsaro jātaṃ pāradaṃ śatayojanam.. 29.87 ..
1.4.d:
विपाट्य जठराण्येषां वीर्यं माहेश्वरं ततः..
निष्क्रांतं तत्सरो जातं पारदं शतयोजनम्.. 29.87 ..
1.4.m: Rupturing their bellies, that seed of Maheśvara / issued forth and became a lake of quicksilver a hundred yojanas wide. 29.87

1.4.s:
vahniśca vyākulībhūto gaṃgāyāṃ mumuce sakṛt..
dahyamānā ca sā devī taraṃgairvahirutsṛjat.. 29.88 ..
1.4.d:
वह्निश्च व्याकुलीभूतो गंगायां मुमुचे सकृत्..
दह्यमाना च सा देवी तरंगैर्वहिरुत्सृजत्.. 29.88 ..
1.4.m: And Agni, becoming distraught, cast it at once into the Gaṅgā. / And she, burning, cast it outside by means of her waves. 29.88

1.4.s:
jātastribhuvanakyātastena ca śvetaparvataḥ..
etasminnaṃtare vahnirāhūtaśca himālaye.. 29.89 ..
1.4.d:
जातस्त्रिभुवनक्यातस्तेन च श्वेतपर्वतः..
एतस्मिन्नंतरे वह्निराहूतश्च हिमालये.. 29.89 ..
1.4.m: From that, the White Mountain, famous in the three worlds, was born. / In the meantime, Agni was summoned to the Himālaya 29.89

1.4.s:
saptarṣibhirvahnihomaṃ kurvadbhirmaṃtravīryataḥ..
āgatya tatra jagrāha vahnirbhāgaṃ ca taṃ hutam.. 29.90 ..
1.4.d:
सप्तर्षिभिर्वह्निहोमं कुर्वद्भिर्मंत्रवीर्यतः..
आगत्य तत्र जग्राह वह्निर्भागं च तं हुतम्.. 29.90 ..
1.4.m: by the seven seers performing a fire oblation by the power of mantras. / Having arrived there, Agni took that offered share. 29.90

1.4.s:
gate'hnyatvasmiṃśca tatrasthaḥ patnī steṣāmapaśyata..
suvarṇakadalīstaṃbhanibhāstāścaṃdralekhayā.. 29.91 ..
1.4.d:
गतेऽह्न्यत्वस्मिंश्च तत्रस्थः पत्नी स्तेषामपश्यत..
सुवर्णकदलीस्तंभनिभास्ताश्चंद्रलेखया.. 29.91 ..
1.4.m: When that day had passed, standing there he saw their wives, / resembling pillars of golden plantain trees, with crescent moons [on their foreheads]. 29.91

1.4.s:
paśyamānaḥ praphullākṣo vahniḥ kāmavaśaṃ gataḥ..
sa bhūyaściṃtayāmāsa na nyāyyaṃ kṣubhito'smi yat.. 29.92 ..
1.4.d:
पश्यमानः प्रफुल्लाक्षो वह्निः कामवशं गतः..
स भूयश्चिंतयामास न न्याय्यं क्षुभितोऽस्मि यत्.. 29.92 ..
1.4.m: Gazing with wide-open eyes, Agni came under the sway of desire. / He reflected repeatedly: “It is not right that I am agitated. 29.92

1.4.s:
sādhvīḥ patnīrdvijeṃdrāṇāmakāmāḥ kāmayāmyaham..
pāpametatkarma cograṃ naśyāmi tṛmavatsphuṭam.. 29.93 ..
1.4.d:
साध्वीः पत्नीर्द्विजेंद्राणामकामाः कामयाम्यहम्..
पापमेतत्कर्म चोग्रं नश्यामि तृमवत्स्फुटम्.. 29.93 ..
1.4.m: I lust after the chaste wives of the foremost brahmins, who do not desire me. / This action is an awful sin; clearly I shall perish like a blade of grass. 29.93

1.4.s:
kṛtvaitannaśyate kīrtiryāvadācaṃdratārakam..
evaṃ saṃciṃtya bahudhā gatvā caiva vanāṃtaram.. 29.94 ..
1.4.d:
कृत्वैतन्नश्यते कीर्तिर्यावदाचंद्रतारकम्..
एवं संचिंत्य बहुधा गत्वा चैव वनांतरम्.. 29.94 ..
1.4.m: By doing this, my fame will be destroyed as long as the moon and stars endure.” / Having reflected thus in many ways and gone to another forest, 29.94

1.4.s:
saṃyantuṃ nābhavacchakta upāyairbahubhirmanaḥ..
tataḥ sa kāmasaṃtapto mūrchitaḥ samapadyata.. 29.95 ..
1.4.d:
संयन्तुं नाभवच्छक्त उपायैर्बहुभिर्मनः..
ततः स कामसंतप्तो मूर्छितः समपद्यत.. 29.95 ..
1.4.m: he was unable to restrain his mind by numerous means. / Then, tormented by passion, he fell into a faint. 29.95

1.4.s:
tataḥ svāhā ca bhāryāsya bubudhe tadviceṣṭitam..
jñātvā ca ciṃtayāmāsa prahṛṣṭā manasi svayam.. 29.96 ..
1.4.d:
ततः स्वाहा च भार्यास्य बुबुधे तद्विचेष्टितम्..
ज्ञात्वा च चिंतयामास प्रहृष्टा मनसि स्वयम्.. 29.96 ..
1.4.m: Then his wife Svāhā became aware of that conduct of his, / and having understood it, she reflected, delighted in her mind: 29.96

1.4.s:
svāṃ bhāryāmatha māṃ tyaktvā bahuvāsādavajñayā..
bhāryāḥ kāmayate nūnaṃ saptarṣīṇāṃ mahātmanām.. 29.97 ..
1.4.d:
स्वां भार्यामथ मां त्यक्त्वा बहुवासादवज्ञया..
भार्याः कामयते नूनं सप्तर्षीणां महात्मनाम्.. 29.97 ..
1.4.m: “Having abandoned me, his own wife, in disdain due to long cohabitation, / he surely lusts for the wives of the great seven seers. 29.97

1.4.s:
tadāsāṃ rūpamāśritya ramiṣye tena cāpyaham..
tatastvaṃgiraso bhāryā śivānāmeti śobhanā.. 29.98 ..
1.4.d:
तदासां रूपमाश्रित्य रमिष्ये तेन चाप्यहम्..
ततस्त्वंगिरसो भार्या शिवानामेति शोभना.. 29.98 ..
1.4.m: Therefore, assuming their form, I too shall sport with him.” / There was the beautiful wife of Aṅgiras, Śivā by name; 29.98

1.4.s:
tasyā rūpaṃ samādhāya pāvakaṃ prāpya sābravīt..
māmagne kāmasaṃtaptāṃ tvaṃ kāmayitumarhasi.. 29.99 ..
1.4.d:
तस्या रूपं समाधाय पावकं प्राप्य साब्रवीत्..
मामग्ने कामसंतप्तां त्वं कामयितुमर्हसि.. 29.99 ..
1.4.m: assuming her form and approaching Agni, she said: / “O Agni, you ought to make love to me, who am tormented by passion. 29.99

1.4.s:
na cetkariṣyase deva mṛtāṃ māmupadhāraya..
ahamaṃgiraso bhāryā śivānāma hutāśana.. 29.100 ..
1.4.d:
न चेत्करिष्यसे देव मृतां मामुपधारय..
अहमंगिरसो भार्या शिवानाम हुताशन.. 29.100 ..
1.4.m: If you do not, O god, know me to be dead. / I am the wife of Aṅgiras, named Śivā, O fire! 29.100

1.4.s:
sarvābhiḥ sahitā prāptā tāśca yāsyaṃtyanukramāt..
asmākaṃ tvaṃ priyo nityaṃ tvaccittāśca vayaṃ tathā.. 29.101 ..
1.4.d:
सर्वाभिः सहिता प्राप्ता ताश्च यास्यंत्यनुक्रमात्..
अस्माकं त्वं प्रियो नित्यं त्वच्चित्ताश्च वयं तथा.. 29.101 ..
1.4.m: I have come together with all [the other wives], and they too will come in turn. / You are ever dear to us, and our minds are likewise devoted to you.” 29.101

1.4.s:
tataḥ sa kāmasaṃtaptaḥ saṃbabhūva tayā saha..
prīte prītā ca sā devī nirjagāma vanāṃtarāt.. 29.102 ..
1.4.d:
ततः स कामसंतप्तः संबभूव तया सह..
प्रीते प्रीता च सा देवी निर्जगाम वनांतरात्.. 29.102 ..
1.4.m: Then, tormented by passion, he united with her; / and when he was gratified, that goddess, delighted, departed from that forest, 29.102

1.4.s:
ciṃtayaṃtī mamedaṃ cedrūpaṃ drakṣyaṃti kānane..
te brāhmaṇīnāmanṛtaṃ doṣaṃ vakṣyaṃti pāvakāt.. 29.103 ..
1.4.d:
चिंतयंती ममेदं चेद्रूपं द्रक्ष्यंति कानने..
ते ब्राह्मणीनामनृतं दोषं वक्ष्यंति पावकात्.. 29.103 ..
1.4.m: thinking: “If they see this form of mine in the forest, / they will speak falsely of a flaw in the brahmin women on account of Agni. 29.103

1.4.s:
tasmādetadrakṣamāṇā garuḍī saṃbhavāmyaham..
suparṇā sā tato bhūtvā dadṛśe śvetaparvatam.. 29.104 ..
1.4.d:
तस्मादेतद्रक्षमाणा गरुडी संभवाम्यहम्..
सुपर्णा सा ततो भूत्वा ददृशे श्वेतपर्वतम्.. 29.104 ..
1.4.m: Therefore, protecting this [reputation], let me become a female Garuḍa bird.” / Then, having become a bird, she saw the White Mountain, 29.104

1.4.s:
śarastaṃbaiḥ susaṃpṛktaṃ rakṣobhiśca piśācakaiḥ..
sā tatra sahasā gatvā śailapūṣṭhaṃ sudurgamam.. 29.105 ..
1.4.d:
शरस्तंबैः सुसंपृक्तं रक्षोभिश्च पिशाचकैः..
सा तत्र सहसा गत्वा शैलपूष्ठं सुदुर्गमम्.. 29.105 ..
1.4.m: thickly covered with clumps of reeds and with demons and piśācas. / Having swiftly gone there, to the summit of the mountain, exceedingly difficult to reach, 29.105

1.4.s:
prākṣipatkāṃcane kuṃḍe śukraṃ taddhāraṇe'kṣamā..
śiṣṭānāmapi devīnāṃ saptarṣīṇāṃ mahātmanām.. 29.106 ..
1.4.d:
प्राक्षिपत्कांचने कुंडे शुक्रं तद्धारणेऽक्षमा..
शिष्टानामपि देवीनां सप्तर्षीणां महात्मनाम्.. 29.106 ..
1.4.m: unable to hold it, she discharged the semen into a golden bowl / [and similarly for the forms] of the remaining noble wives of the great seven seers. 29.106

1.4.s:
patnīsarūpatāṃ kṛtvā kāmayāmāsa pāvakam..
divyaṃ rūpamarūṃdhatyāḥ kartuṃ na śakitaṃ tayā.. 29.107 ..
1.4.d:
पत्नीसरूपतां कृत्वा कामयामास पावकम्..
दिव्यं रूपमरूंधत्याः कर्तुं न शकितं तया.. 29.107 ..
1.4.m: Assuming the form of each of the wives, she united in love with the Fire. / But she was unable to assume the divine form of Arundhatī,

1.4.s:
tasyāstapaḥprabhāveṇa bhartuḥ śuśrūṣaṇena ca..
ṣaṭkṛtvastattu nikṣiptamagniretaḥ kurudvaha.. 29.108 ..
1.4.d:
तस्यास्तपःप्रभावेण भर्तुः शुश्रूषणेन च..
षट्कृत्वस्तत्तु निक्षिप्तमग्निरेतः कुरुद्वह.. 29.108 ..
1.4.m: by virtue of her austerity and her devotion to her husband. / Six times, O bull of the Kurus, that semen of the Fire was cast

1.4.s:
kuṃḍe'smiṃścaitrabahule pratipadyeva svāhayā..
tataśca pāvako duḥkhācchuśoca ca mumoha ca.. 29.109 ..
1.4.d:
कुंडेऽस्मिंश्चैत्रबहुले प्रतिपद्येव स्वाहया..
ततश्च पावको दुःखाच्छुशोच च मुमोह च.. 29.109 ..
1.4.m: into that pit by Svāhā, on the first day of the dark fortnight of Caitra. / And then, out of grief, the Fire sorrowed and was bewildered.

1.4.s:
āḥ pāpaṃ kṛtamityeva dehanyāse'karonmatim..
tatastaṃ khecarī vāṇī prāha mā maraṇaṃ kuru.. 29.110 ..
1.4.d:
आः पापं कृतमित्येव देहन्यासेऽकरोन्मतिम्..
ततस्तं खेचरी वाणी प्राह मा मरणं कुरु.. 29.110 ..
1.4.m: Thinking, 'Alas, a sin has been committed!' he resolved to cast off his body. / Then an ethereal voice spoke to him: 'Do not court death!

1.4.s:
bhāvyametacca bhāvyarthātko hi pāvaka mucyate..
bhāvyarthenāpi yatte ca paradāropa sevanam.. 29.111 ..
1.4.d:
भाव्यमेतच्च भाव्यर्थात्को हि पावक मुच्यते..
भाव्यर्थेनापि यत्ते च परदारोप सेवनम्.. 29.111 ..
1.4.m: This was destined to be; for who, O Fire, can escape destiny? / Yet because you enjoyed the wife of another, even though by fate,

1.4.s:
kṛtaṃ taccetasā tena tvāmajīrṇaṃ pravekṣyati..
śvetaketormahāyajñe ghṛtadhārābhitarpitam.. 29.112 ..
1.4.d:
कृतं तच्चेतसा तेन त्वामजीर्णं प्रवेक्ष्यति..
श्वेतकेतोर्महायज्ञे घृतधाराभितर्पितम्.. 29.112 ..
1.4.m: and did so in your mind, indigestion shall enter you, / even when sated with streams of clarified butter at the great sacrifice of Śvetaketu.

1.4.s:
śokaṃ ca tyaja naitāstāḥ svāhai veyaṃ tava priyā..
śvetaparvatakuṃḍasthaṃ putraṃ tvaṃ draṣṭumarhasi..
tato vahnistatra gatvā dadṛśe tanayaṃ prabhum.. 29.113 ..
1.4.d:
शोकं च त्यज नैतास्ताः स्वाहै वेयं तव प्रिया..
श्वेतपर्वतकुंडस्थं पुत्रं त्वं द्रष्टुमर्हसि..
ततो वह्निस्तत्र गत्वा ददृशे तनयं प्रभुम्.. 29.113 ..
1.4.m: Cast off grief: those were not the women [you thought]; this was only your beloved Svāhā. / You ought to see your son who is in the pit on Mount Śveta.' / Then the Fire went there and saw his lordly son.

1.4.s:
..arjuna uvāca..
kasmātsvāhā karodrūpaṃ ṣaṇṇāṃ tāsāṃ mahāmune.. 29.114 ..
1.4.d:
..अर्जुन उवाच..
कस्मात्स्वाहा करोद्रूपं षण्णां तासां महामुने.. 29.114 ..
1.4.m: Arjuna said: / Why did Svāhā take the forms of those six, O great sage,

1.4.s:
yattā bhartṛparāḥ sādhvyastapasvinyognisaṃnibhāḥ..
na bibheti ca kiṃ tābhyaḥ ṣaḍbhyaḥ svāhā'parādhinī..
bhartṛbhaktyā jagaddagdhuṃ yataḥ śaktāśca tā mune.. 29.115 ..
1.4.d:
यत्ता भर्तृपराः साध्व्यस्तपस्विन्योग्निसंनिभाः..
न बिभेति च किं ताभ्यः षड्भ्यः स्वाहाऽपराधिनी..
भर्तृभक्त्या जगद्दग्धुं यतः शक्ताश्च ता मुने.. 29.115 ..
1.4.m: since they are devoted to their husbands, chaste, ascetic, and like fire itself? / And why was the guilty Svāhā not afraid of those six, / since, by devotion to their husbands, they were capable of burning up the world, O sage?

1.4.s:
..nārada uvāca..
satyametatkuruśreṣṭha śrṛṇu taccāpi kāraṇam..
yena tāsāṃ kṛtaṃ rūpaṃ na vā śāpaṃ daduśca tāḥ.. 29.116 ..
1.4.d:
..नारद उवाच..
सत्यमेतत्कुरुश्रेष्ठ श्रृणु तच्चापि कारणम्..
येन तासां कृतं रूपं न वा शापं ददुश्च ताः.. 29.116 ..
1.4.m: Nārada said: / This is true, O best of the Kurus; listen also to that reason / why she took their forms and yet they did not utter a curse.

1.4.s:
yatra tadvahninā kṣiptaṃ rudratejaḥ sakṛtpurā..
gaṃgāyāṃ tatra sasnustāḥ ṣaṭatnyo'jñanābhāvataḥ.. 29.117 ..
1.4.d:
यत्र तद्वह्निना क्षिप्तं रुद्रतेजः सकृत्पुरा..
गंगायां तत्र सस्नुस्ताः षटत्न्योऽज्ञनाभावतः.. 29.117 ..
1.4.m: Where formerly that splendor of Rudra was cast once into the Gaṅgā by the Fire, / there those six wives bathed, due to ignorance.

1.4.s:
tatastā vihvalībhūtāstejasā tena mohitāḥ..
lajjayā ca svabhartṝṇāṃ gaṃgātīrasthitā rahaḥ.. 29.118 ..
1.4.d:
ततस्ता विह्वलीभूतास्तेजसा तेन मोहिताः..
लज्जया च स्वभर्तॄणां गंगातीरस्थिता रहः.. 29.118 ..
1.4.m: Then, overwhelmed and bewildered by that splendor, / and out of shame toward their own husbands, they remained in secret on the bank of the Gaṅgā.

1.4.s:
etadaṃtamālokya cikīrṣaṃtī manīṣitam..
svāhā śarīramāviśyatāsāṃ tejo jahāra tat.. 29.119 ..
1.4.d:
एतदंतमालोक्य चिकीर्षंती मनीषितम्..
स्वाहा शरीरमाविश्यतासां तेजो जहार तत्.. 29.119 ..
1.4.m: Seeing this state of affairs and desiring to accomplish her wish, / Svāhā entered their bodies and took away that splendor.

1.4.s: cikrīḍa vahnijāyāpi yathā te kathitaṃ mayā.. 29.120 ..
1.4.d: चिक्रीड वह्निजायापि यथा ते कथितं मया.. 29.120 ..
1.4.m: The wife of the Fire then sported [with him], just as I have told you.

1.4.s:
upakāramimaṃ tābhiḥ smaraṃtībhiśca bhārata..
na śaptā sā yataḥ śāpo na deyaścopakāriṇi.. 29.121 ..
1.4.d:
उपकारमिमं ताभिः स्मरंतीभिश्च भारत..
न शप्ता सा यतः शापो न देयश्चोपकारिणि.. 29.121 ..
1.4.m: Remembering this favor from her, O descendant of Bharata, / she was not cursed by them; for a curse should not be given to a benefactor.

1.4.s:
tataḥ saptarṣayo jñātvā jñānenāsucitāṃ gatāḥ..
tatyajuḥ ṣaṭ tadā patnīrvinā devīmaruṃdhatīm.. 29.122 ..
1.4.d:
ततः सप्तर्षयो ज्ञात्वा ज्ञानेनासुचितां गताः..
तत्यजुः षट् तदा पत्नीर्विना देवीमरुंधतीम्.. 29.122 ..
1.4.m: Then the seven seers, having learned by insight that they had incurred impurity, / cast off the six wives at that time, with the exception of the divine Arundhatī.

1.4.s:
viśvāmitrastu bhagavānkumāraṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ..
stavaṃ divyaṃ saṃpracakre mahāsenasya cāpi saḥ.. 29.123 ..
1.4.d:
विश्वामित्रस्तु भगवान्कुमारं शरणं गतः..
स्तवं दिव्यं संप्रचक्रे महासेनस्य चापि सः.. 29.123 ..
1.4.m: Lord Viśvāmitra, however, took refuge in Kumāra; / and he composed a divine hymn of praise to Mahāsena.

1.4.s:
aṣṭottaraśataṃ nāmnāṃ śrṛṇu tvaṃ tāni phālguna..
japena yeṣāṃ pāpāni yāṃti jñānamavāpnuyāt.. 29.124 ..
1.4.d:
अष्टोत्तरशतं नाम्नां श्रृणु त्वं तानि फाल्गुन..
जपेन येषां पापानि यांति ज्ञानमवाप्नुयात्.. 29.124 ..
1.4.m: Listen to the one hundred and eight names, O Phālguna, / by the recitation of which sins depart and one attains knowledge:

1.4.s:
tvaṃ brahmavādī tvaṃ brahmā brāhmaṇavatsalaḥ..
brahmaṇyo brahmadevaśca brahmado brahmasaṃgrahaḥ.. 29.125 ..
1.4.d:
त्वं ब्रह्मवादी त्वं ब्रह्मा ब्राह्मणवत्सलः..
ब्रह्मण्यो ब्रह्मदेवश्च ब्रह्मदो ब्रह्मसंग्रहः.. 29.125 ..
1.4.m: 'You are the speaker of the Veda; you are Brahmā; you are fond of brahmins; / you are friendly to brahmins; you are the god of sacred knowledge; you are the giver of the Veda; you are the collector of sacred lore.

1.4.s:
tvaṃ paraṃ paramaṃ tejo maṃgalānāṃ ca maṃgalam..
aprameyaguṇaścaiva maṃtrāṇāṃ maṃtrago bhavān.. 29.126 ..
1.4.d:
त्वं परं परमं तेजो मंगलानां च मंगलम्..
अप्रमेयगुणश्चैव मंत्राणां मंत्रगो भवान्.. 29.126 ..
1.4.m: You are the highest, supreme splendor; the most auspicious of all auspicious things; / possessing immeasurable virtues; you are the one reachable through mantras.

1.4.s:
tvaṃ sāvitrīmayo deva sarvatraivāparājitaḥ..
maṃtra śarvātmako devaḥ ṣaḍakṣaravatāṃ varaḥ.. 29.127 ..
1.4.d:
त्वं सावित्रीमयो देव सर्वत्रैवापराजितः..
मंत्र शर्वात्मको देवः षडक्षरवतां वरः.. 29.127 ..
1.4.m: You are made of the Sāvitrī, O Lord; undefeated everywhere; / the god whose soul is the mantra and Śarva; the foremost among masters of the six-syllable mantra.

1.4.s:
mālī maulī patākī ca jaṭī muṃḍī śikhaṃḍyapi..
kuṇḍalī lāṃgalī bālaḥ kumāraḥ pravaro varaḥ.. 29.128 ..
1.4.d:
माली मौली पताकी च जटी मुंडी शिखंड्यपि..
कुण्डली लांगली बालः कुमारः प्रवरो वरः.. 29.128 ..
1.4.m: Wearing a garland, crowned, bearing a banner, matted-haired, shaven-headed, crested; / wearing earrings, holding a plow, a youth, Kumāra, eminent, the best.

1.4.s:
gavāṃputraḥ surārighnaḥ saṃbhavo bhavabhāvanaḥ..
pinākī śatruhā śveto gūḍhaḥ skandaḥ karāgraṇīḥ.. 29.129 ..
1.4.d:
गवांपुत्रः सुरारिघ्नः संभवो भवभावनः..
पिनाकी शत्रुहा श्वेतो गूढः स्कन्दः कराग्रणीः.. 29.129 ..
1.4.m: Son of cows, slayer of enemies of the gods, the origin, creator of existence; / armed with the bow Pināka, killer of foes, white, secret, Skanda, foremost in action.

1.4.s:
dvādaśo bhūrbhuvo bhāvī bhuvaḥ putro namaskṛtaḥ..
nāgarājaḥ sudharmātmā nākapṛṣṭhaḥ sanātanaḥ.. 29.130 ..
1.4.d:
द्वादशो भूर्भुवो भावी भुवः पुत्रो नमस्कृतः..
नागराजः सुधर्मात्मा नाकपृष्ठः सनातनः.. 29.130 ..
1.4.m: The twelfth, earth, atmosphere, the future, son of the earth, worshipped; / king of serpents, very righteous-souled, dwelling in heaven, eternal.

1.4.s:
tvaṃ bhartā sarvabhūtātmā tvaṃ trātā tvaṃ sukhāvahaḥ..
śaradakṣaḥ śikhī jetā ṣaḍvaktro bhayanāśanaḥ.. 29.131 ..
1.4.d:
त्वं भर्ता सर्वभूतात्मा त्वं त्राता त्वं सुखावहः..
शरदक्षः शिखी जेता षड्वक्त्रो भयनाशनः.. 29.131 ..
1.4.m: You are the maintainer, the soul of all beings, you are the protector, you are the bringer of happiness; / born in autumn, having a peacock, the conqueror, six-faced, dispeller of fear.

1.4.s:
hemagarbho mahāgarbho jayaśca vijayeśvaraḥ..
tvaṃ kartā tvaṃ vidhātā ca nityo nityārimardanaḥ.. 29.132 ..
1.4.d:
हेमगर्भो महागर्भो जयश्च विजयेश्वरः..
त्वं कर्ता त्वं विधाता च नित्यो नित्यारिमर्दनः.. 29.132 ..
1.4.m: Golden-wombed, containing the universe, victory, lord of victory; / you are the maker, you are the creator, eternal, constant crusher of foes.

1.4.s:
mahāseno mahāteja vīrasenaśca bhūpatiḥ..
siddhāsanaḥ surādhyakṣo bhīmaseno nirāmayaḥ.. 29.133 ..
1.4.d:
महासेनो महातेज वीरसेनश्च भूपतिः..
सिद्धासनः सुराध्यक्षो भीमसेनो निरामयः.. 29.133 ..
1.4.m: Mahāsena, of great splendor, Vīrasena, lord of the earth; / seated upon perfection, overseer of the gods, Bhīmasena, free from disease.

1.4.s:
śauriryadurmahātejā vīryavānsatyavikramaḥ..
tejogarbho'suraripuḥ suramūrtiḥ surorjjitaḥ.. 29.134 ..
1.4.d:
शौरिर्यदुर्महातेजा वीर्यवान्सत्यविक्रमः..
तेजोगर्भोऽसुररिपुः सुरमूर्तिः सुरोर्ज्जितः.. 29.134 ..
1.4.m: Heroic, Yadu, endowed with great splendor, full of valor, of truthful prowess; / womb of light, foe of asuras, embodiment of the gods, strengthened by the gods.

1.4.s:
kṛtajño varadaḥ satyaḥ śaraṇyaḥ sādhuvatsalaḥ..
suvrataḥ sūryasaṃkāśo vahnigarbhaḥ kaṇo bhuvaḥ.. 29.135 ..
1.4.d:
कृतज्ञो वरदः सत्यः शरण्यः साधुवत्सलः..
सुव्रतः सूर्यसंकाशो वह्निगर्भः कणो भुवः.. 29.135 ..
1.4.m: Grateful, giver of boons, true, a refuge, affectionate toward the virtuous; / keeping good vows, sun-like, womb of fire, atom of the earth.

1.4.s:
pippalī śīghrago raudrī gāṃgeyo ripudāraṇaḥ..
kārttikeyaḥ prabhuḥ kṣaṃtā nīladaṃṣṭro mahāmanāḥ.. 29.136 ..
1.4.d:
पिप्पली शीघ्रगो रौद्री गांगेयो रिपुदारणः..
कार्त्तिकेयः प्रभुः क्षंता नीलदंष्ट्रो महामनाः.. 29.136 ..
1.4.m: Pippalī, swift-moving, fierce, son of Gaṅgā, tearer of enemies; / Kārttikeya, the sovereign, forbearing, blue-tusked, noble-minded.

1.4.s:
nigraho nigrahāṇāṃ ca netā tvaṃ suranaṃdanaḥ..
pragrahaḥ paramānaṃdaḥ krodhaghnastāra ucchritaḥ.. 29.137 ..
1.4.d:
निग्रहो निग्रहाणां च नेता त्वं सुरनंदनः..
प्रग्रहः परमानंदः क्रोधघ्नस्तार उच्छ्रितः.. 29.137 ..
1.4.m: Restraint, and the leader of restraints, you are the delighter of the gods; / curb, supreme bliss, destroyer of anger, lofty, exalted.

1.4.s:
kukkuṭī bahulī divyaḥ kāmado bhūrivardhanaḥ..
amogho'mṛtado hyagniḥ śatrughnaḥ sarvamodanaḥ.. 29.138 ..
1.4.d:
कुक्कुटी बहुली दिव्यः कामदो भूरिवर्धनः..
अमोघोऽमृतदो ह्यग्निः शत्रुघ्नः सर्वमोदनः.. 29.138 ..
1.4.m: Having a cock, abundant, divine, granter of desires, greatly flourishing; / unfailing, giver of nectar, fire itself, slayer of enemies, gladdening all.

1.4.s:
avyayo hyamaraḥ śrīmānunnato hyagnisaṃbhavaḥ..
piśācarājaḥ sūryābhaḥ śivātmā śivanaṃdanaḥ.. 29.139 ..
1.4.d:
अव्ययो ह्यमरः श्रीमानुन्नतो ह्यग्निसंभवः..
पिशाचराजः सूर्याभः शिवात्मा शिवनंदनः.. 29.139 ..
1.4.m: Imperishable, immortal, glorious, elevated, born of fire; / king of piśācas, sun-radiant, identical to Śiva, son of Śiva.

1.4.s:
apārapāro durjñeyaḥ sarvabhūtahite rataḥ..
agrāhyaḥ kāraṇaṃ kartā parameṣṭhī paraṃ padam.. 29.140 ..
1.4.d:
अपारपारो दुर्ज्ञेयः सर्वभूतहिते रतः..
अग्राह्यः कारणं कर्ता परमेष्ठी परं पदम्.. 29.140 ..
1.4.m: Shore of the boundless, hard to know, devoted to the welfare of all beings; / ungraspable, the cause, the maker, the supreme deity, the highest state.

1.4.s:
aciṃtyaḥ sarvabhūtātmā sarvātmā tvaṃ sanātanaḥ..
evaṃ sa sarvabhūtānāṃ saṃstutaḥ parameśvaraḥ.. 29.141 ..
1.4.d:
अचिंत्यः सर्वभूतात्मा सर्वात्मा त्वं सनातनः..
एवं स सर्वभूतानां संस्तुतः परमेश्वरः.. 29.141 ..
1.4.m: Inconceivable, the soul of all beings, the universal self, you are eternal.' / Thus was that supreme lord of all beings praised

1.4.s:
nāmnāmaṣṭaśatenāyaṃ viśvāmitramaharṣiṇā..
prasannamūrtirāhedaṃ munīṃdraṃ vriyatāmiti.. 29.142 ..
1.4.d:
नाम्नामष्टशतेनायं विश्वामित्रमहर्षिणा..
प्रसन्नमूर्तिराहेदं मुनींद्रं व्रियतामिति.. 29.142 ..
1.4.m: with this set of one hundred and eight names by the great seer Viśvāmitra. / With a gracious appearance, he said this to the prince of sages: 'Choose a boon!

1.4.s:
mama tvayā dvijaśreṣṭha stutireṣā nirūpitā..
bhaviṣyati mano'bhīṣṭaprāptaye prāṇināṃ bhuvi.. 29.143 ..
1.4.d:
मम त्वया द्विजश्रेष्ठ स्तुतिरेषा निरूपिता..
भविष्यति मनोऽभीष्टप्राप्तये प्राणिनां भुवि.. 29.143 ..
1.4.m: This hymn of praise to me that has been set forth by you, O best of the twice-born, / will bring about the attainment of their hearts' desires for creatures on earth.

1.4.s:
vivardhate kule lakṣmīstasya yaḥ prapaṭhedimam..
na rākṣasāḥ piśācā vā na bhūtāni na cāpadaḥ.. 29.144 ..
1.4.d:
विवर्धते कुले लक्ष्मीस्तस्य यः प्रपठेदिमम्..
न राक्षसाः पिशाचा वा न भूतानि न चापदः.. 29.144 ..
1.4.m: Fortune increases in the family of one who recites this. / Neither rākṣasas nor piśācas, neither spirits nor adversities

1.4.s:
vighnakārīṇi tadgehe yatraiva saṃstuvaṃti mām..
duḥsvapnaṃ ca na paśyetsa baddho mucyate baṃdhanāt.. 29.145 ..
1.4.d:
विघ्नकारीणि तद्गेहे यत्रैव संस्तुवंति माम्..
दुःस्वप्नं च न पश्येत्स बद्धो मुच्यते बंधनात्.. 29.145 ..
1.4.m: shall create obstacles in the home of anyone who praises me thus; / he shall not experience bad dreams, and if bound, he is released from bondage.

1.4.s:
stavasyāsya prabhāveṇa divyabhāvaḥ pumānbhavet..
tvaṃ ca māṃ śrutisaṃskāraiḥ sarvaiḥ saṃskartumarhasi.. 29.146 ..
1.4.d:
स्तवस्यास्य प्रभावेण दिव्यभावः पुमान्भवेत्..
त्वं च मां श्रुतिसंस्कारैः सर्वैः संस्कर्तुमर्हसि.. 29.146 ..
1.4.m: Through the power of this hymn, a man will attain a divine state. / And you ought to consecrate me with all Vedic sacraments;

1.4.s:
saṃskārarahitaṃ janma yataśca paśuvatsmṛtam..
tvaṃ ca madvaradānena brahmarṣiśca bhaviṣyasi.. 29.147 ..
1.4.d:
संस्काररहितं जन्म यतश्च पशुवत्स्मृतम्..
त्वं च मद्वरदानेन ब्रह्मर्षिश्च भविष्यसि.. 29.147 ..
1.4.m: for a birth without sacraments is considered to be like that of a beast. / And by the gift of my boon, you shall become a brahmin seer.'

1.4.s:
tato munistasya cakre jātakarmādikāḥ kriyāḥ..
paurohityaṃ tathā bheje skaṃdasyaivājñayā prabhuḥ.. 29.148 ..
1.4.d:
ततो मुनिस्तस्य चक्रे जातकर्मादिकाः क्रियाः..
पौरोहित्यं तथा भेजे स्कंदस्यैवाज्ञया प्रभुः.. 29.148 ..
1.4.m: Then the sage performed the birth ceremonies and other rites for him; / and the master took up the office of family priest by Skanda's very command.

1.4.s:
tatastaṃ vahnirabhyāgāddadarśa ca sutaṃ guham..
ṣaṭchīrṣaṃ dviguṇaśrotraṃ dvādaśākṣibhujakramam.. 29.149 ..
1.4.d:
ततस्तं वह्निरभ्यागाद्ददर्श च सुतं गुहम्..
षट्छीर्षं द्विगुणश्रोत्रं द्वादशाक्षिभुजक्रमम्.. 29.149 ..
1.4.m: Then the Fire came to him and saw his son Guha, / with six heads, twice that many ears, and twelve eyes, arms, and feet.

1.4.s:
ekagrīvaṃ caikakāyaṃ kumāraṃ sa vyalokayat..
kalilaṃ prathame cāhni dvitīye vyaktitāṃ gatam.. 29.150 ..
1.4.d:
एकग्रीवं चैककायं कुमारं स व्यलोकयत्..
कलिलं प्रथमे चाह्नि द्वितीये व्यक्तितां गतम्.. 29.150 ..
