1.4.m: the playground of the gods; beyond that is Lokāloka, / a mountain ring-shaped, extending for ten thousand yojanas. 37.25

1.4.s:
asya bāhye tamo ghoraṃ duṣprekṣyaṃ jīvavarjitam..
paṃcatriṃśatsmṛtāḥ koṭyo lakṣāṇyekonaviṃśatiḥ.. 37.26 ..
1.4.d:
अस्य बाह्ये तमो घोरं दुष्प्रेक्ष्यं जीववर्जितम्..
पंचत्रिंशत्स्मृताः कोट्यो लक्षाण्येकोनविंशतिः.. 37.26 ..
1.4.m: Outside of this is dreadful darkness, difficult to gaze upon, devoid of life, / recorded as three hundred and fifty million, nineteen hundred thousand, 37.26

1.4.s:
catvāriṃśatsahasrāṇi yojanānāṃ ca phālguna..
saptasāgaramānastu garbhodastadanaṃtaram.. 37.27 ..
1.4.d:
चत्वारिंशत्सहस्राणि योजनानां च फाल्गुन..
सप्तसागरमानस्तु गर्भोदस्तदनंतरम्.. 37.27 ..
1.4.m: and forty thousand yojanas, O Phālguna. / Immediately after that is the Garbhodaka [ocean], having the measure of the seven oceans; 37.27

1.4.s:
koṭiyojanavistāraḥ kaṭāhaṛ saṃvyavasthitaḥ..
brahmaṇoṃ'ḍaṃ kaṭāhena saṃyuktaṃ merumadhyataḥ.. 37.28 ..
1.4.d:
कोटियोजनविस्तारः कटाहऋ संव्यवस्थितः..
ब्रह्मणोंऽडं कटाहेन संयुक्तं मेरुमध्यतः.. 37.28 ..
1.4.m: the cosmic shell, ten million yojanas in extent, is established. / The egg of Brahmā, joined with the cosmic shell from the center of Meru, 37.28

1.4.s:
paṃcāśatkoṭayo jñeyā daśadikṣu samaṃtataḥ..
jaṃbudvīpasya madhye tu merunāmāsti parvataḥ.. 37.29 ..
1.4.d:
पंचाशत्कोटयो ज्ञेया दशदिक्षु समंततः..
जंबुद्वीपस्य मध्ये तु मेरुनामास्ति पर्वतः.. 37.29 ..
1.4.m: is to be known as five hundred million [yojanas] all around in the ten directions. / In the middle of Jambudvīpa, however, is the mountain named Meru. 37.29

1.4.s:
sa lakṣayojano jñeyo hyadhaścordhvaṃ pramāṇataḥ..
ṣoḍaśaiva sahasrāṇi yojanānāmadhaḥ sthitaḥ.. 37.30 ..
1.4.d:
स लक्षयोजनो ज्ञेयो ह्यधश्चोर्ध्वं प्रमाणतः..
षोडशैव सहस्राणि योजनानामधः स्थितः.. 37.30 ..
1.4.m: It is to be known as measuring one hundred thousand yojanas below and above: / it stands sixteen thousand yojanas below, 37.30

1.4.s:
ucchrayaścaturāśītirdvātriṃśanmūrdhni vistṛtaḥ..
tribhiḥ śṛṃgaiḥ samāyuktaḥ śarāvākṛtimastakaḥ.. 37.31 ..
1.4.d:
उच्छ्रयश्चतुराशीतिर्द्वात्रिंशन्मूर्ध्नि विस्तृतः..
त्रिभिः शृंगैः समायुक्तः शरावाकृतिमस्तकः.. 37.31 ..
1.4.m: its height is eighty-four [thousand], and it is thirty-two [thousand] wide at the summit; / furnished with three peaks, its summit has the shape of a saucer. 37.31

1.4.s:
madhyaśṛṃge brahmavāsa aiśānyāṃ tryaṃbakasya ca..
nairṛtye vāsudevasya hemaśṛṃgaṃ ca brahmaṇaḥ.. 37.32 ..
1.4.d:
मध्यशृंगे ब्रह्मवास ऐशान्यां त्र्यंबकस्य च..
नैरृत्ये वासुदेवस्य हेमशृंगं च ब्रह्मणः.. 37.32 ..
1.4.m: On the central peak is the abode of Brahmā; on the north-east, of Tryambaka; / on the south-west, of Vāsudeva; and the peak of Brahmā is of gold, 37.32

1.4.s:
ratnajaṃ śaṃkarasyāpi rājataṃ keśavasya ca..
merudikṣu catasṛṣu viṣkaṃbhā girayaḥ smṛtāḥ.. 37.33 ..
1.4.d:
रत्नजं शंकरस्यापि राजतं केशवस्य च..
मेरुदिक्षु चतसृषु विष्कंभा गिरयः स्मृताः.. 37.33 ..
1.4.m: that of Śaṃkara is of gems, and that of Keśava is of silver. / In the four directions of Meru, the supporting mountains are recorded: 37.33

1.4.s:
pūrveṇa maṃdaro nāmadakṣiṇe gaṃdhamādanaḥ..
vipulaḥ paścimo jñeyaḥ supārśvastu tathottare.. 37.34 ..
1.4.d:
पूर्वेण मंदरो नामदक्षिणे गंधमादनः..
विपुलः पश्चिमो ज्ञेयः सुपार्श्वस्तु तथोत्तरे.. 37.34 ..
1.4.m: to the east, Mandara by name; to the south, Gandhamādana; / Vipula is to be known to the west, and Supārśva to the north. 37.34

1.4.s:
kadaṃbo maṃdare jñeyojaṃburvai gaṃdhamādane..
aśvattho vipule caiva supārśveca vaṭomataḥ.. 37.35 ..
1.4.d:
कदंबो मंदरे ज्ञेयोजंबुर्वै गंधमादने..
अश्वत्थो विपुले चैव सुपार्श्वेच वटोमतः.. 37.35 ..
1.4.m: The kadamba is to be known on Mandara, the rose-apple tree indeed on Gandhamādana, / the peepal tree on Vipula, and the banyan tree is regarded as on Supārśva. 37.35

1.4.s:
ekādaśaśatāyāmāścatvāro giriketavaḥ..
eteṣāṃ saṃti catvāri vanāni jayamūrdhasu.. 37.36 ..
1.4.d:
एकादशशतायामाश्चत्वारो गिरिकेतवः..
एतेषां संति चत्वारि वनानि जयमूर्धसु.. 37.36 ..
1.4.m: There are four flagstaff-like trees on the mountains, eleven hundred [yojanas] in length. / There are four forests on their glorious peaks: 37.36

1.4.s:
pūrvaṃ caitrarathaṃ nāmadakṣiṇe gaṃdhamādanam..
vaibhrājaṃpaścime jñeyamudakcitrarathaṃ vanam.. 37.37 ..
1.4.d:
पूर्वं चैत्ररथं नामदक्षिणे गंधमादनम्..
वैभ्राजंपश्चिमे ज्ञेयमुदक्चित्ररथं वनम्.. 37.37 ..
1.4.m: to the east, the one named Caitraratha; to the south, Gandhamādana; / Vaibhrāja is to be known to the west, and Citraratha forest to the north. 37.37

1.4.s:
sarāṃsi cāpi catvāri caturdikṣu nibodha me..
prācye'ruṇodasaṃjñaṃ tu mānasaṃ dakṣiṇe saraḥ.. 37.38 ..
1.4.d:
सरांसि चापि चत्वारि चतुर्दिक्षु निबोध मे..
प्राच्येऽरुणोदसंज्ञं तु मानसं दक्षिणे सरः.. 37.38 ..
1.4.m: And learn from me the four lakes in the four directions: / in the east is the lake named Aruṇoda, and Mānasa lake in the south; 37.38

1.4.s:
pratyakchīto dakaṃnāma uttare ca mahāhradaḥ..
viṣkaṃbhagirayo hyeta ucchritāḥ paṃcaviṃśatiḥ.. 37.39 ..
1.4.d:
प्रत्यक्छीतो दकंनाम उत्तरे च महाह्रदः..
विष्कंभगिरयो ह्येत उच्छ्रिताः पंचविंशतिः.. 37.39 ..
1.4.m: in the west, the one named Śītodaka; and in the north, Mahāhrada. / Indeed, these supporting mountains are twenty-five 37.39

1.4.s:
yojanānāṃ sahasrāṇi sahasraṃ piṃḍataḥ smṛtam..
anye ca saṃti bahuśastatra vai kesarācalāḥ.. 37.40 ..
1.4.d:
योजनानां सहस्राणि सहस्रं पिंडतः स्मृतम्..
अन्ये च संति बहुशस्तत्र वै केसराचलाः.. 37.40 ..
1.4.m: thousand yojanas in height, and one thousand in thickness, so it is handed down. / And there are many other filament-mountains there. 37.40

1.4.s:
merordakṣiṇataścaiva trayo maryādaparvatāḥ..
niṣadho hemakūṭaśca himavāniti te trayaḥ.. 37.41 ..
1.4.d:
मेरोर्दक्षिणतश्चैव त्रयो मर्यादपर्वताः..
निषधो हेमकूटश्च हिमवानिति ते त्रयः.. 37.41 ..
1.4.m: And to the south of Meru are three boundary mountains: / Niṣadha, Hemakūṭa, and Himavān—these three, 37.41

1.4.s:
lakṣayojanadīrghāśca vistīrṇā dvisahasrakam..
trayaścottarato merornīlaḥ śveto'tha śrṛṃgavān.. 37.42 ..
1.4.d:
लक्षयोजनदीर्घाश्च विस्तीर्णा द्विसहस्रकम्..
त्रयश्चोत्तरतो मेरोर्नीलः श्वेतोऽथ श्रृंगवान्.. 37.42 ..
1.4.m: one hundred thousand yojanas long and two thousand broad. / And three to the north of Meru: Nīla, Śveta, and Śṛṅgavān. 37.42

1.4.s:
mālyavānpūrvato merorgaṃdhākhyaḥ paścime tathā..
ityete girayaḥ proktā jaṃbudvīpe samaṃtataḥ.. 37.43 ..
1.4.d:
माल्यवान्पूर्वतो मेरोर्गंधाख्यः पश्चिमे तथा..
इत्येते गिरयः प्रोक्ता जंबुद्वीपे समंततः.. 37.43 ..
1.4.m: Mālyavān is to the east of Meru, and likewise the one named Gandhamādana is to the west. / Thus these mountains all around Jambudvīpa have been declared. 37.43

1.4.s:
gaṃdhamādanasaṃsthāyā mahāgajapramāṇataḥ..
phalāni jaṃbavāstannāmnā jaṃbūdvīpamiti smṛtam.. 37.44 ..
1.4.d:
गंधमादनसंस्थाया महागजप्रमाणतः..
फलानि जंबवास्तन्नाम्ना जंबूद्वीपमिति स्मृतम्.. 37.44 ..
1.4.m: From the rose-apple fruits that grow on Gandhamādana, which are the size of great elephants, / it is known by that name as Jambudvīpa. 37.44

1.4.s:
āsītsvāyaṃbhuvonāma manurādyaḥ prajāpatiḥ..
āsītstrī śatarūpā tāmuduvoḍha prajāpatiḥ..
priyavratottānapādau tasyā''stāṃ tanayāvubhau.. 37.45 ..
1.4.d:
आसीत्स्वायंभुवोनाम मनुराद्यः प्रजापतिः..
आसीत्स्त्री शतरूपा तामुदुवोढ प्रजापतिः..
प्रियव्रतोत्तानपादौ तस्या'ऽस्तां तनयावुभौ.. 37.45 ..
1.4.m: There was a first progenitor named Svāyambhuva Manu. / There was a woman, Śatarūpā; the progenitor took her in marriage. / Priyavrata and Uttānapāda were both her sons. 37.45

1.4.s:
dhruvaścottānapādasya putraḥ paramadhārmikaḥ..
bhaktyā sa viṣṇumārādhya sthānaṃ caivākṣayaṃ gataḥ.. 37.46 ..
1.4.d:
ध्रुवश्चोत्तानपादस्य पुत्रः परमधार्मिकः..
भक्त्या स विष्णुमाराध्य स्थानं चैवाक्षयं गतः.. 37.46 ..
1.4.m: And Dhruva, the supreme observer of dharma, was Uttānapāda's son. / Having worshipped Viṣṇu with devotion, he attained an imperishable place. 37.46

1.4.s:
priyavratasya rājarṣerutpannā daśa sūnavaḥ..
trayaḥ pravrajitāstatra paraṃbrahma samāśritāḥ.. 37.47 ..
1.4.d:
प्रियव्रतस्य राजर्षेरुत्पन्ना दश सूनवः..
त्रयः प्रव्रजितास्तत्र परंब्रह्म समाश्रिताः.. 37.47 ..
1.4.m: Ten sons were born to the royal sage Priyavrata. / Three among them renounced the world and took refuge in the supreme Brahman. 37.47

1.4.s:
sapta saptasu dvīpeṣu tena putrāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ..
jaṃbūdvīpādhipo jyeṣṭha āgnīdhra iti viśrutaḥ.. 37.48 ..
1.4.d:
सप्त सप्तसु द्वीपेषु तेन पुत्राः प्रतिष्ठिताः..
जंबूद्वीपाधिपो ज्येष्ठ आग्नीध्र इति विश्रुतः.. 37.48 ..
1.4.m: Seven sons were installed by him across the seven continents. / The eldest, known as Āgnīdhra, was the ruler of Jambudvīpa. 37.48

1.4.s:
tasyāsannava sutāḥ pārtha navavarṣeśvarāḥ smṛtāḥ..
teṣāṃ nāmnā ca te varṣāstiṣṭhaṃtyadyāpi cāṃkitāḥ.. 37.49 ..
1.4.d:
तस्यासन्नव सुताः पार्थ नववर्षेश्वराः स्मृताः..
तेषां नाम्ना च ते वर्षास्तिष्ठंत्यद्यापि चांकिताः.. 37.49 ..
1.4.m: He had nine sons, O son of Pṛthā, traditionally known as rulers of nine realms. / Even today, those realms remain marked with their names. 37.49

1.4.s:
yojanānāṃ sahasrāṇi nava pratyekaśaḥ smṛtāḥ..
meroścaturdaśaṃ khaṃḍaṃ gaṃdhamālyavatordvayoḥ.. 37.50 ..
1.4.d:
योजनानां सहस्राणि नव प्रत्येकशः स्मृताः..
मेरोश्चतुर्दशं खंडं गंधमाल्यवतोर्द्वयोः.. 37.50 ..
1.4.m: Each one is said to measure nine thousand yojanas. / The fourteenth section of Meru lies between the two, Gandhamādana and Mālyavān; 37.50

1.4.s:
aṃtare hemabhūmiṣṭhamilāvṛtamihocyate..
mālyavatsāgarāṃtasya bhadrāśvamiti procyate.. 37.51 ..
1.4.d:
अंतरे हेमभूमिष्ठमिलावृतमिहोच्यते..
माल्यवत्सागरांतस्य भद्राश्वमिति प्रोच्यते.. 37.51 ..
1.4.m: situated on the golden land between them, it is here called Ilāvṛta. / The land extending from Mālyavān to the ocean is called Bhadrāśva. 37.51

1.4.s: gaṃdhavatsāgarāṃtasya ketumālamiti smṛtam.. 37.52 ..
1.4.d: गंधवत्सागरांतस्य केतुमालमिति स्मृतम्.. 37.52 ..
1.4.m: The land extending from Gandhamādana to the ocean is known as Ketumāla. 37.52

1.4.s:
śrṛṃgavajjaladheraṃtaḥ kurukhaṃḍamiti smṛtam..
śrṛṃgavacchvetamadhye ca khaṇḍaṃ proktaṃ hiraṇmayam.. 37.53 ..
1.4.d:
श्रृंगवज्जलधेरंतः कुरुखंडमिति स्मृतम्..
श्रृंगवच्छ्वेतमध्ये च खण्डं प्रोक्तं हिरण्मयम्.. 37.53 ..
1.4.m: The region between Śṛṅgavān and the ocean is known as the Kuru realm. / Between Śṛṅgavān and Śveta, the realm is said to be Hiraṇmaya. 37.53

1.4.s:
sunīlaśvetayormadhye khaṃḍamāhuśca ramyakam..
niṣadho hemakūṭaśca harikhaṃḍaṃ tadaṃtarā.. 37.54 ..
1.4.d:
सुनीलश्वेतयोर्मध्ये खंडमाहुश्च रम्यकम्..
निषधो हेमकूटश्च हरिखंडं तदंतरा.. 37.54 ..
1.4.m: Between beautiful Nīla and Śveta, they call the realm Ramyaka. / Between Niṣadha and Hemakūṭa lies the Harikhaṇḍa realm. 37.54

1.4.s:
himavaddhimakūṭāṃtaḥ khaṇḍaṃ kiṃpuruṣaṃ smṛtam..
himādrijaladherantarnābhi khaṇḍamiti smṛtam.. 37.55 ..
1.4.d:
हिमवद्धिमकूटांतः खण्डं किंपुरुषं स्मृतम्..
हिमाद्रिजलधेरन्तर्नाभि खण्डमिति स्मृतम्.. 37.55 ..
1.4.m: Between the snowy mountain and Hemakūṭa, the realm is known as Kiṃpuruṣa. / Between the snowy mountain and the ocean, the realm is known as Nābhi. 37.55

1.4.s:
nābhikhaṇḍaṃ ca kuravo dve varṣe dhanupākṛtī..
himavāṃśca giriśrṛṃgī jyāsthāne parikīrtitau.. 37.56 ..
1.4.d:
नाभिखण्डं च कुरवो द्वे वर्षे धनुपाकृती..
हिमवांश्च गिरिश्रृंगी ज्यास्थाने परिकीर्तितौ.. 37.56 ..
1.4.m: The realm of Nābhi and Kuru are two realms shaped like bows; / the snowy mountain and Mount Śṛṅgavān are declared to stand in the place of bowstrings. 37.56

1.4.s:
nābheḥ putraśca ṛṣabha ṛṣabhādbarato'bhavat..
tasya nāmnā tvidaṃ varṣaṃ bhārataṃ ceti kīrtyate.. 37.57 ..
1.4.d:
नाभेः पुत्रश्च ऋषभ ऋषभाद्बरतोऽभवत्..
तस्य नाम्ना त्विदं वर्षं भारतं चेति कीर्त्यते.. 37.57 ..
1.4.m: The son of Nābhi was Ṛṣabha, and from Ṛṣabha came Bharata. / By his name, this realm is celebrated as Bhārata. 37.57

1.4.s:
atra dharmārthakāmānāṃ mokṣasya ca upārjanam..
anyatra bhogabhūmiśca sarvatra kurunaṃdana.. 37.58 ..
1.4.d:
अत्र धर्मार्थकामानां मोक्षस्य च उपार्जनम्..
अन्यत्र भोगभूमिश्च सर्वत्र कुरुनंदन.. 37.58 ..
1.4.m: Here [alone] is the acquisition of dharma, wealth, pleasure, and liberation; / elsewhere, everywhere [is a] land of enjoyment, O delight of the Kurus. 37.58

1.4.s:
śākadvīpe ca śāko'sti yojanānāṃ sahasrakaḥ..
tasya nāmnā ca tadvarṣaṃ śākadvīpamiti smṛtam.. 37.59 ..
1.4.d:
शाकद्वीपे च शाकोऽस्ति योजनानां सहस्रकः..
तस्य नाम्ना च तद्वर्षं शाकद्वीपमिति स्मृतम्.. 37.59 ..
1.4.m: In Śākadvīpa there is a teak tree measuring a thousand yojanas. / By its name, that realm is known as Śākadvīpa. 37.59

1.4.s: tasya ca priyavrata evādhipatirnāmnā medhātithiriti.. 37.60 ..
1.4.d: तस्य च प्रियव्रत एवाधिपतिर्नाम्ना मेधातिथिरिति.. 37.60 ..
1.4.m: And its ruler was a son of Priyavrata named Medhātithi. 37.60

1.4.s: tasya purojavamanojavavepamānadhūmrānīkacitrarephabahurūpaviśvacārasaṃjñāni putranāmāni sapta varṣāṇi.. 37.61 ..
1.4.d: तस्य पुरोजवमनोजववेपमानधूम्रानीकचित्ररेफबहुरूपविश्वचारसंज्ञानि पुत्रनामानि सप्त वर्षाणि.. 37.61 ..
1.4.m: His seven realms bear the names of his sons: Purojava, Manojava, Vepamāna, Dhūmrānīka, Citrarepha, Bahurūpa, and Viśvacāra. 37.61

1.4.s: śākadvīpe ca varṣa ṛtavratasatyavratānuvratanāmāno vāyyavātkamaṃ bhagavaṃtaṃ japaṃti.. 37.62 ..
1.4.d: शाकद्वीपे च वर्ष ऋतव्रतसत्यव्रतानुव्रतनामानो वाय्यवात्कमं भगवंतं जपंति.. 37.62 ..
1.4.m: In Śākadvīpa, the [classes] of the realm named Ṛtavrata, Satyavrata, and Anuvrata chant [the praise of] the blessed Lord in the form of wind: 37.62

1.4.s:
aṃtaḥ praviśya bhūtāni yo vibhajyātmaketubhiḥ..
aṃtaryāmīśvaraḥ sākṣātpātu no yadvaśe jagat.. 37.63 ..
1.4.d:
अंतः प्रविश्य भूतानि यो विभज्यात्मकेतुभिः..
अंतर्यामीश्वरः साक्षात्पातु नो यद्वशे जगत्.. 37.63 ..
1.4.m: "May the inner controller, the Lord himself, protect us, who, entering into beings and dividing them with his own marks, holds the universe under his sway." 37.63

1.4.s:
..iti japaḥ..
kuśadvīpe kuśastaṃbo yojanānāṃ sahasrakaḥ..
taccihnacihnitaṃ tasmātkuśadvīpaṃ tataḥ smṛtam.. 37.64 ..
1.4.d:
..इति जपः..
कुशद्वीपे कुशस्तंबो योजनानां सहस्रकः..
तच्चिह्नचिह्नितं तस्मात्कुशद्वीपं ततः स्मृतम्.. 37.64 ..
1.4.m: Thus ends the prayer. / In Kuśadvīpa there is a clump of kuśa grass measuring a thousand yojanas. / Because it is marked by that sign, it is therefore known as Kuśadvīpa. 37.64

1.4.s:
taddvīpapatiśca praiyavrato hiraṇyaromā tatputravasuvasudānadṛḍhakavinābhiguptasatyavratavāmadevanāmāṃkitāni sapta varṣāṇi..
varṇāśca kuliśakovidābhiyuktakulakasaṃjñā jātavedasaṃ bhagavaṃtaṃ stuvaṃti.. 37.65 ..
1.4.d:
तद्द्वीपपतिश्च प्रैयव्रतो हिरण्यरोमा तत्पुत्रवसुवसुदानदृढकविनाभिगुप्तसत्यव्रतवामदेवनामांकितानि सप्त वर्षाणि..
वर्णाश्च कुलिशकोविदाभियुक्तकुलकसंज्ञा जातवेदसं भगवंतं स्तुवंति.. 37.65 ..
1.4.m: The lord of that continent is Hiraṇyaroman, a son of Priyavrata. Its seven realms are marked by the names of his sons: Vasu, Vasudāna, Dṛḍhakavi, Nābhigupta, Satyavrata, and Vāmadeva. / And the classes, named Kuliśa, Kovida, Abhiyukta, and Kulaka, praise the blessed Jātavedas: 37.65

1.4.s:
parasya brahṇaḥ sākṣājjātavedāsi havyavāṭ..
devānāṃ puruṣāṃgānāṃ yajñena puruṣaṃ yajaḥ.. 37.66 ..
1.4.d:
परस्य ब्रह्णः साक्षाज्जातवेदासि हव्यवाट्..
देवानां पुरुषांगानां यज्ञेन पुरुषं यजः.. 37.66 ..
1.4.m: "Thou art the bearer of oblations, the manifest Jātavedas of the supreme Brahman. / Worship the Puruṣa through sacrifice on behalf of the gods, who are limbs of the Puruṣa." 37.66

1.4.s:
..iti stutiḥ..
krauṃcadvīpe krauṃcanāmā parvato yojanāyataḥ..
yo'sau guhena nirbhinnastaccihnaṃ krauṃcadvīpakam.. 37.67 ..
1.4.d:
..इति स्तुतिः..
क्रौंचद्वीपे क्रौंचनामा पर्वतो योजनायतः..
योऽसौ गुहेन निर्भिन्नस्तच्चिह्नं क्रौंचद्वीपकम्.. 37.67 ..
1.4.m: Thus ends the praise. / In Krauñcadvīpa there is a mountain named Krauñca, a yojana in extent, / which was pierced by Guha; by that sign it is Krauñcadvīpa. 37.67

1.4.s: tatra ca praiyavrato ghṛtapṛṣṭināmā tatputrāmamadhuruhameghapṛṣṭhasvadāmaṛtāśvalohitārṇavavanaspatiitisaptaputranāmāṃkitāni sapta varṣāṇi.. 37.68 ..
1.4.d: तत्र च प्रैयव्रतो घृतपृष्टिनामा तत्पुत्राममधुरुहमेघपृष्ठस्वदामऋताश्वलोहितार्णववनस्पतिइतिसप्तपुत्रनामांकितानि सप्त वर्षाणि.. 37.68 ..
1.4.m: And there the son of Priyavrata named Ghṛtapṛṣṭha [rules]; its seven realms are marked with the names of his seven sons: Madhuruha, Meghapṛṣṭha, Svadāman, Ṛtāśva, Lohitārṇava, and Vanaspati. 37.68

1.4.s: varṇāśca guruṛṣabhadraviṇadevakasaṃjñāḥ.. 37.69 ..
1.4.d: वर्णाश्च गुरुऋषभद्रविणदेवकसंज्ञाः.. 37.69 ..
1.4.m: And the classes are named Guru, Ṛṣabha, Draviṇa, and Devaka. 37.69

1.4.s: āpomayaṃ bhagavaṃtaṃ stuvaṃti.. 37.70 ..
1.4.d: आपोमयं भगवंतं स्तुवंति.. 37.70 ..
1.4.m: They praise the blessed Lord whose form is water: 37.70

1.4.s:
āpaḥ puruṣavīryāśca punaṃtīrbhūrbhūvaḥsvaśca..
taiḥ punaramīvaghnāḥsaṃspṛśetātmanā bhuvaḥ.. 37.71 ..
1.4.d:
आपः पुरुषवीर्याश्च पुनंतीर्भूर्भूवःस्वश्च..
तैः पुनरमीवघ्नाःसंस्पृशेतात्मना भुवः.. 37.71 ..
1.4.m: "Waters, which are the seed of the Puruṣa, purifying earth, atmosphere, and heaven, / destroying illness, may they again touch the earth along with the self." 37.71

1.4.s:
..iti japaḥ..
śālmalernāma vṛkṣasya tatravāsaḥ sahasraṃ yojanānāṃ taccihnaṃ śālmalidvipamucyate.. 37.72 ..
1.4.d:
..इति जपः..
शाल्मलेर्नाम वृक्षस्य तत्रवासः सहस्रं योजनानां तच्चिह्नं शाल्मलिद्विपमुच्यते.. 37.72 ..
1.4.m: Thus ends the prayer. / A śālmali tree stands there, a thousand yojanas in height; by that sign it is called Śālmalidvīpa. 37.72

1.4.s: tasyādhipatiḥ praiyavrato yajñabāhustatputrasurocanasaumanasyaramaṇakadevabarhipāribhadrāpyāyanābhijñānanāmāni saptavarṣāṇi.. 37.73 ..
1.4.d: तस्याधिपतिः प्रैयव्रतो यज्ञबाहुस्तत्पुत्रसुरोचनसौमनस्यरमणकदेवबर्हिपारिभद्राप्यायनाभिज्ञाननामानि सप्तवर्षाणि.. 37.73 ..
1.4.m: Its ruler is Yajñabāhu, a son of Priyavrata; its seven realms bear the names of his sons: Surocana, Saumanasya, Ramaṇaka, Devabarhis, Pāribhadra, Āpyāyana, and Abhijñāna. 37.73

1.4.s: varṇāśca śrutadharavīryavasuṃdharaiṣaṃdharasaṃjñā bhagavaṃtaṃ somaṃ yajaṃti.. 37.74 ..
1.4.d: वर्णाश्च श्रुतधरवीर्यवसुंधरैषंधरसंज्ञा भगवंतं सोमं यजंति.. 37.74 ..
1.4.m: And the classes, named Śrutadhara, Vīrya, Vasundhara, and Iṣandhara, worship the blessed Soma: 37.74

1.4.s:
svayoniḥ pitṛdevebhyo vibhajañchuklakṛṣṇayoḥ..
adhaḥ prajānāṃ sarvāsāṃ rājā naḥ somostu.. 37.75 ..
1.4.d:
स्वयोनिः पितृदेवेभ्यो विभजञ्छुक्लकृष्णयोः..
अधः प्रजानां सर्वासां राजा नः सोमोस्तु.. 37.75 ..
1.4.m: "Distributing the bright and dark fortnights from his own source to the ancestors and gods, / below, may Soma be the king of all our subjects." 37.75

1.4.s:
iti japaḥ gomedanāmā plakṣosti suramyo yasya cchāyayā..
modovṛddhiṃ gataṃ laulyādgomedaṃ dvīpamucyate.. 37.76 ..
1.4.d:
इति जपः गोमेदनामा प्लक्षोस्ति सुरम्यो यस्य च्छायया..
मोदोवृद्धिं गतं लौल्याद्गोमेदं द्वीपमुच्यते.. 37.76 ..
1.4.m: Thus ends the prayer. There is a very charming plakṣa tree named Gomeda, under whose shade / joy increased; by reason of eagerness, the continent is called Gomeda. 37.76

1.4.s: tatra praiyavrata idhmajihvaḥ patistatputrasivasuramyasubhadra śāṃtyaśaptamṛtābhayanāmāṃkitāni sapta varṣāṇi.. 37.77 ..
1.4.d: तत्र प्रैयव्रत इध्मजिह्वः पतिस्तत्पुत्रसिवसुरम्यसुभद्र शांत्यशप्तमृताभयनामांकितानि सप्त वर्षाणि.. 37.77 ..
1.4.m: There, the son of Priyavrata named Idhmajihva is the lord; its seven realms are marked with the names of his sons: Śiva, Suramya, Subhadra, Śānti, Aśama, Ṛta, and Abhaya. 37.77

1.4.s: varṇāśca haṃsapataṃgordhvāṃcanasatyāṃgasaṃjñāścatvāro bhagavaṃtaṃ sūryaṃ yajaṃte.. 37.78 ..
1.4.d: वर्णाश्च हंसपतंगोर्ध्वांचनसत्यांगसंज्ञाश्चत्वारो भगवंतं सूर्यं यजंते.. 37.78 ..
1.4.m: And the four classes, named Haṃsa, Pataṅga, Ūrdhvāñcana, and Satyāṅga, worship the blessed Sūrya: 37.78

1.4.s:
praśrasya viṣṇurūpaṃyattatrotthasya brahmaṇo'mṛtasya ca..
mṛtyośca sūryamātmānaṃ dhīmahi.. 37.79 ..
1.4.d:
प्रश्रस्य विष्णुरूपंयत्तत्रोत्थस्य ब्रह्मणोऽमृतस्य च..
मृत्योश्च सूर्यमात्मानं धीमहि.. 37.79 ..
1.4.m: "May we meditate upon Sūrya, the self, the form of Viṣṇu of the ancient [one], arisen there from Brahman, of immortality and death." 37.79

1.4.s:
..iti japaḥ..
svarṇapatrāṇi niyutaṃ yojanānāṃ sahasrakam..
puṣkaraṃ jvaladā bhāti taccihnaṃ dvīpapuṣkaram.. 37.80 ..
1.4.d:
..इति जपः..
स्वर्णपत्राणि नियुतं योजनानां सहस्रकम्..
पुष्करं ज्वलदा भाति तच्चिह्नं द्वीपपुष्करम्.. 37.80 ..
1.4.m: Thus ends the prayer. / A lotus with golden petals, radiant, measuring a million and a thousand yojanas, / shines like a flame; by that sign the continent is Puṣkara. 37.80

1.4.s: tasyādhipatiḥ praiyavrato vītahotranāmā tatputrau ramaṇakaghātakau.. 37.81 ..
1.4.d: तस्याधिपतिः प्रैयव्रतो वीतहोत्रनामा तत्पुत्रौ रमणकघातकौ.. 37.81 ..
1.4.m: Its ruler is a son of Priyavrata named Vītahotra; his two sons are Ramaṇaka and Ghātaka. 37.81

1.4.s: tannāmacihnataṃ khaṃḍadvayam.. 37.82 ..
1.4.d: तन्नामचिह्नतं खंडद्वयम्.. 37.82 ..
1.4.m: The two sections are marked with their names. 37.82

1.4.s: tayoraṃtarālemānasācalo nāma valayākāraḥ parvato yasminbhramati bhagavānbhāskara iti.. 37.83 ..
1.4.d: तयोरंतरालेमानसाचलो नाम वलयाकारः पर्वतो यस्मिन्भ्रमति भगवान्भास्कर इति.. 37.83 ..
1.4.m: Between them is a ring-shaped mountain named Mānasācala, upon which the blessed sun revolves. 37.83

1.4.s: tatra varṇāśca na saṃti kevalaṃ samānāste brahma dhyāyaṃti.. 37.84 ..
1.4.d: तत्र वर्णाश्च न संति केवलं समानास्ते ब्रह्म ध्यायंति.. 37.84 ..
1.4.m: There are no classes there; being all equal, they meditate upon Brahman alone: 37.84

1.4.s:
yadyatkarmamayaṃ liṃgaṃ brahmaliṃgaṃ janorcayan..
bhedenaikāṃtamadvaitaṃ tasmai bhagavate namaḥ.. 37.85 ..
1.4.d:
यद्यत्कर्ममयं लिंगं ब्रह्मलिंगं जनोर्चयन्..
भेदेनैकांतमद्वैतं तस्मै भगवते नमः.. 37.85 ..
1.4.m: "Whatever linga consists of ritual action, while people worship the Brahman-liṅga, / being essentially one non-dual [reality] amid distinction—homage to that blessed Lord." 37.85

1.4.s:
..iti japaḥ..
naiṣu krodho na mātsaryaṃ puṇyapāpārjanena ca..
ayutaṃ dviguṇaṃ cāpi kramādāyuḥ prakīrtitam.. 37.86 ..
1.4.d:
..इति जपः..
नैषु क्रोधो न मात्सर्यं पुण्यपापार्जनेन च..
अयुतं द्विगुणं चापि क्रमादायुः प्रकीर्तितम्.. 37.86 ..
1.4.m: Thus ends the prayer. / In these [continents] there is neither anger nor malice through the acquisition of merit and sin; / and the lifespan is proclaimed to double progressively from ten thousand [years]. 37.86

1.4.s:
japaṃtaḥ kāminīyuktā viharaṃtyamarā iva..
atha te saṃpravakṣyāmi ūrdhvalokasya saṃsthitim.. 37.87 ..
iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ prathame māheśvarakhaṇḍe kaumārikākhaṇḍe kumārikākhyāne bhūsaṃsthitivarṇanaṃnāma spatatriṃśo'dhyāyaḥ.. 37 .. cha ..
1.4.d:
जपंतः कामिनीयुक्ता विहरंत्यमरा इव..
अथ ते संप्रवक्ष्यामि ऊर्ध्वलोकस्य संस्थितिम्.. 37.87 ..
इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां प्रथमे माहेश्वरखण्डे कौमारिकाखण्डे कुमारिकाख्याने भूसंस्थितिवर्णनंनाम स्पतत्रिंशोऽध्यायः.. 37 .. छ ..
1.4.m:
Chanting, accompanied by loving women, they sport like the immortals.
Now I will describe to you the arrangement of the upper world.
Thus ends the thirty-seventh chapter, entitled 'Description of the Situation of the Earth,' in the Kumārikākhaṇḍa of the first section, the Māheśvarakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa of eighty-one thousand verses.

1.4.s:
..nārada uvāca..
bhūmeryojanalakṣe ca kauravya ravimaṃḍalam..
yojanānāṃ sahasrāṇi bhāskarasya ratho nava.. 38.1 ..
1.4.d:
..नारद उवाच..
भूमेर्योजनलक्षे च कौरव्य रविमंडलम्..
योजनानां सहस्राणि भास्करस्य रथो नव.. 38.1 ..
1.4.m:
Nārada said:
At one hundred thousand yojanas from the earth, O Kauravya, is the orb of the sun.
The chariot of the sun is nine thousand yojanas [in extent].

1.4.s:
īṣādaṃḍastataivāsya dviguṇaḥ parikīrtitaḥ..
sārdhakoṭistathā sapta niyutāni vivasvataḥ.. 38.2 ..
1.4.d:
ईषादंडस्ततैवास्य द्विगुणः परिकीर्तितः..
सार्धकोटिस्तथा सप्त नियुतानि विवस्वतः.. 38.2 ..
1.4.m:
Its pole is described as being twice that measure.
And the axle of the sun measures fifteen million seven hundred thousand [yojanas].

1.4.s:
yojanānāṃ tu tasyākṣastatra cakraṃ pratiṣṭhitam..
trinābhi tacca paṃcāraṃ ṣaṇnemi parikīrtitam.. 38.3 ..
1.4.d:
योजनानां तु तस्याक्षस्तत्र चक्रं प्रतिष्ठितम्..
त्रिनाभि तच्च पंचारं षण्नेमि परिकीर्तितम्.. 38.3 ..
1.4.m:
Upon its axle of yojanas, the wheel is mounted;
it is described as having three naves, five spokes, and six fellies.

1.4.s:
catvāriṃśatsahasrāṇi dvitīyo'kṣo'pi vistṛtaḥ..
paṃca cānyāni sārddhāni syandanasya tu pāṃḍava.. 38.4 ..
1.4.d:
चत्वारिंशत्सहस्राणि द्वितीयोऽक्षोऽपि विस्तृतः..
पंच चान्यानि सार्द्धानि स्यन्दनस्य तु पांडव.. 38.4 ..
1.4.m:
The second axle extends for forty-five thousand and a half [yojanas],
O Pāṇḍava, belonging to the chariot.

1.4.s:
akṣapramāṇamubhayoḥ pramāṇaṃ tadyugārddhayoḥ..
hrasvo'kṣastadyugārddhaṃ ca dhruvādhāraṃ rathasya vai.. 38.5 ..
1.4.d:
अक्षप्रमाणमुभयोः प्रमाणं तद्युगार्द्धयोः..
ह्रस्वोऽक्षस्तद्युगार्द्धं च ध्रुवाधारं रथस्य वै.. 38.5 ..
1.4.m:
The measure of the two axles is the measure of the two halves of the yoke.
The shorter axle and half the yoke are supported by Dhruva, for the chariot.

1.4.s:
dvitīyo'kṣastathā savye cakraṃ tanmānase sthitam..
hayāśca sapta cchāṃdāṃsi teṣāṃ nāmāni me śrṛṇu.. 38.6 ..
1.4.d:
द्वितीयोऽक्षस्तथा सव्ये चक्रं तन्मानसे स्थितम्..
हयाश्च सप्त च्छांदांसि तेषां नामानि मे श्रृणु.. 38.6 ..
1.4.m:
The second axle is on the left, and that wheel rests on Mount Mānasa.
The horses are the seven meters; hear their names from me:

1.4.s:
gāyatrī ca bṛhatyuṣṇigjagatī triṣṭuveva ca..
anuṣṭuppaṃktirityuktāśchaṃdāṃsi harayo raveḥ.. 38.7 ..
1.4.d:
गायत्री च बृहत्युष्णिग्जगती त्रिष्टुवेव च..
अनुष्टुप्पंक्तिरित्युक्ताश्छंदांसि हरयो रवेः.. 38.7 ..
1.4.m:
Gāyatrī, Bṛhatī, Uṣṇih, Jagatī, and Triṣṭubh,
Anuṣṭubh, and Paṅkti are said to be the meters that are the horses of the sun.

1.4.s:
naivāstamanamarkasya nodayaḥ sarvadā sataḥ..
udayāstamanākyaṃ hi darśanādarśanaṃ raveḥ.. 38.8 ..
1.4.d:
नैवास्तमनमर्कस्य नोदयः सर्वदा सतः..
उदयास्तमनाक्यं हि दर्शनादर्शनं रवेः.. 38.8 ..
1.4.m:
There is never setting nor rising for the sun, which exists always;
its rising and setting are merely its being seen and not being seen.

1.4.s:
śakradīnāṃ pure tiṣṭhanspṛśatyeṣa puratrayam..
vikīrṇo'to vikarṇasthastrikoṇārdhapure tathā.. 38.9 ..
1.4.d:
शक्रदीनां पुरे तिष्ठन्स्पृशत्येष पुरत्रयम्..
विकीर्णोऽतो विकर्णस्थस्त्रिकोणार्धपुरे तथा.. 38.9 ..
1.4.m:
Standing in the city of Śakra and the others, he touches the three cities;
thus spread out, standing at the diagonal, and likewise in the half-city at the triangle,

1.4.s:
ayanasyottarasyādau makaraṃ yāti bhāskaraḥ..
tataḥ kumbhaṃ ca mīnaṃ ca rāśe rāśyaṃtaraṃ tathā.. 38.10 ..
1.4.d:
अयनस्योत्तरस्यादौ मकरं याति भास्करः..
ततः कुम्भं च मीनं च राशे राश्यंतरं तथा.. 38.10 ..
1.4.m:
at the beginning of the northern course, the sun enters Capricorn;
then Aquarius and Pisces, thus passing from one sign of the zodiac to another.

1.4.s:
triṣveteṣvatha bhukteṣu tato vaiṣuvatīṃ gatim..
prayāti savitā kurvannahorātraṃ ca tatsamam.. 38.11 ..
1.4.d:
त्रिष्वेतेष्वथ भुक्तेषु ततो वैषुवतीं गतिम्..
प्रयाति सविता कुर्वन्नहोरात्रं च तत्समम्.. 38.11 ..
1.4.m:
When he has passed through these three, the sun then goes
on the equinoctial course, making day and night equal.

1.4.s:
tato rātriḥ kṣayaṃ yāti vardhate tu dinaṃ dinam..
tataśca mithunasyāṃte parāṃ kāṣṭhāmupāgataḥ.. 38.12 ..
1.4.d:
ततो रात्रिः क्षयं याति वर्धते तु दिनं दिनम्..
ततश्च मिथुनस्यांते परां काष्ठामुपागतः.. 38.12 ..
1.4.m:
From then on the night decreases and the day increases day by day.
Then, at the end of Gemini, having reached the highest point,

1.4.s:
rāśiṃ karkaṭakaṃ prāpya kurute dakṣiṇāyāṃnam..
kulālacakraparyaṃto yathā śīghraṃ nivartate.. 38.13 ..
1.4.d:
राशिं कर्कटकं प्राप्य कुरुते दक्षिणायांनम्..
कुलालचक्रपर्यंतो यथा शीघ्रं निवर्तते.. 38.13 ..
1.4.m:
and arrived at the sign of Cancer, he begins his southern course.
Just as the rim of a potter's wheel revolves swiftly,

1.4.s:
dakṣiṇāyakrame sūryastathā śīghraṃ nivartate..
ativegitayā kālaṃ vāyumārgabalāccaran.. 38.14 ..
1.4.d:
दक्षिणायक्रमे सूर्यस्तथा शीघ्रं निवर्तते..
अतिवेगितया कालं वायुमार्गबलाच्चरन्.. 38.14 ..
1.4.m:
so in the course of the southern journey the sun revolves swiftly,
moving through time with great velocity by the force of the wind's path.

1.4.s:
tasmātprakṛṣṭāṃ bhūmiṃ sa kālenālpena gacchati..
kulālacakramadhyastho yatā maṃdaṃ prasarpati.. 38.15 ..
1.4.d:
तस्मात्प्रकृष्टां भूमिं स कालेनाल्पेन गच्छति..
कुलालचक्रमध्यस्थो यता मंदं प्रसर्पति.. 38.15 ..
1.4.m:
Therefore, he travels over a vast distance of the earth in a short time.
Just as what is at the center of a potter's wheel moves slowly,

1.4.s:
tathodagayane sūryaḥ sarpate maṃdavikramaḥ..
tasmāddīrgheṇa kālena bhūmimalpaṃ nigacchati.. 38.16 ..
1.4.d:
तथोदगयने सूर्यः सर्पते मंदविक्रमः..
तस्माद्दीर्घेण कालेन भूमिमल्पं निगच्छति.. 38.16 ..
1.4.m:
so in the northern course the sun moves with slow speed;
therefore, in a long time he traverses a small extent of the earth.

1.4.s:
saṃdhyākāle ca maṃdehāḥ sūryamicchaṃti khāditum..
prajāpatikṛtaḥ śāpasteṣāṃ phālguna rakṣasām.. 38.17 ..
1.4.d:
संध्याकाले च मंदेहाः सूर्यमिच्छंति खादितुम्..
प्रजापतिकृतः शापस्तेषां फाल्गुन रक्षसाम्.. 38.17 ..
1.4.m:
At twilight the Mandehas desire to devour the sun.
A curse was laid upon those demons by Prajāpati, O Phālguna:

1.4.s:
akṣayatvaṃ śarīrāṇāṃ maraṇaṃ ca dinedine..
tataḥ sūryasya tairyuddhaṃ bhavatyatyaṃtadāruṇam.. 38.18 ..
1.4.d:
अक्षयत्वं शरीराणां मरणं च दिनेदिने..
ततः सूर्यस्य तैर्युद्धं भवत्यत्यंतदारुणम्.. 38.18 ..
1.4.m:
the imperishability of their bodies, and their death day after day.
Then between them and the sun a most dreadful battle takes place.

1.4.s:
tato gāyatripūtaṃ yaddvijāstoyaṃ kṣipaṃti ca..
tena dahyaṃti te pāpāḥ saṃdhyopāsanataḥ sadā.. 38.19 ..
1.4.d:
ततो गायत्रिपूतं यद्द्विजास्तोयं क्षिपंति च..
तेन दह्यंति ते पापाः संध्योपासनतः सदा.. 38.19 ..
1.4.m:
Then, the water purified by the Gāyatrī which the twice-born cast,
by that are those evil beings burned away through the twilight worship at all times.

1.4.s:
ye saṃdhyāṃ nāpyupāsaṃte kṛtaghnā yāṃti rauravam..
pratimāsaṃ pṛthaksūrya ṛṣigandharvarākṣasaiḥ.. 38.20 ..
1.4.d:
ये संध्यां नाप्युपासंते कृतघ्ना यांति रौरवम्..
प्रतिमासं पृथक्सूर्य ऋषिगन्धर्वराक्षसैः.. 38.20 ..
1.4.m:
Those who do not perform twilight worship, ungrateful, go to Raurava.
Month by month the sun travels separately accompanied by seven:

1.4.s:
apsarogrāmaṇīsarpairatho yāti ca saptabhiḥ..
dhātāryamā mitravaruṇau vivasvānindra eva ca.. 38.21 ..
1.4.d:
अप्सरोग्रामणीसर्पैरथो याति च सप्तभिः..
धातार्यमा मित्रवरुणौ विवस्वानिन्द्र एव च.. 38.21 ..
1.4.m:
by seers, gandharvas, rākṣasas, apsarases, village-leaders, and serpents.
Dhātṛ, Aryaman, Mitra and Varuṇa, Vivasvat, and Indra,

1.4.s:
pūṣā ca savitā so'tha bhagastvaṣṭā ca kīrtitaḥ..
viṣṇuścaitrādimāseṣu ādityā dvādaśa smṛtāḥ.. 38.22 ..
1.4.d:
पूषा च सविता सोऽथ भगस्त्वष्टा च कीर्तितः..
विष्णुश्चैत्रादिमासेषु आदित्या द्वादश स्मृताः.. 38.22 ..
1.4.m:
Pūṣan, Savitṛ, Bhaga, and Tvaṣṭṛ are declared,
and Viṣṇu: these are remembered as the twelve Ādityas in the months beginning with Caitra.

1.4.s:
tato divākarasthānānmaṃḍalaṃ śaśinaḥ sthitam..
lakṣamātreṇa tasyāpi tricakro ratha ucyate.. 38.23 ..
1.4.d:
ततो दिवाकरस्थानान्मंडलं शशिनः स्थितम्..
लक्षमात्रेण तस्यापि त्रिचक्रो रथ उच्यते.. 38.23 ..
1.4.m:
From the station of the sun, the orb of the moon is situated
at a distance of one hundred thousand [yojanas]; his chariot is said to have three wheels.

1.4.s:
kuṃdābhā daśa caivāśvā vāmadakṣiṇato yutāḥ..
pūrṇe śatasahasre ca yojanānāṃ niśākarāt.. 38.24 ..
1.4.d:
कुंदाभा दश चैवाश्वा वामदक्षिणतो युताः..
पूर्णे शतसहस्रे च योजनानां निशाकरात्.. 38.24 ..
1.4.m:
Ten horses, white as jasmine, are harnessed on the left and right.
At a full one hundred thousand yojanas from the moon,

1.4.s:
nakṣatramaṇḍalaṃ kṛtsnamupariṣṭātprakāśate..
caturdaśa cārbudānyapyaśītiḥ saritāṃpatiḥ.. 38.25 ..
1.4.d:
नक्षत्रमण्डलं कृत्स्नमुपरिष्टात्प्रकाशते..
चतुर्दश चार्बुदान्यप्यशीतिः सरितांपतिः.. 38.25 ..
1.4.m:
the entire circle of asterisms shines above.
One billion four hundred and eighty million,

1.4.s:
viṃśatiśca tathā koṭyo nakṣatrāṇāṃ prakīrtitāḥ..
dve lakṣe cottare tasmādbudho nakṣatramaṇḍalāt.. 38.26 ..
1.4.d:
विंशतिश्च तथा कोट्यो नक्षत्राणां प्रकीर्तिताः..
द्वे लक्षे चोत्तरे तस्माद्बुधो नक्षत्रमण्डलात्.. 38.26 ..
1.4.m:
and twenty crores are declared to be the number of asterisms.
Two hundred thousand [yojanas] above that circle of asterisms is Mercury.

1.4.s:
vāyvagnidravyasaṃbhūto rathaścaṃdrasutasya ca..
piśaṃgaistura--- soṣṭābhirvāyavegibhiḥ.. 38.27 ..
1.4.d:
वाय्वग्निद्रव्यसंभूतो रथश्चंद्रसुतस्य च..
पिशंगैस्तुर--- सोष्टाभिर्वायवेगिभिः.. 38.27 ..
1.4.m:
The chariot of the son of the Moon is made of the substances of wind and fire,
drawn by eight yellowish horses, swift as the wind.

1.4.s:
dvilakṣaścottare tasmādbudhāccāpyuśanā smṛtaḥ..
śukrasyāpi rathoṣṭābhiryukto'bhūtsaṃbhavairhayaiḥ.. 38.28 ..
1.4.d:
द्विलक्षश्चोत्तरे तस्माद्बुधाच्चाप्युशना स्मृतः..
शुक्रस्यापि रथोष्टाभिर्युक्तोऽभूत्संभवैर्हयैः.. 38.28 ..
1.4.m:
Two hundred thousand [yojanas] above Mercury is remembered Uśanas;
Venus's chariot is also yoked to eight horses of water-born origin.

1.4.s:
lakṣadvayena bhaumasya smṛto devapurohitaḥ..
aṣṭābhiḥ pāṃḍurairaśvairyukto'sya kāṃcanorathaḥ.. 38.29 ..
1.4.d:
लक्षद्वयेन भौमस्य स्मृतो देवपुरोहितः..
अष्टाभिः पांडुरैरश्वैर्युक्तोऽस्य कांचनोरथः.. 38.29 ..
1.4.m:
Two hundred thousand [yojanas] [above] Mars is the priest of the gods;
his golden chariot is yoked to eight pale horses.

1.4.s:
saurirbṛhaspateścordhvaṃ dvilakṣe samupasthitaḥ..
ākāśasaṃbhavairaśvairaṣṭābhiḥ śabalai rathaḥ.. 38.30 ..
1.4.d:
सौरिर्बृहस्पतेश्चोर्ध्वं द्विलक्षे समुपस्थितः..
आकाशसंभवैरश्वैरष्टाभिः शबलै रथः.. 38.30 ..
1.4.m:
Saturn is situated two hundred thousand [yojanas] above Jupiter;
his chariot is drawn by eight dappled horses born of the sky.

1.4.s:
svarbhānosturagāścāṣṭau bhṛṃgābhā dhūsarāratham..
vahaṃti ca sakṛdyuktā ādityādhaḥsthitāstathā.. 38.31 ..
1.4.d:
स्वर्भानोस्तुरगाश्चाष्टौ भृंगाभा धूसरारथम्..
वहंति च सकृद्युक्ता आदित्याधःस्थितास्तथा.. 38.31 ..
1.4.m:
The eight horses of Svarbhānu, black as bees and dusky, draw the chariot,
harnessed only once, and situated below the sun.

1.4.s:
saurerlakṣaṃ smṛtaṃ cordhvaṃ tataḥ saptarṣimaṇḍalam..
ṛṣibhyaścāpi lakṣeṇa dhruvaścordhvaṃ vyavasthitaḥ.. 38.32 ..
1.4.d:
सौरेर्लक्षं स्मृतं चोर्ध्वं ततः सप्तर्षिमण्डलम्..
ऋषिभ्यश्चापि लक्षेण ध्रुवश्चोर्ध्वं व्यवस्थितः.. 38.32 ..
1.4.m:
One hundred thousand [yojanas] above Saturn is known the circle of the Seven Seers;
and one hundred thousand [yojanas] above the seers is situated Dhruva.

1.4.s:
meḍhībhūtaḥ samastasya jyotiścakrasya vai dhruvaḥ..
dhruvo'pi śiṃśumārasya pucchādhāre vyavasthitaḥ.. 38.33 ..
1.4.d:
मेढीभूतः समस्तस्य ज्योतिश्चक्रस्य वै ध्रुवः..
ध्रुवोऽपि शिंशुमारस्य पुच्छाधारे व्यवस्थितः.. 38.33 ..
1.4.m:
Dhruva is the pivot-pole for the entire wheel of constellations;
Dhruva is also situated at the base of the tail of the Śiṃśumāra,

1.4.s:
yamāhurvāsudevasya rūpamātmānamavyayam..
vāyupāśairdhruve baddhaṃ sarvametacca phālguna.. 38.34 ..
1.4.d:
यमाहुर्वासुदेवस्य रूपमात्मानमव्ययम्..
वायुपाशैर्ध्रुवे बद्धं सर्वमेतच्च फाल्गुन.. 38.34 ..
1.4.m:
which they call the form of Vāsudeva, the imperishable Self.
All of this, O Phālguna, is bound to Dhruva with bonds of wind.

1.4.s:
navayojanasāhasraṃ maṇḍalaṃ savituḥ smṛtam..
dviguṇaṃ sūryavistārānmaṇḍalaṃ śaśinaḥ smṛtam.. 38.35 ..
1.4.d:
नवयोजनसाहस्रं मण्डलं सवितुः स्मृतम्..
द्विगुणं सूर्यविस्तारान्मण्डलं शशिनः स्मृतम्.. 38.35 ..
1.4.m:
The orb of the sun is remembered to be nine thousand yojanas [in diameter];
the orb of the moon is remembered to be twice the extent of the sun.

1.4.s:
tulyastayostu svarbhānurbhūtvādhastātprasarpati..
uddhṛtya pṛthivīcchāyāṃ nirmalāṃ maṇḍalākṛtiḥ.. 38.36 ..
1.4.d:
तुल्यस्तयोस्तु स्वर्भानुर्भूत्वाधस्तात्प्रसर्पति..
उद्धृत्य पृथिवीच्छायां निर्मलां मण्डलाकृतिः.. 38.36 ..
1.4.m:
Svarbhānu, equal to them, moving below,
assuming a circular shape, draws up the pure shadow of the earth.

1.4.s:
candrasya ṣoḍaśo bhāgo bhārgavaśca vidhīyate..
bhārgavātpādahīnastu vijñeyo'tha bṛhaspatiḥ.. 38.37 ..
1.4.d:
चन्द्रस्य षोडशो भागो भार्गवश्च विधीयते..
भार्गवात्पादहीनस्तु विज्ञेयोऽथ बृहस्पतिः.. 38.37 ..
1.4.m:
Venus is prescribed as one-sixteenth of the moon;
Jupiter should be understood as one-fourth less than Venus.

1.4.s:
bṛhaspateḥ pādahīnau vakrasaurī budhastathā..
śatāni paṃca catvāritrīṇi dve caikayojanam.. 38.38 ..
1.4.d:
बृहस्पतेः पादहीनौ वक्रसौरी बुधस्तथा..
शतानि पंच चत्वारित्रीणि द्वे चैकयोजनम्.. 38.38 ..
1.4.m:
Mars and Saturn are one-fourth less than Jupiter, and so is Mercury.
Five hundred, four hundred, three hundred, two hundred, and one yojana,

1.4.s:
yojanārdhapramāṇāni bhāni hrasvaṃ na vidyate..
bhūmilokaśca bhūrlokaḥ pādagamyaḥ prakīrtitaḥ.. 38.39 ..
1.4.d:
योजनार्धप्रमाणानि भानि ह्रस्वं न विद्यते..
भूमिलोकश्च भूर्लोकः पादगम्यः प्रकीर्तितः.. 38.39 ..
1.4.m:
and measuring half a yojana are the asterisms; there is none smaller.
Bhūrloka is the terrestrial realm, declared to be accessible on foot.

1.4.s:
bhūmisūryāṃtaraṃ tacca bhuvarlokaḥ prakīrtitaḥ..
dhruvasūryāṃtaraṃ tacca niyutāni caturdaśa.. 38.40 ..
1.4.d:
भूमिसूर्यांतरं तच्च भुवर्लोकः प्रकीर्तितः..
ध्रुवसूर्यांतरं तच्च नियुतानि चतुर्दश.. 38.40 ..
1.4.m:
The space between the earth and the sun is declared to be Bhuvarloka.
The distance between Dhruva and the sun is one million four hundred thousand [yojanas];

1.4.s:
svarlokaḥ so'pi gadito lokasaṃsthānaciṃtakaiḥ..
dhruvādūrdhvaṃ tathā koṭacirmaharlokaḥ prakīrtitaḥ.. 38.41 ..
1.4.d:
स्वर्लोकः सोऽपि गदितो लोकसंस्थानचिंतकैः..
ध्रुवादूर्ध्वं तथा कोटचिर्महर्लोकः प्रकीर्तितः.. 38.41 ..
1.4.m:
that is spoken of as Svarloka by those who contemplate the arrangement of the worlds.
Above Dhruva at ten million [yojanas] is declared Maharloka.

1.4.s:
dve koṭyau ca jano yatra nivasaṃti catuḥsanāḥ..
caturbhiścāpi koṭībhistapolokastataḥ smaॉtaḥ.. 38.42 ..
1.4.d:
द्वे कोट्यौ च जनो यत्र निवसंति चतुःसनाः..
चतुर्भिश्चापि कोटीभिस्तपोलोकस्ततः स्मॉतः.. 38.42 ..
1.4.m: And Janaloka is two crores [yojanas higher], where the Four Sanas reside. / And Tapoloka is remembered four crores [yojanas] from there,

1.4.s:
vairājā yatra te devāḥ sthitā dāhavivarjitāḥ..
ṣaḍguṇena tapolokātsatyaloko virājate.. 38.43 ..
1.4.d:
वैराजा यत्र ते देवाः स्थिता दाहविवर्जिताः..
षड्गुणेन तपोलोकात्सत्यलोको विराजते.. 38.43 ..
1.4.m: Where those Vairāja deities abide, free from burning heat. / Satyaloka shines at six times the distance from Tapoloka,

1.4.s:
apunarmarakā yatra brahmaloko hi sa smṛtaḥ..
aṣṭādasa tathā koṭyo lakṣāṇyaśītipaṃca ca.. 38.44 ..
1.4.d:
अपुनर्मरका यत्र ब्रह्मलोको हि स स्मृतः..
अष्टादस तथा कोट्यो लक्षाण्यशीतिपंच च.. 38.44 ..
1.4.m: Where beings do not die again; it is known indeed as Brahmaloka. / Eighteen crores and eighty-five lakhs [of yojanas higher],

1.4.s:
śubhaṃ nirupamaṃ sthānaṃ tadūrdhvaṃ saṃprakāśate..
bhūrbhūvaḥsvariti proktaṃ trailokyaṃ kṛtakaṃ tvidam.. 38.45 ..
1.4.d:
शुभं निरुपमं स्थानं तदूर्ध्वं संप्रकाशते..
भूर्भूवःस्वरिति प्रोक्तं त्रैलोक्यं कृतकं त्विदम्.. 38.45 ..
1.4.m: Shines that auspicious, peerless abode above. / Bhūḥ, Bhuvaḥ, and Svaḥ are proclaimed: this is the transient threefold world,

1.4.s:
janastapastathā satyamiti cākṛtakaṃ trayam..
kṛtakākṛtayormadhye marharloka iti smṛtaḥ.. 38.46 ..
1.4.d:
जनस्तपस्तथा सत्यमिति चाकृतकं त्रयम्..
कृतकाकृतयोर्मध्ये मर्हर्लोक इति स्मृतः.. 38.46 ..
1.4.m: While Jana, Tapas, and Satya—these three are imperishable. / Between the transient and the imperishable, Maharloka is recorded.

1.4.s:
śūnyo bhavati kalpāṃte yotyaṃtaṃ na vinaśyati..
ete sapta samākhyātā lokāḥ puṇyairupārjitāḥ.. 38.47 ..
1.4.d:
शून्यो भवति कल्पांते योत्यंतं न विनश्यति..
एते सप्त समाख्याता लोकाः पुण्यैरुपार्जिताः.. 38.47 ..
1.4.m: It becomes empty at the end of a kalpa, but it does not completely perish. / These seven worlds have been described, attained through merits,

1.4.s:
yajñairdānairjapairhomaistīrthairvratasamuccayaiḥ..
vedādiproktairanyaiśca sādhyām̐llokānimānviduḥ.. 38.48 ..
1.4.d:
यज्ञैर्दानैर्जपैर्होमैस्तीर्थैर्व्रतसमुच्चयैः..
वेदादिप्रोक्तैरन्यैश्च साध्याम्̐ल्लोकानिमान्विदुः.. 38.48 ..
1.4.m: Through sacrifices, gifts, recitations, oblations, sacred fords, and sets of vows; / they know these worlds are to be attained through other [rites] taught beginning with the Vedas.

1.4.s:
tataścāṃḍasya śiraso dhārā nīramayī śivā..
sarvalokānsamāplāvya gaṃgā merāvupāgatā.. 38.49 ..
1.4.d:
ततश्चांडस्य शिरसो धारा नीरमयी शिवा..
सर्वलोकान्समाप्लाव्य गंगा मेरावुपागता.. 38.49 ..
1.4.m: And then from the crown of the cosmic egg, an auspicious stream composed of water, / bathing all the worlds, the Gaṅgā, arrived at Mount Meru.

1.4.s:
tato mahītalaṃ sarvaṃ pātālaṃ praviveśa sā..
aṃḍamūrdhni sthitā devī satataṃ dvāravāsinī.. 38.50 ..
1.4.d:
ततो महीतलं सर्वं पातालं प्रविवेश सा..
अंडमूर्ध्नि स्थिता देवी सततं द्वारवासिनी.. 38.50 ..
1.4.m: Then it entered the entire surface of the earth and Pātāla. / The goddess residing at the crest of the cosmic egg dwells constantly at the doorway,

1.4.s:
devīnāṃ koṭikoṭībhiḥ saṃvṛtā piṃgalena ca..
tatra sthitā sadā rakṣāṃ kurute'ṇḍasya sā śubhā.. 38.51 ..
1.4.d:
देवीनां कोटिकोटीभिः संवृता पिंगलेन च..
तत्र स्थिता सदा रक्षां कुरुतेऽण्डस्य सा शुभा.. 38.51 ..
1.4.m: Surrounded by crores of crores of goddesses and by Piṅgala. / Remaining there, that auspicious goddess always protects the cosmic egg;

1.4.s:
nihaṃti duṣṭasaṃghātānmahābalaparākramā..
vāyuskaṃdhāni saptāpiśrṛṇuyadvatsthitānyapi.. 38.52 ..
1.4.d:
निहंति दुष्टसंघातान्महाबलपराक्रमा..
वायुस्कंधानि सप्तापिश्रृणुयद्वत्स्थितान्यपि.. 38.52 ..
1.4.m: Possessing great strength and valour, she strikes down hordes of wicked beings. / Hear also how the seven wind-courses are stationed.

1.4.s:
pṛthivīṃ samabhikramya saṃsthito meghamaṃḍale..
pravahonāma yo meghānpravahatyatiśaktimān.. 38.53 ..
1.4.d:
पृथिवीं समभिक्रम्य संस्थितो मेघमंडले..
प्रवहोनाम यो मेघान्प्रवहत्यतिशक्तिमान्.. 38.53 ..
1.4.m: Having encompassed the earth, stationed in the sphere of clouds, / the very powerful wind named Pravaha blows forth the clouds.

1.4.s:
dhūmajāśvoṣmajā meghāḥ sāmudraiyana pūritāḥ..
toyairbhavaṃti nīlāṃgā varṣiṣṭhāścaiva bhārata.. 38.54 ..
1.4.d:
धूमजाश्वोष्मजा मेघाः सामुद्रैयन पूरिताः..
तोयैर्भवंति नीलांगा वर्षिष्ठाश्चैव भारत.. 38.54 ..
1.4.m: Filled by it with ocean waters, the clouds born of smoke and born of heat / become dark-bodied and produce abundant rain, O descendant of Bharata.

1.4.s:
dvitīyaścāvaho nāma nibaddhaḥ sūryamaṃḍale..
tena baddhaṃ dhruveṇedaṃ bhrāmyate sūryamaṃḍalam.. 38.55 ..
1.4.d:
द्वितीयश्चावहो नाम निबद्धः सूर्यमंडले..
तेन बद्धं ध्रुवेणेदं भ्राम्यते सूर्यमंडलम्.. 38.55 ..
1.4.m: The second [wind] is named Āvaha, fastened to the solar sphere; / tied by it to Dhruva, this solar sphere is made to rotate.

1.4.s:
tṛtīyaścodvaho nāma caṃdraskaṃdhe pratiṣṭhitaḥ..
baddhaṃ dhruveṇa yenedaṃ bhrāmyate caṃdramaṃḍalam.. 38.56 ..
1.4.d:
तृतीयश्चोद्वहो नाम चंद्रस्कंधे प्रतिष्ठितः..
बद्धं ध्रुवेण येनेदं भ्राम्यते चंद्रमंडलम्.. 38.56 ..
1.4.m: The third is named Udvaha, established in the lunar sphere; / tied by it to Dhruva, this lunar sphere is made to rotate.

1.4.s:
caturthaḥ saṃvaho nāma sthito nakṣatramaṇḍale..
vātaraśmibhirābaddhaṃ dhruveṇa saha bhrāmyate.. 38.57 ..
1.4.d:
चतुर्थः संवहो नाम स्थितो नक्षत्रमण्डले..
वातरश्मिभिराबद्धं ध्रुवेण सह भ्राम्यते.. 38.57 ..
1.4.m: The fourth is named Saṃvaha, situated in the sphere of the asterisms; / tied together with Dhruva by rays of wind, it is made to rotate.

1.4.s:
graheṣu paṃcamaḥ so'pi vivaho nāma mārutaḥ..
grahacakramidaṃ yena bhrāmyate dhruvasaṃdhitam.. 38.58 ..
1.4.d:
ग्रहेषु पंचमः सोऽपि विवहो नाम मारुतः..
ग्रहचक्रमिदं येन भ्राम्यते ध्रुवसंधितम्.. 38.58 ..
1.4.m: The fifth wind among the planets is Vivaha; / by it this circle of planets, joined to Dhruva, is made to rotate.

1.4.s:
ṣaṣṭhaḥ parivaho nāma sthitaḥ saptarṣimaṃḍale..
bhramaṃti dhruvasaṃbaddhā yena saptarṣayo divi.. 38.59 ..
1.4.d:
षष्ठः परिवहो नाम स्थितः सप्तर्षिमंडले..
भ्रमंति ध्रुवसंबद्धा येन सप्तर्षयो दिवि.. 38.59 ..
1.4.m: The sixth is named Parivaha, stationed in the constellation of the Seven Seers; / tied to Dhruva by it, the Seven Seers revolve in the sky.

1.4.s:
saptamaśca dhruve baddho vāyurnāmnā parāvahaḥ..
yena saṃsthāpitaṃ dhrauvyaṃ cakraṃ cānyāni bhārata.. 38.60 ..
1.4.d:
सप्तमश्च ध्रुवे बद्धो वायुर्नाम्ना परावहः..
येन संस्थापितं ध्रौव्यं चक्रं चान्यानि भारत.. 38.60 ..
1.4.m: And the seventh wind, fastened to Dhruva, is named Parāvaha; / by it the polar cycle and the others have been fixed, O descendant of Bharata,

1.4.s:
yaṃ samāsādya vegena diśāmaṃtaṃ prapedire..
dakṣasya daśa putrāṇāṃ sahasrāṇi prajāpateḥ.. 38.61 ..
1.4.d:
यं समासाद्य वेगेन दिशामंतं प्रपेदिरे..
दक्षस्य दश पुत्राणां सहस्राणि प्रजापतेः.. 38.61 ..
1.4.m: Reaching which with speed, the ten thousand sons / of the Prajāpati Dakṣa attained the end of the directions.

1.4.s:
evamete diteḥ putrāḥ saptasapta vyavasthitāḥ..
anāramaṃtaḥ saṃvāṃti sarvagāḥ sarvadhāriṇaḥ.. 38.62 ..
1.4.d:
एवमेते दितेः पुत्राः सप्तसप्त व्यवस्थिताः..
अनारमंतः संवांति सर्वगाः सर्वधारिणः.. 38.62 ..
1.4.m: Thus these sons of Diti stand arranged in seven groups of seven. / Never ceasing, they blow, going everywhere, supporting all.

1.4.s:
dhruvādūrdhvamasūryaṃ cāpyanakṣatramatārakam..
svatejasā svaśaktyā cādhiṣṭhitāste hi nityadā.. 38.63 ..
1.4.d:
ध्रुवादूर्ध्वमसूर्यं चाप्यनक्षत्रमतारकम्..
स्वतेजसा स्वशक्त्या चाधिष्ठितास्ते हि नित्यदा.. 38.63 ..
1.4.m: Above Dhruva, there is neither sun, nor asterisms, nor stars; / established by their own splendour and power, they are eternal.

1.4.s:
ityūrdhvaṃ te samākhyāṃtaṃ pātālānyatha me śrṛṇu.. 38.64 ..
iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhāsryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ prathame māheśvarakhaṇḍe kaumārikākhaṇḍe kumārikākyāne lokavyavasthitivarmanaṃnāmāṣṭatriṃśo'dhyāyaḥ.. 38 .. cha ..
1.4.d:
इत्यूर्ध्वं ते समाख्यांतं पातालान्यथ मे श्रृणु.. 38.64 ..
इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहास्र्यां संहितायां प्रथमे माहेश्वरखण्डे कौमारिकाखण्डे कुमारिकाक्याने लोकव्यवस्थितिवर्मनंनामाष्टत्रिंशोऽध्यायः.. 38 .. छ ..
1.4.m:
Thus the regions above have been related to you; now hear from me about the subterranean realms."
Thus ends the thirty-eighth chapter, named 'Description of the Arrangement of the Worlds', in the Kumārikā narrative of the Kaumārikākhaṇḍa, in the first Māheśvarakhaṇḍa of the glorious Skandapurāṇa, a compilation of eighty-one thousand verses.

1.4.s:
..nārada uvāca..
sahasrasaptatyucchrāye pātālāni parasparam..
atalaṃ vitalaṃ caiva nitalaṃ ca rasātalam.. 39.1 ..
1.4.d:
..नारद उवाच..
सहस्रसप्तत्युच्छ्राये पातालानि परस्परम्..
अतलं वितलं चैव नितलं च रसातलम्.. 39.1 ..
1.4.m: Nārada said: / "With an extent of seventy thousand [yojanas] mutually are the subterranean realms: / Atala, Vitala, Nitala, Rasātala,

1.4.s:
talātalaṃ ca sutalaṃ pātālaṃ cāpi saptamam..
kṛṣṇaśuklāruṇāḥ pītāḥ śarkarāśailakāṃcanāḥ.. 39.2 ..
1.4.d:
तलातलं च सुतलं पातालं चापि सप्तमम्..
कृष्णशुक्लारुणाः पीताः शर्कराशैलकांचनाः.. 39.2 ..
1.4.m: Talātala, Sutala, and Pātāla is the seventh. / Their grounds are black, white, reddish, yellow, gravelly, rocky, and golden,

1.4.s:
bhūmayo yatra kauravya varaprāsādaśobhitāḥ..
teṣu dānavadaiteyanāgāścaiva sahasrasaḥ.. 39.3 ..
1.4.d:
भूमयो यत्र कौरव्य वरप्रासादशोभिताः..
तेषु दानवदैतेयनागाश्चैव सहस्रसः.. 39.3 ..
1.4.m: Adorned with excellent mansions, O descendant of Kuru. / In them dwell Dānavas, Daiteyas, and serpents by the thousands.

1.4.s:
svarlokādapi ramyāṇi dṛṣṭāni bahuśo mayā..
āhlādakāriṇo nānāmaṇyo yatra pannagaḥ.. 39.4 ..
1.4.d:
स्वर्लोकादपि रम्याणि दृष्टानि बहुशो मया..
आह्लादकारिणो नानामण्यो यत्र पन्नगः.. 39.4 ..
1.4.m: They are more delightful than even heaven, as seen by me many times; / where serpents possess various gems that bring delight.

1.4.s:
daityadānavakanyābhirmahārūpābhiranvite..
pātāle kasya na prītirvimuktasyāpi jāyate.. 39.5 ..
1.4.d:
दैत्यदानवकन्याभिर्महारूपाभिरन्विते..
पाताले कस्य न प्रीतिर्विमुक्तस्यापि जायते.. 39.5 ..
1.4.m: Filled with the daughters of Daityas and Dānavas of magnificent beauty, / in Pātāla, who would not feel joy, even one who is liberated?

1.4.s:
yatra noṣṇaṃ na vā śītaṃ na varṣaṃ duḥkhameva ca..
bhakṣyabhojyamahābhogakālo yatrāpi jāyate.. 39.6 ..
1.4.d:
यत्र नोष्णं न वा शीतं न वर्षं दुःखमेव च..
भक्ष्यभोज्यमहाभोगकालो यत्रापि जायते.. 39.6 ..
1.4.m: Where there is neither heat nor cold, neither rain nor misery, / and where the time is spent in great enjoyment of food and delicacies.

1.4.s:
pātāle saptame cāsti liṃgaṃ śrīhāṭakeśvaram..
brahmaṇā sthāpitaṃ pārtha sahasrayojanocchritam.. 39.7 ..
1.4.d:
पाताले सप्तमे चास्ति लिंगं श्रीहाटकेश्वरम्..
ब्रह्मणा स्थापितं पार्थ सहस्रयोजनोच्छ्रितम्.. 39.7 ..
1.4.m: And in the seventh subterranean realm is the liṅga Śrī-Hāṭakeśvara, / erected by Brahmā, O son of Pṛthā, a thousand yojanas in height.

1.4.s:
hāṭakasya tu liṃgasya prāsādo yojanāyutaḥ..
sarvaratnamayo divyo nānāścayavibhūṣitaḥ.. 39.8 ..
1.4.d:
हाटकस्य तु लिंगस्य प्रासादो योजनायुतः..
सर्वरत्नमयो दिव्यो नानाश्चयविभूषितः.. 39.8 ..
1.4.m: The temple of that golden liṅga measures ten thousand yojanas, / celestial, made of all jewels, adorned with various wonders.

1.4.s:
taccāryaṃti talliṃgaṃ nānānāgendrasattamāḥ..
tadadhastājjalaṃ bhūri tasyādho narakāḥ smṛtāḥ.. 39.9 ..
1.4.d:
तच्चार्यंति तल्लिंगं नानानागेन्द्रसत्तमाः..
तदधस्ताज्जलं भूरि तस्याधो नरकाः स्मृताः.. 39.9 ..
1.4.m: And the best among various serpent-kings worship that liṅga. / Below that is abundant water, and below that, the hells are remembered,

1.4.s:
pāpino yeṣu pātyaṃte tāñchṛṇuṣva mahāmate..
koṭayaḥ paṃcapaṃcāśadrājānaścaikaviṃśati.. 39.10 ..
1.4.d:
पापिनो येषु पात्यंते ताञ्छृणुष्व महामते..
कोटयः पंचपंचाशद्राजानश्चैकविंशति.. 39.10 ..
1.4.m: Into which sinners are cast down; hear of them, O great-minded one. / There are fifty-five crores, and twenty-one are chief [hells]:

1.4.s:
rauravaḥ śūkaro rodhastālo viśasanastathā..
mahājvālastaptakumbho lavaṇotha vimohakaḥ.. 39.11 ..
1.4.d:
रौरवः शूकरो रोधस्तालो विशसनस्तथा..
महाज्वालस्तप्तकुम्भो लवणोथ विमोहकः.. 39.11 ..
1.4.m: Raurava, Śūkara, Rodha, Tāla, as well as Viśasana, / Mahājvāla, Taptakumbha, Lavaṇa, and Vimohaka,

1.4.s:
rudhirāṃdho vaitaraṇī kṛmiśaḥ kṛmibhojanaḥ..
asipatravanaṃ kṛṣṇo lālābhakṣyaśca dārumaḥ.. 39.12 ..
1.4.d:
रुधिरांधो वैतरणी कृमिशः कृमिभोजनः..
असिपत्रवनं कृष्णो लालाभक्ष्यश्च दारुमः.. 39.12 ..
1.4.m: Rudhirāndha, Vaitaraṇī, Kṛmiśa, Kṛmibhojana, / Asipatravana, Kṛṣṇa, and the dreadful Lālābhakṣya,

1.4.s:
tathā pūyavahaḥ pāpo vahnijvālo'pyadhaḥśirāḥ..
saṃdaṃśaḥ kṛṣṇasūtraśca tamaścāvīcirevaca.. 39.13 ..
1.4.d:
तथा पूयवहः पापो वह्निज्वालोऽप्यधःशिराः..
संदंशः कृष्णसूत्रश्च तमश्चावीचिरेवच.. 39.13 ..
1.4.m: Likewise the sinful Pūyavaha, Vahnijvāla, and Adhaḥśiras, / Saṃdaṃśa, Kṛṣṇasūtra, Tamas, and Avīci,

1.4.s:
śvabhojano visūciścāpyavīciśca tathā'paraḥ..
kūṭasākṣī rauravaṃ ca rodhaṃ goviprarodhakaḥ.. 39.14 ..
1.4.d:
श्वभोजनो विसूचिश्चाप्यवीचिश्च तथाऽपरः..
कूटसाक्षी रौरवं च रोधं गोविप्ररोधकः.. 39.14 ..
1.4.m: Śvabhojana, Visūci, and yet another Avīci. / A false witness goes to Raurava, and one who confines cows and brahmins to Rodha;

1.4.s:
surāpaḥ sūkaraṃ yāti tālaṃ mithyāma nuṣyahā..
gurutalpī taptakumbhaṃ taptalohaṃ ca bhaktahā.. 39.15 ..
1.4.d:
सुरापः सूकरं याति तालं मिथ्याम नुष्यहा..
गुरुतल्पी तप्तकुम्भं तप्तलोहं च भक्तहा.. 39.15 ..
1.4.m: A wine-drinker goes to Śūkara; a killer of men through deceit goes to Tāla; / a violator of the guru's bed goes to Taptakumbha; and one who ruins a devotee goes to Taptaloha;

1.4.s:
gurūṇāmavamaṃtā yaco mahājvāle nipātyate..
lavaṇaṃ śāstrahaṃtā ca nirmaryādo vimohake.. 39.16 ..
1.4.d:
गुरूणामवमंता यचो महाज्वाले निपात्यते..
लवणं शास्त्रहंता च निर्मर्यादो विमोहके.. 39.16 ..
1.4.m: One who despises gurus is cast into Mahājvāla; / a destroyer of scriptures goes to Lavaṇa; and a transgressor of bounds to Vimohaka;

1.4.s:
kṛmibhakṣye devadveṣṭā kṛmiśe tu duriṣṭakṛt..
pitṛdevātpūrvamaśrallām̐lābhakṣye prayāti ca.. 39.17 ..
1.4.d:
कृमिभक्ष्ये देवद्वेष्टा कृमिशे तु दुरिष्टकृत्..
पितृदेवात्पूर्वमश्रल्लाम्̐लाभक्ष्ये प्रयाति च.. 39.17 ..
1.4.m: A hater of the gods goes to Kṛmibhakṣya, but a performer of evil sacrifices goes to Kṛmiśa; / one who eats before [offering to] ancestors and gods goes to Lālābhakṣya;

1.4.s:
mithyājīvavirodhī viśasane kūṭaśastrakṛt..
adhomukhe hyasadgrāhī ekāśī pūyavāhake.. 39.18 ..
1.4.d:
मिथ्याजीवविरोधी विशसने कूटशस्त्रकृत्..
अधोमुखे ह्यसद्ग्राही एकाशी पूयवाहके.. 39.18 ..
1.4.m: One who opposes a false livelihood, and a maker of deceitful weapons goes to Viśasana; / one who accepts evil goes indeed to Adhomukha; one who eats alone goes to Pūyavāhaka;

1.4.s:
mārjjārakukkuṭaśvānapakṣipoṣṭā prayāti ca..
badhirāṃdhagṛhakṣetratṛṇadhānyādijvālakaḥ.. 39.19 ..
1.4.d:
मार्ज्जारकुक्कुटश्वानपक्षिपोष्टा प्रयाति च..
बधिरांधगृहक्षेत्रतृणधान्यादिज्वालकः.. 39.19 ..
1.4.m: And a rearer of cats, cocks, dogs, and birds goes [to hell]; / one who sets fire to houses of the deaf and blind, to fields, grass, grain, and the like,

1.4.s:
nakṣatraraṃgajīvī ca yāti vaitaraṇīṃ naraḥ..
dhanayauvanamatto yo dhanahā kṛṣṇameti saḥ.. 39.20 ..
1.4.d:
नक्षत्ररंगजीवी च याति वैतरणीं नरः..
धनयौवनमत्तो यो धनहा कृष्णमेति सः.. 39.20 ..
1.4.m: And a person who lives by astrology or the stage goes to Vaitaraṇī; / one who is arrogant through wealth and youth, and a stealer of wealth, goes to Kṛṣṇa.

1.4.s:
asipatravanaṃ yāti vṛkṣacchedī vṛthaiva yat..
kuhakājīvinaḥ sarve vahnijvāle pataṃti te.. 39.21 ..
1.4.d:
असिपत्रवनं याति वृक्षच्छेदी वृथैव यत्..
कुहकाजीविनः सर्वे वह्निज्वाले पतंति ते.. 39.21 ..
1.4.m: He who fells trees in vain goes to Asipatravana (the Forest of Sword Leaves); / all those who live by deceit fall into the blaze of fire.

1.4.s:
parastrīṃ ca parānnaṃ ca gacchansaṃdaṃśameti ca..
divāsvapnaparā ye vratalopaparāśca ye.. 39.22 ..
1.4.d:
परस्त्रीं च परान्नं च गच्छन्संदंशमेति च..
दिवास्वप्नपरा ये व्रतलोपपराश्च ये.. 39.22 ..
1.4.m: He who approaches another man’s wife and consumes another man’s food goes to Saṃdaṃśa (the Pincers); / and so do those devoted to daytime sleep and those intent on breaking vows.

1.4.s:
śarīramadamattāśca yāṃti caite śvabhojanam..
śivaṃ hariṃ na manyaṃte yāṃtyavīcinameva ca.. 39.23 ..
1.4.d:
शरीरमदमत्ताश्च यांति चैते श्वभोजनम्..
शिवं हरिं न मन्यंते यांत्यवीचिनमेव च.. 39.23 ..
1.4.m: And those intoxicated by bodily pride go to Śvabhojana (Dog-Food); / those who do not respect Śiva and Hari go to Avīci itself.

1.4.s:
ityevamādibhiḥ pāpairaśāstraughasya sevanaiḥ..
pataṃtyeva mahāghoranarakeṣu sahasraśaḥ.. 39.24 ..
1.4.d:
इत्येवमादिभिः पापैरशास्त्रौघस्य सेवनैः..
पतंत्येव महाघोरनरकेषु सहस्रशः.. 39.24 ..
1.4.m: Through sins such as these, by resorting to the multitude of unscriptural ways, / [people] fall by thousands into terrible hells.

1.4.s:
tasmādya icchedetebhyo vimokṣaṃ buddhimānnaraḥ..
śrutimārgeṇa tenārcyau devau hariharāvubhau.. 39.25 ..
1.4.d:
तस्माद्य इच्छेदेतेभ्यो विमोक्षं बुद्धिमान्नरः..
श्रुतिमार्गेण तेनार्च्यौ देवौ हरिहरावुभौ.. 39.25 ..
1.4.m: Therefore, a wise man who desires deliverance from these / should worship both gods, Hari and Hara, according to the Vedic path.

1.4.s:
narakāṇāmadhobhāge sthitaḥ kālāgnisaṃjñakaḥ..
tadadho haṭṭakaścaiva anaṃtastadadhaḥ smṛtaḥ.. 39.26 ..
1.4.d:
नरकाणामधोभागे स्थितः कालाग्निसंज्ञकः..
तदधो हट्टकश्चैव अनंतस्तदधः स्मृतः.. 39.26 ..
1.4.m: In the lower portion of the hells resides the one called Kālāgni; / beneath him is Haṭṭaka, and beneath him Ananta is remembered.

1.4.s:
yasyaitatsakalaṃ viśvaṃ mūrdhāgre sarṣapāyate..
ityanaṃtaprabhāvātsa hyanaṃta iti kīrtyate.. 39.27 ..
1.4.d:
यस्यैतत्सकलं विश्वं मूर्धाग्रे सर्षपायते..
इत्यनंतप्रभावात्स ह्यनंत इति कीर्त्यते.. 39.27 ..
1.4.m: On the tip of whose head this entire universe acts like a mustard seed; / because of his endless (ananta) power, he is celebrated as Ananta.

1.4.s:
diśāṃ gajāstatra padmakumudāṃjanavāmanāḥ..
tadadhoṃ'ḍakaṭāhaśca ekavīrāsti tatra ca.. 39.28 ..
1.4.d:
दिशां गजास्तत्र पद्मकुमुदांजनवामनाः..
तदधोंऽडकटाहश्च एकवीरास्ति तत्र च.. 39.28 ..
1.4.m: There are the elephants of the quarters: Padma, Kumuda, Añjana, and Vāmana; / beneath them is the cosmic egg-shell, and Ekavīrā is there.

1.4.s:
caturlakṣasahasrāṇi navatiśca śatāni ca..
etanaiva pramāṇena udakaṃ ca tataḥ smṛtam.. 39.29 ..
1.4.d:
चतुर्लक्षसहस्राणि नवतिश्च शतानि च..
एतनैव प्रमाणेन उदकं च ततः स्मृतम्.. 39.29 ..
1.4.m: Four hundred and ninety thousand [yojanas]; / the water [there] is recorded to be of that very measure.

1.4.s:
tadadho narakāḥ koṭyo dvikoṭyo'gnistato mahān..
catvāriṃśatsahasraiśca tadadhastama ucyate.. 39.30 ..
1.4.d:
तदधो नरकाः कोट्यो द्विकोट्योऽग्निस्ततो महान्..
चत्वारिंशत्सहस्रैश्च तदधस्तम उच्यते.. 39.30 ..
1.4.m: Beneath that are hells numbering crores; then a great fire of two crores; / beneath that, darkness is spoken of as extending forty thousand [yojanas].

1.4.s:
catvāriṃśccakoṭyastu catasraśca tataḥ parāḥ..
ekonanavatirlakṣāḥ sahasrāśītireva ca.. 39.31 ..
1.4.d:
चत्वारिंश्च्चकोट्यस्तु चतस्रश्च ततः पराः..
एकोननवतिर्लक्षाः सहस्राशीतिरेव च.. 39.31 ..
1.4.m: Then further are forty-four crores, / eighty-nine lakhs, / and eighty thousand [yojanas].

1.4.s:
tadadhoṃ'ḍakaṭāhotha koṭimātrastathāparaḥ..
devī yuktā kapālīśā daṃḍahastena cāpi sā.. 39.32 ..
1.4.d:
तदधोंऽडकटाहोथ कोटिमात्रस्तथापरः..
देवी युक्ता कपालीशा दंडहस्तेन चापि सा.. 39.32 ..
1.4.m: Beneath that is the cosmic egg-shell, another [layer] measuring one crore; / the goddess Kapālīśā is there, holding a staff in her hand,

1.4.s:
devīnāṃ koṭikoṭībhiḥ saṃvṛtā tatra pālinī..
saṃkarṣaṇasya niḥśvāsaprerito dāhako'nalaḥ.. 39.33 ..
1.4.d:
देवीनां कोटिकोटीभिः संवृता तत्र पालिनी..
संकर्षणस्य निःश्वासप्रेरितो दाहकोऽनलः.. 39.33 ..
1.4.m: surrounded by crores upon crores of goddesses, ruling there; / the scorching fire propelled by the exhalation of Saṃkarṣaṇa,

1.4.s:
kālāgniṃ prerayatyeva kalpāṃte dahyate jagat..
evaṃvidhamadhaḥsūtraṃ nirmitaṃ cātra bhārata.. 39.34 ..
1.4.d:
कालाग्निं प्रेरयत्येव कल्पांते दह्यते जगत्..
एवंविधमधःसूत्रं निर्मितं चात्र भारत.. 39.34 ..
1.4.m: drives Kālāgni, and the world is burned at the end of the kalpa. / In this manner, O Bhārata, the lower thread has been laid out.

1.4.s:
madhyasūtre kaṭāhe ca pālakāṃstāñchṛṇuṣva me..
vasudhāmā sthitaḥ pūrve śaṃkhapālaśca dakṣiṇe.. 39.35 ..
1.4.d:
मध्यसूत्रे कटाहे च पालकांस्ताञ्छृणुष्व मे..
वसुधामा स्थितः पूर्वे शंखपालश्च दक्षिणे.. 39.35 ..
1.4.m: Hear from me of those guardians in the central thread and in the cosmic shell: / Vasudhāman is stationed in the east, and Śaṅkhapāla in the south;

1.4.s:
takṣakeśaḥ sthitaḥ paścāduttare ketumāniti..
harasiddhiḥ suparṇākṣī bhāskarā yoganaṃdinī.. 39.36 ..
1.4.d:
तक्षकेशः स्थितः पश्चादुत्तरे केतुमानिति..
हरसिद्धिः सुपर्णाक्षी भास्करा योगनंदिनी.. 39.36 ..
1.4.m: Takṣakeśa stands in the west, and in the north Ketumant; / Harasiddhi, Suparṇākṣī, Bhāskarā, Yoganandinī—

1.4.s:
koṭikoṭī yutā devī devīnāṃ pālayatyadaḥ..
evametanmahāścaryaṃ brahmāṃḍaṃ sthāpitaṃ ca yaiḥ.. 39.37 ..
1.4.d:
कोटिकोटी युता देवी देवीनां पालयत्यदः..
एवमेतन्महाश्चर्यं ब्रह्मांडं स्थापितं च यैः.. 39.37 ..
1.4.m: accompanied by crores upon crores of goddesses, the goddess protects this. / Thus by whom this greatly wondrous brahmāṇḍa has been established,

1.4.s:
namāmi tānahaṃ nityaṃ brahmaviṣṇumaheśvarān..
viṣṇuloko rudraloko bahiścāsmātprakīrtyate.. 39.38 ..
1.4.d:
नमामि तानहं नित्यं ब्रह्मविष्णुमहेश्वरान्..
विष्णुलोको रुद्रलोको बहिश्चास्मात्प्रकीर्त्यते.. 39.38 ..
1.4.m: to them I constantly bow: Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara. / The world of Viṣṇu and the world of Rudra are proclaimed to be outside this.

1.4.s:
taṃ ca varṇayituṃ brahmā śakto naivāsmadādayaḥ..
vimuktā yatra saṃyāṃti nityaṃ hariharavratāḥ.. 39.39 ..
1.4.d:
तं च वर्णयितुं ब्रह्मा शक्तो नैवास्मदादयः..
विमुक्ता यत्र संयांति नित्यं हरिहरव्रताः.. 39.39 ..
1.4.m: And Brahmā is not able to describe it, nor are people like us; / where the liberated go, constantly dedicated to Hari and Hara.

1.4.s:
brahmāṃḍaṃ saṃvṛtaṃ hyetatkaṭāhena samaṃtataḥ..
kapitthasya yathā bījaṃ kaṭāhena susaṃvṛtam.. 39.40 ..
1.4.d:
ब्रह्मांडं संवृतं ह्येतत्कटाहेन समंततः..
कपित्थस्य यथा बीजं कटाहेन सुसंवृतम्.. 39.40 ..
1.4.m: This brahmāṇḍa is enclosed on all sides by an egg-shell, / just as the seed of a wood-apple is firmly enclosed by its shell.

1.4.s:
daśottareṇa payasā vṛtaṃ taccāpi tejasā..
tejaśca vāyunā vāyurnabha sāhaṃtayā ca tat.. 39.41 ..
1.4.d:
दशोत्तरेण पयसा वृतं तच्चापि तेजसा..
तेजश्च वायुना वायुर्नभ साहंतया च तत्.. 39.41 ..
1.4.m: It is surrounded by water ten times [its size], and that by fire; / fire by air, air by space, and that by egoity;

1.4.s:
ahaṃkāraśca mahatā taṃ cāpi prakṛtiḥ parā..
daśottarāṇi sarvāṇi ṣaḍāhuḥ saptamaṃ ca tat.. 39.42 ..
1.4.d:
अहंकारश्च महता तं चापि प्रकृतिः परा..
दशोत्तराणि सर्वाणि षडाहुः सप्तमं च तत्.. 39.42 ..
1.4.m: egoity by the intellect, and that by primordial matter (prakṛti); / all these six are said to be tenfold [the former], and the seventh is that.

1.4.s:
prākṛtaṃ caraṇaṃ pārtha tadanaṃtaṃ prakīrtitam..
aṃḍānāṃ tu sahasrāṇāṃ sahasrāṇyayutāni ca.. 39.43 ..
1.4.d:
प्राकृतं चरणं पार्थ तदनंतं प्रकीर्तितम्..
अंडानां तु सहस्राणां सहस्राण्ययुतानि च.. 39.43 ..
1.4.m: The realm of primordial matter, O Pārtha, is proclaimed to be infinite; / there are thousands, myriad thousands of cosmic eggs,

1.4.s:
īdṛśānāṃ tathā cātra koṭikoṭiśatāni ca..
sarvāṇyevaṃvidhānyeva yādṛśaṃ kīrtitaṃtvidam.. 39.44 ..
1.4.d:
ईदृशानां तथा चात्र कोटिकोटिशतानि च..
सर्वाण्येवंविधान्येव यादृशं कीर्तितंत्विदम्.. 39.44 ..
1.4.m: hundreds of crores upon crores of such eggs here; / all of them are indeed of this kind, such as has been described.

1.4.s:
yasyaivaṃ vaibhavaṃ pārtha taṃ namāmī sadāśivam..
aho maṃdaḥ sa pāpātmā ko vā tasmādacetanaḥ.. 39.45 ..
1.4.d:
यस्यैवं वैभवं पार्थ तं नमामी सदाशिवम्..
अहो मंदः स पापात्मा को वा तस्मादचेतनः.. 39.45 ..
1.4.m: To that Sadāśiva whose majesty is such, O Pārtha, I bow! / Ah, dull and sinful is he—who could be more mindless than he,

1.4.s:
ya evaṃvidhasaṃmohatārakaṃ na śivaṃ bhajet..
atha te kīrthayiṣyāmi kālamānaṃ nibodha tat.. 39.46 ..
1.4.d:
य एवंविधसंमोहतारकं न शिवं भजेत्..
अथ ते कीर्थयिष्यामि कालमानं निबोध तत्.. 39.46 ..
1.4.m: who does not worship Śiva, the deliverer from such delusion? / Now I shall proclaim to you the measure of time; understand that.

1.4.s:
kāṣṭhā nimeṣā daśa paṃca cāhustriṃśacca kāṣṭhā gaṇayetkalā hi..
triṃśatkalāścāpi bhavenmuhurttaṃ tattriṃśatā rātryahanī ubhe ca.. 39.47 ..
1.4.d:
काष्ठा निमेषा दश पंच चाहुस्त्रिंशच्च काष्ठा गणयेत्कला हि..
त्रिंशत्कलाश्चापि भवेन्मुहुर्त्तं तत्त्रिंशता रात्र्यहनी उभे च.. 39.47 ..
1.4.m: Fifteen nimeṣas are called a kāṣṭhā, and thirty kāṣṭhās are reckoned a kalā; / thirty kalās make a muhūrta, and thirty of those make day and night together.

1.4.s:
divase paṃca kālāḥ syustrimuhūrtāḥ śrṛṇuṣva tān..
prātastataḥ saṃgavaśca madhyāhnaścāparāhṇakaḥ.. 39.48 ..
1.4.d:
दिवसे पंच कालाः स्युस्त्रिमुहूर्ताः श्रृणुष्व तान्..
प्रातस्ततः संगवश्च मध्याह्नश्चापराह्णकः.. 39.48 ..
1.4.m: There are five periods in a day, each of three muhūrtas; hear them: / morning (prātar), then mid-morning (saṃgava), midday (madhyāhna), afternoon (aparāhṇa),

1.4.s:
sāyāhnaḥ paṃcamaścāpi muhūrtā daśa paṃca ca..
ahorātrāḥ paṃcadaśa pakṣa ityabhidhīyate.. 39.49 ..
1.4.d:
सायाह्नः पंचमश्चापि मुहूर्ता दश पंच च..
अहोरात्राः पंचदश पक्ष इत्यभिधीयते.. 39.49 ..
1.4.m: and the fifth is evening (sāyāhna); and there are fifteen muhūrtas [in a day]. / Fifteen days and nights are termed a fortnight (pakṣa).

1.4.s:
māsaḥ pakṣadvayenokto dvau māsau cārkajāvṛtuḥ..
ṛtutrayaṃ cāpyayanaṃ dveyane varṣamucyate.. 39.50 ..
1.4.d:
मासः पक्षद्वयेनोक्तो द्वौ मासौ चार्कजावृतुः..
ऋतुत्रयं चाप्ययनं द्वेयने वर्षमुच्यते.. 39.50 ..
1.4.m: A month is spoken of as consisting of two fortnights; two months born of the sun form a season (ṛtu); / three seasons make a solstice (ayana), and two solstices are called a year.

1.4.s:
caturbhedaṃ māsamāhuḥ paṃcabhedaṃ ca vatsaram..
saṃvatsarastu prathamo dvitīyaḥ parivatsaraḥ.. 39.51 ..
1.4.d:
चतुर्भेदं मासमाहुः पंचभेदं च वत्सरम्..
संवत्सरस्तु प्रथमो द्वितीयः परिवत्सरः.. 39.51 ..
1.4.m: They declare the month to have four varieties, and the year to have five varieties: / the first is saṃvatsara, the second parivatsara,

1.4.s:
idvatsarastṛtīyo'sau caturthaścānuvatsaraḥ..
paṃcamaśca yugonāma gaṇanāniścayo hi saḥ.. 39.52 ..
1.4.d:
इद्वत्सरस्तृतीयोऽसौ चतुर्थश्चानुवत्सरः..
पंचमश्च युगोनाम गणनानिश्चयो हि सः.. 39.52 ..
1.4.m: the third is idvatsara, the fourth is anuvatsara, / and the fifth is named yuga; this is indeed the determination of the reckoning.

1.4.s:
māsena ca manuṣyāṇāmahorātraṃ ca paitṛkam..
kṛṣṇapakṣastvahaḥ proktaḥ śuklapakṣaśca śarvarī.. 39.53 ..
1.4.d:
मासेन च मनुष्याणामहोरात्रं च पैतृकम्..
कृष्णपक्षस्त्वहः प्रोक्तः शुक्लपक्षश्च शर्वरी.. 39.53 ..
1.4.m: A month of humans is a day and night of the ancestors: / the dark fortnight is declared their day, and the bright fortnight their night.

1.4.s:
mānuṣeṇa ca varṣeṇa daiviko divasaḥ smṛtaḥ..
ahastatro dagayanaṃ rātriḥ syāddakṣiṇāyanam.. 39.54 ..
1.4.d:
मानुषेण च वर्षेण दैविको दिवसः स्मृतः..
अहस्तत्रो दगयनं रात्रिः स्याद्दक्षिणायनम्.. 39.54 ..
1.4.m: A human year is known as a divine day: / the northern solstice (uttarāyaṇa) is the day, and the southern solstice (dakṣiṇāyana) is the night.

1.4.s:
varṣeṇa caiva devānāṃ mataḥ saptarṣivāsaraḥ..
saptarṣīṇāṃ ca varṣeṇa dhrauvaśca divasaḥ smṛtaḥ.. 39.55 ..
1.4.d:
वर्षेण चैव देवानां मतः सप्तर्षिवासरः..
सप्तर्षीणां च वर्षेण ध्रौवश्च दिवसः स्मृतः.. 39.55 ..
1.4.m: A year of the gods is considered a day of the seven seers; / and a year of the seven seers is known as a day of Dhruva.

1.4.s:
manuṣyāṇāṃ ca varṣāṇi lakṣāsaptadaśaiva tu..
aṣṭāviṃśatisahasrāṇi kṛtaṃ tretāyugaṃ tataḥ.. 39.56 ..
1.4.d:
मनुष्याणां च वर्षाणि लक्षासप्तदशैव तु..
अष्टाविंशतिसहस्राणि कृतं त्रेतायुगं ततः.. 39.56 ..
1.4.m: Seventeen lakhs and twenty-eight thousand years of humans / make the Kṛta [Yuga]; then the Tretā Yuga

1.4.s:
lakṣadvādaśasāhasraṣaṇnavatyadhikāḥ parāḥ..
aṣṭau lakṣāścatuḥṣaṣṭisahasrāṇi ca dvāparaḥ.. 39.57 ..
1.4.d:
लक्षद्वादशसाहस्रषण्नवत्यधिकाः पराः..
अष्टौ लक्षाश्चतुःषष्टिसहस्राणि च द्वापरः.. 39.57 ..
1.4.m: is further twelve lakhs ninety-six thousand; / eight lakhs and sixty-four thousand is the Dvāpara;

1.4.s:
caturlakṣaṃ tu dvātriṃśatsahasrāṇi kaliḥ smṛtaḥ..
caturbhiretairdevānāṃ yugāmityabhidhīyate.. 39.58 ..
1.4.d:
चतुर्लक्षं तु द्वात्रिंशत्सहस्राणि कलिः स्मृतः..
चतुर्भिरेतैर्देवानां युगामित्यभिधीयते.. 39.58 ..
1.4.m: and the Kali is recorded as four lakhs and thirty-two thousand. / These four together are called a yuga of the gods.

1.4.s:
āyurmanoryugānāṃ ca sādhikā hyekasaptatiḥ..
caturdaśamanūnāṃ ca kālena brahmaṇo dinam.. 39.59 ..
1.4.d:
आयुर्मनोर्युगानां च साधिका ह्येकसप्ततिः..
चतुर्दशमनूनां च कालेन ब्रह्मणो दिनम्.. 39.59 ..
1.4.m: The lifespan of a Manu is a little over seventy-one yugas; / and by the time of fourteen Manus a day of Brahmā [is completed].

1.4.s:
yugānāṃ ca sahasreṇa sa ca kalpaḥ śrṛṇuṣva tān..
bhavodbhavastapabhavya ṛturvahnirvarāhakaḥ.. 39.60 ..
1.4.d:
युगानां च सहस्रेण स च कल्पः श्रृणुष्व तान्..
भवोद्भवस्तपभव्य ऋतुर्वह्निर्वराहकः.. 39.60 ..
1.4.m: With a thousand such yugas [there is] a kalpa; hear them: / Bhavodbhava, Tapabhavya, Ṛtu, Vahni, Varāhaka,

1.4.s:
sāvitra āsikaścāpi gāṃdhāraḥ kuśikastathā..
ṛṣabhaśca tathā khaḍgo gāṃdhārīyaśca madhyamaḥ.. 39.61 ..
1.4.d:
सावित्र आसिकश्चापि गांधारः कुशिकस्तथा..
ऋषभश्च तथा खड्गो गांधारीयश्च मध्यमः.. 39.61 ..
1.4.m: Sāvitra, Āsika, Gāndhāra, Kuśika, / Ṛṣabha, Khaḍga, Gāndhārīya, Madhyama,

1.4.s:
vairājaśca niṣādaśca meghavāhanapaṃcamau..
citrako jñāna ākūtirmono daṃśaśca bṛṃhakaḥ.. 39.62 ..
1.4.d:
वैराजश्च निषादश्च मेघवाहनपंचमौ..
चित्रको ज्ञान आकूतिर्मोनो दंशश्च बृंहकः.. 39.62 ..
1.4.m: Vairāja, Niṣāda, and Meghavāhana as the fifth [of that set]; / Citraka, Jñāna, Ākūti, Mona, Daṃśa, Bṛṃhaka,

1.4.s:
śveto lohitaraktau ca pītavāsāḥ śivaḥ prabhuḥ..
sarvarūpaśca māso'yamevaṃ varṣaśatāvadhiḥ.. 39.63 ..
1.4.d:
श्वेतो लोहितरक्तौ च पीतवासाः शिवः प्रभुः..
सर्वरूपश्च मासोऽयमेवं वर्षशतावधिः.. 39.63 ..
1.4.m: Śveta, Lohitarakta, Pītavāsas, the Lord Śiva, / and Sarvarūpa; this makes a month, and thus up to the span of a hundred years.

1.4.s:
pūrvārdhamaparārdhaṃ ca brahmamānamidaṃ smṛtam..
viṣṇośca śaṃkarasyāpi nāhaṃ śaktaśca varṇane.. 39.64 ..
1.4.d:
पूर्वार्धमपरार्धं च ब्रह्ममानमिदं स्मृतम्..
विष्णोश्च शंकरस्यापि नाहं शक्तश्च वर्णने.. 39.64 ..
1.4.m: The first half (pūrvārdha) and the second half (parārdha)—this is recorded as the measure of Brahmā; / and of Viṣṇu and Śaṃkara, I am not capable of describing [their span].

1.4.s:
kvāhamalpamatiḥ pārtha kvāparau haritryaṃbakau..
devikenaiva mānena pātāleṣvapi gaṇyate.. 39.65 ..
1.4.d:
क्वाहमल्पमतिः पार्थ क्वापरौ हरित्र्यंबकौ..
देविकेनैव मानेन पातालेष्वपि गण्यते.. 39.65 ..
1.4.m: Where am I, of little intellect, O Pārtha, and where are the other two, Hari and the Three-Eyed Lord? / Even in the Pātālas, [time] is reckoned solely by divine measure.

1.4.s: iti te sūcitaṃ buddhyā śrṛṇu tatprākṛtaṃ punaḥ.. 39.66 ..
1.4.d: इति ते सूचितं बुद्ध्या श्रृणु तत्प्राकृतं पुनः.. 39.66 ..
1.4.m: Thus has it been indicated to you by intellect; listen again to that which belongs to Prakṛti.

1.4.s:
iti vaidhātravyavasthitiḥ..
..śrīnārada uvāca..
ṛṣabhonāma yannāmnā nānāpāṣaṃḍa kalpanāḥ..
kalau pārtha bhaviṣyaṃti lokānāṃ mohanātmikāḥ.. 39.67 ..
1.4.d:
इति वैधात्रव्यवस्थितिः..
..श्रीनारद उवाच..
ऋषभोनाम यन्नाम्ना नानापाषंड कल्पनाः..
कलौ पार्थ भविष्यंति लोकानां मोहनात्मिकाः.. 39.67 ..
1.4.m:
Thus ends the determination of Brahmā's [lifespan].
Śrī Nārada said:
There was one named Ṛṣabha, by whose name various heretical doctrines / will arise in the Kali age, O Pārtha, deluding the worlds.

1.4.s:
tasya putrastu bharataḥ śataśrṛṃgastu tatsutaḥ..
tasya putrāṣṭakaṃ jātaṃ tathaikāca kumārikā.. 39.68 ..
1.4.d:
तस्य पुत्रस्तु भरतः शतश्रृंगस्तु तत्सुतः..
तस्य पुत्राष्टकं जातं तथैकाच कुमारिका.. 39.68 ..
1.4.m: His son was Bharata, and Śataśṛṅga was his son. / To him were born eight sons and one daughter.

1.4.s:
iṃdradvīpaḥ kaseruśca tāmradvīpo gabhastimān..
nāgaḥ saumyaśca gāṃdharvo varuṇaśca kumārikā.. 39.69 ..
1.4.d:
इंद्रद्वीपः कसेरुश्च ताम्रद्वीपो गभस्तिमान्..
नागः सौम्यश्च गांधर्वो वरुणश्च कुमारिका.. 39.69 ..
1.4.m: Indradvīpa, Kaseru, Tāmradvīpa, Gabhastimān, / Nāga, Saumya, Gāndharva, Varuṇa, and Kumārikā.

1.4.s:
vadanaṃ cāpi kanyāyāḥ pārtha barkarikākṛti..
śrṛṇu tatkāraṇaṃ sarvaṃ mahāścaryasamanvitam.. 39.70 ..
1.4.d:
वदनं चापि कन्यायाः पार्थ बर्करिकाकृति..
श्रृणु तत्कारणं सर्वं महाश्चर्यसमन्वितम्.. 39.70 ..
1.4.m: And the face of the maiden, O Pārtha, had the form of a she-goat. / Hear the entire cause of that, full of great wonder:

1.4.s:
mahīsāgaraparyaṃtaṃ vṛkṣarājivirājite..
jālīgulmalatākīrṇe staṃbhatīrthasya saṃnidhau.. 39.71 ..
1.4.d:
महीसागरपर्यंतं वृक्षराजिविराजिते..
जालीगुल्मलताकीर्णे स्तंभतीर्थस्य संनिधौ.. 39.71 ..
1.4.m: Up to the confluence of the Mahī and the ocean, adorned with rows of trees, / dense with thickets of jālī-shrubs and creepers, in the vicinity of Stambhatīrtha,

1.4.s:
ajāsamajato madhyātkācidekā ca barkarī..
bhrāṃtā satī samāyātā pradeśe tatra duścare.. 39.72 ..
1.4.d:
अजासमजतो मध्यात्काचिदेका च बर्करी..
भ्रांता सती समायाता प्रदेशे तत्र दुश्चरे.. 39.72 ..
1.4.m: A certain she-goat, wandering from the midst of a flock of goats, / wandered and arrived at that impassable region.

1.4.s:
itastato bhramaṃti sā jālimadhye samaṃtataḥ..
nirgaṃtuṃ naiva śaknoti kṣutpipāsārditā śubhā.. 39.73 ..
1.4.d:
इतस्ततो भ्रमंति सा जालिमध्ये समंततः..
निर्गंतुं नैव शक्नोति क्षुत्पिपासार्दिता शुभा.. 39.73 ..
1.4.m: Wandering here and there within the jālī-thicket on all sides, / she was unable to get out, afflicted with hunger and thirst, fair though she was.

1.4.s:
vilagnā jālimadhye tu tataḥ paṃcatvamāgatā..
kālena kiyatā tasya truṭitvā śiraso hyadhaḥ.. 39.74 ..
1.4.d:
विलग्ना जालिमध्ये तु ततः पंचत्वमागता..
कालेन कियता तस्य त्रुटित्वा शिरसो ह्यधः.. 39.74 ..
1.4.m: Entangled in the jālī-thicket, she then met her death. / After some time, her [body] below the head severed,

1.4.s:
papāta śanidarśe ca mahīsāgarasaṃgame..
sarvatīrthamaye tatra sarvapāpapramocane.. 39.75 ..
1.4.d:
पपात शनिदर्शे च महीसागरसंगमे..
सर्वतीर्थमये तत्र सर्वपापप्रमोचने.. 39.75 ..
1.4.m: fell on a new-moon day into the confluence of the Mahī and the ocean, / which consists of all sacred fords and frees from all sins.

1.4.s:
śirastu tadavasthaṃ hi samagraṃ tatra saṃsthitam..
jāligulmāvalagnaṃ ca tasyā naivāpatajjale.. 39.76 ..
1.4.d:
शिरस्तु तदवस्थं हि समग्रं तत्र संस्थितम्..
जालिगुल्मावलग्नं च तस्या नैवापतज्जले.. 39.76 ..
1.4.m: Her head, remaining in that very state, stayed there intact; / caught in the jālī-shrub, it did not fall into the water.

1.4.s:
śeṣakāyaprapātena mahīsāgarasaṃgame..
tattīrthasya prabhāvena barkarīsā kurūdvaha.. 39.77 ..
1.4.d:
शेषकायप्रपातेन महीसागरसंगमे..
तत्तीर्थस्य प्रभावेन बर्करीसा कुरूद्वह.. 39.77 ..
1.4.m: Because the rest of the body fell into the confluence of the Mahī and the ocean, / by the power of that sacred ford, O best of the Kurus, that she-goat

1.4.s:
śakaśrṛṃgasya vai rājñaḥ siṃhaleṣvabhavatsutā..
mukhaṃ barkarikātulyaṃ vyaktaṃ tasyā vyajāyata.. 39.78 ..
1.4.d:
शकश्रृंगस्य वै राज्ञः सिंहलेष्वभवत्सुता..
मुखं बर्करिकातुल्यं व्यक्तं तस्या व्यजायत.. 39.78 ..
1.4.m: became the daughter of King Śakaśṛṅga among the Siṃhalas. / Clearly, her face was born resembling that of a she-goat.

1.4.s:
divyanārī śubhākārā śeṣakāye babhau śubhā..
pūrvaṃ tasyāpyaputrasya rājñaḥ putraśatopamā.. 39.79 ..
1.4.d:
दिव्यनारी शुभाकारा शेषकाये बभौ शुभा..
पूर्वं तस्याप्यपुत्रस्य राज्ञः पुत्रशतोपमा.. 39.79 ..
1.4.m: In the rest of her body, the auspicious girl shone as a divine, beautiful woman. / To the previously childless king, she was equal to a hundred sons,

1.4.s:
putrī jātā pramodena svajanānaṃdavardhinī..
tatastasyā vilokyātha mukhaṃ varkarikākṛti.. 39.80 ..
1.4.d:
पुत्री जाता प्रमोदेन स्वजनानंदवर्धिनी..
ततस्तस्या विलोक्याथ मुखं वर्करिकाकृति.. 39.80 ..
1.4.m: a daughter born with joy, increasing the delight of her kinsmen. / Then, seeing her face with the form of a she-goat,

1.4.s:
vismayaṃ samanuprāptāḥ sarve te rājapūruṣāḥ..
viṣādaṃ paramāpanno rājā sāṃtaḥpurastadā.. 39.81 ..
1.4.d:
विस्मयं समनुप्राप्ताः सर्वे ते राजपूरुषाः..
विषादं परमापन्नो राजा सांतःपुरस्तदा.. 39.81 ..
1.4.m: all those royal attendants were seized with astonishment. / The king, together with his inner quarters, was plunged into profound dejection.

1.4.s:
khinnāḥ prakṛtayaḥ sarvāstādṛgrūpavilokanāt..
tatkimityetadāścaryamūcuḥ paurāḥ suvismitāḥ.. 39.82 ..
1.4.d:
खिन्नाः प्रकृतयः सर्वास्तादृग्रूपविलोकनात्..
तत्किमित्येतदाश्चर्यमूचुः पौराः सुविस्मिताः.. 39.82 ..
1.4.m: All the subjects were grieved at seeing such a form. / Greatly amazed, the citizens said, “What wonder is this?”

1.4.s:
tataḥ sā yauvanaṃ prāptā sākṣāddevasutopamā..
svamukhaṃ darpaṇe vīkṣyasmṛtaḥ pūrvo bhavastayā.. 39.83 ..
1.4.d:
ततः सा यौवनं प्राप्ता साक्षाद्देवसुतोपमा..
स्वमुखं दर्पणे वीक्ष्यस्मृतः पूर्वो भवस्तया.. 39.83 ..
1.4.m: Then, having reached youth, resembling a veritable daughter of the gods, / she looked at her own face in a mirror and remembered her previous birth.

1.4.s:
tattīrthasya prabhāveṇa mātṛpitrorniveditam..
viṣādo naiva kartavyo madarthe tāta niścitam.. 39.84 ..
1.4.d:
तत्तीर्थस्य प्रभावेण मातृपित्रोर्निवेदितम्..
विषादो नैव कर्तव्यो मदर्थे तात निश्चितम्.. 39.84 ..
1.4.m: By the power of that sacred ford, she informed her parents: / “Grief should certainly not be felt on my account, dear father!

1.4.s:
mā śokaṃ kuru me mātaḥ pūrvajanmārjitaṃ phalam..
tataḥ pūrvaṃ svavṛttāṃtamuktvā sā ca kumārikā.. 39.85 ..
1.4.d:
मा शोकं कुरु मे मातः पूर्वजन्मार्जितं फलम्..
ततः पूर्वं स्ववृत्तांतमुक्त्वा सा च कुमारिका.. 39.85 ..
1.4.m: Do not grieve, mother; this is the fruit earned in a previous birth.” / Having spoken thus of her own former history, that maiden

1.4.s:
pūrvajanmodbhavaḥ kāyasyasyā yatrāpatattathā..
gamanāya tamuddeśaṃ vijñaptau pitarau tayā.. 39.86 ..
1.4.d:
पूर्वजन्मोद्भवः कायस्यस्या यत्रापतत्तथा..
गमनाय तमुद्देशं विज्ञप्तौ पितरौ तया.. 39.86 ..
1.4.m: petitioned her parents to travel to that region / where her body from the previous birth had fallen.

1.4.s:
ahaṃ tāta gamiṣyāmi mahīsāgarasaṃgamam..
bhavāmi tatra saṃprāptā yathā kuru tathā nṛpa.. 39.87 ..
1.4.d:
अहं तात गमिष्यामि महीसागरसंगमम्..
भवामि तत्र संप्राप्ता यथा कुरु तथा नृप.. 39.87 ..
1.4.m: “Dear father, I shall go to the confluence of the Mahī and the ocean. / O king, act in such a way that I may reach that place.”

1.4.s:
tataḥ pitrā pratijñātaṃ śataśrṛṃgeṇa tattathā..
tasyāḥ saṃvāhanaṃ cakre rājā potaiḥ saratnakaiḥ.. 39.88 ..
1.4.d:
ततः पित्रा प्रतिज्ञातं शतश्रृंगेण तत्तथा..
तस्याः संवाहनं चक्रे राजा पोतैः सरत्नकैः.. 39.88 ..
1.4.m: Then her father, Śataśṛṅga, promised her accordingly. / The king arranged her conveyance in boats laden with gems.

1.4.s:
staṃbhatīrthaṃ tataḥ sā'pi prāpya potāryasaṃyutā..
bhūridānaṃ tataścakre dānaṃ sarvasvalakṣaṇam.. 39.89 ..
1.4.d:
स्तंभतीर्थं ततः साऽपि प्राप्य पोतार्यसंयुता..
भूरिदानं ततश्चक्रे दानं सर्वस्वलक्षणम्.. 39.89 ..
1.4.m: Then she too, having reached Stambhatīrtha accompanied by boatmen, / made abundant gifts, presenting all her possessions.

1.4.s:
jāligulmāṃtare'nviṣya tato dṛṣṭaṃ nijaṃ śiraḥ..
asthicarmāvaśeṣaṃ ca tadādāya prayatnataḥ.. 39.90 ..
1.4.d:
जालिगुल्मांतरेऽन्विष्य ततो दृष्टं निजं शिरः..
अस्थिचर्मावशेषं च तदादाय प्रयत्नतः.. 39.90 ..
1.4.m: Searching within the jālī-thicket, she then saw her own head / reduced to bones and skin; taking it with great effort,

1.4.s:
dagdhvā saṃgamasāṃnidhye kṣiptānyasthīni saṃgame..
tatastīrthaprabhāveṇa mukhaṃ jātaṃ śaśiprabham.. 39.91 ..
1.4.d:
दग्ध्वा संगमसांनिध्ये क्षिप्तान्यस्थीनि संगमे..
ततस्तीर्थप्रभावेण मुखं जातं शशिप्रभम्.. 39.91 ..
1.4.m: she cremated it in the vicinity of the confluence and cast the bones into the confluence. / Then, by the power of the sacred ford, her face became radiant like the moon.

1.4.s:
na tādṛgdevakanyānāṃ na tādṛṅanāgayoṣitām..
na tādṛṅamartyanārīṇāṃ tasyā yādṛṅamukhaṃ mukham.. 39.92 ..
1.4.d:
न तादृग्देवकन्यानां न तादृङनागयोषिताम्..
न तादृङमर्त्यनारीणां तस्या यादृङमुखं मुखम्.. 39.92 ..
1.4.m: Neither celestial maidens, nor serpent women, / nor mortal women had such a face as her face became.

1.4.s:
surāsuranarāḥ sarve tasyā rūpeṇa mohitāḥ..
bahudhā prārthayaṃtyenāṃ na sā varamabhīpsati.. 39.93 ..
1.4.d:
सुरासुरनराः सर्वे तस्या रूपेण मोहिताः..
बहुधा प्रार्थयंत्येनां न सा वरमभीप्सति.. 39.93 ..
1.4.m: All gods, asuras, and mortals were captivated by her beauty. / They wooed her in many ways, but she did not desire a husband.

1.4.s:
kaṣṭaṃ tayā mudā tatra prārabdhaṃ duścaraṃ tapaḥ..
tataḥ saṃvatsare pūrṇe devadevo maheśvaraḥ.. 39.94 ..
1.4.d:
कष्टं तया मुदा तत्र प्रारब्धं दुश्चरं तपः..
ततः संवत्सरे पूर्णे देवदेवो महेश्वरः.. 39.94 ..
1.4.m: Joyfully, she undertook difficult and severe austerity there. / Then, when a full year had passed, the god of gods, Maheśvara,

1.4.s:
pratyakṣatāṃ gatastasyai varado'smīti cābravīt..
tatastaṃ pūjayitvā ca kumārī vākyamabravīt.. 39.95 ..
1.4.d:
प्रत्यक्षतां गतस्तस्यै वरदोऽस्मीति चाब्रवीत्..
ततस्तं पूजयित्वा च कुमारी वाक्यमब्रवीत्.. 39.95 ..
1.4.m: appeared before her eyes and said, “I am the giver of boons.” / Then, having worshipped him, the maiden spoke these words:

1.4.s:
yadi tuṣṭo'si deveśa yadi deyo varo mama..
sāṃnidhyaṃ kriyatāmatra sarvakālaṃ hi śaṃkara.. 39.96 ..
1.4.d:
यदि तुष्टोऽसि देवेश यदि देयो वरो मम..
सांनिध्यं क्रियतामत्र सर्वकालं हि शंकर.. 39.96 ..
1.4.m: “If you are pleased, O Lord of gods, if a boon is to be granted to me, / then establish your presence here for all time, O Śaṃkara.”

1.4.s:
evamastviti śarveṇa prokte hṛṣṭā kumārikā..
yatra dagdhaṃ śirastasyā barkaryāḥ kurusattama.. 39.97 ..
1.4.d:
एवमस्त्विति शर्वेण प्रोक्ते हृष्टा कुमारिका..
यत्र दग्धं शिरस्तस्या बर्कर्याः कुरुसत्तम.. 39.97 ..
1.4.m: When Śarva said, “So be it,” the maiden was delighted. / Where the head of that she-goat was cremated, O best of the Kurus,

1.4.s:
barkareśaḥ śivastatra tayā saṃsthāpitastadā..
manmukhānmahādāścaryaṃ śrutvedaṃ ca talātalāt.. 39.98 ..
1.4.d:
बर्करेशः शिवस्तत्र तया संस्थापितस्तदा..
मन्मुखान्महादाश्चर्यं श्रुत्वेदं च तलातलात्.. 39.98 ..
1.4.m: there she installed Śiva Barkareśa at that time. / Hearing this great wonder from my mouth, from Talātala

1.4.s:
svastikonāma nāgeṃdraḥ kumārīṃ draṣṭumāgataḥ..
śirasā gacchatā tena yatrotkṣiptā ca bhūrabhūt.. 39.99 ..
1.4.d:
स्वस्तिकोनाम नागेंद्रः कुमारीं द्रष्टुमागतः..
शिरसा गच्छता तेन यत्रोत्क्षिप्ता च भूरभूत्.. 39.99 ..
1.4.m: the lord of serpents named Svastika came to see the maiden. / As he traveled with his head, where the earth was cast up by him,
