1.4.m: and having heard about the supreme liṅga, he approached Mahākāla. / Then, recalling the words of Rudra, Mahākāla, smiling as it were, [addressed him]:

1.4.s:
pratyudgamya nṛpaṃ pūjāmarghaṃ ca pratyapādayat..
tataḥ kuśalapraśnādi kṛtvā śāṃtamukhaṃ nṛpaḥ.. 40.138 ..
1.4.d:
प्रत्युद्गम्य नृपं पूजामर्घं च प्रत्यपादयत्..
ततः कुशलप्रश्नादि कृत्वा शांतमुखं नृपः.. 40.138 ..
1.4.m: Going out to meet the king, he offered him worship and respectful water. / Then, having exchanged greetings of welfare and the like, the king, with a tranquil countenance, 40.138

1.4.s:
mahākālamupāmaṃtrya kathāṃte vākyamabravīt..
bhagavansaṃśayo mahyaṃ sadā'yaṃ parivartate.. 40.139 ..
1.4.d:
महाकालमुपामंत्र्य कथांते वाक्यमब्रवीत्..
भगवन्संशयो मह्यं सदाऽयं परिवर्तते.. 40.139 ..
1.4.m: Addressing Mahākāla, said these words at the end of the conversation: / 'O venerable one, this doubt always revolves in my mind: 40.139

1.4.s:
yadidaṃ tarpaṇaṃnāma pitṝṇāṃ kriyate nṛbhiḥ..
jalamadhye jalaṃ yāti kathaṃ tṛpyaṃti pūrvajāḥ.. 40.140 ..
1.4.d:
यदिदं तर्पणंनाम पितॄणां क्रियते नृभिः..
जलमध्ये जलं याति कथं तृप्यंति पूर्वजाः.. 40.140 ..
1.4.m: As for this offering of water which is made by men for the ancestors: / The water goes into the water; how do the ancestors become satisfied? 40.140

1.4.s:
evaṃ piṃḍādipūjā ca sarvamatraiva dṛśyate..
kathamevaṃ sma manyāmaḥ pitrādyairupabhujyate.. 40.141 ..
1.4.d:
एवं पिंडादिपूजा च सर्वमत्रैव दृश्यते..
कथमेवं स्म मन्यामः पित्राद्यैरुपभुज्यते.. 40.141 ..
1.4.m: Likewise, worship with rice-balls and the like is all seen right here; / how then do we think that it is enjoyed by fathers and the rest? 40.141

1.4.s:
na caitadasti yatteṣāṃ nopatiṣṭhati kiṃcana..
svapne yathākramya naraṃ dṛśyaṃte yācakāśca te.. 40.142 ..
1.4.d:
न चैतदस्ति यत्तेषां नोपतिष्ठति किंचन..
स्वप्ने यथाक्रम्य नरं दृश्यंते याचकाश्च ते.. 40.142 ..
1.4.m: Nor is it the case that nothing reaches them, / for in a dream they are seen approaching a man as beggars. 40.142

1.4.s:
devānāṃ cāpi dṛśyaṃte pratyakṣāḥ pratyayāḥ sadā..
tatkathaṃ pratigṛhṇanti mano me'tra pramuhyati.. 40.143 ..
1.4.d:
देवानां चापि दृश्यंते प्रत्यक्षाः प्रत्ययाः सदा..
तत्कथं प्रतिगृह्णन्ति मनो मेऽत्र प्रमुह्यति.. 40.143 ..
1.4.m: And perceptible proofs of the gods too are always seen. / How then do they receive it? My mind is bewildered in this matter.' 40.143

1.4.s:
..mahākāla uvāca..
yonirevaṃvidā teṣāṃ pitṝṇāṃ ca divaukasām..
dūroktaṃ dūrapūjā ca dūrastutirathāpi yat.. 40.144 ..
1.4.d:
..महाकाल उवाच..
योनिरेवंविदा तेषां पितॄणां च दिवौकसाम्..
दूरोक्तं दूरपूजा च दूरस्तुतिरथापि यत्.. 40.144 ..
1.4.m: Mahākāla said: / 'Such is the origin of those ancestors and of the gods in heaven, / that distant words, distant worship, and also distant praise— 40.144

1.4.s:
bhavyaṃ bhūtaṃ bhaviṣyacca sarvaṃ jānaṃti yāṃti ca..
paṃcatanmātrarūpaṃ ca manobuddhirahaṃjaḍāḥ.. 40.145 ..
1.4.d:
भव्यं भूतं भविष्यच्च सर्वं जानंति यांति च..
पंचतन्मात्ररूपं च मनोबुद्धिरहंजडाः.. 40.145 ..
1.4.m: They know and reach all that was, is, and will be. / Formed of the five subtle elements, mind, intellect, and egoism are insentient; 40.145

1.4.s:
navatattvamayaṃ dehaṃ daśamaḥ puruṣo mataḥ..
tasmādgaṃdhena tṛpyaṃti rasatattvena te tathā.. 40.146 ..
1.4.d:
नवतत्त्वमयं देहं दशमः पुरुषो मतः..
तस्माद्गंधेन तृप्यंति रसतत्त्वेन ते तथा.. 40.146 ..
1.4.m: The body consists of nine principles, and the person is considered the tenth. / Therefore they are satisfied by scent, and likewise by the principle of taste; 40.146

1.4.s:
śabdatattvena tuṣyaṃti sparśatattvaṃ ca gṛhṇate..
śuci dṛṣṭvā ta tuṣyaṃti nātra rājanbhavenmṛṣā.. 40.147 ..
1.4.d:
शब्दतत्त्वेन तुष्यंति स्पर्शतत्त्वं च गृह्णते..
शुचि दृष्ट्वा त तुष्यंति नात्र राजन्भवेन्मृषा.. 40.147 ..
1.4.m: They are pleased by the principle of sound, and they accept the principle of touch. / Seeing what is pure, they are pleased; herein, O king, there is no falsehood. 40.147

1.4.s:
yathā tṛṇaṃ paśūnāṃ ca narāṇāmannamucyate..
evaṃ daivatayonīnāmannasārasya bhojanam.. 40.148 ..
1.4.d:
यथा तृणं पशूनां च नराणामन्नमुच्यते..
एवं दैवतयोनीनामन्नसारस्य भोजनम्.. 40.148 ..
1.4.m: Just as grass is said to be for beasts and [solid] food for men, / even so is the eating of the essence of food for divine beings. 40.148

1.4.s:
śaktayaḥ sarvabhāvānāmaciṃtyā jñānagocarāḥ..
tasmāttattvaṃ pragṛhṇanti śeṣamatraiva dṛśyate.. 40.149 ..
1.4.d:
शक्तयः सर्वभावानामचिंत्या ज्ञानगोचराः..
तस्मात्तत्त्वं प्रगृह्णन्ति शेषमत्रैव दृश्यते.. 40.149 ..
1.4.m: The powers of all entities are unthinkable, accessible only to higher knowledge; / therefore they receive the essence, while the remainder is seen right here.' 40.149

1.4.s:
..karaṃdhama uvāca..
pitṛbhyo dīyate śrāddhaṃ svakarmavaśagāśca te..
svargasthā narakasthā vā kathaṃ tairupabhujyate.. 40.150 ..
1.4.d:
..करंधम उवाच..
पितृभ्यो दीयते श्राद्धं स्वकर्मवशगाश्च ते..
स्वर्गस्था नरकस्था वा कथं तैरुपभुज्यते.. 40.150 ..
1.4.m: Karandhama said: / 'The ancestral rite is offered to the ancestors, but they are subject to their own karma; / staying in heaven or staying in hell, how is it enjoyed by them? 40.150

1.4.s:
atha svarge'tha nareka sthitāḥ karmābhiyaṃtritāḥ..
śaknuvaṃti varānetāndātuṃ te ceśvarāḥ katham.. 40.151 ..
1.4.d:
अथ स्वर्गेऽथ नरेक स्थिताः कर्माभियंत्रिताः..
शक्नुवंति वरानेतान्दातुं ते चेश्वराः कथम्.. 40.151 ..
1.4.m: Moreover, dwelling in heaven or in hell, restrained by their karma, / how are they able to bestow these boons, and how are they masters? 40.151

1.4.s:
āyuḥ prajāṃ dhanaṃ vidyāṃ svargaṃ mokṣaṃ sukāni ca..
prayacchantu tathā rājyaṃ prītā nṝṇāṃ pitāmahāḥ.. 40.152 ..
1.4.d:
आयुः प्रजां धनं विद्यां स्वर्गं मोक्षं सुकानि च..
प्रयच्छन्तु तथा राज्यं प्रीता नॄणां पितामहाः.. 40.152 ..
1.4.m: [When it is said]: “May the ancestors, being pleased, bestow upon men / life, offspring, wealth, learning, heaven, liberation, pleasures, and kingship.”' 40.152

1.4.s:
..mahākāla uvāca..
satyametatasvakarmasthāḥ pitaro yannṛpottama..
kiṃ tu devāsurāṇāṃ ca yakṣādīnāmamūrtakāḥ.. 40.153 ..
1.4.d:
..महाकाल उवाच..
सत्यमेततस्वकर्मस्थाः पितरो यन्नृपोत्तम..
किं तु देवासुराणां च यक्षादीनाममूर्तकाः.. 40.153 ..
1.4.m: Mahākāla said: / 'It is true, O best of kings, that the ancestors abide by their own karma; / nevertheless, formless ancestors of the gods, the asuras, the yakṣas, and others, 40.153

1.4.s:
mūrtāścaturṇāṃ varṇānāṃ pitaraḥ saptadhā smṛtāḥ..
te hi sarve prayacchaṃti dātuṃ sarvaṃ yatopsitam.. 40.154 ..
1.4.d:
मूर्ताश्चतुर्णां वर्णानां पितरः सप्तधा स्मृताः..
ते हि सर्वे प्रयच्छंति दातुं सर्वं यतोप्सितम्.. 40.154 ..
1.4.m: And embodied ancestors of the four castes, are remembered as sevenfold. / Indeed, they all are able to bestow everything desired. 40.154

1.4.s:
ekatriṃśadgaṇā yeṣāṃ pitṝṇāṃ prabalā nṛpa..
kṛtaṃ ca tadidaṃ śrāddhaṃ tarpayettānparānpitṝn.. 40.155 ..
1.4.d:
एकत्रिंशद्गणा येषां पितॄणां प्रबला नृप..
कृतं च तदिदं श्राद्धं तर्पयेत्तान्परान्पितॄन्.. 40.155 ..
1.4.m: O king, the thirty-one groups of these ancestors are powerful; / and this ancestral rite that is performed satisfies those supreme ancestors. 40.155

1.4.s:
te tṛptāstarpayantyasya pūrvajānyatra saṃsthitān..
evaṃ svānāṃ copatiṣṭhecchrāddhaṃ yacchaṃti te varān.. 40.156 ..
1.4.d:
ते तृप्तास्तर्पयन्त्यस्य पूर्वजान्यत्र संस्थितान्..
एवं स्वानां चोपतिष्ठेच्छ्राद्धं यच्छंति ते वरान्.. 40.156 ..
1.4.m: They, being satisfied, satisfy one's own forefathers wherever they may abide. / In this way the ancestral rite reaches one's own people, and they grant boons.' 40.156

1.4.s:
..rājovāca..
bhūtādibhyo yathā vipra nāmnā voddiśya dīyate..
surādīnāṃ kathaṃ caiva saṃkṣepeṇa na dīyate.. 40.157 ..
1.4.d:
..राजोवाच..
भूतादिभ्यो यथा विप्र नाम्ना वोद्दिश्य दीयते..
सुरादीनां कथं चैव संक्षेपेण न दीयते.. 40.157 ..
1.4.m: The king said: / 'O brahmin, just as an offering is given to spirits and the like by name or by dedicating it, / why is it not given to gods and others in a concise manner as well: 40.157

1.4.s:
idaṃ pitṛbhyo devebhyo dvijebhyaḥ pāvakāya ca..
evaṃ kasmādvistarāḥ syurmanaḥ kāyādikaṣṭadāḥ.. 40.158 ..
1.4.d:
इदं पितृभ्यो देवेभ्यो द्विजेभ्यः पावकाय च..
एवं कस्माद्विस्तराः स्युर्मनः कायादिकष्टदाः.. 40.158 ..
1.4.m: “This is for the ancestors, the gods, the twice-born, and the fire”? / Why should there be such elaborate rituals that cause distress to mind, body, and the rest?' 40.158

1.4.s:
..mahākāla uvāca..
ucitā pratipattiśca kāryā sarveṣu nityaśaḥ..
pratipattiṃ cocitāṃ te vinā gṛhṇanti naiva ca.. 40.159 ..
1.4.d:
..महाकाल उवाच..
उचिता प्रतिपत्तिश्च कार्या सर्वेषु नित्यशः..
प्रतिपत्तिं चोचितां ते विना गृह्णन्ति नैव च.. 40.159 ..
1.4.m: Mahākāla said: / 'Proper honor must always be paid to all; / and without proper honor, they do not accept [the offering] at all. 40.159

1.4.s:
yathā śvā gṛhadvārastho baliṃ gṛhṇāti kiṃ tathā..
pradhānapuruṣo rājangṛhṇāti ca śunā samaḥ.. 40.160 ..
1.4.d:
यथा श्वा गृहद्वारस्थो बलिं गृह्णाति किं तथा..
प्रधानपुरुषो राजन्गृह्णाति च शुना समः.. 40.160 ..
1.4.m: Just as a dog standing at the house-door accepts an offering, / does a principal person, O king, accept it in the same manner, like a dog? 40.160

1.4.s:
evaṃ te bhūtavaddevā na hi gṛhṇanti karhicit..
śuci kāmaṃ juṣaṃte na haviraśraddadhānataḥ.. 40.161 ..
1.4.d:
एवं ते भूतवद्देवा न हि गृह्णन्ति कर्हिचित्..
शुचि कामं जुषंते न हविरश्रद्दधानतः.. 40.161 ..
1.4.m: Thus the gods never accept like spirits; / they do not partake of the oblation, pure though it may be, given without faith. 40.161

1.4.s:
vinā maṃtraiśca yaddattaṃ na tadgṛhṇanti te'malāḥ..
śrutirapyatra prāhedaṃ maṃtrāṇāṃ viṣaye nṛpa.. 40.162 ..
1.4.d:
विना मंत्रैश्च यद्दत्तं न तद्गृह्णन्ति तेऽमलाः..
श्रुतिरप्यत्र प्राहेदं मंत्राणां विषये नृप.. 40.162 ..
1.4.m: And what is given without mantras, those stainless ones do not receive. / The Veda also says this regarding mantras, O king: 40.162

1.4.s: "maṃtrā daivatā yadyadvidvānmantravatkaroti devatābhireva tatkaroti yaddadāni devatābhireva taddadāti yatpratigṛhṇāti devatābhireva tatpratigṛhṇāti tasmānnāmantravatpratigṛhṇīyāt nāmantravatpratipadyate" iti.. 40.163 ..
1.4.d: "मंत्रा दैवता यद्यद्विद्वान्मन्त्रवत्करोति देवताभिरेव तत्करोति यद्ददानि देवताभिरेव तद्ददाति यत्प्रतिगृह्णाति देवताभिरेव तत्प्रतिगृह्णाति तस्मान्नामन्त्रवत्प्रतिगृह्णीयात् नामन्त्रवत्प्रतिपद्यते" इति.. 40.163 ..
1.4.m: “The mantras are the deities. Whatever the learned person performs with a mantra, he performs with the deities themselves; whatever he gives, he gives through the deities themselves; whatever he receives, he receives through the deities themselves. Therefore one should not receive without a mantra, nor does one offer without a mantra.” 40.163

1.4.s:
tasmānmaṃtraiḥ sadā deyaṃ paurāṇairvaidikairapi..
anyathā te na gṛhṇanti bhūtānāmupatiṣṭhati.. 40.164 ..
1.4.d:
तस्मान्मंत्रैः सदा देयं पौराणैर्वैदिकैरपि..
अन्यथा ते न गृह्णन्ति भूतानामुपतिष्ठति.. 40.164 ..
1.4.m: Therefore it should always be given with mantras, whether Purāṇic or Vedic; / otherwise they do not accept it, and it reaches [only] the spirits.' 40.164

1.4.s:
..rājovāca..
darbhāṃstilānakṣatāṃśca toyaṃ caitaiḥ susaṃyutam..
kasmātpradīyate dānaṃ jñātumicchāmi kāraṇam.. 40.165 ..
1.4.d:
..राजोवाच..
दर्भांस्तिलानक्षतांश्च तोयं चैतैः सुसंयुतम्..
कस्मात्प्रदीयते दानं ज्ञातुमिच्छामि कारणम्.. 40.165 ..
1.4.m: The king said: / 'Why is a gift given accompanied with darbha-grass, sesame seeds, unbroken grains, and water? / I wish to know the reason.' 40.165

1.4.s:
..mahākāla uvāca..
purā kila pradattāni bhūmerdānāni bhūriśaḥ..
pratyagṛhṇanta daityāśca praviśyābhyaṃtaraṃ balāt.. 40.166 ..
1.4.d:
..महाकाल उवाच..
पुरा किल प्रदत्तानि भूमेर्दानानि भूरिशः..
प्रत्यगृह्णन्त दैत्याश्च प्रविश्याभ्यंतरं बलात्.. 40.166 ..
1.4.m: Mahākāla said: / 'In former times, indeed, gifts on earth were given in abundance, / and the Daityas, entering inside by force, snatched them away. 40.166

1.4.s: tato devāśca pitaraḥ pratyūcuḥ padmasaṃbhavam.. 40.167 ..
1.4.d: ततो देवाश्च पितरः प्रत्यूचुः पद्मसंभवम्.. 40.167 ..
1.4.m: Then the gods and the ancestors said to the lotus-born [Brahmā]: 40.167

1.4.s:
svāminnaḥ paśyatāmeva sarvaṃ daityaiḥ pragṛhyate..
vidhehi rakṣāṃ teṣāṃ tvaṃ na naṣṭaḥ smo yathā vayam.. 40.168 ..
1.4.d:
स्वामिन्नः पश्यतामेव सर्वं दैत्यैः प्रगृह्यते..
विधेहि रक्षां तेषां त्वं न नष्टः स्मो यथा वयम्.. 40.168 ..
1.4.m: “O Lord, while we are watching, everything is seized by the Daityas; / arrange protection for them, so that we are not destroyed.” 40.168

1.4.s:
tato vimṛśyaiva vidhī rakṣopāyamacīkarat..
tilairyuktaṃ pitṝṇāṃ ca devānāmakṣataiḥ saha.. 40.169 ..
1.4.d:
ततो विमृश्यैव विधी रक्षोपायमचीकरत्..
तिलैर्युक्तं पितॄणां च देवानामक्षतैः सह.. 40.169 ..
1.4.m: Then the Creator, having reflected, devised a means of protection: / combined with sesame seeds for the ancestors, and with unbroken grains for the gods, 40.169

1.4.s:
toyaṃ darbhāṃśca sarvatra evaṃ gṛhṇanti nāsurāḥ..
etānvinā pradattaṃ yatphalaṃ daityaiḥ pragṛhyate.. 40.170 ..
1.4.d:
तोयं दर्भांश्च सर्वत्र एवं गृह्णन्ति नासुराः..
एतान्विना प्रदत्तं यत्फलं दैत्यैः प्रगृह्यते.. 40.170 ..
1.4.m: Together with water and darbha-grass everywhere—in this way the asuras do not seize it. / Whatever is given without these, its fruit is seized by the Daityas. 40.170

1.4.s:
niḥśvasya pitaro devā yāṃti dātuḥ phalaṃ na hi..
tasmādyugeṣu sarveṣu dānameva pradīyate.. 40.171 ..
1.4.d:
निःश्वस्य पितरो देवा यांति दातुः फलं न हि..
तस्माद्युगेषु सर्वेषु दानमेव प्रदीयते.. 40.171 ..
1.4.m: Sighing, the ancestors and the gods depart, and there is no fruit for the giver; / therefore, in all the yugas, a gift is given in this very manner.' 40.171

1.4.s:
..karaṃdhama uvāca..
caturyugavyavasthānaṃ śrotumicchami tattvataḥ..
mahatīyaṃ vivitsā me sadaiva parivartate.. 40.172 ..
1.4.d:
..करंधम उवाच..
चतुर्युगव्यवस्थानं श्रोतुमिच्छमि तत्त्वतः..
महतीयं विवित्सा मे सदैव परिवर्तते.. 40.172 ..
1.4.m: Karandhama said: / 'I wish to hear accurately the system of the four yugas; / this great desire to know always turns in my mind.' 40.172

1.4.s:
..mahākāla uvāca..
ādyaṃ kṛtayugaṃ viddhitatastretāyugaṃ smṛtam..
dvāparaṃ ca kaliśceti catvāraśca samāsataḥ.. 40.173 ..
1.4.d:
..महाकाल उवाच..
आद्यं कृतयुगं विद्धिततस्त्रेतायुगं स्मृतम्..
द्वापरं च कलिश्चेति चत्वारश्च समासतः.. 40.173 ..
1.4.m: Mahākāla said: / 'Know that the first is Kṛtayuga; after that is recalled Tretāyuga, / Dvāpara, and Kali—thus there are four in brief. 40.173

1.4.s:
sattvaṃ kṛtaṃ rajastretā dvāparaṃ ca rajastamaḥ..
kalistamastu vijñeyaṃ yugavṛttaṃ yugeṣu ca.. 40.174 ..
1.4.d:
सत्त्वं कृतं रजस्त्रेता द्वापरं च रजस्तमः..
कलिस्तमस्तु विज्ञेयं युगवृत्तं युगेषु च.. 40.174 ..
1.4.m: Sattva is Kṛta, rajas is Tretā, and Dvāpara is rajas and tamas; / Kali is to be known as tamas; such is the conduct in the yugas. 40.174

1.4.s:
dhyānaṃ paraṃ kṛtayuge tretāyāṃ yajña ucyate..
vṛttaṃ ca dvāpare satyaṃ dānameva kalau yuge.. 40.175 ..
1.4.d:
ध्यानं परं कृतयुगे त्रेतायां यज्ञ उच्यते..
वृत्तं च द्वापरे सत्यं दानमेव कलौ युगे.. 40.175 ..
1.4.m: Meditation is supreme in Kṛtayuga; sacrifice is spoken of in Tretā; / in Dvāpara, righteous conduct and truth; [and] giving alone in the Kali yuga. 40.175

1.4.s:
kṛte tu mānasī sṛṣṭirvṛttiḥ sākṣādrasollasā..
tejomayyaḥ prajāstṛptāḥ sadānaṃdāśca bhoginaḥ.. 40.176 ..
1.4.d:
कृते तु मानसी सृष्टिर्वृत्तिः साक्षाद्रसोल्लसा..
तेजोमय्यः प्रजास्तृप्ताः सदानंदाश्च भोगिनः.. 40.176 ..
1.4.m: In Kṛta, creation is mental, and subsistence directly flourishes from [pure] essence; / the beings are luminous, satisfied, ever joyful, and enjoyers of delight. 40.176

1.4.s:
adhamottamo na tāsāṃ tā nirviśeṣāḥ prajāḥ śubhāḥ..
tulyamāyuḥ sukhaṃ rūpaṃ tāsāṃ tasminkṛte yuge.. 40.177 ..
1.4.d:
अधमोत्तमो न तासां ता निर्विशेषाः प्रजाः शुभाः..
तुल्यमायुः सुखं रूपं तासां तस्मिन्कृते युगे.. 40.177 ..
1.4.m: There is no low or high among them; those auspicious beings are without distinction; / their lifespan, happiness, and beauty are equal in that Kṛta yuga. 40.177

1.4.s:
na cāprītirna ca dvaṃdvo na dveṣo nāpi ca klamaḥ..
parvatodadhivāsinyo hyanukrośapriyāstu tāḥ.. 40.178 ..
1.4.d:
न चाप्रीतिर्न च द्वंद्वो न द्वेषो नापि च क्लमः..
पर्वतोदधिवासिन्यो ह्यनुक्रोशप्रियास्तु ताः.. 40.178 ..
1.4.m: There was no dislike, no pairs of opposites, no hatred, and no weariness. / Dwelling on mountains and shores of oceans, they were fond of compassion.

1.4.s:
varṇāśramavyavasthā ca tadāsīnna hi saṃkaraḥ..
ekamanyaṃ na dhyāyaṃti paramaṃ te sadā śivam.. 40.179 ..
1.4.d:
वर्णाश्रमव्यवस्था च तदासीन्न हि संकरः..
एकमन्यं न ध्यायंति परमं ते सदा शिवम्.. 40.179 ..
1.4.m: The order of classes and life-stages existed then, and there was no intermixture. / They meditated on no other [god], always on the one supreme Śiva.

1.4.s:
caturthe ca tataḥ pāde naṣṭa sā'bhūdrasollasā..
prādurāsaṃstatastāsāṃ vṛkṣāśvagṛhasaṃjñitāḥ.. 40.180 ..
1.4.d:
चतुर्थे च ततः पादे नष्ट साऽभूद्रसोल्लसा..
प्रादुरासंस्ततस्तासां वृक्षाश्वगृहसंज्ञिताः.. 40.180 ..
1.4.m: Then, in the fourth quarter, that radiance of sap was lost. / Thereupon, trees known as house-trees appeared for them.

1.4.s:
vastrāṇi ca prasūyaṃte phalānyābharaṇāni ca..
teṣveva jāyate tāsāṃ gaṃdhavarṇarasānvitam.. 40.181 ..
1.4.d:
वस्त्राणि च प्रसूयंते फलान्याभरणानि च..
तेष्वेव जायते तासां गंधवर्णरसान्वितम्.. 40.181 ..
1.4.m: They produced garments, fruits, and ornaments. / In them alone was born for those [creatures] endowed with fragrance, color, and taste,

1.4.s:
sumākṣikaṃ mahāvīryaṃ puṭake puṭake madhu..
tena tā vartayaṃti sma kṛtasyāṃte prajāstadā.. 40.182 ..
1.4.d:
सुमाक्षिकं महावीर्यं पुटके पुटके मधु..
तेन ता वर्तयंति स्म कृतस्यांते प्रजास्तदा.. 40.182 ..
1.4.m: excellent honey of great potency, [stored] in every hollow receptacle. / With that the creatures then sustained themselves at the end of the Kṛta [Yuga].

1.4.s:
hṛṣṭapuṣṭāstathā vṛddhāḥ prajā vai vigatajvarāḥ..
tataḥ kālena kenāpi tāsāṃ vṛddhe raseṃdriye.. 40.183 ..
1.4.d:
हृष्टपुष्टास्तथा वृद्धाः प्रजा वै विगतज्वराः..
ततः कालेन केनापि तासां वृद्धे रसेंद्रिये.. 40.183 ..
1.4.m: The creatures were joyful, robust, well-grown, and free from distress. / Then, in the course of time, as their sense of taste grew,

1.4.s:
yugabhāvāttathā dhyāne svalpībhūte śivasya ca..
vṛkṣāṃstānparyagṛhṇaṃta madhu vā mākṣikaṃ balāt.. 40.184 ..
1.4.d:
युगभावात्तथा ध्याने स्वल्पीभूते शिवस्य च..
वृक्षांस्तान्पर्यगृह्णंत मधु वा माक्षिकं बलात्.. 40.184 ..
1.4.m: and as meditation on Śiva dwindled due to the influence of the Yuga, / they seized those trees and took the sweet honey by force.

1.4.s:
tāsāṃ tenopacāreṇa lobhadoṣakṛtena vai..
pranaṣṭā madhunā sārdhaṃ kalpavṛkṣāḥ kvacitkvacit.. 40.185 ..
1.4.d:
तासां तेनोपचारेण लोभदोषकृतेन वै..
प्रनष्टा मधुना सार्धं कल्पवृक्षाः क्वचित्क्वचित्.. 40.185 ..
1.4.m: Because of that conduct of theirs caused by the fault of greed, / the wish-fulfilling trees disappeared here and there along with the honey.

1.4.s:
tasyāṃ cāpyalpaśiṣṭāyāṃ dvaṃdvānyabhyutthitāni vai..
śītātapairmanoduḥkhaistatastā duḥkhitā bhṛśam.. 40.186 ..
1.4.d:
तस्यां चाप्यल्पशिष्टायां द्वंद्वान्यभ्युत्थितानि वै..
शीतातपैर्मनोदुःखैस्ततस्ता दुःखिता भृशम्.. 40.186 ..
1.4.m: And when only a little of it was left, the pairs of opposites arose indeed. / Then they suffered greatly from cold and heat and mental distress.

1.4.s:
cakrurāvaraṇārthaṃ hi ketanāni tatastataḥ..
tataḥ pradurbabhau tāsāṃ siddhistretāyuge punaḥ.. 40.187 ..
1.4.d:
चक्रुरावरणार्थं हि केतनानि ततस्ततः..
ततः प्रदुर्बभौ तासां सिद्धिस्त्रेतायुगे पुनः.. 40.187 ..
1.4.m: For the sake of shelter, they made dwellings here and there. / Then, in the Tretā Yuga, a means of subsistence appeared for them again.

1.4.s:
vṛṣṭyā babhūvurauṣadhyo grāmyāraṇyāścaturdaśa..
akṛṣṭapacyānūptāstoyabhūmisamāgamāt.. 40.188 ..
1.4.d:
वृष्ट्या बभूवुरौषध्यो ग्राम्यारण्याश्चतुर्दश..
अकृष्टपच्यानूप्तास्तोयभूमिसमागमात्.. 40.188 ..
1.4.m: Through rain, fourteen kinds of plants, both cultivated and wild, came into being; / growing without tilling and unsown, through the union of water and earth.

1.4.s:
ṛtu puṣpaphalaiścaiva vṛkṣagulmāśca jajñire..
taiśca vṛttirabhūttāsāṃ dhānyaiḥ puṣpaiḥ phalaistathā.. 40.189 ..
1.4.d:
ऋतु पुष्पफलैश्चैव वृक्षगुल्माश्च जज्ञिरे..
तैश्च वृत्तिरभूत्तासां धान्यैः पुष्पैः फलैस्तथा.. 40.189 ..
1.4.m: Trees and shrubs were also born with seasonal flowers and fruits. / By means of these—grains, flowers, and fruits—they made their living.

1.4.s:
tataḥ punarabhūttāsāṃ rāgo lobhaśca sarvataḥ..
kālavīryeṇa vā gṛhya nadīkṣetrāṇi parvatān.. 40.190 ..
1.4.d:
ततः पुनरभूत्तासां रागो लोभश्च सर्वतः..
कालवीर्येण वा गृह्य नदीक्षेत्राणि पर्वतान्.. 40.190 ..
1.4.m: Then passion and greed arose everywhere among them once more. / Through the force of time, seizing rivers, fields, and mountains,

1.4.s:
vṛkṣagulmauṣadhīścaiva prasahyāśu yathābalam..
viparyayeṇa cauṣadhyaḥ pranaṣṭāśca caturdaśa.. 40.191 ..
1.4.d:
वृक्षगुल्मौषधीश्चैव प्रसह्याशु यथाबलम्..
विपर्ययेण चौषध्यः प्रनष्टाश्च चतुर्दश.. 40.191 ..
1.4.m: and violently overtaking trees, shrubs, and plants as quickly as they could with their strength, / through their perversity the fourteen kinds of plants vanished.

1.4.s:
natvā dharāṃ praviṣṭāstā oṣadhyaḥ pīḍitāḥ prajāḥ..
dudoha gāṃ pṛthurvainyaḥ sarvabhūtahitāya vai.. 40.192 ..
1.4.d:
नत्वा धरां प्रविष्टास्ता ओषध्यः पीडिताः प्रजाः..
दुदोह गां पृथुर्वैन्यः सर्वभूतहिताय वै.. 40.192 ..
1.4.m: Having bowed down, those plants entered the earth, and the creatures were afflicted. / Pṛthu, the son of Vena, milked the earth for the welfare of all beings.

1.4.s:
tadā prabhṛti cauṣadhyaḥ phālakṛṣṭāḥ prajāstataḥ..
vārttayā vartayaṃti sma pālyamānāśca kṣatriyaiḥ.. 40.193 ..
1.4.d:
तदा प्रभृति चौषध्यः फालकृष्टाः प्रजास्ततः..
वार्त्तया वर्तयंति स्म पाल्यमानाश्च क्षत्रियैः.. 40.193 ..
1.4.m: From that time forward, plants were produced by tilling with a plow. / Then the creatures lived by means of agriculture, protected by kṣatriyas.

1.4.s:
varṇāśramapratiṣṭhā ca yajñastretāsu cocyate..
sadāśivadhyānamayaṃ tyaktvā mokṣamacetanāḥ.. 40.194 ..
1.4.d:
वर्णाश्रमप्रतिष्ठा च यज्ञस्त्रेतासु चोच्यते..
सदाशिवध्यानमयं त्यक्त्वा मोक्षमचेतनाः.. 40.194 ..
1.4.m: The establishment of classes and life-stages, and sacrificial ritual, are declared in the Tretā [yugas]. / Having abandoned liberation consisting in meditation on Sadāśiva, the senseless ones,

1.4.s:
puṣpitāṃ vācamāśritya rāgātsvargamasādhayan..
dvāpare ca pravartaṃte matibhedāstato nṛṇām.. 40.195 ..
1.4.d:
पुष्पितां वाचमाश्रित्य रागात्स्वर्गमसाधयन्..
द्वापरे च प्रवर्तंते मतिभेदास्ततो नृणाम्.. 40.195 ..
1.4.m: resorting to flowery speech, pursued heaven out of passion. / In the Dvāpara, divisions of views arise among men.

1.4.s:
manasā karmaṇā vācā kṛcchrādvārtā prasidhyati..
lobho'dhṛtiḥ śivaṃ tyaktvā dharmāṇāṃ saṃkarastathā.. 40.196 ..
1.4.d:
मनसा कर्मणा वाचा कृच्छ्राद्वार्ता प्रसिध्यति..
लोभोऽधृतिः शिवं त्यक्त्वा धर्माणां संकरस्तथा.. 40.196 ..
1.4.m: By mind, deed, and speech, agriculture is accomplished with hardship. / Greed, impatience, abandoning Śiva, and mixture of duties,

1.4.s:
varṇāśramaparidhvaṃsāḥ pravartaṃte ca dvāpare..
tadā vyāsaiścaturddhā ca vyasyate dvāparāttataḥ.. 40.197 ..
1.4.d:
वर्णाश्रमपरिध्वंसाः प्रवर्तंते च द्वापरे..
तदा व्यासैश्चतुर्द्धा च व्यस्यते द्वापरात्ततः.. 40.197 ..
1.4.m: and the destruction of classes and life-stages occur in the Dvāpara. / Then, by reason of the Dvāpara, [the Veda] is divided fourfold by the Vyāsas.

1.4.s:
eko vedaścatuṣpādaiḥ kriyate dvijahetave..
itihāsapurāṇāni bhidyaṃte lokagauravāt.. 40.198 ..
1.4.d:
एको वेदश्चतुष्पादैः क्रियते द्विजहेतवे..
इतिहासपुराणानि भिद्यंते लोकगौरवात्.. 40.198 ..
1.4.m: The single Veda is made into four parts for the sake of the twice-born. / The Epics and Purāṇas are divided out of respect for the world.

1.4.s:
brāhmaṃ pādmaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ ca śaivaṃ bhāgavataṃ tathā..
tathānyannāradīya ca mārkaṃḍeyaṃ ca saptamama.. 40.199 ..
1.4.d:
ब्राह्मं पाद्मं वैष्णवं च शैवं भागवतं तथा..
तथान्यन्नारदीय च मार्कंडेयं च सप्तमम.. 40.199 ..
1.4.m: The Brāhma, Pādma, Vaiṣṇava, Śaiva, and Bhāgavata; / likewise another, the Nāradīya, and the Mārkaṇḍeya as the seventh;

1.4.s:
āgneyamaṣṭamaṃ proktaṃ bhaviṣyaṃ navamaṃ smṛtam..
daśamaṃ brahmavaivartaṃ laiṃgamekādaśaṃ tathā.. 40.200 ..
1.4.d:
आग्नेयमष्टमं प्रोक्तं भविष्यं नवमं स्मृतम्..
दशमं ब्रह्मवैवर्तं लैंगमेकादशं तथा.. 40.200 ..
1.4.m: the Āgneya is declared as the eighth; the Bhaviṣya is remembered as the ninth; / the tenth is the Brahmavaivarta, and the Liṅga is the eleventh;

1.4.s:
vārāhaṃ dvādaśaṃ caiva skāṃdaṃ caiva trayodaśam..
caturdaśaṃ vāmanaṃ ca kaurmaṃ paṃcadaśaṃ smṛtam.. 40.201 ..
1.4.d:
वाराहं द्वादशं चैव स्कांदं चैव त्रयोदशम्..
चतुर्दशं वामनं च कौर्मं पंचदशं स्मृतम्.. 40.201 ..
1.4.m: the Vārāha as the twelfth, and the Skānda as the thirteenth; / the Vāmana is the fourteenth, and the Kūrma is remembered as the fifteenth;

1.4.s:
mātsyaṃ ṣoḍaśakaṃ proktaṃ gāruḍaṃ ca tataḥ param..
ataḥ paraṃ tu brahmāṃḍamevañcāṣṭādaśāni hi.. 40.202 ..
1.4.d:
मात्स्यं षोडशकं प्रोक्तं गारुडं च ततः परम्..
अतः परं तु ब्रह्मांडमेवञ्चाष्टादशानि हि.. 40.202 ..
1.4.m: the Mātsya is declared as the sixteenth, and after that the Gāruḍa; / and beyond that the Brahmāṇḍa—thus are the eighteen indeed.

1.4.s:
asminvārāhakalpe ca vyāsānākarṇayasva ca..
ṛtuḥ satyo bhārgavaśca aṃgirāḥ savitā tathā.. 40.203 ..
1.4.d:
अस्मिन्वाराहकल्पे च व्यासानाकर्णयस्व च..
ऋतुः सत्यो भार्गवश्च अंगिराः सविता तथा.. 40.203 ..
1.4.m: And in this Vārāha Kalpa, listen to the Vyāsas: / Ṛtu, Satya, Bhārgava, and Aṅgiras, likewise Savitṛ,

1.4.s:
mṛtyuḥ śatakraturdhīmānvasiṣṭho bhavitā'dhunā..
sārasvatastridhāmā ca vedavittrivṛto muniḥ.. 40.204 ..
1.4.d:
मृत्युः शतक्रतुर्धीमान्वसिष्ठो भविताऽधुना..
सारस्वतस्त्रिधामा च वेदवित्त्रिवृतो मुनिः.. 40.204 ..
1.4.m: Mṛtyu, the wise Śatakratu, Vasiṣṭha will be [the next] now, / Sārasvata, Tridhāman, and the sage Trivṛta, knower of the Veda,

1.4.s:
śatatejāḥ svayaṃ viṣṇurnārāyaṇa iti smṛtaḥ..
karakaścāruṇirdhīmāstathā deva ṛtaṃjayaḥ.. 40.205 ..
1.4.d:
शततेजाः स्वयं विष्णुर्नारायण इति स्मृतः..
करकश्चारुणिर्धीमास्तथा देव ऋतंजयः.. 40.205 ..
1.4.m: Śatatejas, Viṣṇu himself remembered as Nārāyaṇa, / Karaka, the wise Āruṇi, and Deva Ṛtañjaya,

1.4.s:
kṛtaṃjayo bharadvājo gautamaḥ kavisattamaḥ..
vājaśravā muniścaiva tathā yuṣmāyaṇo muniḥ.. 40.206 ..
1.4.d:
कृतंजयो भरद्वाजो गौतमः कविसत्तमः..
वाजश्रवा मुनिश्चैव तथा युष्मायणो मुनिः.. 40.206 ..
1.4.m: Kṛtañjaya, Bharadvāja, Gautama best of poets, / the sage Vājaśravas, and likewise the sage Yuṣmāyaṇa,

1.4.s:
tṛṇabiṃdustathā ṛkṣaḥ śaktiḥ pārāśarastathā..
jātūkarṇyo'tha viṣṇuśca svayaṃdvaipāyano muniḥ.. 40.207 ..
1.4.d:
तृणबिंदुस्तथा ऋक्षः शक्तिः पाराशरस्तथा..
जातूकर्ण्योऽथ विष्णुश्च स्वयंद्वैपायनो मुनिः.. 40.207 ..
1.4.m: Tṛṇabindu, Ṛkṣa, Śakti, Pārāśarya, / Jātūkarṇya, and Viṣṇu himself as the sage Dvaipāyana.

1.4.s:
aśvatthāmamukhāścaite bhaviṣyāḥ sūcitāstava..
dharmaśāstrāṇi lokārthaṃ bhidyaṃte cāpi dvāpare.. 40.208 ..
1.4.d:
अश्वत्थाममुखाश्चैते भविष्याः सूचितास्तव..
धर्मशास्त्राणि लोकार्थं भिद्यंते चापि द्वापरे.. 40.208 ..
1.4.m: And these future ones headed by Aśvatthāman have been indicated to you. / Treatises on dharma are also divided in the Dvāpara for the sake of the world.

1.4.s:
manvatriviṣṇuhāritayājñavalkyośanoṃgirāḥ..
yamāpastaṃbasaṃvartāḥ kātyāyanabṛhaspatī.. 40.209 ..
1.4.d:
मन्वत्रिविष्णुहारितयाज्ञवल्क्योशनोंगिराः..
यमापस्तंबसंवर्ताः कात्यायनबृहस्पती.. 40.209 ..
1.4.m: Manu, Atri, Viṣṇu, Hārīta, Yājñavalkya, Uśanas, Aṅgiras, / Yama, Āpastamba, Saṃvarta, Kātyāyana, Bṛhaspati,

1.4.s:
parāśaravyāsaśaṃkhalikhitā dakṣagautamau..
śātātapo vasiṣṭhaśca dharmaśāstraprayojakāḥ.. 40.210 ..
1.4.d:
पराशरव्यासशंखलिखिता दक्षगौतमौ..
शातातपो वसिष्ठश्च धर्मशास्त्रप्रयोजकाः.. 40.210 ..
1.4.m: Parāśara, Vyāsa, Śaṅkha, Likhita, Dakṣa, Gautama, / Śātātapa, and Vasiṣṭha are the promulgators of dharmaśāstra.

1.4.s:
tato dvāparasaṃdhyāyāṃ pravartati kalau yuge..
naśyamāne śaivayoge jāyaṃte yoganaṃdanāḥ.. 40.211 ..
1.4.d:
ततो द्वापरसंध्यायां प्रवर्तति कलौ युगे..
नश्यमाने शैवयोगे जायंते योगनंदनाः.. 40.211 ..
1.4.m: Then, in the twilight of the Dvāpara, the Kali Yuga sets in. / When the Śaiva Yoga is perishing, the sons of Yoga are born:

1.4.s:
ādye śvetakalaurudraḥ sutārastāraṇastathā..
suhotraḥ kaṃkaṇaścaiva lokākhyaśca mahāmuniḥ.. 40.212 ..
1.4.d:
आद्ये श्वेतकलौरुद्रः सुतारस्तारणस्तथा..
सुहोत्रः कंकणश्चैव लोकाख्यश्च महामुनिः.. 40.212 ..
1.4.m: In the first Śveta-kali, Rudra, Sutāra, and Tāraṇa, / Suhotra, Kaṅkaṇa, and the great sage named Lokākhya,

1.4.s:
jaigīṣavyaśca bhāvyo vai bhagavāndadhivāhanaḥ..
ṛṣabhaśca munirdharmaugraścātriḥ sabālakaḥ.. 40.213 ..
1.4.d:
जैगीषव्यश्च भाव्यो वै भगवान्दधिवाहनः..
ऋषभश्च मुनिर्धर्मौग्रश्चात्रिः सबालकः.. 40.213 ..
1.4.m: and Jaigīṣavya, the future lord Dadhivāhana, / the sage Ṛṣabha, Dharmaugra, and Atri with his child,

1.4.s:
gautamau vedaśīrṇaśca gokarṇaśca śikhaṃḍibhṛt..
gṛhāvāsī jaṭāmālī aṭṭahāsaśca dāruṇaḥ.. 40.214 ..
1.4.d:
गौतमौ वेदशीर्णश्च गोकर्णश्च शिखंडिभृत्..
गृहावासी जटामाली अट्टहासश्च दारुणः.. 40.214 ..
1.4.m: Gautama, Vedaśīrṣan, Gokarṇa, Śikhaṇḍibhṛt, / Gṛhāvāsin, Jaṭāmālin, Aṭṭahāsa, and Dāruṇa,

1.4.s:
lāṃgalī saṃyamī śūlī ḍiṃḍī juṇḍīśvaraḥ svayam..
sahiṣṇuḥ somaśarmā ca lakulīśaśca pārthiva.. 40.215 ..
1.4.d:
लांगली संयमी शूली डिंडी जुण्डीश्वरः स्वयम्..
सहिष्णुः सोमशर्मा च लकुलीशश्च पार्थिव.. 40.215 ..
1.4.m: Lāṅgalin, Saṃyamin, Śūlin, Ḍiṇḍin, Juṇḍīśvara himself, / Sahiṣṇu, Somaśarman, and Lakulīśa, O king,

1.4.s:
kāyāvarohaṇo bhāvītyādyā yogeśvarāḥ kramāt..
ete saṃkṣipta vakṣyaṃti śivadharmaṃ kalau yuge.. 40.216 ..
1.4.d:
कायावरोहणो भावीत्याद्या योगेश्वराः क्रमात्..
एते संक्षिप्त वक्ष्यंति शिवधर्मं कलौ युगे.. 40.216 ..
1.4.m: and Kāyāvarohaṇa who is to be—such are the lords of Yoga in succession. / These will concisely teach the Śiva-dharma in the Kali Yuga.

1.4.s:
evaṃ kaliyuge rājañchāstrasaṃkṣepa ucyate..
śrṛṇu tiṣyapravṛttiṃ ca harṣodvegakarīṃ kila.. 40.217 ..
1.4.d:
एवं कलियुगे राजञ्छास्त्रसंक्षेप उच्यते..
श्रृणु तिष्यप्रवृत्तिं च हर्षोद्वेगकरीं किल.. 40.217 ..
1.4.m: Thus, O king, the abridgment of the scriptures in the Kali Yuga is explained. / Hear also the manifestation of the Kali age, which causes both joy and agitation.

1.4.s:
tiṣye māyāmasūyāṃ ca vadhaṃ caiva tapasvinām..
sādhayaṃti narāstatra tamasā vyākuleṃdriyāḥ.. 40.218 ..
1.4.d:
तिष्ये मायामसूयां च वधं चैव तपस्विनाम्..
साधयंति नरास्तत्र तमसा व्याकुलेंद्रियाः.. 40.218 ..
1.4.m: In the Kali age, men whose senses are agitated by darkness / practice deceit, malice, and the killing of ascetics.

1.4.s:
kalau pramāthako rāgaḥ satataṃ kṣudbhayāni ca..
anāvṛṣṭibhayaṃ ghoraṃ deśānāṃ ca viparyayaḥ.. 40.219 ..
1.4.d:
कलौ प्रमाथको रागः सततं क्षुद्भयानि च..
अनावृष्टिभयं घोरं देशानां च विपर्ययः.. 40.219 ..
1.4.m: In the Kali [Yuga] there is tormenting passion, constant fear of hunger, / terrible fear of drought, and ruin of countries.

1.4.s:
na pramāṇaṃ śruterasti nṛṇāṃ cādharmasevanāt..
adhārmikāstvanācārā mahākopālpatejasaḥ.. 40.220 ..
1.4.d:
न प्रमाणं श्रुतेरस्ति नृणां चाधर्मसेवनात्..
अधार्मिकास्त्वनाचारा महाकोपाल्पतेजसः.. 40.220 ..
1.4.m: Due to men practicing unrighteousness, Vedic revelation is no longer an authority. / They are unrighteous, ill-behaved, exceedingly wrathful, and of little splendor.

1.4.s:
anṛtaṃ bruvate lubdhā nārīprāyāśca duṣprajāḥ..
duriṣṭairduradhītaiśca durācārairdurāgamaiḥ.. 40.221 ..
1.4.d:
अनृतं ब्रुवते लुब्धा नारीप्रायाश्च दुष्प्रजाः..
दुरिष्टैर्दुरधीतैश्च दुराचारैर्दुरागमैः.. 40.221 ..
1.4.m: Greedy, they tell lies, and base offspring consist mostly of females, / through improper sacrifices, improper studies, improper conduct, and improper scriptures.

1.4.s:
viprāṇāṃ karmadoṣaiśca prajānāṃ jāyate kṣayaḥ..
utsīdaṃti kṣatraviśo vardhaṃte śūdraviprakāḥ.. 40.222 ..
1.4.d:
विप्राणां कर्मदोषैश्च प्रजानां जायते क्षयः..
उत्सीदंति क्षत्रविशो वर्धंते शूद्रविप्रकाः.. 40.222 ..
1.4.m: And through faults in the deeds of brahmins, the destruction of subjects occurs. / The kṣatriyas and vaiśyas decline, while degraded śūdras and degraded brahmins multiply.

1.4.s:
śūdrā vipraiḥ sahāsaṃte śayanāsanabhojanaiḥ..
śūdrāśca brāhmaṇācārāḥ śūdrācārāśca brāhmaṇāḥ.. 40.223 ..
1.4.d:
शूद्रा विप्रैः सहासंते शयनासनभोजनैः..
शूद्राश्च ब्राह्मणाचाराः शूद्राचाराश्च ब्राह्मणाः.. 40.223 ..
1.4.m: Śūdras live together with brahmins in sleeping, sitting, and dining. / And śūdras practice the conduct of brahmins, while brahmins practice the conduct of śūdras.

1.4.s:
rājavṛttyāṃ sthitāścaurāścaurācārāśca pārthivāḥ..
ekapatnyo na śiṣyaṃti vardhayaṃtyabhisārikāḥ.. 40.224 ..
1.4.d:
राजवृत्त्यां स्थिताश्चौराश्चौराचाराश्च पार्थिवाः..
एकपत्न्यो न शिष्यंति वर्धयंत्यभिसारिकाः.. 40.224 ..
1.4.m: Thieves adopt the livelihood of kings, and rulers adopt the conduct of thieves. / Faithful wives do not remain; unchaste women multiply.

1.4.s:
tadā hyalpaphalā bhūmiḥ kvaciccāpi mahāphalā..
arakṣitāro hartāro rājānaḥ pāpanirbhayāḥ.. 40.225 ..
1.4.d:
तदा ह्यल्पफला भूमिः क्वचिच्चापि महाफला..
अरक्षितारो हर्तारो राजानः पापनिर्भयाः.. 40.225 ..
1.4.m: Then indeed the earth yields little fruit, though in some places it yields great fruit. / Kings become robbers instead of protectors, devoid of fear of sin.

1.4.s:
akṣatriyāstu rājāno viprāḥ śūdropajīvinaḥ..
śūdrā vivādinaḥ sarve brāhmaṇairabhinaṃditāḥ.. 40.226 ..
1.4.d:
अक्षत्रियास्तु राजानो विप्राः शूद्रोपजीविनः..
शूद्रा विवादिनः सर्वे ब्राह्मणैरभिनंदिताः.. 40.226 ..
1.4.m: Non-kṣatriyas become kings; brahmins subsist on śūdras. / All śūdras become disputants, applauded by brahmins.

1.4.s:
āsanasthāndvijāndṛṣṭvā calaṃtyatyalpabuddhayaḥ..
āsye nidhāya vai hastaṃ karṇe śūdrāsya ca dvijāḥ.. 40.227 ..
1.4.d:
आसनस्थान्द्विजान्दृष्ट्वा चलंत्यत्यल्पबुद्धयः..
आस्ये निधाय वै हस्तं कर्णे शूद्रास्य च द्विजाः.. 40.227 ..
1.4.m: Seeing seated twice-born [brahmins], those of very petty intellect do not rise. / And placing a hand over the mouth, twice-born men whisper into the ear of a śūdra;

1.4.s:
nīcasyāpi tadā vākyaṃ vakṣyaṃti vinayena tam..
uccāsanasthāñchūdrāṃśca dvijānāṃ paśyatāmapi.. 40.228 ..
1.4.d:
नीचस्यापि तदा वाक्यं वक्ष्यंति विनयेन तम्..
उच्चासनस्थाञ्छूद्रांश्च द्विजानां पश्यतामपि.. 40.228 ..
1.4.m: even to a low-born man they will then speak words with humility. / And even as the twice-born look on, śūdras occupy high seats.

1.4.s:
jñātvā na hiṃsate rājā paśya kālabalaṃ nṛpa..
puṣpaiḥ śubhasitaiścaiva tathānyairmaṃḍanairdvijāḥ.. 40.229 ..
1.4.d:
ज्ञात्वा न हिंसते राजा पश्य कालबलं नृप..
पुष्पैः शुभसितैश्चैव तथान्यैर्मंडनैर्द्विजाः.. 40.229 ..
1.4.m: Though knowing this, the king does not punish them. Behold the power of time, O king! / With auspicious white flowers and likewise other ornaments, twice-born men,

1.4.s:
śūdrānabhyarcayaṃtyalpaśrutabhāgyabalānvitāḥ..
pāṣaṃḍināṃ ca gṛhṇaṃti brāhmaṇāḥ kupratigraham.. 40.230 ..
1.4.d:
शूद्रानभ्यर्चयंत्यल्पश्रुतभाग्यबलान्विताः..
पाषंडिनां च गृह्णंति ब्राह्मणाः कुप्रतिग्रहम्.. 40.230 ..
1.4.m: endowed with little learning, fortune, and strength, worship śūdras. / And brahmins accept vile gifts from heretics,

1.4.s:
yena te rauravaṃ yāṃti sudustāraṃ dvijādhamāḥ..
tapoyajñaphalānāṃ ca vikretāro dvijāstathā.. 40.231 ..
1.4.d:
येन ते रौरवं यांति सुदुस्तारं द्विजाधमाः..
तपोयज्ञफलानां च विक्रेतारो द्विजास्तथा.. 40.231 ..
1.4.m: by which those basest of the twice-born go to the Raurava [hell], so difficult to cross. / Likewise, twice-born men become sellers of the fruits of austerity and sacrifice.

1.4.s:
yatayaśca bhaviṣyaṃti bahavaḥ koṭiśaḥ kalau..
puruṣālpabahustrīko nṛṇāṃ cāpatyasaṃbhavaḥ.. 40.232 ..
1.4.d:
यतयश्च भविष्यंति बहवः कोटिशः कलौ..
पुरुषाल्पबहुस्त्रीको नृणां चापत्यसंभवः.. 40.232 ..
1.4.m: And there will be renunciants in the Kali [age] by the millions. / The birth of children among men will occur where men are few and women are many.

1.4.s:
niṃdaṃti vedavākyāni vedārthāṃśca kalau yuge..
śūdraiḥ svayaṃ nirmitaṃ yatpramāṇaṃ śāstrameva tat.. 40.233 ..
1.4.d:
निंदंति वेदवाक्यानि वेदार्थांश्च कलौ युगे..
शूद्रैः स्वयं निर्मितं यत्प्रमाणं शास्त्रमेव तत्.. 40.233 ..
1.4.m: In the Kali age, they revile Vedic statements and Vedic meanings. / Whatever scripture has been composed by śūdras themselves—that alone is [regarded as] authoritative.

1.4.s:
śvāpadaprabalatvaṃ ca gavāṃ cāpi parikṣayaḥ..
kasyaciddānaprabhṛtidharmasyāsti na śuddhatā.. 40.234 ..
1.4.d:
श्वापदप्रबलत्वं च गवां चापि परिक्षयः..
कस्यचिद्दानप्रभृतिधर्मस्यास्ति न शुद्धता.. 40.234 ..
1.4.m: Carnivorous beasts become powerful, and there is also a decline of cows. / In no one is there purity of religious duty, such as giving gifts.

1.4.s:
sādhūnāṃ bahavo nāśāḥ pārthivāścāpyarakṣiṇaḥ..
aṭṭaśūlā janapadāḥ śivaśūlāścatuṣpathāḥ.. 40.235 ..
1.4.d:
साधूनां बहवो नाशाः पार्थिवाश्चाप्यरक्षिणः..
अट्टशूला जनपदाः शिवशूलाश्चतुष्पथाः.. 40.235 ..
1.4.m: There are many destructions of the righteous, and rulers do not protect. / The countryside sells food; the crossroads sell the liṅga of Śiva;

1.4.s:
pramadāḥ keśaśūlinyo bhaviṣyaṃti kalau yuge..
strīpradhānāni gehāni kucailāstāśca karkaśāḥ.. 40.236 ..
1.4.d:
प्रमदाः केशशूलिन्यो भविष्यंति कलौ युगे..
स्त्रीप्रधानानि गेहानि कुचैलास्ताश्च कर्कशाः.. 40.236 ..
1.4.m: women in the Kali age will sell their hair. / Households are dominated by women; they are clad in ragged garments and harsh;

1.4.s:
bahubhakṣyāvaliptāśca kṛtyā iva bhavaṃti ca..
sarve vaṇigjanāścāpi citravarṣī ca vāsavaḥ.. 40.237 ..
1.4.d:
बहुभक्ष्यावलिप्ताश्च कृत्या इव भवंति च..
सर्वे वणिग्जनाश्चापि चित्रवर्षी च वासवः.. 40.237 ..
1.4.m: gluttonous and haughty, they become like malevolent spirits. / All men become merchants, and Indra rains capriciously.

1.4.s:
kuśīlacaryāpāṣaṃḍairvṛthārūpaiḥ samāvṛtaḥ..
bahuyācanako loko bhaviṣyati parasparī.. 40.238 ..
1.4.d:
कुशीलचर्यापाषंडैर्वृथारूपैः समावृतः..
बहुयाचनको लोको भविष्यति परस्परी.. 40.238 ..
1.4.m: The world will be full of bad conduct and heretics of vain appearance; / people will mutually become constant beggars.

1.4.s:
aśaṃkaścaiva pāpeṣu tadā loko bhaviṣyati..
hartāraḥ pararatnānāṃ paradārapradharṣakāḥ.. 40.239 ..
1.4.d:
अशंकश्चैव पापेषु तदा लोको भविष्यति..
हर्तारः पररत्नानां परदारप्रधर्षकाः.. 40.239 ..
1.4.m: And then the world will be unhesitating in sins. / They are stealers of others' jewels and violators of others' wives.

1.4.s:
ūnaṣoḍaśavarṣāśca prajāyaṃte yugakṣaye..
tathā dvādaśavarṣāśca prasavaṃti striyastadā.. 40.240 ..
1.4.d:
ऊनषोडशवर्षाश्च प्रजायंते युगक्षये..
तथा द्वादशवर्षाश्च प्रसवंति स्त्रियस्तदा.. 40.240 ..
1.4.m: And at the end of the age, they give birth when under sixteen years of age; / likewise, women then bring forth children at twelve years.

1.4.s:
caurāścaurasya hartāro harturharttā tathāparaḥ..
jñānakarmaṇyuparate loke niṣkriyatāṃ gate.. 40.241 ..
1.4.d:
चौराश्चौरस्य हर्तारो हर्तुर्हर्त्ता तथापरः..
ज्ञानकर्मण्युपरते लोके निष्क्रियतां गते.. 40.241 ..
1.4.m: Thieves are stealers from thieves, and another steals from the stealer. / When knowledge and rituals have ceased, when the world has fallen into inaction,

1.4.s:
kīṭamūṣakasarpāśca dharṣayiṣyaṃti mānavān..
varṇāśramāṇāṃ ye cānye pāṣaṃḍāḥ paripaṃthinaḥ.. 40.242 ..
1.4.d:
कीटमूषकसर्पाश्च धर्षयिष्यंति मानवान्..
वर्णाश्रमाणां ये चान्ये पाषंडाः परिपंथिनः.. 40.242 ..
1.4.m: insects, mice, and snakes will torment human beings. / And those who are other heretics, opponents of the castes and stages of life,

1.4.s:
te tadā prodbhaviṣyaṃti teṣaāṃ vṛddhiśca pārthiva..
duḥkhaṃ putrakalatrādyaṃ dehotsādaḥ sarogatā.. 40.243 ..
1.4.d:
ते तदा प्रोद्भविष्यंति तेषआं वृद्धिश्च पार्थिव..
दुःखं पुत्रकलत्राद्यं देहोत्सादः सरोगता.. 40.243 ..
1.4.m: they will then arise, and an increase of them will take place, O ruler. / Sorrow concerning sons, wives, and the like, destruction of the body, and diseasedness [will follow].

1.4.s:
adharmābhiniveśatvāttamaso jāyate kalau..
kalerdoṣanidheścaiva śrṛṇuṣvaivaṃ mahāguṇam.. 40.244 ..
1.4.d:
अधर्माभिनिवेशत्वात्तमसो जायते कलौ..
कलेर्दोषनिधेश्चैव श्रृणुष्वैवं महागुणम्.. 40.244 ..
1.4.m: Through devotion to unrighteousness, darkness arises in the Kali [age]. / Yet listen to this great virtue of the Kali [age], this storehouse of faults:

1.4.s:
tadālpenaiva kāle na siddhiṃ gacchaṃti mānavāḥ..
triyugīnā vadaṃtyevaṃ dhanyā dharmaṃ caraṃti ye.. 40.245 ..
1.4.d:
तदाल्पेनैव काले न सिद्धिं गच्छंति मानवाः..
त्रियुगीना वदंत्येवं धन्या धर्मं चरंति ये.. 40.245 ..
1.4.m: in that [age], men attain perfection in a very short time. / Those who know the three ages speak thus: Blessed are they who practice righteousness,

1.4.s:
śrutismṛtipurāṇoktaṃ kalau śraddhāparāyaṇāḥ..
tretāyāṃ vārṣiko dharmo dvāpare māsikaḥ smṛtaḥ.. 40.246 ..
1.4.d:
श्रुतिस्मृतिपुराणोक्तं कलौ श्रद्धापरायणाः..
त्रेतायां वार्षिको धर्मो द्वापरे मासिकः स्मृतः.. 40.246 ..
1.4.m: devoted to faith in the Kali [age], as proclaimed by the Vedas, smṛtis, and Purāṇas. / The religious duty [practiced] for a year in the Tretā [age], remembered as practiced for a month in the Dvāpara,

1.4.s:
yathā kleśaṃ caranprājñastadahnā prāpyate kalau..
yugatrayeṇa tāvaṃtaḥ siddhiṃ gacchaṃti pārthivaḥ.. 40.247 ..
1.4.d:
यथा क्लेशं चरन्प्राज्ञस्तदह्ना प्राप्यते कलौ..
युगत्रयेण तावंतः सिद्धिं गच्छंति पार्थिवः.. 40.247 ..
1.4.m: is attained in a single day in the Kali [age] by a wise man enduring hardship. / In the three ages, only so many kings attain perfection

1.4.s:
yāvaṃtaḥ siddhimāyāṃti kalau hariharavratāḥ..
aṣṭāviṃśe kalau yacca bhāvi tattvaṃ nibodha me.. 40.248 ..
1.4.d:
यावंतः सिद्धिमायांति कलौ हरिहरव्रताः..
अष्टाविंशे कलौ यच्च भावि तत्त्वं निबोध मे.. 40.248 ..
1.4.m: as those who attain perfection in the Kali [age] through vows to Hari and Hara. / And learn from me that truth which is to come in the twenty-eighth Kali [age]:

1.4.s:
triṣu varṣasahasreṣu kaleryāteṣu pārthivaḥ..
triśateṣu daśanyūneṣvasyāṃ bhuvi bhaviṣyati.. 40.249 ..
1.4.d:
त्रिषु वर्षसहस्रेषु कलेर्यातेषु पार्थिवः..
त्रिशतेषु दशन्यूनेष्वस्यां भुवि भविष्यति.. 40.249 ..
1.4.m: When three thousand years of the Kali [age] have passed, / and three hundred minus ten [years], there will be a ruler on this earth,

1.4.s:
śūdrakonāma vīrāṇāmadhipaḥ siddhimatra saḥ..
carcitāyāṃ samārādhya lapsyate bhūbharāpahaḥ.. 40.250 ..
1.4.d:
शूद्रकोनाम वीराणामधिपः सिद्धिमत्र सः..
चर्चितायां समाराध्य लप्स्यते भूभरापहः.. 40.250 ..
1.4.m: the lord of heroes named Śūdraka, who, having worshipped Carcitā, / will attain perfection here, a remover of the burden of the earth.

1.4.s:
tatastriṣu sahasreṣu daśādhikaśatatraye..
bhaviṣyaṃ naṃdarājyaṃ ca cāṇakyo yānhaniṣyati.. 40.251 ..
1.4.d:
ततस्त्रिषु सहस्रेषु दशाधिकशतत्रये..
भविष्यं नंदराज्यं च चाणक्यो यान्हनिष्यति.. 40.251 ..
1.4.m: Then, in three thousand [years] and three hundred and ten [years], / there will be the reign of the Nandas, whom Cāṇakya will kill;

1.4.s:
śuklatīrthe sarvapāpanirmuktiṃ yo'bhilapsyati..
tatastriṣu sahasreṣu viṃśatyā cādhikeṣu ca.. 40.252 ..
1.4.d:
शुक्लतीर्थे सर्वपापनिर्मुक्तिं योऽभिलप्स्यति..
ततस्त्रिषु सहस्रेषु विंशत्या चाधिकेषु च.. 40.252 ..
1.4.m: [Cāṇakya,] who will obtain complete freedom from all sin at Śuklatīrtha. / Then, in three thousand and twenty [more] years,

1.4.s:
bhaviṣyaṃ vikramādityarājyaṃ so'tha pralapsyate..
sidadhiprasādāddurgāṇāṃ dīnānyo hyuddhariṣyati.. 40.253 ..
1.4.d:
भविष्यं विक्रमादित्यराज्यं सोऽथ प्रलप्स्यते..
सिदधिप्रसादाद्दुर्गाणां दीनान्यो ह्युद्धरिष्यति.. 40.253 ..
1.4.m: there will be the reign of Vikramāditya, which he will then attain; / who, by the grace of the goddess of perfections, will rescue the wretched from fortresses.

1.4.s:
tataḥ śatasahasreṣu śatenāpyadhikeṣu ca..
śakonāma bhaviṣyaśca yo'tidāridryahārakaḥ.. 40.254 ..
1.4.d:
ततः शतसहस्रेषु शतेनाप्यधिकेषु च..
शकोनाम भविष्यश्च योऽतिदारिद्र्यहारकः.. 40.254 ..
1.4.m: Then, in one hundred thousand years increased by one hundred, / there will be [one] named Śaka, who removes extreme poverty.

1.4.s:
tatastriṣu sahasreṣu ṣaṭ‌śatairadhikeṣu ca..
māgadhe hemasadanādaṃjanyāṃ prabhaviṣyati.. 40.255 ..
1.4.d:
ततस्त्रिषु सहस्रेषु षट्‌शतैरधिकेषु च..
मागधे हेमसदनादंजन्यां प्रभविष्यति.. 40.255 ..
1.4.m: Then, in three thousand years increased by six hundred, / in the city of Magadha, out of the golden palace, will arise from Añjanā

1.4.s:
viṣṇoraṃśo dharmapātā budhaḥ sākṣātsvayaṃ prabhuḥ..
tasya karmāṇi bhūriṇi bhaviṣyaṃti mahātmanaḥ.. 40.256 ..
1.4.d:
विष्णोरंशो धर्मपाता बुधः साक्षात्स्वयं प्रभुः..
तस्य कर्माणि भूरिणि भविष्यंति महात्मनः.. 40.256 ..
1.4.m: a portion of Viṣṇu, protector of righteousness, the wise one, the sovereign Lord in person. / Abundant will be the deeds of that great-souled one;

1.4.s:
jyotirbidumukhānugrānsa haniṣyati koṭiśaḥ..
catuḥṣaṣṭiṃ sa varṣāṇi bhuktvā dvīpāni sapta ca.. 40.257 ..
1.4.d:
ज्योतिर्बिदुमुखानुग्रान्स हनिष्यति कोटिशः..
चतुःषष्टिं स वर्षाणि भुक्त्वा द्वीपानि सप्त च.. 40.257 ..
1.4.m: he will kill millions of terrible [enemies] whose faces are marked with light. / Having enjoyed the seven continents for sixty-four years,

1.4.s:
bhaktebhyaḥ svayaśo muktvā divaṃ paścādgamiṣyati..
sarveṣāṃ cāvatārāṇaāṃ guṇaiḥ samadhiko yataḥ.. 40.258 ..
1.4.d:
भक्तेभ्यः स्वयशो मुक्त्वा दिवं पश्चाद्गमिष्यति..
सर्वेषां चावताराणआं गुणैः समधिको यतः.. 40.258 ..
1.4.m: leaving his fame to his devotees, he will afterwards go to heaven; / for he is superior to all the incarnations in virtues.

1.4.s:
tato vakṣyaṃti taṃ bhaktyā sarvapāpaharaṃ budham..
caturṣu ca sahasreṣu śateṣvapi caturṣu ca.. 40.259 ..
1.4.d:
ततो वक्ष्यंति तं भक्त्या सर्वपापहरं बुधम्..
चतुर्षु च सहस्रेषु शतेष्वपि चतुर्षु च.. 40.259 ..
1.4.m: Then they will speak with devotion of that wise one as the remover of all sins. / And in four thousand and four hundred [years],

1.4.s:
sādhikeṣu mahānrājā pramitiḥ prabhaviṣyati..
gotreṣu vai caṃdramaso bahusenāpatirbalī.. 40.260 ..
1.4.d:
साधिकेषु महान्राजा प्रमितिः प्रभविष्यति..
गोत्रेषु वै चंद्रमसो बहुसेनापतिर्बली.. 40.260 ..
1.4.m: when exceeded [by some years], a great king, Pramiti, will arise / in the lineage of the Moon, powerful, with many generals.

1.4.s:
mlecchānsa koṭiśo hatvā pāṣaṃḍāni ca sarvaśaḥ..
vaidikaṃ kevalaṃ śuddhaṃ saddharmaṃ vartayiṣyati.. 40.261 ..
1.4.d:
म्लेच्छान्स कोटिशो हत्वा पाषंडानि च सर्वशः..
वैदिकं केवलं शुद्धं सद्धर्मं वर्तयिष्यति.. 40.261 ..
1.4.m: Having slain millions of mlecchas and heretics on all sides, / he will establish the pure, true Vedic religion alone.

1.4.s:
gaṃgāyamunayormadhye niṣṭhāṃ yāsyati pārthivaḥ..
tataḥ prajāśca kālena kenāpi bhṛśapīḍitāḥ.. 40.262 ..
1.4.d:
गंगायमुनयोर्मध्ये निष्ठां यास्यति पार्थिवः..
ततः प्रजाश्च कालेन केनापि भृशपीडिताः.. 40.262 ..
1.4.m: Between the Gaṅgā and the Yamunā, that ruler will meet his end. / Then the subjects, exceedingly afflicted by time in some way,

1.4.s:
ghoraṃ vā dharmamāśritya śāṭhyena ca bhavaṃti tāḥ..
apragrahāstatastā vai lobhāviṣṭāśca vṛṃdaśaḥ.. 40.263 ..
1.4.d:
घोरं वा धर्ममाश्रित्य शाठ्येन च भवंति ताः..
अप्रग्रहास्ततस्ता वै लोभाविष्टाश्च वृंदशः.. 40.263 ..
1.4.m: either resorting to terrible conduct, become [full of] deceit. / Unrestrained thereafter, and possessed by greed, [they act] in hordes.

1.4.s:
upahiṃsaṃti cānyonyaṃ vyākulāḥ śramapīḍitāḥ..
naṣṭe śraute tathā smārte parasparahatāstadā.. 40.264 ..
1.4.d:
उपहिंसंति चान्योन्यं व्याकुलाः श्रमपीडिताः..
नष्टे श्रौते तथा स्मार्ते परस्परहतास्तदा.. 40.264 ..
1.4.m:
Agitated and afflicted by exhaustion, they will harm one another;
when Vedic and traditional codes of conduct are destroyed, they will then perish by each other's hands.

1.4.s:
nirmaryādā niṣkaruṇā nissnehā nirapatrapāḥ..
gṛhadārāṇi saṃtyajya hrasvakāḥ paṃṭaviṃśatiḥ.. 40.265 ..
1.4.d:
निर्मर्यादा निष्करुणा निस्स्नेहा निरपत्रपाः..
गृहदाराणि संत्यज्य ह्रस्वकाः पंटविंशतिः.. 40.265 ..
1.4.m:
Deceitful, pitiless, devoid of affection, shameless,
abandoning home and wives, dwarfish, twenty spans tall,

1.4.s:
hāhābhūtāścariṣyaṃti viṣādavyākuleṃdriyāḥ..
anāvṛṣṭihatāścaiva vārtāmutsṛjya duḥkhitāḥ.. 40.266 ..
1.4.d:
हाहाभूताश्चरिष्यंति विषादव्याकुलेंद्रियाः..
अनावृष्टिहताश्चैव वार्तामुत्सृज्य दुःखिताः.. 40.266 ..
1.4.m:
crying 'Alas, alas!', they will wander, their faculties disordered by despair,
and afflicted by drought, abandoning their livelihoods, grieving,

1.4.s:
pratyaṃtāṃstā niṣevaṃti hitvā janapadānsvakān..
saritsāgarakūlāṃśca sevaṃte parvatāṃstathā.. 40.267 ..
1.4.d:
प्रत्यंतांस्ता निषेवंति हित्वा जनपदान्स्वकान्..
सरित्सागरकूलांश्च सेवंते पर्वतांस्तथा.. 40.267 ..
1.4.m:
abandoning their own lands, they will resort to frontier regions;
they will frequent rivers, seacoasts, and mountains.

1.4.s:
māṃsairmūlaphalaiscaiva vartayaṃti suduḥkhitāḥ..
cīrapatrājinadharā niṣkriyā niṣparigrahāḥ.. 40.268 ..
1.4.d:
मांसैर्मूलफलैस्चैव वर्तयंति सुदुःखिताः..
चीरपत्राजिनधरा निष्क्रिया निष्परिग्रहाः.. 40.268 ..
1.4.m:
Exceedingly miserable, they will subsist on meats, roots, and fruits;
wearing rags, leaves, and deer-skins, inactive, destitute of possessions.

1.4.s:
dharmasya vāsamātraṃ ca śālvo mleccho haniṣyati..
uttamādhamamadhyatvaṃ sarvamucchidya ghorakṛt.. 40.269 ..
1.4.d:
धर्मस्य वासमात्रं च शाल्वो म्लेच्छो हनिष्यति..
उत्तमाधममध्यत्वं सर्वमुच्छिद्य घोरकृत्.. 40.269 ..
1.4.m:
The mleccha Śālva will destroy even the mere semblance of righteousness,
uprooting all distinctions of high, low, and middle, doing dreadful deeds.

1.4.s:
tatastasya vadhārthāya viṣṇuḥ sākṣājjagatpatiḥ..
śaṃbhale viṣṇuyaśaso bhūtvā putro nṛpottama.. 40.270 ..
1.4.d:
ततस्तस्य वधार्थाय विष्णुः साक्षाज्जगत्पतिः..
शंभले विष्णुयशसो भूत्वा पुत्रो नृपोत्तम.. 40.270 ..
1.4.m:
Then, for the sake of slaying him, Viṣṇu, the Lord of the universe in person,
becoming the son of Viṣṇuyaśas in Śambhala, O best of kings,

1.4.s:
dvijottamaiḥ parivṛtaḥ śālvaṃ taṃ saṃhariṣyati..
koṭiśo'rbudaśaḥ pāpānnihatya ca nikharvaśaḥ.. 40.271 ..
1.4.d:
द्विजोत्तमैः परिवृतः शाल्वं तं संहरिष्यति..
कोटिशोऽर्बुदशः पापान्निहत्य च निखर्वशः.. 40.271 ..
1.4.m:
surrounded by the best of the twice-born, will destroy that Śālva,
having slain the wicked by crores, arbudas, and nikharvas.

1.4.s: pālayiṣyati taṃ dharmaṃ yo dharmaḥ śrutipūrvakaḥ.. 40.272 ..
1.4.d: पालयिष्यति तं धर्मं यो धर्मः श्रुतिपूर्वकः.. 40.272 ..
1.4.m: He will protect that righteousness which is based upon the Veda.

1.4.s:
kṛtvā potaṃ dharmarūpaṃ sādhūnāṃ parameśvaraḥ..
gamiṣyati paraṃ lokaṃ kṛtvā karmāṇi bhūriśaḥ.. 40.273 ..
1.4.d:
कृत्वा पोतं धर्मरूपं साधूनां परमेश्वरः..
गमिष्यति परं लोकं कृत्वा कर्माणि भूरिशः.. 40.273 ..
1.4.m:
Having fashioned a boat consisting of righteousness for good people, the Supreme Lord,
after performing manifold deeds, will depart to the supreme realm.

1.4.s:
tataḥ kṛtayugaṃ bhūyaḥ pravartiṣyati pārthiva..
ādyaṃ kṛtayugaṃ cānyaṃ tadanyebhyo viśiṣyate.. 40.274 ..
1.4.d:
ततः कृतयुगं भूयः प्रवर्तिष्यति पार्थिव..
आद्यं कृतयुगं चान्यं तदन्येभ्यो विशिष्यते.. 40.274 ..
1.4.m:
Then, O king, the Kṛtayuga will commence anew;
and that primal Kṛtayuga is superior to all the others.

1.4.s:
aṣṭāviṃśakaliścaiva śeṣaḥ prāvarta anyataḥ..
tataḥ kṛte sūryavaṃśaḥ pravatsyati.. 40.275 ..
1.4.d:
अष्टाविंशकलिश्चैव शेषः प्रावर्त अन्यतः..
ततः कृते सूर्यवंशः प्रवत्स्यति.. 40.275 ..
1.4.m:
The twenty-eighth Kali age remaining will have run its course elsewhere;
then, in the Kṛta age, the solar dynasty will advance.

1.4.s:
marurājācca devāpeḥ śrutadevācca brāhmaṇāḥ..
iti cāturyugī rājanvyavasthā parivartate..
caturyuge ca te dhanyā ye bhajaṃti harācyutau.. 40.276 ..
iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ prathame māheśvarakhaṇḍe kaumārikākhaṇḍe mahākālakarandhamasaṃvāde caturyugavyavasthāvarṇanaṃnāma catvāriṃśattamo'dhyāyaḥ.. 40 .. cha ..
1.4.d:
मरुराजाच्च देवापेः श्रुतदेवाच्च ब्राह्मणाः..
इति चातुर्युगी राजन्व्यवस्था परिवर्तते..
चतुर्युगे च ते धन्या ये भजंति हराच्युतौ.. 40.276 ..
इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां प्रथमे माहेश्वरखण्डे कौमारिकाखण्डे महाकालकरन्धमसंवादे चतुर्युगव्यवस्थावर्णनंनाम चत्वारिंशत्तमोऽध्यायः.. 40 .. छ ..
1.4.m:
From King Maru, from Devāpi, and from Śrutadeva the brahmins [will emerge].
Thus, O king, the order of the four ages revolves;
and in the four ages, blessed are those who worship Hara and Acyuta.
Thus ends the fortieth chapter, named 'Description of the Order of the Four Ages' in the dialogue between Mahākāla and Karandhama, in the Kaumārikākhaṇḍa of the first [section], the Māheśvarakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skandapurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.

1.4.s:
..karadhama uvāca..
kecicchivaṃ samāśritya viṣṇumāśritya vedhasam..
varṇayaṃti pare mokṣaṃ tvaṃ tu kasmāttu manyase.. 41.1 ..
1.4.d:
..करधम उवाच..
केचिच्छिवं समाश्रित्य विष्णुमाश्रित्य वेधसम्..
वर्णयंति परे मोक्षं त्वं तु कस्मात्तु मन्यसे.. 41.1 ..
1.4.m:
Karadhama said:
Some, taking refuge in Śiva, some taking refuge in Viṣṇu, or in Brahmā,
describe supreme liberation; but whom do you consider [supreme]?

1.4.s:
..mahākāla uvāca..
apāravaibhavā devāstrayo'pyete nararṣabha..
yogīṃdrāṇāmapi tvatra ceto muhyati kiṃ mama.. 41.2 ..
1.4.d:
..महाकाल उवाच..
अपारवैभवा देवास्त्रयोऽप्येते नरर्षभ..
योगींद्राणामपि त्वत्र चेतो मुह्यति किं मम.. 41.2 ..

1.4.s:
purā kilaivaṃ munayo naimiṣāraṇyavāsinaḥ..
saṃdihyāṃtaḥ śreṣṭhatāyāṃ brahmalokamupāgaman.. 41.3 ..
1.4.d:
पुरा किलैवं मुनयो नैमिषारण्यवासिनः..
संदिह्यांतः श्रेष्ठतायां ब्रह्मलोकमुपागमन्.. 41.3 ..
1.4.m:
Formerly indeed, the sages dwelling in the Naimiṣāraṇya forest,
in doubt regarding [their] supremacy, went to the realm of Brahmā.

1.4.s:
tasminkṣaṇe viriṃco'pi ślokaṃ prahvo'bravītkila..
anaṃtāya namastasmai yasyāṃto nopalabhyate.. 41.4 ..
1.4.d:
तस्मिन्क्षणे विरिंचोऽपि श्लोकं प्रह्वोऽब्रवीत्किल..
अनंताय नमस्तस्मै यस्यांतो नोपलभ्यते.. 41.4 ..
1.4.m:
At that moment, Brahmā too, bowing low, recited a verse:
'Homage to that Ananta whose end is not perceived,

1.4.s:
maheśāya ca bhakte dvau kṛpāyetāṃ sadā mayi..
tataḥ śreṣṭhaṃ ca taṃ matvā kṣīrodaṃ munayo yayuḥ.. 41.5 ..
1.4.d:
महेशाय च भक्ते द्वौ कृपायेतां सदा मयि..
ततः श्रेष्ठं च तं मत्वा क्षीरोदं मुनयो ययुः.. 41.5 ..
1.4.m:
and to Maheśa; may the two ever show mercy to me, their devotee.'
Then, considering him superior, the sages went to the Ocean of Milk.

1.4.s:
tatra yogeśvaraḥ ślokaṃ prabudhyannamumabravīt..
brahmāṇaṃ sarvabhūteṣu paramaṃ brahmarūpiṇam.. 41.6 ..
1.4.d:
तत्र योगेश्वरः श्लोकं प्रबुध्यन्नमुमब्रवीत्..
ब्रह्माणं सर्वभूतेषु परमं ब्रह्मरूपिणम्.. 41.6 ..
1.4.m:
There, the lord of yogins, upon waking, recited a verse:
'To Brahmā among all beings, the supreme one who embodies Brahman,

1.4.s:
sadāśivaṃ ca vaṃde tau bhavetāṃ maṃgalāya me..
tataste vismitā viprā apasṛtya yayuḥ punaḥ.. 41.7 ..
1.4.d:
सदाशिवं च वंदे तौ भवेतां मंगलाय मे..
ततस्ते विस्मिता विप्रा अपसृत्य ययुः पुनः.. 41.7 ..
1.4.m:
and to Sadāśiva, I bow; may the two bring me auspiciousness.'
Then those brahmins, astonished, turned away and went again.

1.4.s:
kailāse dadṛśuḥ sthāṇuṃ vadaṃtaṃ girijāṃ prati..
ekādaśyāṃ pranṛtyāni jāgare viṣṇusadmani.. 41.8 ..
1.4.d:
कैलासे ददृशुः स्थाणुं वदंतं गिरिजां प्रति..
एकादश्यां प्रनृत्यानि जागरे विष्णुसद्मनि.. 41.8 ..
1.4.m:
On Kailāsa they saw Sthāṇu speaking to Girijā:
'On the eleventh day I dance vigorously during the vigil in Viṣṇu's abode.

1.4.s:
sadā tapasyāṃ carāmi prītyarthaṃ harivedhasoḥ..
śrutveti cāpasṛtyaiva khinnāste munayo'bruvan.. 41.9 ..
1.4.d:
सदा तपस्यां चरामि प्रीत्यर्थं हरिवेधसोः..
श्रुत्वेति चापसृत्यैव खिन्नास्ते मुनयोऽब्रुवन्.. 41.9 ..
1.4.m:
I constantly perform austerity to please Hari and Brahmā.'
Having heard this and turning back, those sages, dismayed, said:

1.4.s:
yadvā devā na saṃyāṃti pāraṃ ye ca parasparam..
tatsṛṣṭasṛṣṭasṛṣṭeṣu gaṇanā kā'smadādiṣu.. 41.10 ..
1.4.d:
यद्वा देवा न संयांति पारं ये च परस्परम्..
तत्सृष्टसृष्टसृष्टेषु गणना काऽस्मदादिषु.. 41.10 ..
1.4.m:
'Since even the gods do not reach the limits of one another,
what count can there be among beings like us, created by their creations' creations?

1.4.s:
uttamādhamamadhyatvamamīṣāṃ varṇayaṃti ye..
asatyavādinaḥ pāpāste yāṃti nirayaṃ dhruvam.. 41.11 ..
1.4.d:
उत्तमाधममध्यत्वममीषां वर्णयंति ये..
असत्यवादिनः पापास्ते यांति निरयं ध्रुवम्.. 41.11 ..
1.4.m:
Those who describe high, low, or intermediate status among them,
are untruthful, sinful, and surely go to hell.'

1.4.s:
evaṃ te niściyāmāsurnaimiṣeyā stapasvinaḥ..
satyametacca rājeṃdra mamāpīdaṃ mataṃ sphuṭam.. 41.12 ..
1.4.d:
एवं ते निश्चियामासुर्नैमिषेया स्तपस्विनः..
सत्यमेतच्च राजेंद्र ममापीदं मतं स्फुटम्.. 41.12 ..
1.4.m:
Thus those ascetics of Naimiṣa resolved.
And this is the truth, O king of kings; this is clearly my view as well.

1.4.s:
jāpakānāṃ sahasrāṇi vaiṣṇavānāṃ tathaiva ca..
śaivānāṃ ca vidhiṃ viṣṇuṃ sthāṇuṃ cāpyanvamūmucan.. 41.13 ..
1.4.d:
जापकानां सहस्राणि वैष्णवानां तथैव च..
शैवानां च विधिं विष्णुं स्थाणुं चाप्यन्वमूमुचन्.. 41.13 ..
1.4.m:
Thousands of chanters of prayers, both Vaiṣṇavas
and Śaivas, have attained liberation through Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Sthāṇu.

1.4.s:
tasmādyasya manorāgo yasmindeve bhavetsphuṭam..
sa taṃ bhajedvipāpaḥ syānmamedaṃ matamuttamam.. 41.14 ..
1.4.d:
तस्माद्यस्य मनोरागो यस्मिन्देवे भवेत्स्फुटम्..
स तं भजेद्विपापः स्यान्ममेदं मतमुत्तमम्.. 41.14 ..
1.4.m:
Therefore, towards whichever god one's mind clearly feels love,
he should worship him and become freed from sin; this is my supreme opinion.

1.4.s:
..karaṃdhama uvāca..
kāni pāpāni vipreṃdra yaistu saṃmūḍhacetasaḥ..
na vedeṣu na dharmeṣu ratimāpadyate manaḥ.. 41.15 ..
1.4.d:
..करंधम उवाच..
कानि पापानि विप्रेंद्र यैस्तु संमूढचेतसः..
न वेदेषु न धर्मेषु रतिमापद्यते मनः.. 41.15 ..
1.4.m:
Karandhama said:
What are the sins, O best of brahmins, by which those of deluded mind
find no delight of the intellect either in the Vedas or in righteous duties?

1.4.s:
..mahākāla uvāca..
adharmabhedā vijñeyāścittavṛttiprabhedataḥ..
sthūlāḥ sūkṣmā asūkṣmāśca koṭibhedairanekaśaḥ.. 41.16 ..
1.4.d:
..महाकाल उवाच..
अधर्मभेदा विज्ञेयाश्चित्तवृत्तिप्रभेदतः..
स्थूलाः सूक्ष्मा असूक्ष्माश्च कोटिभेदैरनेकशः.. 41.16 ..
1.4.m:
Mahākāla said:
The varieties of unrighteousness are to be known through the varieties of mental states,
gross, subtle, and non-subtle, in countless millions of varieties.

1.4.s:
tatra ye pāpanicayāḥ sthūlā narakahetavaḥ..
te samāsena kathyaṃte manovākkāyasādhanāḥ.. 41.17 .. tu. mahābhārata anuśāsana 13.2
1.4.d:
तत्र ये पापनिचयाः स्थूला नरकहेतवः..
ते समासेन कथ्यंते मनोवाक्कायसाधनाः.. 41.17 .. तु. महाभारत अनुशासन 13.2
1.4.m:
Among them, those aggregates of sins that are gross and cause hell,
performed through mind, speech, and body, are described in brief:

1.4.s:
parastrīdravyasaṃkalpaścetasāniṣṭaciṃtanam..
akāryābhiniveśaśca caturddhā karma mānasam.. 41.18 ..
1.4.d:
परस्त्रीद्रव्यसंकल्पश्चेतसानिष्टचिंतनम्..
अकार्याभिनिवेशश्च चतुर्द्धा कर्म मानसम्.. 41.18 ..
1.4.m:
Coveting another's wife and property, intending harm in the mind,
and adherence to forbidden actions: fourfold is mental action.

1.4.s:
anibaddhapralāpitvamasatyaṃ cāpriyaṃ ca yat..
parāpavādapaiśunyaṃ caturdhā karma vācikam.. 41.19 ..
1.4.d:
अनिबद्धप्रलापित्वमसत्यं चाप्रियं च यत्..
परापवादपैशुन्यं चतुर्धा कर्म वाचिकम्.. 41.19 ..
1.4.m:
Incoherent babbling, untruth, harsh speech,
and slanderous calumny of others: fourfold is vocal action.

1.4.s:
abhakṣyabhakṣaṇaṃ hiṃsā mithyā kāmasya sevanam..
parasvānāmupādānaṃ caturdhā karma kāyikam.. 41.20 ..
1.4.d:
अभक्ष्यभक्षणं हिंसा मिथ्या कामस्य सेवनम्..
परस्वानामुपादानं चतुर्धा कर्म कायिकम्.. 41.20 ..
1.4.m:
Eating forbidden food, injury, pursuit of illicit lust,
and appropriating the possessions of others: fourfold is bodily action.

1.4.s:
ityetaddvādaśavidhaṃ karma proktaṃ trisaṃbhavam..
asya bhedānpunarvakṣye yeṣāṃ phalamanaṃtakam.. 41.21 ..
1.4.d:
इत्येतद्द्वादशविधं कर्म प्रोक्तं त्रिसंभवम्..
अस्य भेदान्पुनर्वक्ष्ये येषां फलमनंतकम्.. 41.21 ..
1.4.m:
Thus this twelvefold action arisen from the triad [of mind, speech, and body] has been declared.
I shall further explain its varieties, whose consequence is endless.

1.4.s:
ye dviṣaṃti mahādevaṃ saṃsārārṇavatārakam..
sumahātpātakopetāste yāṃti narakāgniṣu.. 41.22 ..
1.4.d:
ये द्विषंति महादेवं संसारार्णवतारकम्..
सुमहात्पातकोपेतास्ते यांति नरकाग्निषु.. 41.22 ..
1.4.m:
Those who hate Mahādeva, the ferryman across the ocean of worldly existence,
possessed of very great sins, go to the fires of hell.

1.4.s:
mahāṃti pātakānyāhurniraṃtaraphalāni ṣaṭ‌..
nābhinaṃdaṃti ye dṛṣṭvā śaṃkaraṃ na stuvaṃti ye.. 41.23 ..
1.4.d:
महांति पातकान्याहुर्निरंतरफलानि षट्‌..
नाभिनंदंति ये दृष्ट्वा शंकरं न स्तुवंति ये.. 41.23 ..
1.4.m:
They declare six great sins that bear unending fruit:
Those who, seeing Śaṅkara, do not rejoice, and those who do not praise him;

1.4.s:
yatheṣṭaceṣṭā niḥśaṃkāḥ saṃtiṣṭhaṃti ramaṃti ca..
upacāravinirmuktāḥ śivasya gurusaṃnidhau.. 41.24 ..
1.4.d:
यथेष्टचेष्टा निःशंकाः संतिष्ठंति रमंति च..
उपचारविनिर्मुक्ताः शिवस्य गुरुसंनिधौ.. 41.24 ..
1.4.m:
those who act as they please, fearless, abiding and sporting,
devoid of reverence, in the presence of Śiva and the guru;

1.4.s:
śivācāraṃ na manyaṃte śivabhaktāndviṣaṃti ṣaṭ..
gurumārttamaśaktaṃ vā videśaprasthitaṃ tathā.. 41.25 ..
1.4.d:
शिवाचारं न मन्यंते शिवभक्तान्द्विषंति षट्..
गुरुमार्त्तमशक्तं वा विदेशप्रस्थितं तथा.. 41.25 ..
1.4.m:
those who do not respect Śiva's conduct, and those who hate Śiva's devotees—these are the six.
He who abandons a guru who is afflicted, incapacitated, departed to a foreign land,

1.4.s:
aribhiḥ paribhūtaṃ vā yastyajati sa pāpakṛt..
tadbhāryāputramitreṣu yaścāvajñāṃ karoti vā.. 41.26 ..
1.4.d:
अरिभिः परिभूतं वा यस्त्यजति स पापकृत्..
तद्भार्यापुत्रमित्रेषु यश्चावज्ञां करोति वा.. 41.26 ..
1.4.m:
or humiliated by enemies, is an evil-doer;
as is he who insults the guru's wife, son, or friends.

1.4.s:
ityetatpātakaṃ jñeyaṃ guruniṃdāsamaṃ mahat..
brahmaghnaśca surāpaśca steyī ca gurutalpagaḥ.. 41.27 ..
1.4.d:
इत्येतत्पातकं ज्ञेयं गुरुनिंदासमं महत्..
ब्रह्मघ्नश्च सुरापश्च स्तेयी च गुरुतल्पगः.. 41.27 ..
1.4.m:
This great sin should be known as equal to reviling the guru.
The slayer of a brahmin, the drinker of liquor, the thief, and the violator of the guru's bed:

1.4.s:
mahāpātakinastvete tatsaṃsargī ca paṃcamaḥ..
krodhāddveṣādbhayāllobhādbrāhmaṇasya vadaṃti ye.. 41.28 ..
1.4.d:
महापातकिनस्त्वेते तत्संसर्गी च पंचमः..
क्रोधाद्द्वेषाद्भयाल्लोभाद्ब्राह्मणस्य वदंति ये.. 41.28 ..
1.4.m:
these are the perpetrators of the great sins, and associating with them is the fifth.
Those who, out of anger, hatred, fear, or greed, speak [evil] against a brahmin—

1.4.s:
marmāṃtikaṃ mahādoṣaṃ brahmaghnaḥ sa prakīrtitaḥ..
brāhmaṇaṃ yaḥ samāhūya yācamānamakiṃcanam.. 41.29 ..
1.4.d:
मर्मांतिकं महादोषं ब्रह्मघ्नः स प्रकीर्तितः..
ब्राह्मणं यः समाहूय याचमानमकिंचनम्.. 41.29 ..
1.4.m: A mortal, grave offense [against a brahmin]—he is declared a slayer of a brahmin. / One who summons a brahmin who is destitute and begging,

1.4.s:
paścānnāstīti yo brūyātsa ca vai brahmahā smṛtaḥ..
yaśca vidyābhimānena nistejayati saddvijam.. 41.30 ..
1.4.d:
पश्चान्नास्तीति यो ब्रूयात्स च वै ब्रह्महा स्मृतः..
यश्च विद्याभिमानेन निस्तेजयति सद्द्विजम्.. 41.30 ..
1.4.m: and then says, "There is nothing," he is considered indeed a slayer of a brahmin. / And one who, through pride of learning, deprives a virtuous twice-born of his luster,

1.4.s:
udāsīnaḥ sabhāmadhye brahmahā sa prakīrtitaḥ..
mithyāguṇaiḥ svamātmānaṃ nayatyutkarṣatāṃ balāt.. 41.31 ..
1.4.d:
उदासीनः सभामध्ये ब्रह्महा स प्रकीर्तितः..
मिथ्यागुणैः स्वमात्मानं नयत्युत्कर्षतां बलात्.. 41.31 ..
1.4.m: becoming indifferent in the assembly, is declared a slayer of a brahmin. / One who by false virtues forcibly elevates himself

1.4.s:
viruddhaṃ gurubhiḥ sārdhaṃ brahmaghnaḥ sa prakīrtitaḥ..
kṣuttṛṣṇātaptadehānāṃ dvijānāṃ bhoktumicchatām.. 41.32 ..
1.4.d:
विरुद्धं गुरुभिः सार्धं ब्रह्मघ्नः स प्रकीर्तितः..
क्षुत्तृष्णातप्तदेहानां द्विजानां भोक्तुमिच्छताम्.. 41.32 ..
1.4.m: in opposition to teachers is declared a slayer of a brahmin. / When twice-born whose bodies are tormented by hunger and thirst wish to eat,

1.4.s:
yaḥ samācarate vighnaṃ tamāhurbrahmagātakam..
piśunaḥ sarvalokānāṃ chidrānveṣaṇatatparaḥ.. 41.33 ..
1.4.d:
यः समाचरते विघ्नं तमाहुर्ब्रह्मगातकम्..
पिशुनः सर्वलोकानां छिद्रान्वेषणतत्परः.. 41.33 ..
1.4.m: whoever causes an obstacle, him they call a slayer of a brahmin. / A slanderer of all people, intent on seeking out faults,

1.4.s:
udvegajananaḥ krūraḥ sa ca vai brahmahā smṛtaḥ..
gavāṃ tṛṣābhibhūtānāṃ jalārthamupasarpatām.. 41.34 ..
1.4.d:
उद्वेगजननः क्रूरः स च वै ब्रह्महा स्मृतः..
गवां तृषाभिभूतानां जलार्थमुपसर्पताम्.. 41.34 ..
1.4.m: causing distress, cruel—he is considered indeed a slayer of a brahmin. / When cows overcome by thirst approach for water,

1.4.s:
yaḥ samācarate vighnaṃ tamāhurbrahmaghātakam..
paradoṣaṃ parijñāya nṛpakarṇe japeta yaḥ.. 41.35 ..
1.4.d:
यः समाचरते विघ्नं तमाहुर्ब्रह्मघातकम्..
परदोषं परिज्ञाय नृपकर्णे जपेत यः.. 41.35 ..
1.4.m: whoever causes an obstacle, him they call a slayer of a brahmin. / One who, having learned another's fault, whispers it into the king's ear,

1.4.s:
pāpīyānpiśunaḥ krūrastamāhurbrahmaghātakam..
nyāyenopārjitaṃ vipraistaddravyaharaṇaṃ ca yat.. 41.36 ..
1.4.d:
पापीयान्पिशुनः क्रूरस्तमाहुर्ब्रह्मघातकम्..
न्यायेनोपार्जितं विप्रैस्तद्द्रव्यहरणं च यत्.. 41.36 ..
1.4.m: a most sinful, cruel slanderer—him they call a slayer of a brahmin. / And the seizure of that wealth which has been lawfully acquired by brahmins,

1.4.s:
chadmanā vā balādvāpi brahmahatyāsamaṃ matam..
adhītya yaśca śāstrāṇi parityajati mūḍhadhīḥ.. 41.37 ..
1.4.d:
छद्मना वा बलाद्वापि ब्रह्महत्यासमं मतम्..
अधीत्य यश्च शास्त्राणि परित्यजति मूढधीः.. 41.37 ..
1.4.m: whether by deceit or by force, is considered equal to slaying a brahmin. / And one of foolish mind who, having studied the scriptures, abandons them,

1.4.s:
surāpānasamaṃ jñeyaṃ jīvanāyaiva vā paṭhet..
agnihotraparityāgaḥ paṃcayajñopakarmaṇām.. 41.38 ..
1.4.d:
सुरापानसमं ज्ञेयं जीवनायैव वा पठेत्..
अग्निहोत्रपरित्यागः पंचयज्ञोपकर्मणाम्.. 41.38 ..
1.4.m: is to be known as equal to drinking liquor; or one who recites them merely for livelihood. / Abandoning the agnihotra and the commencement of the five sacrifices,

1.4.s:
mātṛpitṛparityāgaḥ kūṭasākṣī suhṛdvadhaḥ..
abhakṣyabhakṣaṇaṃ vanyajaṃtūnāṃ kāmyayā vadhaḥ.. 41.39 ..
1.4.d:
मातृपितृपरित्यागः कूटसाक्षी सुहृद्वधः..
अभक्ष्यभक्षणं वन्यजंतूनां काम्यया वधः.. 41.39 ..
1.4.m: abandoning mother and father, giving false witness, slaying a friend, / eating inedible things, slaying wild creatures out of lust [or pleasure],

1.4.s:
grāmaṃ vanaṃ gavāvāsaṃ yaśca krodhena dīpayet..
iti ghorāṇi pāpāni surāpānasamāni ca.. 41.40 ..
1.4.d:
ग्रामं वनं गवावासं यश्च क्रोधेन दीपयेत्..
इति घोराणि पापानि सुरापानसमानि च.. 41.40 ..
1.4.m: and whoever sets fire out of anger to a village, a forest, or a cowpen— / these terrible sins are equal to drinking liquor.

1.4.s:
dīnasarvasvaharaṇaṃ narastrīgajavājinām..
gobhūratnasuvarṇānāmauṣadhīnāṃ rasasya ca.. 41.41 ..
1.4.d:
दीनसर्वस्वहरणं नरस्त्रीगजवाजिनाम्..
गोभूरत्नसुवर्णानामौषधीनां रसस्य च.. 41.41 ..
1.4.m: Taking the entire property of a destitute person; [theft] of men, women, elephants, and horses, / of cattle, land, jewels, gold, herbs, and essences,

1.4.s:
caṃdanāgarukarpūrakastūrīpaṭṭavāsasām..
hastanyāsāpaharaṇaṃ skamasteyasamaṃ smṛtam.. 41.42 ..
1.4.d:
चंदनागरुकर्पूरकस्तूरीपट्टवाससाम्..
हस्तन्यासापहरणं स्कमस्तेयसमं स्मृतम्.. 41.42 ..
1.4.m: of sandalwood, agarwood, camphor, musk, and silk garments; / and the misappropriation of a deposit—is remembered as equal to the theft of gold.

1.4.s:
kanyānāṃ varayogyānāmadānaṃ sadṛśe vare..
putramitrakalatreṣu gamanaṃ bhaginīṣu ca.. 41.43 ..
1.4.d:
कन्यानां वरयोग्यानामदानं सदृशे वरे..
पुत्रमित्रकलत्रेषु गमनं भगिनीषु च.. 41.43 ..
1.4.m: Not giving maidens fit for a bridegroom to a suitable suitor; / having intercourse with the wives of sons and friends, and with sisters,

1.4.s:
kumārīsāhasaṃ ghoramaṃtyajastrīniṣevaṇam..
savarṇāyāśca gamanaṃ gurutalpasamaṃ smṛtam.. 41.44 ..
1.4.d:
कुमारीसाहसं घोरमंत्यजस्त्रीनिषेवणम्..
सवर्णायाश्च गमनं गुरुतल्पसमं स्मृतम्.. 41.44 ..
1.4.m: violating an unmarried girl, resorting to a woman of the lowest caste, / and having intercourse with an [unmarried] woman of one's own caste is considered equal to violating the guru's bed.

1.4.s:
dvijāyārthaṃ pratiśrutya na prayacchati yaḥ punaḥ..
na ca casmārayate vipraṃ tulyaṃ tadupapapātakam.. 41.45 ..
1.4.d:
द्विजायार्थं प्रतिश्रुत्य न प्रयच्छति यः पुनः..
न च चस्मारयते विप्रं तुल्यं तदुपपपातकम्.. 41.45 ..
1.4.m: One who promises wealth to a twice-born and does not give it thereafter, / and does not remind the brahmin—that is equal to a secondary sin.

1.4.s:
abhimānotikopaśca dāṃbhikatvaṃ kṛtaghnatā..
atyaṃtaviṣayāsaktiḥ kārpaṇyaṃ śāṭhyamatsaram.. 41.46 ..
1.4.d:
अभिमानोतिकोपश्च दांभिकत्वं कृतघ्नता..
अत्यंतविषयासक्तिः कार्पण्यं शाठ्यमत्सरम्.. 41.46 ..
1.4.m: Arrogance, extreme wrath, hypocrisy, ingratitude, / extreme attachment to sense-objects, miserliness, dishonesty, envy,

1.4.s:
bhṛtyānāṃ ca parityāgaḥ sādhubaṃdhutapasvinām..
gavāṃ kṣatriyavaiśyānāṃ strīśūdrāṇāṃ ca tāḍanam.. 41.47 ..
1.4.d:
भृत्यानां च परित्यागः साधुबंधुतपस्विनाम्..
गवां क्षत्रियवैश्यानां स्त्रीशूद्राणां च ताडनम्.. 41.47 ..
1.4.m: abandonment of servants, of the virtuous, of relatives, and of ascetics, / beating cattle, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, women, and śūdras,

1.4.s:
śivāśramatarūṇāṃ ca puṣpārāmavināśanam..
ayājyānāṃ yājanaṃ cāpyayācyānāṃ ca yācanam.. 41.48 ..
1.4.d:
शिवाश्रमतरूणां च पुष्पारामविनाशनम्..
अयाज्यानां याजनं चाप्ययाच्यानां च याचनम्.. 41.48 ..
1.4.m: destroying the trees of Śiva's hermitage and flower gardens, / performing sacrifices for those unfit to sacrifice, begging from those from whom one should not beg,

1.4.s:
yajñārāmataḍāgādidārāpatyasya vikrayaḥ..
tīrthayātropavāsānāṃ vratāyatanakarmaṇām.. 41.49 ..
1.4.d:
यज्ञारामतडागादिदारापत्यस्य विक्रयः..
तीर्थयात्रोपवासानां व्रतायतनकर्मणाम्.. 41.49 ..
1.4.m: selling sacrifices, gardens, ponds, and so forth, or a wife and offspring, / [selling the merit of] pilgrimages to sacred fords, fasts, vows, and temple activities,

1.4.s:
strīdhanānyupajīvaṃti strībhiratyaṃtanirjitāḥ..
arakṣaṇaṃ ca nārīṇāṃ madyapastrīniṣevaṇam.. 41.50 ..
1.4.d:
स्त्रीधनान्युपजीवंति स्त्रीभिरत्यंतनिर्जिताः..
अरक्षणं च नारीणां मद्यपस्त्रीनिषेवणम्.. 41.50 ..
1.4.m: those who live off women's wealth, completely dominated by women, / lack of protection of women, and having intercourse with a woman who drinks liquor,

1.4.s:
ṛṇānāmapradānaṃ ca mithyāghṛddhyupajīvanam..
niṃditānāṃ dhanādānaṃ sādvīkanyoktidūṣaṇam.. 41.51 ..
1.4.d:
ऋणानामप्रदानं च मिथ्याघृद्ध्युपजीवनम्..
निंदितानां धनादानं साद्वीकन्योक्तिदूषणम्.. 41.51 ..
1.4.m: non-payment of debts, living by false greed, / taking money from blameworthy sources, slanderous speech against a virtuous woman or a maiden,

1.4.s:
viṣamāraṇayaṃtrāṇāṃ proyago mūlakarmaṇām..
uccāṭanābhicārāśca rāgavidveṣaṇakriyā.. 41.52 ..
1.4.d:
विषमारणयंत्राणां प्रोयगो मूलकर्मणाम्..
उच्चाटनाभिचाराश्च रागविद्वेषणक्रिया.. 41.52 ..
1.4.m: employing deadly poisons and machines, sorcery with roots, / spells for driving away and malevolent incantations, rites to cause hatred and division,

1.4.s:
jihvākāmopabho gārthaṃ yasyāraṃbhaḥ svakarmasu..
mūlyenādhyāpayedyastu mūlyenādhīyate ca ye.. 41.53 ..
1.4.d:
जिह्वाकामोपभो गार्थं यस्यारंभः स्वकर्मसु..
मूल्येनाध्यापयेद्यस्तु मूल्येनाधीयते च ये.. 41.53 ..
1.4.m: undertaking one's own duties merely for the enjoyment of the tongue and lust, / one who teaches for a fee, and those who study for a fee,

1.4.s:
vrātyatā vratasaṃtyāgaḥ sarvāhāraniṣevaṇam..
asacchāstrābhigamanaṃ śuṣkatarkāva laṃbanam.. 41.54 ..
1.4.d:
व्रात्यता व्रतसंत्यागः सर्वाहारनिषेवणम्..
असच्छास्त्राभिगमनं शुष्कतर्काव लंबनम्.. 41.54 ..
1.4.m: being a fallen outcaste, abandoning vows, consuming all kinds of food, / pursuing false scriptures, resorting to dry logic,

1.4.s:
devāgnigurusādhūnāṃ niṃdā gobrāhmaṇasya ca..
pratyakṣaṃ vā parokṣaṃ vā rājñāṃ maṃḍalināmapi.. 41.55 ..
1.4.d:
देवाग्निगुरुसाधूनां निंदा गोब्राह्मणस्य च..
प्रत्यक्षं वा परोक्षं वा राज्ञां मंडलिनामपि.. 41.55 ..
1.4.m: reviling the gods, the fire, gurus, the virtuous, cows, and brahmins, / openly or behind their backs, or [reviling] kings and rulers,

1.4.s:
utsannapatṛdevejyāḥ svakarmatyāginaśca ye..
duḥśīlā nāstikāḥ pāpā na sadā satyavādinaḥ.. 41.56 ..
1.4.d:
उत्सन्नपतृदेवेज्याः स्वकर्मत्यागिनश्च ये..
दुःशीला नास्तिकाः पापा न सदा सत्यवादिनः.. 41.56 ..
1.4.m: those who neglect the worship of ancestors and gods, who abandon their own duties, / the ill-behaved, atheists, sinners, and those who do not always speak the truth,

1.4.s:
parvakāle divā cāpsu viyonau paśuyoniṣu..
rajasvalāsvayonau ca maithunaṃ yaḥ samācaret.. 41.57 ..
1.4.d:
पर्वकाले दिवा चाप्सु वियोनौ पशुयोनिषु..
रजस्वलास्वयोनौ च मैथुनं यः समाचरेत्.. 41.57 ..
1.4.m: whoever has intercourse on forbidden festivals, by day, in water, in unnatural ways, with animals, / with menstruating women, or outside the proper womb,

1.4.s:
strīputramitrasuhṛdāmāśācchedakarāśca ye..
janasyāpriyavaktāraḥ krūrāḥ samayabhedinaḥ.. 41.58 ..
1.4.d:
स्त्रीपुत्रमित्रसुहृदामाशाच्छेदकराश्च ये..
जनस्याप्रियवक्तारः क्रूराः समयभेदिनः.. 41.58 ..
1.4.m: and those who destroy the hopes of wife, son, friend, and companion, / speakers of unpleasant words to people, cruel ones, breakers of agreements,

1.4.s:
bhettā taḍāgakūpānāṃ saṃkramāṇāṃrasasya ca..
ekapaṃktisthitānāṃ ca pākabhedaṃ karoti yaḥ.. 41.59 ..
1.4.d:
भेत्ता तडागकूपानां संक्रमाणांरसस्य च..
एकपंक्तिस्थितानां च पाकभेदं करोति यः.. 41.59 ..
1.4.m: a destroyer of ponds, wells, bridges, and fluid [channels], / and one who discriminates in serving food among those sitting in a single row—

1.4.s:
ityetaiśca narāḥ pāpairupapātakinaḥ smṛtāḥ..
yuktāstadunakaiḥ pāpaiḥ pāpinastānnibodha me.. 41.60 ..
1.4.d:
इत्येतैश्च नराः पापैरुपपातकिनः स्मृताः..
युक्तास्तदुनकैः पापैः पापिनस्तान्निबोध मे.. 41.60 ..
1.4.m: by these sins men are considered guilty of secondary sins. / Now learn from me of those sinners who are attached to sins lesser than these:

1.4.s:
ye gobrāhmaṇakanyānāṃ svāmimitratapasvinām..
antaraṃ yāṃti kāryeṣu te smṛtāḥ pāpino narāḥ.. 41.61 ..
1.4.d:
ये गोब्राह्मणकन्यानां स्वामिमित्रतपस्विनाम्..
अन्तरं यांति कार्येषु ते स्मृताः पापिनो नराः.. 41.61 ..
1.4.m: Those men are considered sinners who cause a rift in the affairs / of cows, brahmins, maidens, masters, friends, and ascetics,

1.4.s:
paraśriyābhitapyaṃte hīnāṃ savaṃti ye striyām..
paṃktyarthaṃ ye na kurvaṃti dānayajñādikāḥ kriyāḥ.. 41.62 ..
1.4.d:
परश्रियाभितप्यंते हीनां सवंति ये स्त्रियाम्..
पंक्त्यर्थं ये न कुर्वंति दानयज्ञादिकाः क्रियाः.. 41.62 ..
1.4.m: those who are distressed by another's fortune, who serve a base woman, / who do not perform gifts, sacrifices, and other rites for the sake of the assembly,

1.4.s:
goṣṭhāgnijalarathyāsu tarucchāyānageṣu ca..
tyajaṃti ye purīṣādyamārāmāyataneṣu ca .. 41.63 ..
1.4.d:
गोष्ठाग्निजलरथ्यासु तरुच्छायानगेषु च..
त्यजंति ये पुरीषाद्यमारामायतनेषु च .. 41.63 ..
1.4.m: those who void feces and the like in cow-pens, fires, water, streets, / in the shade of trees, on hills, and in gardens and temples,

1.4.s:
gītavādyaratā nityā mattāḥ kilakilāparāḥ..
kūṭaveṣakriyācārāḥ kūṭasaṃvyavahāriṇaḥ.. 41.64 ..
1.4.d:
गीतवाद्यरता नित्या मत्ताः किलकिलापराः..
कूटवेषक्रियाचाराः कूटसंव्यवहारिणः.. 41.64 ..
1.4.m: those constantly addicted to song and instruments, intoxicated, given to loud shouts of delight, / wearing false dress, acts, and conduct, engaging in fraudulent business,

1.4.s:
kūṭaśāsanakartāraḥ kūṭayuddhakarāśca ye..
nirdayo'tīva bhṛtyeṣu paśūnāṃ damanaśca yaḥ.. 41.65 ..
1.4.d:
कूटशासनकर्तारः कूटयुद्धकराश्च ये..
निर्दयोऽतीव भृत्येषु पशूनां दमनश्च यः.. 41.65 ..
1.4.m: forgers of edicts, those who fight dishonorably, / one who is excessively merciless to servants, and one who torments beasts,

1.4.s:
mithyāprasādito vākyamākarṇayati yaḥ śanaiḥ..
capalaścāpi māyāvī śaṭho mithyāvinītakaḥ.. 41.66 ..
1.4.d:
मिथ्याप्रसादितो वाक्यमाकर्णयति यः शनैः..
चपलश्चापि मायावी शठो मिथ्याविनीतकः.. 41.66 ..
1.4.m: one who, falsely gratified, listens to speech secretly, / fickle, deceitful, crooked, and falsely humble,

1.4.s:
yo bhāryāputramitrāṇi bālavṛddhakṛśāturān..
bhṛtyānatithibaṃdhūṃśca tyaktvāśnāti bubhukṣitān.. 41.67 ..
1.4.d:
यो भार्यापुत्रमित्राणि बालवृद्धकृशातुरान्..
भृत्यानतिथिबंधूंश्च त्यक्त्वाश्नाति बुभुक्षितान्.. 41.67 ..
1.4.m: one who eats while leaving hungry his wife, children, friends, / children, the elderly, the emaciated, the sick, servants, guests, and relatives,

1.4.s:
yaḥ svayaṃ mṛṣṭamaśnāti viprāyānyatprayacchati..
vṛthāpākaḥ sa vijñeyo brahmavādivigarhitaḥ.. 41.68 ..
1.4.d:
यः स्वयं मृष्टमश्नाति विप्रायान्यत्प्रयच्छति..
वृथापाकः स विज्ञेयो ब्रह्मवादिविगर्हितः.. 41.68 ..
1.4.m: one who eats sweet food himself and gives other [inferior food] to a brahmin— / his cooking is to be known as useless, condemned by those who proclaim the Veda,

1.4.s:
niyamānsvayamādāya ye tyajaṃtyajiteṃdriyāḥ..
ye tāḍayaṃti gāṃ nityaṃ vāhayaṃti muhurmuhuḥ.. 41.69 ..
1.4.d:
नियमान्स्वयमादाय ये त्यजंत्यजितेंद्रियाः..
ये ताडयंति गां नित्यं वाहयंति मुहुर्मुहुः.. 41.69 ..
1.4.m: those who, having taken vows themselves, abandon them through lack of self-control, / those who constantly strike a cow and yoke it repeatedly,

1.4.s:
durbalānnaiva puṣṇaṃti praṇaṣṭārthā dviṣaṃti ca..
pīḍayantyabhicāreṇa sakṣatānvāhayaṃti ca.. 41.70 ..
1.4.d:
दुर्बलान्नैव पुष्णंति प्रणष्टार्था द्विषंति च..
पीडयन्त्यभिचारेण सक्षतान्वाहयंति च.. 41.70 ..
1.4.m: who do not nourish the weak, who hate those who have lost their wealth, / who torment with malevolent rites, and yoke wounded [beasts],

1.4.s:
teṣā madattvā cāśraṃti cikitsaṃti na rogiṇaḥ..
ajāviko māhiṣikaḥ samudrī vṛṣalīpatiḥ.. 41.71 ..
1.4.d:
तेषा मदत्त्वा चाश्रंति चिकित्संति न रोगिणः..
अजाविको माहिषिकः समुद्री वृषलीपतिः.. 41.71 ..
1.4.m: who eat without giving to them, and do not treat the sick, / a keeper of goats and sheep, a keeper of buffaloes, a seafarer, the husband of a śūdra woman,

1.4.s:
hīnavarṇātmavṛttiśca vaidyo dharmadhvajī ca yaḥ..
yaśca śāstramatikramya svecchayaivāharetkaram.. 41.72 ..
1.4.d:
हीनवर्णात्मवृत्तिश्च वैद्यो धर्मध्वजी च यः..
यश्च शास्त्रमतिक्रम्य स्वेच्छयैवाहरेत्करम्.. 41.72 ..
1.4.m: one who makes his living from a lower caste, a physician, one who flaunts righteousness as a banner, / and one who, transgressing the scriptures, collects taxes at his own will,

1.4.s:
sadā daṇḍaruciryaśca yo vā daṇḍarucirna hi..
utkocakairadhikṛtaistaskaraisca prapīḍyate.. 41.73 ..
1.4.d:
सदा दण्डरुचिर्यश्च यो वा दण्डरुचिर्न हि..
उत्कोचकैरधिकृतैस्तस्करैस्च प्रपीड्यते.. 41.73 ..
1.4.m: one who is always fond of punishment, or one who is not fond of punishment at all, / [and a king under whom people are] oppressed by officers taking bribes and by thieves.

1.4.s:
yasya rājñaḥ prajā rāṣṭre pacyate narakeṣu saḥ..
acauraṃ cauravatpaśyeccauraṃ vā'caurarūpiṇam.. 41.74 ..
1.4.d:
यस्य राज्ञः प्रजा राष्ट्रे पच्यते नरकेषु सः..
अचौरं चौरवत्पश्येच्चौरं वाऽचौररूपिणम्.. 41.74 ..
1.4.m: A king in whose realm the subjects are oppressed cooks in the hells. / If he sees an innocent person as a thief, or a thief disguised as innocent,

1.4.s:
ālasyopahato rājā vyasanī narakaṃ vrajet..
evamādīni cānyāni pāpānyāhuḥ purāvidaḥ.. 41.75 ..
1.4.d:
आलस्योपहतो राजा व्यसनी नरकं व्रजेत्..
एवमादीनि चान्यानि पापान्याहुः पुराविदः.. 41.75 ..
1.4.m: a king stricken with sloth and given to vice goes to hell. / These and other sins the knowers of the ancient past proclaim.

1.4.s:
yadvātadvā paradravyamapi sarṣapamātrakam..
apahṛtya naraḥ pāpo nārakī nātra saṃśayaḥ.. 41.76 ..
1.4.d:
यद्वातद्वा परद्रव्यमपि सर्षपमात्रकम्..
अपहृत्य नरः पापो नारकी नात्र संशयः.. 41.76 ..
1.4.m: Whatever it may be, if a man steals another's property even to the size of a mustard seed, / that sinful man goes to hell; of this there is no doubt.

1.4.s:
evamādyairnaraḥ pāpairutkrāntaiḥ samanaṃtaram..
śarīraṃ yātanārthāya pūrvākāramavāpnuyāt.. 41.77 ..
1.4.d:
एवमाद्यैर्नरः पापैरुत्क्रान्तैः समनंतरम्..
शरीरं यातनार्थाय पूर्वाकारमवाप्नुयात्.. 41.77 ..
1.4.m: By such sins, immediately after departure [from life], / a man assumes a body of his former shape to suffer torment.

1.4.s:
tasmāttrividhamapyetannārakīyaṃ vivarjayet..
sadāśivaṃ ca śaraṇaṃ vrajetsacchraddhayā yutaḥ.. 41.78 ..
1.4.d:
तस्मात्त्रिविधमप्येतन्नारकीयं विवर्जयेत्..
सदाशिवं च शरणं व्रजेत्सच्छ्रद्धया युतः.. 41.78 ..
1.4.m: Therefore, one should abandon this threefold [path] leading to hell, / and seek refuge in Sadāśiva, endowed with true faith.

1.4.s:
namaskāraḥ stutiḥ pūjā nāmasaṃkīrtanaṃ tathā..
saṃparkātkautukāllobhānna tasya viphalaṃ bhavet.. 41.79 ..
1.4.d:
नमस्कारः स्तुतिः पूजा नामसंकीर्तनं तथा..
संपर्कात्कौतुकाल्लोभान्न तस्य विफलं भवेत्.. 41.79 ..
1.4.m: Prostration, praise, worship, and likewise chanting [his] name, / whether done through association, curiosity, or greed, will never be futile for him.
