1.4.s:
..karaṃdhama uvāca..
saṃkṣepācchivapūjāyā vidhānaṃ vaktumarhasi..
kṛtena yena manujaḥ śivapūjāphalaṃ labhet.. 41.80 ..
1.4.d:
..करंधम उवाच..
संक्षेपाच्छिवपूजाया विधानं वक्तुमर्हसि..
कृतेन येन मनुजः शिवपूजाफलं लभेत्.. 41.80 ..
1.4.m: Karamdhama said: / You ought to explain concisely the procedure for Śiva's worship, / performed so that a mortal may obtain the fruit of worshipping Śiva.

1.4.s:
..mahākāla uvāca..
prātarmadhyāhnasāyāhne śaṃkaraṃ sarvadā bhajet..
darśanātsparśanānmartyaḥ kṛtatṛtyo bhavetsphuṭam.. 41.81 ..
1.4.d:
..महाकाल उवाच..
प्रातर्मध्याह्नसायाह्ने शंकरं सर्वदा भजेत्..
दर्शनात्स्पर्शनान्मर्त्यः कृततृत्यो भवेत्स्फुटम्.. 41.81 ..
1.4.m: Mahākāla said: / One should always worship Śaṃkara in the morning, at midday, and in the evening. / From seeing and touching [him], a mortal clearly attains his purpose.

1.4.s:
ādau snānaṃ prakurvita bhasmasnānamathāpi vā..
āpadgataḥ kaṇṭhasnānaṃ mantrasnānamathāpi vā.. 41.82 ..
1.4.d:
आदौ स्नानं प्रकुर्वित भस्मस्नानमथापि वा..
आपद्गतः कण्ठस्नानं मन्त्रस्नानमथापि वा.. 41.82 ..
1.4.m: First one should perform a ritual ablution, or an ablution with ashes; / or if in distress, an ablution up to the neck, or an ablution with mantras.

1.4.s:
āvikaṃ paridadhyācca tato vāsaḥ sitaṃ ca vā..
dhāturaktamatho navyaṃ malinaṃ saṃdhitaṃ na ca.. 41.83 ..
1.4.d:
आविकं परिदध्याच्च ततो वासः सितं च वा..
धातुरक्तमथो नव्यं मलिनं संधितं न च.. 41.83 ..
1.4.m: Then one should put on woolen clothing, or a white garment, / or one dyed with mineral red, fresh, not dirty or patched.

1.4.s:
uttarīyaṃ ca saṃdadhyādvinā tanniṣphalārcanam..
bhasmatripuṇḍradhārī ca lalāṭe hṛti cāṃsayoḥ.. 41.84 ..
1.4.d:
उत्तरीयं च संदध्याद्विना तन्निष्फलार्चनम्..
भस्मत्रिपुण्ड्रधारी च ललाटे हृति चांसयोः.. 41.84 ..
1.4.m: One should also put on an upper garment; without it, worship is fruitless. / And wearing the three lines of ash on the forehead, chest, and shoulders,

1.4.s:
pūjayedyo mahādevaṃ prītaḥ paśyati taṃ muhuḥ..
sarvadoṣānbahiḥ kṣipya śivāyatanamāviśet.. 41.85 ..
1.4.d:
पूजयेद्यो महादेवं प्रीतः पश्यति तं मुहुः..
सर्वदोषान्बहिः क्षिप्य शिवायतनमाविशेत्.. 41.85 ..
1.4.m: he who worships Mahādeva, [the god] looks upon him with delight repeatedly. / Casting all impurities outside, one should enter the abode of Śiva.

1.4.s:
praviśya ca praṇamyeśaṃ tato garbhagṛhaṃ viśet..
pāṇī prakṣālya taccitto nirmālyamavaropayet.. 41.86 ..
1.4.d:
प्रविश्य च प्रणम्येशं ततो गर्भगृहं विशेत्..
पाणी प्रक्षाल्य तच्चित्तो निर्माल्यमवरोपयेत्.. 41.86 ..
1.4.m: Having entered and bowed to the Lord, one should then enter the sanctum sanctorum. / Washing both hands and concentrating the mind upon him, one should remove the faded flowers.

1.4.s:
yena rudrāyate bhaktyā kurute mārjanakriyām..
tasmānmārjayate tvevaṃ sthāṇunaitatparasparam.. 41.87 ..
1.4.d:
येन रुद्रायते भक्त्या कुरुते मार्जनक्रियाम्..
तस्मान्मार्जयते त्वेवं स्थाणुनैतत्परस्परम्.. 41.87 ..
1.4.m: Because he cleanses with devotion directed toward Rudra, he performs the act of scrubbing; / therefore he scrubs in this way, mutually with Sthāṇu.

1.4.s:
rudrabhaktyā ca saṃtiṣṭhenamālinyaṃ mārjayettataḥ..
bhaktirdevasya tiṣṭhenna mālinyaṃ mārjataḥ sadā.. 41.88 ..
1.4.d:
रुद्रभक्त्या च संतिष्ठेनमालिन्यं मार्जयेत्ततः..
भक्तिर्देवस्य तिष्ठेन्न मालिन्यं मार्जतः सदा.. 41.88 ..
1.4.m: One should remain intent on devotion to Rudra, and then wipe away the dirt; / for the one who always wipes away dirt, devotion to the god never departs.

1.4.s:
gaḍukānpūrayetpaścānnirmalena jalena vai..
gaḍukāstu samāḥ sarve sarve ca śubhadarśanāḥ.. 41.89 ..
1.4.d:
गडुकान्पूरयेत्पश्चान्निर्मलेन जलेन वै..
गडुकास्तु समाः सर्वे सर्वे च शुभदर्शनाः.. 41.89 ..
1.4.m: Then one should fill small water-pots with pure water. / All the water-pots must be uniform, and all auspicious in appearance,

1.4.s:
nirvraṇāḥ saumyarūpāśca sarve codakapūritāḥ..
vastrapūtajalaiḥ pūrṇāgandhadhūpaiśca vāsitāḥ.. 41.90 ..
1.4.d:
निर्व्रणाः सौम्यरूपाश्च सर्वे चोदकपूरिताः..
वस्त्रपूतजलैः पूर्णागन्धधूपैश्च वासिताः.. 41.90 ..
1.4.m: flawless, pleasant in form, all filled with water, / filled with water filtered through cloth and scented with perfumes and incenses,

1.4.s:
kṣālitāḥ pūritā nītāḥ ṣaḍakṣarajapena ca..
gaḍukāṣcaśataṃ kuryādathavāpyaṣṭaviṃśatiḥ.. 41.91 ..
1.4.d:
क्षालिताः पूरिता नीताः षडक्षरजपेन च..
गडुकाष्चशतं कुर्यादथवाप्यष्टविंशतिः.. 41.91 ..
1.4.m: washed, filled, and brought with the repetition of the six-syllable mantra. / One should prepare one hundred pots, or twenty-eight,

1.4.s:
aṣṭādaśāpi caturastatonyūnaṃ na kārayet..
payo dadhi ghṛtaṃ caiva kṣaudramikṣurasaṃ tathā.. 41.92 ..
1.4.d:
अष्टादशापि चतुरस्ततोन्यूनं न कारयेत्..
पयो दधि घृतं चैव क्षौद्रमिक्षुरसं तथा.. 41.92 ..
1.4.m: or eighteen, or four; one should not make fewer than that. / Milk, curds, ghee, honey, and sugarcane juice—

1.4.s:
evaṃ sarvaṃ ca taddravyaṃ vāmataḥ saṃnyasedbhavāt..
tato bahirviniṣkramya pūjayetpratihārakān.. 41.93 ..
1.4.d:
एवं सर्वं च तद्द्रव्यं वामतः संन्यसेद्भवात्..
ततो बहिर्विनिष्क्रम्य पूजयेत्प्रतिहारकान्.. 41.93 ..
1.4.m: all these substances one should place on the left side of Bhava. / Then going outside, one should worship the doorkeepers.

1.4.s: sarveṣāṃ vācakā mantrāḥ kathyaṃte'taḥ paraṃ kramāt.. 41.94 ..
1.4.d: सर्वेषां वाचका मन्त्राः कथ्यंतेऽतः परं क्रमात्.. 41.94 ..
1.4.m: Next the expressing mantras of all of them are spoken in order: 41.94

1.4.s:
oṃgaṃ gaṇapataye namaḥ.. oṃkṣāṃ kṣetrapālāya namaḥ.. oṃgaṃ gurubhyo namaḥ.. iti ākāśe.. oṃkauṃ kuladevyai namaḥ.. oṃ naṃdine namaḥ.. oṃmahākālāya namaḥ.. oṃdhātre vidhātrai namaḥ..
tataḥ pravisya liṃgācca kiñciddakṣiṇataḥ śuciḥ..
udaṅmukhaḥ kṣaṇaṃ dhyāyetsamakāyāsanasthitaḥ.. 41.95 ..
1.4.d:
ओंगं गणपतये नमः.. ओंक्षां क्षेत्रपालाय नमः.. ओंगं गुरुभ्यो नमः.. इति आकाशे.. ओंकौं कुलदेव्यै नमः.. ओं नंदिने नमः.. ओंमहाकालाय नमः.. ओंधात्रे विधात्रै नमः..
ततः प्रविस्य लिंगाच्च किञ्चिद्दक्षिणतः शुचिः..
उदङ्मुखः क्षणं ध्यायेत्समकायासनस्थितः.. 41.95 ..
1.4.m: “Oṃ Gaṃ, homage to Gaṇapati. Oṃ Kṣāṃ, homage to the Guardian of the Sacred Field. Oṃ Gaṃ, homage to the Gurus.” Thus in the air. “Oṃ Kauṃ, homage to the Goddess of the Family. Oṃ, homage to Nandin. Oṃ, homage to Mahākāla. Oṃ, homage to Dhātṛ and Vidhātṛ.” / Then entering, slightly to the right of the liṅga, pure, / facing north, seated in a steady posture, one should meditate for a moment: 41.95

1.4.s:
darbhādibhiḥ parivṛtaṃ madhyapadmārkamaṃḍalam..
somamaṇḍalamadhyasthaṃ dhyāyedvai vahnimaṃḍalam.. 41.96 ..
1.4.d:
दर्भादिभिः परिवृतं मध्यपद्मार्कमंडलम्..
सोममण्डलमध्यस्थं ध्यायेद्वै वह्निमंडलम्.. 41.96 ..
1.4.m: Surrounded by darbha-grass and the like, on the central lotus the orb of the sun; / situated in the center of the orb of the moon, one should meditate on the orb of fire.

1.4.s:
tanmadhye viśvarūpaṃ ca vāmādyaṣṭādiśaktikam..
paṃcavaktraṃ daśabhujaṃ trinetraṃ caṃdrabhūṣitam.. 41.97 ..
1.4.d:
तन्मध्ये विश्वरूपं च वामाद्यष्टादिशक्तिकम्..
पंचवक्त्रं दशभुजं त्रिनेत्रं चंद्रभूषितम्.. 41.97 ..
1.4.m: In its center, [the god] possessing all forms, endowed with the eight powers beginning with Vāmā, / five-faced, ten-armed, three-eyed, adorned with the moon,

1.4.s:
vāmāṃkagirijaṃ devaṃ dhyāyetsiddhaiḥ stutaṃ muhuḥ..
tataḥ pūrvaṃ pradadyācca pādyārghaṃ śaṃbhave nṛpa.. 41.98 ..
1.4.d:
वामांकगिरिजं देवं ध्यायेत्सिद्धैः स्तुतं मुहुः..
ततः पूर्वं प्रदद्याच्च पाद्यार्घं शंभवे नृप.. 41.98 ..
1.4.m: the god with the Mountain-Born Lady on his left lap, repeatedly praised by the Siddhas, one should meditate upon. / Then first one should offer water for the feet and an arghya offering to Śambhu, O king.

1.4.s:
pānīyamakṣatā darbhā gaṃdhapūṣpaṃ sasarpiṣam..
kṣīraṃ dadhi madhu punarnavāṃgo'rghaḥ prakīrtitaḥ.. 41.99 ..
1.4.d:
पानीयमक्षता दर्भा गंधपूष्पं ससर्पिषम्..
क्षीरं दधि मधु पुनर्नवांगोऽर्घः प्रकीर्तितः.. 41.99 ..
1.4.m: Water, unbroken grains, darbha-grass, fragrant flowers with ghee, / milk, curds, and honey—this is declared to be the nine-limbed arghya offering.

1.4.s:
tataḥ śraddhārdracittasya snānaṃ liṃgasya cācaret..
gṛhītvā gaḍukaṃ pūrvaṃ malasnānaṃ samācaret.. 41.100 ..
1.4.d:
ततः श्रद्धार्द्रचित्तस्य स्नानं लिंगस्य चाचरेत्..
गृहीत्वा गडुकं पूर्वं मलस्नानं समाचरेत्.. 41.100 ..
1.4.m: Then, with a mind softened by faith, one should perform the bathing of the liṅga. / Taking a water-pot first, one should perform the clearing ablution.

1.4.s:
arddhena snāpayetpūrvaṃ kuryācca malagharṣaṇam..
sarveṇa snāpayetpaścātpūjayetsnāpayettataḥ.. 41.101 ..
1.4.d:
अर्द्धेन स्नापयेत्पूर्वं कुर्याच्च मलघर्षणम्..
सर्वेण स्नापयेत्पश्चात्पूजयेत्स्नापयेत्ततः.. 41.101 ..
1.4.m: One should first bathe it with half [the water] and rub away the grime; / afterwards one should bathe it with all of it; then one should worship and bathe it.

1.4.s:
praṇamya ca tato bhaktyā snāpayenmūlamaṃtrataḥ..
oṃhūṃ viśvamūrtaye śivāya nama..
iti dvādaśākṣaro mūlamaṃtraḥ.. 41.102 ..
1.4.d:
प्रणम्य च ततो भक्त्या स्नापयेन्मूलमंत्रतः..
ओंहूं विश्वमूर्तये शिवाय नम..
इति द्वादशाक्षरो मूलमंत्रः.. 41.102 ..
1.4.m: And then, having bowed with devotion, one should bathe it with the basic mantra: / “Oṃ Hūṃ, homage to Śiva, the universal form.” / Such is the twelve-syllable basic mantra. 41.102

1.4.s:
vārikṣaradadhikṣaudraghṛtenekṣurasena ca..
snāpayenmūlamantreṇa jaladhūpārcanātpṛthak.. 41.103 ..
1.4.d:
वारिक्षरदधिक्षौद्रघृतेनेक्षुरसेन च..
स्नापयेन्मूलमन्त्रेण जलधूपार्चनात्पृथक्.. 41.103 ..
1.4.m: With water, milk, curds, honey, ghee, and sugarcane juice, / one should bathe it with the basic mantra, separately from the offering of water and incense.

1.4.s: gaḍukaiḥ snāpayetsarvaiḥ snātaṃ gandhairvirūkṣayet.. 41.104 ..
1.4.d: गडुकैः स्नापयेत्सर्वैः स्नातं गन्धैर्विरूक्षयेत्.. 41.104 ..
1.4.m: One should bathe it with all the pots; once bathed, one should dry it with perfumes.

1.4.s:
virūkṣitaṃ tataḥ snāpya śrīkhaṇḍena vilepayet..
pūjayedvividhaiḥ puṣpairvidhinā yena tacchṛṇu.. 41.105 ..
1.4.d:
विरूक्षितं ततः स्नाप्य श्रीखण्डेन विलेपयेत्..
पूजयेद्विविधैः पुष्पैर्विधिना येन तच्छृणु.. 41.105 ..
1.4.m: Having bathed it after drying, one should smear it with sandalwood. / One should worship it with various flowers according to the rule; listen to that:

1.4.s: āgneyapāde.. oṃdharmāya namaḥ.. nairṛtake.. oṃjñānāya namaḥ.. vāyavye.. oṃvairāgyāya namaḥ.. īśānapāde.. oṃaiśvaryāya namaḥ.. pūrvapāde.. oṃadharmāya namaḥ.. dakṣiṇe.. oṃajñānāya namaḥ.. paścime.. oṃavairāgyāya namaḥ.. uttare oṃanaiśvaryāya namaḥ.. oṃanantāya namaḥ.. oṃpadmāya namaḥ oṃarkamaṇḍalā namaḥ.. oṃsomamaṇḍalāya namaḥ.. oṃvahnimaṇḍalā namaḥ.. oṃvāmājyeṣṭhādipaṃcamantraśaktibhyo namaḥ.. oṃparamaprakṛtyai devyai namaḥ.. oṃīśānatatpuruṣāghoravāmadevasadyojātapañcavaktrāya rudrasādhyavasvādityaviśvedevādidevaviśvarūpāya aṇḍajasvedajodbhijjajarāyujarūpasthāvarajaṅgamamūrtaye parameśvarāya oṃhūṃ viśvamūrtaye śivāya namastriśūladhanuḥkhaḍgakapāladaṇḍakuṭhārebhyaḥ.. 41.106 ..
1.4.d: आग्नेयपादे.. ओंधर्माय नमः.. नैरृतके.. ओंज्ञानाय नमः.. वायव्ये.. ओंवैराग्याय नमः.. ईशानपादे.. ओंऐश्वर्याय नमः.. पूर्वपादे.. ओंअधर्माय नमः.. दक्षिणे.. ओंअज्ञानाय नमः.. पश्चिमे.. ओंअवैराग्याय नमः.. उत्तरे ओंअनैश्वर्याय नमः.. ओंअनन्ताय नमः.. ओंपद्माय नमः ओंअर्कमण्डला नमः.. ओंसोममण्डलाय नमः.. ओंवह्निमण्डला नमः.. ओंवामाज्येष्ठादिपंचमन्त्रशक्तिभ्यो नमः.. ओंपरमप्रकृत्यै देव्यै नमः.. ओंईशानतत्पुरुषाघोरवामदेवसद्योजातपञ्चवक्त्राय रुद्रसाध्यवस्वादित्यविश्वेदेवादिदेवविश्वरूपाय अण्डजस्वेदजोद्भिज्जजरायुजरूपस्थावरजङ्गममूर्तये परमेश्वराय ओंहूं विश्वमूर्तये शिवाय नमस्त्रिशूलधनुःखड्गकपालदण्डकुठारेभ्यः.. 41.106 ..
1.4.m: At the southeast foot: “Oṃ, homage to Dharma.” At the southwest: “Oṃ, homage to Knowledge.” At the northwest: “Oṃ, homage to Detachment.” At the northeast foot: “Oṃ, homage to Sovereignty.” At the eastern foot: “Oṃ, homage to Adharma.” In the south: “Oṃ, homage to Ignorance.” In the west: “Oṃ, homage to Attachment.” In the north: “Oṃ, homage to Lack of Sovereignty.” “Oṃ, homage to Ananta.” “Oṃ, homage to the Lotus.” “Oṃ, homage to the Orb of the Sun.” “Oṃ, homage to the Orb of the Moon.” “Oṃ, homage to the Orb of Fire.” “Oṃ, homage to the Five Mantra-powers beginning with Vāmā and Jyeṣṭhā.” “Oṃ, homage to the Goddess, the Supreme Nature.” “Oṃ, homage to Parameśvara, five-faced as Īśāna, Tatpuruṣa, Aghora, Vāmadeva, and Sadyojāta; universal form containing Rudras, Sādhyas, Vasus, Ādityas, Viśvedevas, and the rest; embodied as unmoving and moving things in the forms of egg-born, sweat-born, plant-born, and womb-born; Oṃ Hūṃ, homage to Śiva, the universal form; homage to the trident, bow, sword, skull-bowl, staff, and axe.”

1.4.s:
tato jalādhāramukhe caṇḍīśvarāya namaḥ..
evaṃ saṃpūjya vidhivattato'rghaṃ saṃniveśayet.. 41.107 ..
1.4.d:
ततो जलाधारमुखे चण्डीश्वराय नमः..
एवं संपूज्य विधिवत्ततोऽर्घं संनिवेशयेत्.. 41.107 ..
1.4.m: Then at the spout of the water-channel: “Homage to Caṇḍīśvara.” / Having thus worshipped according to rule, one should then present the arghya offering:

1.4.s:
pānīyamakṣatāḥ puṣpametairyuktaṃ phalottamaiḥ..
gṛhāṇārghyaṃ mahādeva pūjāsaṃpūrtihetave.. 41.108 ..
1.4.d:
पानीयमक्षताः पुष्पमेतैर्युक्तं फलोत्तमैः..
गृहाणार्घ्यं महादेव पूजासंपूर्तिहेतवे.. 41.108 ..
1.4.m: “Accompanied by water, unbroken grains, flowers, and excellent fruits, / accept the arghya offering, O Mahādeva, for the completion of the worship.”

1.4.s:
arghādanaṃtaraṃ śaktaḥ pūjayedvasupūjayā..
dhūpaṃ dīpaṃ ca naivedyaṃ kramātpaścānnivedayet.. 41.109 ..
1.4.d:
अर्घादनंतरं शक्तः पूजयेद्वसुपूजया..
धूपं दीपं च नैवेद्यं क्रमात्पश्चान्निवेदयेत्.. 41.109 ..
1.4.m: After the arghya offering, if capable, one should worship with the eightfold worship. / Thereafter, one should offer incense, a lamp, and food offerings in due order.

1.4.s:
ghaṇṭāṃ ca vādayettatra tato nīrājanaṃ caret..
bhrāmayeddevadevasya śaṃkhavāditraniḥsvanaiḥ.. 41.110 ..
1.4.d:
घण्टां च वादयेत्तत्र ततो नीराजनं चरेत्..
भ्रामयेद्देवदेवस्य शंखवादित्रनिःस्वनैः.. 41.110 ..
1.4.m: And there he should ring a bell, and then perform the waving of lights (nīrājana); / he should wave it before the God of Gods to the sounds of conches and musical instruments.

1.4.s:
nīrājanaṃ ca yaḥ paśye ddevadevasya śūlinaḥ..
sa mucyetpātakaiḥ sarvaiḥ kiṃ punaryaḥ kariṣyati.. 41.111 ..
1.4.d:
नीराजनं च यः पश्ये द्देवदेवस्य शूलिनः..
स मुच्येत्पातकैः सर्वैः किं पुनर्यः करिष्यति.. 41.111 ..
1.4.m: And whoever sees the waving of lights to the God of Gods, the trident-bearer, / is freed from all sins—what then of one who performs it?

1.4.s:
nṛtyaṃ gītaṃ ca vādyaṃ ca alīkamapi yaścaret..
tasya tuṣyedanaṃtaṃhi gītavādyaphalaṃ yataḥ.. 41.112 ..
1.4.d:
नृत्यं गीतं च वाद्यं च अलीकमपि यश्चरेत्..
तस्य तुष्येदनंतंहि गीतवाद्यफलं यतः.. 41.112 ..
1.4.m: Even if one performs dancing, singing, and instrumental music imperfectly, / he will be endlessly pleased with him, since from song and music comes fruit.

1.4.s:
stotraistataśca saṃstūya daṇḍavatpraṇamedbhuvi..
kṣamāpayecca deveśaṃ sukṛtaṃ kukṛtaṃ kṣama.. 41.113 ..
1.4.d:
स्तोत्रैस्ततश्च संस्तूय दण्डवत्प्रणमेद्भुवि..
क्षमापयेच्च देवेशं सुकृतं कुकृतं क्षम.. 41.113 ..
1.4.m: Then, having praised [him] with hymns, one should bow down on the ground like a rod, / and ask forgiveness of the Lord of Gods: 'Forgive my good and bad deeds.'

1.4.s:
ya evaṃ yajate rudramasmim̐lliṃge viśeṣataḥ..
pitaraṃ pitāmahaṃ caiva tathaiva prapitāmaham.. 41.114 ..
1.4.d:
य एवं यजते रुद्रमस्मिम्̐ल्लिंगे विशेषतः..
पितरं पितामहं चैव तथैव प्रपितामहम्.. 41.114 ..
1.4.m: He who worships Rudra in this way, especially in this liṅga, / raises up his father, his grandfather, and his great-grandfather

1.4.s:
sarvātpāpātsamuttārya rudraloke vasecciram..
evaṃ māheśvaro bhūtvā sadācāravratasthitaḥ.. 41.115 ..
1.4.d:
सर्वात्पापात्समुत्तार्य रुद्रलोके वसेच्चिरम्..
एवं माहेश्वरो भूत्वा सदाचारव्रतस्थितः.. 41.115 ..
1.4.m: from all sin, and will dwell long in the world of Rudra. / Becoming thus a devotee of Maheśvara, established in the vow of right conduct,

1.4.s:
paśupāśavimokṣārthaṃ pūjayettanmanā yadi..
ya evaṃ yajate rudraṃ tenaitattarpitaṃ jagat.. 41.116 ..
1.4.d:
पशुपाशविमोक्षार्थं पूजयेत्तन्मना यदि..
य एवं यजते रुद्रं तेनैतत्तर्पितं जगत्.. 41.116 ..
1.4.m: if, with mind fixed on him, he worships for the release from the bonds of individual souls— / he who worships Rudra in this manner has gratified this entire world.

1.4.s:
kiṃ tvetatsaphalaṃ rājannācārayo na laṃghayet..
ācārātphalate dharmo hyācārātsvargamaśnute.. 41.117 ..
1.4.d:
किं त्वेतत्सफलं राजन्नाचारयो न लंघयेत्..
आचारात्फलते धर्मो ह्याचारात्स्वर्गमश्नुते.. 41.117 ..
1.4.m: Yet this bears fruit, O king, for one who does not transgress right conduct; / from right conduct dharma bears fruit; indeed, from right conduct one attains heaven.

1.4.s:
ācārāllabhate hyāyurācāro haṃtyalakṣaṇam..
yajñadānatapāṃsīha puruṣasya na bhūtaye.. 41.118 ..
1.4.d:
आचाराल्लभते ह्यायुराचारो हंत्यलक्षणम्..
यज्ञदानतपांसीह पुरुषस्य न भूतये.. 41.118 ..
1.4.m: Indeed, from right conduct one obtains long life; right conduct destroys inauspicious marks. / Sacrifices, gifts, and austerities here do not bring prosperity to a man

1.4.s:
bhavanti yaḥ sadācāraṃ samullaṃghya pravartate..
tasya kiñcitsamuddeśaṃ vakṣye taṃ śrṛṇu pārthiva.. 41.119 ..
1.4.d:
भवन्ति यः सदाचारं समुल्लंघ्य प्रवर्तते..
तस्य किञ्चित्समुद्देशं वक्ष्ये तं श्रृणु पार्थिव.. 41.119 ..
1.4.m: who acts transgressing right conduct. / I shall explain a brief outline of it; listen to that, O king.

1.4.s:
trivargasādhane yatnaḥ kartavyo gṛhamedhinā..
tatsaṃsiddhau gṛhasthasya siddhiratra paratra ca.. 41.120 ..
1.4.d:
त्रिवर्गसाधने यत्नः कर्तव्यो गृहमेधिना..
तत्संसिद्धौ गृहस्थस्य सिद्धिरत्र परत्र च.. 41.120 ..
1.4.m: Effort should be made by a householder in the accomplishment of the three aims of life; / upon their attainment, there is success for the householder here and in the hereafter.

1.4.s:
brāhme muhūrte budhyena dharmārthau cāpi cintayet..
samutthāya tathācamya daṃtadhāvanapūrvakam.. 41.121 ..
1.4.d:
ब्राह्मे मुहूर्ते बुध्येन धर्मार्थौ चापि चिन्तयेत्..
समुत्थाय तथाचम्य दंतधावनपूर्वकम्.. 41.121 ..
1.4.m: One should awaken at the hour of Brahmā and reflect upon dharma and wealth; / having risen and having thus sipped water after cleansing the teeth,

1.4.s:
sandhyāmupāsīta budhaḥ saṃśāṃtaḥ prayataḥ śuciḥ..
pūrvāṃ sandhyāṃ sanakṣatrāṃ paścimāṃ sadivākarām.. 41.122 ..
1.4.d:
सन्ध्यामुपासीत बुधः संशांतः प्रयतः शुचिः..
पूर्वां सन्ध्यां सनक्षत्रां पश्चिमां सदिवाकराम्.. 41.122 ..
1.4.m: the wise man, calmed, restrained, and pure, should attend to the twilight ritual: / the morning twilight while the stars are still visible, and the evening twilight while the sun is still present.

1.4.s:
upāsīta yathānyāyaṃ naināṃ jahyādanāpadi..
varjayedanṛtaṃ cāsatpralāpaṃ paruṣaṃ tathā.. 41.123 ..
1.4.d:
उपासीत यथान्यायं नैनां जह्यादनापदि..
वर्जयेदनृतं चासत्प्रलापं परुषं तथा.. 41.123 ..
1.4.m: He should attend to it properly; he must not abandon it except in distress. / He should avoid falsehood, useless chatter, and harsh words,

1.4.s:
asatsevāṃ hyasadvādaṃ hyasacchāstraṃ ca pārthiva..
ādarśadarśanaṃ daṃtadhāvanaṃ keśasādhanam.. 41.124 ..
1.4.d:
असत्सेवां ह्यसद्वादं ह्यसच्छास्त्रं च पार्थिव..
आदर्शदर्शनं दंतधावनं केशसाधनम्.. 41.124 ..
1.4.m: service to wicked people, unrighteous arguments, and bad scriptures, O king. / Looking in a mirror, cleansing the teeth, dressing the hair,

1.4.s:
devārcanaṃ ca pūrvāhṇe kāryāṇyāhurmaharṣayaḥ..
pālāśamāsanaṃ caiva pāduke daṃtadhāvanam..
varjayedāsanaṃ caiva padā nākarṣayedbudhaḥ.. 41.125 ..
1.4.d:
देवार्चनं च पूर्वाह्णे कार्याण्याहुर्महर्षयः..
पालाशमासनं चैव पादुके दंतधावनम्..
वर्जयेदासनं चैव पदा नाकर्षयेद्बुधः.. 41.125 ..
1.4.m: and worship of the gods in the forenoon are duties, the great seers have said. / A seat of palāśa wood, wooden sandals, and a tooth-twig [of it] / one should avoid; and a wise man should not drag a seat with his foot.

1.4.s: jalamagniṃ ca ninayedyagapanna vicakṣaṇaḥ.. 41.126 ..
1.4.d: जलमग्निं च निनयेद्यगपन्न विचक्षणः.. 41.126 ..
1.4.m: A wise man should never bring water and fire together.

1.4.s:
pādau prasārayennaiva gurudevāgnisaṃmukhau..
catuṣpathaṃ caityataruṃ devāgāraṃ tathā yatim.. 41.127 ..
1.4.d:
पादौ प्रसारयेन्नैव गुरुदेवाग्निसंमुखौ..
चतुष्पथं चैत्यतरुं देवागारं तथा यतिम्.. 41.127 ..
1.4.m: He should not stretch out his feet toward a guru, a deity, or fire; / a crossroads, a sacred tree, a temple, and an ascetic,

1.4.s: vidyādhikaṃ guruṃ vṛddhaṃ kuryādetānpradakṣiṇān.. 41.128 ..
1.4.d: विद्याधिकं गुरुं वृद्धं कुर्यादेतान्प्रदक्षिणान्.. 41.128 ..
1.4.m: one superior in learning, a guru, and an elder—he should circumambulate these with the right side turned towards them.

1.4.s:
āhāranīhāravihārayogāḥ susaṃvṛtā dharmavidānukāryāḥ..
vāgbuddhivīryāṇi tapastathaiva vārtāyuṣī guptatame ca kārye.. 41.129 ..
1.4.d:
आहारनीहारविहारयोगाः सुसंवृता धर्मविदानुकार्याः..
वाग्बुद्धिवीर्याणि तपस्तथैव वार्तायुषी गुप्ततमे च कार्ये.. 41.129 ..
1.4.m: Eating, evacuation, and sexual recreation should be done well-concealed by one who knows dharma; / speech, intellect, virility, austerity, occupation, and lifespan are to be kept most secret.

1.4.s:
ubhe mūtrapurīṣe tu divā kuryādudaṅmukhaḥ..
dakṣiṇābhimukho rātrau hyevamāyurna riṣyate.. 41.130 ..
1.4.d:
उभे मूत्रपुरीषे तु दिवा कुर्यादुदङ्मुखः..
दक्षिणाभिमुखो रात्रौ ह्येवमायुर्न रिष्यते.. 41.130 ..
1.4.m: One should discharge both urine and feces facing north by day, / and facing south at night; in this way lifespan is not impaired.

1.4.s:
pratyagniṃ prati sūryaṃ ca prati gāṃ vratinaṃ prati..
prati somodakaṃ sandhyāṃ prajñā naśyati mehataḥ.. 41.131 ..
1.4.d:
प्रत्यग्निं प्रति सूर्यं च प्रति गां व्रतिनं प्रति..
प्रति सोमोदकं सन्ध्यां प्रज्ञा नश्यति मेहतः.. 41.131 ..
1.4.m: Facing fire, facing the sun, facing a cow, facing an ascetic observer of vows, / facing the moon, water, or the twilight—the intellect of one who urinates is destroyed.

1.4.s:
bhojane śayane sthāne utsarge malamūtrayoḥ..
rathyācaṃkramaṇe cārdrapañcakaścācametsadā.. 41.132 ..
1.4.d:
भोजने शयने स्थाने उत्सर्गे मलमूत्रयोः..
रथ्याचंक्रमणे चार्द्रपञ्चकश्चाचमेत्सदा.. 41.132 ..
1.4.m: At meals, sleep, standing, the evacuation of feces and urine, / and when walking on a road, one should always rinse the mouth while moist in the five places.

1.4.s:
na nadyāṃ mehanaṃ kuryānna śmaśāne nabhasmani..
na gomaye na kṛṣṭe ca naivālūne na śāḍvale.. 41.133 ..
1.4.d:
न नद्यां मेहनं कुर्यान्न श्मशाने नभस्मनि..
न गोमये न कृष्टे च नैवालूने न शाड्वले.. 41.133 ..
1.4.m: One should not urinate in a river, nor in a cremation ground, nor on ashes, / nor on cow dung, nor on plowed land, nor on unharvested grain, nor on grassy ground.

1.4.s:
uddhṛttābhistathādbhistu śaucaṃ kuryādvicakṣaṇaḥ..
aṃtarjalāddevakulādvalmīkānmūṣakasthalāt.. 41.134 ..
1.4.d:
उद्धृत्ताभिस्तथाद्भिस्तु शौचं कुर्याद्विचक्षणः..
अंतर्जलाद्देवकुलाद्वल्मीकान्मूषकस्थलात्.. 41.134 ..
1.4.m: A wise man should perform purification with water that has been fetched; / [earth taken] from underwater, from a temple, from an anthill, from a mouse hole,

1.4.s:
apaviddhāpaśaucāśca varjayetpaṃca mṛttikāḥ..
gandhalepāpaharaṇaṃ śaucaṃ kuryāttathā budhaḥ.. 41.135 ..
1.4.d:
अपविद्धापशौचाश्च वर्जयेत्पंच मृत्तिकाः..
गन्धलेपापहरणं शौचं कुर्यात्तथा बुधः.. 41.135 ..
1.4.m: cast-away earth, and earth left after another's purification—one should avoid these five earths. / The wise man should thus perform purification that removes odor and residue.

1.4.s:
nātmānaṃ tāḍayennaiva dadyādduḥ khebhya eva ca..
ubhābhyāmapi pāṇibhyāṃ kaṇḍūyennātmanaḥ śiraḥ.. 41.136 ..
1.4.d:
नात्मानं ताडयेन्नैव दद्याद्दुः खेभ्य एव च..
उभाभ्यामपि पाणिभ्यां कण्डूयेन्नात्मनः शिरः.. 41.136 ..
1.4.m: He should not strike himself, nor should he yield to griefs; / nor should he scratch his head with both hands at once.

1.4.s:
rakṣeddārāṃstyajedīṣyāṃ tāsu niṣkāraṇaṃ budhaḥ..
sūryāstaṃ na vinākāścitkriyā naivācarettathā.. 41.137 ..
1.4.d:
रक्षेद्दारांस्त्यजेदीष्यां तासु निष्कारणं बुधः..
सूर्यास्तं न विनाकाश्चित्क्रिया नैवाचरेत्तथा.. 41.137 ..
1.4.m: The wise man should protect his wife and abandon jealousy toward her without cause; / nor should he perform any religious rites without the sun setting.

1.4.s:
adroheṇaiva bhūtānāmalpadroheṇa vā punaḥ..
śivacittorjayodvittaṃ na cātikṛpaṇo bhavet.. 41.138 ..
1.4.d:
अद्रोहेणैव भूतानामल्पद्रोहेण वा पुनः..
शिवचित्तोर्जयोद्वित्तं न चातिकृपणो भवेत्.. 41.138 ..
1.4.m: With no harm to living beings, or at most very slight harm, / with mind on Śiva, he should acquire wealth, and must not be overly stingy.

1.4.s:
nerṣyuḥ syānna kṛtaghnaḥ syānna paradrohakarmadhīḥ..
na pāṇipādacapalo na netracapalo'nṛjuḥ.. 41.139 ..
1.4.d:
नेर्ष्युः स्यान्न कृतघ्नः स्यान्न परद्रोहकर्मधीः..
न पाणिपादचपलो न नेत्रचपलोऽनृजुः.. 41.139 ..
1.4.m: He should not be envious, nor ungrateful, nor have an intellect intent on harming others; / he should not be fidgety with hands and feet, nor restless with eyes, nor deceitful;

1.4.s:
na ca vāgaṅgacapalo na cāśiṣṭasya gocaraḥ..
na śuṣkavādaṃ kurvīta śuṣkravairaṃ tathaiva ca.. 41.140 ..
1.4.d:
न च वागङ्गचपलो न चाशिष्टस्य गोचरः..
न शुष्कवादं कुर्वीत शुष्क्रवैरं तथैव च.. 41.140 ..
1.4.m: nor reckless in speech and limbs, nor accessible to the undisciplined; / he should not engage in pointless debate, nor in pointless enmity.

1.4.s:
upāyaiḥ sādhayedarthāndaṇḍastvagatikā gatiḥ..
bhinnāśanaṃ bhinnaśayyāṃ varjayedbhinnabhājanam.. 41.141 ..
1.4.d:
उपायैः साधयेदर्थान्दण्डस्त्वगतिका गतिः..
भिन्नाशनं भिन्नशय्यां वर्जयेद्भिन्नभाजनम्.. 41.141 ..
1.4.m: He should accomplish goals through suitable means; force is the last resort when all else fails. / He should avoid a broken seat, a broken bed, and a broken vessel.

1.4.s:
aṃtareṇa na gacchena dvayorjvalanaliṃgayoḥ..
nāgnyorna viprayoścaiva na daṃpatyornṛpottama.. 41.142 ..
1.4.d:
अंतरेण न गच्छेन द्वयोर्ज्वलनलिंगयोः..
नाग्न्योर्न विप्रयोश्चैव न दंपत्योर्नृपोत्तम.. 41.142 ..
1.4.m: He must not pass between two blazing fires or liṅgas, / nor between two fires, nor between two brahmins, nor between a married couple, O best of kings;

1.4.s:
na sūryavyomayornaiva harasya vṛṣabhasya ca..
eteṣāmaṃtaraṃ kurvanyataḥ pāpamavāpnuyāt.. 41.143 ..
1.4.d:
न सूर्यव्योमयोर्नैव हरस्य वृषभस्य च..
एतेषामंतरं कुर्वन्यतः पापमवाप्नुयात्.. 41.143 ..
1.4.m: nor between the sun and the sky, nor between Hara and the bull; / for passing between these, he incurs sin.

1.4.s:
naikavastraśca bhuṃjīta nāgnau homamathācaret..
na cārcayeddvijānnaiva kuryāddevārcanaṃ budhaḥ.. 41.144 ..
1.4.d:
नैकवस्त्रश्च भुंजीत नाग्नौ होममथाचरेत्..
न चार्चयेद्द्विजान्नैव कुर्याद्देवार्चनं बुधः.. 41.144 ..
1.4.m: The wise man should not eat wearing only a single garment, nor perform an oblation in the fire, / nor worship the twice-born, nor perform the worship of the gods [thus].

1.4.s:
khaṃḍanaṃ peṣaṇaṃ mārṣṭiṃ jalasaṃśodhanaṃ tathā..
raṃdhanaṃ bhojanaṃ svāpa utthānaṃ gamanaṃ kṣutam.. 41.145 ..
1.4.d:
खंडनं पेषणं मार्ष्टिं जलसंशोधनं तथा..
रंधनं भोजनं स्वाप उत्थानं गमनं क्षुतम्.. 41.145 ..
1.4.m: Cutting, grinding, sweeping, purifying water, / cooking, eating, sleeping, rising, walking, sneezing,

1.4.s:
kāryāraṃbhaṃ samāptiṃ ca vacaḥ procya tathā priyam..
pibañjighranspṛśañchṛṇvanvivakṣurmaithunaṃ tathā.. 41.146 ..
1.4.d:
कार्यारंभं समाप्तिं च वचः प्रोच्य तथा प्रियम्..
पिबञ्जिघ्रन्स्पृशञ्छृण्वन्विवक्षुर्मैथुनं तथा.. 41.146 ..
1.4.m: undertaking an action and concluding it, speaking pleasant words, / drinking, smelling, touching, hearing, wishing to speak, and sexual intercourse,

1.4.s:
śucitvaṃ ca japaṃ sthāṇuṃ yaḥ kuryādviṃśatiṃ tathā..
māheśvaraḥ sa vijñeyaḥ śeṣonyo nāmadhārakaḥ.. 41.147 ..
1.4.d:
शुचित्वं च जपं स्थाणुं यः कुर्याद्विंशतिं तथा..
माहेश्वरः स विज्ञेयः शेषोन्यो नामधारकः.. 41.147 ..
1.4.m: purification, recitation, and worship of Sthāṇu: he who performs these twenty [with remembrance of Śiva], / he is to be recognized as a true devotee of Maheśvara; another is merely one who bears the name.

1.4.s:
sa vai rudramayo bhūtvā tataścāṃte śivaṃ vrajet..
parastriyaṃ nābhibhāṣettathā saṃbhāṣayedyadi.. 41.148 ..
1.4.d:
स वै रुद्रमयो भूत्वा ततश्चांते शिवं व्रजेत्..
परस्त्रियं नाभिभाषेत्तथा संभाषयेद्यदि.. 41.148 ..
1.4.m: He indeed becomes identical with Rudra and goes to Śiva at the end. / He should not converse with another's wife; if he does speak to her,

1.4.s:
mātaḥ svasaratho putri āryeti ca vadedbudhaḥ..
ucachiṣṭo nālabhetkiṃcinna ca sūryaṃ vilokayet.. 41.149 ..
1.4.d:
मातः स्वसरथो पुत्रि आर्येति च वदेद्बुधः..
उचछिष्टो नालभेत्किंचिन्न च सूर्यं विलोकयेत्.. 41.149 ..
1.4.m: the wise man should address her as 'Mother', 'Sister', 'Daughter', or 'Noble Lady'. / Being impure with food remnants, he should touch nothing, nor look at the sun,

1.4.s:
nenduṃ na tārakāścaiva nādayennātmanaḥ śiraḥ..
svasrā dihitrā mātrā vā naikāṃtāsana mācaret.. 41.150 ..
1.4.d:
नेन्दुं न तारकाश्चैव नादयेन्नात्मनः शिरः..
स्वस्रा दिहित्रा मात्रा वा नैकांतासन माचरेत्.. 41.150 ..
1.4.m: nor at the moon, nor at the stars, nor strike his own head. / He should not sit in solitude with his sister, daughter, or mother;

1.4.s:
durjayo hīṃdriyagrāmo muhyate paṃḍito'pi san..
gurumabhyāgataṃ gehe svayamutthāya yatnataḥ.. 41.151 ..
1.4.d:
दुर्जयो हींद्रियग्रामो मुह्यते पंडितोऽपि सन्..
गुरुमभ्यागतं गेहे स्वयमुत्थाय यत्नतः.. 41.151 ..
1.4.m: for the group of senses is difficult to conquer; even a learned man is deluded by them. / When a guru arrives at the house, rising up himself with diligence,

1.4.s:
āsanaṃ kalpayettasya kuryātpādābhivaṃdanam..
nodakchirāḥ svapejjātu na ca pratyakchirā budhaḥ.. 41.152 ..
1.4.d:
आसनं कल्पयेत्तस्य कुर्यात्पादाभिवंदनम्..
नोदक्छिराः स्वपेज्जातु न च प्रत्यक्छिरा बुधः.. 41.152 ..
1.4.m: he should offer him a seat and bow down to his feet. / A wise man should never sleep with his head toward the north, nor with his head toward the west.

1.4.s:
śirasyagastyamādhāya tathaiva ca puraṃdaram..
udakyādarśanaṃ sparśaṃ varjyaṃ saṃbhāṣaṇaṃ tathā.. 41.153 ..
1.4.d:
शिरस्यगस्त्यमाधाय तथैव च पुरंदरम्..
उदक्यादर्शनं स्पर्शं वर्ज्यं संभाषणं तथा.. 41.153 ..
1.4.m:
placing Agastya at the head, and likewise Purandara.
Seeing a menstruating woman, touching her, and speaking to her must be avoided.

1.4.s:
nāpsu mūtraṃ purīṣaṃ vā maithunaṃ vā samācaret..
kṛtvā vibhavato devamanuṣyarṣisamarcanām.. 41.154 ..
1.4.d:
नाप्सु मूत्रं पुरीषं वा मैथुनं वा समाचरेत्..
कृत्वा विभवतो देवमनुष्यर्षिसमर्चनाम्.. 41.154 ..
1.4.m:
One should not pass urine or feces in water, nor engage in sexual intercourse [there].
Having worshipped the gods, humans, and seers according to one's wealth,

1.4.s:
pitṝṇāṃ ca tataḥ śeṣaṃ bhoktuṃ māheśvaro'rhati..
vāgyataḥ śucirācāṃtaḥ prāṅmukhodaṅmukho'pi vā.. 41.155 ..
1.4.d:
पितॄणां च ततः शेषं भोक्तुं माहेश्वरोऽर्हति..
वाग्यतः शुचिराचांतः प्राङ्मुखोदङ्मुखोऽपि वा.. 41.155 ..
1.4.m:
and the ancestors, a devotee of Maheśvara may then eat the remains,
restraining his speech, pure, having sipped water, facing east or facing north,

1.4.s:
antarjānuśca taccitto bhuñjītānnamakutsayan..
nopaghātaṃ vinā doṣānna tasyodāharedbudhaḥ.. 41.156 ..
1.4.d:
अन्तर्जानुश्च तच्चित्तो भुञ्जीतान्नमकुत्सयन्..
नोपघातं विना दोषान्न तस्योदाहरेद्बुधः.. 41.156 ..
1.4.m:
with his hands within his knees, attentive, eating the food without disparaging it.
Unless it is spoiled, a wise man should not speak ill of it.

1.4.s:
nagnasnānaṃ na kurvīta na śayīta vrajeta vā..
duṣkṛtaṃ na gurorbrūyātkruddhaṃ cainaṃ prasādayet.. 41.157 ..
1.4.d:
नग्नस्नानं न कुर्वीत न शयीत व्रजेत वा..
दुष्कृतं न गुरोर्ब्रूयात्क्रुद्धं चैनं प्रसादयेत्.. 41.157 ..
1.4.m:
One should not bathe naked, nor sleep [naked], nor walk [naked].
One should not speak of a guru's wrongdoing, and if he is angry, one should propitiate him.

1.4.s:
parivādaṃ na śrṛmuyādanyeṣāmapi jalpatām..
sadā cā karṇayeddhamāstyaktvā kṛtyaśatānyapi.. 41.158 ..
1.4.d:
परिवादं न श्रृमुयादन्येषामपि जल्पताम्..
सदा चा कर्णयेद्धमास्त्यक्त्वा कृत्यशतान्यपि.. 41.158 ..
1.4.m:
One should not listen to slander, even when others are prattling.
And abandoning even hundreds of tasks, one should always listen to dharma.

1.4.s:
nityaṃ nityaṃ hi saṃmārṣṭi gehadarpaṇayoriva..
śuklāyāṃ ca caturdaśyāṃ naktabhojī sadā bhavet.. 41.159 ..
1.4.d:
नित्यं नित्यं हि संमार्ष्टि गेहदर्पणयोरिव..
शुक्लायां च चतुर्दश्यां नक्तभोजी सदा भवेत्.. 41.159 ..
1.4.m:
For daily [listening to dharma] cleanses [the mind], as if [cleaning] a house or a mirror.
And on the fourteenth day of the bright fortnight, one should always eat only at night.

1.4.s:
tisro rātrīrna śaktaścedevaṃ māheśvaro bhavet..
saṃyāvakṛśarāmāṃsaṃ nātmānamupasādhayet.. 41.160 ..
1.4.d:
तिस्रो रात्रीर्न शक्तश्चेदेवं माहेश्वरो भवेत्..
संयावकृशरामांसं नात्मानमुपसाधयेत्.. 41.160 ..
1.4.m:
If unable [to fast for] three nights, a devotee of Maheśvara should act thus:
He should not prepare for himself sweet pudding, rice with lentils and sesame, or meat.

1.4.s:
sāyaṃprātaśca bhoktavyaṃ kṛtvā hyatithi bhojanam..
svapnādhyayanabhojyāni saṃdhyayośca vivarjayet.. 41.161 ..
1.4.d:
सायंप्रातश्च भोक्तव्यं कृत्वा ह्यतिथि भोजनम्..
स्वप्नाध्ययनभोज्यानि संध्ययोश्च विवर्जयेत्.. 41.161 ..
1.4.m:
One should eat in the evening and morning, having first fed a guest.
And at the two twilights, one should avoid sleep, study, and eating.

1.4.s:
bhuṃjānaḥ saṃdhyayormohādasurāvasatho bhavet..
snāto na dhūnayetkeśānkṣute niṣṭhīvite'dhvani.. 41.162 ..
1.4.d:
भुंजानः संध्ययोर्मोहादसुरावसथो भवेत्..
स्नातो न धूनयेत्केशान्क्षुते निष्ठीवितेऽध्वनि.. 41.162 ..
1.4.m:
Eating at the two twilights out of delusion, one becomes an abode for asuras.
Having bathed, one should not shake one's hair; upon sneezing, spitting, or walking on a road,

1.4.s:
ālabheddakṣiṇaṃ karṇaṃ sarvabhūtāni kṣāmayet..
na cāpi nīlīvāsāḥ syānna viparyastavastradhṛk.. 41.163 ..
1.4.d:
आलभेद्दक्षिणं कर्णं सर्वभूतानि क्षामयेत्..
न चापि नीलीवासाः स्यान्न विपर्यस्तवस्त्रधृक्.. 41.163 ..
1.4.m:
one should touch one's right ear, [and] ask forgiveness from all beings.
One should not wear blue garments, nor wear reversed clothes.

1.4.s:
varjyaṃ ca malinaṃ vastraṃ daśābhiśca vivarjitam..
prakṣālya mukhahastau ca pādau cāpyupaviśya ca.. 41.164 ..
1.4.d:
वर्ज्यं च मलिनं वस्त्रं दशाभिश्च विवर्जितम्..
प्रक्षाल्य मुखहस्तौ च पादौ चाप्युपविश्य च.. 41.164 ..
1.4.m:
Dirty clothing and clothing lacking fringes must be avoided.
Having washed face and hands, and also feet, and having sat down,

1.4.s:
aṃtajānustrirācāmeddirmukhaṃ parimārjayet..
toyena sparśayetkhāni svamūrdhānaṃ tathaiva ca.. 41.165 ..
1.4.d:
अंतजानुस्त्रिराचामेद्दिर्मुखं परिमार्जयेत्..
तोयेन स्पर्शयेत्खानि स्वमूर्धानं तथैव च.. 41.165 ..
1.4.m:
with hands placed within the knees, one should sip water three times and wipe the mouth twice;
with water one should touch the bodily apertures and likewise one's own head.

1.4.s:
ācamya punarācamya kriyāḥ kurvīta sarvaśaḥ..
kṣute niṣṭhīvite caiva daṃtalagne tathaiva ca.. 41.166 ..
1.4.d:
आचम्य पुनराचम्य क्रियाः कुर्वीत सर्वशः..
क्षुते निष्ठीविते चैव दंतलग्ने तथैव च.. 41.166 ..
1.4.m:
Sipping water again and again, one should perform all religious rites.
Upon sneezing, spitting, and also when food sticks between the teeth,

1.4.s:
patitānāṃ ca saṃbhāṣe kuryādācamanikriyām..
adhyetavyā trayī nityaṃ bhavitavyaṃ vipaścitā.. 41.167 ..
1.4.d:
पतितानां च संभाषे कुर्यादाचमनिक्रियाम्..
अध्येतव्या त्रयी नित्यं भवितव्यं विपश्चिता.. 41.167 ..
1.4.m:
and when conversing with fallen persons, one should perform the act of sipping water.
The threefold Veda must be studied constantly; one must be a learned man.

1.4.s:
dharmato dhanamāhārya yaṣṭavyaṃ cāpi yatnataḥ..
hīnebhyopi na yuṃjīta tvaṃkāraṃ karhicidbadhaḥ..
tvaṃkāro vā vadho vāpi gurūṇāmubhayaṃ samam.. 41.168 ..
1.4.d:
धर्मतो धनमाहार्य यष्टव्यं चापि यत्नतः..
हीनेभ्योपि न युंजीत त्वंकारं कर्हिचिद्बधः..
त्वंकारो वा वधो वापि गुरूणामुभयं समम्.. 41.168 ..

1.4.s:
satyaṃ vācyaṃ nityamaitreṇa bhāvyaṃ kāryaṃ tyājyaṃ nityamāyāsakāri..
loke'muṣminyaddinaṃ syāttathāsminnātmā yoge yejanīyo gabhīraiḥ.. 41.169 ..
1.4.d:
सत्यं वाच्यं नित्यमैत्रेण भाव्यं कार्यं त्याज्यं नित्यमायासकारि..
लोकेऽमुष्मिन्यद्दिनं स्यात्तथास्मिन्नात्मा योगे येजनीयो गभीरैः.. 41.169 ..
1.4.m:
Truth must be spoken; one should always be friendly; work that causes constant distress must be avoided;
as a day passes in this world, so also the self must be engaged in profound meditation.

1.4.s:
tīrthasnānaiḥ sopavāsairvrataiśca pātre dānairhomajapyaiścayajñaiḥ..
bhavārcanairdevapūjāviśeṣairātmā nityaṃ śodhanīyo malāktaḥ.. 41.170 ..
1.4.d:
तीर्थस्नानैः सोपवासैर्व्रतैश्च पात्रे दानैर्होमजप्यैश्चयज्ञैः..
भवार्चनैर्देवपूजाविशेषैरात्मा नित्यं शोधनीयो मलाक्तः.. 41.170 ..
1.4.m:
By bathing at sacred fords, by fasts and vows, by gifts to a worthy recipient, by oblations, silent prayers, and sacrifices,
by worshipping Bhava, and by special forms of divine worship, the defiled self must constantly be purified.

1.4.s:
yatrāpi kurvato nātmā jugupsāmeti pārthiva..
tatkartavyasamasaṃgena yannagopyaṃ mahājane.. 41.171 ..
1.4.d:
यत्रापि कुर्वतो नात्मा जुगुप्सामेति पार्थिव..
तत्कर्तव्यसमसंगेन यन्नगोप्यं महाजने.. 41.171 ..
1.4.m:
And in whatever action the self feels no self-reproach while doing it, O king,
that is to be done with detachment—whatever need not be hidden among eminent people.

1.4.s:
iti te vai samuddeśaḥ kīrtitaḥ kiṃcideva ca..
śeṣaḥ smṛtipurāṇebhyastvayā śrotavya eva ca.. 41.172 ..
1.4.d:
इति ते वै समुद्देशः कीर्तितः किंचिदेव च..
शेषः स्मृतिपुराणेभ्यस्त्वया श्रोतव्य एव च.. 41.172 ..
1.4.m:
Thus this summary has indeed been proclaimed to you in brief;
the rest must indeed be heard by you from the Smṛtis and Purāṇas.

1.4.s:
evamācarato dharmaṃ maheśasya gṛhe sataḥ..
dharmārthakāmasaṃprāptau paratreha ca śobhanam.. 41.173 ..
1.4.d:
एवमाचरतो धर्मं महेशस्य गृहे सतः..
धर्मार्थकामसंप्राप्तौ परत्रेह च शोभनम्.. 41.173 ..
1.4.m:
For a devotee of Maheśa dwelling in the household and practicing dharma in this manner,
there is attainment of dharma, wealth, and pleasure, and good fortune in the hereafter and in this world."

1.4.s:
evaṃ nānāvidhāndharmānmahākālasya phālguna..
vadato dhvanirākāśe sumahānabhyajāyata.. 41.174 ..
1.4.d:
एवं नानाविधान्धर्मान्महाकालस्य फाल्गुन..
वदतो ध्वनिराकाशे सुमहानभ्यजायत.. 41.174 ..
1.4.m:
While Mahākāla was speaking in this way of various kinds of dharma, O Phālguna,
a very great sound arose in the sky.

1.4.s:
yāvatpaśyaṃti ye tatra samājagmuḥ śrṛṇuṣva tān..
brahmā viṣṇuḥ svayaṃ rudro de vī rudragaṇāstathā.. 41.175 ..
1.4.d:
यावत्पश्यंति ये तत्र समाजग्मुः श्रृणुष्व तान्..
ब्रह्मा विष्णुः स्वयं रुद्रो दे वी रुद्रगणास्तथा.. 41.175 ..
1.4.m:
Hear who arrived there as they watched:
Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra himself, the Devī, and also the hosts of Rudras,

1.4.s:
iṃdrādayastathā devā vasiṣṭhādyā munīśvarāḥ..
tuṃbarupravarāścāpi gaṃdharvāpsarasāṃ gaṇāḥ.. 41.176 ..
1.4.d:
इंद्रादयस्तथा देवा वसिष्ठाद्या मुनीश्वराः..
तुंबरुप्रवराश्चापि गंधर्वाप्सरसां गणाः.. 41.176 ..
1.4.m:
and the gods headed by Indra, the lordly sages headed by Vasiṣṭha,
the foremost [musicians] headed by Tumburu, and the hosts of gandharvas and apsarases.

1.4.s:
tānmaheśamukhānsarvānmahākālo mahāmatiḥ..
arcayāmāsa bahudhā bhaktyudrekātipūritaḥ.. 41.177 ..
1.4.d:
तान्महेशमुखान्सर्वान्महाकालो महामतिः..
अर्चयामास बहुधा भक्त्युद्रेकातिपूरितः.. 41.177 ..
1.4.m:
The noble-minded Mahākāla worshipped all of them, headed by Maheśa,
in various ways, filled to overflowing with an abundance of devotion.

1.4.s:
tato brahmādibhirdevairvare ratnamayāsane..
upaviṣṭo'bhiṣiktaśca mahīsāgarasaṃgame.. 41.178 ..
1.4.d:
ततो ब्रह्मादिभिर्देवैर्वरे रत्नमयासने..
उपविष्टोऽभिषिक्तश्च महीसागरसंगमे.. 41.178 ..
1.4.m:
Then, having been seated upon an excellent jeweled throne by the gods headed by Brahmā,
he was consecrated at the confluence of the Mahī and the ocean.

1.4.s:
tato devyā samāliṃgya nītvotsaṃgaṃ svakaṃ mudā..
putratve kalpitaḥ pārtha mahākālo mahāmatiḥ.. 41.179 ..
1.4.d:
ततो देव्या समालिंग्य नीत्वोत्संगं स्वकं मुदा..
पुत्रत्वे कल्पितः पार्थ महाकालो महामतिः.. 41.179 ..
1.4.m:
Then, having embraced him and taken him happily into her lap,
the noble-minded Mahākāla was adopted as a son by the Devī, O Pārtha.

1.4.s:
uktañca yāvadbrahmāṇḍamidamāste śivavrata..
tāvattiṣṭha śivasthāne śivavacchivabhaktitaḥ.. 41.180 ..
1.4.d:
उक्तञ्च यावद्ब्रह्माण्डमिदमास्ते शिवव्रत..
तावत्तिष्ठ शिवस्थाने शिववच्छिवभक्तितः.. 41.180 ..
1.4.m:
And it was said: "As long as this universe remains, O observer of Śiva's vows,
remain in the abode of Śiva like Śiva himself, through devotion to Śiva."

1.4.s:
devena ca varo dattastvalliṃgaṃ yo'rcayiṣyati..
jitendriyaḥ śucirbhūtvā ūrdhvaṃ mallokameṣyati.. 41.181 ..
1.4.d:
देवेन च वरो दत्तस्त्वल्लिंगं योऽर्चयिष्यति..
जितेन्द्रियः शुचिर्भूत्वा ऊर्ध्वं मल्लोकमेष्यति.. 41.181 ..
1.4.m:
And a boon was granted by the god: "Whoever worships your liṅga,
having conquered his senses and become pure, shall go upward to my world.

1.4.s:
darśanaṃ stavanaṃ pūjā praṇāmaśca tato japaḥ..
dānaṃ cātra kṛtaṃ liṃge mamātitṛptikāraṇam.. 41.182 ..
1.4.d:
दर्शनं स्तवनं पूजा प्रणामश्च ततो जपः..
दानं चात्र कृतं लिंगे ममातितृप्तिकारणम्.. 41.182 ..
1.4.m:
Darśana, praise, worship, prostration, and then japa,
and giving gifts performed here at this liṅga, are the cause of my supreme gratification."

1.4.s:
ityukte vismitā devāḥ sādhu sādhviti te jaguḥ..
brahmaviṣṇumukhāścaiva mahākālaṃ pratuṣṭuvuḥ.. 41.183 ..
1.4.d:
इत्युक्ते विस्मिता देवाः साधु साध्विति ते जगुः..
ब्रह्मविष्णुमुखाश्चैव महाकालं प्रतुष्टुवुः.. 41.183 ..
1.4.m:
When this was said, the amazed gods sang out, "Excellent, excellent!"
And [the gods] headed by Brahmā and Viṣṇu praised Mahākāla.

1.4.s:
tataḥ suraiḥstūyamāno vaṃdyamānaśca cāraṇaiḥ..
nṛtyadbhirapsarobhiśca kītairgaṃdharvajaiḥ śubhaiḥ.. 41.184 ..
1.4.d:
ततः सुरैःस्तूयमानो वंद्यमानश्च चारणैः..
नृत्यद्भिरप्सरोभिश्च कीतैर्गंधर्वजैः शुभैः.. 41.184 ..
1.4.m:
Then, being praised by the gods and revered by the cāraṇas,
with dancing apsarases and auspicious songs born of gandharvas,

1.4.s: koṭikoṭigaṇaiścaiva stuvadbhiḥ sarvato vṛtaḥ.. 41.185 ..
1.4.d: कोटिकोटिगणैश्चैव स्तुवद्भिः सर्वतो वृतः.. 41.185 ..
1.4.m: and surrounded on all sides by millions of praising gaṇas,

1.4.s:
mahākālo rudrabhavanaṃ gato bhavapurassaraḥ..
evametanmahāliṃgamutpannaṃ kurunaṃdana.. 41.186 ..
1.4.d:
महाकालो रुद्रभवनं गतो भवपुरस्सरः..
एवमेतन्महालिंगमुत्पन्नं कुरुनंदन.. 41.186 ..
1.4.m:
Mahākāla went to the abode of Rudra, preceded by Bhava.
Thus this great liṅga came into being, O joy of the Kurus.

1.4.s:
kūpaścāpi saraḥ puṇyaṃ mahākālasya siddhidam..
atra ye manujāḥ pārtha liṃgasyārādhane ratāḥ.. 41.187 ..
1.4.d:
कूपश्चापि सरः पुण्यं महाकालस्य सिद्धिदम्..
अत्र ये मनुजाः पार्थ लिंगस्याराधने रताः.. 41.187 ..
1.4.m:
And the holy well and lake of Mahākāla bestow accomplishments.
Those men who are devoted to the worship of the liṅga here, O Pārtha,

1.4.s:
mahākālaḥ samāliṃgya tāñchivāya nivedayet..
etadatyadbhutaṃ liṃgaṃ triṣu lokeṣu viśrutam.. 41.188 ..
1.4.d:
महाकालः समालिंग्य ताञ्छिवाय निवेदयेत्..
एतदत्यद्भुतं लिंगं त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतम्.. 41.188 ..
1.4.m:
Mahākāla embraces and presents them to Śiva.
This most wonderful liṅga is celebrated in the three worlds.

1.4.s: dṛṣṭaṃ spṛṣṭaṃ pūjitaṃ ca gatāste bhavasadma tat evametāni liṃgāni sapta jātāni phālguna.. 41.189 ..
1.4.d: दृष्टं स्पृष्टं पूजितं च गतास्ते भवसद्म तत् एवमेतानि लिंगानि सप्त जातानि फाल्गुन.. 41.189 ..
1.4.m:
Seen, touched, and worshipped, [by them] that abode of Bhava is attained.
Thus these seven liṅgas came into being, O Phālguna.

1.4.s:
ye śrṛṇvaṃti gṛṇaṃtyetattepi dhanyā narottamāḥ.. 41.190 ..
iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśīti sāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ prathame māheśvarakhaṇḍe kaumārikākhaṇḍe śrīmahākālamāhātmye mahākālakaraṃdhamasaṃvāde śivapūjanavidhinityakartavyadharmanirūpaṇapūrvakamahākālaśivalokaprāptivarṇanaṃnāmaikacatvāriṃśo'dhyāyaḥ.. 41 .. cha ..
1.4.d:
ये श्रृण्वंति गृणंत्येतत्तेपि धन्या नरोत्तमाः.. 41.190 ..
इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीति साहस्र्यां संहितायां प्रथमे माहेश्वरखण्डे कौमारिकाखण्डे श्रीमहाकालमाहात्म्ये महाकालकरंधमसंवादे शिवपूजनविधिनित्यकर्तव्यधर्मनिरूपणपूर्वकमहाकालशिवलोकप्राप्तिवर्णनंनामैकचत्वारिंशोऽध्यायः.. 41 .. छ ..
1.4.m:
Those best of men who hear and recite this are also fortunate.
Thus ends the forty-first chapter, entitled "The Description of the Attainment of the World of Śiva by Mahākāla Preceded by the Exposition of the Method of Worshipping Śiva and the Duties to Be Performed Daily, in the Dialogue between Mahākāla and Karandhama, in the Māhātmya of Śrī Mahākāla, in the Kaumārikākhaṇḍa of the First Section, the Māheśvarakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.

1.4.s:
..nārada uvāca..
tato mayā sthāpite ca sthāne kālāṃtareṇa ha..
ciṃtitaṃ hṛdaye bhūyo dvijānugrahakāmyayā.. 42.1 ..
1.4.d:
..नारद उवाच..
ततो मया स्थापिते च स्थाने कालांतरेण ह..
चिंतितं हृदये भूयो द्विजानुग्रहकाम्यया.. 42.1 ..
1.4.m:
Nārada said:
Then, after that place had been established by me, in the course of time,
it was pondered again in my heart, desiring to bestow grace upon the twice-born:

1.4.s:
vāsudevavihīnaṃ hi tīrthametanna rocate..
asūryaṃ hi jagadyadvatsa hi bhūṣaṇa bhūṣaṇam.. 42.2 ..
1.4.d:
वासुदेवविहीनं हि तीर्थमेतन्न रोचते..
असूर्यं हि जगद्यद्वत्स हि भूषण भूषणम्.. 42.2 ..
1.4.m:
“This sacred ford, devoid of Vāsudeva, does not shine,
just as the world [is without light] without the sun; for he is the ornament of ornaments.

1.4.s:
yatra naiva hariḥ svāmī tīrthe gehe'tha mānase..
śāstre vā tadasatsarvaṃ hāṃsaṃ tīrthaṃ na vāyasam.. 42.3 ..
1.4.d:
यत्र नैव हरिः स्वामी तीर्थे गेहेऽथ मानसे..
शास्त्रे वा तदसत्सर्वं हांसं तीर्थं न वायसम्.. 42.3 ..
1.4.m:
A sacred ford, a house, a mind, or a treatise
where Hari is not the lord—all that is worthless: a sacred ford fit for swans, not for crows.”

1.4.s:
tasmātprasādya varadaṃ tīrthe'sminpuruṣottamam..
āneṣye kalayā sākṣādviśvanugrahakāmyayā.. 42.4 ..
1.4.d:
तस्मात्प्रसाद्य वरदं तीर्थेऽस्मिन्पुरुषोत्तमम्..
आनेष्ये कलया साक्षाद्विश्वनुग्रहकाम्यया.. 42.4 ..
1.4.m:
"Therefore, having propitiated Puruṣottama, the granter of boons, in this sacred ford,
I shall bring him in a part visibly, desiring to grace the universe."

1.4.s:
iti saṃciṃtya kauravya tato'haṃ cātra saṃsthitaḥ..
jñānayogena yogīṃdraṃ śataṃ varṣāṇyatoṣayam.. 42.5 ..
1.4.d:
इति संचिंत्य कौरव्य ततोऽहं चात्र संस्थितः..
ज्ञानयोगेन योगींद्रं शतं वर्षाण्यतोषयम्.. 42.5 ..
1.4.m:
"Reflecting thus, O descendant of Kuru, I remained here,
and by the yoga of knowledge I pleased the lord of yogins for a hundred years.

1.4.s:
aṣṭākṣaraṃ japanmaṃtraṃ saṃnigṛhyeṃdriyāṇi ca..
vāsudevamayo bhūtvā sarvabhūtakṛpāparaḥ.. 42.6 ..
1.4.d:
अष्टाक्षरं जपन्मंत्रं संनिगृह्येंद्रियाणि च..
वासुदेवमयो भूत्वा सर्वभूतकृपापरः.. 42.6 ..
1.4.m:
Muttering the eight-syllable mantra and restraining my senses,
I became absorbed in Vāsudeva, intent on compassion toward all beings.

1.4.s:
evaṃ mayārādhyamāno garuḍaṃ harirāsthitaḥ..
gaṇakoṭiparivṛtaḥ pratyakṣaḥ samajāyata.. 42.7 ..
1.4.d:
एवं मयाराध्यमानो गरुडं हरिरास्थितः..
गणकोटिपरिवृतः प्रत्यक्षः समजायत.. 42.7 ..
1.4.m:
As he was thus being worshipped by me, Hari, mounted upon Garuḍa
and surrounded by tens of millions of attendants, became visible to my eyes.

1.4.s:
tamahaṃ prāṃjalirbhūtvā dattvārghyaṃ vidhivaddhareḥ..
pratyavocaṃ pramamyātha prabaddhakarasaṃ puṭaḥ.. 42.8 ..
1.4.d:
तमहं प्रांजलिर्भूत्वा दत्त्वार्घ्यं विधिवद्धरेः..
प्रत्यवोचं प्रमम्याथ प्रबद्धकरसं पुटः.. 42.8 ..
1.4.m:
Joining my palms and having offered the water of hospitality according to rule to Hari,
I bowed down, with hands folded together, and addressed him:

1.4.s:
śvetadvīpe purā dṛṣṭaṃ mayā rūpaṃ tava prabho..
ajaṃ sanātanaṃ viṣṇo naranārāyaṇātmakam.. 42.9 ..
1.4.d:
श्वेतद्वीपे पुरा दृष्टं मया रूपं तव प्रभो..
अजं सनातनं विष्णो नरनारायणात्मकम्.. 42.9 ..
1.4.m:
'In Śvetadvīpa formerly, O Lord, that form of yours was seen by me,
unborn, eternal, O Viṣṇu, consisting of Nara and Nārāyaṇa.

1.4.s:
tadrūpasya kalāmekāṃ sthāpayātra janārdana..
yadi tuṣṭo'si me viṣṇo tadidaṃ kriyatāṃ tvayā.. 42.10 ..
1.4.d:
तद्रूपस्य कलामेकां स्थापयात्र जनार्दन..
यदि तुष्टोऽसि मे विष्णो तदिदं क्रियतां त्वया.. 42.10 ..
1.4.m:
Establish a single portion of that form here, O Janārdana;
if you are pleased with me, O Viṣṇu, let this be done by you.'

1.4.s:
evaṃ mayā prārthito'tha provāca garuḍadhvajaḥ..
evamastu brahmaputra yattvayābhīpsitaṃ hṛdi .. 42.11 ..
1.4.d:
एवं मया प्रार्थितोऽथ प्रोवाच गरुडध्वजः..
एवमस्तु ब्रह्मपुत्र यत्त्वयाभीप्सितं हृदि .. 42.11 ..
1.4.m:
Thus entreated by me, he whose banner is Garuḍa then spoke:
'So be it, O son of Brahmā! Whatever was desired by you in your heart,

1.4.s:
tattathā bhavitā sarvamapyatrasthaṃ sadaiva hi..
evamuktvā gate viṣṇau niveśya svakalāṃ prabho.. 42.12 ..
1.4.d:
तत्तथा भविता सर्वमप्यत्रस्थं सदैव हि..
एवमुक्त्वा गते विष्णौ निवेश्य स्वकलां प्रभो.. 42.12 ..
1.4.m:
all that will be so, staying right here forever.'
Having spoken thus, when Viṣṇu had departed after placing a part of himself, O lord,

1.4.s:
mayā saṃsthāpito viṣṇurlokānugrahakāmyayā..
yasmātsvayaṃ śvetadvīpanivāsyatra hariḥ sthitaḥ.. 42.13 ..
1.4.d:
मया संस्थापितो विष्णुर्लोकानुग्रहकाम्यया..
यस्मात्स्वयं श्वेतद्वीपनिवास्यत्र हरिः स्थितः.. 42.13 ..
1.4.m:
Viṣṇu was consecrated by me out of a desire to grace the world.
Because Hari himself, dweller in Śvetadvīpa, stayed here,

1.4.s:
vṛddho viśvasya viśvākhyo vāsudevastataḥ smṛtaḥ..
kārtike śuklapakṣe yā bhavatye kādaśī śubhā.. 42.14 ..
1.4.d:
वृद्धो विश्वस्य विश्वाख्यो वासुदेवस्ततः स्मृतः..
कार्तिके शुक्लपक्षे या भवत्ये कादशी शुभा.. 42.14 ..
1.4.m:
he was remembered as ancient, as the universe, named Viśva, and as Vāsudeva.
Whatever auspicious eleventh lunar day occurs in the bright half of Kārtika,

1.4.s:
snānaṃ kṛtvā vidhānena toyaprasravaṇādiṣu..
yorcayedacyutaṃ bhaktyā paṃcopacārapūjayā.. 42.15 ..
1.4.d:
स्नानं कृत्वा विधानेन तोयप्रस्रवणादिषु..
योर्चयेदच्युतं भक्त्या पंचोपचारपूजया.. 42.15 ..
1.4.m:
whoever, having bathed according to the ritual in water-springs and the like,
worships Acyuta with devotion through the fivefold ritual service,

1.4.s:
upoṣya jāgaraṃ kuryādgītavādyaṃ hareḥ puraḥ..
kathāṃ vā vaiṣṇavīṃ kuryāddaṃbhakrodhavivarjitaḥ.. 42.16 ..
1.4.d:
उपोष्य जागरं कुर्याद्गीतवाद्यं हरेः पुरः..
कथां वा वैष्णवीं कुर्याद्दंभक्रोधविवर्जितः.. 42.16 ..
1.4.m:
observing a fast, keeps vigil with singing and instrumental music before Hari,
or recites a Vaiṣṇava narrative, free from deceit and anger,

1.4.s:
dānaṃ dadyādyathāśaktyā niyato hṛṣṭamānasaḥ..
anekabhavasaṃbhūtātkalmaṣādakhilādapi.. 42.17 ..
1.4.d:
दानं दद्याद्यथाशक्त्या नियतो हृष्टमानसः..
अनेकभवसंभूतात्कल्मषादखिलादपि.. 42.17 ..
1.4.m:
and gives gifts according to his ability, restrained and with a joyful mind,
from all impurity arising from many births

1.4.s:
mucyate'sau na saṃdeho yadyapi brahmaghātakaḥ..
gāruḍena vimānena vaikuṃṭhaṃ padamāpnuyāt.. 42.18 ..
1.4.d:
मुच्यतेऽसौ न संदेहो यद्यपि ब्रह्मघातकः..
गारुडेन विमानेन वैकुंठं पदमाप्नुयात्.. 42.18 ..
1.4.m:
he is liberated—there is no doubt—even if he is the slayer of a brahmin;
he attains the abode of Vaikuṇṭha on an aerial chariot of Garuḍa.

1.4.s:
kulānāṃ tārayetpārtha śatamekottaraṃ naraḥ..
śraddhāyuktaṃ mudā yuktaṃ sotsāhaṃ saspṛhaṃ tathā.. 42.19 ..
1.4.d:
कुलानां तारयेत्पार्थ शतमेकोत्तरं नरः..
श्रद्धायुक्तं मुदा युक्तं सोत्साहं सस्पृहं तथा.. 42.19 ..
1.4.m:
A man delivers one hundred and one ancestral lines, O son of Pṛthā.
Endowed with faith, filled with joy, enthusiastic and eager,

1.4.s:
ahaṃkāravihīnaṃ ca snānaṃ dhūpānupanam..
puṣpanaivedyasaṃyuktamarghadānasamanvitam.. 42.20 ..
1.4.d:
अहंकारविहीनं च स्नानं धूपानुपनम्..
पुष्पनैवेद्यसंयुक्तमर्घदानसमन्वितम्.. 42.20 ..
1.4.m:
free from egoism, with bathing, incense, and anointing,
accompanied by flowers and food-offerings, joined with the gift of water of hospitality,

1.4.s:
yāmeyāme mahābhaktyā kṛtārārtikasaṃyutam..
cāmarāhlādasaṃyuktaṃ bherīnādapuraskṛtam.. 42.21 ..
1.4.d:
यामेयामे महाभक्त्या कृतारार्तिकसंयुतम्..
चामराह्लादसंयुक्तं भेरीनादपुरस्कृतम्.. 42.21 ..
1.4.m:
accompanied by the waving of lights performed with great devotion in watch after watch,
joined with the delight of flywhisks, preceded by the sound of kettle-drums,

1.4.s:
purāṇaśrutisaṃpannaṃ bhaktinṛtyasamanvitam..
vinidraṃkṣṛttṛṣāsvādaspṛhāhīnaṃ ca bhārata.. 42.22 ..
1.4.d:
पुराणश्रुतिसंपन्नं भक्तिनृत्यसमन्वितम्..
विनिद्रंक्षृत्तृषास्वादस्पृहाहीनं च भारत.. 42.22 ..
1.4.m:
equipped with the Purāṇas and scriptures, accompanied by devotional dance,
free from sleep, devoid of longing for the taste of food and drink, O Bhārata,

1.4.s:
tatpādasaurabhaghrāṇasaṃyutaṃ viṣṇuvallabham..
sagītaṃ sārcanakaraṃ tatkṣetragamanānvitam.. 42.23 ..
1.4.d:
तत्पादसौरभघ्राणसंयुतं विष्णुवल्लभम्..
सगीतं सार्चनकरं तत्क्षेत्रगमनान्वितम्.. 42.23 ..
1.4.m:
joined with inhaling the fragrance of his feet, dear to Viṣṇu,
with songs, offering worship, accompanied by going to his sacred field,

1.4.s:
pāyurodhena saṃyuktaṃ brahmacaryasamanvitam..
stutipāṭhena saṃyuktaṃ pādodakavibhūṣitam.. 42.24 ..
1.4.d:
पायुरोधेन संयुक्तं ब्रह्मचर्यसमन्वितम्..
स्तुतिपाठेन संयुक्तं पादोदकविभूषितम्.. 42.24 ..
1.4.m:
accompanied by restraint of the lower apertures, endowed with celibacy,
accompanied by the recitation of hymns of praise, adorned with the water of his feet,

1.4.s:
satyānvitaṃ satyayogasaṃyutaṃ puṇyavārtayā..
paṃcaviṃśatibhiryuktaṃ guṇairyo jāgaraṃ naraḥ..
ekādaśyāṃ prakurvīta punarna jāyate bhuvi.. 42.25 ..
1.4.d:
सत्यान्वितं सत्ययोगसंयुतं पुण्यवार्तया..
पंचविंशतिभिर्युक्तं गुणैर्यो जागरं नरः..
एकादश्यां प्रकुर्वीत पुनर्न जायते भुवि.. 42.25 ..
1.4.m:
endowed with truth, joined with the union of truth through holy conversation—
whatever man performs a vigil endowed with these twenty-five virtues
on the eleventh lunar day is not born again on earth.

1.4.s:
atra tīrthavare pūrvamaitareya iti dvijaḥ..
siddhiṃ prāpto mahābhāgo vāsudevaprasādataḥ.. 42.26 ..
1.4.d:
अत्र तीर्थवरे पूर्वमैतरेय इति द्विजः..
सिद्धिं प्राप्तो महाभागो वासुदेवप्रसादतः.. 42.26 ..
1.4.m:
Here at this excellent sacred ford, formerly a twice-born named Aitareya
attained perfection, the highly fortunate one, by the grace of Vāsudeva."

1.4.s:
..arjuna uvāca..
aitareyaḥ kasya putro nivāsaḥ kvāsya vā mune..
kathaṃ siddhimāgāddhīmānvāsudevaprasādataḥ.. 42.27 ..
1.4.d:
..अर्जुन उवाच..
ऐतरेयः कस्य पुत्रो निवासः क्वास्य वा मुने..
कथं सिद्धिमागाद्धीमान्वासुदेवप्रसादतः.. 42.27 ..
1.4.m:
Arjuna said:
"Whose son was Aitareya, or where was his dwelling, O sage?
How did the wise one attain perfection by the grace of Vāsudeva?"

1.4.s:
..nārada uvāca..
asminneva mama sthāne hārītasyānvaye'bhavat.. 42.28 ..
1.4.d:
..नारद उवाच..
अस्मिन्नेव मम स्थाने हारीतस्यान्वयेऽभवत्.. 42.28 ..
1.4.m:
Nārada said:
"Right here in my place, in the lineage of Hārīta,

1.4.s: māṃḍūkiriti viprāgryo vedavedāṃgapāragaḥ.. 42.29 ..
1.4.d: मांडूकिरिति विप्राग्र्यो वेदवेदांगपारगः.. 42.29 ..
1.4.m: there was an eminent brahmin named Māṇḍūki, who had crossed to the further shore of the Vedas and auxiliary sciences.

1.4.s:
tasyāsī ditarā nāma bhāryā sādhvīguṇairyutā..
tasyāmutpadyata sutastvaitareya iti smṛtaḥ.. 42.30 ..
1.4.d:
तस्यासी दितरा नाम भार्या साध्वीगुणैर्युता..
तस्यामुत्पद्यत सुतस्त्वैतरेय इति स्मृतः.. 42.30 ..
1.4.m:
He had a wife named Itarā, virtuous and endowed with good qualities.
To her was born a son, remembered as Aitareya.

1.4.s:
sa ca bālyātprabhṛtyeva prāgjanmanyanuśikṣitam..
jajāpamaṃtraṃ tvaniśaṃ dvādaśākṣarasaṃjñitam.. 42.31 ..
1.4.d:
स च बाल्यात्प्रभृत्येव प्राग्जन्मन्यनुशिक्षितम्..
जजापमंत्रं त्वनिशं द्वादशाक्षरसंज्ञितम्.. 42.31 ..
1.4.m:
From childhood onward, he constantly muttered the mantra known as twelve-syllabled,
which had been learned in a previous birth.

1.4.s:
na śrṛṇoti na vaktyeva manasāpi ca kiṃcana..
evaṃprabhāvaḥ so'bhūcca bālye viprasutastadā.. 42.32 ..
1.4.d:
न श्रृणोति न वक्त्येव मनसापि च किंचन..
एवंप्रभावः सोऽभूच्च बाल्ये विप्रसुतस्तदा.. 42.32 ..
1.4.m:
He did not hear, nor did he speak anything at all, even in his mind.
Such was the nature of that son of a brahmin in his childhood.

1.4.s:
tato mūko'yamityeva nānopāyaiḥ prabodhitaḥ..
pitrā yadā na kurute vyavahārāya mānasam.. 42.33 ..
1.4.d:
ततो मूकोऽयमित्येव नानोपायैः प्रबोधितः..
पित्रा यदा न कुरुते व्यवहाराय मानसम्.. 42.33 ..
1.4.m:
Then, thinking, 'He is mute,' he was urged by his father by various means,
[yet] when he did not turn his mind to worldly affairs,

1.4.s:
tato niścitya manasā jaḍoyamiti bhārata..
anyāṃ vivāhayāmāsa dārānputrāṃstathādadhe.. 42.34 ..
1.4.d:
ततो निश्चित्य मनसा जडोयमिति भारत..
अन्यां विवाहयामास दारान्पुत्रांस्तथादधे.. 42.34 ..
1.4.m:
having determined in his mind, 'He is dull-witted,' O Bhārata,
[the father] married another wife and produced sons.

1.4.s:
piṃgānāma ca sā bhāryā tasyāḥ putrāśca jajñire..
catvāraḥ karmakuśalā vedavedāṃgavādinaḥ.. 42.35 ..
1.4.d:
पिंगानाम च सा भार्या तस्याः पुत्राश्च जज्ञिरे..
चत्वारः कर्मकुशला वेदवेदांगवादिनः.. 42.35 ..
1.4.m:
That wife was named Piṅgā, and sons were born to her,
four of them, skilled in rituals, exponents of the Vedas and auxiliary sciences.

1.4.s:
yajñeṣu śāṃtihomeṣu dvijaiḥ sarvatra pūjitāḥ..
aitareyopi nityaṃ ca trikālaṃ harikaṃdire.. 42.36 ..
1.4.d:
यज्ञेषु शांतिहोमेषु द्विजैः सर्वत्र पूजिताः..
ऐतरेयोपि नित्यं च त्रिकालं हरिकंदिरे.. 42.36 ..
1.4.m:
They were honored everywhere by brahmins at sacrifices and propitiatory oblations.
And Aitareya, too, constantly, at the three junctions of the day, in the temple of Hari,

1.4.s:
jajāpa paramaṃ jāpyaṃ nānyatra kurute śramam..
tato mātā nirīkṣyaiva sapatnītanayāṃstathā.. 42.37 ..
1.4.d:
जजाप परमं जाप्यं नान्यत्र कुरुते श्रमम्..
ततो माता निरीक्ष्यैव सपत्नीतनयांस्तथा.. 42.37 ..
1.4.m:
muttered the supreme prayer; he made no effort elsewhere.
Then his mother, observing the sons of her co-wife,

1.4.s:
dāryamāṇena manasā tanayaṃ vākyamabravīt..
kleśāyaiva ca jāto'si dhigme janma ca jīvitam.. 42.38 ..
1.4.d:
दार्यमाणेन मनसा तनयं वाक्यमब्रवीत्..
क्लेशायैव च जातोऽसि धिग्मे जन्म च जीवितम्.. 42.38 ..
1.4.m:
with a rent heart addressed words to her son:
'You were born only for affliction! Fie upon my birth and life!

1.4.s:
nāryāstasyā nṛloke'tra varaivājananiḥ sphuṭam..
vimānitā yā bhartrāsyānna putraḥ syādguṇairyutaḥ.. 42.39 ..
1.4.d:
नार्यास्तस्या नृलोकेऽत्र वरैवाजननिः स्फुटम्..
विमानिता या भर्त्रास्यान्न पुत्रः स्याद्गुणैर्युतः.. 42.39 ..
1.4.m:
For a woman in this human world, it is clearly better not to give birth at all,
since she is despised by her husband and her son lacks virtues.

1.4.s:
piṃgeyaṃ kṛtapuṇyā vai yasyāḥ putrā mahāguṇāḥ..
vedavedāṃgatattvajñāḥ sarvatrābhyarcitā guṇaiḥ.. 42.40 ..
1.4.d:
पिंगेयं कृतपुण्या वै यस्याः पुत्रा महागुणाः..
वेदवेदांगतत्त्वज्ञाः सर्वत्राभ्यर्चिता गुणैः.. 42.40 ..
1.4.m:
This Piṅgā has indeed performed merit, whose sons possess great virtues,
knowers of the truth of the Vedas and auxiliary sciences, worshipped everywhere for their virtues.

1.4.s:
tadahaṃ putra durbhāgyā mahīsāgarasaṃgame..
nimajjīṣye varaṃ mṛtyurjīvite kiṃ phalaṃ mama..
tvamapyevaṃ mahāmaunī nanda bhakto hareściram.. 42.41 ..
1.4.d:
तदहं पुत्र दुर्भाग्या महीसागरसंगमे..
निमज्जीष्ये वरं मृत्युर्जीविते किं फलं मम..
त्वमप्येवं महामौनी नन्द भक्तो हरेश्चिरम्.. 42.41 ..
1.4.m:
Therefore, unfortunate as I am, O son, at the confluence of the Mahī and the ocean
I shall drown myself; death is better! What fruit is there in my living?
You too, as a great silent one, rejoice long as a devotee of Hari!'

1.4.s:
..nārada uvāca..
iti māturvacaḥ śrutvā prahasannaitareyakaḥ.. 42.42 ..
1.4.d:
..नारद उवाच..
इति मातुर्वचः श्रुत्वा प्रहसन्नैतरेयकः.. 42.42 ..
1.4.m:
Nārada said:
"Hearing these words of his mother, the young Aitareya, smiling,

1.4.s:
dhyātvā muhurtaṃ dharmajño mātaraṃ praṇato'bravīt..
mātarmithyābhibhūtāsi ajñāne jñānavatyasi.. 42.43 ..
1.4.d:
ध्यात्वा मुहुर्तं धर्मज्ञो मातरं प्रणतोऽब्रवीत्..
मातर्मिथ्याभिभूतासि अज्ञाने ज्ञानवत्यसि.. 42.43 ..
1.4.m:
meditated for a moment, and, knower of righteousness, bowed down and said to his mother:
'O mother, you are overcome by delusion; possessed of knowledge, you act in ignorance.

1.4.s:
aśocye śocasi śubhe śocye naivā'pi śocasi..
dehasyāsya kṛte mithyāsaṃsāre kiṃ vimuhyasi.. 42.44 ..
1.4.d:
अशोच्ये शोचसि शुभे शोच्ये नैवाऽपि शोचसि..
देहस्यास्य कृते मिथ्यासंसारे किं विमुह्यसि.. 42.44 ..
1.4.m:
You grieve for what should not be grieved for, O auspicious one, and do not grieve at all for what should be grieved for.
Why are you deluded in the false worldly existence for the sake of this body?

1.4.s:
mūrkhācaritametaddhi manmāturucitaṃ na hi..
anyatsaṃsārasāraṃ ca sāramanyacca mohitāḥ.. 42.45 ..
1.4.d:
मूर्खाचरितमेतद्धि मन्मातुरुचितं न हि..
अन्यत्संसारसारं च सारमन्यच्च मोहिताः.. 42.45 ..
1.4.m:
For this is the conduct of fools; it is not fitting for my mother.
The essence of worldly existence is one thing, but those who are deluded regard something else as the essence,

1.4.s:
prapaśyaṃti yathā rātrau khadyotaṃ dīpavatsthitam..
yadidaṃ manyase sāraṃ śrṛṇu tasyāpyasāratām.. 42.46 ..
1.4.d:
प्रपश्यंति यथा रात्रौ खद्योतं दीपवत्स्थितम्..
यदिदं मन्यसे सारं श्रृणु तस्याप्यसारताम्.. 42.46 ..
1.4.m:
just as at night they behold a firefly staying like a lamp.
What you consider to be the essence—hear its essencelessness!

1.4.s:
evaṃvidhaṃ hi mānu'yamā garbhāditi kaṣṭadam
asthipaṭṭatulāstambhe snāyubandhena yaṃtrite.. 42.47 ..
1.4.d:
एवंविधं हि मानुऽयमा गर्भादिति कष्टदम्
अस्थिपट्टतुलास्तम्भे स्नायुबन्धेन यंत्रिते.. 42.47 ..
1.4.m:
Such is this human [body], bringing pain from the very womb,
with beams and pillars of bone-slabs, bound tight with sinews,

1.4.s:
raktamāṃsamadālipte viṇmūtradravyabhājane..
keśaromatṛṇacchanne suvarṇatvaksudhūtake.. 42.48 ..
1.4.d:
रक्तमांसमदालिप्ते विण्मूत्रद्रव्यभाजने..
केशरोमतृणच्छन्ने सुवर्णत्वक्सुधूतके.. 42.48 ..
1.4.m:
smeared with blood, flesh, and fat, a vessel for feces, urine, and [other] substances,
covered with the grass of head-hair and body-hair, clean-washed with a golden skin.'

1.4.s:
vadanaikamahādvāre ṣaḍgavākṣavitabhūṣite..
oṣṭhadvayakāṭe ca tathā daṃtārgalānvite.. 42.49 ..
1.4.d:
वदनैकमहाद्वारे षड्गवाक्षवितभूषिते..
ओष्ठद्वयकाटे च तथा दंतार्गलान्विते.. 42.49 ..
1.4.m:
with a single great door, the mouth, adorned with six window-slits,
and with the two lips as door-leaves, fitted with a bolt of teeth; 42.49

1.4.s:
nāḍīsvedapravāhe ca kālavaktrānalasthite..
evaṃvidhe gṛhe gehī jīvo nāmāsti śobhane.. 42.50 ..
1.4.d:
नाडीस्वेदप्रवाहे च कालवक्त्रानलस्थिते..
एवंविधे गृहे गेही जीवो नामास्ति शोभने.. 42.50 ..
1.4.m:
with channels flowing with sweat, situated in the fire of the mouth of Time:
in such a house, O fair one, dwells the householder named the individual soul. 42.50

1.4.s:
guṇatrayamayī bhāryā prakṛtistasya tatra ca..
bodhāhaṃkārakāmāśca krodhalobhādayo'pi ca .. 42.51 ..
1.4.d:
गुणत्रयमयी भार्या प्रकृतिस्तस्य तत्र च..
बोधाहंकारकामाश्च क्रोधलोभादयोऽपि च .. 42.51 ..
1.4.m:
And there he has Prakṛti as his wife, composed of the three guṇas;
and intellect, egoism, desires, anger, greed, and the rest 42.51

1.4.s:
apatyānyasya hā kaṣṭamevaṃ mūḍhaḥ pravartate..
tasya yoyo yathā mohastathā taṃ śrṛṇu tattvataḥ.. 42.52 ..
1.4.d:
अपत्यान्यस्य हा कष्टमेवं मूढः प्रवर्तते..
तस्य योयो यथा मोहस्तथा तं श्रृणु तत्त्वतः.. 42.52 ..
1.4.m:
are his offspring. Alas, in sorrow thus the deluded one proceeds!
Hear in truth of his various kinds of delusion, just as each occurs: 42.52

1.4.s:
srotāṃsi yasya satataṃ prasravaṃti gireriva..
kaphamūtrādikānyasya kṛte dehasya muhyati.. 42.53 ..
1.4.d:
स्रोतांसि यस्य सततं प्रस्रवंति गिरेरिव..
कफमूत्रादिकान्यस्य कृते देहस्य मुह्यति.. 42.53 ..
1.4.m:
whose streams constantly flow like those of a mountain—
phlegm, urine, and the like: for the sake of this body, he is bewildered. 42.53

1.4.s:
sarvāśucinidhānasya śarīrasya na vidyate..
śucirekapradeśo'pi viṇmūtrasya dṛteriva.. 42.54 ..
1.4.d:
सर्वाशुचिनिधानस्य शरीरस्य न विद्यते..
शुचिरेकप्रदेशोऽपि विण्मूत्रस्य दृतेरिव.. 42.54 ..
1.4.m:
Of the body, a receptacle of every impurity, there exists
not even a single pure spot, like a leather sack filled with feces and urine. 42.54

1.4.s:
spṛṣṭvā svadehasrotāṃsi mṛttoyaiḥ śodhyate karaḥ..
tathāpyaśucibhāṃḍasya na virajyati kiṃ naraḥ.. 42.55 ..
1.4.d:
स्पृष्ट्वा स्वदेहस्रोतांसि मृत्तोयैः शोध्यते करः..
तथाप्यशुचिभांडस्य न विरज्यति किं नरः.. 42.55 ..
1.4.m:
Having touched the orifices of one's own body, the hand is cleansed with earth and water;
even so, why does a person feel no revulsion toward that vessel of impurity? 42.55

1.4.s:
kāyaḥ sugandhatoyādyairyatnenāpi susaṃskṛtaḥ..
na jahāti svakaṃ bhāvaṃ śvapucchamiva nāmitam.. 42.56 ..
1.4.d:
कायः सुगन्धतोयाद्यैर्यत्नेनापि सुसंस्कृतः..
न जहाति स्वकं भावं श्वपुच्छमिव नामितम्.. 42.56 ..
1.4.m:
Though carefully adorned with fragrant waters and the like, the body
does not abandon its innate nature, just like a dog's bent tail [when straightened]. 42.56

1.4.s:
svadehāśucigaṃdhena na virajyati yo naraḥ..
virāge kāraṇaṃ tasya kimanyadu padiśyate.. 42.57 ..
1.4.d:
स्वदेहाशुचिगंधेन न विरज्यति यो नरः..
विरागे कारणं तस्य किमन्यदु पदिश्यते.. 42.57 ..
1.4.m:
A person who is not revolted by the foul stench of his own body—
what other cause for detachment can be taught to him? 42.57

1.4.s:
gandhalepāpanodārthaṃ śaucaṃ dehasya kīrtitam..
dvayasyāpagamātpaścādbhāvaśuddhyā viśudhyati.. 42.58 ..
1.4.d:
गन्धलेपापनोदार्थं शौचं देहस्य कीर्तितम्..
द्वयस्यापगमात्पश्चाद्भावशुद्ध्या विशुध्यति.. 42.58 ..
1.4.m:
Bodily purification is taught for the removal of odor and smearing;
after the removal of the two, one is purified by purity of inner disposition. 42.58

1.4.s:
gaṃgātoyena sarveṇa mṛdbhāraiḥ parvatopamaiḥ..
ā mṛtyorācarañchaucaṃ bhāvaduṣṭo na śudhyati.. 42.59 ..
1.4.d:
गंगातोयेन सर्वेण मृद्भारैः पर्वतोपमैः..
आ मृत्योराचरञ्छौचं भावदुष्टो न शुध्यति.. 42.59 ..
1.4.m:
Practicing purification until death with all the water of the Gaṅgā
and mountain-like loads of earth, one of corrupt disposition is not purified. 42.59

1.4.s:
tīrthasnānaistapobhirvā duṣṭātmā naiva śudhyati..
sveditaḥ kṣālitastīrthe kiṃ śuddhimadhigacchati.. 42.60 ..
1.4.d:
तीर्थस्नानैस्तपोभिर्वा दुष्टात्मा नैव शुध्यति..
स्वेदितः क्षालितस्तीर्थे किं शुद्धिमधिगच्छति.. 42.60 ..
1.4.m:
A corrupt soul is never purified by baths at sacred fords or by austerities;
can [a jar of liquor], steamed and washed at a sacred ford, attain purity? 42.60

1.4.s:
aṃtarbhāvapraduṣṭasya viśato'pi hutāśanam..
na svargo nāpapargaśca dehanirdahanaṃ param.. 42.61 ..
1.4.d:
अंतर्भावप्रदुष्टस्य विशतोऽपि हुताशनम्..
न स्वर्गो नापपर्गश्च देहनिर्दहनं परम्.. 42.61 ..
1.4.m:
For one who is corrupted in inner disposition, even if he enters the fire,
there is neither heaven nor liberation, but merely the incineration of the body. 42.61

1.4.s:
bhāvaśuddhiḥ paraṃ śaucaṃ pramāṇaṃ sarvakarmasu..
anyathāliṃgyate kāṃtā bhāvena duhitā'nyathā.. 42.62 ..
1.4.d:
भावशुद्धिः परं शौचं प्रमाणं सर्वकर्मसु..
अन्यथालिंग्यते कांता भावेन दुहिताऽन्यथा.. 42.62 ..
1.4.m:
Purity of inner disposition is the highest purity, the authority in all actions:
in one spirit a wife is embraced, in another spirit a daughter. 42.62

1.4.s:
anyathaiva stanaṃ putraściṃtayatyanyathā patiḥ..
cittaṃ viśodhayettasmātkimanyairbāhyaśodhanaiḥ.. 42.63 ..
1.4.d:
अन्यथैव स्तनं पुत्रश्चिंतयत्यन्यथा पतिः..
चित्तं विशोधयेत्तस्मात्किमन्यैर्बाह्यशोधनैः.. 42.63 ..
1.4.m:
In one way indeed a son regards the breast, in another way the husband.
Therefore, one should purify the mind; what use are other, external purifications? 42.63

1.4.s:
bhāvataḥ saṃviśuddhātmā svargaṃ mokṣaṃ ca viṃdati..
jñānāmalāṃbhasā puṃsaḥ sadvairāgyamṛdā punaḥ.. 42.64 ..
1.4.d:
भावतः संविशुद्धात्मा स्वर्गं मोक्षं च विंदति..
ज्ञानामलांभसा पुंसः सद्वैराग्यमृदा पुनः.. 42.64 ..
1.4.m:
A person completely purified in inner disposition attains heaven and liberation
by the stainless water of knowledge, and again by the earth of true detachment, 42.64

1.4.s:
avidyārāgaviṇmūtralepagaṃdhaviśodhanam..
evametaccharīraṃ hi nisargādaśuci viduḥ.. 42.65 ..
1.4.d:
अविद्यारागविण्मूत्रलेपगंधविशोधनम्..
एवमेतच्छरीरं हि निसर्गादशुचि विदुः.. 42.65 ..
1.4.m:
washing away the smear and stench of ignorance, passion, feces, and urine.
Thus the wise know this body to be impure by its very nature, 42.65

1.4.s:
tvaṅmātrasāraniḥsāraṃ kadalīsārasaṃnibham..
jñātvaivaṃ doṣavaddehaṃ yaḥ prājñaḥ śithilībhavet.. 42.66 ..
1.4.d:
त्वङ्मात्रसारनिःसारं कदलीसारसंनिभम्..
ज्ञात्वैवं दोषवद्देहं यः प्राज्ञः शिथिलीभवेत्.. 42.66 ..
1.4.m:
having only skin for essence, devoid of core, like the core of a plantain tree.
Knowing the body to be full of faults in this way, the wise man who becomes detached 42.66

1.4.s:
sa niṣkrāmati saṃsāre dṛḍhagrāhī sa tiṣṭhati..
evametanmahākaṣṭaṃ janma duḥkhaṃ prakīrtitam.. 42.67 ..
1.4.d:
स निष्क्रामति संसारे दृढग्राही स तिष्ठति..
एवमेतन्महाकष्टं जन्म दुःखं प्रकीर्तितम्.. 42.67 ..
1.4.m:
departs from saṃsāra, [while] one who clings firmly remains.
Thus this birth has been proclaimed as a great affliction and suffering. 42.67

1.4.s:
puṃsāmajñātadoṣeṇa nānākarmavaśena ca..
yathā girivarākrāṃtaḥ kaścidduḥkhena tiṣṭhati.. 42.68 ..
1.4.d:
पुंसामज्ञातदोषेण नानाकर्मवशेन च..
यथा गिरिवराक्रांतः कश्चिद्दुःखेन तिष्ठति.. 42.68 ..
1.4.m:
Due to human beings not knowing the defect and under the power of various deeds,
just as someone crushed by a great mountain lies in suffering, 42.68

1.4.s:
yathā jarāyuṇā dehī duḥkhaṃ tiṣṭhati veṣṭitaḥ..
patitaḥ sāgare yadvaddṛḥkhamāste samākulaḥ.. 42.69 ..
1.4.d:
यथा जरायुणा देही दुःखं तिष्ठति वेष्टितः..
पतितः सागरे यद्वद्दृःखमास्ते समाकुलः.. 42.69 ..
1.4.m:
so the embodied soul lies in pain, enveloped by the membrane of the womb;
just as one fallen into the ocean remains distressed and agitated, 42.69

1.4.s:
garbhodakena siktāṃgastathā''ste vyākulaḥ pumān..
lohakumbhe yathānyasta pacyate kaścidagninā.. 42.70 ..
1.4.d:
गर्भोदकेन सिक्तांगस्तथा'ऽस्ते व्याकुलः पुमान्..
लोहकुम्भे यथान्यस्त पच्यते कश्चिदग्निना.. 42.70 ..
1.4.m:
so the person lies agitated, his limbs drenched with the fluid of the womb;
just as someone placed in an iron vessel is cooked by fire, 42.70

1.4.s:
garbhakumbhe tathā kṣiptaḥ pacyate jaṭharāgninā..
sūcībhiragnivarṇābhirvibhinnasya nirantaram.. 42.71 ..
1.4.d:
गर्भकुम्भे तथा क्षिप्तः पच्यते जठराग्निना..
सूचीभिरग्निवर्णाभिर्विभिन्नस्य निरन्तरम्.. 42.71 ..
1.4.m:
so cast into the pot of the womb, he is cooked by the digestive fire.
Of one constantly pierced by needles of fire, 42.71

1.4.s:
yadduḥkhaṃ jāyate tasya tadgarbhe'ṣṭaguṇaṃ bhavet..
ityetadgarbhaduḥkhaṃ hi prāṇināṃ parikīrtitam.. 42.72 ..
1.4.d:
यद्दुःखं जायते तस्य तद्गर्भेऽष्टगुणं भवेत्..
इत्येतद्गर्भदुःखं हि प्राणिनां परिकीर्तितम्.. 42.72 ..
1.4.m:
the suffering that arises is eight times greater than that in the womb.
Such is proclaimed to be the suffering in the womb for living beings, 42.72

1.4.s:
carasthirāṇāṃ sarveṣāmātmagarbhānurūpataḥ..
tatrasthasya ca sarveṣāṃ janmanāṃ smaraṇaṃ bhavet.. 42.73 ..
1.4.d:
चरस्थिराणां सर्वेषामात्मगर्भानुरूपतः..
तत्रस्थस्य च सर्वेषां जन्मनां स्मरणं भवेत्.. 42.73 ..
1.4.m:
both moving and unmoving, according to their own wombs.
And to one situated there comes remembrance of all his births: 42.73

1.4.s:
mṛtaścāhaṃ punarjāto jātaścāhaṃ punarmṛtaḥ..
nānāyonisahasrāṇi mayā dṛṣṭānvanekadhā.. 42.74 ..
1.4.d:
मृतश्चाहं पुनर्जातो जातश्चाहं पुनर्मृतः..
नानायोनिसहस्राणि मया दृष्टान्वनेकधा.. 42.74 ..
1.4.m:
“I have died and been born again, and born I have died again;
many thousands of wombs of various kinds have been seen by me in many ways. 42.74

1.4.s:
adhunā jātamātro'haṃ prāptasaṃskāra eva ca..
tataḥ śreyaḥ kariṣyāmi yena garbho na saṃbhavet.. 42.75 ..
1.4.d:
अधुना जातमात्रोऽहं प्राप्तसंस्कार एव च..
ततः श्रेयः करिष्यामि येन गर्भो न संभवेत्.. 42.75 ..
1.4.m:
Now, as soon as I am born and have received my rites of passage,
I shall pursue the highest good so that conception in a womb does not occur again. 42.75

1.4.s:
adhyeṣyāmi harerjñānaṃ saṃsāravinivartanam..
evaṃ saṃciṃtayannāste mokṣopāyaṃ vicintayan.. 42.76 ..
1.4.d:
अध्येष्यामि हरेर्ज्ञानं संसारविनिवर्तनम्..
एवं संचिंतयन्नास्ते मोक्षोपायं विचिन्तयन्.. 42.76 ..
1.4.m:
I will study the knowledge of Hari, which brings an end to saṃsāra.”
Reflecting thus, he dwells pondering the means of liberation. 42.76

1.4.s:
gabhātkoṭiguṇaṃ duḥkhaṃ jāyamānasya jāyate..
garbhavāse smṛtiryāsītsā jātasya praṇaśyati.. 42.77 ..
1.4.d:
गभात्कोटिगुणं दुःखं जायमानस्य जायते..
गर्भवासे स्मृतिर्यासीत्सा जातस्य प्रणश्यति.. 42.77 ..
1.4.m:
A suffering ten million times greater than that of the womb arises for one being born.
Whatever memory he had while dwelling in the womb perishes once he is born. 42.77

1.4.s:
spṛṣṭamātrasya bāhyena vāyunā mūḍhatā bhavet..
saṃmūḍhasya smṛtibhraṃśaḥ śīghraṃ saṃjāyate punaḥ.. 42.78 ..
1.4.d:
स्पृष्टमात्रस्य बाह्येन वायुना मूढता भवेत्..
संमूढस्य स्मृतिभ्रंशः शीघ्रं संजायते पुनः.. 42.78 ..
1.4.m:
The moment he is touched by the external wind, stupefaction occurs;
for the stupefied one, loss of memory swiftly arises again. 42.78

1.4.s:
smṛtibhraṃśāttatastasya pūrvakarmavaśena ca..
ratiḥ saṃjāyate tūrṇaṃ jaṃtostatraiva janmani.. 42.79 ..
1.4.d:
स्मृतिभ्रंशात्ततस्तस्य पूर्वकर्मवशेन च..
रतिः संजायते तूर्णं जंतोस्तत्रैव जन्मनि.. 42.79 ..
1.4.m:
From that loss of memory, and under the influence of past deeds,
attachment quickly arises for the creature in that very birth. 42.79

1.4.s:
rakto mūḍhaśca lokoyamakārye saṃpravartate..
tatrātmānaṃ na jānāti na paraṃ na ca daivatam.. 42.80 ..
1.4.d:
रक्तो मूढश्च लोकोयमकार्ये संप्रवर्तते..
तत्रात्मानं न जानाति न परं न च दैवतम्.. 42.80 ..
1.4.m:
Attached and deluded, this person engages in what ought not to be done;
there he knows neither himself, nor the supreme, nor the divine. 42.80

1.4.s:
na śrṛṇoti paraṃ śreyaḥ sati cakṣuṣi nekṣate..
same pathi samairgacchanskhalatīva padepade.. 42.81 ..
1.4.d:
न श्रृणोति परं श्रेयः सति चक्षुषि नेक्षते..
समे पथि समैर्गच्छन्स्खलतीव पदेपदे.. 42.81 ..
1.4.m:
He does not listen to the highest good; though having eyes, he does not see;
walking on a level path with level feet, he stumbles, as it were, at every step. 42.81

1.4.s:
satyāṃ buddhau na jānāti bodhyamāno budhairapi..
saṃsāre kliśyate tena rāgamohavaśānugaḥ.. 42.82 ..
1.4.d:
सत्यां बुद्धौ न जानाति बोध्यमानो बुधैरपि..
संसारे क्लिश्यते तेन रागमोहवशानुगः.. 42.82 ..
1.4.m:
Though possessing intellect, he does not understand even when instructed by the wise;
thereby he suffers in saṃsāra, subject to passion and delusion. 42.82

1.4.s:
garbhasmṛterabhāvena śāstramuktaṃ maharṣibhiḥ..
taddṛḥkhakathanārthāya svargamokṣaprasādhakam.. 42.83 ..
1.4.d:
गर्भस्मृतेरभावेन शास्त्रमुक्तं महर्षिभिः..
तद्दृःखकथनार्थाय स्वर्गमोक्षप्रसाधकम्.. 42.83 ..
1.4.m:
Due to the absence of the memory of the womb, scripture has been declared by the great seers
in order to explain that suffering, accomplishing heaven and liberation. 42.83

1.4.s:
ye śāstrajñāne satyasminsarvakarmārthasādhake..
na kurvaṃtyātmanaḥ śreyastadatra paramadbhutam.. 42.84 ..
1.4.d:
ये शास्त्रज्ञाने सत्यस्मिन्सर्वकर्मार्थसाधके..
न कुर्वंत्यात्मनः श्रेयस्तदत्र परमद्भुतम्.. 42.84 ..
1.4.m:
Those who, although this knowledge of scripture exists which accomplishes the purpose of all deeds,
do not pursue their own highest good—that is the greatest wonder here! 42.84

1.4.s:
avyaktendriyavṛttitvādbālye duḥkhaṃ mahatpunaḥ..
icchannapi na śaknoti vaktuṃ kartuṃ ca kiñcana.. 42.85 ..
1.4.d:
अव्यक्तेन्द्रियवृत्तित्वाद्बाल्ये दुःखं महत्पुनः..
इच्छन्नपि न शक्नोति वक्तुं कर्तुं च किञ्चन.. 42.85 ..
1.4.m:
Furthermore, in childhood there is great suffering because the functions of the sense-organs are unmanifest:
even though wishing, he is unable to say or do anything. 42.85

1.4.s:
daṃtotthāne mahadduḥkhaṃ maulena vyādhinā tathā..
bālarogaiśca vividhaiḥ pīḍā bālagrahairapi.. 42.86 ..
1.4.d:
दंतोत्थाने महद्दुःखं मौलेन व्याधिना तथा..
बालरोगैश्च विविधैः पीडा बालग्रहैरपि.. 42.86 ..
1.4.m:
There is great pain at the emergence of teeth, as well as from constitutional illness,
and affliction through diverse childhood diseases and spirits seizing children. 42.86

1.4.s:
tṛḍbubhukṣāparītāṃgaḥ kvacittiṣṭhati rāraṭan..
viṇmūtrabhakṣaṇādyaṃ ca mohādbālaḥ samācaret.. 42.87 ..
1.4.d:
तृड्बुभुक्षापरीतांगः क्वचित्तिष्ठति रारटन्..
विण्मूत्रभक्षणाद्यं च मोहाद्बालः समाचरेत्.. 42.87 ..
1.4.m:
With limbs overcome by thirst and hunger, he lies crying somewhere;
and out of delusion the child engages in consuming feces and urine and the like. 42.87

1.4.s:
kaumāre karṇavedhena mātāpitrorvitāḍanaiḥ..
akṣarādhyayanādyaiśca duḥkhaṃ syādguruśāsanāt.. 42.88 ..
1.4.d:
कौमारे कर्णवेधेन मातापित्रोर्विताडनैः..
अक्षराध्ययनाद्यैश्च दुःखं स्याद्गुरुशासनात्.. 42.88 ..
1.4.m:
In boyhood, through the piercing of the ears, through beatings by father and mother,
and through the study of letters and so forth under the teacher's discipline, there is sorrow. 42.88

1.4.s:
pramatteṃdriyavṛttaiśca kāmarāgaprapīḍanāt..
rāgodvṛttasya satataṃ kutaḥ saukhyaṃ hi yauvane.. 42.89 ..
1.4.d:
प्रमत्तेंद्रियवृत्तैश्च कामरागप्रपीडनात्..
रागोद्वृत्तस्य सततं कुतः सौख्यं हि यौवने.. 42.89 ..
1.4.m:
And through reckless behavior of the sense-organs, tormented by passion and lust,
whence can there ever be happiness in youth for one overflowing with passion? 42.89

1.4.s:
īrṣyayā sumahadduḥkhaṃ mohādraktasya jāyate..
mattasya kupitasyaiva rāgo doṣāya kevalam.. 42.90 ..
1.4.d:
ईर्ष्यया सुमहद्दुःखं मोहाद्रक्तस्य जायते..
मत्तस्य कुपितस्यैव रागो दोषाय केवलम्.. 42.90 ..
1.4.m:
Immense suffering arises through jealousy for one who is attached out of delusion;
for one intoxicated and enraged, passion leads solely to fault. 42.90

1.4.s:
na rātrau viṃdate nidrā kāmāgniparikheditaḥ..
divāpi hi kutaḥ saukhyamarthopārjanaciṃtayā.. 42.91 ..
1.4.d:
न रात्रौ विंदते निद्रा कामाग्निपरिखेदितः..
दिवापि हि कुतः सौख्यमर्थोपार्जनचिंतया.. 42.91 ..
1.4.m:
Exhausted by the fire of desire, sleep does not come at night;
and by day, whence could there be happiness, with anxiety over the acquisition of wealth? 42.91

1.4.s:
nārīṣu tvanubhūtāsu sarvadoṣāśrayāsu ca..
viṇmutrotsargasadṛśaṃ saukhyaṃ maithunajaṃ smṛtam.. 42.92 ..
1.4.d:
नारीषु त्वनुभूतासु सर्वदोषाश्रयासु च..
विण्मुत्रोत्सर्गसदृशं सौख्यं मैथुनजं स्मृतम्.. 42.92 ..
1.4.m:
When women, who are the receptacle of all faults, are enjoyed,
the pleasure born of sexual intercourse is considered like the discharge of feces and urine. 42.92

1.4.s:
sanmānamapamānena viyogeneṣṭasaṃgamaḥ..
yauvanaṃ jarayā grastaṃ kva saukhyamanupadravam.. 42.93 ..
1.4.d:
सन्मानमपमानेन वियोगेनेष्टसंगमः..
यौवनं जरया ग्रस्तं क्व सौख्यमनुपद्रवम्.. 42.93 ..
1.4.m: Honor is [overtaken] by insult; union with the beloved, by separation; / youth, swallowed by old age. Where is unmolested happiness?

1.4.s:
valīpalitakāyena śithilīkṛtavigrahaḥ..
sarvakriyāsvaśaktaśca jarayājarjjarīkṛtaḥ.. 42.94 ..
1.4.d:
वलीपलितकायेन शिथिलीकृतविग्रहः..
सर्वक्रियास्वशक्तश्च जरयाजर्ज्जरीकृतः.. 42.94 ..
1.4.m: With a body of wrinkles and grey hair, his frame rendered slack, / powerless in all activities, he is shattered by old age.

1.4.s:
strīpuṃsoryauvanaṃ rūpaṃ yadanyonyāśrayaṃ purā..
tadevaṃ jarayā grastamubhayorapi na priyam.. 42.95 ..
1.4.d:
स्त्रीपुंसोर्यौवनं रूपं यदन्योन्याश्रयं पुरा..
तदेवं जरया ग्रस्तमुभयोरपि न प्रियम्.. 42.95 ..
1.4.m: The youthful form of woman and man, which previously depended on each other— / that very form, swallowed by old age, is pleasing to neither of them.

1.4.s:
jarābhibhūtaḥpuruṣaḥ patnīputrādibāṃdhavaiḥ..
aśaktatvāddurācārairbhṛtyaiśca paribhūyate.. 42.96 ..
1.4.d:
जराभिभूतःपुरुषः पत्नीपुत्रादिबांधवैः..
अशक्तत्वाद्दुराचारैर्भृत्यैश्च परिभूयते.. 42.96 ..
1.4.m: Overcome by old age, a man is treated with contempt by his wife, sons, and other kinsmen, / and because of his helplessness, even by wicked servants.

1.4.s:
dharmamarthaṃ ca kāmaṃ ca mokṣaṃ ca nāturo yataḥ..
śaktaḥ sādhayituṃ tasmādyuvā dharmaṃ samācaret.. 42.97 ..
1.4.d:
धर्ममर्थं च कामं च मोक्षं च नातुरो यतः..
शक्तः साधयितुं तस्माद्युवा धर्मं समाचरेत्.. 42.97 ..
1.4.m: Since a sick man is unable to achieve / virtue, wealth, desire, and liberation, therefore while young one should practice virtue.

1.4.s:
vātapittakaphādīnāṃ vaiṣamyaṃ vyādhirucyate..
vātādīnāṃ samūhaśca deho'yaṃ parikīrtitaḥ.. 42.98 ..
1.4.d:
वातपित्तकफादीनां वैषम्यं व्याधिरुच्यते..
वातादीनां समूहश्च देहोऽयं परिकीर्तितः.. 42.98 ..
1.4.m: The imbalance of wind, bile, phlegm, and the rest is called disease; / and this body is declared to be an aggregate of wind and the other [humors].

1.4.s:
tasmādvyādhimayaṃ jñeyaṃ śarīramidamātmanaḥ..
rogairnānāvidhairyāṃti dehe duḥkhānyanekaśaḥ.. 42.99 ..
1.4.d:
तस्माद्व्याधिमयं ज्ञेयं शरीरमिदमात्मनः..
रोगैर्नानाविधैर्यांति देहे दुःखान्यनेकशः.. 42.99 ..
