1.4.m: Therefore, this physical frame of one's own should be known as full of disease; / through diverse sicknesses, manifold sorrows enter the body.

1.4.s:
tāni na svātmavedyāni kimanyatkathayāmyaham..
ekottaraṃ mṛtyuśatamasmindehe pratiṣṭhitam.. 42.100 ..
1.4.d:
तानि न स्वात्मवेद्यानि किमन्यत्कथयाम्यहम्..
एकोत्तरं मृत्युशतमस्मिन्देहे प्रतिष्ठितम्.. 42.100 ..
1.4.m: They are beyond one's own perception—what else can I say? / One hundred and one deaths are established in this body.

1.4.s:
tatraikaḥ kālasaṃyuktaḥ śeṣāstvāgaṃtavaḥ smṛtāḥ..
ye tvihāgaṃtavaḥ proktāste praśāmyanti bheṣajaiḥ.. 42.101 ..
1.4.d:
तत्रैकः कालसंयुक्तः शेषास्त्वागंतवः स्मृताः..
ये त्विहागंतवः प्रोक्तास्ते प्रशाम्यन्ति भेषजैः.. 42.101 ..
1.4.m: Among them, one is linked to time; the remainder are considered accidental. / Those that are declared accidental here are alleviated by medicines,

1.4.s:
japahomapradānaiśca kālamṛtyurna śāmyati..
vividhā vyādhayaḥ śastāḥ sarpādyāḥ prāṇinastathā.. 42.102 ..
1.4.d:
जपहोमप्रदानैश्च कालमृत्युर्न शाम्यति..
विविधा व्याधयः शस्ताः सर्पाद्याः प्राणिनस्तथा.. 42.102 ..
1.4.m: and by muttering prayers, oblations, and gifts; but timely death is not alleviated. / Diverse illnesses, weapons, living beings such as snakes,

1.4.s:
viṣāṇi cābhicārāśca mṛtyordvārāṇi dehinām..
pīḍitaṃ sarparogādyairapi dhanvaṃtariḥ svayam.. 42.103 ..
1.4.d:
विषाणि चाभिचाराश्च मृत्योर्द्वाराणि देहिनाम्..
पीडितं सर्परोगाद्यैरपि धन्वंतरिः स्वयम्.. 42.103 ..
1.4.m: poisons, and sorceries are the doors of death for embodied beings. / Even Dhanvantari himself cannot restore to health

1.4.s:
svasthīkartuṃ na śaknoti kālaprāptaṃ hi dehinam..
naiṣadhaṃ na tapo maṃtrā na mitrāṇi na bāṃdhavāḥ.. 42.104 ..
1.4.d:
स्वस्थीकर्तुं न शक्नोति कालप्राप्तं हि देहिनम्..
नैषधं न तपो मंत्रा न मित्राणि न बांधवाः.. 42.104 ..
1.4.m: an embodied being who is afflicted by snakebites, illnesses, and the like, when his time has arrived. / Neither remedy nor austerity, mantras, friends, nor relatives

1.4.s:
śaknuvaṃti paritrātuṃ naraṃ kālena pīḍitam..
rasāyanatapojapyairyogasiddhairmahātmabhiḥ.. 42.105 ..
1.4.d:
शक्नुवंति परित्रातुं नरं कालेन पीडितम्..
रसायनतपोजप्यैर्योगसिद्धैर्महात्मभिः.. 42.105 ..
1.4.m: are able to rescue a man afflicted by Time. / By elixirs, austerities, prayers, by great souls perfected in yoga,

1.4.s:
kālamṛtyurapi prājñairnīyate nāpi saṃyutaiḥ..
nāsti mṛtyusamaṃ duḥkhaṃ nāsti mṛtyusamaṃ bhayam.. 42.106 ..
1.4.d:
कालमृत्युरपि प्राज्ञैर्नीयते नापि संयुतैः..
नास्ति मृत्युसमं दुःखं नास्ति मृत्युसमं भयम्.. 42.106 ..
1.4.m: or by the wise, timely death cannot be warded off, even when conjoined [with these]. / There is no sorrow equal to death; there is no fear equal to death;

1.4.s:
nāsti mṛtyusamasrāsaḥ sarveṣāmapi dehinām..
sadbhāryāputramitrāṇi rājyaiśvaryasukhāni ca.. 42.107 ..
1.4.d:
नास्ति मृत्युसमस्रासः सर्वेषामपि देहिनाम्..
सद्भार्यापुत्रमित्राणि राज्यैश्वर्यसुखानि च.. 42.107 ..
1.4.m: there is no terror equal to death for all embodied beings. / A virtuous wife, sons, friends, kingdom, sovereignty, and pleasures—

1.4.s:
ābaddhāni snehapāśairmṛtyuḥ sarvāṇi kṛṃtati..
kiṃ na paśyasi mātastvaṃ sahasrasyāpi madhyataḥ.. 42.108 ..
1.4.d:
आबद्धानि स्नेहपाशैर्मृत्युः सर्वाणि कृंतति..
किं न पश्यसि मातस्त्वं सहस्रस्यापि मध्यतः.. 42.108 ..
1.4.m: all bound by the cords of affection, death cuts them down. / Mother, do you not see that even out of a thousand,

1.4.s:
janāḥ śatāyuṣaḥ paṃcabhavaṃti na bhavanti vā..
aśītikā vipadyante kecitsaptatikā narāḥ.. 42.109 ..
1.4.d:
जनाः शतायुषः पंचभवंति न भवन्ति वा..
अशीतिका विपद्यन्ते केचित्सप्ततिका नराः.. 42.109 ..
1.4.m: scarcely five persons live a hundred years, or perhaps none do? / Some perish at eighty, others at seventy.

1.4.s:
paramāyuḥ sthitā ṣaṣṭistadapyasti na niṣṭhitam..
tasya yāvadbhavedāyurdehinaḥ pūrvakarma bhiḥ.. 42.110 ..
1.4.d:
परमायुः स्थिता षष्टिस्तदप्यस्ति न निष्ठितम्..
तस्य यावद्भवेदायुर्देहिनः पूर्वकर्म भिः.. 42.110 ..
1.4.m: The upper limit of lifespan has settled at sixty, and even that is not certain. / Whatever lifespan an embodied being may have due to past actions,

1.4.s:
tasyārdhamāyuṣo rātrirharate mṛtyurūpiṇī..
bālabhāvena mohena vārdhake jarayā tathā.. 42.111 ..
1.4.d:
तस्यार्धमायुषो रात्रिर्हरते मृत्युरूपिणी..
बालभावेन मोहेन वार्धके जरया तथा.. 42.111 ..
1.4.m: the night, in the form of death, steals half of that life. / Through the state of childhood, through infatuation, and through old age in decrepitude,

1.4.s:
varṣāṇāṃ viṃśatiryāti dharmakāmārthavarjitaḥ..
āgantukairbhavaiḥ puṃsāṃ vyādhiśokairanekadhā.. 42.112 ..
1.4.d:
वर्षाणां विंशतिर्याति धर्मकामार्थवर्जितः..
आगन्तुकैर्भवैः पुंसां व्याधिशोकैरनेकधा.. 42.112 ..
1.4.m: twenty years pass devoid of virtue, pleasure, and wealth. / Due to incidental conditions of men, through sickness and grief in many forms,

1.4.s:
hriyaterddhaṃ hi tatrāpi yaccheṣaṃ taddhi jīvitam..
jīvitāṃteca maraṇaṃ mahāghoramavāpnuyāt.. 42.113 ..
1.4.d:
ह्रियतेर्द्धं हि तत्रापि यच्छेषं तद्धि जीवितम्..
जीवितांतेच मरणं महाघोरमवाप्नुयात्.. 42.113 ..
1.4.m: half of what remains there is also stolen away; that [small fraction] is indeed life. / And at the end of life one meets a most dreadful death.

1.4.s:
jāyate yonikoṭīṣu mṛtaḥ karmavaśātpunaḥ..
dehabhedena yaḥ puṃsāṃ viyogaḥ karmasaṃkhyayā.. 42.114 ..
1.4.d:
जायते योनिकोटीषु मृतः कर्मवशात्पुनः..
देहभेदेन यः पुंसां वियोगः कर्मसंख्यया.. 42.114 ..
1.4.m: Having died, one is born again in ten million wombs under the power of karma. / The separation of men through the dissolution of the body due to the exhaustion of karma—

1.4.s:
maraṇaṃ tadvinirddiṣṭaṃ na nāśaḥ paramārthataḥ..
mahātamaḥpraviṣṭasya cchidyamāneṣu marmasu.. 42.115 ..
1.4.d:
मरणं तद्विनिर्द्दिष्टं न नाशः परमार्थतः..
महातमःप्रविष्टस्य च्छिद्यमानेषु मर्मसु.. 42.115 ..
1.4.m: that is designated as death, not an absolute destruction. / When one has entered great darkness and the vital spots are being severed,

1.4.s:
yadduḥkhaṃ maraṇaṃ jaṃtorna tasyehopamā kvacit..
hā tāta mātarhā kāṃte kraṃdatyevaṃ suduḥkhitaḥ.. 42.116 ..
1.4.d:
यद्दुःखं मरणं जंतोर्न तस्येहोपमा क्वचित्..
हा तात मातर्हा कांते क्रंदत्येवं सुदुःखितः.. 42.116 ..
1.4.m: the agony of death to a creature has no comparison anywhere in this world. / 'Alas, father! Mother! Alas, beloved!' he cries out thus, in deep sorrow.

1.4.s:
maṇḍūka iva sarpeṇa gīryate mṛtyunā janaḥ..
bāṃdhavaiḥ saṃparityaktaḥ priyaiśca parivāritaḥ.. 42.117 ..
1.4.d:
मण्डूक इव सर्पेण गीर्यते मृत्युना जनः..
बांधवैः संपरित्यक्तः प्रियैश्च परिवारितः.. 42.117 ..
1.4.m: Like a frog by a serpent, a person is swallowed by death. / Abandoned by kinsmen, yet surrounded by loved ones,

1.4.s:
niḥśvasandīrghamuṣṇaṃ ca mukena pariśuṣyatā..
caturaṃteṣu khaṭvāyāḥ parivartanmuhurmuhuḥ.. 42.118 ..
1.4.d:
निःश्वसन्दीर्घमुष्णं च मुकेन परिशुष्यता..
चतुरंतेषु खट्वायाः परिवर्तन्मुहुर्मुहुः.. 42.118 ..
1.4.m: breathing out long and hot breaths, dumb with a drying mouth, / turning repeatedly across the four corners of the bed,

1.4.s:
saṃmūḍhaḥ kṣipatetyarthaṃ hastapādāvitastataḥ..
khaṭvāto vāṃchate bhūmiṃ bhūmeḥ khaṭvāṃ punarmahīm.. 42.119 ..
1.4.d:
संमूढः क्षिपतेत्यर्थं हस्तपादावितस्ततः..
खट्वातो वांछते भूमिं भूमेः खट्वां पुनर्महीम्.. 42.119 ..
1.4.m: utterly bewildered, he tosses his hands and feet here and there; / from the bed he craves the floor, and from the floor the bed, then the ground again.

1.4.s:
vivastro muktalajjaśca viṣṭhānulepitaḥ..
yācamānaśca salilaṃ śuṣkakaṇṭhoṣṭhatālukaḥ.. 42.120 ..
1.4.d:
विवस्त्रो मुक्तलज्जश्च विष्ठानुलेपितः..
याचमानश्च सलिलं शुष्ककण्ठोष्ठतालुकः.. 42.120 ..
1.4.m: Naked, devoid of shame, smeared with feces, / begging for water with throat, lips, and palate dried up,

1.4.s:
ciṃtayānaḥ svavittāni kasyaitāni mṛte mayi..
paṃcāvaṭānkhanamānaḥ kālapāśena karṣitaḥ.. 42.121 ..
1.4.d:
चिंतयानः स्ववित्तानि कस्यैतानि मृते मयि..
पंचावटान्खनमानः कालपाशेन कर्षितः.. 42.121 ..
1.4.m: worrying about his possessions: 'To whom will these belong when I am dead?', / digging five pits [with his fingers], dragged by the noose of Time,

1.4.s:
mriyate paśyatāmeva gale ghurghurarāvakṛt..
jīvastṛṇajalūkeva dehāddehaṃ viśetkramāt.. 42.122 ..
1.4.d:
म्रियते पश्यतामेव गले घुर्घुररावकृत्..
जीवस्तृणजलूकेव देहाद्देहं विशेत्क्रमात्.. 42.122 ..
1.4.m: he dies right before their eyes, making a rattling sound in his throat. / The soul, like a grass-leech, enters from body to body in succession;

1.4.s:
saṃprāpyottaramaṃśena dehaṃ tyajati pūrvakam..
maraṇātprārthanā duḥkhamadhikaṃ hi vivekinaḥ.. 42.123 ..
1.4.d:
संप्राप्योत्तरमंशेन देहं त्यजति पूर्वकम्..
मरणात्प्रार्थना दुःखमधिकं हि विवेकिनः.. 42.123 ..
1.4.m: having reached the next [body] with a part [of itself], it abandons the previous one. / Begging is indeed a greater sorrow than death to a discerning person:

1.4.s:
kṣaṇikaṃ maraṇe duḥkhamanaṃtaṃ prārthanākṛtam..
jñātaṃ mayaitadadhunā mṛto bhavati yadguruḥ.. 42.124 ..
1.4.d:
क्षणिकं मरणे दुःखमनंतं प्रार्थनाकृतम्..
ज्ञातं मयैतदधुना मृतो भवति यद्गुरुः.. 42.124 ..
1.4.m: the sorrow in death is momentary; that caused by begging is endless. / Now this has been realized by me: that a venerable person becomes as if dead [when begging].

1.4.s:
na paraḥ prārthayedbhūyastṛṣṇā lāghavakāraṇam..
ādau duḥkhaṃ tathā madhye hyantye duḥkhaṃ ca dāruṇam.. 42.125 ..
1.4.d:
न परः प्रार्थयेद्भूयस्तृष्णा लाघवकारणम्..
आदौ दुःखं तथा मध्ये ह्यन्त्ये दुःखं च दारुणम्.. 42.125 ..
1.4.m: Let no one beg from another again; craving is the cause of degradation. / In the beginning is suffering, likewise in the middle, and at the end there is terrible suffering;

1.4.s:
nisargātsarvabhūtānāmiti duḥkhaparaṃparā..
kṣudhā ca sarvarogāṇāṃ vyādhiḥ śreṣṭhatamaḥ smṛtaḥ.. 42.126 ..
1.4.d:
निसर्गात्सर्वभूतानामिति दुःखपरंपरा..
क्षुधा च सर्वरोगाणां व्याधिः श्रेष्ठतमः स्मृतः.. 42.126 ..
1.4.m: by the very nature of all beings, such is the succession of pain. / And hunger is considered the foremost disease among all sicknesses;

1.4.s:
sa cānnauṣadhilepena kṣaṇamātraṃ praśāmyati..
kṣuddhyādhervedanā tīvrā niḥśeṣabalakṛntanī.. 42.127 ..
1.4.d:
स चान्नौषधिलेपेन क्षणमात्रं प्रशाम्यति..
क्षुद्ध्याधेर्वेदना तीव्रा निःशेषबलकृन्तनी.. 42.127 ..
1.4.m: and it is appeased only for a moment by the medicinal plaster of food. / The pain of the hunger-disease is sharp, cutting down all strength;

1.4.s:
tayābhibhūto mriyate yathānyairvyādhibhirnnaraḥ..
rājño'bhimānamātraṃ hi mamaiva vidyate gṛhe.. 42.128 ..
1.4.d:
तयाभिभूतो म्रियते यथान्यैर्व्याधिभिर्न्नरः..
राज्ञोऽभिमानमात्रं हि ममैव विद्यते गृहे.. 42.128 ..
1.4.m: overcome by it, a man dies just as from other diseases. / In my palace, there is merely the false pride of being a king;

1.4.s:
sarvamābharaṇaṃ bhāraṃ sarvamālepanaṃ mama..
sarvaṃ pralāpitaṃ gītaṃ nityamunmattaceṣṭitam.. 42.129 ..
1.4.d:
सर्वमाभरणं भारं सर्वमालेपनं मम..
सर्वं प्रलापितं गीतं नित्यमुन्मत्तचेष्टितम्.. 42.129 ..
1.4.m: every ornament is a burden to me, every ointment is [a burden], / all singing is raving, ever the antics of a madman.

1.4.s:
ityevaṃ rājyasaṃbhogaiḥ kutaḥ saukhyaṃ vicārataḥ..
nṛpāṇāṃ vyagracittānāmanyonyavijigīṣayā.. 42.130 ..
1.4.d:
इत्येवं राज्यसंभोगैः कुतः सौख्यं विचारतः..
नृपाणां व्यग्रचित्तानामन्योन्यविजिगीषया.. 42.130 ..
1.4.m: Thus, upon reflection, where is happiness from royal pleasures / for kings whose minds are agitated by the desire to conquer one another?

1.4.s:
prāyeṇa śrīmadālepānnahuṣādyā mahānṛpāḥ..
svargaṃ prāpyāpi patitāḥ kaḥ śriyo viṃdate sukham.. 42.131 ..
1.4.d:
प्रायेण श्रीमदालेपान्नहुषाद्या महानृपाः..
स्वर्गं प्राप्यापि पतिताः कः श्रियो विंदते सुखम्.. 42.131 ..
1.4.m: Mostly through the intoxication of royal fortune, great kings like Nahuṣa / have fallen even after reaching heaven. Who finds happiness in fortune?

1.4.s:
uparyupari devānāmanyonyātiśaye sthitam..
naraiḥ puṇyaphalaṃ svarge mūlacchedena bhujyate.. 42.132 ..
1.4.d:
उपर्युपरि देवानामन्योन्यातिशये स्थितम्..
नरैः पुण्यफलं स्वर्गे मूलच्छेदेन भुज्यते.. 42.132 ..
1.4.m: Above and beyond each other, the gods stand in mutual rivalry. / In heaven, the fruit of merit is enjoyed by men with the severance of its root,

1.4.s:
na cānyatkriyate karma so'tra doṣaḥ sudāruṇaḥ..
chinnamūlataruryadvadavaśaḥ patate kṣitau.. 42.133 ..
1.4.d:
न चान्यत्क्रियते कर्म सोऽत्र दोषः सुदारुणः..
छिन्नमूलतरुर्यद्वदवशः पतते क्षितौ.. 42.133 ..
1.4.m: and no other action is performed there—that is a very severe fault. / Just as a tree whose root is severed falls helplessly to the ground,

1.4.s:
puṇyamūlakṣaye tadvatpātayaṃti divaukasaḥ..
iti svargepi devānāṃ nāsti saukhyaṃ vicārataḥ.. 42.134 ..
1.4.d:
पुण्यमूलक्षये तद्वत्पातयंति दिवौकसः..
इति स्वर्गेपि देवानां नास्ति सौख्यं विचारतः.. 42.134 ..
1.4.m: likewise, when the root of merit is exhausted, the dwellers of heaven cast [them] down. / Thus, upon reflection, even in heaven there is no happiness for the gods.

1.4.s:
tathā nārakiṇāṃ duḥkhaṃ prasiddhaṃ kiṃ ca varṇyate..
sthāvareṣvapiduḥkhāni dāvāgnihimaśoṣaṇam.. 42.135 ..
1.4.d:
तथा नारकिणां दुःखं प्रसिद्धं किं च वर्ण्यते..
स्थावरेष्वपिदुःखानि दावाग्निहिमशोषणम्.. 42.135 ..
1.4.m: Likewise, the suffering of the denizens of hell is well known; why describe it further? / Even in immovable beings there are sufferings: forest fires, freezing cold, drying up,

1.4.s:
kuṭhāraiśṭhedanaṃ tīvraṃ valkalānāṃ ca takṣaṇam..
parṇaśakhāphalānāṃ ca pātanaṃ caṃḍavāyunā.. 42.136 ..
1.4.d:
कुठारैश्ठेदनं तीव्रं वल्कलानां च तक्षणम्..
पर्णशखाफलानां च पातनं चंडवायुना.. 42.136 ..
1.4.m: sharp chopping by axes, peeling of the bark, / and the casting down of leaves, branches, and fruits by violent winds.

1.4.s:
apamardaśca satataṃ gajairvanyaiśca dehibhiḥ..
tṛḍ‌bubhukṣā ca sarpāṇāṃ krodho duḥkhaṃ ca dāruṇam.. 42.137 ..
1.4.d:
अपमर्दश्च सततं गजैर्वन्यैश्च देहिभिः..
तृड्‌बुभुक्षा च सर्पाणां क्रोधो दुःखं च दारुणम्.. 42.137 ..
1.4.m: And [there is] constant trampling by elephants and wild creatures. / The thirst, hunger, anger, and dreadful suffering of snakes,

1.4.s:
duṣṭānāṃ ghātanaṃ loke pāśena ca nibandhanam..
evaṃ sarīsṛpāṇāṃ ca duḥkhaṃ mātarmuhurmuhuḥ.. 42.138 ..
1.4.d:
दुष्टानां घातनं लोके पाशेन च निबन्धनम्..
एवं सरीसृपाणां च दुःखं मातर्मुहुर्मुहुः.. 42.138 ..
1.4.m: The slaughter of the wicked in the world, and binding with a noose— / thus, O mother, time and again is the misery of reptiles.

1.4.s:
akasmājjanmamaraṇaṃ kīṭādīnāṃ tathāvidham..
varṣāśītātapairduḥkhaṃ sukaṣṭaṃ mṛgapakṣiṇām.. 42.139 ..
1.4.d:
अकस्माज्जन्ममरणं कीटादीनां तथाविधम्..
वर्षाशीतातपैर्दुःखं सुकष्टं मृगपक्षिणाम्.. 42.139 ..
1.4.m: Likewise is the sudden birth and death of worms, insects, and the like; / the very severe misery of beasts and birds due to rain, cold, and heat.

1.4.s:
kṣuttṛṭ‌kleśena mahatā saṃtrastāśca sadā mṛgāḥ..
paśunāganikāyānāṃ śrṛṇu duḥkhāni yāni ca.. 42.140 ..
1.4.d:
क्षुत्तृट्‌क्लेशेन महता संत्रस्ताश्च सदा मृगाः..
पशुनागनिकायानां श्रृणु दुःखानि यानि च.. 42.140 ..
1.4.m: And wild animals are always terrified by great torment from hunger and thirst. / Listen also to the sufferings of herds of cattle and elephants:

1.4.s:
kṣuttṛṭ‌chītādidamanaṃ vadhabandhanatāḍanam..
nāsāpravedhanaṃ trāsaḥ pratodāṃkuśatāḍanam.. 42.141 ..
1.4.d:
क्षुत्तृट्‌छीतादिदमनं वधबन्धनताडनम्..
नासाप्रवेधनं त्रासः प्रतोदांकुशताडनम्.. 42.141 ..
1.4.m: Subjection to hunger, thirst, cold, and the like; killing, binding, and beating; / piercing the nostrils, fear, beating with goads and ankus,

1.4.s:
veṇukuntādinigaḍamudgarāṃ'kuśatāḍanam..
bhārodvahanasaṃkleśaṃ śikṣāyuddhādipīḍanam.. 42.142 ..
1.4.d:
वेणुकुन्तादिनिगडमुद्गरांऽकुशताडनम्..
भारोद्वहनसंक्लेशं शिक्षायुद्धादिपीडनम्.. 42.142 ..
1.4.m: Striking with bamboo sticks, spears, chains, mallets, and ankus; / the severe pain of carrying burdens, and affliction in training, battles, and the like;

1.4.s:
ātmayūthaviyogaśca vane ca nayanādikam..
durbhikṣaṃ durbhagatvaṃ ca mūrkhatvaṃ ca daridratā.. 42.143 ..
1.4.d:
आत्मयूथवियोगश्च वने च नयनादिकम्..
दुर्भिक्षं दुर्भगत्वं च मूर्खत्वं च दरिद्रता.. 42.143 ..
1.4.m: Separation from one's herd, being led into the forest, and so forth. / Famine, misfortune, foolishness, and poverty;

1.4.s:
adharottarabhāvaśca maraṇaṃ rāṣṭravibhramaḥ..
anyonyābhibhavādduḥkhamanyonyātiśayātpunaḥ.. 42.144 ..
1.4.d:
अधरोत्तरभावश्च मरणं राष्ट्रविभ्रमः..
अन्योन्याभिभवाद्दुःखमन्योन्यातिशयात्पुनः.. 42.144 ..
1.4.m: Reversal of high and low, death, agitation of the realm; / suffering from mutual overcome, and again from mutual superiority;

1.4.s:
anityatā prabhāvāṇāmucchrayāṇāṃ ca pātanam..
ityevamādibhirduḥkhairyasmādvyāptaṃ carācaram.. 42.145 ..
1.4.d:
अनित्यता प्रभावाणामुच्छ्रयाणां च पातनम्..
इत्येवमादिभिर्दुःखैर्यस्माद्व्याप्तं चराचरम्.. 42.145 ..
1.4.m: The transience of powers, and the downfall of lofty positions— / because the animate and inanimate world is pervaded by sufferings such as these,

1.4.s:
nirayādimanuṣyāṃtaṃ tasmātsarvaṃ tyajedbudhaḥ..
skandhātsakandhaṃ nayedbhāraṃ viśrāmaṃ manyatenyathā.. 42.146 ..
1.4.d:
निरयादिमनुष्यांतं तस्मात्सर्वं त्यजेद्बुधः..
स्कन्धात्सकन्धं नयेद्भारं विश्रामं मन्यतेन्यथा.. 42.146 ..
1.4.m: Beginning from hell and ending with humans, a wise person should therefore renounce it all. / [A man] moves a burden from one shoulder to the other, [and] otherwise imagines it to be rest;

1.4.s:
tadvatsarvamidaṃ loke duḥkhaṃ duḥkhena śāmyati..
evametajjagatsarvamanyonyātiśayocchritam.. 42.147 ..
1.4.d:
तद्वत्सर्वमिदं लोके दुःखं दुःखेन शाम्यति..
एवमेतज्जगत्सर्वमन्योन्यातिशयोच्छ्रितम्.. 42.147 ..
1.4.m: In that same way, all this suffering in the world is quieted only by suffering. / Thus, knowing that this entire world, exalted by mutual competition,

1.4.s:
duḥkhairākulitaṃ jñātvā nirvedaṃ paramāpnuyāt..
nirvedācca virāgaḥ syādvirāgājjñānasaṃbhavaḥ.. 42.148 ..
1.4.d:
दुःखैराकुलितं ज्ञात्वा निर्वेदं परमाप्नुयात्..
निर्वेदाच्च विरागः स्याद्विरागाज्ज्ञानसंभवः.. 42.148 ..
1.4.m: Is agitated by sufferings, one should attain supreme dispassion. / From dispassion comes detachment, and from detachment knowledge arises.

1.4.s:
jñānena taṃ paraṃ jñātvā viṣṇuṃ muktimavāpnuyāt..
nāhametādṛśe loke rameyaṃ janani kvacit.. 42.149 ..
1.4.d:
ज्ञानेन तं परं ज्ञात्वा विष्णुं मुक्तिमवाप्नुयात्..
नाहमेतादृशे लोके रमेयं जननि क्वचित्.. 42.149 ..
1.4.m: Knowing that supreme Viṣṇu by knowledge, one attains liberation. / I could never delight in such a world, O mother,

1.4.s:
rājahaṃso yathā śuddhaḥ kākāmedhyapradarśakaḥ..
śrṛṇu mātaryatra saṃstho rameyaṃ nirupadravaḥ.. 42.150 ..
1.4.d:
राजहंसो यथा शुद्धः काकामेध्यप्रदर्शकः..
श्रृणु मातर्यत्र संस्थो रमेयं निरुपद्रवः.. 42.150 ..
1.4.m: Just as a pure royal swan [cannot delight in] a crow pointing to foul filth. / Listen, O mother, where I might dwell and delight, free from afflictions.

1.4.s:
avidyāyanamatyugraṃ nānākarmātiśākhinam..
saṃkalpadaṃśamakaraṃ śokaharṣahimātapam.. 42.151 ..
1.4.d:
अविद्यायनमत्युग्रं नानाकर्मातिशाखिनम्..
संकल्पदंशमकरं शोकहर्षहिमातपम्.. 42.151 ..
1.4.m: The path of ignorance is very terrible, having branches that are diverse actions, / with resolve as gnats and crocodiles, and grief and joy as cold and heat,

1.4.s:
mohāṃdhakāratimiraṃ lobhavyālasarīsṛpam..
viṣayānanyathādhvānaṃ kāmakrodhavimokṣakam.. 42.152 ..
1.4.d:
मोहांधकारतिमिरं लोभव्यालसरीसृपम्..
विषयानन्यथाध्वानं कामक्रोधविमोक्षकम्.. 42.152 ..
1.4.m: With the darkness of delusion as gloom, and greed as venomous serpents and reptiles, / with sense-objects as a false road, and releasing desire and anger—

1.4.s:
tadatītya mahādurgaṃ praviṣṭo'smi mahadvanam..
na tatpraviśya śocaṃti na praduṣyaṃti tadvidaḥ.. 42.153 ..
1.4.d:
तदतीत्य महादुर्गं प्रविष्टोऽस्मि महद्वनम्..
न तत्प्रविश्य शोचंति न प्रदुष्यंति तद्विदः.. 42.153 ..
1.4.m: Having traversed that great impassable place, I have entered the great forest. / Having entered it, those who know it neither grieve nor feel corrupted;

1.4.s: na ca bibhyati keṣāṃcinnāsya bibhyati kecana.. 42.154 ..
1.4.d: न च बिभ्यति केषांचिन्नास्य बिभ्यति केचन.. 42.154 ..
1.4.m: They fear no one, and no one fears them.

1.4.s:
tasminvane saptamahādrumāstu saptaiva nadyaśca phalāni sapta..
saptāśramāḥ sapta samādhayaśca dīkṣāśca saptaitadaraṇyarūpam.. 42.155 ..
1.4.d:
तस्मिन्वने सप्तमहाद्रुमास्तु सप्तैव नद्यश्च फलानि सप्त..
सप्ताश्रमाः सप्त समाधयश्च दीक्षाश्च सप्तैतदरण्यरूपम्.. 42.155 ..
1.4.m: In that forest are seven great trees, seven rivers, and seven fruits; / seven hermitages, seven absorptions, and seven initiations—this is the nature of the wilderness.

1.4.s:
paṃcavarṇāni divyāni caturvarṇāni kānicit..
tridvivarṇaikavarṇāni puṣpāṇi ca phalāni ca.. 42.156 ..
1.4.d:
पंचवर्णानि दिव्यानि चतुर्वर्णानि कानिचित्..
त्रिद्विवर्णैकवर्णानि पुष्पाणि च फलानि च.. 42.156 ..
1.4.m: Producing divine flowers and fruits of five colors, some of four colors, / of three, two, and one color,

1.4.s: sṛjaṃtaḥ pādapāstatra vyāpya tiṣṭhanti tadvanam.. 42.157 ..
1.4.d: सृजंतः पादपास्तत्र व्याप्य तिष्ठन्ति तद्वनम्.. 42.157 ..
1.4.m: The trees stand there, pervading that forest.

1.4.s:
sapta striyastatra vasaṃti satyastvavāṅmukhyo bhānumato bhavaṃti..
ūrdhvaṃ rasānādadate prajābhyaḥ sarvāśca tāstattvataḥ kopi vade.. 42.158 ..
1.4.d:
सप्त स्त्रियस्तत्र वसंति सत्यस्त्ववाङ्मुख्यो भानुमतो भवंति..
ऊर्ध्वं रसानाददते प्रजाभ्यः सर्वाश्च तास्तत्त्वतः कोपि वदे.. 42.158 ..
1.4.m: Seven true women dwell there, facing downward away from the sun; / they draw essence upward from creatures—can someone describe them all according to reality?

1.4.s:
saptaiva girayaścātra dhṛtaṃ yairbhuvanatrayam..
nadyaśca saritaḥ sapta brahmavārivahāḥ sadā.. 42.159 ..
1.4.d:
सप्तैव गिरयश्चात्र धृतं यैर्भुवनत्रयम्..
नद्यश्च सरितः सप्त ब्रह्मवारिवहाः सदा.. 42.159 ..
1.4.m: And there are precisely seven mountains by which the three worlds are held, / and seven rivers, streams that always carry the water of Brahman.

1.4.s:
tejaścābhayadānatvamadrohaḥ kauśalaṃ tathā..
acāpalyamathākrodhaḥ priyavādaśca saptamaḥ.. 42.160 ..
1.4.d:
तेजश्चाभयदानत्वमद्रोहः कौशलं तथा..
अचापल्यमथाक्रोधः प्रियवादश्च सप्तमः.. 42.160 ..
1.4.m: Brilliance, giving freedom from fear, harmlessness, skill, / freedom from fickleness, freedom from anger, and pleasant speech as the seventh—

1.4.s:
ityete girayo jñeyāstasminvidyāvane sthitāḥ..
dṛḍhaniścayastathā bhāsā samatā nigraho guṇaḥ.. 42.161 ..
1.4.d:
इत्येते गिरयो ज्ञेयास्तस्मिन्विद्यावने स्थिताः..
दृढनिश्चयस्तथा भासा समता निग्रहो गुणः.. 42.161 ..
1.4.m: These should be known as the mountains situated in that forest of wisdom. / Firm resolve, radiance, equanimity, self-restraint, virtue,

1.4.s:
nirmamatvaṃ tapaścātra santoṣaḥ saptamo hradaḥ..
bhagavadguṇavijñānādbhaktiḥ syātprathamā nadī.. 42.162 ..
1.4.d:
निर्ममत्वं तपश्चात्र सन्तोषः सप्तमो ह्रदः..
भगवद्गुणविज्ञानाद्भक्तिः स्यात्प्रथमा नदी.. 42.162 ..
1.4.m: Selflessness, austerity, and contentment is the seventh lake. / From discernment of the Lord's attributes, devotion is the first river;

1.4.s:
puṣpādipūjā dvitīyā tṛtīyā ca pradakṣiṇā..
caturthī stutivāgrūpā pañcamī īśvarārpaṇā.. 42.163 ..
1.4.d:
पुष्पादिपूजा द्वितीया तृतीया च प्रदक्षिणा..
चतुर्थी स्तुतिवाग्रूपा पञ्चमी ईश्वरार्पणा.. 42.163 ..
1.4.m: Worship with flowers and the like is the second, and circumambulation is the third; / the fourth has the form of words of praise, the fifth is offering to Īśvara;

1.4.s:
ṣaṣṭhī brahmaikatā proktā saptamī siddhireva ca..
sapta nadyo'tra kathitā brahmaṇā parameṣṭhinā.. 42.164 ..
1.4.d:
षष्ठी ब्रह्मैकता प्रोक्ता सप्तमी सिद्धिरेव च..
सप्त नद्योऽत्र कथिता ब्रह्मणा परमेष्ठिना.. 42.164 ..
1.4.m: The sixth is declared to be oneness with Brahman, and the seventh is perfection itself. / These seven rivers here were proclaimed by Brahmā, the supreme lord.

1.4.s: brahmā dharmo yamaścāgniriṃdro varuṇa eva ca.. 42.165 ..
1.4.d: ब्रह्मा धर्मो यमश्चाग्निरिंद्रो वरुण एव च.. 42.165 ..
1.4.m: Brahmā, Dharma, Yama, Agni, Indra, Varuṇa,

1.4.s:
dhanadaśca dhruvādīnāṃ saptakānarcayaṃtyamī..
nadīnāṃ saṃgamastatra vaikuṃṭhasamupahvare.. 42.166 ..
1.4.d:
धनदश्च ध्रुवादीनां सप्तकानर्चयंत्यमी..
नदीनां संगमस्तत्र वैकुंठसमुपह्वरे.. 42.166 ..
1.4.m: And Dhanada—these worship the groups of seven beginning with Dhruva. / The confluence of the rivers is there in the retreat of Vaikuṇṭha,

1.4.s:
ātmatṛptā yato yāṃti śāṃtā dāṃtāḥ parātparam..
keciddrumāḥ striyaḥ kecitkecittattvavido'pare.. 42.167 ..
1.4.d:
आत्मतृप्ता यतो यांति शांता दांताः परात्परम्..
केचिद्द्रुमाः स्त्रियः केचित्केचित्तत्त्वविदोऽपरे.. 42.167 ..
1.4.m: Whence those content in the self, tranquil, and restrained go to the highest of the high. / Some say they are trees, some women, others knowers of reality;

1.4.s:
saritaḥ kecidāhuḥ sma saptaiva jñānavittamāḥ..
anapetavratakāmo'tra brahmacaryaṃ carāmi ca.. 42.168 ..
1.4.d:
सरितः केचिदाहुः स्म सप्तैव ज्ञानवित्तमाः..
अनपेतव्रतकामोऽत्र ब्रह्मचर्यं चरामि च.. 42.168 ..
1.4.m: Some of the foremost knowers have spoken of seven rivers. / With my desire for vows uninterrupted, I practice celibacy here.

1.4.s:
brahmaiva samidhastatra brahmāgnirbrahma saṃstaraḥ..
āpo brahma gurubrahma brahmacaryamidaṃ mama.. 42.169 ..
1.4.d:
ब्रह्मैव समिधस्तत्र ब्रह्माग्निर्ब्रह्म संस्तरः..
आपो ब्रह्म गुरुब्रह्म ब्रह्मचर्यमिदं मम.. 42.169 ..
1.4.m: Brahman alone is the firewood there, Brahman the fire, Brahman the sacred grass couch; / Brahman the waters, Brahman the guru—such is my celibacy.

1.4.s:
etadevedṛśaṃ sūkṣmaṃ brahmacaryaṃ vidurbudhāḥ..
guruṃ ca śrṛṇu me mātaryo me vidyāprado'bhavat.. 42.170 ..
1.4.d:
एतदेवेदृशं सूक्ष्मं ब्रह्मचर्यं विदुर्बुधाः..
गुरुं च श्रृणु मे मातर्यो मे विद्याप्रदोऽभवत्.. 42.170 ..
1.4.m: This very kind of subtle celibacy the wise know. / Listen also to my guru, O mother, who has imparted knowledge to me:

1.4.s:
ekaḥ śāstā na dvitīyo'sti śāstā hṛdyeva tiṣṭhanpuruṣaṃ praśāsti..
tenābhiyuktaḥ praṇavādivodakaṃ yatā niyuktosmi tathācarāmi.. 42.171 ..
1.4.d:
एकः शास्ता न द्वितीयोऽस्ति शास्ता हृद्येव तिष्ठन्पुरुषं प्रशास्ति..
तेनाभियुक्तः प्रणवादिवोदकं यता नियुक्तोस्मि तथाचरामि.. 42.171 ..
1.4.m: There is one ruler, there is no second ruler; dwelling within the heart, he rules the person. / Commanded by him, just as water [flows] down an incline, as I am directed, so I act.

1.4.s:
eko gururnāsti tathā dvitīyo hṛdi sthitastamahaṃ nṛ bravīmi..
yaṃ cāvamānyaiva guruṃ mukundaṃ parābhūtā dānavāḥ sarva eva.. 42.172 ..
1.4.d:
एको गुरुर्नास्ति तथा द्वितीयो हृदि स्थितस्तमहं नृ ब्रवीमि..
यं चावमान्यैव गुरुं मुकुन्दं पराभूता दानवाः सर्व एव.. 42.172 ..
1.4.m: There is one guru, there is likewise no second; dwelling in the heart, him I declare [to you], O man— / having insulted which guru, Mukunda, all the Dānavas were utterly ruined.

1.4.s:
eko baṃdhurnāsti tato dvitīyo hṛdī sthitaṃ tamahamanubravīmi..
tenānuśiṣṭā bāṃdhavā baṃdhumaṃtaḥ saptarṣayaḥ sapta divi prabhāṃti.. 42.173 ..
1.4.d:
एको बंधुर्नास्ति ततो द्वितीयो हृदी स्थितं तमहमनुब्रवीमि..
तेनानुशिष्टा बांधवा बंधुमंतः सप्तर्षयः सप्त दिवि प्रभांति.. 42.173 ..
1.4.m: There is one kinsman, there is none second to him; dwelling in the heart, him I proclaim. / Instructed by him, kinsmen possessing kinship, the seven seers, shine in the sky.

1.4.s:
brahmacaryaṃ ca saṃsevyaṃ gārhasthya śrṛṇu yādṛśam..
patnī prakṛtirūpā me taccitto nāsmi karhicit.. 42.174 ..
1.4.d:
ब्रह्मचर्यं च संसेव्यं गार्हस्थ्य श्रृणु यादृशम्..
पत्नी प्रकृतिरूपा मे तच्चित्तो नास्मि कर्हिचित्.. 42.174 ..
1.4.m: And celibacy is to be practiced; listen to the nature of the householder's life: / my wife has the form of Prakṛti, [yet] I am never attached to her.

1.4.s:
maccittā sā sadā mātarmama sarvārthasādhanī..
ghrāṇaṃ jihvā ca cakṣuśca tvakca śrotraṃ ca paṃcamam.. 42.175 ..
1.4.d:
मच्चित्ता सा सदा मातर्मम सर्वार्थसाधनी..
घ्राणं जिह्वा च चक्षुश्च त्वक्च श्रोत्रं च पंचमम्.. 42.175 ..
1.4.m: Her mind is ever focused on me, O mother, accomplishing all my goals. / Smell, tongue, eye, skin, and hearing as the fifth,

1.4.s:
mano buddhiśca saptaite dīpyaṃte pāvakā mama..
gaṃdho rasaśca rūpaṃ ca śabdaḥ sparśaśca paṃcamam.. 42.176 ..
1.4.d:
मनो बुद्धिश्च सप्तैते दीप्यंते पावका मम..
गंधो रसश्च रूपं च शब्दः स्पर्शश्च पंचमम्.. 42.176 ..
1.4.m: Mind, and intellect—these seven fires of mine blaze brightly. / Odor, taste, form, sound, and touch as the fifth,

1.4.s:
maṃtavyamatha boddhavyaṃ saptaitāḥ samidho mama..
hutaṃ nārāyaṇadhyānādbhuṃkte nārāyaṇaḥ svayam.. 42.177 ..
1.4.d:
मंतव्यमथ बोद्धव्यं सप्तैताः समिधो मम..
हुतं नारायणध्यानाद्भुंक्ते नारायणः स्वयम्.. 42.177 ..
1.4.m: What is to be thought, and what is to be understood—these seven are my fuel sticks. / What is offered through meditation on Nārāyaṇa, Nārāyaṇa himself enjoys.

1.4.s:
evaṃvidhena yajñena yajāmyasmi tamīśvaram..
akāmayānasya ca sarvakāmo bhavedadviṣāṇasya ca sarvadoṣaḥ.. 42.178 ..
1.4.d:
एवंविधेन यज्ञेन यजाम्यस्मि तमीश्वरम्..
अकामयानस्य च सर्वकामो भवेदद्विषाणस्य च सर्वदोषः.. 42.178 ..
1.4.m: With such a sacrifice, I worship that Īśvara. / For one free from desire, all desires are fulfilled; and for one who harbors hatred, every fault arises.

1.4.s:
na me svabhāveṣu bhavaṃti lepāstoyasya biṃdoriva puṣkareṣu..
nityasya me naiva bhavaṃtyanityā nirīkṣamāṇasya bahusyabhāvāt.. 42.179 ..
1.4.d:
न मे स्वभावेषु भवंति लेपास्तोयस्य बिंदोरिव पुष्करेषु..
नित्यस्य मे नैव भवंत्यनित्या निरीक्षमाणस्य बहुस्यभावात्.. 42.179 ..
1.4.m: Taints do not occur in my nature, just as drops of water do not cling to lotus leaves. / To me, who am eternal, non-eternal things do not belong, because of my beholding the manifold nature of existence.

1.4.s: na sajjate karmasu bhogajālaṃ divīva sūryasya mayūkhajālam.. 42.180 ..
1.4.d: न सज्जते कर्मसु भोगजालं दिवीव सूर्यस्य मयूखजालम्.. 42.180 ..
1.4.m: The web of experiences does not cling to my actions, just as the network of sunbeams does not stick in the sky.

1.4.s:
evaṃvidhena putreṇa mā mātarduḥkhinī bhava..
tatpadaṃ tvā ca neṣyāmi na yatkratuśatairapi.. 42.181 ..
1.4.d:
एवंविधेन पुत्रेण मा मातर्दुःखिनी भव..
तत्पदं त्वा च नेष्यामि न यत्क्रतुशतैरपि.. 42.181 ..
1.4.m: Mother, do not grieve with such a son! / For I will take you to that state which cannot be reached even by hundreds of sacrifices.

1.4.s:
iti putravacaḥ śrutvā vismitā itarābhavat..
ciṃtayāmāsa yadyevaṃ vidvānmama suto dṛḍham.. 42.182 ..
1.4.d:
इति पुत्रवचः श्रुत्वा विस्मिता इतराभवत्..
चिंतयामास यद्येवं विद्वान्मम सुतो दृढम्.. 42.182 ..
1.4.m: Hearing her son’s words, Itarā was astonished. / She thought: ‘If my son is truly so learned,

1.4.s:
lokeṣu khyātimāyāti tato me syādyaśaḥ param..
ityādi ciṃtayaṃtyāṃ ca rajanyāṃ bhagavānhariḥ.. 42.183 ..
1.4.d:
लोकेषु ख्यातिमायाति ततो मे स्याद्यशः परम्..
इत्यादि चिंतयंत्यां च रजन्यां भगवान्हरिः.. 42.183 ..
1.4.m: he will attain renown in the worlds, and from that supreme fame will be mine!’ / As she was thus reflecting in the night, the blessed Lord Hari,

1.4.s:
prahṛṣṭastasya tairvākyairvismitaḥ prādurāsa ca..
mūrteḥ svayaṃ viniṣkramya śaṃkhacakragadādharāḥ.. 42.184 ..
1.4.d:
प्रहृष्टस्तस्य तैर्वाक्यैर्विस्मितः प्रादुरास च..
मूर्तेः स्वयं विनिष्क्रम्य शंखचक्रगदाधराः.. 42.184 ..
1.4.m: delighted and astonished by his words, manifested himself directly, / emerging of his own accord from the image, bearing the conch, discus, and mace,

1.4.s:
jagadudbhāsayanbhāsā sūryakoṭisamaprabhaḥ..
tato niṣpatya dharaṇīṃ hṛṣṭaromāśrudgadaḥ.. 42.185 ..
1.4.d:
जगदुद्भासयन्भासा सूर्यकोटिसमप्रभः..
ततो निष्पत्य धरणीं हृष्टरोमाश्रुद्गदः.. 42.185 ..
1.4.m: illuminating the world with his radiance, shining like ten million suns. / Then, falling prostrate upon the ground, his hair standing on end, his voice choked with tears,

1.4.s: mūrdhni baddhāṃjaliṃ dhīmānaitareyo'tha tuṣṭuve.. 42.186 ..
1.4.d: मूर्ध्नि बद्धांजलिं धीमानैतरेयोऽथ तुष्टुवे.. 42.186 ..
1.4.m: the wise Aitareya folded his hands upon his head and praised him:

1.4.s:
namastubhyaṃ bhagavate vāsudevāya dhīmahi..
pradyumnāyāniruddhāya namaḥ saṃkarṣaṇāya ca.. 42.187 ..
1.4.d:
नमस्तुभ्यं भगवते वासुदेवाय धीमहि..
प्रद्युम्नायानिरुद्धाय नमः संकर्षणाय च.. 42.187 ..
1.4.m: ‘Homage to you, the Blessed One, Vāsudeva! We meditate upon [you]. / Homage to Pradyumna and Aniruddha, and to Saṃkarṣaṇa!

1.4.s:
namo vijñānamātrāya paramānaṃdamūrtaye..
ātmārāmāya śāṃtāya nivṛttadvaitadṛṣṭaye.. 42.188 ..
1.4.d:
नमो विज्ञानमात्राय परमानंदमूर्तये..
आत्मारामाय शांताय निवृत्तद्वैतदृष्टये.. 42.188 ..
1.4.m: Homage to you who are pure consciousness, whose form is supreme bliss, / who delight in the Self, who are peaceful, whose perception of duality has ceased!

1.4.s:
ātmānaṃdānuruddhāya samyaktayaktormaye namaḥ..
hṛṣīkeśāya mahate namaste'naṃtaśaktaye.. 42.189 ..
1.4.d:
आत्मानंदानुरुद्धाय सम्यक्तयक्तोर्मये नमः..
हृषीकेशाय महते नमस्तेऽनंतशक्तये.. 42.189 ..
1.4.m: Homage to you who are devoted to the bliss of the Self, who have thoroughly cast aside the waves [of worldly existence], / to Hṛṣīkeśa, the great one! Homage to you of infinite power!

1.4.s:
vacasyuparate prāpyo ya eko manasā saha..
anāmarūpacinmātraḥ so'vyānnaḥ sadasatparaḥ.. 42.190 ..
1.4.d:
वचस्युपरते प्राप्यो य एको मनसा सह..
अनामरूपचिन्मात्रः सोऽव्यान्नः सदसत्परः.. 42.190 ..
1.4.m: Attainable when speech has ceased along with the mind, the one / without name and form, who is pure consciousness, beyond being and non-being—may he protect us!

1.4.s:
yasminnidaṃ yataścedaṃ tiṣṭhatyapaiti jāyate..
mṛnmayeṣviva mṛjjātistasmai te brahmaṇe namaḥ.. 42.191 ..
1.4.d:
यस्मिन्निदं यतश्चेदं तिष्ठत्यपैति जायते..
मृन्मयेष्विव मृज्जातिस्तस्मै ते ब्रह्मणे नमः.. 42.191 ..
1.4.m: In whom this [universe] rests, from whom it arises and passes away, / just as clay objects arise from clay—homage to that Brahman, to you!

1.4.s:
yaṃ na spṛśaṃti na vidurmanobuddhīṃdriyāsavaḥ..
aṃtarbahiśca vitataṃ vyomavatpraṇato'smyaham.. 42.192 ..
1.4.d:
यं न स्पृशंति न विदुर्मनोबुद्धींद्रियासवः..
अंतर्बहिश्च विततं व्योमवत्प्रणतोऽस्म्यहम्.. 42.192 ..
1.4.m: Whom the mind, intellect, senses, and vital breaths do not touch or know, / pervading inside and outside like the sky—to him I bow down.

1.4.s:
deheṃdriyaprāṇamanodhiyo'mī yadaṃśabddhāḥ pracaraṃti karmasu..
naivānyadālohamiva prataptaṃ sthāneṣu taddṛṣṭapadena ete.. 42.193 ..
1.4.d:
देहेंद्रियप्राणमनोधियोऽमी यदंशब्द्धाः प्रचरंति कर्मसु..
नैवान्यदालोहमिव प्रतप्तं स्थानेषु तद्दृष्टपदेन एते.. 42.193 ..
1.4.m: These bodies, senses, vital breaths, mind, and intellect, bound to your part, engage in actions; / never otherwise, just as iron when heated [acts like fire]—by his observed presence they exist in their places.

1.4.s:
caturbhiśca tribhirdvābhyāmekadhā praṇamāmi tam..
pūrvāparāparayuge śāstāraṃ paramīśvaram.. 42.194 ..
1.4.d:
चतुर्भिश्च त्रिभिर्द्वाभ्यामेकधा प्रणमामि तम्..
पूर्वापरापरयुगे शास्तारं परमीश्वरम्.. 42.194 ..
1.4.m: I bow down to him fourfold, threefold, twofold, and as one, / the ruler and supreme Lord across former, later, and subsequent ages.

1.4.s:
hitvā gatīrmokṣakāmā yaṃ bhajaṃti daśātmakam..
taṃ paraṃ satyamamalaṃ tvāṃ vayaṃ paryupāsmahe.. 42.195 ..
1.4.d:
हित्वा गतीर्मोक्षकामा यं भजंति दशात्मकम्..
तं परं सत्यममलं त्वां वयं पर्युपास्महे.. 42.195 ..
1.4.m: Desiring liberation, renouncing all courses of rebirth, [sages] worship him of tenfold nature. / We attend upon you, the supreme, untainted Truth.

1.4.s: oṃnamo bhagavate mahāpuruṣāya mahānubhāvāya vibhūtipataye sakalasātvataparivṛḍhanikarakarakamalotpalakuḍmalopalālitacaraṇāraviṃdayugala paramaparameṣṭhinnamaste.. 42.196 ..
1.4.d: ओंनमो भगवते महापुरुषाय महानुभावाय विभूतिपतये सकलसात्वतपरिवृढनिकरकरकमलोत्पलकुड्मलोपलालितचरणारविंदयुगल परमपरमेष्ठिन्नमस्ते.. 42.196 ..
1.4.m: Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the supreme person, the exalted one, the lord of divine majesty, whose lotus feet are caressed by the lotus and water-lily buds of the hands of the multitude of all Sātvata leaders, supreme Parameṣṭhin, homage to you!

1.4.s:
tavāgnirāsyaṃ vasudhāṃghriyugmaṃ nabhaḥ śiraścaṃdraravī ca netre..
samastalokā jaṭharaṃ bhujāśca diśaścatasro bhagavannamaste.. 42.197 ..
1.4.d:
तवाग्निरास्यं वसुधांघ्रियुग्मं नभः शिरश्चंद्ररवी च नेत्रे..
समस्तलोका जठरं भुजाश्च दिशश्चतस्रो भगवन्नमस्ते.. 42.197 ..
1.4.m: Fire is your mouth, the earth your pair of feet, the sky your head, the moon and sun your eyes, / all the worlds your belly, and the four cardinal directions your arms. O Blessed One, homage to you!

1.4.s:
janmāni tāvaṃti na saṃti deva niṣpīḍya sarvāṇi ca sarvakālam..
bhūtāni yāvaṃti mayātra bhīme pītāni saṃsāramahāsamudre.. 42.198 ..
1.4.d:
जन्मानि तावंति न संति देव निष्पीड्य सर्वाणि च सर्वकालम्..
भूतानि यावंति मयात्र भीमे पीतानि संसारमहासमुद्रे.. 42.198 ..
1.4.m: O Lord, there are not as many births as there are beings / crushed by me throughout all time and swallowed here in this terrible, great ocean of saṃsāra.

1.4.s:
saṃpacchilānāṃ himavanmaheṃdrakailāsamervādiṣu naiva tādṛk..
dehānanekānanugṛhṇato me prāptāsti saṃpanmahatī tatheśa.. 42.199 ..
1.4.d:
संपच्छिलानां हिमवन्महेंद्रकैलासमेर्वादिषु नैव तादृक्..
देहाननेकाननुगृह्णतो मे प्राप्तास्ति संपन्महती तथेश.. 42.199 ..
1.4.m: The heap of rocks upon Himavat, Mahendra, Kailāsa, Meru, and other mountains does not equal / the vast mass of countless bodies assumed and cast off by me, O Lord!

1.4.s:
na saṃtite deva bhuvi pradeśā na yeṣu jāto'smi tathā vinaṣṭaḥ..
bhūtvā mayā yeṣu na jaṃtavaśca saṃbhakṣito vā na ca bhūtasaṃghaiḥ.. 42.200 ..
1.4.d:
न संतिते देव भुवि प्रदेशा न येषु जातोऽस्मि तथा विनष्टः..
भूत्वा मया येषु न जंतवश्च संभक्षितो वा न च भूतसंघैः.. 42.200 ..
1.4.m: O Lord, there are no places on earth where I have not been born or died, / or where creatures have not been devoured by me, or where I have not been devoured by hosts of beings.

1.4.s:
śokābhibhūtasya mamāśru deva yāvatpramāṇaṃ patitaṃ bhaveṣu..
tāvatpramāṇaṃ na jalaṃ payodā muṃcaṃti divyairapi varṣalakṣaiḥ.. 42.201 ..
1.4.d:
शोकाभिभूतस्य ममाश्रु देव यावत्प्रमाणं पतितं भवेषु..
तावत्प्रमाणं न जलं पयोदा मुंचंति दिव्यैरपि वर्षलक्षैः.. 42.201 ..
1.4.m: O Lord, the measure of tears shed by me when overcome with grief in my births / is not equaled by the rain released by clouds even in a hundred thousand divine years.

1.4.s:
manye dharitrīparamāṇusaṃkhyāmupaiti pitrorgaṇanā na mahyam..
mitrāvyamitrāṇyanujīvyabaṃdhūnsaṃkhyātumīśo'smina devadeva.. 42.202 ..
1.4.d:
मन्ये धरित्रीपरमाणुसंख्यामुपैति पित्रोर्गणना न मह्यम्..
मित्राव्यमित्राण्यनुजीव्यबंधून्संख्यातुमीशोऽस्मिन देवदेव.. 42.202 ..
1.4.m: I consider that the number of my parents exceeds the count of the atoms of the earth; / O God of gods, I am unable to calculate my friends, enemies, dependents, and kinsmen!

1.4.s:
tvayyarpitaṃ nātha punaḥ punarme manaḥ samākṣipya sudurddharāri..
kāmo vaśaṃ kradhamukhaiḥ sahāyaiḥ karoti kiṃ tadbhagavankaromi.. 42.203 ..
1.4.d:
त्वय्यर्पितं नाथ पुनः पुनर्मे मनः समाक्षिप्य सुदुर्द्धरारि..
कामो वशं क्रधमुखैः सहायैः करोति किं तद्भगवन्करोमि.. 42.203 ..
1.4.m: O Lord, my mind, offered repeatedly to you, is forcibly dragged away by desire—that invincible enemy— / which, with anger and other allies, brings me under its sway. What, O Blessed One, shall I do?

1.4.s:
so'haṃ bhṛśārtaḥ karuṇākarastvaṃ saṃsāragarte patitasya viṣṇo..
mahātmanāṃ saṃśrayamabhyupeto naivāvasīdatyapi durgato'pi.. 42.204 ..
1.4.d:
सोऽहं भृशार्तः करुणाकरस्त्वं संसारगर्ते पतितस्य विष्णो..
महात्मनां संश्रयमभ्युपेतो नैवावसीदत्यपि दुर्गतोऽपि.. 42.204 ..
1.4.m: I am terribly afflicted, and you are the mine of compassion. For one who has fallen into the pit of worldly existence, O Viṣṇu, / he who has sought the refuge of the great-souled never sinks down, even if he is destitute.

1.4.s:
parāyaṇaṃ rogavato hi vaidyo mahābdhimagnasya ca naurnarasya..
bālasya mātāpitarau sughorasaṃsārakhinnasya hare tvameva.. 42.205 ..
1.4.d:
परायणं रोगवतो हि वैद्यो महाब्धिमग्नस्य च नौर्नरस्य..
बालस्य मातापितरौ सुघोरसंसारखिन्नस्य हरे त्वमेव.. 42.205 ..
1.4.m: The physician is the refuge of the sick, and a boat for a man sinking in the great ocean; / parents are the refuge of a child, and you alone, O Hari, are the refuge for one exhausted by terrible saṃsāra.

1.4.s:
prasīda sarveśvara sarvabhūta sarvasya heto paramārthasāra..
māmuddharāsmāduruduḥkhasaṃghātsaṃsāragartātsvaparigraheṇa.. 42.206 ..
1.4.d:
प्रसीद सर्वेश्वर सर्वभूत सर्वस्य हेतो परमार्थसार..
मामुद्धरास्मादुरुदुःखसंघात्संसारगर्तात्स्वपरिग्रहेण.. 42.206 ..
1.4.m: Be pleased, Lord of all, being of all, cause of all, essence of the supreme truth! / Deliver me by your acceptance from this pit of worldly existence, this mass of great sorrows!

1.4.s:
kṣṛttṛṭ‌tridhātubhirimaṃ muhurardyamānaṃ śītoṣṇa vātasalilairitaretarācca..
kāmāgninācyuta ruṣā ca sudurbhareṇa saṃpaśyato mama urukrama sīdato hi.. 42.207 ..
1.4.d:
क्षृत्तृट्‌त्रिधातुभिरिमं मुहुरर्द्यमानं शीतोष्ण वातसलिलैरितरेतराच्च..
कामाग्निनाच्युत रुषा च सुदुर्भरेण संपश्यतो मम उरुक्रम सीदतो हि.. 42.207 ..
1.4.m: Afflicted repeatedly by hunger, thirst, and the three humors, by cold, heat, wind, and water, and by one another, / and by the fire of desire and intolerable anger, O Acyuta, O Urukrama, I am sinking as I behold this!

1.4.s:
bhavaṃtu bhadrāṇi samastadoṣāḥ prayāṃtu nāśaṃ jagato'khilasya..
mayādya bhaktyā parameśvare prabhau stute jagaddhātari vāsudeve.. 42.208 ..
1.4.d:
भवंतु भद्राणि समस्तदोषाः प्रयांतु नाशं जगतोऽखिलस्य..
मयाद्य भक्त्या परमेश्वरे प्रभौ स्तुते जगद्धातरि वासुदेवे.. 42.208 ..
1.4.m: May blessings arise! May all defects of the entire world perish, / now that the supreme Lord, the ruler, the creator of the world, Vāsudeva, has been praised by me with devotion today!

1.4.s:
ye bhūtale ye divi cāṃtarikṣe rasātale prāṇigaṇāśca kecit..
bhavaṃtu te siddhiyujo mayādya stute jagaddhātari vāsudeve.. 42.209 ..
1.4.d:
ये भूतले ये दिवि चांतरिक्षे रसातले प्राणिगणाश्च केचित्..
भवंतु ते सिद्धियुजो मयाद्य स्तुते जगद्धातरि वासुदेवे.. 42.209 ..
1.4.m: Whatever multitudes of living beings exist on earth, in heaven, in the atmosphere, and in Rasātala, / may they all attain perfection, now that the creator of the world, Vāsudeva, has been praised by me today!

1.4.s:
ajñānino jñānavido bhavaṃtu praśāntibhājaḥ satatogracittāḥ..
mayā ca viśvaṃbharaṇe hyanaṃte stute jagaddhātari vāsudeve.. 42.210 ..
1.4.d:
अज्ञानिनो ज्ञानविदो भवंतु प्रशान्तिभाजः सततोग्रचित्ताः..
मया च विश्वंभरणे ह्यनंते स्तुते जगद्धातरि वासुदेवे.. 42.210 ..
1.4.m: May the ignorant become knowers of wisdom, and may those with ever-violent minds attain tranquility, / now that the sustainer of the universe, the infinite creator of the world, Vāsudeva, has been praised by me!

1.4.s:
śrṛṇvaṃti ye me stuvatastathānye paśyaṃti ye māmidamīrayaṃtam..
devāsurādyā manujāstiraśco bhavaṃtu te'pyacyutayogabhājaḥ.. 42.211 ..
1.4.d:
श्रृण्वंति ये मे स्तुवतस्तथान्ये पश्यंति ये मामिदमीरयंतम्..
देवासुराद्या मनुजास्तिरश्चो भवंतु तेऽप्यच्युतयोगभाजः.. 42.211 ..
1.4.m: Those who hear me as I praise, and others who behold me uttering this, / whether gods, asuras, humans, or animals—may they too partake of union with Acyuta!

1.4.s:
ye cāpi mūkā vikaleṃdriyatvātpaṭhaṃti no naiva vilokayaṃti..
paśvādayaḥ kīṭapipīlikādyā bhavaṃtu te'pyacyutayogabhājaḥ.. 42.212 ..
1.4.d:
ये चापि मूका विकलेंद्रियत्वात्पठंति नो नैव विलोकयंति..
पश्वादयः कीटपिपीलिकाद्या भवंतु तेऽप्यच्युतयोगभाजः.. 42.212 ..
1.4.m: And those who, being mute or possessing defective senses, neither recite nor see, / animals, insects, ants, and the rest—may they too partake of union with Acyuta!

1.4.s:
naśyaṃtu duḥkhāni jagatyapetu lobhādiko doṣagaṇaḥ prajābhyaḥ..
yathātmani bhrātari cātmaje vā tathā narasyāstu janepi bhāvaḥ.. 42.213 ..
1.4.d:
नश्यंतु दुःखानि जगत्यपेतु लोभादिको दोषगणः प्रजाभ्यः..
यथात्मनि भ्रातरि चात्मजे वा तथा नरस्यास्तु जनेपि भावः.. 42.213 ..
1.4.m: May sorrows perish in the world; may the host of defects such as greed depart from the subjects! / As a man feels toward himself, his brother, or his son, so may his feeling be toward any person!

1.4.s:
saṃsāravaidyai'khiladoṣahānivicakṣaṇe nirvṛtihetubhūte..
saṃsārabaṃdhāḥ śithilībhavaṃtu hṛdi sthite sarvajanasya viṣṇau.. 42.214 ..
1.4.d:
संसारवैद्यैऽखिलदोषहानिविचक्षणे निर्वृतिहेतुभूते..
संसारबंधाः शिथिलीभवंतु हृदि स्थिते सर्वजनस्य विष्णौ.. 42.214 ..
1.4.m: When the physician of worldly existence, skilled in destroying all defects, the cause of supreme beatitude, / Viṣṇu, dwells in the heart of every person, may the bonds of saṃsāra become loosened!

1.4.s:
pāpaṃ praṇāśaṃ mama ca prayātu yanmānasaṃ yacca karomi vācā..
śarīramapyācaritaṃ ca yanme smṛte jagaddhātari vāsudeve.. 42.215 ..
1.4.d:
पापं प्रणाशं मम च प्रयातु यन्मानसं यच्च करोमि वाचा..
शरीरमप्याचरितं च यन्मे स्मृते जगद्धातरि वासुदेवे.. 42.215 ..
1.4.m: May my sin perish—that which is mental, that which I commit with speech, / and that which has been performed with my body—now that the creator of the world, Vāsudeva, is remembered!’

1.4.s:
yathā hi vā vāsudeveti prokte saṃkīrttane viṣṇubhaktasya vāpi..
smṛte harau vāpi prayāti pāpaṃ satyena me naśyatāṃ tena pāpam.. 42.216 ..
1.4.d:
यथा हि वा वासुदेवेति प्रोक्ते संकीर्त्तने विष्णुभक्तस्य वापि..
स्मृते हरौ वापि प्रयाति पापं सत्येन मे नश्यतां तेन पापम्.. 42.216 ..
1.4.m: For just as sin departs when 'Vāsudeva' is uttered, / or when chanting by a devotee of Viṣṇu takes place, or when Hari is remembered, by that truth let my sin be destroyed. 42.216

1.4.s:
mūḍho'yamalpamatiralpaviceṣṭito'yaṃ kliṣṭaṃ mano'pi viṣayairmayi na prasaṃgi..
itthaṃ kṛpāṃ kuru mayi praṇate'khileśa tvāṃ stotumaṃbujabhavo'pi hi deva neśaḥ.. 42.217..
1.4.d:
मूढोऽयमल्पमतिरल्पविचेष्टितोऽयं क्लिष्टं मनोऽपि विषयैर्मयि न प्रसंगि..
इत्थं कृपां कुरु मयि प्रणतेऽखिलेश त्वां स्तोतुमंबुजभवोऽपि हि देव नेशः.. 42.217..
1.4.m: I am foolish, of small intellect, of petty actions, / and my troubled mind does not cling to worldly objects in me. / Show mercy thus to me who am bowed down, Lord of all; / even the lotus-born [Brahmā] is not able, O god, to praise you. 42.217

1.4.s:
sa tvaṃ prasīda bhagavankuru mayyanāthe viṣṇo kṛpāṃ paramakāruṇikaḥ kila tvam..
saṃsārasāgaranimagnamanaṃta dīnamuddhartumarhasi hare puruṣottamosi.. 42.218 ..
1.4.d:
स त्वं प्रसीद भगवन्कुरु मय्यनाथे विष्णो कृपां परमकारुणिकः किल त्वम्..
संसारसागरनिमग्नमनंत दीनमुद्धर्तुमर्हसि हरे पुरुषोत्तमोसि.. 42.218 ..
1.4.m: Therefore be pleased, O Lord! Grant your grace to me who am helpless, / O Viṣṇu, for you are indeed supremely compassionate! / Sunk in the ocean of saṃsāra, wretched, O Infinite One, / you ought to uplift [me], O Hari; you are the Supreme Person! 42.218

1.4.s:
itthaṃ stutaḥ sa bhagavānaitareyeṇa bhārata..
vāsudevo viśālātmā sānaṃdamidamāha tam.. 42.219 ..
1.4.d:
इत्थं स्तुतः स भगवानैतरेयेण भारत..
वासुदेवो विशालात्मा सानंदमिदमाह तम्.. 42.219 ..
1.4.m: Praised in this manner by Aitareya, O descendant of Bharata, / the broad-minded Lord Vāsudeva / joyfully said this to him: 42.219

1.4.s:
vatsaitareya tuṣṭosmi bhaktyānena stavena te..
varaṃ vṛṇuṣva mattastvaṃ durlabhaṃ yadabhīpsitam.. 42.220 ..
1.4.d:
वत्सैतरेय तुष्टोस्मि भक्त्यानेन स्तवेन ते..
वरं वृणुष्व मत्तस्त्वं दुर्लभं यदभीप्सितम्.. 42.220 ..
1.4.m: "Child Aitareya, I am pleased by your devotion through this hymn. / Choose a boon from me, whatever rare thing is desired." 42.220

1.4.s:
..aitareya uvāca..
eṣa eva varo nāthamama nityamabhīpsitaḥ..
majjato ghorasaṃsāre karṇadhāro hare bhava.. 42.221 ..
1.4.d:
..ऐतरेय उवाच..
एष एव वरो नाथमम नित्यमभीप्सितः..
मज्जतो घोरसंसारे कर्णधारो हरे भव.. 42.221 ..
1.4.m: Aitareya said: / "This alone is the boon, O Lord, that is ever desired by me: / to me drowning in dreadful saṃsāra, O Hari, be the helmsman." 42.221

1.4.s:
..śrībhagavānuvāca..
mukta evāsi saṃsārādyasya te bhaktirīdṛśī..
grahairmahāgrahairbaddho naiva te dvitrayodaśī.. 42.222 ..
1.4.d:
..श्रीभगवानुवाच..
मुक्त एवासि संसाराद्यस्य ते भक्तिरीदृशी..
ग्रहैर्महाग्रहैर्बद्धो नैव ते द्वित्रयोदशी.. 42.222 ..
1.4.m: The Holy Lord said: / "You are indeed liberated from saṃsāra, you whose devotion is such; / bound by the grasping organs and great grasped objects, the second group of thirteen does not [bind] you. 42.222

1.4.s:
yaśca stotreṇa satataṃ guptakṣetrasamīhitam..
stoṣyate vāsudevaṃ māṃ sa pāpakṣayamāpsyati.. 42.223 ..
1.4.d:
यश्च स्तोत्रेण सततं गुप्तक्षेत्रसमीहितम्..
स्तोष्यते वासुदेवं मां स पापक्षयमाप्स्यति.. 42.223 ..
1.4.m: And whoever constantly praises me, Vāsudeva, / who am sought after in Guptakṣetra, with this hymn, shall attain the destruction of sin. 42.223

1.4.s:
yasmādetena stotreṇa pāpaṃ nāśamavāpsyati..
aghanāśanamityeva tasmātkhyātimavāpsyati.. 42.224 ..
1.4.d:
यस्मादेतेन स्तोत्रेण पापं नाशमवाप्स्यति..
अघनाशनमित्येव तस्मात्ख्यातिमवाप्स्यति.. 42.224 ..
1.4.m: Since by this hymn sin will be destroyed, / therefore it will indeed become renowned as 'Destroyer of Sin' (Aghanāśana). 42.224

1.4.s:
ekādaśyāmupoṣyaiva mamāgre yaḥ paṭhiṣyati..
stavamenaṃ sa pūtātmā mama lokamavāpsyati.. 42.225 ..
1.4.d:
एकादश्यामुपोष्यैव ममाग्रे यः पठिष्यति..
स्तवमेनं स पूतात्मा मम लोकमवाप्स्यति.. 42.225 ..
1.4.m: Whoever fasts on the eleventh day (Ekādaśī) / and recites this hymn before me, purified in soul, shall attain my realm. 42.225

1.4.s:
sarveṣāmeva kṣetrāṇāṃ guptakṣetraṃ priyaṃ yathā..
tathā sarvastavānāṃ ca stavoyaṃ supriyomama.. 42.226 ..
1.4.d:
सर्वेषामेव क्षेत्राणां गुप्तक्षेत्रं प्रियं यथा..
तथा सर्वस्तवानां च स्तवोयं सुप्रियोमम.. 42.226 ..
1.4.m: Just as Guptakṣetra is dearest among all sacred fields, / so among all hymns is this hymn very dear to me. 42.226

1.4.s:
yāni coddiśya bhūtāni japyate'sau mahātmabhiḥ..
tāni śāṃtiṃ bhagaṃ prajñāṃ prāpsyaṃti kṛpayā mama.. 42.227 ..
1.4.d:
यानि चोद्दिश्य भूतानि जप्यतेऽसौ महात्मभिः..
तानि शांतिं भगं प्रज्ञां प्राप्स्यंति कृपया मम.. 42.227 ..
1.4.m: And whatever living beings it is recited for by great souls, / they will attain peace, good fortune, and wisdom through my grace. 42.227

1.4.s:
tvaṃ ca vatsa śrautadharmānsamyagācara śraddhayā..
na tairbaṃdhaṃ mayi nyastairāpsyasyanabhisaṃdhitaiḥ.. 42.228 ..
1.4.d:
त्वं च वत्स श्रौतधर्मान्सम्यगाचर श्रद्धया..
न तैर्बंधं मयि न्यस्तैराप्स्यस्यनभिसंधितैः.. 42.228 ..
1.4.m: And you, child, perform Vedic duties properly with faith; / with them surrendered to me, without attachment to results, you will not incur bondage. 42.228

1.4.s:
yaja yajñairavāpyaiva dārānnandaya mātaram..
mayi dhyānena tīvreṇa māmavāpsyasyasaṃśayam.. 42.229 ..
1.4.d:
यज यज्ञैरवाप्यैव दारान्नन्दय मातरम्..
मयि ध्यानेन तीव्रेण मामवाप्स्यस्यसंशयम्.. 42.229 ..
1.4.m: Sacrifice with sacrifices, obtain a wife, gladden your mother; / through intense meditation on me, you will reach me without doubt. 42.229

1.4.s:
buddhirmanotha bhūtāni buddhikarmendriyāṇi ca..
trayodaśagrahairye syustrayodaśa mahāgrahāḥ.. 42.230 ..
1.4.d:
बुद्धिर्मनोथ भूतानि बुद्धिकर्मेन्द्रियाणि च..
त्रयोदशग्रहैर्ये स्युस्त्रयोदश महाग्रहाः.. 42.230 ..
1.4.m: Intellect, mind, then the elements, and the senses of perception and action, / these would be the thirteen graspers, and the thirteen great grasped objects: 42.230

1.4.s:
boddhavyamatha maṃtavyamahaṃtā śabda eva ca..
sparśo raso rūpagandhau vacanādānameva ca.. 42.231 ..
1.4.d:
बोद्धव्यमथ मंतव्यमहंता शब्द एव च..
स्पर्शो रसो रूपगन्धौ वचनादानमेव च.. 42.231 ..
1.4.m: what is to be understood, what is to be thought, I-ness, and sound itself, / touch, taste, form, and smell, speech, and grasping, 42.231

1.4.s:
vihṛtyutsarga ānaṃdastrayodaśa mahāgrahāḥ..
etānmahāgrahanputra śuddhāñchuddhaiḥ svakairgrahaiḥ.. 42.232 ..
1.4.d:
विहृत्युत्सर्ग आनंदस्त्रयोदश महाग्रहाः..
एतान्महाग्रहन्पुत्र शुद्धाञ्छुद्धैः स्वकैर्ग्रहैः.. 42.232 ..
1.4.m: movement, excretion, and pleasure—these are the thirteen great grasped objects. / Grasp these great grasped objects, O son, purified, with your own purified grasping organs 42.232

1.4.s:
gṛhāṇa dhyānayogena mamaivaṃ mokṣamāpsyasi..
evaṃ tvaṃ karmabhirvīra naiṣkarmyaṃ samavāpsyasi.. 42.233 ..
1.4.d:
गृहाण ध्यानयोगेन ममैवं मोक्षमाप्स्यसि..
एवं त्वं कर्मभिर्वीर नैष्कर्म्यं समवाप्स्यसि.. 42.233 ..
1.4.m: by the yoga of meditation on me; thus you will attain liberation. / Thus, O hero, through actions you will attain actionlessness. 42.233

1.4.s:
śulbaṃrasena saṃviddhaṃ dakṣo hema yathāśnute..
varṇāśramācāravatā mayi saṃnyastakarmaṇā.. 42.234 ..
1.4.d:
शुल्बंरसेन संविद्धं दक्षो हेम यथाश्नुते..
वर्णाश्रमाचारवता मयि संन्यस्तकर्मणा.. 42.234 ..
1.4.m: Just as a skilled person obtains gold when copper is penetrated with quicksilver, / so for one observing the conduct of castes and stages of life, who has renounced actions to me, 42.234

1.4.s:
madanudhyānayuktena mokṣo nāstīha durlabhaḥ..
tasmādevaṃ vartamāno nanda vrataparāyaṇaḥ.. 42.235 ..
1.4.d:
मदनुध्यानयुक्तेन मोक्षो नास्तीह दुर्लभः..
तस्मादेवं वर्तमानो नन्द व्रतपरायणः.. 42.235 ..
1.4.m: and is engaged in continuous meditation on me, liberation is not hard to attain here. / Therefore, living in this manner, devoted to vows, rejoice! 42.235

1.4.s:
uddhṛtya saptapuruṣāllam̐yaṃ mayi gamiṣyasi..
sāṃprataṃ pratibhāsyaṃti vedaścāpaṭhitā api.. 42.236 ..
1.4.d:
उद्धृत्य सप्तपुरुषाल्लम्̐यं मयि गमिष्यसि..
सांप्रतं प्रतिभास्यंति वेदश्चापठिता अपि.. 42.236 ..
1.4.m: Having delivered seven generations, you will attain dissolution in me. / Even unstudied, the Vedas will shine forth to you right now. 42.236

1.4.s:
tatastvaṃ koṭitīrthe ca yajñe vai harimedhasaḥ..
yāhi tatra bhaviṣyaṃ te sarvaṃ māturabhīpsitam.. 42.237 ..
1.4.d:
ततस्त्वं कोटितीर्थे च यज्ञे वै हरिमेधसः..
याहि तत्र भविष्यं ते सर्वं मातुरभीप्सितम्.. 42.237 ..
1.4.m: Then go to Koṭitīrtha, / to the sacrifice of Harimedhas; there all that your mother desires will come to pass for you." 42.237

1.4.s:
ityuktvā bhagavānviṣṇurmūrtimadhye viveśa ha..
vilokya māno nimiṣaṃ mātrā caiva sutena ca.. 42.238 ..
1.4.d:
इत्युक्त्वा भगवान्विष्णुर्मूर्तिमध्ये विवेश ह..
विलोक्य मानो निमिषं मात्रा चैव सुतेन च.. 42.238 ..
1.4.m: Having spoken thus, the Lord Viṣṇu entered the interior of the image, / while being watched for a moment by the mother and her son. 42.238

1.4.s:
tato mūrti namaskṛtya vāsudevasya vismitaḥ..
aitareyaḥ svajananīṃ mudito vākyamabravīt.. 42.239 ..
1.4.d:
ततो मूर्ति नमस्कृत्य वासुदेवस्य विस्मितः..
ऐतरेयः स्वजननीं मुदितो वाक्यमब्रवीत्.. 42.239 ..
1.4.m: Then, having bowed to the image of Vāsudeva, astonished, / Aitareya, overjoyed, spoke words to his mother: 42.239

1.4.s:
purāhamabhavaṃ śūdro bhītaḥ saṃsāradoṣataḥ..
pariniṣṭhāgataṃ dharmaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ.. 42.240 ..
1.4.d:
पुराहमभवं शूद्रो भीतः संसारदोषतः..
परिनिष्ठागतं धर्मं ब्राह्मणं शरणं गतः.. 42.240 ..
1.4.m: "Formerly I was a Śūdra, afraid of the evil of saṃsāra; / I took refuge in a brahmin who had attained supreme steadfastness in duty. 42.240

1.4.s:
sa kṛpālurmama prāha mantraṃ vai dvādaśākṣaram..
sademaṃ japacetyuktvā tamahaṃ japtavānsadā.. 42.241 ..
1.4.d:
स कृपालुर्मम प्राह मन्त्रं वै द्वादशाक्षरम्..
सदेमं जपचेत्युक्त्वा तमहं जप्तवान्सदा.. 42.241 ..
1.4.m: That compassionate one told me the twelve-syllable mantra, / saying: 'Always recite this!' and I recited it constantly. 42.241

1.4.s:
tena jāpyaprabhāvena mamotpattistavodarāt..
jātasmṛtirviṣṇubhaktiḥ sthitiratra ca sarvadā.. 42.242 ..
1.4.d:
तेन जाप्यप्रभावेन ममोत्पत्तिस्तवोदरात्..
जातस्मृतिर्विष्णुभक्तिः स्थितिरत्र च सर्वदा.. 42.242 ..
1.4.m: By the power of that recitation came my birth from your womb, / remembrance of previous births, devotion to Viṣṇu, and constant residence here. 42.242

1.4.s:
idānīṃ ca prayāmyeṣa yajñaṃ taṃ harimedhasaḥ..
tvadrūpaṃ viṣṇuprītyarthaṃ praṇamya tvāṃ prasādaye.. 42.243 ..
1.4.d:
इदानीं च प्रयाम्येष यज्ञं तं हरिमेधसः..
त्वद्रूपं विष्णुप्रीत्यर्थं प्रणम्य त्वां प्रसादये.. 42.243 ..
1.4.m: And now I go to that sacrifice of Harimedhas. / Having bowed to your form for the pleasure of Viṣṇu, I propitiate you." 42.243

1.4.s:
tato mahīnagarakākhye koṭitīrthatalasthitam..
yajantaṃ saṃvṛtaṃ vipraiḥ koṭiśastamupāgamat.. 42.244 ..
1.4.d:
ततो महीनगरकाख्ये कोटितीर्थतलस्थितम्..
यजन्तं संवृतं विप्रैः कोटिशस्तमुपागमत्.. 42.244 ..
1.4.m: Then he approached him who was sacrificing at the site of Koṭitīrtha, / in what is named Mahīnagarakā, surrounded by brahmins in their millions. 42.244

1.4.s:
gehāya mātaraṃ procya sa yajñe proktavāndvijaḥ..
namastasmai bhagavate viṣṇave'kuṇṭhamedhase.. 42.245 ..
1.4.d:
गेहाय मातरं प्रोच्य स यज्ञे प्रोक्तवान्द्विजः..
नमस्तस्मै भगवते विष्णवेऽकुण्ठमेधसे.. 42.245 ..
1.4.m: Having told his mother [to go] home, that twice-born recited at the sacrifice: / 'Homage to that Holy Lord Viṣṇu of unimpaired intellect, 42.245

1.4.s:
yanmāyāmohitadhiyo bhramāmaḥ karmasāgare..
iti ślokaṃ mahārthaṃ te harimedhamukhā dvijāḥ.. 42.246 ..
1.4.d:
यन्मायामोहितधियो भ्रमामः कर्मसागरे..
इति श्लोकं महार्थं ते हरिमेधमुखा द्विजाः.. 42.246 ..
1.4.m: deluded by whose māyā we wander in the ocean of karma.' / Hearing this verse of great meaning, those brahmins headed by Harimedhas 42.246

1.4.s:
ākarṇyāsanapūjādyaiḥ pūjayāmāsuraṃga tam..
tato vedārthanaipuṇyaistena te toṣitā dvijāḥ.. 42.247 ..
1.4.d:
आकर्ण्यासनपूजाद्यैः पूजयामासुरंग तम्..
ततो वेदार्थनैपुण्यैस्तेन ते तोषिता द्विजाः.. 42.247 ..
1.4.m: honored him, dear one, with seat, hospitality, and the like. / Then those twice-born, pleased by his mastery of the meaning of the Vedas, 42.247

1.4.s:
pradadurdakṣiṇāṃ sarvāṃ harimedhāḥ sutāmapi..
dravyaṃ kanyāṃ ca saṃgṛhya svagṛhaṃ samupāgamat.. 42.248 ..
1.4.d:
प्रददुर्दक्षिणां सर्वां हरिमेधाः सुतामपि..
द्रव्यं कन्यां च संगृह्य स्वगृहं समुपागमत्.. 42.248 ..
1.4.m: gave all their sacrificial gifts, and Harimedhas gave his daughter too. / Taking the wealth and the maiden, he went to his home. 42.248

1.4.s:
vandayitvā svajananīṃ putrānutpādya cāmalān..
iṣṭvā yajñairaitareyo dvādaśīvratatatparaḥ.. 42.249 ..
1.4.d:
वन्दयित्वा स्वजननीं पुत्रानुत्पाद्य चामलान्..
इष्ट्वा यज्ञैरैतरेयो द्वादशीव्रततत्परः.. 42.249 ..
1.4.m: Having paid homage to his mother and begotten faultless sons, / having sacrificed with sacrifices, Aitareya, devoted to the vow of the twelfth day (Dvādaśī), 42.249

1.4.s:
vāsudevānudhyānena mokṣaṃ paścādupāgataḥ..
evaṃvidho vāsudevaḥ svayamatrāsti bhārata.. 42.250 ..
1.4.d:
वासुदेवानुध्यानेन मोक्षं पश्चादुपागतः..
एवंविधो वासुदेवः स्वयमत्रास्ति भारत.. 42.250 ..
1.4.m: later attained liberation through continuous meditation on Vāsudeva. / Such a Vāsudeva is here in person, O descendant of Bharata! 42.250

1.4.s:
yoryayetpūjayetstauti sarvaṃ tasyākṣayaṃ viduḥ..
śivadharmeṣu yatproktaṃ phalaṃ pūrvaṃ mayā tava.. 42.251 ..
1.4.d:
योर्ययेत्पूजयेत्स्तौति सर्वं तस्याक्षयं विदुः..
शिवधर्मेषु यत्प्रोक्तं फलं पूर्वं मया तव.. 42.251 ..
1.4.m: Whoever praises, worships, or lauds [him], they know that all becomes imperishable for him. / Whatever fruit was previously told to you by me regarding Śaiva duties, 42.251

1.4.s:
tādṛśaṃ labhate martyo vāsudevaprasādataḥ.. 42.252 ..
iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ prathame māheśvarakhaṇḍe kaumārikākhaṇḍe śrīvṛddhavāsudevamāhātmyavarṇana aitareyabrāhmaṇacaritravarṇanaṃnāma dvicatvāriṃśo'dhyāyaḥ.. 42 .. cha ..
1.4.d:
तादृशं लभते मर्त्यो वासुदेवप्रसादतः.. 42.252 ..
इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां प्रथमे माहेश्वरखण्डे कौमारिकाखण्डे श्रीवृद्धवासुदेवमाहात्म्यवर्णन ऐतरेयब्राह्मणचरित्रवर्णनंनाम द्विचत्वारिंशोऽध्यायः.. 42 .. छ ..
1.4.m:
such [fruit] a mortal obtains through the grace of Vāsudeva. 42.252
Thus ends the forty-second chapter, named 'The Description of the Deeds of the Brahmin Aitareya, in the Description of the Greatness of the Venerable Vṛddhavāsudeva', in the Kaumārikākhaṇḍa of the first section, the Māheśvarakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skandapurāṇa, a collection of eighty-one thousand [verses]. 42.

1.4.s:
..śrīnārada uvāca..
tato'haṃ pārtha bhūyo'pi janānugrahakāmyayā..
pratyakṣadevaṃ mārtaṃḍamatrānetumiyeṣa ha.. 43.1 ..
1.4.d:
..श्रीनारद उवाच..
ततोऽहं पार्थ भूयोऽपि जनानुग्रहकाम्यया..
प्रत्यक्षदेवं मार्तंडमत्रानेतुमियेष ह.. 43.1 ..
1.4.m: The venerable Nārada said: / "Then, O son of Pṛthā, desiring to show grace to the people once more, / I wished to bring here the manifest god, the sun. 43.1

1.4.s:
sarveṣāṃ prāṇināṃ yasmāduḍupo bhagavānraviḥ..
ihāmutra ca kauṃteya viśvaddhārī ravirmataḥ.. 43.2 ..
1.4.d:
सर्वेषां प्राणिनां यस्मादुडुपो भगवान्रविः..
इहामुत्र च कौंतेय विश्वद्धारी रविर्मतः.. 43.2 ..
1.4.m: For the Lord Sun is the boat for all living beings; / in this world and the next, O son of Kuntī, the Sun is held to be the sustainer of the universe. 43.2

1.4.s:
ye smaraṃti raviṃ bhaktyā kīrtayaṃti ca ye narāḥ..
pūjayaṃti ca ye nityaṃ kṛtārthāste na saṃśayaḥ.. 43.3 ..
1.4.d:
ये स्मरंति रविं भक्त्या कीर्तयंति च ये नराः..
पूजयंति च ये नित्यं कृतार्थास्ते न संशयः.. 43.3 ..
1.4.m: Those men who remember the Sun with devotion and who praise him, / and who constantly worship him, have accomplished their ends—there is no doubt. 43.3

1.4.s:
sūryabhaktiparā ye ca nityaṃ tadgatamānasāḥ..
ye smaraṃti sadā sūryaṃ na te duḥkhasya bhājinaḥ.. 43.4 ..
1.4.d:
सूर्यभक्तिपरा ये च नित्यं तद्गतमानसाः..
ये स्मरंति सदा सूर्यं न ते दुःखस्य भाजिनः.. 43.4 ..
1.4.m: And those who are devoted to devotion to the Sun, their minds ever fixed on him, / who constantly remember the Sun, do not experience sorrow. / (43.4)

1.4.s:
bhavanāni manojñāni vividhābharaṇāḥ striyaḥ..
dhanaṃ cādṛṣṭaparyaṃtaṃ sūryapūjāvidheḥ phalam.. 43.5 ..
1.4.d:
भवनानि मनोज्ञानि विविधाभरणाः स्त्रियः..
धनं चादृष्टपर्यंतं सूर्यपूजाविधेः फलम्.. 43.5 ..
1.4.m: Delightful mansions, women adorned with varied jewels, / and limitless wealth are the fruit of the rites of worshipping the Sun. / (43.5)

1.4.s:
durlabhā bhaktiḥ sūrye vā durlabhaṃ tasya cārcanam..
dānaṃ ca durlabhaṃ tasmai tato homaśca durlabhaḥ.. 43.6 ..
1.4.d:
दुर्लभा भक्तिः सूर्ये वा दुर्लभं तस्य चार्चनम्..
दानं च दुर्लभं तस्मै ततो होमश्च दुर्लभः.. 43.6 ..
1.4.m: Devotion to the Sun is rare indeed, and worshipping him is hard to attain; / giving to him is hard to attain, and offering oblation to him is harder still. / (43.6)

1.4.s:
namaskārādisaṃyuktaṃ ravirityakṣaradvayam..
jihvāgre vartate yasya saphalaṃ tasya jīvitam.. 43.7 ..
1.4.d:
नमस्कारादिसंयुक्तं रविरित्यक्षरद्वयम्..
जिह्वाग्रे वर्तते यस्य सफलं तस्य जीवितम्.. 43.7 ..
1.4.m: He on the tip of whose tongue rests the two-syllable word 'Ravi', / joined with obeisance and the rest—fruitful is his life. / (43.7)

1.4.s:
ityahaṃ hṛdi saṃciṃtya māhātmyaṃ ravijaṃ mahat..
pūrṇaṃ varṣaśataṃ pārtha raviṃ bhaktyā hyatoṣayam.. 43.8 ..
1.4.d:
इत्यहं हृदि संचिंत्य माहात्म्यं रविजं महत्..
पूर्णं वर्षशतं पार्थ रविं भक्त्या ह्यतोषयम्.. 43.8 ..
1.4.m: Reflecting in my heart on this great māhātmya born of the Sun, / for a full hundred years, O Pārtha, I gratified the Sun with devotion. / (43.8)

1.4.s:
japena suviśuddhena cchandasāṃ vāyubhojanaḥ..
tataḥ khāddvitīyāṃ mūrtiṃ kṛtvā yogabalādvibhuḥ.. 43.9 ..
1.4.d:
जपेन सुविशुद्धेन च्छन्दसां वायुभोजनः..
ततः खाद्द्वितीयां मूर्तिं कृत्वा योगबलाद्विभुः.. 43.9 ..
1.4.m: Subsisting on air with completely pure recitation / of the Vedic metres, the Lord then formed a second form from the sky by the power of yoga, / (43.9)

1.4.s: tejasā durdṛśo bhāsvānpratyakṣaḥ samajāyata.. 43.10 ..
1.4.d: तेजसा दुर्दृशो भास्वान्प्रत्यक्षः समजायत.. 43.10 ..
1.4.m: and the shining one, difficult to behold with his brilliance, became visible before my eyes. / (43.10)

1.4.s:
tamahaṃ prāṃjalirbhūtvā namaskṛtya raviṃ prabhum..
sāmabhirvividhairdevaṃ paryatoṣayamīśvaram.. 43.11 ..
1.4.d:
तमहं प्रांजलिर्भूत्वा नमस्कृत्य रविं प्रभुम्..
सामभिर्विविधैर्देवं पर्यतोषयमीश्वरम्.. 43.11 ..
1.4.m: Folding my hands in reverence and bowing to the Lord, the Sun, / I fully gratified the divine Īśvara with varied Sāman chants. / (43.11)

1.4.s:
tuṣṭo māmāha varado devarṣe suciraṃ tvayā..
tapasārādhito'smīti varaṃ vṛṇu yathepsitam.. 43.12 ..
1.4.d:
तुष्टो मामाह वरदो देवर्षे सुचिरं त्वया..
तपसाराधितोऽस्मीति वरं वृणु यथेप्सितम्.. 43.12 ..
1.4.m: Pleased, the boon-giver said to me: 'O celestial seer, for a very long time / I have been worshipped by you with austerity; choose a boon as you desire.' / (43.12)

1.4.s:
ityukto'haṃ lokanāthaṃ prāṃjaliḥ prāstuvaṃ vacaḥ..
yadi tuṣṭo bhavānmahyaṃ yadi deyo varo mama.. 43.13 ..
1.4.d:
इत्युक्तोऽहं लोकनाथं प्रांजलिः प्रास्तुवं वचः..
यदि तुष्टो भवान्मह्यं यदि देयो वरो मम.. 43.13 ..
1.4.m: Thus addressed, I praised the lord of the world with folded hands and words: / 'If you are pleased with me, if a boon is to be granted to me, / (43.13)

1.4.s:
tataste kāmarūpe yā kalā nātha pravartate..
rājavardhanarājñā yā''rādhitā ca janaiḥ purā.. 43.14 ..
1.4.d:
ततस्ते कामरूपे या कला नाथ प्रवर्तते..
राजवर्धनराज्ञा या'ऽराधिता च जनैः पुरा.. 43.14 ..
1.4.m: then, O Lord, that part of you which is present in Kāmarūpa, / which was formerly worshipped by King Rājavardhana and by the people— / (43.14)

1.4.s:
tayā ca kalayā bhāno sadātra sthātumarhasi..
tatastatheti devena prokte tuṣṭena bhārata.. 43.15 ..
1.4.d:
तया च कलया भानो सदात्र स्थातुमर्हसि..
ततस्तथेति देवेन प्रोक्ते तुष्टेन भारत.. 43.15 ..
1.4.m: O Sun, you should remain here forever by that very part.' / Then, when the delighted god said, 'So be it,' O Bhārata, / (43.15)

1.4.s:
asthāpayamahaṃ sūryaṃ bhaṭṭādityābhidhānakam..
bhaṭṭenasthāpitaṃ yasmānmayā tasmādravirjagau.. 43.16 ..
1.4.d:
अस्थापयमहं सूर्यं भट्टादित्याभिधानकम्..
भट्टेनस्थापितं यस्मान्मया तस्माद्रविर्जगौ.. 43.16 ..
1.4.m: I installed the Sun under the name Bhaṭṭāditya; / because it was installed by me, a bhaṭṭa, the Sun declared it so. / (43.16)

1.4.s:
tataḥ saṃpūjya taṃ puṣpaiḥ kṛtāveśamahaṃ ravim..
bhaktyudrekāplutāṃgo'tha stutimetāmathācaram.. 43.17 ..
1.4.d:
ततः संपूज्य तं पुष्पैः कृतावेशमहं रविम्..
भक्त्युद्रेकाप्लुतांगोऽथ स्तुतिमेतामथाचरम्.. 43.17 ..
1.4.m: Then, having worshipped that Sun who had entered into [the icon] with flowers, / my limbs bathed in an excess of devotion, I then performed this hymn of praise / (43.17)

1.4.s:
sarvavedarahasyaiśca nāmabhiśca śatāṣṭabhiḥ..
saptasaptiraciṃtyātmā mahākāruṇikottamaḥ.. 43.18 ..
1.4.d:
सर्ववेदरहस्यैश्च नामभिश्च शताष्टभिः..
सप्तसप्तिरचिंत्यात्मा महाकारुणिकोत्तमः.. 43.18 ..
1.4.m: with the one hundred and eight names that are the secrets of all the Vedas: / 'Possessor of seven steeds, Unfathomable in Self, Supreme Great Compassionate One, / (43.18)

1.4.s:
saṃjīvano jayo jīvo jīvanātho jagatpatiḥ..
kālāśrayaḥ kālakartā mahāyogī mahāmatiḥ.. 43.19 ..
1.4.d:
संजीवनो जयो जीवो जीवनाथो जगत्पतिः..
कालाश्रयः कालकर्ता महायोगी महामतिः.. 43.19 ..
1.4.m: Reviver, Victorious, Life-principle, Lord of Life, Master of the World, / Refuge of Time, Maker of Time, Great Yogin, Great of Intellect, / (43.19)

1.4.s:
bhūtāṃtakaraṇo devaḥ kamalānandanandanaḥ..
sahasrapācca varado divyakuṇḍalamaṇḍitaḥ.. 43.20 ..
1.4.d:
भूतांतकरणो देवः कमलानन्दनन्दनः..
सहस्रपाच्च वरदो दिव्यकुण्डलमण्डितः.. 43.20 ..
1.4.m: Bringer of the End of Beings, God, Delighter in the Joy of the Lotus, / Thousand-footed, Giver of Boons, Adorned with Divine Earrings, / (43.20)

1.4.s:
dharmapriyocitātmā ca savitā vāyuvāhanaḥ..
ādityo'krodhanaḥ sūryo raśmimālī vibhāvasuḥ.. 43.21 ..
1.4.d:
धर्मप्रियोचितात्मा च सविता वायुवाहनः..
आदित्योऽक्रोधनः सूर्यो रश्मिमाली विभावसुः.. 43.21 ..
1.4.m: Lover of Dharma, Fit in Nature, Savitṛ, Borne on the Wind, / Āditya, Free from Anger, Sūrya, Garlanded with Rays, Fire, / (43.21)

1.4.s:
dinakṛddinahṛnmaunī suratho rathināṃvaraḥ..
rājñīpatiḥ svarṇaretāḥ pūṣā tvaṣṭā divākaraḥ.. 43.22 ..
1.4.d:
दिनकृद्दिनहृन्मौनी सुरथो रथिनांवरः..
राज्ञीपतिः स्वर्णरेताः पूषा त्वष्टा दिवाकरः.. 43.22 ..
1.4.m: Maker of Day, Destroyer of Day, Silent Sage, He of the Fine Chariot, Foremost of Charioteers, / Husband of Rājñī, Golden-seeded, Pūṣan, Tvaṣṭṛ, Day-maker, / (43.22)

1.4.s:
ākāśatilako dhātā saṃvibhāgī manoharaḥ..
prajñaḥ prajāpatirdhanyo viṣṇuḥ śrīśo bhiṣagvaraḥ.. 43.23 ..
1.4.d:
आकाशतिलको धाता संविभागी मनोहरः..
प्रज्ञः प्रजापतिर्धन्यो विष्णुः श्रीशो भिषग्वरः.. 43.23 ..
1.4.m: Ornament of the Sky, Sustainer, Allotter of Shares, Charming One, / Wise, Lord of Creatures, Auspicious, Viṣṇu, Lord of Śrī, Foremost Physician, / (43.23)

1.4.s:
ālokakṛllokanātho lokapālanamaskṛtaḥ..
viditāśayaśca sunayo mahātmā bhaktavatsalaḥ.. 43.24 ..
1.4.d:
आलोककृल्लोकनाथो लोकपालनमस्कृतः..
विदिताशयश्च सुनयो महात्मा भक्तवत्सलः.. 43.24 ..
1.4.m: Maker of Light, Lord of the World, Saluted by the World-Guardians, / Discerner of Intentions, Rightly Guided, Great Soul, Fond of Devotees, / (43.24)

1.4.s:
kīrtikīrtikaro nityo rociṣṇuḥ kalmaṣāpahaḥ..
jitānando mahāvīryo haṃsaḥ saṃhārakārakaḥ.. 43.25 ..
1.4.d:
कीर्तिकीर्तिकरो नित्यो रोचिष्णुः कल्मषापहः..
जितानन्दो महावीर्यो हंसः संहारकारकः.. 43.25 ..
1.4.m: Fame, Bestower of Fame, Eternal, Radiant, Dispeller of Sins, / Victorious in Joy, Of Great Valour, Swan, Cause of Dissolution, / (43.25)

1.4.s:
kṛtakṛtyaḥ susaṃgaśca bahujño vacasāṃ patiḥ..
viśvapūjyo mṛtyuhāri ghṛṇī dharmasya kāraṇam.. 43.26 ..
1.4.d:
कृतकृत्यः सुसंगश्च बहुज्ञो वचसां पतिः..
विश्वपूज्यो मृत्युहारि घृणी धर्मस्य कारणम्.. 43.26 ..
1.4.m: Accomplisher of Goals, Excellent in Company, All-Knowing, Lord of Speech, / Worshipful to All, Remover of Death, Compassionate, Cause of Dharma, / (43.26)

1.4.s:
praṇatārtiharo'roga āyuṣyamānsukhadaḥ sukhī..
maṅgalaṃ puṇḍarīkākṣo vratī vrataphalapradaḥ.. 43.27 ..
1.4.d:
प्रणतार्तिहरोऽरोग आयुष्यमान्सुखदः सुखी..
मङ्गलं पुण्डरीकाक्षो व्रती व्रतफलप्रदः.. 43.27 ..
1.4.m: Remover of the Affliction of the Bowed, Free from Disease, Long-lived, Giver of Happiness, Happy, / Auspiciousness, Lotus-eyed, Observant of Vows, Bestower of the Fruit of Vows, / (43.27)

1.4.s:
śuciḥ pūrṇo mokṣamārgadātā bhoktā maheśvaraḥ..
dhanvaṃtariḥ priyābhāṣī dhanurvedavidekarāṭa.. 43.28 ..
1.4.d:
शुचिः पूर्णो मोक्षमार्गदाता भोक्ता महेश्वरः..
धन्वंतरिः प्रियाभाषी धनुर्वेदविदेकराट.. 43.28 ..
1.4.m: Pure, Complete, Giver of the Path of Liberation, Enjoyer, Great Lord, / Dhanvantari, Speaking Kindly, Knower of Archery, Sole Monarch, / (43.28)

1.4.s:
jagatpitā dhūmaketurvidhūto dhvāṃtahā guruḥ..
gopatiśca kṛtātithyaḥ śubhācāraḥ śucipriyaḥ.. 43.29 ..
1.4.d:
जगत्पिता धूमकेतुर्विधूतो ध्वांतहा गुरुः..
गोपतिश्च कृतातिथ्यः शुभाचारः शुचिप्रियः.. 43.29 ..
1.4.m: Father of the Universe, Comet, Cleansed, Dispeller of Darkness, Guru, / Lord of the Rays, Host of Guests, Of Auspicious Conduct, Fond of the Pure, / (43.29)

1.4.s:
sāmapriyo lokabandhurnaikarūpo yugādikṛt..
dharmaseturlokasākṣī kheṭataṛ sarvadaḥ prabhuḥ.. 43.30 ..
1.4.d:
सामप्रियो लोकबन्धुर्नैकरूपो युगादिकृत्..
धर्मसेतुर्लोकसाक्षी खेटतऋ सर्वदः प्रभुः.. 43.30 ..
1.4.m: Lover of Sāman Chants, Friend of the World, Multiform, Originator of the Yugas, / Bridge of Dharma, Witness of the World, Roamer of the Sky, All-Giver, Sovereign Lord.' / (43.30)

1.4.s:
mayaivaṃ saṃstuto bhānurnāmnāmaṣṭaśatena ca..
tuṣyatāṃ sarvalokānāṃ sarvalokapriyo vibhuḥ.. 43.31 ..
1.4.d:
मयैवं संस्तुतो भानुर्नाम्नामष्टशतेन च..
तुष्यतां सर्वलोकानां सर्वलोकप्रियो विभुः.. 43.31 ..
1.4.m: Thus was the Sun praised by me with the one hundred and eight names. / May the all-pervading Lord, dear to all the worlds, be pleased with all beings! / (43.31)

1.4.s:
ityevaṃ saṃstavātprīto bhāskaro māmavocata..
sadātra kalayā sthāsye devarṣe tvatpriyepsayā.. 43.32 ..
1.4.d:
इत्येवं संस्तवात्प्रीतो भास्करो मामवोचत..
सदात्र कलया स्थास्ये देवर्षे त्वत्प्रियेप्सया.. 43.32 ..
1.4.m: Delighted by this hymn of praise, the Sun said to me: / 'O celestial seer, desiring to do what is pleasing to you, I shall always dwell here by my part. / (43.32)

1.4.s:
yo māmatra mahābhaktyā bhaṭṭādityaṃ prapūjayet..
sahasraśaḥ kā marūpe saṃpūjyāpnoti tatphalam.. 43.33 ..
1.4.d:
यो मामत्र महाभक्त्या भट्टादित्यं प्रपूजयेत्..
सहस्रशः का मरूपे संपूज्याप्नोति तत्फलम्.. 43.33 ..
1.4.m: Whoever worships me here as Bhaṭṭāditya with great devotion, / attains the same fruit as worshipping me a thousand times in Kāmarūpa. / (43.33)

1.4.s:
māmuddiśya ca yo vipraḥ svalpaṃ vā yadi vā bahu..
dāsyate'trākṣayaṃ tacca grahīṣye karajaṃ yathā.. 43.34 ..
1.4.d:
मामुद्दिश्य च यो विप्रः स्वल्पं वा यदि वा बहु..
दास्यतेऽत्राक्षयं तच्च ग्रहीष्ये करजं यथा.. 43.34 ..
1.4.m: And whatever a brahmin offers here for my sake, whether little or much, / that shall become inexhaustible, and I will accept it as if handed to me. / (43.34)

1.4.s:
raktotpalaiśca kahlāraiḥ kesaraiḥ karavīrakaiḥ..
śatatrayairmahāpdamai ravivāreṇa mānavaḥ.. 43.35 ..
1.4.d:
रक्तोत्पलैश्च कह्लारैः केसरैः करवीरकैः..
शतत्रयैर्महाप्दमै रविवारेण मानवः.. 43.35 ..
1.4.m: With red lotuses, kahlāra water-lilies, saffron blossoms, oleanders, / and three hundred great lotuses, a person on a Sunday, / (43.35)

1.4.s:
saptamyāmatha ṣaṣṭhyāṃ vā ye'rcayiṣyaṃti māmiha..
yānyānprārthayate kāmāṃstāṃtānprāpsyati niścitam.. 43.36 ..
1.4.d:
सप्तम्यामथ षष्ठ्यां वा येऽर्चयिष्यंति मामिह..
यान्यान्प्रार्थयते कामांस्तांतान्प्राप्स्यति निश्चितम्.. 43.36 ..
1.4.m: or those who worship me here on the seventh or the sixth lunar day, / whatever desires one prays for, all those one will surely attain. / (43.36)

1.4.s:
darśanānmama bhaktyā ca nāśo vyādhidaridrayoḥ..
praṇāmātsvargamāpnoti śrutvā mokṣaṃ ca nityaśaḥ.. 43.37 ..
1.4.d:
दर्शनान्मम भक्त्या च नाशो व्याधिदरिद्रयोः..
प्रणामात्स्वर्गमाप्नोति श्रुत्वा मोक्षं च नित्यशः.. 43.37 ..
1.4.m: From the darśana of me with devotion, illness and poverty are destroyed; / from obeisance one attains heaven, and by constantly listening [to this] one attains liberation. / (43.37)

1.4.s:
abhaktiṃ yaśca kartā me sa gacchenniściṃtaṃ kṣayam..
aṣṭottaraśataṃ nāma mamāgre yattvayeritam.. 43.38 ..
1.4.d:
अभक्तिं यश्च कर्ता मे स गच्छेन्निश्चिंतं क्षयम्..
अष्टोत्तरशतं नाम ममाग्रे यत्त्वयेरितम्.. 43.38 ..
1.4.m: And whoever acts without devotion toward me shall surely go to ruin. / As for this hymn of one hundred and eight names uttered by you before me, / (43.38)

1.4.s:
trikālamekakālaṃ vā paṭhataḥ śrṛṇuyatphalam..
kīrtimānsubhago vidvānsusukhī priyadarśanaḥ.. 43.39 ..
1.4.d:
त्रिकालमेककालं वा पठतः श्रृणुयत्फलम्..
कीर्तिमान्सुभगो विद्वान्सुसुखी प्रियदर्शनः.. 43.39 ..
1.4.m: hear the fruit for one reciting it thrice daily or once daily: / he shall be famous, fortunate, learned, very happy, pleasant to look upon, / (43.39)

1.4.s:
bhavedvarṣaśatāyuśca sarvarogavivarjitaḥ..
yastvidaṃ śrṛṇuyānnityaṃ paṭhedvā prayataḥ śuciḥ.. 43.40 ..
1.4.d:
भवेद्वर्षशतायुश्च सर्वरोगविवर्जितः..
यस्त्विदं श्रृणुयान्नित्यं पठेद्वा प्रयतः शुचिः.. 43.40 ..
1.4.m: endowed with a life of a hundred years, and free from all diseases. / Moreover, whoever listens to this daily, or recites it, restrained and pure, / (43.40)

1.4.s:
akṣayaṃ svalpamapyannaṃ bhavettasyopasādhitam..
vijayī ca bhavennityaṃ tathā jātismaro bhavet.. 43.41 ..
1.4.d:
अक्षयं स्वल्पमप्यन्नं भवेत्तस्योपसाधितम्..
विजयी च भवेन्नित्यं तथा जातिस्मरो भवेत्.. 43.41 ..
1.4.m: even a little food prepared for him shall become inexhaustible; / he shall always be victorious, and he shall remember his past births. / (43.41)

1.4.s:
tasmādetattvayā jāpyaṃ paraṃ svastyayanaṃ mahat..
tathā mamāgre kuṃḍaṃ ca kuru snānārthamuttamam.. 43.42 ..
1.4.d:
तस्मादेतत्त्वया जाप्यं परं स्वस्त्ययनं महत्..
तथा ममाग्रे कुंडं च कुरु स्नानार्थमुत्तमम्.. 43.42 ..
1.4.m: Therefore, this supreme, great benediction must be recited by you; / likewise, create an excellent pool before me for the purpose of ablutions. / (43.42)

1.4.s:
kāmarūpakalā yatra tatra kuṃḍaṃ vane bhavet..
evaṃ dattvā varānbhānustatraivāṃ taradhīyata.. 43.43 ..
1.4.d:
कामरूपकला यत्र तत्र कुंडं वने भवेत्..
एवं दत्त्वा वरान्भानुस्तत्रैवां तरधीयत.. 43.43 ..
1.4.m: Where the part from Kāmarūpa is, there shall be a pool in the forest.' / Having thus granted boons, the Sun vanished on that very spot. / (43.43)

1.4.s:
tato bhāskaravākyena siddheśasya ca savyataḥ..
vanamadhye mayā kuṃḍaṃ kṛtaṃ darbhaśalākayā.. 43.44 ..
1.4.d:
ततो भास्करवाक्येन सिद्धेशस्य च सव्यतः..
वनमध्ये मया कुंडं कृतं दर्भशलाकया.. 43.44 ..
1.4.m: Then, according to the words of the Sun, on the right side of Siddheśa / in the middle of the forest, a pool was made by me with a blade of darbha grass. / (43.44)

1.4.s:
kāmarūpabhavaṃ kuṃḍaṃ vṛkṣāste cāpi bhārata..
saṃlīnāstanmahāścaryaṃ mamājāyata cetasi.. 43.45 ..
1.4.d:
कामरूपभवं कुंडं वृक्षास्ते चापि भारत..
संलीनास्तन्महाश्चर्यं ममाजायत चेतसि.. 43.45 ..
1.4.m: The pool produced from Kāmarūpa, and those trees, O Bhārata, / became merged together—a great wonder arose in my mind. / (43.45)

1.4.s:
māghamāsasya śuklāyāṃ saptamyāṃ strī naro'pi vā..
snānaṃ kuṃḍe śubhaṃ kṛtvā bhaṭṭādityaṃ prapaśyati.. 43.46 ..
1.4.d:
माघमासस्य शुक्लायां सप्तम्यां स्त्री नरोऽपि वा..
स्नानं कुंडे शुभं कृत्वा भट्टादित्यं प्रपश्यति.. 43.46 ..
1.4.m: On the bright seventh day of the month of Māgha, whether a woman or a man / performs an auspicious ablution in the pool and beholds Bhaṭṭāditya, / (43.46)

1.4.s:
tasyānaṃtaṃ bhavetpuṇyaṃ rathaṃ yaśca prapūjayet..
rathayātrāṃ ca kurute yasminyasminnasau pathi.. 43.47 ..
1.4.d:
तस्यानंतं भवेत्पुण्यं रथं यश्च प्रपूजयेत्..
रथयात्रां च कुरुते यस्मिन्यस्मिन्नसौ पथि.. 43.47 ..
1.4.m: limitless merit shall be theirs; and whoever worships his chariot / and performs a chariot procession along whatever path it goes, [attains great reward]. / (43.47)

1.4.s:
ye ca paśyaṃti lokāste dhanyāḥ sarve na saṃśayaḥ..
putradhānyadhanairyuktā nīrujastejasā'nvitāḥ.. 43.48 ..
1.4.d:
ये च पश्यंति लोकास्ते धन्याः सर्वे न संशयः..
पुत्रधान्यधनैर्युक्ता नीरुजस्तेजसाऽन्विताः.. 43.48 ..
1.4.m: And those people who see [it] are all blessed, without a doubt; / endowed with sons, grain, and wealth, free from disease, and possessed of splendor,

1.4.s:
bhaviṣyaṃti narāste ye kārayaṃti rathotsavam..
gaṃgādisarvatīrtheṣu yatphalaṃ kīrtitaṃ budhaiḥ.. 43.49 ..
1.4.d:
भविष्यंति नरास्ते ये कारयंति रथोत्सवम्..
गंगादिसर्वतीर्थेषु यत्फलं कीर्तितं बुधैः.. 43.49 ..
1.4.m: those men will become—they who cause the chariot festival to be performed. / Whatever fruit is proclaimed by the wise at all the sacred fords such as the Gaṅgā,

1.4.s:
bhaṭṭādityasya kuṃḍe ca tatphalaṃ saptamīdine..
tatra kuṃḍe ca yaḥ snātvā sūryārghyaṃ prayacchati..
kapilā gośatasyāsau dattasya phalamaśnute.. 43.50 ..
1.4.d:
भट्टादित्यस्य कुंडे च तत्फलं सप्तमीदिने..
तत्र कुंडे च यः स्नात्वा सूर्यार्घ्यं प्रयच्छति..
कपिला गोशतस्यासौ दत्तस्य फलमश्नुते.. 43.50 ..
1.4.m: that fruit is [obtained] at the pool of Bhaṭṭāditya on the seventh day. / And he who, having bathed in that pool, offers an arghya water-oblation to the sun, / attains the fruit of giving a hundred brown cows.

1.4.s:
..arjura uvāca..
vāsudevādayaḥ sarve vadaṃtyevaṃ mahāmune.. 43.51 ..
1.4.d:
..अर्जुर उवाच..
वासुदेवादयः सर्वे वदंत्येवं महामुने.. 43.51 ..
1.4.m: Arjuna said: / All [sages], beginning with Vāsudeva, say this, O great sage:

1.4.s:
bhāskarārghaṃ vinā pātaḥ kṛtaṃ sarvaṃ ca niṣphalam..
tasyāhaṃ śrotumicchāmi vidhiṃ vidhividāṃ vara.. 43.52 ..
1.4.d:
भास्करार्घं विना पातः कृतं सर्वं च निष्फलम्..
तस्याहं श्रोतुमिच्छामि विधिं विधिविदां वर.. 43.52 ..
1.4.m: Without the morning arghya water-oblation to the sun, everything done is fruitless. / I desire to hear the rule for that, O best among knowers of rules!

1.4.s:
..nārada uvāca..
yathā brahmādayo devā yacchaṃtyarghaṃ mahātmane..
bhāskarāya śrṛṇu tvaṃ taṃ vidhiṃ sarvāghanāśanam.. 43.53 ..
1.4.d:
..नारद उवाच..
यथा ब्रह्मादयो देवा यच्छंत्यर्घं महात्मने..
भास्कराय श्रृणु त्वं तं विधिं सर्वाघनाशनम्.. 43.53 ..
1.4.m: Nārada said: / Listen to that rule, destroyer of all sins, / by which the gods, beginning with Brahmā, offer the arghya water-oblation to the high-souled Bhāskara.

1.4.s: prathamaṃ tāvatpratyuṣe udite sūrye śucirbhūtvā gomayakṛtamaṃḍalasyopari raktacaṃdanena maṃḍalakaṃ kṛtvā tatastāmrapātre raktacaṃdanodakaśvetacaṃdanādidravyaiḥ prapūraṇaṃ kṛtvā tanmadhye hemākṣatadūrvādadhisarpīṣi parikṣipya sthāpayet.. 43.54 ..
1.4.d: प्रथमं तावत्प्रत्युषे उदिते सूर्ये शुचिर्भूत्वा गोमयकृतमंडलस्योपरि रक्तचंदनेन मंडलकं कृत्वा ततस्ताम्रपात्रे रक्तचंदनोदकश्वेतचंदनादिद्रव्यैः प्रपूरणं कृत्वा तन्मध्ये हेमाक्षतदूर्वादधिसर्पीषि परिक्षिप्य स्थापयेत्.. 43.54 ..
1.4.m: First, having become pure at dawn when the sun has risen, having drawn a small maṇḍala with red sandalwood paste upon a maṇḍala made with cow dung, having then filled a copper vessel with substances such as red sandalwood water and white sandalwood, and having placed inside it gold, unbroken grains, dūrvā grass, curd, and clarified butter, one should set it down.

1.4.s:
svaśarīramālabhet anena maṃtreṇa..
oṃkhakholkāya namaḥ..
saptavārānuccārya sthātavyam..
tena śuddhirupasaṃjāyate dehasyārcārhatā bhavati..
paścādāsanasthaṃ devaṃ savitāraṃ maṃḍalamadhye dvādaśātmakaṃ surādibhiḥ saṃpūjyamānaṃ dhyātvā pūrvoktamarghapātraṃ śirasi kṛtvā bhūmau jānunī nipātya sūryābhimukhastadgatamanābhūtvārghamaṃtramudāharet..
taducyate sūryavaktrādvinirgatamiti.. 43.55 ..
1.4.d:
स्वशरीरमालभेत् अनेन मंत्रेण..
ओंखखोल्काय नमः..
सप्तवारानुच्चार्य स्थातव्यम्..
तेन शुद्धिरुपसंजायते देहस्यार्चार्हता भवति..
पश्चादासनस्थं देवं सवितारं मंडलमध्ये द्वादशात्मकं सुरादिभिः संपूज्यमानं ध्यात्वा पूर्वोक्तमर्घपात्रं शिरसि कृत्वा भूमौ जानुनी निपात्य सूर्याभिमुखस्तद्गतमनाभूत्वार्घमंत्रमुदाहरेत्..
