तदुच्यते सूर्यवक्त्राद्विनिर्गतमिति.. 43.55 ..
1.4.m: One should touch one's own body with this mantra: / 'Oṃ, homage to Khakholka.' / One should stand having recited it seven times. / By that, purification arises, and the body becomes fit for worship. / Afterward, having meditated upon the god Savitṛ seated on his seat in the middle of the maṇḍala, twelve-souled, being worshipped by the gods and others; having placed the previously mentioned arghya vessel on one's head; having lowered both knees to the earth; facing the sun with a mind fixed on him, one should utter the arghya mantra. / It is spoken as having issued from the mouth of the sun:

1.4.s:
yasyoccāraṇaśabdena rathaṃ saṃsthāpya bhāskaraḥ..
pratigṛhṇāti caivārghyaṃ varamiṣṭaṃ ca yacchati.. 43.56 ..
1.4.d:
यस्योच्चारणशब्देन रथं संस्थाप्य भास्करः..
प्रतिगृह्णाति चैवार्घ्यं वरमिष्टं च यच्छति.. 43.56 ..
1.4.m: At the sound of the recitation of which, having stopped his chariot, / the Sun receives the arghya water-oblation and grants the desired boon:

1.4.s:
oṃyasyāhuḥ sapta cchaṃdāṃsi rathe tiṣṭhaṃti vājinaḥ..
aruṇaḥ sārathiryasya rathavāho'grataḥ sthitaḥ.. 43.57 ..
1.4.d:
ओंयस्याहुः सप्त च्छंदांसि रथे तिष्ठंति वाजिनः..
अरुणः सारथिर्यस्य रथवाहोऽग्रतः स्थितः.. 43.57 ..
1.4.m: 'Oṃ, [to him] whose horses standing on the chariot, they say, are the seven meters; / whose charioteer is Aruṇa, standing in front drawing the chariot;

1.4.s:
jayā ca vijayā caiva jayaṃtī pāpanāśanī..
iḍā ca piṃgalā caiva vahaṃto'śvamukhāstathā.. 43.58 ..
1.4.d:
जया च विजया चैव जयंती पापनाशनी..
इडा च पिंगला चैव वहंतोऽश्वमुखास्तथा.. 43.58 ..
1.4.m: Jayā, Vijayā, and Jayantī, who destroys sin; / Iḍā and Piṅgalā, and those having horse-faces who pull;

1.4.s:
ḍiṃḍiśca śeṣanāgaśca gaṇādhyakṣastathaiva ca..
skaṃdarevaṃtatārkṣyāśca tathā kalmāṣapakṣiṇau.. 43.59 ..
1.4.d:
डिंडिश्च शेषनागश्च गणाध्यक्षस्तथैव च..
स्कंदरेवंततार्क्ष्याश्च तथा कल्माषपक्षिणौ.. 43.59 ..
1.4.m: Ḍiṇḍi, the serpent Śeṣa, and likewise the leader of the gaṇas, / Skanda, Revanta, Tārkṣya, and likewise the two Kalmāṣa birds;

1.4.s:
rājñī ca nikṣubhā devī lalitā caiva saṃjñikā..
tathā yajñabhujo devā ye cānye parikīrtitāḥ.. 43.60 ..
1.4.d:
राज्ञी च निक्षुभा देवी ललिता चैव संज्ञिका..
तथा यज्ञभुजो देवा ये चान्ये परिकीर्तिताः.. 43.60 ..
1.4.m: and Rājñī, the goddess Nikṣubhā, and Lalitā named Saṃjñā; / likewise the gods who partake of sacrifices, and whatever others are proclaimed;

1.4.s:
ebhiḥ parivṛto yo'sāvadharottaravāsibhiḥ..
tamahaṃ lokakartāramāhvayāmi tamopaham.. 43.61 ..
1.4.d:
एभिः परिवृतो योऽसावधरोत्तरवासिभिः..
तमहं लोककर्तारमाह्वयामि तमोपहम्.. 43.61 ..
1.4.m: surrounded by these who dwell below and above— / him, the creator of the world, dispeller of darkness, I invoke.

1.4.s:
ammayo bhagavānbhānuramuṃ yajñaṃ pravartayan..
idamarghyaṃ ca pādyaṃ ca pragṛhāṇa namonamaḥ.. 43.62 ..
1.4.d:
अम्मयो भगवान्भानुरमुं यज्ञं प्रवर्तयन्..
इदमर्घ्यं च पाद्यं च प्रगृहाण नमोनमः.. 43.62 ..
1.4.m: The Lord Sun, consisting of water, setting this sacrifice into motion: / receive this arghya water-oblation and pādya water for washing the feet! Homage, homage [to you]!'

1.4.s:
..āvāhanam..
sahasrakiraṇa varada jīvanarūpa te namaḥ..
iti sāṃnidhyakaraṇam..
oṃvaṣaṭ ityuccārya sūryasya caraṇayugalaṃ paśyan bhuvi padmyāṃ pātrīṃ nirvāpayet pādyaṃ taducyate..
evaṃ pādyaṃ dattvā baddhāṃjaliḥ susvāgatamiti kuryāt..
svāgataṃ bhagavannehi mama prasādaṃ vidhāya āsyatām..
iha gṛhāṇa pūjāṃ ca prasādaṃ ca dhiyā kuru..
tiṣṭha tvaṃ tāvadatraiva yāvatpūjāṃ karomyaham.. 43.63 ..
1.4.d:
..आवाहनम्..
सहस्रकिरण वरद जीवनरूप ते नमः..
इति सांनिध्यकरणम्..
ओंवषट् इत्युच्चार्य सूर्यस्य चरणयुगलं पश्यन् भुवि पद्म्यां पात्रीं निर्वापयेत् पाद्यं तदुच्यते..
एवं पाद्यं दत्त्वा बद्धांजलिः सुस्वागतमिति कुर्यात्..
स्वागतं भगवन्नेहि मम प्रसादं विधाय आस्यताम्..
इह गृहाण पूजां च प्रसादं च धिया कुरु..
तिष्ठ त्वं तावदत्रैव यावत्पूजां करोम्यहम्.. 43.63 ..
1.4.m: The invocation: / 'O thousand-rayed one, giver of boons, whose form is life, homage to you!' / Thus is the bringing of presence. / Uttering 'Oṃ vaṣaṭ', beholding the pair of feet of the sun, one should pour out the vessel into the lotus on the ground; that is called pādya water for washing the feet. / Having thus given the pādya water, with hands folded in reverence, one should perform the welcome: / 'Welcome, O Lord! Come, having shown your favor to me, be seated! / Accept worship here, and grant your favor with your mind! / Remain right here so long as I perform the worship!'

1.4.s:
evaṃ vijñāpanaṃ dadyādanena maṃtreṇa kamalāsanam..
tatkamalāsanaṃ kamalanaṃdana upāviśati..
āsana upaviṣṭasya śeṣāṃ pūjāṃ niyojayet anena vidhānena..
oṃsomamūrtikṣīrodapataye namaḥ..
iti kṣīrādisnapanam..
oṃbhāskarāya nīrava sine namaḥ..
..iti jalasnānam..
tato vāsoyugaṃ śubhraṃ dadyāt anena maṃtreṇa..
idaṃ vāsoyugaṃ sūrya gṛhāṇa kṛpayā mama..
kaṭibhūṣaṇamekaṃ te dvitīyaṃ cāṃgaprāvaraṇam.. 43.64 ..
1.4.d:
एवं विज्ञापनं दद्यादनेन मंत्रेण कमलासनम्..
तत्कमलासनं कमलनंदन उपाविशति..
आसन उपविष्टस्य शेषां पूजां नियोजयेत् अनेन विधानेन..
ओंसोममूर्तिक्षीरोदपतये नमः..
इति क्षीरादिस्नपनम्..
ओंभास्कराय नीरव सिने नमः..
..इति जलस्नानम्..
ततो वासोयुगं शुभ्रं दद्यात् अनेन मंत्रेण..
इदं वासोयुगं सूर्य गृहाण कृपया मम..
कटिभूषणमेकं ते द्वितीयं चांगप्रावरणम्.. 43.64 ..
1.4.m: Thus one should offer a respectful address and a lotus seat with this mantra. / The son of the lotus sits upon that lotus seat. / For him seated upon the seat, one should perform the remainder of the worship according to this procedure: / 'Oṃ, homage to the moon-formed lord of the milk ocean!' / Thus the ceremonial bath with milk and other liquids. / 'Oṃ, homage to the Sun who dwells in water!' / Thus the ritual bath with water. / Then one should offer a pair of clean garments with this mantra: / 'O Sun, accept with mercy this pair of garments of mine: / one an ornament for your waist, and the second a covering for your body.'

1.4.s:
tato yajñopavītaṃ dadyāt anena maṃtreṇa..
sūtrataṃtumayaṃ śuddhaṃ pavitramidamuttamam..
yajñopavītaṃ deveśa pragṛhāṇa namo'stu te.. 43.65 ..
1.4.d:
ततो यज्ञोपवीतं दद्यात् अनेन मंत्रेण..
सूत्रतंतुमयं शुद्धं पवित्रमिदमुत्तमम्..
यज्ञोपवीतं देवेश प्रगृहाण नमोऽस्तु ते.. 43.65 ..
1.4.m: Then one should offer a sacred thread with this mantra: / 'Made of woven threads, pure, this highest sanctifying object, / the sacred thread, O Lord of the gods, accept! Homage be to you!'

1.4.s:
tato yathāśakti śvetamukuṭamudrikādibhūṣaṇāni dadyāt anena maṃtreṇa..
mukuṭo ratnanaddho'yaṃ mudrikāṃ bhūṣaṇāni ca..
alaṃkāraṃ gṛhaṇemaṃ mayā bhaktyā samarpitam.. 43.66 ..
1.4.d:
ततो यथाशक्ति श्वेतमुकुटमुद्रिकादिभूषणानि दद्यात् अनेन मंत्रेण..
मुकुटो रत्ननद्धोऽयं मुद्रिकां भूषणानि च..
अलंकारं गृहणेमं मया भक्त्या समर्पितम्.. 43.66 ..
1.4.m: Then, according to one's means, one should offer ornaments such as a white crown and rings with this mantra: / 'This crown is fastened with jewels, and [this] ring and ornaments; / accept this embellishment offered by me with devotion.'

1.4.s: evamalaṃkāraṃ nivedya paścātkeśarakuṃkumakarpūraraktacaṃdanamiśramanulepanaṃ dadyāt.. 43.67 ..
1.4.d: एवमलंकारं निवेद्य पश्चात्केशरकुंकुमकर्पूररक्तचंदनमिश्रमनुलेपनं दद्यात्.. 43.67 ..
1.4.m: Having thus offered the adornment, one should afterward offer an unguent mixed with saffron, vermilion, camphor, and red sandalwood.

1.4.s:
oṃtavātipriya vṛkṣāṇāṃ raso'yaṃ tigmadīdhite..
sa tavaivocitaḥ svāmingṛhāṇa kṛpayā mama.. 43.68 ..
1.4.d:
ओंतवातिप्रिय वृक्षाणां रसोऽयं तिग्मदीधिते..
स तवैवोचितः स्वामिन्गृहाण कृपया मम.. 43.68 ..
1.4.m: 'Oṃ, this sap of trees is very dear to you, O hot-rayed one; / it is indeed suitable for you, O Lord! Accept it with mercy from me.'

1.4.s: tataścaṃpakajapākaravīrakarṇakakesarakokanadādibhiḥ pūjāṃ kuryāt.. 43.69 ..
1.4.d: ततश्चंपकजपाकरवीरकर्णककेसरकोकनदादिभिः पूजां कुर्यात्.. 43.69 ..
1.4.m: Then one should perform worship with campaka, japā, karavīra, karṇaka, saffron, and red lotus flowers, and others.

1.4.s:
oṃvanaspatiraso divyo gaṃdhāḍhyo gaṃdha uttamaḥ..
āhāraḥ sarvadevānāṃ dhūpo'yaṃ pratigṛhyatām.. 43.70 ..
1.4.d:
ओंवनस्पतिरसो दिव्यो गंधाढ्यो गंध उत्तमः..
आहारः सर्वदेवानां धूपोऽयं प्रतिगृह्यताम्.. 43.70 ..
1.4.m: 'Oṃ, the sap of forest trees, divine, rich in fragrance, the highest scent, / the nourishment of all the gods—may this incense be accepted!'

1.4.s:
..śallakīdhūpamaṃtraḥ..
tataḥ pāyasādiniṣpannaṃ naivedyaṃ nivedayedanena maṃtreṇa..
naivedyamamṛtaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ prāṇavardhanam..
pūrṇapātre mayā dattaṃ pratigṛhṇa prasīda me.. 43.71 ..
1.4.d:
..शल्लकीधूपमंत्रः..
ततः पायसादिनिष्पन्नं नैवेद्यं निवेदयेदनेन मंत्रेण..
नैवेद्यममृतं सर्वभूतानां प्राणवर्धनम्..
पूर्णपात्रे मया दत्तं प्रतिगृह्ण प्रसीद मे.. 43.71 ..
1.4.m: The mantra for the incense of frankincense. / Then one should present a food offering prepared with rice pudding and the like, with this mantra: / 'The food offering is nectar, increasing the life of all beings; / given by me in a full vessel, receive it, be gracious to me!'

1.4.s:
tataḥ śaucodakatāṃbūladīpārārtikaśītalikāpunaḥ pūjādi nivedya yathāśaktyā stutvā sukṛtaṃ duṣkṛtaṃ vā kṣamasveti procya visarjayet..
tato bhūyo namasya hemavastropavītālaṃkārān brāhmaṇāya nivedya nirmālyaṃ saṃhṛtyāṃbhasi nikṣipet.. 43.72 ..
1.4.d:
ततः शौचोदकतांबूलदीपारार्तिकशीतलिकापुनः पूजादि निवेद्य यथाशक्त्या स्तुत्वा सुकृतं दुष्कृतं वा क्षमस्वेति प्रोच्य विसर्जयेत्..
ततो भूयो नमस्य हेमवस्त्रोपवीतालंकारान् ब्राह्मणाय निवेद्य निर्माल्यं संहृत्यांभसि निक्षिपेत्.. 43.72 ..
1.4.m: Then, having presented water for rinsing, betel, a lamp, an ārātika light, a cooling fan, repeated worship, and the like, having praised him according to one's capacity, and saying, 'Forgive good deeds or bad deeds,' one should dismiss him. / Then, having bowed again, having presented the gold, cloth, sacred thread, and ornaments to a brahmin, and having gathered the remnant of the offerings, one should cast it into the water.

1.4.s:
..ityarghyadānavidhiḥ..
ya evaṃ bhāskarāyārghyaṃ mūrtau maṃḍalake'pi vā..
nityaṃ nivedayetprātaḥ syādraverātmavatpriyaḥ.. 43.73 ..
1.4.d:
..इत्यर्घ्यदानविधिः..
य एवं भास्करायार्घ्यं मूर्तौ मंडलकेऽपि वा..
नित्यं निवेदयेत्प्रातः स्याद्रवेरात्मवत्प्रियः.. 43.73 ..
1.4.m: Thus is the rule for offering the arghya water-oblation. / He who, in this manner, offers the arghya water-oblation to the Sun daily in the morning, either in an image or in a maṇḍala, / becomes as dear to the sun as his own self.

1.4.s:
anena vidhinā karṇo bhāskarārghyaṃ prayacchati..
tataḥ sūryasya pārthāsāvātmavadvallabho mataḥ.. 43.74 ..
1.4.d:
अनेन विधिना कर्णो भास्करार्घ्यं प्रयच्छति..
ततः सूर्यस्य पार्थासावात्मवद्वल्लभो मतः.. 43.74 ..
1.4.m: By this rule, Karṇa offers the arghya water-oblation to the Sun; / therefore, O son of Pṛthā, he is considered by the sun as beloved as his own self.

1.4.s:
aśaktaścennityamekamarghyaṃ dadyāddivākṛte..
tato'tra rathasaptamyāṃ kuṃḍe deyaḥ prayatnataḥ.. 43.75 ..
1.4.d:
अशक्तश्चेन्नित्यमेकमर्घ्यं दद्याद्दिवाकृते..
ततोऽत्र रथसप्तम्यां कुंडे देयः प्रयत्नतः.. 43.75 ..
1.4.m: If one is unable [to do the whole rite], one should daily offer a single arghya water-oblation to the Maker of Day; / then, here on the Rathasaptamī, it should be offered with special effort in the pool.

1.4.s:
aśvamedhaphalaṃ prāpya sūryaloka mavāpnuyāt..
tasmātsarvaprayatnena dātavyo'rgho'tra bhārata.. 43.76 ..
1.4.d:
अश्वमेधफलं प्राप्य सूर्यलोक मवाप्नुयात्..
तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन दातव्योऽर्घोऽत्र भारत.. 43.76 ..
1.4.m: Having obtained the fruit of a horse sacrifice, he will attain the world of the sun; / therefore, with every effort, the arghya water-oblation must be offered here, O Bhārata.

1.4.s:
evaṃvidhastvasau devo bhaṭṭādityo'tra tiṣṭhati..
bhūyānato'pi bahuśaḥ pāpahā dharmavardhanaḥ.. 43.77 ..
1.4.d:
एवंविधस्त्वसौ देवो भट्टादित्योऽत्र तिष्ठति..
भूयानतोऽपि बहुशः पापहा धर्मवर्धनः.. 43.77 ..
1.4.m: Indeed, such a god, Bhaṭṭāditya, remains here; / even far greater than this in many ways, destroying sin and increasing righteousness.

1.4.s:
divyamaṣṭavidhaṃ cātra sadyaḥ pratyayakārakam..
pāpānāṃ copabhuktaṃ hi yathā pārtha halāhalam.. 43.78 ..
iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ prathame māheśvarakhaṇḍe kaumārikākhaṇḍe sāgarasaṃgame bhaṭṭādityamāhātmyavarṇanaṃnāma tricatvāriṃśo'dhyāyaḥ.. 43 .. cha ..
1.4.d:
दिव्यमष्टविधं चात्र सद्यः प्रत्ययकारकम्..
पापानां चोपभुक्तं हि यथा पार्थ हलाहलम्.. 43.78 ..
इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां प्रथमे माहेश्वरखण्डे कौमारिकाखण्डे सागरसंगमे भट्टादित्यमाहात्म्यवर्णनंनाम त्रिचत्वारिंशोऽध्यायः.. 43 .. छ ..
1.4.m:
And here the ordeal is eightfold, producing immediate proof; / for it is consumed by the sinful like the halāhala poison, O Pārtha.
Thus ends the forty-third chapter, named 'Description of the Glory of Bhaṭṭāditya at the Confluence with the Ocean', in the Kaumārikākhaṇḍa of the first section, the Māheśvarakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.

1.4.s:
..arjuna uvāca..
divyaprākāramicchāmi śrotuṃ cāhaṃ munīśvara..
kathaṃ kāryāṇi kānīha sphuṭaṃ yaiḥ puṇyapāpakam.. 44.1 ..
1.4.d:
..अर्जुन उवाच..
दिव्यप्राकारमिच्छामि श्रोतुं चाहं मुनीश्वर..
कथं कार्याणि कानीह स्फुटं यैः पुण्यपापकम्.. 44.1 ..
1.4.m: Arjuna said: / I desire to hear about the kinds of ordeals, O lord of sages; / how should they be performed, and which ones here clearly reveal merit and sin?

1.4.s:
..nārada uvāca..
śapaṣāḥ pośaghaṭakau viṣāgna taptamāṣakau..
phalaṃ ca taṃdulaṃ caiva divyānyaṣṭau vidurbudhāḥ.. 44.2 ..
1.4.d:
..नारद उवाच..
शपषाः पोशघटकौ विषाग्न तप्तमाषकौ..
फलं च तंदुलं चैव दिव्यान्यष्टौ विदुर्बुधाः.. 44.2 ..
1.4.m: Nārada said: / The oath, sacred water, the balance, poison, fire, the heated coin, / the [plow]share, and grain: the wise know these as the eight ordeals.

1.4.s:
asākṣikeṣu cārtheṣu mitho vivadamānayoḥ..
rājadrohābhiśāpeṣu sāhaseṣu tathaiva ca.. 44.3 ..
1.4.d:
असाक्षिकेषु चार्थेषु मिथो विवदमानयोः..
राजद्रोहाभिशापेषु साहसेषु तथैव च.. 44.3 ..
1.4.m: In matters without witnesses, where two parties dispute with each other, / in accusations of treason against the king, and likewise in reckless crimes,

1.4.s:
avidastattvataḥ satyaṃ śapathenābhilaṃghayet..
maharṣibhiśca devaiśca satyārthāḥ śapathāḥ kṛtāḥ.. 44.4 ..
1.4.d:
अविदस्तत्त्वतः सत्यं शपथेनाभिलंघयेत्..
महर्षिभिश्च देवैश्च सत्यार्थाः शपथाः कृताः.. 44.4 ..
1.4.m: if he does not know the truth as it really is, he should confirm it by an oath; / for oaths to establish the truth have been undertaken by great seers and deities.

1.4.s:
javano nṛpatiḥ kṣīṇo mithyāśapathamācaret..
vasiṣṭhāgre varṣamadhye sānvayaḥ kila bhārata.. 44.5 ..
1.4.d:
जवनो नृपतिः क्षीणो मिथ्याशपथमाचरेत्..
वसिष्ठाग्रे वर्षमध्ये सान्वयः किल भारत.. 44.5 ..
1.4.m: A king of the Yavanas, having taken a false oath / before Vasiṣṭha, perished within a year along with his lineage, O Bhārata.

1.4.s:
aṃdhaḥ śatrugṛhaṃ gacchedyo mithyāśapathāṃścaret..
rauravasya svayaṃ dvāramuddhāṭayati durmatiḥ.. 44.6 ..
1.4.d:
अंधः शत्रुगृहं गच्छेद्यो मिथ्याशपथांश्चरेत्..
रौरवस्य स्वयं द्वारमुद्धाटयति दुर्मतिः.. 44.6 ..
1.4.m: Whoever takes false oaths will go blind to the house of his enemy; / the wicked-minded man opens for himself the gate of Raurava hell.

1.4.s:
manyaṃte vai pāpakṛto na kaścitapaśyatīti naḥ..
tāṃśca devāḥ prapaśyaṃti svasyaivāṃtarapauruṣāḥ.. 44.7 ..
1.4.d:
मन्यंते वै पापकृतो न कश्चितपश्यतीति नः..
तांश्च देवाः प्रपश्यंति स्वस्यैवांतरपौरुषाः.. 44.7 ..
1.4.m: Wrongdoers indeed think: 'No one sees us'; / yet the gods, residing as the inner witness of one's own self, watch them.

1.4.s:
ādityacaṃdrāvanilo'nalaśca dyaurbhūmirāpo hṛdayaṃ yamaśca..
ahaśca rātriśca ubhe ca saṃdhye dharmo hi jānāti narasya vṛttam.. 44.8 ..
1.4.d:
आदित्यचंद्रावनिलोऽनलश्च द्यौर्भूमिरापो हृदयं यमश्च..
अहश्च रात्रिश्च उभे च संध्ये धर्मो हि जानाति नरस्य वृत्तम्.. 44.8 ..
1.4.m: The sun, the moon, wind and fire, heaven, earth, water, the heart and Yama, / day and night, both twilights, and Dharma know the conduct of man.

1.4.s:
evaṃ tasmādabhijñāya satyarthaśapathāṃścaret..
vṛthā hi śapathānkurvanpretya ceha vinaśyati.. 44.9 ..
1.4.d:
एवं तस्मादभिज्ञाय सत्यर्थशपथांश्चरेत्..
वृथा हि शपथान्कुर्वन्प्रेत्य चेह विनश्यति.. 44.9 ..
1.4.m: Knowing this thus, one should undertake oaths for the sake of truth; / for taking false oaths, a man is destroyed both in the hereafter and here.

1.4.s:
idaṃ satyaṃ vadāmīti bruvansākṣī bhavānyataḥ..
śubhāśubhaphalaṃ dehi śuciḥ pādau raveḥ svṛśet.. 44.10 ..
1.4.d:
इदं सत्यं वदामीति ब्रुवन्साक्षी भवान्यतः..
शुभाशुभफलं देहि शुचिः पादौ रवेः स्वृशेत्.. 44.10 ..
1.4.m: Saying 'I speak this truth, wherefore you be my witness, / give me good or bad fruit', being purified, he should touch the feet of the sun.

1.4.s:
atha śāstrasya vipro'pi śastrasyāpi ca kṣatriyaḥ..
māṃ saṃspṛśaṃstathā vaiśyaḥ śudraḥ svagurumeva ca.. 44.11 ..
1.4.d:
अथ शास्त्रस्य विप्रोऽपि शस्त्रस्यापि च क्षत्रियः..
मां संस्पृशंस्तथा वैश्यः शुद्रः स्वगुरुमेव च.. 44.11 ..
1.4.m: Now, a brahmin [should touch] scripture, a kṣatriya a weapon, / a vaiśya touching cattle, and a śūdra his own teacher.

1.4.s:
mātaraṃ pitaraṃ pūjyaṃ spṛśetsādhāraṇaṃ tvidam..
kośasya rūpaṃ pūrvaṃ te vyākhyātaṃ pāṃḍunaṃdana.. 44.12 ..
1.4.d:
मातरं पितरं पूज्यं स्पृशेत्साधारणं त्विदम्..
कोशस्य रूपं पूर्वं ते व्याख्यातं पांडुनंदन.. 44.12 ..
1.4.m: One may touch mother, father, or an elder; this is the common practice. / The nature of the sacred water was explained to you before, O son of Pāṇḍu.

1.4.s:
vipravarjyaṃ tathā keśaṃ varṇināṃ dāpayennṛpaḥ..
yo yo yaddevatābhaktaḥ pāyayettasya taṃ naram.. 44.13 ..
1.4.d:
विप्रवर्ज्यं तथा केशं वर्णिनां दापयेन्नृपः..
यो यो यद्देवताभक्तः पाययेत्तस्य तं नरम्.. 44.13 ..
1.4.m: The king should administer the sacred water to members of the castes, excluding the brahmin; / he should make that man drink [the water] of whatever deity he is devoted to.

1.4.s:
samabhaktaṃ ca devānāmādityasyaiva pāyayet..
sarveṣāṃ cogradevānāṃ snāpayedāyudhāstrakam.. 44.14 ..
1.4.d:
समभक्तं च देवानामादित्यस्यैव पाययेत्..
सर्वेषां चोग्रदेवानां स्नापयेदायुधास्त्रकम्.. 44.14 ..
1.4.m: To one devoted equally to all gods, he should administer that of the sun; / and he should bathe the weapons and missiles of all fierce deities.

1.4.s:
snānodakaṃ vā saṃkalpaṃ gṛhītvā pāyayennavam..
trisaptarātramadhye ca phalaṃ kośasya nirdiśet.. 44.15 ..
1.4.d:
स्नानोदकं वा संकल्पं गृहीत्वा पाययेन्नवम्..
त्रिसप्तरात्रमध्ये च फलं कोशस्य निर्दिशेत्.. 44.15 ..
1.4.m: Taking a vow, he should make him drink the fresh bathing water; / and he should declare the result of the sacred water within three times seven nights.

1.4.s:
ataḥ paraṃ mahādivyavidhānaṃ śrṛṇu yadbhavet..
saṃśayacchedi sarveṣāṃ dhārṣṭyattaddivyameva ca.. 44.16 ..
1.4.d:
अतः परं महादिव्यविधानं श्रृणु यद्भवेत्..
संशयच्छेदि सर्वेषां धार्ष्ट्यत्तद्दिव्यमेव च.. 44.16 ..
1.4.m: Hear further the procedure for the great ordeal that may be [undertaken]; / it dispels the doubts of all, and that ordeal is [given] in case of obstinacy.

1.4.s:
saśiraskaṃpradātavyamiti brahmā purābravīt..
mahogrāṇāṃ ca dātavyamaśiraskamapi sphuṭam.. 44.17 ..
1.4.d:
सशिरस्कंप्रदातव्यमिति ब्रह्मा पुराब्रवीत्..
महोग्राणां च दातव्यमशिरस्कमपि स्फुटम्.. 44.17 ..
1.4.m: Brahmā declared of old: 'It must be administered with a penalty [on the head]'; / and in the case of very fierce persons, it should clearly be administered without a penalty.

1.4.s:
sādhūnāṃ varṇināṃ rājā na śiraskaṃ pradāpayet..
na pravātedhaṭaṃ deyaṃ noṣṇakāle hutāśanam.. 44.18 ..
1.4.d:
साधूनां वर्णिनां राजा न शिरस्कं प्रदापयेत्..
न प्रवातेधटं देयं नोष्णकाले हुताशनम्.. 44.18 ..
1.4.m: To pious men and those belonging to the castes, the king should not give [the ordeal] with a capital penalty; / the balance should not be given in high wind, nor fire in hot weather,

1.4.s: varṇināṃ ca tathā kālaṃ taṃdulaṃ mukharogiṇām.. 44.19 ..
1.4.d: वर्णिनां च तथा कालं तंदुलं मुखरोगिणाम्.. 44.19 ..
1.4.m: and [not] the dark [grain] to caste members, nor grain to those suffering from mouth disease.

1.4.s:
kuṣṭhapittārditānāṃ ca brāhmaṇānāṃ ca no viṣam..
taptamāṣakamarhaṃti sarve dharmyaṃ niratyayam.. 44.20 ..
1.4.d:
कुष्ठपित्तार्दितानां च ब्राह्मणानां च नो विषम्..
तप्तमाषकमर्हंति सर्वे धर्म्यं निरत्ययम्.. 44.20 ..
1.4.m: Poison is not for those afflicted with leprosy or bilious disease, nor for brahmins; / all are entitled to the heated coin, which is lawful and free from danger.

1.4.s:
na vyādhimarake deśe śapathānkośameva ca..
divyānyāsurakairmaṃtraiḥ staṃbhayaṃtīha kecana.. 44.21 ..
1.4.d:
न व्याधिमरके देशे शपथान्कोशमेव च..
दिव्यान्यासुरकैर्मंत्रैः स्तंभयंतीह केचन.. 44.21 ..
1.4.m: Oaths and sacred water should not be [given] in a region stricken with disease and pestilence. / Some people here paralyze ordeals with demonic mantras.

1.4.s:
pratighātavidasteṣāṃ yojayeddharmavatsalān..
divyānāṃ stabhakāñjñātvā pāpānnityaṃ mahīpatiḥ.. 44.22 ..
1.4.d:
प्रतिघातविदस्तेषां योजयेद्धर्मवत्सलान्..
दिव्यानां स्तभकाञ्ज्ञात्वा पापान्नित्यं महीपतिः.. 44.22 ..
1.4.m: Knowing those who counteract them, he should employ those who love righteousness; / discovering the wicked paralyzers of ordeals, the king should constantly

1.4.s:
vivāsayetsvakādrāṣṭrātte hi lokasya kaṃṭakāḥ..
teṣāmanveṣaṇe yatnaṃ rājā nityaṃ samācaret.. 44.23 ..
1.4.d:
विवासयेत्स्वकाद्राष्ट्रात्ते हि लोकस्य कंटकाः..
तेषामन्वेषणे यत्नं राजा नित्यं समाचरेत्.. 44.23 ..
1.4.m: banish them from his realm, for they are thorns to the world; / the king should always make an effort to seek them out.

1.4.s:
te hi pāpasamācārāstaskarebhyo'pi taskarāḥ..
prāgdṛṣṭadoṣānsvalpeṣu divyeṣu viniyojayet.. 44.24 ..
1.4.d:
ते हि पापसमाचारास्तस्करेभ्योऽपि तस्कराः..
प्राग्दृष्टदोषान्स्वल्पेषु दिव्येषु विनियोजयेत्.. 44.24 ..
1.4.m: For they are of evil conduct, worse thieves than thieves. / He should assign those whose fault was seen previously to minor ordeals,

1.4.s:
mahatsvapi na cārtheṣu dharmajñāndharmavatsalān..
na mithyāvacanaṃ yeṣāṃ janmaprabhṛti vidyate.. 44.25 ..
1.4.d:
महत्स्वपि न चार्थेषु धर्मज्ञान्धर्मवत्सलान्..
न मिथ्यावचनं येषां जन्मप्रभृति विद्यते.. 44.25 ..
1.4.m: and not those who know righteousness and love righteousness, even in great matters, / in whom no false speech has existed since their birth.

1.4.s:
śraddadhyātpārthivasteṣāṃ vacanā deva bhārata..
jñātvā dharmiṣṭhatāṃ rājā puruṣasya vicakṣaṇaḥ.. 44.26 ..
1.4.d:
श्रद्दध्यात्पार्थिवस्तेषां वचना देव भारत..
ज्ञात्वा धर्मिष्ठतां राजा पुरुषस्य विचक्षणः.. 44.26 ..
1.4.m: A king should trust in their word alone, O Bhārata; / knowing a man's righteousness, a discerning king,

1.4.s:
krodhāllobhātkārayaṃśca svayameva praduṣyati..
tasmātpāpiṣu divyaṃ syāttatrādau procyate dhaṭe.. 44.27 ..
1.4.d:
क्रोधाल्लोभात्कारयंश्च स्वयमेव प्रदुष्यति..
तस्मात्पापिषु दिव्यं स्यात्तत्रादौ प्रोच्यते धटे.. 44.27 ..
1.4.m: if causing [him to undergo an ordeal] out of anger or greed, becomes corrupted himself. / Therefore, an ordeal should be for the wicked; among them, [that of] the balance is spoken of first.

1.4.s:
susamāyāṃ pṛthivyāṃ ca digbhāge pūrvadakṣiṇe..
yajñiyasya tu vṛkṣasya sthāpyaṃ syānmuṃḍakadvayam.. 44.28 ..
1.4.d:
सुसमायां पृथिव्यां च दिग्भागे पूर्वदक्षिणे..
यज्ञियस्य तु वृक्षस्य स्थाप्यं स्यान्मुंडकद्वयम्.. 44.28 ..
1.4.m: On very level ground, in the south-eastern quarter, / two pillars of sacrificial wood should be erected.

1.4.s:
staṃbhakasya pramāṇaṃ ca saptahastaṃ prakīrtitam..
dvau hastau nikhanetkāṣṭhaṃ dṛśyaṃ syāddhastapaṃcakam.. 44.29 ..
1.4.d:
स्तंभकस्य प्रमाणं च सप्तहस्तं प्रकीर्तितम्..
द्वौ हस्तौ निखनेत्काष्ठं दृश्यं स्याद्धस्तपंचकम्.. 44.29 ..
1.4.m: The measurement of the post is stated to be seven cubits: / he should bury two cubits of wood, and five cubits should be visible.

1.4.s:
aṃtaraṃ tu tayoḥ kāryaṃ tathā hastacatuṣṭayam..
muṃḍakopari kāṣṭhaṃ ca dṛḍhaṃ kuryādvicakṣaṇaḥ.. 44.30 ..
1.4.d:
अंतरं तु तयोः कार्यं तथा हस्तचतुष्टयम्..
मुंडकोपरि काष्ठं च दृढं कुर्याद्विचक्षणः.. 44.30 ..
1.4.m: The space between the two should be made four cubits; / and a wise man should fix a sturdy piece of wood on top of the two posts.

1.4.s:
caturhastaṃ tulākāṣṭhamavraṇaṃ kārayetsthiram..
khadirārjunavṛkṣāṇāṃ śiṃśapāśālajaṃ tvatha.. 44.31 ..
1.4.d:
चतुर्हस्तं तुलाकाष्ठमव्रणं कारयेत्स्थिरम्..
खदिरार्जुनवृक्षाणां शिंशपाशालजं त्वथ.. 44.31 ..
1.4.m: He should have a balance beam of four cubits made, unblemished and firm, / of khadira, arjuna, śiṃśapā, or śāla wood.

1.4.s:
tulākāṣṭhe tu kartavyaṃ tathā vai śikyakadvayam..
prāṅmukho niścalaḥ kāryaḥ śucau deśe dhaṭastathā.. 44.32 ..
1.4.d:
तुलाकाष्ठे तु कर्तव्यं तथा वै शिक्यकद्वयम्..
प्राङ्मुखो निश्चलः कार्यः शुचौ देशे धटस्तथा.. 44.32 ..
1.4.m: Two hanging pans should be attached to the balance beam; / the balance should be made facing east and motionless in a clean place.

1.4.s:
pāṣāṇasyāpi jāyet staṃbheṣu ca dhaṭastathā..
vaṇiksuvarṇakāro vā kuśalaḥ kāṃsyakārakaḥ.. 44.33 ..
1.4.d:
पाषाणस्यापि जायेत् स्तंभेषु च धटस्तथा..
वणिक्सुवर्णकारो वा कुशलः कांस्यकारकः.. 44.33 ..
1.4.m: The balance may also be set up with stone pillars; / a merchant, a goldsmith, or a skilled worker in bronze,

1.4.s:
tulādhāradharaḥ kāryo ripau mitre ca yaḥ samaḥ..
śrāvayetprāḍvivāko'pi tulādhāraṃ vicakṣaṇaḥ.. 44.34 ..
1.4.d:
तुलाधारधरः कार्यो रिपौ मित्रे च यः समः..
श्रावयेत्प्राड्विवाकोऽपि तुलाधारं विचक्षणः.. 44.34 ..
1.4.m: who is impartial towards enemy and friend, should be appointed as the balance-holder; / and the learned chief judge should instruct the balance-holder:

1.4.s:
brahmaghne ye smṛtā lokā ye ca strībālaghātake..
tulādhārasya te lokāstulāṃ dhārayato mṛṣā.. 44.35 ..
1.4.d:
ब्रह्मघ्ने ये स्मृता लोका ये च स्त्रीबालघातके..
तुलाधारस्य ते लोकास्तुलां धारयतो मृषा.. 44.35 ..
1.4.m: 'The realms recorded for the slayer of a brahmin, and those for the killer of a woman or a child, / those realms belong to the balance-holder who holds the balance falsely.'

1.4.s:
ekasmiṃstolayecchikye jñātaṃ sūpoṣitaṃ naram..
dvitīye mṛttikāṃ śubhrāṃ gaurāṃ tu tulayedbudhaḥ.. 44.36 ..
1.4.d:
एकस्मिंस्तोलयेच्छिक्ये ज्ञातं सूपोषितं नरम्..
द्वितीये मृत्तिकां शुभ्रां गौरां तु तुलयेद्बुधः.. 44.36 ..
1.4.m: In one pan, the wise man should weigh the well-fasted accused man; / in the second, he should balance clear, pale earth.

1.4.s:
iṣṭikābhasmapāṣāṇakapālāsthīni varjayet..
tolayitvā tataḥ pūrvaṃ tasmāttamavatārayet.. 44.37 ..
1.4.d:
इष्टिकाभस्मपाषाणकपालास्थीनि वर्जयेत्..
तोलयित्वा ततः पूर्वं तस्मात्तमवतारयेत्.. 44.37 ..
1.4.m: He should avoid bricks, ashes, stones, potsherds, and bones; / having weighed him first, he should then take him down from it.

1.4.s:
mūrdhni patraṃ tato nyasya nyastapatraṃ niveśayet..
patre maṃtrastvayaṃ lekhyo yaḥ puroktaḥ śvayaṃbhuvā.. 44.38 ..
1.4.d:
मूर्ध्नि पत्रं ततो न्यस्य न्यस्तपत्रं निवेशयेत्..
पत्रे मंत्रस्त्वयं लेख्यो यः पुरोक्तः श्वयंभुवा.. 44.38 ..
1.4.m: Then, placing an inscription on his head, he should seat him with the inscription placed [there]; / and this mantra, spoken formerly by Svayambhū, is to be written on the leaf:

1.4.s:
brahmaṇastvaṃ sutā devī tulānāmneti kathyate..
tukāro gaurave nityaṃ lakāro laghuni smṛtaḥ.. 44.39 ..
1.4.d:
ब्रह्मणस्त्वं सुता देवी तुलानाम्नेति कथ्यते..
तुकारो गौरवे नित्यं लकारो लघुनि स्मृतः.. 44.39 ..
1.4.m: 'You are the goddess, daughter of Brahmā, called by the name Tulā (Balance); / the syllable "tu" is remembered as always meaning weight, and the syllable "la" as lightness.

1.4.s:
gurulāghavasaṃyogāttulā tena nigadyase..
saṃśayānmocayasvainamabhiśastaṃ naraṃ śubhe.. 44.40 ..
1.4.d:
गुरुलाघवसंयोगात्तुला तेन निगद्यसे..
संशयान्मोचयस्वैनमभिशस्तं नरं शुभे.. 44.40 ..
1.4.m: By the conjunction of heaviness and lightness, you are therefore called Tulā; / release this accused man from doubt, O auspicious one!'

1.4.s:
bhūya āropayettaṃ tu naraṃ tasminsapatrakam..
tulito yadi vardheta śuddho bhavati dharmataḥ.. 44.41 ..
1.4.d:
भूय आरोपयेत्तं तु नरं तस्मिन्सपत्रकम्..
तुलितो यदि वर्धेत शुद्धो भवति धर्मतः.. 44.41 ..
1.4.m: He should place that man upon it again along with the leaf. / If, when weighed, he increases [in weight], he is pure according to dharma.

1.4.s:
hīyamāno na śuddhaḥ syāditi dharmavido viduḥ..
śikyacchede tulābhaṃge punarāropayennaram.. 44.42 ..
1.4.d:
हीयमानो न शुद्धः स्यादिति धर्मविदो विदुः..
शिक्यच्छेदे तुलाभंगे पुनरारोपयेन्नरम्.. 44.42 ..
1.4.m: If he decreases [in weight], he is not pure; so know the knowers of dharma. / If the scale-cord snaps or the balance breaks, he should place the man upon it again.

1.4.s:
evaṃ niḥsaṃśayaṃ jñānaṃ yaccānyāyaṃ na lopayet..
etatsarvaṃ ravau vāre kāryaṃ saṃpūjya bhāskaram.. 44.43 ..
1.4.d:
एवं निःसंशयं ज्ञानं यच्चान्यायं न लोपयेत्..
एतत्सर्वं रवौ वारे कार्यं संपूज्य भास्करम्.. 44.43 ..
1.4.m: In this way [there is] knowledge free of doubt, and it does not violate justice. / All of this should be performed on a Sunday, having worshipped the Sun.

1.4.s: athātaḥ saṃpravakṣyāmi viṣadivyaṃ śrṛṇuṣva me.. 44.44 ..
1.4.d: अथातः संप्रवक्ष्यामि विषदिव्यं श्रृणुष्व मे.. 44.44 ..
1.4.m: Now next I shall explain the poison ordeal; listen to me:

1.4.s:
dviprakāraṃ ca tatproktaṃ ghaṭasarpaviṣaṃ tathā..
śṛṃgiṇo vatsanābhasya himaśailabhavasya vā.. 44.45 ..
1.4.d:
द्विप्रकारं च तत्प्रोक्तं घटसर्पविषं तथा..
शृंगिणो वत्सनाभस्य हिमशैलभवस्य वा.. 44.45 ..
1.4.m: And it is said to be of two kinds: [the ordeal of] a serpent in a jar, and likewise poison / of the horned [plant] or of the vatsanābha plant grown on the snowy mountains.

1.4.s:
yavāḥ sapta pradātavyā athavā ṣaḍghṛtaplutāḥ..
mūrdhni vinyastapatrasya patre caivaṃ niveśayet.. 44.46 ..
1.4.d:
यवाः सप्त प्रदातव्या अथवा षड्घृतप्लुताः..
मूर्ध्नि विन्यस्तपत्रस्य पत्रे चैवं निवेशयेत्.. 44.46 ..
1.4.m: Seven barley-corns should be administered, or six, smeared with ghee. / After placing the written leaf on his head, he should place [the mantra] on the leaf thus:

1.4.s:
tvaṃ viṣa brahmaṇaḥ putra satyadharme vyavasthitaḥ..
trāyasvainaṃ naraṃ pāpātsatyenāsya bhavāmṛtam.. 44.47 ..
1.4.d:
त्वं विष ब्रह्मणः पुत्र सत्यधर्मे व्यवस्थितः..
त्रायस्वैनं नरं पापात्सत्येनास्य भवामृतम्.. 44.47 ..
1.4.m: "You, O poison, are the son of Brahmā, established in truth and righteousness; / protect this man from sin; through truth, become nectar for him!"

1.4.s:
yena vegairvinā jīrṇaṃ chardimūrcchāvivarjitam..
taṃ tu śuddhaṃ vijānīyāditi dharmavido viduḥ.. 44.48 ..
1.4.d:
येन वेगैर्विना जीर्णं छर्दिमूर्च्छाविवर्जितम्..
तं तु शुद्धं विजानीयादिति धर्मविदो विदुः.. 44.48 ..
1.4.m: One by whom it is digested without spasms, free from vomiting and fainting, / he should be known as pure; so know the knowers of dharma.

1.4.s:
kṣudhitaṃ kṣudhitaḥ sarpaṃ ghaṭasthaṃ procya pūrvavat..
saṃspṛśettālikāḥ sapta na daśecchudhyatīti saḥ.. 44.49 ..
1.4.d:
क्षुधितं क्षुधितः सर्पं घटस्थं प्रोच्य पूर्ववत्..
संस्पृशेत्तालिकाः सप्त न दशेच्छुध्यतीति सः.. 44.49 ..
1.4.m: Hungry, he should address as before the hungry serpent in a jar; / he should touch [it] for seven claps; if it does not bite, he is purified.

1.4.s:
agnidivyaṃ yathā prāha viraṃcistacchṛṇuṣva me..
saptamaṃḍalakānkuryāddevasyāgre ravestathā.. 44.50 ..
1.4.d:
अग्निदिव्यं यथा प्राह विरंचिस्तच्छृणुष्व मे..
सप्तमंडलकान्कुर्याद्देवस्याग्रे रवेस्तथा.. 44.50 ..
1.4.m: Listen from me to the fire ordeal as Brahmā declared it: / He should make seven circles in front of the sun god.

1.4.s:
maṃḍalānmaṃḍalaṃ kāryaṃ pūrveṇeti viniścayaḥ..
ṣoḍaśāṃtulakaṃ kāryaṃ maṃḍalāttāvadaṃ taram.. 44.51 ..
1.4.d:
मंडलान्मंडलं कार्यं पूर्वेणेति विनिश्चयः..
षोडशांतुलकं कार्यं मंडलात्तावदं तरम्.. 44.51 ..
1.4.m: Circle should be made from circle towards the east—this is the rule; / the space from one circle to the next should be sixteen angulas.

1.4.s:
ārdravāsasamāhūya tathā caivāpyupopitam..
kārayetsarvadivyāni devabrāhmaṇasaṃnidhau.. 44.52 ..
1.4.d:
आर्द्रवाससमाहूय तथा चैवाप्युपोपितम्..
कारयेत्सर्वदिव्यानि देवब्राह्मणसंनिधौ.. 44.52 ..
1.4.m: Summoning [him] clad in wet clothes and having fasted, / he should cause all the ordeals to be performed in the presence of gods and brahmins,

1.4.s:
pratyakṣaṃ kārayeddivyaṃ rājño vādhikṛtasya vā..
brāhmaṇānāṃ śrutavatāṃ prakṛtīnāṃ tathaiva ca.. 44.53 ..
1.4.d:
प्रत्यक्षं कारयेद्दिव्यं राज्ञो वाधिकृतस्य वा..
ब्राह्मणानां श्रुतवतां प्रकृतीनां तथैव च.. 44.53 ..
1.4.m: before the eyes of the king or his appointed officer, / and likewise of learned brahmins and subjects.

1.4.s:
paścime dinakāle hi prāṅmukhaḥ prāñjaliḥ śuciḥ..
caturasre maṃḍale'nye kṛtvā caiva samau karau.. 44.54 ..
1.4.d:
पश्चिमे दिनकाले हि प्राङ्मुखः प्राञ्जलिः शुचिः..
चतुरस्रे मंडलेऽन्ये कृत्वा चैव समौ करौ.. 44.54 ..
1.4.m: In the western part of the day, facing east, with cupped hands, clean, / holding his two hands flat and even in another four-cornered circle,

1.4.s:
lakṣayeyuḥ kṛtādīni hastayostasya hāriṇaḥ..
saptāśvatthasya patrāṇi bhadhnīyuḥ karayostataḥ.. 44.55 ..
1.4.d:
लक्षयेयुः कृतादीनि हस्तयोस्तस्य हारिणः..
सप्ताश्वत्थस्य पत्राणि भध्नीयुः करयोस्ततः.. 44.55 ..
1.4.m: they should examine scars and the like on the hands of that taker [of the ordeal]. / Then they should bind seven leaves of the holy fig tree on his two hands

1.4.s:
navena kṛtasūtreṇa kārpāsena dṛḍhaṃ yathā..
tatastu susamaṃ kṛtvā aṣṭāṃgulamathāyasam.. 44.56 ..
1.4.d:
नवेन कृतसूत्रेण कार्पासेन दृढं यथा..
ततस्तु सुसमं कृत्वा अष्टांगुलमथायसम्.. 44.56 ..
1.4.m: with a new cotton thread, firmly. / Then, making it completely smooth, an iron ball of eight angulas,

1.4.s:
piṃḍaṃ hutāśasaṃtaptaṃ paṃcāśatpalikaṃ dṛḍham..
ādau pūjāṃ raveḥ kṛtvā hutāśasyātha kārayet.. 44.57 ..
1.4.d:
पिंडं हुताशसंतप्तं पंचाशत्पलिकं दृढम्..
आदौ पूजां रवेः कृत्वा हुताशस्याथ कारयेत्.. 44.57 ..
1.4.m: weighing fifty palas, solid, heated by fire. / Having first performed worship of the Sun, he should then perform [worship] of the Fire

1.4.s:
raktacaṃdanadhūpābhyāṃ raktapuṣpaistathaiva ca..
abhiśastasya patraṃ ca badhnīyāccaiva mūrdhani.. 44.58 ..
1.4.d:
रक्तचंदनधूपाभ्यां रक्तपुष्पैस्तथैव च..
अभिशस्तस्य पत्रं च बध्नीयाच्चैव मूर्धनि.. 44.58 ..
1.4.m: with red sandalwood and incense, and likewise with red flowers. / And he should bind the leaf upon the head of the accused,

1.4.s:
maṃtreṇānena saṃyuktaṃ brāhmaṇābhihitena ca..
tvamagne vedāścatvārastvaṃ ca yajñeṣu hūyase.. 44.59 ..
1.4.d:
मंत्रेणानेन संयुक्तं ब्राह्मणाभिहितेन च..
त्वमग्ने वेदाश्चत्वारस्त्वं च यज्ञेषु हूयसे.. 44.59 ..
1.4.m: accompanied by this mantra uttered by a brahmin: / "You, O Fire, are the four Vedas, and you are offered in sacrifices.

1.4.s:
pāpaṃ punāsi vai yasmāttasmātpāvaka ucyase..
tvaṃ mukhaṃ sarvadevānāṃ tvaṃ mukhaṃ brahmavādinām.. 44.60 ..
1.4.d:
पापं पुनासि वै यस्मात्तस्मात्पावक उच्यसे..
त्वं मुखं सर्वदेवानां त्वं मुखं ब्रह्मवादिनाम्.. 44.60 ..
1.4.m: Because you purify sin, therefore you are called Pāvaka. / You are the mouth of all the gods; you are the mouth of the knowers of Brahman.

1.4.s:
jaṭharastho'si bhūtānāṃ tato vetsi śubhāśubham..
pāpeṣu darśayātmānamarciṣmānbhava pāvaka.. 44.61 ..
1.4.d:
जठरस्थोऽसि भूतानां ततो वेत्सि शुभाशुभम्..
पापेषु दर्शयात्मानमर्चिष्मान्भव पावक.. 44.61 ..
1.4.m: You reside in the belly of living beings; therefore you know the good and the bad. / Reveal yourself in matters of sin, be blazing, O Purifier!

1.4.s:
athavā śuddhabhāveṣu śīto bhavamahābala..
tato'bhiśastaḥ śanakairmaṃḍalāni parikramet.. 44.62 ..
1.4.d:
अथवा शुद्धभावेषु शीतो भवमहाबल..
ततोऽभिशस्तः शनकैर्मंडलानि परिक्रमेत्.. 44.62 ..
1.4.m: Or, in cases of pure intent, become cold, O mighty one!" / Then the accused should slowly pace through the circles.

1.4.s:
parikramya śanairjahyāllohapiṃḍaṃ tataḥ kṣitau..
vipatrahastaṃ taṃ paścātkārayedvrīhimardanam.. 44.63 ..
1.4.d:
परिक्रम्य शनैर्जह्याल्लोहपिंडं ततः क्षितौ..
विपत्रहस्तं तं पश्चात्कारयेद्व्रीहिमर्दनम्.. 44.63 ..
1.4.m: Having paced through, he should slowly drop the iron ball on the ground. / Afterwards, with the leaves removed from his hands, he should make him rub grains of unhusked rice.

1.4.s:
nirvikārau karau dṛṣṭvā śuddho bhavati dharmataḥ..
bhayādvā pātayedyastu tadadho vā vibhāvyate.. 44.64 ..
1.4.d:
निर्विकारौ करौ दृष्ट्वा शुद्धो भवति धर्मतः..
भयाद्वा पातयेद्यस्तु तदधो वा विभाव्यते.. 44.64 ..
1.4.m: Having seen that his hands are uninjured, he is pure according to dharma. / But if through fear he drops [it], or if [a burn] is observed under it,

1.4.s:
punastvāhārayellohaṃ vidhireṣa prakīrtitaḥ..
athātaḥ saṃpraaivakṣyāmi taptamāṣavidhiṃ śrṛṇu.. 44.65 ..
1.4.d:
पुनस्त्वाहारयेल्लोहं विधिरेष प्रकीर्तितः..
अथातः संप्रऐवक्ष्यामि तप्तमाषविधिं श्रृणु.. 44.65 ..
1.4.m: he should make him take the iron again; this is the prescribed rule declared. / Now next I shall explain: hear the rule of the heated bean.

1.4.s:
kārayedāyasaṃ pātraṃ tāmraṃ vā ṣoḍaśāṃgulam..
caturaṃgulakhātaṃ tu mṛnmayaṃ vāpi kārayet.. 44.66 ..
1.4.d:
कारयेदायसं पात्रं ताम्रं वा षोडशांगुलम्..
चतुरंगुलखातं तु मृन्मयं वापि कारयेत्.. 44.66 ..
1.4.m: He should cause a vessel to be made of iron or copper, sixteen angulas [wide], / with a depth of four angulas, or he may make it of clay.

1.4.s:
pūrayed‌ghṛtatailābhyāṃ palairviśatibhistataḥ..
sutapte nikṣipettatra suvarṇasya tu māṣakam.. 44.67 ..
1.4.d:
पूरयेद्‌घृततैलाभ्यां पलैर्विशतिभिस्ततः..
सुतप्ते निक्षिपेत्तत्र सुवर्णस्य तु माषकम्.. 44.67 ..
1.4.m: Then he should fill it with twenty palas of ghee and oil. / When it is well heated, he should drop a golden bean into it.

1.4.s:
vahnyuktaṃ vinyasenmaṃtramabhiśastasya mūrdhani..
aṃguṣṭhāṃguliyogena taptamāṣaṃ samuddharet.. 44.68 ..
1.4.d:
वह्न्युक्तं विन्यसेन्मंत्रमभिशस्तस्य मूर्धनि..
अंगुष्ठांगुलियोगेन तप्तमाषं समुद्धरेत्.. 44.68 ..
1.4.m: He should place the mantra prescribed for Fire upon the head of the accused. / With the thumb and fingers, he should take out the heated bean.

1.4.s:
śuddhaṃ jñeyamasaṃdigdhaṃ visphoṭādivivarjitam..
phālaśuddhiṃ pravakṣyāmi tāṃ śrṛṇu tvaṃ dhanaṃjaya.. 44.69 ..
1.4.d:
शुद्धं ज्ञेयमसंदिग्धं विस्फोटादिविवर्जितम्..
फालशुद्धिं प्रवक्ष्यामि तां श्रृणु त्वं धनंजय.. 44.69 ..
1.4.m: If it is free of blisters and the like, he should be known as pure beyond doubt. / I shall explain the plowshare ordeal; hear that, O Dhanaṃjaya!

1.4.s:
āyasaṃ dvādaśapalaṃ ghaṭitaṃ phālamucyate..
aṣṭāṃgulamadīrghaṃ ca caturaṃgulavistṛtam.. 44.70 ..
1.4.d:
आयसं द्वादशपलं घटितं फालमुच्यते..
अष्टांगुलमदीर्घं च चतुरंगुलविस्तृतम्.. 44.70 ..
1.4.m: An iron plowshare forged to twelve palas is prescribed, / eight angulas in length and four angulas in width.

1.4.s:
vahnyuktaṃ vinyasenmaṃtramabhiśastasya mūrdhani..
triḥparāvartayejjihvā lihannasmātṣaḍaṃgulam.. 44.71 ..
1.4.d:
वह्न्युक्तं विन्यसेन्मंत्रमभिशस्तस्य मूर्धनि..
त्रिःपरावर्तयेज्जिह्वा लिहन्नस्मात्षडंगुलम्.. 44.71 ..
1.4.m: He should place the mantra prescribed for Fire upon the head of the accused. / He should turn his tongue over three times, licking six angulas from it.

1.4.s:
gavāṃ kṣīraṃ pradātavyaṃ jihvāśodhanamuttamam..
jihvāparīkṣaṇaṃ kuryāddagdhā cenna tu vimocyate.. 44.72 ..
1.4.d:
गवां क्षीरं प्रदातव्यं जिह्वाशोधनमुत्तमम्..
जिह्वापरीक्षणं कुर्याद्दग्धा चेन्न तु विमोच्यते.. 44.72 ..
1.4.m: Cow's milk should be given, the best purifier of the tongue. / He should conduct an examination of the tongue; if it is burned, he is not cleared;

1.4.s:
taṃ viśuddhaṃ vijānīyādviśuddhā cettu jāyate..
taṃdulasyātha vakṣyāmi vidhidharmaṃ sanātanam.. 44.73 ..
1.4.d:
तं विशुद्धं विजानीयाद्विशुद्धा चेत्तु जायते..
तंदुलस्याथ वक्ष्यामि विधिधर्मं सनातनम्.. 44.73 ..
1.4.m: if it proves to be unblemished, he should know him to be purified. / Now I will speak of the eternal rule and law of the rice grain.

1.4.s:
caurye tu taṃdulā deyā na cānyatra kathaṃcana..
taṃdulānudake siktvā rātrau tatraiva sthāpayet.. 44.74 ..
1.4.d:
चौर्ये तु तंदुला देया न चान्यत्र कथंचन..
तंदुलानुदके सिक्त्वा रात्रौ तत्रैव स्थापयेत्.. 44.74 ..
1.4.m: Grains of rice are to be given in theft, and never in any other case. / Having sprinkled the grains with water, he should leave them there overnight.

1.4.s:
prabhāte kāriṇe deyā bhakṣaṇāya na saṃśayaḥ..
triḥkaॉtvaḥ prāṅ‌mukhaścaiva patre niṣṭhīvayettataḥ.. 44.75 ..
1.4.d:
प्रभाते कारिणे देया भक्षणाय न संशयः..
त्रिःकॉत्वः प्राङ्‌मुखश्चैव पत्रे निष्ठीवयेत्ततः.. 44.75 ..
1.4.m: In the morning, they must without doubt be given to the accused to eat. / Then, facing east, he should spit [them out] onto a leaf three times: 44.75

1.4.s:
pippalasyātha bhūrjasya na tvanyasya kathaṃcana..
tāṃstu vai kārayecchuddhāṃstaṃdulāñchālisaṃbhavān.. 44.76 ..
1.4.d:
पिप्पलस्याथ भूर्जस्य न त्वन्यस्य कथंचन..
तांस्तु वै कारयेच्छुद्धांस्तंदुलाञ्छालिसंभवान्.. 44.76 ..
1.4.m: either of a pippala tree or of a birch, but never of any other. / One must have those clean grains of rice taken from śāli rice, 44.76

1.4.s:
mṛnmaye bhājane kṛtvā savituḥ purataḥ sthitaḥ..
tandulānmaṃtrayecchuddhānmantreṇānena dharmataḥ.. 44.77 ..
1.4.d:
मृन्मये भाजने कृत्वा सवितुः पुरतः स्थितः..
तन्दुलान्मंत्रयेच्छुद्धान्मन्त्रेणानेन धर्मतः.. 44.77 ..
1.4.m: placed in an earthen vessel, and standing before the Sun, / one should consecrate the pure grains of rice with this mantra according to dharma: 44.77

1.4.s:
dīyase dharmatattvajñairmānuṣāṇāṃ viśodhanam..
stutastandula satyena dharmatastrātumarhasi.. 44.78 ..
1.4.d:
दीयसे धर्मतत्त्वज्ञैर्मानुषाणां विशोधनम्..
स्तुतस्तन्दुल सत्येन धर्मतस्त्रातुमर्हसि.. 44.78 ..
1.4.m: ‘You are given by those who know the truth of dharma as the purifier of human beings. / Praised, O grain of rice, you ought in truth to protect [him] through dharma.’ 44.78

1.4.s:
niṣṭhīvane kṛte teṣāṃ savituḥ purataḥ sthite..
śoṇitaṃ dṛśyate yasya tamaśuddhaṃ vinirdiśet.. 44.79 ..
1.4.d:
निष्ठीवने कृते तेषां सवितुः पुरतः स्थिते..
शोणितं दृश्यते यस्य तमशुद्धं विनिर्दिशेत्.. 44.79 ..
1.4.m: When they have been spat out while he stands before the Sun, / he on whose [grains] blood is seen, him one should declare impure. 44.79

1.4.s:
evamaṣṭavidhaṃ divyaṃ pāpasaṃśayacchedanam..
bhaṭṭādityasya purato jāyate kurunaṃdana.. 44.80 ..
1.4.d:
एवमष्टविधं दिव्यं पापसंशयच्छेदनम्..
भट्टादित्यस्य पुरतो जायते कुरुनंदन.. 44.80 ..
1.4.m: Thus the eightfold divine ordeal which cuts away doubt about sin / takes place before Bhaṭṭāditya, O joy of the Kurus. 44.80

1.4.s:
jaladivyaṃ tathā prāhurdviprakāraṃ purāvidaḥ..
jalahastaṃ smṛtaṃ caikaṃ majjanaṃ cāparaṃ viduḥ.. 44.81 ..
1.4.d:
जलदिव्यं तथा प्राहुर्द्विप्रकारं पुराविदः..
जलहस्तं स्मृतं चैकं मज्जनं चापरं विदुः.. 44.81 ..
1.4.m: Likewise, those who know antiquity speak of the water-ordeal as being of two kinds: / one is remembered as the ‘water-hand’ [ordeal], and the other they know as immersion. 44.81

1.4.s:
bāṇakṣepastathādānaṃ yāvadvīryavatā kṛtam..
tāvattaṃ majjayejjīvettathā tacchuddhimādiśet.. 44.82 ..
1.4.d:
बाणक्षेपस्तथादानं यावद्वीर्यवता कृतम्..
तावत्तं मज्जयेज्जीवेत्तथा तच्छुद्धिमादिशेत्.. 44.82 ..
1.4.m: For as long as the discharge of an arrow and its retrieval are performed by a strong man, / for that long one should keep him immersed; if he survives, one should accordingly declare his purity. 44.82

1.4.s:
evaṃvidhamidaṃ sthānaṃ bhaṭṭādityasya bhārata..
mamaiva kṛpayā bhānorjātametanmahītale.. 44.83 ..
iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ prathame māheśvarakhaṇḍe kaumārikākhaṇḍe bhaṭṭādityamāhātmye divyavarṇanaṃnāma catuścatvāriṃśo'dhyāyaḥ.. 44 .. cha ..
1.4.d:
एवंविधमिदं स्थानं भट्टादित्यस्य भारत..
ममैव कृपया भानोर्जातमेतन्महीतले.. 44.83 ..
इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां प्रथमे माहेश्वरखण्डे कौमारिकाखण्डे भट्टादित्यमाहात्म्ये दिव्यवर्णनंनाम चतुश्चत्वारिंशोऽध्यायः.. 44 .. छ ..
1.4.m:
Such is this holy place of Bhaṭṭāditya, O Bhārata; / it was produced on the face of the earth solely through my grace and the Sun’s. 44.83
Thus ends the forty-fourth chapter, named ‘Description of the Divine Ordeals,’ in the glorification of Bhaṭṭāditya, in the Kaumārikākhaṇḍa of the first [section], the Māheśvarakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa of eighty-one thousand verses. 44.

1.4.s:
..nārada uvāca..
tathā bahūdakasthāne kathāmākarṇayādbhutām..
yasmādbahūdakaṃ kuṇḍaṃ kāmarūpe yadasti ca.. 45.1 ..
1.4.d:
..नारद उवाच..
तथा बहूदकस्थाने कथामाकर्णयाद्भुताम्..
यस्माद्बहूदकं कुण्डं कामरूपे यदस्ति च.. 45.1 ..
1.4.m: Nārada said: / So also listen to a wonderful tale concerning the holy place Bahūdaka. / For the pool Bahūdaka which is in Kāmarūpa, 45.1

1.4.s:
tadasti cātra saṃkrāṃtaṃ tasmātproktaṃ bahūdakam..
kapilenātra taptvā ca varṣāṇi subahūnyapi.. 45.2 ..
1.4.d:
तदस्ति चात्र संक्रांतं तस्मात्प्रोक्तं बहूदकम्..
कपिलेनात्र तप्त्वा च वर्षाणि सुबहून्यपि.. 45.2 ..
1.4.m: has transferred its presence here; therefore it is called Bahūdaka. / And here Kapila, having performed austerities for very many years, 45.2

1.4.s:
sthāpitaṃ śobhanaṃ liṃgaṃ kapilaśvarasaṃjñitam..
tacca ligaṃ sadā pārtha nandabhadra iti samṛtaḥ.. 45.3 ..
1.4.d:
स्थापितं शोभनं लिंगं कपिलश्वरसंज्ञितम्..
तच्च लिगं सदा पार्थ नन्दभद्र इति समृतः.. 45.3 ..
1.4.m: installed an auspicious liṅga known as Kapileśvara. / And that liṅga, O Pārtha, a merchant named Nandabhadra 45.3

1.4.s:
vaṇiksaṃpūjayāmāsa trikālaṃ ca kṛtādaraḥ..
sarvadharmaviśeṣajñaḥ sākṣāddharma ivāparaḥ.. 45.4 ..
1.4.d:
वणिक्संपूजयामास त्रिकालं च कृतादरः..
सर्वधर्मविशेषज्ञः साक्षाद्धर्म इवापरः.. 45.4 ..
1.4.m: constantly worshipped three times a day with deep respect. / He knew the distinctions of all dharmas, like Dharma himself in visible form. 45.4

1.4.s:
nājñātaṃ tasya kiṃcicca yaddharmeṣu prakīrtyate..
sarveṣāṃ ca suhṛnnityaṃ sarveṣāṃ ca hite rataḥ.. 45.5 ..
1.4.d:
नाज्ञातं तस्य किंचिच्च यद्धर्मेषु प्रकीर्त्यते..
सर्वेषां च सुहृन्नित्यं सर्वेषां च हिते रतः.. 45.5 ..
1.4.m: Nothing that is proclaimed in dharmas was unknown to him. / He was always a friend to everyone and devoted to the welfare of all. 45.5

1.4.s:
karmaṇā manasā vācā dharmamenamupāśritaḥ..
na bhūto na bhaviṣyaśca na sa dharmo'sti kiṃcana.. 45.6 ..
1.4.d:
कर्मणा मनसा वाचा धर्ममेनमुपाश्रितः..
न भूतो न भविष्यश्च न स धर्मोऽस्ति किंचन.. 45.6 ..
1.4.m: He took refuge in this dharma in action, thought, and speech; / there has been no dharma, nor will there be, nor is there any 45.6

1.4.s:
vidoṣo yo hi sarvatra niścityaivaṃ vyavasthitaḥ..
asya dharmasamudrasya saṃpravṛddhasya sarvataḥ.. 45.7 ..
1.4.d:
विदोषो यो हि सर्वत्र निश्चित्यैवं व्यवस्थितः..
अस्य धर्मसमुद्रस्य संप्रवृद्धस्य सर्वतः.. 45.7 ..
1.4.m: that is flawless everywhere—having thus resolved, he stood firm. / From this ocean of dharma, which had expanded in every direction, 45.7

1.4.s:
nirmathya nandabhadreṇa āhṛtaṃ tanniśāmaya..
vāṇijyaṃ manyate śreṣṭhaṃ jīvanāya tadā sthitaḥ.. 45.8 ..
1.4.d:
निर्मथ्य नन्दभद्रेण आहृतं तन्निशामय..
वाणिज्यं मन्यते श्रेष्ठं जीवनाय तदा स्थितः.. 45.8 ..
1.4.m: hear what was extracted after Nandabhadra churned it. / Considering commerce best for livelihood, he then engaged [in it]. 45.8

1.4.s:
paricchinnaiḥ kāṣṭhatṛṇaiḥ śaraṇaṃ tena kāritam..
madyavarjaṃ bhedavarjaṃ kūṭavarjaṃ samaṃ tathā.. 45.9 ..
1.4.d:
परिच्छिन्नैः काष्ठतृणैः शरणं तेन कारितम्..
मद्यवर्जं भेदवर्जं कूटवर्जं समं तथा.. 45.9 ..
1.4.m: He had a shelter constructed out of measured wood and grass. / Free from intoxicants, free from discrimination, free from dishonesty, and equitable, 45.9

1.4.s:
sarvabhūteṣu vāṇijyamalpalābhena so'carat..
amāyayā parebhyo'sau gṛhītvaiva krayāṇakam.. 45.10 ..
1.4.d:
सर्वभूतेषु वाणिज्यमल्पलाभेन सोऽचरत्..
अमायया परेभ्योऽसौ गृहीत्वैव क्रयाणकम्.. 45.10 ..
1.4.m: he carried on trade among all living beings with small profit. / Having acquired merchandise from others without deception, 45.10

1.4.s:
amāyayaiva bhūtebhyo vikrīṇātyasya sadvratam..
kecidyajñaṃ praśaṃsaṃti nandabhadro na manyate.. 45.11 ..
1.4.d:
अमाययैव भूतेभ्यो विक्रीणात्यस्य सद्व्रतम्..
केचिद्यज्ञं प्रशंसंति नन्दभद्रो न मन्यते.. 45.11 ..
1.4.m: he sold it to creatures without any deceit: this was his noble practice. / Some praise sacrifice; Nandabhadra did not approve of it. 45.11

1.4.s:
doṣamenaṃ viniścitya śrṛṇu taṃ pāṃḍunandana..
lubdho'nṛtī dāṃbhīkaśca svapraśaṃsāparāyaṇaḥ.. 45.12 ..
1.4.d:
दोषमेनं विनिश्चित्य श्रृणु तं पांडुनन्दन..
लुब्धोऽनृती दांभीकश्च स्वप्रशंसापरायणः.. 45.12 ..
1.4.m: Ascertaining this fault, hear of it, O son of Pāṇḍu: / A greedy, untruthful, and deceitful man, intent on praising himself, 45.12

1.4.s:
yajanyajñairjagaddhaṃti svaṃ cāṃdhatamasaṃ nayet..
agnau prāstāhutiḥ samyagādityamupatiṣṭhate.. 45.13 ..
1.4.d:
यजन्यज्ञैर्जगद्धंति स्वं चांधतमसं नयेत्..
अग्नौ प्रास्ताहुतिः सम्यगादित्यमुपतिष्ठते.. 45.13 ..
1.4.m: by performing sacrifices destroys the world and leads himself to blinding darkness. / An oblation properly cast into the fire reaches the Sun; 45.13

1.4.s:
ādityājjāyate vṛṣṭirvṛṣṭerannaṃ tataḥ prajāḥ..
yadyadā yajamānasya ṛtvijo dravyameva ca.. 45.14 ..
1.4.d:
आदित्याज्जायते वृष्टिर्वृष्टेरन्नं ततः प्रजाः..
यद्यदा यजमानस्य ऋत्विजो द्रव्यमेव च.. 45.14 ..
1.4.m: from the Sun rain is born; from rain, food; and from that, living beings. / But whenever the patron of the sacrifice, the officiating priest, and the sacrificial goods 45.14

1.4.s:
cauraprāyasya kaluṣājjanma jāyejjanasya hi..
adakṣiṇe vṛthā yajñe kṛte cāpyavidhānataḥ.. 45.15 ..
1.4.d:
चौरप्रायस्य कलुषाज्जन्म जायेज्जनस्य हि..
अदक्षिणे वृथा यज्ञे कृते चाप्यविधानतः.. 45.15 ..
1.4.m: are essentially stolen, the birth of people arises from impurity. / When a sacrifice is performed without the priest's fee, in vain, and contrary to the injunctions, 45.15

1.4.s:
paśavo lakuṭairhanyuryajamānaṃ mṛtaṃ hatāḥ..
tasmācchuddhairyavadravyairyajamānaḥ śubhaḥ smṛtaḥ.. 45.16 ..
1.4.d:
पशवो लकुटैर्हन्युर्यजमानं मृतं हताः..
तस्माच्छुद्धैर्यवद्रव्यैर्यजमानः शुभः स्मृतः.. 45.16 ..
1.4.m: the slaughtered sacrificial beasts strike the dead patron of the sacrifice with cudgels. / Therefore, the patron of the sacrifice is considered auspicious [only] with pure barley materials. 45.16

1.4.s:
yajña evaṃ vicāryāsau yajñasāraṃ samāsthitaḥ..
śraddhayā devapūjā yā namaskāraḥ stutiḥ śubhā.. 45.17 ..
1.4.d:
यज्ञ एवं विचार्यासौ यज्ञसारं समास्थितः..
श्रद्धया देवपूजा या नमस्कारः स्तुतिः शुभा.. 45.17 ..
1.4.m: Having thus deliberated upon sacrifice, he adhered to the essence of sacrifice: / worship of the gods performed with faith, reverent bowing, auspicious praise, 45.17

1.4.s:
naivedyaṃ haviṣaścaiva yajño'yaṃ hi vikalmaṣaḥ..
sa eva yajñaḥ prokto vai yena tuṣyanti devatāḥ.. 45.18 ..
1.4.d:
नैवेद्यं हविषश्चैव यज्ञोऽयं हि विकल्मषः..
स एव यज्ञः प्रोक्तो वै येन तुष्यन्ति देवताः.. 45.18 ..
1.4.m: and the food-offering consisting of sacrificial food—this indeed is a sacrifice free from sin. / That alone is truly declared to be sacrifice by which the deities are pleased. 45.18

1.4.s:
kecicchaṃsanti saṃnyāsaṃ nandabhadro na manyate..
yo hi saṃnyasya viṣayānmanasā gṛhyate punaḥ.. 45.19 ..
1.4.d:
केचिच्छंसन्ति संन्यासं नन्दभद्रो न मन्यते..
यो हि संन्यस्य विषयान्मनसा गृह्यते पुनः.. 45.19 ..
1.4.m: Some praise renunciation; Nandabhadra did not approve of it. / For one who renounces the objects of sense and yet grasps them again in his mind 45.19

1.4.s:
ubhayabhraṣṭa evāsau bhinnā bhūmirvinaśyati..
saṃnyāsasya tu yatsāraṃ tattenāvṛtamuttamam.. 45.20 ..
1.4.d:
उभयभ्रष्ट एवासौ भिन्ना भूमिर्विनश्यति..
संन्यासस्य तु यत्सारं तत्तेनावृतमुत्तमम्.. 45.20 ..
1.4.m: has fallen from both; like fragmented ground, he is destroyed. / But what is the highest essence of renunciation, that was embraced by him: 45.20

1.4.s:
kasyacinnaiva karmāṇi śapate vā praśaṃsati..
nānāmārgasthitām̐llokāṃścandravallīyate kṣitau.. 45.21 ..
1.4.d:
कस्यचिन्नैव कर्माणि शपते वा प्रशंसति..
नानामार्गस्थिताम्̐ल्लोकांश्चन्द्रवल्लीयते क्षितौ.. 45.21 ..
1.4.m: He neither curses nor praises the actions of anyone; / observing the world established in diverse paths, he remains absorbed upon earth like the moon. 45.21

1.4.s:
na dveṣṭi no kāmayate na viruddho'nurudhyate..
samāśmakāṃcano dhīrastulyaniṃdātmasaṃstutiḥ.. 45.22 ..
1.4.d:
न द्वेष्टि नो कामयते न विरुद्धोऽनुरुध्यते..
समाश्मकांचनो धीरस्तुल्यनिंदात्मसंस्तुतिः.. 45.22 ..
1.4.m: He neither hates nor desires; he is neither hostile nor fawning; / stone and gold are equal to him; he is wise, looking upon blame and praise of himself as the same; 45.22

1.4.s:
abhayaḥ sarvabhūtebhyo yathāṃdhabadhirākṛtiḥ..
na karmaṇāṃ phalākāṃkṣā śivasyārādhanaṃ hi tat.. 45.23 ..
1.4.d:
अभयः सर्वभूतेभ्यो यथांधबधिराकृतिः..
न कर्मणां फलाकांक्षा शिवस्याराधनं हि तत्.. 45.23 ..
1.4.m: granting safety to all living beings, appearing as if blind and deaf; / having no desire for the fruit of actions—for that is worship of Śiva. 45.23

1.4.s: kāraṇāddharmamanvicchanna lobhaṃ ca tataścaran.. 45.24 ..
1.4.d: कारणाद्धर्ममन्विच्छन्न लोभं च ततश्चरन्.. 45.24 ..
1.4.m: Seeking dharma by reasonable grounds and not acting out of greed, 45.24

1.4.s:
vivicya naṃdabhadrastatsāraṃ mokṣeṣu jagṛhe..
kṛṣiṃ kecitpraśaṃsaṃti naṃdabhadro na manyate.. 45.25 ..
1.4.d:
विविच्य नंदभद्रस्तत्सारं मोक्षेषु जगृहे..
कृषिं केचित्प्रशंसंति नंदभद्रो न मन्यते.. 45.25 ..
1.4.m: Nandabhadra, having discriminated, grasped its essence among the ways of liberation. / Some praise agriculture; Nandabhadra did not approve of it, 45.25

1.4.s:
yasyāṃ chiṃdaṃti vṛṣaṇā vṛṣāṇāṃ caiva nāsikām..
karṣayaṃti mahābhārānbadhnaṃti damayaṃti ca.. 45.26 ..
1.4.d:
यस्यां छिंदंति वृषणा वृषाणां चैव नासिकाम्..
कर्षयंति महाभारान्बध्नंति दमयंति च.. 45.26 ..
1.4.m: in which they castrate bulls and pierce their noses, / make them drag heavy loads, bind them, and break them in, 45.26

1.4.s:
bahudaṃśamayāndeśānnayaṃti bahukardamān..
vāhasaṃpīḍitā dhuryāḥ sīdaṃtyavidhinā pare.. 45.27 ..
1.4.d:
बहुदंशमयान्देशान्नयंति बहुकर्दमान्..
वाहसंपीडिता धुर्याः सीदंत्यविधिना परे.. 45.27 ..
1.4.m: lead them to regions infested with gadflies and full of thick mud; / oppressed by burdens, the draft animals suffer, and others [perish] unlawfully. 45.27

1.4.s:
manyaṃte bhrūṇahatyāpi viśiṣṭā nāsya karmaṇaḥ..
aghnyā iti gavāṃ nāma śrutau tāḥ pīḍayetkatham.. 45.28 ..
1.4.d:
मन्यंते भ्रूणहत्यापि विशिष्टा नास्य कर्मणः..
अघ्न्या इति गवां नाम श्रुतौ ताः पीडयेत्कथम्.. 45.28 ..
1.4.m: They consider even the killing of an embryo to be no worse than this work. / In the Veda the name for cows is ‘unslayable’; how then could one torment them? 45.28

1.4.s:
bhūmiṃ bhūmiśayāṃścaiva haṃti kāṣṭhamayomukham..
paṃceṃdriyeṣu jīveṣu sarvaṃ vasati daivatam.. 45.29 ..
1.4.d:
भूमिं भूमिशयांश्चैव हंति काष्ठमयोमुखम्..
पंचेंद्रियेषु जीवेषु सर्वं वसति दैवतम्.. 45.29 ..
1.4.m: The iron-tipped wood strikes the earth and creatures living in the earth. / In living beings endowed with five senses, all divinity resides. 45.29

1.4.s:
ādityaścaṃdramā vāyuḥ prabhūtyaiva ca tāṃstu yaḥ..
vikrīṇāti sumūḍhasya tasya kā nu vicāraṇā.. 45.30 ..
1.4.d:
आदित्यश्चंद्रमा वायुः प्रभूत्यैव च तांस्तु यः..
विक्रीणाति सुमूढस्य तस्य का नु विचारणा.. 45.30 ..
1.4.m: The Sun, the Moon, and the Wind, after producing them—for one who / sells them, exceedingly foolish, what consideration can there be? 45.30

1.4.s:
ajo'gnirvaruṇo meṣaḥ sūryaśca pṛthivī virāṭ..
dhenurvatsaśca somo vai vikrīyaitānna sidhyati.. 45.31 ..
1.4.d:
अजोऽग्निर्वरुणो मेषः सूर्यश्च पृथिवी विराट्..
धेनुर्वत्सश्च सोमो वै विक्रीयैतान्न सिध्यति.. 45.31 ..
1.4.m: The goat is Agni, the ram is Varuṇa, the Sun is earth and Virāṭ, / the cow and the calf are Soma; by selling these, one does not attain success. 45.31

1.4.s:
evaṃvidhasahasraiśca yutā doṣaiḥ kṛṣiḥ sadā..
aṣṭāgavaṃ syāddhi halaṃ triṃśadbhāgaṃ tyajetkṛṣeḥ.. 45.32 ..
1.4.d:
एवंविधसहस्रैश्च युता दोषैः कृषिः सदा..
अष्टागवं स्याद्धि हलं त्रिंशद्भागं त्यजेत्कृषेः.. 45.32 ..
1.4.m: Agriculture is always accompanied by thousands of faults of this kind: / A plow should have eight oxen, and one should abandon a thirtieth share of the farm; 45.32

1.4.s:
dharme dadyātpaśūnvṛddhānpuṣyādeṣā kṛṣiḥ kutaḥ..
sārametatkṛṣestena naṃdabhadreṇa cādṛtam.. 45.33 ..
1.4.d:
धर्मे दद्यात्पशून्वृद्धान्पुष्यादेषा कृषिः कुतः..
सारमेतत्कृषेस्तेन नंदभद्रेण चादृतम्.. 45.33 ..
1.4.m: one should give aged beasts for dharma—how could this agriculture ever prosper? / That essence of agriculture was respected by that Nandabhadra. 45.33

1.4.s:
visādhitavyānyannāni svaśaktyā devapitṛṣu..
manuṣya dvijabhūteṣu niyujyāśnīta sarvadā.. 45.34 ..
1.4.d:
विसाधितव्यान्यन्नानि स्वशक्त्या देवपितृषु..
मनुष्य द्विजभूतेषु नियुज्याश्नीत सर्वदा.. 45.34 ..
1.4.m: Food should be prepared and offered according to one's capacity to the gods and ancestors; / having assigned it to men, twice-born, and living beings, one should always eat.

1.4.s:
kecicchaṃsaṃti caiśvaryaṃ naṃdabhadro na manyate..
mānuṣā mānuṣāneva dāsabhāvena bhuṃjate.. 45.35 ..
1.4.d:
केचिच्छंसंति चैश्वर्यं नंदभद्रो न मन्यते..
मानुषा मानुषानेव दासभावेन भुंजते.. 45.35 ..
1.4.m: Some praise lordly power, but Nandabhadra did not value it: / humans exploit fellow humans in the condition of servitude;

1.4.s:
vadhabaṃdhanirodhena pīḍayaṃti divāniśam..
dehaṃ kimetaddhātuḥ svaṃ māturvā janakasya vā.. 45.36 ..
1.4.d:
वधबंधनिरोधेन पीडयंति दिवानिशम्..
देहं किमेतद्धातुः स्वं मातुर्वा जनकस्य वा.. 45.36 ..
1.4.m: day and night they torment [them] with slaughter, binding, and imprisonment. / Whose own body is this: the Creator's, the mother's, or the father's,

1.4.s:
mātuḥ piturvā balinaḥ kreturagneḥ śuno'pi vā..
iti saṃciṃtya vyaharannamarā iva īśvarāḥ.. 45.37 ..
1.4.d:
मातुः पितुर्वा बलिनः क्रेतुरग्नेः शुनोऽपि वा..
इति संचिंत्य व्यहरन्नमरा इव ईश्वराः.. 45.37 ..
1.4.m: the mother's, the father's, the powerful buyer's, or even of fire and dogs? / Thinking thus, masters lived like the immortals.

1.4.s:
aiśvaryamadapāpiṣṭhā mahāmadyamadādayaḥ..
aiśvaryamadamatto hi nā patitvā hi mādyati.. 45.38 ..
1.4.d:
ऐश्वर्यमदपापिष्ठा महामद्यमदादयः..
ऐश्वर्यमदमत्तो हि ना पतित्वा हि माद्यति.. 45.38 ..
1.4.m: The intoxication of lordly power is the most sinful of all, surpassing the intoxication of strong wine; / for a man intoxicated with the pride of lordly power falls and is driven mad.

1.4.s: ātmavatsarvabhṛtyeṣu śriyā naiva ca mādyati.. 45.39 ..
1.4.d: आत्मवत्सर्वभृत्येषु श्रिया नैव च माद्यति.. 45.39 ..
1.4.m: [Looking] upon all servants as upon himself, he was never intoxicated by wealth.

1.4.s:
ātmapratyayavāndehī kveśvaraścedṛśo'sti hi..
aiśvaryasyāpi sāraṃ sa jagrāhaitanniśāmaya.. 45.40 ..
1.4.d:
आत्मप्रत्ययवान्देही क्वेश्वरश्चेदृशोऽस्ति हि..
ऐश्वर्यस्यापि सारं स जग्राहैतन्निशामय.. 45.40 ..
1.4.m: An embodied soul possessing self-conviction—where indeed is there such a master? / He seized the essence even of lordship; listen to this:

1.4.s:
svaśaktyā sarva bhūteṣu yadasau na parāṅmukhaḥ..
tīrthāyeke praśaṃsaṃti naṃdabhadro na manyate.. 45.41 ..
1.4.d:
स्वशक्त्या सर्व भूतेषु यदसौ न पराङ्मुखः..
तीर्थायेके प्रशंसंति नंदभद्रो न मन्यते.. 45.41 ..
1.4.m: according to his capacity he was never indifferent towards all beings. / Some praise sacred fords, but Nandabhadra did not value [them]:

1.4.s:
śrameṇa saṃkarāttāpaśītavātakṣudhā tṛṣā..
krodhena dharmagehasya nāpi nāśamavāpnuyāt.. 45.42 ..
1.4.d:
श्रमेण संकरात्तापशीतवातक्षुधा तृषा..
क्रोधेन धर्मगेहस्य नापि नाशमवाप्नुयात्.. 45.42 ..
1.4.m: one should not incur the destruction of the house of virtue through fatigue, confusion, heat, cold, wind, hunger, thirst, / or anger.

1.4.s:
saukhyena vā dhanasyāpi śraddhayā svalpagorthavān..
samartho hi mahatpuṇyaṃ śakta āptuṃ kva vāsti saḥ.. 45.43 ..
1.4.d:
सौख्येन वा धनस्यापि श्रद्धया स्वल्पगोर्थवान्..
समर्थो हि महत्पुण्यं शक्त आप्तुं क्व वास्ति सः.. 45.43 ..
1.4.m: Whether through comfort, wealth, or faith, one who has few possessions, / being capable of great merit—where is he who is able to attain [it]?

1.4.s:
sadā śucirdevayājī tīrthasāraṃ gṛhegṛha..
nāpaḥ punaṃti pāpāni na śailā na mahāśramāḥ.. 45.44 ..
1.4.d:
सदा शुचिर्देवयाजी तीर्थसारं गृहेगृह..
नापः पुनंति पापानि न शैला न महाश्रमाः.. 45.44 ..
1.4.m: Always pure, sacrificing to the gods, the essence of the sacred ford is in every house. / Waters do not purify sins, nor do mountains, nor great hermitages;

1.4.s:
ātmā punāti pāpāni yadi pāpānnivartate..
evameva samācāraṃ prādurbhūtaṃ tatastataḥ.. 45.45 ..
1.4.d:
आत्मा पुनाति पापानि यदि पापान्निवर्तते..
एवमेव समाचारं प्रादुर्भूतं ततस्ततः.. 45.45 ..
1.4.m: the self purifies sins if it turns away from sin. / Thus the wise Nandabhadra constantly adhered to / the righteous conduct that manifested here and there, unifying it.

1.4.s:
ekīkṛtya sadā dhīmānnaṃdabhadraḥ samāsthitaḥ..
tasyaivaṃ vartataḥ sādhoḥ spṛhayaṃtyapi devatāḥ.. 45.46 ..
1.4.d:
एकीकृत्य सदा धीमान्नंदभद्रः समास्थितः..
तस्यैवं वर्ततः साधोः स्पृहयंत्यपि देवताः.. 45.46 ..
1.4.m: While that virtuous man conducted himself in this manner, even the gods envied [him]. / All, headed by Vāsava, experienced supreme astonishment.

1.4.s:
vāsavapramukhāḥ sarve vismayaṃ ca paraṃ yayuḥ..
atraiva sthānake cāpi śūdro'bhūtprativeśmakaḥ.. 45.47 ..
1.4.d:
वासवप्रमुखाः सर्वे विस्मयं च परं ययुः..
अत्रैव स्थानके चापि शूद्रोऽभूत्प्रतिवेश्मकः.. 45.47 ..
1.4.m: And in this very place there was a śūdra neighbor; / he constantly envied the highly righteous Nandabhadra.

1.4.s:
sa naṃdabhadraṃ dharmiṣṭhaṃ punaḥ punarasūyata..
nāstikaḥ sa durācāraḥ satyavrata iti śrutaḥ.. 45.48 ..
1.4.d:
स नंदभद्रं धर्मिष्ठं पुनः पुनरसूयत..
नास्तिकः स दुराचारः सत्यव्रत इति श्रुतः.. 45.48 ..
1.4.m: A non-believer of wicked conduct, he was known by the name Satyavrata. / He was always watching for a vulnerability in Nandabhadra:

1.4.s:
sa sadā naṃdabhadrasya vilokayati cāṃtaram..
chidraṃ cedasya paśyāmi tato dharmānnivartaye.. 45.49 ..
1.4.d:
स सदा नंदभद्रस्य विलोकयति चांतरम्..
छिद्रं चेदस्य पश्यामि ततो धर्मान्निवर्तये.. 45.49 ..
1.4.m: "If I see an opening in him, then I will turn him away from righteousness." / Such is the very nature of cruel, atheistic, wicked souls:

1.4.s:
svabhāva eva krūrāṇāṃ nāstikānāṃ durātmanām..
ātmānaṃ pātayaṃtyeva pātayaṃtyaparaṃ ca yat.. 45.50 ..
1.4.d:
स्वभाव एव क्रूराणां नास्तिकानां दुरात्मनाम्..
आत्मानं पातयंत्येव पातयंत्यपरं च यत्.. 45.50 ..
1.4.m: they cause their own downfall and cause the downfall of others too.

1.4.s:
tatastvevaṃ vartato'sya naṃdabhadrasya dhīmataḥ..
eko'bhūttanayaḥ kaṣṭādvārdhike so'pyanaśyata.. 45.51 ..
1.4.d:
ततस्त्वेवं वर्ततोऽस्य नंदभद्रस्य धीमतः..
एकोऽभूत्तनयः कष्टाद्वार्धिके सोऽप्यनश्यत.. 45.51 ..
1.4.m: Then, as this wise Nandabhadra was living in this manner, / an only son was born with difficulty, and he died in his old age.

1.4.s:
tacca daivakṛtaṃ matvā na śuśoca mahāmatiḥ..
devo vā mānavo vāpi ko hi devādvimucyate.. 45.52 ..
1.4.d:
तच्च दैवकृतं मत्वा न शुशोच महामतिः..
देवो वा मानवो वापि को हि देवाद्विमुच्यते.. 45.52 ..
1.4.m: Considering that to be caused by fate, the great-minded one did not grieve: / whether a god or a human being, who indeed is freed from fate?

1.4.s:
tato'sya supriyā bhāryā sarvaiḥ sādhvīguṇairyutā..
gṛhadharmasya mūrtiryā sākṣādiva aruṃdhatī.. 45.53 ..
1.4.d:
ततोऽस्य सुप्रिया भार्या सर्वैः साध्वीगुणैर्युता..
गृहधर्मस्य मूर्तिर्या साक्षादिव अरुंधती.. 45.53 ..
1.4.m: Then his dearly beloved wife, endowed with all virtues of a faithful wife, / who was the embodiment of household virtue, as if Arundhatī in visible form,

1.4.s:
vināśamāgatā pārtha kanakānāma nāmataḥ..
tato yateṃdriyo'pyeṣa gṛhadharmavināśataḥ.. 45.54 ..
1.4.d:
विनाशमागता पार्थ कनकानाम नामतः..
ततो यतेंद्रियोऽप्येष गृहधर्मविनाशतः.. 45.54 ..
1.4.m: came to destruction, O Pārtha, Kanakā by name. / Then, although he had restrained his senses, due to the destruction of household duty,

1.4.s:
śuśoca hā kaṣṭamiti pāpohamiti cāsakṛt..
tattasya cāṃtaraṃ dṛṣṭvā'hṛṣyatyavrataścirāt.. 45.55 ..
1.4.d:
शुशोच हा कष्टमिति पापोहमिति चासकृत्..
तत्तस्य चांतरं दृष्ट्वाऽहृष्यत्यव्रतश्चिरात्.. 45.55 ..
1.4.m: he grieved, "Alas, what misery! I am a sinner!" repeatedly. / Seeing that vulnerability in him, Satyavrata rejoiced after a long time.

1.4.s:
upāvrajya ca hā kaṣṭaṃ bruvaṃstaṃ naṃdabhadrakam..
dadhikarṇa ivāsādya naṃdabhadramuvāca saḥ.. 45.56 ..
1.4.d:
उपाव्रज्य च हा कष्टं ब्रुवंस्तं नंदभद्रकम्..
दधिकर्ण इवासाद्य नंदभद्रमुवाच सः.. 45.56 ..
1.4.m: Approaching and saying, "Alas, what misery!" to that Nandabhadra, / coming near like [the cat] Dadhikarṇa, he spoke to Nandabhadra:

1.4.s:
hā naṃdabhadra yadyevaṃ tavāpyevaṃvidhaṃ phalam..
etena manye manasi dharmopyeṣa vṛthaiva yat.. 45.57 ..
1.4.d:
हा नंदभद्र यद्येवं तवाप्येवंविधं फलम्..
एतेन मन्ये मनसि धर्मोप्येष वृथैव यत्.. 45.57 ..
1.4.m: "Alas, Nandabhadra, if such a result befalls even you, / because of this I consider in my mind that even this virtue is utterly in vain.

1.4.s:
ityādi bahudhā procya tattadvākyaṃ tatastataḥ..
satyavratastataḥ prāha naṃdabhadraṃ kṛpānvitaḥ.. 45.58 ..
1.4.d:
इत्यादि बहुधा प्रोच्य तत्तद्वाक्यं ततस्ततः..
सत्यव्रतस्ततः प्राह नंदभद्रं कृपान्वितः.. 45.58 ..
1.4.m: Speaking thus in various ways, uttering such words from here and there, / Satyavrata, full of [feigned] pity, then said to Nandabhadra:

1.4.s:
naṃdabhadra sadā tubhyaṃ vaktukāmosmi kiṃcana..
prastāvasyāpyabhāvācca noditaṃ ca mayā kvacit.. 45.59 ..
1.4.d:
नंदभद्र सदा तुभ्यं वक्तुकामोस्मि किंचन..
प्रस्तावस्याप्यभावाच्च नोदितं च मया क्वचित्.. 45.59 ..
1.4.m: "Nandabhadra, I have always wished to say something to you, / but due to the absence of an occasion, nothing was spoken by me anywhere.

1.4.s:
aprastāvaṃ bruvanvākyaṃ bṛhaspatirapidhruvam..
labhate buddhyavajñānamavamānaṃ ca hīnavat.. 45.60 ..
1.4.d:
अप्रस्तावं ब्रुवन्वाक्यं बृहस्पतिरपिध्रुवम्..
लभते बुद्ध्यवज्ञानमवमानं च हीनवत्.. 45.60 ..
1.4.m: Speaking words without an occasion, even Bṛhaspati certainly / incurs disrespect for his intellect and contempt like an inferior."

1.4.s:
..nandabhadra uvāca..
brūhibrūhi na me kiṃcitsādhu gopyaṃ priyaṃ param..
vacobhiḥ śuddhasattvānāṃ na mokṣo'pyupamīyate.. 45.61 ..
1.4.d:
..नन्दभद्र उवाच..
ब्रूहिब्रूहि न मे किंचित्साधु गोप्यं प्रियं परम्..
वचोभिः शुद्धसत्त्वानां न मोक्षोऽप्युपमीयते.. 45.61 ..
1.4.m: Nandabhadra said: / "Speak, speak! Nothing good and supremely dear should be concealed from me. / Even liberation cannot be compared with the words of those whose minds are pure."

1.4.s:
..satyavrata uvāca..
navabhirnavabhiścaiva vimuktaṃ vāgvidūṣaṇaiḥ..
navabhirbuddhidoṣaiśca vākyaṃ vakṣyāmyadoṣavat.. 45.62 ..
1.4.d:
..सत्यव्रत उवाच..
नवभिर्नवभिश्चैव विमुक्तं वाग्विदूषणैः..
नवभिर्बुद्धिदोषैश्च वाक्यं वक्ष्याम्यदोषवत्.. 45.62 ..
1.4.m: Satyavrata said: / "Free from twice nine faults of speech / and nine defects of the intellect, I will speak faultless words.

1.4.s:
saukṣmyaṃ saṃkhyākramaścāpi nirṇayaḥ saprayojanaḥ..
paṃcaitānyarthajātāni yatra tadvākyamucyate.. 45.63 ..
1.4.d:
सौक्ष्म्यं संख्याक्रमश्चापि निर्णयः सप्रयोजनः..
पंचैतान्यर्थजातानि यत्र तद्वाक्यमुच्यते.. 45.63 ..
1.4.m: Subtlety, enumeration, sequence, and resolution endowed with a purpose— / where these five classes of meaning are present, that is called a proper statement.

1.4.s:
dharmamarthaṃ ca kāmaṃ ca mokṣaṃ coddiśya cocyate..
prayojanamiti proktaṃ prathamaṃ vākyalakṣaṇam.. 45.64 ..
1.4.d:
धर्ममर्थं च कामं च मोक्षं चोद्दिश्य चोच्यते..
प्रयोजनमिति प्रोक्तं प्रथमं वाक्यलक्षणम्.. 45.64 ..
1.4.m: What is spoken with aim towards virtue, wealth, pleasure, and liberation / is declared to be the 'purpose,' the first characteristic of speech.

1.4.s:
dharmārthakāmamokṣeṣu pratijñāya viśeṣataḥ..
idaṃ taditi vākyāṃte procyate sa vinirṇayaḥ.. 45.65 ..
1.4.d:
धर्मार्थकाममोक्षेषु प्रतिज्ञाय विशेषतः..
इदं तदिति वाक्यांते प्रोच्यते स विनिर्णयः.. 45.65 ..
1.4.m: Having specifically made a proposition regarding virtue, wealth, pleasure, and liberation, / stating 'it is this' at the end of a sentence is 'resolution.'

1.4.s:
idaṃ pūrvamidaṃ paścādvaktavyaṃ yatkrameṇa hi..
kramayogaṃ tamapyāhurvākyatattavido budhāḥ.. 45.66 ..
1.4.d:
इदं पूर्वमिदं पश्चाद्वक्तव्यं यत्क्रमेण हि..
क्रमयोगं तमप्याहुर्वाक्यतत्तविदो बुधाः.. 45.66 ..
1.4.m: That which must be spoken in sequence, 'this first, this next,' / the wise who know the truth of speech call that the 'application of sequence.'

1.4.s:
doṣāṇāṃ ca guṇānāṃ ca pramāṇaṃ pravibhāgataḥ..
ubhayārthamapi prekṣya sā saṃkhyetyupadhāryatām.. 45.67 ..
1.4.d:
दोषाणां च गुणानां च प्रमाणं प्रविभागतः..
उभयार्थमपि प्रेक्ष्य सा संख्येत्युपधार्यताम्.. 45.67 ..
1.4.m: The measure of faults and merits according to their division, / discerning both purposes—let that be understood as 'enumeration.'

1.4.s:
vākyajñeyeṣu bhinneṣu yatrābhedaḥ pradṛśyate..
tatrātiśayahetutvaṃ tatsaukṣmyamiti nirdiśet.. 45.68 ..
1.4.d:
वाक्यज्ञेयेषु भिन्नेषु यत्राभेदः प्रदृश्यते..
तत्रातिशयहेतुत्वं तत्सौक्ष्म्यमिति निर्दिशेत्.. 45.68 ..
1.4.m: Where non-difference is seen among distinct objects to be known through speech, / because it is the cause of distinction there, one should designate that as 'subtlety.'

1.4.s:
iti vākyaguṇānāṃ ca vāgdoṣāndvinava śrṛṇu..
apetārthamabhinnārthamapavṛttaṃ tathādhikam.. 45.69 ..
1.4.d:
इति वाक्यगुणानां च वाग्दोषान्द्विनव श्रृणु..
अपेतार्थमभिन्नार्थमपवृत्तं तथाधिकम्.. 45.69 ..
1.4.m: Thus of the merits of speech; now hear the eighteen faults of speech: / devoid of meaning, redundant, metre-breaking, superfluous,

1.4.s:
aślakṣṇaṃ cāpi saṃdigdhaṃ padāṃte guru cākṣaram..
parāṅmukhamukhaṃ yacca anṛtaṃ cāpyasaṃskṛtam.. 45.70 ..
1.4.d:
अश्लक्ष्णं चापि संदिग्धं पदांते गुरु चाक्षरम्..
पराङ्मुखमुखं यच्च अनृतं चाप्यसंस्कृतम्.. 45.70 ..
1.4.m: harsh, ambiguous, having a heavy syllable at the end of a word, / turning its face away from the topic, untruthful, unrefined,

1.4.s:
viruddhaṃ yattrivargeṇa nyūnaṃ kaṣṭātiśabdakam..
vyutkramābhihṛtaṃ yac saśeṣaṃ cāpyahetukam.. 45.71 ..
1.4.d:
विरुद्धं यत्त्रिवर्गेण न्यूनं कष्टातिशब्दकम्..
व्युत्क्रमाभिहृतं यच् सशेषं चाप्यहेतुकम्.. 45.71 ..
1.4.m: contrary to the three aims of life, deficient, using harsh and excessive words, / stated out of order, incomplete, groundless,

1.4.s:
niṣkāraṇaṃ ca vāgdoṣānbuddhijāñchṛṇu tvaṃ ca yān..
kāmātkrodhādbhayāccaiva lobhāddainyādanāryakāt.. 45.72 ..
1.4.d:
निष्कारणं च वाग्दोषान्बुद्धिजाञ्छृणु त्वं च यान्..
कामात्क्रोधाद्भयाच्चैव लोभाद्दैन्यादनार्यकात्.. 45.72 ..
1.4.m: and purposeless. And hear those faults born of the intellect: / from desire, anger, fear, greed, wretchedness, ignobility,

1.4.s:
hīnānukrośato mānānna ca vakṣyāmi kiṃcana..
vaktā śrotā ca vākyaṃ ca yadā tvavikalaṃ bhavet.. 45.73 ..
1.4.d:
हीनानुक्रोशतो मानान्न च वक्ष्यामि किंचन..
वक्ता श्रोता च वाक्यं च यदा त्वविकलं भवेत्.. 45.73 ..
1.4.m: deficient compassion, or pride, I shall speak nothing. / When speaker, listener, and statement are unimpaired,

1.4.s:
samameti vivakṣāyāṃ tadā so'rthaḥ prakāśate..
vaktavye tu yadā vaktā śrotāramavamanyate.. 45.74 ..
1.4.d:
सममेति विवक्षायां तदा सोऽर्थः प्रकाशते..
वक्तव्ये तु यदा वक्ता श्रोतारमवमन्यते.. 45.74 ..
1.4.m: and united in the intention to speak, then that meaning shines forth. / But when the speaker scorns the listener in what is to be spoken,

1.4.s:
śrotā cāpyatha vaktāraṃ tadā vākyaṃ na rohati..
atha yaḥ svapriyaṃ brūyācchroturvotsṛjyayadṛtam.. 45.75 ..
1.4.d:
श्रोता चाप्यथ वक्तारं तदा वाक्यं न रोहति..
अथ यः स्वप्रियं ब्रूयाच्छ्रोतुर्वोत्सृज्ययदृतम्.. 45.75 ..
1.4.m: or the listener scorns the speaker, then the statement does not take root. / Moreover, one who speaks what is pleasing to oneself or to the listener, having abandoned the truth,

1.4.s:
viśaṃkā jāyate tasminvākyaṃ tadapi doṣavat..
tasmādyaḥ svapriyaṃ tyaktvā śrotuścāpyatha yatpriyam.. 45.76 ..
1.4.d:
विशंका जायते तस्मिन्वाक्यं तदपि दोषवत्..
तस्माद्यः स्वप्रियं त्यक्त्वा श्रोतुश्चाप्यथ यत्प्रियम्.. 45.76 ..
1.4.m: doubt arises in that, and that statement also becomes faulty. / Therefore, one who, having abandoned what is pleasing to oneself or what is pleasing to the listener,

1.4.s:
satyameva prabhāṣeta sa vaktā netaro bhuvi..
mithyāvādāñchāstrajālasaṃbhavānyadvihāya ca.. 45.77 ..
1.4.d:
सत्यमेव प्रभाषेत स वक्ता नेतरो भुवि..
मिथ्यावादाञ्छास्त्रजालसंभवान्यद्विहाय च.. 45.77 ..
1.4.m: speaks only the truth—he is the speaker, none other on earth, / having abandoned false statements arising from the web of scriptures."

1.4.s:
satyameva vrataṃ yasmāttasmātsatyavratastvaham..
satyaṃ te saṃpravakṣyāmi maṃtumarhasi tattathā.. 45.78 ..
1.4.d:
सत्यमेव व्रतं यस्मात्तस्मात्सत्यव्रतस्त्वहम्..
सत्यं ते संप्रवक्ष्यामि मंतुमर्हसि तत्तथा.. 45.78 ..
1.4.m:
Because truth alone is my vow, therefore I am Satyavrata.
I shall tell you the truth; you ought to understand it as such.

1.4.s:
yadāprabhṛti bhadra tvaṃ pāṣāṇasyārcane rataḥ..
tadāprabhṛti kiṃcicca na hi paśyāmi śobhanam.. 45.79 ..
1.4.d:
यदाप्रभृति भद्र त्वं पाषाणस्यार्चने रतः..
तदाप्रभृति किंचिच्च न हि पश्यामि शोभनम्.. 45.79 ..
1.4.m:
Ever since you, my good man, have been devoted to worshipping a stone,
from that time on I do not see any good at all [for you].

1.4.s:
ekaḥ so'pi suto naṣṭo bhāryā cāryā'pyanaśyata..
kūṭānāṃ karmaṇāṃ sādho phalamevaṃvidhaṃ bhavet.. 45.80 ..
1.4.d:
एकः सोऽपि सुतो नष्टो भार्या चार्याऽप्यनश्यत..
कूटानां कर्मणां साधो फलमेवंविधं भवेत्.. 45.80 ..
1.4.m:
Even that one son was lost, and your noble wife also perished.
O good man, such indeed is the fruit of deceptive rites.

1.4.s:
kva devāḥ saṃti mithyaitaddṛśyaṃte cedbhavaṃtyapi..
sarvā ca kūṭaviprāṇāṃ dravyāyaiṣā vikalpanā.. 45.81 ..
1.4.d:
क्व देवाः संति मिथ्यैतद्दृश्यंते चेद्भवंत्यपि..
सर्वा च कूटविप्राणां द्रव्यायैषा विकल्पना.. 45.81 ..
1.4.m:
Where are the gods? This is false. If they exist, they would be visible.
This whole fabrication is made by deceitful brahmins for the sake of wealth.

1.4.s:
pitṝnuddiśya yacchaṃti mama hāsaḥ prajāyate..
annasyopadravaṃ yacca mṛto hi kimaśiṣyata.. 45.82 ..
1.4.d:
पितॄनुद्दिश्य यच्छंति मम हासः प्रजायते..
अन्नस्योपद्रवं यच्च मृतो हि किमशिष्यत.. 45.82 ..
1.4.m:
When they offer gifts in the name of the ancestors, laughter arises in me.
And that waste of food—for would a dead man eat?

1.4.s:
yattvidaṃ bahudhā mūḍhā varṇayaṃti dvijādhamāḥ..
viśvanirmāṇamakhilaṃ tathāpi śrṛṇu satyataḥ.. 45.83 ..
1.4.d:
यत्त्विदं बहुधा मूढा वर्णयंति द्विजाधमाः..
विश्वनिर्माणमखिलं तथापि श्रृणु सत्यतः.. 45.83 ..
1.4.m:
As for how the foolish, base twice-born describe in many ways
the entire creation of the universe, listen nevertheless to the truth [about it]:

1.4.s:
utpattiścāpi bhaṃgaśca viśvasyaitaddvayaṃ mṛṣā..
evameva hi sarvaṃ ca sadidaṃ vartate jagat.. 45.84 ..
1.4.d:
उत्पत्तिश्चापि भंगश्च विश्वस्यैतद्द्वयं मृषा..
एवमेव हि सर्वं च सदिदं वर्तते जगत्.. 45.84 ..
1.4.m:
Both the origin and the dissolution of the universe are false.
In this very way does this entire world always exist.

1.4.s:
svabhāvato viśvamidaṃ hi vartate svabhāvataḥ sūryamukhā bhramaṃtyamī..
svabhāvato vāyavo vāṃti nityaṃ svabhāvato varṣati cāṃbudo'yam.. 45.85 ..
1.4.d:
स्वभावतो विश्वमिदं हि वर्तते स्वभावतः सूर्यमुखा भ्रमंत्यमी..
स्वभावतो वायवो वांति नित्यं स्वभावतो वर्षति चांबुदोऽयम्.. 45.85 ..
1.4.m:
By inherent nature this universe exists; by inherent nature these [luminaries] headed by the sun revolve;
by inherent nature the winds blow constantly; and by inherent nature this cloud rains.

1.4.s:
svabhāvato rohati dhānyajātaṃ svabhāvato varṣaśītātapatvam..
svabhāvataḥ saṃsthitā medinī ca svabhāvataḥ saritaḥ saṃsravaṃti.. 45.86 ..
1.4.d:
स्वभावतो रोहति धान्यजातं स्वभावतो वर्षशीतातपत्वम्..
स्वभावतः संस्थिता मेदिनी च स्वभावतः सरितः संस्रवंति.. 45.86 ..
1.4.m:
By inherent nature the variety of grains sprouts; by inherent nature rain, cold, and heat occur;
by inherent nature the earth remains firm; and by inherent nature rivers flow.

1.4.s:
svabhāvataḥ parvatā bhāṃti nityaṃ svabhāvato vāridhireṣa saṃsthitaḥ..
svabhāvato garbhiṇī saṃprasūte svabhāvato'mī bahavaśca jīvāḥ.. 45.87 ..
1.4.d:
स्वभावतः पर्वता भांति नित्यं स्वभावतो वारिधिरेष संस्थितः..
स्वभावतो गर्भिणी संप्रसूते स्वभावतोऽमी बहवश्च जीवाः.. 45.87 ..
1.4.m:
By inherent nature the mountains constantly shine; by inherent nature this ocean remains situated;
by inherent nature a pregnant woman gives birth; and by inherent nature these many living beings exist.

1.4.s:
yathā svabhāvena bhavaṃti vakrā ṛtusvabāvādbadarīṣu kaṇṭakāḥ..
tathā svabhāvena hi sarvametatprakāśate ko'pi kartā na dṛśyaḥ.. 45.88 ..
1.4.d:
यथा स्वभावेन भवंति वक्रा ऋतुस्वबावाद्बदरीषु कण्टकाः..
तथा स्वभावेन हि सर्वमेतत्प्रकाशते कोऽपि कर्ता न दृश्यः.. 45.88 ..
1.4.m:
Just as by inherent nature, due to the nature of the season, thorns grow crooked on the jujube tree,
even so by inherent nature all this appears; no creator at all is seen.

1.4.s:
tadevaṃ saṃsthite loke mūḍho muhyati mattavat..
mānuṣyamapi yaddhūrtā vadaṃtyagryaṃ śrṛṇuṣvatat.. 45.89 ..
1.4.d:
तदेवं संस्थिते लोके मूढो मुह्यति मत्तवत्..
मानुष्यमपि यद्धूर्ता वदंत्यग्र्यं श्रृणुष्वतत्.. 45.89 ..
1.4.m:
The world being thus constituted, a fool is bewildered like a madman.
As for human birth being the foremost, which scoundrels declare—listen to that:

1.4.s:
mānuṣyānna paraṃ kaṣṭaṃ vairiṇāṃ no bhaveddhi tat..
śokasthānasahasrāṇi manuṣyasya kṣaṇekṣaṇe.. 45.90 ..
1.4.d:
मानुष्यान्न परं कष्टं वैरिणां नो भवेद्धि तत्..
शोकस्थानसहस्राणि मनुष्यस्य क्षणेक्षणे.. 45.90 ..
1.4.m:
There is no misery greater than human birth; may our enemies not have it!
For a human being, there are thousands of grounds for grief at every moment.

1.4.s:
mānuṣyaṃ hi smṛtākāraṃ sabhāgyo'smādvimucyate..
paśavaḥ pakṣiṇaḥ kīṭāḥ kṛmayaśca yathāsukham.. 45.91 ..
1.4.d:
मानुष्यं हि स्मृताकारं सभाग्योऽस्माद्विमुच्यते..
पशवः पक्षिणः कीटाः कृमयश्च यथासुखम्.. 45.91 ..
1.4.m:
Human birth has only an imaginary form; fortunate is one who is freed from it.
Beasts, birds, insects, and worms [live] as they please;

1.4.s:
abaddhā viharaṃtyete yonireṣāṃ sudurlabhā..
niściṃtāḥ sthāvarā hyete saukhyameṣāṃ mahadbhuvi.. 45.92 ..
1.4.d:
अबद्धा विहरंत्येते योनिरेषां सुदुर्लभा..
निश्चिंताः स्थावरा ह्येते सौख्यमेषां महद्भुवि.. 45.92 ..
1.4.m:
Unfettered, they roam about; their womb is exceedingly difficult to attain.
Stationary beings are free from care; their happiness on earth is great.

1.4.s:
bahunā kiṃ manuṣyebhyaḥ sarvo dhanyo'nyayonijaḥ..
svabhāvameva jānīhi puṇyāpuṇyādikalpanā.. 45.93 ..
1.4.d:
बहुना किं मनुष्येभ्यः सर्वो धन्योऽन्ययोनिजः..
स्वभावमेव जानीहि पुण्यापुण्यादिकल्पना.. 45.93 ..
1.4.m:
What need of much words? Everyone born in other wombs is more blessed than humans.
Recognize that the idea of merit and demerit is merely inherent nature.

1.4.s:
yadeke sthāvarāḥ kīṭāḥ pataṃgā mānuṣādikāḥ..
tasmānmityā parityajya naṃdabhadra yathāsukham..
piba krīḍanakaiḥ sārdhaṃ bhogānsatyamidaṃ bhuvi.. 45.94 ..
1.4.d:
यदेके स्थावराः कीटाः पतंगा मानुषादिकाः..
तस्मान्मित्या परित्यज्य नंदभद्र यथासुखम्..
पिब क्रीडनकैः सार्धं भोगान्सत्यमिदं भुवि.. 45.94 ..
1.4.m:
Because some are immobile things, worms, birds, and humans and the rest,
therefore, abandoning falsehood, O Nandabhadra, enjoy pleasures at will
and drink along with companions: this is the truth on earth.

1.4.s:
..nārada uvāca..
ityetairamukhairvākyairayuktairasamaṃjasaiḥ.. 45.95 ..
1.4.d:
..नारद उवाच..
इत्येतैरमुखैर्वाक्यैरयुक्तैरसमंजसैः.. 45.95 ..
1.4.m:
Nārada said:
At these words that were unpleasant, unreasonable, and improper,

1.4.s:
satyavratasya nākampannaṃdabhadro mahāmanāḥ..
prahasanniva taṃ prāha svakṣobhyaḥ sāgaro yathā.. 45.96 ..
1.4.d:
सत्यव्रतस्य नाकम्पन्नंदभद्रो महामनाः..
प्रहसन्निव तं प्राह स्वक्षोभ्यः सागरो यथा.. 45.96 ..
1.4.m:
spoken by Satyavrata, the high-minded Nandabhadra was not shaken.
As if laughing, he said to him, being unshakeable like the ocean:

1.4.s:
yadbhavānāha dharmiṣṭhāḥ sadā duḥkhasya bhāginaḥ..
tanmithyā duḥkhajālāni paśyāmaḥ pāpināmapi.. 45.97 ..
1.4.d:
यद्भवानाह धर्मिष्ठाः सदा दुःखस्य भागिनः..
तन्मिथ्या दुःखजालानि पश्यामः पापिनामपि.. 45.97 ..
1.4.m:
"As to what you say—that the virtuous are always partakers of sorrow—
that is false; we see webs of sorrows even for sinners.

1.4.s:
vadhabaṃdhaparikleśāḥ putradārādi paṃcatā..
pāpināmapi dṛśyaṃte tasmāddharmo gururmataḥ.. 45.98 ..
1.4.d:
वधबंधपरिक्लेशाः पुत्रदारादि पंचता..
पापिनामपि दृश्यंते तस्माद्धर्मो गुरुर्मतः.. 45.98 ..
1.4.m:
Slaying, binding, extreme afflictions, and the death of sons, wives, and the like
are seen even among sinners; therefore, dharma is considered supreme.

1.4.s:
ayaṃ sādhuraho kaṣṭaṃ kaṣṭamasya mahājanāḥ..
sādhorvadaṃtyetadapi pāpināṃ durlabhaṃ tvidam.. 45.99 ..
1.4.d:
अयं साधुरहो कष्टं कष्टमस्य महाजनाः..
साधोर्वदंत्येतदपि पापिनां दुर्लभं त्विदम्.. 45.99 ..
1.4.m:
'This is a righteous man! Ah, what misery, what misery is his!'—great people say this
even of a righteous man; but even such [pity] is hard for sinners to attain.

1.4.s:
dārādidravyalobhāryaṃ viśataḥ pāpino gṛhe..
bhavānapi bibhetyasmāddveṣṭi kupyati tadvṛthā.. 45.100 ..
1.4.d:
दारादिद्रव्यलोभार्यं विशतः पापिनो गृहे..
भवानपि बिभेत्यस्माद्द्वेष्टि कुप्यति तद्वृथा.. 45.100 ..
1.4.m:
When a sinner enters a house to seize the wealth, wife, and possessions of a noble person,
even you fear him, hate him, and get angry; so [your philosophy is] pointless.

1.4.s:
