yathāsya jagato brūṣe nāsti heturmaheśvaraḥ..
tadbālabhāṣitaṃ tubhyaṃ kiṃ rājānaṃ vinā prajāḥ.. 45.101 ..
1.4.d:
यथास्य जगतो ब्रूषे नास्ति हेतुर्महेश्वरः..
तद्बालभाषितं तुभ्यं किं राजानं विना प्रजाः.. 45.101 ..
1.4.m:
As for your saying that Maheśvara is not the cause of this world,
that is childish talk on your part: can there be subjects without a king?

1.4.s:
yacca bravīṣi pāṣāṇaṃ mithyā liṃgaṃ samarcasi..
tadbhavām̐lliṃgamāhātmyaṃ vetti nāṃdho yathā ravim.. 45.102 ..
1.4.d:
यच्च ब्रवीषि पाषाणं मिथ्या लिंगं समर्चसि..
तद्भवाम्̐ल्लिंगमाहात्म्यं वेत्ति नांधो यथा रविम्.. 45.102 ..
1.4.m:
And when you say, 'You falsely worship a stone, a liṅga,'
you do not know the greatness of the liṅga, just as a blind man does not know the sun.

1.4.s:
brahmādāyaḥ surā sarve rājānaśca maharddhikāḥ..
mānavā munayaścaiva sarve liṃgaṃ yajaṃti ca.. 45.103 ..
1.4.d:
ब्रह्मादायः सुरा सर्वे राजानश्च महर्द्धिकाः..
मानवा मुनयश्चैव सर्वे लिंगं यजंति च.. 45.103 ..
1.4.m:
All gods beginning with Brahmā, kings of great prosperity,
humans, and sages indeed all worship the liṅga.

1.4.s:
svanāmakāni cihnāni teṣāṃ liṃgāni saṃti ca..
ete kiṃ tvabhavatmūrkhāstvaṃ tu satyavrataḥ sudhīḥ.. 45.104 ..
1.4.d:
स्वनामकानि चिह्नानि तेषां लिंगानि संति च..
एते किं त्वभवत्मूर्खास्त्वं तु सत्यव्रतः सुधीः.. 45.104 ..
1.4.m:
They have liṅgas marked with their own names.
Were these [all] fools, and are you alone, Satyavrata, the wise one?

1.4.s:
pratiṣṭhāpya purā brahmā puṣkare nīlalohitam..
prāptavānparamāṃ siddhiṃ sasarjemāḥ prajāḥ prabhuḥ.. 45.105 ..
1.4.d:
प्रतिष्ठाप्य पुरा ब्रह्मा पुष्करे नीललोहितम्..
प्राप्तवान्परमां सिद्धिं ससर्जेमाः प्रजाः प्रभुः.. 45.105 ..
1.4.m:
In ancient times, having established Nīlalohita at Puṣkara,
the lord Brahmā attained supreme perfection and created these creatures.

1.4.s:
viṣṇunāpi nihatyājau rāvaṇaṃ payasāṃnidheḥ..
tīre rāmeśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ sthāpitaṃ cāsti kiṃ mudhā.. 45.106 ..
1.4.d:
विष्णुनापि निहत्याजौ रावणं पयसांनिधेः..
तीरे रामेश्वरं लिंगं स्थापितं चास्ति किं मुधा.. 45.106 ..
1.4.m:
By Viṣṇu too, having slain Rāvaṇa in battle, the Rāmeśvara liṅga
was established on the shore of the ocean; is that in vain?

1.4.s:
vṛtraṃ hatvā purā śakro maheṃdre sthāpya śaṃkaram..
liṃgaṃ vimuktapāpo'tha tridivedyāpi modate.. 45.107 ..
1.4.d:
वृत्रं हत्वा पुरा शक्रो महेंद्रे स्थाप्य शंकरम्..
लिंगं विमुक्तपापोऽथ त्रिदिवेद्यापि मोदते.. 45.107 ..
1.4.m:
In ancient times Śakra, having slain Vṛtra and established Śaṃkara
as a liṅga on Mount Mahendra, was freed from sin and rejoices in heaven even today.

1.4.s:
sthāpayitvā śivaṃ sūryo gaṃgāsāgarasaṃgame..
nirāmayo'bhūtsomaśca prabhāse paścimodadhau.. 45.108 ..
1.4.d:
स्थापयित्वा शिवं सूर्यो गंगासागरसंगमे..
निरामयोऽभूत्सोमश्च प्रभासे पश्चिमोदधौ.. 45.108 ..
1.4.m:
The Sun, having established Śiva at the confluence of the Gaṅgā and the ocean,
became free from disease; and Soma [did so] at Prabhāsa on the western ocean.

1.4.s:
kāśyāṃ yamaśca dhanadaḥ sahye garuḍakaśyapau..
naimiṣe vāyuvaruṇau sthāpya liṃgaṃ pramoditāḥ.. 45.109 ..
1.4.d:
काश्यां यमश्च धनदः सह्ये गरुडकश्यपौ..
नैमिषे वायुवरुणौ स्थाप्य लिंगं प्रमोदिताः.. 45.109 ..
1.4.m:
Yama and Kubera in Kāśī, Garuḍa and Kaśyapa on the Sahya mountain,
and Vāyu and Varuṇa in Naimiṣa, having established liṅgas, were filled with joy.

1.4.s:
asminneva staṃbhatīrthe kumāreṇaṃ guho vibhuḥ..
liṃgaṃ saṃsthāpayāmāsa sarvapāpaharaṃ na kim.. 45.110 ..
1.4.d:
अस्मिन्नेव स्तंभतीर्थे कुमारेणं गुहो विभुः..
लिंगं संस्थापयामास सर्वपापहरं न किम्.. 45.110 ..
1.4.m:
Right at this Stambhatīrtha, did not the all-powerful Lord Guha, Kumāra,
establish a liṅga that destroys all sins?

1.4.s:
evamanyaiḥ surairyāni pārthivairmunibhistathā..
saṃstāpitāni liṃgāni tanna saṃkhyātumutsahe.. 45.111 ..
1.4.d:
एवमन्यैः सुरैर्यानि पार्थिवैर्मुनिभिस्तथा..
संस्तापितानि लिंगानि तन्न संख्यातुमुत्सहे.. 45.111 ..
1.4.m:
Likewise, the liṅgas established by other gods,
kings, and sages—I cannot venture to count them all.

1.4.s:
pṛthivīvāsinaḥ sarve ye ca svarganivāsinaḥ..
pātālavāsinastṛptā jāyaṃte liṃgapūjayā.. 45.112 ..
1.4.d:
पृथिवीवासिनः सर्वे ये च स्वर्गनिवासिनः..
पातालवासिनस्तृप्ता जायंते लिंगपूजया.. 45.112 ..
1.4.m:
All the dwellers on earth, those who dwell in heaven,
and the dwellers of Pātāla become satisfied through the worship of the liṅga.

1.4.s:
yacca bravīṣi gīrvāṇā na saṃti santi cetkutaḥ..
kutrāpi naiva dṛśyaṃte tena me vismayo mahān.. 45.113 ..
1.4.d:
यच्च ब्रवीषि गीर्वाणा न संति सन्ति चेत्कुतः..
कुत्रापि नैव दृश्यंते तेन मे विस्मयो महान्.. 45.113 ..
1.4.m:
And when you say, 'Gods do not exist; if they exist, why
are they not seen anywhere?'—at that I feel great astonishment.

1.4.s:
raṃkavatkiṃ sma te devā yācaṃtāṃ tvāṃ kulatthavat..
yamicchisi mahāprājña sādhako hi gurustava.. 45.114 ..
1.4.d:
रंकवत्किं स्म ते देवा याचंतां त्वां कुलत्थवत्..
यमिच्छिसि महाप्राज्ञ साधको हि गुरुस्तव.. 45.114 ..
1.4.m:
Should those gods beg from you like a beggar for horsegram,
[that] which you wish for, O very wise one? Truly your teacher must be an adept!

1.4.s:
svabāvānnaiva sarvārthāḥ saṃsiddhā yadi te mate..
bhojanādi kathaṃ sidhyedvada kartāramaṃtarā.. 45.115 ..
1.4.d:
स्वबावान्नैव सर्वार्थाः संसिद्धा यदि ते मते..
भोजनादि कथं सिध्येद्वद कर्तारमंतरा.. 45.115 ..
1.4.m:
If in your view all things are accomplished from inherent nature alone,
tell me, how could [prepared] food and the like be accomplished without a maker?

1.4.s:
badarīmaṃtareṇāpi dṛśyaṃte kaṇṭakā na hi..
tasmātkasyāsti nirmāṇaṃ yasya yāvattathaiva tat.. 45.116 ..
1.4.d:
बदरीमंतरेणापि दृश्यंते कण्टका न हि..
तस्मात्कस्यास्ति निर्माणं यस्य यावत्तथैव तत्.. 45.116 ..
1.4.m:
Thorns are not seen without a jujube tree either;
therefore, everything has a maker, however much [it exists], just so it is.

1.4.s:
yacca bravīṣi paśvādyāḥ sukhino dhanyakāstvamī..
tvadṛte nedamuktaṃ ca kenāpi śrutameva vā.. 45.117 ..
1.4.d:
यच्च ब्रवीषि पश्वाद्याः सुखिनो धन्यकास्त्वमी..
त्वदृते नेदमुक्तं च केनापि श्रुतमेव वा.. 45.117 ..
1.4.m:
And when you say, 'Beasts and other animals are happy and blessed,'
except for you, this has never been spoken or heard by anyone.

1.4.s:
tāmasā vikalā ye ca kaṣṭaṃ teṣāṃ ca ślāghyatām..
sarveṃdriyayutāḥ śreṣṭhāḥ kuto dhanyā na mānuṣāḥ.. 45.118 ..
1.4.d:
तामसा विकला ये च कष्टं तेषां च श्लाघ्यताम्..
सर्वेंद्रिययुताः श्रेष्ठाः कुतो धन्या न मानुषाः.. 45.118 ..
1.4.m:
Alas, [to think of] those that are tamasic and defective as praiseworthy!
Why are humans, who possess all sense-organs and are superior, not the blessed ones?"

1.4.s:
satyaṃ tava vrataṃ manye narakāya tvayā''dṛtam..
atyanarthe na bhīḥ kāryā kāmoyaṃ bhavitācirāt.. 45.119 ..
1.4.d:
सत्यं तव व्रतं मन्ये नरकाय त्वया'ऽदृतम्..
अत्यनर्थे न भीः कार्या कामोयं भविताचिरात्.. 45.119 ..
1.4.m: "Truly I consider your resolve has been adopted by you for hell. / One should not fear extreme misfortune; this desire of yours will soon be [fulfilled].

1.4.s:
ādāvāḍaṃbareṇaiva dhruvato'jñānameva me..
itthaṃ niḥsāratā vyaktamādāvāḍaṃbārāttu yat.. 45.120 ..
1.4.d:
आदावाडंबरेणैव ध्रुवतोऽज्ञानमेव मे..
इत्थं निःसारता व्यक्तमादावाडंबारात्तु यत्.. 45.120 ..
1.4.m: From the very beginning, by your mere ostentation, I was certain of your ignorance; / for emptiness is evident in this way from an initial show of ostentation.

1.4.s:
māyāvināṃ hi bruvatāṃ vākyaṃ cāṃḍabarāvṛtam..
kunāṇakamivoddīptaṃ parīkṣeyaṃ sadā satām.. 45.121 ..
1.4.d:
मायाविनां हि ब्रुवतां वाक्यं चांडबरावृतम्..
कुनाणकमिवोद्दीप्तं परीक्षेयं सदा सताम्.. 45.121 ..
1.4.m: The speech spoken by deceitful people is enveloped in pomp, / like a counterfeit coin that is shiny; this should always be examined by the virtuous.

1.4.s:
ādau madhye tathā cāṃte yeṣāṃ vākyamadoṣavat..
kaṣadāhaiḥ svarṇamiva cchede'pi syācchubhaṃ śubham.. 45.122 ..
1.4.d:
आदौ मध्ये तथा चांते येषां वाक्यमदोषवत्..
कषदाहैः स्वर्णमिव च्छेदेऽपि स्याच्छुभं शुभम्.. 45.122 ..
1.4.m: Those whose words are faultless in the beginning, in the middle, and at the end, / would be pure and auspicious even when cut, like gold through rubbing and heating.

1.4.s:
tvayānyathā pratijñātamuktaṃ caivānyathā punaḥ..
tvaddoṣo nāyamasmākaṃ tadvacaḥ śrṛṇumo hi ye.. 45.123 ..
1.4.d:
त्वयान्यथा प्रतिज्ञातमुक्तं चैवान्यथा पुनः..
त्वद्दोषो नायमस्माकं तद्वचः श्रृणुमो हि ये.. 45.123 ..
1.4.m: You made one pledge, but spoke differently again; / this fault is not ours, but belongs to you, since we listen to your words.

1.4.s:
nāstikānāṃ ca sarpāṇāṃ viṣasya ca guṇastvayam..
mohayaṃti paraṃ yacca doṣo naiṣaparasya tu.. 45.124 ..
1.4.d:
नास्तिकानां च सर्पाणां विषस्य च गुणस्त्वयम्..
मोहयंति परं यच्च दोषो नैषपरस्य तु.. 45.124 ..
1.4.m: Indeed, this is the quality of atheists, serpents, and poison: / that they bewilder others; but the fault does not belong to another.

1.4.s:
āpo vastraṃ tilāstailaṃ gaṃdho vā sa yathā tathā..
puṣpāṇāmadhivāsena tathā saṃsargajā guṇāḥ.. 45.125 ..
1.4.d:
आपो वस्त्रं तिलास्तैलं गंधो वा स यथा तथा..
पुष्पाणामधिवासेन तथा संसर्गजा गुणाः.. 45.125 ..
1.4.m: Just as water, cloth, sesame seeds, oil, or fragrance / take on qualities by the infusion of flowers, so too are the qualities born of association.

1.4.s:
mohajālasya yo yonirmūḍhairiha samāgamaḥ..
ahanyahani dharmasya yoniḥ sādhusamāgamaḥ.. 45.126 ..
1.4.d:
मोहजालस्य यो योनिर्मूढैरिह समागमः..
अहन्यहनि धर्मस्य योनिः साधुसमागमः.. 45.126 ..
1.4.m: Association with fools here is the source of the net of delusion; / day after day, association with the virtuous is the source of righteousness.

1.4.s:
tasmātprājñaiśca vṛddhaiśca śuddhabhāvaistapasvibhiḥ..
sadbhiśca saha saṃsargaḥ kāryaḥ śamaparāyaṇaiḥ.. 45.127 ..
1.4.d:
तस्मात्प्राज्ञैश्च वृद्धैश्च शुद्धभावैस्तपस्विभिः..
सद्भिश्च सह संसर्गः कार्यः शमपरायणैः.. 45.127 ..
1.4.m: Therefore, association should be made with the wise, the elderly, those of pure intent, ascetics, / and the virtuous who are devoted to tranquility;

1.4.s:
na nīcairnāpyavidvadbhirnānātmajñairviśeṣataḥ..
yeṣāṃ trīṇyavadātāni yonirvidyā ca karma ca.. 45.128 ..
1.4.d:
न नीचैर्नाप्यविद्वद्भिर्नानात्मज्ञैर्विशेषतः..
येषां त्रीण्यवदातानि योनिर्विद्या च कर्म च.. 45.128 ..
1.4.m: not with the low, nor with the unlearned, especially not with those who do not know the Self. / Those whose three things are pure—origin, learning, and conduct—

1.4.s:
tāṃśca sevedviśeṣeṇa śāstraṃ yeṣāṃ hi vidyate..
asatāṃ darśanasparśasaṃjalpāsanabhojanaiḥ.. 45.129 ..
1.4.d:
तांश्च सेवेद्विशेषेण शास्त्रं येषां हि विद्यते..
असतां दर्शनस्पर्शसंजल्पासनभोजनैः.. 45.129 ..
1.4.m: and especially those who possess knowledge of the scriptures, one should serve. / By seeing, touching, conversing, sitting, and dining with the wicked,

1.4.s:
dharmācārātprahīyaṃte na ca sidhyaṃti mānavāḥ..
buddhiśca hīyate puṃsāṃ nīcaiḥ saha samāgamāt.. 45.130 ..
1.4.d:
धर्माचारात्प्रहीयंते न च सिध्यंति मानवाः..
बुद्धिश्च हीयते पुंसां नीचैः सह समागमात्.. 45.130 ..
1.4.m: human beings fall away from righteous conduct and do not attain success; / and the intellect of men declines from association with the low.

1.4.s:
madhyaiśca madhyatāṃ yāti śreṣṭhatāṃ yāti cottamaiḥ..
iti dharmaṃ smarannāhaṃ saṃgamārthī punastava..
yannindasi dvijāneva yairapeyo'rṇavaḥ kṛtaḥ.. 45.131 ..
1.4.d:
मध्यैश्च मध्यतां याति श्रेष्ठतां याति चोत्तमैः..
इति धर्मं स्मरन्नाहं संगमार्थी पुनस्तव..
यन्निन्दसि द्विजानेव यैरपेयोऽर्णवः कृतः.. 45.131 ..
1.4.m: With middling people it reaches mediocrity, and with the highest it reaches excellence.' / Remembering this righteousness, I do not wish to associate with you again, / since you revile the very brahmins by whom the ocean was rendered undrinkable.

1.4.s:
vedāḥ pramāṇaṃ smṛtayaḥ pramāṇaṃ dharmārthayuktaṃ vacanaṃ pramāṇam..
naitattrayaṃ yasya bhavetpramāṇaṃ kastasya kuryādvacanaṃ pramāṇam.. 45.132 ..
1.4.d:
वेदाः प्रमाणं स्मृतयः प्रमाणं धर्मार्थयुक्तं वचनं प्रमाणम्..
नैतत्त्रयं यस्य भवेत्प्रमाणं कस्तस्य कुर्याद्वचनं प्रमाणम्.. 45.132 ..
1.4.m: The Vedas are an authority; the Smṛtis are an authority; speech endowed with righteousness and purpose is an authority. / For one to whom these three are not an authority, who would regard his word as an authority?"

1.4.s:
itīrayitvā vacanaṃ mahātmā sa naṃdabhadraḥ sahasā tadaiva..
gṛhādviniḥsṛtya jagāma puṇyaṃ bahūdakaṃ bhaṭṭaravestu kuṃḍam.. 45.133 ..
iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ prathame māheśvarakhaṇḍe kaumārikākhaṃḍe kapileśvaratīrthamāhātmye naṃdabhadravaṇigvṛttāntavarṇanaṃ nāma pañcacatvāriṃśattamo'dhyāyaḥ.. 45 .. cha ..
1.4.d:
इतीरयित्वा वचनं महात्मा स नंदभद्रः सहसा तदैव..
गृहाद्विनिःसृत्य जगाम पुण्यं बहूदकं भट्टरवेस्तु कुंडम्.. 45.133 ..
इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां प्रथमे माहेश्वरखण्डे कौमारिकाखंडे कपिलेश्वरतीर्थमाहात्म्ये नंदभद्रवणिग्वृत्तान्तवर्णनं नाम पञ्चचत्वारिंशत्तमोऽध्यायः.. 45 .. छ ..
1.4.m:
Having spoken this word, that noble-minded Nandabhadra immediately / stepped out from the house and went to the sacred Bahūdaka, the pool of Bhaṭṭaravi.
Thus ends the forty-fifth chapter, titled 'The Description of the Merchant Nandabhadra's Account' in the māhātmya of the Kapileśvara tīrtha, in the Kaumārikākhaṇḍa of the first [section], the Māheśvarakhaṇḍa, in the Mahāpurāṇa of Śrī Skanda containing eighty-one thousand verses.

1.4.s:
..nārada uvāca..
bahūdakasya kuṃḍasya tīrasthaṃ liṃgamuttamam..
kapileśvaramabhyarcya naṃdabhadrastataḥ sudhī.. 46.1 ..
1.4.d:
..नारद उवाच..
बहूदकस्य कुंडस्य तीरस्थं लिंगमुत्तमम्..
कपिलेश्वरमभ्यर्च्य नंदभद्रस्ततः सुधी.. 46.1 ..
1.4.m: Nārada said: / Having worshipped the supreme liṅga, Kapileśvara, / standing on the bank of the Bahūdaka pool, the wise Nandabhadra then,

1.4.s:
praṇamya cāgratastasthau prabaddhakarasaṃpuṭaḥ..
saṃsāracaritaiḥ kiṃcidduḥkhī gāthāṃ vyagāyata.. 46.2 ..
1.4.d:
प्रणम्य चाग्रतस्तस्थौ प्रबद्धकरसंपुटः..
संसारचरितैः किंचिद्दुःखी गाथां व्यगायत.. 46.2 ..
1.4.m: having bowed, stood before it with folded hands; / somewhat grieved by the ways of worldly existence, he sang a verse:

1.4.s:
sraṣṭāramasya jagataścetpaśyāmi sadāśivam..
nānāpṛcchābhiratha taṃ kuryāṃ nāthaṃ vilajjitam.. 46.3 ..
1.4.d:
स्रष्टारमस्य जगतश्चेत्पश्यामि सदाशिवम्..
नानापृच्छाभिरथ तं कुर्यां नाथं विलज्जितम्.. 46.3 ..
1.4.m: "If I see Sadāśiva, the creator of this world, / then I will make the Lord ashamed with various inquiries:

1.4.s:
apūryamāṇaṃ tava kiṃ jagatsaṃsṛjanaṃ vinā..
nirīha bahudhā yatte sṛṣṭaṃ bhārgavavajjagat.. 46.4 ..
1.4.d:
अपूर्यमाणं तव किं जगत्संसृजनं विना..
निरीह बहुधा यत्ते सृष्टं भार्गववज्जगत्.. 46.4 ..
1.4.m: 'Without your creation of the world, would it remain incomplete? / O desireless one, why has the world been created by you manifoldly like a potter's work?

1.4.s:
sacetanena śuddhena rāgādirahitena ca..
atha kasmādātmasadṛśaṃ na sṛṣṭaṃ nirmitaṃ jaḍam.. 46.5 ..
1.4.d:
सचेतनेन शुद्धेन रागादिरहितेन च..
अथ कस्मादात्मसदृशं न सृष्टं निर्मितं जडम्.. 46.5 ..
1.4.m: Why was [the world] created insentient by one who is conscious, pure, / and devoid of attachment and other passions, and not made similar to yourself?

1.4.s:
nirvaireṇa samenātha sukhaduḥkhabhavābhavaiḥ..
brahmādikīṭaparyantaṃ kimeva kliśyate jagat.. 46.6 ..
1.4.d:
निर्वैरेण समेनाथ सुखदुःखभवाभवैः..
ब्रह्मादिकीटपर्यन्तं किमेव क्लिश्यते जगत्.. 46.6 ..
1.4.m: By one free from enmity, impartial to pleasure and pain, existence and non-existence, / why indeed is the world afflicted, from Brahmā down to an insect?

1.4.s:
kāṃścitsvargetha narake pātayaṃstvaṃ sadāśiva..
kiṃ phalaṃ samavāpnoṣi kimevaṃ kuruṣe vada.. 46.7 ..
1.4.d:
कांश्चित्स्वर्गेथ नरके पातयंस्त्वं सदाशिव..
किं फलं समवाप्नोषि किमेवं कुरुषे वद.. 46.7 ..
1.4.m: Cast down some into heaven and others into hell, O Sadāśiva, / what fruit do you obtain? Tell me, why do you act in this way?

1.4.s:
iṣṭaiḥ putrādibhirnātha viyuktā mānavā hyamī..
kraṃdaṃti karuṇāsāra kiṃ ghṛṇāpi bhavenna te.. 46.8 ..
1.4.d:
इष्टैः पुत्रादिभिर्नाथ वियुक्ता मानवा ह्यमी..
क्रंदंति करुणासार किं घृणापि भवेन्न ते.. 46.8 ..
1.4.m: Separated from dear ones such as sons, O Lord, these human beings / weep, O shower of compassion; would you not have even pity?

1.4.s:
atīva nocitaṃ sarvametadīśvara sarvathā..
yatte bhaktāḥ samaṃ pāpairmajjaṃte duḥkhasāgare.. 46.9 ..
1.4.d:
अतीव नोचितं सर्वमेतदीश्वर सर्वथा..
यत्ते भक्ताः समं पापैर्मज्जंते दुःखसागरे.. 46.9 ..
1.4.m: All this is exceedingly unfitting in every way, O Īśvara: / that your devotees sink into the ocean of sorrow along with sinners.'

1.4.s:
evaṃvidhena saṃsāracāritreṇa vimohitāḥ..
sthānāṃ taraṃ na yāsyāmi bhokṣye pāsyāmi nodakam.. 46.10 ..
1.4.d:
एवंविधेन संसारचारित्रेण विमोहिताः..
स्थानां तरं न यास्यामि भोक्ष्ये पास्यामि नोदकम्.. 46.10 ..
1.4.m: Deluded by such conduct of worldly existence, / I shall not go to another place; I shall not eat, nor drink water.

1.4.s:
maraṇāṃtameva yāsyāmi sthāsye saṃciṃtayannadaḥ..
sa evaṃ vimṛśanneva naṃdabhadraḥ svayaṃ sthitaḥ.. 46.11 ..
1.4.d:
मरणांतमेव यास्यामि स्थास्ये संचिंतयन्नदः..
स एवं विमृशन्नेव नंदभद्रः स्वयं स्थितः.. 46.11 ..
1.4.m: I shall remain until death contemplating this." / Reflecting thus, Nandabhadra remained there alone.

1.4.s:
tataścaturthe divase bahūkataṭe śubhe..
kaścidbālaḥ saptavarṣaḥ pīḍāpīḍita āyayau.. 46.12 ..
1.4.d:
ततश्चतुर्थे दिवसे बहूकतटे शुभे..
कश्चिद्बालः सप्तवर्षः पीडापीडित आययौ.. 46.12 ..
1.4.m: Then, on the fourth day, on the auspicious bank of the Bahūdaka, / a certain seven-year-old boy arrived, afflicted by pain,

1.4.s:
kṛśotīva galatkuṣṭhī pramuhyaṃśca padepeda..
naṃdabhadramuvācedaṃ kṛcchrātsaṃstabhya bālakaḥ.. 46.13 ..
1.4.d:
कृशोतीव गलत्कुष्ठी प्रमुह्यंश्च पदेपेद..
नंदभद्रमुवाचेदं कृच्छ्रात्संस्तभ्य बालकः.. 46.13 ..
1.4.m: extremely emaciated, suffering from ulcerated leprosy, swooning at every step. / Steadying himself with difficulty, the boy said this to Nandabhadra:

1.4.s:
aho surūpasarvāṃga kasmādduḥkhī bhavānapi..
tatosya kāraṇaṃ sarvaṃ vyācaṣṭa naṃdabhadrakaḥ.. 46.14 ..
1.4.d:
अहो सुरूपसर्वांग कस्माद्दुःखी भवानपि..
ततोस्य कारणं सर्वं व्याचष्ट नंदभद्रकः.. 46.14 ..
1.4.m: "O one whose entire body is handsome, why are you too distressed?" / Then Nandabhadra explained the whole reason to him.

1.4.s:
śrutvā tatkāraṇaṃ sarvaṃ bālo dīnamanā bravīt..
aho hā kaṣṭamatyugraṃ budhānāṃ yadabuddhitā.. 46.15 ..
1.4.d:
श्रुत्वा तत्कारणं सर्वं बालो दीनमना ब्रवीत्..
अहो हा कष्टमत्युग्रं बुधानां यदबुद्धिता.. 46.15 ..
1.4.m: Having heard that whole reason, the boy, dejected at heart, said: / "Alas! What severe misery that the wise should lack discernment!

1.4.s:
saṃpūrṇeṃdriyagātrā yanmartumicchaṃti vai vṛthā..
muhūrtāddhyatra khaṭvāṃgo mokṣamārgamupāgataḥ.. 46.16 ..
1.4.d:
संपूर्णेंद्रियगात्रा यन्मर्तुमिच्छंति वै वृथा..
मुहूर्ताद्ध्यत्र खट्वांगो मोक्षमार्गमुपागतः.. 46.16 ..
1.4.m: That those with complete limbs and senses should wish to die in vain! / For in this place, within a moment, Khaṭvāṅga attained the path of liberation.

1.4.s:
tadaho bhārataṃ khaṃḍaṃ satyāyuṣi tyajeddhi kaḥ..
ahameva dṛḍho manye pitṛbhyāṃ yo vivarjitaḥ.. 46.17 ..
1.4.d:
तदहो भारतं खंडं सत्यायुषि त्यजेद्धि कः..
अहमेव दृढो मन्ये पितृभ्यां यो विवर्जितः.. 46.17 ..
1.4.m: Then, alas, who indeed would abandon the land of Bhārata while life remains? / I consider myself resolute, who have been abandoned by my parents,

1.4.s:
aśaktaścalituṃ vāpi martumicchāmi nāpi ca..
sarve lābhāḥ sātimānā iti satyā bata śrutiḥ.. 46.18 ..
1.4.d:
अशक्तश्चलितुं वापि मर्तुमिच्छामि नापि च..
सर्वे लाभाः सातिमाना इति सत्या बत श्रुतिः.. 46.18 ..
1.4.m: and am unable even to walk, yet I do not wish to die. / Truly, the Vedic statement that 'all gains come with great pride' is true.

1.4.s:
saṃtoṣo'pyucitastubhyaṃ dehaṃ yasya dṛḍhaṃ tvidam..
śarīraṃ nīrujaṃ cenme bhavedapi kathaṃcana.. 46.19 ..
1.4.d:
संतोषोऽप्युचितस्तुभ्यं देहं यस्य दृढं त्विदम्..
शरीरं नीरुजं चेन्मे भवेदपि कथंचन.. 46.19 ..
1.4.m: Contentment is fitting for you, whose body is strong; / if my body could somehow become free from disease,

1.4.s:
kṣaṇekṣaṇe ca tatkuryāṃ bhujyate yadyugeyuge..
iṃdriyāṇi vaśe yasya śarīraṃ ca dṛḍhaṃ bhavet.. 46.20 ..
1.4.d:
क्षणेक्षणे च तत्कुर्यां भुज्यते यद्युगेयुगे..
इंद्रियाणि वशे यस्य शरीरं च दृढं भवेत्.. 46.20 ..
1.4.m: at every single moment I would perform that which is enjoyed in age after age! / He whose senses are under control and whose body is firm,

1.4.s:
so'pyanyadicchate cecca ko'nyastasmādacetanaḥ..
śokasthānasahasrāṇi harṣasthānaśatāni ca.. 46.21 ..
1.4.d:
सोऽप्यन्यदिच्छते चेच्च कोऽन्यस्तस्मादचेतनः..
शोकस्थानसहस्राणि हर्षस्थानशतानि च.. 46.21 ..
1.4.m: if he too desires something else, who else could be more mindless than he? / A thousand grounds for sorrow and a hundred grounds for joy

1.4.s:
divase divase mūḍhamāvaśaṃti na paṃḍitam..
na hi jñānaviruddheṣu bahvapāyeṣu karmasu.. 46.22 ..
1.4.d:
दिवसे दिवसे मूढमावशंति न पंडितम्..
न हि ज्ञानविरुद्धेषु बह्वपायेषु कर्मसु.. 46.22 ..
1.4.m: overtake the fool day after day, but not the learned man. / For the wise like you do not attach themselves to actions

1.4.s:
mūlaghātiṣu sajjaṃte buddhimaṃto bhavadvidhāḥ..
aṣṭāṃgāṃ buddhimāhuryāṃ sarvāśreyovighātinīma.. 46.23 ..
1.4.d:
मूलघातिषु सज्जंते बुद्धिमंतो भवद्विधाः..
अष्टांगां बुद्धिमाहुर्यां सर्वाश्रेयोविघातिनीम.. 46.23 ..
1.4.m: that are opposed to knowledge, full of danger, and destructive at the root. / They speak of eightfold intellect, which destroys all misfortune;

1.4.s:
śrutismṛtyaviruddhā sā buddhistvayyasti nirmalā..
atha kṛcchreṣu durgeṣu vyāpatsu svajanasya ca.. 46.24 ..
1.4.d:
श्रुतिस्मृत्यविरुद्धा सा बुद्धिस्त्वय्यस्ति निर्मला..
अथ कृच्छ्रेषु दुर्गेषु व्यापत्सु स्वजनस्य च.. 46.24 ..
1.4.m: that pure intellect, not contrary to the Śruti and Smṛti, is in you. / Even in difficulties, dangers, and calamities of one's own people,

1.4.s:
śārīramānasairduḥkhairna sīdaṃti bhavadvidhāḥ..
nāprāpyamabhivāṃchaṃti naṣṭaṃ necchaṃti śocitum.. 46.25 ..
1.4.d:
शारीरमानसैर्दुःखैर्न सीदंति भवद्विधाः..
नाप्राप्यमभिवांछंति नष्टं नेच्छंति शोचितुम्.. 46.25 ..
1.4.m: those like you do not despair with bodily and mental sorrows; / they do not crave the unobtainable, nor do they wish to grieve over what is lost.

1.4.s:
āpatsu ca na muhyaṃti narāḥ paṃḍitabuddhayaḥ..
manodehasamutthābhyāṃ duḥkhābhyāmarpitaṃ jagat.. 46.26 ..
1.4.d:
आपत्सु च न मुह्यंति नराः पंडितबुद्धयः..
मनोदेहसमुत्थाभ्यां दुःखाभ्यामर्पितं जगत्.. 46.26 ..
1.4.m: And men of learned intellect are not bewildered in calamities. / The world is afflicted by sufferings arising from both mind and body.

1.4.s:
tayorvyāsasamāsābhyāṃ śamopāyamimaṃ śrṛṇu..
vyādheraniṣṭasaṃsparśācchramādiṣṭavisarjanāt.. 46.27 ..
1.4.d:
तयोर्व्याससमासाभ्यां शमोपायमिमं श्रृणु..
व्याधेरनिष्टसंस्पर्शाच्छ्रमादिष्टविसर्जनात्.. 46.27 ..
1.4.m: Hear this method for pacifying the two, in detail and in brief: / From disease, from contact with the disagreeable, from exertion, and from separation from what is agreeable,

1.4.s:
caturbhiḥ kāraṇairduḥkhaṃ śīrīraṃ mānasaṃ ca yat..
mānasaṃ cāpyapriyasya saṃyogaḥ priyavarjanam.. 46.28 ..
1.4.d:
चतुर्भिः कारणैर्दुःखं शीरीरं मानसं च यत्..
मानसं चाप्यप्रियस्य संयोगः प्रियवर्जनम्.. 46.28 ..
1.4.m: arises suffering through four causes, both bodily and mental; / and the mental [suffering consists of] union with the unloved and separation from the loved.

1.4.s:
dviprakāraṃ mahākaṣṭaṃ dvayoretadudāhṛtam..
mānasena hi duḥkhena śarīramupatapyate.. 46.29 ..
1.4.d:
द्विप्रकारं महाकष्टं द्वयोरेतदुदाहृतम्..
मानसेन हि दुःखेन शरीरमुपतप्यते.. 46.29 ..
1.4.m: This twofold great distress is declared of the two; / for indeed, the body is tormented by mental suffering,

1.4.s:
ayaḥpiṃḍena taptena kuṃbhasaṃsthamivodakam..
tadāśu prati kārācca satataṃ ca vivarjanāt.. 46.30 ..
1.4.d:
अयःपिंडेन तप्तेन कुंभसंस्थमिवोदकम्..
तदाशु प्रति काराच्च सततं च विवर्जनात्.. 46.30 ..
1.4.m: like water in a pot by a heated lump of iron. / Therefore, by prompt remedy and constant avoidance,

1.4.s:
vyādherādheśca praśamaḥ kriyāyogadvayena tu..
mānasaṃ śamayettasmājjñānenāgnimivāṃbunā.. 46.31 ..
1.4.d:
व्याधेराधेश्च प्रशमः क्रियायोगद्वयेन तु..
मानसं शमयेत्तस्माज्ज्ञानेनाग्निमिवांबुना.. 46.31 ..
1.4.m: the pacification of bodily disease and mental anguish is achieved through the twofold application of action. / Therefore, one should pacify the mind with knowledge, as fire is quenched with water.

1.4.s:
praśāṃte mānase hyasya śārīramupaśāmti..
manaso duḥkhamūlaṃ tu sneha ityupalabhyate.. 46.32 ..
1.4.d:
प्रशांते मानसे ह्यस्य शारीरमुपशाम्ति..
मनसो दुःखमूलं तु स्नेह इत्युपलभ्यते.. 46.32 ..
1.4.m: For when the mind is calmed, his bodily [affliction] also subsides. / Attachment is known to be the root of mental suffering.

1.4.s:
snehācca sajjano nityaṃ janturduḥkhamupaiti ca..
snehamūlāni duḥkhāni snehajāni bhāyāni ca.. 46.33 ..
1.4.d:
स्नेहाच्च सज्जनो नित्यं जन्तुर्दुःखमुपैति च..
स्नेहमूलानि दुःखानि स्नेहजानि भायानि च.. 46.33 ..
1.4.m: And through attachment, an embodied being constantly experiences suffering. / Sufferings have their root in attachment, and fears are born of attachment;

1.4.s: śokaharṣau tathāyāsaḥ sarvaṃ snehātpravartate.. 46.34 ..
1.4.d: शोकहर्षौ तथायासः सर्वं स्नेहात्प्रवर्तते.. 46.34 ..
1.4.m: grief, joy, and likewise weariness—all arise from attachment.

1.4.s:
snehātkaraṇarāgaśca prajajñe vaiṣayastathā..
aśreyaskāvubhāvatau pūrvastatra guruḥ smṛtaḥ.. 46.35 ..
1.4.d:
स्नेहात्करणरागश्च प्रजज्ञे वैषयस्तथा..
अश्रेयस्कावुभावतौ पूर्वस्तत्र गुरुः स्मृतः.. 46.35 ..
1.4.m: From attachment also arises attachment to the senses and to sense-objects; / both of these are detrimental, and of the two, the former is considered the weightier.

1.4.s:
tyāgī tasmānna duḥkhī syānnarvairo niravagrahaḥ..
atyāgī janmamaraṇe prāpnotīha punaḥpunaḥ.. 46.36 ..
1.4.d:
त्यागी तस्मान्न दुःखी स्यान्नर्वैरो निरवग्रहः..
अत्यागी जन्ममरणे प्राप्नोतीह पुनःपुनः.. 46.36 ..
1.4.m: Therefore, one who renounces will not suffer, being free of enmity and free of constraint; / but one who does not renounce incurs birth and death again and again in this world.

1.4.s:
tasmātsnehaṃ na lipsena mitrebhyo dhanasaṃcayāt..
svaśarīrasamutthaṃ ca jñānena vinirvatayet.. 46.37 ..
1.4.d:
तस्मात्स्नेहं न लिप्सेन मित्रेभ्यो धनसंचयात्..
स्वशरीरसमुत्थं च ज्ञानेन विनिर्वतयेत्.. 46.37 ..
1.4.m: Therefore, one should not seek attachment from friends or from hoarding wealth; / and that which arises from one's own body, one should dispel with knowledge.

1.4.s:
jñānānviteṣu siddheṣu śāstrūjñeṣu kṛtātmasu..
na teṣu sajjate snehaḥ padmapatreṣvivodakam.. 46.38 ..
1.4.d:
ज्ञानान्वितेषु सिद्धेषु शास्त्रूज्ञेषु कृतात्मसु..
न तेषु सज्जते स्नेहः पद्मपत्रेष्विवोदकम्.. 46.38 ..
1.4.m: In those endowed with knowledge, the perfected, the knowers of the scriptures, the self-controlled, / attachment does not cling to them, just as water does not cling to lotus leaves.

1.4.s:
rāgābhibhūtaḥ puruṣaḥ kāmena parikṛṣyate..
icchā saṃjāyate cāsya tatastṛṣṇā pravardhate.. 46.39 ..
1.4.d:
रागाभिभूतः पुरुषः कामेन परिकृष्यते..
इच्छा संजायते चास्य ततस्तृष्णा प्रवर्धते.. 46.39 ..
1.4.m: A man overcome by passion is dragged along by desire; / and longing is born in him, from which craving expands.

1.4.s:
tṛṣṇā hi sarvapāpiṣṭhā nityodvegakarī matā..
adharmabahulā caiva ghorarūpānubaṃdhinī.. 46.40 ..
1.4.d:
तृष्णा हि सर्वपापिष्ठा नित्योद्वेगकरी मता..
अधर्मबहुला चैव घोररूपानुबंधिनी.. 46.40 ..
1.4.m: Craving is indeed considered the most sinful of all, always producing agitation; / it abounds in unrighteousness and is attended by terrible consequences.

1.4.s:
yā dustyajā durmatibhiryā na jīryataḥ..
yāsau prāṇāṃtiko rogastāṃ tṛṣṇāṃ tyajataḥ sukham.. 46.41 ..
1.4.d:
या दुस्त्यजा दुर्मतिभिर्या न जीर्यतः..
यासौ प्राणांतिको रोगस्तां तृष्णां त्यजतः सुखम्.. 46.41 ..
1.4.m: That which is hard for the evil-minded to abandon, which does not age [even as one] ages, / which is a fatal disease—for one who abandons that craving, there is happiness.

1.4.s:
anādyaṃtā tu sā tṛṣṇā hyaṃtardehagatā nṛṇām..
vināśayati saṃbhūtā lohaṃ lohamalo yathā.. 46.42 ..
1.4.d:
अनाद्यंता तु सा तृष्णा ह्यंतर्देहगता नृणाम्..
विनाशयति संभूता लोहं लोहमलो यथा.. 46.42 ..
1.4.m: That craving, having no beginning or end, residing within the bodies of men, / destroys them once born, just as rust destroys iron.

1.4.s:
yathaivaidhaḥ samutthena vahninā nāśamṛcchati..
tathā'kṛtātmā lobena svotpannena vinaśyati.. 46.43 ..
1.4.d:
यथैवैधः समुत्थेन वह्निना नाशमृच्छति..
तथाऽकृतात्मा लोबेन स्वोत्पन्नेन विनश्यति.. 46.43 ..
1.4.m: Just as firewood meets destruction by the fire that arises from itself, / so an undisciplined person is destroyed by the greed that arises from himself.

1.4.s:
tasmāllobho na kartavyaḥ śarīre cātmabaṃdhuṣu..
prāpteṣu va na hṛṣyeta nāśo vāpi na śocayet.. 46.44 ..
1.4.d:
तस्माल्लोभो न कर्तव्यः शरीरे चात्मबंधुषु..
प्राप्तेषु व न हृष्येत नाशो वापि न शोचयेत्.. 46.44 ..
1.4.m: Therefore, greed should not be harbored toward the body or toward one's kinsmen; / nor should one rejoice when they are obtained, nor grieve when they are lost.

1.4.s:
..naṃdabhadra uvāca..
aho bāla na bālastvaṃ mato me tvāṃ namāmyaham..
tvadvākyairatitṛpto'haṃ tvāṃ tu prakṣyāmi kiṃcana.. 46.45 ..
1.4.d:
..नंदभद्र उवाच..
अहो बाल न बालस्त्वं मतो मे त्वां नमाम्यहम्..
त्वद्वाक्यैरतितृप्तोऽहं त्वां तु प्रक्ष्यामि किंचन.. 46.45 ..
1.4.m: Nandabhadra said: / Ah, boy, you are not considered a boy by me! I bow to you. / I am greatly satisfied by your words, but I would ask you something.

1.4.s:
kāmakrodhāvahaṃkāramiṃdriyāṇi ca mānavāḥ..
niṃdaṃti tatra me nityaṃ vivakṣeyaṃ prajāyate.. 46.46 ..
1.4.d:
कामक्रोधावहंकारमिंद्रियाणि च मानवाः..
निंदंति तत्र मे नित्यं विवक्षेयं प्रजायते.. 46.46 ..
1.4.m: Men constantly condemn desire, anger, egoism, and the senses; / concerning that, this question arises in me:

1.4.s:
ahameṣa mamedaṃ ca kāryamīdṛśakastvaham..
ityādi cātmavijñānamahaṃkāra iti smṛtaḥ.. 46.47 ..
1.4.d:
अहमेष ममेदं च कार्यमीदृशकस्त्वहम्..
इत्यादि चात्मविज्ञानमहंकार इति स्मृतः.. 46.47 ..
1.4.m: ‘I am this; this is mine; and I must do such-and-such’— / this kind of consciousness of self is called egoism.

1.4.s:
parihāryaḥ ya cettaṃ ca vinonmattaḥ prakīryate..
kāmo'bhilāṣa ityuktaḥ saṃ cetpuṃsā vivarjyate.. 46.48 ..
1.4.d:
परिहार्यः य चेत्तं च विनोन्मत्तः प्रकीर्यते..
कामोऽभिलाष इत्युक्तः सं चेत्पुंसा विवर्ज्यते.. 46.48 ..
1.4.m: If it is to be abandoned, one without it is proclaimed to be insane. / Desire is declared to be longing; if that is abandoned by a man,

1.4.s:
kathaṃ svargo mumukṣā vā sādhyate dṛṣadā yathā..
krodho vā yadi saṃtyājyastataḥ śatrukṣayaḥ katham.. 46.49 ..
1.4.d:
कथं स्वर्गो मुमुक्षा वा साध्यते दृषदा यथा..
क्रोधो वा यदि संत्याज्यस्ततः शत्रुक्षयः कथम्.. 46.49 ..
1.4.m: how can heaven or liberation be attained, [any more than] by a stone? / Or if anger is to be renounced, how then can enemies be destroyed?

1.4.s:
bāhyānāmāṃtarāṇāṃ vā vinā taṃ tṛṇavadviduḥ..
iṃdriyāṇi nigṛhyaiva duṣṭānīti nipīḍayet.. 46.50 ..
1.4.d:
बाह्यानामांतराणां वा विना तं तृणवद्विदुः..
इंद्रियाणि निगृह्यैव दुष्टानीति निपीडयेत्.. 46.50 ..
1.4.m: Without it, they consider [all beings], whether external or internal, as mere grass. / If one simply restrains the senses and torments them because they are corrupt,

1.4.s:
kathaṃ syāddharmaśravaṇaṃ kathaṃ vā jīvanaṃ bhavet..
etasminme mano viddhaṃkhidyate'jñānasaṃkaṭe.. 46.51 ..
1.4.d:
कथं स्याद्धर्मश्रवणं कथं वा जीवनं भवेत्..
एतस्मिन्मे मनो विद्धंखिद्यतेऽज्ञानसंकटे.. 46.51 ..
1.4.m: how could hearing the Dharma take place, or how could there be living? / In this dilemma of ignorance, my mind is pierced and distressed.

1.4.s:
tathā kasmādidaṃ sṛṣṭaṃ jaḍaṃ viśvaṃ cidātmanā..
evaṃ yadbahudhā kleśaḥ pīḍyate hā kutastvidam.. 46.52 ..
1.4.d:
तथा कस्मादिदं सृष्टं जडं विश्वं चिदात्मना..
एवं यद्बहुधा क्लेशः पीड्यते हा कुतस्त्विदम्.. 46.52 ..
1.4.m: Likewise, why was this insentient universe created by the conscious Self? / In this way, when one is afflicted by diverse suffering, alas, from where does this come?

1.4.s:
..bāla uvāca..
samyagetadyathā pṛṣṭaṃ yatra muhyaṃti jaṃtavaḥ..
śrṛṇvekāgramanā bhūtvā jñātaṃ dvaipāyanānmayā.. 46.53 ..
1.4.d:
..बाल उवाच..
सम्यगेतद्यथा पृष्टं यत्र मुह्यंति जंतवः..
श्रृण्वेकाग्रमना भूत्वा ज्ञातं द्वैपायनान्मया.. 46.53 ..
1.4.m: The boy said: / This has been rightly asked by you, regarding that wherein creatures are bewildered. / Listen with a one-pointed mind to what was learned by me from Dvaipāyana.

1.4.s:
prakṛtiḥ puruṣaścaiva anādī śrṛṇumaḥ purā..
sādharmyeṇāvatiṣṭhete sṛṣṭeḥ prāgajarāmarau.. 46.54 ..
1.4.d:
प्रकृतिः पुरुषश्चैव अनादी श्रृणुमः पुरा..
साधर्म्येणावतिष्ठेते सृष्टेः प्रागजरामरौ.. 46.54 ..
1.4.m: We hear that of old, Prakṛti and Puruṣa are beginningless; / ageless and immortal, the two stood in equal nature before creation.

1.4.s:
tataḥ kālasvabāvābhyāṃ preritā prakṛtiḥ purā..
puṃsaḥ saṃyogamaicchatsā tadabhāvātprakupyata.. 46.55 ..
1.4.d:
ततः कालस्वबावाभ्यां प्रेरिता प्रकृतिः पुरा..
पुंसः संयोगमैच्छत्सा तदभावात्प्रकुप्यत.. 46.55 ..
1.4.m: Then of old, Prakṛti, impelled by time and inherent nature, / desired union with Puruṣa; in the absence of that, she became agitated.

1.4.s:
tatastamomayī sā ca līlayā devavīkṣitā..
rājasī samabhūddūṣṭā sāttvikī samajāyata.. 46.56 ..
1.4.d:
ततस्तमोमयी सा च लीलया देववीक्षिता..
राजसी समभूद्दूष्टा सात्त्विकी समजायत.. 46.56 ..
1.4.m: Then she, who was made of tamas, looked upon playfully by God, / became rājasika, and being purified, became sāttvika.

1.4.s:
evaṃ triguṇatāṃ yātā prakṛtirdevadarśanāt..
tāṃ samāsthāya paramastrimūrtiḥ samajāyata.. 46.57 ..
1.4.d:
एवं त्रिगुणतां याता प्रकृतिर्देवदर्शनात्..
तां समास्थाय परमस्त्रिमूर्तिः समजायत.. 46.57 ..
1.4.m: Having thus attained the state of the three guṇas from the gaze of God, / the Supreme One, taking resort in her, became the three forms (Trimūrti).

1.4.s:
tasyāḥ proccāraṇārthaṃ ca pravṛttaḥ svāṃśatastataḥ..
asūyata mahattattvaṃ triguṇaṃ tadvidurbudhāḥ.. 46.58 ..
1.4.d:
तस्याः प्रोच्चारणार्थं च प्रवृत्तः स्वांशतस्ततः..
असूयत महत्तत्त्वं त्रिगुणं तद्विदुर्बुधाः.. 46.58 ..
1.4.m: And proceeding from his own portion for the sake of her evolution, / he brought forth the principle of the cosmic intellect (mahat-tattva) endowed with the three guṇas; so the wise know it.

1.4.s:
ahaṃkāra stato jātaḥ sattvarājasatāmasaḥ..
tamo rajastvamāpadya rajaḥ satt‌vaguṇaṃ nayet.. 46.59 ..
1.4.d:
अहंकार स्ततो जातः सत्त्वराजसतामसः..
तमो रजस्त्वमापद्य रजः सत्त्‌वगुणं नयेत्.. 46.59 ..
1.4.m: From that arose egoism, sāttvika, rājasika, and tāmasika. / Bringing tamas to rajas, one should lead rajas to the quality of sattva.

1.4.s:
śuddhasattve tato mokṣaṃ pravadaṃti manīṣiṇaḥ..
tamaso rajasasta smātsaṃśuddhyarthaṃ ca sarvaśaḥ.. 46.60 ..
1.4.d:
शुद्धसत्त्वे ततो मोक्षं प्रवदंति मनीषिणः..
तमसो रजसस्त स्मात्संशुद्ध्यर्थं च सर्वशः.. 46.60 ..
1.4.m: The wise declare liberation to be in pure sattva. / Therefore, for the complete purification of tamas and rajas,

1.4.s:
jīvātmasaṃjñānsvīyāṃśānvyabhajatparameśvaraḥ..
tāvaṃtaste ca kṣetrjñā dehā yāvaṃta eva hi.. 46.61 ..
1.4.d:
जीवात्मसंज्ञान्स्वीयांशान्व्यभजत्परमेश्वरः..
तावंतस्ते च क्षेत्र्ज्ञा देहा यावंत एव हि.. 46.61 ..
1.4.m: the Supreme Lord divided his own portions, which are called individual souls (jīvātman). / As many as there are bodies, so many indeed are those knowers of the field (kṣetrajña),

1.4.s:
niḥsaraṃti yathā lohāttaptalliṃgātsphuliṃgakāḥ..
tanmātrabhūtasargoyamahaṃkārāttu tāmasāt.. 46.62 ..
1.4.d:
निःसरंति यथा लोहात्तप्तल्लिंगात्स्फुलिंगकाः..
तन्मात्रभूतसर्गोयमहंकारात्तु तामसात्.. 46.62 ..
1.4.m: just as sparks emerge from a heated lump of iron. / But this creation of the subtle elements and gross elements arose from the tāmasika egoism,

1.4.s:
iṃdriyāṇāṃ sāttvikācca triguṇāni ca tānyapi..
etaiḥ saṃsiddhayaṃtreṇa saccidānandavīkṣaṇāt.. 46.63 ..
1.4.d:
इंद्रियाणां सात्त्विकाच्च त्रिगुणानि च तान्यपि..
एतैः संसिद्धयंत्रेण सच्चिदानन्दवीक्षणात्.. 46.63 ..
1.4.m: and that of the senses arose from the sāttvika [egoism]; and these also possess the three guṇas. / Through the instrument fully fashioned by these, through contemplation of Being-Consciousness-Bliss,

1.4.s:
rajastamaśca śodhyaṃte sattvenaiva mumukṣubhiḥ..
tasmātkāmaṃ ca krodhaṃ ca iṃdriyāṇāṃ pravartanam.. 46.64 ..
1.4.d:
रजस्तमश्च शोध्यंते सत्त्वेनैव मुमुक्षुभिः..
तस्मात्कामं च क्रोधं च इंद्रियाणां प्रवर्तनम्.. 46.64 ..
1.4.m: rajas and tamas are purified by sattva alone by those who seek liberation. / Therefore, directing desire, anger, and the operation of the senses,

1.4.s:
ahaṃkāraṃ ca saṃsevya sāttvikīṃ siddhimaśnute..
rājasāstāmasāścaiva tyājyāḥ kāmādayastvamī.. 46.65 ..
1.4.d:
अहंकारं च संसेव्य सात्त्विकीं सिद्धिमश्नुते..
राजसास्तामसाश्चैव त्याज्याः कामादयस्त्वमी.. 46.65 ..
1.4.m: and utilizing egoism, one attains sāttvika perfection. / Those [passions] such as desire that are rājasika and tāmasika should indeed be abandoned;

1.4.s:
sāttvikāḥ sarvadā sevyāḥ saṃsāravijigīṣubhiḥ..
guṇatrayasya vakṣyāmi saṃkṣepāllakṣaṇaṃ tava.. 46.66 ..
1.4.d:
सात्त्विकाः सर्वदा सेव्याः संसारविजिगीषुभिः..
गुणत्रयस्य वक्ष्यामि संक्षेपाल्लक्षणं तव.. 46.66 ..
1.4.m: the sāttvika ones are always to be cultivated by those who wish to conquer worldly existence. / I will explain to you in brief the characteristics of the three guṇas:

1.4.s:
sāstrābhyāsastato jñānaṃ śaucamiṃdriyanigrahaḥ..
dharmakriyātmaciṃtā ca sāttvikaṃ guṇa lakṣaṇam.. 46.67 ..
1.4.d:
सास्त्राभ्यासस्ततो ज्ञानं शौचमिंद्रियनिग्रहः..
धर्मक्रियात्मचिंता च सात्त्विकं गुण लक्षणम्.. 46.67 ..
1.4.m: Study of scriptures, then knowledge, purity, restraint of the senses, / righteous action, and contemplation of the Self—these are the characteristics of the sāttvika guṇa.

1.4.s:
anyāyena dhanādānaṃ taṃdrī nāstikyameva ca..
krauryaṃ ca yācakādyaṃ ca tāmasaṃ guṇalakṣaṇam.. 46.68 ..
1.4.d:
अन्यायेन धनादानं तंद्री नास्तिक्यमेव च..
क्रौर्यं च याचकाद्यं च तामसं गुणलक्षणम्.. 46.68 ..
1.4.m: Acquisition of wealth through unjust means, sloth, lack of faith in the hereafter, / cruelty, and living by begging and the like—these are the characteristics of the tāmasika guṇa.

1.4.s:
tasmādbuddhimukaistvataiḥ sāttvikairdevatāṃ bhajet..
rājasairmānavatvaṃ ca tāmasaiḥ sthāṇuyonitā.. 46.69 ..
1.4.d:
तस्माद्बुद्धिमुकैस्त्वतैः सात्त्विकैर्देवतां भजेत्..
राजसैर्मानवत्वं च तामसैः स्थाणुयोनिता.. 46.69 ..
1.4.m: Therefore, with these sāttvika [faculties] led by the intellect, one should worship the deity. / Through rājasika [qualities] one attains human birth, and through tāmasika ones, the state of immobile beings.

1.4.s: buddhyādyaireva muktiḥ syādetaireva ca yātanā.. 46.70 ..
1.4.d: बुद्ध्याद्यैरेव मुक्तिः स्यादेतैरेव च यातना.. 46.70 ..
1.4.m: Through intellect and the rest [when purified], liberation ensues; and through these very same [when impure], torment [results].

1.4.s:
amīṣāṃ cāpya bhāve vai na kiṃcidupapadyate..
kalādo hi kalādīnāṃ suvarṇaṃ śodhayedyathā.. 46.71 ..
1.4.d:
अमीषां चाप्य भावे वै न किंचिदुपपद्यते..
कलादो हि कलादीनां सुवर्णं शोधयेद्यथा.. 46.71 ..
1.4.m: And in the absence of these [guṇas], nothing indeed comes into being. / For just as a goldsmith purifies gold of impurities and the like,

1.4.s:
tathā rajastamaścaiva saṃśodhye sāttvikairguṇaiḥ..
asmādeva guṇānāṃ ca samavāyādanādijāt.. 46.72 ..
1.4.d:
तथा रजस्तमश्चैव संशोध्ये सात्त्विकैर्गुणैः..
अस्मादेव गुणानां च समवायादनादिजात्.. 46.72 ..
1.4.m: even so must rajas and tamas be purified by the qualities of sattva. / And solely from this conjunction of the qualities, born without beginning,

1.4.s:
sukhino duḥkhinaścaiva prāṇinaḥ śāstradarśinaḥ..
aṣṭāviṃśatilakṣaiśca guṇamekaikamīśvaraḥ.. 46.73 ..
1.4.d:
सुखिनो दुःखिनश्चैव प्राणिनः शास्त्रदर्शिनः..
अष्टाविंशतिलक्षैश्च गुणमेकैकमीश्वरः.. 46.73 ..
1.4.m: beings who observe the treatises are happy and unhappy. / And the Lord divided each single quality

1.4.s:
vyabhajaccaturā śītilakṣāstā jīvayonayaḥ..
sakāśānmanasastadvadātmanaḥ prabhavaṃti hi.. 46.74 ..
1.4.d:
व्यभजच्चतुरा शीतिलक्षास्ता जीवयोनयः..
सकाशान्मनसस्तद्वदात्मनः प्रभवंति हि.. 46.74 ..
1.4.m: into twenty-eight hundred thousand [parts]; these are eighty-four hundred thousand wombs of living beings. / In that manner, from the vicinity of the mind, they arise from the Self;

1.4.s:
īśvarāṃśāśca te sarve mohitāḥ prākṛtairguṇaiḥ..
kleśānāsādayaṃtyeva yathaivādhikṛtā vibhoḥ.. 46.75 ..
1.4.d:
ईश्वरांशाश्च ते सर्वे मोहिताः प्राकृतैर्गुणैः..
क्लेशानासादयंत्येव यथैवाधिकृता विभोः.. 46.75 ..
1.4.m: and all of them, being portions of the Lord, are deluded by the qualities of Prakṛti. / They indeed encounter afflictions, just as those commissioned by the all-pervading Lord do.

1.4.s:
annānāṃ payasāṃ cāpi jīvānāṃ cātha śreyase..
mānuṣyamāhustattvajñāḥ śivabhāvena bhāvitam.. 46.76 ..
1.4.d:
अन्नानां पयसां चापि जीवानां चाथ श्रेयसे..
मानुष्यमाहुस्तत्त्वज्ञाः शिवभावेन भावितम्.. 46.76 ..
1.4.m: For the highest good of food, water, and living beings, / the knowers of truth say that human existence is transformed by the being of Śiva."

1.4.s:
..naṃdabhadra uvāca..
evametatkiṃ tu bhūyaḥ prakṣyāmyetanmahāmate..
īśvarāḥ sarvadātāraḥ pūjyaṃte yaiśca devatāḥ.. 46.77 ..
1.4.d:
..नंदभद्र उवाच..
एवमेतत्किं तु भूयः प्रक्ष्याम्येतन्महामते..
ईश्वराः सर्वदातारः पूज्यंते यैश्च देवताः.. 46.77 ..
1.4.m: Nandabhadra said: / "So it is. But again I shall ask this, O great-minded one: / the deities who are all-bestowing lords are worshipped by men;

1.4.s:
svabhaktāṃstānna duḥkhebhyaḥ kasmādrakṣaṃti mānavān..
viśeṣātkepi dṛśyaṃte duḥkhamagnāḥ surānratāḥ.. 46.78 ..
1.4.d:
स्वभक्तांस्तान्न दुःखेभ्यः कस्माद्रक्षंति मानवान्..
विशेषात्केपि दृश्यंते दुःखमग्नाः सुरान्रताः.. 46.78 ..
1.4.m: why do they not protect those devoted to them from sufferings? / In particular, some who are devoted to the gods are seen plunged in suffering.

1.4.s: iti me muhyate buddhistvaṃ vā kiṃ bāla manyase.. 46.79 ..
1.4.d: इति मे मुह्यते बुद्धिस्त्वं वा किं बाल मन्यसे.. 46.79 ..
1.4.m: Thus my intellect is bewildered; or what do you think, O boy?"

1.4.s:
..bāla uvāca..
aśuciśca śuciścāpi devabhakto dvidhā smṛtaḥ..
karmaṇā manasā vācā tadrato bhakta ucyate.. 46.80 ..
1.4.d:
..बाल उवाच..
अशुचिश्च शुचिश्चापि देवभक्तो द्विधा स्मृतः..
कर्मणा मनसा वाचा तद्रतो भक्त उच्यते.. 46.80 ..
1.4.m: The boy said: / "The devotee of a deity is remembered as twofold: impure and pure. / One who is devoted to him in deed, mind, and speech is called a devotee.

1.4.s:
aśucirdevatāścaiva yadā pūjayate naraḥ..
tadā bhūtānyā viśaṃti sa ca muhyati tatkṣaṇāt.. 46.81 ..
1.4.d:
अशुचिर्देवताश्चैव यदा पूजयते नरः..
तदा भूतान्या विशंति स च मुह्यति तत्क्षणात्.. 46.81 ..
1.4.m: When an impure man worships the deities, / then spirits enter him, and he is bewildered in that very moment.

1.4.s:
vimūḍhaścāpṭayakāryāṇi tāni tāni niṣevate..
tato vinaśyati kṣipraṃ nāśuciḥ pūjayettataḥ..
śucirvābhyarcayedyaśca tasya cedaśubhaṃ bhavet.. 46.82 ..
1.4.d:
विमूढश्चाप्टयकार्याणि तानि तानि निषेवते..
ततो विनश्यति क्षिप्रं नाशुचिः पूजयेत्ततः..
शुचिर्वाभ्यर्चयेद्यश्च तस्य चेदशुभं भवेत्.. 46.82 ..
1.4.m: Utterly deluded, he commits those various improper deeds; / then he quickly perishes. Therefore, an impure person should not worship. / But if an evil should befall one who, being pure, worships,

1.4.s:
tasya pūrvakṛtaṃ vyaktaṃ karmaṇāṃ koṭi mucyate..
maheśvaro brahmahatyābhayādyatra tatastataḥ.. 46.83 ..
1.4.d:
तस्य पूर्वकृतं व्यक्तं कर्मणां कोटि मुच्यते..
महेश्वरो ब्रह्महत्याभयाद्यत्र ततस्ततः.. 46.83 ..
1.4.m: the crore of deeds done by him in a previous life is clearly released. / Since Maheśvara, out of fear of killing a brahmin, ran here and there,

1.4.s:
sasnau tīrtheṣu kasmācca itaro mucyate katham..
ambarīṣasutāṃ hṛtvā parvatānnāradāttathā.. 46.84 ..
1.4.d:
सस्नौ तीर्थेषु कस्माच्च इतरो मुच्यते कथम्..
अम्बरीषसुतां हृत्वा पर्वतान्नारदात्तथा.. 46.84 ..
1.4.m: and bathed in sacred fords, how then can another be freed? / Having seized the daughter of Ambarīṣa from Parvata and Nārada,

1.4.s:
sītāpahāramāpede rāmo'nyo mucyate katham..
brahmāpi śirasaśchedaṃ kāmayitvā sutāmagāt.. 46.85 ..
1.4.d:
सीतापहारमापेदे रामोऽन्यो मुच्यते कथम्..
ब्रह्मापि शिरसश्छेदं कामयित्वा सुतामगात्.. 46.85 ..
1.4.m: Rāma suffered the abduction of Sītā; how can another be freed? / Brahmā too, having lusted after his own daughter, incurred the severing of his head.

1.4.s:
iṃdracaṃdraraviviṣṇupramukhāḥ prāpnuyuḥ kṛtam..
tasmādavaśyaṃ ca kṛtaṃ bhojyameva naraiḥ sadā.. 46.86 ..
1.4.d:
इंद्रचंद्ररविविष्णुप्रमुखाः प्राप्नुयुः कृतम्..
तस्मादवश्यं च कृतं भोज्यमेव नरैः सदा.. 46.86 ..
1.4.m: Indra, the Moon, the Sun, Viṣṇu, and the others must experience [the fruit of] what was done. / Therefore, that which has been done must always inevitably be experienced by men.

1.4.s:
mucyate ko'pi svakṛtānnaiveti śrutinirṇayaḥ..
kiṃ tu devaprasādena labhyamekaṃ suravrataiḥ.. 46.87 ..
1.4.d:
मुच्यते कोऽपि स्वकृतान्नैवेति श्रुतिनिर्णयः..
किं तु देवप्रसादेन लभ्यमेकं सुरव्रतैः.. 46.87 ..
1.4.m: No one is freed from what he himself has done; such is the determination of the scripture. / But by the grace of the deity, one thing is obtained by those keeping vows to the gods:

1.4.s:
bahubhirjanmabhirbhojyaṃ bhujyetaikena janmanā..
tacca bhuktvāta tastvartho bhavediti viniścayaḥ.. 46.88 ..
1.4.d:
बहुभिर्जन्मभिर्भोज्यं भुज्येतैकेन जन्मना..
तच्च भुक्त्वात तस्त्वर्थो भवेदिति विनिश्चयः.. 46.88 ..
1.4.m: that which is to be experienced through many births may be experienced in a single birth; / and having experienced that, from then on his goal is attained; this is the certitude.

1.4.s:
ye tapyaṃte gataiḥ pāpaiḥ śucayo devatāvratāḥ..
iha te putrapautraiśca modaṃte'mutra ceha ca.. 46.89 ..
1.4.d:
ये तप्यंते गतैः पापैः शुचयो देवताव्रताः..
इह ते पुत्रपौत्रैश्च मोदंतेऽमुत्र चेह च.. 46.89 ..
1.4.m: Those who, being pure and keeping vows to the deities, are tormented by past sins, / rejoice here with sons and grandsons, both in the other world and in this.

1.4.s:
tasmāddevāḥ sadā pūjyāḥ śucibhiḥ śraddhayānvitaiḥ..
prakṛtiḥ śodhanīyā ca svavarṇoditakarmabhiḥ.. 46.90 ..
1.4.d:
तस्माद्देवाः सदा पूज्याः शुचिभिः श्रद्धयान्वितैः..
प्रकृतिः शोधनीया च स्ववर्णोदितकर्मभिः.. 46.90 ..
1.4.m: Therefore, the gods must always be worshipped by the pure, endowed with faith; / and Prakṛti must be purified by the duties prescribed for one's own caste.

1.4.s:
svanuṣṭhito'pi dharmaḥ syātkleśāyaiva vināśivam..
durācārasya devopi prāheti bhagavānharaḥ.. 46.91 ..
1.4.d:
स्वनुष्ठितोऽपि धर्मः स्यात्क्लेशायैव विनाशिवम्..
दुराचारस्य देवोपि प्राहेति भगवान्हरः.. 46.91 ..
1.4.m: Even duty well performed would lead only to affliction without Śiva; / even a god becomes an evil-doer [without him], so says the venerable Hara.

1.4.s:
bhoktavyaṃ svakṛtaṃ tasmātpūjanīyaḥ sadāśivaḥ..
svācāreṇa parityājyau rāgadveṣāvidaṃ param.. 46.92 ..
1.4.d:
भोक्तव्यं स्वकृतं तस्मात्पूजनीयः सदाशिवः..
स्वाचारेण परित्याज्यौ रागद्वेषाविदं परम्.. 46.92 ..
1.4.m: Therefore, what was done by oneself must be experienced, and Sadāśiva must be worshipped. / By proper conduct, passion and hatred are to be abandoned; this is supreme."

1.4.s:
..nandabhadra uvāca..
śuddhaprajña kimetacca pāpino'pi narā yadā..
modamānāḥ pradṛśyante dārairapi dhanairapi.. 46.93 ..
1.4.d:
..नन्दभद्र उवाच..
शुद्धप्रज्ञ किमेतच्च पापिनोऽपि नरा यदा..
मोदमानाः प्रदृश्यन्ते दारैरपि धनैरपि.. 46.93 ..
1.4.m: Nandabhadra said: / "O you of pure intellect, what is this: when even sinful men / are seen rejoicing with wives and wealth?"

1.4.s:
..bāla uvāca..
vyaktaṃ taistamasā dattaṃ dānaṃ pūrveṣu janmasu..
rajasā pūjitaḥ śaṃbhustatprāptaṃ svakṛtaṃ ca taiḥ.. 46.94 ..
1.4.d:
..बाल उवाच..
व्यक्तं तैस्तमसा दत्तं दानं पूर्वेषु जन्मसु..
रजसा पूजितः शंभुस्तत्प्राप्तं स्वकृतं च तैः.. 46.94 ..
1.4.m: The boy said: / "Evidently, a gift was given by them in previous births with tamas, / and Śambhu was worshipped with rajas; thus what they themselves did has been attained by them.

1.4.s:
kiṃ tu yattamasā karma kṛtaṃ tasya prabhāvataḥ..
dharmāya na ratirbhūyāttatasteṣāṃ vidāṃvara.. 46.95 ..
1.4.d:
किं तु यत्तमसा कर्म कृतं तस्य प्रभावतः..
धर्माय न रतिर्भूयात्ततस्तेषां विदांवर.. 46.95 ..
1.4.m: However, by the power of the deed done with tamas, / they will have no pleasure in dharma; hence, O best of the wise,

1.4.s:
bhuktvā puṇyaphalaṃ yāti narakaṃ saṃśayaḥ..
asmiṃśca saṃśaye proktaṃ mārkaṃḍeyena śrūyate.. 46.96 ..
1.4.d:
भुक्त्वा पुण्यफलं याति नरकं संशयः..
अस्मिंश्च संशये प्रोक्तं मार्कंडेयेन श्रूयते.. 46.96 ..
1.4.m: having experienced the fruit of merit, [such a person] goes to hell, without doubt. / And on this doubt, what was spoken by Mārkaṇḍeya is heard:

1.4.s:
ihaivaikasya nāmutra amutraikasya no iha..
iha cāmutra caikasya nāmutraikasya no iha.. 46.97 ..
1.4.d:
इहैवैकस्य नामुत्र अमुत्रैकस्य नो इह..
इह चामुत्र चैकस्य नामुत्रैकस्य नो इह.. 46.97 ..
1.4.m: '[Pleasure is] for one only here, not in the other world; for one, in the other world, not here; / for one, both here and in the other world; for one, neither in the other world nor here.

1.4.s:
pūrvopāttaṃ bhavetpuṇyaṃ bhuktirnaivārjayantyapi..
iha bhogaḥ sa vai prokto durbhagasyālpamedhasaḥ.. 46.98 ..
1.4.d:
पूर्वोपात्तं भवेत्पुण्यं भुक्तिर्नैवार्जयन्त्यपि..
इह भोगः स वै प्रोक्तो दुर्भगस्याल्पमेधसः.. 46.98 ..
1.4.m: When merit has been acquired in the past, yet they do not earn enjoyment [anew], / that enjoyment here is indeed said to belong to the unfortunate person of little intelligence.

1.4.s:
pūrvopāttaṃ yasya nāsti tapobhiścārjayatyapi..
paraloke tasya bhogo dhīmataḥ sa kriyātsphuṭam.. 46.99 ..
1.4.d:
पूर्वोपात्तं यस्य नास्ति तपोभिश्चार्जयत्यपि..
परलोके तस्य भोगो धीमतः स क्रियात्स्फुटम्.. 46.99 ..
1.4.m: He who has none acquired in the past, yet earns it through austerities, / has enjoyment in the other world; that wise man acts clearly.

1.4.s:
pūrvopāttaṃ yasya nāsti puṇyaṃ cehāpi nārjayet..
tataścohāmutra vāpi bho dhiktaṃ ca narādhamam.. 46.100 ..
1.4.d:
पूर्वोपात्तं यस्य नास्ति पुण्यं चेहापि नार्जयेत्..
ततश्चोहामुत्र वापि भो धिक्तं च नराधमम्.. 46.100 ..
1.4.m: He who has none acquired in the past and does not earn merit here either, / from that, neither here nor in the other world—alas, fie upon that lowest of men!'

1.4.s:
iti jñātvā mahābhāgatyaktvā śalyāni kṛtsnaśaḥ..
bhaja rudraṃ varṇadharmaṃ pālayāsmātparaṃ na hi.. 46.101 ..
1.4.d:
इति ज्ञात्वा महाभागत्यक्त्वा शल्यानि कृत्स्नशः..
भज रुद्रं वर्णधर्मं पालयास्मात्परं न हि.. 46.101 ..
1.4.m: Knowing this, O fortunate one, having discarded all thorns, / worship Rudra and uphold the duty of your caste; there is nothing higher than this.

1.4.s:
yohi naṣṭeṣvabhīṣṭeṣu prāpteṣvapi ca śocati..
tṛpyeta vā bhavedbandho niścitaṃ so'nyajanmanaḥ.. 46.102 ..
1.4.d:
योहि नष्टेष्वभीष्टेषु प्राप्तेष्वपि च शोचति..
तृप्येत वा भवेद्बन्धो निश्चितं सोऽन्यजन्मनः.. 46.102 ..
1.4.m: For he who grieves when desired things are lost, or even when they are obtained, / or becomes satisfied, that is certainly a bondage for another birth."

1.4.s:
..nandabhadra uvāca..
namastubhyamabālāya bālarūpāya dhīmate..
ko bhavāṃstattvato vettumicchāmi tvāṃ śucismitam.. 46.103 ..
1.4.d:
..नन्दभद्र उवाच..
नमस्तुभ्यमबालाय बालरूपाय धीमते..
को भवांस्तत्त्वतो वेत्तुमिच्छामि त्वां शुचिस्मितम्.. 46.103 ..
1.4.m: Nandabhadra said: / "Homage to you, who are no child, though in the form of a child, O wise one! / Who are you in truth? I wish to know you of pure smile.

1.4.s:
bahavo'pi mayā vṛddhā dṛṣṭāścopāsitāḥ sadā..
teṣāmīdṛśakā buddhirna dṛṣṭā na śrutāmayā.. 46.104 ..
1.4.d:
बहवोऽपि मया वृद्धा दृष्टाश्चोपासिताः सदा..
तेषामीदृशका बुद्धिर्न दृष्टा न श्रुतामया.. 46.104 ..
1.4.m: Many elders have been seen and always served by me, / [yet] such an intellect has not been seen or heard of by me in them,

1.4.s:
yena me janmasaṃdehā nāśitā līlayaiva ca..
tasmātsāmānyarūpastvaṃ niścitaṃ na mataṃ mama.. 46.105 ..
1.4.d:
येन मे जन्मसंदेहा नाशिता लीलयैव च..
तस्मात्सामान्यरूपस्त्वं निश्चितं न मतं मम.. 46.105 ..
1.4.m: by which the doubts of my existence have been destroyed as if in play. / Therefore, my opinion is certain that you are not of ordinary nature."

1.4.s:
..bāla uvāca..
mahadetatsamākhyeyamekāgraḥ śrṛṇu tattvataḥ..
itaḥ saptādhike cāpi saptame janmani tvaham.. 46.106 ..
1.4.d:
..बाल उवाच..
महदेतत्समाख्येयमेकाग्रः श्रृणु तत्त्वतः..
इतः सप्ताधिके चापि सप्तमे जन्मनि त्वहम्.. 46.106 ..
1.4.m: The boy said: / "This great matter must be related; listen attentively, in truth: / In the fourteenth birth from this one, I myself

1.4.s:
vaidiśe nagare vipro nāmnā'saṃ dharmajālikaḥ..
vedavedāṃgatattvatraḥ smṛtiśāstrārthavidvaraḥ.. 46.107 ..
1.4.d:
वैदिशे नगरे विप्रो नाम्नाऽसं धर्मजालिकः..
वेदवेदांगतत्त्वत्रः स्मृतिशास्त्रार्थविद्वरः.. 46.107 ..
1.4.m: was a brahmin named Dharmajālika in the city of Vidiśā, / a knower of the truth of the Vedas and Vedāṅgas, the best knower of the meaning of smṛti treatises,

1.4.s:
vyākhyātā dharmaśāstrāṇāṃ yathā sākṣādbṛhaspatiḥ..
kiṃ tvahaṃ vividhāndharmālloṃkānāṃ varṇaye bhṛśam.. 46.108 ..
1.4.d:
व्याख्याता धर्मशास्त्राणां यथा साक्षाद्बृहस्पतिः..
किं त्वहं विविधान्धर्माल्लोंकानां वर्णये भृशम्.. 46.108 ..
1.4.m: an expounder of the treatises on dharma, like Bṛhaspati incarnate. / But I described various dharmas exceedingly to the people,

1.4.s:
svayaṃ cātidurācāraḥ pāpināmapi pāparāṭ..
maṃsāśī madyasevī ca paradārarataḥ sadā.. 46.109 ..
1.4.d:
स्वयं चातिदुराचारः पापिनामपि पापराट्..
मंसाशी मद्यसेवी च परदाररतः सदा.. 46.109 ..
1.4.m: while I myself was of utterly bad conduct, a king of sins even among sinners: / eating meat, consuming liquor, and always devoted to the wives of others,

1.4.s:
asatyabhāṣī dambhīca sadā dharmadhvajī khalaḥ..
lobhī durātmā kathako na kartā karhicitkvacit.. 46.110 ..
1.4.d:
असत्यभाषी दम्भीच सदा धर्मध्वजी खलः..
लोभी दुरात्मा कथको न कर्ता कर्हिचित्क्वचित्.. 46.110 ..
1.4.m: speaking falsehood, hypocritical, a rogue always bearing the hypocritical badge of dharma, / greedy, evil-minded, a speaker, never a doer at any time or anywhere.

1.4.s:
yasmājjālikavajjālaṃ lokebhyo'haṃ kṣipāmi ca..
tattvajñā māṃ tataḥ prāhurdharmajālika ityuta.. 46.111 ..
1.4.d:
यस्माज्जालिकवज्जालं लोकेभ्योऽहं क्षिपामि च..
तत्त्वज्ञा मां ततः प्राहुर्धर्मजालिक इत्युत.. 46.111 ..
1.4.m: Because like a fowler (jālika) I cast a net (jāla) over the people, / the knowers of truth therefore called me 'Dharmajālika' (a dealer in religious fraud).

1.4.s:
so'haṃ tairbahubhiścīrṇaiḥ pātakairaṃta āgate..
mṛto gato yamasthānaṃ pātitaḥ kūṭaśālmalīm.. 46.112 ..
1.4.d:
सोऽहं तैर्बहुभिश्चीर्णैः पातकैरंत आगते..
मृतो गतो यमस्थानं पातितः कूटशाल्मलीम्.. 46.112 ..
1.4.m: When the end arrived, I, burdened by those many sins that had been committed, / died and went to the realm of Yama, and was cast upon the Kūṭaśālmalī tree.

1.4.s:
yamadutaistataḥ kṛṣṭaḥ smāryamāmaḥ svaceṣṭitam..
khaḍgaiśca kṛtyamāno'haṃ jīvāmi pramiyāmi ca.. 46.113 ..
1.4.d:
यमदुतैस्ततः कृष्टः स्मार्यमामः स्वचेष्टितम्..
खड्गैश्च कृत्यमानोऽहं जीवामि प्रमियामि च.. 46.113 ..
1.4.m: Then, dragged by the messengers of Yama, reminded of my own conduct, / and hacked with swords, I lived and died repeatedly.

1.4.s:
ātmānaṃ bahudhā niṃdañchāśvatīrnyavasaṃ samāḥ..
narake yā matirbhūyāddharmaṃ prati prapīḍataḥ.. 46.114 ..
1.4.d:
आत्मानं बहुधा निंदञ्छाश्वतीर्न्यवसं समाः..
नरके या मतिर्भूयाद्धर्मं प्रति प्रपीडतः.. 46.114 ..
1.4.m: Blaming myself in many ways, I dwelt [there] for eternal years. / If that mind directed toward righteousness when tortured in hell

1.4.s:
sā cenmuhūrtamātraṃ syādapi dhanyastataḥ pumān..
namonamaḥ karmabhūmyai sukṛtaṃ duṣkṛtaṃ ca vā.. 46.115 ..
1.4.d:
सा चेन्मुहूर्तमात्रं स्यादपि धन्यस्ततः पुमान्..
नमोनमः कर्मभूम्यै सुकृतं दुष्कृतं च वा.. 46.115 ..
1.4.m: were to exist for just a single moment, a man would indeed be blessed thereby. / Obeisance, obeisance to the realm of action, where good and bad deeds [bear fruit],

1.4.s:
yasyāṃ muhūrtamātreṇa yugairapi na naśyati..
tato vipaścijjanako mokṣayāmāsa nārakāt.. 46.116 ..
1.4.d:
यस्यां मुहूर्तमात्रेण युगैरपि न नश्यति..
ततो विपश्चिज्जनको मोक्षयामास नारकात्.. 46.116 ..
1.4.m: in which [an action done] in just a moment does not perish even in yugas! / Then wise Janaka freed [me] from hell.

1.4.s:
taiḥ sahāhaṃ pramuktaśca kathaṃcidavapīḍitaḥ..
sthāṇutvamanubhūyātha kleśānāsādya bhūriśaḥ.. 46.117 ..
1.4.d:
तैः सहाहं प्रमुक्तश्च कथंचिदवपीडितः..
स्थाणुत्वमनुभूयाथ क्लेशानासाद्य भूरिशः.. 46.117 ..
1.4.m: Along with them, I, being tormented, was somehow released. / Then, experiencing the state of an immobile post and enduring numerous afflictions,

1.4.s:
kīṭohamabhavaṃ paścāttīre sārasvate śubhe..
tatra mārge sukhamiva saṃsuptohaṃ yadṛcchayā.. 46.118 ..
1.4.d:
कीटोहमभवं पश्चात्तीरे सारस्वते शुभे..
तत्र मार्गे सुखमिव संसुप्तोहं यदृच्छया.. 46.118 ..
1.4.m: I afterwards became a worm on the auspicious bank of the Sarasvatī. / There on the road, as if at ease, I fell fast asleep by chance.

1.4.s:
āgacchato rathasyāsya śabdamaśrauṣamunnatam..
taṃ meghaninadaṃ śrutvā bhītohaṃ sahasā javāt.. 46.119 ..
1.4.d:
आगच्छतो रथस्यास्य शब्दमश्रौषमुन्नतम्..
तं मेघनिनदं श्रुत्वा भीतोहं सहसा जवात्.. 46.119 ..
1.4.m: I heard the loud sound of an approaching chariot. / Hearing that roar like a cloud, frightened, I quickly and with haste,

1.4.s:
mārgamutsṛjya dūreṇa prapalāyanamācaram..
etasminnaṃtare vyāsastatra prāpto yadṛcchayā.. 46.120 ..
1.4.d:
मार्गमुत्सृज्य दूरेण प्रपलायनमाचरम्..
एतस्मिन्नंतरे व्यासस्तत्र प्राप्तो यदृच्छया.. 46.120 ..
1.4.m: leaving the road far behind, took to flight. / In the meantime, Vyāsa arrived there by chance.

1.4.s:
sa māmapaśyattrastaṃ ca kṛpayā saṃyuto muniḥ..
yanmayā sarvalokānāṃ nānādharmāḥ prakīrtitāḥ.. 46.121 ..
1.4.d:
स मामपश्यत्त्रस्तं च कृपया संयुतो मुनिः..
यन्मया सर्वलोकानां नानाधर्माः प्रकीर्तिताः.. 46.121 ..
1.4.m: The sage, filled with compassion, saw me terrified. / Because various dharmas had been proclaimed by me to all people

1.4.s:
viprajanmani tasyaiva prabhāvādvyāsasaṃgamaḥ..
tataḥ sarvarutajño māṃ prāhārcyaḥ kīṭabhāṣayā.. 46.122 ..
1.4.d:
विप्रजन्मनि तस्यैव प्रभावाद्व्याससंगमः..
ततः सर्वरुतज्ञो मां प्राहार्च्यः कीटभाषया.. 46.122 ..
1.4.m: in [my former] birth as a brahmin, by that very power came meeting with Vyāsa. / Then he, who knows the cries of all creatures and is worthy of worship, addressed me in the speech of worms:

1.4.s:
kimevaṃ naśyase kīṭa kasmānmṛtyorbibheṣi ca..
aho samucitā bhītirmanuṣyasya kutastava.. 46.123 ..
1.4.d:
किमेवं नश्यसे कीट कस्मान्मृत्योर्बिभेषि च..
अहो समुचिता भीतिर्मनुष्यस्य कुतस्तव.. 46.123 ..
1.4.m: "Why do you flee thus, O worm, and why do you fear death? / Ah, fear is fitting for a human, but whence comes yours?"

1.4.s:
ityukto matimānpūrvapuṇyādvyāsaṃ tadocivān..
na me bhayaṃ jagadvaṃdya mṛtyorasmātkathaṃcana.. 46.124 ..
1.4.d:
इत्युक्तो मतिमान्पूर्वपुण्याद्व्यासं तदोचिवान्..
न मे भयं जगद्वंद्य मृत्योरस्मात्कथंचन.. 46.124 ..
1.4.m: Thus addressed, being endowed with intellect due to past merit, I then spoke to Vyāsa: / "O you praised by the world, I have no fear whatsoever of this death.

1.4.s:
etadeva bhayaṃ mānya gaccheyamadhamāṃ gatim..
asyā api kuyoneśca saṃtyanyāḥ koṭiśo'dhamāḥ.. 46.125 ..
1.4.d:
एतदेव भयं मान्य गच्छेयमधमां गतिम्..
अस्या अपि कुयोनेश्च संत्यन्याः कोटिशोऽधमाः.. 46.125 ..
1.4.m: This alone is my fear, O venerable one: that I may go to an even lower state. / For even lower than this base womb are ten million other vile [births].

1.4.s: tāsu garbhādikakleśabhītastrasto'smi nānyathā.. 46.126 ..
1.4.d: तासु गर्भादिकक्लेशभीतस्त्रस्तोऽस्मि नान्यथा.. 46.126 ..
1.4.m: Afraid of the sufferings of the womb and so forth in those, I am terrified, not otherwise."

1.4.s:
..vyāsa uvāca..
mā bhayaṃ kuru sarvābhyo yonibhyaśca cirādiva..
mokṣayiṣyāmi brāhmaṇyaṃ prāpayiṣyāmi niścitam.. 46.127 ..
1.4.d:
..व्यास उवाच..
मा भयं कुरु सर्वाभ्यो योनिभ्यश्च चिरादिव..
मोक्षयिष्यामि ब्राह्मण्यं प्रापयिष्यामि निश्चितम्.. 46.127 ..
1.4.m: Vyāsa said: / "Do not be afraid! From all wombs, as if after a long time, / I will release you and certainly bring you to the status of a brahmin."

1.4.s:
ityuktohaṃ kāliyena taṃ praṇamya jagadgurum..
mārgamāgatya cakreṇa pīḍito mṛtyumāgamam.. 46.128 ..
1.4.d:
इत्युक्तोहं कालियेन तं प्रणम्य जगद्गुरुम्..
मार्गमागत्य चक्रेण पीडितो मृत्युमागमम्.. 46.128 ..
1.4.m: Having been told this, I bowed to that teacher of the world through Kāliya, / and coming to the path, crushed by the wheel, I met my death.

1.4.s:
tataḥ kākaśrṛgālādiyoniṣvasmi yadā'bhavam..
tadātadā samāgamya vyāso māṃ smārayacca tat.. 46.129 ..
1.4.d:
ततः काकश्रृगालादियोनिष्वस्मि यदाऽभवम्..
तदातदा समागम्य व्यासो मां स्मारयच्च तत्.. 46.129 ..
1.4.m: Then, whenever I was born into the wombs of crows, jackals, and others, / Vyāsa approached and reminded me of that each time.

1.4.s:
tato bahuvidhā yonīḥ parikramyāsmi karṣitaḥ..
brāhmaṇasya ca gehesyāṃ yonau jāto'tiduḥkhitaḥ.. 46.130 ..
1.4.d:
ततो बहुविधा योनीः परिक्रम्यास्मि कर्षितः..
ब्राह्मणस्य च गेहेस्यां योनौ जातोऽतिदुःखितः.. 46.130 ..
1.4.m: Then, having wandered through various kinds of wombs, I was exhausted; / and born exceedingly miserable in this womb in the house of a brahmin,

1.4.s:
tato janmaprabhṛtyasmi pitṛbhyāṃ parivarjitaḥ..
galatkuṣṭhī mahāpīḍāmetāṃ yo'nubhavāmi ca.. 46.131 ..
1.4.d:
ततो जन्मप्रभृत्यस्मि पितृभ्यां परिवर्जितः..
गलत्कुष्ठी महापीडामेतां योऽनुभवामि च.. 46.131 ..
1.4.m: I have been abandoned by my parents ever since birth, / suffering from advanced leprosy, and I experience this great torment.

1.4.s:
tato māṃ paṃcame varṣe vyāsa āgatya japtavān..
karṇe sārasvataṃ maṃtraṃ tenāhaṃ saṃsmarāmi ca.. 46.132 ..
1.4.d:
ततो मां पंचमे वर्षे व्यास आगत्य जप्तवान्..
कर्णे सारस्वतं मंत्रं तेनाहं संस्मरामि च.. 46.132 ..
1.4.m: Then in my fifth year, Vyāsa came and whispered / the hymn of Sarasvatī into my ear, by which I remember

1.4.s:
anadhītāni śāstrāṇi vedāndharmāṃśca kṛtsnaśaḥ..
uktaṃ vyāsena cedaṃ me gaccha kṣetraṃ guhasya ca..
tatra tvaṃ naṃdabhadraṃ ca āśvāsayamahāmatim.. 46.133 ..
1.4.d:
अनधीतानि शास्त्राणि वेदान्धर्मांश्च कृत्स्नशः..
उक्तं व्यासेन चेदं मे गच्छ क्षेत्रं गुहस्य च..
तत्र त्वं नंदभद्रं च आश्वासयमहामतिम्.. 46.133 ..
1.4.m: the unstudied scriptures, the Vedas, and all the dharmas in full. / And this was said to me by Vyāsa: 'Go to the sacred field of Guha; / there console the high-minded Nandabhadra.

1.4.s:
tyatkvā bahūdake prāṇānasthikṣepaṃ mahījale..
kārāyya tvaṃ tato bhāvī maitreya iti sanmuniḥ.. 46.134 ..
1.4.d:
त्यत्क्वा बहूदके प्राणानस्थिक्षेपं महीजले..
काराय्य त्वं ततो भावी मैत्रेय इति सन्मुनिः.. 46.134 ..
1.4.m: Having cast off your vital breaths at Bahūdaka and having caused your bones / to be thrown into the water of the Mahī, you will then become the good sage named Maitreya.

1.4.s:
gamiṣyasi tato mokṣamiti māṃ vyāsa uktavān..
āgataśca tataścātra vāhīkebhyo'yo'tikleśataḥ.. 46.135 ..
1.4.d:
गमिष्यसि ततो मोक्षमिति मां व्यास उक्तवान्..
आगतश्च ततश्चात्र वाहीकेभ्योऽयोऽतिक्लेशतः.. 46.135 ..
1.4.m: Then you will go to liberation'—so Vyāsa told me. / And then, with extreme suffering, I came here from the Vāhīkas.

1.4.s:
iti te kathitaṃ sarvamātmanaścaritaṃ mayā..
pāpamevaṃvidhaṃ kaṣṭaṃ naṃdabhadra sadā tyaja.. 46.136 ..
1.4.d:
इति ते कथितं सर्वमात्मनश्चरितं मया..
पापमेवंविधं कष्टं नंदभद्र सदा त्यज.. 46.136 ..
1.4.m: Thus my entire life has been narrated to you. / Always shun such terrible sin, O Nandabhadra!"

1.4.s:
..naṃdabhadra uvāca..
aho mahādbhutaṃ tubhyaṃ caritaṃ yena me hṛdi..
bhūyaḥ śataguṇaṃ jātaṃ dharmāyadṛḍhamānasam.. 46.137 ..
1.4.d:
..नंदभद्र उवाच..
अहो महाद्भुतं तुभ्यं चरितं येन मे हृदि..
भूयः शतगुणं जातं धर्मायदृढमानसम्.. 46.137 ..
1.4.m: Nandabhadra said: / "Ah, wonderful indeed is your life, by which my mind / has again become a hundredfold firm in righteousness!

1.4.s:
kiṃ tu tvayoktadharmasya kartukāmos‌mi niṣkṛtim..
dharmaṃ smara bhavāṃstasmātkiṃcidādiśa niścitam.. 46.138 ..
1.4.d:
किं तु त्वयोक्तधर्मस्य कर्तुकामोस्‌मि निष्कृतिम्..
धर्मं स्मर भवांस्तस्मात्किंचिदादिश निश्चितम्.. 46.138 ..
1.4.m: Yet I desire to perform expiation for the duty spoken of by you. / Remember dharma, and therefore definitely command me something."

1.4.s:
..bāla uvāca..
atra tīrthe ca saptāhaṃ nirāhārastvahaṃ sthitaḥ..
sūryamaṃtrāñjamiṣyāmi tyakṣyāmi ca tatastvasūn.. 46.139 ..
1.4.d:
..बाल उवाच..
अत्र तीर्थे च सप्ताहं निराहारस्त्वहं स्थितः..
सूर्यमंत्राञ्जमिष्यामि त्यक्ष्यामि च ततस्त्वसून्.. 46.139 ..
1.4.m: The boy said: / "Remaining at this sacred ford for seven days without food, / I shall mutter the solar mantras, and then cast off my life-breaths.

1.4.s:
tato barkarikātīrthe dagdhavyohaṃ tvayā taṭe..
asthīni sāgare cāpi mama kṣepyāṇi cātra hi.. 46.140 ..
1.4.d:
ततो बर्करिकातीर्थे दग्धव्योहं त्वया तटे..
अस्थीनि सागरे चापि मम क्षेप्याणि चात्र हि.. 46.140 ..
1.4.m: Then I must be cremated by you on the bank at the Barkarikātīrtha, / and indeed my bones must be cast into the ocean here.

1.4.s:
yadi sāpahnavaṃ cittaṃ mayyatīva tavāsti cet..
tatastvāṃ gurukāryārthamādekṣyāmi śrṛṇuṣva tat.. 46.141 ..
1.4.d:
यदि सापह्नवं चित्तं मय्यतीव तवास्ति चेत्..
ततस्त्वां गुरुकार्यार्थमादेक्ष्यामि श्रृणुष्व तत्.. 46.141 ..
1.4.m: If you have a very candid heart toward me, / then I shall instruct you for the purpose of a great task; listen to it.

1.4.s:
asminbahūdake tīrthe yatra prāṇāṃstyajāmyaham..
tatra mannāmacihnaste saṃsthāpyo bhāskaro vibhuḥ.. 46.142 ..
1.4.d:
अस्मिन्बहूदके तीर्थे यत्र प्राणांस्त्यजाम्यहम्..
तत्र मन्नामचिह्नस्ते संस्थाप्यो भास्करो विभुः.. 46.142 ..
1.4.m: At this Bahūdaka sacred ford, where I abandon my life-breaths, / there the all-pervading Sun-god bearing my name and mark should be installed by you.

1.4.s:
ārogyaṃ dhanadhānyaṃ ca putradārādisaṃpadaḥ..
bhāskaro bhagavāṃstuṣṭo dadyādetacchrutervacaḥ.. 46.143 ..
1.4.d:
आरोग्यं धनधान्यं च पुत्रदारादिसंपदः..
भास्करो भगवांस्तुष्टो दद्यादेतच्छ्रुतेर्वचः.. 46.143 ..
1.4.m: Health, wealth, grain, and fortunes such as sons and wives / the pleased Lord Sun-god will grant: this is the statement of the Veda.

1.4.s:
savitā paramo devaḥ sarvasvaṃ vā dvijanmanām..
vedavedāṃgagītaśca tvamapyenaṃ sadā bhaja.. 46.144 ..
1.4.d:
सविता परमो देवः सर्वस्वं वा द्विजन्मनाम्..
वेदवेदांगगीतश्च त्वमप्येनं सदा भज.. 46.144 ..
1.4.m: Savitṛ is the supreme deity, the all-in-all of the twice-born, / and sung in the Vedas and Vedāṅgas; you too should always worship him.

1.4.s:
bahūdakamidaṃ kuṃḍaṃ saṃsevyaṃ ca sadā tvayā..
māhātmyamasya vakṣyāmi saṃkṣepādvyāsa sūcitam.. 46.145 ..
1.4.d:
बहूदकमिदं कुंडं संसेव्यं च सदा त्वया..
माहात्म्यमस्य वक्ष्यामि संक्षेपाद्व्यास सूचितम्.. 46.145 ..
1.4.m: This Bahūdaka pool should always be resorted to by you. / I shall tell its māhātmya in brief, as indicated by Vyāsa.

1.4.s:
bahūdake kuṃḍavare snāti yo vidhivannaraḥ..
ārogyaṃ dhanadhānyādyaṃ tasya syātsarvajanmasu.. 46.146 ..
1.4.d:
बहूदके कुंडवरे स्नाति यो विधिवन्नरः..
आरोग्यं धनधान्याद्यं तस्य स्यात्सर्वजन्मसु.. 46.146 ..
1.4.m: Whatever man bathes according to the rules in the excellent Bahūdaka pool / will have health, wealth, grain, and the like in all his births.

1.4.s:
bahūdake ca yaḥ snātvā saptamyāṃ māghamāsake..
dadyātpiṃḍaṃ pitṝṇāṃ ca te'kṣyāṃ tṛptimāpnuyuḥ.. 46.147 ..
1.4.d:
बहूदके च यः स्नात्वा सप्तम्यां माघमासके..
दद्यात्पिंडं पितॄणां च तेऽक्ष्यां तृप्तिमाप्नुयुः.. 46.147 ..
1.4.m: And who, having bathed in Bahūdaka on the seventh day of the month of Māgha, / offers a funeral cake to the ancestors, they attain imperishable satisfaction.

1.4.s:
bahūdakasya tīre yaḥ śuciryajati vai kratum..
śatakratuphalaṃ tasya nāsti kācidvicāraṇā.. 46.148 ..
1.4.d:
बहूदकस्य तीरे यः शुचिर्यजति वै क्रतुम्..
शतक्रतुफलं तस्य नास्ति काचिद्विचारणा.. 46.148 ..
1.4.m: Pure, he who performs a sacrifice on the bank of Bahūdaka / attains the fruit of a hundred sacrifices; of this there is no doubt.

1.4.s:
atra yastyajati prāṇānbahūdakataṭe naraḥ..
modate sūryaloke'sau dharmiṇāṃ ca suto bhavet.. 46.149 ..
1.4.d:
अत्र यस्त्यजति प्राणान्बहूदकतटे नरः..
मोदते सूर्यलोकेऽसौ धर्मिणां च सुतो भवेत्.. 46.149 ..
1.4.m: The man who abandons his life-breaths here on the bank of Bahūdaka / rejoices in the world of the Sun and will be born as the son of righteous people.

1.4.s:
bahūdakasya tīre ca yaḥ kuryyājjapasādhanam..
sarvaṃ lakṣaguṇaṃ proktaṃ japo homaśca pūjanam.. 46.150 ..
1.4.d:
बहूदकस्य तीरे च यः कुर्य्याज्जपसाधनम्..
सर्वं लक्षगुणं प्रोक्तं जपो होमश्च पूजनम्.. 46.150 ..
1.4.m: And whoever performs the practice of recitation on the bank of Bahūdaka, / all recitation, oblations, and worship are declared to be multiplied a hundred-thousandfold.

1.4.s:
bahūdakasya tīre ca dvijamekaṃ ca bhojayet..
yo miṣṭānnena tasya syādviprakoṭiśca bhojitā.. 46.151 ..
1.4.d:
बहूदकस्य तीरे च द्विजमेकं च भोजयेत्..
यो मिष्टान्नेन तस्य स्याद्विप्रकोटिश्च भोजिता.. 46.151 ..
1.4.m: And he who feeds even a single twice-born on the bank of Bahūdaka / with sweet food, it is as if ten million brahmins were fed by him.

1.4.s:
bahūdakasya tīre yā nārī gauriṇikāḥ śubhāḥ..
saṃbhojayati tasyāśca kuryātsusvāgataṃ hyumā.. 46.152 ..
1.4.d:
बहूदकस्य तीरे या नारी गौरिणिकाः शुभाः..
संभोजयति तस्याश्च कुर्यात्सुस्वागतं ह्युमा.. 46.152 ..
1.4.m: Whatever woman feeds auspicious young virgin girls on the bank of Bahūdaka, / to her Umā will certainly extend a gracious welcome.

1.4.s:
bahūdakasya tīre ca yaḥ kuryādyogasādhanam..
ṣaṇmāsābhyantare siddhirbhavettasya na saṃśayaḥ.. 46.153 ..
1.4.d:
बहूदकस्य तीरे च यः कुर्याद्योगसाधनम्..
षण्मासाभ्यन्तरे सिद्धिर्भवेत्तस्य न संशयः.. 46.153 ..
1.4.m: And whoever performs the practice of yoga on the bank of Bahūdaka, / within six months perfection will be his, without doubt.

1.4.s:
bahūdakasya tīre ca pretānuddiśya dīyate..
yatkiṃcidakṣayaṃ teṣāmupatiṣṭhenna cānyathā.. 46.154 ..
1.4.d:
बहूदकस्य तीरे च प्रेतानुद्दिश्य दीयते..
यत्किंचिदक्षयं तेषामुपतिष्ठेन्न चान्यथा.. 46.154 ..
1.4.m: And whatever is given on the bank of Bahūdaka dedicated to the departed spirits, / it reaches them imperishably, not otherwise.

1.4.s:
snānaṃ dānaṃ japo homaḥ svādhyāyaḥ pitṛtarpaṇam..
kṛtaṃ bahūdakataṭe sarvaṃ syātsumahātphalam.. 46.155 ..
1.4.d:
स्नानं दानं जपो होमः स्वाध्यायः पितृतर्पणम्..
कृतं बहूदकतटे सर्वं स्यात्सुमहात्फलम्.. 46.155 ..
1.4.m: Bathing, gifting, recitation, oblations, Vedic study, and offering libations to ancestors / performed on the bank of Bahūdaka will all yield exceedingly great fruit.

1.4.s:
tvayaitaddhṛdi saṃdhārya phalaṃ vyāsena sūcitam..
bahūdakasya kuṃḍasya naṃdabhadra mahāmate.. 46.156 ..
1.4.d:
त्वयैतद्धृदि संधार्य फलं व्यासेन सूचितम्..
बहूदकस्य कुंडस्य नंदभद्र महामते.. 46.156 ..
1.4.m: This fruit of the Bahūdaka pool indicated by Vyāsa / must be held firmly in your heart, O high-minded Nandabhadra!"

1.4.s:
ityuktvā so'bhavanmaunī snātvā kuṃḍe tataḥ śuciḥ..
tīre prastaramāśritya svayaṃ maṃtrāñjāpa ha.. 46.157 ..
1.4.d:
इत्युक्त्वा सोऽभवन्मौनी स्नात्वा कुंडे ततः शुचिः..
तीरे प्रस्तरमाश्रित्य स्वयं मंत्राञ्जाप ह.. 46.157 ..
1.4.m: Having spoken thus, he became silent; then, having bathed in the pool, pure, / leaning against a stone on the bank, he himself muttered mantras.

1.4.s:
..śrīnārada uvāca..
tataḥ sa saptarātrāṃte jahau bālo nijānasūn..
saṃskārito yathoktaṃ ca naṃdabhadreṇa brāhmaṇaiḥ.. 46.158 ..
1.4.d:
..श्रीनारद उवाच..
ततः स सप्तरात्रांते जहौ बालो निजानसून्..
संस्कारितो यथोक्तं च नंदभद्रेण ब्राह्मणैः.. 46.158 ..
1.4.m: Śrī Nārada said: / Then, at the end of seven nights, that boy gave up his life-breaths; / and the funeral rites were performed as prescribed by Nandabhadra and by brahmins.

1.4.s:
yatra bālaḥ sa ca prāṇāñjahau japaparāyaṇaḥ..
bālādityamiti khyātaṃ tatrāsthāpayata prabhum.. 46.159 ..
1.4.d:
यत्र बालः स च प्राणाञ्जहौ जपपरायणः..
बालादित्यमिति ख्यातं तत्रास्थापयत प्रभुम्.. 46.159 ..
1.4.m: Where that boy, intent upon recitation, gave up his life-breaths, / there he established the Lord known as Bālāditya.

1.4.s:
bahūdake ca yaḥ snātvā bālādityaṃ prapūjayet..
tasya syādbhāskarastuṣṭo mokṣopāyaṃ ca viṃdati.. 46.160 ..
1.4.d:
बहूदके च यः स्नात्वा बालादित्यं प्रपूजयेत्..
तस्य स्याद्भास्करस्तुष्टो मोक्षोपायं च विंदति.. 46.160 ..
1.4.m: And whoever, having bathed in the Bahūdaka, worships Bālāditya, / the Sun becomes pleased with him, and he finds the means to liberation.

1.4.s:
naṃdabhadro 'pyathānyasyāṃ bhāryāyāmaparānsutān..
utpādyātmasamandhīmāñchivasūryaparāyaṇaḥ.. 46.161 ..
1.4.d:
नंदभद्रो ऽप्यथान्यस्यां भार्यायामपरान्सुतान्..
उत्पाद्यात्मसमन्धीमाञ्छिवसूर्यपरायणः.. 46.161 ..
1.4.m: Nandabhadra too, then, having begotten other sons upon another wife, / intelligent sons equal to himself, devoted to Śiva and the Sun,

1.4.s:
rudradehaṃ yayau pārtha punarāvṛttidurlabham..
evametanmahākuṃḍaṃ bahūdakamiti smṛtam.. 46.162 ..
1.4.d:
रुद्रदेहं ययौ पार्थ पुनरावृत्तिदुर्लभम्..
एवमेतन्महाकुंडं बहूदकमिति स्मृतम्.. 46.162 ..
1.4.m: went to the body of Rudra, O son of Pṛthā, from which return is hard to attain. / Thus is this great pool known as Bahūdaka.

1.4.s:
asya tīre svamaṃśaṃ ca vallīnāthaḥ pramekṣyati..
dattātreyasya yo yogī hyavatāro bhaviṣyati.. 46.163 ..
1.4.d:
अस्य तीरे स्वमंशं च वल्लीनाथः प्रमेक्ष्यति..
दत्तात्रेयस्य यो योगी ह्यवतारो भविष्यति.. 46.163 ..
1.4.m: On its bank, Vallīnātha will cast his own portion, / the yogin who will be an avatāra of Dattātreya.

1.4.s:
arcayitvā ca taṃ devaṃ yogasiddhimavāpnuyāt..
paśūnāmṛddhimāpnoti gośaraṇyo hyasau prabhuḥ.. 46.164 ..
1.4.d:
अर्चयित्वा च तं देवं योगसिद्धिमवाप्नुयात्..
पशूनामृद्धिमाप्नोति गोशरण्यो ह्यसौ प्रभुः.. 46.164 ..
1.4.m: And having worshipped that god, one would obtain perfection in yoga; / he attains an abundance of cattle, for that Lord is a refuge to cows.

1.4.s:
paścimāyāṃ budhasutastathā kṣetraṃ sa bhārata..
purūravādityamiti sthāpayāmāsa pārthivaḥ.. 46.165 ..
1.4.d:

Whoever listens to this with faith, the Sun will be pleased with him; / holding liberation in his heart, he is freed from the ocean of worldly existence.

1.4.m: Nārada said: / Then the brahmins and Nārada, having worshipped Maheśvara, / established Śaṃkara in the holy Mahīnagaraka; (1) / and for the welfare of the worlds, the supreme liṅga Kedāra, / to the north of Atrīśa, destroying grave sins. (2) / A man who bathes in Atrikuṇḍa, performs a śrāddha according to rule, / and bows to Atrīśa, beholding Kedāra, (3) / drinks his mother’s milk never again, and partakes of liberation. / Then Rudra, having personally given Nīlakaṇṭha to the great-souled Nārada, (4) / remained there himself in the auspicious Mahīnagaraka. / A man who bathes in Koṭitīrtha and beholds Nīlakaṇṭha, (5) / bowing to Jayāditya, attains the world of Rudra. / The best of men who worship Jayāditya having bathed in the well (6) / suffer no destruction of their lineage, by the grace of Jayāditya. / This has been told to you, O Pārtha, regarding Mahīnagaraka; (7) / having heard the entire narrative, one is freed from all sins. (8) / Thus ends the fifty-seventh chapter, named 'Description of the Māhātmya of Nīlakaṇṭha', in the Kaumārikākhaṇḍa of the first [section], the Māheśvarakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa of eighty-one thousand verses. Homage to the Infinite One, the thousand-headed, who reclines on the ocean of milk, whose couch is the coils of Śeṣa, who rides upon Garuḍa, clad in yellow garments! Vāsudeva, Saṃkarṣaṇa, Pradyumna, Aniruddha, Horse-headed One, Boar, Man-Lion, Dwarf, Trivikrama, Rāma, Rāma, granter of boons, homage, homage be to you! Strike, strike, burn, burn, cook, cook, churn, churn, destroy, destroy, rout, rout the asuras, daityas, dānavas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, bhūtas, pretas, piśācas, kumbhāṇḍas, siddhayoginīs, ḍākinīs, the planets headed by Skanda, and other asterisms and planets! Reduce them to ashes with your conch, discus, thunderbolt, mace, pestle, and plough! O thousand-armed one, O one whose weapons are your thousand feet, conquer, conquer! Be victorious, be victorious! Unconquered one, unhindered one, thousand-eyed one, flame, flame, blaze forth, blaze forth! All-formed one, many-formed one, slayer of Madhu, Great Boar, Great Person, Vaikuṇṭha, Nārāyaṇa, Lotus-naveled One, Govinda, Dāmodara, Hṛṣīkeśa, extirpator of all asuras, subduer of all beings, breaker of all sorrows, destroyer of all mechanical devices, crusher of all serpents, Great Lord of all gods, deliverer from all bonds, crusher of all harm, destroyer of all fevers, averter of all planetary afflictions, pacifier of all sins, Janārdana, bringer of joy to people, homage be to you, svāhā! // 53

1.4.m: "Hail, hail to you, O king of the yakṣas named Sūryavarcas, with an entourage of eighty-four crores! Hail to you who engaged in the removal of the earth's burden, who took birth in the womb of a Nairṛta on account of a light curse! Hail to the royal swan in the womb of Kāmakaṭaṅkaṭā! Hail to the increaser of Ghaṭotkaca's joy, named Barbarīka! Hail to you who attained peerless valor through the propitiation of the goddess of the holy Guptakṣetra instructed by Kṛṣṇa! Hail to the granter of victory and accomplishment! Hail to the forest fire consuming the demons Piṅgalā, Repala, Indra, Duha, Druha, and Navakoṭīśvara! Hail to the rescuer of the nāga maidens between the earth and Pātāla! Hail to the crusher of Bhīma's pride! Hail to you who were prepared to slay the entire Kaurava army in an instant!
