1.4.s: 1 sūtaśaunakasaṃvāde dakṣiṇārṇavatīrasthatīrthamāhātmyavarṇanopakrame pañcāpsarastīrtha māhātmya vṛttāntavarṇane'rjunatīrthayātrāvṛttāntaḥ, tatrārjunasya dakṣiṇasamudratīrasthatīrthasnānārthaṃ pravṛttasya pañcasu tīrtheṣu tatratyaistapasvibhiḥ snānārthaṃ tatratyagrāhabhītyā nivāraṇama, arjunasya dharmabuddhiṃ dṛṣṭvā tāpasairarjunāya dīrghāyuṣṭvavarapradānam, tato'rjune saubhadratīrthamabhyetya snānārthamavatīrya snānaṃ kartuṃ pravṛtte grāheṇa grahaṇam, arjunena balena grāhoddharaṇe grāhasya nārīrūpatā,tayā nāryā svasyāścatasṛbhiḥ sakhībhiḥ saha ratyarthaṃ prārthitasya brāhmaṇasya śāpena grāhatvaprāptivṛttāntavarṇanam, nāradoktyā ca pañcasu tīrtheṣu grāhatvenāvasthitivarṇanam, tato'rjunenānyepu caturṣu tīrtheṣu praviśya snātvā tatratyagrāhoddharaṇapūrvaka sarvāsāmapsarasāṃ samuddhāravarṇanam, arjunasya tīrthasaṃrodhakāraṇajijñāsayā śaṃkāprāptāvapsarobhirnāradaṃ pratyetadviṣaye praṣṭavyamityuktvā svargaṃ prati gamanam.... 75 2
1.4.d: 1 सूतशौनकसंवादे दक्षिणार्णवतीरस्थतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनोपक्रमे पञ्चाप्सरस्तीर्थ माहात्म्य वृत्तान्तवर्णनेऽर्जुनतीर्थयात्रावृत्तान्तः, तत्रार्जुनस्य दक्षिणसमुद्रतीरस्थतीर्थस्नानार्थं प्रवृत्तस्य पञ्चसु तीर्थेषु तत्रत्यैस्तपस्विभिः स्नानार्थं तत्रत्यग्राहभीत्या निवारणम, अर्जुनस्य धर्मबुद्धिं दृष्ट्वा तापसैरर्जुनाय दीर्घायुष्ट्ववरप्रदानम्, ततोऽर्जुने सौभद्रतीर्थमभ्येत्य स्नानार्थमवतीर्य स्नानं कर्तुं प्रवृत्ते ग्राहेण ग्रहणम्, अर्जुनेन बलेन ग्राहोद्धरणे ग्राहस्य नारीरूपता,तया नार्या स्वस्याश्चतसृभिः सखीभिः सह रत्यर्थं प्रार्थितस्य ब्राह्मणस्य शापेन ग्राहत्वप्राप्तिवृत्तान्तवर्णनम्, नारदोक्त्या च पञ्चसु तीर्थेषु ग्राहत्वेनावस्थितिवर्णनम्, ततोऽर्जुनेनान्येपु चतुर्षु तीर्थेषु प्रविश्य स्नात्वा तत्रत्यग्राहोद्धरणपूर्वक सर्वासामप्सरसां समुद्धारवर्णनम्, अर्जुनस्य तीर्थसंरोधकारणजिज्ञासया शंकाप्राप्तावप्सरोभिर्नारदं प्रत्येतद्विषये प्रष्टव्यमित्युक्त्वा स्वर्गं प्रति गमनम्.... 75 2
1.4.m: 1. In the dialogue between Sūta and Śaunaka, at the commencement of the description of the māhātmya of the tīrthas situated on the shore of the southern ocean, in the narration of the account of the māhātmya of the Pañcāpsarastīrtha, the account of Arjuna's pilgrimage to tīrthas: there, of Arjuna setting out to bathe in the tīrthas on the southern ocean shore, his being restrained from bathing in the five tīrthas by the ascetics living there out of fear of the crocodiles residing there; the ascetics, seeing Arjuna's righteous mind, granting Arjuna the boon of long life; then Arjuna, approaching the Saubhadratīrtha and stepping down to bathe, being seized by a crocodile as he proceeded to bathe; upon Arjuna pulling the crocodile out by force, the crocodile turning into the form of a woman; that woman describing the account of her attaining the state of a crocodile through the curse of a brahmin who had been solicited for sexual union by her together with her four female friends, and her residing as a crocodile in the five tīrthas according to Nārada's word; then Arjuna, entering the other four tīrthas and bathing, pulling out the crocodiles residing there and rescuing all the apsarases; when Arjuna felt doubt through a desire to know the cause of the obstruction of the tīrthas, the apsarases saying, 'You should ask Nārada regarding this matter,' and departing to heaven.... 75 2

1.4.s: 2 arjunasya nāradena saha samāgamaḥ, nāradamukhātpāṇḍavakuśalavṛttāntaśravaṇottaramarjunena tīrthamāhātmyajijñāsayā nāradaṃ prati praśnakaraṇam, atha nāradena brahmalokavṛttāntavarṇanaprastāvapūrvakaṃ suśravaḥprokta kātyāyanasārasvatasaṃvādavarṇanam tatra sārasvatamaharṣiṇā- kātyāyanamaharṣaye dharmatattvakathanam, tataśca dānamāhātmyavarṇanam, dānamāhātmyaśravaṇottaraṃ dānārthamutsukamānasasya svasyārthānnāradasya dānadānārthaṃ dravyopārjanāya nānādeśaparyaṭanavṛttāntaḥ - - .. .... 77 1
1.4.d: 2 अर्जुनस्य नारदेन सह समागमः, नारदमुखात्पाण्डवकुशलवृत्तान्तश्रवणोत्तरमर्जुनेन तीर्थमाहात्म्यजिज्ञासया नारदं प्रति प्रश्नकरणम्, अथ नारदेन ब्रह्मलोकवृत्तान्तवर्णनप्रस्तावपूर्वकं सुश्रवःप्रोक्त कात्यायनसारस्वतसंवादवर्णनम् तत्र सारस्वतमहर्षिणा- कात्यायनमहर्षये धर्मतत्त्वकथनम्, ततश्च दानमाहात्म्यवर्णनम्, दानमाहात्म्यश्रवणोत्तरं दानार्थमुत्सुकमानसस्य स्वस्यार्थान्नारदस्य दानदानार्थं द्रव्योपार्जनाय नानादेशपर्यटनवृत्तान्तः - - .. .... 77 1
1.4.m: 2. Arjuna's meeting with Nārada; after hearing the news of the welfare of the Pāṇḍavas from the mouth of Nārada, Arjuna asking a question to Nārada out of a desire to know the māhātmya of the tīrthas; then Nārada, with an introduction narrating the news of the world of Brahmā, recounting the dialogue between Kātyāyana and Sārasvata related by Suśravas; there, the great seer Sārasvata expounding the truth of dharma to the great seer Kātyāyana; and then the description of the māhātmya of gifts; after hearing the māhātmya of gifts, the account of his own—that is, Nārada's—wandering through various regions to acquire wealth for the sake of giving gifts, his mind being eager for giving gifts.... 77 1

1.4.s: 3 pṛthivīṃ paryaṭato nāradasya narmadātīre bhṛgorāśramaṃ pratyāgamanama, bhṛgave nāradena svoddeśakathanottaraṃ bhṛguṇā nāradāya dānārhapavitrasthānakathanoddeśena mahīsāgarasaṃgamasthastambhatīrthamāhātmyavarṇanam, tatra tīrthatīrasthita prāṃśudevaśarmabrāhmaṇasya vṛttāntaḥ, mahīsāgarasaṃgame svapitṛbhyo darśaśrāddhadānārthaṃ tattīrthatīrasthitasubhadrabrāhmaṇāya nijapuṇyacaturthāṃśapradānam bhṛguproktamahīsāgarasaṃgamasthastaṃbhatīrthamāhātmyaṃ śrutvā nāradasya mahīsāgarasaṃgame sthānakaraṇārthaṃ cintākaraṇam. - 79 2
1.4.d: 3 पृथिवीं पर्यटतो नारदस्य नर्मदातीरे भृगोराश्रमं प्रत्यागमनम, भृगवे नारदेन स्वोद्देशकथनोत्तरं भृगुणा नारदाय दानार्हपवित्रस्थानकथनोद्देशेन महीसागरसंगमस्थस्तम्भतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनम्, तत्र तीर्थतीरस्थित प्रांशुदेवशर्मब्राह्मणस्य वृत्तान्तः, महीसागरसंगमे स्वपितृभ्यो दर्शश्राद्धदानार्थं तत्तीर्थतीरस्थितसुभद्रब्राह्मणाय निजपुण्यचतुर्थांशप्रदानम् भृगुप्रोक्तमहीसागरसंगमस्थस्तंभतीर्थमाहात्म्यं श्रुत्वा नारदस्य महीसागरसंगमे स्थानकरणार्थं चिन्ताकरणम्. - 79 2
1.4.m: 3. Nārada, wandering the earth, coming to the hermitage of Bhṛgu on the bank of the Narmadā; after Nārada stated his purpose to Bhṛgu, Bhṛgu describing the māhātmya of the Stambhatīrtha situated at the confluence of the Mahī and the ocean with the purpose of declaring a holy place worthy for giving gifts; there, the account of the brahmin Prāṃśudevaśarman residing on the bank of the tīrtha; the bestowing of one-fourth of his own merit to the brahmin Subhadra residing on the bank of that tīrtha for the sake of offering the darśa-śrāddha to his ancestors at the confluence of the Mahī and the ocean; having heard the māhātmya of the Stambhatīrtha situated at the confluence of the Mahī and the ocean spoken by Bhṛgu, Nārada contemplating establishing a place at the confluence of the Mahī and the ocean. 79 2

1.4.s: 4 nāradena mahīsāgarasaṃgame sthānasthāpanārthaṃ dravyasyāpekṣitatvācchuddhanyāyena dravyārjanaviṣayaka cintāprāptau munīnāṃ mukhato dharmavarmanṛpatiṃ prati gatvā dharmavarmanṛpatiśrutākāśāvāṇīkathita dvihetu ṣaḍadhiṣṭhānam' ityādyekaślokārthavyākhyākaraṇena nṛpaṃ santoṣya tasya svoddiṣṭadānadharmakāryasādhanāya sāhāyyasaṃpādanam. 81
1.4.d: 4 नारदेन महीसागरसंगमे स्थानस्थापनार्थं द्रव्यस्यापेक्षितत्वाच्छुद्धन्यायेन द्रव्यार्जनविषयक चिन्ताप्राप्तौ मुनीनां मुखतो धर्मवर्मनृपतिं प्रति गत्वा धर्मवर्मनृपतिश्रुताकाशावाणीकथित द्विहेतु षडधिष्ठानम्' इत्याद्येकश्लोकार्थव्याख्याकरणेन नृपं सन्तोष्य तस्य स्वोद्दिष्टदानधर्मकार्यसाधनाय साहाय्यसंपादनम्. 81
1.4.m: 4. Nārada, requiring wealth to establish a settlement at the confluence of the Mahī and the ocean, feeling concern regarding the acquisition of wealth through pure and righteous means; from the mouth of the sages, going to King Dharmavarman and gladdening the king by explaining the meaning of a single verse heard by King Dharmavarman from a heavenly voice beginning with 'Having two causes, six foundations...', and obtaining his assistance to accomplish his intended pious duty of giving gifts. 81

1.4.m: 5. Then Nārada, searching everywhere to find a worthy brahmin recipient for the gifts, subsequently going to the village of Kalāpa in the disguise of a brahmin; going there and asking questions in verse form to test the brahmins; an eight-year-old boy among those brahmins alone giving the correct answers to the extremely profound questions posed by Nārada. 84 1

1.4.s: 6 tato nāradena svarūpeṇa prakaṭībhūya mahīsāgarasaṃgamamahātīrthe brāhmaṇānāmājīvikāpradānapūrvakaṃ saṃsthāpanāya saṃprārthya daṇḍāgra āropyānayanavarṇanam, tatprasaṃgena kalāpagrāmamārgavarṇanam, nāradena viprapādaprakṣālanasamaye samāgatasyātitheḥ kapilamaharṣeḥ prārthanayā tasmā ānītabrāhmaṇamadhyato'ṣṭasahasrabrāhmaṇasamarpaṇam, madhuparkārhaṇasamaye hārītabrāhmaṇena prathamataḥ prakṣālanārthaṃ vāmapāde purataḥ kṛte sati nāradena sarveṣāṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ 'yūyaṃ mūrkhā bhaviṣyatha' iti śāpapradānam, tairbrāhmaṇairapi nāradāya tathāvidhasyaiva śāpasya pradānam, purato vāmapādasya karaṇe kāraṇavarṇanam, tato nāradasya paścāttāpena cirakāribrāhmaṇavṛttāntasmaraṇam, tatra medhātithigautamasutasya cirakāriṇaḥ pitrājñayā vyabhicāriṇyā māturhananāya gamane vicāravaśena vilaṃbakaraṇam, etasminnantare brāhmaṇarūpeṇāgatasya śakrasyopadeśena gautamasya paścāttāpaḥ, vadhārthaṃ mātṛsamīpaṃ gacchataścirakāriṇaḥ pṛṣṭhato gautamasya gamanam, pitaraṃ dṛṣṭvā cirakāriṇā śastraṃ bhūmau nikṣipya pituḥ prārthanākaraṇam gautamena pitrā cirakāriṇaścirakāritvapraśaṃsāpūrvakamāśīḥpradānaṃ gṛhaṃ prati bhāryāyāḥ putrasya cānayanam, nāradena brāhmaṇānāṃ pradattasya śāpasya kalāvudayo bhaviṣyatīti śāpakālaparivartanam, tataḥ sarveṣāṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ mahīsāgarasaṃgame kāṃcanagogṛhadhanādipradānapṛrvka svayaṃ viśvakarmadvārā nirmāpite mahīnagare sthāpanavarṇanam.... ... 87 1
1.4.d: 6 ततो नारदेन स्वरूपेण प्रकटीभूय महीसागरसंगममहातीर्थे ब्राह्मणानामाजीविकाप्रदानपूर्वकं संस्थापनाय संप्रार्थ्य दण्डाग्र आरोप्यानयनवर्णनम्, तत्प्रसंगेन कलापग्राममार्गवर्णनम्, नारदेन विप्रपादप्रक्षालनसमये समागतस्यातिथेः कपिलमहर्षेः प्रार्थनया तस्मा आनीतब्राह्मणमध्यतोऽष्टसहस्रब्राह्मणसमर्पणम्, मधुपर्कार्हणसमये हारीतब्राह्मणेन प्रथमतः प्रक्षालनार्थं वामपादे पुरतः कृते सति नारदेन सर्वेषां ब्राह्मणानां ऽयूयं मूर्खा भविष्यथ' इति शापप्रदानम्, तैर्ब्राह्मणैरपि नारदाय तथाविधस्यैव शापस्य प्रदानम्, पुरतो वामपादस्य करणे कारणवर्णनम्, ततो नारदस्य पश्चात्तापेन चिरकारिब्राह्मणवृत्तान्तस्मरणम्, तत्र मेधातिथिगौतमसुतस्य चिरकारिणः पित्राज्ञया व्यभिचारिण्या मातुर्हननाय गमने विचारवशेन विलंबकरणम्, एतस्मिन्नन्तरे ब्राह्मणरूपेणागतस्य शक्रस्योपदेशेन गौतमस्य पश्चात्तापः, वधार्थं मातृसमीपं गच्छतश्चिरकारिणः पृष्ठतो गौतमस्य गमनम्, पितरं दृष्ट्वा चिरकारिणा शस्त्रं भूमौ निक्षिप्य पितुः प्रार्थनाकरणम् गौतमेन पित्रा चिरकारिणश्चिरकारित्वप्रशंसापूर्वकमाशीःप्रदानं गृहं प्रति भार्यायाः पुत्रस्य चानयनम्, नारदेन ब्राह्मणानां प्रदत्तस्य शापस्य कलावुदयो भविष्यतीति शापकालपरिवर्तनम्, ततः सर्वेषां ब्राह्मणानां महीसागरसंगमे कांचनगोगृहधनादिप्रदानपृर्व्क स्वयं विश्वकर्मद्वारा निर्मापिते महीनगरे स्थापनवर्णनम्.... ... 87 1
1.4.m: 6. Then, Nārada, manifesting in his own form, requested the brahmins to settle at the great sacred ford where the Mahī meets the ocean, providing for their livelihood, and brought them mounted on the tip of his staff, with a description of the route from Kalāpagrāma in that context; at the time of washing the brahmins' feet, upon the request of the great sage Kapila who had arrived as a guest, the handing over to him of eight thousand brahmins from among those brought; at the time of offering the honey-mixture (madhuparka), because the brahmin Hārīta first put forward his left foot for washing, Nārada’s pronouncement of a curse upon all the brahmins: "You will become fools!"; the casting of a similar curse upon Nārada by those brahmins as well; the explanation of the reason for putting forward the left foot; then Nārada, out of remorse, remembering the story of the brahmin Cirakārin; therein, Cirakārin, the son of Medhātithi Gautama, going at his father's command to kill his unfaithful mother, delayed through reflection; meanwhile, Gautama's remorse through the counsel of Indra who had come in the form of a brahmin; Gautama following Cirakārin who had gone near his mother to kill her; upon seeing his father, Cirakārin casting his weapon onto the ground and offering a prayer to his father; the father Gautama, while praising the deliberateness of Cirakārin, conferring a blessing and bringing his wife and son back home; Nārada's alteration of the time of the curse so that the curse given to the brahmins would take effect in the Kali age; then the description of the settlement of all the brahmins in Mahīnagara, built by Viśvakarman himself, through gifts of gold, cows, houses, wealth, and the like at the confluence of the Mahī and the ocean. 87 1

1.4.s: 7 arjunena vistārapūrvakaṃ mahīsāgarasaṃgamamāhātmyaśravaṇecchayā nāradaprārthanam, nāradena savistaramahīsāgaramāhātmyavarṇanārthamupakramaṇam, tatrendradyumnabhūpativṛttāntārambhaḥ, brahmalokaṃ gatasyendrayumnasya bahukālaṃ tatra nivāsānantaraṃ brahmaṇā cirakālādbhūmau kīrteḥ punarvyaktīkaraṇarthamindradyumnasya bhūlokaṃprati preṣaṇam, bhūlokaṃ pratyāgatenendradyumnena bhūlokasthitebhyo'pekṣayā dīrghajīvino mārkaṇḍeyasya samīpaṃ gatvā nijavārtāvijñānaviṣaye praśnakaraṇam, tena tadvārtā'nabhijñānakathana indradyumnasyāgnipraveśodyogaḥ, tato mārkaṇḍeyena tato'pi dīrghāyuṣo nāḍījaṃghabakasya samīpe tannayanam, tenāpīndradyumnavārtā'nabhijñānakathanam, tataścendragrumnapṛṣṭena nāḍījaṃghabakena nijadīrghāyuṣṭvakāraṇavarṇanāya nijapūrvodantakathanam. ....... ...... . 90
1.4.d: 7 अर्जुनेन विस्तारपूर्वकं महीसागरसंगममाहात्म्यश्रवणेच्छया नारदप्रार्थनम्, नारदेन सविस्तरमहीसागरमाहात्म्यवर्णनार्थमुपक्रमणम्, तत्रेन्द्रद्युम्नभूपतिवृत्तान्तारम्भः, ब्रह्मलोकं गतस्येन्द्रयुम्नस्य बहुकालं तत्र निवासानन्तरं ब्रह्मणा चिरकालाद्भूमौ कीर्तेः पुनर्व्यक्तीकरणर्थमिन्द्रद्युम्नस्य भूलोकंप्रति प्रेषणम्, भूलोकं प्रत्यागतेनेन्द्रद्युम्नेन भूलोकस्थितेभ्योऽपेक्षया दीर्घजीविनो मार्कण्डेयस्य समीपं गत्वा निजवार्ताविज्ञानविषये प्रश्नकरणम्, तेन तद्वार्ताऽनभिज्ञानकथन इन्द्रद्युम्नस्याग्निप्रवेशोद्योगः, ततो मार्कण्डेयेन ततोऽपि दीर्घायुषो नाडीजंघबकस्य समीपे तन्नयनम्, तेनापीन्द्रद्युम्नवार्ताऽनभिज्ञानकथनम्, ततश्चेन्द्रग्रुम्नपृष्टेन नाडीजंघबकेन निजदीर्घायुष्ट्वकारणवर्णनाय निजपूर्वोदन्तकथनम्. ....... ...... . 90
1.4.m: 7. Arjuna's request to Nārada out of a desire to hear at length the māhātmya of the confluence of the Mahī and the ocean; Nārada's undertaking to describe at length the māhātmya of the Mahī-ocean confluence; therein, the commencement of the account of King Indradyumna; of Indradyumna who had gone to the world of Brahmā, after residing there for a long time, his being sent back to the mortal world by Brahmā in order to make his fame manifest once again on earth after a long lapse of time; Indradyumna, having returned to the mortal world, approaching Mārkaṇḍeya—who was longer-lived than any inhabitant of the earth—and questioning him regarding knowledge of his own history; upon his stating that he was unaware of his history, Indradyumna's attempt to enter the fire; then Mārkaṇḍeya leading him into the presence of the crane Nāḍījaṅgha, who was even longer-lived than himself; his also stating his unawareness of Indradyumna's history; and then, questioned by Indradyumna, the crane Nāḍījaṅgha recounting his own past history to explain the cause of his long life. 90

1.4.m: 8. Then, in order to find knowledge of the history of the despondent Indradyumna, Nāḍījaṅgha leading Mārkaṇḍeya and Indradyumna into the presence of an owl named Prākārakarṇa, who was longer-lived than himself; after that owl Prākārakarṇa also stated his unawareness of Indradyumna's history, his explaining the cause of his own long life upon Indradyumna's question; in that connection, the description of the māhātmya of the bilva leaf. 92 2

1.4.m: 9. When Indradyumna became indifferent because the owl Prākārakarṇa did not know his history, and Nāḍījaṅgha pointed out the necessity of finding knowledge of Indradyumna's history, the owl Prākārakarṇa leading Indradyumna, Mārkaṇḍeya, and the crane Nāḍījaṅgha to a vulture residing on Mount Gandhamādana, who was longer-lived than himself; that vulture also stating his unawareness of Indradyumna's history, and recounting the narrative explaining the cause of his own long life. 93

1.4.s: 10 gandhamādanasthagṛdhreṇa nijavārtānabhijñānādudāsīnasyendradyumnasyāgnipraveśodyogaṃ dṛṣṭvā prākārakarṇaprārthanayā gṛdhreṇātmano'pi dīrghāyuṣo mānasasaronivāsinaḥ kūrmasya samīpaṃ pratīndradyumnamārkaṇḍeyanāḍījaṅghaprākārakarṇānāṃ nayanama, tatra sarastīre samāgatāna teṣāṃ madhya indradyumnaṃ nṛpaṃ dṛṣṭvā kūrmasya tānasatkṛtyaiva jalamadhye praveśaḥ, tato gṛdhreṇa tasmai jalapraveśakāraṇapṛcchāyāṃ tena kūrmeṇendradyumnasya purākṛtayajñavṛttāntavarṇanasamaya indradyumnasya kīrtyuddhāre satīndradyumnopari devaiḥ puṣpavṛṣṭikaraṇapūrvakaṃ vimānamānīya devadūtenendradyumnāya brahmalokaṃ prati gamanāyendradyumnaprārthanākaraṇam, indradyumnena brahmalokaṃ prati gantumanicchāṃ pradarśya kūrmaṃ prati tasyaiva dīrghāyuṣṭvakāraṇajijñāsayā praśnakaraṇam. 95
1.4.d: 10 गन्धमादनस्थगृध्रेण निजवार्तानभिज्ञानादुदासीनस्येन्द्रद्युम्नस्याग्निप्रवेशोद्योगं दृष्ट्वा प्राकारकर्णप्रार्थनया गृध्रेणात्मनोऽपि दीर्घायुषो मानससरोनिवासिनः कूर्मस्य समीपं प्रतीन्द्रद्युम्नमार्कण्डेयनाडीजङ्घप्राकारकर्णानां नयनम, तत्र सरस्तीरे समागतान तेषां मध्य इन्द्रद्युम्नं नृपं दृष्ट्वा कूर्मस्य तानसत्कृत्यैव जलमध्ये प्रवेशः, ततो गृध्रेण तस्मै जलप्रवेशकारणपृच्छायां तेन कूर्मेणेन्द्रद्युम्नस्य पुराकृतयज्ञवृत्तान्तवर्णनसमय इन्द्रद्युम्नस्य कीर्त्युद्धारे सतीन्द्रद्युम्नोपरि देवैः पुष्पवृष्टिकरणपूर्वकं विमानमानीय देवदूतेनेन्द्रद्युम्नाय ब्रह्मलोकं प्रति गमनायेन्द्रद्युम्नप्रार्थनाकरणम्, इन्द्रद्युम्नेन ब्रह्मलोकं प्रति गन्तुमनिच्छां प्रदर्श्य कूर्मं प्रति तस्यैव दीर्घायुष्ट्वकारणजिज्ञासया प्रश्नकरणम्. 95
1.4.m: 10. Seeing Indradyumna’s resolve to enter the fire out of indifference due to the Gandhamādana vulture's unawareness of his history, upon the request of Prākārakarṇa, the vulture leading Indradyumna, Mārkaṇḍeya, Nāḍījaṅgha, and Prākārakarṇa into the presence of a tortoise residing in Lake Mānasa, who was longer-lived than himself; when they arrived at the shore of the lake, the tortoise, seeing King Indradyumna among them, plunging into the water without offering them hospitality; then, upon the vulture asking him the reason for entering the water, as that tortoise recounted the narrative of a sacrifice performed by Indradyumna in the past, Indradyumna's fame was restored; whereupon the gods showered flowers upon Indradyumna, brought an aerial chariot, and a divine messenger urged Indradyumna to go to the world of Brahmā; Indradyumna, expressing his unwillingness to go to the world of Brahmā, questioned the tortoise out of a desire to know the cause of his long life. 95

After the meeting of Indradyumna and the others with the great sage Lomaśa, when asked why the exceedingly long-lived sage Lomaśa had built no hermitage, Lomaśa, describing the nature of worldly existence, explained the cause of his own long life—in that context, the description of the māhātmya of worshipping the Śiva-liṅga. 97

1.4.m: 13. After hearing the words of Lomaśa, all [of them] headed by Indradyumna pray to Lomaśa to receive initiation into Śiva's cult out of exclusive devotion to Śiva; great sage Lomaśa confers initiation into Śiva's cult on all of them and instructs them in the worship of the Śivaliṅga; thereupon Mārkaṇḍeya and the others perform austerity following the commencement of the yoga of action; Nārada arrives before those performing austerities; Nāḍījaṅgha and the others who had fallen due to a curse question Nārada desiring to know the means for their own liberation; Nārada instructs them that they should go to see the great sage Saṃvarta residing in Vārāṇasī; he explains the means to test Saṃvarta in Vārāṇasī; Nāḍījaṅgha and the others go to Vārāṇasī, recognize Saṃvarta by the method told by Nārada, and meet with him; Saṃvarta gives permission to Nāḍījaṅgha and the others to go to the confluence of the Mahī and the ocean in order to be freed from the curse; in that context, the narration of the story of the origin of the river Mahī; description of the incident of the disrespect shown by the mongoose, which was the reason for Yājñavalkya's stay at the confluence of the Mahī and the ocean; extensive description of the māhātmya of the sacred ford of the confluence of the Mahī and the ocean; after hearing the māhātmya of the confluence of the Mahī and the ocean from Saṃvarta, the five—the crane, the owl, the vulture, the tortoise, and Indradyumna—reach the confluence of the Mahī and the ocean, and their liberation consisting in attaining Śiva's own form by establishing a Śivaliṅga is described; the living liberation of Lomaśa and Mārkaṇḍeya is described; and therein the description of the māhātmya of the Indradyumneśvara liṅga established by Indradyumna; and the description of the māhātmya of the Śatarudrīya and other liṅgas at the confluence of the Mahī and the ocean. . .... 98 2

1.4.s: 14 atha kumāranāthamāhātmyavarṇanam-tatprasaṃgena kumāracaritavarṇanopakramaḥ, tatra dakṣakanyāyāṃ dityākhyāyāṃ vajrāṃganāmakasutotpattiḥ, vajrāṃgeṇa māturājñayā svargaṃ gatvā deveṃdraṃ pādenākṛṣya bhānuḥ samīpa ānayanam, tato brahmakaśyapayoḥ prārthanayā vajrāṃgeṇa vāsavasya mocanam, tato brahmājñayā vajrāṃgasya tapasi pravṛttiḥ, vajrāṃge tapasi pravṛtte tatparicaryaikaniṣṭhāyā varāṃgīnāmnyā vajrāṃgapatnyāḥ śakreṇa vividhavibhīṣikādarśana- . pūrvakamativiḍambanam-tato brahmaṇaḥ sakāśādvaraṃ prāpya tapasaḥ saṃnivṛttena vajrāṃgeṇa svapatnyā varāṃgyākhyāyā vitrāsakāraṇajijñāsayā praśnakaraṇam. .. 103 1
1.4.d: 14 अथ कुमारनाथमाहात्म्यवर्णनम्-तत्प्रसंगेन कुमारचरितवर्णनोपक्रमः, तत्र दक्षकन्यायां दित्याख्यायां वज्रांगनामकसुतोत्पत्तिः, वज्रांगेण मातुराज्ञया स्वर्गं गत्वा देवेंद्रं पादेनाकृष्य भानुः समीप आनयनम्, ततो ब्रह्मकश्यपयोः प्रार्थनया वज्रांगेण वासवस्य मोचनम्, ततो ब्रह्माज्ञया वज्रांगस्य तपसि प्रवृत्तिः, वज्रांगे तपसि प्रवृत्ते तत्परिचर्यैकनिष्ठाया वरांगीनाम्न्या वज्रांगपत्न्याः शक्रेण विविधविभीषिकादर्शन- . पूर्वकमतिविडम्बनम्-ततो ब्रह्मणः सकाशाद्वरं प्राप्य तपसः संनिवृत्तेन वज्रांगेण स्वपत्न्या वरांग्याख्याया वित्रासकारणजिज्ञासया प्रश्नकरणम्. .. 103 1
1.4.m: 14. Now the description of the māhātmya of Kumāranātha; in that context, the commencement of the account of Kumāra's deeds; therein, the birth of a son named Vajrāṅga to Dakṣa's daughter named Diti; Vajrāṅga, by the command of his mother, goes to heaven, drags the lord of the gods by his foot, and brings him near the sun; then, at the request of Brahmā and Kaśyapa, Vajrāṅga releases Vāsava; then, by the command of Brahmā, Vajrāṅga undertakes austerity; while Vajrāṅga is engaged in austerity, his wife named Varāṅgī, intent solely on his service, is severely mocked by Śakra through the display of various terrors; then Vajrāṅga, having obtained a boon from Brahmā and returned from his austerity, asks a question desiring to know the cause of the terror of his wife named Varāṅgī. .. 103 1

1.4.s: 15 varāṃgyāḥ śakrakṛtāṃ viḍambanāṃ nirīkṣya tapaḥprabhāveṇā''surabhāvanivṛttasyāpi vajrāṃgasya priyāyāḥ priyakaraṇārthaṃ mahendrapratīkārārtha ca bhūyo'pi tapaścaryākaraṇam, tatastattapastuṣṭena brahmaṇā vajrāṃgasya devadarpadalanaputraprāptirūpavaraṃ pradāya tapaso nivartanam, tato vajrāṃgādvarāṃgyāṃ tārakāsurasyotpattiḥ, sarvadaityaistārakāsurasya daityarājyābhiṣekaḥ, tatastārakāsurasya devanirjigīṣayā pāriyātraparvatakandarāṃ gatvā tapaḥkaraṇam, tattapastuṣṭena brahmaṇā saptavāsaraṃ bālakaṃ vinā'nyaiḥ sarvairavadhyatvarupavarapradānam, brahmavarorjitasya tārakāsurasya nijarājye'vasthānam......... ... 105 1
1.4.d: 15 वरांग्याः शक्रकृतां विडम्बनां निरीक्ष्य तपःप्रभावेणा'ऽसुरभावनिवृत्तस्यापि वज्रांगस्य प्रियायाः प्रियकरणार्थं महेन्द्रप्रतीकारार्थ च भूयोऽपि तपश्चर्याकरणम्, ततस्तत्तपस्तुष्टेन ब्रह्मणा वज्रांगस्य देवदर्पदलनपुत्रप्राप्तिरूपवरं प्रदाय तपसो निवर्तनम्, ततो वज्रांगाद्वरांग्यां तारकासुरस्योत्पत्तिः, सर्वदैत्यैस्तारकासुरस्य दैत्यराज्याभिषेकः, ततस्तारकासुरस्य देवनिर्जिगीषया पारियात्रपर्वतकन्दरां गत्वा तपःकरणम्, तत्तपस्तुष्टेन ब्रह्मणा सप्तवासरं बालकं विनाऽन्यैः सर्वैरवध्यत्वरुपवरप्रदानम्, ब्रह्मवरोर्जितस्य तारकासुरस्य निजराज्येऽवस्थानम्......... ... 105 1
1.4.m: 15. Seeing the mockery of Varāṅgī done by Śakra, Vajrāṅga, though his demonic nature had ceased through the power of austerity, undertakes austerity once again in order to please his beloved and to retaliate against Mahendra; then Brahmā, pleased by that austerity, dissuades Vajrāṅga from austerity by granting the boon of obtaining a son who would crush the pride of the gods; then from Vajrāṅga is born Tārakāsura upon Varāṅgī; all the Daityas coronate Tārakāsura over the Daitya kingdom; then Tārakāsura, desiring to conquer the gods, goes to a cave of Mount Pāriyātra and performs austerity; Brahmā, pleased by that austerity, grants the boon that he cannot be killed by any others except an infant of seven days; fortified by Brahmā's boon, Tārakāsura stays in his own kingdom......... ... 105 1

1.4.m: 16. Tārakāsura deliberates with his ministers and, marshalling his army, marches towards heaven to conquer all the gods; then the lord of the gods, with the consent of Bṛhaspati, marshals the entire army of the gods; commencement of the battle between Tārakāsura and the lord of the gods.

1.4.m: 18. In the battle between the Lord of Wealth and Jambha, when Jambha is killed by the Lord of Wealth, the Lord of Wealth fights with Kujambha and the Lord of Wealth is defeated; then in the battle between Kujambha and Nirṛti, upon Nirṛti's defeat, Varuṇa binds Kujambha's two arms with his noose; then, when Mahiṣāsura prepares to swallow Nirṛti and Varuṇa, the Moon, by spreading cool rays, causes great distress to all the Daityas through extreme cold; then, seeing the removal of cold effected by Kālanemi spreading fiery flames, the Sun discharges an arrow infused with the Śambara weapon and, through illusory power, inverts the appearances of the gods and the Dānavas; and bewildered by this, Kālanemi slays countless Daityas themselves, mistaking them for gods. .. 109

1.4.m: 19. Then Kālanemi's son named Nimi awakens Kālanemi from the illusion created by the Sun; then the awakened Kālanemi releases the Brahmā-weapon to ward off all weapons; the Sun, employing great sorcery, makes his form terrible and, by spreading intensely hot rays of heat, throws the entire army of the Daityas into disarray; Kālanemi, assuming the form of a black cloud and raining down, inflicts defeat upon the whole army of the gods, including the horses, with a shower of weapons; then, hearing the prayer of all the gods, the blessed Mahāviṣṇu rises from his couch on the milk ocean, mounts Garuḍa, arrives at the battleground, fights with Kālanemi, and inflicts defeat upon Kālanemi... 111 1

1.4.d:
20 समस्तदैत्यैर्विष्णुना सह तुमुलयुद्धे विष्णुनाऽसंख्यातदैत्यविध्वंसे कृते जम्भासुरेण
पराजयं प्राप्य संग्रामांगणतः पराङ्मुखीभूय पलायनम्.. 112
1.4.m: 20. In the fierce battle of all the Daityas with Viṣṇu, when countless Daityas are destroyed by Viṣṇu, the demon Jambha meets with defeat, turns his back on the battlefield, and flees.. 112

1.4.s: 21 atha palāyitasya viṣṇorindrakṛtastutyā sthirībhavanam, viṣṇorājñayā jambhāsurahananārthamindrasya saṃnāhapūrvakaṃ jambhāsureṇa saha tumulayuddhavarṇanam, tasminyuddhe jambhāsurasya vadhaḥ,jambhāsuravadhottaraṃ devasainyatrastānāṃ kāndiśīkānāṃ samastadaityānāṃ tārakāsurāntikaṃ pratyāgamanam, tatastārakāsureṇa sarvadaityaiḥ saha yuddhabhūmiṃ samāsādya mahatā parākrameṇa sarvadevasainyavidhvaṃsakaraṇam, tadvīryamālokya viṣṇunā sarvadevānpalāyanārthamājñāpya svayamantardhānam ' tārakāsurasya vijayalabdhipūrvakaṃ mahīsāgarasaṃgamatīravartistaṃbhapure ( khambāyatanāmni) rājyasiṃhāsanopari mahatā samārambheṇārohaṇam, siṃhāsanādhirūḍhaṃ tārakāsuraṃ prati trailokyalakṣmyā āgamanapūrvakaṃ praveśanam, nārāyaṇenedrādidevānāṃ markarūpeṇa tārakāsuraṃ pratyānayanapūrvakaṃ tārakāsurato'bhayapradāpanam, tataśca tasmādabhayaṃ prāpyeṃdrādīnāṃ viṣṇorājñayā brahmāṇaṃ prati gamanam, tārakāsureṇeṃdrādidevānāṃ sthāneṣvātmādidaityānāmadhikārakaraṇam.. - 114 5
1.4.d: 21 अथ पलायितस्य विष्णोरिन्द्रकृतस्तुत्या स्थिरीभवनम्, विष्णोराज्ञया जम्भासुरहननार्थमिन्द्रस्य संनाहपूर्वकं जम्भासुरेण सह तुमुलयुद्धवर्णनम्, तस्मिन्युद्धे जम्भासुरस्य वधः,जम्भासुरवधोत्तरं देवसैन्यत्रस्तानां कान्दिशीकानां समस्तदैत्यानां तारकासुरान्तिकं प्रत्यागमनम्, ततस्तारकासुरेण सर्वदैत्यैः सह युद्धभूमिं समासाद्य महता पराक्रमेण सर्वदेवसैन्यविध्वंसकरणम्, तद्वीर्यमालोक्य विष्णुना सर्वदेवान्पलायनार्थमाज्ञाप्य स्वयमन्तर्धानम् ' तारकासुरस्य विजयलब्धिपूर्वकं महीसागरसंगमतीरवर्तिस्तंभपुरे ( खम्बायतनाम्नि) राज्यसिंहासनोपरि महता समारम्भेणारोहणम्, सिंहासनाधिरूढं तारकासुरं प्रति त्रैलोक्यलक्ष्म्या आगमनपूर्वकं प्रवेशनम्, नारायणेनेद्रादिदेवानां मर्करूपेण तारकासुरं प्रत्यानयनपूर्वकं तारकासुरतोऽभयप्रदापनम्, ततश्च तस्मादभयं प्राप्येंद्रादीनां विष्णोराज्ञया ब्रह्माणं प्रति गमनम्, तारकासुरेणेंद्रादिदेवानां स्थानेष्वात्मादिदैत्यानामधिकारकरणम्.. - 114 5
1.4.m: 21. Now, [the description of] Viṣṇu, who had fled, becoming steady through praise offered by Indra; the description of Indra's preparing [for battle] by the command of Viṣṇu to slay the demon Jambha, and the tumultuous battle with the demon Jambha; the slaying of the demon Jambha in that battle; after the slaying of the demon Jambha, the retreat to the demon Tāraka of all the demons who were terrified by the army of the gods and fleeing in panic; then the demon Tāraka, having reached the battlefield with all the demons, devastating the entire army of the gods with great prowess; Viṣṇu, having seen his valor, commanding all the gods to flee and himself disappearing; the demon Tāraka, having obtained victory, ascending with great pomp onto the royal throne at Stambhapura (known as Khambāyata), situated on the bank of the confluence of the Mahī and the ocean; the fortune of the three worlds coming and entering into the demon Tāraka who had mounted the throne; Nārāyaṇa, having brought the gods headed by Indra in the form of monkeys before the demon Tāraka, procuring safety for them from the demon Tāraka; and then, having obtained safety from him, the departure of Indra and the others toward Brahmā by the command of Viṣṇu; the demon Tāraka placing his own demons in authority over the realms of the gods headed by Indra... 114 [5]

1.4.s: 22 indrādidevairbrahmāṇaṃ prati gatvā stutipūrvakamātmano duḥkhanivedanam, brahmaṇā himālayagṛhe jagadaṃbā'vatariṣyatīti devānpratyāśvāsanam, tato devahitārthaṃ rātridevīstutikaraṇapūrvakaṃ himālayabhāryāyāṃ jagadambāmahādevīpraveśātpūrvaṃ praveśāya prārthanākaraṇam, brahmaṇaḥ prārthanena vibhāvaryā menānetrayorāveśanam, tato menāyāḥ sakāśājjagadambāyāḥ prādurbhāvaḥ, jagadambājanmakālikotsavavarṇanam-. 121 1,
1.4.d: 22 इन्द्रादिदेवैर्ब्रह्माणं प्रति गत्वा स्तुतिपूर्वकमात्मनो दुःखनिवेदनम्, ब्रह्मणा हिमालयगृहे जगदंबाऽवतरिष्यतीति देवान्प्रत्याश्वासनम्, ततो देवहितार्थं रात्रिदेवीस्तुतिकरणपूर्वकं हिमालयभार्यायां जगदम्बामहादेवीप्रवेशात्पूर्वं प्रवेशाय प्रार्थनाकरणम्, ब्रह्मणः प्रार्थनेन विभावर्या मेनानेत्रयोरावेशनम्, ततो मेनायाः सकाशाज्जगदम्बायाः प्रादुर्भावः, जगदम्बाजन्मकालिकोत्सववर्णनम्-. 121 1,
1.4.m: 22. The gods headed by Indra, having approached Brahmā, reporting their distress accompanied by praise; Brahmā consoling the gods [with the assurance] that the Mother of the Universe would incarnate in the house of Himālaya; then, for the sake of the welfare of the gods, having praised the goddess Rātri, making a prayer for her to enter the wife of Himālaya before the entry of the Great Goddess, the Mother of the Universe; by the prayer of Brahmā, the Night Goddess entering into the eyes of Menā; then the manifestation of the Mother of the Universe from Menā; the description of the festival at the time of the birth of the Mother of the Universe... 121 [1]

1.4.s: 23 śakravākyena himālayaṃ prati nāradenāgatya pārvatīsāmudrikalakṣaṇepu vacanabhaṃgyā yathā-ayukteṣu cintāturayorhimālayamenayoścāturyeṇa sarvadeveśvaramahādevavaraprāptikathanena punaḥ saṃtoṣajananāyāśvāsanam.... 122 2
1.4.d: 23 शक्रवाक्येन हिमालयं प्रति नारदेनागत्य पार्वतीसामुद्रिकलक्षणेपु वचनभंग्या यथा-अयुक्तेषु चिन्तातुरयोर्हिमालयमेनयोश्चातुर्येण सर्वदेवेश्वरमहादेववरप्राप्तिकथनेन पुनः संतोषजननायाश्वासनम्.... 122 2
1.4.m: 23. Nārada, having approached Himālaya at the word of Śakra, while [discussing] the bodily marks of Pārvatī through turn of phrase, tactfully comforting Himālaya and Menā, who were anxious when [the marks] seemed inappropriate, so as to produce joy once again by stating that she would obtain the Great God, the Lord of all Gods, as her husband... 122 [2]

1.4.s: 24 pārvatyāḥ sadaivottānapāṇitayā sarvaprāṇināmabhayapradatvalakṣaṇavarṇanam, śivasevārthaṃ pārvatyā niyojanāya himavata upadeśakaraṇam, tato nāradena himālayātsakāśādindraṃ pratyāgatya sakalavṛttāṃtanivedanapṛrvakaṃ harasya vivāhena devyā saha saṃyojanārthamājñākaraṇama, śakreṇa śaṃkaramohanāya madanāyājñākaraṇam, pārvatīparicaraṇavelāyāṃ madanena śaṃkare bāṇavedhakaraṇam, tato madanātureṇa hareṇa madanaṃ dṛṣṭvā tṛtīyanetrāgninā madanadahanam, tato ratiprārthanayā śaṃkareṇa madanasyānaṃgarūpeṇa saṃjīvanam .. 122:
1.4.d: 24 पार्वत्याः सदैवोत्तानपाणितया सर्वप्राणिनामभयप्रदत्वलक्षणवर्णनम्, शिवसेवार्थं पार्वत्या नियोजनाय हिमवत उपदेशकरणम्, ततो नारदेन हिमालयात्सकाशादिन्द्रं प्रत्यागत्य सकलवृत्तांतनिवेदनपृर्वकं हरस्य विवाहेन देव्या सह संयोजनार्थमाज्ञाकरणम, शक्रेण शंकरमोहनाय मदनायाज्ञाकरणम्, पार्वतीपरिचरणवेलायां मदनेन शंकरे बाणवेधकरणम्, ततो मदनातुरेण हरेण मदनं दृष्ट्वा तृतीयनेत्राग्निना मदनदहनम्, ततो रतिप्रार्थनया शंकरेण मदनस्यानंगरूपेण संजीवनम् .. 122:
1.4.m: 24. The description of Pārvatī's characteristic of granting fearlessness to all living beings by having her hands always turned upward; the advice given to Himavat to engage Pārvatī in the service of Śiva; then Nārada, having returned from Himālaya to Indra, reporting the entire event and giving the command to unite Hara with the Goddess through marriage; Śakra commanding Madana to enchant Śaṃkara; Madana piercing Śaṃkara with an arrow at the time of Pārvatī's service; then Hara, agitated by passion, having seen Madana, burning Madana with the fire of his third eye; then, upon the prayer of Rati, Śaṃkara reviving Madana in the bodiless form (Anaṅga)... 122:

1.4.s: 25 punarhimādriṃ pratyāgatasya nāradasyopadeśena śivaprāptaye pārvatyāstapaḥkaraṇavṛttāṃtavarṇanam, śivena tapaḥsthitāyāḥ pārvatyā nikaṭe viprarūpeṇāgatya nijaniṣṭhāparīkṣaṇam, tataḥ suprasannena śivena nijarūpaprakaṭanapūrvakaṃ pārvatyā āśvāsanam, tataḥ pārvatyāḥ svayaṃva- varavaivāhikotsavārthaṃ sarvadevānāṃ nimaṃtraṇam, tatra śrīśaṃkarasya bālarūpaṃ vidhāyāgamanam, tatra samāgatānāṃ tārakādīnāṃ daityānāṃ śivena huṃkāramātreṇa svasvasthānaṃ prati samutsāraṇam sarveṣāṃ brahmādidevānāṃ vivāhasthalaṃ pratyāgamanam tataḥ pārvatyā sarvadevānāṃ pratyakṣaṃ śrīśaṃkaracaraṇayorvaraṇamālāsamarpaṇam. . 125 1
1.4.d: 25 पुनर्हिमाद्रिं प्रत्यागतस्य नारदस्योपदेशेन शिवप्राप्तये पार्वत्यास्तपःकरणवृत्तांतवर्णनम्, शिवेन तपःस्थितायाः पार्वत्या निकटे विप्ररूपेणागत्य निजनिष्ठापरीक्षणम्, ततः सुप्रसन्नेन शिवेन निजरूपप्रकटनपूर्वकं पार्वत्या आश्वासनम्, ततः पार्वत्याः स्वयंव- वरवैवाहिकोत्सवार्थं सर्वदेवानां निमंत्रणम्, तत्र श्रीशंकरस्य बालरूपं विधायागमनम्, तत्र समागतानां तारकादीनां दैत्यानां शिवेन हुंकारमात्रेण स्वस्वस्थानं प्रति समुत्सारणम् सर्वेषां ब्रह्मादिदेवानां विवाहस्थलं प्रत्यागमनम् ततः पार्वत्या सर्वदेवानां प्रत्यक्षं श्रीशंकरचरणयोर्वरणमालासमर्पणम्. . 125 1
1.4.m: 25. The narration of the story of Pārvatī performing austerity to attain Śiva upon the counsel of Nārada, who had returned once again to Himādri; Śiva, having approached Pārvatī while she stood in austerity in the guise of a brahmin, testing her devotion; then Śiva, being very pleased, comforting Pārvatī by revealing his own form; then the invitation to all the gods for the festival of the self-choice and marriage of Pārvatī; Śrī Śaṃkara coming there assuming the form of a child; Śiva, by a mere roar, driving away to their own realms the demons headed by Tāraka who had arrived there; the arrival of all the gods headed by Brahmā at the place of the marriage; then Pārvatī placing the wedding garland at the feet of Śrī Śaṃkara before the eyes of all the gods... 125 [1]

1.4.s:
26 tato brahmādidevānāṃ samanumodanapuraḥsaraṃ yathāśāstravidhānoktapaddhatyā harapārvatyoḥ
savistaravivāhamaṃgalotsavavarṇanam. .. .. 127 2
1.4.d:
26 ततो ब्रह्मादिदेवानां समनुमोदनपुरःसरं यथाशास्त्रविधानोक्तपद्धत्या हरपार्वत्योः
सविस्तरविवाहमंगलोत्सववर्णनम्. .. .. 127 2
1.4.m: 26. Then, with the assent of the gods headed by Brahmā, the detailed description of the auspicious wedding festival of Hara and Pārvatī according to the procedure prescribed in the injunctions of the scriptures... 127 [2]

1.4.s: 27 vivāhottaraṃ śivasya pārvatyā saha maṃdarācalodyāne bhavyasuṃdaramaṃdire gatvā ramaṇam- tasminnavasare tārakāsuratrastairdevaiḥ stutikaraṇottaraṃ pārvatyā nijāṃgamalato gaṇapatiṃ nirmāya devānāṃ sāhāyyārthaṃ gaṇapatipradānam, gaṇapatinā devahitārthadaityānāṃ śaśvadvighnakaraṇam, tato vīrakākhyasya gaṇasya pārvatyā putrīkaraṇavṛttāṃtavarṇanam, tataḥ śivapārvatyoḥ parasparaṃ narmoktivaśena śivena pārvatyāḥ kālīnāmnā''hvāne kṛte kupitāyāḥ pārvatyāḥ śivaṃ prati marmaspṛṅmarmoktibhirnirbhartsanam -. 129 2
1.4.d: 27 विवाहोत्तरं शिवस्य पार्वत्या सह मंदराचलोद्याने भव्यसुंदरमंदिरे गत्वा रमणम्- तस्मिन्नवसरे तारकासुरत्रस्तैर्देवैः स्तुतिकरणोत्तरं पार्वत्या निजांगमलतो गणपतिं निर्माय देवानां साहाय्यार्थं गणपतिप्रदानम्, गणपतिना देवहितार्थदैत्यानां शश्वद्विघ्नकरणम्, ततो वीरकाख्यस्य गणस्य पार्वत्या पुत्रीकरणवृत्तांतवर्णनम्, ततः शिवपार्वत्योः परस्परं नर्मोक्तिवशेन शिवेन पार्वत्याः कालीनाम्ना'ऽह्वाने कृते कुपितायाः पार्वत्याः शिवं प्रति मर्मस्पृङ्मर्मोक्तिभिर्निर्भर्त्सनम् -. 129 2
1.4.m: 27. After the wedding, Śiva going with Pārvatī to a grand and beautiful mansion in the garden of Mount Mandara and sporting [there]; on that occasion, after praise was offered by the gods who were terrified of the demon Tāraka, Pārvatī fashioning Gaṇapati from the dirt of her own body and giving Gaṇapati to the gods for their assistance; Gaṇapati constantly creating obstacles for the demons for the welfare of the gods; then the narration of the story of Pārvatī taking the gaṇa named Vīraka as her son; then, by virtue of playful banter between Śiva and Pārvatī, when Śiva addressed Pārvatī by the name 'Kālī', Pārvatī becoming enraged and rebuking Śiva with sharp, heart-wounding words... 129 [2]

1.4.s: 28 tataḥ pārvatyā maṃdirānnirgamya gamanāvasare śivasamīpe'nyasyāḥ striyāḥ praveśanirodhāya, vīrakanāmakaṃ gaṇaṃ pratyājñākaraṇam, gaṇapatiṃ samādāya himavantaṃ prati ttapo'rthaṃ gamanam
1.4.d: 28 ततः पार्वत्या मंदिरान्निर्गम्य गमनावसरे शिवसमीपेऽन्यस्याः स्त्रियाः प्रवेशनिरोधाय, वीरकनामकं गणं प्रत्याज्ञाकरणम्, गणपतिं समादाय हिमवन्तं प्रति त्तपोऽर्थं गमनम्
1.4.m: 28. Then Pārvatī departing from the mansion, and at the time of her departure, commanding the gaṇa named Vīraka to prevent the entry of any other woman near Śiva; taking Gaṇapati and departing for Himavat to perform austerity.

1.4.s:
29 tataḥ pārvatyā nijamātṛsakhyāḥ kusumāmodinyāḥ svasyai śivasamīpe vrajantyā anyasyāḥ striyāḥ praveśavārtānivedanāyājñāpanam-tatastapaścaryārambhakaraṇam, etasminnaṃtare śivasamīpaṃ prati pārvatīrūpeṇāḍināmakadaityasyāgamanam , śivena maithunapravṛtto tāmāsurīṃ māyāṃ vijñāya nijameḍhramadhye raudrāstramādhāya maithunena tadvadhakaraṇam, atha tatkṣaṇādvāyunā pārvatīkarṇe śivasamīpe'nyastrīpraveśavārtāsamudīraṇam, tacchrutvā pārvatyā vīrakagaṇāya śāpapradānam tatastanmukhātkrodhasya siṃharūpeṇa bahirnirgamanam, tapaḥ kurvantyāḥ pārvatyāḥ samīpe brahmaṇa āgamanam, brahmaṇā devyai varapradānam, tataḥ pārvatīdevyāḥ śarīrānnīlavarṇāyā devyā nirgamanam, tasyāḥ kauśikītināmakaraṇam, tataḥ pārvatyāḥ pūrvagauratvaprāptiḥ, atha pārvatyāḥ śivasamīpaṃ prati gamanam, tatra dvāristhitena vīrakagaṇena gauryā antaḥpraveśārthaṃ niṣedhakaraṇam, vīrakavacanaṃ śrutvā pārvatyāḥ pūrvaṃ vṛthāsmai mayā śāpo datta iti paścāttāpaḥ, tataḥ pārvatyā vīrakāya nijavṛttakatha-
napūrvakaṃ śilādaputrananditvaprāptirūpavarapradānam, devyāḥ śivasamīpaṃ pratyetya śivena saha premakaraṇam, tataḥ śivapārvatyoḥ suratasamārambhaḥ, tatra devapreraṇayā pārāvatarūpeṇāgatasyāgnermukhe mahādevena vīryabhakṣaṇārthaṃ preraṇam, īśājñayā'gnineśaretobhakṣaṇam, tata ṛṣipatnīḥ kāmayamānaṃ svapatimagniṃ nirīkṣya ṣaḍṛṣipatnīnāṃ ṣaṭkṛttikānāṃ rūpeṇa svāhayā'gnipatnyā'gneḥ sakāśātkāmadharmeṇa ṣaḍvārakrameṇa vīryaṃ gṛhītvā śarastambe nikṣepaṇam-ṛṣipatnīsaṃbhogabhrāṃtyā śokasaṃtaptasyāgnerākāśavāṇyā sāntvanam-tatogninā śvetaparvatopari śarastaṃbamadhyasthe kuṇḍe divyaprabhatanayanirīkṣaṇam-ṣaḍṛṣipatnīnāṃ ṣaṇṇāṃ caritama, atha viśvāmitreṇa kumārasamīpamāgatyāṣṭottaraśatanāmabhiḥ kumārastutikaraṇam-viśvāmitramaharṣiṇā skandakumārasya jātakarmādikarmakaraṇapuraḥsaraṃ paurohityakarmakaraṇam-agninā kumārāyā'valokanapūrvakaṃ putretyuktyanaṃtaraṃ śaktyastrapradānam tataḥ kumārasya devendrādibhirdarśanam - tataḥ śivapārvatyoḥ kumāraṃ pratyāgamya kumāraṃ prati putrasnehakaraṇam, tataḥ kumāreṇa sarveṣāṃ manorathaprapūraṇena priyakaraṇam- ... 132 1
1.4.d:
29 ततः पार्वत्या निजमातृसख्याः कुसुमामोदिन्याः स्वस्यै शिवसमीपे व्रजन्त्या अन्यस्याः स्त्रियाः प्रवेशवार्तानिवेदनायाज्ञापनम्-ततस्तपश्चर्यारम्भकरणम्, एतस्मिन्नंतरे शिवसमीपं प्रति पार्वतीरूपेणाडिनामकदैत्यस्यागमनम् , शिवेन मैथुनप्रवृत्तो तामासुरीं मायां विज्ञाय निजमेढ्रमध्ये रौद्रास्त्रमाधाय मैथुनेन तद्वधकरणम्, अथ तत्क्षणाद्वायुना पार्वतीकर्णे शिवसमीपेऽन्यस्त्रीप्रवेशवार्तासमुदीरणम्, तच्छ्रुत्वा पार्वत्या वीरकगणाय शापप्रदानम् ततस्तन्मुखात्क्रोधस्य सिंहरूपेण बहिर्निर्गमनम्, तपः कुर्वन्त्याः पार्वत्याः समीपे ब्रह्मण आगमनम्, ब्रह्मणा देव्यै वरप्रदानम्, ततः पार्वतीदेव्याः शरीरान्नीलवर्णाया देव्या निर्गमनम्, तस्याः कौशिकीतिनामकरणम्, ततः पार्वत्याः पूर्वगौरत्वप्राप्तिः, अथ पार्वत्याः शिवसमीपं प्रति गमनम्, तत्र द्वारिस्थितेन वीरकगणेन गौर्या अन्तःप्रवेशार्थं निषेधकरणम्, वीरकवचनं श्रुत्वा पार्वत्याः पूर्वं वृथास्मै मया शापो दत्त इति पश्चात्तापः, ततः पार्वत्या वीरकाय निजवृत्तकथ-
नपूर्वकं शिलादपुत्रनन्दित्वप्राप्तिरूपवरप्रदानम्, देव्याः शिवसमीपं प्रत्येत्य शिवेन सह प्रेमकरणम्, ततः शिवपार्वत्योः सुरतसमारम्भः, तत्र देवप्रेरणया पारावतरूपेणागतस्याग्नेर्मुखे महादेवेन वीर्यभक्षणार्थं प्रेरणम्, ईशाज्ञयाऽग्निनेशरेतोभक्षणम्, तत ऋषिपत्नीः कामयमानं स्वपतिमग्निं निरीक्ष्य षडृषिपत्नीनां षट्कृत्तिकानां रूपेण स्वाहयाऽग्निपत्न्याऽग्नेः सकाशात्कामधर्मेण षड्वारक्रमेण वीर्यं गृहीत्वा शरस्तम्बे निक्षेपणम्-ऋषिपत्नीसंभोगभ्रांत्या शोकसंतप्तस्याग्नेराकाशवाण्या सान्त्वनम्-ततोग्निना श्वेतपर्वतोपरि शरस्तंबमध्यस्थे कुण्डे दिव्यप्रभतनयनिरीक्षणम्-षडृषिपत्नीनां षण्णां चरितम, अथ विश्वामित्रेण कुमारसमीपमागत्याष्टोत्तरशतनामभिः कुमारस्तुतिकरणम्-विश्वामित्रमहर्षिणा स्कन्दकुमारस्य जातकर्मादिकर्मकरणपुरःसरं पौरोहित्यकर्मकरणम्-अग्निना कुमारायाऽवलोकनपूर्वकं पुत्रेत्युक्त्यनंतरं शक्त्यस्त्रप्रदानम् ततः कुमारस्य देवेन्द्रादिभिर्दर्शनम् - ततः शिवपार्वत्योः कुमारं प्रत्यागम्य कुमारं प्रति पुत्रस्नेहकरणम्, ततः कुमारेण सर्वेषां मनोरथप्रपूरणेन प्रियकरणम्- ... 132 1
1.4.m: 29. Then Pārvatī commands her mother's friend Kusumāmodinī to report to her if any other woman should enter Śiva's presence; then she begins the practice of austerities; in the meantime, the demon named Āḍi arrives in the guise of Pārvatī before Śiva; Śiva, engaging in intercourse, recognizes this demonic illusion, places the weapon of Rudra in his penis, and slays him through intercourse; then at that moment Vāyu whispers into Pārvatī's ear the news that another woman entered Śiva's presence; hearing that, Pārvatī curses the gaṇa Vīraka; then anger comes out of her mouth in the form of a lion; Brahmā arrives before Pārvatī as she performs austerities; Brahmā grants a boon to the goddess; then a dark-complexioned goddess emerges from Goddess Pārvatī's body; she is named Kauśikī; then Pārvatī regains her former fair complexion; then Pārvatī goes to Śiva; there, the gaṇa Vīraka standing at the door forbids Gaurī from entering; hearing Vīraka's words, Pārvatī repents, thinking, "I cursed him in vain before"; then Pārvatī relates her story to Vīraka and grants him the boon of becoming Nandī, the son of Śilāda; the goddess approaches Śiva and makes love with him; then Śiva and Pārvatī begin their dalliance; there, Mahādeva urges Agni, who has arrived in the form of a pigeon at the instigation of the gods, to swallow his semen into his mouth; by the Lord's command, Agni consumes the seed of Īśa; then Svāhā, the wife of Agni, seeing her husband Agni longing for the sages' wives, assumes the form of six sages' wives, the six Kṛttikās, takes the semen from Agni in six turns following the law of desire, and deposits it in a thicket of reeds; Agni, tormented with grief by the false delusion of union with the sages' wives, is consoled by a heavenly voice; then on the White Mountain Agni sees in a basin situated within the reed-thicket a child of divine splendor; the legend of the six wives of the sages; then Viśvāmitra approaches Kumāra and praises him with a hundred and eight names; the great sage Viśvāmitra performs the birth-rites and other rites for Skanda Kumāra, acting as household priest; Agni looks upon Kumāra, addresses him as "son", and gives him the śakti weapon; then Kumāra is beheld by Devendra and others; then Śiva and Pārvatī approach Kumāra and show him parental love; then Kumāra brings joy to all by fulfilling their desires. 132 1

1.4.s: 30 tārakāsuraṃ haṃtuṃ kumārasya samastadevairmahīsāgarasaṃgame devasainādhipatye'bhiṣekavarṇanama 136
1.4.d: 30 तारकासुरं हंतुं कुमारस्य समस्तदेवैर्महीसागरसंगमे देवसैनाधिपत्येऽभिषेकवर्णनम 136
1.4.m: 30. Description of the consecration of Kumāra by all the gods as supreme commander of the divine army at the confluence of the Mahī and the ocean, in order to slay the demon Tāraka. 136

1.4.s: 31 kumārasvāminā tārakāsurahananāya pratijñākaraṇam, tārakāsurapuraṃ prati sarvadevasainikaiḥ saha gatvā kumāreṇa yuddhārthaṃ tārakāsuraṃ prati nāradasya preṣaṇam, tasminnavasare tārakāsureṇa gavākṣamadhiruhya kiṃnarairudgīyamānasya kumārajayamaṃgaladhvaneḥ śravaṇam- 137
1.4.d: 31 कुमारस्वामिना तारकासुरहननाय प्रतिज्ञाकरणम्, तारकासुरपुरं प्रति सर्वदेवसैनिकैः सह गत्वा कुमारेण युद्धार्थं तारकासुरं प्रति नारदस्य प्रेषणम्, तस्मिन्नवसरे तारकासुरेण गवाक्षमधिरुह्य किंनरैरुद्गीयमानस्य कुमारजयमंगलध्वनेः श्रवणम्- 137
1.4.m: 31. Kumārasvāmin makes a vow to slay the demon Tāraka; Kumāra advances towards the city of the demon Tāraka with all the soldiers of the divine army, and dispatches Nārada to the demon Tāraka for battle; at that moment, the demon Tāraka, mounting to a lattice window, hears the auspicious sounds of Kumāra's victory being sung by kiṃnaras. 137

1.4.s: 32 kiṃnarairgīyamānāṃ kumārastutiṃ śrutvā tārakāsureṇopasthitādbālakānnijavadhaṃ niścitya mantribhiḥ saha samantrya samastadaityasenāsaṃnāhapūrvakaṃ devaiḥ saṃgrāmārthaṃ svapurānniryāṇam, tato devadaityasaṃgrāmārambhaḥ, tasminghorasaṃgrāme tārakāsurasainikairdevasainyaparābhavakaraṇam, atha kumārasvāminastārakāsurasaṃmukhe yuddhārthamavasthānam tārakāsuraṃ śivabhaktaṃ dṛṣṭvā kumārasvāmino manasi viṣṇorupadeśe'pi tadvadhakaraṇe'pravṛttiḥ,tasminnavasare tārakāsureṇa viṣṇurudrādidevajarjarīkaraṇam, śaṃkaraṃ pratyabhiyāṃtaṃ tārakaṃ dṛṣṭvā''kāśavāṇyā kumārasvāminastārakāsurahananecchotpattiḥ, tataḥ kumāreṇa tārakavadhārthaṃ mayūrādyutplutya viṣṇuṃ praśasya tārakasya śirasā nirgatāṃ śaktiṃ nirīkṣya niḥśaktikasya tārakāsurasyopari nijaśaktiṃ visṛjya tārakāsuravadhakaraṇam, tataḥ keśavapreraṇayā nijaśaktyā bāṇādidaityavyālādisamanvitakrauñcaparvatabhammīkaraṇama tataḥ kumārasvāmino devagandharvādikṛtavijayotsavavarṇanam ... . ... ... 139 1
1.4.d: 32 किंनरैर्गीयमानां कुमारस्तुतिं श्रुत्वा तारकासुरेणोपस्थिताद्बालकान्निजवधं निश्चित्य मन्त्रिभिः सह समन्त्र्य समस्तदैत्यसेनासंनाहपूर्वकं देवैः संग्रामार्थं स्वपुरान्निर्याणम्, ततो देवदैत्यसंग्रामारम्भः, तस्मिन्घोरसंग्रामे तारकासुरसैनिकैर्देवसैन्यपराभवकरणम्, अथ कुमारस्वामिनस्तारकासुरसंमुखे युद्धार्थमवस्थानम् तारकासुरं शिवभक्तं दृष्ट्वा कुमारस्वामिनो मनसि विष्णोरुपदेशेऽपि तद्वधकरणेऽप्रवृत्तिः,तस्मिन्नवसरे तारकासुरेण विष्णुरुद्रादिदेवजर्जरीकरणम्, शंकरं प्रत्यभियांतं तारकं दृष्ट्वा'ऽकाशवाण्या कुमारस्वामिनस्तारकासुरहननेच्छोत्पत्तिः, ततः कुमारेण तारकवधार्थं मयूराद्युत्प्लुत्य विष्णुं प्रशस्य तारकस्य शिरसा निर्गतां शक्तिं निरीक्ष्य निःशक्तिकस्य तारकासुरस्योपरि निजशक्तिं विसृज्य तारकासुरवधकरणम्, ततः केशवप्रेरणया निजशक्त्या बाणादिदैत्यव्यालादिसमन्वितक्रौञ्चपर्वतभम्मीकरणम ततः कुमारस्वामिनो देवगन्धर्वादिकृतविजयोत्सववर्णनम् ... . ... ... 139 1
1.4.m: 32. Hearing the praise of Kumāra sung by the kiṃnaras, the demon Tāraka realizes his own death will come from the child who has arrived, confers with his ministers, equips the entire demon army, and marches out of his city to fight the gods; then the battle between the gods and demons begins; in that terrible battle, the soldiers of the demon Tāraka defeat the divine army; then Kumārasvāmin stands before the demon Tāraka to fight; seeing that the demon Tāraka is a devotee of Śiva, Kumārasvāmin is reluctant to slay him despite Viṣṇu's instruction; at that moment, the demon Tāraka batters the gods headed by Viṣṇu and Rudra; seeing Tāraka advance towards Śaṃkara, Kumārasvāmin conceives the desire to slay the demon Tāraka due to a heavenly voice; then Kumāra leaps from his peacock to slay Tāraka, praises Viṣṇu, observes the energy departing from Tāraka's head, and hurling his own śakti at the powerless demon Tāraka, slays him; then, prompted by Keśava, he smashes with his śakti Mount Krauñca along with Bāṇa and other demons and serpents; then the victory celebration performed for Kumārasvāmin by the gods, gandharvas, and others is described. 139 1

1.4.s: 33 tārakāsuravadhena kumārasvāmino rudrabhaktahananajanyapāpaśaṃkayā śokakaraṇam, tato mahāviṣṇūpadeśena kumārasvāminā rudrabhaktavadhajanitapātakaśāṃtaye viśvakarmadvārā trīṇi śivaliṃgāni nirmāpya tanmadhye pratijñeśvaracchidreśvarayoḥ sthāpanavarṇanama .. 142 2
1.4.d: 33 तारकासुरवधेन कुमारस्वामिनो रुद्रभक्तहननजन्यपापशंकया शोककरणम्, ततो महाविष्णूपदेशेन कुमारस्वामिना रुद्रभक्तवधजनितपातकशांतये विश्वकर्मद्वारा त्रीणि शिवलिंगानि निर्माप्य तन्मध्ये प्रतिज्ञेश्वरच्छिद्रेश्वरयोः स्थापनवर्णनम .. 142 2
1.4.m: 33. Over the slaying of the demon Tāraka, Kumārasvāmin grieves out of fear of the sin incurred by slaying a devotee of Rudra; then, on the advice of Mahāviṣṇu, Kumārasvāmin, to appease the transgression born from killing a devotee of Rudra, has three Śiva-liṅgas fashioned through Viśvakarman, and among them sets up Pratijñeśvara and Chidreśvara. 142 2

1.4.s: 34 tataḥ kumārasvāminā vrahmadevānītasya liṅgasya kumāreśvaranāmnā sthāpanam kumārasya tatsthāpanottaraṃ śaṃkarācchivapūjāvidhiśravaṇamama, kumārasvāmikṛtā kumāreśvaramahādevastutiḥ, kumāreśvareṇa kumārasvāmine varapradānam, jagadambāyāḥ sadā kumāreśvarasaṃnidhānakathanapūrvakaṃ kumārasvāmine varapradānam, tataḥ kapardigaṇeśvarakṛtavarapradānam, . kumāreśvarasaṃnidhau kumārasvāminoṃ'śenāvasthānam, mahīsāgarasaṃgamasthakumāreśvaramahā- devasevāmāhātmyavarṇanam. ...... -. ... ... .144 1
1.4.d: 34 ततः कुमारस्वामिना व्रह्मदेवानीतस्य लिङ्गस्य कुमारेश्वरनाम्ना स्थापनम् कुमारस्य तत्स्थापनोत्तरं शंकराच्छिवपूजाविधिश्रवणमम, कुमारस्वामिकृता कुमारेश्वरमहादेवस्तुतिः, कुमारेश्वरेण कुमारस्वामिने वरप्रदानम्, जगदम्बायाः सदा कुमारेश्वरसंनिधानकथनपूर्वकं कुमारस्वामिने वरप्रदानम्, ततः कपर्दिगणेश्वरकृतवरप्रदानम्, . कुमारेश्वरसंनिधौ कुमारस्वामिनोंऽशेनावस्थानम्, महीसागरसंगमस्थकुमारेश्वरमहा- देवसेवामाहात्म्यवर्णनम्. ...... -. ... ... .144 1
1.4.m: 34. Then Kumārasvāmin installs the liṅga brought by Brahmā under the name Kumāreśvara; after its installation, Kumāra hears the procedure for the worship of Śiva from Śaṃkara; the praise of Kumāreśvara Mahādeva recited by Kumārasvāmin; Kumāreśvara grants a boon to Kumārasvāmin; the Mother of the Universe, declaring her constant presence in Kumāreśvara, grants a boon to Kumārasvāmin; then the boon granted by the lord of gaṇas Kapardin; Kumārasvāmin resides in part near Kumāreśvara; description of the māhātmya of the service of Kumāreśvara Mahādeva situated at the confluence of the Mahī and the ocean. 144 1

1.4.s: 35 atha mahīsāgarasaṃgame devānāṃ prārthanayā jayastambhaṃ saṃsthāpya tadupari viśvakarmavinirmitasya tṛtīyasya liṅgasya staṃbheśvaranāmnā saṃsthāpanam, kūpatīrthanirmāṇaṃ ca, stambheśvaramāhātmyavarṇanam 146 2
1.4.d: 35 अथ महीसागरसंगमे देवानां प्रार्थनया जयस्तम्भं संस्थाप्य तदुपरि विश्वकर्मविनिर्मितस्य तृतीयस्य लिङ्गस्य स्तंभेश्वरनाम्ना संस्थापनम्, कूपतीर्थनिर्माणं च, स्तम्भेश्वरमाहात्म्यवर्णनम् 146 2
1.4.m: 35. Then, at the confluence of the Mahī and the ocean, at the prayer of the gods, a victory pillar is erected, and upon it the third liṅga fashioned by Viśvakarman is installed under the name Stambheśvara; the creation of the well tīrtha, and the description of the māhātmya of Stambheśvara. 146 2

1.4.s:
36 mahīsāgarasaṃgame brahmendrarudrapramukhadevādibhiḥ koṭiśo liṅgasthāpanama, tanmāhātmyaṃ ca,
siddhāmbikāsiddhakūpasiddheśvarādimāhātmyapūrvakaṃ pañcaliṅgopākhyānavarṇanama. -.. 147 1
1.4.d:
36 महीसागरसंगमे ब्रह्मेन्द्ररुद्रप्रमुखदेवादिभिः कोटिशो लिङ्गस्थापनम, तन्माहात्म्यं च,
सिद्धाम्बिकासिद्धकूपसिद्धेश्वरादिमाहात्म्यपूर्वकं पञ्चलिङ्गोपाख्यानवर्णनम. -.. 147 1
1.4.m: 36. The installation of crores of liṅgas at the confluence of the Mahī and the ocean by the gods headed by Brahmā, Indra, and Rudra, and their māhātmya; and the narration of the episode of the five liṅgas accompanied by the māhātmya of Siddhāmbikā, the Siddhā well, Siddheśvara, and others. 147 1

1.4.s: 37 barbarītīrthamāhātmyaprasaṃgena kaumārikākhaṇḍanāmakāraṇībhūtakanyākumārikācaritravarṇanam, tatprasaṃgena jagadupattibrahmāṇḍaparimāṇabhūgolasaṃsthitiprakārakathanam... 148
1.4.d: 37 बर्बरीतीर्थमाहात्म्यप्रसंगेन कौमारिकाखण्डनामकारणीभूतकन्याकुमारिकाचरित्रवर्णनम्, तत्प्रसंगेन जगदुपत्तिब्रह्माण्डपरिमाणभूगोलसंस्थितिप्रकारकथनम्... 148
1.4.m: 37 In connection with the māhātmya of the Barbarītīrtha, an account of the deeds of the Maiden Kumārikā, who was the cause of the name Kaumārikākhaṇḍa; in connection with that, an exposition of the manner of the world's creation, the dimensions of the cosmic egg, and the arrangement of the terrestrial globe... 148

1.4.s:
38 brahmāṇḍaparimāṇaprasaṃgena khagolasaṃsthitivarṇanapūrvakasamastordhvalokavyavasthitikatha-
nam.. - ... -. - -. -. -.. -. -.. 150 1
1.4.d:
38 ब्रह्माण्डपरिमाणप्रसंगेन खगोलसंस्थितिवर्णनपूर्वकसमस्तोर्ध्वलोकव्यवस्थितिकथ-
नम्.. - ... -. - -. -. -.. -. -.. 150 1
1.4.m: 38 In connection with the dimensions of the cosmic egg, a description of the celestial sphere, followed by an account of the arrangement of all the upper worlds... 150 1

1.4.s: 39 atha brahmāṇḍaparimāṇaprasaṃgena pātālalokavyavasthitivarṇanapūrvakaṃ pātālādadhobhāge vividhanarakanirūpaṇam, tattatpātakināṃ tattannarakaṣu yātanābhogavarṇanam, evaṃ samastabrahmāṇḍasya pālakānāṃ devānāṃ vasudhānādīnāṃ varṇanama, evamanaṃtakoṭibrahmāṇḍarūpavaibhavaśālino maheśvarasya sarvātiśāyimāhātmyakathanam, atha kālaparimāṇakathanama, evaṃ samastavaidhātraprapañcasya vyavasthitivarṇanam, atha ṛṣabhātmajabharatabhūpaputrasya śataśṛṃgākhyasya navāpatyamadhye jāyamānāyā ekasyāḥ kumārikāyā barkarīmukhatvakāraṇakathanaprasaṃgena prāgjanmīyavṛttāntasmaraṇapūrvakaṃ mahīsāgarasaṃgame jāligulmāntaravilagnanijā'jāvaktranikṣepaṇātsadyaḥ sundarastrīmukhatvaprāptivṛttāntavarṇanam, tayā kumārikayā barkareśasthāpanam, barkareśānena kumāryai varapradānam śataśṛṃgabhūpena nijakanyāyai kumāryākhyāyai navadhā vibhaktaraya bharatakhaṇḍasyaikavibhāgapradānāttannāmnā tadvibhāgasya kaumārikākhaṇḍākhyayā prasiddhivarṇanam-bharatakhaṇḍasthadeśagrāmanagarasaṃkhyāparigaṇanam , tayā ca kumāryā nijabhrātṛputrebhyaḥ svakīyabhāgānāṃ yathāsaṃkhyaṃ vibhajya pradānapūrvekaṃ stambhatīrthaṃ pratyāgatya kumāreśvarakumārīśvarasevākaraṇasuprasannabhavānīśaṅkaravaraprasādasaṃpādanam-vṛddhayā tayā rudropadeśena sarasvatītīrasthamahākālanāmakasiddhavaraṇam-mahākālavallabhāyāstasyāstapaḥprabhāveṇa citralekhāpsaratvaprāptivarṇanam-barkareśvaraliṅgamāhātmyavarṇanam.. ..... 151 2
1.4.d: 39 अथ ब्रह्माण्डपरिमाणप्रसंगेन पाताललोकव्यवस्थितिवर्णनपूर्वकं पातालादधोभागे विविधनरकनिरूपणम्, तत्तत्पातकिनां तत्तन्नरकषु यातनाभोगवर्णनम्, एवं समस्तब्रह्माण्डस्य पालकानां देवानां वसुधानादीनां वर्णनम, एवमनंतकोटिब्रह्माण्डरूपवैभवशालिनो महेश्वरस्य सर्वातिशायिमाहात्म्यकथनम्, अथ कालपरिमाणकथनम, एवं समस्तवैधात्रप्रपञ्चस्य व्यवस्थितिवर्णनम्, अथ ऋषभात्मजभरतभूपपुत्रस्य शतशृंगाख्यस्य नवापत्यमध्ये जायमानाया एकस्याः कुमारिकाया बर्करीमुखत्वकारणकथनप्रसंगेन प्राग्जन्मीयवृत्तान्तस्मरणपूर्वकं महीसागरसंगमे जालिगुल्मान्तरविलग्ननिजाऽजावक्त्रनिक्षेपणात्सद्यः सुन्दरस्त्रीमुखत्वप्राप्तिवृत्तान्तवर्णनम्, तया कुमारिकया बर्करेशस्थापनम्, बर्करेशानेन कुमार्यै वरप्रदानम् शतशृंगभूपेन निजकन्यायै कुमार्याख्यायै नवधा विभक्तरय भरतखण्डस्यैकविभागप्रदानात्तन्नाम्ना तद्विभागस्य कौमारिकाखण्डाख्यया प्रसिद्धिवर्णनम्-भरतखण्डस्थदेशग्रामनगरसंख्यापरिगणनम् , तया च कुमार्या निजभ्रातृपुत्रेभ्यः स्वकीयभागानां यथासंख्यं विभज्य प्रदानपूर्वेकं स्तम्भतीर्थं प्रत्यागत्य कुमारेश्वरकुमारीश्वरसेवाकरणसुप्रसन्नभवानीशङ्करवरप्रसादसंपादनम्-वृद्धया तया रुद्रोपदेशेन सरस्वतीतीरस्थमहाकालनामकसिद्धवरणम्-महाकालवल्लभायास्तस्यास्तपःप्रभावेण चित्रलेखाप्सरत्वप्राप्तिवर्णनम्-बर्करेश्वरलिङ्गमाहात्म्यवर्णनम्.. ..... 151 2
1.4.m: 39 Then, in connection with the dimensions of the cosmic egg, a description of the arrangement of the subterranean worlds of Pātāla, followed by an account of the various hells situated beneath Pātāla; a description of the suffering endured in those respective hells by the corresponding sinners; likewise, a description of the gods, lords of the earth, and others who protect the entire cosmic egg; an account of the supreme māhātmya of Maheśvara, whose glory consists of endless millions of cosmic eggs; then an exposition of the measures of time; thus a description of the arrangement of the entire phenomenal world of Brahmā; then, in connection with explaining the reason why one maiden among the nine children born to King Śataśṛṅga, the son of King Bharata who was born of Ṛṣabha, had the face of a she-goat, an account of how, upon remembering the events of her previous birth, she plunged her own she-goat's face into the thicket of Jāli shrubs at the confluence of the Mahī and the sea, instantly obtained the face of a beautiful woman; the installation of Barkareśa by that maiden; Barkareśāna's granting of a boon to the maiden; a description of that division becoming renowned by the name Kaumārikākhaṇḍa because King Śataśṛṅga gave one division of the ninefold divided land of Bharatakhaṇḍa to his own daughter named Kumārī; an enumeration of the countries, villages, and cities located in Bharatakhaṇḍa; how that maiden, after duly dividing and giving her own shares to the sons of her brothers, returned to Stambhatīrtha, served Kumāreśvara and Kumārīśvara, and obtained boons and grace from Bhavānī and Śaṅkara who were well pleased; how she, when old, on Rudra's instruction chose the perfected sage named Mahākāla on the bank of the Sarasvatī; an account of how she, as the beloved of Mahākāla, attained the status of the apsaras Citralekhā through the power of her austerities; and a description of the māhātmya of the Barkareśvara liṅga... 151 2

1.4.s: 40 atha mahākālanāmakasya siddhasya caritravarṇanam, tatra vārāṇasīnivāsino māṇṭi maharṣeḥ śivaprasādena patnyāścaṭikākhyāyā udare garbhasya caturvarṣaparyantaṃ sthitāvapi tasya garbhasya bahirnirgamanābhāvaṃ nirīkṣya māṇṭinā tasya vahirnirgamanāyājñākaraṇam-janmasaṃsārabhītyā garbhasya bahirnirgamane'nicchāṃ dṛṣṭvā māṇṭinā śivaṃ prati prasādanam śivena tasya garbhasyāśvāsanārthaṃ nijavibhūtīnāmājñākaraṇam, śivavibhūtibhirdharmādibhistasya sāntvane kṛte sati garbhagṛhādbālakasya prasūtiḥ,tasya bālakasya kālādbhītimāpannatayā kālabhītināmakasya bilvavṛkṣasyādhastāttapaḥ kurvataḥ samīpe śaṃkareṇa nararūpeṇāgatya nijacaraṇāṃguṣṭhena gartapūraṇena tīrthaṃ nirmāya nijarūpaprakaṭanam tataḥ kālabhītiprārthanayā mahākālaliṅgarūpeṇa bhagavato'vasthānam, mahākālaprasādena kālabhītermocanānmahākālatvaprāptipūrvakaṃ mahākālabhagavataḥ prasādena nandigaṇarūpeṇa śivapratīhāratvaprāptivṛttāntavarṇanam, atha mahākālena karaṃdhamabhūpataye dharmasvarūpacatuyurgavyavasthādidharmakarmopadeśavarṇanam.. 155
1.4.d: 40 अथ महाकालनामकस्य सिद्धस्य चरित्रवर्णनम्, तत्र वाराणसीनिवासिनो माण्टि महर्षेः शिवप्रसादेन पत्न्याश्चटिकाख्याया उदरे गर्भस्य चतुर्वर्षपर्यन्तं स्थितावपि तस्य गर्भस्य बहिर्निर्गमनाभावं निरीक्ष्य माण्टिना तस्य वहिर्निर्गमनायाज्ञाकरणम्-जन्मसंसारभीत्या गर्भस्य बहिर्निर्गमनेऽनिच्छां दृष्ट्वा माण्टिना शिवं प्रति प्रसादनम् शिवेन तस्य गर्भस्याश्वासनार्थं निजविभूतीनामाज्ञाकरणम्, शिवविभूतिभिर्धर्मादिभिस्तस्य सान्त्वने कृते सति गर्भगृहाद्बालकस्य प्रसूतिः,तस्य बालकस्य कालाद्भीतिमापन्नतया कालभीतिनामकस्य बिल्ववृक्षस्याधस्तात्तपः कुर्वतः समीपे शंकरेण नररूपेणागत्य निजचरणांगुष्ठेन गर्तपूरणेन तीर्थं निर्माय निजरूपप्रकटनम् ततः कालभीतिप्रार्थनया महाकाललिङ्गरूपेण भगवतोऽवस्थानम्, महाकालप्रसादेन कालभीतेर्मोचनान्महाकालत्वप्राप्तिपूर्वकं महाकालभगवतः प्रसादेन नन्दिगणरूपेण शिवप्रतीहारत्वप्राप्तिवृत्तान्तवर्णनम्, अथ महाकालेन करंधमभूपतये धर्मस्वरूपचतुयुर्गव्यवस्थादिधर्मकर्मोपदेशवर्णनम्.. 155
1.4.m: 40 Then the account of the deeds of the perfected sage named Mahākāla: therein, by the grace of Śiva, a child was conceived in the womb of Caṭikā, the wife of the great sage Māṇṭi who resided in Vārāṇasī; Māṇṭi, seeing that although it remained in the womb for four years the embryo did not come out, commanded it to emerge; seeing its reluctance to emerge out of fear of birth and worldly existence, Māṇṭi propitiated Śiva; Śiva instructed his own manifestations to reassure the embryo; when the manifestations of Śiva, Dharma and others, comforted it, the child was born from the womb-chamber; because that boy was overcome with fear of Kāla, he was named Kālabhīti, and while he was performing austerities beneath a bilva tree, Śaṃkara arrived in human form, created a sacred ford by filling a pit with his big toe, and revealed his true form; then, at Kālabhīti's request, the Lord assumed the form of the Mahākāla liṅga; by the grace of Mahākāla, Kālabhīti was released, attained the status of Mahākāla, and by the grace of Lord Mahākāla obtained the role of Śiva's door-keeper in the form of a Nandi attendant; then a description of the teaching on the nature of righteousness, the arrangement of the four ages, and other duties and rites given by Mahākāla to King Karaṃdhama... 155

1.4.s: 41 atha karaṃdhamapṛṣṭena mahākālasiddhena brahmaviṣṇurudradevānāṃ bhaktiviṣayakasaṃśayanirākaraṇama, nānāvidhakarmabhedasavistaravivaraṇam, saṃkṣepato yathāśāstraśivapūjāvidhānavarṇanam, nityācaraṇīyasadācāravarṇanam, tataśca mahākālasiddhasya śivalokaprāptivṛttāṃtavarṇanam - -. -. - 161 1
1.4.d: 41 अथ करंधमपृष्टेन महाकालसिद्धेन ब्रह्मविष्णुरुद्रदेवानां भक्तिविषयकसंशयनिराकरणम, नानाविधकर्मभेदसविस्तरविवरणम्, संक्षेपतो यथाशास्त्रशिवपूजाविधानवर्णनम्, नित्याचरणीयसदाचारवर्णनम्, ततश्च महाकालसिद्धस्य शिवलोकप्राप्तिवृत्तांतवर्णनम् - -. -. - 161 1
1.4.m: 41 Then, questioned by Karaṃdhama, the perfected sage Mahākāla dispelled doubts concerning devotion to the gods Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Rudra, gave an elaborate explanation of the various kinds of rituals, described in brief the scriptural procedure for worshiping Śiva, and described the righteous conduct to be practiced daily; and then the account of the perfected sage Mahākāla's attainment of Śiva's world... 161 1

1.4.s: 42 atha nāradasthāpitavṛddhavāsudevamāhātmyavṛttāntavarṇanam, tatprasaṃgenaitareyabrāhmaṇacaritravarṇanam, mahīsāgarasaṃgamatīrasthahārītānvayotpannamāṇḍūkināmakasya brāhmaṇasyetarānāmnyāḥ patnyā udare samutpannasyaitareyabrāhmaṇasya janmāntarīyasiddhatve'pi prakṛtajanmani mūkabhāvaṃ samāśritya harimandire niraṃtaraṃ bhagavanmantrajapatatparatve sati mātuḥ khedāpanodārthaṃ śāstrapūtayā vāṇyā mātre saṃsārāsāratopadeśavarṇanapūrvakaṃ nijapūrṇajñānitvaprakaṭanenānandasamutpādanavṛttāntavarṇanam, tataścetarākhyāyāstanmātustasya mahājñānitvaṃ dṛṣṭvā'tyānandaprāptiḥ,tatastayormātāputrayoragrato bhagavato vāsudevasyāvirbhāvaḥ, aiterayakṛtā bhagavatstutiḥ, tatkṛtastutiprasannena bhagavataitareyavrāhmaṇāya varapradānam, bhagavatprasādenetareyabrāhmaṇasya vivāhādisrvamaṃgalaprāptipūrvakaihikasakalabhogabhogānaṃtaraṃ mokṣaprāptivṛttāntavarṇanam.... ......165.... 1
1.4.d: 42 अथ नारदस्थापितवृद्धवासुदेवमाहात्म्यवृत्तान्तवर्णनम्, तत्प्रसंगेनैतरेयब्राह्मणचरित्रवर्णनम्, महीसागरसंगमतीरस्थहारीतान्वयोत्पन्नमाण्डूकिनामकस्य ब्राह्मणस्येतरानाम्न्याः पत्न्या उदरे समुत्पन्नस्यैतरेयब्राह्मणस्य जन्मान्तरीयसिद्धत्वेऽपि प्रकृतजन्मनि मूकभावं समाश्रित्य हरिमन्दिरे निरंतरं भगवन्मन्त्रजपतत्परत्वे सति मातुः खेदापनोदार्थं शास्त्रपूतया वाण्या मात्रे संसारासारतोपदेशवर्णनपूर्वकं निजपूर्णज्ञानित्वप्रकटनेनानन्दसमुत्पादनवृत्तान्तवर्णनम्, ततश्चेतराख्यायास्तन्मातुस्तस्य महाज्ञानित्वं दृष्ट्वाऽत्यानन्दप्राप्तिः,ततस्तयोर्मातापुत्रयोरग्रतो भगवतो वासुदेवस्याविर्भावः, ऐतेरयकृता भगवत्स्तुतिः, तत्कृतस्तुतिप्रसन्नेन भगवतैतरेयव्राह्मणाय वरप्रदानम्, भगवत्प्रसादेनेतरेयब्राह्मणस्य विवाहादिस्र्वमंगलप्राप्तिपूर्वकैहिकसकलभोगभोगानंतरं मोक्षप्राप्तिवृत्तान्तवर्णनम्.... ......165.... 1
1.4.m: 42 Then the account of the māhātmya of Vṛddhavāsudeva installed by Nārada; in connection with that, the account of the deeds of the Aitareya brahmin: born from the womb of the wife named Itarā of a brahmin named Māṇḍūki of the lineage of Hārīta, who lived on the bank of the confluence of the Mahī and the sea, the Aitareya brahmin, although a perfected soul from a previous birth, assumed the state of a mute in his present life and constantly engaged in the repetition of the Lord's mantra in the temple of Hari; to remove his mother's sorrow, he taught his mother the vanity of worldly existence in speech purified by the scriptures, and produced joy in her by revealing his complete state of knowledge; then his mother, named Itarā, upon seeing his great wisdom, felt immense joy; then the appearance of Lord Vāsudeva before the mother and son; the hymn of praise sung by Aitareya to the Lord; pleased by the hymn composed by him, the Lord granted a boon to the Aitareya brahmin; and the account of the Aitareya brahmin obtaining all auspicious things such as marriage by the Lord's grace, and attaining liberation after enjoying all worldly pleasures... 165 1

1.4.s:
43 mahīsāgarasaṃgame nāradasthāpitabhaṭṭādityasūryamūrtivṛttāntavarṇanam, tatprasaṃgena sūryapūjā-
vidhivarṇanam. ............., 170 2
