1.4.m: 66 Next, after thirteen years, returning from their forest-dwelling to regain their own kingdom, when the Pāṇḍavas and Kauravas have assembled on the battlefield with their armies, and an enumeration of heroes capable of destroying all the enemy's host is begun, Caṇḍila, the son of Ghaṭotkaca, out of pride in demonstrating his supreme prowess over all, in order to give a test, unites the vermilion-like ash formerly given by the perfected brahmin named Vijaya through an oblation made before the Goddess to the tip of his arrow and, by discharging the arrow, indicates the vulnerable death-spots of the entire enemy host; next, seeing this, when all, led by Yudhiṣṭhira, praise him and a mighty acclaim ensues, Kṛṣṇa suddenly severs the head of that son of Ghaṭotkaca with his discus; next, seeing that he has severed his head, the fourteen goddesses, beginning with Siddhāmbikā, arrive on that battlefield before the Pāṇḍavas and others and Ghaṭotkaca, who are agitated by grief; and by recounting the narrative of Caṇḍila's previous birth as the yakṣa named Suvarcas, they console all; next, Śrī Kṛṣṇa states the reason for severing his head; then, by the Goddess's sprinkling of nectar, that head is rendered immortal; next, Śrī Kṛṣṇa grants a boon to Caṇḍila who is in the form of a head; next, by Śrī Kṛṣṇa's command, climbing the mountain peak situated near the battlefield, Barbarīka watches the battle of the Pāṇḍavas and Kauravas; next, after the conclusion of the great Bhārata war, to the pride-filled Bhīma, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, through the mouth of Barbarīka, confirms that the whole army was crushed by a certain Supreme Person who is identical with Hari-Hara, and recounts the narrative of dispelling his pride by showing him the skull of Kumbhakarṇa's head situated at the gate of Laṅkā; next, returning to the field of battle, Śrī Kṛṣṇa grants a boon to Barbarīka, the son of Ghaṭotkaca; next, the hymn to Barbarīka; the māhātmyas of the worship of Barbarīka; next, the māhātmya of Kedāreśvara, Atrīśvara, Nīlakaṇṭheśvara, and Jayāditya situated in Mahīnagara; thus ends the hearing and reciting of the māhātmya of the Guptakṣetra measuring seven krośas, otherwise known as the Mahīsāgarasaṃgamakṣetra... 209

1.4.s:
..atha śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇe prathame māheśvarakhaṇḍe kaumārikākhaṇḍaḥ prārabhyate.. 2 ..
śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ..
oṃ namo bṛhaspataye..
namatasmai brahmaṇe..
viṣṇave namaḥ..
..śrīmunaya ūcuḥ..
dakṣiṇārṇavatīreṣu yāni tīrthāni paṃca ca..
tāni brūhi viśālākṣa varṇayaṃtyati tāni ca.. 1.1 ..
sarvatīrthaphalaṃ yeṣu nāradādya vadaṃti ca..
teṣāṃ caritamāhātmyaṃ śrotumicchāmahe vayam.. 1.2 ..
1.4.d:
..अथ श्रीस्कांदे महापुराणे प्रथमे माहेश्वरखण्डे कौमारिकाखण्डः प्रारभ्यते.. 2 ..
श्रीगणेशाय नमः..
ओं नमो बृहस्पतये..
नमतस्मै ब्रह्मणे..
विष्णवे नमः..
..श्रीमुनय ऊचुः..
दक्षिणार्णवतीरेषु यानि तीर्थानि पंच च..
तानि ब्रूहि विशालाक्ष वर्णयंत्यति तानि च.. 1.1 ..
सर्वतीर्थफलं येषु नारदाद्य वदंति च..
तेषां चरितमाहात्म्यं श्रोतुमिच्छामहे वयम्.. 1.2 ..
1.4.m:
Now begins the Kaumārikākhaṇḍa in the first section, the Māheśvarakhaṇḍa, of the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa. 2.
Salutation to the glorious Gaṇeśa.
Oṃ, salutation to Bṛhaspati.
Salutation to that Brahmā.
Salutation to Viṣṇu.
The glorious sages said: / Speak of those five sacred fords on the shores of the southern ocean, / O large-eyed one, and describe them fully. 1.1
Those in which Nārada and others proclaim the fruit of all sacred fords— / we desire to hear their history and māhātmya. 1.2

1.4.s:
..ugraśravā uvāca..
śrṛṇudhvacatyadbhutapuṇyasatkathaṃ kumāranāthasya mahāprabhāvam..
dvaipāyano yanmama cāha pūrvaṃ harṣāburomodgamacarcitāṃgaḥ.. 1.3 ..
1.4.d:
..उग्रश्रवा उवाच..
श्रृणुध्वचत्यद्भुतपुण्यसत्कथं कुमारनाथस्य महाप्रभावम्..
द्वैपायनो यन्मम चाह पूर्वं हर्षाबुरोमोद्गमचर्चितांगः.. 1.3 ..
1.4.m: Ugraśravas said: / Hear the exceedingly wonderful and auspicious tale of the great power of Kumāranātha, / which Dvaipāyana formerly told me, his body covered with tears of joy and horripilation. 1.3

1.4.s:
kumāragītā gāthātra śrūyatāṃ munisattamāḥ..
yā sarvadevairmunibhiḥ pitṛbhiśca prapūjitā.. 1.4 ..
1.4.d:
कुमारगीता गाथात्र श्रूयतां मुनिसत्तमाः..
या सर्वदेवैर्मुनिभिः पितृभिश्च प्रपूजिता.. 1.4 ..
1.4.m: Let the song sung by Kumāra be heard here, O best of sages, / which is worshipped by all the gods, sages, and ancestors: 1.4

1.4.s:
madhvācārastaṃ bhatīrthaṃ yo niṣeveta mānavaḥ..
niyataṃ tasya vāsaḥ syādbrahmaloke yathā mama.. 1.5 ..
1.4.d:
मध्वाचारस्तं भतीर्थं यो निषेवेत मानवः..
नियतं तस्य वासः स्याद्ब्रह्मलोके यथा मम.. 1.5 ..
1.4.m: "A person of right conduct who resorts to the Stambhatīrtha, / his abode shall surely be in the world of Brahmā, just like mine. 1.5

1.4.s:
brahmalokādviṣṇulokastasmādapi śivasya ca..
putrāpriyatvāttasyāpi guhaloko mahattamaḥ.. 1.6 ..
1.4.d:
ब्रह्मलोकाद्विष्णुलोकस्तस्मादपि शिवस्य च..
पुत्राप्रियत्वात्तस्यापि गुहलोको महत्तमः.. 1.6 ..
1.4.m: Higher than the world of Brahmā is the world of Viṣṇu, and higher still than that is Śiva's; / and because he is his dear son, the world of Guha is the highest of all." 1.6

1.4.s:
atrāścaryakathā yā ca phālgunasya pureritā..
nāradena muniśreṣṭhāstāṃ vo vakṣyāmi vistarāt.. 1.7 ..
1.4.d:
अत्राश्चर्यकथा या च फाल्गुनस्य पुरेरिता..
नारदेन मुनिश्रेष्ठास्तां वो वक्ष्यामि विस्तरात्.. 1.7 ..
1.4.m: The wonderful story here that was formerly told to Phālguna / by Nārada, O best of sages, that I shall narrate to you in detail. 1.7

1.4.s:
purā nimitte kasmiṃścitkarīṭī maṇikūṭataḥ..
samudre dakṣiṇe'bhyāgātsnātuṃ tīrthāni paṃca ca.. 1.8 ..
1.4.d:
पुरा निमित्ते कस्मिंश्चित्करीटी मणिकूटतः..
समुद्रे दक्षिणेऽभ्यागात्स्नातुं तीर्थानि पंच च.. 1.8 ..
1.4.m: Formerly, for a certain reason, the crowned one [Arjuna] came from Maṇikūṭa / to the southern ocean to bathe in the five sacred fords, 1.8

1.4.s:
varjayaṃti sadā yāni bhayāttīrthāni tāpasāḥ..
kumāreśasya pūrvaṃ ca tīrthamasti muneḥ priyam.. 1.9 ..
1.4.d:
वर्जयंति सदा यानि भयात्तीर्थानि तापसाः..
कुमारेशस्य पूर्वं च तीर्थमस्ति मुनेः प्रियम्.. 1.9 ..
1.4.m: which sacred fords ascetics always avoid out of fear. / The first is the sacred ford of Kumāreśa, dear to the sage; 1.9

1.4.s:
staṃbheśasya dvitīyaṃ ca saubhadrasya muneḥ priyam..
barkareśvaramanyacca paulomīpriyamuttamam.. 1.10 ..
1.4.d:
स्तंभेशस्य द्वितीयं च सौभद्रस्य मुनेः प्रियम्..
बर्करेश्वरमन्यच्च पौलोमीप्रियमुत्तमम्.. 1.10 ..
1.4.m: and the second is that of Stambheśa, dear to the sage Saubhadra; / another is the excellent Barkareśvara, dear to Paulomī; 1.10

1.4.s:
caturthaṃ ca mahākālaṃ karaṃdhama nṛpapriyayam..
bharadvājasya tīrthaṃ ca siddheśākhyaṃ hi paṃcamam.. 1.11 ..
1.4.d:
चतुर्थं च महाकालं करंधम नृपप्रिययम्..
भरद्वाजस्य तीर्थं च सिद्धेशाख्यं हि पंचमम्.. 1.11 ..
1.4.m: and the fourth is Mahākāla, dear to King Karandhama; / and the fifth is the sacred ford of Bharadvāja, named Siddheśa. 1.11

1.4.s:
etāni paṃca tīrthāni dadarśa kurupuṃgavaḥ..
tapasvibhirvarjitāni mahāpuṇyāni tāni ca.. 1.12 ..
1.4.d:
एतानि पंच तीर्थानि ददर्श कुरुपुंगवः..
तपस्विभिर्वर्जितानि महापुण्यानि तानि च.. 1.12 ..
1.4.m: The bull of the Kurus saw these five sacred fords, / avoided by ascetics, yet exceedingly meritorious. 1.12

1.4.s:
dṛṣṭvā pārśve nāradīyānapṛcchata mahāmunīn..
tīrthānīmāni ramyāṇi prabhāvādbhutavaṃti ca.. 1.13 ..
1.4.d:
दृष्ट्वा पार्श्वे नारदीयानपृच्छत महामुनीन्..
तीर्थानीमानि रम्याणि प्रभावाद्भुतवंति च.. 1.13 ..
1.4.m: Seeing them, he questioned the great sages at his side, followers of Nārada: / "These sacred fords are delightful and possess wonderful power; 1.13

1.4.s:
kimarthaṃ brūta varjyaṃte sadaiva brahmavādibhiḥ..
..tāpasā ūcuḥ..
grāhaḥ paṃca vasaṃtyeṣu haraṃti ca tapodhanān.. 1.14 ..
1.4.d:
किमर्थं ब्रूत वर्ज्यंते सदैव ब्रह्मवादिभिः..
..तापसा ऊचुः..
ग्राहः पंच वसंत्येषु हरंति च तपोधनान्.. 1.14 ..
1.4.m: tell me, why are they always avoided by exponents of the Veda?" / The ascetics said: / "Five crocodiles dwell in them and carry off those rich in austerity. 1.14

1.4.s:
ata etāni varjyaṃte tīrthāni kurunaṃdana..
iti śrutvā mahābāhurgamanāya mano dadhe.. 1.15 ..
1.4.d:
अत एतानि वर्ज्यंते तीर्थानि कुरुनंदन..
इति श्रुत्वा महाबाहुर्गमनाय मनो दधे.. 1.15 ..
1.4.m: Therefore, O scion of Kuru, these sacred fords are avoided." / Hearing this, the mighty-armed one set his mind upon going. 1.15

1.4.s:
tatastaṃ tāpasāḥ procuthaṃtuṃ nārhasi phālguna..
bahavo bhakṣitā grāhai rājāno munayastathā.. 1.16 ..
1.4.d:
ततस्तं तापसाः प्रोचुथंतुं नार्हसि फाल्गुन..
बहवो भक्षिता ग्राहै राजानो मुनयस्तथा.. 1.16 ..
1.4.m: Then the ascetics said to him: "You ought not to go, O Phālguna! / Many kings and sages have been devoured by the crocodiles. 1.16

1.4.s:
tattva dvāraśavarṣāṇi tīrthānāmarbudeṣvapi..
snātaḥ kimetaistīrthaiste mā pataṃgavrato bhava.. 1.17 ..
1.4.d:
तत्त्व द्वारशवर्षाणि तीर्थानामर्बुदेष्वपि..
स्नातः किमेतैस्तीर्थैस्ते मा पतंगव्रतो भव.. 1.17 ..
1.4.m: Indeed, for twelve years you have bathed in hundreds of millions of sacred fords; / what need have you of these sacred fords? Do not follow the moth's vow!" 1.17

1.4.s:
..arjuna uvāca..
yaduktaṃ karuṇāsāraiḥ sāraṃ kiṃ tadihocyatām..
dharmārthī manujo yaśca na sa vāryo mahātmabhiḥ.. 1.18 ..
1.4.d:
..अर्जुन उवाच..
यदुक्तं करुणासारैः सारं किं तदिहोच्यताम्..
धर्मार्थी मनुजो यश्च न स वार्यो महात्मभिः.. 1.18 ..
1.4.m:
Arjuna said:
What has been spoken by [you], the essence of compassion—let the essence of that be told here.
A human being who desires righteousness should not be restrained by great-souled ones.

1.4.s:
dharmakāmaṃ hi manujaṃ yo vārayati maṃdadhīḥ..
tadāśritasya jagato niḥśvāsairbhasmasādbhavet.. 1.19 ..
1.4.d:
धर्मकामं हि मनुजं यो वारयति मंदधीः..
तदाश्रितस्य जगतो निःश्वासैर्भस्मसाद्भवेत्.. 1.19 ..
1.4.m:
For whatever dull-witted person restrains a man who desires righteousness,
the world dependent on him would turn to ashes through his sighs.

1.4.s:
yajjīvitaṃ cācirāṃśusamānakṣaṇabhaṃguram..
tacceddharmakṛte yāti yātu doṣo'sti ko nanu.. 1.20 ..
1.4.d:
यज्जीवितं चाचिरांशुसमानक्षणभंगुरम्..
तच्चेद्धर्मकृते याति यातु दोषोऽस्ति को ननु.. 1.20 ..
1.4.m:
Since life is as momentary and fragile as a flash of lightning,
if it is spent for the sake of righteousness, let it go; what fault is there indeed?

1.4.s:
jīvitaṃ ca dhanaṃ dārāḥ putrāḥ kṣetragṛhāṇi ca..
yānti yeṣaāṃ dharmakṛte ta eva bhuvi mānavāḥ.. 1.21 ..
1.4.d:
जीवितं च धनं दाराः पुत्राः क्षेत्रगृहाणि च..
यान्ति येषआं धर्मकृते त एव भुवि मानवाः.. 1.21 ..
1.4.m:
Those whose life, wealth, wives, sons, fields, and houses
are spent for the sake of righteousness, they alone are truly human on this earth.

1.4.s:
..tāpasā ūcuḥ..
evaṃ te bruvataḥ pārtha dīrghamāyuḥ pravardhatām..
sadā dharme ratirbhūyādyāhi svaṃ kuru vāṃchitam.. 1.22 ..
1.4.d:
..तापसा ऊचुः..
एवं ते ब्रुवतः पार्थ दीर्घमायुः प्रवर्धताम्..
सदा धर्मे रतिर्भूयाद्याहि स्वं कुरु वांछितम्.. 1.22 ..
1.4.m:
The ascetics said:
As you speak thus, O Pārtha, may a long life increase for you!
May your delight always be in righteousness; go, fulfill your desire!

1.4.s:
evamuktaḥ praṇamyaitānāśīrbhirabhisaṃstutaḥ..
jagāma tāni tīrthāni draṣṭuṃ bharatasattamaḥ.. 1.23 ..
1.4.d:
एवमुक्तः प्रणम्यैतानाशीर्भिरभिसंस्तुतः..
जगाम तानि तीर्थानि द्रष्टुं भरतसत्तमः.. 1.23 ..
1.4.m:
Having been addressed thus, having bowed to them and been praised with blessings,
the best of the Bharatas went to see those sacred fords.

1.4.s:
tataḥ saubhadramāsādya maharṣestīrthumuttamam..
vigāhya tarasā vīraḥ snānaṃ cakre paraṃtapaḥ.. 1.24 ..
1.4.d:
ततः सौभद्रमासाद्य महर्षेस्तीर्थुमुत्तमम्..
विगाह्य तरसा वीरः स्नानं चक्रे परंतपः.. 1.24 ..
1.4.m:
Then, having reached Saubhadra, the excellent sacred ford of the great seer,
the hero, the scorcher of foes, plunged in with haste and performed his ritual ablution.

1.4.s:
atha taṃ puruṣavyāghramaṃtarjalacaro mahān..
nijagrāha jale grāhaḥ kuṃtīputraṃ dhanaṃjayam.. 1.25 ..
1.4.d:
अथ तं पुरुषव्याघ्रमंतर्जलचरो महान्..
निजग्राह जले ग्राहः कुंतीपुत्रं धनंजयम्.. 1.25 ..
1.4.m:
Then a huge crocodile moving underwater seized that tiger among men,
the son of Kuntī, Dhanañjaya, in the water.

1.4.s:
tamādāyaiva kauteyo visphuraṃtaṃ jalecaram..
udatiṣṭhanmahābāhurbalena balināṃ varaḥ.. 1.26 ..
1.4.d:
तमादायैव कौतेयो विस्फुरंतं जलेचरम्..
उदतिष्ठन्महाबाहुर्बलेन बलिनां वरः.. 1.26 ..
1.4.m:
Taking that squirming water-creature [with him],
the mighty-armed son of Kuntī, the best of the strong, rose up by his strength.

1.4.s:
uddhṛtaścaiva tu grāhaḥ so'rjunena yaśasvinā..
babhūva nārī kalyāṇī sarvābharaṇabhūṣitā.. 1.27 ..
1.4.d:
उद्धृतश्चैव तु ग्राहः सोऽर्जुनेन यशस्विना..
बभूव नारी कल्याणी सर्वाभरणभूषिता.. 1.27 ..
1.4.m:
And that crocodile, lifted out by the renowned Arjuna,
became an auspicious woman adorned with all ornaments,

1.4.s:
dīpyamānaśikhā viprā divyarūpā manoramā..
tadadbhutaṃ mahaddṛṣṭvā kuṃtīputro dhanaṃjayaḥ.. 1.28 ..
1.4.d:
दीप्यमानशिखा विप्रा दिव्यरूपा मनोरमा..
तदद्भुतं महद्दृष्ट्वा कुंतीपुत्रो धनंजयः.. 1.28 ..
1.4.m:
with a shining crest, O brahmins, having a divine form and pleasing to the mind.
Seeing that great wonder, the son of Kuntī, Dhanañjaya,

1.4.s:
tāṃ striyaṃ paramaprīta idaṃ vacanamabravīt..
kā vai tvamasi kalyāṇi kuto vā jalacāriṇī.. 1.29 ..
1.4.d:
तां स्त्रियं परमप्रीत इदं वचनमब्रवीत्..
का वै त्वमसि कल्याणि कुतो वा जलचारिणी.. 1.29 ..
1.4.m:
exceedingly pleased, addressed this speech to that woman:
'Who are you, auspicious one, or whence did you move in the water?

1.4.s:
kimarthaṃ ca mahātpāpamidaṃ kṛtavatī hyasi..
..nāryuvāca..
apsarā hyasmi kauteya devāraṇyanivāsinī.. 1.30 ..
1.4.d:
किमर्थं च महात्पापमिदं कृतवती ह्यसि..
..नार्युवाच..
अप्सरा ह्यस्मि कौतेय देवारण्यनिवासिनी.. 1.30 ..
1.4.m:
And for what reason did you commit this great sin?'
The woman said:
'I am an apsaras, O son of Kuntī, dwelling in the forest of the gods.

1.4.s:
iṣṭā dhanapaternityaṃ varcānāma mahābala..
mama sakhyaścatasro'nyāḥ sarvāḥ kāmagamāḥ śubhāḥ.. 1.31 ..
1.4.d:
इष्टा धनपतेर्नित्यं वर्चानाम महाबल..
मम सख्यश्चतस्रोऽन्याः सर्वाः कामगमाः शुभाः.. 1.31 ..
1.4.m:
Beloved ever of the lord of wealth, named Varcā, O you of great might!
I have four other companions, all moving at will, auspicious.

1.4.s:
tābhiḥ sārdhaṃ prayātāsmi devarājaniveśanāt..
tataḥ paśyāmahe sarvā brāhmaṇaṃ cāniketanam.. 1.32 ..
1.4.d:
ताभिः सार्धं प्रयातास्मि देवराजनिवेशनात्..
ततः पश्यामहे सर्वा ब्राह्मणं चानिकेतनम्.. 1.32 ..
1.4.m:
Together with them I set forth from the abode of the king of gods.
Then we all saw a homeless brahmin,

1.4.s:
rūpavaṃtamadhīyānamekamekāṃtacāriṇam..
tasya vai tapasā vīra tadvanaṃ tejasāvṛtam.. 1.33 ..
1.4.d:
रूपवंतमधीयानमेकमेकांतचारिणम्..
तस्य वै तपसा वीर तद्वनं तेजसावृतम्.. 1.33 ..
1.4.m:
handsome, studying [the Vedas], alone, wandering in solitude.
By his austerity indeed, O hero, that forest was enveloped in fiery splendor;

1.4.s:
āditya iva taṃ deśaṃ kṛtsnamevānva bhāsayat..
tasya dṛṣṭvā tapastādṛgrūpaṃ cādbhutadarśanam.. 1.34 ..
1.4.d:
आदित्य इव तं देशं कृत्स्नमेवान्व भासयत्..
तस्य दृष्ट्वा तपस्तादृग्रूपं चाद्भुतदर्शनम्.. 1.34 ..
1.4.m:
like the sun he illuminated that whole region.
Having seen his austerity of such a kind, and his form wonderful to behold,

1.4.s:
avatīrṇāsti taṃ deśaṃ tapovighnacikīrṣayā..
ahaṃ ca saurabheyī ca sāmeyī budbudālatā.. 1.35 ..
1.4.d:
अवतीर्णास्ति तं देशं तपोविघ्नचिकीर्षया..
अहं च सौरभेयी च सामेयी बुद्बुदालता.. 1.35 ..
1.4.m:
we descended to that region with the desire to cause an obstacle to his austerity—
myself, and Saurabheyī, Sāmeyī, Budbudā, [and] Latā.

1.4.s:
yaugapadyena taṃ vipramabhyagacchāma bhārata..
gāyaṃtyo lalamānāśca lobhayaṃtyaśca taṃ dvijam.. 1.36 ..
1.4.d:
यौगपद्येन तं विप्रमभ्यगच्छाम भारत..
गायंत्यो ललमानाश्च लोभयंत्यश्च तं द्विजम्.. 1.36 ..
1.4.m:
Simultaneously we approached that brahmin, O Bhārata,
singing, flirting, and enticing that twice-born.

1.4.s:
sa ca nāsmāsu kṛtavānmanovīraḥ kathaṃcana..
nākaṃpata mahātejāḥ sthitastapasi nirmale.. 1.37 ..
1.4.d:
स च नास्मासु कृतवान्मनोवीरः कथंचन..
नाकंपत महातेजाः स्थितस्तपसि निर्मले.. 1.37 ..
1.4.m:
Yet that heroic one did not set his mind upon us in any way;
endowed with great splendor, he did not tremble, remaining steadfast in pure austerity.

1.4.s:
so'śapatkupito'smāsu brāhmaṇaḥ kṣatriyarṣabha..
grāhabhūtā jale yūyaṃ bhaviṣyatha śataṃ samāḥ.. 1.38 ..
1.4.d:
सोऽशपत्कुपितोऽस्मासु ब्राह्मणः क्षत्रियर्षभ..
ग्राहभूता जले यूयं भविष्यथ शतं समाः.. 1.38 ..
1.4.m:
Becoming angry, that brahmin cursed us, O bull of the kṣatriyas:
"Having become crocodiles in the water, you shall remain for a hundred years."

1.4.s:
tato vayaṃ pravyathitāḥ sarvā bharatasattama..
āyātāḥ śaraṇaṃ vipraṃ tapodhanamakalmaṣam.. 1.39 ..
1.4.d:
ततो वयं प्रव्यथिताः सर्वा भरतसत्तम..
आयाताः शरणं विप्रं तपोधनमकल्मषम्.. 1.39 ..
1.4.m:
Then, all of us greatly afflicted, O best of the Bharatas,
came for refuge to the brahmin whose wealth was austerity, the faultless one:

1.4.s:
rūpeṇa vayasā caiva kaṃdarpeṇa ca darpitāḥ..
ayuktaṃ kṛtavatyaḥ sma kṣaṃtumarhasi no dvija.. 1.40 ..
1.4.d:
रूपेण वयसा चैव कंदर्पेण च दर्पिताः..
अयुक्तं कृतवत्यः स्म क्षंतुमर्हसि नो द्विज.. 1.40 ..
1.4.m:
"Arrogant on account of our beauty, youth, and love,
we have done what was improper; you ought to forgive us, O twice-born!

1.4.s:
eṣa eva vadho'smākaṃ sa paryāptastapodhana..
yadvayaṃ śaṃsitātmānaṃ pralobdhuṃ tvāmupāgatāḥ.. 1.41 ..
1.4.d:
एष एव वधोऽस्माकं स पर्याप्तस्तपोधन..
यद्वयं शंसितात्मानं प्रलोब्धुं त्वामुपागताः.. 1.41 ..
1.4.m:
This itself is our death; that is sufficient, O you whose wealth is austerity,
that we have approached to seduce you whose self is praised!

1.4.s:
avadhyāśca striyaḥ sṛṣṭā manyaṃte dharmaciṃtakāḥ..
tasmāddharmeṇa dharmajña eṣa vādo manīṣiṇām.. 1.42 ..
1.4.d:
अवध्याश्च स्त्रियः सृष्टा मन्यंते धर्मचिंतकाः..
तस्माद्धर्मेण धर्मज्ञ एष वादो मनीषिणाम्.. 1.42 ..
1.4.m:
And women are created not to be killed, so consider the ponderers of righteousness;
therefore, in accordance with righteousness, O knower of righteousness, this is the doctrine of the wise.

1.4.s:
śaraṇaṃ ca prapannānāṃ śiṣṭāḥ kurvaṃti pālanam..
śaraṇyaṃ tvāṃ prapannāḥ smastasmāttvaṃ kṣaṃtumarhasi.. 1.43 ..
1.4.d:
शरणं च प्रपन्नानां शिष्टाः कुर्वंति पालनम्..
शरण्यं त्वां प्रपन्नाः स्मस्तस्मात्त्वं क्षंतुमर्हसि.. 1.43 ..
1.4.m:
And the virtuous afford protection to those who have sought refuge;
we have sought refuge in you, a protector; therefore you ought to forgive us."

1.4.s:
evamuktastu dharmātmā brāhmaṇaḥ śubhakarmakṛt..
prasādaṃ kṛtavāñchūraravisomasamaprabhaḥ.. 1.44 ..
1.4.d:
एवमुक्तस्तु धर्मात्मा ब्राह्मणः शुभकर्मकृत्..
प्रसादं कृतवाञ्छूररविसोमसमप्रभः.. 1.44 ..
1.4.m:
Addressed thus, the righteous brahmin who performs auspicious deeds,
valiant, with radiance equal to the sun and moon, showed grace.

1.4.s:
..brāhmaṇa uvāca..
bhavatīnāṃ caritreṇa parimuhyāmi cetasi..
aho dhārṣṭyamaho moho yatpāpāya pravartanam.. 1.45 ..
1.4.d:
..ब्राह्मण उवाच..
भवतीनां चरित्रेण परिमुह्यामि चेतसि..
अहो धार्ष्ट्यमहो मोहो यत्पापाय प्रवर्तनम्.. 1.45 ..
1.4.m:
The brahmin said:
'My mind is bewildered by your conduct!
Ah, what audacity! Ah, what delusion, to engage in sin!

1.4.s:
masta kasthāyinaṃ mṛtyuṃ yadi paśyedayaṃ janaḥ..
āhāro'pi na roceta kimutākāryakāritā.. 1.46 ..
1.4.d:
मस्त कस्थायिनं मृत्युं यदि पश्येदयं जनः..
आहारोऽपि न रोचेत किमुताकार्यकारिता.. 1.46 ..
1.4.m:
If a person were to see death standing upon their head,
even food would not be pleasing, let alone the doing of improper deeds!

1.4.s:
āho mānuṣyakaṃ janma sarvajanmasu durlabham..
tṛṇavatkriyate kaiścidyoṣinmūḍhairdurādharaiḥ.. 1.47 ..
1.4.d:
आहो मानुष्यकं जन्म सर्वजन्मसु दुर्लभम्..
तृणवत्क्रियते कैश्चिद्योषिन्मूढैर्दुराधरैः.. 1.47 ..
1.4.m:
Ah, human birth is rare among all births,
yet it is treated like a blade of grass by some who are infatuated with women and uncontrollable!

1.4.s:
tānvayaṃ samapṛcchāmo janirvaḥ kiṃnimittataḥ..
ko vā lābho vicāryaitanmanāsā saha procyatām.. 1.48 ..
1.4.d:
तान्वयं समपृच्छामो जनिर्वः किंनिमित्ततः..
को वा लाभो विचार्यैतन्मनासा सह प्रोच्यताम्.. 1.48 ..
1.4.m:
We ask them: for what purpose is your birth?
Or what is the gain? Having reflected on this with the mind, let it be said!

1.4.s:
na caitāḥ parinindāmo janiryārbhyaḥ pravartate..
kevalaṃ tānviniṃdāmo ye ca tāsu nirargalāḥ.. 1.49 ..
1.4.d:
न चैताः परिनिन्दामो जनिर्यार्भ्यः प्रवर्तते..
केवलं तान्विनिंदामो ये च तासु निरर्गलाः.. 1.49 ..
1.4.m:
We do not blame those [women] from whom birth proceeds;
we only blame those men who are unbridled toward them.

1.4.s:
yataḥ padmabhuvā sṛṣṭaṃ mithunaṃ viśvavṛddhaye..
tattathā paripālyaṃ vai nātra doṣo'sti kaścana.. 1.50 ..
1.4.d:
यतः पद्मभुवा सृष्टं मिथुनं विश्ववृद्धये..
तत्तथा परिपाल्यं वै नात्र दोषोऽस्ति कश्चन.. 1.50 ..
1.4.m:
Because the couple was created by the lotus-born [Brahmā] for the increase of the universe,
that is to be maintained in that way; there is no fault in this whatever.

1.4.s:
yā bāṃdhavaiḥ pradattā syādvahnidvijasamāgame..
gārhasthyapālanaṃ dhanyaṃ tayā sākaṃ hi sarvadam.. 1.51 ..
1.4.d:
या बांधवैः प्रदत्ता स्याद्वह्निद्विजसमागमे..
गार्हस्थ्यपालनं धन्यं तया साकं हि सर्वदम्.. 1.51 ..
1.4.m:
She who is given by kinsmen in the presence of fire and the twice-born—
the maintenance of household life with her is blessed, indeed granting everything.

1.4.s:
yathāprakṛti puṃyomo yatnenāpi parasparam..
sādhyāmāno guṇāya syādaguṇāyāpyasādhitaḥ.. 1.52 ..
1.4.d:
यथाप्रकृति पुंयोमो यत्नेनापि परस्परम्..
साध्यामानो गुणाय स्यादगुणायाप्यसाधितः.. 1.52 ..
1.4.m:
Just as the natural union of a man [and woman], even when cultivated with effort
for one another, leads to virtue, while uncultivated it leads to vice,

1.4.s:
evaṃ yatnātsādhyamānaṃ svakaṃ gārhasthyamuttamam..
guṇāya mahate bhūyādaguṇāyāpyasādhitam.. 1.53 ..
1.4.d:
एवं यत्नात्साध्यमानं स्वकं गार्हस्थ्यमुत्तमम्..
गुणाय महते भूयादगुणायाप्यसाधितम्.. 1.53 ..
1.4.m:
so one's own excellent household life, being cultivated with effort,
leads to great virtue, while uncultivated it leads to vice.

1.4.s:
pure paṃcamukhe dvāḥstha ekādaśabhaṭairyutaḥ..
sākaṃ nāryā bahvapatyaḥ sa kathaṃ syādacetanaḥ.. 1.54 ..
1.4.d:
पुरे पंचमुखे द्वाःस्थ एकादशभटैर्युतः..
साकं नार्या बह्वपत्यः स कथं स्यादचेतनः.. 1.54 ..
1.4.m:
In a city with five gates, the gatekeeper accompanied by eleven warriors,
together with a woman, having many offspring—how could he be devoid of consciousness?

1.4.s:
yaścastriyā samāyogaḥ paṃcayajñādikarmabhiḥ..
viśvopakṛtaye sṛṣṭā mūḍhairhā sādhyate'nyathā.. 1.55 ..
1.4.d:
यश्चस्त्रिया समायोगः पंचयज्ञादिकर्मभिः..
विश्वोपकृतये सृष्टा मूढैर्हा साध्यतेऽन्यथा.. 1.55 ..
1.4.m:
And the union with a woman by rites such as the five sacrifices,
created for the benefit of the universe—alas, it is undertaken otherwise by fools!

1.4.s:
aho śrṛṇudhvaṃ no cedvaḥ śuśrūṣā jāyate śubhā..
tathāpi bāhumuddhṛtya rorūyāmaḥ śrṛṇoti kaḥ.. 1.56 ..
1.4.d:
अहो श्रृणुध्वं नो चेद्वः शुश्रूषा जायते शुभा..
तथापि बाहुमुद्धृत्य रोरूयामः श्रृणोति कः.. 1.56 ..
1.4.m:
Ah! Listen! If a good desire to hear does not arise in you,
nonetheless, raising our arms, we cry out aloud: who listens?

1.4.s:
ṣaḍdhātusāraṃ tadvīryaṃ samānaṃ parihāya ca..
vinikṣepe kuyonau tu tasyedaṃ proktavānyamaḥ.. 1.57 ..
1.4.d:
षड्धातुसारं तद्वीर्यं समानं परिहाय च..
विनिक्षेपे कुयोनौ तु तस्येदं प्रोक्तवान्यमः.. 1.57 ..
1.4.m:
And shedding that semen, the essence of the six elements, equally,
if one casts it into an improper womb, Yama has declared this concerning him:

1.4.s:
prathamaṃ cauṣadhīdrogdhā ātmadrogdhā tataḥ punaḥ..
pitṛdrogdhā viśvadrogdhā yātyaṃdhaṃ śāśvatīḥ samāḥ.. 1.58 ..
1.4.d:
प्रथमं चौषधीद्रोग्धा आत्मद्रोग्धा ततः पुनः..
पितृद्रोग्धा विश्वद्रोग्धा यात्यंधं शाश्वतीः समाः.. 1.58 ..
1.4.m:
"First he is an injurer of plants, then further an injurer of himself,
an injurer of the ancestors, an injurer of the universe; he goes to darkness for eternal years."

1.4.s:
manuṣyaṃ pitaro devā munayo mānavāstathā..
bhṛtāni copajīvaṃti tadarthaṃ niyato bhavet.. 1.59 ..
1.4.d:
मनुष्यं पितरो देवा मुनयो मानवास्तथा..
भृतानि चोपजीवंति तदर्थं नियतो भवेत्.. 1.59 ..
1.4.m:
Upon a human being, ancestors, gods, sages, and humans,
as well as dependents, subsist; for that purpose one should be self-restrained.

1.4.s:
vacasā manasā caiva jihvayā karaśrotrakaiḥ..
dāṃtamāhurhi sattīrthaṃ kākatīrthamataḥ param.. 1.60 ..
1.4.d:
वचसा मनसा चैव जिह्वया करश्रोत्रकैः..
दांतमाहुर्हि सत्तीर्थं काकतीर्थमतः परम्.. 1.60 ..
1.4.m:
By speech, by mind, by tongue, hands, and ears,
one who is restrained is said to be a true sacred ford; beyond this is a crow's ford.

1.4.s:
kākaprāye nare yasminramaṃte tāmasā janāḥ..
haṃso'yamiti devānāṃ ko'rthastena viciṃtyatām.. 1.61 ..
1.4.d:
काकप्राये नरे यस्मिन्रमंते तामसा जनाः..
हंसोऽयमिति देवानां कोऽर्थस्तेन विचिंत्यताम्.. 1.61 ..
1.4.m:
In a crow-like man in whom dark-natured persons take delight,
thinking "This is a swan!"—what purpose do the gods have with him? Let that be considered!'

1.4.s:
evaṃvidhaṃ hi viśvasya nirmāṇaṃ smaratohṛdi..
api kṛte trilokyāśca kathaṃ pāpe ramenmanaḥ.. 1.62 ..
1.4.d:
एवंविधं हि विश्वस्य निर्माणं स्मरतोहृदि..
अपि कृते त्रिलोक्याश्च कथं पापे रमेन्मनः.. 1.62 ..
1.4.m: "Indeed, remembering in the heart such an arrangement of the universe, / even if [sovereignty over] the three worlds were gained, how could the mind take delight in sin? 1.62

1.4.s:
tadidaṃ cānyamartyānāṃ śāstradṛṣṭamaho striyaḥ..
yamaloke mayā dṛṣṭaṃ muhye pratyakṣataḥ katham.. 1.63 ..
1.4.d:
तदिदं चान्यमर्त्यानां शास्त्रदृष्टमहो स्त्रियः..
यमलोके मया दृष्टं मुह्ये प्रत्यक्षतः कथम्.. 1.63 ..
1.4.m: And that is seen by other mortals through scripture, O women; / it has been seen by me directly in Yama's realm—how could I be deluded? 1.63

1.4.s:
bhavatīṣu ca kaḥ kopo ye yadarthe hi nirmitāḥ..
te tamarthaṃ prakurvaṃti satyamastubhameva ca.. 1.64 ..
1.4.d:
भवतीषु च कः कोपो ये यदर्थे हि निर्मिताः..
ते तमर्थं प्रकुर्वंति सत्यमस्तुभमेव च.. 1.64 ..
1.4.m: And what anger can there be toward you? For those who are made for a certain purpose / carry out that purpose; let it indeed be true. 1.64

1.4.s:
śataṃ sahasraṃ viśvaṃ ca sarvamakṣaya vācakam..
parimāṇaṃ śataṃ tveva naitadakṣayyavācakam.. 1.65 ..
1.4.d:
शतं सहस्रं विश्वं च सर्वमक्षय वाचकम्..
परिमाणं शतं त्वेव नैतदक्षय्यवाचकम्.. 1.65 ..
1.4.m: A hundred, a thousand, and all—these words signify the imperishable; / but indeed 'a hundred' as a measure does not signify the imperishable [here]. 1.65

1.4.s:
yadā ca vo grāhabhūtā gṛhṇatīḥ puruṣāñjale..
utkarṣati jalātkaścitsthale puruṣasattamaḥ.. 1.66 ..
1.4.d:
यदा च वो ग्राहभूता गृह्णतीः पुरुषाञ्जले..
उत्कर्षति जलात्कश्चित्स्थले पुरुषसत्तमः.. 1.66 ..
1.4.m: And when you, having become crocodiles, seizing men in the water, / are pulled up from the water onto dry land by an excellent man, 1.66

1.4.s:
tadā yūyaṃ punaḥ sarvāḥ svaṃ rūpaṃ pratipatsyatha..
anṛtaṃ noktapūrvaṃ me hasatāpi kadācana..
kalyāṇasya supṛktasya śuddhistadvadvarā hi vaḥ.. 1.67 ..
1.4.d:
तदा यूयं पुनः सर्वाः स्वं रूपं प्रतिपत्स्यथ..
अनृतं नोक्तपूर्वं मे हसतापि कदाचन..
कल्याणस्य सुपृक्तस्य शुद्धिस्तद्वद्वरा हि वः.. 1.67 ..
1.4.m: then all of you will attain your own forms again. / An untruth has never been spoken by me, even in jest. / Your purification will be just like the excellent purification of one well-joined to good fortune." 1.67

1.4.s:
..nāryuvāca..
tatobhivādya taṃ vipraṃ kṛtvā caiva pradakṣiṇam.. 1.68 ..
1.4.d:
..नार्युवाच..
ततोभिवाद्य तं विप्रं कृत्वा चैव प्रदक्षिणम्.. 1.68 ..
1.4.m: The woman said: / "Then, having bowed to that brahmin and circumambulated him, 1.68

1.4.s:
aciṃtayāmāpasṛtya tasmāddeśātsuduḥkhitāḥ..
kva nu nāma vayaṃ sarvāḥ kālenālpena taṃ naram.. 1.69 ..
1.4.d:
अचिंतयामापसृत्य तस्माद्देशात्सुदुःखिताः..
क्व नु नाम वयं सर्वाः कालेनाल्पेन तं नरम्.. 1.69 ..
1.4.m: we departed from that place, deeply afflicted, and wondered: / 'Where on earth might all of us, in a short time, 1.69

1.4.s:
samāgacchema yo naḥ svaṃ rūpamāpādayetpunaḥ..
tā vayaṃ ciṃtayitveha muhūrtādiva bhārata.. 1.70 ..
1.4.d:
समागच्छेम यो नः स्वं रूपमापादयेत्पुनः..
ता वयं चिंतयित्वेह मुहूर्तादिव भारत.. 1.70 ..
1.4.m: meet that man who could restore our own forms to us?' / As we were pondering this here, after merely a moment, O descendant of Bharata, 1.70

1.4.s:
dṛṣṭavatyo mahābhāgaṃ devarṣimatha nāradam..
sarvā dṛṣṭāḥ sma taṃ dṛṣṭvā devarṣimamitadyutim.. 1.71 ..
1.4.d:
दृष्टवत्यो महाभागं देवर्षिमथ नारदम्..
सर्वा दृष्टाः स्म तं दृष्ट्वा देवर्षिममितद्युतिम्.. 1.71 ..
1.4.m: we saw the highly fortunate celestial seer, Nārada. / Having seen that celestial seer of boundless splendor, we were all seen [by him]. 1.71

1.4.s:
abhivādya ca taṃ pārtha sthitāḥ smo vyathitānanāḥ..
sa no'pṛcchaddṛḥkhamūlamuktavatyo vayaṃ ca tam.. 1.72 ..
1.4.d:
अभिवाद्य च तं पार्थ स्थिताः स्मो व्यथिताननाः..
स नोऽपृच्छद्दृःखमूलमुक्तवत्यो वयं च तम्.. 1.72 ..
1.4.m: And having greeted him, O son of Pṛthā, we stood with distressed faces. / He asked us the root of our sorrow, and we told him. 1.72

1.4.s:
śrutvā tacca yathātattvamidaṃ vacanamabravīt..
dakṣiṇe sāgare'nūpe paṃca tīrthāni saṃtivai.. 1.73 ..
1.4.d:
श्रुत्वा तच्च यथातत्त्वमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्..
दक्षिणे सागरेऽनूपे पंच तीर्थानि संतिवै.. 1.73 ..
1.4.m: And having heard that as it truly was, he spoke these words: / 'On the shore of the southern ocean there are indeed five sacred fords, 1.73

1.4.s:
puṇyāni ramaṇīyāni tāni gacchata mā ciram..
tatrasthāḥ puruṣavyāghraḥ pāṃḍavo vo dhanaṃjayaḥ.. 1.74 ..
1.4.d:
पुण्यानि रमणीयानि तानि गच्छत मा चिरम्..
तत्रस्थाः पुरुषव्याघ्रः पांडवो वो धनंजयः.. 1.74 ..
1.4.m: meritorious and delightful; go to them without delay. / While you dwell there, that tiger among men, the Pāṇḍava Dhanañjaya, 1.74

1.4.s:
mokṣayiṣyati śuddhātmā duḥkhā dasmānna saṃśayaḥ..
tasya sarvā vayaṃ vīra śrutvā vākyamihāgatāḥ.. 1.75 ..
1.4.d:
मोक्षयिष्यति शुद्धात्मा दुःखा दस्मान्न संशयः..
तस्य सर्वा वयं वीर श्रुत्वा वाक्यमिहागताः.. 1.75 ..
1.4.m: a pure-souled one, will free you from this sorrow; of this there is no doubt.' / O hero, having heard his words, all of us came here. 1.75

1.4.s:
tvamidaṃ satyavacanaṃ kartumarhasi pāṃḍava..
tvadvidhānāṃ hi sādhūnāṃ janma dīnopakārakam.. 1.76 ..
1.4.d:
त्वमिदं सत्यवचनं कर्तुमर्हसि पांडव..
त्वद्विधानां हि साधूनां जन्म दीनोपकारकम्.. 1.76 ..
1.4.m: You ought to make this word true, O Pāṇḍava; / for the birth of virtuous men like you brings aid to the wretched." 1.76

1.4.s:
śrutveti vacanaṃ tasyāḥ sasnau tīrtheṣvanukramāt..
grāhabhūtāścojjahāra yathāpūrvāḥ sa pāṃḍavaḥ.. 1.77 ..
1.4.d:
श्रुत्वेति वचनं तस्याः सस्नौ तीर्थेष्वनुक्रमात्..
ग्राहभूताश्चोज्जहार यथापूर्वाः स पांडवः.. 1.77 ..
1.4.m: Having heard her speech, he bathed in the sacred fords in succession, / and that Pāṇḍava lifted up those who had become crocodiles, restored to their former states. 1.77

1.4.s:
tataḥ praṇamya tā vīraṃ procyamānā jayāśiṣaḥ..
gaṃtuṃ kṛtābhilāṣāśca prāha pārtho dhanaṃjayaḥ.. 1.78 ..
1.4.d:
ततः प्रणम्य ता वीरं प्रोच्यमाना जयाशिषः..
गंतुं कृताभिलाषाश्च प्राह पार्थो धनंजयः.. 1.78 ..
1.4.m: Then, having bowed to the hero and pronounced blessings of victory, / as they were eager to depart, the son of Pṛthā, Dhanañjaya, said: 1.78

1.4.s:
eṣa me hṛdi saṃdehaḥ sudṛḍhaḥ parivartate..
kasmādvonāradamuniranujajñe pravāsitum.. 1.79 ..
1.4.d:
एष मे हृदि संदेहः सुदृढः परिवर्तते..
कस्माद्वोनारदमुनिरनुजज्ञे प्रवासितुम्.. 1.79 ..
1.4.m: "This doubt turns firmly within my heart: / Why did the sage Nārada permit you to dwell abroad [here]? 1.79

1.4.s:
sarvaḥ ko'pyatihīno'pi svapūjyasyārthasādhakaḥ..
svapūjyatīrtheṣvāvāsaṃ proktavānnāradaḥ katham.. 1.80 ..
1.4.d:
सर्वः कोऽप्यतिहीनोऽपि स्वपूज्यस्यार्थसाधकः..
स्वपूज्यतीर्थेष्वावासं प्रोक्तवान्नारदः कथम्.. 1.80 ..
1.4.m: Everyone, even the most lowly, accomplishes the welfare of that which he reveres; / why did Nārada direct you to dwell in the sacred fords he reveres? 1.80

1.4.s:
tathaiva navadurgāsu satīṣvatibalāsu ca..
siddheśe siddhagaṇape cāpi vo'tra sthitiḥ katham.. 1.81 ..
1.4.d:
तथैव नवदुर्गासु सतीष्वतिबलासु च..
सिद्धेशे सिद्धगणपे चापि वोऽत्र स्थितिः कथम्.. 1.81 ..
1.4.m: Likewise, while the nine Durgās are present, exceedingly powerful, / and also Siddheśa and Siddhagaṇapa, how did you come to remain here? 1.81

1.4.s:
ekaika eṣāṃ śakto hi api devānnivāritum..
tīrthasaṃrodhakāriṇyaḥ sarvā nāvārayatkatham.. 1.82 ..
1.4.d:
एकैक एषां शक्तो हि अपि देवान्निवारितुम्..
तीर्थसंरोधकारिण्यः सर्वा नावारयत्कथम्.. 1.82 ..
1.4.m: For each one of these is able even to ward off the gods; / why did they not ward off all of you who were obstructing the sacred fords? 1.82

1.4.s:
iti ciṃtayate mahyaṃ bhṛśaṃ dolāyate manaḥ..
mahanme kautukaṃ jātaṃ satyaṃ vā vaktumarhatha.. 1.83 ..
1.4.d:
इति चिंतयते मह्यं भृशं दोलायते मनः..
महन्मे कौतुकं जातं सत्यं वा वक्तुमर्हथ.. 1.83 ..
1.4.m: As I reflect on this, my mind wavers greatly. / Great curiosity has arisen in me; you ought to speak the truth." 1.83

1.4.s:
..apsarasa ūcuḥ..
yogyaṃ pṛcchasi kaunteya punaḥ paśyottarāṃ diśam.. 1.84 ..
iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ prathame māheśvarakhaṇḍe kaumārikākhaṃḍe pārthena pañcāpsaraḥ samuddharaṇaṃnāma prathamo'dhyāyaḥ.. 1 .. cha ..
1.4.d:
..अप्सरस ऊचुः..
योग्यं पृच्छसि कौन्तेय पुनः पश्योत्तरां दिशम्.. 1.84 ..
इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां प्रथमे माहेश्वरखण्डे कौमारिकाखंडे पार्थेन पञ्चाप्सरः समुद्धरणंनाम प्रथमोऽध्यायः.. 1 .. छ ..
1.4.m:
The apsarases said: / "You ask what is fitting, O son of Kuntī; look once again toward the northern direction." 1.84
Thus ends the first chapter, named "The Deliverance of the Five Apsarases by the Son of Pṛthā," in the Kaumārikākhaṇḍa of the first [section], the Māheśvarakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.

1.4.s:
..sūta uvāca..
evaṃ sthānāni puṇyāni yāniyānīha vai bhuvi..
nirīkṣaṃstatra tatrāhaṃ nārado vīrasattama.. 3.1 ..
1.4.d:
..सूत उवाच..
एवं स्थानानि पुण्यानि यानियानीह वै भुवि..
निरीक्षंस्तत्र तत्राहं नारदो वीरसत्तम.. 3.1 ..
1.4.m: Sūta said: / "'Observing such sacred places wherever they are here on earth, / I, Nārada, O best of heroes, 3.1

1.4.s:
vicaranmedinīṃ sarvāṃ prāpto'hamāśramaṃ bhṛgoḥ..
yatra revānadī puṇyā saptakalpasmarā varā.. 3.2 ..
1.4.d:
विचरन्मेदिनीं सर्वां प्राप्तोऽहमाश्रमं भृगोः..
यत्र रेवानदी पुण्या सप्तकल्पस्मरा वरा.. 3.2 ..
1.4.m: wandering over the whole earth, arrived at the hermitage of Bhṛgu, / where the holy river Revā flows, excellent, remembering seven aeons, 3.2

1.4.s:
mahāpuṇyā pavitrā ca sarvatīrthamayī śubhā..
punāni kīrtanenaiva darśanena viśeṣataḥ.. 3.3 ..
1.4.d:
महापुण्या पवित्रा च सर्वतीर्थमयी शुभा..
पुनानि कीर्तनेनैव दर्शनेन विशेषतः.. 3.3 ..
1.4.m: greatly meritorious, pure, containing all sacred fords, auspicious. / It purifies by mere recitation of its name, and especially by sight. 3.3

1.4.s:
tatrāvagāhanātpārtha mucyate jaṃturaṃhasā..
yathā sā piṅgalā nāḍī dehamadhye vyavasthitā.. 3.4 ..
1.4.d:
तत्रावगाहनात्पार्थ मुच्यते जंतुरंहसा..
यथा सा पिङ्गला नाडी देहमध्ये व्यवस्थिता.. 3.4 ..
1.4.m: From plunging into it, O son of Pṛthā, a living creature is freed from sin. / Just as that channel called Piṅgalā is situated within the body, 3.4

1.4.s:
iyaṃ brahmāṃḍapiṇḍasya sthāne tasminprakīrtitā..
tatrāste śuklatīrthākhyaṃ revāyāṃ pāpanāśanam.. 3.5 ..
1.4.d:
इयं ब्रह्मांडपिण्डस्य स्थाने तस्मिन्प्रकीर्तिता..
तत्रास्ते शुक्लतीर्थाख्यं रेवायां पापनाशनम्.. 3.5 ..
1.4.m: so this one is celebrated in that place of the cosmic egg. / There on the Revā lies the sin-destroying sacred ford called Śuklatīrtha, 3.5

1.4.s:
yatra vai snānamātreṇa brahmahatyā praṇaśyati..
tasyāpi sannidhau pārtha revāyā uttare taṭe.. 3.6 ..
1.4.d:
यत्र वै स्नानमात्रेण ब्रह्महत्या प्रणश्यति..
तस्यापि सन्निधौ पार्थ रेवाया उत्तरे तटे.. 3.6 ..
1.4.m: where, by mere bathing, the sin of killing a brahmin is destroyed. / Near that as well, O son of Pṛthā, on the northern bank of the Revā, 3.6

1.4.s:
nānāvṛkṣasamākīrṇaṃ latāgulmopaśobhitam..
nānāpuṣpaphalo petaṃ kadalīkhaṃḍamaṃḍitam.. 3.7 ..
1.4.d:
नानावृक्षसमाकीर्णं लतागुल्मोपशोभितम्..
नानापुष्पफलो पेतं कदलीखंडमंडितम्.. 3.7 ..
1.4.m: abounding in various trees, adorned with creepers and shrubs, / endowed with various flowers and fruits, adorned with groves of plantains, 3.7

1.4.s:
anekāśvāpadākīrṇaṃ vihagairanunāditam..
sugaṃdhapuṣpaśobhāḍhyaṃ mayūraravanāditam.. 3.8 ..
1.4.d:
अनेकाश्वापदाकीर्णं विहगैरनुनादितम्..
सुगंधपुष्पशोभाढ्यं मयूररवनादितम्.. 3.8 ..
1.4.m: crowded with many wild beasts, resounding with birds, / rich in the beauty of fragrant flowers, echoing with the calls of peacocks, 3.8

1.4.s:
bhramaraiḥ sarvamutsṛjya nilīnaṃ rāvasaṃyutam..
yathā saṃsāramutsṛjya bhaktena harapādayoḥ.. 3.9 ..
1.4.d:
भ्रमरैः सर्वमुत्सृज्य निलीनं रावसंयुतम्..
यथा संसारमुत्सृज्य भक्तेन हरपादयोः.. 3.9 ..
1.4.m: clinging with buzzing sounds, leaving everything else behind, by bees— / just as worldly existence is abandoned by a devotee at the feet of Hara— 3.9

1.4.s:
kokilā madhuraiḥ svānairnādayaṃti tathā munīn..
yathā kathāmṛtākhyānairbrāhmaṇā bhavabhīrukān.. 3.10 ..
1.4.d:
कोकिला मधुरैः स्वानैर्नादयंति तथा मुनीन्..
यथा कथामृताख्यानैर्ब्राह्मणा भवभीरुकान्.. 3.10 ..
1.4.m: where cuckoos make the sages resound with their sweet cries, / just as brahmins cause those afraid of worldly existence to resound with nectar-like discourses and narratives, 3.10

1.4.s:
yatra vṛkṣā hlādayaṃti phalaiḥ puṣpaiśca patrakaiḥ..
chāyābhirapi kāṣṭhaiśca lokāniva haravratāḥ.. 3.11 ..
1.4.d:
यत्र वृक्षा ह्लादयंति फलैः पुष्पैश्च पत्रकैः..
छायाभिरपि काष्ठैश्च लोकानिव हरव्रताः.. 3.11 ..
1.4.m: where the trees gladden the people with fruits, flowers, and leaves, / as well as shade and timber, like those devoted to Hara, 3.11

1.4.s:
putraputreti vāśaṃte yatra putrapriyāḥ khagāḥ..
yathā śivapriyāḥ śaivā nityaṃ śivaśiveti ca.. 3.12 ..
1.4.d:
पुत्रपुत्रेति वाशंते यत्र पुत्रप्रियाः खगाः..
यथा शिवप्रियाः शैवा नित्यं शिवशिवेति च.. 3.12 ..
1.4.m: where birds affectionate to their offspring cry 'Son, son!', / just as Śaivas devoted to Śiva continually cry 'Śiva, Śiva!', 3.12

1.4.s:
evaṃvidhaṃ munestasya bhṛgorāśramamaṃḍalam..
vipraistraividyasaṃyuktaiḥ sarvataḥ samalaṃkṛtam.. 3.13 ..
1.4.d:
एवंविधं मुनेस्तस्य भृगोराश्रममंडलम्..
विप्रैस्त्रैविद्यसंयुक्तैः सर्वतः समलंकृतम्.. 3.13 ..
1.4.m: such was the circle of the hermitage of that sage Bhṛgu, / adorned on all sides by brahmins endowed with the three Vedas, 3.13

1.4.s:
ṛgyajuḥ sāmanirghopairārūritadigantaram..
rudrabhaktena dhīreṇa yathaiva bhuvanatrayam.. 3.14 ..
1.4.d:
ऋग्यजुः सामनिर्घोपैरारूरितदिगन्तरम्..
रुद्रभक्तेन धीरेण यथैव भुवनत्रयम्.. 3.14 ..
1.4.m: filling the quarters of the sky with the resonant chanting of Ṛg, Yajus, and Sāman, / just as the three worlds are filled by a steadfast devotee of Rudra. 3.14

1.4.s:
tatrāhaṃ pārtha saṃprāpto yatrāste munisattamaḥ..
bhṛguḥ paramadharmātmātapasā dyotitaprabhaḥ.. 3.15 ..
1.4.d:
तत्राहं पार्थ संप्राप्तो यत्रास्ते मुनिसत्तमः..
भृगुः परमधर्मात्मातपसा द्योतितप्रभः.. 3.15 ..
1.4.m: There I arrived, O son of Pṛthā, where the best of sages dwells, / Bhṛgu, supreme in righteousness, his splendor illuminated by austerity. 3.15

1.4.s:
āgacchaṃtaṃ tu māṃ dṛṣṭvā dīnaṃ ca muditaṃ tathā..
abhyutthānaṃ kṛtaṃ sarvairviprairbhṛgupurogamaiḥ.. 3.16 ..
1.4.d:
आगच्छंतं तु मां दृष्ट्वा दीनं च मुदितं तथा..
अभ्युत्थानं कृतं सर्वैर्विप्रैर्भृगुपुरोगमैः.. 3.16 ..
1.4.m: Seeing me arriving, both distressed and joyful, / all the brahmins led by Bhṛgu rose up in respect. 3.16

1.4.s:
kṛtvā susvāgataṃ dattvā arghādyaṃ bhṛguṇā saha..
āsaneṣūpaviṣṭāste munīṃdrā grāhitā mayā.. 3.17 ..
1.4.d:
कृत्वा सुस्वागतं दत्त्वा अर्घाद्यं भृगुणा सह..
आसनेषूपविष्टास्ते मुनींद्रा ग्राहिता मया.. 3.17 ..
1.4.m: Having offered a gracious welcome and given water offerings and the rest along with Bhṛgu, / those foremost sages were seated on seats provided by me. 3.17

1.4.s:
viśrāṃtaṃ tu tato jñātvā bhṛgurmāmapyuvācaha..
kva gaṃtavyaṃ muniśreṣṭha kasmādiha samāgataḥ.. 3.18 ..
1.4.d:
विश्रांतं तु ततो ज्ञात्वा भृगुर्मामप्युवाचह..
क्व गंतव्यं मुनिश्रेष्ठ कस्मादिह समागतः.. 3.18 ..
1.4.m: Knowing that I was rested, Bhṛgu then spoke to me: / 'Where are you going, O best of sages? Why have you come here? 3.18

1.4.s:
āgamanakāraṇaṃ sarvaṃ samācakṣva parisphuṭam..
tatastaṃ ciṃtayāviṣṭo bhṛguṃ pārthāhamabruvam.. 3.19 ..
1.4.d:
आगमनकारणं सर्वं समाचक्ष्व परिस्फुटम्..
ततस्तं चिंतयाविष्टो भृगुं पार्थाहमब्रुवम्.. 3.19 ..
1.4.m: Explain clearly the entire reason for your coming.' / Then, filled with thought, O son of Pṛthā, I said to Bhṛgu: 3.19

1.4.s:
śrūyatāmabhidhāsyāmi yadarthamahāmāgataḥ..
mayā paryaṭitā sarvā samudrāṃtā ca medinī.. 3.20 ..
1.4.d:
श्रूयतामभिधास्यामि यदर्थमहामागतः..
मया पर्यटिता सर्वा समुद्रांता च मेदिनी.. 3.20 ..
1.4.m: 'Listen, I shall declare the purpose for which I have come. / The entire earth bounded by the oceans has been traversed by me. 3.20

1.4.s:
dvijānāṃ bhūmidānārthaṃ mārgamāṇaḥ padepade..
nirdoṣāṃ ca pavitrāṃ ca tīrtheṣvapi samanvitām.. 3.21 ..
1.4.d:
द्विजानां भूमिदानार्थं मार्गमाणः पदेपदे..
निर्दोषां च पवित्रां च तीर्थेष्वपि समन्विताम्.. 3.21 ..
1.4.m: seeking at every step to make a gift of land to brahmins, / [a land] faultless, pure, and endowed even among sacred fords.

1.4.s:
ramyāṃ manoramāṃ bhūmiṃ na paśyāmi kathaṃcana..
..bhṛguruvāca..
viprāṇāṃ sthāpanārthāya mayāpi bhramatā purā.. 3.22 ..
1.4.d:
रम्यां मनोरमां भूमिं न पश्यामि कथंचन..
..भृगुरुवाच..
विप्राणां स्थापनार्थाय मयापि भ्रमता पुरा.. 3.22 ..
1.4.m:
I do not see anywhere a charming and pleasing land."
Bhṛgu said:
"Formerly, while wandering about to establish brahmins,

1.4.s:
pṛthvī sāgaraparyaṃtā dṛṣṭā sarvā tadānagha..
mahīnāma nadī puṇyā sarvatīrthamayī śubhā.. 3.23 ..
1.4.d:
पृथ्वी सागरपर्यंता दृष्टा सर्वा तदानघ..
महीनाम नदी पुण्या सर्वतीर्थमयी शुभा.. 3.23 ..
1.4.m: the whole earth bounded by the ocean was seen by me, O sinless one. / There is an auspicious, holy river named Mahī, embodying all sacred fords,

1.4.s:
divyā manoramā saumyā mahāpāpapraṇāśinī..
nadīrūpeṇa tatraiva pṛthvī sā nātra saṃśayaḥ.. 3.24 ..
1.4.d:
दिव्या मनोरमा सौम्या महापापप्रणाशिनी..
नदीरूपेण तत्रैव पृथ्वी सा नात्र संशयः.. 3.24 ..
1.4.m: divine, pleasing, gentle, destroying great sins. / In the form of a river, the earth herself is there without doubt.

1.4.s:
pṛthivyāṃ yāni tīrthāni dṛṣṭādṛṣṭāni nārada..
tāni sarvāṇi tatraiva nivasaṃti mahījale.. 3.25 ..
1.4.d:
पृथिव्यां यानि तीर्थानि दृष्टादृष्टानि नारद..
तानि सर्वाणि तत्रैव निवसंति महीजले.. 3.25 ..
1.4.m: Whatever sacred fords there are on the earth, visible and invisible, O Nārada, / all of them dwell right there in the waters of the Mahī.

1.4.s:
sā samudreṇa saṃprāptā puṇyatoyā mahānadī..
saṃjātastatra devarṣe mahīsāgarasaṃgamaḥ.. 3.26 ..
1.4.d:
सा समुद्रेण संप्राप्ता पुण्यतोया महानदी..
संजातस्तत्र देवर्षे महीसागरसंगमः.. 3.26 ..
1.4.m: That great river of holy water joined the ocean; / there, O divine seer, the confluence of the Mahī and the ocean was formed.

1.4.s:
staṃbhākhyaṃ tatra tīrthaṃ tu triṣu lokeṣu viśrutam..
tatra ye manujāḥ snānaṃ prakurvaṃti vipaścitaḥ.. 3.27 ..
1.4.d:
स्तंभाख्यं तत्र तीर्थं तु त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतम्..
तत्र ये मनुजाः स्नानं प्रकुर्वंति विपश्चितः.. 3.27 ..
1.4.m: The sacred ford there called Stambha is famed throughout the three worlds. / The wise men who take a ritual ablution there,

1.4.s:
sarvapāpavinirmuktā nopasarpaṃti vai yamam..
tatrādbhutaṃ hi dṛṣṭaṃ me purā snātuṃ gatena vai.. 3.28 ..
1.4.d:
सर्वपापविनिर्मुक्ता नोपसर्पंति वै यमम्..
तत्राद्भुतं हि दृष्टं मे पुरा स्नातुं गतेन वै.. 3.28 ..
1.4.m: completely freed from all sins, indeed do not approach Yama. / For a wonder was seen there by me in the past, having gone to bathe.

1.4.s:
tadahaṃ kīrtayiṣyāmi mune śrṛṇu mahādbhutam..
yāvatsnātuṃ vrajāmyasminmahīsāgarasaṃgame.. 3.29 ..
1.4.d:
तदहं कीर्तयिष्यामि मुने श्रृणु महाद्भुतम्..
यावत्स्नातुं व्रजाम्यस्मिन्महीसागरसंगमे.. 3.29 ..
1.4.m: I shall recount that great wonder to you, O sage; listen! / As I was going to bathe at this confluence of the Mahī and the ocean,

1.4.s:
tīre sthitaṃ prapaśyāmi munīṃdraṃ pāvakopamam..
prāṃśuṃ vṛddhaṃ cāsthiśeṣaṃ tapolakṣmyā vibhūṣitam.. 3.30 ..
1.4.d:
तीरे स्थितं प्रपश्यामि मुनींद्रं पावकोपमम्..
प्रांशुं वृद्धं चास्थिशेषं तपोलक्ष्म्या विभूषितम्.. 3.30 ..
1.4.m: I saw an eminent sage resembling fire standing on the bank, / tall, old, reduced to mere bones, adorned with the splendor of austerity,

1.4.s:
bhujāvūrdhvau tataḥ kṛtvā prarudaṃtaṃ muhurmuhuḥ..
taṃ tathā duḥkhitaṃ dṛṣṭvā duḥkhito'hamathābhavam.. 3.31 ..
1.4.d:
भुजावूर्ध्वौ ततः कृत्वा प्ररुदंतं मुहुर्मुहुः..
तं तथा दुःखितं दृष्ट्वा दुःखितोऽहमथाभवम्.. 3.31 ..
1.4.m: raising both his arms and weeping repeatedly. / Seeing him so afflicted, I then became distressed.

1.4.s:
satāṃ lakṣaṇametaddhi yaddṛṣṭvā duḥkhitaṃ janam..
śatasaṃkhya tasya bhavettathāhaṃ vilalāpa ha.. 3.32 ..
1.4.d:
सतां लक्षणमेतद्धि यद्दृष्ट्वा दुःखितं जनम्..
शतसंख्य तस्य भवेत्तथाहं विललाप ह.. 3.32 ..
1.4.m: For this is the mark of the virtuous: seeing a person who is afflicted, / his [affliction] becomes a hundredfold; likewise, I lamented.

1.4.s:
ahiṃsā satyamasteyaṃ mānuṣye sati durlabham..
tatastamupasaṃgamya paryapṛcchamahaṃ tadā.. 3.33 ..
1.4.d:
अहिंसा सत्यमस्तेयं मानुष्ये सति दुर्लभम्..
ततस्तमुपसंगम्य पर्यपृच्छमहं तदा.. 3.33 ..
1.4.m: Non-violence, truth, non-stealing—these are difficult to attain in human existence. / Then, approaching him, I questioned him at that time:

1.4.s:
kimarthaṃ rodiśi mune śoke kiṃ kāraṇaṃ tava..
suguhyamapi cedbūhi jijñāsā mahatī hi me.. 3.34 ..
1.4.d:
किमर्थं रोदिशि मुने शोके किं कारणं तव..
सुगुह्यमपि चेद्बूहि जिज्ञासा महती हि मे.. 3.34 ..
1.4.m: "Why are you weeping, O sage? What is the cause of your sorrow? / Even if it is a great secret, speak, for my curiosity is great."

1.4.s:
munistato māmavadadbhṛgo nirbhāgyavānaham..
tena rodimi mā pṛccha durbhāgyaṃ cālapeddhi kaḥ.. 3.35 ..
1.4.d:
मुनिस्ततो मामवदद्भृगो निर्भाग्यवानहम्..
तेन रोदिमि मा पृच्छ दुर्भाग्यं चालपेद्धि कः.. 3.35 ..
1.4.m: The sage then said to me, "O Bhṛgu, I am unfortunate; / therefore I weep. Do not ask me, for who would speak of his misfortune?"

1.4.s:
tamahaṃ vismayāviṣṭaḥ punarevedamabruvam..
durlabhaṃ bhārate janma tatrāpi ca manuṣyatā.. 3.36 ..
1.4.d:
तमहं विस्मयाविष्टः पुनरेवेदमब्रुवम्..
दुर्लभं भारते जन्म तत्रापि च मनुष्यता.. 3.36 ..
1.4.m: Filled with astonishment, I spoke to him yet again: / "Birth in Bhārata is hard to attain, and even there, human state is hard to attain.

1.4.s:
manuṣyatve brāhmaṇatvaṃ munitvaṃ tatra durlabham..
tatrāpi ca tapaḥsiddhiḥ prāpyaitatpaṃcakaṃ param.. 3.37 ..
1.4.d:
मनुष्यत्वे ब्राह्मणत्वं मुनित्वं तत्र दुर्लभम्..
तत्रापि च तपःसिद्धिः प्राप्यैतत्पंचकं परम्.. 3.37 ..
1.4.m: Among humans, the state of a brahmin is rare, and the state of a sage is rare therein; / even there, accomplishment in austerity is rare. Having attained these supreme five,

1.4.s:
kimarthaṃ rodiṣi mune vismayo'tra mahānmama..
evaṃ saṃpṛcchate mahyametasminneva cāṃtare.. 3.38 ..
1.4.d:
किमर्थं रोदिषि मुने विस्मयोऽत्र महान्मम..
एवं संपृच्छते मह्यमेतस्मिन्नेव चांतरे.. 3.38 ..
1.4.m: why are you weeping, O sage? There is great amazement in me regarding this." / As I was questioning him in this manner, in that very interval,

1.4.s:
subhadronāma nāmnā ca munistatrābhyupāyayau..
sa hi meruṃ parityajya jñātvā tīrthasya sāratām.. 3.39 ..
1.4.d:
सुभद्रोनाम नाम्ना च मुनिस्तत्राभ्युपाययौ..
स हि मेरुं परित्यज्य ज्ञात्वा तीर्थस्य सारताम्.. 3.39 ..
1.4.m: a sage named Subhadra came there. / Having abandoned Mount Meru upon knowing the essential worth of the sacred ford,

1.4.s:
kṛtāśramaḥ pūjayati sadā staṃbheśvaraṃ muniḥ..
so'pyevaṃ māmi vāpṛcchanmuniṃ rodanakāraṇam.. 3.40 ..
1.4.d:
कृताश्रमः पूजयति सदा स्तंभेश्वरं मुनिः..
सोऽप्येवं मामि वापृच्छन्मुनिं रोदनकारणम्.. 3.40 ..
1.4.m: having established a hermitage, that sage perpetually worships Stambheśvara. / He too asked the weeping sage about the cause of his weeping, just as I did.

1.4.s:
athāhācamya sa muniḥ śrūyatāṃ kāraṇaṃ munī..
ahaṃ hi devaśarmākhyo muniḥ saṃyatavāṅmanāḥ.. 3.41 ..
1.4.d:
अथाहाचम्य स मुनिः श्रूयतां कारणं मुनी..
अहं हि देवशर्माख्यो मुनिः संयतवाङ्मनाः.. 3.41 ..
1.4.m: Then, having sipped water, that sage said: "Listen to the reason, O two sages! / I am indeed a sage named Devaśarman, with restrained speech and mind.

1.4.s:
nivasāmi kṛtasthāno gaṃgāsāgarasaṃgame..
tatra darśetarpayāmi sadaiva ca pitṝnaham.. 3.42 ..
1.4.d:
निवसामि कृतस्थानो गंगासागरसंगमे..
तत्र दर्शेतर्पयामि सदैव च पितॄनहम्.. 3.42 ..
1.4.m: I dwell, having made my abode, at the confluence of the Gaṅgā and the ocean. / There, on every new-moon day, I always offer libations to the ancestors.

1.4.s:
śrāddhāṃte te ca pratyakṣā hyāśiṣo me vadaṃti ca..
tataḥ kadācitpitaraḥ prahṛṣṭā māmathābravan.. 3.43 ..
1.4.d:
श्राद्धांते ते च प्रत्यक्षा ह्याशिषो मे वदंति च..
ततः कदाचित्पितरः प्रहृष्टा मामथाब्रवन्.. 3.43 ..
1.4.m: At the end of the ancestral rite, they appear visibly and utter blessings to me. / Then, one day, the ancestors, being delighted, said to me:

1.4.s:
vayaṃ sadātra cāyāmo devaśarmaṃstavāṃtike..
sthāne'smākaṃ kadācittvaṃ na cāyāsi kutaḥ sutaḥ.. 3.44 ..
1.4.d:
वयं सदात्र चायामो देवशर्मंस्तवांतिके..
स्थानेऽस्माकं कदाचित्त्वं न चायासि कुतः सुतः.. 3.44 ..
1.4.m: 'We always come here into your presence, O Devaśarman; / why, O son, do you never come to our abode?'

1.4.s:
sthānaṃ didṛkṣustaccāhaṃ na śakto'smi nivoditum..
tataḥ paramamityuktvā gatavānpitṛbhiḥ saha.. 3.45 ..
1.4.d:
स्थानं दिदृक्षुस्तच्चाहं न शक्तोऽस्मि निवोदितुम्..
ततः परममित्युक्त्वा गतवान्पितृभिः सह.. 3.45 ..
1.4.m: Desiring to see that place, I was not able to comprehend it. / Then, saying 'Very well,' I went along with the ancestors

1.4.s:
pitṝṇāṃ maṃdiraṃ puṇyaṃ bhaumalokasamāsthitam..
tatratatra sthitaścāhaṃ tejomaṇḍaladurdṛśān.. 3.46 ..
1.4.d:
पितॄणां मंदिरं पुण्यं भौमलोकसमास्थितम्..
तत्रतत्र स्थितश्चाहं तेजोमण्डलदुर्दृशान्.. 3.46 ..
1.4.m: to the holy abode of the ancestors situated in the terrestrial world. / Standing here and there, seeing [beings] in front who were difficult to look upon due to a circle of light,

1.4.s:
dṛṣṭvāgrataḥ pūjayāḍhyānapṛcchaṃ svānpitṝniti..
ke hyamī samupāyāṃti bhṛśaṃ tṛptā bhṛśārcitāḥ..
bhṛśaṃpramuditā naiva tathā yūyaṃ yathā hyamī.. 3.47 ..
1.4.d:
दृष्ट्वाग्रतः पूजयाढ्यानपृच्छं स्वान्पितॄनिति..
के ह्यमी समुपायांति भृशं तृप्ता भृशार्चिताः..
भृशंप्रमुदिता नैव तथा यूयं यथा ह्यमी.. 3.47 ..
1.4.m: and richly honored with worship, I asked my ancestors: / 'Who are these arriving, extremely satisfied, greatly worshipped, / and exceedingly rejoiced, unlike you who are not so as these are?'

1.4.s:
..pitara ūcuḥ..
bhadraṃ te pitaraḥ puṇyāḥ subhadrasya mahāmuneḥ..
tarpitāstena muninā mahīsāgarasaṃgame.. 3.48 ..
1.4.d:
..पितर ऊचुः..
भद्रं ते पितरः पुण्याः सुभद्रस्य महामुनेः..
तर्पितास्तेन मुनिना महीसागरसंगमे.. 3.48 ..
1.4.m: The ancestors said: / 'May all be well with you! These are the holy ancestors of the great sage Subhadra. / They were offered libations by that sage at the confluence of the Mahī and the ocean,

1.4.s:
sarvatīrthamayī yatra nilīnā hyudadhau mahī..
tatra darśe tarpayati subhadrastānamūnsuta.. 3.49 ..
1.4.d:
सर्वतीर्थमयी यत्र निलीना ह्युदधौ मही..
तत्र दर्शे तर्पयति सुभद्रस्तानमून्सुत.. 3.49 ..
1.4.m: where the Mahī, which embodies all sacred fords, merges into the ocean. / There, on the new-moon day, Subhadra offers libations to them, O son.'

1.4.s:
ityākarṇya vacasteṣāṃ lajjito'haṃ bhṛśaṃtadā..
vismitaśca praṇamyaitānpitṝnsvaṃ sthānamāgataḥ.. 3.50 ..
1.4.d:
इत्याकर्ण्य वचस्तेषां लज्जितोऽहं भृशंतदा..
विस्मितश्च प्रणम्यैतान्पितॄन्स्वं स्थानमागतः.. 3.50 ..
1.4.m: Hearing their words, I was then greatly ashamed / and astonished. Having bowed to those ancestors, I returned to my own place.

1.4.s:
yathā tathā ciṃtitaṃ ca tatra yāsyāmyahaṃ śphuṭam..
puṇyo yatrāpi vikhyāto mahīsāgarasaṃgamaḥ.. 3.51 ..
1.4.d:
यथा तथा चिंतितं च तत्र यास्याम्यहं श्फुटम्..
पुण्यो यत्रापि विख्यातो महीसागरसंगमः.. 3.51 ..
1.4.m: Somehow I resolved: 'I will certainly go there, / where the holy confluence of the Mahī and the ocean is celebrated.

1.4.s:
kṛtāśramaśca tatraiva tarpayiṣye nijānpitṝn..
darśedarśe yathā cāsau stutyanāmā subhadrakaḥ.. 3.52 ..
1.4.d:
कृताश्रमश्च तत्रैव तर्पयिष्ये निजान्पितॄन्..
दर्शेदर्शे यथा चासौ स्तुत्यनामा सुभद्रकः.. 3.52 ..
1.4.m: Having established a hermitage right there, I will offer libations to my own ancestors / on each new-moon day, just like that Subhadra of praiseworthy name.

1.4.s:
kiṃ tena nanu jātena kulāṃgāreṇa pāpinā..
yasmiñjīvatyavi nijāḥ pitaro'nyaspṛhākarāḥ.. 3.53 ..
1.4.d:
किं तेन ननु जातेन कुलांगारेण पापिना..
यस्मिञ्जीवत्यवि निजाः पितरोऽन्यस्पृहाकराः.. 3.53 ..
1.4.m: What is the use of the birth of that sinner, a coal to his lineage, / while living, his own ancestors long for someone else?'

1.4.s:
iti saṃciṃtya mudito ruciṃ bhāryāmathābravum..
ruce tvayā samāyukto mahīsāgagarasaṃgamam.. 3.54 ..
1.4.d:
इति संचिंत्य मुदितो रुचिं भार्यामथाब्रवुम्..
रुचे त्वया समायुक्तो महीसागगरसंगमम्.. 3.54 ..
1.4.m: Reflecting thus, I said with delight to my wife Ruci: / 'O Ruci, accompanied by you to the confluence of the Mahī and the ocean,

1.4.s:
gatvā sthāsyāmi tatraiva śīghraṃ tvaṃ sammukhībhava..
pativratāsi śuddhāsikulīnāsi yaśasvini..
tasmādetanmama śubhe kartumarhasi ciṃtitam.. 3.55 ..
1.4.d:
गत्वा स्थास्यामि तत्रैव शीघ्रं त्वं सम्मुखीभव..
पतिव्रतासि शुद्धासिकुलीनासि यशस्विनि..
तस्मादेतन्मम शुभे कर्तुमर्हसि चिंतितम्.. 3.55 ..
1.4.m: having gone, I shall dwell right there; quickly prepare yourself! / You are devoted to your husband, pure, noble-born, and renowned; / therefore, O auspicious woman, you ought to carry out this plan of mine.'

1.4.s:
..ruciruvāca..
hatā tasya janirnābhūtkathaṃ pāpa durātmanā.. 3.56 ..
1.4.d:
..रुचिरुवाच..
हता तस्य जनिर्नाभूत्कथं पाप दुरात्मना.. 3.56 ..
1.4.m: Ruci said: / 'Why was the birth of that wicked soul not destroyed, O sinner,

1.4.s:
śmaśānastaṃbha yenāhaṃ dattā tubhyaṃ kṛtaṃtvāya..
iha kaṃdaphalāhārairyatkiṃ tena na pūryate.. 3.57 ..
1.4.d:
श्मशानस्तंभ येनाहं दत्ता तुभ्यं कृतंत्वाय..
इह कंदफलाहारैर्यत्किं तेन न पूर्यते.. 3.57 ..
1.4.m: O pillar of the cremation ground, by whom I was given to you, like [an offering to] Yama? / With the diet of roots and fruits here, what is not satisfied?

1.4.s:
netumicchasi māṃ tatra yatra kṣārodakaṃ sadā..
tvameva tatra saṃyāhi naṃdaṃtu tava pūrvajāḥ.. 3.58 ..
1.4.d:
नेतुमिच्छसि मां तत्र यत्र क्षारोदकं सदा..
त्वमेव तत्र संयाहि नंदंतु तव पूर्वजाः.. 3.58 ..
1.4.m: You wish to take me there, where there is constantly salt water! / You go there alone; let your ancestors rejoice!

1.4.s:
gaccha vā tiṣṭha vā vṛddha vasa vā kākavacciram..
tathā bruvantyāṃ tasyāṃ tu karṇāvasmi pidhāya ca.. 3.59 ..
1.4.d:
गच्छ वा तिष्ठ वा वृद्ध वस वा काकवच्चिरम्..
तथा ब्रुवन्त्यां तस्यां तु कर्णावस्मि पिधाय च.. 3.59 ..
1.4.m: Go, or stay, O old man, or live for a long time like a crow!' / While she was speaking thus, having covered my ears,

1.4.s:
vipulaṃ śiṣyamādiśya gṛha eko'tra āgataḥ..
so'haṃ snātvātra saṃtarpya pitṝñchraddhāparāyaṇaḥ.. 3.60 ..
1.4.d:
विपुलं शिष्यमादिश्य गृह एकोऽत्र आगतः..
सोऽहं स्नात्वात्र संतर्प्य पितॄञ्छ्रद्धापरायणः.. 3.60 ..
1.4.m: having instructed my disciple Vipula regarding the house, I came here alone. / Having bathed here and offered libations to the ancestors with devotion,

1.4.s:
ciṃtāṃ suvipulāṃ prāpto narake duṣkṛtī yathā..
yadi tiṣṭhāmi cātraiva ardhadehadharo hyaham.. 3.61 ..
1.4.d:
चिंतां सुविपुलां प्राप्तो नरके दुष्कृती यथा..
यदि तिष्ठामि चात्रैव अर्धदेहधरो ह्यहम्.. 3.61 ..
1.4.m: I fell into very deep anxiety, like an evil-doer in hell. / If I remain right here, I possess only half a body.

1.4.s:
naro hi gṛhiṇīhīno ardhadeha iti smṛtaḥ..
yathātmanā vinā dehe kāryaṃ kiṃcinna sidhyati.. 3.62 ..
1.4.d:
नरो हि गृहिणीहीनो अर्धदेह इति स्मृतः..
यथात्मना विना देहे कार्यं किंचिन्न सिध्यति.. 3.62 ..
1.4.m: For a man destitute of a wife is remembered as having half a body. / Just as in the body no action succeeds without the self,

1.4.s:
anayorhi phalaṃ grāhyaṃ sāratā nātra kācana..
ardhadehī ca manujastvasaṃspṛśyaḥ satāṃmataḥ.. 3.63 ..
1.4.d:
अनयोर्हि फलं ग्राह्यं सारता नात्र काचन..
अर्धदेही च मनुजस्त्वसंस्पृश्यः सतांमतः.. 3.63 ..
1.4.m: the fruit is to be obtained from both of them; there is no substance here without it. / And a man with only half a body is considered untouchable by the virtuous.

1.4.s:
anayorhiphalaṃ grāhyaṃ sāratā nātra kācana..
ardhadehī ca manujastvasaṃspṛśyaḥ satāṃmataḥ.. 3.64 ..
1.4.d:
अनयोर्हिफलं ग्राह्यं सारता नात्र काचन..
अर्धदेही च मनुजस्त्वसंस्पृश्यः सतांमतः.. 3.64 ..
1.4.m:
Indeed, the fruit of both must be taken; there is no essential difference here.
And a man of half a body is considered untouchable by the virtuous.

1.4.s:
auttānapādiraspṛśya uttamo hi suraiḥ kṛtaḥ..
atha cettatra saṃyāmi na mahīsāgarastataḥ.. 3.65 ..
1.4.d:
औत्तानपादिरस्पृश्य उत्तमो हि सुरैः कृतः..
अथ चेत्तत्र संयामि न महीसागरस्ततः.. 3.65 ..
1.4.m:
Auttānapādi, though untouchable, was made foremost by the gods.
Now if I go there, Mahīsāgara will not be [visited] from there.

1.4.s:
yāmi vā tatkathaṃ pādau calato me kathaṃcana..
etasminme mano viddhaṃ khidyate'jñānasaṃkaṭe.. 3.66 ..
1.4.d:
यामि वा तत्कथं पादौ चलतो मे कथंचन..
एतस्मिन्मे मनो विद्धं खिद्यतेऽज्ञानसंकटे.. 3.66 ..
1.4.m:
Or how shall I go? In what way can my feet move at all?
Pierced by this, my mind grieves in this crisis of ignorance.

1.4.s:
ato'hamatimuhyāmi bhṛśaṃ śocāmi rodimi..
itiśrutvā vacastasya bhṛśaṃ romāṃcapūritam.. 3.67 ..
1.4.d:
अतोऽहमतिमुह्यामि भृशं शोचामि रोदिमि..
इतिश्रुत्वा वचस्तस्य भृशं रोमांचपूरितम्.. 3.67 ..
1.4.m:
Therefore I am utterly bewildered, I grieve exceedingly, I weep.'
Hearing his words, my hair was thrilled with goosebumps.

1.4.s:
sādhusādhvityathovāca taṃ subhadro'pyahaṃ tathā..
daṇḍavacca praṇamito mahīsāgarasaṅgamam.. 3.68 ..
1.4.d:
साधुसाध्वित्यथोवाच तं सुभद्रोऽप्यहं तथा..
दण्डवच्च प्रणमितो महीसागरसङ्गमम्.. 3.68 ..
1.4.m:
Then Subhadra as well as I said to him, 'Well done, well done!'
And having bowed down like a staff to the confluence of the Mahī and the ocean,

1.4.s:
cintayāvaśca manasi pratīkāraṃ munerubhau..
yo hi mānuṣyamāsādya jalabudbudabhaṃguram.. 3.69 ..
1.4.d:
चिन्तयावश्च मनसि प्रतीकारं मुनेरुभौ..
यो हि मानुष्यमासाद्य जलबुद्बुदभंगुरम्.. 3.69 ..
1.4.m:
We both pondered in our minds a remedy for the sage.
'For that person who, having attained human birth, which is fleeting like a water bubble,

1.4.s:
parārthāya bhavatyeṣa puruṣo'nye purīṣakāḥ..
tataḥ saṃciṃtya prāhedaṃ subhadro munisattamam.. 3.70 ..
1.4.d:
परार्थाय भवत्येष पुरुषोऽन्ये पुरीषकाः..
ततः संचिंत्य प्राहेदं सुभद्रो मुनिसत्तमम्.. 3.70 ..
1.4.m:
Exists for the sake of others, is truly a man; others are merely excrement.'
Then, having reflected thus, Subhadra said this to the best of sages:

1.4.s:
mā mune parikhidyasva devaśarmansthiro bhava..
ahaṃ te nāśayiṣyāmi śokaṃ sūryastamo yathā.. 3.71 ..
1.4.d:
मा मुने परिखिद्यस्व देवशर्मन्स्थिरो भव..
अहं ते नाशयिष्यामि शोकं सूर्यस्तमो यथा.. 3.71 ..
1.4.m:
'Do not grieve, O sage Devaśarman; be firm.
I shall dispel your sorrow just as the sun [dispels] darkness.

1.4.s:
gamiṣyāmyāśramaṃ tvaṃ ca nātrāpi parihāsyate..
śrṛṇu tatkāraṇaṃ tubhyaṃ tarpayiṣye pitṝnaham.. 3.72 ..
1.4.d:
गमिष्याम्याश्रमं त्वं च नात्रापि परिहास्यते..
श्रृणु तत्कारणं तुभ्यं तर्पयिष्ये पितॄनहम्.. 3.72 ..
1.4.m:
I shall go to the hermitage, and you will not suffer neglect here either.
Hear the reason for that: I shall offer satiation to the ancestors for you.'

1.4.s:
..devaśarmovāca..
evaṃ te vadamānasya āyurastu śataṃ samāḥ..
yadaśakyaṃ mahatkarma kartumicchasi matkṛte.. 3.73 ..
1.4.d:
..देवशर्मोवाच..
एवं ते वदमानस्य आयुरस्तु शतं समाः..
यदशक्यं महत्कर्म कर्तुमिच्छसि मत्कृते.. 3.73 ..
1.4.m:
Devaśarman said:
'May your life endure for a hundred years as you speak thus,
Since you wish to perform a great deed, impossible [for others], for my sake.

1.4.s:
harṣasthāne viṣādaśca punarmāṃ bādhate śrṛṇu..
api vākyaṃ śubhaṃ santo na gṛhṇanti mudhā mune.. 3.74 ..
1.4.d:
हर्षस्थाने विषादश्च पुनर्मां बाधते श्रृणु..
अपि वाक्यं शुभं सन्तो न गृह्णन्ति मुधा मुने.. 3.74 ..
1.4.m:
Yet in this occasion for joy, dejection troubles me once again; hear [why]:
Even auspicious words the good do not accept in vain, O sage.

1.4.s:
kathametanmahatkarma kārayāmi mudhāvada..
punaḥ kiṃcitpravakṣyāmi yathā me niṣkṛtirbhavet.. 3.75 ..
1.4.d:
कथमेतन्महत्कर्म कारयामि मुधावद..
पुनः किंचित्प्रवक्ष्यामि यथा मे निष्कृतिर्भवेत्.. 3.75 ..
1.4.m:
Tell me, how can I have this great deed done for nothing?
I shall say something further so that an expiation may be mine.

1.4.s:
śāpito'si mayā prāṇairyathā vacmi tathā kuru..
ahaṃ sadā kariṣyāmi darśe coddiśyate pitṝn.. 3.76 ..
1.4.d:
शापितोऽसि मया प्राणैर्यथा वच्मि तथा कुरु..
अहं सदा करिष्यामि दर्शे चोद्दिश्यते पितॄन्.. 3.76 ..
1.4.m:
You are bound by oath by my life-breaths: act as I tell you.
I shall always perform [offerings] intended for the ancestors on the new moon.

1.4.s:
śrāddhaṃ gaṃgārṇave cātra matpitṝṇāṃ tvamācara..
ahaṃ caivāpi tapasaḥ saṃcitasyāpi janmanā..
caturbhāgaṃ pradāsyāmi evamevaitadācara.. 3.77 ..
1.4.d:
श्राद्धं गंगार्णवे चात्र मत्पितॄणां त्वमाचर..
अहं चैवापि तपसः संचितस्यापि जन्मना..
चतुर्भागं प्रदास्यामि एवमेवैतदाचर.. 3.77 ..
1.4.m:
Perform the funeral rite here at the confluence of the Gaṅgā and the ocean for my ancestors,
And I shall indeed bestow a fourth part of the austerity accumulated over a lifetime.
Carry it out in this very manner.'

1.4.s:
..subhadra uvāca..
yadyevaṃ tava saṃtoṣastvevamastu munīśvara..
sādhūnāṃ ca yathā harṣastathā kāryaṃ vijānatā.. 3.78 ..
1.4.d:
..सुभद्र उवाच..
यद्येवं तव संतोषस्त्वेवमस्तु मुनीश्वर..
साधूनां च यथा हर्षस्तथा कार्यं विजानता.. 3.78 ..
1.4.m:
Subhadra said:
'If such is your satisfaction, O lord of sages, let it be so.
For one who knows should act in such a way that the good rejoice.'

1.4.s:
..bhṛguruvāca..
devaśarmā tato hṛṣṭo dattvā puṇyaṃ trivācikam..
caturthāśaṃ yayau dhāma svaṃ subhadro'pi ca sthitaḥ.. 3.79 ..
1.4.d:
..भृगुरुवाच..
देवशर्मा ततो हृष्टो दत्त्वा पुण्यं त्रिवाचिकम्..
चतुर्थाशं ययौ धाम स्वं सुभद्रोऽपि च स्थितः.. 3.79 ..
1.4.m:
Bhṛgu said:
Then, delighted, having pledged the religious merit thrice verbally,
Devaśarman gave a fourth share and departed to his abode; Subhadra too remained there.

1.4.s:
evaṃvidho nāradāsau mahī sāgarasaṃgamaḥ..
yamanusmarato mahyaṃ romāṃco'dyāpi vartate.. 3.80 ..
1.4.d:
एवंविधो नारदासौ मही सागरसंगमः..
यमनुस्मरतो मह्यं रोमांचोऽद्यापि वर्तते.. 3.80 ..
1.4.m:
Such, O Nārada, is that confluence of the Mahī and the ocean,
Remembering which my hair stands on end even today.

1.4.s:
..nārada uvāca..
iti śrutvā phālgunāhaṃ harṣagadgadayā girā..
mṛtomṛta ivā vocaṃ sādhusādhviti taṃbhṛgum.. 3.81 ..
1.4.d:
..नारद उवाच..
इति श्रुत्वा फाल्गुनाहं हर्षगद्गदया गिरा..
मृतोमृत इवा वोचं साधुसाध्विति तंभृगुम्.. 3.81 ..
1.4.m:
Nārada said:
Hearing this, O Phālguna, with a voice choked with joy,
As if a dead man had come back to life, I said to that Bhṛgu: 'Well done, well done!

1.4.s:
yūyaṃ vayaṃ gamiṣyāmo mahītīraṃ suśobhanam..
āvāmīkṣāvahe sarvaṃ sthānakaṃ tadanuttamam.. 3.82 ..
1.4.d:
यूयं वयं गमिष्यामो महीतीरं सुशोभनम्..
आवामीक्षावहे सर्वं स्थानकं तदनुत्तमम्.. 3.82 ..
1.4.m:
You and we shall go to the extremely beautiful bank of the Mahī;
Let the two of us look upon that entire unsurpassed place.'

1.4.s:
mama caivaṃ vacaḥ śrutvā bhṛguḥ saha mayayayau..
samastaṃ tu mahāpuṇyaṃ mahīkūlaṃ nirīkṣitam.. 3.83 ..
1.4.d:
मम चैवं वचः श्रुत्वा भृगुः सह मयययौ..
समस्तं तु महापुण्यं महीकूलं निरीक्षितम्.. 3.83 ..
1.4.m:
And hearing my words, Bhṛgu went together with me;
The entire greatly holy bank of the Mahī was viewed.

1.4.s:
taddṛṣṭvā cātihṛṣṭohamāsaṃ romāṃcakaṃcukaḥ..
abravaṃ muniśārdūlaṃ harṣagadgadayā girā.. 3.84 ..
1.4.d:
तद्दृष्ट्वा चातिहृष्टोहमासं रोमांचकंचुकः..
अब्रवं मुनिशार्दूलं हर्षगद्गदया गिरा.. 3.84 ..
1.4.m:
Beholding it, I was exceedingly delighted, my coat of hair standing on end;
With a voice choked with joy, I spoke to the tiger among sages:

1.4.s:
tvatprasādātkariṣyāmi bhṛgo sthānamanuttamam..
svasthānaṃ gamyatāṃ brahmannataḥ kṛtyaṃ viciṃtaye.. 3.85 ..
1.4.d:
त्वत्प्रसादात्करिष्यामि भृगो स्थानमनुत्तमम्..
स्वस्थानं गम्यतां ब्रह्मन्नतः कृत्यं विचिंतये.. 3.85 ..
1.4.m:
'By your favor, O Bhṛgu, I shall make an unsurpassed place.
Go to your own abode, O brahmin; henceforth I shall contemplate what is to be done.'

1.4.s:
evaṃ bhṛguṃ cāsmivisarjayitvā kallolakolāhalakautukītaṭe..
athopaviśyedamaciṃtayaṃ tadā kiṃ kṛtyamātmānamivaikayogī.. 3.86 ..
iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ prathame māheśvarakhaṇḍe kaumārīkākhaṃḍe nāradārjunasaṃvāde mahīsāgarasaṃgamatīrthamāhātmye tṛtīyo'dhyāyaḥ.. 3 .. cha ..
1.4.d:
एवं भृगुं चास्मिविसर्जयित्वा कल्लोलकोलाहलकौतुकीतटे..
अथोपविश्येदमचिंतयं तदा किं कृत्यमात्मानमिवैकयोगी.. 3.86 ..
इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां प्रथमे माहेश्वरखण्डे कौमारीकाखंडे नारदार्जुनसंवादे महीसागरसंगमतीर्थमाहात्म्ये तृतीयोऽध्यायः.. 3 .. छ ..
1.4.m:
Having thus dismissed Bhṛgu, on the bank charming with the uproar of billows,
Then sitting down, like a solitary yogin within his own self, I reflected: 'What is to be done?'
Thus ends the third chapter, named 'The Glorification of the Mahīsāgarasaṅgama Ford' in the dialogue between Nārada and Arjuna, in the Kaumārikākhaṇḍa of the first section, the Māheśvarakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand [verses].
